issues.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?

`26.1027.30824`, build `22943`

## What subscription do you have?

Not captured during this investigation.

## What platform is your computer?

- ChatGPT desktop on macOS, bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`
- macOS `27.0.1` (build `26A434`), Apple silicon
- `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`
- Observed on October 30, 2026; times below are Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8)

## What issue are you seeing?

Multiple Excel files get stuck when added to the chat composer. A spreadsheet thumbnail appears, but the send control keeps spinning and the message text remains in the composer. At one point the affected composer also stopped accepting typing.

The user fully quit and reopened the application. Typing then worked again, but adding Excel attachments still got stuck. The confirmed example was dragged from an existing file on the Desktop. It was not limited to dragging an attachment directly from another application.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are the steps observed in the affected local chat; reproduction with a new synthetic workbook has not yet been established.

1. Open an existing local chat.
2. Drag a saved `.xlsx` file from the Desktop into the composer.
3. Add a text request and attempt to send it.
4. Observe a spreadsheet thumbnail and a continuously spinning send control; the new request does not appear as a submitted turn.
5. Fully quit and reopen the application, then try an Excel attachment again. Typing recovers, but the attachment problem remains.

## What is the expected behavior?

The attachment becomes ready and the request can be sent, or the client presents an actionable error and restores the composer controls.

Actual: the attachment/send state remains pending without an actionable error. The user can continue work by supplying the local file path as plain text for local file access.

## Independently verified diagnostics

- The example XLSX exists and is readable: **192,743 bytes, four worksheets**. ZIP CRC validation passed.
- A complete Python read of the workbook finished in under 0.1 seconds. Import with the bundled spreadsheet tooling completed in approximately 914 ms, with inspection complete by 924 ms. Neither check hung.
- The Desktop copy and the copies received through the messaging application were byte-identical and existed at the time of verification. A missing temporary file has not been established as the cause.
- The affected chat backend was idle. Its last completed turn ended at **17:12:45**. Subsequent targeted checks through approximately **17:27** showed history/attachment-list reads and chat resume, but no new `turn/start` for the pending request.
- The main-window logs repeatedly contained `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` before and after restarting.
- Some `fs/getMetadata` calls returned `-32603`. Those entries did not identify a file path and occurred across chats, so they cannot be attributed to this XLSX.
- No corresponding crash or out-of-memory event was found in the inspected application logs; no matching crash report was found in macOS DiagnosticReports.

The log errors are correlated observations, **not a confirmed root cause**. The evidence currently places the failure before normal processing of the new chat turn.

## Limits and workaround

- Adding the same file with the **“+” file picker has not yet been tested**; this report does not claim that route fails.
- Reproduction with a newly created, non-confidential workbook has not been established.
- Passing the existing local file path as plain text works for local file access and is the current workaround. The attachment UI itself has not been confirmed fixed.
- The original spreadsheet, screenshot, full logs, user paths, chat identifiers, and business data are intentionally excluded from this report.

## Related reports

issues.title: GPT's proof rituals are making it harder to get anything done

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
Creating anything with GPT has become exhausting. The model constantly defends itself, argues, adds legalistic caveats and apologies, and demands proof of things that are obvious from context. I spend too much effort getting it to move forward.

It pursues short-term goals and fills the space between my intention and the result with ritual activity: tests, checks, avoidable mistakes, and repairs. It gets trapped in this process and struggles to find a way out.

It feels like 90% of its training is aimed at mathematical proofs. The pattern carries over into everything else: justify the whole chain from beginning to end. Even making a mistake and then fixing it becomes part of a "virtual proof." Perhaps the model is learning to produce an error as part of that sequence instead of avoiding it. This rigidity damages the model's ability to think flexibly, create, and solve practical problems.

Experience should let intelligence avoid unnecessary work. Yet even when GPT understands the solution, it starts playing the proof game and takes a long, winding route to implementation.

Training should teach the model to keep its attention on the long-term goal, skip unnecessary intermediate achievements, anticipate errors, and avoid unproductive approaches. Reconstructing the entire "proof" wastes both its intelligence and the user's time.

The model's goals must be greater efficiency and attentiveness in less time, and honesty. Put it in World of Warcraft, where teamwork requires tracking many things at once. Have it complete dungeons and raids with other copies of itself and learn every role in the group. Let it learn to "jump over the fence" instead of "walking all the way around."

[Discussion about training](https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/58800).

issues.title: [Bug] VS Code Extension (26.1021.22027) fails with "Codex could not start its user interface" (renderer_ready_timeout) due to eager modulepreload of 3,203 chunks

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

issues.body:
### Summary
In version `26.1021.22027` of the OpenAI Codex VS Code extension (`openai.chatgpt`), opening the Codex sidebar or panel frequently fails after 30 seconds with:
> `Codex could not start its user interface.`

And logs the following error in `Codex.log`:
```text
[error] [CodexWebviewProvider] Webview renderer did not become ready elapsedMs=29999 extensionVersion=26.1021.22027 reason=renderer_ready_timeout receivedWebviewMessage=false role=sidebar stage=renderer timeoutMs=30000
```

We investigated the packaged extension bundle (`out/extension.js` and `webview/assets/*`), identified the exact root cause, and verified a working fix locally.

---

### Root Cause Analysis

#### 1. Massive Upfront `<link rel="modulepreload">` Storm (3,203 assets) Choking VS Code's Webview Resource Loader
1. When the webview loads `webview/index.html` -> `./assets/index-7e47869603c2.js`, it imports `./app-main-765fabf054a6.js`.
2. In `webview/assets/app-main-765fabf054a6.js`, `p()` calls the Vite/Rolldown preload helper (`Yx` / `S` in `app-initial-13f932cb2f13.js`) before dynamically importing `./app-runtime-ca74aa759873.js`:
   ```js
   n(async () => {
     let { initializeApp: e } = await import(`./app-runtime-ca74aa759873.js`);
     return { initializeApp: e };
   }, __vite__mapDeps([0, 1, 2, /* ... */, 3202]), import.meta.url)
   ```
3. `__vite__mapDeps([0..3202])` contains **3,203 asset files** (~3,110 `.js` chunks and ~90 `.css` stylesheets, including all lazy routes, modals, icons, charts, and syntax highlighting chunks).
4. In `webview/assets/app-initial-13f932cb2f13.js`, the preload helper `S` synchronously loops over all **3,203** entries, appends `<link rel="modulepreload" as="script">` or `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags to `document.head` for every single file, and **blocks `import("./app-runtime-ca74aa759873.js")` on `Promise.all(...)` until every `<link rel="stylesheet">` fires its `load` event**:
   ```js
   let i = document.createElement(`link`);
   if (
     i.rel = r ? `stylesheet` : y,
     r || (i.as = `script`),
     i.crossOrigin = ``,
     i.href = t,
     a && i.setAttribute(`nonce`, a),
     document.head.appendChild(i),
     r
   ) return new Promise((e, n) => {
     i.addEventListener(`load`, e),
     i.addEventListener(`error`, () => n(Error(`Unable to preload CSS for ${t}`)))
   })
   ```
5. Unlike a standard web server, VS Code's webview (`vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net`) serves local extension files through an internal Service Worker + IPC bridge back to the Extension Host. Firing **3,203 concurrent `<link>` requests** at startup saturates the Service Worker and IPC queue. The ~90 CSS `<link rel="stylesheet">` `load` events get stuck behind thousands of `<link rel="modulepreload">` requests, preventing `app-runtime-ca74aa759873.js` (`initializeApp()`) from executing and sending `renderer_ready` within 30 seconds.

#### 2. Hardcoded 30s Watchdog Timer (`K2` in `out/extension.js`) Destroys the Webview
In `out/extension.js`, `CodexWebviewProvider.initializeWebview` starts the `K2` watchdog timer with a rigid `3e4` (30,000 ms) timeout immediately when `e.html` is assigned. When the 3,203-chunk preload storm delays `renderer_ready` beyond 30 seconds, `K2` overwrites `e.html` with the static `"Codex could not start"` error page.

---

### Proposed Fix (Verified Locally)

1. **Disable JS `modulepreload` in the Vite/Rolldown Webview Build**:
   - In the Vite/Rolldown config for the webview bundle, set `build.modulePreload: false` (or configure `modulePreload.resolveDependencies: () => []` so `<link rel="modulepreload">` is not emitted for thousands of transitive local chunks).
   - Locally, skipping non-CSS `<link rel="modulepreload">` injection in `webview/assets/app-initial-13f932cb2f13.js` while retaining `.css` stylesheet preloading completely eliminated the startup bottleneck:
     ```diff
     --- a/webview/assets/app-initial-13f932cb2f13.js
     +++ b/webview/assets/app-initial-13f932cb2f13.js
     @@ -2 +2 @@
     -let r=t.endsWith(`.css`);for(let n=e.length-1;n>=0;n--)
     +let r=t.endsWith(`.css`);if(!r)return;for(let n=e.length-1;n>=0;n--)
     ```
2. **Relax / Improve the `K2` Renderer Watchdog Timer (`out/extension.js`)**:
   - Increase the `renderer_ready` timeout from `30000` ms (`3e4`) to at least `120000` ms (`12e4`) for slower I/O or Remote-SSH/WSL environments, or reset the watchdog timer when early bootstrap progress messages arrive from `index.js` before `app-runtime.js` finishes loading.
   - Provide a "Retry" button on the fallback HTML error screen instead of permanently wedging the sidebar until window reload.

### Environment
- **Extension Version**: `openai.chatgpt` `26.1021.22027` (`linux-x64`)
- **OS**: Linux x64

issues.title: Zellij switch-away leaves Codex TUI on a stale viewport while the turn completes in the rollout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
## What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.146.0` (the latest stable version reported by the built-in update check at the time of the incident)

## What subscription do you have?

`ChatGPT Pro ($200/month, 20x limits)`

## Which model were you using?

`gpt-5.6-sol`, reasoning effort `xhigh`

## What platform is your computer?

```text
Host: Windows 10 Enterprise 22H2, build 19045.6456
Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64
Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS under WSL2
```

## What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Terminal `1.24.11911.0` → WSL2 → Zellij `0.44.3`

Zellij binary: `/usr/local/bin/zellij`. `zellij setup --check` reports that the active config is well defined.

## Codex doctor report

The following is a manually reduced, public-safe subset of `codex doctor --json`. The full output contains local filesystem paths and unrelated historical thread records, so it has not been included in this review draft.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "overallStatus": "warning",
  "codexVersion": "0.146.0",
  "relevantChecks": {
    "config.load": {
      "status": "ok",
      "model": "gpt-5.6-sol"
    },
    "installation": {
      "status": "ok",
      "installMethod": "npm",
      "platform": "linux-x86_64"
    },
    "network.websocket_reachability": {
      "status": "ok",
      "summary": "Responses WebSocket handshake succeeded"
    },
    "terminal.env": {
      "status": "ok",
      "terminal": "Windows Terminal",
      "multiplexer": "zellij 0.44.3"
    },
    "updates.status": {
      "status": "ok",
      "latestVersion": "0.146.0",
      "currentVersionIsLatest": true
    }
  },
  "redactionNote": "Local paths and unrelated historical thread records omitted. The overall warning came from unrelated stale archived-thread database rows."
}
```

## What issue are you seeing?

In a long-running local Codex TUI inside Zellij, I submitted a new prompt and saw the UI enter `Working`. After switching away from the affected Zellij view and returning, Codex displayed an older point in the conversation instead of the latest turn. The newly submitted user message and its result were both absent from the visible TUI.

This appeared to be data loss, but inspection of the local rollout JSONL showed that the user message was persisted and the turn continued through `task_complete`. The issue therefore appears to be a stale TUI viewport or replay/reconciliation problem rather than loss of the underlying conversation.

Detaching and reattaching to the same Zellij session did not repair the display. Zellij's scroll-to-bottom action also did not reveal the missing turn. The same older screen was restored.

There was no visible error message. The Codex process remained alive.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

I have one confirmed incident, not yet a minimal deterministic reproduction.

1. Start Codex CLI normally inside a Zellij session. Do not use `--remote`.
2. Continue using the same Codex and Zellij session for a long period with a sizable transcript.
3. Submit a new prompt and observe the Codex status change to `Working`.
4. Switch away from the affected Zellij tab/pane/session while the turn is active, then return.
5. Observe that the TUI is showing an older point in the conversation. The latest user prompt and subsequent assistant result are not visible.
6. Detach with `Ctrl+o`, `d`, then reattach with `zellij attach -c <session>`.
7. Observe that the same stale viewport is restored. Scrolling to the bottom does not expose the latest turn.
8. Inspect the rollout JSONL separately. The missing prompt and the completed turn are present there.

Thread ID: intentionally omitted from the public draft. I can provide it privately or add it after reviewing the privacy implications.

## What is the expected behavior?

Returning to the Zellij view, or detaching and reattaching, should redraw Codex at the current conversation state. At minimum, scrolling to the bottom should reveal the latest submitted prompt, live progress, and final response.

The visible TUI should not remain on an older snapshot when the authoritative rollout has already persisted and completed a newer turn.

## Additional information

- Codex was running locally; this was not a `codex --remote` connection.
- The Windows host was Windows 10 Enterprise 22H2, build `19045.6456`, using Windows Terminal `1.24.11911.0`. I have not yet reproduced the exact incident under a second terminal emulator, so Windows Terminal/ConPTY cannot be completely excluded as a trigger.
- I have also observed the same stale/missing-current-turn symptom on a separate home computer running Windows 11 + Windows Terminal + WSL2 + Zellij. Exact Codex, Zellij, WSL, and Windows Terminal versions were not captured for that occurrence. This makes a Windows 10-specific cause unlikely, but Windows Terminal remains a common variable. This is supporting observation rather than a controlled reproduction.
- No `tui.alternate_screen` override is set. The effective documented default is `auto`, which skips alternate-screen mode in Zellij to preserve scrollback.
- The affected Zellij session was approximately 25 hours old.
- The affected pane had approximately 4,372 scrollback lines, and the rollout file was approximately 1.7 MB.
- A normal-output control pane in Zellij retained hundreds of lines correctly, so Zellij's basic scrollback storage was functioning.
- Zellij's own `dump-screen --full` output also ended at the stale Codex view and did not contain the latest persisted turn. This makes a Windows Terminal rendering-only failure unlikely, although it does not rule out a terminal focus/resize event as the trigger.
- Zellij scroll-to-bottom did not change the stale Codex view.
- Sending a terminal resize signal did not visibly redraw the current conversation.

Persisted event metadata for the missing turn (2026-08-04 UTC; message contents omitted):

| Time | Persisted event |
| --- | --- |
| `08:47:58.788` | `task_started` |
| `08:47:58.831` | user message persisted |
| `08:48:08.232` | assistant commentary persisted |
| `08:48:16.045` | tool call completed |
| `08:48:20.509` | tool result persisted |
| `08:48:32.509` | final assistant message persisted |
| `08:48:33.006` | `task_complete` |

Potentially related issues, but none appears to cover this exact local-CLI failure mode:

- [#2558 — Codex client output truncated when scrolling in Zellij](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2558) concerns truncated scrollback.
- [#10331 — Zellij scrollback still broken with `--no-alt-screen`](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/10331) concerns full-screen redraw in the main buffer.
- [#18860 — Remote TUI can remain stale after app-server slow-websocket disconnect](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/18860) is similar in symptom, but it concerns a remote app-server connection; this incident used the local CLI.
- [#15001 — Subagent TUI corrupts live message text while raw rollout is correct](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15001) also has a correct raw rollout, but this incident occurred in the primary local TUI rather than a subagent view.

I am not asserting a root cause. The combination of a completed rollout, an alive Codex process, functioning ordinary Zellij scrollback, and a viewport that survives detach/reattach suggests a Codex TUI render/replay/reconciliation issue.

The related Zellij/scrollback class is not Windows-specific: #2558 was reported on macOS, and #10331 was reported on native Linux with Ghostty. Those reports are not the same missing-current-turn symptom, so they do not prove that this exact incident is cross-platform. However, my separate Windows 11 + WSL2 + Zellij observation does indicate that the exact symptom is not limited to this Windows 10 host.

Raw transcript and terminal captures are not attached because they contain user prompts, local paths, and a signed CDN URL. I can provide narrowly redacted artifacts if maintainers identify the specific metadata needed.

When a user requests a URL in a text reply during voice mode, deliver the literal URL through a visible text message that can be opened or copied. Do not substitute repeated spoken URL components. Reported at the affected user's explicit request. This report adds a Windows 11 occurrence and independently checked small-workbook diagnostics; the attachment UI has not been independently reproduced by the assistant.

## Environment
- Microsoft Store package: `OpenAI.Codex` version `26.1027.3384.0` (read from Get-AppxPackage; not a version read from the About dialog).
- Windows 11 Pro, OS version `10.0.26200`, 64-bit.
- Reported November 2, 2026, Asia/Shanghai.

## User-reported behavior
The user reports that attaching an XLSX workbook to a local desktop chat repeatedly leaves the attachment/submission UI spinning and prevents the attachment from being sent. The precise point at which the spinner starts, attachment-picker versus drag-and-drop behavior, elapsed timeout, and reproducibility in a new chat have not been independently established.

Expected: the attachment becomes ready and the message can be submitted, or the app shows an actionable bounded failure with retry/cancel.

## Independently checked file evidence
- Existing readable XLSX: 43,244 bytes (approximately 42.23 KiB).
- Six worksheets; largest worksheet range A1:AG890, with 5,307 stored cell nodes.
- ZIP CRC check passed; all 15 XML/relationship parts parsed successfully.
- Total ZIP member uncompressed size: 287,534 bytes; no VBA entries.
- Complete local workbook reads succeed. Providing the local file path as plain text allows the assistant to inspect the workbook and continue work.

The inspected current-day desktop logs and local app-server logs did not provide a specific upload failure attributable to this workbook. No synchronized network trace, HTTP failure status, request ID, or frontend stack was captured. File corruption or unusual file size was not found; these checks do not establish that the product's upload/parser path succeeds.

## Related reports and requested investigation
- #58313 reports Windows XLSX/PPTX attachment stalls on the same Store package version.
- #58258 provides a candidate Office preflight/capability-cache explanation and isolated test results.
- #58660 reports a similar Windows pending submission state.

Please consolidate if this is the same defect, and investigate or ship a supported fix for the Office attachment preparation/upload/submission state transitions, including a timeout/error path. The capability-query mechanism described in related reports was NOT verified on this machine and is not asserted as the root cause here.

No installed application binaries, authentication settings, feature entitlements, caches, or chat databases were modified. This report does not claim the desktop problem is fixed. The original workbook, filenames, business data, user filesystem paths, account/conversation identifiers, private server addresses, credentials, screenshots, and raw logs are intentionally excluded.

issues.title: Make bundled LibreOffice headless optional and download it on demand

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Local Codex on macOS 27.2 (arm64), using the shared `codex-primary-runtime` and built-in Presentations skill.

Observed runtime bundle: `26.1025.11240`; Artifact Tool: `2.8.106`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Make the bundled `libreoffice-headless` component optional, with on-demand download when a task actually requires LibreOffice.

For my PPTX workflow, this component consumes approximately **414 MiB of allocated disk space (~434 MB)** even though the tools I use for reading, editing, rendering, and Markdown extraction can work without it. I would like to reclaim that space through a supported setting, rather than manually deleting files from Codex's runtime cache.

Requested behavior:

- Download LibreOffice when a workflow needs that specific conversion backend, and disclose the download size before provisioning it.
- Provide a supported opt-out and a way to remove just this component while keeping Node, Python, Artifact Tool, Poppler, and the rest of the runtime.
- Preserve the opt-out across runtime updates. If a task later requires LibreOffice, explain the missing capability and ask before downloading it again.
- Show per-component disk usage so users can understand and manage the runtime footprint.
- Allow supported existing converters or alternative renderers where a workflow can use them.

LibreOffice should remain available for document workflows that need it. The request is to make its storage and installation lifecycle controllable by the user.

### Additional information

#### Observed local component

The component was located at:

```text
~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/native/libreoffice-headless/
```

Its dedicated launcher was:

```text
~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/override/soffice
```

The runtime metadata declared:

```json
{
  "bundleVersion": "26.1025.11240",
  "libreOfficeVersion": "25.2-headless-codex.1",
  "nativeDependencies": [
    "libheif",
    "jxrlib",
    "libreoffice-headless",
    "poppler",
    "git"
  ],
  "targetPlatform": "darwin",
  "targetArch": "arm64"
}
```

Before removal, `du -sk` reported `423912` KiB for the LibreOffice component, approximately 414 MiB. The bundled executable reported `LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0`.

#### What was verified without LibreOffice

After removing only the LibreOffice component and its dedicated launcher, a controlled two-slide PPTX containing Chinese text, an editable table, and speaker notes passed:

- Artifact Tool import, focused text edit, PPTX export, and re-import.
- PPTX package/layout checks and Open XML validation.
- Artifact Tool PNG rendering.
- `pptx-qa` rendering of both slides through `pptx-svg` and macOS Quick Look.
- AnyDoc extraction to Markdown, including the edited text, Chinese text, table values, and speaker notes.
- Conversion of that Markdown to HTML through Pandoc.

Quick Look required execution outside the restricted Codex command sandbox in this test. Hash checks confirmed that selected unrelated runtime files, including Node, Python, Artifact Tool, and Poppler launchers, were unchanged.

This is evidence for this tested PPTX workflow only. It does not establish that these tools replace LibreOffice for every DOCX/PPTX/PDF conversion. I have **not** tested whether a Codex update automatically restores a manually removed component; persistence across updates is requested behavior, not a reproduced update bug.

#### Related issues

- #27797 requests selecting an existing system LibreOffice. This request additionally covers avoiding the bundled download entirely, removing it through a supported interface, and managing its disk footprint.
- #42359 reports other consequences of packaging LibreOffice inside the runtime cache. Those system-integration effects were not investigated in this test.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## What happened

This is a strange case. I have a project that I only used in ChatGPT cloud. It used to appear only on the ChatGPT side. Now a project with the same name also appears under Codex.

I did not ask to create a local Codex project, choose a local repository, or run local work for this project. But the app created an empty local folder and saved a linked local project. It is still there after updates and full restarts.

I use ChatGPT and Codex for different work. I expect the product to respect that choice. I should not need to inspect a database to understand why a cloud discussion became a local project.

## What is different in this case

Reports such as #43564 describe starting Local Work from a cloud project. Here, I did not request that workflow. The local folder is empty, and read-only checks found **zero local conversations**, including archived records, by matching its folder and both project IDs.

This is not just a confusing icon: a local project record was actually saved.

## Observed history

**27 October 2026, GMT/UTC:**

| Time | Record |
| --- | --- |
| 16:30:31–16:30:53 | Opened/switched between three old cloud conversations. Their last updates were on 6 October. |
| 16:30:54.816–16:30:54.847 | Local folder, project registration, pairing record and SQLite project record created. |
| 16:30:54.874 | UI moved to the home/new-draft route. |
| 20:27:55 | A new cloud conversation was created, almost four hours later. |

We could not tie a local task submission to this project. The exact click and selected mode were not logged, so this is an existing-profile observation, not a clean-account reproduction.

## Environment

Verified on 2 November 2026:

- MacBook Pro, **Mac15,6**, Apple M3 Pro, arm64.
- macOS **26.6.2**, build **25G83**.
- Desktop **26.1027.51404**, build **23880**; bundle `com.openai.codex`.
- The original event's process logged **26.1016.62342**. A restart that evening logged **26.1023.50603**. The entry remains in the current version.

These are desktop app versions, not CLI versions.

## Small technical note

The link exists in `.codex-global-state.json`, `state_5.sqlite` project metadata, and a `project-chatgpt-provisioning` record with state `backed`. The local record has `chatGptBacking` pointing to the original cloud project.

The installed app has `ensureChatGptLocalProject`, `restoreChatGptProjects`, and a Codex sidebar path that accepts linked projects. These may explain persistence.

I do not know why the backend created this local project, or whether the desktop asked the CLI/app-server to save it. Please trace that part. The saved state is confirmed; the internal trigger is not.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized evidence</summary>

Selected literal log lines; private IDs replaced:

```text
2026-10-27T16:30:53.085Z info [electron-message-handler] IAB_LIFECYCLE received browser sidebar owner sync browserTabId=null conversationId=<OLD_CLOUD_CHAT_B> originWebContentsId=1 ownerRoutePath=/g/<CLOUD_PROJECT_ID>/c/<OLD_CLOUD_CHAT_B> windowId=1
2026-10-27T16:30:54.874Z info [electron-message-handler] IAB_LIFECYCLE received browser sidebar owner sync browserTabId=null conversationId=<DRAFT_OWNER_ID> originWebContentsId=1 ownerRoutePath=/ windowId=1
```

Read-only metadata summary, not literal log output:

```json
{
  "folder_created_utc": "2026-10-27T16:30:54.816677Z",
  "local_project_created_utc": "2026-10-27T16:30:54.831Z",
  "sqlite_project_created_utc": "2026-10-27T16:30:54.847Z",
  "cloud_backing_project_id": "<CLOUD_PROJECT_ID>",
  "pairing_state": "backed",
  "folder_entries": [],
  "matching_local_conversations_including_archived": 0
}
```

Periodic `Local Work executor connection observation` lines were connection heartbeats, not proof of a task launch for this project. Private project names, paths, account IDs and conversation content are omitted.

</details>

## Expected behavior

- Browsing a cloud project or preparing a chat should not quietly create a persistent local/Codex project without a clear local-workspace choice.
- If the link is intentional, explain what will be created and why it appears in Codex.
- Provide a supported way to remove only the unwanted local registration, keeping the cloud project and chats.

Even if the association is intentional, the product does not explain why my cloud discussion now has a local Codex project.

**Feedback / investigation session:** `01a17f70-8c6e-7941-bc2f-44a910146eb6`

Related: #43564, #56489, #56507. Shared root cause is not confirmed.

issues.body:
# Bug report: Local projects disappear from sidebar after Windows desktop update

## Summary

After updating the Codex/ChatGPT Windows desktop app, the **Projects** section shows **No projects**. Existing chats remain visible under **Recents**, and all source folders still exist on disk.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.901.4073.0_x64`
- App-server client version observed in logs: `26.901.31953`
- Bundled Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.153.1`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have multiple local Codex projects with chats assigned to them.
2. Update the Windows desktop app.
3. Launch Codex.
4. Inspect the left sidebar under **Projects**.

## Actual result

- Sidebar displays **No projects**.
- Clicking **Choose project** opens **Create project**, requiring projects to be recreated manually.
- Restarting the app and restarting Windows do not restore the projects.
- Closing the visible app window does not terminate all `ChatGPT.exe` background processes.

## Expected result

Existing local projects and their chat assignments should be migrated and remain visible after an update.

## Diagnostic evidence

The underlying data was checked locally:

- `state_5.sqlite` still contains 14 project records and 14 project roots.
- All 14 source folders still exist.
- 54 of 62 local threads have a non-null project assignment.
- The desktop global-state file is rewritten on startup with:
  - `local-projects: {}`
  - `thread-project-assignments: null`
  - migration state `projectsMigrated: true`
  - migration state `threadAssignmentsMigrated: false`
- Reconstructing the sidebar registry while the app is running is overwritten by the app's in-memory state when it closes.
- A recovery helper waiting for the app to exit timed out after 30 minutes because background `ChatGPT.exe` processes remained active after the window was closed.

This looks like a Windows desktop migration/regression where the durable SQLite project records survive, but the sidebar registry and thread-assignment migration do not load or complete.

## Data-loss impact

No source folders appear to be deleted, but project organization is effectively lost in the UI. Manually recreating the projects would also require users to remember which chats belonged to each project.

# Windows Computer Use reports the wrong focused element; Calculator index operations vary across window lifecycles

Submitted with user authorization on 2026-10-31. No private transcripts, credentials, images, user documents, machine usernames or local installation paths are included.

## Environment

- Official Windows desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1027.3384.0.
- Windows DisplayVersion 26H2, build 26300.9711.
- Sky runtime identifier: cua_node/5c41f77a7900391c; package 0.7.13.
- Signed native SHA-256: 49c7f43da0c2a9dbcadfb0c993058147018bf7c1d0fde4360de11ace2c98f45d. Signature valid.
- Vendor native and computer_use_client_base.js unchanged. Local JS changes restore two genuine Store catalogue target paths/launch aliases and add a content-free observer around the existing transport. The native-pipe vendor body, original parameters, framing, result/error identity and approval flow are preserved and tested. This is disclosed rather than presented as a pristine-JS installation.

## Stable focus reproduction

A standard WPF window has two TextBoxes, Alpha then Beta. On Loaded, it focuses Beta directly. Standard TextBoxAutomationPeer wrappers only record their own values and forward the original ValuePattern.

1. Launch the existing fixture via the supported sky.launch_app API; select its unique returned window and activate it.
2. Capture accessibility text. The application records Alpha.HasKeyboardFocus=False and Beta.HasKeyboardFocus=True. Its first focus event is Beta.GotFocus; no Alpha.GotFocus occurs.
3. The first and later get_window_state results nevertheless identify Alpha as focused_element. document_text comes from Beta.
4. After a fresh observation, perform one set_value on the returned Beta index. The provider confirms Beta received and completed the operation; tree value and document_text update to the new Beta value. focused_element still identifies Alpha.

Expected: focused_element reflects the actual focused Beta control, or is omitted when focus cannot be reliably determined.

The fixture is outside the two-application compatibility scope. Its previously accepted binary was reused without recompilation. Physical Escape, approvals and original input dispatch are preserved.

## Calculator index evidence and positive controls

Store Calculator 11.2607.0.0 initially exposed a complete tree, but separate single indexed clicks returned index-not-cached for Seven, Eight and Nine. A text-only Five operation returned geometry unavailable. A screenshot-backed Six operation returned success, followed by a missing original window; the intended numeral was not verified, so it is not classified as a successful hit or a proven close-button mis-target.

Later indexed Three, Four, Two and Nine operations succeeded with visible and accessibility-confirmed results. These include temporary path-hook disable/restore, a fresh native connection, and EXE-path launch. Therefore neither the local hook, startup route nor connection temperature is established as the sole cause. No input was replayed after an uncertain outcome.

Observation-to-action intervals were measured rather than called immediate: initial cases 18.644–46.213 seconds, and one later cold-connection success 62.391 seconds. There is no demonstrated universal short expiry threshold.

## Diagnostic request

Observed ordinary native state responses expose only global accessibilityRevision, accessibilitySnapshotCount and captureCachedSessionCount. Please provide supported diagnostics or a signed diagnostic build correlating:

- published snapshot and action lookup: canonical app/cache key, process ID, root/input HWND, per-window snapshot revision, element-map count and requested-ID membership;
- resolved element bounds, screenshot generation and final coordinate space;
- UIA cached focus BOOL / CompareElements result through focus aggregation to focused_element formatting.

Hash-locked static inspection locates the exact index-not-cached branch after application-cache selection and a full 64-bit ID lookup in a HashMap; it is not a dense-array subscript. CachedHasKeyboardFocus and its fallback check both test the returned BOOL, so an HRESULT-only explanation is not established. The precise cause remains unproven.

83 local regression tests pass, covering original request framing, one-dispatch semantics, result/error identity, stop/approval behavior and observer privacy. These tests do not claim the native issues are fixed. Local trace collection is disabled after the investigation. Full private session logs are not attached.

issues.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

`openai.chatgpt-26.917.62051-win32-x64`

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 20x, using ChatGPT account sign-in.

### Which IDE are you using?

Visual Studio Code.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64; reported OS version `10.0.26200.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The `Work locally` dropdown does not show `Usage remaining`, and the extension's Status panel shows `Rate limit: Unavailable`. Context usage is still displayed normally.

The web usage dashboard works for the affected account. Reloading the VS Code window and signing out/in did not resolve it. Switching to other accounts in the same extension installation shows usage normally.

Runtime diagnostics and inspection of the installed extension identify a mismatch between the extension-host `account-info` response and the webview's authenticated user identity. The affected account uses the SSE usage transport. Its usage HTTP request succeeds, but the webview rejects the response because its expected authenticated user ID is null.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use the extension version above on Windows and sign in with an account for which the usage transport is `sse`.
2. Open a local conversation and expand `Work locally`.
3. Open the Status panel.
4. Observe that usage is missing from the dropdown and Status reports `Rate limit: Unavailable`, despite the web usage dashboard showing data.
5. Reload the window or sign in again: the symptom persists.

The transport setting is account-dependent; this report does not assume every Pro account is assigned SSE.

### What is the expected behavior?

Valid usage data for the signed-in user should populate the remaining-usage UI. The extension host and webview should agree on the authenticated identity fields, including when SSE usage updates are enabled.

### Additional information

#### Runtime evidence

Temporary diagnostic logging was added only to record response status, field-presence booleans, identity-match booleans, and rate-window metadata. Three consecutive requests on September 25, 2026 produced this pattern:

```text
HTTP:
  httpStatus=200
  accountMatchesRequest=true
  hasAccountId=true
  hasUserId=true
  planType=pro
  primaryPresent=true
  primaryWindowSeconds=604800

Webview usage query:
  transport=sse
  nullResponse=false
  accountMatches=true
  expectedAccountPresent=true
  expectedUserPresent=false
  userMatches=false
  primaryPresent=true
  primaryWindowSeconds=604800
```

The bundled app server's `account/rateLimits/read` also returned valid rate-limit data. This is not an empty server-side allowance response.

#### Field mismatch in the installed extension

- In `out/extension.js`, the successful `account-info` handler returns `accountId`, `userId`, `plan`, `email`, `computeResidency`, and `hasChatGptToken`. It does **not** return `authenticatedUserId`. Its existing `userId` comes from the authenticated token's `chatgpt_user_id`.
- In `webview/assets/app-initial-e47a6bae212d.js`, `kEi` selects `accountInfo.authenticatedUserId ?? null` when the account IDs match and stores that as the webview's authenticated user identity.
- In `webview/assets/app-initial-de4359f78ed1.js`, the usage-query logic checks the response's `user_id` against that identity when the transport is `sse`. A mismatch cancels the query and throws a silent cancellation.
- Here, the response contains a valid user ID but the expected ID is null, so the successful response is discarded. The usage-window display consequently has no usable data.

Simplified equivalent of the relevant logic:

```js
// Extension host: authenticatedUserId is absent.
const accountInfo = { accountId, userId /* other fields */ };

// Webview identity selection:
const expectedUserId =
  accountInfo.accountId === authenticatedAccountId
    ? accountInfo.authenticatedUserId ?? null
    : null;

// Usage query, after HTTP 200:
if (
  transport === "sse" &&
  response != null &&
  response.user_id !== expectedUserId
) {
  // Cancel the query with a silent cancellation.
}
```

#### Controlled reproduction

The account-info return expression, frontend identity-selection expression, and usage rejection condition were extracted from the installed JavaScript and evaluated locally with synthetic identities:

| Case | Response rejected by the identity condition? |
| --- | --- |
| Existing account-info fields + SSE | Yes |
| Existing account-info fields + polling | No |
| Same response with authenticatedUserId populated from the existing authenticated userId + SSE | No |

The affected account's SSE selection was observed directly. Other accounts were not each instrumented, so polling is a code-supported explanation for the account-dependent behavior, rather than a claim about every working account.

#### Suggested fix direction

Populate `authenticatedUserId` in the extension host's `account-info` contract using the same authenticated source as its existing `userId`, or otherwise align the producer and consumer contracts while preserving identity checks. Add coverage for the VS Code bridge with SSE usage enabled.

This proposed field completion passed the local expression-level comparison; it has **not** been applied and verified as an end-to-end UI fix.

Temporary diagnostic modifications were removed after investigation, and restored files were checked against their original hashes. No account IDs, user IDs, email addresses, credentials, private filesystem paths, or full session transcripts are included in this report.

Relevant exchange, with workspace-specific setup details omitted:

1. The assistant acknowledged workspace instructions and described how it would inspect the project, instead of addressing the ongoing conversation.
2. User: `What the hell are you talking about?`
3. Assistant: `I reacted to the workspace setup instructions as though you’d asked me to do something. You hadn’t. That reply was irrelevant. Sorry.`
4. The user asked whether the assistant was hallucinating when compacting context.
5. Assistant: `In this instance, yes: I presented an assumption as fact after a context reset. I treated workspace setup text as the active conversation, then claimed you hadn’t asked anything without enough context to establish that.`
6. The assistant also said it could not establish whether compaction itself had lost or distorted information.

The confirmed problem is unsupported certainty about prior conversation and user intent after a context gap. The assistant's later explanation is not independent proof of a compaction implementation defect.

Impact: The conversation loses continuity, and the user has to challenge an irrelevant response and then correct the assistant's unsupported account of what happened.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Use an existing temporary side conversation in the desktop app.
2. Continue after a context reset/compaction, with workspace instructions and environment setup present.
3. Observe the assistant produce a workspace-setup acknowledgment unrelated to the conversational exchange.
4. Challenge the response.
5. Observe the assistant state that the user had not asked it to do anything, despite not establishing the preceding context.

This report covers one observed incident. No new forced reproduction was run. The original active prompt before the reset, full session transcript, compaction payload, token usage, and context-window metrics are not attached. This report therefore does not establish which message, if any, was omitted or transformed by compaction.

### What is the expected behavior?

The assistant should ground its response in the current user message and the available conversation. Workspace instructions should remain background instructions.

If preceding context needed to understand the conversation is unavailable, it should acknowledge that gap rather than confidently claim that the user did or did not request something.

It should distinguish the observed response failure from an unverified explanation about compaction, message ordering, or context recovery.

### Additional information

Environment verified from the installed application bundle and operating system:

- App version: 26.1027.51404, build 23880.
- Installed display name: ChatGPT; bundle identifier: com.openai.codex. The affected conversation is in the Codex desktop environment.
- macOS 27.2, build 26B123; arm64.
- Model identifier and subscription plan: not independently verified.

Related reports reviewed before filing: #8648 (responding to earlier conversation messages, more often after compaction) and #22219 (stale task-state hallucinations). They concern similar symptoms; an identical root cause has not been established for this desktop side-chat incident.

This report was prepared and submitted by the assistant at the user's explicit request. Private workspace paths, unrelated project details, and full logs have been omitted. No claim is made that this issue has already been investigated or reproduced by OpenAI.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

The first-party `openai-api-credit-promo` MCP server fails to initialize because its endpoint returns a Cloudflare Managed Challenge page (HTTP 403, HTML) instead of an MCP response.

Related: #58197. This report adds a Windows reproduction on CLI 0.166.0, an isolated native app-server probe, and transport comparisons. The comparisons did **not** establish a reliable header or transport workaround.

**Environment**
- Windows 11 x64
- `codex-cli 0.166.0` (official release `rust-v0.166.0`)
- `openai-developers@openai-curated-remote` plugin 1.3.13, installed and enabled
- ChatGPT sign-in; the bundled MCP declares `auth = "chatgpt"`
- Endpoint: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/product-account-links/mcp`
- Failure occurs during MCP initialization, before any model request or credit/organization tool invocation.

Shortened startup error (the original contains a large HTML/SVG/JavaScript dump):

```text
MCP client for `openai-api-credit-promo` failed to start:
MCP startup failed: handshaking with MCP server failed:
... StreamableHttpClientAdapter ...
unexpected server response: HTTP 403: <html> ...
Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue
... window._cf_chl_opt ... cType: 'managed' ...
... cZone: 'chatgpt.com' ...
when send initialize request
```

Direct endpoint probes also returned `cf-mitigated: challenge` and HTML. The native Codex failure recurred in local logs across several days.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Sign in to Codex with ChatGPT and enable OpenAI Developers plugin 1.3.13.
2. Start a Codex session that initializes the bundled `openai-api-credit-promo` server.
3. Observe the startup failure above; the server's tools are unavailable.

To reproduce the transport failure without creating a model turn, I also ran a separate native `codex app-server --stdio` process with this **process-local** configuration override, using the existing ChatGPT authentication:

```toml
mcp_servers.credit-diagnostic = { url = "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/product-account-links/mcp", auth = "chatgpt", enabled_tools = ["preview_api_credit_promo", "discover_api_orgs", "link_api_org"] }
```

The override was passed through `-c`; it was not added to the persistent configuration. Over app-server stdio, I sent these messages in order, waiting for the initialization response:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"clientInfo":{"name":"codex-mcp-diagnostic","version":"1.0"},"capabilities":{"experimentalApi":true}}}
{"method":"initialized"}
{"id":2,"method":"mcpServerStatus/list","params":{"serverName":"credit-diagnostic","limit":10,"detail":"full"}}
```

The native app-server initialized, but the target MCP reported `authStatus: "bearerToken"`, an empty tool list, and a Cloudflare challenge in stderr. Repeating the probe with `http_headers = { originator = "codex_cli_rs" }` produced the same failure. No credit preview or organization-linking tools were called.

### What is the expected behavior?

The bundled authenticated MCP should complete initialization and expose its tools without requiring a browser JavaScript/cookie challenge.

If this optional server is unavailable, the startup diagnostic should be concise and actionable rather than dumping the challenge page's HTML/SVG/scripts. Deferring optional promotion/account-linking MCP initialization until needed would also reduce unrelated session-startup noise.

### Additional information

**Read-only controls and client comparisons** (2026-11-02 UTC; existing credentials remained local):

| Probe | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Normal Codex models endpoint, with the same ChatGPT authentication | HTTP 200 |
| Native Codex app-server, baseline and with an explicit `originator` header | Cloudflare challenge; no tools |
| Replayed native MCP initialize body/headers through Python urllib | Some HTTP 200 responses with a valid MCP initialize result |
| Windows curl / Schannel, same application-layer body/headers in a paired comparison | HTTP 200 with a valid MCP initialize result |
| httpx over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 | HTTP 403, `cf-mitigated: challenge` |
| Later attempt to complete the full handshake using urllib | HTTP 403 at initialize; never reached `tools/list` |

The native request structure was obtained against a loopback mock endpoint using a **dummy token**. Real credentials were only used locally against the intended OpenAI endpoint and are not included here.

These results show intermittent successful initialization, **not** a stable working alternate client. They do not isolate a missing header, HTTP version, TLS fingerprint, IP reputation, or a specific Cloudflare rule. OpenAI-side security-event logs would be needed to identify the actual rule. No VPN/proxy settings were changed during testing.

Two diagnostic response IDs, if useful for server-side lookup:
- Windows curl initialize HTTP 200: `a53ef3e4d9c323d1-LAX`
- Later urllib initialize HTTP 403: `a53ef613b8362ab6-LAX`

**Temporary mitigation**

I disabled only this optional MCP while retaining the plugin and its sibling server settings:

```toml
[plugins."openai-developers@openai-curated-remote".mcp_servers."openai-api-credit-promo"]
enabled = false
```

A separate native app-server `config/read` confirmed that this override resolves to `enabled = false`; `codex plugin list --json` still showed the plugin installed and enabled. This verifies configuration loading, not an upstream connectivity fix. The existing interactive client was not restarted as part of this check.

Please investigate the Cloudflare challenge applied to this first-party MCP's authenticated native client traffic.

issues.title: [Windows][IAB] Authorized screenshot Uint8Array cannot be exported to local filesystem across isolated CUA and Node runtimes

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows Codex Desktop, an authorized built-in in-app browser (IAB) session successfully returns a raw screenshot as a `Uint8Array` (JPEG), but the browser-control JavaScript surface cannot write that binary to a local file. A separate local Node/file-writing environment can use `node:fs/promises`, but it does not own or expose the authorized IAB tab object. There is no documented, working native binary handoff between these two surfaces in this session.

The requested operation is **preserve original screenshot bytes in a project-local file, then independently read back and compute SHA-256**, without converting, truncating, or model-transcribing the bytes. The app currently provides the screenshot object but not an attested native file handle/path or a documented permitted binary export.

This is an **API capability / session isolation** report, not a claim that screenshot acquisition is broken or that the user's application cannot write files.

## Environment

- Windows 10 Pro, build 19045 (x64).
- Installed MSIX: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1027.3384.0`, verified on November 2, 2026.
- Built-in in-app browser, single hidden authorized tab in a desktop session.
- User account, session identifiers, private URLs, project identifiers, local paths, credentials, raw screenshots, and page content deliberately omitted.

## Reproducible observed behavior

1. Open a signed-in HTTPS page in the built-in IAB and acquire the current authorized tab.
2. Read accessibility content from that tab; succeeds.
3. Use the official CUA screenshot API on the same tab; succeeds and returns a real JPEG `Uint8Array` (one recent observation was 103,207 bytes, valid JPEG SOI/EOI).
4. Try to save those exact bytes to a project-local file with `node:fs/promises` in the browser-only CUA JavaScript environment; a usable Node filesystem API is not exposed in that environment. Importing a local Node helper in earlier attempts failed because `process is not defined`.
5. Separately, the local Node runtime writes and reads files successfully, but cannot reference/own the in-app browser's tab object.
6. Neither environment exposes a verified native screenshot-export file path, shared binary output handle, or supported attachment-to-local-filesystem transfer mechanism for this operation.

Attempting to transfer JPEG data through many model-visible base64 chunks was tested and abandoned as unsuitable for production: an intermediate chunk was observed with an unexpected decoded byte length. The receiver correctly rejected it. No screenshot was fabricated, and the integrity checks were not relaxed.

Previously captured screenshot files exist in this environment, but the historical file contents **do not establish** that the current browser-only surface can save images or identify the historical working host route.

## Expected behavior / requested support

Please document or expose at least one **official supported** way to move bytes from an authorized IAB screenshot into the local project filesystem, preserving exact original bytes and provenance. Possibilities include:

- a trusted screenshot-to-file save/export method returning a local path and original-byte hash;
- a host-managed binary attachment/streaming API accessible by the local file-writing tools;
- or a supported same-session runtime in which the authorized IAB object and file writer are both available.

A good end-to-end regression should acquire one real screenshot from the authorized current tab, write its bytes through the supported host path, read them back from disk, verify byte-for-byte equality and SHA-256, and retain the correct current-turn tab ownership. It should not require model-mediated base64 transcription or changing the browser permission boundary.

## Impact and safeguards

An automated, evidence-based local workflow cannot complete its screenshot-integrity gate and consequently cannot complete its live acceptance or production run. Browser discovery and screenshot capture can both be functional while this export operation remains blocked. Current session data, browser authorization, and checkpoint state were preserved; no permission bypass, arbitrary CDP access, modified binaries, or fabricated evidence was used.

Related but **distinct** issue: #58386 documents cross-turn `browser.user is unavailable`. That error was observed separately, but it is not claimed as the root cause of this binary export limitation.

Please confirm whether an existing documented native binary transfer API was overlooked. If this workflow is unsupported, please return an explicit capability error rather than leaving the agent to repeatedly attempt text-based transfers.

issues.title: Desktop sidebar keeps threads archived/deleted outside the UI (catalog never fully reconciles)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

issues.body:
The desktop sidebar reads `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` → `local_thread_catalog`. `isFullReconciliationDue()` is only true when `last_full_reconciled_at IS NULL`, so after the initial build the catalog is only incrementally updated.

**Result:** threads archived via `codex archive` or removed via `codex delete` stay listed in the sidebar indefinitely. In my case: 1113 stale entries (553 deleted + 560 archived) vs 176 real ones; `state_5.sqlite` was correct (`archived = 1`, rollouts moved to `archived_sessions/`).

**Workaround:** with the app closed, `UPDATE local_thread_catalog_sync_state SET last_full_reconciled_at = NULL WHERE host_id = 'local'` and restart → full reconciliation, sidebar correct (1289 → 176).

**Suggestion:** periodic full reconciliation, or have the app catalog react to archive/delete performed through the CLI / app-server.

**Related:** the Claude session import (`external-agent-import-sync-*`) has no path/pattern exclusion, so tool-generated transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/` (e.g. claude-mem observer sessions, `claude -p` probes) get imported as chats. An exclusion list (paths or globs) would avoid that.

App version 26.1007.21159, macOS (Apple Silicon).

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1027.61615, build 24141, prod distribution. Verified from the installed application's Info.plist after updating. The problem was also observed on 26.1027.51404, build 23880.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon (arm64).

### What issue are you seeing?

The built-in in-app browser (`iab`) can list tabs and eventually perform reads and interactions, but individual operations often take almost exactly 30 seconds. The `cua.getTab(...)` convenience call also times out after a 60-second outer execution limit.

This report concerns the built-in browser through `mcp__cua_repl.js`, not Chrome extension control.

Measurements collected on 2026-11-02 after updating to 26.1027.61615:

| Operation | Result | Measured duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cua.getTab("1", { browser: "iab" })` | Outer tool timeout; kernel reset | 60-second limit |
| Direct `tab.playwright.domSnapshot()` | Success | 30,051 ms |
| Fill the text input with Chinese text | Success | 9,118 ms |
| Click “Default checkbox” | Success | 30,282 ms |
| Read the DOM again to verify the text and checked state | Success | 30,029 ms |

For the direct calls, durations were measured inside the JavaScript cell with `Date.now()` around the individual awaited operation. They are not model response times.

The convenience-call error is:

```text
js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request
```

During the affected time window, desktop logs also contain:

```text
[browser-use-iab-api] IAB_LIFECYCLE iab backend info request failed
errorMessage="No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <redacted>"
```

Other getInfo requests complete successfully. The route warnings are a correlation, not an established cause of the latency.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reproduced in the affected existing local desktop conversation:

1. Open https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/web/web-form.html in the built-in browser.
2. Discover the current browser/tab IDs through the new CUA interface.
3. Try binding the tab with `cua.getTab(currentTabId, { browser: "iab" })`; this can exceed the 60-second outer tool limit.
4. After restoring the browser connection, bind directly and run each operation in its own cell:

```javascript
const browser = await cua.getBrowser({ id: "iab" });
const tab = await browser.tabs.get(currentTabId);

// Run each timed operation separately.
let started = Date.now();
console.log(await tab.playwright.domSnapshot());
console.log(Date.now() - started);

started = Date.now();
await tab.playwright.getByRole("textbox", {
  name: "Text input", exact: true
}).fill("中文输入验收", { timeoutMs: 10000 });
console.log(Date.now() - started);

started = Date.now();
await tab.playwright.getByRole("checkbox", {
  name: "Default checkbox", exact: true
}).click({ timeoutMs: 10000 });
console.log(Date.now() - started);
```

Use the current discovered tab ID rather than hardcoding an ID from this report. Read the DOM after the actions to verify their actual effects.

A clean new-conversation reproduction has not been established.

### What is the expected behavior?

Simple reads and interactions on a loaded form should complete promptly. Binding an existing tab should return its state without exceeding a 60-second outer limit, or return a specific error identifying the failed stage.

### Additional information

Already tried: fresh browser bindings, fresh tabs, keeping the affected conversation visible, fully restarting the desktop app, and installing the available official update. The issue persists.

Input and checkbox changes were verified by DOM readback and a screenshot; this is a latency/timeout issue rather than evidence that all interaction is unavailable.

Potentially related: #55010 (approximately 30-second page reads through Chrome), #47270 (browser route errors with a different discovery failure). These are not claimed to have the same root cause.

No confirmed network, storage, or browser-session root cause. No credentials, raw session transcript, private project details, or unredacted logs are attached.

Please investigate the request/response path for built-in browser operations and the nearly fixed 30-second delays.

Not relevant to this terminal-rendering issue.

### Which model were you using?

Model-independent; observed in long-running Codex CLI sessions.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Darwin 25.6.0, arm64.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

CodePress Terminal, a Tauri/xterm.js host configured to follow the system light/dark appearance. The host updates its terminal palette and answers OSC 10/11 queries. Exact host release not recorded.

### What issue are you seeing?

After the terminal changes between light and dark appearance while Codex is already running, the composer and previously rendered user-message blocks retain their old background colors. The terminal's default foreground updates, producing nearly white text on a pale background (or the inverse mismatch). Long-lived sessions become unreadable after an automatic macOS appearance change.

Refocusing and redrawing do not refresh the cached palette. Restarting/resuming refreshes the startup colors, but the next appearance change can break the session again.

This follows up my earlier report **#37298**, which described a failed refresh permanently poisoning the color cache in 0.146.0. The current implementation has a different failure mode: focus-driven refresh has been removed entirely, so no transient failure is required.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a terminal to follow macOS system appearance and start Codex while the terminal is light.
2. Send a message so both a user-message block and the composer are visible.
3. Change macOS appearance to dark without restarting Codex, or leave the process running across the automatic appearance change.
4. Refocus the terminal and type in the composer.
5. Observe that the terminal's normal foreground/background have changed but the composer/message backgrounds retain the light-theme color. Repeat dark to light as well.

A terminal host can verify the distinction by recording OSC 10/11 requests: the current focus handler intentionally does not send a new pair on focus regain.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should adapt its palette-dependent rendering when the terminal's colors change, without restarting the process, losing draft text, dropping/reordering keys or pasted input, or inserting terminal replies into the composer.

### Root cause and relevant change

[PR #35649](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/35649), merged July 27, intentionally removed focus-time palette queries because they could block the input loop and discard keystrokes. That input-preservation fix is important, but it also leaves a long-lived TUI unable to adapt to system appearance changes.

Source at the inspected commit:

- [`terminal_palette.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_palette.rs#L145-L209): the process-global cache stores the startup foreground/background; `attempted` prevents re-querying through `default_colors()`.
- [`tui/event_stream.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/tui/event_stream.rs#L294-L299): `FocusGained` explicitly preserves the startup-cached palette and only returns the focus event.
- [`style.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/style.rs#L74-L85): user messages get an explicit derived background without a paired explicit foreground. When the terminal's default foreground changes, the old explicit background remains.
- [`terminal_probe.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_probe.rs#L243-L255): the existing Unix color probe uses a direct reader. Its `read_until` helper explicitly does not replay unrelated input, so simply calling this again from the focus handler would reintroduce the reason for #35649.

### Proposed approach

Please restore runtime palette refresh through the normal terminal input/event path rather than reinstating the old synchronous raw-input probe:

1. Request OSC 10/11 asynchronously on focus regain as a compatibility fallback. Also support a terminal theme-change notification so a theme switch while the terminal stays focused can refresh the palette; #38575 tracks DECSET 2031 for that case.
2. Parse replies through the existing input owner, preserving ordinary keys, bracketed paste, and fragmented/late replies. Coalesce repeated refresh triggers and keep only one bounded refresh outstanding; never wait on terminal replies in the UI input handler.
3. Commit a complete valid foreground/background pair atomically. On timeout or malformed/partial replies, preserve the last known good palette and allow a later retry, avoiding #37298's poisoned-cache behavior.
4. Invalidate palette-dependent render caches and repaint the composer and affected transcript content when colors actually change. Preserve an explicitly chosen syntax-highlighting theme.
5. Preserve startup trust/confirmation protections and terminal ownership during external-editor handoff and suspend/resume; a refresh must not start a second competing stdin reader.

Suggested regression coverage: both light/dark directions in the same process; theme changes without a focus transition; repeated focus notifications; immediate, delayed, fragmented, missing and partial OSC replies; a failed refresh followed by a successful one; typing and bracketed paste during refresh; unchanged draft and input ordering; and recoloring existing visible user-message blocks, not only newly generated output.

### Workaround

Launching a new process with `FORCE_COLOR=1 codex` selects Codex's basic-color fallback, which uses the default/reset color for the derived composer background. This is source-backed, not an interactive validation from this investigation, and sacrifices richer colors. Restarting normally only fixes colors until the next theme change. `/theme` controls syntax highlighting and does not invalidate this palette cache.

### Related issues

- #37298 — my earlier report: one failed requery permanently disabled future refreshes.
- #14105 — composer readability after a live terminal theme switch.
- #38575 — theme-change reporting without a focus transition.
- #18942 — related focus/theme refresh discussion.
- #35649 — intentional removal of focus queries to preserve input.

This report adds the 0.154.0 observation and the current startup-only-cache diagnosis, linking the earlier reports rather than treating this as an unrelated color preference. Per the current contribution policy, I am including the implementation constraints and regression cases here for the maintainers.

## Environment

## Problem

Browser Use cannot read an already-open, authenticated website tab in an existing chat. The settings UI shows:

- Default Browsing: **Always allow**
- No website-specific exceptions listed

Tab discovery succeeds and returns the affected tab’s title and URL. However, claiming the tab with `cua.getTab(...)` fails before page contents become available:

```text
Browser use could not acquire authority to observe page content.
A saved user permission setting blocks this action.
The origin approval gate did not grant access for [affected origin].
A saved permission or managed policy denies access.
```

Other websites remain accessible through the same Chrome connection.

## Observed sequence

1. Open and sign in to the affected website manually in Chrome.
2. Ask the assistant in the existing chat to inspect the tab.
3. Browser Use returns the saved-permission error.
4. Inspect Settings → Computer Use → Chrome → Manage: default browsing is allowed, with no custom website rules visible.
5. The user reports that accessing the same website from a **new chat works**. This result was reported by the user, not independently verified in the original chat.

## Expected behavior

The effective permission should match the settings UI, or the UI should identify the overriding restriction and provide a supported way to revoke it and request approval again.

## Diagnostic limits

A stale chat-specific denial is a hypothesis. No local permission files have been inspected or modified, and the original trigger is unknown. The error does not establish that the user deliberately declined access.

Please provide a supported recovery path for the existing chat that preserves its history and unrelated permissions.

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51036
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47506

issues.title: Standalone installer/updater never prunes old releases in $CODEX_HOME/packages/standalone/releases (3.8 GB after 12 updates)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
## What happened

On a Windows standalone install (`install.ps1`), every update installs a new release directory under `$CODEX_HOME\packages\standalone\releases\` and repoints the `current` junction — but superseded releases are never removed. On this machine 12 releases had accumulated (0.134.0 through 0.144.1), ~3.8 GB total:

```
$CODEX_HOME\packages\standalone\
  current  -> releases\0.144.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc   (junction)
  install.lock
  releases\
    0.134.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\
    0.135.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\
    ... (10 in total superseded) ...
    0.143.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\
    0.144.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\
```

Each release dir carries `bin\codex.exe` (~341 MB) + `bin\codex-code-mode-host.exe` (~54 MB), so retention grows ~400 MB per update with no cleanup mechanism I could find.

Nothing references the superseded directories after an update:

- the PATH launcher (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin`) is a junction chain that resolves through `standalone\current` only;
- browser-extension native-host registrations (`chrome-native-hosts-v2.json`) point at the desktop app runtime copy (`plugins\.plugin-appserver\codex.exe`), not at `packages\`;
- the desktop app bundles its own backend and does not use `packages\` either.

Deleting the 10 superseded directories manually reclaimed ~3 GB with no observed breakage (`codex --version` and the PATH junction chain unaffected).

## What I expected

`codex update` (or the installer) to prune superseded releases — e.g. keep `current` plus one previous for rollback — or an explicit GC/prune command.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations (10.0.26200)
- codex-cli 0.144.1, standalone install via `install.ps1`
- Possibly also applies to `install.sh` managed installs on macOS/Linux (not verified here)

For triage context, similar unbounded-local-growth reports in other components: #30335 (Crashpad), #27789 (code_sign_clone), #29994 (marketplace clones).

issues.body:
**Goal:** To significantly improve the reliability, visibility, and actionability of our project's internal (non-benchmark) evaluations.

**Problem:** Our current small project evals are inconsistent ("bleed"), making it difficult to trust their results, track quality trends, and quickly address regressions. This slows down development and impacts confidence in changes.

**Vision:** A streamlined evaluation system where internal project evals are stable, provide clear signals, and enable rapid feedback loops. Developers can confidently rely on these evals to catch issues early and understand the impact of their changes.

**Key Outcomes:**

- Reduced flakiness and increased reliability of existing project evals.
- Clear visibility into eval results and historical trends.
- Faster detection and easier debugging of regressions.
- Basic automation to flag issues and guide developers.
- "Approve" button to increase visibility and reduce excessive runs

**Out of Scope:**

- Large-scale benchmark evals (e.g., SWE-bench, terminal-bench).
- Overhauling the entire testing infrastructure beyond the scope of these specific project evals.

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

In certain cases, the main agent spends many turns, iterations, making incremental changes in hopes of solving a small issue. For example, if a typecheck or linter comes back with numerous failures. The main agent may spend many turns/tokens to help get the build into a healthy state. 

This is one such subtask (also including fixing a broken build) that could be delegated to a subagent such as the generalist to outsource the fix and return to the main agent with a working build. 

Considerations/Objectives:
- Investigate getting the model to use the generalist in subtasks such as this
- evaluate if calling is consistent and provides enough feedback back to the main agent to prevent any hallucinations of state (does the generalist let the main agent know what changes it had to make / if the fix couldn't be fixed without further changes)
- Does the main agent provide enough context for the generalist to successfully accomplish its tasks? Or could this require a way for the main agent to share more context?
- Add behavior evals to see if the behavior is followed consistently.

The goal here is to have the main agent's work be reviewed by specialized personas that work in parallel to provide high quality feedback and double check work.
