issues.title: Prompt is discarded after 'Submission failed' (host-ack timeout): composer cleared, not saved to history, delivered late or never

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When `session.send` fails because the session host stopped acknowledging events (the #5100 state), the CLI clears the prompt the user just submitted and keeps no copy of it. What happens to the prompt afterwards is unpredictable: sometimes it's delivered later anyway, and sometimes it's never delivered. The CLI shows:

```
Submission failed: Error: Request session.send failed with message: session event delivery failed: session host did not acknowledge the assistant.reasoning_delta event within 120s
```

After that, the composer is empty and the text is not put back. Up arrow and Ctrl+R don't find it, and there is no resend option. In the case below:

- **One "failed" prompt was most likely delivered 73 seconds later, after the user had been told it failed.** Input history points to a late delivery rather than a retype (see the timeline).
- **A later multi-paragraph prompt was never delivered.** The user had to rewrite it from memory.

**Why this happens (from reading the shipped `cli-main.js` in 1.0.103 and 1.0.104):** in the interactive submit path, the prompt is added to input history only in the success branch after `session.send` resolves. The error branch only emits `Submission failed`. The pending-submission tracker retires the draft when the send throws, and nothing restores the text to the composer. This means any `session.send` rejection leaves the user with no copy of the prompt, not only the 120s acknowledgement timeout. Whether the prompt still reaches the agent later is decided out of the user's sight.

**How often:** since October 23, this machine's retained session data has **20 `Submission failed` errors across 5 sessions, all with this host-acknowledgement error (the event named varies)**. #5100 notes that the agent's own output keeps being saved to `events.jsonl` after delivery fails. The user's input is the one thing nobody keeps a copy of.

### Affected version

1.0.103 (`copilotVersion` in `session.start`). The same submit and history code is in 1.0.104.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

This isn't deterministic, because it depends on first reaching the #5100 state.

1. Run a long interactive session. Ours was launched through a wrapper that loads several extensions. It used autopilot, many subagents, and a recurring scheduled prompt every 30 minutes. It ran 15 hours with 13 auto-compactions and no resume.
2. Wait until the host stops acknowledging events (#5100). The first visible sign is `Submission failed: ... did not acknowledge ... within 120s`.
3. Keep working. Submit prompts while the agent is busy.
4. Some submissions show `Submission failed`, and each one clears the composer. In our case, after the CLI logged `queue drain abandoned`, the next failed prompt (14:19:03) was never delivered before the user exited 11 minutes later, and no copy of it remained.

Timeline of the affected session (UTC, 2026-10-27):

| Time | What happened |
|---|---|
| 02:59:42 | First `Submission failed ... assistant.reasoning_delta ... within 120s`. The session was about 3.5 hours old. |
| 03:00–13:48 | The session stays partly usable. The agent keeps running turns. Two more `Submission failed` errors appear, at 04:56 and 04:59. Each of the three failures is followed 71–73 seconds later by a typed message arriving as a steering message. The first of these (03:00:55) was most likely the "failed" 02:59:42 prompt delivered late, not a retype. Successful submits write input history, and the history file suggests this one never did (see the explanation below the table). We can't tell whether the 04:58 and 05:00 messages were retypes or late deliveries. All 22 runs of the 30-minute scheduled prompt in this period log a `schedule_delivery_failed` warning ("Scheduled prompt #1 ... failed"), yet each run arrives 3 seconds to 4 minutes later. |
| 14:11:40 | `Submission failed`. A typed steering message arrives 21 seconds later. Like the 04:56 and 04:59 cases, we can't tell whether it was a retype or a late delivery. |
| 14:17:15 | The scheduled run fails again. This time it is not delivered. |
| 14:17:26 | `Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned` |
| 14:19:03 | `Submission failed` for a long multi-paragraph prompt. At the same moment the log shows two `Scheduled queue processing failed; retrying once` lines, and no later line reports the retry's outcome. **This prompt was never delivered and no copy of it remains.** |
| 14:29:52 | The user exits. Shutdown also fails with the same cached delivery error. |

Evidence that the 14:19:03 prompt was lost:

- `events.jsonl` has no user-typed `user.message` after 14:12:01. The only later `user.message` is a subagent prompt at 14:14:46.
- The text wasn't restored to the composer.
- It isn't in input history. That file also has a separate overwrite problem (#5265), so the code path above is the stronger evidence here.

Why the 03:00:55 message was most likely a late delivery and not a retype:

1. A second process (call it C) saved two prompts to history at 02:58 and 03:00:13. That process started after this session did, so this session's in-memory history list didn't include those two entries.
2. A third process loaded the history file when it started at 03:01:34, and it wrote the final version of the file at 14:29:54. The final file still contains the 02:58 and 03:00:13 entries.
3. If this session had saved a history entry at 03:00:55, it would have written its own list, which lacked those two entries, over the file before 03:01:34. They survived, so this session saved nothing between 03:00:55 and 03:01:34. Process C didn't write again in that window, because no later C entry from that window appears in the file.
4. In the shipped code, every interactive submit path saves to history when the send call returns. For steering submissions, the submit tracker resolves `true` once the send returns, and history is skipped only if an internal `skipHistory` option is set. No `Submission failed` appeared near 03:00:55, so a retyped prompt's send didn't fail. If it succeeded, it would have saved to history, unless its send took more than 39 seconds to return. The 03:00:55 message was therefore most likely the 02:59:42 prompt, delivered late. Either way, the user was told the 02:59:42 prompt failed and had no copy of it.

### Expected behavior

- Save the draft before sending it (for example, in session state), and clear it only after the session confirms it has the prompt.
- If the send fails, put the text and attachments back in the composer, or keep the prompt visibly marked as failed with a resend option.
- Add the prompt to input history whether or not the send succeeds. History records what the user typed.
- Report delivery honestly. If a "failed" prompt is still queued and will run later, don't say it failed. If it's dropped (for example, after `queue drain abandoned`), say so explicitly.
- If the session is in the permanent failed state from #5100, say so. Carry unsent drafts across `--resume` or `/restart` so they can be resent.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64, 96 GiB RAM
- Ghostty, zsh
- Launched through a wrapper that adds several native extensions. Several other interactive `copilot` processes were running on the same machine.
- `events.jsonl` for the affected session was 444 MB.
- Related: #5100 (the root failure state), #5253, and #5018 (same family). #1780 asks to recover queued prompts after a crash. #4477 covers a prompt lost on stop.

The full logs contain private content and can't be shared publicly. I can provide filtered excerpts on request.

issues.title: Constrain `run_factory` to registered factory names to prevent repeated guesses

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Summary

`run_factory` can be exposed with an unconstrained `name` argument even when no matching factory is registered. The model can interpret tool availability as factory availability, invent plausible names, and retry them serially.

Originally reported from the VS Code Agents Window in microsoft/vscode#329551.

### Observed behavior

With Copilot CLI 1.0.78 and GPT-5.6 Sol, one session produced 13 distinct model-authored `run_factory` calls. Every call failed immediately with:

```text
RpcResponseError: No factory registered with name "<name>"
```

The model first tried eight implementation-oriented names:

- `apply_finding`
- `code_implementation_factory`
- `single_task`
- `implementation`
- `code-task`
- `fix-factory`
- `repo_task`
- `review_then_implement`

It later tried five more names for video analysis:

- `video_analysis`
- `analyze_video`
- `single_video_analysis`
- `video-analysis`
- `media_analysis`

These were separate assistant-authored calls after each rejection, not host retries. No factory ran.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Expose `run_factory` in a session where no matching factories are registered.
2. Ask the agent to perform a routine single-session task, such as a small implementation or media-analysis task.
3. Observe that the model may invent and repeatedly retry factory names.

### Expected behavior

Invalid factory names should be impossible or strongly bounded. Ideally:

- Dynamically constrain `name` to registered factory names.
- Do not expose `run_factory` when there are no registered factories or resumable runs.
- If dynamic enum generation is not possible, require registry discovery before invocation and include available names in validation errors.
- Enforce exactly one of `name` and `resumeFromRunId` at the schema level.

### Actual behavior

`name` is effectively a free-form string, so failures occur only after a costly tool round trip. Prompt guidance to use factories selectively did not prevent repeated guesses.

issues.title: Streaming long Markdown links repeatedly reflow tables

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

While a response is streaming, inline Markdown links inside tables cause repeated table re-layout and visually disruptive jumping.

For a Markdown link such as `[foo](https://very-long-url...)` inside a table, the URL arrives character by character. Each character appears to trigger another table layout/render pass using the incomplete raw Markdown. The columns continuously resize and wrap; once the closing `)` arrives, the whole link collapses to its visible text (`foo`) and the table jumps again.

This makes tables containing several long links very slow and visually unstable even though the final rendered table may look correct.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start GitHub Copilot CLI in interactive mode.
2. Enter this prompt:

   > Render a Markdown table with several rows. Each row must contain an inline Markdown link whose destination URL is at least 150 characters long.

3. Watch the table while the response streams.
4. Observe columns repeatedly resizing and wrapping while each link destination arrives.
5. Observe another layout jump when each completed link collapses to its visible text.

### Expected behavior

Streaming incomplete Markdown should not cause a full table re-layout on every character. Table columns should remain visually stable while link destinations stream, then render using the visible link text when complete.

### Additional context

- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- CPU architecture: arm64
- Shell: zsh
- Video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98bc24df-27e5-47f6-aab2-345dd3e995e2

The video uses a trivial example. The effect becomes much more disruptive with additional columns and rows. The demo also rendered unusually quickly; normal rendering is approximately 0.3-0.5 times this speed.

issues.title: Copilot CLI grep compaction corrupts filenames and line numbers, and merges distinct files
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in rg tool returns incorrect filenames and line numbers when output compaction interprets numeric filename suffixes or directory components as grep field delimiters. Standalone ripgrep output launched in bash is correct.

This can misattribute search results during debugging. Distinct files can also be merged into one reported file.

### Affected version

1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Create a directory whose absolute path reaches at least 64 characters, then place the attached rg-compactor-repro.log-3.txt file into that directory and rename it to rg-compactor-repro.log-3 (strip the '.txt', I couldn't attach the file without adding that to the end). Start a new copilot session and tell it :

```
Validate a suspected Copilot CLI grep-output compaction bug using this existing file:
/path/to/rg-compactor-repro.log-3

Do not modify the file. Use its full absolute path: output length affects whether compaction activates. The file contains 20 identical RG_REPRO lines.

Perform these checks using the built-in rg tool (functions.rg), NOT shell ripgrep or another search tool:

1. Control: pattern="RG_REPRO", paths="<file_path>, output_mode="content", head_limit=19, -n=true.
2. Reproduction: use exactly the same arguments, except head_limit=20.

Then independently obtain the correct baseline using Bash:
rg -H -n -m 20 RG_REPRO <file_path>

Compare the literal tool responses, without silently correcting filenames or line numbers.

On the affected CLI 1.0.105 build, the control retains the filename ending in .log-3 and actual line numbers 1 through 19. The reproduction instead groups results under rg-compactor-repro.log (losing -3), gives every result apparent line number 3, and moves the real line number into the text, such as "3: 1:RG_REPRO". The Bash baseline retains .log-3 and actual line numbers 1 through 20.

Report REPRODUCED only if that corruption is observed. Otherwise report NOT REPRODUCED or INCONCLUSIVE and explain the actual results. Merely grouping results is not a failure if filenames and line numbers remain correct. Preserve the tool responses as evidence; do not assume a different CLI version has the same defect.
```

Ensure you update /path/to to whatever path you actually used. 

What this test does it demonstrate that the built in rg tool is returning corrupt/different results than using ripgrep directly in bash.

Additional confirmed impact

• Numeric directory components can trigger the same corruption.
• Disabling line-number output still produces fabricated line numbers.
• Two files,  plain.log  and  plain.log-3 , containing 32 matching lines each, are incorrectly reported as 64 matches across one file.

### Expected behavior

built in rg tool shouldn't produce corrupt results pointing to non-existent files.

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Fix browser login URL wrapping and fallback

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

The Device Code login flow works as expected: it displays a one-time code and URL, opens the URL automatically, and offers to copy the code to the clipboard when a key is pressed.

The **Sign in with your browser (recommended)** flow behaves differently. Although it displays a message such as “If your browser didn't open, visit:”, pressing a key does not open the browser. The fallback URL is also difficult or impossible to use in the terminal:

- The URL is long enough to wrap across terminal lines.
- Only the beginning of the URL (for example, `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?`) is rendered as a clickable link.
- The query string containing `client_id` and the remaining parameters appears after the line break and is neither clickable nor reliably selectable/copied.
- Resizing the terminal changes the wrapping behavior unpredictably; depending on the width, the URL may appear on one line with its end clipped or wrap inconsistently.

This prevents users from completing browser authentication when automatic browser opening fails.

## Affected environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI
- Linux under WSL2

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the GitHub Copilot CLI login flow.
2. Select **Sign in with your browser (recommended)**.
3. Observe the fallback message and URL.
4. Press a key when prompted.
5. If the browser does not open, try selecting or clicking the displayed URL, then resize the terminal and observe the URL again.

## Expected behavior

The browser login flow should use the same browser-opening behavior as the Device Code flow: pressing a key should open the browser automatically.

If automatic browser opening fails, the complete fallback URL should be rendered as one usable clickable link without being split into a non-interactive suffix. The CLI should also provide a final copy-to-clipboard option so users can paste the complete URL into a browser manually.

## Additional context

Please preserve the full URL and its query parameters across terminal widths, or otherwise provide a terminal-safe presentation that remains clickable and copyable.

issues.title: MCP OAuth: initialize request after successful OAuth login omits User-Agent header, ignoring configured custom headers

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary When connecting to a remote MCP server (HTTP/Streamable-HTTP transport) that requires OAuth authentication, the underlying `rmcp`/`reqwest`-based HTTP client used by Copilot CLI/App does not send a `User-Agent` header on the `initialize` request that follows a successful OAuth token exchange. Custom headers configured for the MCP server in `mcp-config.json` (via `copilot mcp add --header "..."`) are also not applied to this specific request. This causes `initialize` requests to fail against any MCP server that is fronted by infrastructure which rejects requests without a `User-Agent` header (e.g. AWS WAF's managed rule `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` / `NoUserAgent_HEADER`, or similar reverse-proxy/WAF configurations), even though the OAuth handshake itself (authorize/token exchange) completes successfully. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a remote HTTP MCP server that requires OAuth, optionally with a custom header: ```bash copilot mcp add --transport http my-server https://example.com/mcp --header "User-Agent: MyCustomAgent/1.0" ``` 2. Trigger authentication (e.g. via `Authenticate` in the Copilot App, or by using the tool in Copilot CLI). 3. Complete the browser-based OAuth login/consent flow successfully. 4. Observe that the subsequent `initialize` request fails if the target server (or infrastructure in front of it) rejects requests lacking a `User-Agent` header — even though the configured custom `User-Agent` header was set on the server config. ## Expected Behavior - The MCP client should always send a non-empty `User-Agent` header (e.g. an SDK/product default such as `GitHubCopilotCLI/`) on all requests, including the post-OAuth `initialize` request. - Any custom headers configured for the MCP server (via `--header`, or the `headers` field in `mcp-config.json`) should be honored consistently across all requests sent to that server, including the OAuth-authenticated `initialize` request — not only a subset of requests. ## Actual Behavior - The `initialize` request sent after a successful OAuth token exchange appears to omit the `User-Agent` header entirely (confirmed via server-side testing: a request without any `User-Agent` header reproduces the exact same generic, non-JSON `403 Forbidden` response observed by the client). - Configuring a custom `User-Agent` header via `copilot mcp add --header "User-Agent: ..."` does not change this behavior — the header is stored in `mcp-config.json` but is not applied to the `initialize` request. - The resulting error surfaces as: ``` RPC error -32603: Request session.mcp.oauth.login failed with message: failed to initialize MCP client: Send message error Transport [rmcp::transport::worker::WorkerTransport>] error: unexpected server response: HTTP 403 Forbidden: 403 Forbidden

403 Forbidden

, when send initialize request ``` - The prior OAuth challenge/token exchange step succeeds (HTTP 401 with a proper `WWW-Authenticate`/OAuth challenge, then successful browser login/consent) — the failure occurs specifically on the follow-up `initialize` call. ## Environment - GitHub Copilot CLI/App version: 1.0.82 (latest at time of testing) - OS: macOS (Darwin) - MCP server transport: `http` (Streamable HTTP), OAuth-protected (dynamic client registration / RFC 9728 protected resource metadata) - Same MCP server + OAuth flow works correctly in VS Code's Copilot Chat extension, suggesting this is specific to the `rmcp`-based client used by Copilot CLI/App rather than a server-side issue. ## Additional Notes - This was root-caused by directly testing the target MCP server with and without a `User-Agent` header: omitting it reproduces byte-for-byte the same generic HTML 403 response seen by the CLI/App, while including any non-empty `User-Agent` returns the expected JSON response from the server's own application layer. - No corporate proxy, VPN, or network-level header rewriting was involved — headers were confirmed to pass through the network unmodified in isolated testing. - We suspect the `initialize` request after OAuth is issued via a code path (`RawCapturingReqwestClient` in `rmcp::transport::streamable_http_client`) that either uses a fresh/default `reqwest::Client` without the configured `User-Agent`/custom headers, or otherwise doesn't propagate the per-server header configuration used for other requests.

issues.title: The checkpoint list in the system prompt changes after /compact, so the next call writes the prompt cache again
issues.body:
### Describe the bug After a compaction, the CLI adds the new checkpoint to the `` part of the system prompt ("N prior checkpoints" plus their titles). The system prompt sits near the start of every request, so once it changes, the provider can't reuse the cached prefix from that point on. The next call writes everything after it again: the rest of the system prompt and the whole conversation. In a small test chat that's only a few thousand tokens. My real chats are usually 150K to 270K tokens, so each change writes all of that again. Over four days of my own sessions, the checkpoint list was the most common reason the system prompt changed in the middle of a chat (14 of 21 changes). ### Affected version GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (also seen on 1.0.88) ### Steps to reproduce the behavior I used a clean `COPILOT_HOME`, an empty git repo, and Claude Haiku 4.5. The token numbers come from the `session.usage_record` events in the session's `events.jsonl`. 1. `copilot -p "Reply with just: one" --model claude-haiku-4.5` 2. `copilot --resume= -p "/compact" --model claude-haiku-4.5` 3. `copilot --resume= -p "Reply with just: two" --model claude-haiku-4.5` 4. Compare the two `system.message` events in `events.jsonl`. The second one is 330 characters longer. The only difference is these lines, added inside ``: ```text - checkpoints/: 1 prior checkpoints (index.md has full list) Checkpoints (read those relevant to your current task): 001-session-initialized-awaiting-t.md - Session initialized, awaiting task Checkpoint titles indicate what was accomplished. Read relevant checkpoints for prior history, technical decisions, and file changes. ``` The call after the compaction read 10,732 tokens from the cache and wrote 5,580 (input 16,322). For comparison, the same two messages without `/compact` in between: the system prompt stays identical and the second call reads 15,788 and writes 41. What happens to the cache, as I understand it: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Call 1
system prompt v1 + messages"] -->|writes| C[("cache")] B["/compact
adds checkpoint 001"] --> D["Call 2
system prompt v2 + messages"] C -->|"prefix only matches
up to session_context"| D D -->|"writes the rest again"| C ``` ### Expected behavior A new checkpoint doesn't change the system prompt of a chat that's already running, so the next call can still read its whole prefix from the cache. ### Additional context - macOS 27.0, arm64, zsh - In my own long chats the list doesn't always change right at the compaction. It sometimes changes much later in the same chat (anywhere from a few to over a thousand events after it). So one compaction can cost two full writes: one when the conversation is summarised, and one more when the list catches up. I couldn't reproduce that timing in a clean setup, so I may be wrong about what triggers it.

issues.title: Options passed to a custom skill invocation are dropped before reaching the model

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When invoking a custom skill using `/skill-name --option value`, Copilot CLI records the complete input but omits the option arguments from the prompt dispatched to the skill.

Environment:
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.81-6
- Windows
- Session: 2da2d958-a8cd-4eeb-9760-241fac5b53ed
- Occurred around 2026-08-21 04:10:27 UTC

The session event log contains the complete command and arguments. However, the model-visible invocation contains only that the skill was explicitly invoked plus its SKILL.md instructions. Because the arguments are absent, the skill follows its no-arguments behavior.

### Affected version

1.0.81-6

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Define a repository skill that supports command-line-style arguments and has different behavior when no arguments are supplied.
2. Invoke it with arguments, for example:
   /evaluate-meeting-prep --slides week-over-week,speed,tokens --current "Model=C:\path\to\cohort"
3. Observe that the skill loads successfully.
4. Observe that the skill behaves as if no arguments were supplied and displays its interactive slide-selection menu.
5. Inspect the session event log: the original user.message contains the complete command, including --slides and --current, but those arguments are absent from the prompt delivered to the model with the skill context.

### Expected behavior

When a custom skill is invoked as `/skill-name <arguments>`, the complete argument text should be included in the model-visible skill invocation. In this example, the skill should receive `--slides week-over-week,speed,tokens` and the supplied cohort paths, then proceed without asking the user to select slides again.

### Additional context

- Copilot CLI: 1.0.81-6
- Operating system: Windows x64
- Shell: PowerShell
- Session ID: 2da2d958-a8cd-4eeb-9760-241fac5b53ed
- Timestamp: 2026-08-21 04:10:27 UTC

Diagnostic detail: the session's raw `user.message` event contains the complete 521-character invocation, including `--slides`, `--current`, `--prior`, and `--outdir`. The subsequent model-visible skill invocation contains the loaded skill instructions but none of those options. This indicates the options are lost during skill dispatch rather than input parsing.

issues.title: Remote Control: voice mode from GitHub Mobile (talk to the session, hear spoken replies)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

With `/remote on` I can steer a running Copilot CLI / Agent Host session from the GitHub Mobile app, which is great when I'm away from the keyboard. But the remote side is text only: I type on a phone keyboard (or use the OS dictation), then read long replies on a small screen. There is no way to simply talk to the session and hear what it did.

Voice exists on both ends, just not across Remote Control:

- The CLI's `/voice` uses the microphone of the machine running the session, so it doesn't help when the session is driven from the phone.
- VS Code's Voice Mode (hands-free, spoken responses, "approve"/"reject" by voice) covers the desktop, but only in the chat view and the Agents window, not for a session steered remotely.

### Proposed solution

A voice mode for Remote Control in GitHub Mobile (and the github.com task page), reusing the Voice Mode semantics VS Code already ships:

- Hold-to-talk or hands-free listening; the transcript is sent to the session as a normal remote prompt (the same `command-…` path that text uses today).
- Spoken replies: a short summary of each turn while the agent works, with the full tool output left in the transcript to read later.
- Approvals and questions by voice ("approve", "reject", an option label or number), with the card still shown on screen.
- Interrupting a spoken reply by talking.
- Language selection, since OS dictation on the phone handles non-English speech noticeably better than a fixed-language transcriber.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. Start a long refactor in VS Code / the CLI, `/remote on`, leave the desk.
2. On the phone, say: "How is the migration going? Did the tests pass?" and hear a 10-second summary.
3. The agent asks for permission to delete the old table; the card appears on the phone and I say "approve".
4. Say: "Also update the README, then open a PR" and get a spoken confirmation when it's done.

### Additional context

- Related: microsoft/vscode#341760 / microsoft/vscode#345426 (remote prompts not rendered in VS Code; fixed there), which is the same Remote Control path this feature would build on.
- VS Code Voice Mode docs: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice

issues.title: Remote Control: show nested (child) sessions on GitHub Mobile and github.com, like the VS Code Agents window
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

In the VS Code Agents window, a session can spawn child sessions (nested sessions / sub-chats). The sidebar shows them as a tree under the parent, for example `Playground Project` → `Greeting`, and I can open each one and read or steer it.

When I steer the same parent session from GitHub Mobile or the github.com task page via `/remote on`, the child sessions are not visible at all. I only see the parent conversation. Work that the parent delegated to a child (and the child's questions, permission prompts and results) is invisible from the phone, so I can't follow or steer it until I'm back at the desk.

### Proposed solution

Mirror the Agents window's session tree in Remote Control:

- List child sessions under their parent (with status: running, waiting for input, done) on GitHub Mobile and github.com.
- Open a child session to read its transcript and steer it, with the same Remote Control semantics as the parent.
- Surface a child's pending permission prompts or questions in the parent's view (or as a notification), so a blocked child doesn't stall silently.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. In VS Code, ask a session to "create a Greeting chat for this task and hand it the details" (nested session).
2. Leave the desk, open the session on the phone: the sidebar/tree shows `Greeting` under the parent with its status.
3. Tap `Greeting`, read what it did, answer its question by steering it, go back to the parent.

### Additional context

- The Agents window already models this (parent/child sessions, "Open in Agents window", nested sessions with separate workspaces as of VS Code 1.144), so the data exists host-side; this is about exposing it through Mission Control / Remote Control clients.
- Related Remote Control work: microsoft/vscode#345426 (remote prompts rendering), github/copilot-cli#5315 (voice mode for Remote Control).

issues.title: GitHub Mobile (iOS): Copilot CLI Remote Sessions Stuck on “Working” Indefinitely
issues.body:
### Describe the bug


The GitHub Mobile app on iOS fails to display GitHub Copilot CLI remote sessions correctly. When opening any remote CLI session, the application remains stuck on the “Working” indicator indefinitely and does not render the session conversation or progress.

The exact same sessions work correctly when accessed through Safari on the same iPhone.

This appears to be an issue specific to the GitHub Mobile iOS application rather than the Copilot CLI backend or remote session connectivity.

Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a GitHub Copilot CLI session with remote access enabled.
2. Open the GitHub Mobile app on an iPhone.
3. Navigate to Copilot agent sessions.
4. Select an active remote CLI session.
5. Observe that the session displays “Working” indefinitely without loading the conversation.

issues.title: Model "auto" always runs with reasoning effort disabled (reasoningEffort: null), and rejects any attempt to configure one

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the model is set to `auto`, every request is sent **without any reasoning effort**:

1. Selecting `auto` sets the session's `reasoningEffort` to `null` (visible in the session's `events.jsonl` as `session.model_change → "reasoningEffort": null`).
2. The auto router (`auto_v2`) picks a model per prompt (`session.auto_mode_resolved`) but **never assigns a reasoning effort** to it — the request goes out with none, confirmed by `reasoning_effort = NULL` and `reasoning_tokens = 0` in `~/.copilot/session-store.db` (`assistant_usage_events`).
3. Trying to set one explicitly is rejected: `copilot --model auto --effort xhigh` fails with `Error: Model "auto" does not support reasoning effort configuration (requested: "xhigh").`

So with `auto` there is **no way at all** to run with reasoning enabled. The degradation is silent — no error, no indication in the UI — and the impact on agentic work is severe: on a large agentic prompt (spec generation with mandatory file reads), the routed model (`gpt-5.3-codex`) ends its turn **without making a single tool call**, replying that it "could not perform the investigation". The exact same prompt, on the exact same routed model, works flawlessly when a reasoning effort is set (see "Same model, only effort differs" below).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```bash
# 1) auto → no reasoning (silent)
copilot --model auto --allow-all-tools -p "Reply with exactly: ok"

# 2) control: explicit model → reasoning works
copilot --model gpt-5.4 --allow-all-tools -p "Reply with exactly: ok"

# 3) auto + explicit effort → hard error
copilot --model auto --effort xhigh --allow-all-tools -p "Reply with exactly: ok"
```

Then inspect what was actually sent (replace the session ids printed in the `Resume` line):

```bash
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.copilot/session-store.db \
  "SELECT session_id, model, reasoning_effort, reasoning_tokens
   FROM assistant_usage_events ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Observed results:

| Run | Routed/used model | `reasoning_effort` | `reasoning_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — `--model auto` | `gpt-5.4-mini` (via `auto_v2`) | **NULL** | **0** |
| 2 — `--model gpt-5.4` | `gpt-5.4` | `xhigh` | 21 |
| 3 — `--model auto --effort xhigh` | — | — | `Error: Model "auto" does not support reasoning effort configuration (requested: "xhigh").` |

The same happens in interactive mode: switching to `auto` logs
`session.model_change ... "previousReasoningEffort": "xhigh", "reasoningEffort": null`
in `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl`, and every subsequent `session.auto_mode_resolved` runs the chosen model with no effort.

### Same model, only effort differs — night and day

Real-world case that led us here (a large spec-generation prompt, ~19.6k input tokens, requiring file reads and skill loading):

- `auto` → routed to `gpt-5.3-codex`, `reasoning_effort = NULL`: the model ends the turn after **158 output tokens, 0 reasoning tokens, 0 tool calls**, claiming it could not perform the investigation. Reproduced consistently across several sessions.
- Same prompt, same `gpt-5.3-codex`, with `reasoning_effort = xhigh`: normal agentic behavior — tool calls, thousands of reasoning tokens, task completed.

The only variable is the reasoning effort. `auto` mode currently guarantees the degraded path.

### Expected behavior

`auto` should never silently disable reasoning. Either:

- the auto router assigns an appropriate reasoning effort for the routed model on each request (clamping to what that model supports), and/or
- a user-provided effort (`--effort`, settings `effortLevel`, session config) is honored under `auto` and clamped per routed model — instead of being cleared on switch and rejected on the CLI flag.

### Additional context

- This looks like an overcorrection of #2870: there, switching to `auto` **kept** the previous effort and caused loud `400` errors on models that don't support it; the fix apparently clears the effort entirely, trading a loud error for a silent, permanent degradation. #4459 and #4445 show the invalid-combination side of this is still not fully solved either — both symptoms share the same root: the auto router does not manage effort per routed model.
- The ACP server mode (`copilot --acp`) is affected identically, with no workaround at all: `session/set_config_option` with `model=auto` clears the effort and removes the reasoning-effort config option from the session, so ACP clients cannot restore it.

issues.body:
## Summary
Startup hint "No copilot instructions found" is misleading when user-level instructions exist at `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`

## Environment
- **Product/Service**: GitHub Copilot CLI
- **Version**: v0.0.413-0
- **OS**: Windows 11

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create user-level instructions at `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`
2. Launch `copilot` from a directory that is **not** inside a git repository (e.g., `$HOME` — which is typically not git-tracked but is where user-level instructions live)
3. Observe startup output

## Expected Behavior
The startup hint should either:
- Not appear when user-level instructions (`~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`) are detected, OR
- Distinguish between project-level and user-level instructions (e.g., "No **project** instructions found. User-level instructions loaded from ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md")

## Actual Behavior
Displays:
```
💡 No copilot instructions found. Run /init to generate a copilot-instructions.md file for this project.
```

This message appears even though user-level instructions at `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` **are** being loaded and applied correctly. The hint creates unnecessary confusion — users believe their instructions are not working.

## Impact
**Low** — Cosmetic/UX issue. Instructions load correctly, but the message undermines developer confidence in their setup and may lead to unnecessary troubleshooting.

## Additional Context
- The CLI documentation confirms `$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` is a supported instructions location
- The hint only checks for project-level instructions (`.github/copilot-instructions.md` in a git root) and ignores the user-level file
- Particularly confusing for users who primarily work from their home directory or non-repo folders
- The user home directory (`$HOME` / `%USERPROFILE%`) is typically not git-tracked, yet it is the standard location for user-level Copilot instructions — this makes the hint appear in the most common non-repo launch context

issues.title: Context window rollover still fails after #5205 closed as completed: checkpoint.md absent recurs on 1.0.105

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
Filing this as a new issue because #5205 — which carries the original report, an independent reproduction, and my 1.0.105 reproduction — was closed as completed on 2026-10-30 with no closing comment, no linked PR or commit, and no release containing a fix. The latest release is still 1.0.105 (2026-10-28), and no changelog entry in any version mentions checkpoint.md or the rollover refusal. Only the author or maintainers can reopen #5205, so the post-closure evidence also lives here. (Reopen request with the same evidence: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5205#issuecomment-6543292385; my original reproduction: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5205#issuecomment-6485623208)

**Environment:** Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (current latest release), Windows 11.

**Failure:** "Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

**Recurrences since the #5205 closure, both on 1.0.105:**

1. **2026-10-30 ~18:44 UTC** — resuming a parked long-running session: the rollover was refused with the exact error above. The session had zero compaction events and its checkpoints/ folder held only the stub index.md, so no checkpoint existed to satisfy the gate.
2. **2026-10-31T03:05:38Z** — a delegated agent launch died at startup with the same refusal delivered as a session.error event ("Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"), aborting the parent run's shutdown records mid-sequence.

**Pattern (unchanged across all reports):** in a session where no compaction has run, no checkpoint is ever registered — automatic compaction does not create one — and any fresh-context rollover in that session is then refused. The agent cannot create the checkpoint itself, and no documented mechanism lets it; the only workaround is a manual /compact by the user before the rollover point.

**Expected:** either rollover does not require a checkpoint the system never created, or the checkpoint is created by the automatic path the documentation describes. If a fix has shipped somewhere not visible in the releases or on #5205, a pointer to the PR or release would settle both issues.

### Describe the bug

Native Computer Use on Windows discovered an Edge window, but a subsequent text-only, depth-limited state request could not establish its URL or web accessibility tree. Browser content was withheld. Please route this report to the native Computer Use Windows maintainers for prerequisite/diagnostic guidance or a verification-preserving fix.

**Prior observed result, not newly reproduced for this report:**

- `url: (missing - fail-closed)`
- The tool reported that the window exposed neither a web accessibility tree nor a verified URL and that browser pixels were withheld.
- Its instruction was: "Stop this attempt instead of inferring page identity or content from an unverified screenshot."

The attempt stopped. No screenshot retry, navigation, alternate content-extraction path, or configuration change followed. This report is not a request to weaken the fail-closed behavior.

### Affected version / environment

Installed executable version metadata checked on 2026-10-28:

- GitHub Copilot CLI: **1.0.105**.
- Microsoft Edge: **155.0.4283.62**.
- Windows 11: OS version **10.0.26300.0**, 64-bit operating system.

These are installed-file/OS observations, not fresh `copilot --version` output or verification of the running browser version. The native Computer Use backend/plugin version, exact launch transport/arguments, terminal/shell, and browser window mode are **unverified**. No new Copilot or browser session was started to collect these details.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

**Historical operation sequence only; not a verified minimal reproduction:**

1. In a local Windows Copilot CLI session exposing native `computer-use` MCP tools, window discovery succeeded.
2. A text-only, depth-limited state request targeted an Edge window.
3. The native tool returned the missing-URL/accessibility result above and withheld content.

The exact state-tool name, parameter payload, and depth value have not been verified. Reproduction frequency and behavior on other browser windows/versions are unknown. No claim is made that an arbitrary Edge page reproduces this issue.

### Expected behavior / clarification requested

Preserve URL verification before exposing browser content. If a supported prerequisite is missing, provide an actionable, non-content-bearing diagnostic rather than requiring users to guess or broaden permissions.

Could maintainers identify:

1. Supported Windows/Edge prerequisites for obtaining a verified URL and web accessibility tree, including any browser/window-mode limitations?
2. Metadata-only diagnostics for identifying the native backend/plugin version and the verification stage that failed, without capturing URLs, page content, screenshots, credentials, or raw session logs?
3. A documented correction or fixed version that preserves fail-closed verification, if this is a known defect?

### Additional context

The reviewed [native Computer Use setup/troubleshooting documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/computer-use) establishes Windows availability but did not establish an Edge compatibility matrix or a missing-URL remedy. The [CLI URL-permission documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/configure-copilot-cli) does not establish that URL allowlisting repairs native browser identity verification.

A setup prerequisite, browser accessibility integration problem, and backend defect remain hypotheses, not findings. The error does not establish that a particular destination is prohibited.

Open/closed issue searches found no matching report. The closest inspected reports concern different failures: #5049 (plugin unavailable in ACP), #4265 (browser-tool iframe traversal), and #4536 (MCP image delivery).

issues.body:
### Description

A Go subscription's usage meters report **lower** limits than the documented ones for `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, by a constant factor of 0.6.

`GET /console/api/go/status` (with `x-org-id`) returns:

```
fiveHour  limitMicroCents 1200000000   ($12)
week      limitMicroCents 3000000000   ($30)
month     limitMicroCents 6000000000   ($60)
```

The Console renders those as 0% / 30% / 15%, so the percentages are computed from the $60 base.

Docs (`opencode.ai/docs/go`) and the Console's own model table both say `deepseek-v4.1-flash` on Go has a monthly limit of **$100** — and the docs state `5-hour: 20% / weekly: 50% / monthly: 100%`, i.e. $20 / $50 / $100.

So the three reported limits are exactly **0.6×** the documented ones ($12/$20, $30/$50, $60/$100): same shape, different base.

Additionally, `opencode.ai/go` still shows "Previously $15; now $60" (4x Usage badge) for this model.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Subscribe to Go, then call `GET /console/api/go/status` with the `x-org-id` header.
2. Compare `access.meters.{fiveHour,week,month}.limitMicroCents` against the `deepseek-v4.1-flash` monthly limit on `opencode.ai/docs/go`.
3. Ratios come out at 0.6 for all three windows.

Account: a Personal workspace on Go. Details moved to email as requested.

### Expected

Either the meters report $20 / $50 / $100, or the docs and console table report $12 / $30 / $60. Right now a user planning against the documented $100 hits the wall at 60% of it.

Related context: PR #60532 noted that a docs change could ship while "the registry and the Console are back at the old limits", so docs/registry drift seems to be a known failure mode here.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### OpenCode version

Using the Go API from a custom agent (Hermes), not the OpenCode CLI, so billing was checked via the Console UI and the endpoint above.

issues.title: desktop: browser tools disappear from a running session after auto-update (2.2.0 -> 2.2.2)
issues.body:
## Summary

After the desktop app auto-updated from 2.2.0 to 2.2.2 and restarted, an already-running session lost the entire `browser` tool namespace (`search("browser")` returned 0). The browser attach RPCs returned HTTP 499 exactly at restart and were never retried for the resumed session. New sessions are not affected.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.2 (upgraded from 2.2.0 during the session)
- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045), x64
- Terminal: desktop app (no terminal env vars set)
- Shell: `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: desktop app, channel `latest`, generic auto-updater (`https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/`)
- Active plugins: none found (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` only contains a `providers` block)

## Reproduction

1. Start the desktop app on 2.2.0 and open a session in a project.
2. Use browser tools successfully in that session (open a tab, take a screenshot).
3. Let the app auto-update to 2.2.2 and restart.
4. Resume / re-open the same session (the conversation is still live).
5. Run `search("browser")` → 0 matching tools; `browser.*` calls are unknown.

Expected reproduction rate: consistent for the session that was running during the update; a brand new session gets the tools back.

## Expected Behavior

The resumed session should keep the browser tools, or the desktop client should re-attach the browser bridge after restarting on the new version.

## Actual Behavior

The tool catalog for the resumed session no longer contains `browser.*`, even though browser calls worked minutes earlier. The desktop UI still works and the session continues on the new server.

Server log excerpt (UTC; local time is UTC+8):

```
01:24:04 cli starting version=2.2.0 channel=latest
...
02:21:15 Sent HTTP response ... POST /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
02:21:15 Sent HTTP response ... POST /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
02:21:15 Sent HTTP response ... POST /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
02:21:39 cli starting version=2.2.2 channel=latest args=["serve","--service"]
```

The running process list shows the desktop app restarted at 10:21:25 local time and the install directory was updated at 10:21:23.

## Additional Context

- The three `499` responses are the only browser-related errors around the update; there is no later re-attach attempt for the resumed session.
- Tool registration appears to be negotiated when the session/agent starts; because the session was started under 2.2.0, the new client did not re-advertise the browser capability for it.
- Workaround used: start a new session (tools return), or drive a local headless Chrome with `puppeteer-core` from the shell instead of the built-in browser.
- Related symptom: the same restart also canceled a running background dev-server command with "server restarted", which is expected behavior for the restart itself.

If it helps, I can provide the full `opencode.log` slice around the update with paths redacted.

### Description

## Summary

The latest public CLI release (1.19.5) fails at startup with `Error: Database is not empty and has no session table` because the shared database at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` was migrated by the OpenCode desktop app's newer server build. issues.title: Session history replay truncates after edit-and-resend of a message on legacy-schema long sessions (data intact, UI stops rendering earlier checkpoint)
issues.body:
### Description
---

**Title:** Session history replay truncates after edit-and-resend of a message on legacy-schema long sessions (data intact, UI stops rendering earlier checkpoint)

**Labels (suggestion):** `bug`, `desktop`, maybe `triage`

---

### Bug description

In a long-running session (2 days old, legacy storage structure predating the `part` migration), using the **retract / edit-and-resend** action on an earlier user message caused the **session history replay (UI) to stop rendering at a much earlier checkpoint** — every agent message after that old checkpoint is invisible in the UI, including the re-sent message itself.

Important: this is **display-only**. The agent's internal context kept working correctly, all subsequent tool calls and file changes happened, and everything is present in local storage (`opencode.db`). Nothing is lost — only the history replay in the UI no longer shows the tail of the conversation.

Reproduction in a fresh short session failed (session stored in the new `part` schema), which suggests the trigger is the combination of (a) legacy `session_message`-stream sessions and (b) the revert flow created by edit-and-resend.

### Environment

- OpenCode: 2.2.5 (desktop client, latest channel)
- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Client: desktop app; HTML preview opened via Review pane
- Affected session profile: 2 days of activity, ~30 user/agent exchanges, 22+ background subagent dispatches (incl. 1 task_cancel, 1 task_revive), local sqlite `opencode.db` grew to ~11.8 GB

### Steps to reproduce

1. Continue a long-running session created **before** the `session_part`/`part` storage migration (its messages live in the legacy `session_message` stream table), with heavy tool/subagent activity.
2. Use **retract / edit-and-resend** on an earlier user message (a `session.revert.stage` → `session.revert.commit` flow; the re-sent message gets a new message id).
3. Continue normally for 10+ exchanges (agent replies, tools run).
4. Reopen the session view / scroll back through history.
5. History replay stops at an agent message from **before** the revert; all later messages (including the re-sent one and subsequent agent replies) are missing from the UI.

### Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** replay shows the resent message and everything after it.
- **Actual:** replay stops at a stale checkpoint; tail of the conversation is invisible in UI, while the agent continues working and storage records everything.

### Evidence from local storage (SQLite `opencode.db`, read-only queries)

For the affected session:

```sql
-- message stream intact and contiguous:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_message WHERE session_id = '<affected-session-id>';  -- 503 rows, seq spans normally
-- legacy schema: no rows in the migrated structures for this session:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM message      WHERE session_id = '<affected-session-id>';  -- 0
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_part WHERE session_id = '<affected-session-id>';  -- 0
```

Server log confirms the flow on the affected session:

```text
session.revert.stage   messageID=msg_<retracted-message-id>   (retract action)
session.revert.commit                                          (few minutes later)
-- subsequent exchanges got new message ids and appended to the stream normally
```

So the launcher-side data is complete; the replay UI does not render it.

### Hypothesis (unverified)

The history replay renderer reads the migrated `part`-based chain (or an inconsistent subset) instead of the legacy `session_message` stream for sessions that still live in the old schema — reverting/branching on such a session moves the expected chain beyond what the renderer walks, so it renders up to a stale checkpoint.

### Impact & workaround

- Impact: audit/history view only (display misled the user into thinking the conversation was lost). Agent execution, storage, and disk artifacts are unaffected; the current-position view (newest messages) still works while streaming.
- Suggested workaround: avoid edit-and-resend on legacy sessions; start a fresh message instead.

### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Let built-in and third-party GUI plugins contribute actions alongside **Copy** on fenced code blocks in assistant messages.

Today, Copy is hardcoded in the Markdown renderer, and GUI plugins have no supported way to add code-block buttons. This prevents features such as **Run in terminal** from being implemented within the terminal plugin without app-specific wiring or DOM manipulation.

**Proposed scope:**
- Add a code-block action registry to the GUI plugin API.
- Let actions declare when they apply—for example, only to particular languages—and receive the original code, language, completion state, and owning session.
- Support accessible labels, icons, and disabled/busy states, with contributions removed when their plugin unloads.
- Refactor Copy onto the same action mechanism, preserving its existing behavior and availability without requiring a plugin.

Keep the API focused on actions rather than replacing Markdown rendering, and avoid adding per-row work when no plugin actions are registered.

**Motivating use case:** the built-in terminal plugin could contribute **Run in terminal** for shell blocks. That feature is already requested in #60875; execution semantics and terminal selection would be reviewed separately. This proposal does not enable command execution itself.

Related: #54126 proposed extensible fenced-code rendering for the TUI. This request concerns additive actions in the desktop/web Markdown UI.

Would this be an acceptable extension point before an implementation is started?

issues.title: desktop: SSH remote reports "running OpenCode 1" for a patch-version mismatch
issues.body:
## Summary

The desktop app's SSH remote connection refuses to connect when the remote service runs a different patch version of OpenCode 2, and reports it as "running OpenCode 1". The displayed `1` is a fallback value, not the real server version.

## Environment

- opencode version: Desktop 2.2.5; remote service 2.2.0
- OS: macOS (desktop), Linux (remote)
- Terminal: Not applicable (desktop app)
- Shell: zsh (remote)
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: None

## Reproduction

1. On a remote Linux host, run an OpenCode 2.2.0 background service (`service.json` reports `"version":"2.2.0"`).
2. In OpenCode Desktop 2.2.5, add an SSH remote connection to that host and try to connect.
3. The connection is marked incompatible and shows: `This server is running OpenCode 1, which isn't compatible with this app. Upgrade it to OpenCode V2 to continue.`
4. Click "Update and reconnect": the desktop installs its matching CLI version, restarts the remote service, and connects successfully.

## Expected Behavior

The message should report the actual version mismatch (2.2.0 vs 2.2.5), or offer the update action directly. A patch-level mismatch should not be presented as an OpenCode 1 server that must be upgraded to V2.

## Actual Behavior

The connection is presented as an incompatible OpenCode 1 server. Both sides are OpenCode V2; only the patch version differs. The message hides the real cause and the recovery action.

## Additional Context

- The SSH bootstrap compares the remote service registration version with the desktop app's bundled CLI version using strict equality. On mismatch it fails with a `version` error and marks the connection incompatible.
- The row message uses `server.row.incompatible` with `version: health?.version ?? "1"`. For an SSH target that never reaches the connected state, `health.version` is unavailable, so the UI displays the hardcoded fallback `1`.
- Frequency: consistent.
- Workaround: "Update and reconnect" resolves it.

issues.title: [FEATURE]:Per-Session OAuth Account Isolation for OpenAI Codex
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

# Feature Request: Isolate OAuth Accounts Per Session/Tab

## Problem

When using OpenCode with the native OpenAI Codex OAuth integration, switching accounts can potentially affect other active sessions or tabs.

For example:

1. Open OpenCode in Tab 1 and authenticate using **Account A**.
2. Start a coding task in Tab 1.
3. Open another OpenCode tab (Tab 2).
4. Switch the Codex OAuth account to **Account B** in Tab 2.
5. Return to Tab 1 and continue working.

The concern is that switching the active OAuth account in Tab 2 may also change the account used by Tab 1.

This makes it difficult to work with multiple OpenAI accounts simultaneously.

## Expected Behavior

OAuth authentication should be isolated per OpenCode session or instance.

- Tab 1 should remain authenticated with Account A.
- Tab 2 should remain authenticated with Account B.
- Switching accounts in Tab 2 should not affect Tab 1.
- Existing tasks and conversations should retain their original account.
- New requests in each session should consistently use the account assigned to that session.

## Proposed Solution

Provide session-level or instance-level OAuth account isolation instead of relying exclusively on a globally shared active account.

Ideally, users should be able to:

- Authenticate multiple Codex accounts.
- Assign a specific OAuth account to each session.
- Run multiple sessions concurrently using different accounts.
- Switch accounts in one session without affecting other sessions.

## Questions

1. Is OAuth account selection currently shared globally across all OpenCode sessions?
2. Is there already a supported way to isolate Codex OAuth accounts per session?
3. If not, could this be considered as a feature enhancement?

**Use case:** Developers who have multiple OpenAI accounts and want to run parallel coding tasks using different Codex subscriptions without authentication conflicts.

issues.title: project: session list returns empty in a directory that became a git repo after first open
issues.body:
### Description

`opencode session list` returns nothing for a directory that opencode first opened *before* it became a git repo, even though sessions exist.

The project registry ends up with two entries for the same directory:

- `9ed4d1ef…` — registered pre-git (no `vcs`), and still the identity that CLI invocations resolve and mark active
- `efe4468c…` — registered on the next session after `git init` + first commit (`vcs: git`, id equals `git rev-parse HEAD`)

All sessions are stored under the newer VCS identity, but `session list` resolves the stale pre-git entry and finds zero sessions. Resuming by explicit ID (`opencode -s <id>`) and `GET /api/session?directory=<dir>` both work, which points at project resolution rather than storage.

A session started *after* `git init` also reported `Is directory a git repo: no` in its harness environment snapshot, so the stale identity appears to win in more places than just `session list`.

Expected: the CLI should resolve the same project identity the sessions are stored under — prefer the VCS entry once the directory has a repo, or deduplicate identities that share a canonical directory.

Workarounds: `opencode api get "/api/session?directory=$(pwd)"`, or resume explicitly with `opencode -s <sessionID>`.

### Plugins

None — user config only contains `{"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"}`.

### OpenCode version

v2.2.2 (channel: latest)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open opencode in a plain, non-git directory and create a session. This registers project A (id = directory hash, no VCS).
2. `git init && git commit` in that directory.
3. Open opencode again and create a session. This registers project B (`vcs: git`, id = HEAD commit hash); sessions are now stored under B.
4. Run `opencode session list` in the directory → empty (`--format json` → `[]`).
5. `opencode api get "/api/session?directory=$(pwd)"` → the sessions exist, all with `projectID` = B.

Consistently reproducible. Control: in a directory that was a git repo before first being opened, `session list` shows all 44 sessions.

Observed data (Linux; timestamps are epoch ms):

```
$ opencode api get /api/project | jq '.[] | select(.canonical=="/home/<user>/projects/<project>")'
{"id":"9ed4d1ef70cc462c80c0de397404b84c8e28323f","canonical":"/home/<user>/projects/<project>","time":{"created":1793331031829,"updated":1793331031829,"active":1793506432664},"sandboxes":[]}   # created 2026-10-30 (pre-git), still receiving active bumps from CLI runs
{"id":"efe4468cff211797ecc2935bafb7db9931aad692","canonical":"/home/<user>/projects/<project>","vcs":"git","time":{"created":1793504166172,"updated":1793504166172,"active":1793504166172},"sandboxes":[]}   # created 2026-10-31 23:42, after git init at ~23:33

$ opencode api get "/api/session?directory=/home/<user>/projects/<project>" | jq -r '.data[].projectID'
efe4468cff211797ecc2935bafb7db9931aad692   # all 4 sessions

$ opencode session list --format json
[]

$ git rev-parse HEAD
efe4468cff211797ecc2935bafb7db9931aad692
```

### Screenshot

n/a — API outputs above.

### Operating System

Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu, kernel 5.15.0-179-generic)

### Terminal

tmux (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)

Related: #52501 — same failure class (split project identity → empty session list), there via Windows path case.

issues.title: fix(core): avoid holding models.dev refresh lock across network timeout
issues.body:
### Description
When OpenCode boots, the background `ModelsDev.refresh()` loop in `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts` acquires `lock.withPermit` before awaiting `fetchApi()`, which has an `Effect.timeout("10 seconds")`.

If `models.dev` is slow, firewalled, or unreachable, `lock` is held for up to 10 seconds. Meanwhile, foreground initialization calls `ModelsDev.get()`, which executes `populate()` and attempts to acquire `lock.withPermit()`. Consequently, foreground provider and agent initialization blocks for up to 10 seconds waiting on the lock, even when a valid cache or bundled snapshot already exists on disk. This causes the server to return HTTP 503 on `/api/model`, `/api/agent`, and `/api/provider`, stalling client startup.

`fetchApi()` only needs to run before taking the lock; `lock.withPermit` is only needed when decoding and writing to the cache.

### Plugins
none

### OpenCode version
2.2.5 (dev)

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run OpenCode in an environment with high latency or a firewall blocking outbound requests to `models.dev`.
2. Start OpenCode (`opencode`).
3. Notice `/api/model` and `/api/agent` return HTTP 503 for up to 10 seconds while the log records:
   `message="Failed to fetch models.dev" cause="Cause([Fail(TimeoutError: Operation timed out after '10s')])"`

### Screenshot
Not applicable (server lifecycle and background network lock timing issue).

### Operating System
Windows 11, macOS, Linux

### Terminal
Windows Terminal

prs.title: feat(core): add Node-style fs and path to Code Mode
prs.body:
### Problem

Models write Node code: `fs.readFileSync`, `fs.promises.writeFile`, `path.join`. Code Mode had no file access, so scripts had to call tools with custom shapes. In our benchmark, scripts with `fs` used 0.61× the tokens of the dedicated tools on bulk scans, and Code Mode with `fs` plus tools broke even on edits in long files.

### Change

Core adds `fs` and `path` globals. They're also importable as `node:fs`, `fs/promises` and `node:path`, through https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61151.

Every `fs` call reuses the file tools' checks; nothing is duplicated:

```text
readFile, readdir, stat, lstat, access, existsSync  → FileAccess.authorizeRead      (read rules)
writeFile, appendFile, copyFile (dest)              → FileWrite.write               (edit rule, diff, format, BOM)
mkdir, unlink, binary writes                        → FileWrite.target + authorize  (edit rule)
rm, rename                                          → one edit request for every path touched
```

- Both styles work: `fs.promises.*`, and `*Sync` on `fs`. Sync calls block on the same Effect. To make that possible, Code Mode now runs a synchronous global's returned Effect as a blocking host call.
- Errors look like Node's (`code`, `errno`, `syscall`, `path`), so `e.code === "ENOENT"` works. User feedback on a rejection becomes the error message, like for `fetch`.
- Each call gets a progress row (tool `fs`, method and path).
- The `execute` description says `fs` and `path` exist, how to import them, and that other modules and packages don't.
- `path` is Node's posix module, with no permissions.

The Tool registry now depends on the file services, so eight tests that build it without a Location now provide one.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
  <style>
    .dot { animation: go 2.6s ease-in-out infinite; }
    @keyframes go { 0% { transform: translateX(0); opacity: 1 } 45%, 60% { transform: translateX(62px); opacity: 1 } 100% { transform: translateX(124px); opacity: 0 } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .dot { animation: none } }
  </style>
  <rect x="8" y="22" width="76" height="28" rx="6" opacity=".6"/>
  <text x="46" y="40" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">fs.readFile</text>
  <path d="M88 36 H202" opacity=".3" stroke-dasharray="3 4"/>
  <path d="M146 20 L160 25 V36 C160 45 153 50 146 53 C139 50 132 45 132 36 V25 Z" opacity=".8"/>
  <circle class="dot" cx="88" cy="36" r="4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/>
  <path d="M206 24 h14 l6 6 v20 h-20 z" opacity=".6"/>
</svg>
```

### Out of scope

- Callback-style `fs.readFile(path, cb)`.
- Known differences from Node: `writeFile` creates missing parent directories, written files are formatted like the write tool's, `rename` onto an existing directory fails, and `rm` of a large folder lists every file in one permission request.
- `process`, `Buffer` and `os`.

### Verification

- New tests in `packages/core/test/tool-execute.test.ts`: reads and writes through `fs` ask read and edit for the right paths, session and call ids; a denied write never touches disk; ENOENT has Node's shape. New test in `packages/codemode`: a synchronous global blocks on its Effect.
- `bun test` in `packages/codemode`: 1501 pass. `bun run test` in `packages/core`: 7189 pass; the 3 failures are shell tests that also fail on `dev` locally. `bun run check` from the root is clean.


---

_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Public API: adds optional experimental.codemode_fs to config, the OpenAPI spec and the generated client types (backwards compatible)

prs.title: docs(opencode): document shell advisory gap for sandbox
prs.body:
## Summary

Permission gate is advisory only; OS sandbox is still missing (#2242).

```diff
 on(shell.execute)
-  collect static paths -> ask external_directory/bash
+  collect static paths -> ask external_directory/bash
+  dynamic/symlink/rename/script-body skips collection -> only bash ask
+  spawn with no OS enforcement
```

Full flow today:

```text
shell.execute
  parse(command)
  collect(tree, cwd)
    argPath (static only, dynamic returns early)
  ask(external_directory + bash)
  run(spawn with no sandbox)
```

This PR changes no runtime behavior. It names the boundary at the collection seam and pins it with a regression test so a future `SandboxProvider` has a failing-to-passing gate to build on.

Related #2242 (not Fixes — full OS sandbox remains open). Prior art: #20316 (srt/bubblewrap provider, closed by cleanup), #21538 (macOS seatbelt, closed by cleanup).

## Evidence

- **Before:** `cat $HOME/.ssh/config` produced only `bash` ask, no `external_directory` ask — silent skip in `argPath` early return. Static `cat /etc/*` correctly produced `external_directory`.
  **After:** same behavior, now pinned by test `documents dynamic-path advisory gap for external_directory` + source comment at the early-return seam.

Test evidence (from `packages/opencode`):

```
bun test test/tool/shell.test.ts -t "documents dynamic-path advisory gap"
 1 pass, 23 filtered out, 0 fail, 3 expect() calls

bun test test/tool/shell.test.ts
 24 pass, 0 fail, 63 expect() calls

bun typecheck (tsgo --noEmit): clean
```

Repro (pre-fix fail → post-fix pass is behavior-preserving by design):

1. `capture` asks with `stop after permission` error
2. `command: "cat $HOME/.ssh/config"` → `requests` contains `bash`, contains no `external_directory`
3. `command: "cat /etc/*"` → `requests` contains `external_directory` with `/etc/*`

Expect vs actual: expect advisory gate to be named as non-boundary; actual before was unnamed silent skip, after is named + tested.

Env: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS aarch64, bun 1.4.2, node v24.21.0, gh 2.102.0, git 2.53.0, base `5d9cd9b` (refs/remotes/origin/dev). Counter-scenarios tried: static vs dynamic path (isolates parser from enforcement); base unmoved since branch cut (`workspace-containment` from `FETCH_HEAD 5d9cd9b`); minimal vs full diff (each hunk maps to one claim, no runtime change).

Scope: `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` (3-line comment only), `packages/opencode/test/tool/shell.test.ts` (22-line documenting test). No config, no spawn, no PTY, no MCP.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Comment + test only; revert restores unnamed behavior with zero runtime delta.

**Blast Radius:** minimal

Docs/test touch shell permission tests only. No behavior change, no new dependency, no OS-specific path.

prs.title: fix(release): leave non-client packages out of the changelog
prs.body:
The stable changelog was built from every commit since the last V2 tag, so console, docs, stats, cloud function and website changes could end up in it. Now `script/release.ts` has one list of excluded paths and leaves out commits that only touch those.

- The script runs `git log ... -- . ':(exclude)...'` itself and puts the resulting commit list in the prompt, so a commit that only touches excluded paths never reaches the model. A commit that touches both is still listed.
- The prompt shows the same command and tells the model to read diffs with `git show <commit> -- <same pathspecs>` and ignore the excluded parts. The `packages/ai` rule stays.
- Everything else counts by default, so a new client package shows up without touching this list.
- `--print`, `--from` and `--to` work as before. The script now stops early if no commits are in scope.

Excluded:

| Area | Paths |
| --- | --- |
| Console, stats, cloud | `packages/console`, `packages/stats`, `packages/function` |
| Docs, sites, assets | `packages/web` (docs site), `packages/posts`, `packages/identity`, `services` |

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Selecting text in the TUI toasted "Copied to clipboard" even when nothing reached any clipboard. Root cause in `packages/tui/src/clipboard.ts` (base `5d9cd9b`): `write()` fired OSC52 and then the native tool with every failure swallowed (`.catch(() => undefined)` on each backend), so it always resolved, and `util/selection.ts:39` toasted success and cleared the highlight unconditionally.

prs.title: feat(ai): share headers, fetch and timeout across every request
prs.body:
### Change

Every request (text, image, decision, speech, transcription, video, extraction) takes the same transport fields at the top level, in both the Promise and Effect APIs:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `http.headers` | `headers` |
| `http.timeout` | `timeout` (a number or `false`), or `timeout.total` |
| `http.headerTimeout` | `timeout.headers` |
| `http.chunkTimeout` | `timeout.chunk` |
| `http.query`, `http.body`, `http.encoding` | unchanged |
| (none) | `fetch`, so one call can go through your own fetch |

```diff
 ai.generate({
   model,
   prompt,
-  http: { headers: { "x-trace": "1" }, timeout: 30_000, headerTimeout: 1_000 },
+  headers: { "x-trace": "1" },
+  timeout: { total: 30_000, headers: 1_000 },
+  fetch: myFetch,
 })
```

The `HttpOptions` Schema class is gone. Requests, model defaults and route defaults (`route.with(...)`, `configure(...)`) all use the same plain `{ headers, timeout, http }` shape, merged by one `mergeTransport` function. `HttpOptions` is now just the `{ query, body, encoding }` interface.

- `fetch` runs as the innermost per-call middleware, so executor middleware and status classification still apply. Media calls use it too.
- Media calls still ignore `timeout`, as they do today.
- Transport fields are plain typed fields and are no longer validated at runtime.
- Wire bodies are unchanged and every recorded cassette replays.

### Core call sites

Mechanical only: `http: { headers }` becomes `headers`, and the model resolver writes provider timeouts as `timeout: { total, headers, chunk }` instead of building an `HttpOptions`.

- src: +261 / −299
- tests: +158 / −82

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/52054
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51247 (the loopback half)

Supersedes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57030 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57744 (both authors are co-authors here).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

With `HTTPS_PROXY` set and no `NO_PROXY`, the TUI's requests to its own background service on `127.0.0.1` go through the proxy, and the TUI hangs on "Restarting service...".

```text
TUI ──GET 127.0.0.1:<port>/api/event──▶ proxy ──✗   (today)
TUI ──GET 127.0.0.1:<port>/api/event──────────▶ service   (after)
```

At CLI startup, loopback is added to `NO_PROXY`. Desktop already did this, but wrote each spelling separately. Bun reads lowercase `no_proxy` alone whenever it is set, so a user with only `NO_PROXY=corp.internal` got `no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost,::1` and lost their own entry. Both spellings now get one merged list:

```text
NO_PROXY unset              → both = 127.0.0.1,localhost,::1
NO_PROXY=corp.internal      → both = corp.internal,127.0.0.1,localhost,::1
NO_PROXY=a, no_proxy=b      → both = a,b,127.0.0.1,localhost,::1
```

Bun reads the env on every request, so this covers health checks, the event stream, API calls and the background service the CLI starts. Desktop's copy gets the same fix.

### How did you verify your code works?

Ran `opencode api get /api/info --server http://127.0.0.1:<port>` with `HTTP(S)_PROXY` pointed at a fake proxy that returns 502. Before: the request went through the proxy and failed.
