prs.title: refactor(core): share Console config and skill fetches across projects
prs.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61074.

## Problem

Every open project ran its own copy of the Console integration: each one fetched the Console config every minute and downloaded every Console skill itself. With 5 projects open, Console got 5 config requests a minute, and opening several projects at once (desktop startup) downloaded each skill once per project. A network blip also had no retry, so it left that project on stale config until the next minute.

## Change

The network side now goes through `SharedCache`, once per sign-in and workspace for the whole process. Each project only applies the result.

```text
SharedCache (once per process)
  opencode-console:<server, sign-in, org>
    -> config, fetched at most once a minute
  opencode-console-skill:<server, sign-in, org>:<slug>
    -> one skill, downloaded again only for a new version

each project (no requests of its own)
  every minute or on an account switch: read the config entry, apply if changed
  admin blocks Console here -> apply nothing
  read skill entries in the background
```

- Network errors and 5xx responses retry 3 times, then keep the last good config or skill copy, as `SharedCache` does for the other providers.
- Signed-out and SSO-required responses are stored as results rather than failures, so every project reports them instead of quietly serving the last config.
- Re-checking after rejected inference reuses a fetch from the last 30 seconds, now shared across projects.
- The sign-in is part of every key, since API keys carry no account or org.
- Replaces the module-level skill map from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61074.

## Out of scope

- A skill whose very first download fails tries once more right away (each attempt with retries), since a cached failure has to be forced to retry later.
- Retrying a failed skill download without a config change, and keeping skills across restarts.

## Verification

- `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck:tsc`, oxlint
- `bun run --cwd packages/core test test/plugin test/skill.test.ts test/tool-read.test.ts test/config test/shared-cache.test.ts` (0 fail). Two Console tests now count the 3 retries after a failed config fetch.
- Throwaway probe with two plugin instances on one Console: opening both sent 1 config request and 1 skill download; a minute later, 1 config request and no download; a new version whose download returned 500 made 4 attempts in total, shared, and kept the old copy; the next config change downloaded the new version once.

prs.title: refactor(ai): read Anthropic media options from provider metadata
prs.body:
Follows https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61018 (merged).

### Why

`@opencode/ai` is still experimental and hasn't launched, so I'm making a breaking change here instead of carrying a deprecated alias.

`MediaPart.metadata` was a free-form bag that only the Anthropic protocol read. It looked for undocumented keys (file ID, citations, title, context, image transformations) under two locations and up to four spellings each. Nothing in the repo ever set them, and they weren't documented anywhere. These options now live where every other per-part provider option does: `providerMetadata`, keyed by the route, with Anthropic's own field names and a schema.

### Change

```diff
 Message.media(asset, {
-  metadata: { anthropic: { fileId: "file_1" }, citations: { enabled: true } },
+  providerMetadata: { anthropic: { file_id: "file_1", citations: { enabled: true } } },
 })
```

- `MediaPart.metadata` is removed.
- The five lookup helpers in `anthropic-messages.ts` are replaced by one schema decode. Invalid values now fail the request instead of being silently ignored.
- The key is the route's `providerMetadataKey`, the same rule OpenAI's media `detail` already follows (`anthropic`, `mantle` on Bedrock Mantle, `vertex` on Vertex).

prs.title: feat(core): share MCP connections across locations with pool: true
prs.body:
### Problem

One opencode server hosts many directories, and each one opens its own connection to every MCP server. With about 20 directories open, that's 20 connections to Cloudflare and 20 copies of its 3,762-tool list, and 20 `cua-driver` processes for a local server.

### Change

A new `pool: true` on a local or remote server lets directories with identical settings share one connection and one tool list. Unset or `false` behaves exactly as before.

```
dir A ─┐
dir B ─┼─ claim ─► McpPool (global) ─ key ─► one connection, one tools array
dir C ─┘                                      (closed when the last claim goes)
```

- **Only 2026-07-28 connections are shared.** With `pool` set, an unset `protocol` becomes `auto`. If the server answers legacy, I drop that probe connection, remember the verdict for the key, and the directory connects on its own exactly like today (its own roots, its own process). `protocol: "legacy"` never pools.
- **Key.** Remote: url, headers (fingerprinted), OAuth settings (secret fingerprinted), protocol, timeouts, whether `?codemode=false` is added, and the active credential's ID (a token refresh keeps it, a new sign-in changes it). Local: command, resolved cwd, environment (fingerprinted), protocol, timeouts. Both include clientInfo. The server's name isn't part of it.
- **Local servers pool only for directories on the host.** Workspace-backed directories keep private connections, since their processes run on another execution plane. Pooled local servers spawn through a host environment the pool owns.
- **Roots.** A pooled connection declares no roots and registers no `roots/list` handler, so it can't answer with one directory.
- **Elicitation.** The SDK fulfils `input_required` through one connection-wide handler, but calls the request's `onprogress` right before dispatching, in the same synchronous run. Each pooled request passes its directory's handler, which claims that run, so the form opens in the directory whose call caused it. Anything unattributed goes to every holder, the first answer wins, and the others are interrupted, which cancels their forms.
- **Lifecycle.** Each directory holds a claim, released when the entry stops, is replaced or removed, or the directory shuts down. The last release closes the connection right away. When a shared connection closes on its own, every holder goes `failed` with its events, and the next start opens a fresh one.
- **No leak through the pool.** The shared connection, its scope, fibers and SDK callbacks run in the pool's own runtime and context. Fan-out and elicitation go through the holders registered right now. Elicitation handlers provide their own Location so forms still belong to the right directory.

Cleanup:

- Pooled servers skip the per-URL `endpointLoads` lock. It moved into `McpConnection` for unpooled remotes, and `Input.handshake` is gone.
- `toolsChanged` / `promptsChanged` / `resourcesChanged` and `stopped` are now one `changed(kind)`.
- `McpClient.connect` takes an options object.

### Out of scope

- Pooling legacy servers
- An on-disk tool list cache
- A grace period before closing

### Verification

- `packages/core`: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, all `test/mcp*` (154 pass), `test/tool*` and `test/tool/` (all pass except the two `ShellTool conditional process substitution` cases, which also fail on dev locally).
- New tests in `test/mcp.test.ts` under "MCP pool", reusing the in-process 2026-07-28 harness: sharing (one `tools/list`, same tool objects), different headers, key fields, legacy stays private (one probe, then each directory spawns through its own environment), `pool` unset, last release closes, a killed local process fails both holders and a restart reconnects, elicitation routed to the caller, unattributed elicitation raced across holders, tool list fan-out, no roots. Ran the block 40 times in a row without a failure.
- Leak check: a directory opens the shared connection, answers an elicitation through it, and shuts down while another keeps it. A `FinalizationRegistry` confirms its Mcp and Form services get collected. The test fails if the connect runs in the opener's fiber or if the pool keeps a holder.
- `MCP.tools()` with 4,000 tools, median of 7 rounds of 500 calls: about 0.150 ms on dev, 0.150 ms here unpooled and 0.150 ms pooled; repeated calls return the same objects.
- `packages/server`: `bun test test/client-mcp.test.ts`. `packages/schema` typecheck. `bun run check` at the root. Regenerated `packages/client` and `packages/protocol/openapi.json`.
- End to end: a dev server with a temp config and two directories using `cua-driver mcp` with `pool: true` ran one `cua-driver` process; with `pool: false` it ran two. After both directories were evicted, the pooled process exited.

prs.title: feat(core): detect repeated reasoning and text within a step
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Stacked on the cross-step tool-call detector; review that one first. Until it lands this PR's diff also contains it.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The cross-step detector only sees tool calls. A model can also loop inside a single step, repeating the same reasoning or text until it runs out of output budget.

This adds a per-step detector that reads the reasoning and text deltas as they stream. It has four rules: a tight loop of a short repeated unit, an exact repeat, a long period repeated several times, and many identical lines. When one fires, the stream is cut and the step returns a nudge carrying the work from before the loop started, so the model can continue from there instead of starting over.

Kill switches: `OPENCODE_LOOP_REPEAT_DETECT` and `OPENCODE_LOOP_FAST_DETECT`.

prs.title: feat(core): detect repeated tool calls across steps
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue. Related: #53032, which handles repeated identical tool calls through the `doom_loop` permission. This change is complementary: it also catches multi-call cycles, not just one call repeated.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A model can get stuck calling the same tool over and over. The existing `doom_loop` permission asks the user about one identical call; it does not notice a model alternating between two or three calls forever.

This adds a detector that watches tool calls across the steps of one user turn. It fires on three identical calls in a row, and on cycles of length two to four (four copies of a pair, three copies of a triple or quadruple). When it fires, the repeated call is failed and the turn continues with a nudge that tells the model to stop repeating and wrap up. After two nudges in the same turn the turn is ended instead.

The detector state is keyed by session and cleared when a new user turn starts, including when a queued prompt is promoted mid-drain. A nudged step settles through the normal step path, so its assistant message closes and its usage, snapshot and file changes are recorded; only the repeated call is failed.

Kill switch: `OPENCODE_TOOL_LOOP_DETECT=0`.

### How did you verify your code works?

`bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core` is clean. `bun test test/tool-loop.test.ts test/session-loop.test.ts test/session-step.test.ts` passes (18 tests). The detector tests use small inline synthetic call sequences; the session tests drive the real step runner through a test LLM.

prs.title: refactor(ai): remove unused metadata fields
prs.body:
### Problem

`@opencode/ai` had a free-form `metadata` bag on almost every message type. Most of them were never read by the package or anything else. Core copied its own session metadata into some of them, but nothing read it back.

### Change

Removed the `metadata` fields nothing reads, and the writes that fed them.

| Field | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Message.metadata` | core copied session metadata in, nothing read it | removed |
| `TextPart.metadata` | core wrote attachment info, nothing read it | removed |
| `ToolCallPart.metadata` | never written or read | removed |
| `ToolResultPart.metadata` | only copied by `ToolResultPart.make` | removed |
| `ReasoningPart.metadata` | never written or read | removed |
| `ToolDefinition.metadata` | never written or read | removed |
| `LLMRequest.metadata` | accepted, never sent anywhere | removed |
| `SystemPart.metadata` | read by the Claude agent plugin, documented plugin API | kept |
| `MediaPart.metadata` | read by Anthropic lowering (`file_id`, citations, title, context, transformations) | kept, core no longer writes an unused `description` into it |

```diff
 core to-llm-message
-  Message.make({ role: "user", content, metadata: { ...session.metadata, agents } })
+  Message.make({ role: "user", content })
-  { type: "text", text, metadata: { attachment: { source, name, description } } }
+  { type: "text", text }
```

Stored native compaction windows that contain the removed fields still decode. The extra keys are dropped.

### Breaking change

`@opencode/ai` is published, and plugins receive `Message` and part objects through session hooks. Code that sets or reads the removed fields needs to drop them.

### Out of scope

- Moving the Anthropic options on `MediaPart.metadata` to a typed provider option.

prs.title: fix(ai): retry Cohere streams that end early
prs.body:
### Problem

When a Cohere stream got cut off before `message-end`, the step just failed. Every other provider retries in that case.

Cohere had its own end-of-stream check that ran before the shared one and failed with a plain "Cohere stream ended without message-end" error. That error has no `incomplete-stream` classification, so `AIError.isRetryable` returned false.

```diff
 stream ends without a finish event
-  cohere onHalt -> "Cohere stream ended without message-end"   (not retryable)
+  shared requireTerminalEvent -> "The provider response ended unexpectedly."
+                                 classification: incomplete-stream (retryable)
```

### Change

I removed Cohere's `onHalt`. Cohere's `message-end` step already emits a `finish` event, so the shared client check passes for complete streams and gives cut-off streams the same retryable error as everyone else.

I kept the `finished` state field even though nothing reads it now, because it shows up in the exported `CohereChat.protocol` type. The emitted `.d.ts` is identical before and after.

### Verification

- `bun run test` in `packages/ai` (includes recorded fixtures): 2030 pass, 0 fail
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/ai`
- `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --emitDeclarationOnly` before and after: no diff
- `bun run check` from the root

prs.title: feat(core): dsv4 recovery middleware (DSML guard + history cleanup + diagnostics)
prs.body:
Recovery middleware for a local OpenAI-compatible provider (provider-specific).

- `session/llm/dsml.ts` + `dsml-recovery.ts`: DSML scanner and empty-vetting loop guard. Runs on **both** provider paths — the AI SDK `doStream` seam in `aisdk.ts` and the native `@opencode/ai/providers/*` route via `DSMLGuard.layer` wrapping `LLMClient.Service` (llmgw actually uses the native route). The native guard stops the provider stream with `Stream.takeWhile` and fails it with `InvalidProviderOutputError`, since the `provider-error` LLMEvent no longer exists upstream; the failure maps to a `provider.invalid-output` step error that `runner/to-llm-message.ts` recognizes for outgoing-history cleanup.
- `provider/dsml-recovery-audit.ts` + `request-diagnostic.ts`: metadata-only audit and default-off request capture.
- Env contract: `OPENCODE_DSV4_RECOVERY_ENABLED=1` enables full recovery (promotes textual invocations back into tool calls); unset keeps the strict guard only; `=0` turns the middleware off entirely.

Known gaps: history cleanup lives in `to-llm-message.ts` (the `session.context` hook lacks stored error metadata); the non-streaming `LLMClient.generate` path is not covered by the guard.

prs.title: refactor(core): share credential helpers in provider plugins
prs.body:
### Problem

The provider plugins copy the same few blocks over and over. About ten of them build the same "when this integration's account switches, do X" subscription by hand, seven resolve the active connection's credential with the same three lines, and a few hooks check the provider ID even though the hook already filters by it.

### Change

I added two small helpers inside core and used them everywhere. Nothing here is plugin API.

```diff
 refresh.ts (ProviderRefresh)
+  onSwitch(integrationID, effect)      # bus.subscribe(Switched) + filter + runForEach + forkScoped
+  reloadIfChanged(load, reload)        # load, then provider reload only when it changed
 credential-settings.ts
+  activeCredential(ctx, integrationID) # -> { connection, credential }
```

```diff
-yield* bus.subscribe(Credential.Event.Switched).pipe(
-  Stream.filter((event) => event.data.integrationID === integrationID),
-  Stream.runForEach(() => load().pipe(Effect.flatMap((changed) => (changed ? ctx.provider.reload() : Effect.void)))),
-  Effect.forkScoped({ startImmediately: true }),
-)
+yield* ProviderRefresh.onSwitch(integrationID, ProviderRefresh.reloadIfChanged(load(), ctx.provider.reload()))
```

Smaller bits:
- Hooks in github-copilot and azure that are registered with `{ providerID }` no longer re-check it. The inline-checked `sdk`/`language` hooks in github-copilot, sap-ai-core and gitlab now pass `{ providerID }` instead, which the host filters the same way.
- The opencode web search compares connections with `IntegrationConnection.key`.
- azure: one predicate for "is an Azure provider", one for "usable credential", and the model baseURL is computed once instead of twice.

### Out of scope

- I left the opencode web search headers as they are. `ConsoleAccess.headers` sends `x-org-id: ""` for an empty org ID, while the current code drops it, so switching would change requests.
- OAuth callback server and PKCE code.

prs.title: feat(codemode): let programs import globals by Node module name
prs.body:
### Problem

Models write Node-style code: `import fs from "node:fs"`, `require("path")`, `import { URL } from "url"`. Code Mode rejected every `import` at parse time and had no `require`, so even things it already has (`URL`, `crypto`) weren't reachable the way models ask for them, and each attempt wasted a step on a syntax error.

### Change

`import` and `require` are another way to reach a global. There's no separate module registry.

```text
import/require("x")  →  the global named x
"node:x"             →  same as "x"
fs/promises          →  fs.promises
url / util / buffer  →  { URL, URLSearchParams } / { TextEncoder, TextDecoder } / { Buffer, atob, btoa }
anything else        →  Cannot import "yaml": it isn't available in Code Mode, which can't load packages or files.
```

```js
import fs, { readFile } from "node:fs"   // works once a host adds an `fs` global
import { URL } from "url"                // works today
const { randomUUID } = require("crypto") // works today
```

To let hosts provide things like `fs`, an extension global can now be an object of functions, not only a function. Every function reachable from it fires `extension.before` / `extension.after` named by its path (`fs.readFile`, `fs.promises.readFile`), so the host's permission checks see each call.

- A missing named export: `"fs" has no export named "writeFile".`
- Programs keep today's non-strict parsing: imports are allowed in script mode. `export` stays unsupported.

### Out of scope

Real `fs`, `path`, `Buffer` and `process`. Core adds those as globals in follow-ups, and they become importable automatically.

- `bun test` in `packages/codemode`: 1500 pass, including test262. `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc` and `bun run build` are clean. `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` is clean.

prs.title: feat(core): reasoning + cross-step tool-call loop detection (LD-05/05e/05f)
prs.body:
Ports the fork's loop protection to the new core.

- `reasoning-loop.ts`: per-step reasoning/text repetition detector (tight/repeat/period/line rules) scoped to the step.
- `tool-loop.ts`: cross-step tool-call detector — period-1 (3 identical calls) and period-2..4 cycles (the "flapper": 4 copies of a pair, 3 of a triple/quadruple), driven by session-keyed state in `runner/loop-state.ts` (cleared on a new user turn).
- Wiring: `step.ts` gains `Outcome.LoopNudge`, feeds deltas, hooks the tool-call fork point, settles a dropped already-durable partial call via `failTool`, and cuts the provider stream with `Stream.takeWhile` so the rest of a looped response is never drained. `llm.ts` handles `LoopNudge` like `Continue` (nudge + continue; at the cap it becomes a `StepFailedError`).
- A nudged step is settled with `session.step.failed` (`type: "aborted"`) so its assistant message closes and its snapshot and file changes are recorded.
- Kill switches: `OPENCODE_TOOL_LOOP_DETECT=0`, `OPENCODE_LOOP_REPEAT_DETECT`, `OPENCODE_LOOP_FAST_DETECT`.

Not ported: the LD-05d transcript cut (durable deltas cannot be removed), the `LOOP_AT_CAP` length-finish path, and `loopNudged` part metadata.

prs.title: refactor(core): share tool permission invocation and registry steps
prs.body:
### Problem

Every built-in tool hand-built the same three permission fields (`sessionID`, `agent`, `source`) from its call context, about 20 times. FileAccess already had a private helper for it. `tool.ts` also repeated "run the before hook, then execute" and the add/update registration step, and `McpTool.name` copied the naming rules from `tool/runtime.ts`.

### Change

I added `Permission.invocation(context)` and use it everywhere the fields were identical. The spread sits where the old fields were, so request key order doesn't change.

```diff
 yield* permission.assert({
   action: "read",
   resources: [target.resource],
   save: ["*"],
-  sessionID: context.sessionID,
-  agent: context.agent,
-  source: { type: "tool", messageID: context.messageID, id: context.id },
+  ...Permission.invocation(context),
 })
```

In `tool.ts`:

```diff
 editor.add / editor.update
-  register, push error or set tools + definitions
+  commit(editor, id, tool)
 CodeMode create / check callbacks
-  beforeExecute -> executeTool(event.input)
+  run(tool, name, input, context)
```

`McpTool.namespace` and `McpTool.name` now call `normalizedName` and `effectiveName` from the runtime. A sanitized server name never has dots, so the output matches the old version for every input.

I also updated the snippet in `tool/AGENTS.md`.

### Out of scope

The `inputSchema` fallback in `tool/mcp.ts` was already removed on dev, so I didn't touch it.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #60857

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

The snapshot store path includes the project ID, which changes when a repo gains a remote. Older turns point at trees in the old store, so `/session/:id/diff` fails with `bad object` and returns a 500.

When the current store is missing a tree, the diff reruns with the other stores for the same worktree passed as `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, which works even when `from` and `to` are in different stores. Revert (`Snapshot.restore`) has the same problem; I'll fix it in a follow-up.

### Problem

The Responses WebSocket channel built a full `WebSocketChannelDriver` (`create` + `observe` + `observeEvent`) and handed it to the continuation driver as `base`. But the continuation driver only ever calls `observeEvent`. It never calls `base.create`, only falls back to `base.observe` when `observeEvent` is missing (the channel always sets it), and never reads `input.message`. So the channel's `create`/`observe`, the encoded `body` and `message` were dead in production.

### Change

```diff
 OpenResponsesContinuation.driver({
   id, name, request,
-  message,
-  base: { create, observe, observeEvent },   // BaseDriver
+  base: observeEvent,                         // (create, frame, event) => Effect<ChannelObservation>
   continuation,
 })
```

prs.title: refactor(ai): share provider endpoint and bearer auth setup
prs.body:
### Problem

About 17 provider facades in `packages/ai` start `configure` with the same lines: drop `apiKey`, `auth` and `baseURL` from the input, then build route defaults with a fallback base URL and bearer auth. The two Cloudflare providers also each had their own copy of the account URL and `/ai/run` logic.

### Change

I added an internal `bearerRouteDefaults` next to `toConfig` in `src/providers/settings.ts` and used it in cerebras, deepinfra, deepseek, fireworks, togetherai, groq, mistral, meta, baseten, digitalocean, openrouter, vercel-ai-gateway, cohere, minimax, moonshot, zai and zai-coding-plan.

```diff
 export const configure = (input: Config = {}) => {
-  const { apiKey: _apiKey, auth: _auth, baseURL: endpoint, ...defaults } = input
-  const configured = route.with({
-    ...defaults,
-    endpoint: { baseURL: endpoint ?? baseURL },
-    auth: AuthOptions.bearer(input, "CEREBRAS_API_KEY"),
-  })
+  const configured = route.with(bearerRouteDefaults(input, "CEREBRAS_API_KEY", baseURL))
```

Without a default base URL it leaves `endpoint` undefined when no `baseURL` is given, which is what minimax, moonshot and the zai providers did before.

For Cloudflare, the account URL, the `/ai/run` conversion and the account check now live in an internal `cloudflare-shared.ts`. The exported `baseURL` and `runBaseURL` in both providers are thin wrappers with the same signatures and the same error messages.

### Out of scope

- I left digitalocean's own settings `config` alone. It always sets `http: { body }`, even with no body, and swapping in `toConfig` would change `decisionModel(...).http` and `imageModel(...).http` from an empty `HttpOptions` to `undefined`. Chat and responses would be unaffected, but the model objects would differ.
- google-vertex files are not touched.

The pty and persistent pty code had a few copies of the same logic, plus a field in `pty.ts` that could always be worked out from two others.

issues.title: max_tokens clamp is defeated by a 4K safety margin when the estimate undercounts; "Input too long: model limit N tokens" is not recognized as overflow

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
pi 1.4.0, provider `command-code` (an `openai-completions` proxy), model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` configured as `contextWindow: 1000000, maxTokens: 384000` — the provider's own published output cap for this model. Two failures, one cause each.

## 1. A 400 at ~65% of the window, because the clamp trusted an estimate

```
400: This model's maximum context length is 1048576 tokens. However, you requested
1064930 tokens (680930 in the messages, 384000 in the completion).
```

`packages/ai/src/api/simple-options.ts:18`:

```ts
const available = model.contextWindow - estimateContextTokens(context).tokens - CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS;
return Math.min(maxTokens, Math.max(MIN_MAX_TOKENS, available));
```

`estimateContextTokens` is the last assistant usage plus `estimateMessageTokens` for everything after it — chars/4 for text, 4800 chars per image. In this session the trailing messages were Chinese tool output, which chars/4 undercounts by roughly 2–4x. The estimate landed at least 16,354 tokens below the real prompt, `available` still exceeded 384,000, the full output cap went out, and `680930 + 384000 > 1048576`.

So the clamp only holds while the estimate is within `CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS` (4,096) of the truth. With `maxTokens: 384000` the budget tolerates ~16K of estimation error on a ~680K prompt — 2.4%. That is not a margin. RX14 described the same shape in #8061 ("the tokens estimation doesn't seem conservative enough") on this same model; what landed was the clamp, not a conservative estimate.

Any one of these would fix it:

- use the real prompt size from the previous response's usage and estimate only the delta — which is what `estimateContextTokens` intends, but the delta is exactly where the error lives;
- scale the safety margin with the output cap (`max(CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS, maxTokens / N)`): the larger `maxTokens` is, the more an estimation error costs;
- on this specific 400, retry once with `max_tokens = providerLimit - realPrompt` before falling back to compaction.

## 2. "Input too long" is not treated as an overflow

Same provider and model, different wording, later session:

```
400: Input too long: model limit 1048576 tokens, requested 1080887 tokens
```

`isContextOverflow({ role: "assistant", stopReason: "error", errorMessage: <above> })` returns **false** on 1.4.0. Nothing in `OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` (`packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts`) matches `Input too long: model limit N tokens, requested M`; `input is too long for requested model` is Bedrock's wording and does not match it.

Consequence: no overflow compaction, no retry — the turn simply dies. The provider's other phrasing (`maximum context length is N tokens`) *is* recognized and recovered from. Same endpoint, same failure, opposite handling.

Suggested pattern: `/input too long:.*model limit [\d,]+ tokens/i`

## 3. Why this is hard to attribute afterwards

The declared `contextWindow` is trusted in four places with four different meanings: compaction trigger (`contextWindow - reserveTokens`), the clamp above (as a hard ceiling), the silent-overflow branch of `isContextOverflow(message, contextWindow)`, and the UI percentage. Here the provider serves 1,048,576 while the model entry declares 1,000,000, and it counts `max_tokens` against that one budget.

Declaring the window too small is harmless. Declaring it too large silently removes the trigger and loosens the clamp. If everything were derived from it — usable input = `contextWindow - maxTokens`, used by both the trigger and the clamp — a bad declaration would at least fail at the boundary the user declared, instead of at a boundary no single subsystem owns.

issues.title: bash tool has no default timeout, so one unbounded command blocks the turn indefinitely

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

I asked the agent to look into WSL memory usage. It issued one bash call:

    wsl -- bash -c "…; sudo find / -maxdepth 6 -name 'docker-compose*.y*ml' -path '*link*' 2>/dev/null; …"

Inside WSL, `/mnt/c`, `/mnt/d` and `/mnt/e` are 9p mounts of the Windows drives, so that `find /` never finishes.

The tool call never returned. The session sat in `running` for 12+ minutes: no elapsed time, no progress, no error, and nothing appended to the session jsonl after the assistant message that contains the call — the tool result was never written. My only way out was the Stop button. The command was still running inside WSL 20 minutes later (`ps -eo pid,etime,args` showed `sudo find / -maxdepth 6 …`).

The schema is explicit that this is by design: `timeout` is described as "Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)", `resolveTimeoutMs(undefined)` returns `undefined`, so no timer is armed and `waitForChildProcess(child)` waits forever. (`BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000` exists in the bundle, but only `betaBashTool` uses it.)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11 + Git Bash, `pi -ne` (no extensions); also reproduces through an RPC client, since the tool implementation is the same.
2. Ask the model to run a bash command that does not terminate, e.g. `sleep 600`, without passing `timeout`.
3. The turn never returns, no timeout fires, and nothing in the UI distinguishes it from a slow model.


Validated with `pi -ne` (no extensions): a single `sleep 600` call is still running after 4 minutes with no timeout error — the node process is alive and its child bash is still executing `sleep 600`.

### Expected behavior

A bounded default, configurable in settings (Claude Code uses a 120 s default / 600 s max for Bash; Codex has `yield_time_ms` plus a `terminal_max_timeout` backstop). Small/fast models routinely omit the parameter, and the failure mode is a wedged turn.

Also useful: show elapsed time for a running tool call, so a stalled call is visible.

Windows-specific half: `killProcessTree` uses `taskkill /F /T /PID` on win32, which cannot reach the WSL PID namespace, so even an explicit abort leaves the real process running (related: #9129). On macOS/Linux `process.kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` kills the group.

Workaround today is a user extension with a `tool_call` hook that sets `event.input.timeout`, but bounded-by-default shouldn't require writing an extension.


### Version

1.4.0

issues.title: pi-durable: let beforeRequest reject a request
issues.body:
## Problem

`GenerationHooks.beforeRequest` can rewrite a request's messages, but it cannot stop the request. A throw from the hook goes to `onReport`, the next handler runs, and the request is still sent. The throw only propagates after the invocation has been signalled (`HookRunner.each`).

That means there is no clean way to gate a model request: a spend budget, a policy or account check, or a kill switch. Each of these needs to happen before every request, including recovery attempts and every round of a long tool loop, not only before a prompt is admitted.

## What we do today (pi-durable 1.3.0)

When a request is refused, the hook does the following:

1. Calls `conversation.abort()` without awaiting it. Awaiting would deadlock, because the abort waits for the very invocation the hook runs in.
2. Waits for `context.abortSignal`.
3. Throws.

The run then settles `unanswered` and no request is sent. This works, but it borrows the abort path for something that is really a refusal. The conversation records a user abort instead of a reason, and the hook needs a harness handle it would not otherwise need.

## Ask

Let `beforeRequest` refuse the request. For example, return `{ reject: string }` (or throw a dedicated `RequestRejected`). The generation task would then settle the run with a terminal assistant error carrying that message, without retrying and without calling the provider. This mirrors the `{ block }` result `beforeTool` already has.

Happy to send a PR if the shape sounds right.

issues.title: `schemaToType` function in codemode is incorrect with `prefixItems` and `items` under json schema draft 2020-12

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

`schemaToType()` converts a tuple such as { type: "array", prefixItems: [A, B], items: false } as `Array<never>` under JSON Schema draft 2020-12. `arrayType()` [checks `items` first](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/f1b2e77f5b13b2a199b1052cb79c235451afe7d7/packages/codemode/src/declarations.ts#L310-L313) and uses it as the type. According to the [changes of JSON Schema 2020-12 - 10.3.1.2](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core#section-10.3.1.2): 
> Note that the behavior of "items" without "prefixItems" is identical to that of the schema form of "items" in prior drafts. When "prefixItems" is present, the behavior of "items" is identical to the former "additionalItems" keyword.

This affects the customized tool definitions with tuple arguments using some MCP pacakages, e.g.,  a `z.tuple()` argument on [@modelcontextprotocol/server 2.x](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/1613-establish-json-schema-2020-12-as-default-dialect-f#why-2020-12) converts zod schemas to draft 2020-12.

### Steps to reproduce

```js
import { schemaToType } from "@earendil-works/pi-codemode";

const pair = [{ type: "string" }, { type: "number" }];
console.log(schemaToType({ type: "array", prefixItems: pair, items: false }));               // Array<never>
console.log(schemaToType({ type: "array", prefixItems: pair, items: { type: "boolean" } })); // Array<boolean>
```

### Expected behavior

`[string, number]` and `[string, number, ...boolean[]]`

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-codemode 1.1.0

issues.title: pi-durable: a JSON value nested ~1000 deep fails the whole Harness on SQLite storage

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
Potentially not a big issue, but something I found while implementing a DO agent and some effect libraries on top of pi-durable. 

### What happened?

A JSON value nested about 1000 levels deep ends the whole Harness when it is stored over SQLite storage.

Every record column has `CHECK (json_valid(...))`, and SQLite's JSON parser stops at 1000 levels. The failed CHECK is not one of Durable's own refusals, so `Storage.commit()` rejects as an unknown outcome. The Session then fails with `SessionFailed`, reported as `storage_failed` with `CHECK constraint failed: json_valid(record)`.

Every conversation of that Harness fails, not just the one that produced the value. After a reopen, the re-sent model request can produce the same answer and fail it again. pi-ai passes such arguments through intact on all three stream paths I tested, and nothing checks nesting depth before storage. So a prompt injection costing about 2 KB of brackets is enough.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Harness over `openNodeSqliteStorage(path)`.
2. Submit a write entry whose `data` is 1000 nested arrays. A depth of 999 is stored fine.
3. The submission rejects with the CHECK error, and a write to any other conversation then rejects with `SessionFailed`.

Same result when the faux model answers with a tool call whose arguments are 1000 levels deep. A self-contained vitest repro (public APIs only, faux provider) and the full analysis are in the comment below.

### Expected behavior

One oversized value fails only the operation that carried it, without ending every conversation of the Harness.

### Version

pi-durable 1.4.0, and `main` at b556cfe5b. Node v26.13.0, SQLite 3.54.0 (`node:sqlite`).

Drafted with an AI agent; the comment below is the full AI-generated analysis.

issues.title: OAuth flows ignore HTTP(S)_PROXY: token requests bypass the proxy

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Route the provider OAuth requests in `packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/*` through a proxy-aware fetch. Today they call the global `fetch()` directly, which ignores `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY`, so on networks where the identity endpoints are only reachable through a local proxy, every OAuth login (OpenAI Codex, Anthropic, xAI, GitHub Copilot, Kimi, ...) fails with no in-app way out.

### Why?

Concrete case from today: OpenAI Codex browser login completes, then the token exchange fails with `OpenAI Codex token exchange failed (403): unsupported_country_region_territory` - the exchange left through the direct connection and OpenAI rejected it by region. The same request succeeds through the proxy with curl.

The rest of pi-ai already handles proxies: `bedrock-converse-stream.ts` and `openai-codex-responses.ts` resolve them through `resolveHttpProxyUrlForTarget`; only the OAuth layer misses it. Node's global fetch never reads proxy env vars (undici behavior; `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` is Node 24+, pi requires >=22.19), so this cannot be fixed from outside the process.

### How? (optional)

Small `proxyAwareFetch(input, init)` wrapper in `packages/ai/src/utils/`: reuse the existing `node-http-proxy.ts` resolution (NO_PROXY included); when a proxy applies, dispatch through an undici `ProxyAgent`, otherwise fall back to the global fetch. Swap the bare fetch calls in the nine oauth files. Adds `undici` as a direct dependency of pi-ai (same version already in the lock tree). Tests included; `npm run check` passes locally. I'd implement this myself if there's interest.

issues.title: bash tool reports "Command timed out after N seconds" for a command that already exited with a real exit code
issues.body:
**What happened?**

When a bash command has already exited with a real exit code, but a descendant keeps the inherited stdout/stderr pipe busy, the tool reports:

```
Command timed out after N seconds
```

The command did not time out. Example measured here: the shell exited with code 1 after ~1.06s, the tool returned at 12.75s with `timeout: 3`, and the model was told `Command timed out after 3 seconds`. The real exit code 1 never reached the model, so it treats a finished-and-failed command as a slow one.

Root cause: `dist/core/tools/bash.js:107` only tests the `timedOut` flag:

```js
if (timedOut) throw new Error(`timeout:${timeout}`);
```

`waitForChildProcess` had already resolved with the real exit code (the child exited long before the deadline), and `killProcessTree` at the deadline is a no-op on a pid that no longer exists (`taskkill` exits 128), so nothing about that call is actually a timeout.

Related: #6787 asked for the timeout deadline to be enforced when descendants keep stdio active (auto-closed by the new-contributor gate). This report is narrower — I am not asking to change the wait, only to stop reporting a false `timed out` when the child already exited. That is a one-condition fix and it also preserves the wait behavior added for #5303.

**Steps to reproduce**

Windows 11, Git Bash, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0:

```bash
bash(command: "bash -c 'while true; do echo tick; sleep 0.05; done' & sleep 1; echo boom >&2; exit 1", timeout: 3)
```

Result: returns after 12.75s (varies: 5.1s, 12.0s, 22.7s in repeated runs) with output ending `Command timed out after 3 seconds`.

Control cases on the same machine:

| command | timeout | shell exited | tool returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| above (chatty descendant) | 3s | 1059ms, code 1 | 22744ms → `timed out` |
| same but descendant stdio redirected | 3s | 1050ms, code 1 | 1050ms → `Command exited with code 1` |
| `sleep 1; echo boom; sleep 300` | 3s | 3310ms (killed) | 3310ms → `timed out` (correct) |

**Expected behavior**

If the shell had already exited before the deadline, report its real exit code (the same `Command exited with code N` path), not `timed out`. Keep `timed out` for commands whose process was still alive at the deadline.

Suggested condition: record the exit timestamp, and in the `timedOut` branch throw only when the child had not exited before `start + timeoutMs`; otherwise return `{ exitCode }`.

**Version**

pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 (also present on `main`), Windows 11 + Git for Windows bash. Reached through pi-web-ui 0.113.1, which passes `timeout` through unchanged — reproduced directly against the SDK, no extension loaded.

---
_Filed by the reporter's coding agent; the measurements above were produced and re-run locally, not generated._

issues.title: Bedrock: a new BedrockRuntimeClient is created for every request
issues.body:
### What happened?

`bedrock-converse-stream.ts` does `new BedrockRuntimeClient(config)` inside `stream()`, so every model call gets a fresh client: new credential provider and new HTTP/2 session.

With an SSO profile that means every call does a `GetRoleCredentials` round trip to `portal.sso` plus a new TLS handshake to `bedrock-runtime`. I measured 2 new TLS handshakes per call, around 0.35 s before the request even starts (0.24 s SSO + 0.11 s TLS from eu-west-1). In an agent loop with ~35 calls per run that adds up fast. The old SSO sockets also stay open, I had 29 idle connections to `portal.sso` in one process.

I patched it locally to keep one client per config (region, profile, endpoint, hashed credentials, proxy) in a small LRU with an idle timeout, and dropping the cached clients on credential/auth errors so a refreshed or rotated key is picked up. Time to first byte on EU Haiku went from ~1.25 s to ~0.69 s, and calls after the first one do 0 handshakes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `amazon-bedrock` with an SSO profile (`AWS_PROFILE`).
2. Run any session with a few tool calls.
3. Watch `lsof -i` (or count TLS handshakes): every call opens a new connection to `portal.sso.<region>.amazonaws.com` and `bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com`.

### Expected behavior

The client, credential provider and HTTP/2 connection are reused across requests with the same config.

### Version

1.4.0, still the same on main (cc9c52310)

Happy to open a PR for this if you want it.

But the command itself is always saved verbatim: interactive-mode and rpc-mode both call `recordBashResult(command, ...)` with the typed command, even when an extension returned `result` or `operations`. A token typed literally in a `!` command ends up in the JSONL, and no extension hook can change that short of rewriting the session file.

issues.title: A codemode script fails before it runs when it declares a top-level variable named `tools`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Hello!
First thank you for creating Pi and numerous blog posts which truly resonate with me. I switched from Claude Code to Pi recently and it is like breath of fresh air.
I came across small issue and thought that you may be open for a PR to fix. My AI told me that I need to open issue first and got a lgtm before opening PR, that's why I am so detailed here. PR itself perhaps would be shorter 🙂 

So, here is what happened.
I configured a new mcp, called fluffyjaws, which is a knowledge base search assistant.
The problem is that when I ask him at the first time I see the following codemode block:
```
 codemode                                                                                                                                                             
 const tools = await searchTools('fluffyjaws');                                                                                                                       
 console.log(JSON.stringify(tools, null, 2));                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                      
 Script error:                                                                                                                                                        
 SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name                                                                                                                  
     at codemode.js:1:41                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                      
 No tool calls were made.                                                                                                                                             
 ```

On the next turn it recovers and everything works.

I talked with claude opus 5.5 model trying to understand if this is a bug or something which can be fixed upstream. And it turned out that the problem is in variable name `tools`. Here is what it told me:
> Models write `const tools = await searchTools(...)` on their own, so this happens without the user doing anything unusual. It costs a turn to recover. 
> The cause is that the script body is wrapped as `(async (tools, console) => { ... })` in `packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts:327`, so those two names are function parameters.

I am happy to submit a small PR with the fix. Let me know if you're willing to accept such contribution.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne` with codemode enabled
2. Ask pi to run **_exactly_** this codemode script:                                                                                                                       
    ```js
      const tools = await searchTools("read");
      return tools.length;
    ```

### Expected behavior
That script runs and returns a number.

### Actual behavior 
codemode ends up with an error:
```
Script error:
   SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name
       at codemode.js:1:41
```

### Version

1.3.0


### Potential approach for fix

`tools` and `console` are already globals: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L451-L453 so the wrapper could be `(async () => { ... })`, without `tools` and `console` arguments:
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L327
A script's `const tools` would then hide the global for that script only. Line numbers and `"use strict"` would keep working.

issues.title: pi-durable: permanently delete a conversation from storage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a way to permanently delete a conversation from pi-durable storage, e.g. `harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx)`: it refuses (or aborts first) while a run is active, then removes the conversation's entries, docs, inbox items and scheduler state from the store.

### Why?

We host pi-durable for end users (SQLite storage, one harness per process). When a user deletes a conversation we can drop our own index row and files, but the message history stays in the durable store forever: in 1.2.0 the store is append-only and the only removal I could find is for inbox items (`removeInboxItem`). So "delete" only means "nobody can look it up any more", which is a weaker privacy guarantee than users expect, and the store only ever grows.

Deleting rows from the SQLite file ourselves would depend on the internal schema and break on upgrades.

### How? (optional)

A storage-level `deleteConversation` implemented by each backend, plus a harness method that checks the live run state, evicts the conversation from memory (rooms/subscriptions get a terminal "deleted" signal), and calls it. Tombstoning the id so a later `submit`/`entries` fails with a clear "not found" error would keep callers honest.

issues.title: pi-durable: hand off at the context limit and keep the run going
issues.body:
We run pi-durable 1.4.0 in a Cloudflare Durable Object for a coding agent. We want to use the whole context window and never compact: near the limit, the model writes a handoff note, and the work continues in a fresh context built from the note.

`reset(note)` and a tool's `control: { handoff }` start the new context, but they also end the current run (`finishToolRound` → final boundary). To carry on, the host has to notice that, submit a new input itself, and pick what that input should be.

Automatic compaction does continue the run. It can be bent into a handoff (`keepRecentTokens: 1`, `backgroundTokens: 0`, a `beforeCompact` hook that returns a model-written note), but the summary is framed by the fixed `SUMMARY_PREFIX`, and mid-run it keeps the last tool round rather than the latest user message.

Request: a first-class "handoff and continue" mode, for example `compaction.mode: "handoff"` or `reset(note, { continue: true })`. In that mode:
- the run carries on in the new context: system prompt, the note, then the latest user input;
- the host supplies the note, from a hook or the model;
- the wording around the note is configurable.

Happy to test a prerelease.

issues.title: `getContextUsage()` massively overestimates context after retryable network error

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Pi 0.99.2, a retryable network error caused `getContextUsage()` to jump from about 42k tokens to 330,081 tokens.

Immediately before the spike:

```text
07:53:53  tokens=42707  hostTokens=42707  inMsgs=583 outMsgs=36
```

After a WebSocket/fetch failure:

```text
07:53:55  tokens=330081 hostTokens=330081 inMsgs=583 outMsgs=36
```

The session history shows:

```text
07:53:52 assistant toolUse  usage=33977
07:53:53 assistant error    usage=0
07:53:53 context_edit       replacement=null
07:53:55 assistant error    usage=0
07:53:55 context_edit       replacement=null
```

Pi's retry path creates these `context_edit` entries via `_omitRecoveryAttempt()`. It appears that the later edit invalidates the previous valid usage anchor, causing `estimateProjectedContextTokens()` to fall back to estimating the whole projection.

This looks like the same underlying issue as #10068, and is still reproducible on 0.99.2, which is the reason why I create a new issue. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a sufficiently long Pi session.
2. Trigger a retryable transport failure, e.g. a WebSocket/fetch failure.
3. Let Pi automatically retry the failed turn.
4. Observe `getContextUsage()` / the context indicator immediately after the retry omission is recorded.
5. The reported context can jump far above the value reported immediately before the failure, without corresponding new conversation content.


### Expected behavior

issues.title: Context overflow from llama.cpp server ("Context size has been exceeded.") is not detected, so auto-compaction never triggers
issues.body:
**Setup**: pi-coding-agent 1.2.0, provider `openai-completions` against llama.cpp `llama-server` (build b11342), model with `contextWindow` 262144, compaction enabled.

**What happens**: when the server's KV pool is full during decode, llama-server fails the request with the error message `Context size has been exceeded.` (llama.cpp `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, the `llama_decode` failure path: `if (n_batch == 1 && ret == 1) err = "Context size has been exceeded.";`). pi surfaces this as a plain error in the assistant message (`stopReason: "error"`, zero usage) and does nothing else: no compaction, no overflow retry.

**Why**: `isContextOverflow()` in `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` has no pattern matching this phrase. The only llama.cpp pattern is `/exceeds the available context size/i` (line 51 on current main), which covers the prompt-too-long case but not the decode-time pool exhaustion message. I checked the other patterns on main (OpenAI, LiteLLM, Gemini, xAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Together, Copilot, LM Studio, MiniMax, Kimi, Mistral, DS4, Ollama, DashScope, generic fallbacks); none matches.

Note that this path sends the error through `send_error(slot, err)` with the default error type (`ERROR_TYPE_SERVER`), so unlike the prompt-too-long case there is no `exceed_context_size_error` type to match on; matching on the text is the only option.

**Suggestion**: add `/context size has been exceeded/i` to the pattern list (with a `// llama.cpp server (KV pool exhausted during decode)` comment).

**Repro**: run llama-server with `-c <N> -np 2 --kv-unified`, start two pi sessions whose combined context exceeds N; the server returns the message above to the session that hits the limit and pi shows `Error: Context size has been exceeded.` with the context bar well below 100%.

prs.title: fix(durable): suspend code mode deadlines during human input
prs.body:
A code-mode script awaiting an external human decision can currently exhaust its wall-clock deadline while no code is running. Add host-controlled input waits that suspend the live timer and persist the wait interval in the durable run document, so a restart during the wait preserves the remaining execution budget.

`setCodemodeInputWait(tx, taskId, waitId, waiting)` is a trusted-host boundary. Overlapping waits share one elapsed interval; duplicate and late events cannot reopen resolved waits. Resuming restarts the deadline before execution, while ordinary external-tool latency remains timed. `CodemodeRun.setDeadline()` updates the existing host timer without replacing the VM or pending calls.

Validation: full `npm run check` and 42 focused host/durable tests passed, including timeout suspension, ordinary timeout, overlapping waits, duplicate decisions, and SQLite restart across a wait longer than the original budget. Checks used the pinned public model catalog because the live catalog had drifted; no generated catalog changes are included.

prs.title: Reconcile changed pinned git SHAs on startup
prs.body:
Fixes #10758

When a configured git package uses a pinned commit SHA, startup resolution currently only checks whether the checkout directory exists. Editing the SHA directly in settings therefore leaves the old checkout loaded until `pi update --extensions` is run.

This change inspects an existing checkout for pinned commit-like refs during `resolve()`. If HEAD no longer matches the configured SHA, it reuses the existing `updateGit()` path to fetch and reset the checkout before resources are collected. Offline behavior is unchanged.

Also adds a regression test that changes the configured pinned SHA from one local commit to another and verifies `resolve()` checks out the new commit.

labels.name: scope/interactive

issues.body:
## Summary

Extend the existing `/btw` side-question capability so that, while an Agent turn is still running, a side question can inspect a read-only snapshot of that turn's **current execution state** — not just the conversation context available before or between turns.

The goal is a lightweight, non-interrupting observer: users should be able to ask what the Agent is doing, what has completed, and what is currently running without sending a new instruction to the main Agent or waiting for the turn to finish.

## Current gap

The original `/btw` feature ([#2370](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/2370)) is designed for ephemeral, context-aware side questions. Its description says it uses the current conversation history and has no tool access.

That is useful for questions about already available conversation context, but it does not define a way for the side question to inspect authoritative events from an in-flight turn. During a long tool-using task, users need to distinguish:

- which tool calls have completed and what their results were;
- which tool call is currently running or waiting for approval/input;
- which files have been changed, and which tests or commands have actually completed;
- what is still unknown or pending.

A normal prompt can ask the main Agent to report progress, but that changes the main interaction and may interfere with the task. The existing Activity View ([#16022](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16022)) helps users find sessions that need attention, but it is not an interactive, execution-aware Q&A interface for the active turn.

## Proposed behavior

When a user invokes `/btw <question>` during an active turn:

1. Build a bounded, read-only execution-context snapshot for the exact active session/turn.
2. Make the latest available runtime events available to the side-question model, in addition to the ordinary conversation context.
3. Answer questions such as:
   - "What is the Agent doing right now?"
   - "Which steps and tool calls have completed?"
   - "Which command is still running?"
   - "Which files have been changed so far?"
   - "Did the tests finish, and what was the actual result?"
   - "Is the Agent waiting for permission or user input?"
4. Clearly distinguish **completed**, **in progress**, **waiting**, **failed**, and **unknown/not yet observed** states. Do not present a started tool call as completed or infer completion from a lack of output.
5. Keep the side question and its answer ephemeral, separate from the main conversation history, preserving the existing `/btw` behavior.

The snapshot should be refreshed when the side question starts. Reusing existing session/runtime event infrastructure is preferred over introducing a parallel event protocol. The implementation can choose the appropriate bounded event window and representation.

## Non-goals for the initial version

- Sending instructions or messages to the running Agent (mid-turn steering/injection).
- Pausing, resuming, cancelling, or otherwise controlling the main turn.
- Giving the side question permission to execute tools or modify files.
- Building a new full-screen activity dashboard or a persistent execution-trace database.
- Exposing events from sessions or workspaces the current user is not authorized to access.

The key distinction is **read-only observation and Q&A**, not intervention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Start a task that performs several sequential tool calls and keep the main turn running.
- [ ] After tool call A completes and tool call B starts, ask `/btw` what has happened so far. The answer identifies A as completed and B as in progress; it does not claim that B or later steps have completed.
- [ ] After another runtime event arrives, ask a second `/btw` question. The answer reflects the newer state rather than reusing a stale snapshot.
- [ ] The side answer can report observed tool activity and results, file changes, and test/command outcomes when those facts are present in the runtime events.
- [ ] Waiting-for-approval, waiting-for-user-input, failed, completed, and unavailable/unknown states are not conflated.
- [ ] Asking or cancelling a side question does not cancel, pause, inject a prompt into, or otherwise alter the main turn.
- [ ] The side question and answer do not pollute the main Agent conversation history.
- [ ] Runtime context is scoped to the exact active session/turn and respects existing workspace/session authorization boundaries.
- [ ] If live execution data is unavailable or incomplete, the answer says so instead of guessing.

## Related work

- [#2370](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/2370) — original ephemeral `/btw` side-question feature.
- [#6569](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/6569) — subagent execution observability and intervention. This proposal focuses on read-only side Q&A over the active turn's runtime state, including the main session; it does not add subagent controls.
- [#5239](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/5239) — communication and state awareness between the main session and subagents.
- [#11327](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/11327) — workspace session live-state subscription over SSE.
- [#16022](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16022) — Web Shell Activity View.
- [#15634](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15634) — delivery of injected messages into a running turn. This proposal deliberately does not inject messages into the main turn.

## Open design questions

- Which existing runtime/event source is authoritative for tool-call lifecycle, file changes, and command/test results?
- Should the first implementation target the interactive CLI only, or also expose the same capability through the Web Shell?
- What is the smallest useful bounded event window that provides fresh context without adding excessive prompt cost?

I'm happy to help investigate the current event flow and prepare a focused implementation after the maintainers confirm the intended scope.

prs.title: fix(ci): preserve Maven suite results across cache write-back failures
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR hardens the SDK Java Maven cache path after the suite/write-back lock split. Failed MySQL integration suites can still publish downloaded artifacts while preserving the original suite status, cache setup failures preserve the already-known suite result, and the final error annotation identifies the failed Maven stage. Cache seeds report copy failures, tolerate an unavailable cache or failed best-effort prune, and detach mutable resolver metadata before Maven runs — including single-link resolver state inherited from a previous job, since RUNNER_TEMP persists across jobs on the self-hosted pool. Write-back excludes the same metadata and partial-download files.

## Why it's needed

The lock relocation associated with #15262 already landed on main through #15128 and #15254. This branch is the remaining hardening delta: a failed suite should not throw away reusable downloads, a best-effort cache operation should not replace the suite result, and mutable resolver state should not be published as an immutable shared artifact. The test repair in 11c0f4b2fb12c also includes the deferred-status reporter in extracted shell snippets so those tests can exercise their intended paths.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

prs.title: fix(ci): keep sdk-java resolver bookkeeping and in-house jars out of the host cache (#15281)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The job-local Maven repository that the sdk-java suites resolve from no longer shares mutable inodes with the host cache:

- Every seed site drops `maven-metadata-local.xml` together with the other resolver bookkeeping names (`_remote.repositories`, `resolver-status.properties`, `*.lastUpdated`, `*.tmp`), so the unlocked Maven runs cannot rewrite a host-cache file through a seeded hardlink.
- The locked write-back removes every in-house fixed-release coordinate from the host cache (the `qwen-managed-agent-*` modules are purged by glob, tracking #15871's module split), prunes them at any depth rather than only at the repository root, publishes only job-produced files (the same five names stay job-local), and downgrades a failed cache-directory creation to a warning instead of reddening a green suite.
- The self-hosted Managed Agent Checkstyle leg resolves the SDK from the job-local repository the suite installed it into.
- The release builder's seed copies into the job-local repository instead of nesting a second `repository/` inside it, and drops the same bookkeeping names.
- The workflow meta-tests pin the five exclusions at every seed and both prunes, the write-back's children and their fd 9 closure, the host-side removal, the warning path, and the Checkstyle repository.

## Why it's needed

Moving Maven above the per-host lock is only safe while the job-local repository has no inode in common with the host cache. Maven's resolver rewrites its bookkeeping files in place, and the suites `install` fixed-release in-house artifacts: seeded as hardlinks, they let an unlocked run mutate state that every sibling job on the host reads.

Correction to the earlier description: the lock-scope change itself ("only the write-back takes the lock") landed through #15128 and #15254 and is already on main. #15274 remains open with overlapping cache and deferred-status changes. This PR is the cache-isolation half that makes that scope safe, and it is judged on that, not on the lock wait from #15281.

Reconciliation on 2026-10-31: merged main `812a8c7ccb` and reconciled with #15871's split of the Managed Agent server into nine Maven modules. The seed drops, the write-back prunes and the host-cache purge now cover the full in-house coordinate set; the purge globs `qwen-managed-agent-*` so a future module rename cannot leave a stale host copy behind. All four unique behaviors are retained: the host-cache purge, the seed nesting fix, the self-hosted Checkstyle repository, and the reference-release seed isolation. When #15274 lands, this branch reconciles against its delivered code again.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the `SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` job of a PR that touches a managed-agent path. The self-hosted step should show the `cp -aln` seed and all three Maven invocations before any `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock` line; the lock wait should appear only at the cache write-back, and the write-back should remove the in-house coordinates before copying. Grep the job-local repository for `maven-metadata-local.xml` after the suite: it should hold only job-produced files.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: a seeded `maven-metadata-local.xml` and a seeded `qwencode-sdk` jar were the same inode as the host cache, so the unlocked `mvn install` changed the host file (same inode, SHA and mtime both moved). After: the host file is byte- and mtime-identical while the job-local copy is still written, the write-back publishes zero bookkeeping files and never the in-house coordinates, and the host cache loses the pre-PR in-house trees. N/A for UI.

### Tested on

|     OS     |                       Status                        |
| :--------: | :-------------------------------------------------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ meta-tests (367 passed, 11 Linux-only skipped), shell probes, Prettier |
| 🪟 Windows |                   ⚠️ not tested                    |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ CI is authoritative for the Linux-only behavioral legs; earlier heads ran the full meta-tests there |

### Environment (optional)

Meta-tests at head `28eedc0e1a` (macOS): `scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`, `scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js`, `scripts/tests/sdk-java-lock.test.js` — 367 passed, 11 skipped (the Linux-only behavioral legs run in CI). Local shell probes confirmed the nine-coordinate any-depth prune, the five-name exclusion and the glob host purge. No JDK 21 / Maven locally, so the real Java suite is left to CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a cold host pays the seed cost once, and the write-back is best-effort and capped at 300 seconds, matching the MariaDB lane. The write-back also deletes pre-existing in-house copies from the host cache — intended, because they are the stale fixed-release jars the in-house prune exists to stop publishing.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real ECS pool and its ticketed lock queue; the full JDK 21 Maven suite; the MySQL / MariaDB integration lanes; the hosted legs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Related to #15281 (the lock-scope change landed through #15128 and #15254; this PR closes the cache-isolation gap that the smaller lock scope depends on).

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

### 证据（Before & After）

Before：播种出的 `maven-metadata-local.xml` 与 `qwencode-sdk` jar 与宿主缓存是同一 inode，不持锁的 `mvn install` 会改写宿主文件（inode 相同，SHA 与 mtime 都变化）。After：宿主文件字节与 mtime 完全不变，同时 job 本地副本仍被写入；写回不发布任何记账文件、也从不发布内部坐标；宿主缓存中遗留的内部目录被删除。UI 不适用。

prs.title: feat(serve): add user-scope Skill activation routes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds two daemon routes that enable or disable Skills in the **user** settings scope, which every workspace merges: `PUT /skills/:name/activation` and `PUT /skills/activation` (batch, up to 100 names). Like `PUT /extensions/activation`, they take no workspace selector. The body is `{ state: "enabled" | "disabled", mode?: "hard" | "default" }`; `mode` applies to disables only. Each request leaves the name in exactly one user list: a `hard` disable (the default) writes `skills.disabled`, a `default` disable writes `skills.defaultDisabled`, and an enable writes `skills.enabled`; the name is removed from the other two.

An enable is refused without writing, answering `200` with `changed: false` and a `block` naming the entry, when the merged config would still keep the Skill disabled: a System/SystemDefaults `skills.disabled` entry under either spelling, a User entry in the other spelling, or a `skills.defaultDisabled` entry no identically spelled grant cancels. Workspace entries never refuse a user write; they keep gating only their own workspace. Batch enables recheck refused names until the batch converges, so the outcome does not depend on request order.

After a change, every registered workspace runtime is reconciled and each changed key emits `settings_changed` with `scope: "user"` and the existing `skill_toggle` mutation object on every workspace event stream. To make the change reach live sessions, `workspaceSkillsRefresh` gains an optional `settingsScopes` parameter: user writes ask the ACP child and its sessions to re-read the user file as well, while every other refresh keeps re-reading only the workspace file. The runtime coordinator keeps that user reload pending until a refresh carrying it succeeds.

The routes are advertised as `user_skill_activation`, with `DaemonClient.setUserSkillActivation` / `setUserSkillsActivation` in the TypeScript SDK and documentation in the serve protocol and capabilities docs.

## Why it's needed

The daemon could only toggle Skills in workspace settings. Hosts that manage Skills across workspaces (for example an embedding product that centrally enables or disables Skills for a user) had no API for the user settings file: the generic `/workspace/settings` route rejects `skills.*`, so they wrote `~/.qwen/settings.json` directly. That bypasses the daemon's settings lock (risking lost updates against other user-scope writers), duplicates the block/spelling rules, and never reaches running sessions, because the Skills refresh only re-read the workspace file. These routes give a supported, locked, consistently validated write path that also applies to live sessions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start `qwen serve` and check `GET /capabilities` lists `user_skill_activation`.
2. `PUT /skills/<name>/activation` with `{"state":"disabled"}`: `~/.qwen/settings.json` gains `skills.disabled: ["<name>"]`; a live session's command list drops the Skill; every workspace stream receives `settings_changed` with `scope: "user"`.
3. Repeat with `{"state":"disabled","mode":"default"}`: the name moves to `skills.defaultDisabled`; a workspace `skills.enabled` entry with the same spelling re-enables it in that workspace only.
4. `{"state":"enabled"}`: the name moves to `skills.enabled`. Add `skills.disabled: ["<name>"]` to System settings and repeat: the response is `changed: false` with `block.scope: "System"` and the file is untouched.
5. Unit tests:
   - `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/config/skill-settings.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-skills.test.ts src/serve/workspace-runtime-coordinator.test.ts src/serve/run-qwen-serve.test.ts src/serve/capability-parity.test.ts`
   - `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/acpAgent.test.ts -t skill`
   - `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts -t "serve capability registry"`
   - `cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx vitest run test/unit/DaemonClient.test.ts`

Locally all of the above pass, along with `tsc --noEmit` for `packages/cli` and `packages/sdk-typescript`, eslint, and prettier. A full `src/serve/server.test.ts` run shows one or two different unrelated failures per run under load; the same happens on an unmodified `origin/main`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (daemon API; covered by the unit tests above).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (vitest) on macOS, Node 26.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a `hard` user disable cannot be lifted by any workspace, which is the existing meaning of a user `skills.disabled` entry; callers that want per-workspace opt-in use `mode: "default"`. Re-reading the user file in live sessions now happens only when a user Skill write requests it, so other user settings edited behind those sessions are picked up at the same time.
- Not validated / out of scope: no read route for user-scope Skill lists (reads stay workspace-scoped); `skills.disabledLevels` and `skills.directories` are not writable through these routes; no Managed Agent equivalent (recorded in the capability parity matrix).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New routes and an optional refresh parameter; existing routes and refresh behavior are unchanged.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

新增两个 daemon 路由，用于在**用户级** settings（所有工作区都会合并的那一层）中启用或禁用 Skill：`PUT /skills/:name/activation` 和 `PUT /skills/activation`（批量，最多 100 个名字）。与 `PUT /extensions/activation` 一样，它们不带工作区选择器。请求体为 `{ state: "enabled" | "disabled", mode?: "hard" | "default" }`，`mode` 只对禁用生效。每次请求后该名字只会出现在一个用户级名单中：`hard` 禁用（默认）写入 `skills.disabled`，`default` 禁用写入 `skills.defaultDisabled`，启用写入 `skills.enabled`，并从另外两个名单中移除。

当合并后的配置仍会让该 Skill 保持禁用时，启用请求会被拒绝且不写文件，返回 `200`、`changed: false` 以及指明具体条目的 `block`：System/SystemDefaults 中任一拼写的 `skills.disabled` 条目、User 中另一种拼写的条目，或没有同拼写授权可以抵消的 `skills.defaultDisabled` 条目。工作区条目从不拒绝用户级写入，它们只继续约束各自的工作区。批量启用会对被拒绝的名字反复重查直到收敛，因此结果与请求顺序无关。

发生变更后，所有已注册的工作区 runtime 都会 reconcile，每个变更的 key 会在每个工作区的事件流上发出带 `scope: "user"` 和现有 `skill_toggle` mutation 对象的 `settings_changed`。为了让变更作用到运行中的会话，`workspaceSkillsRefresh` 新增可选参数 `settingsScopes`：用户级写入会要求 ACP 子进程及其会话同时重读用户级文件，其他刷新仍然只重读工作区文件。runtime coordinator 会一直保留这次用户级重读请求，直到某次携带它的刷新成功。

这些路由以 `user_skill_activation` 能力标签发布，TypeScript SDK 提供 `DaemonClient.setUserSkillActivation` / `setUserSkillsActivation`，并更新了 serve 协议文档与 capabilities 文档。

## 为什么需要

此前 daemon 只能在工作区 settings 中切换 Skill。需要跨工作区管理 Skill 的宿主（例如为用户统一启停 Skill 的嵌入式产品）没有操作用户级 settings 文件的 API：通用的 `/workspace/settings` 路由会拒绝 `skills.*`，于是它们只能直接写 `~/.qwen/settings.json`。这样绕过了 daemon 的 settings 锁（可能与其他用户级写入互相覆盖），重复实现了锁定与拼写规则，而且永远不会作用到运行中的会话，因为 Skill 刷新只重读工作区文件。这两个路由提供了受支持、加锁、校验一致，并且能作用到运行中会话的写入路径。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 启动 `qwen serve`，确认 `GET /capabilities` 包含 `user_skill_activation`。
2. 对 `PUT /skills/<name>/activation` 发送 `{"state":"disabled"}`：`~/.qwen/settings.json` 中出现 `skills.disabled: ["<name>"]`；运行中会话的命令列表不再包含该 Skill；每个工作区的事件流都收到 `scope: "user"` 的 `settings_changed`。
3. 改为发送 `{"state":"disabled","mode":"default"}`：该名字移到 `skills.defaultDisabled`；某个工作区中同拼写的 `skills.enabled` 条目只会在该工作区重新启用它。
4. 发送 `{"state":"enabled"}`：该名字移到 `skills.enabled`。在 System settings 中加入 `skills.disabled: ["<name>"]` 后重复：响应为 `changed: false` 且 `block.scope: "System"`，文件不变。
5. 单元测试：
   - `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/config/skill-settings.test.ts src/serve/routes/workspace-skills.test.ts src/serve/workspace-runtime-coordinator.test.ts src/serve/run-qwen-serve.test.ts src/serve/capability-parity.test.ts`
   - `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/acpAgent.test.ts -t skill`
   - `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts -t "serve capability registry"`
   - `cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx vitest run test/unit/DaemonClient.test.ts`

本地以上全部通过，`packages/cli` 与 `packages/sdk-typescript` 的 `tsc --noEmit`、eslint、prettier 也通过。完整运行 `src/serve/server.test.ts` 时，在负载下每次会出现一到两条不同的无关失败；在未修改的 `origin/main` 上同样如此。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A（daemon API，由上述单元测试覆盖）。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|   🍏 macOS   |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows  |  ⚠️  |
|   🐧 Linux   |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

仅在 macOS、Node 26 上运行单元测试（vitest）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：`hard` 用户级禁用无法被任何工作区解除，这本就是用户级 `skills.disabled` 条目的既有含义；需要按工作区单独开启的调用方应使用 `mode: "default"`。运行中会话重读用户级文件只在用户级 Skill 写入请求时发生，因此在这些会话背后编辑的其他用户级设置也会同时生效。
- 未验证或范围外：没有读取用户级 Skill 名单的路由（读取仍按工作区）；`skills.disabledLevels` 与 `skills.directories` 不能通过这些路由写入；没有 Managed Agent 对应能力（已记录在 capability parity 矩阵中）。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无。仅新增路由和一个可选的刷新参数，现有路由与刷新行为不变。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>
