prs.title: refactor(web-shell): share session view reset state
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR consolidates the shared transcript-view reset used by session changes and `/clear`. It also makes the component contract explicit: when a consumer keeps the same transcript component mounted across a session-key change, a reading pause from the previous session is cleared. A reconnect within the same session continues to preserve that pause.

## Why it's needed

The two reset paths maintained overlapping state independently. Sharing their common reset keeps those paths consistent and covers the component's mount-stable session-switch contract. The shipped routes already remount the transcript or render an empty transcript when switching sessions, so this is component-level hardening, not a demonstrated user-visible fix on those routes.

The main-CI failure tracked in #15038 is an unhandled rejection in the hosted workspace tool-turn tests. This Web Shell change does not fix that failure and must not close its tracker.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Keep one transcript component mounted, pause following, and change its session key while supplying the next session's non-empty transcript. Following should resume, both with and without a replay transition.
- Reconnect within the same session after pausing. The reading position should remain paused.
- Clear the transcript within the same session. The existing clear/reset behavior should remain intact.
- Treat the session-switch DOM cases as component-contract coverage; the shipped routes' remount/empty-first behavior is not a before/after reproduction of this change.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Earlier review reports establish that the added DOM cases fail without the session-switch pause reset and pass with it. The same reports establish that shipped-route-shaped cases already pass on the base. Those historical results support the component contract only; they are not new validation of the current head.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | No local checks run in this closeout |
| Windows | No local checks run in this closeout |
| Linux | Earlier DOM evidence is recorded in the PR discussion; the previous head's smoke check failed and checks for this closeout are pending |

## Risk & Scope

- The shared reset clears reading-pause, pagination-snapshot and expansion state. Each caller retains its additional resets; the settled-stale latch is cleared by `/clear`, not by the render-phase session switch.
- This PR changes no shipped route's mounting or empty-transcript behavior and does not repair the hosted workspace tool-turn failure.
- No local tests, build, lint or typecheck were run during this closeout, as requested. The previous smoke failure is reported separately and checks for the new head are pending; no passing browser result is claimed.
- No public API or migration change.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15038; this PR does not resolve it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

合并会话切换与 `/clear` 共用的视图重置逻辑，并明确组件契约：调用方若在切换 session key 时保留同一个消息列表实例，上一会话的阅读暂停状态会被清除。同一会话重连仍保留阅读暂停。

## 为什么需要

两条路径原先分别维护重叠的重置状态。共用重置逻辑可以保持行为一致，并补全不重建组件时的会话切换契约。当前已发布页面在切换会话时会重建消息列表，或先渲染空记录，因此本 PR 是组件层加固，不是已证实的现有页面可见缺陷修复。

#15038 跟踪的是 hosted workspace tool-turn 测试中的未处理拒绝。该 Web Shell 改动不能修复此 CI 故障，也不应自动关闭它。

## Reviewer 测试计划

- 保持消息列表实例不变，暂停跟随后，改变 session key 并传入下一会话的非空记录。有回放与无回放两种情况下都应恢复跟随。
- 同一会话暂停后重连，应继续保持阅读位置。
- 在同一会话清空记录，原有清空和重置行为应保持。
- 新增 DOM 用例验证组件契约；已发布页面重建组件或先清空记录的路径不能作为本改动的前后对照复现。

## 已有证据与验证边界

此前评审记录表明，移除会话切换时的暂停重置会使新增 DOM 用例失败，保留时通过；按已发布页面形态编写的对照用例在 base 上原本就通过。这些历史结果只支撑组件契约，不代表本轮重新验证了当前 head。

本轮按用户要求未运行本地测试、构建、lint 或 typecheck。上一 head 的 Web Shell smoke 失败另行记录，新 head 的检查尚未完成；未声称浏览器验证通过。macOS 与 Windows 本轮均未验证，Linux 既有 DOM 证据见 PR 讨论。

## 风险与范围

公共重置处理阅读暂停、分页快照和展开状态；调用方保留各自额外的重置。settled-stale 状态只在 `/clear` 路径清除，不在渲染期会话切换路径清除。本 PR 不改变页面挂载方式，也不修复 hosted workspace tool-turn 故障。无公共 API 或迁移变更。

## 关联 Issue

Refs #15038；本 PR 不解决该 issue。

</details>


### Latest repair

The latest repair also cancels old-session follow/animation callbacks and strengthens continued-follow assertions. It carries the two smoke selector corrections already landed in #15860. These new cases were not run locally; current-head CI remains pending.

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(web-shell): reset follow pause when the session changes (#15038) (#15060)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(web-shell): reset follow pause when the session changes (#15038)

Preserving a reading pause across reconnects also preserved it across a
session switch, because the pause lives in a ref that outlives the
displayed transcript. Switching sessions while paused then left the new
transcript stranded above the latest content even though the reader never
paused it. Drop the pause in the existing session-scoped reset.

Add a DOM test that pauses session A, switches to session B mid-replay,
and asserts B lands at the bottom once catch-up completes.

* test(web-shell): pin the no-replay session switch and share the reset (#15038)

* test(ci): exempt the TUI parity suites from the no-AK gate (#15038)

The no-AK wiring meta-test requires every runnable integration test to be selected or explicitly exempted. The OpenTUI parity suites added by #14964 run in the tui-parity workflow, so list them in the exemption map with the same runtime-budget reason as the neighboring interactive suites.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(ci): drop duplicate TUI parity exemptions from the no-AK gate (#15038)

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* docs(web-shell): correct the session-switch reset premise (#15038)

* docs(web-shell): correct the sessionKey reset contract note (#15038)

prs.title: fix(serve): serialize overlapping cleanup retries
prs.body:
## What this PR does

I serialize background and resident-load cleanup retries within each attached Session. A queued request rechecks unsettled work and durable cleanup debt after its predecessor, using its own authorization options. A failed attempt remains an error for its caller and leaves the next request free to retry. An older caller cannot erase a successor's queue slot. Java unit validation also bounds JVM-held H2 catalogs to a test class instead of retaining every class's catalog in one process.

## Why it's needed

I reproduced a wake retry and passive reload observing the same unpaid owner before either confirms its release. This produces three release calls where two are expected. A late background refusal can also leave recovery blocked after successful cleanup. This is the cleanup-debt case in #14101, encountered while checking #14937.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Hold the background original-owner release while admitting a passive load. Success must produce exactly two total release calls, one terminal turn, one subsequent cleanup confirmation, an unblocked Session, and no repeated model turn.
- Refuse the held release. The queued load must make its own retry, with exactly three calls after two refusals and the same final state. Every call must retain the original binding, generation and Runtime owner.
- Admit a real later prompt while a cleanup is queued. After the predecessor refuses, queued cleanup must recheck the prompt before touching its owner.
- For three callers, hold the second release after the first fails. The first caller must preserve the successor's slot, and the third must wait. Once all callers settle, the retry promise must clear.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Current head: `888fc1fd01ada97b7eb16dcf38d70b52df0b641d`. I merged upstream main `4cd3372b` to include the current lint gate. The cleanup implementation and regression-test file are byte-identical to `0967b44b`, and the PR retains its five-file scope, including the class-fork setting in the verification module. All nine gate-freshness tests pass locally. Fresh upstream CI is pending; the successful checks previously recorded at `3fd698a2` remain historical evidence for that revision. Configured skipped lanes remain coverage limits.

The recorded original-source control fails the duplicate-release and stale-recovery assertions. This does not claim that both baseline branches fail deterministically on every host. Prior guard mutations were caught by the unsettled-prompt, settled-promise and successor-slot cases; those mutation receipts belong to the earlier recorded candidate.

Root build, bundle, complete TypeScript typecheck, scoped ESLint/Prettier, nine gate-freshness tests and 44 lint-scope tests pass at `2470302a0a`. The selected cleanup suite passes **29/29** with no retry or timeout override. These are earlier revision-specific receipts; the H2 increment changed only Java unit-fork configuration and its two regression classes, and the latest main merge awaits fresh CI. Other Harness cases were filtered; this is not the complete Harness suite.

The Java run at `2470302a0a` reports 5,573 tests, zero assertion failures, four errors and 19 skips. Three fresh-schema errors terminate in H2 heap exhaustion; a separate provisioner happy-path case exceeds its one-second startup deadline. The earlier run exhausted heap in two different schema cases. The relation between GC pressure and the deadline error remains unproven.

A bounded probe of the actual schema, its 38 canonical tables and H2 2.4.240 confirms one retention mechanism: after four databases are initialized, all connections are closed and all four data sources are collected, H2 still retains all four catalogs after GC. Explicit shutdown removes them. The default reused test JVM lets such fixture state accumulate across 375 classes. Ordinary Surefire now starts a fresh JVM per class, with its default single fork keeping classes sequential. Failsafe MySQL/Hosted settings and the overriding fault-gate profile remain unchanged; JaCoCo continues appending fork execution data.

Two real H2 regression classes deliberately reuse one catalog name. With the old reused fork, the second class sees the first class's table and fails; with class forks, both pass. The local Maven harness uses the unmodified test sources, actual default plugin configuration, Surefire 3.5.6, JUnit 5.14.1, H2 2.4.240 and JDK 21.0.7: **before one passed/one failed; after two passed, zero skips**. It is an isolated harness, not a full server-module compile. Direct JUnit controls also confirm both build-oracle tests skip outside Maven and both fail when a synthetic CI run lacks the Surefire marker; restored fork reuse still fails normally under Maven.

I verified that the required Java 21 fast gate, including the module compile and unit/H2 verification, passed on `3fd698a2`; the job took 59m35s including build, tests and static checks. The Java 11 real-daemon E2E job also passed. The MySQL-backed Hosted/EventTransport profiles were not selected by this CI tier. I retain the earlier failures and their qualifications; the focused local harness alone was not the acceptance evidence.

An earlier cleanup run also had two 15-second timeouts, followed by a 29/29 pass on an unchanged candidate; their cause remains unresolved and the failed logs are retained. No source timeout increase is included.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | No local current-head run |
| Windows | No local current-head cleanup run |
| Linux | Current-head upstream lint/static, unit/integration/Web Shell/Serve A/B checks and the Managed Agent fast tier pass. The earlier 29-case and H2 controls remain revision-specific receipts. |

### Environment

Node 22.21.1, frozen pnpm dependencies, 4 CPU / 8 GiB isolated Linux container, 6 GiB build/typecheck heap. Public HTTP/journal tests use mocked model and Runtime Broker responses; no live provider or TUI was exercised.

## Risk & Scope

- Serialization is per attached Session; each waiter retains its own authorization and recovery options.
- I record the unselected macOS/Windows unit lanes, installed-npm lanes and MySQL-backed Hosted/EventTransport profiles as coverage limits. Class isolation adds JVM startup and reduces cross-class Spring cache reuse; the 59m35s fast-gate duration is a combined build/test/static-check measurement, not an isolated estimate of that overhead.
- No protocol or migration change. Timeout-policy work remains in #14625 / #10892 rather than this concurrency fix.

## Linked Issues

Related to #14101 and #15483; encountered while checking #14937.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

我在每个已附加 Session 内串行执行后台和驻留加载触发的清理重试。排队请求等待前序完成后，使用自身授权选项重新检查未结束工作和持久清理债务。失败仍返回给对应调用者，同时允许后续请求重试。较早调用者不能清除后继请求的队列槽位。Java 单元验证还将 JVM 保留的 H2 目录限定在一个测试类的生命周期内，而不是在一个进程中累积所有类的目录。

## 为什么需要

我复现了唤醒重试与被动重新加载在任一方确认释放之前同时发现同一未偿还所有者的情况。这会产生三次释放，而预期为两次。后台较晚的拒绝还可能在成功清理后重新阻塞恢复。这对应 #14101 的清理债务场景，在检查 #14937 时再次遇到。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

- 阻塞后台对原始所有者的释放，同时允许被动加载。成功时必须恰好有两次释放调用、一个终态回合、其后一个清理确认、解除阻塞的 Session，且不重复模型回合。
- 拒绝被阻塞的释放。排队加载必须自行重试，两次拒绝后恰好有三次调用，并得到相同最终状态。每次调用都必须保持原始绑定、代次和 Runtime 所有者。
- 清理排队时接受一个真实的后续提示。前序拒绝后，排队清理必须在操作所有者之前重新检查该提示。
- 三个调用者场景中，第一次失败后阻塞第二次释放。第一个调用者必须保留后继槽位，第三个必须等待。所有调用结束后，重试 promise 必须清除。

### 前后对比证据

当前提交：`888fc1fd01ada97b7eb16dcf38d70b52df0b641d`。我合并了上游 main `4cd3372b`，纳入当前 lint 门槛。清理实现及回归测试文件与 `0967b44b` 的字节完全一致；PR 仍保持五文件范围，包括 verification 模块中的按类分叉设置。本地九个门槛新鲜度测试全部通过。新的上游 CI 尚待完成；此前 `3fd698a2` 的成功检查仍仅作为该版本的历史证据。配置中跳过的车道仍列为覆盖限制。

已记录的原始源码对照会触发重复释放和过时恢复状态的断言失败。这不意味着两个基线分支在每个主机上都确定失败。此前的守卫变异被未结束提示、已结束 promise 和后继槽位用例捕获；这些变异记录对应先前记录的候选提交。

根目录构建、打包、完整 TypeScript 类型检查、限定范围 ESLint/Prettier、九个门槛新鲜度测试及 44 个 lint 范围测试在 `2470302a0a` 通过。选定的清理套件 **29/29 通过**，没有修改重试或超时。这些证据对应前述提交；H2 增量仅修改 Java 单元分叉配置及两个回归类，最新 main 合并仍待新的 CI 验证。其他 Harness 用例被过滤；这不是完整 Harness 套件。

`2470302a0a` 的 Java 运行报告 5,573 个测试、零断言失败、四个错误和 19 个跳过。三个新建模式错误终止于 H2 堆耗尽；另一个提供器正常路径用例超过其一秒启动期限。更早的运行在另外两个模式用例中耗尽堆。GC 压力与启动期限错误之间的关系仍未证实。

对真实模式、其 38 张规范表及 H2 2.4.240 的有界探针确认了一种保留机制：初始化四个数据库后，全部连接关闭且四个数据源均被回收，GC 后 H2 仍保留全部四个目录。显式关闭可将其移除。默认复用测试 JVM 会让此类夹具状态在 375 个类之间累积。普通 Surefire 现为每个类启动新 JVM，其默认单分叉保持类串行执行。Failsafe 的 MySQL/Hosted 设置及覆盖配置的 fault-gate profile 不变；JaCoCo 继续追加各分叉执行数据。

两个真实 H2 回归类有意复用同一目录名称。旧的复用分叉让第二个类看到第一个类的表并失败；按类分叉时两者均通过。本地 Maven 夹具使用未修改的测试源、真实默认插件配置、Surefire 3.5.6、JUnit 5.14.1、H2 2.4.240 和 JDK 21.0.7：**修改前一个通过、一个失败；修改后两个通过、零跳过**。这是独立夹具，不是完整服务端模块编译。直接 JUnit 对照还确认两个构建检查在 Maven 之外跳过，模拟 CI 缺少 Surefire 标记时两个均失败；在 Maven 中恢复复用分叉仍正常触发回归。

我确认 `3fd698a2` 上必需的 Java 21 fast gate 已通过，包括模块编译和单元/H2 验证；该任务包含构建、测试和静态检查，共用时 59 分 35 秒。Java 11 真实 daemon E2E 任务也已通过。本 CI 层级未选择 MySQL 支撑的 Hosted/EventTransport profiles。我保留此前失败及其限定说明；本地定向夹具本身不是验收证据。

此前一次清理运行还出现两个 15 秒超时，之后未修改的候选提交 29/29 通过；原因仍未确定，失败日志已保留。本改动不增加源码超时上限。

### 已测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | 当前提交未在本地运行 |
| Windows | 当前提交的清理用例未在本地运行 |
| Linux | 当前提交的上游 lint/静态检查、单元/集成/Web Shell/Serve A/B 检查及 Managed Agent fast tier 已通过。此前 29 用例和 H2 对照仍对应各自列出的提交。 |

### 环境

Node 22.21.1，冻结 pnpm 依赖，4 CPU / 8 GiB 独立 Linux 容器，构建和类型检查使用 6 GiB 堆。公开 HTTP/日志测试使用模拟模型与 Runtime Broker 响应；未测试真实提供商或 TUI。

## 风险与范围

- 串行化按已附加 Session 生效；每个等待者保留自身的授权和恢复选项。
- 我将未选择的 macOS/Windows 单元车道、installed-npm 车道及 MySQL 支撑的 Hosted/EventTransport profiles 列为覆盖限制。按类隔离增加 JVM 启动并减少跨类 Spring 缓存复用；59 分 35 秒是 fast gate 构建/测试/静态检查的合计测量，不是该额外开销的独立估计。
- 无协议或迁移变更。超时策略工作保持在 #14625 / #10892，不纳入此并发修复。

## 关联问题

关联 #14101 和 #15483；在检查 #14937 时遇到。

</details>

prs.title: fix(memory): match reader advice to the binding index budget
prs.body:
## What this PR does

I match memory-index overflow advice to the binding line and character budgets and direct durable edits to topic-file frontmatter. I preserve complete link targets and keep description-shortening advice conditional when an unfamiliar format or the writer's type fallback prevents a guarantee. I merged main, including #14937, while preserving its bounded, single-paragraph writer diagnostics outside the entry budget.

## Why it's needed

170 ordinary 150-unit entries total 25,669 UTF-16 code units: descriptions can be shortened even though no entry exceeds the ordinary line length. Conversely, 160 bare 200-unit links cannot safely be cut to 150 units. Editing a generated index can also be undone by a rebuild, and an empty description can fall back to the memory type.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Exceed the character budget with ordinary entries, shorten topic-file descriptions, and check the regenerated index. Advice must identify this durable remedy without promising that descriptions alone always make it fit.
- Load bare long links, one huge link, and a protected long link mixed with removable descriptions. Retained links must remain complete; advice must not prescribe cutting their targets.
- Exercise the writer's empty-description type fallback, grouped or ambiguous suffixes, and unfamiliar formats. Keep uncertain remedies conditional.
- Exceed the line cap with a very long excluded tail. Preserve the first 200 candidates and base character-budget advice on those candidates.
- Load bounded writer diagnostics describing scan-cap or body-budget omissions. Preserve the actual saved notice without falsely reporting another omission during loading.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Current head: `702d722bcf1abb128a4d6830f06736991fb6f212`. My [Linux validation](https://github.com/jabrailkhalil/qwen-code/actions/runs/41194754221) passes the root build, bundle, repository-wide typecheck, scoped ESLint/Prettier over all eight PR paths, and the complete memory suite: **1,287 passed, 1 skipped** across 54 files. The built-module filesystem probe passes seven checks over eight fixtures; built CLI version/help and startup-bundle checks pass. This is author-side verification; upstream CI still needs to complete on this head.

Two selected character-budget tests fail as assertions with the prompt source restored to main `4cd3372b`; both pass after restoration. Disabling the length-cause predicate makes two separate cases fail; both pass when the predicate is restored. Local Windows verification also passes all 138 prompt/budget/writer-integration cases and the same four selected negative-control witnesses.

The first merged-source run had 1,286 passes, 1 skip and one failed writer-integration expectation for the old reader wording. I updated that expectation to the precise line-count remedy, retained the assertions preserving all 200 entries and forbidding blind length advice, and added a check that the candidate window is not also blamed for character pressure. The complete rerun above passes. Earlier revision-specific cold-scan failures remain historical evidence; I have not changed performance ceilings, retries or runner identity, or claimed a performance fix.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| Linux | Complete author validation linked above |
| Windows | 138 source tests and selected negative controls |
| macOS | No current-head local run |

### Environment

Node 22 and frozen pnpm dependencies. The filesystem checks are deterministic; I did not exercise a live provider or interactive TUI.

## Risk & Scope

- Conservative recognition can withhold a definite remedy for unfamiliar entry formats. Complete links, ordering and budget limits remain protected.
- I did not rerun the entire repository or Hosted Harness suites for this reader change. Upstream CI remains pending.
- #14937 has merged; this update preserves its writer diagnostics while completing the reader correction. Items 2–5 of #15277 remain separate. No migration or settings change.

## Linked Issues

Related to #15277 (item 1) and #14834.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

我让读取端建议准确区分行数和字符预算，将持久修改指向主题文件的 frontmatter，并保留完整链接。未知格式和写入端类型回退使结果不确定时，缩短建议保持条件性。我已合并包含 #14937 的 main，并保留其有界、单段写入诊断；这些诊断不占条目预算。

## 为什么需要

170条各150单位的普通条目共占25,669个 UTF-16 单位，即使单条未超长，仍可尝试缩短描述。160条各200单位的纯链接则不能裁剪到150单位。索引编辑可能被重建覆盖，空描述也可能回退为内存类型。

## 审阅者测试计划

检查普通条目的字符压力、不可裁剪的链接、描述类型回退、有歧义的分组后缀、行数上限以外的长尾，以及真实写入诊断的保留。应保留前200个候选，不用已排除的尾部误判候选字符压力。

### 前后对比证据

当前提交：`702d722bcf1abb128a4d6830f06736991fb6f212`。上述 [Linux验证](https://github.com/jabrailkhalil/qwen-code/actions/runs/41194754221)的根构建、打包、全仓类型检查、八个 PR 路径的格式与 ESLint 检查，以及完整 memory 套件均通过：**1,287通过，1跳过**，共54个文件。构建模块的八个文件系统场景通过七项检查；CLI版本、帮助及启动包检查也通过。这是作者侧验证，上游 CI 尚待完成。

恢复 main `4cd3372b` 的读取源码，使两个字符预算用例按断言失败；恢复修复后二者通过。关闭长度原因判定，使另两个用例失败；恢复判定后二者通过。Windows本地138个读取/预算/写入集成用例及相同负向对照也通过。

首次合并源码运行有1,286通过、1跳过和一个仍期待旧读取建议文字的写入集成断言失败。我将其改为准确的行数处理建议，保留前200条完整保留和禁止盲目长度建议的断言，并新增候选窗口未超字符预算的断言。完整重跑已通过。此前提交的冷扫描失败仍保留为历史证据；没有改变性能上限、重试或 runner 标识，也不声称修复了性能问题。

### 平台与范围

Linux运行完整作者侧验证；Windows运行138个源码用例和选定负向对照；macOS未运行当前提交。本次未运行真实提供商、交互TUI、完整仓库或 Hosted Harness 套件。#14937 已合并；此更新保留其写入诊断并完成读取端修正。#15277第2–5项保持独立，没有迁移或设置变更。

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): add an E2B Cloud runtime provider
prs.body:
## What this PR does Adds opt-in external Workspace profiles for Hosted file tools and foreground Shell execution in E2B Cloud, while keeping the Harness, model access, approvals and journals in the central deployment. An operator publishes a registered Workspace with its OWNER grant; clients then select that Workspace through the existing Session API. A standalone provider owns Cloud credentials, a private durable placement journal and protected worker ingress. Closing a Session requires committed results and an identity-checked durable drain proof before stopping the original sandbox, retaining the Volume and replaying the physical-stop receipt after a lost response. The new external worker profiles accept up to 64 request headers on both listeners to accommodate Cloud proxy forwarding headers while retaining the byte limit and application authentication. The previous external profiles keep their existing behavior and 32-header limit. Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2382bcce7d6bb40316b69251ccbc4470fa357359/docs/design/2026-10-28-e2b-managed-runtime.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2382bcce7d6bb40316b69251ccbc4470fa357359/docs/design/2026-10-28-e2b-managed-runtime.zh-CN.md). Both versions describe the same boundaries and acceptance requirements. ## Why it's needed Registered external storage currently has provisioning prerequisites but cannot provide the Hosted Workspace tools or qualify Session close. This connects remote execution to the existing Workspace authorization, tool, publication and retirement contracts so that a central Agent can use persistent remote files without treating an expired sandbox as a clean close. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify 1. With matching central/worker builds, a protected ingress and a real existing E2B Volume, register the external storage and publish its Workspace/OWNER grant through the operator listener. A Session selecting that Workspace should support Read/Write/Edit; tools mode should also support foreground Shell with output in the central publication store. 2. Confirm that unbound/local-storage Sessions, foreign owners, paths outside the Workspace, background Shell, PTY, Monitor, MCP, Hooks, child Workspaces and file rewind are refused. Rewind must fail before a pending undo is journaled. 3. Close after committed ACKs and released tool Sessions. The exact original sandbox must disappear, the Volume must remain, and published Shell artifacts must remain readable. Repeat a lost retire response and confirm that the saved proof and original physical-stop receipt replay without launching a replacement worker. 4. Replay provisioning with the same request and reject conflicting input. A lost create response without saved traffic credentials must remain UNKNOWN, with no second create or resume operation. Require the affected Java/SDK, MySQL, Hosted/fault and Cloud acceptance gates before marking this draft ready. The current increment passed the root build, typecheck and bundle, 72 focused worker tests, and 15 independent compiled-worker header-count, byte-limit and authentication boundary checks. The final 19-test publication subset was rerun after assertion cleanup, and the commit hook passed formatting and ESLint. A real macOS protocol client completed 80 protected HTTPS worker requests against Linux x64 in an existing AgentSandbox template, covering files, foreground Shell, replay, ACK and retirement proofs; the original sandbox was killed and confirmed absent. The Shell publication producer remained inside the sandbox. These scoped results do not qualify the complete Hosted deployment; see the separate E2E report for boundaries and retained failed attempts. ### Evidence (Before & After) N/A — no UI/TUI change. prs.title: fix(core): note failed servers on partial LSP diagnostics
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a diagnostics query fans out to several language servers and at least one returns diagnostics while another could not contribute, the LSP tool now keeps the retrieved diagnostics as a successful result. It then appends one trailing line to the model-facing text, in the form `Note: some LSP servers could not be queried (<server>: <reason>; <server> is in progress); this report is partial.` This applies to both single-file and workspace diagnostics. To carry that information, the two diagnostics queries on the LSP client interface now resolve to the retrieved items plus an optional bounded description of what is missing, instead of a bare list. The tool remains the only production consumer of that interface.

The note names exactly what the service already treats as vetoing a clean answer when nothing is retrieved: a failed or unusable pull from a server that could own the file, and a configured server that was never reached (for example, still starting). It leaves out a server that answered "method not found" (it never implemented pull diagnostics) and a server whose declared languages provably exclude the queried file. A workspace sweep that stops at its result limit does not name the ready servers it deliberately left unasked. The text is bounded the same way as the existing rejection: each cause is reduced to its last non-empty line and capped, and the whole list shares the same aggregate budget, so a stack-packed error or a long server list cannot flood the diagnostics. The tool's error field stays unset on this path; once it is set, the model receives only the error message and would lose the diagnostics that were retrieved. The design document for this contract is updated in both languages.

## Why it's needed

This is finding 1 of #13143. Before this change, the service already rejected a diagnostics query that retrieved nothing while a server had failed or was unreachable. But when at least one server answered, the other servers' failures and states were logged and dropped. The tool rendered a complete-looking list, so the model read a knowingly incomplete report as the full picture, for example believing a file has one warning when the server that owns its type errors had crashed or had not finished starting. Finding 2 of the same issue landed in #15946; this PR completes the issue.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Configure two servers for the same file type. Have one fail its diagnostics pull and the other return a warning, then run single-file diagnostics. The result lists the warning, ends with a note naming the failing server and its error, and is not reported as a tool error. Repeat with workspace diagnostics and expect the same trailing note.
- Leave the second server still starting instead of failing: the note names it as in progress.
- Give the failing server a multi-line, very long error: the note keeps only the last line of each cause and stays bounded.
- Replace the failing server with one that answers "method not found", or with one whose declared languages do not cover the queried file: the report lists the warning with no note.
- Unchanged behavior to spot-check: when nothing is retrieved while a relevant server failed or was unreachable, the query is still rejected with the existing "No LSP diagnostics could be retrieved" message, and a clean report from a healthy server still reads "No diagnostics found".

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (model-facing tool text, no TUI change). The existing partial-results test pins the complete tool output for both operations, including the note, and asserts that no error is set. New cases pin these behaviors:
- a still-starting server is named (both operations)
- a stack-packed cause is reduced to its last line and the note stays bounded (both operations)
- a "method not found" sibling produces no note (both operations), and neither does an irrelevant failing server
- a workspace sweep stopped at its limit names the server that is still starting but not the ready server it skipped

Against the unfixed production code, the partial-result cases fail on the missing note. The "method not found" and irrelevant-server cases pass there by design, because they guard against over-reporting. Each guard was also checked by mutation: dropping the note, letting "method not found" refusals in, removing the relevance filter, dropping unreached servers, dropping the last-line bound, and either mishandling of the limit case each turn the corresponding test red.

Locally: build and typecheck pass, the LSP service and tool suites pass (507/507), the CLI config suite passes, and ESLint and Prettier are clean on the changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit and integration tests only, Node 24.16.0 on macOS. No real language server was started.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the two diagnostics queries change their resolved shape on the public LSP client interface. Every consumer was checked and updated: the LSP tool, the client adapter, the manual end-to-end LSP script, and the CLI config test's service mock. The edit and write tools, the slash command, and the hot-reload path do not call these queries. Only the tool's text to the model changes. The user-facing display keeps the plain diagnostics list, so the user does not see the note, as the issue specified.
- Not validated / out of scope: a workspace report truncated at its result limit still does not say it was truncated. That gap predates this PR and is left for a follow-up. A server whose report was unusable (for example, every item failed normalization) is named in the note with that reason, the same way it vetoes an empty answer today. No real language-server end-to-end run; Windows and Linux were not run locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: any out-of-tree implementation or consumer of the LSP client interface must read the diagnostics from the new items field. There are no settings or schema changes. This touches the same diagnostics method tails as #12286 (all-failed guards, currently stale with changes requested); whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

Design document updated in both languages: [English](https://github.com/404khai/qwen-code/blob/fix/lsp-partial-diagnostics-note/docs/design/lsp-disk-document-sync.md) / [中文](https://github.com/404khai/qwen-code/blob/fix/lsp-partial-diagnostics-note/docs/design/lsp-disk-document-sync.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13143

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做什么

当一次诊断查询分发给多个语言服务器，且至少有一个返回了诊断、而另一个无法提供结果时，LSP 工具现在会把已取回的诊断作为成功结果保留，并在面向模型的文本末尾追加一行说明，格式为 `Note: some LSP servers could not be queried (<server>: <reason>; <server> is in progress); this report is partial.`。单文件诊断与工作区诊断都适用。为了传递这一信息，LSP 客户端接口上的两个诊断查询现在返回"已取回的条目"加上一段可选的、已限界的"缺失内容描述"，而不再是单纯的列表。该接口唯一的生产环境调用方仍是 LSP 工具。

说明中列出的，正是服务层在什么都没取回时本就会据以否决干净结果的情形：可能负责该文件的服务器的失败或不可用的拉取，以及从未被触达的已配置服务器（例如仍在启动）。回复 "method not found" 的服务器（它根本没有实现拉取诊断）不会被列出；声明的语言可证明不覆盖被查询文件的服务器也不会被列出。因达到结果上限而停止的工作区扫描，不会点名其有意未询问的就绪服务器。说明文本按与现有拒绝信息相同的方式限界：每个原因只保留最后一行非空内容并截断，整个列表共享同一总量预算，因此堆栈式的错误或很长的服务器列表都不会淹没诊断内容。这条路径上工具的 error 字段保持未设置：一旦设置，模型只会收到错误信息，从而丢失已经取回的诊断。描述该契约的设计文档已同步更新中英文两个版本。

## 为什么需要

这是 #13143 的第一项发现。修改前，服务层在"什么都没取回且有服务器失败或不可达"时已经会拒绝诊断查询；但只要至少有一个服务器作答，其他服务器的失败和状态就只会写入日志然后被丢弃。工具输出的列表看起来是完整的，于是模型会把一份明知不完整的报告当成全貌。例如负责某文件类型错误的服务器已经崩溃或尚未启动完成，模型却以为该文件只有一个警告。同一 issue 的第二项发现已在 #15946 中合入；本 PR 完成该 issue。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

- 为同一文件类型配置两个服务器，让其中一个的诊断拉取失败、另一个返回一条警告，然后执行单文件诊断：结果列出该警告，末尾附有一行说明，点名失败的服务器及其错误，且不会被报告为工具错误。对工作区诊断重复同样操作，应看到同样的结尾说明。
- 让第二个服务器保持启动中而不是失败：说明会将其点名为 in progress。
- 让失败的服务器返回多行且很长的错误：说明只保留每个原因的最后一行，并保持在限界之内。
- 把失败的服务器换成回复 "method not found" 的服务器，或换成声明的语言不覆盖被查询文件的服务器：报告列出该警告，没有说明行。
- 需要抽查的未变行为：什么都没取回而有相关服务器失败或不可达时，查询仍以原有的 "No LSP diagnostics could be retrieved" 信息被拒绝；健康服务器的干净报告仍显示为 "No diagnostics found"。

### 前后对比证据

不适用（面向模型的工具文本，无 TUI 变化）。原有的部分结果测试对两种操作的完整工具输出（包括说明行）做精确断言，并断言 error 未被设置。新增用例固定了以下行为：
- 仍在启动的服务器会被点名（两种操作）
- 堆栈式原因被缩减为最后一行且说明保持限界（两种操作）
- 存在 "method not found" 同伴时不出现说明（两种操作），存在不相关的失败服务器时同样不出现
- 因达到上限而停止的工作区扫描会点名仍在启动的服务器，但不会点名被跳过的就绪服务器

在未修复的生产代码上，部分结果用例会因缺少说明行而失败；"method not found" 与不相关服务器的用例在那里按设计会通过，因为它们防的是过度报告。每个防护还做了变异验证：去掉说明、让 "method not found" 拒绝进入说明、移除相关性过滤、去掉未触达的服务器、去掉最后一行的限界，以及对上限情形的两种错误处理，都会让对应测试变红。

本地结果：build 与 typecheck 通过，LSP 服务与工具测试套件通过（507/507），CLI 配置测试套件通过，改动文件的 ESLint 与 Prettier 检查无问题。

### 已验证平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境（可选）

仅单元与集成测试，macOS 上的 Node 24.16.0。未启动真实语言服务器。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：两个诊断查询在公开的 LSP 客户端接口上改变了返回结构。所有调用方都已核查并更新：LSP 工具、客户端适配器、手动运行的 LSP 端到端脚本、CLI 配置测试中的服务 mock。编辑与写入工具、斜杠命令以及热重载路径都不调用这些查询。只有工具发给模型的文本发生变化；面向用户的展示仍是原来的诊断列表，因此用户看不到该说明，这与 issue 的要求一致。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：按结果上限截断的工作区报告仍不会说明自己被截断。这是本 PR 之前就存在的问题，留待后续处理。报告不可用的服务器（例如所有条目都未通过规范化）会以该原因出现在说明中，这与它如今否决空结果的方式一致。未做真实语言服务器端到端运行；未在本地运行 Windows 与 Linux。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：仓库外任何实现或使用 LSP 客户端接口的代码，需要改为从新的 items 字段读取诊断。没有设置项或 schema 变更。本 PR 与 #12286（其他查询的全部失败保护，目前已停滞且被要求修改）触及相同的诊断方法末尾；后合入的一方需要做一次小的 rebase。

设计文档已同步更新中英文两个版本：[English](https://github.com/404khai/qwen-code/blob/fix/lsp-partial-diagnostics-note/docs/design/lsp-disk-document-sync.md) / [中文](https://github.com/404khai/qwen-code/blob/fix/lsp-partial-diagnostics-note/docs/design/lsp-disk-document-sync.zh-CN.md)。

prs.title: test(managed-agent): Reconnect Hosted fault probes to execution owners
prs.body:
## What this PR does Reconnects the Hosted fault probes to the components that now own transport calls. The cancellation probe observes dispatch and physical cancellation and restores both original references during cleanup. The lost-reply fixture holds result delivery at the execution owner so it can observe execution before settlement. New component regressions use the actual fixture installers and public Broker API to check observation, completion ordering and cleanup. ## Why it's needed After the execution workflows were extracted in #16029 and #16084, replacing the public service's transport field no longer updated the references captured by its collaborators. The cancellation probe therefore counted zero executions while a call was running, and the lost-status-reply case settled before its result gate opened. These stale fixture injection points caused the two failures observed in the full Hosted lane. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify 1. Start an execution with its result still pending. The cancellation probe must record one execution, then one cancellation while completion remains zero. Completing the physical result must produce settlement and one completion. After closing the probe, subsequent public execution/cancellation must work without changing the closed probe's counters. 2. Complete the underlying execution result while the lost-reply gate is closed. The Broker must still report EXECUTING; opening the gate must allow SETTLED. The selected Harness condition and original full-lane no-replay/physical-settlement assertions must remain intact. 3. In CI, rerun the existing cancellation and lost-Broker-reply Hosted/MySQL cases against the packaged CLI. The cancellation evidence endpoint must reach its intended physical-settlement cut, and the status-reply loss must occur only after observing an executing call. Local component verification passed both new regressions with 0 failures/errors/skips. Five unchanged Dispatcher regressions passed and their evidence was reused. Both Checkstyle goals have applicable successful evidence across the reactor. Two clean self-audits and independent read-only review found no actionable defect introduced by this change. The original two witnesses were reproduced before the fix using the old injection pattern. The two original Hosted/MySQL methods then passed locally with FG6a `status` and FG6d `running` selected: 2 tests, 0 failures/errors/skips, using the current packaged CLI, real Harness/worker processes and disposable MySQL 8.4.11. The cancellation ledger reported one execution, one completion and SETTLED; the status case dropped one reply with one model call and one start. Complete qualification remains pending in the [full SDK Java CI run](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/41382228709). ### Evidence (Before & After) N/A ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested (component and selected Hosted/MySQL checks) | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested | | 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ pending CI | ### Environment (optional) macOS 26.7.1 arm64, JDK 21.0.8, Maven 3.9.14, Node 26.12.1, a source-matching Java SDK and an isolated Maven repository. Component checks use real Broker logic and in-memory repositories with bounded transport/assembly doubles. The installed global Qwen CLI 0.24.1 rejects the required Hosted arguments, so the original Hosted checks used a successfully bundled current-source CLI and task-owned MySQL 8.4.11. Effective database settings were `max_allowed_packet=134217728`, native AIO off and binary logging off; macOS uses `lower_case_table_names=2`, unlike the Linux CI environment. The existing fixture uses a controlled loopback model; upstream-provider acceptance is outside this check. The preceding bounded CLI build timed out and is not counted as a successful build. All local setup, reproduction, builds, tests, retries and cleanup consumed 366.282 seconds of the shared 600-second budget. Task-owned processes and database files were cleaned up. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: A probe attached to the wrong owner cannot observe or block the intended call. The selected running cell's cold reload passed; this does not clear other previously recorded cold-recovery failures. Original CI evidence, the initial regression-fixture setup failure, dependency setup failures and the bounded build timeout remain preserved in the verification report. - Breaking changes / migration notes: None. All changes are in Java verification sources; production execution, protocols, SQL/schema, dependencies and CI selectors are unchanged. No migration is required. ## Linked Issues Fixes #16092. prs.title: feat(serve): allow configuring the Conversations working-directory root
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds `--conversations-dir` to `qwen serve` and `qwen daemon start`, with `QWEN_CONVERSATIONS_DIR` for launch environments and user-level `.env` files. Embedded launchers can use `ServeOptions.conversationsDir`. The explicit CLI/API value wins over the environment; omission preserves `~/Documents/Qwen Code/Conversations`.

The selection is fixed at daemon startup. Project environment files, top-level `settings.json` `env` at every scope, reloads, and session requests cannot redirect it. Explicit values must be nonempty, fully qualified absolute paths without NUL; invalid syntax fails before listening without fallback. Directory creation and filesystem acceptance remain lazy for both configured and default roots.

Standalone and Live retain their shared Conversations runtime and deterministic private session children. Current discovery records retain the selected root across `daemon restart`, including when the restarting shell's environment changes; older records continue resolving from environment/default. Automatic update relaunch also receives the pinned selection. Intentional reconfiguration uses stop followed by start with the new value.

This PR requests maintainer review of naming and semantics; automated triage is not approval. Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/135847076ff06dce326a3d4e92fc89f3377f1672/docs/design/conversations-working-directory-root.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/135847076ff06dce326a3d4e92fc89f3377f1672/docs/design/conversations-working-directory-root.zh-CN.md).

## Why it's needed

Containers can place working files on persistent volumes independently of OS home. Mounting the default path or changing home remain valid alternatives. `QWEN_HOME` selects global Qwen configuration, while `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` and `advanced.runtimeOutputDir` select runtime storage; neither selects this working root.

Working files and shared root configuration stay under the selected Conversations tree. Transcripts and sidecars remain in runtime-base storage keyed by canonical Conversations cwd. Deletion journals and stable Live discovery retain their home-based locations. Persisting only one storage category does not preserve the others.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start without an override and check health: the unused default root should remain absent. Select a custom root through the environment, then provide a different CLI root: the explicit option should win. Empty, relative, and unexpanded-tilde values should fail before listening.
2. Supply a user-level `.env` root and competing project `.env`/`settings.env` values. Create a standalone session and confirm its actual shell cwd and written file are in the selected private child. Registering that root or child should remain rejected; an unrelated workspace should still register.
3. Restart with the same home, runtime base, and canonical root; list/load the session and read the original file. Separately use `daemon start` and `daemon restart` with a changed ambient root and confirm the recorded selection wins.

Validation passed: **520 focused tests**, **107 CI-wiring metatests**, **8 Linux process E2E cases**, repository build, typecheck, bundle, startup bundle closure checks, and lint. The process suite is selected by the no-AK integration CI gate. **Full `npm run preflight` did not pass.** Clean installation, repository-wide formatting/lint, build, and typecheck completed. The unchanged Browser Use missing-runtime test failed because ambient `NODE_PATH` supplied a global `playwright-core` after the fixture deleted its staged dependency. The same isolated case passed with `NODE_PATH` unset, without changing source or assertions. After diagnosing that failure, the remaining workspace test run was stopped; this preflight invocation did not reach its subsequent script-test and final bundle-closure stages. The 107 CI-wiring tests and the earlier bundle-closure check passed separately.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the unmodified source launcher rejected the new flag; isolated helper checks confirmed that the environment variable was ignored and the existing default remained lazy. No installed global `qwen` was available, and the baseline did not exercise a usable daemon or recovery.

After: the fresh bundle passed all eight process cases: ACP shell cwd/files, same-root history restoration, project-injection rejection, and discovery-backed restart preservation. No real model request was made. Screenshots are N/A: this changes headless deployment configuration, with command/API evidence. See the [separate E2E report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16105#issuecomment-6568615171).

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ Focused tests and process E2E |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node.js 24.19.0, bundle, isolated temporary home/config/runtime/work directories, loopback synthetic credentials.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: changing the canonical root changes history discovery/storage namespace and shared root configuration. Existing ownership, permissions, identity, direct-child, link/reparse, writer-lease, ordinary-workspace isolation, and recovery checks remain in force, with their existing platform limits.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS/Windows runtime behavior, Live voice, pending-deletion-journal recovery, and actual automatic-update relaunch were not exercised end to end. Update handoff has unit coverage; the prior focused verification did not run complete shared-runtime/recovery suites. No browser/per-session selector, global workspace policy, configurable locks, or migration is added.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: default placement is unchanged. No working files, history, shared configuration, or control state migrate automatically. Resolve pending recovery against the original root and stop all its writers before switching; changing roots does not repair recovery failures or guarantee old-history visibility.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15298.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

为 `qwen serve` 和 `qwen daemon start` 增加 `--conversations-dir`，并支持启动环境和用户级 `.env` 文件中的 `QWEN_CONVERSATIONS_DIR`。嵌入启动方可以使用 `ServeOptions.conversationsDir`。显式 CLI/API 值优先于环境变量；都未配置时保留 `~/Documents/Qwen Code/Conversations`。

目录选择在 daemon 启动时固定。项目环境文件、所有作用域的顶层 `settings.json` `env`、重载及会话请求都不能重定向它。显式值必须是非空、不含 NUL 的完全限定绝对路径；无效语法会在监听前失败，不回退到其他位置。配置路径和默认路径的目录创建及文件系统接受都保持惰性。

Standalone 和 Live 保留共享的 Conversations runtime 及确定性的会话私有子目录。当前发现记录使 `daemon restart` 保留选定根目录，即使发起重启的 shell 环境已经变化；旧记录仍按环境变量/默认值重新解析。自动更新重启同样接收固定的目录选择。有意重新配置时，先 stop，再使用新值 start。

此 PR 请求维护者审阅名称和语义；自动 triage 不代表批准。设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/135847076ff06dce326a3d4e92fc89f3377f1672/docs/design/conversations-working-directory-root.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/135847076ff06dce326a3d4e92fc89f3377f1672/docs/design/conversations-working-directory-root.zh-CN.md)。

## 为什么需要

容器可以将工作文件放在独立于操作系统 home 的持久卷上。在默认路径挂卷或调整 home 仍然是有效替代方案。`QWEN_HOME` 选择全局 Qwen 配置目录，`QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` 和 `advanced.runtimeOutputDir` 选择运行时存储；它们都不选择此工作根目录。

工作文件和共享根配置保留在选定的 Conversations 目录树下。Transcript 和 sidecar 仍位于按规范 Conversations cwd 定位的 runtime-base 存储中。删除 journal 和稳定 Live 发现状态保留基于 home 的位置。只持久化其中一类存储并不能保存其他类别。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 不提供覆盖配置并启动，检查 health：未使用的默认根目录应仍不存在。通过环境变量选择自定义根目录，再提供另一个 CLI 根目录：显式参数应优先。空值、相对路径和未展开的波浪号路径应在监听前失败。
2. 在用户级 `.env` 中配置根目录，并在项目 `.env`/`settings.env` 中提供冲突值。创建 standalone 会话，确认实际 shell cwd 和写入文件位于选定的私有子目录。注册该根目录或子目录仍应被拒绝；无关普通工作区仍应能注册。
3. 使用同一 home、runtime base 和规范根目录重启；列出/加载会话并读取原文件。另外通过 `daemon start` 和 `daemon restart` 验证：即使环境中的根目录改变，记录中的选择仍然优先。

验证已通过：**520 项定向测试**、**107 项 CI 配置元测试**、**8 项 Linux 进程级 E2E 用例**、仓库 build、typecheck、bundle、启动 bundle 依赖闭包检查及 lint。进程测试套件已纳入 no-AK 集成 CI。**完整 `npm run preflight` 未通过。** 已完成干净安装、全仓格式/lint、构建和类型检查。未改动的 Browser Use 缺失运行时测试失败，原因是继承的 `NODE_PATH` 在 fixture 删除临时依赖后仍提供了全局 `playwright-core`。仅对该进程移除 `NODE_PATH` 后，同一单独用例通过，没有修改源码或断言。确认原因后停止了剩余工作区测试；本次 preflight 未到达后续脚本测试及最终 bundle 依赖闭包阶段。107 项 CI 配置测试和此前的 bundle 依赖闭包检查分别通过。

### 证据（改动前后）

改动前：未修改源码的启动入口拒绝新参数；隔离的 helper 检查确认该环境变量被忽略，原默认路径保持惰性。环境中没有已安装的全局 `qwen`，基线也未验证可用 daemon 或恢复行为。

改动后：新构建的 bundle 通过全部八项进程用例：ACP shell cwd/文件、同根目录历史恢复、项目注入拒绝，以及基于发现记录的重启保留。未发送真实模型请求。截图不适用：本改动调整无界面的部署配置，证据来自命令/API。详见[独立 E2E 报告](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16105#issuecomment-6568615171)。

### 已测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ 定向测试及进程级 E2E |

### 环境（可选）

Linux、Node.js 24.19.0、bundle、隔离的临时 home/config/runtime/工作目录、回环地址上的合成凭据。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：改变规范根目录会改变历史发现/存储命名空间及共享根配置。现有所有权、权限、身份、直接子目录、link/reparse、writer lease、普通工作区隔离及恢复检查继续生效，并保留现有平台限制。

- 兼容与迁移说明：默认存储位置不变。不自动迁移工作文件、历史、共享配置或控制状态。切换前应在原根目录完成未结束的恢复并停止所有使用它的 writer；改变根目录不能修复恢复失败，也不保证旧历史继续可见。

## 关联 Issue

关联 #15298。

prs.title: fix(serve): keep gated MCP approvals across session cd within the same config source
prs.body:
> **Draft:** this implements one of the options raised in #16058, and the contract is not settled yet. Opening it early so the shape of the fix can be reviewed together with that question — please treat the direction as pending your call.

## What this PR does

When a session changes its working directory, an already-approved gated MCP server keeps that decision if the new directory resolves the server's configuration file to the same real path and the stored decision still matches the server configuration hash. The change only carries an existing decision; it never creates one. A different configuration file, a configuration edited after the decision, a server that was never decided, and a server that exists only in the new directory all stay behind the existing approval gate, and a carried rejection stays a rejection instead of being cleared.

A design note accompanies this change and records the contract, the security properties it preserves, and the alternatives still open in #16058.

## Why it's needed

A session that follows the documented flow — load, cd into its own working directory, then prompt — silently loses the workspace's approved MCP servers. The session reports the server as disconnected with a pending approval, and after a daemon restart the server is not connected at all, because the approval record is keyed by the working directory that the cd just changed. Reproducing this needs no source changes and no model calls: an approved server disappears as soon as the session moves into a child directory whose `.qwen` is a symlink back to the same configuration.

The loss predates #15323 and reproduces on the primary workspace in 0.26.1, so it is not a regression from that change; #15323 made the path reachable for sessions owned by dynamically registered workspaces, which previously could not cd at all. #16058 records the reproduction, the version matrix, and the alternative contracts (bind approvals to the configuration source everywhere, add a session/cwd approval endpoint, or pin the configuration root).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused unit tests:

```bash
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/mcp-approval-carry.test.ts
```

For an end-to-end check, use the reproduction from #16058 against a daemon built from this branch: approve a gated MCP server for a workspace, create a session there, cd into a child directory whose `.qwen` symlinks the workspace configuration, and read the session's resources. Expected after this change: the server is still approved and connected, immediately after the cd and after a workspace reload with `forceReconnectAll`.

Then repeat the same run with a child directory that carries its own copy of the settings file instead of a symlink. Expected: the server is still pending, because the configuration source changed even though its content did not. That distinction is the whole point of the change and is worth checking directly.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Official 0.26.5, same source through a symlink — server lost at cd:

```
{"stage":"before cd","cwd":"<root>/agent","mcpStatus":"connected","approvalState":null}
{"stage":"after cd","cwd":"<root>/agent/sessions/A","mcpStatus":"disconnected","approvalState":"pending"}
{"stage":"after reload","cwd":"<root>/agent/sessions/A","mcpStatus":"disconnected","approvalState":"pending"}
```

This branch, same source through a symlink — decision carried:

```
{"stage":"before cd","cwd":"<root>/agent","mcpStatus":"connected","approvalState":null}
{"stage":"after cd","cwd":"<root>/agent/sessions/A","mcpStatus":"connected","approvalState":null}
{"stage":"after reload","cwd":"<root>/agent/sessions/A","mcpStatus":"connected","approvalState":null}
```

This branch, identical content in a different file — still gated:

```
{"stage":"before cd","cwd":"<root>/agent","mcpStatus":"connected","approvalState":null}
{"stage":"after cd","cwd":"<root>/agent/sessions/A","mcpStatus":"disconnected","approvalState":"pending"}
{"stage":"after reload","cwd":"<root>/agent/sessions/A","mcpStatus":"disconnected","approvalState":"pending"}
```

Also run locally: the focused unit tests pass, the agent unit suite passes in full, the existing session-cd integration test passes on a rebuilt bundle, and build, typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

prs.title: feat(web-shell): make GitHub channel configuration usable
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Configuring a GitHub Channel from the Web Shell now reads like a GitHub form rather than a generic key/value dialog. The editor picks notification reasons from a checklist whose entries explain themselves, requires a token or an explicit local gh login and keeps the two from silently competing, names allowlisted groups as repositories and validates the `owner/repo` shape, and separates credentials from connection settings and notification routing.

Repository allowlists are also matched the way GitHub means them. A repository path is case-insensitive, but the runtime looked the group up verbatim, so an allowlist typed as `qwenlm/qwen-code` connected and then dropped every notification. The editor now stores the canonical lower-case key, and the GitHub adapter matches configured repositories case-insensitively — for admission and for that repository's sender policy alike. Every other platform keeps matching group IDs verbatim.

It also stops writing a setting that never had an effect. Every manageable Channel receives a direct-message policy from the shared registry, and the editor dutifully persisted that default for GitHub — a platform whose adapter only ever produces group traffic. Editing a GitHub Channel no longer shows that policy, and the next save removes the value it left behind.

## Why it's needed

The GitHub Channel has the most fields of any platform and the least room for error: a notification filter taken from a closed vocabulary of fifteen values, a repository allowlist written as `owner/repo`, and two mutually exclusive ways to authenticate. All of it was rendered as plain text boxes with a paragraph of prose above them, so an operator had to memorise spellings, could only learn a value was wrong after pressing Save, and could tick "use local gh" while a stored token quietly kept winning.

Two of the fields also lied about the platform. The direct-message policy appeared on a Channel that never receives a direct message, and its "pairing" default was saved into `settings.json`, which made the pairing panel appear for an access path GitHub does not have. The group allowlist was labelled in chat terms while the adapter keys it by repository full name, so following the placeholder guaranteed a Channel that connects and then never admits anything.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open Settings → Channels → Configure GitHub. Confirm the form is grouped as Identity, Credentials, Connection, Notifications and routing, Access control; that Credentials holds only the token and the local gh switch while the API base URL and the reason filter sit in their own groups; and that the base URL shows a GitHub Enterprise example.

The reason filter is a checklist of fifteen entries, each spelling out when GitHub produces that reason. Tick two of them, save, and the stored configuration contains exactly those two in declaration order; untick everything and the key disappears, which the adapter reads as "process every reason".

Switch on local GitHub CLI authentication. The token field becomes unavailable and says the stored token is removed on save; save, and a previously stored token is gone, so the switch is the thing that takes effect. Fill in a repository allowlist with a bare name such as `qwen-code` and save — the form refuses it and asks for `owner/repo`; `QwenLM/qwen-code` is accepted and stored as `qwenlm/qwen-code`. Notifications for that repository are admitted whatever case GitHub reports, and the repository's own sender allowlist still applies rather than falling back to the open default.

Nothing about the direct-message policy should appear for this platform, and saving should leave no such key in the stored configuration, including on a Channel created by an older build that already had one written into it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

These are captures from the repository's own visual harness: the real Web Shell rendered in Chromium at the harness viewport (1280×800), in both themes, with the daemon's HTTP layer mocked by `page.route`. The mocked daemon means the pictures prove rendering and interaction, not backend behaviour; what gets stored is covered by the unit tests further down. Before each capture the scenario asserts that the reason checklist exists with four entries, so a regression that falls back to a text box fails the test instead of quietly re-publishing the old picture. The captures were re-run at the current head after the review fixes and are byte-identical to the published files, so they still depict this branch.

**GitHub Channel editor — dark**

| Before | After |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![GitHub channel editor before: reason filter as a text box, base URL and filter under Credentials, allowed group IDs with a group-a placeholder, and a Direct message policy section](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/raw/assets-pr16096/pr16096/01-editor-before-dark.png) | ![GitHub channel editor after: reason checklist with explanations, separate Connection and Notifications and routing groups, and no direct-message policy](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/raw/assets-pr16096/pr16096/02-editor-after-dark.png) |

**GitHub Channel editor — light**

| Before | After |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![GitHub channel editor before, light theme](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/raw/assets-pr16096/pr16096/03-editor-before-light.png) | ![GitHub channel editor after, light theme](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/raw/assets-pr16096/pr16096/04-editor-after-light.png) |

**Pressing Save with no credential — dark**

| Before | After |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![Pressing Save with no credential before the change, dark theme](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/raw/assets-pr16096/pr16096/05-credential-error-before-dark.png) | ![Pressing Save with no credential after the change, dark theme](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/raw/assets-pr16096/pr16096/06-credential-error-after-dark.png) |

What the comparison shows:

- The reason filter is a checklist whose fifteen entries each explain when GitHub produces that reason; before, it was one text box above a sentence listing the same values.
- The API base URL and the reason filter moved out of "Credentials" into "Connection" and "Notifications and routing", and the base URL now shows a GitHub Enterprise example.
- The allowlist reads "Allowed repositories" with an `owner/repo` placeholder instead of "Allowed group IDs" with `group-a, group-b`, and a bare name is rejected before saving.
- The direct-message policy is gone from a Channel that only ever receives repository traffic.

Verification commands run locally:

```text
$ cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/channels client/i18n.test.ts
Test Files  6 passed (6)
     Tests  170 passed (170)

$ cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
Test Files  25 passed (25)
     Tests  1655 passed (1655)

$ cd packages/channels/github && npx vitest run
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  216 passed (216)

$ npx eslint <changed files>            # no output
$ npx prettier --check <changed paths>  # All matched files use Prettier code style!
$ npm run build --workspace=@qwen-code/channel-base    # tsc --build, clean
$ npm run build --workspace=@qwen-code/channel-github  # tsc --build, clean

$ npx playwright test --config playwright.visuals.config.ts -g "GitHub channel editor"
  2 passed
```

Every behavioural claim is pinned by a mutation that was introduced and then reverted. For the editor: dropping the repository-scoped skip for private-access fields, making the checklist write an empty value, removing the token lock, comparing reasons case-sensitively, deleting the pairing guard, deleting the group-pairing branch, keeping the `allowedUsers` residue, and showing the private allowlist in the pairing panel. For the repository casing, on both sides as the review asked: the adapter stops normalizing, the editor stops writing canonical keys, `ChannelBase.groupConfigFor` stops normalizing, and the `GroupGate` allowlist lookup stops normalizing. Each mutation failed exactly the cases that describe it and nothing else.

### Tested on

|     OS     |  Status   |
| :--------: | :-------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |    ✅     |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, vitest with jsdom for the component tests. The host image cannot run a browser — its Chromium build fails to load `libatk-1.0.so.0`, the library is absent, and `sudo` needs a password — so the visual captures were produced inside a Playwright container image (Playwright 1.61.1, Chromium build 1228, Node 22) with this worktree mounted, writing the PNGs back to the host. Only the GitHub editor scenario was run, not the whole visual suite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the editor now deletes the stored private-access set (`privatePolicy` and `allowedUsers`) from repository-scoped Channels on save, and drops a stored token when local gh authentication is already selected. These values are dead weight for this platform — group traffic never reads them, and the token would otherwise defeat the visible authentication choice — but the removal is silent apart from the field copy that states it. Repository allowlists are also rewritten to lower case, which is what makes them match at runtime.
- Cross-package scope: the fix touches the shared channel base (an optional group-ID normalizer, defaulting to today's verbatim matching) and the GitHub adapter. No other platform's behaviour changes, and a base test pins that group IDs still match verbatim without a normalizer.
- Not validated / out of scope: no end-to-end Channel run against GitHub, and only the GitHub editor scenario of the visual suite was executed. Per-repository `requireMention`, the poll interval, and per-repository sender allowlists remain editable only through `settings.json`. The plugin still declares `Open` as the default group policy while the runtime and the user documentation treat an absent policy as `Disabled`; that default is unchanged here and is worth a separate decision, since a Channel created from the Web Shell on a public repository starts out permissive.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The stored configuration stays valid; the only change is that a value the adapter ignores is no longer written.

## Linked Issues

No linked issue.

prs.title: fix(core): surface Anthropic refusal details
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR reads Anthropic refusal metadata from both streaming and non-streaming responses and carries it through the existing finish event as a category-specific user-facing message. The Ink and OpenTUI renderers prefer that message over the generic SAFETY notice while preserving the existing fatal SAFETY semantics.

The pinned Anthropic SDK does not expose `stop_details` in its TypeScript response types, so the new code reads the field defensively without changing the SDK pin or relying on provider-authored free text.

## Why it's needed

Anthropic can return HTTP 200 with an empty or partial response and `stop_reason: refusal`. The existing mapping already turns that into SAFETY, but the provider's refusal category was dropped, leaving the user with only the generic safety message. This closes the remaining actionable part of finding 5 in #9005 and gives users a concrete reason such as cyber policy, biological policy, frontier-model policy, hidden-reasoning extraction, or general harms.

Interleaved-thinking beta gating, SDK upgrades, `recommended_model` routing, and a full refusal recovery protocol remain out of scope.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that a streamed Anthropic `message_delta` with `stop_reason: refusal` and `stop_details.category: cyber` produces a SAFETY finish carrying `Response refused due to cyber-related safety policy.` and that the same field is produced by the non-streaming converter.

Confirm that a deferred finish chunk after a tool result retains the same `finishMessage`, and that both terminal renderers prefer it over the generic SAFETY text.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: a refusal produced `Response stopped due to safety reasons.` in the terminal UI.

After: the same refusal shows the stable category-specific message listed above. No local tests, build, typecheck, lint, or live UI run was performed under the task's speed constraints; focused regression tests were added in this PR for the parser, converter, deferred finish path, event propagation, and both renderers.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A. No local check was run. CI is the authoritative validation path for this PR.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the refusal copy is intentionally stable and category-specific rather than forwarding Anthropic's `explanation`, which the provider documents as unstable.
- Not validated / out of scope: no local tests or live provider request; `recommended_model`, automatic recovery, SDK updates, interleaved-thinking gating, and issue #9006 remain out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `finishMessage` is optional and existing finish-reason handling is unchanged when it is absent.

## Linked Issues

Related to #9005. This advances the remaining actionable `stop_details` gap without claiming the whole issue is complete.

## 本 PR 做了什么

当前锁定的 Anthropic SDK 类型没有暴露 `stop_details`，因此新增代码采用防御式读取，不改 SDK pin，也不依赖供应商生成的不稳定自由文本。

## 为什么需要

Anthropic 可能返回 HTTP 200，同时给出空响应或部分响应并设置 `stop_reason: refusal`。现有映射已经将其转换为 SAFETY，但供应商的拒绝分类被丢弃，用户只能看到通用安全提示。本 PR 补齐 #9005 中 finding 5 剩余可执行的部分，让用户看到 cyber、bio、frontier model、hidden reasoning extraction 或 general harms 等具体原因。

interleaved-thinking beta gating、SDK 升级、`recommended_model` 路由和完整 refusal 恢复协议不在本 PR 范围内。

## Reviewer Test Plan

修改前：refusal 在终端显示 `Response stopped due to safety reasons.`。

修改后：同一 refusal 显示上述稳定的分类提示。按照本次任务的速度约束，没有运行本地测试、构建、typecheck、lint 或实时 UI；本 PR 增加了覆盖解析器、转换器、延迟 finish 路径、事件透传和两个渲染器的定向回归测试。

prs.title: fix(desktop): stop the bundled runtime from the Windows installer
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an installer-side fallback for the one Windows update that is still driven by a desktop build released before the app-side runtime stop. The NSIS pre-install hook terminates processes whose executable path is inside the installed bundled Node directory, waits boundedly until `node.exe` is writable, and aborts before the copy stage unless the helper returns an explicit success. The desktop release gate pins the hook, path-based matching, bounded unlock wait, and fail-closed behavior.

## Why it's needed

A pre-fix desktop binary registers no updater exit hook, and its bundled daemon can keep `runtime\qwen-code\node\node.exe` mapped while NSIS replaces the runtime. That leaves the Retry / Abort / Ignore dialog with no recovery path. The installer performing the transition update is already the new one, so it can clear the lock itself. Matching by image path avoids killing unrelated `node.exe` processes; a `qwen` session started from this installation uses the same image and is stopped because the copy cannot proceed while it holds the lock.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Review the pre-install hook ordering in the NSIS migration file and the corresponding release-gate assertion. The hook must run before the Tauri copy stage, enumerate processes by executable path under `$INSTDIR\runtime\qwen-code\node\`, stop matching processes, poll for the image to become writable, and continue only when the helper returns `0`. A surviving lock or helper launch failure must abort before any files are replaced.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — Windows installer behavior; this change has no interactive product surface to capture on macOS or Linux.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Static source and release-gate review only. Per the execution request for this task, no local tests, builds, formatting, or type checks were run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: An interactive `qwen` session launched from the installed runtime is also stopped because it holds the same image. Preserving the lock would make the transition install fail; the abort message tells the user to close Qwen Code and retry.
- Not validated / out of scope: Real NSIS execution against a pre-fix desktop build was not run here. That end-to-end confirmation still needs a Windows host with the affected release installed.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: This removes the requirement to fully quit the app before the one update that installs the app-side fix. Later updates continue to use the app-side runtime stop.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15933

prs.title: feat(desktop): build and publish rpm installers
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds Fedora 44 and RHEL 10 x64 RPM builds to the Desktop release workflow, publishes those RPMs alongside the existing installers, and extends the Linux installer smoke suite to verify the distribution-owned WebKitGTK dependency, the root glibc contract, and the packaged runtime.

The build matrix now carries an explicit per-leg glibc floor and artifact suffix. AppImage and deb continue to build directly on the pinned Ubuntu 22.04 runners; the two RPM roots use digest-pinned Fedora 44 and CentOS Stream 10 containers, with EPEL enabled and SHA256-verified on the RHEL 10 leg. Each RPM gets a root-specific filename before upload so the two roots cannot overwrite each other.

## Why it's needed

Fedora and RHEL users currently receive only an AppImage, which does not run on those distributions without manually supplying libraries that the package does not declare. This adds native RPMs for the two supported roots while preserving the existing AppImage and deb release contract. RHEL 9 remains excluded because it provides only WebKitGTK 4.0, not the 4.1 API Tauri requires.

This work does not fix the AppImage dependency-closure problem tracked by #16030.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the Desktop release workflow in dry-run mode and confirm that five Linux build legs complete: x64 AppImage/deb, arm64 AppImage/deb, Fedora 44 RPM, and RHEL 10 RPM. The RPM legs should produce artifacts ending in `linux-x64-rpm-fedora44.rpm` and `linux-x64-rpm-rhel10.rpm`.

For each RPM, confirm that `rpm -qp --requires` names `libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0`, `rpm -qpl` does not contain a bundled WebKitGTK library, the architecture is not `noarch`, and the strongest glibc requirement is no newer than the matrix floor for that root. Confirm the RPM installer smoke test extracts and runs the bundled Node.js and ripgrep payload.

On a fresh artifact build, confirm the OSS mirror rejects the release if either root-specific RPM is missing. Re-mirroring an older release should remain tolerant because releases before this change have no RPM assets.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, the Linux artifact allowlist and collection step omitted RPM files and the smoke script required only AppImage and deb. After, the workflow has two root-specific RPM legs, unique artifact and cache names, and strict RPM dependency and runtime checks.

No installer artifact was produced in this run, so there is no local Before/After artifact evidence. The release dry run is the first end-to-end validation of both container roots.

### Tested on

|     OS     |                         Status                         |
| :--------: | :----------------------------------------------------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested; workflow syntax reviewed only            |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested; workflow syntax reviewed only            |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not built locally; workflow and script syntax checked |

### Environment (optional)

Static checks run: `actionlint .github/workflows/desktop-release.yml .github/workflows/sync-desktop-to-oss.yml`, `node --check packages/desktop/scripts/smoke-linux-installers.js`, `node --check packages/desktop/scripts/test-release.js`, and `git diff --check`.

No repository test suite, build, typecheck, npm lint, or dependency installation was run. The Fedora and RHEL container builds were not executed locally. RHEL 10 was not independently built locally; its first build validation will be the release workflow.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the two RPM roots add release time and make distribution package availability part of the release path. The container images are digest-pinned and the EPEL bootstrap RPM is SHA256-verified to reduce supply-chain drift.
- Not validated / out of scope: no local RPM build, no RHEL 10 build, no GPG repository signing or Copr setup, no RPM updater-feed entry, and no RHEL 9 RPM. RPM updates are expected to come from the package manager. The AppImage issue in #16030 remains out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for existing macOS, Windows, AppImage, deb, or updater consumers. RPM assets are additive and named per root.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16034

Related: #16030

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

### 证据（修改前与修改后）

修改前，Linux 产物白名单和收集步骤都不包含 RPM，冒烟脚本也只要求 AppImage 和 deb。修改后，工作流包含两个按构建根区分的 RPM 任务、唯一的产物与缓存名称，以及严格的 RPM 依赖和运行时检查。

本次运行没有生成安装包产物，因此没有本地的修改前后产物证据。发布 dry run 将是两个容器构建根的首次端到端验证。

### 测试环境

|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试；仅审查工作流语法            |

### 环境（可选）

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：两个 RPM 构建根会增加发布时间，并把发行版软件包可用性纳入发布路径。容器镜像按 digest 固定，EPEL 引导 RPM 经过 SHA256 校验，以降低供应链漂移。
