prs.title: fix(permissions): report malformed rules instead of dropping them silently
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A permission rule whose parentheses do not balance is parsed as inert: it matches nothing. On the current base (#15794) such a rule already produces one generic warning, but that line cannot say which list owns it — the same malformed rule in `allow` and `deny` prints two identical lines — it repeats for every manager the hosted path builds, and `/permissions` still filters the rule out, so it cannot be seen or deleted there. This PR makes the drop visible: the permission manager warns on the console, naming the list, the raw rule and the consequence, using the same operator-facing breadcrumb `tools.eager` already prints from the same initializer; and `/permissions` keeps the unparsable rule in the listing, marked `(unparsable)`, so it can be seen and deleted instead of being filtered out. Matching semantics are unchanged — a malformed rule still matches nothing, so no allow/deny decision moves.

## Why it's needed

The asymmetry is what makes this a security problem rather than a logging nit: a malformed allow rule fails closed (nothing gets auto-approved), but a malformed deny/ask rule fails open — the restriction the operator wrote does not exist, and neither startup output nor `/permissions` mentioned it. The operator's mental model is "docker is blocked"; the runtime's behaviour is "no such rule". Turning silent fail-open into visible fail-open is the minimal, semantics-preserving step the issue asks for first: the operator still has to fix the configuration, but now they know there is something to fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Write a malformed deny rule into a settings file:

```json
{ "permissions": { "deny": ["Bash(docker *"] } }
```

Start the CLI. Before any prompt, stderr shows:

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (no closing parenthesis at the end): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; write it as "Tool(specifier)" so it ends at the closing ")" of the specifier.
```

Open `/permissions`, switch to the Deny tab: the rule is listed as `(unparsable) Bash(docker *`. Select it and delete it — the row disappears and stays gone on the next open. Then fix the rule to `Bash(docker *)` and restart: no warning, no marker, and a denied command prompts as before.

Focused suites:

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/permissions
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.tsx src/i18n
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: starting with `deny: ["Bash(docker *"]` printed a generic line with no list name — `[permissions] ignoring malformed rule (unbalanced parentheses): Bash(docker *` — emitted by `packages/core/src/permissions/permission-rules.ts`, once per manager the hosted path builds; and `/permissions` simply did not list the rule.

After, from the built CLI with that settings file:

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (no closing parenthesis at the end): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; write it as "Tool(specifier)" so it ends at the closing ")" of the specifier.
```

With the corrected rule `Bash(docker *)` the same run prints no warning — the negative control.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

macOS: Node 22.23.4, `npm run build`, all focused suites green, plus the headless run quoted above. Linux: Docker `node:22-bookworm`, same suites green, and `tsc --noEmit` clean for both packages. Windows was not run.

### Environment (optional)

Focused unit suites and a headless `dist/index.js` run with a temporary `HOME`; the Linux pass used a Docker volume workspace because a bind-mounted tree trips `rimraf` with `ENOTEMPTY`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a configuration that keeps a malformed rule now prints one line per bad rule from the permission manager at startup (the pre-existing `permission-rules.ts` line can still fire for the same configuration, so a single run may show both shapes), and `/permissions` shows an extra row. No permission decision changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the issue's other two asks — failing closed (rejecting a malformed deny/ask at load, or denying the tool it names) and the analogous `tools.disabled` typo check — are deliberately left out. The first changes runtime matching semantics, the second is a separate registry check; both fit a follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `parseRules` no longer writes to the debug log; reporting moved into the permission manager, its only caller.
- Coordination: #15775 implements the same fix for the same issue, so only one of the two can land; whoever merges second will conflict on the dialog, data and parser files.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15752 (closed by #15794, which landed the generic warning). The deferred shapes — `Bash(rm -rf /))`, `Bash)` and the `tools.disabled` typo check — are tracked in #16078.

prs.title: fix(vscode): keep sibling model settings when writing provider config
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Configuring a Coding Plan or a model provider from the VS Code companion rewrote the entire `settings.model` object with only `name`, silently deleting everything else the CLI keeps there. This change writes `name` and its paired `baseUrl` key by key through the writer's existing nested-object helper, so the rest of the model section survives.

## Why it's needed

`model` carries 23 settings — reasoning effort, session turn and wall-time caps, goal budgets, loop protection, logging flags, generation config. A user who tuned any of them through the CLI and then signed in or edited providers in the panel lost all of them without warning. Losing `baseUrl` is the sharpest case: it is the disambiguator when several providers share a model id, so the next launch can resolve to the wrong provider.

The paired `baseUrl` is written, not merely preserved. The model resolver documents an invariant that every writer of `model.name` also writes `model.baseUrl` in the same scope — a real URL, or an empty-string tombstone when there is none — because an omitted key cannot override a stale value from a lower-priority scope on merge. The old wholesale replacement satisfied that by accident (it deleted the stale value too); a key-only fix would have kept the previous provider's URL and used it as the disambiguator for the new model. Both call sites already have the URL at hand: the Coding Plan template entry, or the provider map entry with the same fallback the sibling provider entry uses.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start from a settings file whose `model` is `{ name, baseUrl, reasoningEffort, maxSessionTurns }`, then configure a Coding Plan and then an api-key provider from the panel. Expected: only `name` and `baseUrl` change; `reasoningEffort` and `maxSessionTurns` are still present, and `baseUrl` matches the provider entry just written. Before the fix, `model` is reduced to `{ name }`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for screenshots — settings-file behavior is covered by unit tests. The new cases `preserves sibling model settings when writing a Coding Plan` and `preserves sibling model settings when writing api-key providers` fail on the pre-fix code (sibling keys dropped) and pass after; the existing api-key assertion was updated to expect the paired `baseUrl`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Linux was verified in a `node:22-bookworm` container: full companion suite, 46 files / 663 passed / 1 skipped.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only: `npx vitest run` in the companion package, plus Docker for the Linux run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk: the panel now writes `model.baseUrl` where it previously wrote nothing. When the active model is missing from the provider map the value falls back to the same default the provider entry receives, so the pair stays consistent.
- Not validated / out of scope: VS Code panel end-to-end and Windows.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; the change only stops deleting existing keys.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15822

## 为什么需要

`model` 下有 23 项设置：reasoningEffort、会话轮次与墙钟上限、goal 预算、循环保护、日志开关、generationConfig 等。用户用 CLI 调好这些之后，只要在面板里登录或改一次 provider，就会在无提示的情况下全部丢失。`baseUrl` 是最尖锐的一例：同名模型来自多个 provider 时，它是消歧符，丢了之后下次启动可能解析到错误的 provider。

配对的 `baseUrl` 是「写入」而不只是「保留」。模型解析器依赖一条已写明的不变量：每个写 `model.name` 的地方都要在同一 scope 写 `model.baseUrl` —— 真实 URL，或者没有时写空串墓碑 —— 因为缺失的键在合并时无法覆盖低优先级 scope 里的过期值。原先的整体替换是碰巧满足了它（过期值一起被删掉）；只保留兄弟键的修法会把上一个 provider 的 URL 留下来，并把它当作新模型的消歧符。两个调用点手上都已有该 URL：Coding Plan 模板条目，或 provider map 条目（兜底与相邻 provider 条目一致）。

- 主要风险：面板现在会写 `model.baseUrl`，而之前什么都不写。当 active model 不在 provider map 中时，取值兜底为 provider 条目收到的同一默认值，保证两者一致。

- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无，改动只是不再删除既有键。

prs.title: fix(cli): reply to SDK initialize only after config is ready
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The SDK `initialize` control response is now sent after config initialization finishes, not right after the request is handled. The initialize request is still handled first, so its SDK MCP servers and staged SDK-only config are in place before extensions load. If config initialization fails, the request receives an error response instead of no reply at all.

In protocol terms, the frame's meaning changes from "request accepted" to "SDK mode is ready": a client may treat a successful `initialize` reply as permission to send its first prompt.

## Why it's needed

`initialize` was answered before `config.initialize()` ran, so the reply only meant "request accepted". A client that sent its first prompt on that reply then blocked on readiness; when the shared extension store was locked by another process, it waited out the ~28s retry budget and surfaced "Extension store is busy". Making the reply wait for config initialization turns it into the readiness signal clients already assume it is, and gives initialization failures a place to be reported.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Use the controlled repro from the issue: hold the `extension-store/lock` and start a stream-json SDK session.
2. Send `initialize`, then one user frame.
Before: `initialize` replies while the lock is still held, and the first prompt later fails with "Extension store is busy". After: the `initialize` reply arrives only once config initialization has completed, so a prompt sent after it no longer races extension loading. If initialization fails, the same request gets an error response.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change, so N/A for screenshots. `replies to initialize only after config initialization finishes` fails on the previous ordering (reply sent while initialization is pending) and passes here; `replies to initialize with an error when SDK mode initialization fails` covers the new failure reply. Existing dispatch behaviour is unchanged and covered by `ControlDispatcher` tests, including the deferred failure path: with `deferResponse` the dispatcher must send nothing and leave the reply to the caller.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Unit tests on macOS and in a `node:22-bookworm` container; Windows not exercised.

### Environment (optional)

`cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/nonInteractive/control/ControlDispatcher.test.ts src/nonInteractive/session.test.ts` (97 tests).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the initialize reply now includes config initialization latency, so clients that pipelined work on the old "accepted" ack see a later reply. That is the intended protocol meaning of the frame.
- Not validated / out of scope: the read path still takes the exclusive extension-store lock; concurrent sessions sharing one config dir can still serialize. Only the readiness ordering is changed here.
- Known pre-existing limitation, stated because the reply is now a readiness signal: duplicate `initialize` request ids. `registerIncomingRequest` overwrites the entry by id and a cancel answers only one frame, so the earlier caller waits out the SDK timeout. The registry behaviour is unchanged by this PR.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15796

prs.title: fix(cli): report pre-send refusals instead of replaying answers
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When the client refuses a turn before sending it — the session token limit or a UserPromptSubmit hook block — the stream carries no content, and the shared result builder fell back to the previous turn's assistant message. A persistent stream-json session therefore reported the refused message as a success carrying the earlier answer. This records the refusal on the adapter that stream-json, json, and text output share, and turns that would-be success into an error result with the refusal text and no `result` field. An error the caller already classified keeps its own subtype but reports the real refusal as its message, and the latch is cleared when the result that ends the turn is built, so it cannot relabel a later turn. A refusal that lands after the turn already streamed text leaves that text as the turn's answer and keeps the success envelope. The error reuses the existing `error_during_execution` subtype, so all three SDK protocol definitions stay unchanged and this does not depend on #15358.

## Why it's needed

Consumers branch on the result envelope (`is_error` / `subtype`), so a refused message currently looks answered and silently repeats stale content — a shell wrapper that only checks the status proceeds with the previous answer. The issue reproduces it with a two-message stream-json session, where the refused turn returned `{"subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"answer 1"}`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the adapter suite from `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/nonInteractive/io/StreamJsonOutputAdapter.test.ts`. The added cases feed each refusal event after a previous assistant message exists, then assert `is_error: true`, `subtype: "error_during_execution"`, the refusal text in `error.message`, and the absence of a `result` field. They also cover the neighbouring shapes: text produced before the refusal, a refusal in a later model round, a caller-classified error, and a refused turn followed by a turn that answers normally. Each case fails before the change and passes after it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the refused turn emits `{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"<previous answer>"}`. After: it emits `{"type":"result","subtype":"error_during_execution","is_error":true,"error":{"message":"Session token limit exceeded: ..."}}` with no `result`. This is a non-user-visible protocol change in headless output, so there is no TUI before/after.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Linux was verified inside a `node:22-bookworm` container; Windows was not exercised, and the change has no platform-specific code.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the latch is cleared when a result is built and consumed by that same build, so it cannot relabel a later turn's result. Refusals still end the turn; in a single-shot `-p` run a refusal that has nothing of its own to report exits with code 1 so the process status agrees with the error envelope, while a refusal that lands after the turn streamed text keeps the success envelope and exits 0. A persistent `--input-format stream-json` session ignores the per-turn status and keeps its existing behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: the max-turns sibling refusal stays with #15358.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — no new subtype, no configuration, no SDK type change. Single-shot `-p` exit status for these two refusals changes from 0 to 1 for scripts that relied on the old value.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15704

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

当客户端在发送前拒绝一轮请求（会话 token 上限，或 UserPromptSubmit hook 拦截）时，流里没有任何内容，而共用的 result 构建逻辑会回退到上一轮的助手消息。持久化的 stream-json 会话因此把被拒绝的消息报告成一次成功，并带上之前的答案。本改动在 stream-json、json、text 三种输出共用的适配器上记录拒绝原因，把原本会生成的成功结果转换成错误结果：带拒绝原因、不带 `result` 字段。调用方已经判定为错误的结果保留原有 subtype，但文案换成真实的拒绝原因；记录在构建 result 时清空，因此不会污染后续回合。拒绝发生时本轮已经输出过文本的，那段文本就是本轮的答案，结果保持成功信封。错误复用现有的 `error_during_execution` subtype，因此三套 SDK 的协议定义都不需要改，也不依赖 #15358。

## 为什么需要

调用方根据 result 信封（`is_error` / `subtype`）分支处理，现在被拒绝的消息看起来像已回答，并且静默重复旧内容——只判断退出码的 shell 包装脚本会拿着上一轮答案继续执行。issue 里用两条消息的 stream-json 会话复现：被拒绝的一轮返回 `{"subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"answer 1"}`。

## 评审验证方式

在 `packages/cli` 下运行 `npx vitest run src/nonInteractive/io/StreamJsonOutputAdapter.test.ts`。新增用例在已有上一轮助手消息的前提下注入拒绝事件，断言 `is_error: true`、`subtype: "error_during_execution"`、`error.message` 为拒绝原因，且没有 `result` 字段；同时覆盖相邻形态：拒绝前本轮已有文本、拒绝发生在后续模型轮次、调用方已判定的错误、以及被拒绝的一轮之后紧跟正常回答的一轮。这些用例改动前为红，改动后为绿。

## 改动前后

改动前被拒绝的一轮输出 `{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"<上一轮答案>"}`；改动后输出 `{"type":"result","subtype":"error_during_execution","is_error":true,"error":{"message":"Session token limit exceeded: ..."}}`，且不含 `result`。这是无头输出的协议行为变化，不涉及 TUI，因此没有界面前后对比。

## 测试环境

macOS 通过；Linux 在 `node:22-bookworm` 容器内通过；Windows 未验证，改动不含平台相关代码。

## 风险与范围

记录在构建 result 时清空、并被这次构建消费，不会污染后续回合。拒绝仍然结束回合：单次 `-p` 运行下没有自身输出的拒绝现在以退出码 1 结束、与错误信封一致；本轮已经有文本的拒绝保持成功信封、退出码 0。持久 `--input-format stream-json` 会话丢弃每轮状态、行为不变。max-session-turns 的同类处理仍归 #15358。没有新增 subtype、配置或 SDK 类型变更。单次 `-p` 下这两种拒绝的退出码由 0 变为 1，依赖旧值的脚本需要留意。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #15704

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): report a cancelled shell as interrupted, not completed
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an explicit `interruptedBeforeCompletion` marker to a tool result and sets it when the shell tool is cancelled by the user. The scheduler's post-execute cancellation branch now chooses the cancellation notice from that marker instead of assuming that a returned result means the tool finished. The ACP session pipeline, which mirrors that branch for `qwen --acp`, the web shell and IDE clients, reads the same marker and keeps the producer's partial output as the detail.

## Why it's needed

On Esc/Ctrl+C the shell tool kills the process group but returns an ordinary result whose own content already says the command was cancelled. The scheduler's `aborted` branch hardcoded "The tool had already completed; its output was discarded", which discards that truthful text and tells the model the work finished — and not to retry it. For half-run migrations or deploys, a step that was killed is recorded as done.

The shell tool is not the only possible producer of this shape: any tool that reports interruption by returning rather than throwing was mislabelled the same way, so the signal lives on the result rather than being inferred from shell's wording. Of the producers that now set it, only `create_sub_session` was shown reachable in measurement. `monitor`, `workflow` (early abort) and `ask_user_question` set it as defence: the scheduler cancels those calls before `execute()` runs, so the marker is not read on those paths today. `ask_user_question` sets it only when the turn was actually aborted — a plain decline is a completed decision and leaves the marker unset.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Follow the reproduction in #15833 (`work.sh` writing `start`, sleeping, then `done`), run it through the CLI and press Esc about 1s in.
2. Ask the model whether the command finished.
Before: the tool result says the tool had already completed and that the output was discarded. After: it says the call was intentionally cancelled and that it must not retry or work around it.
Timeouts and background-promote refusals keep their existing outcomes; only a user cancel sets the marker on the shell path.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change, so N/A for screenshots. The new scheduler table case fails on the previous code with `The tool had already completed; its output was discarded` and passes here; the shell test asserts the marker is set only on a user cancel; the question-tool tests assert it is set only when the turn was aborted; and the new ACP case asserts an interrupted result reaches the model as interrupted, with its partial output appended, while the unflagged case keeps the old wording.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Unit tests on macOS and in a `node:22-bookworm` container; Windows not exercised.

### Environment (optional)

`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts src/tools/askUserQuestion.test.ts` (942 tests); `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: one optional field on the result type. It is written by the shell tool and three returned-cancellation producers (only `create_sub_session` was reachable in measurement), and read only by the cancelled branch.
- Not validated / out of scope: `monitor`, `workflow` (early abort) and `ask_user_question` set the marker defensively; the scheduler cancels them before execution, so no model-visible change is claimed for those paths. A call cancelled before it starts ("cancelled before it could start") is not covered. A cancel that lands while the shell's confirmation dialog is still open (approval mode `default`) is also uncovered: it reports the generic cancelled reason, identically before and after this change. The managed-runtime surface still reports the old wording — its wrapper rebuilds a tool result from an explicit field whitelist that does not forward this marker — so this PR does not reach sessions whose tools run through that wrapper. Tracked as a follow-up rather than treated as fixed here. The sub-agent tool is also not covered: it returns its cancel as content parts and sets no marker, and the scheduler's detail gate requires a string `llmContent`, so setting the marker alone would not preserve its partial result. The ACP pipeline is covered by this PR.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15833

Thanks @stars-spark for the detailed reproduction.

prs.title: feat(web-shell): surface task Q&A activity above the composer
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a waiting card to the main Web Shell composer. A compact heatmap button at the end of the streaming status row opens a card whose primary purpose is to surface the current task's Q&A activity over time. The activity view is a fixed 44-week daily calendar (44 columns × 7 rows) where columns are Monday-to-Sunday weeks and each cell is one local day; the calendar ends with the current week, future days are empty placeholders, cell color shows that day's Q&A count, month labels sit below the grid, hovering a day shows its date and count, and clicking a populated day scrolls the transcript to the first Q&A of that day and highlights the message. An Activity / Usage switch shows the task's total, input, output, cached and context tokens instead of a credits balance. The header, tab row, body and footer keep a fixed frame across the activity, usage, intro and game views, so switching does not resize the card. When the configuration-gated waiting games entry is enabled, a white square with a dark gamepad icon appears after five seconds on a random cold day; clicking it starts horizontal Tetris or Snake at random, with a QWEN CODE pixel intro first (Tetris blocks fly to the right edge and settle into the random start cluster, while Snake keeps its intro static). Best scores and the sound preference stay in `localStorage`. The card closes when the turn ends, renders only on the main composer, and is hidden on coarse-pointer devices. The activity and token summaries are framework-free (`utils/waitingActivity.ts`), as are the Tetris (`utils/waitingMinigame.ts`) and Snake (`utils/waitingSnake.ts`) engines.

### Configuration

The activity and usage views are always available. The game entry is off by default and can be enabled with any of: `?waitingGames=1` on the Web Shell URL (`?waitingGames=0` forces it off), `localStorage['qwen-code-web-shell-waiting-games'] = '1'`, or a host-injected `window.__QWEN_CODE_WAITING_GAMES__ = true`. Without that configuration, the gamepad entry and all game controls stay out of the card.

## Why it's needed

A long turn currently shows only a spinner, elapsed time, token count and a rotating phrase. The card gives the wait a useful reading state (Q&A activity and token usage) and a way back into the transcript, without leaving the conversation or hijacking typing. The game is an optional waiting-time extra behind configuration, not the default experience.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the Web Shell, send a prompt, and look for the heatmap button at the end of the streaming status row. Clicking it opens the activity calendar; hover a populated day to see its date and count, click one to jump to that day's first Q&A, switch to Usage to see the token breakdown, and confirm the card frame does not resize between views. With the game configuration enabled, wait five seconds for the gamepad square on a cold day, click it to play the intro and then Tetris or Snake, and confirm Escape (or the card's collapse control) closes the card. End the turn and the card disappears. From `packages/web-shell`:

```sh
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/utils/waitingActivity.test.ts client/utils/waitingSnake.test.ts client/utils/waitingMinigame.test.ts client/utils/waitingGamesConfig.test.ts client/components/WaitingMinigame.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts
# 71 passed

../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/App.test.tsx
# 1363 passed

../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
../../node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config playwright.config.ts --project=chromium client/e2e/waiting-minigame.spec.ts
# 5 passed
```

ESLint and Prettier pass for the changed files. A local UI harness needs no daemon: run `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173` and open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/e2e/waiting-minigame-harness.html`. The harness provides synthetic daily activity and token data, theme and language switches, a `Games: off/on` toggle (off by default, matching the product), an entry-delay toggle and a `Next game` selector for Tetris/Snake.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (base `main`): the composer status row shows only the spinner, phrase, elapsed time, token count and cancel hint, with no waiting card or entry point. After (this revision): a heatmap button at the end of the row opens the activity calendar, the usage view, and the optional game views below.

| Activity heatmap with hover details | QWEN CODE intro |
| --- | --- |
| ![Activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-heatmap-tooltip.png) | ![Intro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-intro.png) |

| Blocks flying to the right cluster | Settled start cluster |
| --- | --- |
| ![Flight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-flight.png) | ![Landed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-landed.png) |

| Tetris | Snake with an apple |
| --- | --- |
| ![Tetris](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-board.png) | ![Snake](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-snake.png) |

| Token usage (sample) | Dark theme, Chinese heatmap |
| --- | --- |
| ![Usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-tokens.png) | ![Dark Chinese](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-dark-zh-heatmap.png) |

| Configured game entry on a cold day |
| --- |
| ![Game entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-game-entry.png) |

The activity, usage and dark-theme screenshots use the local harness sample data with the game entry off. The game-entry frame uses the local harness with `?waitingGames=1`. The intro and game frames use the Chromium E2E (`packages/web-shell/client/e2e/waiting-minigame.spec.ts`) with the game entry enabled.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS run through `npm run dev` in `packages/web-shell` with the browser harness and the Playwright mock daemon (no real backend); CI covers Linux.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the card expands in normal flow inside the composer footer, so opening it temporarily resizes the transcript instead of overlaying it; the game entry is off by default and only renders behind explicit configuration, so third-party hosts must opt in.
- Not validated / out of scope: split and side-task panes, touch controls, a real daemon beyond the mock harness, Firefox/WebKit, Android WebView, sound output, and per-commit attribution are not covered by this round; an intermittent ~36 px composer shift when starting a game was observed in external verification and the root cause is not isolated; the host-level opt-out for third-party hosts remains an open design-doc question.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No new dependencies, and no daemon route, transcript, telemetry or host prop changes beyond the optional configuration reads; best scores and the sound preference keep their existing `localStorage` keys.

Design notes: [English](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/2026-11-01-web-shell-waiting-minigame.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/2026-11-01-web-shell-waiting-minigame.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Closes #16036.

<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 这个 PR 做了什么

为主 Web Shell 输入框增加一个等待卡片。流式状态行末尾的紧凑热力图按钮会打开卡片，主要用于按时间展示当前任务的问答活动。活动视图是固定的 44 周每日日历（44 列 × 7 行），列是周一到周日的自然周，每个格子代表一个本地自然日；日历以当前周结束，未来日期是空占位，格子颜色表示该日的问答数量，月份标签在网格下方，悬停某天会显示日期和数量，点击有数据的日期会把对话滚动到当天第一条问答并高亮该消息。Activity / Usage 切换可以在活动视图和用量视图之间切换，用量展示任务的总量、输入、输出、缓存和上下文 token，而不是余额。头部、标签行、正文和底部在所有视图中保持固定框架，因此在活动、用量、开场和游戏之间切换不会改变卡片尺寸。启用配置门控的等待游戏入口后，五秒后会在随机一个冷门日期上出现带深色手柄图标的白色小方块；点击它会随机开始横向俄罗斯方块或贪吃蛇，并先播放 QWEN CODE 像素开场（俄罗斯方块方块飞到右边缘并落成随机起始簇，贪吃蛇保持静态开场）。最高分和音效偏好保存在 `localStorage`。回复结束时卡片关闭；卡片只在主输入框渲染，并在粗指针设备上隐藏。活动与 token 汇总是不依赖框架的 `utils/waitingActivity.ts`，俄罗斯方块（`utils/waitingMinigame.ts`）和贪吃蛇（`utils/waitingSnake.ts`）引擎同样不依赖框架。

#### 配置

活动和用量视图始终可用。游戏入口默认关闭，可通过以下任一方式开启：Web Shell URL 上的 `?waitingGames=1`（`?waitingGames=0` 会强制关闭）、`localStorage['qwen-code-web-shell-waiting-games'] = '1'`，或宿主注入 `window.__QWEN_CODE_WAITING_GAMES__ = true`。没有该配置时，手柄入口和所有游戏控件都不会出现在卡片中。

### 为什么需要

一次长回复目前只显示转圈、耗时、token 数和轮换文案。卡片让等待期间有可用的阅读状态（问答活动和 token 用量），也能回到对话中的具体日期，既不需要离开会话，也不会抢占输入。游戏只是配置门控的可选等待消遣，不是默认体验。

### 评审验证计划

#### 如何验证

打开 Web Shell 并发送一条提问，查看流式状态行末尾的热力图按钮。点击打开活动日历；悬停有数据的日期查看日期和数量，点击某天会跳到当天第一条问答；切换到 Usage 查看 token 细分，并确认卡片框架在各视图之间不改变尺寸。开启游戏配置后，等待五秒出现冷门日期上的手柄小方块，点击播放开场后进入俄罗斯方块或贪吃蛇，按 Esc（或卡片的收起控件）关闭卡片。结束该轮回复后卡片消失。在 `packages/web-shell` 目录下执行：

```sh
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/utils/waitingActivity.test.ts client/utils/waitingSnake.test.ts client/utils/waitingMinigame.test.ts client/utils/waitingGamesConfig.test.ts client/components/WaitingMinigame.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts
# 71 passed

../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/App.test.tsx
# 1363 passed

../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
../../node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config playwright.config.ts --project=chromium client/e2e/waiting-minigame.spec.ts
# 5 passed
```

改动文件的 ESLint 和 Prettier 检查通过。本地 UI harness 不需要 daemon：运行 `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173`，打开 `http://127.0.0.1:5173/e2e/waiting-minigame-harness.html`。harness 提供合成的每日活动与 token 数据、主题和语言切换、`Games: off/on` 开关（默认关闭，与产品一致）、入口延迟开关，以及俄罗斯方块/贪吃蛇的 `Next game` 选择器。

#### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

修改前（`main` 基线）：输入框状态行只有转圈、文案、耗时、token 数和取消提示，没有等待卡片或入口。修改后（本版本）：状态行末尾的热力图按钮可以打开活动日历、用量视图，以及可选的游戏视图。

本地 macOS，在 `packages/web-shell` 下通过 `npm run dev` 运行浏览器 harness 和 Playwright mock daemon（无真实后端）；CI 覆盖 Linux。

prs.title: fix(core): reject symlink escapes in memory imports
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Memory imports now compare the real filesystem locations of the imported path and the allowed roots before reading. Symbolic links committed inside a repository can no longer authorize reads outside the project. Relative link targets containing `..` are expanded in filesystem order, so an intermediate directory link is followed before moving to its parent. This applies to both synchronous and asynchronous path resolution. Projects reached through a symbolic link continue to support imports.

Rejected imports in tree output now say `Path is outside allowed directories`, which describes the enforced boundary without claiming that a benign link to shared documentation is an attack. Debug logs retain the resolved path and allowed roots in both formats.

## Why it's needed

A repository can contain a Markdown link whose target is a private file outside the checkout. Comparing only the written path lets that link pass a project-boundary check while the actual read follows it outside. Automatically loading project memory can therefore read local files merely because the user opens an untrusted repository. Resolving `sub/..` lexically also disagrees with the filesystem when `sub` is itself a symbolic link, so canonicalization must preserve that order.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Create an allowed project directory and a sibling directory containing a marker file. Import the marker through a directory symbolic link inside the project and confirm that neither tree nor flat output includes the marker. Tree output should identify the allowed-directory boundary rather than call the link a traversal attempt. Repeat with a dangling link pointing outside the project and with a relative link target that traverses an intermediate directory link before `..`.

Confirm that ordinary in-project imports, in-project symbolic links, and allowed roots reached through a symbolic link still work. Compare synchronous and asynchronous canonicalization of a relative target containing `sub/..` with the filesystem's actual resolved path; both should agree.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before this follow-up, a real-filesystem reproduction rejected a benign shared-document link with `Path traversal attempt`, and its accurate-label assertion failed. Both formats already excluded the outside marker and preserved an ordinary in-project import.

Published-release baseline: globally installed `qwen` 0.26.5 was run against the same real-file and symbolic-link fixture using a localhost mock API. Both tree and flat formats exited 0 and made two requests each, but included both synthetic outside markers in the captured model requests. The local PR bundle excludes both markers while retaining the legitimate import. This release comparison is separate from the pre-follow-up source reproduction above.

Current local verification: 247 core tests passed with 1 skipped, and 464 daemon worktree guard tests passed with 4 skipped. These cover memory imports, path canonicalization, file-read permissions, shell policy, and the daemon guard. Full build, repository typecheck, changed-file ESLint, and Prettier passed.

Temporarily reverting only the asynchronous relative-target expansion makes the new kernel-equivalence assertion fail at the asynchronous call. The source was restored byte-for-byte, and the focused suites passed again.

The built CLI passed headless verification in tree and flat formats against a localhost mock API, with two requests and exit 0 in each format. Captured model requests preserved the legitimate import marker, excluded both the shared-document marker and the original intermediate-link escape marker, and contained no inaccurate attack label. Tree requests contained the accurate allowed-directory label. The original source reproduction now exits 0 as well.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js 24.22.1, pnpm 11.24.0. Published-release baseline: globally installed `qwen` 0.26.5. Candidate: the locally built PR bundle, version 0.26.2. Both CLI runs used isolated configuration and runtime directories, real files and symbolic links, and a localhost mock API.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: path canonicalization is shared infrastructure. The change also affects file-read permission checks, runtime shell policy, sandbox execution, team and automatic memory path checks, and the daemon worktree guard. Both synchronous and asynchronous consumers now follow the filesystem's interpretation of relative link targets. These consumers are part of the review scope, rather than this being limited to memory imports.
- Allowed roots are canonicalized alongside candidate paths so projects opened through a symbolic link keep working. These roots must represent filesystem boundaries, rather than paths an untrusted repository can redefine through tracked contents.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux were not exercised locally. Platform-dependent tests report visible skips where applicable. CI still requires maintainer authorization for this fork; local checks do not replace those platform lanes. The pre-existing time-of-check/time-of-use window between validation and reading is unchanged.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: imports that escape through a symbolic link are rejected. Tree output uses an accurate boundary label; flat output keeps its existing omission behavior, and detailed rejection paths remain in the opt-in debug log.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15431

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve startup banner when opening short dialogs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps constrained dialogs at their natural height when their content fits, while retaining the existing maximum-height clipping for dialogs that exceed the available terminal space.

## Why it's needed

The dialog container used the calculated row budget as a fixed height. A short startup prompt was therefore padded to nearly the full terminal height. Combined with the committed startup banner, that oversized frame overflowed the viewport and triggered Ink's full-terminal clear path. Repainting the oversized frame then scrolled the banner's first rows out of view, which appeared as an intermittently truncated first paint.

Using the row budget as a maximum instead of a required height avoids the unnecessary overflow without changing how tall dialogs are constrained.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start the interactive CLI with a pending built-in provider update and height constraints enabled. The startup banner should remain fully visible when the update prompt appears. Dismiss the prompt and confirm the normal composer appears without duplicate banner output. Also open a dialog taller than the terminal and confirm that it remains clipped to the available rows. With height constraints disabled, confirm that tall dialogs retain their existing uncapped behavior.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: a one-line dialog in a 24-row terminal produced a 24-row layout, consuming the entire viewport and displacing the top of the startup banner.

After: the same constrained short dialog matches its natural unconstrained height (3 rows in the regression fixture), while the existing tall-dialog tests continue to verify clipping.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 24.18.0 on Windows 11. Verified against the historical nightly from the original report and the current main branch.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: short dialogs no longer fill unused vertical space; tall dialogs preserve the existing cap and clipping behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: reporter-specific provider credentials and terminal combinations; the reporter can confirm the original end-to-end launch configuration.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8124

## 为什么需要

对话框容器此前把计算出的行数预算当作固定高度。因此，一个很短的启动提示也会被填充到接近整个终端的高度。它与已经提交的启动横幅叠加后会超过视口，并触发 Ink 的全终端清屏路径。随后重新绘制这个过高的帧时，横幅顶部几行会被滚出可见区域，看起来就像首次绘制偶发截断。

prs.title: fix(ci): resume linter archive downloads
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR makes the cold-cache linter install survive a throttled release-asset download. Before this change, every curl attempt restarted at byte zero with the same 90-second ceiling; three stalls in a row failed the required lint gate. After this change, up to five attempts resume from the bytes already received, with increasing delays between them.

It does not change which archives are downloaded or which versions are pinned. The archive still has to pass the existing SHA-256 verification before extraction or caching.

## Why it's needed

The failing jobs in #16005 were diagnosed as a missing Node runtime, but the `Node.js is not on PATH` text is echoed script source from the preflight action. On `ecs-qwen-hz5-2` and `ecs-qwen-hz6-20`, Node 22.23.4 was found and that preflight step succeeded. The actual failure was `Install linters`:

- `actionlint`: three timeouts, each receiving roughly 1.2-1.5 MB of 2.1 MB.
- `shellcheck`: three timeouts, each receiving roughly 2.4-2.6 MB of 6.8 MB.

The same cold-cache plus degraded-egress pattern made unrelated commits fail the only required status context. Starting over on each retry discards the useful progress from the prior attempt.

The more durable infrastructure fix is still to pre-warm these pinned archives on the runner pool or serve them from an internal mirror. This PR only removes one repository-side failure mode until that lands.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm the generated installer retries with `--continue-at -` and that the focused suite exercises a truncated first transfer followed by a completed resume.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: a timeout on attempt 1 was followed by an unrelated request from byte zero. After: the failed partial file is retained and the next attempt resumes at that offset. The fake curl in the new regression writes a partial archive on the first request and appends the remainder on the resumed request; the SHA-256 check then accepts the complete file.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

Per the standing local-execution constraint for this task, no tests, formatting, lint, build, or typecheck were run locally. The new focused regression is left to CI. The regression is skip-gated on Windows because the installer's POSIX shell path is not exercised there.

### Environment (optional)

N/A

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a server that does not support range requests makes a resumed attempt fail with curl exit 33 or 36; the loop then discards the partial file and starts cleanly on the next attempt. The bounded attempt count prevents an indefinite retry loop.
- Not validated / out of scope: runner-pool pre-warming and an internal mirror are not included; that is the durable infrastructure fix. The retry path was not executed locally under this task's no-test constraint.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

References #16005. This PR hardens the repository-side cold-cache download path but does not prove the runner-pool infrastructure issue is fully resolved, so it intentionally does not auto-close the issue.

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：如果服务器不支持 range 请求，续传会以 curl exit 33 或 36 失败；循环随后会丢弃部分文件，并在下一次尝试时从头开始。尝试次数有上限，不会无限重试。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：runner 池预热和内网镜像不包含在内；那才是持久的基础设施修复。受本任务不跑本地测试的约束，续传路径未在本地执行。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

引用 #16005。这个 PR 加强了仓库侧冷缓存下载路径，但不能证明 runner 池的基础设施问题已完全解决，因此有意不自动关闭该 issue。

prs.title: refactor(managed-agent): Extract runtime execution dispatcher
prs.body:
## What this PR does Extracts Runtime Broker dispatch into one internal owner for reservations, physical invocation tracking, dispatch-lease renewal, v3 result waiting, completion and persisted SSH acknowledgement. Cancellation queries and calls that owner directly instead of receiving a mutable invocation set and a service callback. The public service retains admission, Session/drain orchestration, the shared close fence, both executors and provisioner lifetime. Preserves the existing dispatch algorithms, durable repository authority, generation fencing, caller lock regions, exception mappings, completion order and shutdown order. Adds focused ownership regressions and synchronized English/Chinese designs. ## Why it's needed After the workflow extraction in #16029, dispatch state and completion still lived in the public service while cancellation depended on its mutable state and callback. Keeping reservations, physical invocations and their completion together clarifies their distinct lifetimes and removes that dependency without changing Runtime behavior. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify 1. Submit concurrent dispatch attempts for the same prepared execution while its repository claim is blocked. Only one claim proceeds, and the physical invocation begins only after the claim is released. A synchronous claim failure must release the reservation so a later attempt can proceed. 2. Complete an invocation successfully, then exercise a worker failure. Physical invocation membership must be removed before either durable settlement or UNKNOWN persistence, so cancellation cannot treat a finished call as running. Existing v3, cancellation/fencing, SSH receipt and HTTP behavior must stay unchanged. 3. Cancel internal pending-operation reservations while transport is still pending. The underlying invocation must remain uncancelled and retain its physical membership until completion; shared executors and provisioner lifetime remain controlled by the public service. Local baseline: 280 selected tests passed. After extraction: 285 tests passed with 0 failures, 0 errors and 0 skips, including five new dispatcher cases. Both Checkstyle goals passed. Two clean self-audit passes and independent read-only review found no actionable defect introduced by the extraction. > Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Network responses, files, child pipes, and artifact reads are consumed with `.text()`/`read_to_string`/`read_to_end` (or a growing buffer) before any size bound. A single oversized response, artifact, or pipe can OOM the process or wedge a worker, and several paths buffer the whole body before they even consult the configured cap. The sources differ (HTTP, filesystem, child stdin/stdout, artifact store) but the failure mode is the same and the fix is one bounded reader. Apply a byte cap with a truncation note at ingest, not after materialising content.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **23** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Apply a bounded reader (byte cap + truncation note) at every listed site before materialising content; add a regression test per reader.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

## Key files
- `crates/tui/src/tools/web_run.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/skills/audit.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/skills/install.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/repl/runtime.rs`
- `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/mcp/server.mjs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/diff_render.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_output.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/workflow_panel.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/fetch_url.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/truncate.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/tool_result_retrieval.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/anthropic.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every listed candidate is either fixed with a test, or downgraded with a written reason in the PR.
- [ ] No new instance of this class is introduced (guarded by the test/budget).
- [ ] Existing behavior for unrelated paths is unchanged.

## Verification
```sh
cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-release -p codewhale-telemetry -p codewhale-workflow-js
cargo test  -p codewhale-tui --lib
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
( cd web && npm run check )
( cd integrations/bridge-core && npm run test )
```

## Out of scope
- Findings that belong to another systemic class or to the localized backlog.
- Re-architecture beyond the listed sites.

## Related existing work (do not duplicate)
#6147 (bound engine channels), #6333 (read budgets), #6504 (sub-agent input cap), #6540 (compaction), #5404/#5468 (SSE tail fail-closed)

## Candidate findings (23)
- [x] **D03-07** · D03 — Git/GitHub/review/web tools · `crates/tui/src/tools/web_run.rs:367` — operation fan-out and `.text()` bodies are unbounded; one model call can exhaust memory/network.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [x] **F02-02** · F02 — Skills, hooks, LSP, snapshots, REPL, RLM, work graph · `crates/tui/src/skills/audit.rs:426`, `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:503` — special/unbounded files can hang/OOM audit/discovery.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [x] **F02-04** · F02 — Skills, hooks, LSP, snapshots, REPL, RLM, work graph · `crates/tui/src/skills/install.rs:557` — remote download fully buffers response before the `max_size` check.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [x] **F02-06** · F02 — Skills, hooks, LSP, snapshots, REPL, RLM, work graph · `crates/tui/src/repl/runtime.rs:292` — stdout unbounded and stderr drained after round, allowing OOM/deadlock.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **CU01-09** · CU01 — Computer-use · `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/mcp/server.mjs:1319` — JSON-lines/socket/CDP frames and screenshots unbounded.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [x] **U04-01** · U04 — History, transcript, markdown, diff, streaming · `crates/tui/src/tui/diff_render.rs:49`, `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_output.rs:379` — huge tool output/diff materializes all wrapped rows and unbounded summary before head/tail.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [x] **U05-03** · U05 — Work surface, widgets, agent cards/panels · `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/workflow_panel.rs:777` — attacker `child_count` causes huge allocation/OOM.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **D01-08** · D01 — Shell/file/read/search tools · `crates/tui/src/tools/fetch_url.rs:520` — JSONPath fan-out does not bound fields/matches/serialized result.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [x] **D01-09** · D01 — Shell/file/read/search tools · `crates/tui/src/tools/truncate.rs:530` — on artifact publication failure the original unbounded result returns to model context.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [x] **D01-10** · D01 — Shell/file/read/search tools · `crates/tui/src/tools/tool_result_retrieval.rs:137` — retrieval fully reads artifact before applying `max_bytes`; a single giant line already bloats memory.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_

- Live OAuth token exchanges/rotation/revocation, durable credential custody(CW-6643), arbitrary bootstrap and tenant/filesystem isolation are explicit separate boundaries, not claimed by30local fixture groups
- Do not promote this slice to whole MCP/DSH readiness or live external-server qualification

**Next action:** Mark the five accepted v1 scope items delivered with carrying commit/30actual groups and keep explicit design/lifecycle limits. Root decides tracker closure for current accepted scope; no new framework or I/O provider required.

Counts: actual observation groups=30; ordinary public engine groups=24; plugin groups=6; independent oracles=20; loopback http requests=118; stdio launches=18; existing tui mcp passed=125; existing engine mcp passed=447; existing engine mcp ignored=2. 

Accepted v1 implementation is complete and locally qualified: 30 actual groups, 20 independent oracles, 118 loopback HTTP requests and 18 stdio launches. Closing this design/implementation issue for that accepted scope. Final candidate validation and the listed separate lifecycle/live-provider boundaries remain open at their owning gates. This is not a shipped-release claim.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-status-20261025 -->
## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

Slice 1 landed in [f98cb165a3](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/f98cb165a3acad3ad67a19e67d40a4ce03d163c5): MCP placeholder, header, bearer and OAuth reads share one resolver; reviewed plugins use their captured pre-dotenv host environment. The shared batch passed 426 existing local tests. OAuth/env-header specifics additionally rely on source audit and compilation. A host-injected secret store is still outstanding; no live MCP-server qualification is claimed.

<!-- /cw-0103-status-20261025 -->

---

## Problem

Embedded hosts may keep MCP credentials in a keyring or another host-owned secret store. Supplying those values by mutating the process environment at runtime is not sound once other threads can read the environment, and it also makes secret lifetime process-global.

A process-wide callback is a useful compatibility bridge, but it still couples every engine in the process to the first installer and makes multi-runtime, multi-tenant, and isolated tests awkward.

## Suggested direction

Consider an optional host-provided MCP secret provider scoped to a runtime or `McpPool`:

- Inject an `Arc<dyn McpSecretProvider>` (exact type intentionally open) when constructing the owning runtime/MCP context.
- Use one resolution seam for stdio `${...}` expansion, request `env_headers`, `bearer_token_env_var`, and OAuth discovery/login/refresh headers.
- Keep process-environment fallback as an explicit compatibility policy rather than an implicit second implementation.
- Preserve the reviewed-plugin trust boundary: plugin-contributed MCPs should continue to use their captured, reviewed `HostEnvironment`, not an ambient host secret store.
- Keep errors and diagnostics privacy-bounded: variable names and typed outcomes may be useful; secret values must never enter logs or user-facing errors.

The provider can remain a synchronous in-memory lookup if hosts hydrate it from their keyring ahead of time. Whether an async provider, cache invalidation, zeroizing value wrapper, or per-server authorization belongs in the public contract is left open for maintainer input.

## Current downstream bridge

[Pinvou/CodeWhale PR #25](https://github.com/Pinvou/CodeWhale/pull/25) uses a process-wide first-install-wins resolver to remove runtime environment writes from an embedded desktop host. It is deliberately narrow and should not grow into the general lifecycle design in the downstream fork.

## Non-goal

This issue is a design direction, not a complete implementation proposal or an implementation commitment from the downstream fork.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**not adopted: no gix dependency in canonical Cargo graph.**

Source reconciled against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c).

Credited source:

- **CLI lock avoidance predecessor**: [f704e0c9c0](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/f704e0c9c05e0e82917d6d57b3d5f6131660a934)
- **hardened Git read/source prerequisites**: existing shared real-Git facade remains; does not implement gix or zero-spawn acceptance

Remaining:

- Exact pinned minimal dependency/MSRV/advisory/target closure and compatible upstream backport must be reviewed/adopted
- Migrate every admitted internal discovery/HEAD/status/diff/aheadbehind/worktree/config consumer; keep writes and agent shell on realGit
- Observe actual zero internal read subprocesses, no hooks/filters/fsmonitor/lazyfetch/optionalwrites, hostile repository failclosed behavior, cancellation, Windows and maintained targets. Later log/show/blame phase remains explicitly labeled by existing maintainer scope

**Next action:** Review frozen gix artifact/backport packet against the full required operation-family ledger, resolve real gaps, then one coordinated native batch and actual normal/hostile/no-spawn/no-write controls.

Whole issue remains open. Uncommitted Pager corrections and uncompiled gix/host-band artifacts are excluded from delivered source. Current routing: CW-7763. 0.10.3 remains unpublished; previous dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Problem

codewhale shells out to the real `git` CLI for all internal read operations — repository badge probes, workspace context, `@status`/`@diff` mentions, and the model-callable Git tools. After #5617, two costs remain:

1. **Process spawn overhead**: the internal probes still spawn roughly **48 git processes per minute** while the TUI is idle in a git repo (≈190/min before the lock-reduction issue). Each spawn pays process creation + CLI startup for a computation that is a few milliseconds in-process.
2. **Unnecessary dependency on the git binary**: internal badge and context reads could work purely from the repository's on-disk format, without requiring git to be installed at all.

## Proposed solution

Migrate codewhale's **internal read-only** git operations from the `git` CLI to **gix** (gitoxide, pure Rust). Requirement-level scope (implementation follows the project's own conventions; no specific files are prescribed). This issue only makes sense after the lock-reduction issue is merged: the migration replaces the lock-free CLI reads with in-process reads and removes the event-driven refresh path's remaining process spawns.

- Add `gix` as a workspace dependency, pinned to an exact version, with the minimal feature set covering the read paths.
- Replace the following internal operations with gix in-process equivalents:
  - repository discovery / work-tree root resolution
  - HEAD / branch resolution (including detached-HEAD short hash)
  - working-tree status computation (staged / modified / untracked / conflicts)
  - ahead/behind counts vs upstream
  - worktree listing
  - remote origin URL and git config reads
  - commit log / show / blame (model-facing Git tool — may be a later phase)
- **Keep the `git` CLI for real write operations** (side-repo snapshot commits, worktree create/remove, branch deletion) and for agent-executed shell commands (`exec_shell` remains the model's surface and must stay a real CLI).

## Expected gains

- **Zero subprocess spawns for internal reads**: the idle ~48 processes/min (baseline after the lock-reduction issue) drop to **~0** — badge and context data become pure in-process computation.
- **No lock files, permanently**: gix reads never touch `.git/index.lock`, eliminating the commit-collision problem at the root, without environment-variable mitigations.
- **Faster refresh**: in-process status computation (~5-30ms) vs. process spawn + CLI startup per probe.
- **Works without the git binary**: badge and context reads succeed from the on-disk format even where `git` is not installed; write paths still report cleanly when git is missing.
- **Consistent with the event-driven direction**: when combined with `.git` metadata watching (lock-reduction issue, point 3), the refresh path becomes event-triggered in-process computation with near-zero idle cost.

## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

>
> **What remains**

---

## Combined Core execution: C09

[Core execution plan](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/document/codewhale-core-execution-plan-a11e2e1c601d>) owns order and scope. This issue contributes to C09; the linked plan owns the complete packet and any outstanding candidate acceptance. Record this issue's path claims and implementation evidence here.

**Issue mapping:** [SHA-6291 / GitHub #5586](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6291/decompose-the-mega-files-librs-187k-configrs-123k-clientrs-111k>)
  covers cohesive large-file decomposition across C03–C09; move whole behaviors
  and owning tests, with checked dependency boundaries rather than line-count
  targets. [SHA-6286 / GitHub #5580](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6286/streamline-tui-monoliths-split-event-looprs-match-into-per-domain>) moves remaining
  event handling into domain reducers and leaves dispatch in `event_loop.rs`;
  preserve the existing reducer pattern and migrate touched arms completely.
  [SHA-6287 / GitHub #5581](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6287/event-granularity-audit-surfaces-that-stall-at-turn-boundaries-despite>) supplies the per-call
  telemetry consumer requirements implemented in C11 with #6011: live token/time
  display, cache visibility and durable mid-turn accounting, with authoritative
  completion reconciliation and no double counting. Credit already-live cost,
  background cost, timing and context surfaces.

[SHA-5509 / GitHub #3957](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-5509/refactor-split-shared-modal-infrastructure-and-owned-views>) separates shared modal
  infrastructure from owned Config/SubAgents views and makes all provider
  credential entry use the same masking, validation and geometry primitive.
  Prove paste/delete/Enter/Esc/failure/retry and 80x24/120x32 wrapping; secrets
  must never reach screenshots, logs or errors.
  [SHA-5506 / GitHub #3954](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-5506/refactor-split-setup-wizard-constitution-runtime-provider-and>) splits setup by
  constitution, runtime, provider, persistence/report and navigation ownership
  where warranted; preserve constitution checkpoints and onboarding handoff.
  These client refactors keep behavior and private-test visibility intact.

[SHA-6251 / GitHub #5528](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6251/workflow-runs-fail-silently-dispatchschema-errors-never-surface-in-the>) requires visible
  workflow dispatch/schema failures even before a child starts, with preserved
  error/status receipts over the shared event authority.
  [SHA-6156 / GitHub #5268](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6156/mid-turn-control-queue-send-now-esc-keep-draft-named-waits>) requires visible queue,
  send-now, cancel/keep-draft and named waits over existing runtime channels;
  qualify those states with C12 and C08's submitted-steer consume/ack contract.
  C01's #5479 register and controls must use this same runtime projection.

**Owner: client-adapter owner. Dependencies: C08.** Fold the embedded HTTP
  API into the existing app-server HTTP/SSE/stdio surface over the shared
  runtime, preserving routes and authentication. Move argument parsing and
  headless presentation from TUI `lib.rs` into CLI; preserve binary names and
  public commands. TUI owns terminal lifecycle, rendering, input, pickers and
  slash-command presentation, calling the same runtime operations. Use existing
  in-process `EngineHandle`/`Op`/`Event` seams; local terminal use need not hop
  through HTTP. Separate wire DTOs from internal reply channels/capabilities.

**Completion evidence required:** all three clients reach the same lifecycle/execution owner,
  transport/auth/protocol parity and reconnect/recovery pass, no UI-owned
  provider I/O/policy/store/loop remains, and obsolete dependencies and temporary
  internal shims are removed. Adopt `core/protocol_parity.rs` in real consumers
  or retire it; unused parity code is not convergence. Resize UI files only by
  remaining responsibility. Apps product work is not part of this packet.

---

## Original issue and contributor history

User ask for the 0.9.12 cleanup lane: the 10k+-line files keep causing pain. Measured today (prod code, excluding the 20k-line test files which should split alongside their subjects):

* `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` — 18,747
* `crates/tui/src/config.rs` — 12,346
* `crates/tui/src/client.rs` — 11,122
* `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs` — 9,322
* `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs` — 6,891, `core/engine/turn_loop.rs` — 6,668, `runtime_api.rs` — 6,542, `tui/ui/event_loop.rs` — 5,721 (event_loop already tracked in #5580)

Approach (same discipline as #5580): mechanical module extraction, one cohesive region per commit, no behavior change, moves verified by `cargo check` + the file's existing test slice. Suggested first cuts: [client.rs](<http://client.rs>) wire-parsing (parse_usage/SSE chunk parsing + their tests) into `client/wire.rs`; [config.rs](<http://config.rs>) merge/persistence into `config/merge.rs`; [lib.rs](<http://lib.rs>) engine-config assembly into its own module. Declared one-way per AGENTS.md once started: new code lands in the extracted modules, touched regions migrate.

Tracker: #5573. Related: #5580, #5581.

## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**partial: 3 fixed, 2 partial, 4 still inline.**

Source reconciled against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c).

Partial findings:

- U08-08:6b89d572 validated names/-- and removed duplicate probe; TUI worktree Enter still calls synchronous create_worktree and Engine git_output.output() remains inline

Remaining:

- C02-09: Engine turn metadata still calls git_status::collect; stable prompt preparation and emit_tool_audit retain synchronous file work on async callers
- C01-07: concrete command handlers retain blocking filesystem/subprocess work on the UI path
- T02-12: ResolvedRuntimeRoute::preflight/CodewhaleClient::from_candidate synchronously read credential/certificate inputs; earlier offload was withdrawn after hangs and has not been replaced
- T03-m2: async update_provider_catalog holds account-model-access read guard while record_success_if_current performs cache publication I/O

**Next action:** Use existing bounded owner_work or established supervised blocking owner at exact callsites, preserve env-scope membership/cancellation, and qualify each changed family. Do not resurrect canceled umbrella or treat cancellation as waiver.

Counts: roster=9; fixed=3; partial=2; open=4. 

Whole issue remains open. Uncommitted Pager corrections and uncompiled gix/host-band artifacts are excluded from delivered source. Current routing: CW-6942 canceled; public requirement remains, domain ownership must be explicit. 0.10.3 remains unpublished; previous dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->


> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Filesystem, subprocess, git, secret-store, and tempfile work is executed synchronously inside `async` call chains (engine tasks, tool handlers, UI event loop, runtime API). Parking a Tokio worker stalls every task sharing that runtime: the TUI stops responding to input, unrelated tools and streaming freeze, and cancellation/timeouts are delayed. Repository convention #6149 requires `tokio::fs`/`tokio::process` or `spawn_blocking`, and `scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` ratchets the unprotected-site count precisely to stop this class from creeping back. Each site below must move to async IO, `spawn_blocking`, or a dedicated thread without raising that budget.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **9** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Move each listed site to `tokio` async IO, `spawn_blocking`, or a dedicated thread; do not raise the blocking-calls budget.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

## Key files
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_execution.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/test_runner.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/commands/contract.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/route_runtime.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/sessions.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/runtime_chat_relay.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/task_manager.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/git_status.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/worktree_manager.rs`
- `crates/core/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/provider_lake.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every listed candidate is either fixed with a test, or downgraded with a written reason in the PR.
- [ ] No new instance of this class is introduced (guarded by the test/budget).
- [ ] Existing behavior for unrelated paths is unchanged.

## Verification
```sh
python3 scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py   # count must not increase
cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-core
cargo test  -p codewhale-tui --lib
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
```

## Out of scope
- Findings that belong to another systemic class or to the localized backlog.
- Re-architecture beyond the listed sites.

## Related existing work (do not duplicate)
#6149 (blocking calls in async paths), #6211 (polling/blocking shapes), #6333 (async I/O hardening), #6140 (MCP stdio async-native), #5616, #6371/#6372 (terminal routes off runtime)
