<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**wire controls landed; economic acceptance open.**

Verified: Wire-budget/supersession repair9633c9fafa is landed.13actual DeepSeek request captures retained stable provider headers.

Remaining: Captured runs contained no eviction, so they cannot establish eviction/re-admission cost or net savings.

Next action: Perform matched eviction/re-admission intervention and reconcile authoritative provider usage/cost per call; retain unknown price/cache fields as unknown. New provider spending requires applicable approval.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one \~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs \~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR [#101](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/101>) does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (\~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| \# | Cost item | Tok-eq |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | \~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | \~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | \~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | \~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | \~34,500 |
|  | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (\~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is \~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper \~69 B/tool, Anthropic \~40 B, Responses \~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update** `docs/CACHE.md`'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

### Before you start 前置确认

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

Verified prepared-schema hashes, prefix observations and provider-reported cache usage for 13 previously captured real DeepSeek requests. The five source-default requests kept one 6,768-byte tool header, and the eight host-eager requests kept one 12,352-byte header. All observed prefix checks were stable. These receipts contain no eviction intervention, so they cannot establish eviction costs or a net saving. Source 9633c9fafa already measures provider-wire admission and supersedes stale eviction notices. Evidence: toolbox-6969-recorded-wire.json in the October 31 continuation artifacts.

## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**existing functionality measured; savings claim unqualified.**

Verified: Existing bounded read/execute_tools paths retrieved the same three independently seeded values. Controlled serial/composed comparison used4vs2 requests and52202vs22160 wire bytes. Ordinary local Ollama completed both allowed-tool arms in2 requests and never invoked execute_tools.

Remaining: Ordinary planning did not demonstrate a default savings improvement. Arms shared a cache and differed in declared tools; usage/latency cannot establish causation.

Next action: Reconcile the six requested principles to existing consumers and retain the negative ordinary result. Any benefit claim needs matched task/provider/cache intervention; do not build a duplicate reader merely to close the issue.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

### Before you start

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

Significantly reduce context overhead

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

[https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx](<https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx>)

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

### Where? 在哪里？

*No response*

### Workarounds or other tools (optional)

*No response*

### Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this. 我愿意提交 PR。

A scripted local provider requested lines 10–19 of three real files. Both approaches recovered the same three independently seeded values with the same read-only sandbox. Serial reads used four requests, 52,202 total request-body bytes and 4,455 final tool-content bytes. The composed read used two requests, 22,160 total bytes and 501 final tool-content bytes, with three nested calls. No new read tool was required. Model token/cache usage was unreported by the fixture. These are controlled wire measurements and do not qualify ordinary model planning. Evidence: linux-package/reads-6991-q4.json in the October 31 continuation artifacts.

The read-only sandbox, file bytes and prompt are fixed. The serial arm exposes read alone and the composition arm also exposes execute_tools. Capture the actual tools, independently compare the three returned values and record provider-reported input/output usage when available. No source or provider policy change in this run.

November 1 result. The actual Ubuntu ARM64 CLI binary `5996280091ef` returned all three seeded values in order on both ordinary runs. Installed Ollama qwen3:4b requested the three reads together on the first provider request and answered on the second, with or without the VM in its allowed tools. Read-only alone used 4,981 input, 3,431 output and 2,061 cached-input tokens across 23,225 request bytes. Offering execute_tools as well used 6,191 input, 2,437 output and 4,122 cached-input tokens across 29,317 bytes. The model never invoked execute_tools. The runs shared a cache and the read-only arm ran first. The controlled four-versus-two serial comparison does not establish an ordinary planning or latency improvement. Local ACP initialization observed Ask by default and Full Access for both global and post-subcommand --full-access/--yolo forms; 36 focused CLI and 61 focused TUI tests passed in that batch. Managed policy still takes precedence. The reporter's Paseo/Windows retest remains outstanding; per-call ACP elevation is deferred beyond 0.10.3.

---

# ACP regression in 0.10.1: `sandbox_mode` / `ask` from config ignored again — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

## Summary

The ACP posture bug from [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) (fixed in the 0.10.0 nightlies and verified in Paseo) is back in stable **0.10.1**: sessions launched via `codewhale serve --acp` ignore `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `ask = "never"` from `~/.codewhale/config.toml`, and run with the OS sandbox on, network off, and approval gates firing on every shell call.

## Environment

* codewhale **0.10.1** (build `fead51eeea0f`), macOS (Apple Silicon)
* Launched as an ACP provider for the Paseo app (verified: multiple `codewhale serve --acp` processes owned by Paseo)
* `~/.codewhale/config.toml`:

  ```toml
  approval_policy = "suggest"
  sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
  ask = "never"
  ```

## Observed (live session, 2026-10-15)

* `CODEWHALE_SANDBOX=seatbelt` is set in the session environment → the OS sandbox is applied despite `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
* `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind("/tmp/x.sock")'` → `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — the exact [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) signature; this breaks Node test runners and Playwright webServer.
* `ps` → `operation not permitted` (can't even list processes).
* Network is blocked: `curl -sI https://example.com` returns nothing (`000`).
* Every shell call still hits the typed-ask gate and requires a manual approval in the client UI, even though `ask = "never"`. (`gh` could not even read its own config at `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` — EPERM — until the shell was escalated.)
* The policy engine itself agrees these should be skipped: `codewhale sandbox check --ask never 'ls -la /tmp'` → `{"allow": true, "requires_approval": false}`. So the disconnect is between the policy engine and the posture actually applied to live ACP sessions.

## Difference vs the original [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) report

* Writes to `/tmp` now succeed (in 0.9.13 they were EPERM), but AF_UNIX socket creation is still blocked — the one thing Playwright/Node runners need.
* Approval prompts now reach the Paseo UI and can be approved manually (in 0.9.13 they were auto-denied). Still: `ask = "never"` should not gate at all.

## Suspected relation

[#6473](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6473>) (Full Access now requires per-session confirmation) combined with [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>)'s fix ("makes Full Access discoverable **without letting a client select it**") leaves the ACP path with no way to enter Full Access at all. `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` is effectively dead config for Paseo users, and every real workflow — network, sockets, process listing, CLI tools like `gh` — breaks. If per-session confirmation is the intended mechanism, the ACP client needs a way to request/confirm it. Until then this is a regression from the verified-working 0.10.0 nightly.

## Ask

1. Restore config-derived posture for ACP sessions when the client does not pin one, or
2. Expose a Full Access selection/confirmation path to ACP clients (Paseo), or
3. At minimum, honor `ask = "never"` so gated commands skip instead of prompting.

Happy to provide full transcripts or run a nightly/repro build. Greetings from Colombia 🇨🇴

Current 0.10.3 qualification is exercising the shipping ACP stdio entry, the reporter's exact approval settings, CLI opt-in forms, a stricter read-only floor, and local-only socket effects on macOS. No Paseo or Windows result is inferred. Source ownership remains in crates/tui/src/acp_server.rs, its runtime adapter, and the Engine's existing approval/sandbox authority.

Seven macOS source-candidate ACP stdio scenarios passed (binary codewhale-hq/codewhale-app#334 03fcb66028f5aefc7252f99c0357638deb39b008bb8cc421e2c0645299a71e27). The reported suggest/danger-full-access/ask-never config advertised Ask and rejected client-side escalation. A terminal-capable client saw one permission request, denied it and produced no effect. Explicit post-serve --full-access bound a Unix socket and reached a loopback HTTP server with no prompt. Global/post-serve --yolo, config yolo=true, a stricter Plan floor and rejection of approval_policy=never behaved as specified. Ports, provider responses, workspace and account state were local fixtures. Published macOS 0.10.2 independently passed the Ask vs Full Access socket comparison. Paseo and native Windows acceptance remain open.

**Engine repaired; selected client acceptance open.**

### Engine local-catalog slice landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `7c49574a6b` probes unknown Ollama tag capabilities with bounded concurrency, publishes an authoritative catalog only when the probe is complete, and fences automatic adoption against superseded discovery and changed endpoints. Four focused existing checks passed on the shared frozen Engine source; the local discovery checks used synthetic loopback fixtures. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/engine-shared-check-20261028/focused-checks.log`.

Desktop installed-model discovery and a real Ollama interaction have not been requalified with the current app and Engine. The issue remains open; no live-model or release proof is claimed.

## What a new user hits

Fresh desktop app (QA bundle codewhale-app `40766826`, bundled Engine 0.10.2, isolated `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), with Ollama running two tags: `qwen3:4b` (chat) and `nomic-embed-text:latest` (embedding).

1. Composer → **Choose a model** → the **Ollama** chip shows *Ready*; the Model list offers only **Default**.
2. Send "Reply with exactly: DESKTOP-QA-OK" → `Invalid request (400): "nomic-embed-text:latest" does not support chat`, card "Couldn't finish: this model can't chat. Pick another model."
3. **Choose model** again: the list still shows only `nomic-embed-text:latest`; `qwen3:4b` is not offered. The user has to know to expand **More** and type `qwen3:4b` into *Model ID* → **Use** (Return in that field does nothing).

So on the desktop, "Default" for Ollama resolves to an embedding model, and installed chat models are not listed. The TUI on main picks `qwen3:4b` from the same Ollama, using `choose_chat_tag` (`crates/tui/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`, capability `completion`), so the desktop/app-server default path appears to bypass that rule.

Expected: the Ollama default is a chat-capable tag, and the model list shows the installed chat tags from `/api/tags`.

Not yet rechecked against current codewhale-app main + main Engine (build slots were busy); the 0.10.3 desktop bundles a newer Engine.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/jD1-desktop-default-embed-model.jpg`.

## 2026-10-28 current Engine + real local Ollama

A clean-source Engine build matching `bd9d4422ed` was made on macOS (all 4,160 source inputs rehashed unchanged; binary digest `3eb1b93a0614f519c18e0f88811d805f4a0e035f8f2f874ed668b47ba6eebe7f`). In an isolated product home and workspace, with outbound network sandboxed to localhost, the actual local Ollama daemon exposed `qwen3:4b` for completion and `nomic-embed-text:latest` for embedding. Runtime API refresh returned only `qwen3:4b`; switching with no model selected it and persisted it, a new thread used it, and a tiny local turn completed successfully. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/7116-local-ollama-2/receipt.json`. The first harness start failed because its Unix socket path exceeded macOS limits; the shorter retry passed. This is Engine/runtime proof, not current desktop picker or installed-app proof, and the original cause remains unconfirmed. Source review also found that incomplete `/api/show` capability probes fail the authoritative roster refresh and can leave an older roster in place. Keep the issue open.

## Coordinator follow-up — provider verification roster

Claimed canonical Engine `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/provider_setup.rs` and the existing provider-key roster fixture in `crates/tui/src/tui/ui.rs`. Source review found a separate path from the native Ollama refresh: successful generic `/v1/models` key verification can publish untyped entries as an authoritative Ollama roster, including embedding-only ids. The native `/api/tags` plus `/api/show` refresh requires complete capabilities and filters for completion; an incomplete native refresh retains its prior roster. The narrow guard will prevent the generic verification response from overwriting the native roster. This is source-derived, not a reproduced desktop report; previously contaminated caches and installed desktop behavior remain open.

0.10.3 Engine terminal follow-up for #5848 and #7116. A fresh installed 0.10.2 and a current source-built TUI both retained Ollama · unknown after discovery on the configured Ollama route. The installed picker did list the sole chat tag and excluded the embedding tag, and the selected model completed a real turn. Working in the shared TUI startup/adoption policy in crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs and its existing provider-route checks. Desktop and installed-candidate acceptance remain separate.

Main a595ca40c88179d519626c17856a56b517ba0351 repairs TUI cold startup and retry of an unresolved selected Ollama route. Published 0.10.2 and prior main had left the label unknown. The repaired cold TUI picked qwen3:4b, excluded nomic-embed-text, answered 9+7 with 16 and persisted it. A separate actual private daemon started after the TUI, had an empty roster and then only an embedding model; both kept the model unknown. Adding a real chat tag and selecting /provider ollama resolved the model and restart retained it. Artifacts ollama-main-after/receipt.json and ollama-late-q4/receipt.json. The Desktop report needs the selected client’s own journey.

November 1 Engine acceptance. Checking the desktop’s existing HTTP routes on an isolated App Server with the real local Ollama chat and embedding models. Scope is the provider catalog, native refresh, default thread admission and completed-turn receipts in `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs` and `crates/engine/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`. Record the exact executable and distinguish this from observing the Electron picker.

The desktop-facing Engine HTTP path passed on an isolated macOS App Server. Native Ollama reported one completion model (`qwen3:4b`) and one embedding model. The first-open and refreshed catalogs contained exactly the chat model. Creating a thread with `model_provider_id=ollama` and no model selected `qwen3:4b` before an explicit refresh. The real local chat endpoint received that same model and the terminal assistant item was exactly `DESKTOP-QA-OK`. The five relevant Engine/App Server source files match current main byte for byte. The executable under test was the frozen source build with executable digest prefix `1313ae509f95`. This covers the Engine API. The selected Electron client’s own picker remains open.

Follow-up from the terminal reproduction of #5848. Holding the native `/api/tags` reply during `/provider ollama` on an already selected, unresolved local route blocked composer echo for the full 12-second observation. Claiming `crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs`, `tui/app/init.rs`, `tui/ui/apply.rs` and `tui/ui/event_loop.rs` under `crates/tui/src`. Reuse the existing ticketed discovery task so the terminal stays usable, preserves the unresolved state on failure and rechecks the active route before adopting a result.

Engine [ccf211dc5f](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ccf211dc5fad21f132923c07e55f20a39943fb06>) keeps an explicit retry on the already selected unresolved local Ollama route responsive. On an Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 terminal with `/api/tags` held for 4.85 s, the baseline had no input echo within 1.25 s. The candidate displayed the typed marker in 45 ms. Failed discovery preserved the unresolved label, a late success preserved the interacted provider picker and its highlight, and the next deliberate retry selected `qwen3:4b`. Both builds passed the authenticated route control. The Electron picker remains open.

A real local Auto turn saved `qwen3:4b` and the answer 16. When the daemon subsequently served 32,768 context tokens, the second turn still used the 8,192-token fallback and refused before making another chat request. Investigating the active local inventory, served-context observation and admission in `crates/engine/src/model_routing.rs`, `provider_lake.rs` and the existing fixed-route callers.

Engine [f774358892](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/f774358892faa5c65b2b540cedb1eca30587ad30>) qualified Auto on the active keyless local Ollama route. With the same model files, fresh private Ollama 0.40.11 daemons and Ubuntu ARM64 terminals, prior main made one chat request, answered 16, then refused turn two using its 8,192-token fallback even though the daemon independently reported 32,768. The candidate saved three answers, 16, 17 and 18. The first turn used the cold fallback, the second observed the 32,768-token served window, and the third reused it without a catalog request. Another process kept its configured 24,576-token window. Its ordinary Auto preview made zero network requests. The source-built macOS App Server and Ubuntu terminal have separate receipts. The selected Electron picker and the final release package remain open.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**source fixes landed; incident evidence open.**

Verified: Automatic-off recovery guard 7b54e7f572 and original PR #7180 merge 00226bbfbb8 retain exact ancestry; 42 focused checks and repeated-input macOS PTY cover that specific defect. Source also emits reroot/resume/compaction lifecycle records.

Remaining: The reported long-session Windows seam is not reproduced. Root-count alone includes preserved alternate branches and does not prove the actual prepared request omitted distinct authored turns.

Next action: Capture sanitized before/after journal plus prepared model request, route/window/usage and compaction-state ledger at the seam; qualify retained ancestry and visible seam behavior.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Landed setting fix — 2026-10-29

Engine main/origin commit 7b54e7f5724daa88ed29b6479f8ea0b7cf353b0c fixes the concrete automatic-off bypass. Preflight/provider overflow recovery now refuses before summary/start/replacement when compaction is disabled, retains original messages and records an actionable typed refusal through the existing audit/error owners. Both overflow paths preserve the recovery failure's actual cause; cancellation takes priority after the awaited recovery. Explicit manual compaction remains available.

Local proof: initial libtest compile and137focused compaction/error/Engine checks passed. After the final model-step cancellation guard, libtest recompiled and69affected Engine/recovery/cancellation checks passed; unchanged pure-check evidence is retained. The renamed existing emergency fixture covers disabled-but-compactable and enabled-but-unnecessary history, zero model calls/attempts, unchanged messages and one typed refusal. Format, boundary, blocking budget569sites169files, dead-code164, changelog/facts and diff checks pass. No new test functions/comments. Exact receipts: artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029/compaction-off-landing-verification.json. Source files are released, not held for another build.

Keep this issue and public Engine7142 open. The setting bypass is established and repaired, but it does not explain every reported Windows seam or complete the remaining lifecycle/continuity acceptance. A read-only local Mac journal inspection did not reproduce the reported multi-root shape; that does not prove no context loss or disprove the reporter's sample. No real-provider, hosted CI, Windows/installed/device or release proof is claimed.

---

## Summary

A session's live `messages` window can be re-rooted partway through a conversation. When
that happens, every `journal` entry before the new root becomes unreachable to the model
while the on-disk journal keeps it in full. The window stays internally consistent — it
equals its own new branch exactly — so nothing looks truncated from the inside.

Three things are missing at the moment it happens:

* **no summary entry at the seam.** The new root is a bare `kind: "message"` with
  `parent_id: null`; the entry immediately before it is an ordinary turn on the branch
  that was just abandoned. Real compaction leaves a condensed account of what it replaced.
  This leaves a copy and a hole.
* **no marker in the interface.** No banner, no notice, no error.
* **no session-lifecycle event in** `audit.log`**.** In 8,792 events across five event types,
  every one is `tool.approval.*` or `tool.gate.decision`. Nothing announces that the model's
  working context was replaced.

`settings.toml` has `auto_compact = false` and `auto_compact_threshold_percent = 80.0`
throughout. If this is compaction, the setting is not describing what the runtime does.

## Environment

* `codewhale --version`: **0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)** — verified against the binary
* OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), PowerShell 5.1
* Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` (provider `deepseek`)
* Install: npm global; `~/.codewhale/{config,settings,permissions}.toml`, no `[compaction]`
  block and no `retained_user_message_tokens` in `config.toml`
* Reproduces on **0.10.1 and 0.10.2**

## What it looks like

Dump of four consecutive documents from this host. `entries` = `journal.entries`;
`window` = `len(messages)`; `root` = the journal index the live branch starts at.

```
created (UTC)        window  entries  root   coverage
2026-10-28T13:08:15     944      986     1      99.9%   <- intact (benign doubled opening)
2026-10-28T15:24:44     632     1639   987      39.8%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T07:11:22     403      473    50      89.4%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T08:20:46      61      325   259      20.3%   <- re-rooted (this one, mid-report)
```

The seam itself, from `2026-10-29T07:11:22`:

```
[48] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y     3970 chars
[49] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=Y     1362 chars
[50] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=NONE  2054 chars   <- window begins here
[51] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y      360 chars
```

Prose for scale: the `journal` for that session holds 473 entries; the model could see 403
of them. The boot turn, including the whole startup sequence, was gone from the window and
present on disk.

## Prevalence on this host, and an onset date

87 session documents were parsed structurally. `journal` + `leaf_id` on this host arrives
between 11 and 12 Aug 2026 (before that, documents carry `artifacts` and no journal, so this
signature cannot exist and cannot be tested — that period is **untestable, not clean**).

| period | sessions | shape |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 12 Aug – 17 Oct 2026 | 47 | one branch root, window == journal, 100% reachable |
| 18 Oct – 29 Oct 2026 | 40 | two or three roots; **15 re-rooted mid-session** |

The onset boundary is narrow: `…d6832ea3` (17 Oct 18:33:49Z) is clean at 113/113;
`…021a7d6a` (18 Oct 01:46:51Z) is the first re-root at 962 window / 1045 entries.

Across the 15 mid-session re-roots, the root lands at journal indices 8, 20, 30, 50, 67, 97,
160, 259, 295, 347, 367, 472, 733, 987. Post-re-root coverage ranges from **14.1%** to
89.4%; combined unreachable entries **3,909**.

**In 0 of 87 sessions is the window shorter than its own branch.** This is not truncation —
the window is always a complete branch. The branch is simply no longer the session.

## Reproduction

No special configuration; it appears on ordinary long sessions. A read-only probe against
any session document:

```python
import json, hashlib

doc = json.load(open(PATH, encoding="utf-8"))
msgs, entries = doc["messages"], doc["journal"]["entries"]

by_id = {e["id"]: i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if e.get("id")}
chain, seen, cur = [], set(), len(entries) - 1
while cur is not None and cur not in seen:
    seen.add(cur); chain.append(cur)
    cur = by_id.get(entries[cur].get("parent_id"))

root = min(chain)
print("window", len(msgs), "branch", len(chain),
      "root", root, "coverage %.1f%%" % (100 * (len(entries) - root) / len(entries)))
```

* `window == branch` and `root <= 1` → healthy (a root at 1 is the benign doubled opening;
  do not flag it — see *What I got wrong*, below).
* `root > 1` → the window re-rooted mid-session. `root` entries are unreachable.

To inspect a seam, print `entries[root-2 : root+2]` and check for anything summary-shaped.
On this host there is never one.

## How this differs from the nearby open reports

* [#6842](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6842>) (journal has no bound; compaction retires live messages but keeps superseded
  versions in RAM) names the same underlying machinery and is about **memory growth**. This
  report is about **model visibility**: the earlier turns were not merely retained
  redundantly, they became unreachable while the record survived. Different harm, possibly
  the same call site.
* #7133 (automatic compression at \~40% against an 80% setting) is the closest
  behavioural neighbour and may share a cause — it reports the *threshold* being wrong,
  where this reports a *silent re-root with no summary*. Worth triaging together.
* #7095 (history lost, labelled v0.10.3) is a different fault: there the record does not
  survive because the last save did not flush. Here every byte survives and is correct, and
  only the window is replaced.

## What I am asking for

In order of value, and each is independently useful:

1. **Emit a session-lifecycle event.** `session.opened`, `session.window.rerooted`,
   `session.compacted`, `session.resumed` — with both sizes and a reason, into `audit.log`
   beside the existing `tool.*` events. This is the smallest change and it converts an
   unexplained amnesia into a dated, attributable event. It is worth having **even if the**
   **re-root turns out to be intended**, so please do not let the other two asks gate it.
2. **Honour** `auto_compact = false`**, or rename it.** A setting that says compaction is off
   while the window is replaced is worse than no setting: it is a claim the operator can
   rely on and cannot verify.
3. **If a window re-root is intended, summarise at the seam.** A bounded, visible,
   summarised compaction is a feature. An unannounced re-root that leaves a bare copy of an
   existing message is a data-visibility defect.

## What I have not established, and will not guess at

**The trigger.** Observed re-roots span 78 to 1639 journal entries, 11 to 1437 window
messages, and roughly 1.3 MB to 5 MB of document. That spread is inconsistent with a single
simple threshold, and two documents is not a sample. It could be turn count, cumulative
tokens, document size, wall clock, or a path that only runs on resume.

**Whether it is intended.** [#5262](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5262>) (closed, shipped v0.9.5) specifies an append-only journal
forest where branching "only moves the leaf — it never rewrites history", so multiple roots
are expected by that design and a re-root is legal in that model. What is not
design-legible is doing it silently, mid-session, with no summary, while
`auto_compact = false`.

## What I got wrong on the way here

Recorded because it is the reason this report is careful, and because a maintainer deserves
to know which tests have already failed.

My first pass used a **positional** test — does `messages[0]` start where `journal.entries[0]`
starts — and produced two confident wrong answers in one morning: first "41 of 93 sessions
lost turns", then, over-correcting, "nothing was lost at all". The positional test fires on
the benign doubled opening, which is why I checked a session minutes old and never restarted
before trusting any number here. The figures above come from a **membership** test: walk the
branch by `parent_id` and ask whether the window can reach every entry its own session wrote.

If this report is wrong, it is wrong in the direction of under-claiming: 15 measured re-roots
on one host, with the mechanism named and the unknowns listed.

---

*Reproduction and evidence kept locally. Happy to provide sanitised session documents or run*
*any probe upstream asks for.*

October 31 continuation. Codex is reviewing contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 and the #7178 bare/stamped history reproducer against the current Engine. Claimed paths are crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs, crates/models/src/turn_classify.rs, crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs and the TUI send/snapshot paths as needed. Verify preservation of authored text, turn authority, sibling history and single-send behavior. The related Windows incident remains open until its own acceptance is established.

The contributor head c80c16c14a on original Engine PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 has 42 focused checks and a macOS PTY receipt. Two deliberate identical submissions yielded two requests and two answers on one intact active path. GitHub's base-branch policy blocked a normal merge. The Windows incident and the wider session window investigation remain open.

Original contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 merged normally as 00226bbfbb8e421e93dfcf9730f48413aeb10385. Its final head 0079c86058849dfba17105948a28e3084cb432ba resolved only release-note conflicts. The verified Rust changes retain stable patch ID b6620900da6e16abc104326d2061fdd5776b10a0. The live macOS repeated-input receipt and 42 focused tests cover the specific journal defect. Issue #7178 remains open for Windows acceptance, and this wider re-root report retains its separate recovery gates.

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Two original observability items are implemented; the two explicitly remaining acceptance items remain missing.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **live-tokens — source complete:** TurnUsage accrues display-only pending input/output/cache tokens; authoritative turn completion clears/reconciles. Carrying source: [59a1d317f1](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/59a1d317f196e653181f74c1362f30e6b573a0e6), [f7a5c519d1](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/f7a5c519d14de72d0a29813861fc64f98df78510).
- **worked — source complete:** Phase strip adds cumulative_turn_duration and live elapsed; persistent cumulative seconds remain separate.
- **cache-steps — implementation missing:** TurnCacheRecord remains one completed-turn row; event_loop pushes it at TurnComplete. Per-step TurnUsage updates metrics and pending counters, not per-call cache history/spread.
- **midturn-persist — implementation missing:** sync_cost_to_metadata persists settled totals and cumulative completed duration, not pending_turn cost/tokens. Durable per-call Runtime usage is useful evidence, but no equivalent session pending-counter restore/reconcile path is established here.

**Next action:** Finish cache-call projection and exact-identity pending usage checkpoint/reconciliation; retain the two already-complete items and contributor credit.

Current owner: [CW-6234](https://linear.app/shannonlabs/issue/CW-6234).

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against v0.9.11 (filed 2026-08-23).
>
> **What remains**
> - Per-step visibility in `/cache`: either per-model-call rows or a per-turn min/max cache-hit spread, fed from the per-call TurnUsage receipts (record built at crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:3174)
> - Mid-turn checkpoint of pending token/cost counters into session metadata (crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs save path near :4440) so a crash in a long turn keeps that turn's usage, reconciled without double counting at TurnComplete
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Item 1 (live session token totals) done: commits 59a1d317f1 / merge f7a5c519d1 (PR #5624); pending counters at crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:1130-1135, folded into displayed totals at :1418-1423
> - Item 2 (worked chip) done: the chip is finished-turn total plus the live turn - crates/tui/src/tui/phase_strip.rs:854-856 (doc) and :883-885 (`cumulative_turn_duration.saturating_add(turn.unwrap_or_default())`)
> - Item 3 (/cache rows) not done: one TurnCacheRecord is pushed per completed turn - crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:3174; struct at crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:359 has no per-call rows
> - Item 4 (mid-turn persistence) not done in session metadata: the save path writes settled totals and cumulative_turn_secs only - crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:4440-4462; pending counters are display-only and cleared at :1408
> - Related mitigation: per-call usage receipts are written by the runtime and read by `codewhale metrics` - commit 666f4075a6 (c11); this does not restore the session's own totals after a mid-turn crash

---

Follow-up to #5578 (cost fixed) and the same user report: with turns spanning many model calls, anything that only updates at `TurnComplete` reads as frozen. Audited 2026-08-23; findings ordered by value.

## Already live (no action)
- **Cost** — fixed in #5578 (per-step `TurnUsage` priced into a pending estimate).
- **Subagent/background cost** — `cost_status::drain()` sweeps every loop tick.
- **Timing metrics strip** — folds per-step `TurnUsage` already.
- **Context meter** — live-estimate driven; its trigger-mismatch question is #5577.

## Stalled at TurnComplete (candidates)
1. **Session token totals** (`total_tokens`, `total_input/output_tokens`, cache-class totals in the sidebar) — accrue only in the `TurnComplete` handler (`event_loop.rs` ~1615-1655). Live source exists: the same per-step `TurnUsage` receipts. Apply the exact #5578 pattern: display-only pending token counters, cleared at `TurnComplete` before the authoritative cumulative usage lands. Mechanical; the quickest win here.
2. **'worked Nh Mm' chip** — `cumulative_turn_duration` rolls up only at turn end; mid-turn the chip understates by the whole current turn. `turn_started_at` is available: display cumulative + live elapsed.
3. **`/cache` table rows** — one `TurnCacheRecord` per turn is by design, but a 50-call turn collapses all cache behavior into one row. `TurnUsage` carries per-call cache classes; consider optional per-step rows or a per-turn min/max spread.
4. **Session persistence** — metadata (cost, tokens) persists at turn boundaries; a crash mid-giant-turn loses that turn's telemetry entirely. Consider a periodic mid-turn checkpoint of the pending counters.

## Principle (from the Codex comparison)
A turn is the unit of *conversation*; it must not be the unit of *observability*. Every user-facing meter should update from per-model-call receipts; `TurnComplete` reconciles, it does not reveal.

Tracker: #5573. Related: #5577, #5578, #5580 (reducer refactor is the natural home for these handlers).

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Prepared request is shared and Moonshot stopgap exists; the accepted general projection layer remains absent.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **canonical — source complete existing seam:** PreparedOutboundRequest is consumed by preview and dispatch, retaining canonical catalog provider neutrality.
- **moonshot-stopgap — source complete stopgap:** Moonshot sanitizer drops incompatible tools and uses omitted_tool_names in prepared result. This is expressly documented as stopgap, not general projection.
- **general-projection — implementation missing:** PreparedOutboundRequest has omitted names but no general per-tool projection outcome table. Moonshot/xAI compatibility remains in individual request-builder branches.
- **deferred — implementation missing:** No shared tool projection result is threaded through discovery/deferred state. Existing route-shaped body alone does not reconcile advertised catalog.
- **diagnostics — partial:** Bounded omitted-name warning exists; full outcome diagnostic parity across every caller depends on the general projection result. Never log raw schemas/values.

**Next action:** Implement one typed projection result in existing request preparation and migrate all actual builder/deferred/preview consumers; no new catalog, host-layer projection or cache before the typed seam.

Current owner: [CW-6256](https://linear.app/shannonlabs/issue/CW-6256).

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Problem

Provider routes accept different tool-schema subsets and sometimes require different wire shapes. Today those compatibility decisions live inside individual request builders. That can make the wire tool list, `tool_choice`, deferred/tool-search discovery, request preview, and user diagnostics disagree. It also gives one incompatible tool a much larger blast radius than necessary.

## Suggested direction

Consider a route-specific tool projection seam in the CodeWhale request-preparation layer (not in an embedding app):

- Keep the canonical tool catalog unchanged.
- Project that catalog for the resolved provider route into a small typed result containing the wire tools, a reconciled `tool_choice`, and bounded diagnostics.
- Let request preview and actual dispatch consume the same projection result.
- Represent compatibility outcomes explicitly (for example: exact, safely relaxed, or omitted) so deferred/tool-search surfaces can avoid advertising a tool that the active route cannot send, or can at least explain that state.
- Keep user-facing diagnostics privacy-bounded: tool names and outcome codes are useful; raw schemas and schema values are not.

The exact type, cache/fingerprint strategy, and how tool search should consume projection state are intentionally left open for maintainer input.

## Why this belongs upstream

This is provider-routing and request-lifecycle behavior shared by every host. Implementing it in an app layer would duplicate CodeWhale's tool catalog and could still drift from the final provider request.

## Current stopgap

[PR #5636](https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/5636) proposes a narrow Moonshot fix: omit only MFJS-incompatible tools, reconcile named `tool_choice`, and surface a typed warning. That PR should remain a stopgap rather than growing into the general projection layer.

## Non-goal

This issue is a design direction, not a complete implementation proposal or an implementation commitment from the downstream fork.

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Manual skill creation is present; the proposed continuous learning feature is not built.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **manual-existing — source complete existing workflow:** skills command maps new to bundled skill-creator; this remains an explicit user-directed skill-authoring workflow.
- **pattern-detection — implementation missing:** No production occurrence threshold, pattern detection or correction-to-skill pipeline exists in the searched owners.
- **generation-approval — implementation missing:** Manual skill-creator is not automatic generation with confidence/occurrence policy and ratification. No suggest/approve/reject learning command flow exists.
- **evolution — implementation missing:** No learned-skill evolution/version history/merge or confidence pruning authority is present.
- **cross-session-controls — implementation missing:** Proposed learning config fields/learning history controls are absent. Existing session/skill discovery is not cross-session learning.

**Next action:** Root confirms current release admission and assigns the existing Backlog issue. If retained, implement the explicit suggest+preview+approve first phase over existing Skills owner; preserve all later evolution/privacy scope as unfinished.

Current owner: [CW-6300](https://linear.app/shannonlabs/issue/CW-6300).

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Problem
CodeWhale has a powerful Skills System where users can manually create `SKILL.md` files that the agent can reference. However, the knowledge remains static:

1. **No automatic pattern extraction** - The agent doesn't recognize when it's solving the same type of problem repeatedly
2. **No skill evolution** - When a user provides corrections or better approaches, the agent doesn't update existing skills
3. **No cross-session learning** - Lessons learned in one session don't automatically improve future sessions
4. **Manual overhead** - Users must proactively identify patterns and write skills themselves, which breaks flow

**Example**: A developer builds 3 FastAPI endpoints with MongoDB over a week. Each time, they go through similar steps (configure connection, create models, implement CRUD, add error handling, write tests). The agent executes these steps each time but never "learns" that this is a repeatable pattern worth codifying as a skill.

## Proposed Solution
Implement a **self-learning loop** that automatically observes, extracts, and codifies patterns from successful interactions:

#### Core Components:

**1. Pattern Detection Engine**
- Monitor dialog history for repeated solution patterns
- Identify multi-step workflows that occur 3+ times
- Detect corrections and incorporate them into skills
- Track successful outcomes vs. failures

**2. Automated Skill Generation**
- Create `SKILL.md` files based on detected patterns
- Generate structured YAML frontmatter with:
  - Name, description, version
  - Step-by-step instructions
  - Common pitfalls (learned from corrections)
  - Usage examples from real dialog
  - Confidence scores based on success rate

**3. Skill Evolution System**
- Update existing skills when better approaches are discovered
- Merge related skills into more comprehensive ones
- Archive unused or low-confidence skills
- Version tracking with change history

**4. Learning Triggers**

```toml
# Example configuration
[learning]
auto_create_skills = true          # Default: false (requires confirmation)
confidence_threshold = 0.8          # Only auto-create if pattern confidence > 80%
pattern_occurrence_threshold = 3    # Pattern must appear 3+ times
enable_cross_session_learning = true
skill_review_frequency = "weekly"   # Suggest reviewing skills periodically
```

**5. User Control & Transparency**

- Preview suggested skills before creation (/suggest-skills)
- Approve/deny skill creation (/approve-skill fastapi-crud)
- Review learning history (/learning-history)
- Manual override and pruning (/delete-skill old-pattern, /merge-skills)

## Use Case

Scenario: A development team building a FastAPI + React + MCP application over 6 months:

Month 1: Manual Mode

- Developers work with CodeWhale, solving problems

- Agent silently observes patterns but doesn't act

- Team reviews /suggest-skills weekly and creates the most useful ones manually

Month 2-3: Semi-Automated Mode

- Agent automatically creates skills for patterns with 90%+ confidence

- Team reviews and approves skills weekly

- Skills begin covering 40% of repetitive tasks

Month 4-6: Fully Automated Mode

- Agent creates, updates, and merges skills autonomously

- Skills cover 80% of repetitive patterns

- Development speed increases 2-3x for common tasks

Specific Example:

```text
Session 1: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth"
Session 2: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth and role-based permissions"
Session 3: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth, roles, and rate limiting"

→ Agent detects the pattern and creates skill "fastapi-jwt-crud"
→ Future request: "Build user management API" 
→ Agent uses the skill, saving 30 minutes of work
→ User adds "also needs email verification" 
→ Agent updates the skill with email verification step
→ Next team member gets the improved skill automatically
```

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Pros | Cons |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Manual Skills** | Full control, simple to implement | High overhead, knowledge loss between sessions |
| **Third-party Learning Tools** | Could use external ML | Integration complexity, additional dependencies |
| **Prompt-based Learning** | Simple to implement | Temporary, lost between sessions |
| **MCP-based Learning** | Extensible, modular | Requires separate MCP server, not built-in |


This proposal leverages CodeWhale's existing infrastructure (skills, hooks, MCP) while adding intelligence on top, keeping everything integrated and user-friendly.

## Impact 

This feature would transform CodeWhale from a static assistant into an adaptive pair programmer that grows with its users. It's technically feasible using CodeWhale's existing infrastructure (skills, hooks, MCP) and would provide immense value to both individual developers and teams.

For Individual Developers:

- ⚡ 2-3x faster for repetitive coding tasks

- 🧠 Preserves knowledge - don't need to remember every best practice

- 🔄 Continuous improvement - your assistant gets smarter every day

For Teams:

- 📚 Shared knowledge base - skills become team documentation

- 🎯 Consistent code quality - best practices automatically enforced

- 🚀 Faster onboarding - new members learn patterns through skills

For the CodeWhale Project:

- 🏆 Unique competitive advantage - no other open-source agent has this

- 🌟 Stronger community - users will share their learned skills

- 📈 Increased adoption - teams will choose CodeWhale for the learning capability

Metrics to Track:

- Number of skills created automatically vs. manually

- Time saved per task (before/after learning)

- Skill usage rates and success rates

- User satisfaction scores



## Additional context

### Why Now?

- The skills system is already built - this adds the "learning" layer

- MCP provides the perfect hook for pattern detection

- Users are already asking for smarter assistants

#### Potential Challenges & Mitigations:

- False positives → Confidence thresholds and human approval (especially initially)

- Skill bloat → Automatic archiving and merging of similar skills

- Security → Version control and rollback for skills, opt-in feature with clear controls

### Implementation Phases (Suggestion)

#### Phase 1: Pattern Detection (MVP)

- Add /suggest-skills command that analyzes current session

- Show proposed skill template for user approval

- Implement via MCP server (external)

#### Phase 2: Automated Creation

- Detect patterns without prompting

- Auto-create skills with configurable confidence threshold

- Add /approve-skill and /reject-skill commands

#### Phase 3: Evolution

- Update skills when corrections are detected

- Merge related skills automatically

- Track skill usage and confidence scores

#### Phase 4: Cross-Session Learning

- Share learned skills across all projects

- Aggregate best practices from multiple sessions

- Privacy controls for sensitive code

### Example

```bash
$ codewhale

> Build a FastAPI endpoint for user registration with email validation

[Agent builds the feature through 8 steps]

> Now build a product listing endpoint

[Agent notices pattern...]

🧠 I've noticed you're building FastAPI CRUD endpoints with validation.
   I've seen this pattern 3 times this week.

   Would you like me to create a skill called "fastapi-crud-with-validation"? [y/n] y

✅ Skill created! It includes:
   - MongoDB connection setup
   - Pydantic model generation
   - CRUD endpoint implementation
   - Email validation pattern
   - Error handling best practices

   Type `/skill fastapi-crud-with-validation` to use it next time.

[Next week...]

> Build a blog post API

💡 I see you're building FastAPI CRUD again. Using skill: fastapi-crud-with-validation
   [Executes in 3 steps instead of 8, with best practices applied]

> Also add category filtering

🔄 I've added category filtering to the skill. This will be available for future tasks.
```

>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Shortlist toggle shipped: `toggle_fleet_model` is 'the picker's one-key toggle' editing only explicit shortlist rows (crates/tui/src/fleet/members.rs:365-372); docs/FLEET.md:136 documents `⇧F` in `/model`, and docs/FLEET.md:123-135 documents `/fleet models`, `/fleet add`, `/fleet remove`.
> - Storage differs from the proposal: the shortlist is `shortlist = true` rows in the selected fleet file, not a `[fleet] models` config key (docs/FLEET.md:114-121, :127; crates/tui/src/fleet/identity.rs:560-613). No `[fleet] models` key exists in docs/FLEET.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md or config.example.toml at v0.10.1.
> - Spawn constraint shipped: an off-list model is refused with the list in the message — 'Requested model is outside the selected Fleet. Available routes: {choices}. Use action=roster' (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:16511-16531); ambiguity across providers is refused at :16535-16537.
> - Operator awareness shipped as an on-demand tool result, not a stable prompt block: `agent(action=roster)` returns `models` rows from `fleet_models()` plus saved `profiles` (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:11537-11563), each with route provider/model, context_window, capability_badges, cost_class (mod.rs:16901-16913).
> - Reachability is not actually checked: the roster row hardcodes `"reachability": "unverified"` (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:16913).
> - No prompt-level fleet block: `git grep -iE 'fleet models|fleet_models|your fleet' v0.10.1 -- crates/tui/src/prompts crates/tui/src/prompts.rs crates/core/src` returns nothing.

---

## Founder direction (2026-09-06)

> we still need to make it so we are making like a shortlist of models that the user wants to be considered for sub agents — the flow from provider → model → model shortlist (that becomes the fleet models for the operator to choose from and assign roles, and then a user can choose if they want to save that model in that role) — and we want that + the manual configuration.

Plus the standing goals this serves: truly model-agnostic, cache-maxxing, and the working model being aware of every model in its fleet.

## What exists today (receipts)

- Fleet profiles already persist a provider, model, and thinking setting per role (#4137, #5042), and `roster.model_overrides()` plus `config.subagent_model_overrides()` are merged into the subagent runtime's `role_models` at launch (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs` ~11964, `tools/subagent/mod.rs` ~12914).
- `[subagents] providers.<name>` carries per-provider fan-out and budget knobs (`config.rs` ~2725) but no model list.
- The spawn `model` parameter is validated per provider (`normalize_requested_subagent_model`) but the operator is never told which concrete models it may pick; the prompt only documents `model_strength`.
- The model picker shows the live catalog per provider; there is no "consider this for the fleet" mark, so the only way to a role→model binding is editing a Fleet profile or TOML.

## Proposed flow

1. **Provider** — connected providers (exists).
2. **Model** — the live catalog for that provider (exists).
3. **Shortlist** (new) — in the model picker, a one-key toggle marks a model "fleet". Persisted as `[fleet] models = ["provider/model", ...]` in config; the same list is editable by hand. Entries are `provider/model` ids resolved through the model registry, so nothing is provider-specific.
4. **Roles** (extend) — at spawn time the operator sees the shortlist as *fleet models* and assigns one per role; the `model` parameter is constrained to the shortlist (plus the session model) and the error for an off-list model names the list. In the Agents view, a role row offers "save this model in this role", which writes the existing Fleet profile — no second store.
5. **Manual configuration** stays authoritative: `[subagents.roles.<role>] model = "provider/model"` and Fleet profiles win over the shortlist; the shortlist is what the operator may choose from when nothing is pinned.

## Operator awareness and cache

- The subagent tool description (or a stable system-prompt block) lists the fleet models with the tags the registry already knows: strength tier, context window, price class, and whether the route is currently reachable. Stable ordering, rebuilt only when the shortlist or a pin changes, so the block is prefix-cache friendly.
- When the shortlist is empty the block says so and the operator falls back to today's `model_strength` behaviour.

## Acceptance

- Toggle a model in the picker → it appears in `[fleet] models` and in `/fleet` as a fleet model; remove it → it disappears from both.
- Operator spawn with a shortlisted model succeeds on any provider; an off-list model is refused with the list in the message.
- "Save in role" from the Agents view produces the same Fleet profile a manual TOML edit would, and the next session spawns that role on that model without the operator choosing.
- The operator prompt/tool description shows every fleet model with its tags; snapshot test pins the block and its ordering.
- Narrow terminal and localized labels covered like the rest of the picker.

## Out of scope

Automatic model routing or pricing decisions (`--model auto` stays as is); provider onboarding; any change to how a single-session model is chosen.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Local metrics and durable worker receipts cover useful slices; requested global stats/reporting contract is not implemented.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **A-component — partial:** Live context inspector already shows system prompt/tool schema costs, but not a complete persisted exact latest-wire component/history/tool-result/reasoning ledger report.
- **stats-default — implementation missing:** CLI defines metrics with json/since only. Rollup has tool/compaction/agent/capacity/credential/runtime-request aggregates, not the requested stats contract.
- **models — implementation missing:** Provider/model information exists on turn receipts but no requested global per-model rows or --models selection.
- **cache — partial:** TurnCacheRecord and parent/agent rates exist; requested global cache-cause/rebuild view is absent.
- **tools — partial:** metrics ToolStats counts calls/success/failure/denial/duration. Context-token sinks, spool/replay share, repeated signatures and retry recovery analytics are missing.
- **compaction — partial:** Existing metrics records compaction events/triggers/summarizer tokens and reduction ratios. This is not the full attributable cost/history-drop ledger requested. Carrying source: [666f4075a6](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/666f4075a601e51795dd1d402dcaba09924d6e3e), [51849b93ce](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/51849b93ce87d315cd4f7a640b72276b175f59cb).
- **project-flags — implementation missing:** metrics accepts since/json; no --days/--models/--tools/--project contract or project aggregation.
- **roles-workers — partial:** Measured durable per-worker usage is exposed via agent_get/list and metrics agent outcomes, with unknown preserved. Per-role/custom-role global grouping and full failure/recovery report are absent. Carrying source: [7a1d1cab1f](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/7a1d1cab1f736f3167caee2010eec204372c3e87).
- **local-only — criterion satisfied source:** metrics run reads resolved local audit/session/runtime stores and prints locally. The founder explicitly confirmed local CLI/TUI diagnostics remain telemetry-optional; do not replace this requirement with hosted D14 analytics.

**Next action:** Resolve current admission/owner, then extend the existing local metrics/report owner and its receipt producers; do not create a parallel reporting store or treat hosted telemetry as completion.

The former Linear packet CW-6361 stays Canceled. The October 31 founder instruction replans Engine work against App Server v2; cancellation is neither proof of implementation nor an implicit removal of this public requirement. Current release routing must be recorded in the Core plan. No canceled packet was reopened.

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Combined Core execution: C11

[Core execution plan](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/document/codewhale-core-execution-plan-a11e2e1c601d>) owns order and scope. This issue contributes to C11; the linked plan owns the complete packet and any outstanding candidate acceptance. Record this issue's path claims and implementation evidence here.

**Owner: diagnostics owner. Dependencies: C00; coordinate domain paths**
  **with C03/C08.** Finish
  [SHA-6414 / GitHub #6011](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6414/feattui-usage-and-tool-diagnostics-token-accounting-per-component-per>)'s seven admitted areas:
  component/model/cache/tool/compaction/fleet/error diagnostics and persistence.
  Credit existing counters and the retained usage-checkpoint implementation;
  neither covers the full request. Implement against the current owning domain
  and migrate the consumer with that domain, not a second reporting store.

**Completion evidence required:** every requested area has attributable receipts, persistence
  and presentation tests; unknown usage/cost remains unknown; actual provider
  charges are not inferred from estimates or completion timestamps.

---

## Original issue and contributor history

## Problem

Session cost and context are a black box. In-session surfaces exist (`/tokens`, `/cost`, `/context report`, the TUI Context panel) but they are **session-scoped and live only**: after the session ends there is no way to answer "where did my tokens/cache/money go over the last week", "which model is burning cache", or "which tool calls fail constantly". When a session eats 2M tokens you cannot tell whether it was replayed `read` output, cache-thrashing tool-schema churn, thinking spend, or a model re-running the same failing tool call. When the model "keeps making the same mistake" there is no report that names the tool + error signature so you can fix the tool description or the global `AGENTS.md`.

Affected: everyone who debugs token spend, tunes prompt-cache layout, or wants data-driven fixes to tool descriptions / `AGENTS.md`.

## Proposed solution

A global CLI `codewhale stats` that aggregates **persisted session data** (already on disk — see code refs) into token/cost/cache/tool reports, mirroring `opencode stats`:

```
codewhale stats [--days N] [--models N] [--tools N] [--project <id>]
```

* `--days N` — window (default: all time)
* `--models N` — top-N model usage breakdown (default: all)
* `--tools N` — top-N tool usage (default: all)
* `--project <id>` — filter by project/worktree

Report sections (mirroring opencode, plus improvements):

**A. Request composition (per-session, best-effort)**

1. **Per-component breakdown of the latest request**: system prompt, tool schemas (wire payload), message history, tool results, reasoning/ledger — mirroring VTCode's `token_budget_breakdown` and Claude Code's `/context`. Uses the existing conservative estimator (`estimate_input_tokens_conservative`); no tokenizer dependency required for the first pass.

**B. Lifetime accounting (global)**
2\. **Per-model usage + cost + cache hit rate**: input / output / cache read / cache write + $ per model + **hit rate %** (`cache_read/(cache_read+input+cache_write)`), plus **reasoning/thinking tokens as their own line** (Codewhale already tracks thinking replay tokens; opencode hides reasoning inside output — we can do better).
3\. **Prompt-cache statistics** (per session, aggregate): requests, share of input served from cache, misses with likely cause, expected rebuilds (compaction / tool-result clearing), warm/cold — mirroring Claude Code's `Prompt cache (main)` line. `/cache` today is per-turn DeepSeek-specific.
4\. **Per-tool / per-command token sinks**: `read`, `grep`, `bash`, `git diff`, `webfetch`, … — calls, tokens added to history, and how much was truncated/spooled (recoverable) vs replayed verbatim (the real leak). Sizes/truncation decisions already exist (`truncate.rs`, `fetch_url.rs`); missing is the ledger + aggregation.
5\. **Compaction cost as a metered line**: count, trigger (manual/auto/threshold), summarizer input/output tokens + cost, history tokens dropped. Codewhale already attributes compaction to a turn owner (`runtime_cost_owner`); this is reporting, not new plumbing — compaction looks "free" today but costs tokens+cache (Claude Code documents it).

**C. Reliability analytics (global)**
6\. **Tool-call error analytics**: per tool (and per model/provider): calls, failures, failure rate, error taxonomy (schema/validation, execution, timeout, policy/permission denial, empty/unusable result, parse failure), **retry recovery rate** (does the model correct itself or repeat the identical mistake), and recurring failure signatures across sessions. Actionable: fix a confusing tool description; put repeated bash mistakes into global `AGENTS.md`. Data exists (`ToolResult` error status, lifecycle outbox events); missing is the aggregation + patterns view.

**D. Sub-agent / fleet statistics (from the durable fleet ledger)**
7\. **Per-subagent and per-fleet analytics**: aggregate worker usage by **role** (built-in roles + custom names from `[fleet.roles]`) and per run/worker:

* calls, tokens, cost, and status counts (queued / running / completed / partial / failed / restarted / escalated / cancelled / stale);
* **failure sources** (verifier / transport / task) and retry/recovery rate — same "where do agents keep failing" signal as slice 6, but per delegated worker;
* grouping survives custom roles: the ledger records the role name at run time, so aggregation keys on that name even when `[fleet.roles]` changes later.
* Data already exists: `.codewhale/fleet.jsonl` ledger, `codewhale fleet status|inspect|logs|artifacts`, Runtime API `/v1/fleet/runs/{run_id}/workers`, and `SessionCostSnapshot.subagent_cost_usd/cny` for money already attributed to sub-agents.

## Use case

* `codewhale stats --days 30 --tools 10` → `bash` shows 60% of replayed tokens → switch to spooling/truncation or smaller commands.
* `codewhale stats --days 30 --models 5` → hit rate dropped 96% → 70% last week → something (tool-catalog churn, model/effort switches, compaction) is invalidating the cache; slice 3 names the cause.
* "The model keeps failing at X" → `codewhale stats --days 30 --tools 10` shows `bash` failing 30% with the same usage error → fix lands in `AGENTS.md`, next sessions stop repeating it.
* Extended thinking on → per-model reasoning split shows thinking is 40% of spend → tune `reasoning_effort`.
* `codewhale stats --days 30 --roles 5` (or `codewhale fleet stats`) → role `explore` shows 70% of sub-agent cost with 30% verifier-failure receipts → fix the explore role instructions / verifier scorers.

## Alternatives considered

* **opencode** `stats` — per-model tokens/cost/cache read-write with `--days/--tools/--models/--project`; but no cache hit rate (must hand-compute), no per-component request breakdown, no tool errors. Real output below — this is the target shape.
* **Claude Code** `/usage` **+** `/context` — closest: per-model usage, prompt-cache line with misses/expected rebuilds, category breakdown with optimization suggestions. Missing: per-tool sinks, compaction cost ledger, error analytics; and it's in-session only.
* **VTCode** `token_budget_breakdown` — per-request component metrics + spooling; closest on slice 1. Requires HF tokenizers for per-component tracking (follow-up option).
* **rtk-style shell hooks** — measure *pre-agent* trimming savings; cannot see actual in-context cost of built-in tools, no error patterns, requires an external wrapper. Real output below.
* Chosen: **persist + aggregate inside the runtime** — covers all built-in tools, measures real context cost, adds reliability signals no competitor has. In-session TUI `/tokens` enrichments remain an **open question** (see below).

## Impact

Every session; high value for token-spend debugging, cache tuning, and turning "model keeps failing" from anecdote into a data-driven fix. **All source data already exists and persists** — this is aggregation + presentation, not new capture.

## Additional context

**Precedent: opencode (real output,** `opencode stats --days 30 --models 8`**)**

This is the actual current output of `opencode stats` — per-model Cache Read / Cache Write are already rendered. **But there is no cache hit rate anywhere** — you must compute it by hand per model (e.g. deepseek-v4-flash: 3473.7 / (3473.7+110.1) ≈ **96.9%**):

```text

├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│Sessions                                            976 │
│Messages                                         68,219 │
│Days                                                 30 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    COST & TOKENS                       │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│Total Cost                                       $14.49 │
│Avg Cost/Day                                      $0.48 │
│Avg Tokens/Session                                 9.1M │
│Median Tokens/Session                              1.4M │

│Output                                            23.8M │
│Cache Read                                      8402.2M │
│Cache Write                                           0 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      MODEL USAGE                       │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash                 │
│  Messages                                       25,371 │
│  Input Tokens                                   110.1M │
│  Output Tokens                                   14.7M │
│  Cache Read                                    3473.7M │   → hit ≈ 96.9%
│  Cache Write                                         0 │
│  Cost                                          $0.0000 │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ opencode/x-preview-f-free                              │
│  Messages                                       17,109 │

│  Cache Read                                    1941.9M │   → hit ≈ 92.3%
```

(Hand-computed hit rates annotated inline with `→`; opencode prints no such column.)

**Precedent: rtk hook (real output)**

Users already track token leakage manually with shell-wrapper hooks. This real report shows where tokens actually go across 89k commands (hook-side savings, i.e. what the wrapper trimmed before the agent saw it):

```text
RTK Token Savings (Global Scope)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Total commands:    89010
Input tokens:      2006.2M
Output tokens:     576.9M
Tokens saved:      1429.3M (71.2%)
Efficiency meter: █████████████████░░░░░░░ 71.2%

By Command
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  #  Command                   Count    Saved    Avg%    Time  Impact
 1.  rtk read                   2343  1030.7M   23.2%    45ms  ██████████
 2.  rtk grep                  12298   158.4M   23.9%   197ms  ██░░░░░░░░
 3.  rtk git diff output/p...      3   105.2M  100.0%    1.2s  █░░░░░░░░░

 5.  rtk diff                     27    35.2M   64.3%   153ms  ░░░░░░░░░░
```
