**scoped CPU improvements; reported platform open.**

Verified: Existing macOS release wake/CPU repair and three-version Ubuntu idle measurements are retained; orphaned companion stops periodic work after leases expire.

Remaining: No FreeBSD15 reported approval-wait/background-workload measurement on current release bytes. Ubuntu idle is a different surface.

Next action: Measure native FreeBSD release idle, approval wait and background-job CPU/wakeups with the reported workload; reuse unchanged macOS/Ubuntu receipts.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

**Platform**: FreeBSD 15.0 (x86-64)
**Binaries analyzed**:

* `cw00912` — Codewhale v0.9.12 (82 MB ELF, dynamically linked)
* `cw00913` — Codewhale v0.9.13 (89 MB ELF, dynamically linked)
* `cw01000` — Codewhale v0.10.0 (90 MB ELF, dynamically linked)

All three binaries are Rust executables (ELF 64-bit LSB pie, compiled for FreeBSD).

## Observed Behavior

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200,200 -->
| Version | Idle CPU (top) | Threads | event_loop.rs size |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| v0.9.12 | \~1% (uwait) | 17 | \~4264 lines |
| v0.9.13 | \~5-8% | \~25-30 | \~7323 lines |
| v0.10.0 | \~8-15% | \~30+ | \~7323 + dispatch |

`uwait` state = waiting on user event (interrupt-driven). Later versions show active polling.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Between v0.9.12 and v0.9.13 (+7 MB, major CPU increase)

The event loop grew from \~4264 to \~7323 lines (+70%). Multiple **background polling workers** were added:

1. **@-mention discovery worker** (`crates/tui/src/tui/mention_completion.rs`)
   * Background thread `codewhale-mention-discovery` that continuously scans the workspace for @-mention candidates
   * Polls filesystem even when user is idle
2. **LSP (Language Server Protocol) integration**
   * New modules: `crates/tui/src/lsp/mod.rs`, `lsp/client.rs`, `core/engine/lsp_hooks.rs`, `tools/lsp.rs`
   * Spawns `lsp-writer`, `lsp-reader`, `lsp-dispatcher` threads
   * Supports rust-analyzer, gopls, typescript-language-server, clangd, etc.
   * Background language analysis runs continuously, even with no files open
3. **Runtime event tap / store monitoring**
   * `runtime event tap lagged; a store-failure notice may have been missed`
   * Polls runtime store state periodically
4. **Thread goal stall monitoring**
   * `failed to initialize durable goal stall schema`
   * Tracks `stalled_ms`, `pause_reason`, `repeated_gap_count`, `last_gap_fingerprint`
   * Continuously checks if threads are stalled
5. **Engine tick & telemetry bucket aggregation**
   * `engineTick` increments every iteration, bucket aggregation every 12 ticks
   * Telemetry events with timestamps, agent IDs, tool tracking
6. **Session persistence polling**
   * Polls `session_index.jsonl` for job status changes
   * Periodic SQLite queries for thread status (`SELECT id, rollout_path, preview...`)
7. **File frecency tracking** (`crates/tui/src/tui/file_frecency.rs`)
   * Background tracking of file access frequency
8. **[Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) live fetch** (`crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs`)
   * Periodic HTTP fetch of model catalog

### Between v0.9.13 and v0.10.0 (+1 MB, additional CPU)

1. **Fleet manager** (`crates/tui/src/fleet/manager.rs:1338`)
   * Fleet worker coordination with active polling
   * `Fleet worker coordination is not currently admissible`
2. **Background hooks**
   * `background hooks cannot deny tool calls because they exit immediately with no result`
   * Hooks run for every tool call/event
3. **Dispatch completion mailbox**
   * `dispatch completion mailbox is unavailable/full/closed`
   * Polls mailbox for dispatch results
4. **VM thread management**
   * `VM thread exited without reporting a result`
   * `VM admission gate closed`
5. **Agent profile permissions** (`AgentProfilePermissionsToml`)

## Architectural Shift

**v0.9.12** uses an **interrupt-driven** event loop: it sleeps on `kevent`/`kqueue` and wakes only on user input. The TUI event loop had \~4264 lines.

**v0.9.13+** switches to a **polling-driven** architecture: background workers wake periodically regardless of user activity. The event loop grew to \~7323 lines with runtime tap lag detection, persistence health checks, and session validation — all running on every iteration.

## Impact

* Significant battery drain on laptops
* Unnecessary CPU contention on shared/small VPS
* Background LSP scanning may be redundant with external editor LSP

2026-10-08 Codex continuation: [owner.rs](<http://owner.rs>) now stops world advancement and periodic saves after viewer/producer/audio leases expire, with authenticated /v1/frame wake messages on its existing bounded queue and a frame-deadline wait replacing 2 ms polling. Existing archives and active producer/audio semantics are retained. Exact checkout: engine-0102, local 80e1d2a9be plus owned changes. Focused native validation is starting at one build job and lower CPU priority. This addresses an orphaned-companion cause seen on macOS; it does not yet establish the reported FreeBSD idle/focus behavior or installed acceptance. No new tests or code comments, no new branch.

issues.title: 0.10.3: stop re-sending the whole goal snapshot on every continuation pass, and give the model the honest context figure

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
Reporter's build: `codewhale 0.10.2 (dev)`; code read at `main` `ecd256c90`.

## Problem

Every automatic goal-continuation pass appends a new user message carrying the **entire**
`GoalSnapshot` as pretty-printed JSON. In a long operate-mode goal those blocks are never
superseded, never deduplicated, and grow as the goal accumulates notes. In one measured
session they became the largest single occupant of the model's live history.

Measured on a 10.8-hour operate-mode session (833 messages in the saved history, compacted
once — the history carries one "Earlier turns of this session were condensed" checkpoint):

* 13 continuation blocks, 135,916 characters of block text in total (mean 10,455).
* That is **45.5% of all message text** in the live history; the per-message `<turn_meta>`
  accounts for a further 16.4%, leaving 38.1% for the actual conversation.
* The last eight blocks were the same size — 11,852 characters each, including that
  message's 812-character `<turn_meta>` — and all eight arrived within the final 65
  messages, so the model re-read the same goal state at the moment its context was
  tightest.
* One block decomposes as: 8,972 characters of JSON (1,571 `objective`, identical every
  pass; 6,883 `advisories`; \~518 for every other field), 2,056 characters of fixed
  instruction text (the `GOAL_CONTINUATION_PROMPT` preamble plus the closing "Continuation
  pass #N" paragraph), 812 of `<turn_meta>`, and \~12 of Markdown/JSON framing.

### The second half of the defect: the only token number the model sees is a lifetime bill

`tokens_used` inside those blocks ran 391,812,347 → 480,189,075 and never resets, because
it is a durable lifetime counter — `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads/manager.rs:5276` adds
`input_tokens + output_tokens` for every turn (`:5283`), and compaction rewrites history
without touching the goal record. It is a billing volume, not a context measurement.

With automatic compaction enabled the model receives **no** context-fill number at all:
`crates/tui/src/core/engine/compaction.rs:207` returns `None` from `context_pressure_line`
whenever `compaction.enabled`. So the only token figure in front of the model is that
lifetime sum, sitting next to `token_budget: null`. In the same session the model then
concluded, in its own words, that its context was exhausted:

> "In each Goal Continuation message the runtime sends me a goal-state block, and it has a
> `tokens_used` field — currently \~480M. That is accumulated token spend for the session,
> not context-window occupancy. I read it as 'the context is finished' — and that was my
> inference, not a fact." (translated from the session's original Russian)

That is the failure this issue is about, in both halves: the block spends 45% of the live
history re-stating one goal, and the one number it does supply is a bill that reads like a
budget. Trimming the block alone would delete the misleading field without giving the model
anything true to replace it.

Where the block comes from:

* `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:820` — `render_continuation_prompt` serializes the whole
  snapshot with `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, then prints "Continuation pass #N" after it.
* `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:651` — `GoalSnapshot`; `tokens_used` at `:656`.
* `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:449` — `MAX_ADVISORY_NOTES: usize = 16` (a function-local
  const inside `record_advisory` at `:445`); advisories are the model's own past
  `update_goal status: "advisory"` notes. `update_goal` returns the snapshot — advisories
  included — as its tool result (`json_result(&snapshot)` at `:1306`), so the model already
  receives them when it writes one.
* `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:5463` and
  `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:5880` — the two dispatch sites that turn the
  rendered string into the next user message.

## What Codewhale should do

1. **Render the continuation block as a delta, not a snapshot.** Send `objective` on the
   first pass (or when it changed); on later passes send a compact state line instead.

   *Implementation note (this is the part that needs a decision):*
   `render_continuation_prompt(&GoalSnapshot, u32)` has no access to history today — it
   cannot tell whether a previous continuation block is still in the transcript. Two
   workable shapes:
   * use `continuation_index` (objective only when `<= 1`) — zero new state, but loses the
     objective if compaction folded the first block away; or
   * add one caller-supplied flag (e.g. `objective_in_history: bool`), which the two
     dispatch sites set from the live session — the engine already knows whether history
     was replaced by a compaction checkpoint.
2. **Drop model-useless telemetry.** `tokens_used`, `time_used_seconds`, `elapsed_seconds`
   and `continuation_count` are not inputs to any decision the model makes. The pass number
   is already printed in the sentence after the JSON ("Continuation pass #N"). If a spend
   figure must stay for the model, name it for what it is — `billed_tokens_lifetime` — and
   never leave it as the only token number beside `token_budget`.
3. **Stop re-serializing** `advisories`**.** They are the model's own words: `update_goal`
   already returns the snapshot, advisories included, at the moment it writes one, and the
   note stays in the transcript. At 16 entries they were 6,883 of the block's 8,972 JSON
   characters in the measurement above.
4. **Give the model the honest context figure, in the same** `<turn_meta>` **block it already**
   **reads.** One passive line, for example:

   ```
   Context: 82400 / 131072 tokens (62.9%); auto-compaction at 90%
   ```
   * Numbers come from machinery that already exists: `route_context_budget_with_window`
     and `crates/tui/src/context_report.rs` (the same canonical pressure estimate the
     context meter, the compaction gate and `/context` read). No new estimator.
   * Informational only. It must **not** say "run /compact" or ask the model to take over
     compaction — that was the legitimate objection in [#5620](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5620>) and the reason
     `context_pressure_line` was gated off. The engine stays the only force path.
   * Emitted whether or not automatic compaction is enabled; while it is enabled the line is
     the model's only view of its own window.
   * `<turn_meta>` is per-message append-only content, not the session-pinned prefix, so a
     number that changes every turn costs no cache hit (`docs/CACHE.md`).

   **This is the explicit ask to revisit** [#6425](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6425>)**.** That issue was closed `NOT_PLANNED` on
   2026-10-25 with: "no model-facing context notice while auto-compaction is enabled …
   revisit if users report surprise compactions." The measured session above is such a
   report, and so are the open #7133 and [#6721](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6721>). What [#6425](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6425>) asked for is what this asks for;
   the difference is that the evidence now includes a model that diagnosed its own context
   as exhausted from a billing counter.
5. **Keep everything that steers:** `status`, `blocker`, `evidence`, `progress`, gap state
   (`last_gap_fingerprint`, `repeated_gap_count`) and the completion/verification
   instructions.

Expected effect on the measured session: the last block shrinks from 11,040 to roughly
2,600 characters (11,040 − 8,454 for `objective` and `advisories`), and across 13 passes
the saving is **up to** \~110k characters — \~27k tokens at the four-characters-per-token
heuristic. It is an upper bound: advisories are FIFO-capped at 16, so earlier blocks were
smaller than the 11,852-character ones measured at the end. The context line adds \~55
characters per user message.

**Scope boundary.** Trimming changes the model-facing rendering only. The durable
`thread_goals` record, the TUI status/progress surfaces and `update_goal`'s own tool output
keep `tokens_used` and `advisories`; nothing is deleted from storage.

## Where (surface)

TUI / engine — the goal loop's continuation prompt and `<turn_meta>`
(`TUI (terminal interface)`, and `Providers and models` for the budget fields).
`codewhale exec` and the Runtime API reach the same renderer through
`render_continuation_prompt`.

## Workarounds or other tools

Today the only workaround is to keep goals short, or to clear and recreate the goal so
`tokens_used` and `advisories` start over. Neither is discoverable, neither addresses the
repeated objective, and neither tells the model how full its window is.

## Evidence and reproduction

Any long goal session reproduces it; the saved session JSON is the record. To measure a
session of your own:

```python
import json, sys
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
text = ["".join(b.get("text", "") for b in m.get("content", [])) for m in d["messages"]]
blocks = [t for t in text if "## Active Goal State" in t]
print("messages:", len(text))
print("continuation blocks:", len(blocks))
print("block chars:", sum(map(len, blocks)), "of", sum(map(len, text)))
print("largest block:", max(map(len, blocks), default=0))
```

No session identifiers, host paths, or credentials are included. The measurement is from
the reporter's own saved session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A continuation block no longer carries the whole snapshot: for an active goal whose
      earlier block is still in history, `render_continuation_prompt` output is < 4 KiB
      (unit test on the existing fixture).
- [ ] The block no longer contains `tokens_used`, `time_used_seconds`, `elapsed_seconds` or
      `continuation_count`, or a renamed field states its scope (`billed_`/`session_`); a
      test pins whichever shape is chosen.
- [ ] `advisories` are absent from the block, or bounded by a byte budget covered by a test.
- [ ] An active goal that reaches continuation pass 3 sends the objective at most once
      (test), and still sends it once after a compaction checkpoint replaces history.
- [ ] With automatic compaction enabled, a turn's `<turn_meta>` carries one line naming used
      tokens, the window total and the percentage, and that line contains no "/compact"
      instruction (test).
- [ ] `cargo test -p codewhale-tui goal` passes. The existing pins are updated in the same
      change: `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:1599`
      (`assert!(prompt.contains("\"blocker\": null"))`) and `:2235`–`:2238`
      (which assert `"Goal Continuation"`, `"finish issue 2199"` — the objective — and
      `"Continuation pass #2"`). `shared_prompt_text_names_only_callable_tools` in
      `crates/tui/src/tools/canonical_action_tests.rs:106` stays green.

## Related

* [#6425](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6425>) — soft model-facing context notice under auto-compaction (closed `NOT_PLANNED`,
  2026-10-25, "revisit if users report surprise compactions"). **Point 4 above is the**
  **revisit**, requested on the trigger that decision named; the measured session is the
  report, together with the open #7133 and [#6721](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6721>).
* [#6490](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6490>) — spend and context visible to the model plus a pre-compaction notice (closed
  `NOT_PLANNED`; point 4 covers the context half only, not the spend/cost half).
* [#6217](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6217>) — model-facing `context_status` tool (closed `NOT_PLANNED`; a passive turn-meta line
  is the cheap version of the same number, without a new tool).
* #7133, [#6721](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6721>) — open reports of compaction trouble.
* [#6011](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6011>) — TUI usage/token accounting diagnostics (open, human-facing surface).

## Contributing

No pull request is attached. Happy to test a patch, or to review one.

## Open questions for maintainers

* Should `objective` be re-sent once after a compaction checkpoint, on the theory that the
  summary may have folded it? (I lean yes; a one-shot repeat costs \~1.5 KB per compaction.)
* Is `tokens_used` in the model-facing block useful to anyone today? If not, dropping it
  entirely is simpler than renaming it.
* Should the context line name the auto-compaction threshold as well, or only used/total?
* Should advisory notes be readable on demand through a `goal_status` tool instead of being
  pushed on every pass?

Engine packet, October 31. Reduce repeated goal state using the existing continuation renderer and live transcript, and report passive request pressure using the existing route budget. Scope covers crates/engine/src/tools/goal.rs, core/engine turn and compaction paths, runtime_threads/manager.rs and their existing checks. Preserve the durable goal, verification, cancellation and hard budget gates.

Engine main 2fad14825ebb88d0a73a32814b50dc5949fe0336 sends a typed runtime continuation through the ordinary gates, omits repeated objective/advisory text until a trusted new window, and reports estimated conversation input and matching compaction settings. Fourteen continuation and nine pressure checks passed. On macOS and Ubuntu ARM64 the real TUI sent a 1,238-byte objective on the first provider request only. Following passes including metadata measured 3,076 and 3,055 bytes respectively. Both used a scripted loopback provider. The durable get_goal snapshot remains available. Artifacts goal-wire-host-abs/receipt.json and linux-package/goal-q4-receipt.json. Ready for release review.

prs.title: fix(tui): decode HTML character references in replies
prs.body:
## What and why Replies print HTML character references as written: `<`, `&`, `|`, ` `. A link keeps the `&` in its target as well, so `?q=rust&page=2` opens with a parameter named `amp;page` instead of `page`. This reply, at 80 columns: ``` A few things from the page: - The function returns Result<Vec<u8>, Error> on every path. - Sales & Marketing owns the form, not Support & Success. - Search link: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new - Same link with a label: [search](https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2) | Syntax | Meaning | |---|---| | a | b | a or b | | Option<T> | maybe a T | |   nested | indented | In code it stays: `&` and `<T>`. ``` Before: ``` ▏ - The function returns Result<Vec<u8>, Error> on every path. ▏ - Sales & Marketing owns the form, not Support & Success. ▏ - Search link: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new ▏ - Same link with a label: search ▏ ▏ │ a | b │ a or b │ ▏ │ Option<T> │ maybe a T │ ▏ │   nested │ indented │ ▏ ▏ In code it stays: & and <T>. targets: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2 ``` After: ``` ▏ - The function returns Result, Error> on every path. ▏ - Sales & Marketing owns the form, not Support & Success. ▏ - Search link: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new ▏ - Same link with a label: search ▏ ▏ │ a | b │ a or b │ ▏ │ Option │ maybe a T │ ▏ │ nested │ indented │ ▏ ▏ In code it stays: & and <T>. targets: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2 ``` Plain text decodes the whole run instead of stopping at each `&`, because a token boundary is a wrap point and `Vec<u8>` has to stay one word. Link labels and link targets decode too; code spans and fences don't. The result is text, so `<br>` prints as `
` and `*x*` doesn't go italic. The names are the ones `decode_html_entities` in the web scraper knows, which is in the engine crate, so tui-kit can't call it; an unknown name or `R&D;` prints as before. ` ` becomes U+00A0, so it doesn't wrap or drop at the edge of a row. A reference at the end of a bare URL stays outside it, as in GFM, so `<https://a.test>` links to `https://a.test`. A numeric reference to a control or hidden character stays as written, by the `hidden_chars` check the GitHub report tool uses, so a reply can't put ESC or a bidi override on screen this way. `escape_review_text` now escapes `&` too: that's how plugin review text stays literal, and `&` has just become markup. This touches the link arm #7182 rewrites. If #7182 lands first I'll merge `main` in. ## Issue No-Issue: HTML character references print as text in replies and leave `&` in link targets; I searched and found no issue for it ## How I tested it - Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 982c6408a in a pseudo-terminal at 80x34 and 100x34 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows and targets above come from those runs, and 100 columns showed the same difference. A further reply on this build covered the cases in the two paragraphs above at 80 and 50 columns, including `\‮`, which is what `escape_review_text` now produces. I didn't run the plugin review flow itself. - `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6589 of 6589 passed, with the 685 tests whose names match `markdown`, `inline`, `link`, `wrap`, `table`, `keycap`, `transcript`, `plugin` or `url` among them. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, on 982c6408a; it merges cleanly into current `main` - [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): render markdown images as their alt text
prs.body:
## What and why

Markdown images go through the link arm with the `!` left behind in the plain text, and a linked image, the usual badge form, is split at the image's own `]`. This reply, at 100 columns:

```
The README opens with two badges:

[![CI](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/tool.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/tool)

and a screenshot: ![Main window](https://example.com/shot.png)

Wow! [Docs](https://example.com/docs) are linked too.
```

Before:

```
● The README opens with two badges:
▏
▏ ![CI](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions) ![crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/tool)
▏
▏ and a screenshot: !Main window
▏
▏ Wow! Docs are linked too.
```

`![CI` was a link to the badge image, and `](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions)` was text with the bare URL linked. After:

```
● The README opens with two badges:
▏
▏ CI crates.io
▏
▏ and a screenshot: Main window
▏
▏ Wow! Docs are linked too.
```

`CI` links to https://github.com/acme/tool/actions, `crates.io` to https://crates.io/crates/tool and `Main window` to https://example.com/shot.png.

An image now shows its alt text linked to its source, and a linked image shows its alt text linked to the outer destination, which is where a badge is meant to take you. The link arm takes an optional leading `!`, `![` ends a plain-text run, and the label and destination parsing moved into `split_markdown_link` and `split_link_destination`. Only one level of nesting is read, without recursion, so a long run of `[![` can't grow the stack. A `!` that isn't followed by a link, like `Wow!` above, prints as before.

## Issue

No-Issue: markdown images show a stray `!` and badge links print as markdown source; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 3070c0056 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 and 100x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above, and recorded the OSC 8 targets in the output; the rows and targets above come from those runs. The change was rebased onto ca75613cb afterwards; the only change to `markdown_render.rs` in between is #7181, in the table code.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6586 of 6588 passed, with the 276 tests whose names match `markdown`, `link`, `url`, `osc8`, `inline` or `image` among them. The two failures, `context_routing_and_report_branches_match_baseline` and `golden_turn_events_match`, fail the same way on ca75613cb without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on ca75613cb; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): close inline code at a backtick run of the same length
prs.body:
## What and why

Inline code opens with a run of backticks and closes at the next run of the same length, which is how a span carries a backtick. The renderer closed every span at the next single backtick, so a doubled span lost the backticks inside it, and `` ` `` turned the text after it into code. This reply, at 80 columns:

```
Two ways to build the greeting in JavaScript:

- concatenation: `"Hello, " + name`
- a template literal: `` `Hello, ${name}` ``

In a shell, `` echo "today is `date`" `` runs `date` first.
```

Before:

```
▏ - concatenation: "Hello, " + name
▏ - a template literal:  Hello, ${name}
▏
▏ In a shell,  echo "today is date"  runs date first.
```

After:

```
▏ - concatenation: "Hello, " + name
▏ - a template literal: `Hello, ${name}`
▏
▏ In a shell, echo "today is `date`" runs date first.
```

Codewhale writes these spans itself: `code_span` in the receipts puts a command holding a backtick in a longer fence. After the model ran that `echo` command, `/receipts` on `main` shows `1. ran echo "today is date" · approved by you`; with this change it shows the command as it ran.

A span now closes at the next run as long as its opener, which is how the LaTeX pass before it already skips code spans, and a run that never closes prints as text. One space comes off each end when both are there and the span isn't only spaces, as CommonMark does; that also applies to a single-backtick span like `` ` padded ` ``, while a span with spaces on one side only, like the `  port: 8080` cell from #7184, keeps them.

## Issue

No-Issue: inline code holding a backtick loses it in replies and in `/receipts`; I searched and found no issue for it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 19dc81980 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 and 100x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows above come from those runs, and 100 columns showed the same difference. For `/receipts`, the mock asked for one `bash` call running `` echo "today is `date`" ``, I allowed it and ran `/receipts` on each build.

prs.title: fix(catalog): give the bare deepseek-v4.1-flash spelling its own row
prs.body:
## Summary

A custom `openai-compatible` endpoint names the model the way the endpoint does — `model = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"`, no vendor prefix. The catalogue has rows for `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, but **no row under the bare spelling**.

For a `Custom` route the context window comes straight from the model-only lookup (`crates/engine/src/provider_lake.rs`):

```rust
context_window: context_window_for_model(resolved_model)
    .unwrap_or(LEGACY_DEEPSEEK_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS),   // 128_000
```

so the bare spelling got **128K** for a model the catalogue documents at 1M. Built-in routes (`deepseek`, `orcarouter`, …) do not show this because they resolve through a provider offering instead.

This is independent of #7179 / 1d750e5, which fixed the *output* side for custom endpoints. That work made a custom route stop inheriting a hosted output ceiling; it does not change where the context window comes from.

## What the user actually gets

On `main` at `31723e5`, with no route limits configured:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| context window | 128,000 | **1,000,000** |
| output request cap | 64,000 | **65,536** |

The output change is a side effect of the window: since 1d750e5 a custom route takes `generation_default_for_model(model).unwrap_or(window / 2).min(API_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS)`, so a larger window lifts the `/2` term above the 65,536 cap. The curated row carries no `generation_default`, and `API_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is untouched — this PR does not raise any cap, and 384,000 stays a documented capability that appears in labels and receipts only.

## What changes

- `crates/config/assets/catalog_corrections.json` — new `reviewed.intrinsic` row under `deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
- `crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json` — the same row, byte-identical.
- `crates/config/src/catalog/reviewed.rs` — regression test asserting on the **bundled** catalogue.
- `crates/models/src/lib.rs` — `deepseek_v4_output_caps_require_exact_catalog_metadata` moves the bare spelling from the must-not-resolve list to the resolved list, with a comment saying why.

The row takes the canonical Models.dev numbers (context 1000000, output 384000, reasoning, text+image) and follows the pattern `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-flash` already use: a bare row beside the namespaced spellings. The near-miss spellings (`deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910`, `deepseek-v4.1-pro`, `vendor/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vendor`) still assert `None` — an exact row documents one identifier, never a family.

## Why a data fix and not a lookup change

An earlier revision of this branch taught `intrinsic_model_in` to adopt a namespaced row when exactly one carried the bare tail. That was wrong and is dropped. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` is already claimed by two transport rows (`opencode-go`, `opencode-zen`), so the shared-spelling rule from #6032 would have kept it unknown; the fallback only appeared to work because its guard happened not to read the transport table. Curating the row keeps the lookup exact and leaves the resolver untouched.

The twin rows also disagree: `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash` is curated at **1048576** (source: DeepInfra listing + ModelScope card, verified 2026-10-20) while `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` is **1000000**. A tail-matching resolver would have silently chosen one layer. The new bare row takes the canonical Models.dev numbers and names them in its `source` string; the 1048576-vs-1000000 disagreement between the two namespaced spellings is pre-existing and left alone.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config` — 796 + 9 + 1 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-models` — 108 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-config -p codewhale-models --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `python3 scripts/catalog_models_dev.py seed render --check` reproduces the committed bundle exactly, apart from the OS path separator in `_meta.generated_by`, so the hand-added row keeps the seed/corrections contract.
- The new config test fails without the row and passes with it, so it is a real regression test rather than a fixture that would have passed either way.

Not run locally: the `codewhale-engine` test target. `rustc` aborts with `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` while codegen'ing that crate on this machine, before any test executes and independently of this change. `route_budget::uncatalogued_deepseek_variants_require_exact_output_metadata` was checked by reading it: its only mention of the bare name is `output_ceiling_source(Deepseek, "deepseek-v4.1-flash") == Documented(384_000)`, which held before through the canonical `models` row surfaced as a gap-fill offering and holds now through the curated row — `max_output_tokens_for_model` returns the same 384000 either way. Leaving the workspace-wide gates to CI.

## Scope — what this does not do

- It does **not** touch the output-budget policy for custom endpoints from #7179 / 1d750e5.
- It does **not** add bare rows for the other namespaced-only entries. 16 more exist (`gemma-4-31b-it`, `qwen3.6-27b`, `nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`, …). Each needs its own sourcing decision.

## Context

Found while investigating why a `freeshare` openai-compatible route reported a 128K context window for `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. That provider's `/models` publishes no limits — verified, the body carries only `id`, `type`, `display_name`, `created_at` — so nothing can be auto-detected from the wire and the catalogue is the remaining source.

## Related Issues

No-Issue: a catalogue gap found while investigating a 128K context window on a custom endpoint; no tracking issue was filed. #7179 / 1d750e5 cover the separate output-ceiling policy for custom endpoints and are not what this changes.

prs.body:
## What and why

Since #7181 every table cell goes through the paragraph wrapper, which drops spaces at the start and end of a row. A cell always starts a row, so inline code that leads with spaces loses them, even when the cell fits its column, and a cell holding only `` ` ` `` comes out empty. This reply, at 80 columns:

```
Each line of the YAML file, with its indentation:

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `server:` | top-level key |
| `  port: 8080` | two spaces in, under `server` |
| `  hosts:` | two spaces in, under `server` |
| `    - api.example.com` | four spaces in, an item of `hosts` |
```

Before:

```
│ server:                            │ top-level key                      │
│ port: 8080                         │ two spaces in, under server        │
│ hosts:                             │ two spaces in, under server        │
│ - api.example.com                  │ four spaces in, an item of hosts   │
```

After:

```
│ server:                            │ top-level key                      │
│   port: 8080                       │ two spaces in, under server        │
│   hosts:                           │ two spaces in, under server        │
│     - api.example.com              │ four spaces in, an item of hosts   │
```

A cell that fits its column is now laid out straight from its parsed spans, as cells were before #7181, with its links recorded the same way; only a cell that doesn't fit is wrapped. This is the case Codex raised on #7181.

prs.title: fix(session): keep history matched when turn metadata differs
prs.body:
fix(session): keep history matched when turn metadata differs

## Summary

A single chat message can be persisted in two shapes — bare user text, and the
same text followed by a trailing `<turn_meta>` block — while the session journal
compared the two with strict structural equality. One shape mismatch zeroed the
shared prefix, so the journal treated the entire history as new: it cleared the
leaf, re-rooted the tree, and appended the rest of the transcript as a sibling
branch. Nothing was deleted, but everything before the mismatch stopped being
the active path.

The visible symptom, from #7178: one message produced two replies that differed
in length (1103 vs 234 characters), and a session whose document held 1231
journal entries had an active path of 53 — every earlier assistant reply
stranded on a branch that was still stored and never shown again.

This makes the comparison aware of the engine-owned envelope, and makes the
journal converge on the live transcript instead of forking over a payload it can
replace in place.

## Changes

- **Mask only the engine envelope, never the payload**: `normalized_blocks` in
  `crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs` strips a leading `<turn_meta>…</turn_meta>`
  out of a text block instead of dropping whole blocks. A fused single block
  (`<turn_meta>…</turn_meta>\nhi`) normalizes to `Text("hi")` and matches the bare
  `"hi"`; a block that merely starts and ends with the tags keeps its trailing
  text, so a message whose real content looks like metadata is never masked away.
  The view borrows the existing blocks — nothing is cloned, nothing is allocated.
- **Refresh a metadata-only prefix instead of forking**:
  `rebranch_active_messages_stamped` rewrites a stored payload that differs only
  by the envelope to the live one, keeping the entry id, `created_at` and parent
  link (ordering comes from the parent chain), then appends only what is past the
  prefix. Journal and `session.messages` therefore converge instead of drifting.
- **Keep the strict comparison for synthesized kinds**: the relaxed match is
  limited to `SessionEntryKind::Message`, the only kind that stores an
  engine-stamped payload. `Compaction`, `BranchSummary`, `User`, `Assistant` and
  `System` still require byte equality with their projection, because a kind that
  could only match relaxed would be selected for a rewrite it cannot receive.
  This is also why `codewhale_models::turn_classify` is not reused here: its test
  is `starts_with("<turn_meta>") && ends_with("</turn_meta>")`, which accepts
  `<turn_meta>x</turn_meta>REAL CONTENT</turn_meta>`, and its
  `message.content.len() < 2` guard cannot see the fused single-block shape at
  all. Reusing it would restore both defects.
- **Converge the two other write paths**: `crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs` applies
  the same predicate to `journal_branch_to` and `update_session`, so a
  metadata-only difference falls through to the rebranch instead of being skipped
  and left divergent. Both append-only fast paths stay strict on purpose; they
  are safe now because a failing strict test no longer means "do nothing".
- **Unrelated Windows build fix, kept in its own commit**: `runtime_log.rs`
  imports `windows::Win32::System::Console` under `cfg(windows)`, but the
  `windows` dependency never enabled that feature, so `codewhale-runtime` does
  not build on Windows. CI is Linux-only, which is why it never surfaced. One
  line in `crates/runtime/Cargo.toml`; happy to split it into its own PR if you
  prefer.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Tests

## Testing

- `cargo test -p codewhale-runtime --lib -- session_tree` → `test result: ok. 25
  passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 886 filtered out`
- `cargo check -p codewhale-runtime -p codewhale-engine --lib` → `Finished dev profile` (13m07s, no errors)
- Both gates were re-run after merging `upstream/main` (`4b85ac2cc`), which moved
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs` to `crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs`; the merge
  carried these edits onto the new paths unchanged.
- Workspace-level clippy and tests are left to CI.

Three tests cover the new behaviour. Two are regression pins that fail on the
parent commit — `rebranch_refreshes_a_metadata_only_prefix_in_place` and
`a_metadata_shaped_payload_never_matches_a_shorter_turn` — and one guards against
over-eager masking (`rebranch_forks_when_the_content_actually_changed`), plus a
guard test asserting every non-`Message` kind still compares strictly. A
history-rewriting defect in the session tree had no pin at all, so the pins are
part of the fix rather than a separate test change.

## Checklist

- [x] Updated docs or comments as needed
- [x] Added or updated tests where relevant
- [ ] Verified TUI behavior manually if UI changes
- [ ] Harvested/co-authored credit uses a GitHub numeric noreply address

## Related Issues

Closes #7178

prs.title: fix(tui): parse a table cell's markup before wrapping it
prs.body:
## What and why

A table cell is wrapped as raw markdown, and each wrapped row is then parsed on its own. A code span, bold run or link that crosses a row break loses its pair, so the backticks and asterisks show and a link prints as its source with the URL split over two rows. Table rows also carry no hyperlinks, even for a link that fits. This reply, at 80 columns:

```
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cargo build --release --locked --workspace` | Builds every crate in **release mode with the lockfile pinned** |
| `codewhale --config ~/.codewhale/config.toml` | See [the configuration guide](https://example.com/docs/configuration) for details |
| `codewhale doctor` | [Troubleshooting](https://example.com/docs/doctor) |
```

Before:

```
│ `cargo build --release --locked    │ Builds every crate in **release    │
│ --workspace`                       │ mode with the lockfile pinned**    │
│ `codewhale --config                │ See [the configuration             │
│ ~/.codewhale/config.toml`          │ guide](https://example.com/docs/co │
│                                    │ nfiguration) for details           │
│ codewhale doctor                   │ [Troubleshooting](https://example. │
│                                    │ com/docs/doctor)                   │
```

After, with `the configuration guide` and `Troubleshooting` linked:

```
│ cargo build --release --locked     │ Builds every crate in release mode │
│ --workspace                        │ with the lockfile pinned           │
│ codewhale --config                 │ See the configuration guide for    │
│ ~/.codewhale/config.toml           │ details                            │
│ codewhale doctor                   │ Troubleshooting                    │
```

At 120 columns the first two rows still wrapped, and `**` and the link source showed the same way; `Troubleshooting`, which fit, was drawn in the link style with no hyperlink behind it.

Each cell is now wrapped by `render_line_with_links_tagged`, the paragraph wrapper, which parses before it wraps and records link columns; the row shifts those columns to the cell's place. `wrap_cell_text` and `push_word_breaking_graphemes`, which only it used, are gone, along with `wrap_cell_text_already_handled_long_words_remains_correct`, which called it directly. `table_cell_wider_than_column_wraps_instead_of_truncating` and `table_render_keeps_cjk_cells_within_qa_widths` still cover an overlong cell.

## Issue

No-Issue: markup in a wrapped table cell shows as written, and links in tables can't be opened; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at c4f1e726d (`markdown_render.rs` is the same on 785f7d0d4) in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 and 120x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the table above, and recorded the OSC 8 targets in the output; the rows above come from those runs. After the change both links carry their full targets at both widths; before, there were none.

On this branch merged with current `main`, `cargo test -p codewhale-tui-kit` (216 passed, including `keycap_table_puts_every_border_in_the_same_column`) and its clippy are clean too.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

prs.body:
Bumps [codewhale-hq/Codewhale/scripts/github-action/publish](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale) from c2a48723285c48978279f6c10672bbade49cc0cb to b92540d882b8e7c66389aa35e5fa0c3c178fe4ce.
Changelog

Sourced from codewhale-hq/Codewhale/scripts/github-action/publish's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[Unreleased]

Added

  • Runcrate is a bundled provider: runcrate reaches the OpenAI-compatible host at https://api.runcrate.ai/v1 with RUNCRATE_API_KEY, and model ids come from its public GET /v1/models listing. Thanks @​heydryft for the request and the vendor details. (#7085)

  • MCP connection status reaches the model: one existing history snapshot now records permitted configured, connecting, failed, authorization-required, unknown and connected servers, with bounded inert names and no raw errors. Stale status and server guidance are withdrawn on contention, configuration/scope changes and restore; observation does not connect servers or promise callable tools. (#6866)

  • Bundled-skill policy: [skills.bundled] separates automatic, authoritative and disabled installation from discovery, with per-name selection, disable and explicit-only controls. Aliases share policy; disabled shipped copies reveal user alternatives. Modified and managed files remain intact, and doctor plus /skills inspect show the effective policy. (#7066)

  • Configurable skill routing index: [skills] listing_max_description_chars and listing_budget_fraction control the shared parent/child catalogue. Defaults stay 400 characters and 5% of the route window, within the existing total bounds. Load warnings, localized inspect notes and /context explain shortening; full skill loading stays available. (#7073)

  • Compact approvals keep their authority visible: cards show three choices and default to Deny. An exact saved rule requires its scope preview on screen. Shortcuts for additional actions require opening Details; a hidden saved-rule choice never falls back to granting the session.

  • Quicker everyday navigation: top-level help separates everyday and advanced commands, doctor --all expands path/backend details, and the launch screen labels how to resume recent work. Up selects the newest recent session. Whale cameos stay out of transcript text.

  • Session-window diagnostics: the audit log records when a saved window starts a new journal root while retaining the previous branch, helping distinguish window replacement from lost durable history. session.window.rerooted now names a cause (engine_projection, session_restore or unattributed) and also fires when a journal with entries has no active path. (#7142)

  • Usage reporting counts models, tokens and tools: when usage reporting is on, each session now also reports, per provider and model, its turns by outcome, input, output and prompt-cache tokens, and turn-time buckets, plus how many times each built-in tool ran and failed. A model is named only when it is in Codewhale's bundled public model catalog; custom, local and fine-tuned names are sent as other, and MCP and plugin tools as mcp or other. No prompts, outputs, tool arguments or paths are sent. Runs under CI or the GitHub Action report the ci session source. The first-run notice is shown once more to describe this. DO_NOT_TRACK=1 now turns usage reporting off for that run, like CODEWHALE_TELEMETRY=0; codewhale config set telemetry false still turns it off for good. See docs/TELEMETRY.md.

  • exec and doctor follow the TUI onto local Ollama: with no cloud key and no explicit route, codewhale exec uses a running local Ollama chat model and says so, and codewhale doctor --probe-local checks that route. Nothing is saved. (#7115)

  • Thinking starts at auto: new configurations and the built-in default use reasoning_effort = "auto" instead of max; an effort you set is never changed.

  • DSH Git review scopes: the extension host brokers bounded, read-only Git metadata to reviewed DSH plugins through a new git_review_scope action (extension-host policy v8).

  • Safer uninstall: program removal never edits shell profiles; matching Codewhale PATH blocks are reported for manual cleanup. Data purge requires a receipted removal in the same confirmed run. Both Unix installers reject unsafe or managed destinations before creating them and keep shell profiles unchanged. Uninstall instructions now match the explicit-home purge scope in English and Chinese.

  • Nested and deletable threads (Runtime API): a fork (including a backtrack fork) records parent_thread_id, POST /v1/threads accepts one naming an existing thread, and GET /v1/threads/summary returns it so clients can nest child conversations. DELETE /v1/threads/{id} removes an idle thread with its turns, items, events and goal, and its saved session unless another thread shares it or a terminal holds it open; a running thread answers 409.

  • Hunk actions in Review (Runtime API): POST /v1/git/stage, /v1/git/unstage and /v1/git/discard take a patch holding hunks of the one path in paths and apply only those hunks through git apply, under the same expect preconditions as whole-path writes. A patch that no longer applies fails with git's message and writes nothing; renames, mode changes and binary patches are refused. The tasks tool can also suggest a task, shown as a Start/Hide card, without starting anything.

  • Live /models ceilings reach the route: a provider that states per-model context and output limits in its own /models body now keeps them instead of falling back to the legacy 128K window. OpenAI limit blocks, flat context_length / context_window / max_model_len / max_context_length fields, max_output_tokens / max_completion_tokens, and a relay metadata block (context_limit, context_budget, output_budget) are read; metadata.context_limit outranks context_budget because the first is the model capability and the second the share one deployment accepts. Each field is parsed on its own, so an unreadable one costs only its own candidate instead of hiding the readable fields below it.

  • Change mode and permissions while the agent works: Tab, Shift+Tab, /mode, the hotbar and /config mode no longer refuse while a turn is running. A response that is already streaming is not restarted; the change applies at the agent's next step in the same turn (before its next tool batch, at every approval gate, and before its next model request, which carries the new mode notice). The status line says so until it applies. A call still waiting for approval goes back to the model under the new posture, and a call you already approved runs only if the new posture is equal or broader. Model, thinking level and provider stay locked until the turn ends.

  • Steering interrupts thinking: a steer (Ctrl+Enter, or Enter twice after queueing) now closes the in-flight model request at once, whether the model is waiting on headers, reasoning, writing text or emitting a tool call, and continues the same turn with your message. Text already shown is kept as interrupted output; unfinished reasoning and partial tool calls are discarded, never run.

  • Modern MCP client: MCP servers now connect through the official MCP SDK (2.4) behind Codewhale's Rust broker by default (mcp_backend = "host"; "rust" stays available for one release). Servers that speak the 2026-07-28 revision are discovered with server/discover; other stdio and HTTP servers fall back to the legacy initialize handshake, and configured SSE servers keep theirs. Rust keeps process, network, credential, catalog, approval and cancellation authority.

  • DeepSeek Harness plugins: reviewed DSH plugins (definition API pinned to DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 in a shared compatibility table) run in the Native extension host. Tool output is validated against its declared schema, unsupported options are refused instead of ignored, and plugin commands can submit a prompt with visible plugin attribution. Terminal command receipts are kept in thread snapshots without entering model history. Changing the compatibility table invalidates earlier trust. A newly enabled plugin's tools are offered on the first turn: the turn waits up to 10 seconds for the plugin host to finish loading instead of adding them only from the next turn. Plugin UI views stay disabled, and the import receipt says why: WebKit's network restrictions do not stop WebRTC, so plugin UI waits for an isolated renderer. A plugin tool can call ctx.sessions.flush(exec.agent.session) to have the Engine save the conversation so far before it continues (Runtime, terminal and exec sessions); it reports failure instead of claiming a save. Installing a plugin whose bytes changed after review now returns a 409 conflict instead of a server error. A plugin tool can ask you a question with ctx.userQuestions.ask and gets back the options you picked, your own text, or a skip; the question shows like any other Codewhale question in the terminal and through the Runtime API. A plugin tool can start a child agent with ctx.subagents.startActivation (the spawn provider): the child runs through Codewhale's own sub-agent manager, needs the same approval as the model's agent tool, can carry an extra persona section and a narrower tool list set in its agent/created handler, and returns its result to the plugin.

  • MCP catalogs stay fresh: a server's tools, resources, prompts and skills are rediscovered on their own connection when an advertised ttlMs expires or the server sends a list-changed notice. A tool resolved against the old catalog is refused with "retry the call", a removed tool cannot run, and a failed refresh reconnects instead of serving stale entries. Catalogs are never shared across servers, credentials or reconnects.

  • MCP Skills extension: servers that advertise the published Skills extension have their skills listed in list_mcp_resources. Listing never activates a skill, and reading a skill file is refused unless its size and sha256 digest match the listing. MCP skills do not yet join /skills.

  • Updates install themselves: release-binary installs check for a new release every 6 hours (was 1), download and checksum-verify it in the background, and apply it the next time codewhale starts, never during a session. One line says Updated to v… · What's new: … · Undo: codewhale update --rollback. Until releases are signed, the download waits for your OK (one [y/N] question at the next start, or /update install); a release with a valid Ed25519 manifest signature applies on its own. codewhale update --rollback puts back the version the last update replaced and keeps the rolled-back version from returning automatically. Turn it down with codewhale config set update.mode notify (or off, or CODEWHALE_UPDATE_MODE); an organization's root-owned policy.toml overrides both. Offline and rate-limited checks retry about an hour later instead of on every launch. Package-manager and desktop-app copies only get their manager's command. Builds with the release key refuse a missing or invalid signature, and re-check the staged binary against the signed manifest at start. The checksum manifest now always comes from GitHub Releases; on Linux x64 the CNB mirror can still serve the binary, but only bytes that GitHub's manifest lists.

  • One view of every Codewhale on the machine: codewhale doctor has an Installations section and codewhale doctor --installs (--json, --brief) lists every codewhale, codew, codewhale-tui, deepseek and deepseek-tui with its owner: install receipt, package manager (with its exact removal command), the desktop app, a backup, or not ours. Nothing found is ever run. codewhale doctor --fix adds one plan to tidy them: old backups move to ~/.codewhale/recovery/<stamp>/ (kept 30 days, then deleted by a later --fix), an unreceipted codew is brought in line with codewhale, and the directory gets an install receipt; each move prints its undo and codewhale doctor --restore <stamp> reverses the lot. Package-managed, desktop-app, symlinked and foreign files are never touched, and neither is user data. codewhale uninstall now lists other copies with the same classification.

  • Uninstall guidance on every install route: codewhale uninstall previews receipt-owned release files and --yes removes only checked files, with the running command last. Both Unix installers and the Windows archive installer record command ownership; self-update renews existing receipts on both. On Windows the running codewhale.exe is renamed and deleted once the command exits. Package-managed copies are left alone, and the command prints their exact removal command: npm with its prefix, Cargo with its root, the Homebrew formula, scoop uninstall codewhale, winget uninstall --id HunterBown.CodeWhale, or the Windows setup's Uninstall.exe. Every other codewhale/codew still on PATH is listed. User data is kept unless you add --purge-data. With --yes it runs only after a receipted installation was removed in that same run, and then deletes only ~/.codewhale (or a CODEWHALE_HOME named .codewhale) and ~/.deepseek/snapshots, refusing symlinks, home ancestors and directories owned by another user. A copy from an older curl | sh installer that wrote no receipt is adopted on --yes when it sits in a known older curl-installer directory: the commands byte-identical to the running program get a receipt and are removed, anything else is preserved, and a symlink or hard link among them stops adoption before any receipt is written. Windows removal is compile-checked but not yet exercised on a Windows host. (Refs #7091)

  • GitHub Action reviews: analysis can export a structured Engine review for a separate trusted publisher job. The publisher checks the current PR revision and line anchors, deduplicates its findings, and keeps uncertain or preexisting claims out of inline comments.

  • DingTalk bridge: an optional internal-app Stream adapter reuses the same Engine, shared admission and approval helpers. Tenant/staff allowlists, durable acceptance before acknowledgement and retained uncertain deliveries protect recovery. Managed account linking is separate from this advanced self-hosted bridge.

  • Answerless output-limit recovery: opt into [reasoning_only] on_output_limit = true to request an answer again after a length stop with no answer or tool call, including hidden reasoning and ordinary Fleet workers. Retries share max_reprompts, retain existing output and control limits, and record request-scoped nudge receipts without adding them to resumed conversation context. RLM keeps its existing stop protocol. Thanks @​M-Maciej for the long-proof Fleet report. (#6990)

  • OrcaRouter recommendation: /provider and /model offer a shared partner recommendation with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 30% top-up-match link, public referral disclosure and localized offer details. F7 or a click opens the existing pager while retaining the current route.

  • Per-scope instruction budgets: global and project standing instructions now have separate token budgets (100,000 estimated tokens each, capped at 25% of the usable context window), every trim, skip or refusal reaches the model and /context report, and [instruction_budget] policy = "refuse" stops a request before dispatch. Other tools' instruction files stay opt-in through project_instruction_imports or claude_fallback, and the table is user config only. Thanks @​7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the design and implementation. (#6526, #7086)

  • The TUI Terminal dock now also shows the model's shell commands for the session: each running or recent command is a read-only tab with its live output, beside the interactive shells. "No live terminals" appears only when there are neither.

  • Preview: dispatch --computer starts an account cloud conversation that can also be opened in desktop. --thread continues or inspects it; --stop, --approve and --deny control its current task. Explicit --key-stdin installs provider access in the running computer's memory. Retries retain one operation key and the account/VM binding. Existing Agent Work dispatch

... (truncated)

Commits
  • b92540d test(engine): give the user-input probe a timer gap Windows cannot eat
  • 84acb83 test: refresh the providers golden and install the paired window in two more ...
  • fd9f06d fix(cli): gate the hashing module with the only module that uses it
  • 36f058c docs: unlink intra-doc references to private items so the docs gate builds
  • 3a02722 fix(release): publish codewhale-util before the crates that depend on it
  • c96f4ed refactor(runtime): own the workspace drive lease and share its path helpers (...
  • e31dcd4 refactor(runtime): own workspace trust, delivery files and session diagnostic...
  • 41592ac ci(main): also allow a manual run of the landing gate
  • 193cd7a ci(main): run the checked-in preflight on every push to main
  • f285377 style: reformat the S2 rewrite sites and repoint the blocking-calls budget
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

Tool output is validated against its declared schema, unsupported options are refused instead of ignored, and plugin commands can submit a prompt with visible plugin attribution. Terminal command receipts are kept in thread snapshots without entering model history. Changing the compatibility table invalidates earlier trust. A newly enabled plugin's tools are offered on the first turn: the turn waits up to 10 seconds for the plugin host to finish loading instead of adding them only from the next turn. Plugin UI views stay disabled, and the import receipt says why: WebKit's network restrictions do not stop WebRTC, so plugin UI waits for an isolated renderer. A plugin tool can call ctx.sessions.flush(exec.agent.session) to have the Engine save the conversation so far before it continues (Runtime, terminal and exec sessions); it reports failure instead of claiming a save. Installing a plugin whose bytes changed after review now returns a 409 conflict instead of a server error. A plugin tool can ask you a question with ctx.userQuestions.ask and gets back the options you picked, your own text, or a skip; the question shows like any other Codewhale question in the terminal and through the Runtime API. A plugin tool can start a child agent with ctx.subagents.startActivation (the spawn provider): the child runs through Codewhale's own sub-agent manager, needs the same approval as the model's agent tool, can carry an extra persona section and a narrower tool list set in its agent/created handler, and returns its result to the plugin.

  • MCP catalogs stay fresh: a server's tools, resources, prompts and skills are rediscovered on their own connection when an advertised ttlMs expires or the server sends a list-changed notice. A tool resolved against the old catalog is refused with "retry the call", a removed tool cannot run, and a failed refresh reconnects instead of serving stale entries. Catalogs are never shared across servers, credentials or reconnects.

  • MCP Skills extension: servers that advertise the published Skills extension have their skills listed in list_mcp_resources. Listing never activates a skill, and reading a skill file is refused unless its size and sha256 digest match the listing. MCP skills do not yet join /skills.

  • Updates install themselves: release-binary installs check for a new release every 6 hours (was 1), download and checksum-verify it in the background, and apply it the next time codewhale starts, never during a session. One line says Updated to v… · What's new: … · Undo: codewhale update --rollback. Until releases are signed, the download waits for your OK (one [y/N] question at the next start, or /update install); a release with a valid Ed25519 manifest signature applies on its own. codewhale update --rollback puts back the version the last update replaced and keeps the rolled-back version from returning automatically. Turn it down with codewhale config set update.mode notify (or off, or CODEWHALE_UPDATE_MODE); an organization's root-owned policy.toml overrides both. Offline and rate-limited checks retry about an hour later instead of on every launch. Package-manager and desktop-app copies only get their manager's command. Builds with the release key refuse a missing or invalid signature, and re-check the staged binary against the signed manifest at start. The checksum manifest now always comes from GitHub Releases; on Linux x64 the CNB mirror can still serve the binary, but only bytes that GitHub's manifest lists.

  • One view of every Codewhale on the machine: codewhale doctor has an Installations section and codewhale doctor --installs (--json, --brief) lists every codewhale, codew, codewhale-tui, deepseek and deepseek-tui with its owner: install receipt, package manager (with its exact removal command), the desktop app, a backup, or not ours. Nothing found is ever run. codewhale doctor --fix adds one plan to tidy them: old backups move to ~/.codewhale/recovery/<stamp>/ (kept 30 days, then deleted by a later --fix), an unreceipted codew is brought in line with codewhale, and the directory gets an install receipt; each move prints its undo and codewhale doctor --restore <stamp> reverses the lot. Package-managed, desktop-app, symlinked and foreign files are never touched, and neither is user data. codewhale uninstall now lists other copies with the same classification.

  • Uninstall guidance on every install route: codewhale uninstall previews receipt-owned release files and --yes removes only checked files, with the running command last. Both Unix installers and the Windows archive installer record command ownership; self-update renews existing receipts on both. On Windows the running codewhale.exe is renamed and deleted once the command exits. Package-managed copies are left alone, and the command prints their exact removal command: npm with its prefix, Cargo with its root, the Homebrew formula, scoop uninstall codewhale, winget uninstall --id HunterBown.CodeWhale, or the Windows setup's Uninstall.exe. Every other codewhale/codew still on PATH is listed. User data is kept unless you add --purge-data. With --yes it runs only after a receipted installation was removed in that same run, and then deletes only ~/.codewhale (or a CODEWHALE_HOME named .codewhale) and ~/.deepseek/snapshots, refusing symlinks, home ancestors and directories owned by another user. A copy from an older curl | sh installer that wrote no receipt is adopted on --yes when it sits in a known older curl-installer directory: the commands byte-identical to the running program get a receipt and are removed, anything else is preserved, and a symlink or hard link among them stops adoption before any receipt is written. Windows removal is compile-checked but not yet exercised on a Windows host. (Refs #7091)

  • GitHub Action reviews: analysis can export a structured Engine review for a separate trusted publisher job. The publisher checks the current PR revision and line anchors, deduplicates its findings, and keeps uncertain or preexisting claims out of inline comments.

  • DingTalk bridge: an optional internal-app Stream adapter reuses the same Engine, shared admission and approval helpers. Tenant/staff allowlists, durable acceptance before acknowledgement and retained uncertain deliveries protect recovery. Managed account linking is separate from this advanced self-hosted bridge.

  • Answerless output-limit recovery: opt into [reasoning_only] on_output_limit = true to request an answer again after a length stop with no answer or tool call, including hidden reasoning and ordinary Fleet workers. Retries share max_reprompts, retain existing output and control limits, and record request-scoped nudge receipts without adding them to resumed conversation context. RLM keeps its existing stop protocol. Thanks @​M-Maciej for the long-proof Fleet report. (#6990)

  • OrcaRouter recommendation: /provider and /model offer a shared partner recommendation with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 30% top-up-match link, public referral disclosure and localized offer details. F7 or a click opens the existing pager while retaining the current route.

  • Per-scope instruction budgets: global and project standing instructions now have separate token budgets (100,000 estimated tokens each, capped at 25% of the usable context window), every trim, skip or refusal reaches the model and /context report, and [instruction_budget] policy = "refuse" stops a request before dispatch. Other tools' instruction files stay opt-in through project_instruction_imports or claude_fallback, and the table is user config only. Thanks @​7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the design and implementation. (#6526, #7086)

  • The TUI Terminal dock now also shows the model's shell commands for the session: each running or recent command is a read-only tab with its live output, beside the interactive shells. "No live terminals" appears only when there are neither.

  • Preview: dispatch --computer starts an account cloud conversation that can also be opened in desktop. --thread continues or inspects it; --stop, --approve and --deny control its current task. Explicit --key-stdin installs provider access in the running computer's memory. Retries retain one operation key and the account/VM binding. Existing Agent Work dispatch

prs.body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7.0.0 to 8.0.2.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.2

What's Changed

  • Update the readme by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#473
  • Improves artifact download retries when the service returns HTTP 429 (rate limiting), including honoring valid Retry-After headers.
  • Update @​actions/artifact to 6.3.1 by @​tunc-d in actions/download-artifact#492
  • Prepare download-artifact v8.0.2 by @​tunc-d in actions/download-artifact#493

New Contributors

  • @​tunc-d made their first contribution in actions/download-artifact#492

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v8.0.1...v8.0.2

v8.0.1

What's Changed

  • Support for CJK characters in the artifact name by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#471
  • Add a regression test for artifact name + content-type mismatches by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#472

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v8...v8.0.1

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0
