issues.title: [Feature]: Support keyterm prompting in ElevenLabs batch transcription

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:feature
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

<!-- openclaw-feature-id: OCF-20261026-elevenlabs-batch-stt-keyterm-prompting-1d2dc2de -->

issues.title: [Feature]: Generate short multi-speaker dialogue with the bundled ElevenLabs plugin

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:feature
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an optional tool to the existing ElevenLabs plugin that turns an ordered script with two selected voices into one generated dialogue MP3.

### Problem to solve

A scripted interview or podcast scene needs a relationship between each line and its speaker, together with the surrounding exchange. The [podcast_generator project](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/README.md) implements this task using batches of speaker turns. Its author explains why synthesizing each turn separately and assembling the recordings does not provide the same conversational context. That is an external implementation and reported motivation; I have not independently evaluated its audio quality.

There is also an OpenClaw-specific consumer surface: [pixcli's registry README](https://hub.openclaw.ai/shellbot/plugins/openclaw-pixcli) advertises optional dialogue and podcast tools. It is an existing alternative, not a request from its author to migrate.

The bundled ElevenLabs integration currently accepts one text and one voice per synthesis request. A speaker name written into that text does not become a second voice assignment. The requested output is a short jointly generated exchange using the operator's ElevenLabs voices, rather than an ordinary spoken assistant reply. Applicability to operators of the bundled plugin is an inference from these public workflows, not a reported OpenClaw outage.

### Proposed solution

Keep this capability inside `extensions/elevenlabs`, behind an explicitly enabled plugin tool; `elevenlabs_dialogue` is a suggested name. Use the existing optional-tool registration and manifest contracts. Do not expand the core `tts` tool or the shared speech interface.

The initial tool would accept an ordered array of nonempty `{text, voiceId}` turns, with exactly two distinct voice IDs. Generate a single bounded scene using Eleven v3 and return one MP3 artifact. Preserve turn order and inline audio tags. Reject scripts above a total of 2,000 text characters before making a request; this intentionally excludes automatic long-form episode production.

Reuse the plugin's configured authentication, runtime-resolved secrets, trusted base URL and guarded HTTP helpers for `POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`. Use `mp3_44100_128`. Do not accept credentials, arbitrary endpoints or publication destinations in tool arguments. Keep normal tool admission, cancellation and current invocation authority. A provider error must not silently substitute another provider or turn the script into single-voice narration. Do not automatically regenerate or replay a request whose paid outcome is unknown.

Return the audio through existing media storage and tool-result/reply contracts. Artifact creation and delivery must be distinguished; do not claim delivery from a local path alone.

### Alternatives considered

- Repeated TTS calls followed by audio assembly preserve voice assignments, but each synthesis lacks the complete exchange. They remain useful when independently editable stems are the goal.
- The external Python project or a direct ElevenLabs SDK integration can already perform the vendor request; a custom OpenClaw tool can wrap that existing contract. An equivalent multi-voice operation in the current hosted ElevenLabs MCP was not established. These are valid alternatives; this proposal adds a narrowly scoped operation to an existing bundled owner, rather than claiming that OpenClaw cannot run such a workflow at all.
- pixcli already supplies dialogue tooling through its separately configured Meterkey service. Its README permits private output; it does not force public publishing. Keeping the existing ElevenLabs account and voice catalog is the distinction here, not an invented ban on other plugins.
- Other speech providers can offer dialogue, but their voices are not the selected ElevenLabs voice IDs.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: operators generating two-voice scripted scenes with the bundled ElevenLabs integration. The public projects establish the task, not the size of this population.
- Severity/urgency: an additional authoring capability; existing single-voice speech remains available. No production incident or urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Each qualifying scene needs one bounded dialogue request.
- Practical consequences: the bundled integration cannot currently express both speaker assignments in a joint synthesis. Operators use a separate integration or assemble independently generated turns. No measured time savings or quality improvement is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [External batch producer](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/generate_podcast.py): `build_batches` and `generate_dialogue_batch` preserve speaker turns. Its older batch-size assumptions should not be copied.
- [ElevenLabs API contract](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert): ordered text/voice pairs produce audio. This proposal uses a smaller two-voice subset and the current short-request guidance.
- [Current bundled request builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts) and [plugin entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts): scalar synthesis and no dialogue tool.
- [Existing optional-tool contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/docs/plugins/building-plugins.md#registering-tools).
- Related [issue #165655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165655) / [PR #165656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165656) concern dialogue-model transport for a single speaking voice and phone-call socket reuse. The inspected open PR sends one text/voice pair; this proposal concerns a structured multi-voice script and an audio file.

This is static source and public-contract research. No vendor request, installed-plugin execution or listening test was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Suggested implementation: register an optional version 2 tool in the existing plugin and declare its manifest ownership; factor reusable plugin-local credential/config and request helpers rather than copying their policy. The public factory context already supplies runtime config, provider-key resolution and `assertInvocationCurrent`; recheck current authority after awaited preparation and before the request and artifact admission. Reuse focused media-store and bounded binary-response helpers. For a finished direct reply, the existing `canDeliverSourceReply` / `details.sourceReply` contract can deliver the artifact; nested Code Mode execution remains program data under that contract.

Non-goals: real-time calls, WebSocket pooling, new v4 model support, voice cloning, speaker identification, transcription, pronunciation-dictionary management, long-script chunking, audio editing, podcast hosting, public uploads, new persistent jobs, and a generic dialogue SDK. Existing TTS defaults, personas and fallback behavior remain outside this tool's operation.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the tool explicitly enabled and usable ElevenLabs credentials, submit a short A/B/A script with two accessible voice IDs. One dialogue request preserves the three turns and both IDs, and returns a playable MP3. Confirm the supplied voice assignments with a listening test as well as the request trace; do not promise subjective quality.
- The returned artifact is usable through the actual tool/result path. A direct source reply reaches only the admitted source conversation; a nested program call returns data without an unsolicited send.
- Empty text, malformed voice ID syntax, a missing second voice, and a script over the character budget fail before the vendor request. A syntactically valid voice ID may still be unavailable to the account; surface that provider access/validation failure honestly rather than claiming local validation proves access. The disabled tool is absent from discovery. Cancellation, a retired invocation, and credential/plugin disablement do not admit a new request or publish a success artifact.
- Authentication, validation, timeout, malformed audio and size-limit failures produce an actionable error, without silent voice/provider substitution or automatic paid regeneration. Existing single-voice TTS still works with its previous defaults.

Implementer unknown. Live synthesis, real tool delivery, failure/cancellation proof and focused plugin/contract checks remain work for the eventual implementation. Maintainers should decide whether this existing-owner enhancement is worth maintaining relative to the external alternatives.

issues.title: [Bug]: exec (zsh) — heredoc on non-first pipeline stage receives upstream pipe output ⊕ heredoc body instead of overriding the pipe → false "Exec failed" NameError alerts

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.7.1-2** (launchd gateway, exec host = local/gateway)
- macOS 15.8.2 (x64), `/bin/zsh` **5.9** (x86_64-apple-darwin24, Apple build)
- exec tool with default shell config (zsh)

## Summary

When an agent runs a command that combines a **pipeline** with a **heredoc attached to a non-first pipeline member** — e.g. the very common monitoring pattern:

```
openclaw cron list --json | python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, sys
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
...
EOF
```

the last-stage process does **not** receive the heredoc on stdin (POSIX/bash semantics: an explicit stdin redirection overrides the implicit pipe). Instead it receives **the upstream pipe output concatenated with the heredoc body**. For `python3 -`, the piped JSON gets executed as Python source and dies at the first bare `true` / `false` / `null`:

```
NameError: name 'true' is not defined. Did you mean: 'True'?
```

This produced **6 false "Exec failed" alerts in a single day** in our heartbeat monitoring (the cron fleet itself was fully healthy; each run self-healed same-run via a write-to-file-then-read pattern).

## Root-cause isolation — not an OpenClaw command-mangling bug

- **ps forensics**: exec runs the command as `/bin/zsh -f -c "<shell-snapshot preamble>; export PATH=…; eval '<command>'"`. The command text is passed **intact** (shQuote-wrapped, real newlines preserved). Replaying this exact argv from a plain Python subprocess reproduces the anomaly, so the snapshot preamble and the `eval` wrapper are **not** the cause.
- The anomaly reproduces **entirely outside OpenClaw** with bare `zsh -f -c` and with zsh **script files**: on zsh 5.9 (this build), a heredoc/here-string attached to a **non-first** pipeline member is *concatenated after* the upstream pipe output instead of overriding it. `bash` and `/bin/sh` behave correctly (heredoc wins).
- OpenClaw merely inherits zsh behavior. Filing here because exec is the surface where agents hit it, and a warning/normalization in exec would have saved a day of false alerts.

## Minimal repro (no OpenClaw involved)

```zsh
% printf 'PIPE-CONTENT' | cat <<'EOF'
HEREDOC-CONTENT
EOF
PIPE-CONTENTHEREDOC-CONTENT      # zsh 5.9 actual: concatenated

% bash -c "printf 'PIPE-CONTENT' | cat <<'EOF'
HEREDOC-CONTENT
EOF"
HEREDOC-CONTENT                  # bash: correct POSIX semantics
```

Interpreter-from-stdin hazard (the incident shape):

```zsh
% echo '{"enabled": true}' | python3 - <<'EOF'
print("hello")
EOF
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
NameError: name 'true' is not defined. Did you mean: 'True'?
```

## Probe matrix (subprocess with exact argv control)

| # | Scenario | zsh 5.9 | bash | POSIX expectation |
|---|----------|---------|------|-------------------|
| 1 | `printf P \| cat <<EOF` via `-c`, multi-line | P⊕body ❌ | body ✅ | body |
| 2 | leading `export PATH=…` line + same command | P⊕body ❌ | — | body |
| 3 | `eval '…'` wrapper (exec's exact shape) | P⊕body ❌ | body ✅ | body |
| 4 | script-file mode | P⊕body ❌ | body ✅ | body |
| 5 | 3-stage pipe, heredoc on last member | P⊕body ❌ | — | body |
| 6 | heredoc on **middle** member | P⊕body ❌ | — | body |
| 7 | heredoc on **first** member: `cat <<EOF \| cat` | body ✅ | — | body |
| 8 | standalone heredoc (no pipe) | body ✅ | body ✅ | body |
| 9 | empty upstream output `printf '' \| cat <<EOF` | body only (proves concat, not duplication) | — | body |
| 10 | here-string `printf P \| cat <<< H` | P⊕H ❌ | — | H |
| 11 | `/bin/sh -c` | — | body ✅ | body |

(⊕ = in-order byte concatenation, no separator. The heredoc body always arrives as **data**; a `echo SHOULD-NOT-RUN` probe confirms the body is never re-parsed as commands.)

## Suggested mitigations (OpenClaw side)

1. **Warn** when a command under shell=zsh combines a pipe with a heredoc/here-string on a non-first pipeline member. bash-tools already parses segments/tokens (e.g. the `token.startsWith("<<")` heredoc-approval path), so the hook point exists.
2. Alternatively, normalize heredoc-containing commands to bash-compatible execution, or document that heredocs are only safe **standalone or on the first pipeline stage** when exec uses zsh.
3. zsh upstream will be notified separately (mailing list; the zsh GitHub mirror has issues disabled). This box has no Homebrew zsh to distinguish Apple patches vs upstream, so the zsh-side report will carry that caveat.

## Notes

- Searched existing issues; no prior report of this specific behavior found. (Related but distinct: #114128 literal-`\n` via unquoted heredocs; #179890 `$<digit>` redaction.)
- Local incident log: 6 Exec-failed pushes on 2026-10-31 (03:12/05:12/07:00/09:11/11:43/14:41 GMT+8), all `NameError: name 'true'` from cron-list JSON being fed to `python3 -` as source code.

issues.title: [Feature]: Search and send native Zalo stickers through the existing zalouser channel

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Support native sticker search and sending in the official Zalo Personal plugin using the existing `sticker-search` and `sticker` message actions.

### Problem to solve

An OpenClaw extension author built a [patch for `@openclaw/zalouser`](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md) so group replies could include a native Zalo sticker selected by an emotion keyword. The [implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js) locates and rewrites the installed plugin's generated JavaScript, then calls `getStickers`, `getStickersDetail`, and `sendSticker` on its existing client. This is a concrete use case for sending a platform sticker object from an OpenClaw group conversation; an image attachment or emoji is a different output.

At [OpenClaw main `82c8ad576b31`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts), the plugin exposes only `react` as an additional shared message action. Its separate [`zalouser` tool](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts) accepts text, image, link, directory, profile, and status operations, with no sticker operation. Users of the official channel cannot perform this task through its supported actions.

The patch is historical, with its latest commit dated June 8, 2026. The same author's current [Setup project](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-setup/blob/0f12991d9787c1d3cf331b8b9ba1a256df2d559f/README.md) says the old integration and Sticker add-on were retired in favor of a maintained alternative channel. That is a valid solution. This request concerns supporting the same native object in the existing official channel, without maintaining a private patch or adopting another channel runtime. Current demand to migrate back to the official channel is unknown.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing `zalouser` channel action adapter; add no new core action, tool, SDK surface, credential store, or channel.

- `sticker-search`: for the selected account and an authorized group conversation, accept a bounded keyword query and return a bounded set of native sticker choices. Each choice must include a send-compatible selector carrying the native sticker ID, category ID, and type. Reuse the existing `query`, `limit`, and `stickerId`/`fileId` fields where appropriate. Exact selector encoding is a plugin implementation decision.
- `sticker`: send exactly one selected native sticker to that group using the same account/profile and existing target resolution and action authorization. Return the platform message ID and normal channel delivery result. Reject malformed selectors and unsupported targets before sending.
- Reuse the current plugin's API/session owner and cancellation/effect-boundary handling. Include the native `/api/group/sticker` POST in its dispatch tracking. Stop before submission if the admitted operation is canceled or no longer current. An ambiguous network outcome must not trigger a blind resend or a claim of confirmed delivery.

Initial scope is explicit group sticker search and send. Suggested search budget: default 5, maximum 10 choices; these are proposed resource bounds, not Zalo API limits. No automatic interpretation of `[Sticker: ...]` in ordinary text, automatic emotional replies, mention changes, sticker uploads, whole-catalog collection, or DM support is requested.

### Alternatives considered

- **Alternative channel:** [OpenClaw Zalo Connect](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-zalo-connect/blob/0e5908c6ccc00cde6f539a82fd82086fc90285de/README.md) already advertises native stickers and many other actions. It is a valid option. The remaining proposed benefit is for installations retaining the official `zalouser` channel and its current account/session owner; no claim is made that all OpenClaw users are blocked.
- **Patch the generated plugin:** the cited implementation targets generated `zalo-js-*.js` files. It expresses the exact missing behavior, but does not establish compatibility with current main. We have not executed it.
- **Skill or separate tool:** a skill can call supported tools, but cannot obtain this missing behavior from the official tool's closed action enum. A separate code plugin could own another Zalo connection or use an alternative channel's bridge; the official channel's client implementation is private. This does not establish a missing generic SDK contract.
- **Send an image, emoji, or reaction:** these remain useful existing outputs but do not send a native sticker object.

### Impact

- Affected: users who retain the official Zalo Personal channel and want native sticker replies in groups. A historical plugin patch demonstrates the task; the current affected population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: this particular output is unavailable through the official channel; text, media, and reactions remain usable. No urgent incident or quantitative severity has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Keyword-based group replies are described by the source; no usage frequency has been measured.
- Practical consequences: the documented approaches are patching generated plugin code or using a different channel. No time savings, user counts, or account-migration failure rates are claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original task and patch](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md), plus [native lookup/send implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js), commit `6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2`. This is implementation evidence, not an independently observed live send.
- [Current channel action adapter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts) and [optional tool schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts). A pinned scan of the plugin's non-test TypeScript, JSON, and Markdown found no sticker implementation.
- The plugin already pins [`zca-js` 2.2.0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/package.json). That package's published Git revision `dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9` contains [`getStickers`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickers.ts), [`getStickersDetail`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickersDetail.ts), and [`sendSticker`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/sendSticker.ts). The last accepts `id`, `cateId`, and `type`, supports group targets, and returns `msgId`.
- [Shared action vocabulary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts) and [schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/agents/tools/message-tool-schema.ts) already contain sticker search/send concepts. This is an adapter gap, not a new common contract.
- PRs [#27905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/27905) and [#29075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/29075) concern `zalo` Bot API inbound handling and emoji replies; neither supplies `zalouser` native sticker sending. Both are closed and unmerged at the research time.

Research is static. No dependency installation, external patch execution, paid service, account login, or authenticated Zalo delivery was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation entry points are the plugin's `channel.ts` action descriptor/handler, its lazy `channel.runtime.ts` exports, the private `zca-client.ts` API typing, and the existing `zalo-js.ts` API/session owner. The existing [`send-context.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-context.ts) checks cancellation and current effect authority; its message dispatch path matcher currently excludes `/sticker`. Reuse that owner and [`send-receipt.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-receipt.ts) rather than introducing a second sender. These are implementation suggestions, not a claim that the change has been built.

Preserve plugin lazy loading, existing account isolation, target and access policies, credential ownership, and current delivery outcome semantics. No configuration migration, new persistent catalog, new authorization scope, or dependency upgrade is proposed. Search can return fewer choices when detail lookup is partial; it must not claim catalog completeness. The existing unofficial Zalo integration and its account/platform limitations continue to apply. No implementer has committed. Selector encoding and the exact bounded search defaults remain owner decisions.

Acceptance criteria:

1. In an authorized group conversation on a configured `zalouser` account, search a keyword, choose one returned selector, and send it through the shared message tool. Zalo displays one native sticker in that group and the tool reports its platform message ID.
2. The selected account/profile is used for lookup and send. Another configured account is not silently selected; malformed selectors and unsupported non-group targets do not issue a sticker POST.
3. Cancellation or retirement during lookup/session preparation prevents a later send. A recorded accepted send retains its ID; an uncertain outcome is not reported as confirmed or blindly retried.
4. Empty/partially unavailable search results are bounded and explicit. Existing text/media/react paths continue to work, and ordinary text containing `[Sticker: ...]` does not acquire a new side effect.

An implementer should run focused action, routing, send-context, and receipt tests, then the affected plugin checks and startup profiler. A real authorized Zalo group is needed to verify native rendering and actual transport outcomes; mocked API responses alone cannot establish that acceptance criterion.

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.5, two native Codex turns in a Telegram direct conversation failed during local context preparation after approximately 60 seconds with `WorkerTaskError: worker task timed out`; OpenClaw surfaced each failure as a model request timeout / HTTP 408.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The same existing conversation can prepare its context and complete a native Codex turn: a diagnostic request succeeded before any changes, and another succeeded after the local mitigation described below. When context preparation fails locally, the diagnostic should identify that stage and preserve its local origin rather than suggest a confirmed upstream model HTTP failure.

### Actual behavior

Two production turns on September 21 failed at the `context` preparation stage. One spent 60,096 ms in context preparation; the other spent 60,059 ms. Both produced `worker task timed out`, then a model-fallback decision with `reason=timeout`, `status=408`, and no fallback configured. Telegram successfully delivered the warning:

> openai/gpt-6-astra request failed (request timed out, HTTP 408). This is usually temporary — try again shortly.

These logs establish a local preparation failure. They do not establish that the OpenAI API returned HTTP 408.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5, build ec9c1a1. Packaged installation. The production incidents were on the unmodified context-worker implementation.

### Operating system

macOS 12.7.6 (21H1320), x86_64; Node v24.20.0.

### Install method

Installed global Node package; gateway managed by a macOS LaunchAgent.

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

Telegram direct conversation → OpenClaw gateway → native Codex harness/app-server → OpenAI. The observed failure was in local context preparation before native turn handoff.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The failure logs identify `harnessId=codex`, `provider=openai`, `modelId=gpt-6-astra`, and `fallbackConfigured=false`. No model switch or session reset was used for the successful diagnostic checks.

### Logs

Selected fields only; account, chat, session, run identifiers, and local paths omitted:

```text
Incident 1:
  preparation stage=context outcome=error totalMs=61344
  stages=connection:177ms,runtime:8ms,tools:1063ms,context:60096ms
  harnessId=codex error="worker task timed out"
  errorName=WorkerTaskError
  model-fallback reason=timeout status=408 fallbackConfigured=false

Incident 2:
  preparation stage=context outcome=error totalMs=60614
  stages=connection:408ms,runtime:8ms,tools:139ms,context:60059ms
  harnessId=codex error="worker task timed out"
  errorName=WorkerTaskError
  model-fallback reason=timeout status=408 fallbackConfigured=false
  telegram outbound send ok
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The installed path inspected was:

```text
Codex prepareCodexAttemptContext / readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages
  → SessionManager.openModelContextAsync
  → readSessionTranscriptModelContextAsync
  → modelContextReads.run(..., { timeoutMs: 60000, signal })
```

The installed model-context pool has one worker and inherits the pool's 60-second idle retirement. Isolated reads of the affected conversation succeeded during diagnosis: approximately 2–15 seconds with a fresh worker, then approximately 0.14 seconds on subsequent reads with the same worker. The historical failure did not recur naturally during these checks.

A controlled test using that installed context-read path delayed the worker entrypoint by 61 seconds before importing the original compiled session-transcript worker. The original implementation failed at 60.006 seconds with the same `WorkerTaskError`. With the local mitigation below, it returned 569 messages in 62.494 seconds. This verifies the deadline behavior under an injected delay; it does **not** establish that a 61-second worker startup caused the production incidents.

An idle-retirement test shortened the existing idle timer only in the test harness: baseline created two workers; the mitigation reused one and returned identical message-array hashes. Cancellation during delayed startup still completed in 112 ms.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed installation and its Telegram direct conversation using native Codex.

Severity/consequence: the two affected turns returned an error instead of an assistant answer. The model-labelled warning made the local preparation failure look like an upstream request problem.

Frequency: intermittent; two observed production incidents, with successful same-session requests during subsequent diagnosis. No population-wide frequency or data-loss claim.

### Additional information

**Local mitigation, not a proposed final upstream design:** retain the single idle model-context worker (`idleTimeoutMs: 0`) and increase only its task deadline from 60 to 180 seconds. This retains worker memory and permits a longer wait; the existing cancellation and transcript-admission validation remain in place.

After restart, a first diagnostic check completed context preparation in 42.244 seconds but exceeded a shortened overall test budget while loading other components. A subsequent check with the normal 600-second budget completed successfully on the same model/session: context preparation 925 ms, complete agent turn 53.924 seconds, no tool calls, channel delivery disabled. Authenticated health reported Telegram running and connected. This is mitigation evidence, not proof that every underlying slowdown is fixed.

There were also slow SQLite transactions and broad startup/event-loop delays. Their causal contribution to the original context timeout is unproven. Last known good / first bad version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

**Current source check:** at main commit `9a472a998e1a97905850fabd89073ec6cc468276`, the code has moved to [session-transcript-read-worker-runtime.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a472a998e1a97905850fabd89073ec6cc468276/src/config/sessions/session-transcript-read-worker-runtime.ts), where `readSessionTranscriptModelContextAsync` still passes `timeoutMs: 60_000`. Main was inspected but not built or live-tested; this report does not claim a current-main reproduction.

Related context: #145708 explicitly addresses source-backed test worker startup and does not claim an installed-gateway improvement. #119720 tracks broader persistence/event-loop starvation; an identical root cause is not established here. No exact duplicate was found in the issue/PR searches performed.

Please triage the local timeout and its model-error classification, and advise whether an existing change addresses it before a timeout/worker-lifetime PR is proposed. This report was prepared with Codex assistance from local logs and controlled checks; private transcript contents and credentials are omitted.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`pnpm qa:e2e` (the QA self-check entry, `scripts/qa-e2e.ts` → `runQaE2eSelfCheck`) is not hermetic: the in-process qa-channel gateway loop resolves the session store from the **operator's real default state dir** (`~/.openclaw`). On a dev machine with an older installed OpenClaw, the self-check aborts with a `SqliteSchemaMismatchError` pointing at the real agent database — and the error text instructs the operator to run `openclaw doctor --fix` against their live installation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a machine with an existing `~/.openclaw` installation whose agent DB schema is older than the repo's `OPENCLAW_AGENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` (here: installed schema 21, repo requires 39), clone openclaw at `main` (`38ca38eb2cd`) and `pnpm install`.
2. Build the private QA runtime: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime`.
3. Run `pnpm qa:e2e` **without** setting `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
4. Observe the self-check exit 1 with the real-state schema error below. Setting `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/<isolated>` makes the same error disappear (verified), confirming the read targets the default state dir.

### Expected behavior

The repo-backed QA self-check runs against isolated state, like the other QA stack components already do:

- the model-catalog child builds a full temp `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` set (`extensions/qa-lab/src/model-catalog.runtime.ts`, `loadQaRunnerModelOptions`);
- gateway child processes get a temp state dir asserted by tests (`extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts`, `expect(env.OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR).toBe(path.join(path.dirname(env.OPENCLAW_HOME!), "state"))`).

### Actual behavior

`pnpm qa:e2e` exits 1 with:

```shell
OpenClaw agent database /home/<user>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite uses schema version 21; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 39 before using it.
```

Captured stack (node `--stack-trace-limit=40`, paths relative to repo root):

```shell
SqliteSchemaMismatchError
  at decodeSessionTranscriptWorkerReadError (src/config/sessions/session-history-worker-errors.ts:111)
  at Object.runRequest (src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-runtime.ts:354)
  at async readSessionEntryWithRetainedFacts (src/config/sessions/session-entry-read-facts.ts:418)
  at async readSessionUpdatedAtInWorker (src/config/sessions/session-entry-read-runtime.ts:222)
  at async createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync (src/channels/inbound-event/envelope.ts:48)
  at async handleQaInbound (extensions/qa-channel/src/inbound.ts:291)
  at async handleMessage (extensions/qa-channel/src/gateway.ts:88)
  at async startQaGatewayAccount (extensions/qa-channel/src/gateway.ts:207)
  at async <anonymous> (extensions/qa-lab/src/lab-server.ts:154)
  at async runQaE2eSelfCheck (extensions/qa-lab/src/self-check-runner.ts:11)
```

Root cause: `createQaChannelGatewayConfig` (`extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-channel-transport.ts`) does not set `session.store`, so `createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync` calls `resolveSessionStorePathCore(params.cfg.session?.store /* undefined */, ...)` and falls back to the default state dir — the operator's real `~/.openclaw` when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` is unset. The rejection only surfaces later, when `runQaE2eSelfCheck`'s `finally` calls `server.stop()` and awaits the gateway task, which also masks the scenario-level failure report (no report file is written on this path).

### OpenClaw version

main @ 38ca38eb2cd (package version 2026.10.9)

### Operating system

Linux (glibc 2.31, EL8-class), Node v26.12.1

### Install method

pnpm dev (git worktree of the repo, `pnpm install`)

### Model

None — the failure happens before any model call; the self-check uses the synthetic qa-channel echo harness.

### Provider / routing chain

None (in-process qa-channel + qa-lab bus; no provider traffic on this path).

### Logs

See reproduction output above; full run logs and the 40-frame stack are attached to my verification notes.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: contributors running the repo-backed QA self-check (`pnpm qa:e2e`) on any machine that has (or had) a real OpenClaw installation with an older agent-DB schema — a common contributor setup.
- Severity: blocks the workflow (the documented self-check entry cannot run), and the error message actively suggests `openclaw doctor --fix` against the operator's live installation, which would migrate the schema out from under their installed version.
- Frequency: always (2/2 runs without `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; disappears with an isolated state dir).
- Consequence: QA self-check unusable on affected machines; misleading remediation advice risks the operator's real state.

### Additional information

The QA stack's own components treat hermetic state as the intended contract (model-catalog child and gateway child both pin temp state); only the in-process self-check path misses it. A minimal fix is for the `qa:e2e` entry to default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` to a temp directory when unset (mirroring `loadQaRunnerModelOptions`), while still respecting explicit operator overrides. I plan to open a PR with a regression test in `test/scripts/qa-e2e.test.ts`.

issues.body:
## Problem

Cloud worker lifecycle and workspace settlement improvements are mixed across two large, dependent commits. They need independently reviewable fixes and coherent retained-disk changes before adoption in OpenClaw.

Source commits:
- https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27
- https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/8c2d1d7a98f6299d6cc08126244efdd178d4c6f9

## Published first wave

All four first-wave PRs are merged into main: #188802, #188805, #188807 and #188817. They retain existing configuration and Gateway checkpoint durability; no deployment was performed. The production counts and initial proof below describe the original extraction candidates; final landing evidence is recorded in each PR.

| PR | Delivered functionality | Production lines (+/−) |
|---|---|---:|
| #188802 | Linux platform certificate registration before fresh/cached enrollment | +20/−1 |
| #188805 | Interrupted Stop recovery through the existing final-save owner | +21/−2 |
| #188807 | Accepted-parent incremental transfer, immutable-object and unchanged-checkpoint reuse | +239/−102 |
| #188817 | Deferred GitHub publication with frozen turn/session snapshots and queued-request reuse | +111/−74 |

Net production growth: **212 lines**. Each has focused regression proof and clean independent full-candidate review. Parent verification matched every published tree to its reviewed implementation and checked contributor credit and work-session links. The checkpoint fixture imports 263,529 bytes, then 1,580 bytes, then zero for an unchanged follow-up; this is work-count evidence, not a live latency benchmark.

Original implementation CI: #188817 passed its then-current exact-head aggregate gate. The original heads of the first three failed the test-line ratchet on unchanged inherited debt: exact main-parent excesses are 1,025, 1,025, and 1,013 lines respectively. Each PR adds exactly matching allocation for its own regression tests. Detailed attribution is in each PR; the shared baseline was not raised.

## Published second wave

[PR #188914](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188914) rejects new worker-turn and remote-exec input before claiming it when the exact attached provider lease cannot be qualified. Unavailable observations preserve ownership for retry; dormant devices retain reconnect behavior; confirmed loss uses the existing cleanup owner. It does not allocate a replacement or replay input.

- **Merged later at source7ed59f9b; see current landing evidence below.** Historical intermediate published head: `da87c635972f1cf8aada5fdd4410defc0012388d`. Original implementation proof below applies to head `8ac83252f073102fadf7dae6ee08a41835c7c808`, tree `7752a51579578515de57cd14993f061b31397951`; the later same-PR repair updates its direct consumers and fixtures.
- Six production files: **+199/−42 (net +157)**. Tests/support: +232/−3 with exactly 229 allocated regression lines; no shared baseline increase. All five implementation PRs total **+590/−221 (net +369) production lines**.
- Production-path baseline reproduction: 1 input claim / 0 inspections. Fixed: 0 claims / 1 exact-lease inspection. Real SQLite/service/launcher and recovery coverage qualifies 73 cases through separate receipts: 71 passed in the combined run, followed by both repaired fixture cases passing. No claim of a single 73-case final pass.
- Targeted type checks, type-aware lint, formatting, pre-commit, diff and documentation-link checks passed. Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 findings. Provider I/O is fixture-backed; no live provider allocation or model-driven Gateway run was performed.
- Published tree, contributor trailers, and both exact Work sessions links verified. Exact-head aggregate CI for `da87c635972f1cf8aada5fdd4410defc0012388d` is **successful**, rechecked October 31 at 05:02 UTC: [ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160199574/job/124420827764). Production and test type checks also succeeded on that head.
- No schema, configuration, public provider API, same-node restart, retained-disk behavior, merge or deployment is included.

## Current implementation status — November 1, twelve landings; final acceptance remains open

The full S4/S5 extraction goal remains active. **Thirteen implementation PRs are published; twelve are merged into main.** No deployment has been performed. Retained-disk mode is landed as opt-in; no live profile has been activated by this task. Galin has now explicitly authorized applying review comments and merging ready PRs. One finalizer owns guarded landing in dependency order; deployment, paid allocation, and Crabbox release/adoption remain excluded.

**Source closeout complete through S9:** all three native lifecycle/S8/S9 outcomes are complete, with exact-head CI, main containment, landed-tree composition, Galin credit and cleanup verified. The disk-feature cut is `8085604eb96542931b3a9fc79ef337d2d8c5c969` / tree `df6dd7d8f4e2e2588d6da081991ebde2da9ccb6a`. Fifty feature blobs and fourteen review-context blobs match qualified source; nine critical R5 owners remain byte-identical to exact0b2a, so completed R5 is not reopened.

**Remaining installed acceptance — November 2:** landed disk-feature cut `8085604e` is selected independently of optional same-node restart. [Package Acceptance 41374216130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41374216130), attempt 1/workflow `d0177edd`, passed: 9 successful/15 skipped jobs, all 7 artifact ZIP digests verified. Exact package SHA256 `1ca74e8e97b02c2ee6c052817383f15428140adeeb959a62381bf386a2405f52`, build `2026.10.9-8085604eb965-2026-11-02T01-48-56.865Z`; config reload passed once in 18s with joined cleanup.

The executable installed-activation fixture is qualified: all four canonical assignments covered the complete eight-file/72-context delta and found one P2. Its 13-line complete-inventory repair received a scoped-clean independent review. The original aggregate remains findings/exit 1; earlier incomplete/unavailable reviews remain preserved. Parent verified all 79 archive members and all 35 fixture/helper files against the final manifest, plus exact raw package/image digests. The existing functional image is truthfully bound and the independent installed CLI/SDK excludes its preinstalled /app application.

**Installed native acceptance remains unqualified.** [Native infrastructure run41383750758](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41383750758) is terminal, but its successful infrastructure conclusion is **not** an installed-test pass.

- Attempt1 correctly refused the parent's combined8CPU/16GiB budgets after read-only Docker info: actual daemon4CPU/16,556,183,552bytes RAM despite the nominal16vCPU label. It remains FAIL. No image load, test container/volume, Gateway, worker or model execution followed.
- Attempt2 used the same lease and unchanged35-file fixture with corrected2CPU/4GiB budgets per container. Local source preparation took998,231ms. The workflow enforces a15-minute idle cap despite config/inspect showing30m; its exact job log records idle shutdown at04:04:51UTC. At04:10:59 the native owner refused reuse of the completed lease before synchronization or command execution (exit2, syncMs0, commandMs0, settledtrue). Attempt2 remains FAIL/unexecuted, not a runtime defect or pass.
- Normal claim-guarded stop returned0. 4. Disk-authoritative repository activation with its migration/downgrade protection, pending-result recovery, refusal to restore stale mirrors, on-demand file access, and explicit publication capture in the same coherent feature.

Separately reviewable: evidence-backed missing-checkpoint reconstruction (blocked by the donor predicate's data-loss counterexamples below); explicit lossy lost-worker recovery; optional diagnostics. Do not mix non-lossy reconstruction with a reset to a repository ref.

The retained-disk sequence through opt-in activation is now landed in main, culminating in #189668. Its no-per-turn-Gateway-backup tradeoff remains the accepted contract below. This task has not deployed or activated a live profile. Same-node restart and final integrated acceptance remain open. Current main owns supervised TLS inheritance and the final-save helper; this extraction does not duplicate them.

## Original extraction scope

Independent fixes:
- Register provider-installed Linux certificate authorities before enrollment, including snapshot forks, without exposing bootstrap credentials.
- Complete interrupted worker drains through the existing pending-result recovery owner.
- Transfer only repository changes since the last accepted checkpoint and reuse unchanged immutable objects/checkpoints.
- Move GitHub network publication out of workspace settlement after its exact snapshot and recovery receipt are durable.

Retained-disk functionality requires a dependent sequence: provider-owned retention receipts and pause/resume, exact-node recovery, then disk-authoritative repository workspaces with explicit file/publication transfer. Schema migration, original-owner checks, pending-result recovery, and prevention of stale mirror restoration must ship together with their consumers. The later disk-authoritative mode would remove automatic per-turn Gateway backups; confirmed disk loss can lose unpushed changes. Retained lifecycle is proposed first with Gateway backups preserved.

## Scope and validation

Reimplement minimal behavior on current main; do not cherry-pick the donor commits wholesale. Their commit boundaries contain missing contracts and incomplete wiring. Each implementation PR should include focused regression proof and independent review. Galin's subsequent explicit instruction authorizes ready-PR merges through the guarded workflow; cloud deployment remains excluded. Already-shipped supervised TLS inheritance is not part of the extraction.

Original work by @galiniliev; extraction requested by the contributor.


## Review follow-up and next wave

Requested 2026-10-31: final review of the four published PRs and continued extraction. The completed independent P0–P3 review found no actionable defects in the first four patches. Exact-lease admission is now published as #188914. Its initial managed checkout failed before edits; the existing clean extraction checkout was reused through the supported session owner. Same-node restart remains the next dependency-ordered feature.

Publication PR #188817 still has passing exact-head aggregate CI and local independent review, but its hosted ClawSweeper review was stopped at input safety. The first locator in the redacted failure manifest identifies an unchanged base diagnostic-redaction fixture; two findings were reported and only the first has a locator. Its PR body records the evidence and scanner-owner qualification remains outstanding. No scanner policy or baseline was weakened.

## Source-only reconstruction: feasibility finding

The donor rule is **not non-lossy**: equality of the accepted file manifest and pinned source does not prove equality of Git history or publication membership.

- A private commit followed by restoring source working-tree bytes produces matching manifests while production capture retains a private HEAD and a 335-byte history pack. Rebuilding from source discards that accepted history.
- Removing an ignored tracked file from the index with `git rm --cached` leaves its recovery-file manifest unchanged but changes the publication digest/membership. Source reconstruction reverses the accepted removal.

The production-capture harness used real isolated Git repositories at upstream `4a393be419f30ecfd65972fe3ea1416c6f707316`; both counterexamples passed (exit 0). The exercised sources were unchanged at observed newer main `a32d79a2c763d3dab52022027fce38c34c7b3dea`. Independent P0–P3 feasibility review confirmed both P1 findings. This is capture-boundary proof, not an end-to-end restore pass. No donor code was executed and no implementation was published.

Keep accepted-but-missing checkpoints fail-closed. The repository row does not retain accepted HEAD/publication digest or a positive source-only certificate outside the lost artifact. Settled custody and a low revision number do not supply that evidence; a fresh fork can already contain private history. A future safe extraction needs durable positive reconstruction evidence in the existing owner, or a separately proved narrower first-checkpoint/non-fork/no-setup policy. Neither is currently accepted or certified.

[Investigation and proof session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/06ccfc21-23e4-4a52-b337-0c6cfa8b4966)

## Accepted feature contracts — historical specification

Exact-lease turn admission is implemented in #188914 without changing public-provider or storage contracts. Source-only reconstruction is not currently a safe minimal extraction; it needs the positive evidence described above. Galin accepted the same-node restart and retained lifecycle proposal, then explicitly requested disk-authoritative Azure Sandbox workspaces in smaller PRs. Implementation remains subject to the new public-provider and persistence contracts under [the storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes).

### 1. Same enrolled-node restart

Add one optional `WorkerProvider.resumeNode` capability to the existing provider contract, with exact lease ID, enrolled device ID, saved runtime identity, cancellation signal and live-authority callback. The runtime-refresh owner calls it only for an exclusively attached dedicated machine with no live enrolled-node process. Crabbox verifies retained runtime/config/device identity and process death before restarting that same node. It never allocates, pairs, changes repository contents or replays a turn. Providers without the capability retain today's reconnect behavior. A generic setup-command replay is not equivalent because it can rerun provisioning and grants.

### 2. Retained disk lifecycle while preserving Gateway backups

Opt-in `retention: { mode: "session-disk", computeWindowSeconds: <positive finite duration> }`, limited initially to a capable Linux Azure Sandbox Crabbox profile. Non-opted profiles remain unchanged. Reuse the environment store, writer, lock, maintenance sweep and teardown owner; no separate queue, timer or state file.

Persist a nullable session-retention record on each environment before allocation. It binds the exact session/agent, environment, original operation, policy, provider resource identity, current provider receipt and pending pause/resume intent. An existing shared/reserve allocation cannot silently become a session-private disk. Add a forward state-schema migration using the current upstream version rather than the donor's obsolete v32. Preserve existing rows; older binaries must refuse the new schema because their teardown code does not understand retained disks. PostgreSQL parity and generated schemas are part of the same PR.

Persist each lifecycle operation ID before the provider effect; after restart retry that exact operation. Validate receipts at the provider boundary and preserve unknown ownership. Only an active finite compute window admits execution; its deadline does not promise an exact provider billing cutoff. Idle suspension keeps the disk but stops compute; explicit Stop/Delete still final-saves and deletes through confirmed provider teardown. Failed or ambiguous deletion remains visibly pending. Routine turn settlement continues to create Gateway checkpoints in this first retention PR.

Rollback means disabling new retention admissions, safely settling/deleting or explicitly migrating every retained environment, then restoring the matching pre-migration backup with its binary. A package-only downgrade cannot safely forget retained resources. Suspended disks may continue to incur provider storage costs; this PR creates no live allocations during review.

Proof must cover fresh/old-state migration, PostgreSQL parity, same-session resume, interrupted operation/restart, expired compute admission, changed owner/resource refusal, offline observation, cancellation, final-save/Stop and confirmed deletion. The real provider CLI/controller must advertise `session-disk-retention-v1` and `pause-resume`; deterministic protocol tests alone are not live provider proof.

### 3. Classified provider-outage containment

Separate follow-up on the retention owner: hold only environments whose provider observation is specifically unavailable, allowing unrelated startup recovery to proceed. Storage corruption, cancellation and authority failures remain failures. No blanket catch-and-continue.

### 4. Disk-authoritative repositories — accepted target

Only after retained lifecycle is complete, optionally let the retained disk replace automatic per-turn Gateway file checkpoints for repository-only sessions. This can eliminate ordinary capture/upload/mirror scans but means confirmed disk loss can lose unpushed/private files. Keeping Gateway backups is a supported alternative and avoids this changed guarantee.

Activation must include the repository store's authority identity and downgrade fence, migration of existing pending results, refusal to restore stale Gateway mirrors, on-demand attachment/download/file access, and fresh explicit publication capture. These are required consumers, not optional follow-ups. Default behavior remains mirrored. Galin has authorized implementing opt-in activation in the PR series. Galin's later ready-PR merge instruction supersedes the original no-merge scope. It does not authorize migration of the live Team server, deployment, paid allocations, or lossy recovery.

### Other separable work

- Explicit lost-worker recovery from the recorded repository ref is a separate lossy opt-in. Reuse the existing loss-confirmation owner; never default to an arbitrary branch or confuse it with exact checkpoint reconstruction.
- Provisioning/settlement diagnostics can follow the finished owners using current loggers. No dedicated timing subsystem.

### Design acceptance and implementation boundary — 2026-10-31

Galin approved the restart and retained lifecycle proposal and subsequently requested: “the benefits of Azure Sandboxes and snapshot are Disk-authoritative workspace — let's implement it in smaller prs.” This accepts disk-authoritative workspaces as the target of the implementation series, including the previously explained removal of automatic per-turn Gateway file checkpoints. Source: [original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd).

The backup-preserving retention stage is an intermediate prerequisite, not a substitute for the requested final feature. Keep migration, exact resource ownership, old pending-result recovery, on-demand file/attachment reads, frozen publication capture, and refusal of stale mirror restoration complete before enabling disk authority. Snapshots do not imply continuous backup of every subsequent write.

Plugin boundary: extend the existing Crabbox worker integration and its Azure backend for vendor-specific allocation, snapshots and retained-resource operations. Core owns only generic capability/receipt contracts and workspace/recovery semantics; do not copy the donor's hard-coded Crabbox/Azure eligibility checks into core. A direct-Azure plugin independent of Crabbox is not part of this extraction.

PR boundaries are behavior-based: same-enrolled-node process restart; retained-resource lifecycle; durable repository/result authority and recovery prerequisites; explicit file/publication consumers; final opt-in activation. Foundation PRs must be labeled as prerequisites, compile with current consumers, and keep existing behavior until activation. Do not publish a design-only PR as implementation.

The original #188914 CI failures were repaired in the same PR; its exact-head aggregate gate is now successful as recorded above. Earlier focused receipts alone were not treated as broad CI qualification.
