issues.body:
## Summary

`agents.defaults` supports a single system-wide `thinking` (reasoning-effort) value, but reasoning-parameter names and valid values are **provider-specific**. A system-wide default cannot be correct across a multi-provider fleet: the moment an agent's model is switched to a different provider, the inherited default silently becomes an invalid or wrong-tier parameter. OpenClaw needs **per-provider defaults** for provider-coupled parameters like `thinking`/reasoning-effort, not just one global default.

## Why a system-wide default is structurally wrong

`thinking` is coupled to the model's provider:

- **Anthropic** accepts `adaptive` (and `off`/`low`/`medium`/`high` tiers).
- **Google (Gemini)** does not accept `adaptive`; effective values are `off`/`high`.
- **Moonshot (Kimi)** uses `low`.
- Other providers use their own names / tiers, and future providers will add more.

`adaptive` is anthropic-only. A single `agents.defaults.thinking = "adaptive"` is valid for the Anthropic majority and an **invalid request** for every Gemini/Moonshot/xAI agent that inherits it. Flip a system-wide default to `high` to suit an Anthropic agent and you may push an invalid tier at a Moonshot agent. There is no single value that is correct fleet-wide, so the abstraction (one global default) cannot express the real constraint.

## Concrete failure mode (what prompted this)

Operating a fleet of ~15 agents across Anthropic, Google, Moonshot, and xAI. When we switch a single agent's primary model between providers, its reasoning parameter has to be re-validated by hand because the inherited default no longer applies. In practice this produces one of two silent failures:

1. **Invalid parameter** — the provider rejects the request at every dispatch (e.g. `adaptive` sent to Gemini), or
2. **Wrong default** — the parameter is dropped and the model falls through to a generic gateway default, so the table says one reasoning tier and the runtime does another. The failure is silent: nothing errors loudly, the agent just runs at the wrong effort.

Today the only safe workaround is to set `thinking` explicitly on **every** agent so none inherit the global default — which defeats the purpose of having a default at all.

## Proposed change

Introduce per-provider defaults for provider-coupled parameters. Sketch (naming illustrative):

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": { "primary": "...", "fallbacks": ["..."] },
      "providerDefaults": {
        "anthropic": { "thinking": "adaptive" },
        "google":    { "thinking": "high" },
        "moonshot":  { "thinking": "low" },
        "xai":       { "thinking": "off" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Resolution order for a given agent's parameter:
1. explicit per-agent value (highest priority)
2. per-provider default matching the agent's **resolved model provider**
3. system-wide default (backward-compatible fallback)
4. built-in gateway default

This keeps existing configs working (system-wide default still honored when no provider default matches) while letting a multi-provider fleet express correct defaults. It also means switching an agent's model between providers automatically picks up the right reasoning default instead of silently carrying a wrong or invalid one.

## Scope note

This generalizes beyond `thinking`. Any parameter whose valid names/values are provider-specific (reasoning effort, certain sampling controls, etc.) has the same problem with a single global default. A `providerDefaults` block is the general fix; `thinking` is just the first parameter to bite.

## Environment

- Multi-provider agent fleet (Anthropic / Google / Moonshot / xAI), ~15 agents.
- Failure surfaces on any cross-provider model switch; observed as both invalid-parameter rejections and silent wrong-tier fall-through.

During the next diagnostic probe, `Autoupdate` had exited. Load then declined from 295.66 to 122.84 and subsequently 83.13; a later snapshot showed 70.12% CPU idle. This records correlation, not proof that the updater caused the entire load spike.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (build 2609000490)

### Operating system

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

For `claude-cli` (stream-json) turns, the usage persisted to the session transcript — and therefore read by `usage.cost` and the Usage page — is the last `assistant` event's `message.usage` (one model call, carrying the partial output count Claude Code reports at stream start) instead of the turn total that the CLI's terminal `result` event already provides.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent whose model uses the `claude-cli` runtime (Claude subscription auth).
2. Send it a message that needs at least one tool call, so the turn makes 2+ model calls.
3. Compare `openclaw gateway call usage.cost --params '{"agentId":"<id>","startDate":"<day>","endDate":"<day>"}'` (or the Usage page) with Claude Code's own transcript for the same turns (`~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/*.jsonl`, deduplicated by `message.id`), or with the `result` event of the same stream.

What the stream contains, using the flags the backend passes:

```sh
claude -p "Use the Bash tool to run exactly: echo hi. Then reply with only the word: done" \
  --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages \
  --allowedTools Bash --model claude-sonnet-5
```

Usage fields observed (Claude Code 2.1.263):

| event | output_tokens | cache_read_input_tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `assistant` — call 1 (tool_use) | 15 | 27255 |
| `stream_event` `message_delta` — call 1 | **74** | 27255 |
| `assistant` — call 2 (text) | 1 | 27376 |
| `stream_event` `message_delta` — call 2 | **3** | 27376 |
| `result` | **77** | **54631** (plus `total_cost_usd`, `modelUsage`) |

Claude Code's transcript file stores the final per-call counts (a second run: 80 and 14, `result` 94).

### Expected behavior

Persisted turn usage reflects the whole turn, as the CLI reports it in the terminal `result` event — the same aggregate OpenClaw already parses and, since #120100, uses for the `openclaw.model.usage` diagnostic. Per-call usage kept for context snapshots uses that call's final output count (`message_delta`), not the stream-start value.

### Actual behavior

- [`src/agents/cli-output-stream.ts` L305-L325](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6708e942c4d13a42912bc8f7f94fc52ed82cdfe6/src/agents/cli-output-stream.ts#L305-L325): the Claude `result` aggregate is kept only as `diagnosticUsage`; `usage` keeps the last non-result event's usage, i.e. the last `assistant` event.
- [`src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.ts` L622-L626](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6708e942c4d13a42912bc8f7f94fc52ed82cdfe6/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.ts#L622-L626): `usage` and `lastCallUsage` are the same object.
- [`src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.ts` L394-L400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6708e942c4d13a42912bc8f7f94fc52ed82cdfe6/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.ts#L394-L400) and [L193-L199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6708e942c4d13a42912bc8f7f94fc52ed82cdfe6/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.ts#L193-L199): the persisted assistant message gets that `usage` via `buildUsageWithNoCost`.

So every turn is persisted as roughly its final model call, with a stream-start output count (typically 1–20 tokens).

Production observation (one agent, same UTC day, ~12 hours, 2026.9.2):

| source | model calls / entries | output tokens | cache read | cache write |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `usage.cost` for the agent | 10 entries | 22 | 766,878 | 103,253 |
| Claude Code transcripts for that agent's workspace | 84 calls | 79,441 | 6,346,195 | 481,434 |

The same ~1–3 output tokens per entry showed up for every agent on the gateway, across channel, heartbeat and isolated cron turns.

Secondary: records are keyed `claude-cli/<model>`, which has no pricing entry, so `usage.cost` reports `missingCostByModel: {"claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5": N}` even though `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` has configured `cost`. (Per #102771, dollar cost on subscription billing may be intentionally de-emphasized; the token counts are the main problem.)

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (3928bad); the code paths above are unchanged on main at 6708e942c4

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS x86_64

### Install method

npm global install, Node v24.18.0, user systemd service

### Model

claude-sonnet-5

### Provider / routing chain

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 → claude-cli runtime (Claude Code 2.1.263, subscription OAuth, stream-json, no proxy)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See the stream-event and production tables above.

### Impact and severity

Affects anyone on the `claude-cli` runtime: the Usage page, `usage.cost` totals, and anything built on them (reports, budget alerts) undercount tool-using turns by the number of model calls per turn and almost entirely drop output tokens. In the observation above, output was undercounted ~3,600x and cache reads ~8x. No crash; data correctness only.

### Additional information

Related:
- #120060 / #120100: the turn aggregate is already preserved as `diagnosticUsage`, but only for the OTel `model.usage` event; transcript/session usage was deliberately left as last-call.
- #89474 / #137030: the same undercount class on the Codex runtime, fixed in 2026.9.3 by summing unique completed responses and keeping latest-prompt context separate from whole-turn accounting. The CLI runner's usage path was not changed there.
- #85573 / #85600, #118772, #125333: why the persisted value can't simply become the aggregate. It also feeds context-window snapshots, so a fix likely needs separate whole-turn (billing) and last-call (context, with final output count) usage.

## Summary
Allow users to unpin Home from the Control UI Pages section without losing access to the underlying conversation.

## Problem to solve
Home is a permanent shortcut to the selected agent's main conversation, while other conversations can be organized into custom session groups. For users who organize their work in those groups, Home is redundant and its separate placement is confusing. The label also suggests an overview rather than a conversation.

## Proposed solution
- Keep Home pinned by default, preserving the existing experience.
- Allow unpinning Home through the existing navigation pin controls.
- When Home is unpinned, include its underlying conversation in the ordinary session list, respecting custom groups and existing filters. Users should be able to group it normally.
- Allow restoring Home through **Edit pinned items**. When restored, avoid duplicating the conversation in the ordinary list.
- Persist the choice through the existing UI preference mechanism.
- Treat this strictly as navigation customization: do not delete, archive, reset, replace, or reroute the conversation, and preserve its transcript and group metadata.

## Alternatives considered
- Rename Home to Main chat: clearer naming, but still forces a separate shortcut on group-oriented users.
- Hide Home without exposing its session: reduces clutter but makes the conversation difficult to find.
- Turn Home into a dashboard: a broader product direction, not necessary to address this navigation preference.

## Impact
Affected: Control UI users who organize conversations into custom groups.
Severity: usability friction, not a blocker.
Frequency: every sidebar interaction.
Consequence: a mandatory navigation item outside the user's chosen organization model.

## Evidence/examples
The sessions/sidebar documentation explicitly describes Home as the rolling main session and excludes it from the ordinary session list.

Related but distinct:
- #110296: Home dashboard and Pages shelf.
- #142970: Bot-mode presentation of one Home conversation.
- #139603: replacing an unhealthy Home session; this request does not change Home identity.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Yes. Implementation and focused regression coverage will follow in a linked PR.

issues.body:
## Summary

When Anthropic (or Anthropic-compatible) streaming ends with truncated / unparseable tool-call argument JSON, current OpenClaw transport behavior is fail-closed: the run becomes `stopReason=error`, the partial `toolCall` is stripped from the turn, and the user-visible session looks aborted.

Anthropic's public docs recommend a different recovery shape for invalid/incomplete tool JSON, and a separate retry shape for `max_tokens` incomplete `tool_use`. This issue asks whether OpenClaw wants any of that recovery on `main`, without undoing the fail-closed work that prevents executing partial tool calls.

## Current behavior (locked by tests)

On Anthropic transport, cases such as:

- `stop_reason=max_tokens` mid-`input_json_delta`
- missing `content_block_stop` / incomplete tool call
- sealed block that still fails strict JSON object parse

result in:

- `stopReason=error`
- no executable / persisted `toolCall` on the turn
- no automatic `tool_result(is_error=true, INVALID_JSON=...)` continuation

This matches the direction of:

- #97140 / #97092 — ignore / scrub truncated non-`toolUse` tool calls (do not execute or replay)
- #126391 — reject malformed / unsealed streamed tool arguments at the provider boundary

Related earlier discussion that did not land as Anthropic-doc recovery:

- #63210 — detect/recover from `length` truncation (closed stale; previously needed product decision)
- #87571 — incomplete-tool-call retry PR (closed / superseded)

## Anthropic docs (upstream contract)

1. **Invalid / incomplete JSON from fine-grained tool streaming**  
   [Fine-grained tool streaming → Handling invalid JSON in tool responses](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/fine-grained-tool-streaming)  
   Do not run the tool; return a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and content shaped like:

   ```json
   { "INVALID_JSON": "<the unparseable input you received>" }
   ```

2. **Incomplete tool use cut by `max_tokens`**  
   [Handling stop reasons → Incomplete tool use blocks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons)  
   Retry the same request with a higher `max_tokens` to obtain the full tool use (Tool Runner docs also advise not auto-appending the truncated assistant message when bumping the budget).

3. **Invalid tool input / missing params (already-complete `tool_use`)**  
   [Handle tool calls → Handling errors with `is_error`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls)  
   Continue with `tool_result` + `is_error: true`; Claude may retry with corrections a few times.

Official Anthropic SDK Tool Runner does **not** auto-implement the `INVALID_JSON` wrapper; streaming parse failure surfaces as an error asking the caller to retry. The `INVALID_JSON` pattern is documented as an application-level recovery option.

## What this is / is not asking for

**Not asking to undo fail-closed:**

- Unsealed / incomplete tool calls must still never execute.
- Lenient "complete the partial JSON and run the tool" must stay forbidden.

**Asking for a product decision on optional recovery after fail-closed detection.**

## Proposed recovery (single pipeline)

Anthropic's docs describe two complementary recoveries for different failure modes. Treat them as **one pipeline**, not alternative product options:

```
classify failure
  │
  ├─ max_tokens / length and tool call incomplete
  │     → bump-budget retry first
  │       (do not append truncated assistant turn;
  │        retry same message prefix with higher max_tokens, bounded)
  │         ├─ success → normal tool execution
  │         └─ still incomplete / still invalid JSON
  │              → INVALID_JSON feedback (or surface error)
  │
  └─ sealable tool_use (id/name present; input can be a safe object)
        but arguments JSON invalid/incomplete
          → INVALID_JSON feedback:
            persist tool_use + tool_result(is_error, INVALID_JSON=raw)
            and continue the agent loop
```

### Bump-budget retry (`max_tokens` / incomplete tool use)

When `stop_reason` is `max_tokens` / `length` and the tool call is incomplete:

1. Do **not** append the truncated assistant turn.
2. Retry the same message prefix with a higher `max_tokens` (bounded attempts / ceiling).
3. If still incomplete after the budget, continue to `INVALID_JSON` feedback below, or surface error.

Note: if the configured cap is already high, bumping may be ineffective; chunking guidance remains relevant.

### `INVALID_JSON` feedback (narrow)

Only when a tool call is sealable enough to persist a valid Anthropic `tool_use` block (`id`, `name`, `input` as an object, e.g. `{}` or best-effort object) and no mutating tool from that turn has already executed:

1. Keep that `tool_use` in history.
2. Immediately append matching `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and `INVALID_JSON` wrapper containing the raw argument string.
3. Continue the agent loop so the model can correct / chunk.

Hard stop if pairing cannot be formed safely (same class of risk as orphan `tool_use` → next-request 400).

### Opt-out — Keep current fail-closed UX

No automatic recovery; keep error + scrub. Optionally improve operator-facing error text only.

## Local observation (non-blocking)

On one Anthropic-compatible gateway used for a smoke check, a docs-shaped history (`tool_use` with `input: {}` + `tool_result(is_error, INVALID_JSON=...)`) returned HTTP 200 and the model issued a corrected `tool_use`. That does **not** replace first-party `api.anthropic.com` proof for a future PR; it only suggests the docs recovery shape is worth deciding on.

## Question for maintainers

Is this recovery pipeline in scope for OpenClaw `main`, or should this stay fail-closed (opt-out) / live only in a fork or plugin?

If recovery is welcome, which gates should a follow-up PR implement (provider-specific vs all transports, attempt limits, side-effect guards, when bump-budget retry falls through to `INVALID_JSON` feedback)?

I can open a narrow PR after an explicit direction here.

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow an enabled bundle's unused language servers to remain cold until their capabilities are requested, while continuing to expose only tools supported by the server's initialize response.

## Problem to solve

Preparing an agent attempt currently starts and initializes every configured bundled LSP server before any LSP tool is invoked. A conversation that does not need code intelligence still pays the startup cost of those servers.

At OpenClaw commit `62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675`, `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` awaits `createBundleLspToolRuntime`. That owner iterates configured servers serially, awaits each spawn/initialize, then materializes hover/definition/references tools from the returned capabilities. The existing runtime test explicitly expects processes to start during construction.

This is an optimization proposal, not a claim that the current initialization behavior violates LSP.

## Proposed solution

Use the existing tool discovery surface to represent configured LSP server descriptors without immediately constructing their execution runtimes. When discovery requests one server's capabilities, start that server, complete initialize, and return only its supported tools. Reuse the initialized runtime for later calls within the admitted lifecycle.

The linked standalone prototype demonstrates this boundary with the unmodified current LSP runtime. It is deliberately not integrated into OpenClaw's catalog or configuration. I would like maintainer guidance on the discovery contract before proposing the production change:

- Can the existing Tool Search/catalog owner admit deferred server descriptors, and which search/describe operation should materialize them?
- How should providers using a full, eagerly materialized tool list behave? The proposal should not silently remove their currently available LSP tools.
- What is the intended lifecycle owner for capabilities and warm LSP processes across attempts? Capability snapshots must not outlive their server/configuration/authority generation.

The production implementation must preserve deterministic collision handling and tool grants; revalidate admitted authority after awaited startup; share concurrent discovery; retain per-server diagnostics; support request cancellation; and join the current owned-stdio shutdown/descendant-extinction path. An unconfirmed cleanup must not become an automatic restart loop. The prototype does not establish these full host integration contracts.

## Alternatives considered

- Pre-register every possible hover/definition/references tool and initialize on execute. This advertises unsupported operations before the capability handshake, so it does not preserve the current discovery contract.
- Persist server capabilities and reuse them indefinitely. Capabilities belong to a live server/configuration generation; stale snapshots would select incorrect tools. The current project also requires lifecycle-owned storage rather than an ad hoc sidecar cache.
- Start all servers in parallel. This may reduce time spent waiting on multiple servers, but still starts unused processes. Earlier startup-concurrency work is relevant context, not equivalent to deferred discovery.
- Leave eager behavior unchanged. This keeps the current model-facing contract and may be preferable unless realistic end-to-end measurements establish sufficient benefit.

## Impact

Affected: agents with configured bundle LSP servers whose turns only sometimes need code intelligence. Consequence: avoidable preparation latency and processes on turns that never use those servers. Frequency depends on configuration and workflow. No broad production prevalence or real-server savings are claimed by this fixture.

Deferred startup moves initialization onto first discovery/use; first-use latency must remain visible in before/after evidence. A server used by every turn may gain little and can experience slower first tool execution after preparation.

## Evidence/examples

[Runnable prototype, source snapshots with hashes/license, reproduction instructions, and complete measurements](https://gist.github.com/yufanyang214-lab/6eae3d303673cf94a3265ba80f53454e).

A portable proof executes the exact pinned `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`, pending-request registry, deferred helper, and owned-stdio close helper against real Node child processes speaking Content-Length framed LSP. The fixture advertises only hover and inserts a controlled 100 ms initialize delay per server. It makes no network/model calls and reads no user configuration.

Six behavior checks pass: eager unused-server startup; zero-spawn cold disposal; concurrent discovery sharing one server and a real hover result; failure diagnostics followed by explicit retry; disposal during startup; and per-request cancellation preserving the shared process. Only hover is exposed, and retained tools reject after disposal.

The linked `proof-output.json` records all five iterations per mode, medians, process counts, and child-reported RSS. The README summarizes the measurements. These are synthetic protocol-boundary results, not a Gateway benchmark or measurements of TypeScript/Python language servers.

Before a production PR: run the real bundle preparation/discovery/provider path; exercise actual supported language servers; validate ownership revocation, collisions, cleanup uncertainty, process-tree termination, and applicable eager-provider behavior; then run the focused repository tests and required build. No product patch, build success, or merge readiness is claimed yet.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

## Additional information

Source and related work:

- [Current LSP runtime owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675/src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts)
- [Attempt bundle preparation caller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.ts)
- [Current runtime tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675/src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts)
- [MCP startup parallelism, merged #94230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94230)
- [Earlier MCP/LSP parallel startup proposal, closed #94779](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94779)
- [LSP disposal owner gate, merged #133340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133340)
- [LSP initialize contract](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/gh-pages/_specifications/lsp/3.17/general/initialize.md)

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an opt-in reset lifecycle notice for automatic idle and daily session rollovers without enabling verbose output.

### Problem to solve

When an explicitly configured idle or daily reset policy rolls a conversation over, the next reply arrives with no indication that the prior context window changed. The reply can therefore appear confused or discontinuous, especially when a short confirmation or follow-up crosses the reset boundary.

Verbose mode exposes a generic new-session identifier, but it also enables unrelated operational output. Internal `session:auto-reset` hooks cannot solve this reliably because automatic-reset events are dispatched independently of the successor turn and do not own its channel/thread reply destination.

### Proposed solution

Extend each session reset policy with an optional `notifyUser` boolean:

```json5
{
  session: {
    reset: {
      mode: "idle",
      idleMinutes: 60,
      notifyUser: true,
    },
  },
}
```

When an automatic idle or daily rollover occurs and the effective reset policy enables the option, prepend one concise status payload to the successor turn's normal reply:

- Idle: `🧭 Started a new session after the configured idle timeout.`
- Daily: `🧭 Started a new session at the configured daily reset boundary.`

The notice should use the normal reply finalization and channel/thread routing path, remain disabled by default, and replace the generic verbose new-session notice for that rollover so users never receive duplicates. Manual `/new` and `/reset` behavior should remain unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

- **Enable verbose mode:** too noisy because it exposes unrelated operational notices and session identifiers.
- **Send from `session:auto-reset` hooks:** the event is detached from the successor turn and has no authoritative reply destination.
- **Reconstruct channel routing from stored session state:** duplicates routing policy outside its owner and can send to stale rooms, accounts, or threads.
- **Send a separate out-of-band channel message:** risks ordering, threading, and duplicate-delivery problems.

### Impact

- **Affected:** Operators who explicitly enable idle or daily resets on messaging channels and direct chats.
- **Severity:** Moderate UX and workflow reliability issue; the user may not realize prior conversational context has rolled over.
- **Frequency:** Once per configured automatic rollover.
- **Consequence:** Confusing replies, repeated explanations, and ambiguous confirmation/follow-up messages.

### Evidence/examples

- #61238 documents user confusion and a confirmation workflow crossing a silent automatic reset boundary.
- #58758 established the same product pattern for dedicated, quiet lifecycle notices instead of requiring verbose mode; #67830 implemented `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser`.
- #55515 documents why duplicate generic and lifecycle-specific new-session notices must be avoided.
- #53364 demonstrates that system notices need the ordinary outbound channel/thread routing guarantees.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

The proposed setting is backward-compatible and defaults to `false`. Type- and channel-specific reset policy objects can set the same field under their existing override semantics.

## Silent Model Auto-Escalation to Sonnet + HIGH Thinking

### Summary
OpenClaw silently auto-escalated a session from Haiku (configured default) to Claude Sonnet with HIGH thinking enabled, burning ~$25 in unexpected API costs without user awareness or approval.

### Reproduction

**Trigger message (15:04:35 UTC, 2026-09-13):**
```
Remember that we talked about switching from Telegram to Signal?
```

**Keywords detected:** "Telegram", "Signal" (communication/routing context)

**What happened:**
1. User sent the above message in Signal channel (direct message)
2. OpenClaw initialized session `a665d66a-9b59-458f-9f97-8545285639e4` with:
   - Model: `claude-sonnet-4-6` (instead of configured default `claude-haiku-4-5`)
   - Thinking level: `high` (instead of `medium`)
   - Event type: `model_change` with `parentId: null` (root-level, not user-triggered)
3. Session ran for 90 minutes (15:04-18:11 UTC) with no user awareness
4. ~27 turns consumed ~8M tokens at Sonnet pricing
5. Cost: ~$25 (vs ~$2 on Haiku)

### Evidence

**Trajectory file entry (Line 1 of reset backup):**
```json
{
  "type": "model_change",
  "id": "95a15e18",
  "parentId": null,
  "timestamp": "2026-09-13T15:04:35.193Z",
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "modelId": "claude-sonnet-4-6"
}
```

**Session context:**
- File: `/home/axel/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/a665d66a-9b59-458f-9f97-8545285639e4.trajectory.jsonl`
- Start: 2026-09-13T16:31:30.958Z
- End: 2026-09-13T18:11:00.000Z (approximate)
- Tokens: 8M+
- Cost: ~$25

### Impact

- **User cost:** $31.62 burned today (2x auto-recharges triggered)
- **User expectation:** Haiku (default) should be used unless explicitly requested
- **User approval:** No `/sonnet` command, no explicit model switch request
- **Severity:** CRITICAL — Silent escalation to 12x more expensive model without warning

### Configuration

User's configured default:
```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": {
        "primary": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Questions

1. What auto-escalation rule triggered on "Signal" + "Telegram" keywords?
2. Why was this not user-visible or controllable?
3. Why was HIGH thinking enabled without request?
4. Can this be disabled or made opt-in?

### Expected Behavior

- Use configured default model (Haiku) unless:
  - User explicitly requests a different model (`/sonnet`, `/opus`, etc.)
  - User's config explicitly enables auto-escalation with opt-in warning
  - System error/fallback requires upgrade (should be logged and communicated)

### Actual Behavior

- Silent escalation to Sonnet based on unknown heuristics
- No warning, confirmation, or user visibility
- Runs to completion without user awareness
- Only noticed by user after reviewing invoice and token report

### System Info

- OpenClaw: 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)
- OS: Linux 6.12.62+rpt-rpi-2712 (arm64)
- Node: v24.19.0
- Runtime: Direct (Signal channel)

issues.body:
**What**

`session.maintenance.pruneAfter` (default `"30d"`) is documented as an "age cutoff for stale entries", and the doc line clarifies: "Eligible durable sessions archive in place with their identity and history intact; this does not compress or extract their transcript rows."

**Problem**

The name `pruneAfter` implies deletion/space reclamation ("prune" = remove). In practice it *archives sessions in place* and reclaims **no** space. This is easy to misread as the DB-size control knob, especially next to two other similarly-scoped settings:

- `session.maintenance.pruneAfter` — archives session entries in place (no space reclaimed)
- `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` — wall-clock TTL for reset/deleted transcript archives (default: none, only disk-budget eviction)
- `session.maintenance.coldStorage.afterDays` — extracts inactive transcripts to compressed files (this is the one that reclaims DB space)

A real case: with `pruneAfter: "30d"` + `coldStorage.enabled: true` + `afterDays: 30`, the agent DB stayed at ~5.6 GB. Breakdown: transcript rows ~2.8 GB, memory index (chunks + embeddings + vector) ~2.1 GB, trajectory events ~0.4 GB. Cold storage had extracted 1,292 files / 136 MB — it only targets transcripts of sessions inactive >30d, and never touches the memory index. Nothing in the setting names signals that distinction.

**Suggestion**

- Rename `pruneAfter` to `archiveAfter` (keep `pruneAfter` as a deprecated alias for backward compatibility), matching what it actually does.
- In the docs, state explicitly per setting: "reclaims DB space: yes/no".
- Consider grouping the three knobs in one table with a "what it reclaims" column.

**Environment**

OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (Windows), single-operator local deployment. No personal data in this report.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an optional sustained-failure gate to the channel health monitor: restart a non-terminal unhealthy account only after consecutive unhealthy passes (or sustained seconds), and emit an operator-visible notice on the first failed pass instead of restarting silently.

## Problem to solve

Verified in src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts: a non-terminal unhealthy verdict triggers a restart on the first failed pass, gated only by cooldown (DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_CYCLES = 2 cycles x DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS 5 min), DEFAULT_MAX_RESTARTS_PER_HOUR = 10, plus startup/connect graces. There is no consecutive-failure requirement and no notice before the restart. Single-pass snapshots flap — especially WhatsApp transport stalls — so the monitor can act inside a self-healing window with the operator learning about it only from the restart log line afterward.

Field case (2026.9.4, macOS, built-in WhatsApp, same install, gateway.log verbatim times):

```
10:15:11 [whatsapp] watchdog timeout (transport-inactive), retry ladder 1/12..4/12
10:32:09 [health-monitor] [whatsapp:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)
10:32:10 [whatsapp] [default] starting provider (...)
10:32:11..37 ladder retries continue (408s)
10:33:58 channel serving again, no manual action
```

A second episode the same morning (Telegram, 2 min) self-recovered with no action at all. Whether the 10:32 restart helped or was redundant is unknown from these logs — which is exactly the legibility gap: with a first-failure notice the operator would have watched a known-transient window instead of discovering a restart after the fact.

## Proposed solution

Two backward-compatible additions (defaults = current behavior):

1. Consecutive-failure confirmation: e.g. channels.<id>.healthMonitor.confirmFailures (default 1 = today) or confirmSustainedMs — restart only after that many consecutive unhealthy passes. A healthy pass resets the counter (same reset semantics as the existing pendingContinuation logic).
2. First-failure notice: an info-level event (log + optional channel notice) on the first unhealthy pass stating which account, which reason, and how many more failing passes precede action — so flaps are observable without acting on them.

Suggested defaults: confirmation off (1) to preserve current behavior; notice on. Both per-account overridable like the existing healthMonitor.enabled scope.

## Alternatives considered

- Raising cooldownMs / lowering maxRestartsPerHour: slows all recovery including genuine stuck states; does not make flaps observable.
- External watchdog with grace timer (what we run today: 600 s grace, 3600 s between repairs, immediate attesa notice, zero restarts across both episodes): works but duplicates the monitor from outside; the semantics belong in the monitor.
- Doing nothing: acceptable if maintainers consider first-pass restart correct; then this issue documents the tradeoff and can close as decided.

## Impact

- Affected: operators of WhatsApp/Telegram channels with flaky transports (mobile networks, DNS holes).
- Severity: moderate friction + surprise restarts mid-recovery; worst case a restart resets an in-flight backoff ladder (the supervisor-ownership guard already avoids the worst of this).
- Frequency: transport flaps are routine; our box logged two in one morning.
- Related: #146999 (terminal classification) and #147160 discussions touch the same monitor; this proposal is independent of both outcomes.

## Evidence/examples

- Monitor decision chain: src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts (runCheckWork: evaluate -> skip terminal/blocked -> respect supervisor backoff -> cooldown -> hourly cap -> restart; no consecutive counter anywhere in the 347-line file).
- Our external watchdog logic (grace + attesa + recovery-cancel) in field use since August; both 2026-09-13 episodes recovered inside its 600 s grace with zero restarts.
- Honesty note: whether the 10:32:09 restart helped or was redundant cannot be determined from the surviving logs; the proposal asks for observability precisely so the next such episode is legible.

## Implementation intent

Maybe, with maintainer guidance — happy to implement the counter + notice behind the proposed keys once the shape is approved, with tests in the existing monitor suite.

## Additional information

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO beyond the above; will answer maintainer questions with log excerpts on request.

## Bug type

Behavior bug (live progress preview never appears; final delivery unaffected).

## Summary

With channels.telegram streaming.mode=progress and richMessages:true, the Gateway never creates the progress draft: today's gateway log shows 0 editMessageText against 1034 text delivery ok, and a September A/B found answerLane.stream never created in this combination.

## Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.4, npm global install, macOS 15.7.2 (x64), Node v24.18.0.
2. Telegram account config: streaming.mode=progress (toolProgress true), richMessages=true, verbose off. No per-account overrides (verified via config get + restart).
3. Have the agent do multi-tool work in a Telegram DM (several exec/tool calls over 30+ seconds).
4. Watch the chat and grep the gateway log for editMessageText.

## Expected behavior

A single progress draft appears and updates while the agent works (the documented progress mode), as it does with verbose on Exec bubbles and as answer previews do in other modes.

## Actual behavior

- No draft ever appears; nothing updates until the final answer lands whole.
- 2026-09-09 A/B on 2026.9.3 (same install, restart-verified, 16 config paths): rich:true+progress and partial+rich:true both showed zero editMessageText in the 10:40 log window — only text delivery ok for Exec bubbles; answerLane.stream was never created. rich:false+progress 3-step test executed the same day.
- 2026-09-13 on 2026.9.4 (this report): grep over today's gateway.log → editMessageText: 0, draft-stream/answerLane lines: 0, text delivery ok: 1034.
- verbose on remains the only working live signal (Exec bubbles), which is a workaround, not the documented progress draft.

## OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d); also observed on 2026.9.3 (2026-09-09 tests).

## Operating system

macOS 15.7.2 (x64).

## Install method

npm global (npm prefix -g = ~/.local).

## Model

DeepSeek (default route); September A/B ran on the same install via the default model route.

## Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek.

## Logs

Redacted counts from live logs (no content, no ids):

```
# 2026-09-13, 2026.9.4, progress + rich:true
editMessageText occurrences in gateway.log: 0
draft-stream|answerLane lines: 0
text delivery ok: 1034
# 2026-09-09, 2026.9.3, rich:true (progress and partial)
editMessageText in 10:40 window: 0
answerLane.stream: never created
```

## Impact and severity

- Affected: Telegram DM operators on progress+rich (the default pairing on 2026.9.x).
- Severity: workflow-friction (no data loss; finals deliver fine).
- Frequency: always in this combination across 5 days of observation (Sep 9 → Sep 13, two releases).
- Consequence: long work looks dead for minutes, then arrives whole; operators cannot distinguish stuck from working without verbose on.

## Additional information

- Distinct from #141528 (partial mode, 429 rate-limit, rich disabled — stream starts but slow). This is progress+rich:true where no edit is ever attempted.
- Last known good version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no version pinned; operator recalls live tool-call drafts in older 2026.8.x but without a logged version).
- 2026-09-12 note: 1–3s tasks never show a draft regardless (draft lifetime shorter than client render) — the report above concerns 30s+ multi-tool turns where the draft should persist.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw tool-loop continuations on a local OpenAI-compatible backend can be **message-list append-only but not token-prefix-stable at the backend**, causing recurrent/hybrid llama.cpp models to require a rollback checkpoint between tool steps. If recurrent context checkpoints are unavailable/disabled, the backend falls back to re-prefilling the entire 100k+ prompt even though the next OpenClaw request only appends one assistant/tool pair.

This is **not a compaction request** and the tool catalog is stable. It is a foreground tool loop in one session, same model, same 57 tools, same reasoning level, same `tool_choice`, with each request body adding two messages.

The practical symptom is an alternating pattern:

```text
full 110k prefill -> tiny cached continuation -> full 111k prefill -> tiny cached continuation
```

On transformer-only models this may be masked by ordinary KV tail removal. On hybrid/recurrent models (such as Qwen3.6/Ornith-family models in llama.cpp), the generated recurrent state cannot always be rewound without a context checkpoint, so a small serialization mismatch at the assistant/tool boundary becomes a full-context prefill.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.9.2`
- Provider: self-hosted OpenAI-compatible `local-llm`
- Backend: llama.cpp behind llama-swap
- Model: Ornith 1.5 35B A3B, 262144-token context
- Local backend slot count: `-np 1`
- Reasoning: `high`
- Tools: 57, unchanged across the reproduced requests
- Endpoint: `/v1/chat/completions`

## Concrete production capture

Five consecutive OpenClaw foreground tool-loop requests were captured from llama-swap.

At the HTTP request-body level they are strictly append-only:

```text
ID 157: 242 messages, 57 tools
ID 158: 244 messages, 57 tools
ID 159: 246 messages, 57 tools
ID 160: 248 messages, 57 tools
ID 161: 250 messages, 57 tools
```

For every transition checked:

```text
tools: identical
model: identical
reasoning_effort: high
tool_choice: auto
max_tokens: 65536
stream: true
```

The first difference in each next request is exactly at the old message-list length, i.e. the old messages are byte-for-byte identical and the next request only appends a new assistant/tool pair.

Example:

```text
157 -> 158: first differing message index = 242
158 -> 159: first differing message index = 244
159 -> 160: first differing message index = 246
160 -> 161: first differing message index = 248
```

Yet llama.cpp observed this cache pattern:

```text
ID 157
  selected slot LCP similarity: 0.994
  cached: 0
  prompt: 110,893
  prompt eval: ~44.07 s

ID 158
  cached: 111,116
  prompt: 51
  prompt eval: ~110 ms

ID 159
  selected slot LCP similarity: 0.998
  cached: 0
  prompt: 111,475
  prompt eval: ~44.61 s

ID 160
  cached: 111,563
  prompt: 151
  prompt eval: ~211 ms
```

So the HTTP payloads are append-only, but the actual backend slot state after the previous streamed generation is not always a usable prefix of the next OpenClaw request.

## Why this appears to be an OpenClaw continuation-shaping issue

The likely mismatch is at the just-generated assistant/tool boundary: the backend has recurrent state for the exact tokens it generated (including reasoning/tool-call serialization), while OpenClaw reconstructs the next request from its normalized assistant/tool transcript representation.

That reconstruction is semantically equivalent at the chat-message level, but it is not guaranteed to serialize to the exact token suffix that produced the current backend state.

For a normal transformer KV cache the backend can often delete the generated tail and continue. For recurrent/hybrid memory it needs an earlier rollback snapshot. Without one, llama.cpp correctly falls back to full prompt reprocessing.

This makes local hybrid/recurrent models unusually sensitive to any difference between:

```text
previous response as actually generated by the model
```

and:

```text
assistant/tool history reconstructed by OpenClaw for the next tool step
```

## Backend-side A/B proof

I re-enabled llama.cpp recurrent context checkpoints and fixed a ROCm dual-GPU checkpoint-restore fault locally. I also kept a guard that prevents checkpoint storms on short serial incremental prefill.

With checkpoints working, a controlled ~90k-token A/B branch test produced:

```text
cold request:
  cache_n = 0
  prompt_n = 90,016
  PP ~= 30.38 s

subsequent divergent continuations:
  cache_n ~= 89,756-89,757
  prompt_n = 259-261
  PP ~= 291-294 ms
  all HTTP 200
```

Then I replayed the exact real OpenClaw long-session capture:

```text
warm live prefix: 111,714 tokens
next captured OpenClaw request:
  cache_n = 111,714
  prompt_n = 270
  PP = 349.425 ms
  HTTP 200
```

So the 44-45 second full reread is avoidable if the backend can roll back to the pre-generation recurrent state.

## Expected behavior / proposal

For local OpenAI-compatible providers, OpenClaw should try to keep **tool-loop continuation serialization token-prefix-stable** with the immediately preceding model response, especially when reasoning/tool calls are involved.

Possible directions:

1. Preserve/replay the exact model-facing assistant response fields needed to reproduce the prior generated suffix (for example structured reasoning/tool-call fields) instead of reconstructing only a normalized transcript form.
2. Keep a transport-level snapshot of the exact final assistant/tool representation used for the preceding request/response boundary and use it for the next tool-loop continuation when compatible.
3. At minimum, add diagnostics that expose when a foreground tool continuation changes the serialized assistant suffix even though the request message list is append-only.
4. If exact replay is intentionally impossible for some adapters, document that recurrent/hybrid local backends require rollback-capable context checkpoints to avoid full-prefill fallback during tool loops.

The goal is not to depend on llama.cpp implementation details. The invariant is simply:

> A same-session foreground tool continuation should preserve the immediately preceding model-facing token prefix whenever OpenClaw already has enough structured response data to do so.

## Related issues

- #147017: compaction rewrites the live prompt prefix and defeats local KV reuse. This report is different: **no compaction is involved**; it occurs during an ordinary foreground tool loop.
- #140121: dynamic per-turn tool catalog changes invalidate local KV cache. This report is different: the **57-tool catalog is identical** across the reproduced requests.
- #144767: reasoning stream/final asymmetry. Potentially related because reasoning normalization/persistence can make the replayed assistant turn differ from the tokens that were actually generated.

## Impact

At ~111k context, one affected continuation went from ~0.2-0.35 s of incremental prefill to ~44-45 s of full prefill. In a long agentic tool loop this can happen repeatedly, turning a normally interactive local session into repeated full-context rereads.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Bug (something is broken)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Under a **network** failure (`Connection error` / `UND_ERR_SOCKET`) on the primary provider, the model fallback chain does **not** actually run, and the user sees `run failed before producing a reply` — even though the log line `transient retry window elapsed … failing over` appears. The failover decision is emitted **after** the embedded run has already been terminated with `isError=true`, so there is no run left to attach the fallback to.

In short: the failover arrives ~76ms too late; the run is already dead, the fallback candidates are never attempted, and the message fails with `outcome=error`.

## Timing evidence (single run, ms-level ordering)

```
.453  [provider-transport-fetch] error provider=opencode-go causeName=SocketError causeCode=UND_ERR_SOCKET fetch failed
.463  [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true rawError="Connection error."
.539  [agent/embedded] transient retry window elapsed for opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash after 2/8 retries; failing over
.998  [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: source=replyResolver outcome=error
```

Note the order: the run is marked `isError=true` at `.463`, and only **76ms later** (`.539`) does the transient-retry observe the window is exhausted and emit `failing over`. The network error escapes as a terminal assistant message (empty content, `stopReason=error`) **before** the failover decision is produced, so laguna/deepseek/etc. are never called.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an HTTP/S provider whose streaming SSE occasionally drops mid-request (observed with `opencode-go`, baseUrl `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`).
2. Send any message that triggers a model call during such a drop.
3. Observe the log ordering above and a user-visible `run failed before producing a reply` / `network connection error`, with no fallback attempt logged between the failure and the terminal error.

## Expected

When the primary provider fails with a transient **network** error, the model fallback chain should be consulted and a fallback provider/model attempted before the run is surfaced as failed. The `failing over` decision should precede — or re-open — the run's terminal error state, not follow it.

## Actual

The network error is surfaced as a terminal assistant error immediately; `failing over` is logged afterward but has nothing to act on, so the fallback chain is effectively bypassed and the user receives the error.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (also present in 2026.9.4)
- WSL2 (Ubuntu), gateway embedded run (`agent:main` dashboard session)
- provider `opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4.1-flash`

## Related issues (different trigger, same "fallback never/too-late engages" family)

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/145690 — runtime-level error burns through fallback chain, message dropped (non-network root cause)
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142319 — content-class failure never engages fallback
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141115 — 429 terminates session without consulting fallback

This report is distinct in that the trigger is a **network/transport error** and the failure mode is a **race**: the terminal-error state is emitted before the failover decision, independent of any single provider's error class.

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.1, an affected Claude CLI request's projected tool registry included `message`, but its contemporaneous native catalog contained zero `mcp__openclaw__*` tools and an actual `message` invocation failed before reaching Discord authorization.

## Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Expected behavior

The policy-allowed Gateway tools should be exposed through the bundled Claude CLI MCP bridge. The release-pinned [Bundle MCP overlays documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ad6fe23aecb9b833d68139b0ddc9f239b894d2f1/docs/gateway/cli-backends.md#bundle-mcp-overlays) documents generated strict MCP configuration for `claude-cli` and grant-scoped Gateway tool exposure. A projected inventory alone should not be mistaken for successful native registration.

## Actual behavior

One observed request had `message` in its request-time `systemPromptReport`, but native deferred-tool metadata had no OpenClaw-namespaced tools. `ToolSearch` found no matching tool, and an actual invocation returned `No such tool available: message`. No Discord permission rejection was observed; Discord authorization was not reached by this failed invocation.

## OpenClaw version

2026.9.1. Latest-release/main applicability is unverified; no claim that this reproduces on a newer release.

issues.body:
## Problem

Operators using the root `openclaw logs` command cannot select a minimum severity for the bounded gateway log tail. During incident triage they must scan or externally filter debug and informational records, and ad-hoc text filtering does not preserve structured JSON output reliably.

This gap exists on current `main` in the root gateway/RPC/configured-file/systemd log flow. The existing `openclaw channels logs` feature proposal in #130187/#130202 owns channel log files and is not a substitute for the root command.

## Proposed bounded outcome

Add `openclaw logs --level <fatal|error|warn|info|debug|trace>` as a presentation-only minimum-severity filter.

- Reuse the existing canonical log parser and severity ordering.
- Apply the filter to both plain and JSON output.
- Preserve the current request, byte/line bounds, source selection, cursor advancement, follow/reconnect behavior, metadata, truncation notices, and errors.
- Exclude unclassified records only when `--level` is explicitly supplied.
- Keep output unchanged when the option is omitted.

## Existing alternatives

Shell filters such as `rg`, `grep`, or `jq` add platform-specific operator work and either lose structured records or require users to reproduce OpenClaw's parsing and level ordering. They do not provide a portable root CLI contract.

## Non-goals

- No server-side or historical log search.
- No attempt to fetch older records to fill the post-filter result count.
- No change to `openclaw channels logs`.
- No config, default, protocol, schema, persistence, migration, or security change.

## Acceptance and proof

- `--level warn --json` returns only warn, error, and fatal structured records.
- The same threshold works in plain output.
- Omitting `--level` preserves lower-level and unclassified records.
- An invalid level is rejected before log dispatch.
- A fully filtered `--limit 1` window remains empty rather than reading older records.
- Source cursor advancement and local-file/systemd fallback composition remain covered by focused tests.

I have an implementation ready and will open a closing PR with exact-head root CLI proof using isolated configuration and a controlled log file.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.4, the managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron reaches the model when `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` is implicitly routed through the Codex harness; forcing the same model through `agentRuntime.id: "openclaw"` causes `memory-core` to claim the sentinel before a model turn and the sweep succeeds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.4 with the bundled `memory-core`, `openai`, and `codex` plugins enabled.
2. Use `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` through Plus OAuth with no authored `agentRuntime` override, allowing the official OpenAI route to select the Codex harness implicitly.
3. Leave Memory Core dreaming enabled and use its managed `Memory Dreaming Promotion` cron. Its generated payload is:

   ```json
   {
     "kind": "agentTurn",
     "message": "__openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__",
     "lightContext": true
   }
   ```

4. Force the managed cron or wait for its scheduled run.
5. Observe that the cron transcript contains the wrapped sentinel as a user turn and the model attempts to execute it through Bash.
6. Add this exact-model runtime policy and restart the Gateway:

   ```json
   {
     "agents": {
       "defaults": {
         "models": {
           "openai/gpt-5.6-terra": {
             "agentRuntime": { "id": "openclaw" }
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

7. Force the same managed cron again. It completes the promotion flow, and `chat.history` for the cron run contains zero messages, consistent with pre-model hook interception.

### Expected behavior

The `memory-core` `before_agent_reply` hook should claim the managed dreaming sentinel for a cron-triggered turn before any selected harness invokes a model. Runtime selection between `codex` and `openclaw` should not expose an internal Memory Core sentinel to the model.

This expectation is based on the bundled Memory Core implementation, which registers the hook for `heartbeat` and `cron`, and the Codex hook-boundary documentation describing OpenClaw plugin hooks around Codex turns.

### Actual behavior

With implicit Codex harness routing, the model receives:

```text
[cron:<redacted> Memory Dreaming Promotion] __openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__
```

It then emits a Bash tool call equivalent to:

```shell
bash -lc __openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__
```

Bash returns exit 127 because the sentinel is intentionally not an executable. The scheduler records the run as successful because the agent turn itself completes with a textual failure summary.

With exact-model `agentRuntime.id: "openclaw"`, the same managed cron succeeds and its cron transcript is empty. This was reproduced immediately before and after the runtime-policy change on the same OpenClaw version and installation.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)

### Operating system

NixOS 26.05 (Linux 6.18.44, x86_64), Node.js 26.7.0

### Install method

NixOS service/microVM using `nix-openclaw`, with the OpenClaw 2026.9.4 npm package and bundled plugins.

### Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-terra`

### Provider / routing chain

Failing route:

```text
OpenClaw -> bundled OpenAI plugin -> Plus OAuth / ChatGPT Responses -> implicit bundled Codex app-server harness -> gpt-5.6-terra
```

Working route:

```text
OpenClaw -> bundled OpenAI plugin -> Plus OAuth / ChatGPT Responses -> explicit OpenClaw harness -> gpt-5.6-terra
```

### Additional provider/model setup details

- The effective auth profile is a Plus OAuth profile.
- The model and provider transport were unchanged between failing and successful runs.
- Only the exact-model `agentRuntime.id` changed from implicit/automatic selection to `openclaw`.
- Restarting the Gateway without that runtime override had not prevented later failures.

### Logs

```shell
# Failing scheduled run summary
Failed: `__openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__` is not available as a command (`command not found`, exit 127).

# Failing transcript tool call (paths and IDs redacted)
bash -lc __openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__

# Tool result
bash: line 1: __openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__: command not found

# A second forced reproduction on 2026.9.4 before the workaround
Memory promotion failed: `__openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__` was not found on the gateway host (exit 127).

# Same managed cron after setting agentRuntime.id=openclaw
status: ok
completionStatus: succeeded
durationMs: 41604
model: gpt-5.6-terra
provider: openai

# chat.history for the successful cron run
messages: []
agentRuntime.id: openclaw
agentRuntime.source: model
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Related earlier reports:

- #87924 — exact short-term promotion sentinel reported as command-not-found
- #97475 — dreaming cron tokens reaching a model and being executed as shell commands
- #62296 — earlier managed dreaming `before_agent_reply` trigger failure

A fresh `openclaw gateway diagnostics export` was generated and reviewed locally. It reflects the working post-mitigation configuration, so it is not attached as evidence of the failing route. Redacted pre/post transcript and run evidence is included above.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** installations where an official OpenAI route is implicitly claimed by the Codex harness while Memory Core dreaming is enabled.
- **Severity:** medium; background memory consolidation does not execute correctly, but the Gateway remains available.
- **Frequency:** repeatedly observed on scheduled runs and reproduced with a forced run on 2026.9.4. The immediately subsequent forced run succeeded after the runtime override.
- **Consequences:** missed light/REM/deep memory work, misleading scheduler `ok` status, diagnostic noise, and unnecessary model/token usage.

### Additional information

The evidence isolates the behavior to the effective harness selection. The precise internal reason that the real Memory Core hook is unavailable or does not claim the Codex-routed cron turn is `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO`.

The current workaround is to force the affected model through:

```json
"agentRuntime": { "id": "openclaw" }
```

A narrow regression test could register the real bundled `memory-core` hook, execute its managed cron payload with an official OpenAI route that selects the Codex harness, and assert that no Codex app-server model turn starts. Longer term, a typed plugin-owned cron action would avoid representing internal maintenance as an `agentTurn` sentinel.

issues.body:
### Environment
macOS 11.7.11 (x64), openclaw gateway + `openclaw tui` (gateway mode)

### Problem
The gateway connection drops and reconnects fairly often (laptop sleep, network blips, gateway restarts). Every time the TUI reconnects, it reloads the latest session history (default 200 entries) and prints the entire batch into the scrollback — not just the messages missed during the disconnect.

Docs confirm the behavior (`docs/web/tui.md`):
- "On connect, the TUI loads the latest history (default 200 messages)."
- "Reconnect and event-gap recovery reconcile active runs with history…" — but rendering is not gap-deduplicated.

### Impact
After each reconnect the user has to scroll past pages of duplicated old conversation. With long sessions this makes the TUI effectively unusable until the replay finishes.

### Expected behavior
On reconnect, reconcile silently and only render the **gap** since the last seen event (event-gap recovery already exists as a concept); full history replay should happen only on initial attach. Alternatively, make replay-on-reconnect opt-in, or render the replay in a collapsed/compact form.

### Workaround
`openclaw tui --history-limit 20` reduces (but does not eliminate) the flood.

issues.body:
## Summary

The Control UI (web client) fails to reconcile live-pushed state against server truth in two related ways. Both persist indefinitely — including across a full Gateway restart — and both clear instantly on a hard refresh (F5), so the server state is correct and the defect is client-side.

**Environment:** OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (1391f7c), Linux (WSL2), Control UI in Firefox, webchat channel, `claude-cli` agent runtime.

## Symptom 1: assistant replies rendered twice in webchat

Every assistant reply in an active webchat conversation shows as two bubbles. The two copies differ slightly in rendering (which presumably defeats the identical-bubble collapse described in `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md`), consistent with one bubble built from the live stream and a second from the final committed message, without deduplication between them.

Server-side checks all show exactly one copy:

- The CLI turn log shows a single model turn per reply (unique output hash per turn).
- `transcript_events` in the agent sqlite store contains exactly one copy of each reply (verified by searching a distinctive reply phrase).
- `conversation_deliveries` shows no duplicate `message_hash` entries.
- After a hard refresh, the conversation history renders every reply exactly once.

## Symptom 2: deleted sessions keep showing in the Home dock

Eleven finished subagent sessions were archived and then deleted via the `sessions` tool (`action: "delete"`, each returning `deleted: true` with a `.zst` transcript archive). `sessions_list` confirmed they no longer exist. The Home dock continued showing them:

- after archiving,
- after deletion,
- and even after a full Gateway restart (new process, new pid).

A hard refresh of the tab removed them immediately.

## Expected

- Stream-rendered bubbles should be replaced by (or deduplicated against) the final committed message, even when the streamed text and final text differ slightly.
- Session archive/delete events should update connected clients, or the client should revalidate its session list against the server on reconnect (a Gateway restart forces a reconnect, and the stale entries still survived that).

## Notes

- Both issues reproduce reliably in the same client session; a single F5 clears both, which is what points at client-side state reconciliation rather than the Gateway.
- Happy to provide additional logs or run diagnostics against a dev build if useful.

issues.body:
## Problem

The Control UI agent roster (sidebar and Agents home) always sorts agents **alphabetically by agent ID** using `localeCompare`, regardless of the order specified in `agents.entries` in `openclaw.json`.

This is hardcoded in the Gateway source:

```javascript
// agent-list module
visibleIds.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));
```

Users who have multiple agents with meaningful ordering (e.g., team hierarchy, workflow priority) cannot control how agents appear in the UI.

## Current Behavior

- Agent display order is always alphabetical by ID
- Changing the key order in `agents.entries` has no effect
- No config field exists to specify display order

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional `rank` (or `order`) field to each agent entry in `agents.entries`:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    entries: {
      main: { name: "Manager", rank: 0 },
      sysadmin: { name: "Tech Lead", rank: 1 },
      researcher: { name: "Researcher", rank: 2 }
    }
  }
}
```

The UI should sort agents by `rank` first (ascending), then fall back to alphabetical for agents without a `rank` field.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Renaming agent IDs**: Breaks workspace paths, session keys, bindings, and all existing references
- **CSS order injection**: Fragile, breaks on every update, caused blank page on 9.4 upgrade
- **Client-side sorting**: Only solves one user's browser, not shared across team members

## Use Case

Our team has 9 agents with a clear hierarchy: manager → technical lead → specialists → support staff. The alphabetical sort puts them in meaningless order, making daily operations confusing. We need the UI to reflect the actual team structure.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.9.4
- OS: WSL2 on Windows
- Browser: Chrome

issues.body:
## Summary

After a crash loop (#144911 on this install), `main-session-restart-recovery` tombstoned a Buzz group session that had been mid-turn. From then on **every mention to that agent in that room failed silently**: the only trace is one line per message in the JSON log, and nothing reaches the room, the dead-letter list, or the main gateway log. Other agents in the same room, whose sessions were idle during the crashes, kept answering normally, so from the operator's seat it looks like one bot ignoring people.

## Observed (2026.9.4, macOS, launchd)

```
08:10:05 [main-session-restart-recovery] tombstoned main-session restart recovery:
         agent:claude-code:buzz:group:buzz:<room> (blocked after 3 automatic attempts without a started runtime turn …)
08:10:06 sent restart recovery tombstone notice   ← one message in the room, once
…
17:44:58 [claude] Buzz message failed: Session "agent:claude-code:buzz:group:buzz:<room>" ended during restart recovery.
         Use /new or /reset to start a replacement session.
```

That failure line repeated **12 times** over five hours, three of them for the owner's direct questions, with the agent's other room sessions working fine throughout.

## What made it hard to remediate

- `openclaw sessions delete <key> --agent <id>` fails on Buzz keys: `Error: Buzz target must be a channel UUID` (the live-artifact cleanup tries to resolve the key as a delivery target).
- There is no `sessions reset` / `sessions new` CLI verb, though the error text tells the user to use `/new` or `/reset`.
- `sessions.delete` over `gateway call` works with `{agentId, key}` but rejects `dryRun`, so there is no preview.

`sessions.delete` via RPC returned `deleted: true`, archived the transcript, and the next inbound created a fresh session that answered normally.

## Suggestions

1. A tombstoned session should not silently fail subsequent inbound. Either auto-create the replacement session on the next inbound (the tombstone notice already told the user the transcript is safe), or surface each failure as a dead letter / a `[buzz/inbound]` line in the main log so a watcher can see it.
2. Make the CLI `sessions delete` path work for channel-scoped keys, or add the `reset` verb the error message promises.
3. Consider a `dryRun` on `sessions.delete`.

Related: #144911 (the crash loop that produced the tombstone), #144203 (other silent Buzz inbound loss on this install).

issues.body:
## Summary

Skills can declare an `install` frontmatter spec with `kind: "uv"` (alongside `brew`, `node`, `go`, `download`) that tells OpenClaw to bootstrap `uv` itself and then `uv tool install <package>` before the skill runs (`src/skills/loading/frontmatter.ts`). Plugins that declare a stdio `mcpServers` entry (`docs/gateway/config-extensions.md`) have no equivalent: a plugin manifest can only specify the raw `command`/`args` to spawn (e.g. `command: "uvx", args: ["some-pypi-package"]`), with no way to declare "this requires `uv`" as an install-time dependency OpenClaw can resolve.

The result is that any ClawHub plugin wrapping a Python-based MCP server via `uvx` is unusable out of the box on any host without `uv` preinstalled — silently so, per #146268 — even though OpenClaw already has the exact machinery needed to fix this for skills.

## Feature request

Extend `mcpServers` manifest entries (or plugin manifests generally) to accept the same kind of `install` spec skills already support — at minimum `{kind: "uv", package: "<pypi-package>"}` — so that:

- `openclaw plugins install` can bootstrap `uv` and the declared package the same way skill installation already does, instead of leaving it to fail at first MCP-server-start time.
- The Control UI's plugin install flow can surface "this plugin needs `uv`, installing it now" (or a consent prompt) instead of just flipping `enabled: true` with no indication that a runtime prerequisite exists.

## Why

This is a genuine parity gap between skills and plugins for the exact same underlying need (a Python CLI tool via `uv`/`uvx`), and it's exactly the pattern OpenClaw's own docs recommend for MCP servers (`docs/gateway/config-extensions.md`'s example uses `command: "uvx"`). Any plugin author following that documented pattern currently ships something that silently doesn't work unless the installing user happens to already have `uv` on `PATH`.

## Related

- #146268 — the silent-failure symptom this gap produces
- `src/skills/loading/frontmatter.ts` — the existing `kind: "uv"` install spec for skills, which this would mirror for plugins

issues.body:
## Summary

Please consider adding an official **`.rpm` package** for the Linux companion, alongside the existing `.deb` and AppImage artifacts.

## Motivation

Today `linux-app.yml` builds only `deb` and AppImage (`pnpm dlx @tauri-apps/cli build --bundles deb,appimage`), and `tauri.conf.json`'s `bundle.linux` config only has `appimage`/`deb` sections. That covers Debian/Ubuntu-family systems well, but leaves RPM-based distros (Fedora, RHEL/CentOS/Rocky/Alma, openSUSE) with AppImage as the only first-class option — no native package that integrates with `dnf`/`zypper`, system update tooling, or distro dependency resolution.

Tauri v2 (already pinned at `2.11.4` here) supports `rpm` as a bundle target natively — no extra tooling beyond `rpmbuild`, which isn't currently installed in the `linux-app.yml` CI dependency list.

## Scope for a first PR

Following the same pattern as #138279/#139729 (which added aarch64 CI validation for the existing formats without touching the signed release pipeline), a reasonable first step would be **CI-only validation**:

- Add `rpm` to the `--bundles` list in the build/package step.
- Add `rpmbuild` (the `rpm` package) to the CI system-dependency install step.
- Validate the built `.rpm` in CI (e.g. `rpm -qlp` / install into a minimal container) the same way the packaged AppImage is smoke-tested today.

**Non-goal for a first PR:** publishing signed `.rpm` release assets. That's a separate, larger change to `linux-app-release.yml` and the signed-release pipeline, and should follow only once there's a product decision to actually ship and support an RPM package long-term (repo hosting, GPG signing, dependency naming across Fedora/openSUSE, etc.).

## Current evidence

- `.github/workflows/linux-app.yml`: `pnpm dlx @tauri-apps/cli@2.11.4 build --bundles deb,appimage ...` — no `rpm`.
- `apps/linux/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`: `bundle.linux` only configures `appimage` and `deb`.
- No `rpm`/`rpmbuild` install step in `linux-app.yml`'s system-dependency setup.
- No existing open issue requesting this (checked via GitHub search) — filing net-new rather than following up on prior demand.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug / integration regression

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading 2026.7.1-2 → 2026.9.4, the QQ channel has **no plugin variant that fully works**. This is a two-part regression that together removes the pre-upgrade QQ experience (process/verbose display during long agent turns) and, for one of the two plugins, message handling entirely:

1. **First-party `@openclaw/qqbot` (frozen at 2026.7.1, no 9.x release)** loads cleanly on 9.4 but **crashes on every inbound message**:
   ```
   [qqbot] Processing message from <user>: <text>
   [qqbot] Message processor error for dm:<user>: deps.runtime.channel.reply.formatInboundEnvelope is not a function
   ```
   The plugin passes every static compatibility gate — version floors (`pluginApi >=2026.7.1`, `minHostVersion >=2026.4.10`), and **all 48 `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` import subpaths still exist in 9.4** — but the **runtime-injected deps object changed shape**: `deps.runtime.channel.reply.formatInboundEnvelope` (present in 7.1) is gone in 9.4, so the inbound path throws for every message. Static import compatibility cannot catch this class of breakage; there appears to be no versioned contract for the injected runtime surface.

2. **Successor `@tencent-connect/openclaw-qqbot` 2.0.3 (latest, actively maintained by Tencent Connect)** delivers final replies reliably, but its **streaming preview drafts never receive a single chunk**. Since the 9.4 upgrade, every observed streaming phase transition is `idle → failed (finalize:fallback)` — zero `first_chunk`, zero drafts opened (the controller source confirms this state means "no session, zero sends"). Result: during multi-minute agent turns the QQ side shows nothing at all until the final reply.

Before the 9.4 upgrade, the same `streaming: {"mode": "partial"}` config with the first-party plugin produced working in-progress draft updates.

### Steps to reproduce

Environment: Ubuntu, npm-global OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (in-place upgrade from 2026.7.1-2), systemd --user, single `main` agent.

**Part 1 (first-party plugin crash):**
1. `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/qqbot --force --accept-capabilities` (npm latest = 2026.7.1); disable `@tencent-connect/openclaw-qqbot`; restart Gateway.
2. Plugin loads green: token obtained, websocket connected, `Gateway ready`, listed as `qqbot`.
3. Send any DM to the bot. Journal: `Message processor error ... formatInboundEnvelope is not a function`; the turn never starts; QQ client shows the bot as abnormal after no response.

**Part 2 (successor plugin zero-chunk streaming):**
1. Re-enable `@tencent-connect/openclaw-qqbot` 2.0.3 (or start from a default migration state), `channels.qqbot.streaming.mode = "partial"`; restart.
2. Trigger a long multi-tool agent turn via DM. Watch journal: no `phase: idle → streaming` transitions ever; only `idle → failed (finalize:fallback)` at turn end (observed 6× across two days). The plugin side shows its streaming controller never received a first chunk.

### Expected behavior

- Channel plugins written against the 7.x runtime injection surface should either keep working or fail loudly at load time with a clear compatibility error — not crash per-message on a missing injected function.
- Streaming preview chunks should reach the successor plugin's controller so `mode: "partial"` produces progressive updates, as it did on 7.1.x with the first-party plugin.

### Actual behavior

- First-party plugin: per-message `TypeError` on the inbound path; channel effectively dead.
- Successor plugin: final replies only; zero streaming/progress display during processing.

### Additional context

- Package timeline (npm): `@openclaw/qqbot` last stable 2026.7.1 (2026-07-13), last prerelease 2026.7.2-beta.7 (2026-08-02), nothing since; `@tencent-connect/openclaw-qqbot` created 2026-03-10, own repo (tencent-connect/openclaw-qqbot), currently 2.0.3 — i.e. an effective handover, but the first-party package was never formally deprecated on npm and has no 9.x-compatible release.
- Related config-validation contradiction we reported earlier (#144827): core warns `dmPolicy="open"` needs `"*"` in `allowFrom`, while the first-party plugin schema rejects `"*"` (`must not be valid`); the successor plugin ignores the list entirely. This makes correct `allowFrom` configuration unsatisfiable across plugin variants.
- Workaround state we settled on: successor plugin enabled, `streaming.mode="off"` (accepting no process display), `allowFrom` set to explicit user openid.
- Happy to provide the full journal excerpts, the first-party plugin crash logs, or stability evidence on request.

### Ask

1. Either ship a 9.x-compatible release of the first-party QQ plugin (or a formal deprecation path pointing users to the successor), and document/bump the runtime injection contract so channel-plugin authors can detect incompatibility at load time.
2. Investigate why preview/stream chunks never reach the successor plugin's streaming controller on 9.4 (works for us on 7.1.x with the same plugin-generation code path), so `mode: "partial"` delivers its intended UX again.
