issues.body:
### Summary

Give a collector that the registry settled as un-continuable a machine-readable `reason` in the `agents_wait` result (part 1). Separately, ask maintainers where pause age and continuation-stage diagnostics for a continuable parked leaf should live (part 2); `agents_wait` stays collector-only.

### Problem to solve

Follow-up to #141474 and #164445, from review feedback on that PR (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164445#pullrequestreview-5417876406). Two gaps remain once #164445 settles a legacy parked collector.

**1. The settled failure has no machine-readable reason.** `agents_wait` reports a collector the registry settled (it yielded with no recorded result, so nothing can continue it) as `status: "failed"` plus free text. `CollectorCompletionSchema` in `src/agents/tools/agents-wait-tool.ts` has `status` (`done | failed | killed | timeout`), `result`, `error`, `schemaError` and nothing else that classifies a failure, so a consumer that wants "the run died, a retry may help" versus "an older build parked this collector, rerun it differently" has to match the `error` string. Observed result for the settled shape, from a real isolated Gateway at PR head `abfb0abb3d7` (seeded legacy rows, see Evidence):

```
agents_wait run-collector-absent timeout=0: completed:failed (Collector yielded without recording a result, and no continu...)
```

I did not capture an ordinary crashed-collector result on the same Gateway, so the "same shape as a crash" claim rests on the schema above, not on a side-by-side capture. A stacked PR will capture both.

**2. A continuable parked leaf shows no pause age.** #164445 deliberately settles only the shape where "can this be continued?" is provably no, and leaves a deliberate `waitFor: "message"` leaf wait alone however old the pause. `agents_wait` is collector-only (`readWaitState` returns `not_found` for a run without `collect`), so for an ordinary leaf the surface an operator sees is `subagents list`. Observed there on the same Gateway after the first sweep window, for a leaf whose pause ended 2026-10-01T19:08Z (about 1.8 days earlier):

```
subagents list (main): ... run-parked-leaf=active:waiting for external continuation
```

The list carries the wait kind, `deliveryStatus`, runtime and `endedAt`, but no pause age, and nothing that says whether a continuation was never enqueued, enqueued but not accepted, or accepted but not applied. I did not call `agents_wait` on this leaf and make no claim about its result.

### Proposed solution

Part 1 (PR to follow): add an optional `reason` string to the collector completion, set to `"yielded_without_result"` only by the registry settlement path from #164445 and absent for every other outcome. Additive only: no change to `status` values, no new status literal, no persisted-shape migration, no change to when anything settles. The existing human text stays. Docs: `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md` and `docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`.

Part 2 (decision for maintainers, no behaviour change proposed): keep `agents_wait` collector-only and expose a bounded, read-only pause age for a continuable yielded leaf through `subagents list` and the existing native `subagents action=wait` snapshots. Continuation stage (never enqueued, enqueued, accepted, applied) would be reported only where the registry holds authoritative evidence for it, and as an explicit "unknown" otherwise, because pause age or `deliveryStatus` alone cannot establish which stage is missing. Whether a declared message wait should ever expire is the open maintainer question on #141474 and is not part of this request. I will not open a PR for part 2 until the surface is agreed.

### Alternatives considered

- A new `status` literal such as `"abandoned"`: breaks exhaustive switches in existing consumers of the closed `status` union; the optional field does not.
- Parsing the `error` text: brittle, and the text is meant to change as wording improves (the reviewer asked for a more specific diagnostic, now being added on #164445).
- Settling a leaf message wait after an age threshold: rejected in #164445 review, elapsed time does not prove no continuation can arrive.

### Impact

Affected: operators and integrations that consume `agents_wait` for swarm collectors, and operators looking at yielded runs in `subagents list`.
Severity: low to medium. Nothing is lost or hung after #164445; the cost is misclassification and a stall that is hard to see.
Frequency: part 1 only for rows persisted by builds before the yield admission gate, and only once #164445 (still open) settles them; part 2 whenever a leaf declares a message wait and the continuation never arrives.
Consequence: extra manual triage, and retry logic that cannot tell a dead run from an abandoned-by-design one. The reviewer reports a fleet with the same yield semantics where a live, resumable row sat 7 days with no owner (second-hand, not reproduced here).

### Evidence/examples

- Real isolated Gateway, base `28a6f71449a` versus PR head `abfb0abb3d7`, 5 seeded persisted rows (collector with no result, collector with `outcome: ok` and no completion, orchestrator waiting on a child, awaited child, parked leaf). At the base, `agents_wait` for both collector rows stays `pending` after a 240 s sweep window. At the head, the first sweep settles both within about 19 s and `agents_wait` returns `completed:failed` with the diagnostic above. In both arms the parked leaf row stays `waiting for external continuation` in `subagents list`. These observations are at the PR head and base named above, not at current main, and were not rerun against main. Receipts: `arm-base/receipt.txt` and `arm-branch/receipt.txt` from the #164445 evidence set (will be attached to the PR body for the follow-up).
- Source anchors: `CollectorCompletionSchema` and `completionResult()` in `src/agents/tools/agents-wait-tool.ts`; the settle path `resolveYieldedRunContinuation` in `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-run-pause.ts`; the list display status in `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.ts`; `readWaitState` in `src/agents/tools/agents-wait-tool.ts` for the collector-only boundary.
- Review text that prompted this: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164445#pullrequestreview-5417876406

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, for part 1: a draft PR stacked on #164445 is in progress. Part 2 waits for a maintainer decision on the surface.

### Additional information

Related: #141474, #164445. The stacked PR will not use `Closes`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `channels.mattermost.accounts.<id>.streaming: { "mode": "off", "block": { "enabled": true, "coalesce": { "minChars": 1, "idleMs": 300 } } }`, every block reply emitted mid-turn fails with `mattermost block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized`, while the same turn's final reply — and a coalesced end-of-turn flush under the default `minChars: 1500` — deliver normally; reproduced on a fresh gateway process with no config reload or account restart between process start and the failing turn.

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.8 gateway; `@openclaw/mattermost` 2026.9.8 (installed from npm via the plugin installer); self-hosted Mattermost; agent on the bundled `claude-cli` backend (Claude Code 2.1.289); Node v24.21.0.
2. Set the account's streaming config to `{"mode":"off","block":{"enabled":true,"coalesce":{"minChars":1,"idleMs":300}}}`.
3. In a channel thread, ask the agent for a turn that alternates short text paragraphs with tool calls — e.g. "write one sentence, run `sleep 3`, write one sentence, read a file, write one sentence, run `sleep 2`, then answer". (Our probe: 3 paragraphs, 7 tool calls, ~25 s.)
4. Watch the thread and the gateway log.

### Expected behavior

Per *Streaming and chunking* → Mattermost: "`off` disables preview streaming. With `streaming.block.enabled: true`, completed assistant blocks are still delivered as normal block replies (separate posts)". Each paragraph should post as its own message as it is written, then the final answer.

With the default coalesce this does work: the buffered paragraphs land as one post at turn end, just before the final — so the block delivery path itself is fine when it runs at turn end.

### Actual behavior

None of the mid-turn blocks reach the channel. The gateway logs one error per block; the final posts normally.

Three runs, two processes: 15:26 (process A), a clean `SIGUSR2` restart at 15:39, then 15:59 and 16:03 (process B). The gateway log shows no config reload and no channel-account restart between process B's start and the 15:59 turn. Nothing else records the loss: the transcript holds the text, the audit ledger reports the run `succeeded`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (fc23bc8); `@openclaw/mattermost` 2026.9.8

### Operating system

Linux (Kubernetes pod), Node v24.21.0

### Install method

Official image; `@openclaw/mattermost` 2026.9.8 from npm via the plugin installer

### Model

`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on the bundled `claude-cli` backend (Claude Code 2.1.289, subscription login)

### Provider / routing chain

`claude-cli` (Anthropic plugin) → stdio to a warm Claude Code subprocess; fallbacks not exercised

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

One turn; all eleven records share a single `traceId`:

```
15:26:03.605 [agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 promptChars=679 trigger=user …
15:26:03.617 [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 activeSessions=4
15:26:09.516 [mattermost] block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized
15:26:14.979 [mattermost] block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized
15:26:20.915 [mattermost] block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized
15:26:25.326 [auto-reply/agent-turn-timing] agent turn milestone runId=<run-id> sessionId=<session-id> sessionKey=agent:<agent>:mattermost:group:<channel-id>:thread:<post-id> …
15:26:25.346 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=21741 outBytes=283
15:26:26.134 [mattermost] delivered reply to channel:<channel-id>
```

After the restart (fresh process, no reload in between):

```
15:39:27.342 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
15:39:36.324 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 8955ms
15:44:16.482 [gateway] http server listening (21 plugins: … mattermost …)
15:58:55.700 [agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 …
15:59:01.645 [mattermost] block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized
15:59:07.143 [mattermost] block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized
15:59:16.238 [mattermost] block reply failed: Error: Mattermost runtime not initialized
15:59:21.355 [mattermost] delivered reply to channel:<channel-id>
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

`off` + `block.enabled` is the only Mattermost configuration that streams assistant text as separate posts without tool rows (the progress-draft `commentary` lane is `.omit()`ed from the Mattermost streaming schema), so this blocks "narration while working" on Mattermost outright, and the interim text is lost silently — a log line is the only trace.

### Additional information

Root-cause reading from the installed dist, checked against `main`:

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts`: `sendMessageMattermost` and `resolveMattermostSendContext` both begin with `const core = getMattermostRuntime();`, used only for logging (`getChildLogger`, `shouldLogVerbose`).
- `extensions/mattermost/src/runtime.ts` creates the store with `createPluginRuntimeStore({ pluginId: "mattermost" })`. `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-store.ts` resolves the slot as `getPluginInstanceRuntimeSlot(instanceKey) ?? defaultSlot`, and `src/plugins/plugin-instance-scope.ts` returns the instance slot only when `pluginInstanceInvocation.getStore()?.instance` is set — i.e. inside the plugin's AsyncLocalStorage invocation frame. `setMattermostRuntime` runs inside that frame at registration, so the runtime lives in the instance slot and the global default slot stays `null`.
- A mid-turn block reply reaches `deliverMattermostReplyPayload` (`reply-delivery.ts`) through the monitor's `delivery.deliver` closure (`monitor-turn.ts`) from the agent run's streaming pipeline, and calls `params.sendMessage` = `sendMessageMattermost`. The symptom pattern — same process, same code, mid-turn fails while the end-of-turn flush and the final succeed — fits that callback running outside the invocation frame, so the lookup falls through to the never-set default slot.
- `deliverMattermostReplyPayload` already receives `core: PluginRuntime`, and `sendMessageMattermost` needs the runtime only for logging; passing `core` through (or using the optional getter with a no-op logger fallback) would take the store lookup off the send path — the same shape as #155354, which fixed the identical error for Matrix progress callbacks (#155298). `recordMattermostOutboundActivity` in `send.ts` already special-cases this exact error on this path.
- Possibly related: #163685 describes the same error for queued replies during channel retirement. This case has no retirement or reload, so it may be a distinct trigger; happy to test a build.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On the native macOS app, choosing **Settings** from the OpenClaw menu-bar item briefly flashes but does not surface the Settings window, while **Owner → Settings** inside the dashboard opens the same settings page successfully.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch OpenClaw 2026.9.4 from `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`.
2. Click the OpenClaw macOS menu-bar item.
3. Choose **Settings**.
4. Observe a brief flash, after which no Settings window is visible.
5. Bring the OpenClaw dashboard window forward.
6. Click **Owner** in the bottom-left corner, then **Settings**.
7. Observe that the Settings page opens normally.

### Expected behavior

Choosing **Settings** from the macOS menu-bar item should bring the existing dashboard window to the foreground and navigate it to the Settings page, matching the observed working behavior of **Owner → Settings**.

### Actual behavior

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect session state without a crash)

## Summary

Completed assistant replies from Codex agent-harness sessions do not make the session unread in the Control UI. The reply is durably present after the user's last read acknowledgement, but the session row remains `unread: false`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a session to use the Codex agent runtime.
2. Open the session in the Control UI and send a message.
3. Navigate away before the assistant reply completes.
4. Wait for the completed reply.
5. Inspect the session list.

## Expected behavior

A completed user-facing assistant reply after `lastReadAt` advances unread-worthy activity and the session shows an unread badge.

## Actual behavior

The assistant message is committed and the session `updatedAt` advances, but `lastActivityAt` remains absent. Since `deriveSessionUnread()` intentionally ignores `updatedAt`, the row stays read.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (base release behavior; deployed build `83c63dc` has no changes in the relevant unread/session-store files)
- Fedora Linux, Node 26
- Control UI in browser
- Agent runtime: Codex
- Models observed: `openai/gpt-6-astra`

## Redacted evidence from two independent sessions

### Session A (Telegram-backed Codex session)

- `lastReadAt`: 2026-09-08 09:37:03 +02:00
- durable assistant message: 2026-09-08 09:37:14 +02:00
- `updatedAt`: after the assistant message
- `lastActivityAt`: NULL
- derived `unread`: false

### Session B (dashboard Codex session)

- `lastReadAt`: 2026-09-07 14:28:52 +02:00
- durable assistant message: 2026-09-07 14:29:15 +02:00
- `updatedAt`: after the assistant message
- `lastActivityAt`: NULL
- derived `unread`: false

No transcript text or private identifiers are included.

## Source analysis

`deriveSessionUnread()` in `src/gateway/session-utils-core.ts` derives unread state only from:

- an explicit `markedUnreadAt`, or
- `max(lastInteractionAt, lastActivityAt) > (lastReadAt ?? createdAt)`

This is consistent with the documented contract: `lastActivityAt` is the timestamp of the last completed unread-worthy agent run, while `updatedAt` is not an activity signal.

The canonical completion writer in `src/agents/command/session-store.ts` normally computes `lastActivityAt`, but its preserved-user-facing-state metadata patch explicitly omits it. The observed Codex harness completions advance `updatedAt` and commit the assistant transcript while leaving `lastActivityAt` NULL, so the unread derivation has no completion signal.

The same relevant logic is present on current `origin/main` at `8ac88a1a335aa5f6ec467e539f6bbce3df478d84`.

## Existing issues / PRs checked

- #100739 introduced the unread contract and states that completed activity should drive unread state.
- #128986 covers never-opened modern sessions.
- #129373 / #129386 cover preserving explicit manual unread markers.
- #134158 / #134160 cover optimistic clearing when a session opens.
- #126837 reported widespread NULL `last_activity_at` for retention tooling, but was closed as not planned because qualifying ordinary completions are expected to populate it. This report demonstrates a current qualifying Codex completion path where they do not.

## Suggested repair

Ensure every completed, user-facing Codex/CLI harness turn persists `lastActivityAt`, even when model/accounting fields are intentionally preserved. Keep heartbeat, internal-event, and metadata-only paths excluded. Add an end-to-end regression that:

1. records `lastReadAt`,
2. completes a Codex harness assistant turn later,
3. asserts `lastActivityAt` advances and `sessions.list` returns `unread: true`.

### Summary
When the gateway is draining (admission closed, "suspend phase" after a native restart request), every inbound Discord message fails with `GatewayDrainingError`. In `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts`, `applyFailureDisposition` handles that error by releasing the claim immediately (`releaseClaim(claim, { recordAttempt: false })`), and the pump re-claims and re-dispatches it at once. Observed on 2026.9.2: 7,098 `message run failed: GatewayDrainingError` lines in three minutes for one message, until the process was restarted. #136684 / #136713 fixed the same pattern for the follow-up queue drain, not for the channel ingress drain.

### Environment
openclaw 2026.9.2, @openclaw/discord 2026.9.2. The drain never completed because a session parked by `sessions_yield` counts as active work, so the storm lasted until an external restart.

### Expected behavior
While the gateway drains, a held claim should wait (a bounded backoff, or until admission reopens) instead of retrying immediately. A parked session (no live turn) should not block the drain indefinitely.

### Local candidate
Hold the claim for five seconds before releasing it when the error is `GatewayDrainingError`.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a packaged `2026.9.2` install (Node 24.15.0, Linux x64, pnpm layout), any `openclaw` CLI invocation that triggers plugin discovery fails to load the bundled `memory-core` extension. The CLI's source-transform (jiti) plugin loader resolves the compiled ESM plugin graph with CommonJS require semantics, and the dependency chain `execa@10.0.1 → npm-run-path@6.0.0 → unicorn-magic@0.3.0` ends at a package whose `exports` map has no require-resolvable `"."` entry (flat `node`/`default` conditions, import-only), so the native require inside the transform loader throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`.

The Gateway (native ESM import path) loads the same plugin fine — only the CLI path is affected. Side effect: the plugin-registered `openclaw memory` command disappears from the CLI, which makes the memory engine look unavailable when diagnosing from the CLI.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a packaged OpenClaw `2026.9.2` install with its frozen dependencies (`execa@10.0.1`, `npm-run-path@6.0.0`, `unicorn-magic@0.3.0` in the pnpm store) on Node 24.15.0, Linux x64.
2. Run `openclaw memory status` (or any command that loads the plugin registry).
3. Observe:

```
[plugins] memory-core failed to load from <install>/dist/extensions/memory-core/index.js: Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "exports" main defined in <install>/node_modules/.pnpm/npm-run-path@6.0.0/node_modules/unicorn-magic/package.json
OpenClaw does not know the command "memory".
```

4. Control: `node -e "require('<install>/dist/extensions/memory-core/index.js')"` loads the same entry fine (native require(ESM) on Node 24.15.0), so the entry itself is require(esm)-compatible.
5. Control: the Gateway process loads `memory-core` normally at startup (shown as enabled; its registry/recall paths work).

Relevant `unicorn-magic@0.3.0` package.json (no `"."` key at all, and the `node` branch is import-only):

```json
"type": "module",
"main": null,
"exports": {
  "node": { "types": "./node.d.ts", "import": "./node.js" },
  "default": { "types": "./default.d.ts", "import": "./default.js" }
}
```

Under require semantics the `node` condition matches first, has no `require`/`default` fallback, and resolution fails. `npm-run-path@6.0.0` resolves under require (its `default` condition is a plain string), which is why the failure surfaces one hop later at `unicorn-magic`.

### Expected behavior

The CLI loads compiled plugin ESM graphs preserving their dependency export semantics (or falls back to native `require(esm)`/import for import-only dependencies). `memory-core` registers and `openclaw memory status` works, matching Gateway behavior.

### Actual behavior

`memory-core` (and any bundled plugin whose dist graph reaches an import-only ESM dependency) fails to load in the CLI, and its plugin-registered commands vanish. In our case `openclaw memory status` disappeared, which initially looked like a memory-engine outage from the CLI side.

### Workaround applied locally

Patched `unicorn-magic@0.3.0`'s `exports` to include a `"."` entry with a `require` condition (Node ≥22.12 then loads it via require(ESM); `node.js` has no top-level await):

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "node": { "types": "./node.d.ts", "import": "./node.js", "require": "./node.js" },
    "default": { "types": "./default.d.ts", "import": "./default.js" }
  }
}
```

After the patch, `openclaw memory status` returns a healthy report (`Provider: openai-compatible`, all sources indexed) and `openclaw plugins list` shows `memory-core` enabled. The same exports patch pattern was previously needed for `@vectorize-io/hindsight-all`, so this looks like a recurring class of problem rather than a one-off package quirk. The workaround lives in `node_modules`, so it is lost on update/reinstall.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (3928bad), packaged dist install.

### Operating system

Linux x64 (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8), Node 24.15.0.

### Install method

Packaged release (not a source checkout; the failure is in the shipped `dist/` CLI plugin-loading path).

### Model

n/a — plugin loading path, independent of model routing.

### Provider / routing chain

n/a.

### Logs

```
[plugins] memory-core failed to load from /data/opt/openclaw-v2026.9.2/dist/extensions/memory-core/index.js: Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "exports" main defined in /data/opt/openclaw-v2026.9.2/node_modules/.pnpm/npm-run-path@6.0.0/node_modules/unicorn-magic/package.json
```

### Impact and severity

Medium. No crash, but bundled plugins silently fail to load on the CLI path, plugin-registered commands disappear, and the resulting diagnostics are misleading. The local workaround requires editing `node_modules` and must be reapplied after updates.

### Additional information

Related closed reports cover the source-checkout variants of this class:

- #132153 (source plugin artifacts fail on import-only dependencies)
- #134864 (source Gateway preload breaks compiled plugin ESM dependencies — fixed by PR #135077 by selecting tsx's ESM entry in the source preload)

This report is the packaged-dist CLI path: the jiti/source-transform plugin loader still converts compiled ESM graphs to CJS requires and fails on import-only dependency exports in 2026.9.2. Possible fix directions: when the transform loader resolves a dependency, preserve import-condition resolution (or retry via native require(ESM)/dynamic import when require resolution fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`-style errors), so compiled plugin graphs keep their intended export semantics in the CLI just as they do in the Gateway.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An empty legacy `auth_profile_store` table in the per-agent SQLite makes every agent request fail with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED, while dropping that same table makes startup migrations fail and the gateway refuse to become ready, so no database state satisfies both checks.

### Steps to reproduce

Starting state (observed on our install): `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` has table `auth_profile_store` with one row `('primary', '{"version":1,"profiles":{}}')` — an empty profile set. `state/openclaw.sqlite` has four `auth-profile-v2:*` rows in `migration_runs` marked `completed`, whose `report_json.targetTable` is `auth_profile_stores`, but that table does not exist in the database.
1. Send any message to the agent. Every request fails with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, and separately `openclaw doctor --fix --force` (offline, container stopped). Both report `Failed relocating the shared auth store: shared auth credential rows conflict with the relocation target` and only archive the legacy JSON again. Requests still fail.
3. Delete the single row from `auth_profile_store`, leaving the table. Requests still fail with the same error, so the block is triggered by the table existing, not by its content.
4. Drop the `auth_profile_store` table. `openclaw models auth list` now works for the first time, but the gateway refuses to start: `OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.` / `Skipped historical transcript directive migration ... SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical ... missing table auth_profile_store` / `OpenClaw exited with code 1`.
5. Recreate `auth_profile_store` empty and create `auth_profile_stores` in the state DB with one row `('shared', '{"version":1,"profiles":{}}')`. The gateway boots and reports ready, but requests fail again with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
6. Delete the four `auth-profile-v2:*` rows from `migration_runs`, plus the orphaned `migration_sources` rows. `doctor --fix` now performs a real migration (`Migrated auth profile JSON for ...`) but ends with `Failed relocating the shared auth store: shared auth state rows conflict with the relocation target`. Requests still fail.

### Expected behavior

A legacy store holding an empty profile set (`"profiles":{}`) should be treated as having nothing to migrate and retired, letting requests proceed. When a `migration_runs` receipt is marked `completed` but its `targetTable` does not exist, `doctor --fix` should be able to reconcile that state rather than reporting a relocation conflict on every run. Before the legacy store entered this state, this same install answered Telegram messages normally on the same config and credentials.

### Actual behavior

100% of agent requests fail. The gateway reports ready and Telegram polling runs normally, but each inbound message produces, in the gateway log: `lane task error: lane=main ... error="Couldn't sign in to deepseek. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. ... (Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.) | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED"`, then `Embedded agent failed before reply`, and the user receives only the generic fallback "Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session." The fallback model is attempted and fails identically, so the failure is independent of the provider. `openclaw models auth list --agent main` fails with the same error, so there is no CLI path to inspect or repair the profiles. Docker reports the container as `healthy` throughout. This has been ongoing for over two weeks; each `doctor --fix` run buys a shorter working window than the last (from ~30-90 minutes down to a single message) and leaves another `auth-profiles.json.migrated-*` archive behind (14 accumulated so far).

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2 (0965053)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (container), host Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on a KVM VPS

### Install method

docker (image ghcr.io/hostinger/hvps-openclaw:latest, docker compose)

### Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, fallback openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek (direct), fallback openclaw -> openrouter

### Additional provider/model setup details

Four agents are configured (main, claude, gpt, gemini); the failing one is main. Both providers are custom OpenAI-completions-compatible entries under `models.providers` in openclaw.json with inline API keys, so the working credentials never lived in the auth profile store that is blocking them — the store being migrated is empty. The `migration_runs` receipts reference archive paths such as `/data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-<timestamp>-<uuid>`. The `auth_profile_state` table in the same per-agent DB holds only provider usage stats (a DeepSeek billing cooldown), and it is that table which produces the "shared auth state rows conflict" in step 6.

### Logs

```shell
Per-message failure (gateway log, timestamps local -04:00):
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=32 error="Couldn't sign in to deepseek. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. Run `openclaw models auth login --provider deepseek` or `openclaw configure`. (Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.) | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED"
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash candidate=openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free reason=auth next=none detail=Couldn't sign in to openrouter ... | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
Embedded agent failed before reply: Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.
[diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=telegram ... outcome=error

doctor --fix / --fix --force (steps 2 and 5):
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Failed relocating the shared auth store: Error: shared auth credential rows conflict with the relocation target
Doctor changes: Archived a previously migrated legacy auth source without replaying credentials (~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-...).

Gateway refusing to start with the table dropped (step 4):
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Skipped historical transcript directive migration for /data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: Error: SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for /data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: missing table auth_profile_store
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the same state/config, then restart the gateway.
WARN: OpenClaw exited with code 1

doctor --fix after clearing the receipts (step 6):
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Failed relocating the shared auth store: Error: shared auth state rows conflict with the relocation target
Migrated auth profile JSON for ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-2026-09-08T02-36-43...

Foreign key breakage when receipts are deleted without their sources:
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: SQLite foreign_key_check failed for /data/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite: migration_sources row 1 references migration_runs (foreign key 0); ... row 4 ...
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: all Telegram users of this deployment; the main agent on a self-hosted Docker install.
Severity: High — the agent cannot answer any message, and no supported CLI path can repair it (the auth commands are gated behind the same error).
Frequency: Always, on every inbound message, for over two weeks.
Consequence: The assistant is unusable in production. Docker still reports the container as healthy, so the outage is invisible without reading gateway logs, and the end user only ever sees "Something went wrong while processing your request."

### Additional information

Copies of both SQLite databases were taken before any modification, so the original broken state can be reproduced or shared on request. Steps 3 to 6 were manual database edits made only after the supported paths (`doctor --fix`, `doctor --fix --force`, `gateway stop --force` followed by `doctor --fix`, and plain container restarts) had all been exhausted; they are reported here as diagnostic evidence of the contradiction, not as a recommended workaround. Related but distinct: #41634 (legacy auth profiles accumulate and cannot be cleaned up) describes the same accumulation of archived profile files that we see (14 and counting), though it does not cover the migration deadlock above.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (regression — worked before 2026.9.2)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading 2026.8.2 → 2026.9.2 (`3928bad`), the **`browser` tool wedges for agent turns while the CLI path stays fully healthy**.

Once wedged, every `browser` action issued from an agent turn fails after a long stall with:

> `timed out. Restart the OpenClaw gateway (OpenClaw.app menubar, or 'openclaw gateway'). This may be a transient browser error.`

At the same moment, against the **same managed profile**:

- `openclaw browser tabs` returns in **~1.9s**
- `openclaw browser open <url>` navigates the same URL in **~2.8s**
- `openclaw browser doctor` reports **every check OK**

So this is not Chrome, not page weight, and not the target site — the CLI drives the same profile fine while the agent-side tool path times out.

Onset is delayed (works for a while after restart, then wedges), and it **recurs after recovery**.

This looks like the same failure family as #141615 (session/task RPCs wedge until gateway restart, while `chat.send` keeps working) and #141269 ("CLI works; data layer healthy", fails ~12 min after upgrade with no restart in between) — a subsystem stops serving one class of caller while the rest of the gateway stays healthy.

### Steps to reproduce

1. macOS, npm global install, upgrade 2026.8.2 → 2026.9.2.
2. Configure a managed browser profile (`driver: openclaw`, CDP port 18800) as `browser.defaultProfile`.
3. Have an agent turn call the `browser` tool (`action: navigate`) against a login-walled SPA. Use it normally for a while.
4. After some period of use, agent-side `browser` calls begin timing out with the message above.
5. While wedged, from a shell: `openclaw browser tabs`, `openclaw browser open <same url>`, `openclaw browser doctor` — all succeed in ~2s with all checks OK.

### Expected behavior

An agent-side `browser` action should behave like the CLI path against the same profile: succeed in seconds, or fail fast with a specific error.

### Actual behavior

Agent-side `browser` actions stall for the full timeout and return the generic "transient browser error / restart the gateway" text, while the CLI path against the same profile is healthy and fast.

Observed on multiple action kinds, not just navigation — both `action: navigate` and `action: act` (`kind: type`, using a ref from a fresh snapshot) timed out in the same run.

**Recovery (what works):**

- `openclaw gateway restart`, **then** `openclaw browser start` — note the browser reports `running: false` after the gateway restart and must be started explicitly. `browser doctor` then passes and agent-side navigation works again (~25s incl. model turn).

**Recovery (what makes it worse):**

- `openclaw browser stop` + `openclaw browser start` **without** a gateway restart. After this, browser RPCs failed with `gateway timeout after 45000ms` while unrelated gateway RPCs (`openclaw health`, `openclaw sessions list`) still responded normally. Only a gateway restart cleared it.

**Ruled out during triage:**

- Stale/unknown `targetId` — fails fast (~1.7s) with a clear `tab not found`, so it is not the hang path.
- Page weight / target site — CLI navigates the identical URL in 2.8s.
- Chrome itself — process healthy, CDP port listening, `browser doctor` all-OK.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (`3928bad`)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6 (Darwin 25.6.0), Apple Silicon

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew node), upgraded in place with `openclaw update` from 2026.8.2

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenAI via ChatGPT-account route (`api: openai-chatgpt-responses`, `baseUrl: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api`), built-in OpenClaw runtime (not Codex).

### Additional provider/model setup details

Managed browser profile `openclaw` (`driver: openclaw`, CDP 18800, non-headless), set as `browser.defaultProfile`. Multiple browser profiles configured; the wedge was observed on the managed CDP profile.

### Logs

Frequency changed sharply at the upgrade — same machine, same workload:

```
openclaw-2026-09-06.log   (2026.8.2)  "Chrome MCP attach failed": 0   "browser failed": 0
openclaw-2026-09-07.log   (2026.9.2)  "Chrome MCP attach failed": 2   "browser failed": 4+
```

Representative agent-side failure (params retained, message body is the standard untrusted-content wrapper):

```
ERROR [tools] browser failed: ... timed out. Restart the OpenClaw gateway ...
raw_params={"action":"navigate","targetId":"<label>","url":"https://<login-walled-spa>/sales-history"}

ERROR [tools] browser failed: ... timed out. Restart the OpenClaw gateway ...
raw_params={"action":"act","targetId":"<label>","kind":"type","ref":"<ref>","text":"...","submit":true}
```

Separately, an attach-only (`chrome-mcp`, `attachOnly: true`, `cdpPort: null`) profile pointed at a normal desktop Chrome logs:

```
WARN Chrome MCP attach failed for profile "user". Subprocess stderr:
(node:####) Warning: `--localstorage-file` was provided without a valid path
```

and `browser doctor --browser-profile user` fails its `tabs` check with `Could not find DevToolsActivePort`. That profile is arguably user error (Chrome not started with remote debugging), but the retained-stderr behaviour from #137993 is what made it diagnosable, and #138486 / #138524 (startup failure reporting cleanup complete while the subprocess is still running) look adjacent to the wedge described here.

### Impact and severity

High friction for any browser-backed agent workflow. Each wedged call burns a full timeout before the agent can react, and agents typically need several browser actions per task. A routine "price this card" request that should take well under a minute took **8–10 minutes**, with roughly a quarter of wall-clock time spent in two navigate timeouts alone; the remainder was the extra reasoning loops each failed call forced.

No data loss. Workaround exists (`gateway restart` + `browser start`) but it is not durable — the wedge returns.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a model calls a tool by a name that is not a real tool (for example a Tool Search catalog id used as if it were a function name), the failure is recorded as the run's `lastToolError` under that wrong name. If the model then recovers by calling the correct entry point and finishes with an intentional `NO_REPLY`, the earlier error is never cleared and the run is reported as failed. Scheduled (cron) runs then send an "automation failed" notice although the work completed.

## Observed

OpenClaw 2026.9.7, Linux, gateway in a container, isolated cron runs, a stdio/HTTP MCP server exposed through Tool Search.

- In 5 cron runs over one afternoon, one hosted model emitted 18 calls whose function name was the catalog id of an MCP tool instead of calling the Tool Search call tool with `{id, args}`. Each such call returned `Tool ... not found`.
- In every one of those runs the same search succeeded a moment later through the proper call tool, the agent finished its work, and the final reply was the declared `NO_REPLY`.
- The runs were still marked failed, with the first tool error as the run error. The next scheduled run was fine each time. Other models on the same jobs did not produce the bad name, so this is a model-quality problem, but the run outcome is decided by OpenClaw.

## Where I think it comes from (from reading current `main`, not yet reproduced with a test)

- `src/agents/tool-terminal-outcome.ts`: a failed observation sets `lastToolError`; it is only cleared (`else if` branch) when a later observation has the same normalized `toolName` and is not a failure. A recovery through a different tool (here the Tool Search call tool) never matches, so the error stays.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts`: `preserveOriginalTerminal` is true whenever `initial.attempt.lastToolError` is set, and its comment says that intentional silence does not replace a tool error. So the leftover error wins over `NO_REPLY`.
- `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.replay-safety.test.ts` already models this case ("unknown-tool fallback", `executionStarted=false`), so the failure is known to be pre-dispatch and side-effect free.

## Possible fix

A tool failure with `executionStarted === false` for a name that is not a registered tool is not a failed action. Either do not record it as `lastToolError`, or let any later successful tool call clear a pre-dispatch (`executionStarted === false`, non-mutating) error. Mutating errors would keep today's behavior.

I am happy to send a PR with a regression test if this direction fits; I wanted to check first because the current behavior looks deliberate for real tool failures.

## Not verified

- Not reproduced on current `main` with a unit test yet; the above is from logs of 2026.9.7 and reading `main`.
- Which model produced the bad names is deliberately left out; I do not think it matters for the lifecycle question.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw 2026.9.2 webchat: after an update + `openclaw onboard`, the Control UI WS connection enters a permanently pending state where **every profile-dependent RPC** fails with:

> `UNAVAILABLE: Authenticated profile verification is unavailable. Retry shortly; if this continues, contact a gateway administrator.`

Affected methods seen in gateway ws logs (all, repeatedly, ~2 s after connect): `chat.startup`, `sessions.list`, `sessions.groups.list`, `sessions.catalog.list`, `sessions.describe`, `sessions.subscribe`, `sessions.messages.subscribe`, `sessions.viewers.set`, `sessions.observer.visibility`, `tasks.list`, `taskSuggestions.list`, `workboard.cards.list`, `progressCard.get`, `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe`, `openclaw.approval.list`.

Notably `chat.send` kept working, so the agent stayed reachable while the UI looked dead — very confusing UX.

## Root-cause pointer

`isGatewayClientProfilePending(client)` = `client.authenticatedGitHubIdentitySync && !client.authenticatedUserProfile` (src/gateway/server-methods/gateway-client-identity.ts) never clears for the connection — the async GitHub identity sync presumably fails silently and the client is stuck "pending" for its lifetime. Every gated method returns retryable UNAVAILABLE.

## Workaround that fixed it

Restarting the gateway (and hard-refreshing the tab). Per-connection state, so there is no self-heal retry for the user.

## Suggestions

1. Retry profile sync on the connection (with backoff) instead of wedge-until-restart.
2. Surface a one-click "reconnect" (new WS) affordance in the UI error.
3. If chat.send must stay allowed while profile is pending, make the UI clearly show "degraded" instead of blank panels.

## Environment

- 2026.9.2 (3928bad), gateway on Linux/Debian 13, webchat over Tailscale serve HTTPS
- Same build also produced intermittent `exec` child SIGTERM kills (separate issue) and the `openclaw` plugin tool error `prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded` (resolved by `openclaw onboard`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A `system.run.prepare` command whose shape cannot be bound to an approval returns a single response carrying three different error classifications (`errorCode=UNAVAILABLE`, message prefix `INVALID_REQUEST:`, inner text `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED:`), emits no approval request, and names no corrective action — so the agent concludes its exec access was revoked and reports that to end users, while the operator is actively approving other commands in the same session.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a lane where approval binding is active (any lane that is not `security: full` + `ask: off`).

1. In a session where the operator is present and answering exec approvals, run a single absolute-path command (e.g. `rg -c -F "it(" <abs-path>`). An approval card is presented, the operator answers, the command runs.
2. In the same session, run a compound command through the exec tool — a `cd <dir> && <command>` chain or a pipeline.
3. Observe the response: `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command`, returned in 5–8 ms.
4. Observe that no approval request accompanies step 3 — the 5–8 ms turnaround excludes a human decision, and the surrounding operator-answered approvals took 3.3–11.3 s (see Logs).
5. Reshape to a single absolute-path command and resend. An approval card appears again and is answered normally.

Counter-check on the same gateway and the same `node.invoke` transport: a `cd … && …` compound command issued from a `security: full` + `ask: off` lane returns `res ✓ node.invoke` and executes normally. On that policy `bindApproval` is false, so the binding step that produces this message is never reached — which places the trigger in the binding path rather than in the command text or the host.

Note on provenance: the gateway log records the denial responses but not the request payloads, so the exact denied command strings are taken from the affected agent's own transcript rather than from the gateway log.

### Expected behavior

The message should identify the command **shape** as the cause and name the corrective action the agent can take unilaterally (resend as a single command), consistent with the repo's own stated principle in root `AGENTS.md` → Product Judgment:

> Every action ends with a visible outcome or a recorded intentional non-outcome. Failure messages explain the next useful step.

and

> Prioritize broken existing behavior, especially silent failure.

A single response should also carry one coherent error classification rather than three.

### Actual behavior

One response carries three mutually inconsistent classifications:

- `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE` — reads as a service/resource outage
- `errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST:` — the actual class (malformed request)
- inner text `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED:` — reads as a policy refusal, or a human saying no

None of the three names the real cause (unbindable command shape) or the remedy. No approval request is emitted, so no human denied anything.

Observed consequence: the agent reported to end users in a public channel that its shell access was gated and had not cleared ("exec is locked", "gate's shut"), abandoned the task, and did not retry the single-command shape that had succeeded ninety seconds earlier. When the operator stated that no approval had been requested — the fact that falsifies the access-loss reading — the agent restated it as confirmation and continued.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.8.2 (0965053)` — observed.

Source paths cited below verified against `main` at `9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12` (2026-09-07); the routing described is unchanged there.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure (x64)

### Install method

npm global (`node_modules/openclaw`), Node v24.20.0

### Model

`claude-opus-4-8` via the `claude-cli` provider (gateway log: `cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-4-8`).

### Provider / routing chain

Not a model-provider path. The denial occurs in the gateway → node-host exec chain (`node.invoke` → `system.run.prepare`) before any provider request is made. The affected agent executes against a paired node.

### Logs

Redacted gateway log, single session, times UTC. Approval traffic and denials interleaved:

```text
19:53:01  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 11294ms      <- operator present, answering
19:53:08  res ✗ node.invoke 6ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
19:53:12  res ✗ node.invoke 5ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
19:53:24  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 5389ms
19:53:44  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 5569ms
19:54:06  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 6034ms
19:54:21  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 9877ms
19:54:38  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 6677ms
19:56:12  res ✗ node.invoke 7ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
19:56:28  res ✗ node.invoke 6ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
20:01:24  res ✗ node.invoke 8ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
20:02:14  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 6703ms      <- operator still present
20:02:35  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 7573ms
20:02:42  res ✓ exec.approval.waitDecision 3331ms
```

Nine operator-answered approvals bracket five denials. Every denial resolves in 5–8 ms with no corresponding approval request.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** agents on any lane where approval binding is active (not `security: full` + `ask: off`), on the node exec path.
- **Severity:** Blocks workflow, and produces false statements about system state to end users. The agent's own recovery path (reshape and retry) is available, but the message points away from it.
- **Frequency:** 5 denials in the ~8-minute window above, plus 2 more of the same class earlier the same day (16:57:53). Every compound-shape attempt in that session was denied; the per-command payloads are not in the gateway log, so the shape of each individual attempt comes from the agent transcript rather than the log.
- **Consequence:** task abandoned mid-answer in a public channel; the agent asserted an access restriction that did not exist, and stated it to community members. Operator time spent diagnosing a gate that was open the whole time.

### Additional information

**Why the message cannot currently carry a remedy.** Neither path that produces this text passes through `sendSystemRunDenied`, so the per-class escalation hints added by open PR #130972 cannot attach to it. On `main` at `9a4114bc`:

- [`src/node-host/invoke.ts:912`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12/src/node-host/invoke.ts#L912) — `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan()` failure routes to `sendErrorResult(client, frame, "INVALID_REQUEST", prepared.message)`. The wire error *code* is `INVALID_REQUEST` while the message text begins `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED:`.
- [`src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-approval.ts:214`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-approval.ts#L214) — `prepareSystemRunMutableFileBinding()` runs *before* the `callGatewayTool(...)` approval request at [`:250`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-approval.ts#L250). On failure it returns `{ kind: "deny", reason: "operand-binding", message }` at [`:221`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12/src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-approval.ts#L221), which reaches the model via `denyTool(outcome.message)`. No approval request is ever made.

PR #130972's description states that `sendSystemRunDenied` "is the single choke point every `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED` denial flows through before reaching the agent." The two paths above are counterexamples on the same tree, and that PR changes only `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts`. Noting this as coverage information for that PR rather than a criticism of its approach — its per-class hint design looks like exactly what this path needs.

**The binder behavior itself is not in question here.** Refusing to bind an ambiguous shape is intentional and has regression coverage. This report is only about the response being unattributable and unactionable. For reference, the shape rules on `9a4114bc` are [`src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts:615`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12/src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts#L615) (a shell group with more than one executable candidate) and [`:468`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9a4114bc4691bdb1293fd48ef1ed1b1790485d12/src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts#L468) (a cwd mutator that is not the final segment).

**Prior art checked.**

- #138422 (closed as duplicate, 2026-09-04) — same binder, framed against headless cron where the approval owner was genuinely absent. Distinct here: the owner is present and answering approvals on both sides of the denials. That issue's closing comment flagged this class of problem as "a diagnostics gap rather than a functional one… separately worth noting (not necessarily here)"; this is that report.
- #137337 (open) — `tools.exec.mode=auto` auto-reviewer never firing. Different mechanism; not claimed here.
- #48457 (closed) — interpreter one-liners denied under `security: full, ask: off`. About the denial existing, not about how it is reported.
- #130972 (open PR) — related coverage, addressed above.

**Separate observation, deliberately not part of this report.** In the same window, seven `plugin.approval.request` calls were rejected in 0–1 ms with `errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=signed plugin approval owner is unavailable` (19:58:02–19:58:07), while the same operator answered `exec.approval.waitDecision` at 19:54:38 and again at 20:02:14. That suggests the plugin-approval lane and the exec-approval lane can disagree about owner availability, which is a different mechanism from the one reported above and is not claimed as part of it. Happy to file separately if that would be useful.

**Outer `UNAVAILABLE` wrap.** I traced the `INVALID_REQUEST` and `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED` layers to the sites above. I did not identify what maps the response to `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE` at the `node.invoke` boundary, so that layer is reported as observed rather than source-attributed.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary Summary — In one webchat session driving a Windows node via exec host=node: (1) the same [OpenClaw exec completion] batch — same ids, output and exit codes — was republished ~15 times over ~40 minutes, each delivery running a turn; (2) the operator's attempts to stop it were silently dropped, with two mid-loop messages recorded as pendingInputs entries in state: "cancelled" that never became turns. Environment — Gateway OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d) Linux x64; node host OpenClaw 2026.9.5, Windows 10; webchat; single main session; no subagents, no cron, no at jobs; tools.exec unset → backgroundMs: 10000, notifyOnExit: true. Finding 1 — The batch grew with slow commands and froze without them (15 → 19 → 20 ids, then no further deliveries once nothing exceeded backgroundMs). Reply length was irrelevant: long digests, single-line replies and silent handling all produced the same rate. Ids: e4b55390, d93557f9, 6e38e4b0, 09bd3c4d, 64b5c3e2, 650bd5bc, 61f61316, 094a3213, 04b38852, 68d958b2, 6f6ded5a, d667d75d, cf2cc13a, 4b26a54d, d606b941, 912ce242, 8bddaf71, f5d80025, 19a9467a, 2a6ed384. Finding 2 — While the loop ran, "you can stop now." and a second correction were cancelled rather than delivered, so there was no way to interrupt from the chat; the loop ended only when a later message happened to be admitted. Requested: surface dropped/cancelled inputs back to the sender, or let a stop instruction preempt pending wake deliveries. Mitigations, all unsatisfactory — tools.loopDetection doesn't apply (it targets repeated tool calls within a run; cf. #34574); heartbeat.every: "0m" doesn't stop targeted completion wakes; tools.exec.notifyOnExit: false removes legitimate completion signals too (cf. #141973); the agent can only self-impose "report once" discipline, which changes chat volume, not wake count. Ask — dedupe/coalesce already-delivered batches (per #150598 rule 3); give cancelled inputs a visible outcome; consider a per-session wake rate limit. ### Steps to reproduce Preconditions Gateway on defaults: openclaw config get tools.exec shows no overrides for backgroundMs (10s) or notifyOnExit (true) One agent session (we used webchat), Node ≥ v22, no subagents, cron or at jobs configured Steps In a single session, issue a burst of exec commands that each run longer than backgroundMs — e.g. ten of sleep 12 && echo step-N Let the agent handle them normally; no special reply handling needed Watch the notices: completions arrive as a batch of command ids, not one notice per command Keep issuing slow commands: the batch's id set grows while earlier ids keep reappearing (we went 15 → 19 → 20 ids) Stop issuing slow commands: the id set freezes and the re-deliveries stop Measure amplification as (deliveries of the same id set) ÷ (distinct completed commands) — we observed ~15 deliveries for 20 ids over ~40 minutes, each delivery running one agent turn Controls, to isolate the trigger A single slow command produces one notice and no repetition Commands under backgroundMs (e.g. sleep 5) produced no notices and no batch growth — so the aggregation appears gated on backgrounding tools.exec.notifyOnExit: false removes the notices entirely (blunt: also removes legitimate completion signals) suppressNotifyOnExit: true per invocation is untested — our probe completed under backgroundMs and so generated no notice regardless, leaving the flag's effect unconfirmed Secondary repro (dropped stop signal) While the loop is active, have the user send a stop message ("stop", "you can stop now."). In our run two such messages never became turns; both appear in the session's pendingInputs with state: "cancelled". The loop ended only when a later message happened to be admitted. Expected vs actual Expected: each backgrounded command yields at most one completion notice, delivered once Actual: one batch of ids re-presented ~15 times, each presentation running a turn, batch content byte-identical Not the trigger (ruled out in our run) Reply length — long digests, single-line replies and silent handling all gave the same rate Subagents/cron — none existed in the session ### Expected behavior one message and stopped ### Actual behavior a loop every few second with no way of stopping it. ### OpenClaw version OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d) ### Operating system Debian 13 ### Install method npm global ### Model Deepseek V4.1 flash ### Provider / routing chain platform.deepseek ### Additional provider/model setup details _No response_ ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence # Evidence log: repeated `[OpenClaw exec completion]` deliveries Session: `agent:main:main` · sessionId `a2da274a-bdd6-4c82-9131-5a8fa75cb375` · channel webchat · agent=main Extraction: `sessions_search` (query `OpenClaw exec completion`, role `user`). issues.body:
### Summary

Add a supported, targeted way to list and retire one stranded requester settle wake (a `subagent_runs` row whose `requesterSettleWake` keeps retrying without ever settling), without editing the state database by hand. This is the operator recovery part of #154252 ("a supported operator command for this would be valuable on its own"). It is separate from bounding the retry (the closed #158518) and from the owner-changed diagnostic in #164529, and is still needed after both, because rows that are already stranded stay stranded.

### Problem to solve

A completed subagent run can keep a durable `requesterSettleWake` that never settles. The reported state shape (#154252, observed on 2026.9.4, same code in 2026.9.5):

```
subagent_runs.payload_json
  execution.status            terminal
  endedReason                 subagent-killed (killReconciliation set)
  expectsCompletionMessage    true
  delivery.status             pending
  requesterSettleWake.status  dispatching
  requesterSettleWake.attemptCount  3   (= REQUESTER_SETTLE_WAKE_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
  matching task_runs row      purged by cleanupAfter
```

A second report on #154252 (2026.9.6) shows `requesterSettleWake = {status: "dispatching", attemptCount: 1, batchRunIds: [<own run>], requesterYieldBatch: true, rearmGeneration: 1}`, `delivery.status = "pending"`, `cleanupHandled = true`, and `requester settle wake failed ... subagent completion owner changed before settlement: <runId>` about once per minute per run, surviving a Gateway restart.

On #154252 the only recovery that worked was deleting the `subagent_runs` rows directly; the reporter found no supported RPC or CLI for it. No producer of these states is established on current main (#159612, the owner-changed variant, is closed), but the rows are durable and survive upgrades, so a database that already holds one needs a recovery path regardless.

What current main (`c5b1c315d05`) offers:

- `cancelRequesterSettleWake` (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle-wake.ts:148`) can retire a terminal wake: it sets `suppressCompletionDelivery` and clears `requesterSettleWake`. It returns without retiring the wake of a `sessions_yield` member (`:154`).
- It is reached only through session-wide stops that pass `suppressTaskDelivery: true`: `/reset` (`stopSessionResetSubagents`, `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts:108`, calls `killSessionSubagentRuns`, `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control-kill.ts:543`) and abort (`src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts:247` and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-descendants.ts:183`, both call `killAllControlledSubagentRuns`). These act on the requester session's whole child selection, so retiring one stranded row also stops the other running children, and `/reset` also starts a fresh conversation.
- The per-run kill path `killSubagentRunAdmin` is reached from the `subagents` tool `cancel` action (`src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.ts:398`), `src/gateway/session-kill-http.ts:116` and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts:144`. None of them passes `suppressTaskDelivery`, so none enters the wake cancellation branch (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control-kill-runtime.ts:133`).
- `doctor` state integrity (`src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts`) reports wedged subagent recovery sessions but has no check for a retained `requesterSettleWake`.

So an operator cannot list stranded wakes, and cannot retire one without stopping or resetting the whole requester session (which still does not retire the wake of a `sessions_yield` member) or editing SQLite.

### Proposed solution

A Doctor check with an explicit, per-run fix:

1. Detect (default, read-only): list `subagent_runs` rows whose `requesterSettleWake` is present on a terminal run, with run id, requester session key, wake status, `attemptCount`, `nextAttemptAt`, age, `batchRunIds`, `rearmGeneration`, delivery status, and whether a captured result exists. Rank by stored `attemptCount` and age, since the per-episode failure count is in memory only.
2. Retire one row, named by run id, through the running Gateway using the same ownership-checked mutation `cancelRequesterSettleWake` already uses, never as a direct SQLite write from the Doctor process. Keep the `rearmGeneration` and `batchRunIds` checks, so a stale listing fails closed with the existing "changed during cancellation; retry" rejection. Leave every other child of the requester untouched.
3. Make the outcome explicit: the captured outcome and result stay on the row, but `suppressCompletionDelivery` means the requester never receives this child's result. Print that, and require explicit confirmation (or `--yes`) before retiring.
4. Handle `sessions_yield` cohort members explicitly: retire the whole cohort together or refuse with a reason, rather than skipping silently.

### Alternatives considered

- Bounding the dispatching retry by count: #158518 tried this in the admission path and was closed because it discards completions behind a pending requester turn or an unspent ambiguous replay. A bound also does nothing for rows that are already stranded.
- `/stop` or `/reset` of the requester session: stops the other running children (and `/reset` also resets the conversation) to retire one row, and does not retire the wake of a `sessions_yield` member.
- An automatic clear of retained wakes, the direction of #166267: that covers markers kept after a successful delivery, not rows that can never settle because their stored state is rejected.
- Deleting `subagent_runs` rows by hand: unsupported, bypasses the ownership checks and the in-memory registry of a running Gateway, and loses the captured result.

### Impact

- Affected: requester sessions holding a subagent completion whose settle wake cannot settle (#154252 and the 2026.9.6 report on it).
- Severity: blocks workflow; the wake keeps retrying and logging until someone edits the database.
- Frequency: edge case, but persistent once entered; it survives restarts and upgrades.
- Consequence: manual SQLite edits on a live state database, or a session-wide stop or reset that interrupts unrelated work.

### Evidence/examples

- #154252: state shape, logs, and "Only recovery found: Deleting the orphaned `subagent_runs` rows directly".
- The triage review on #154252 includes in its best solution: "provide an in-product Doctor or Fix recovery path for already stranded batches".
- Source references above are at `c5b1c315d05`.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Related: #154252, #164529, #159612, #166267, #155163 (retirement of failed deliveries after the task record is pruned, a different state).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a memory-wiki compile process ends between registering its compiled-cache candidate and committing or deleting it, nothing short of vault re-initialization (`vault.ts` 121) or the owner leaving the active set (`index.ts` 159) removes that row, so dead rows build up in the shared state database (23 attributable rows, 34,821,095 B on one host) until oldest-first eviction at the namespace's 256-row or 512 MiB cap, which reaches the active publication only after rows written since its commit fill the cap on their own.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on origin/main 0fc11d74d3ed (built from source, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.9.0) with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, memory-wiki `vaultMode: "isolated"`, `vault.scope: "global"`, `obsidian.enabled: false`, `bridge.enabled: false`, and 3,000 generated concept pages, so that validation (the step between candidate write and commit) lasts long enough to observe:

1. `openclaw wiki init`, generate the pages (generator below), then `openclaw wiki compile` once so the vault has an active publication.
2. Start `openclaw wiki compile` in its own process group. Wait until `.openclaw-wiki/log.jsonl` has the new `compiledCacheReservationId` record and the state database (opened read-only) shows a new `memory-wiki/compiled-cache` row, then SIGKILL the process group (harness below; doing this by hand is impractical, since step 3 committed 0.55 s after its candidate write).
3. Run `openclaw wiki compile` again to completion.
4. Query `plugin_blob_entries` read-only after steps 2 and 3.

| step | compiled-cache rows (publicationId, created UTC) | log.jsonl |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `3ee78bb2` 23:54:26 (active) | committed |
| 2, killed 7 ms after its row appeared | `3ee78bb2` 23:54:26; `979a1787` 23:54:59 | reservation `8c2cea30` 23:54:58.025, no commit record |
| 3 | `979a1787` 23:54:59; `08d45db7` 23:55:15 (active) | `08d45db7` committed with parent `3ee78bb2` |

Step 3 deleted its parent `3ee78bb2` and kept `979a1787`, whose publication id appears nowhere in the log (`grep -c` 0; the same check on `3ee78bb2` returns 4).

<details>
<summary>Page generator (stdlib Python; equivalent to the one used, which the repro record describes field by field, except that the filler sentence is replaced by neutral text of the same length, 75 ASCII bytes, so every page has the same byte count as in the run; the gzip row size, 60,164 B in the run, can differ slightly)</summary>

```python
# usage: python3 -I gen.py <vault>
import os, sys
root = sys.argv[1]
body = " ".join(["Each generated page repeats this neutral sentence so that its body is long."] * 12)
for i in range(3000):
    with open(os.path.join(root, "concepts", f"repro-concept-{i:04d}.md"), "w") as f:
        f.write(
            "---\n"
            "pageType: concept\n"
            f"id: concept.repro-{i:04d}\n"
            f'title: "Repro concept {i:04d}"\n'
            "status: draft\n"
            "updatedAt: 2026-10-10T00:00:00.000Z\n"
            "---\n\n"
            f"# Repro concept {i:04d}\n\n## Summary\n\n{body}\n"
        )
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kill harness used in step 2 (stdlib Python; opens the state database read-only)</summary>

```python
# Start `openclaw wiki compile` in its own process group, wait for its compile
# reservation in the vault log, then for a new compiled-cache row in the state DB
# (opened read-only), then SIGKILL the whole process group.
# usage: python3 -I kill-after-candidate.py <openclaw checkout> <vault> <state>/openclaw.sqlite
import json, os, signal, sqlite3, subprocess, sys, time
repo, vault, db = sys.argv[1:4]
log = os.path.join(vault, ".openclaw-wiki", "log.jsonl")
def now(): return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime()) + f".{int(time.time()*1000)%1000:03d}Z"
lines0 = sum(1 for _ in open(log))
con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)
q = "select count(*) from plugin_blob_entries where plugin_id='memory-wiki' and namespace='compiled-cache'"
rows0 = con.execute(q).fetchone()[0]
p = subprocess.Popen(["node", "openclaw.mjs", "wiki", "compile"], cwd=repo, start_new_session=True,
                     stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
print(f"{now()} started pid={p.pid} pgid={os.getpgid(p.pid)} log_lines={lines0} rows={rows0}", flush=True)
seen_res = False
while p.poll() is None:
    if not seen_res:
        for line in list(open(log))[lines0:]:
            d = json.loads(line).get("details") or {}
            if d.get("compiledCacheReservationId") and not d.get("compiledCachePublicationId"):
                print(f"{now()} reservation logged: {line.strip()}", flush=True); seen_res = True; break
    else:
        n = con.execute(q).fetchone()[0]
        if n > rows0:
            os.killpg(os.getpgid(p.pid), signal.SIGKILL)
            print(f"{now()} compiled-cache rows {rows0} -> {n}; sent SIGKILL to process group", flush=True)
            break
    time.sleep(0.005)
rc = p.wait()
print(f"{now()} exit returncode={rc}", flush=True)
print("--- compile output ---"); print(p.stdout.read().decode(errors="replace"), end="")
```

</details>

<summary>Repro records, steps 2 and 3 (every command with its whole output; the record's comment lines are omitted, the vault path is shortened to <vault> and the home directory to ~)</summary>

Row `979a1787` has `created_at` 1791676499453 (23:54:59.453Z), 7 ms before the SIGKILL at 23:54:59.460Z. The final `stat` is of the host's real state database, outside the isolated state directory; it printed the same mtime before step 1.

</details>

Path, from source: `writeMemoryWikiCompiledCache` calls `store.write`, which registers `owner:<sha256(owner)>:publication:<sha256(publicationId)>`; then `validatePublication` (a full rescan), then `commitPublication` (appends the `compiledCachePublicationId` record to `log.jsonl`), then deletes the parent publication. Every in-process exit before the candidate becomes the owner's active publication deletes it before rethrowing. Nothing deletes it when the process ends inside that window: the plugin service `memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup` calls `deleteOwnersExcept(activeOwnerIds)`, which skips every row whose owner is active, and `delete(config)` (all rows of one owner) runs only from `invalidateMemoryWikiCompiledCache`, which only vault initialization calls.

### Expected behavior

The owner deletes a candidate that can no longer become the durable publication, instead of leaving it to the namespace cap. The owner's own code is the reference: `writeMemoryWikiCompiledCache` deletes the candidate on every in-process exit before it becomes the owner's active publication (`compiled-cache.ts` 547, 551, 559, 570 / 614, 618, 626, 637), and `compile.ts` 1121-1122 / 1276-1277 states the contract: "Persist an immutable candidate, then commit its causal publication. A stale compiler cannot overwrite the accepted row or activate before validation." A process that exits inside that window should not change the outcome.

### Actual behavior

The candidate stays until `evict-oldest` removes it. The store is opened with `maxEntries: 256`, `maxBytesPerNamespace: 512 MiB`, `overflowPolicy: "evict-oldest"` (`compiled-cache.ts` 13-15 and 305-311 / 13-15 and 387-393). After every upsert `writeBlob` calls `deleteOldestUntilWithinLimits` (`plugin-blob-store.sqlite.ts` 417-419 / 493-495), which deletes this namespace's live rows by `created_at` ascending, excluding only the key being written, and stops as soon as the namespace is within its limits (309-363 and 174-191 / 385-439 and 231-248). On this host memory-wiki has only this namespace (`group by plugin_id, namespace` over `plugin_blob_entries` returns one row), so the per-plugin 512 MiB cap (28-30) adds nothing here.

Eviction is not aware of the active publication, but it reaches it only under a precondition. A successful commit deletes its parent (`compiled-cache.ts` 580-582 / 647-649), so while publication A is active, every row older than A is a leftover and every row newer than A is a candidate written after A's commit (leftover or in flight). Oldest-first eviction removes all older leftovers first; A goes only when the rows written since its commit fill the cap on their own:

One convention throughout: N is the largest number of newer rows that fit alongside A, so the (N+1)th newer write evicts A. `withinLimits` compares with `<=` (`plugin-blob-store.sqlite.ts` 315-319), so by count N = 256 - 1, and by bytes N = floor(536,870,912 / row size) - 1, which is approximate because row sizes vary.

| row size | N, rows written after A before the next write evicts A |
|---|---:|
| 2,404,868 B (this vault) | about 222 (floor(536,870,912 / 2,404,868) - 1 = floor(223.2) - 1) |
| near `COMPILED_CACHE_MAX_BYTES_PER_ENTRY`, 100 MiB (`compiled-cache.ts` 14) | about 4 (floor(536,870,912 / 104,857,600) - 1 = floor(5.1) - 1) |
| any size, by row count | 255 (256 - 1) |

Even then, harm needs the evicting compile itself not to commit; if it commits, it deletes A as its parent anyway. When A is gone and nothing replaced it, adoption fails and the next sync step recompiles the vault with reason `missing-compiled-cache` (`compile.ts` 1249-1272 / 1404-1430). On this host A (`b9898fd5`) is the newest of 27 rows, so at the cap the 26 older rows go first.

The process killed before it reached the candidate write left no row. The 11:08:14 row is the second in-process compile cycle of its command: reservation `0daeabc3` follows the first cycle's commit `345ff303` (11:07:00.551) by 0.6 s.

The 2026-10-06 20:13:01.651 row (`c3e410e9`) is attributed to the Gateway process; its commit status is unknown because it sits in the log gap. The dashboard session's earlier CLI `openclaw wiki search` calls returned at 20:03:49Z, and its in-Gateway `wiki_search` tool call was active from 20:04:37Z. A separate operator recovery session found the Gateway process at 138% CPU and 5,362,640 KiB RSS (after memory-pressure warnings at 20:05:19Z and 20:10:20Z, 5.64 GiB at the second) and stopped it with SIGKILL (`kill -9 81833`) after a 3 s `sample` started at 20:14:27Z. The in-Gateway `wiki_search` call returned `ECONNRESET` at 20:14:30.665Z, 89 s after the row. The attribution rests on that kill and that reset. Supporting context only: `gateway.log` has no shutdown or signal record before the next start at 20:14:39Z, while the same day's clean stop at 19:36:31Z logged its whole sequence from `signal SIGTERM received` to `[shutdown] completed cleanly`; the later start at 20:55:39Z, outside the row's window, also has no stop record before it (Logs), so a missing stop record alone does not identify a SIGKILL.

Negative control: the known abort path cleans up. "Memory Wiki vault changed while its compiled cache was being built." is thrown only inside `validatePublication` (`compile.ts` 1132-1135 / 1287-1295), after the candidate write, and `compiled-cache.ts` 544-549 / 611-616 deletes the candidate and rethrows. On 2026-10-10, reservation `355cb060` (22:41:18.489Z, a CLI `openclaw wiki search` that ran 122.45 s) was superseded by reservation `11dea28c` (22:42:26.384Z), failed with that message (Logs), and left no row.

|---|---|---|---|
