</details>

### Impact and severity

Affected: memory-wiki users whose compile processes can end between candidate write and commit. Observed causes: CLI `wiki compile`, `wiki lint` and `wiki status` ended by an exec timeout (SIGTERM); attributed: a Gateway process stopped with SIGKILL during an in-Gateway compile.
Severity: dead rows build up in the shared state database, bounded by the namespace cap of 256 rows or 512 MiB, so up to 512 MiB of dead snapshots can sit in `openclaw.sqlite`. Conditional: oldest-first eviction removes the active publication only after rows written since its last commit fill the cap on their own (about 222 rows of this vault's size, about 4 near the 100 MiB per-row limit, 255 by count) and the compile whose write evicts it does not commit; the next sync step then recompiles the whole vault.
Frequency: 23 attributable rows on 13 of the 19 September nights on which the log shows a nightly compile, while the nightly ran under exec timeouts; none from that job since 2026-09-27. Each row is a full compiled snapshot (1,180,874 to 2,404,868 B here, growing with the vault).
Consequence here: 34,821,095 B in attributable rows, and 41,515,058 B in the 26 non-active rows; `plugin_blob_entries` is 43,999,232 of 191,750,144 `dbstat` bytes. A full compile cycle of this vault took 178.0 to 334.9 s on 2026-10-10 (companion report #168784, every compile publishes even when unchanged), which is what a recompile after losing the active row would cost.

### Additional information

Possible fix, at the producer: at the existing parent-delete step (`compiled-cache.ts` 580-582 / 647-649), delete every row of the same owner whose `created_at` is earlier than a timestamp taken just before `commitPublication`, except the publication that just committed. That subsumes today's parent delete. No in-flight window is needed:
- The log adopts a commit only when its reservation is the latest reservation and its parent is the current publication (`log.ts` 75-83 / 85-93). So once the commit is confirmed (main 565-569 / 632-636), every compile that reserved before it has been superseded, and its validate-time checks fail it (`compile.ts` 1132-1135 and 1149-1152 / 1287-1295 and 1309-1317).
- A compile that reserves after the commit writes its row after its reservation, so after the cutoff. A compile that loaded the identity before the commit but reserves after it fails the pre-scan check (`compile.ts` 1056-1059 / 1199-1206) and writes no row.
- Deleting a superseded compile's row while that compile still runs is harmless: it fails validation and its own `deletePublication` finds nothing.
- The cost is one `entries()` listing per successful commit; `entries()` lists metadata, including `createdAt`, without loading BLOBs (`docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/state-and-system.md` 196 / 182; `PluginBlobEntryInfo` in `plugin-blob-store.types.ts`).
- Accepted edge case: `created_at` comes from `Date.now()` in the writing process (`plugin-blob-store.sqlite.ts` 407 / 483), so the rule assumes one host clock across the CLI and the Gateway.
- The first successful commit after the change also collects rows left by earlier versions, without a migration.

This composes with the keep-active fix proposed in companion report #168784 (a compile with no file updates and the same source generation still publishes and deletes the active row). If an unchanged compile stops committing, commits become rarer and a sweep that runs only after a commit runs rarely. The same sweep fits that keep-active return: before the early return, delete the owner's rows created before a timestamp taken just before the compile's reservation append, except the parent publication, which stays active. That return path writes no candidate and runs no `validatePublication`, and the sweep is safe regardless: every row created before the cutoff belongs to a compile that reserved earlier, and this compile's reservation alone prevents any of those from being adopted (`log.ts` 75-83 / 85-93), while any compile that commits later writes its row after the cutoff.

A sweep in `memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup` is not proposed: #155908 reports that service already missing its 4,999 ms lifecycle deadline. "Skip rows whose reservation is still held" would need a reservation id in row metadata (`CompiledCacheMetadata`, `compiled-cache.ts` 123-131 / 190-198), which is a stored-format change. A SIGTERM handler in the CLI would not cover SIGKILL, crashes or OOM.

Root `AGENTS.md` says: "Outside writers, including CLI, Doctor, cron, and plugin children, must use the Gateway or hold exclusive ownership while it is stopped." `openclaw wiki compile` runs `compileMemoryWikiVault` in the CLI process (`cli.ts` 551-562 / 569-584). Routing it through the Gateway would not close this gap: the Gateway's own sync step calls `compileMemoryWikiVault` (`compile.ts` 1262-1265 / 1420-1423), which writes through the same `writeMemoryWikiCompiledCache`, so a Gateway SIGKILL, crash or OOM inside the window leaves the same row (the 2026-10-06 row is attributed to that case). memory-wiki also already expects cross-process compilers (`compiled-cache.ts` 418-419 / 490-491: "A cross-process write that races this boundary stays unreadable until the next lifecycle refresh").

Companion report: #168783 (`openclaw wiki compile` compiles twice when its sync step compiles; `wiki lint` double-compiles only when its sync step compiles). The second cycle doubles the command's wall time, and with it the window an external kill can hit: the 2026-09-07 11:08:14 row came from such a second cycle.

Version detail: the 23 attributable rows were written on 2026.8.1 (build ea806575e645) through 2026.9.6, the other 3 on 2026.9.7 and 2026.9.8 (Control UI build lines and "Installation replaced" records). The register, delete and evict paths behave the same on every one of those releases, on v2026.9.9 and on origin/main (table under Screenshots, recordings, and evidence).

The docs (`docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md` 243 / 239: "Compiled caches are rebuildable: cache rows from before publication epochs are treated as misses and replaced by the next compile") cover rows from older formats. Candidate rows of the current version are neither read nor replaced.

Code (origin/main 4d77effe1e2a / v2026.9.9 bcfc88812a35):

- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/compiled-cache.ts`: limits 13-15 / 13-15; store opened with `evict-oldest` 305-311 / 387-393; `CompiledCacheMetadata` 123-131 / 190-198; key 166-172 / 248-254; candidate `store.register` 383 / 459; `writeMemoryWikiCompiledCache` 527 / 599; candidate deletes before it becomes active: validation failure 547 / 614, owner retired 551 / 618, commit failure 559 / 626 (skipped when the reloaded identity shows the commit, 557-560 / 624-627), durable identity mismatch 570 / 637; post-commit deletes of a publication whose owner retired 577 / 644 and 584 / 651; post-commit row retained on reload failure 563-565 / 630-632; parent publication deleted 580-582 / 647-649; `delete(config)` 428 / 500, called only by `invalidateMemoryWikiCompiledCache` 512 / 584 from `vault.ts` 121 / 128; `deleteOwnersExcept` skips active owners 443-454 / 515-526.
- `src/plugin-state/plugin-blob-store.sqlite.ts`: per-plugin caps 28-30; `selectEvictionCandidates` 174-191 / 231-248; `deleteOldestUntilWithinLimits` 309-363 / 385-439; `writeBlob` evicts after upsert 417-419 / 493-495.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/index.ts`: service `memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup` 117 / 117, calls `deleteOwnersExcept(activeOwnerIds)` 159 / 159.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.ts`: reservation append 1038-1046 / 1190-1198; pre-scan check 1056-1059 / 1199-1206; publication id 1092 / 1240; candidate comment 1121-1122 / 1276-1277; validate-time checks 1132-1135 and 1149-1152 / 1287-1295 and 1309-1317; commit record append 1160 / 1325; sync-step adoption (main only, 1250-1256) and `missing-compiled-cache` recompile 1262-1272 / 1420-1430.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/log.ts`: commit adoption rule 75-83 / 85-93.

prs.title: fix: explain state lease renewal failures before expiry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace operations can lose a state lease with no indication whether renewal failed or remained pending.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish an unsettled renewal, a rejected renewal, and no renewal since the last successful commit. Lease durations, retry policy, and ownership checks stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing parent timer records attempts, emits one warning for the first non-loss failure, and includes the accumulated failure count at timer close or expiry. Expiry errors carry the same cause-specific diagnostics as the warning. Logs contain scope/key, attempt numbers, timing, and error classification; they omit error prose, stacks, and database paths.

The simplification pass reused the existing timer and shared expiry publication, consolidated repeated timer cleanup, and added no new policy or state owner. Production code grows by 44 net lines. The existing lifetime suite grows by 78 lines for five table-driven cases: native and wrapped broker failures, pending renewal, idle expiry, and release. It previously did not exercise this timer; deleting unrelated contracts to offset that growth would weaken coverage. The separate 78-line allocation leaves the shared test budget unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged production source at `db41a6a3a2e44726c08e2ba64442c27f2fd45ae1`: all five final cases fail. Rejected renewals make zero warning calls; pending and idle expiry return only `state lease expired`. The test-only patch and complete log are retained by the reliability loop. Baseline: 32.77 seconds including worker preparation, 35.68 seconds through the wrapper.
- Focused lifetime and async timer files: 28/28 tests pass in 32.67 seconds (34.81 seconds through the wrapper); test bodies take less than one second, with worker compilation accounting for almost all wall time.
- Touched-file TypeScript, source/test lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass. The first lint attempt selected unrelated declaration preparation and timed out; rerunning with the supported core/test configurations passed. No dependencies were reinstalled. Review findings about omitted broker codes were fixed, including broker errors wrapping native SQLite errors; the refreshed full review is clean.
- Independent Codex-backed autoreview through P2 on the complete final staged and working-tree diff against `db41a6a3a2e44726c08e2ba64442c27f2fd45ae1`: scoped-clean, no findings (final diagnostics and cleanup simplification reviewed). Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the automatic hosted review has acknowledged and queued this exact PR, so no duplicate request was posted.
- PR CI will attach to the corrected head and supply broad proof. No production Gateway/state or lease timing was changed; no live production fault was injected. These diagnostics identify an unsettled operation, not the precise blocked actor phase.

prs.title: fix(qa-lab): run the e2e self-check against an isolated state dir
prs.body:
Fixes #190865

## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm qa:e2e` (the QA self-check) was not hermetic: the in-process qa-channel gateway loop resolved the session store from the operator's default state directory, so on a machine with an older installed OpenClaw the self-check aborted with `SqliteSchemaMismatchError` pointing at the real agent database instead of checking the source tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runQaE2eSelfCheck()` started the lab server directly, and nothing in that path redirected `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, so state resolution fell through to the default `~/.openclaw`. The runner now wraps the whole self-check in an isolated, freshly created temp state dir and restores the previous environment afterwards (removing the temp dir), so the gateway loop it starts can only see its own state.

Scope is deliberately small: only the self-check entry is wrapped. Lane runs that take an explicit state dir keep their current behaviour.

## User Impact

`pnpm qa:e2e` works on a dev machine that also has OpenClaw installed, without touching the operator's real state, and leaves no state behind after the run.

## Evidence

Head `d24b5f6ad1`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/qa-lab/src/self-check-runner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
2 passed

# with the runner reverted:
× runs against an isolated state dir and restores the operator's
× restores an operator state dir that was already configured
  expected '/operator/state' not to be '/operator/state'

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <2 touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <2 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The two cases pin both directions: a bare environment gets a temp state dir that is removed and unset afterwards, and an operator-configured `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` is replaced only for the run and restored verbatim.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Traced the schema failure to the self-check path never redirecting the state dir, wrapped that entry point, and pinned the isolation/restore contract with red/green cases. The implementer understands the code: the self-check must read only the source tree plus its own temp state, and the operator's state must be untouched.

prs.title: fix: await Doctor process and restart lease inspection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor service inspection and repair can enter synchronous lease/snapshot readers while resolving Gateway processes and restart intent.

Related: #178359, #187900, #185879. This is a dependent follow-up to #190788. Its temporary base is `roboclaw/doctor-awaited-readers`; it will target main after the preceding stage lands.

## User Impact

Use the existing async lease and dispatch hooks. Preserve synchronous final authority checks and PID incarnation checks before signals, and retain the runtime supervisor’s synchronous contract. Share the stale-process decision kernel across both drivers.

prs.body:
Replaces closed experiment #190840; GitHub refused to reopen it after the branch was rebased.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of an archived chat deep link reveals the complete cached transcript before its position rail has final overflow and visible-marker highlights. The rail then fades for 240 ms and changes highlight after appearing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript reveal owner already measures mounted rows before revealing the accepted initial range. Measure only mounted bubbles in that same read pass, then publish overflow and visible/active markers through the existing rail controller before reveal. Native IntersectionObserver owns later updates. Only the existing cached-session restore lifetime disables the entrance fade; live send/resize keeps it.

The startup-resize anchoring comment and active-ID-change layout scheduling are retained. Root client bounds use named locals. Native browser tests confirm zero-area bubbles, positive-area edge touches and horizontal clipping match the observer, and assert no visible-marker toggles between seed and a subsequent real observer delivery. The synchronous syncLayout after observeLayout is needed because observeLayout otherwise queues publication for another frame.

## User Impact

Warm reload shows final navigation alongside cached rows. No schema, protocol, configuration or snapshot field changes.

## Evidence

Draft pending final-head quiet-host proof, A/A, full UI e2e, and broad CI. The prior measured candidate improved first-frame rail correctness from 0/11 to 11/11 at a median/max 0.1 ms mounted-bubble read and zero Layout events in its read/commit windows. Those are prior-head results, not final-head proof.

Maintainer granted a size exception for this visible every-reload artifact. Compression target was 40 runtime LOC; the clarified candidate is +47, retaining explicit read/commit ordering and existing live resize behavior. Exact +216 test-line allocation covers native ordering and real observer edge parity; unit IO stubs cannot protect these boundaries.

Focused native warm e2e: 2/2 pass, 15.88 s wall; warm regression fails current main, 12.90 s wall. Native edge test: 1/1 pass, 2.37 s runner; fails the earlier candidate. Rail units: 18/18 pass, 4.72 s runner. Independent autoreview is clean through P2. Final proof tables and inspected synthetic strips will replace this pending section before readiness. No private captures used. Do not merge; lead owns landing.

prs.title: fix(database): preserve recovery images during offline ports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes offline database ports that run migration SQL against durable network recovery images, reject legally absent first-use agent tables, or reject a recognized historical pending-input recovery column.

## User Impact

Ports keep verified originals and the durable recovery journal intact while migration and source materialization use private local scratch. Resume reconstructs scratch from the recorded migrated image. Failed scratch is retained; only successfully joined work is removed. Set the existing XDG_CACHE_HOME environment variable to local storage when the default cache is network-backed or unclassifiable.

Only the owned agent copy receives missing declared tables or retires recognized recovery envelopes. Original bytes retain the envelopes, and v24 input interruption runs before retirement. Unknown schema shapes still refuse the operation. No schema versions, permissions, state resource/disk contracts, or retention policies change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing port owner now scopes migration/checkpoint/stage to one local image and uses the existing verified file publisher for both copies. The descriptor consumes the existing schema compatibility declarations rather than adding fork schema or runtime compatibility infrastructure. Adapted from Galin Iliev's database portability work.

## Evidence

- Core typecheck, formatting, and git diff --check passed. Documentation link audit: 16,224 internal links checked, zero broken.
- 28 native worker/descriptor tests passed, including legal first-use omission, v24/current recovery-envelope retirement, unknown-schema refusal, and legacy migration siblings. Public resume/failed-scratch/local-cache refusal regression passed (0.499s test time); the two infra files took approximately 61s test time under severe host I/O contention. Combined four-file run including independent batching: 584.36s wall time, mostly cold compiler preparation. CI seconds unavailable.
- Focused ten-file lint and core/infra/Doctor/config regression typechecks passed.
- Independent canonical autoreview, P0–P2, complete local delta from b612f55ebf698a6cc87eec12526fc50ae798d539 plus five unchanged ownership modules: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Reviewer did not execute code.
- Red/green owner proof now qualified for missing-table completion and retired recovery columns: exact baseline4221 source blobs loaded process-locally into the real executeDatabasePortTask migration owner fail with “Unknown or missing columns” for session_goal_operations/session_pending_inputs. Identical synthetic SQLite fixtures pass with the fix. This narrow Node proof avoids rebuilding unrelated workers; baseline source blob hashes were verified. Public-command local-copy regression also fails on baseline4221 during private migration because the old path opens SQLite in the durable recovery directory; identical resume/custody fixture passes with the fix (134ms). The independent new nonlocal-cache refusal control was omitted from both comparison runs to isolate this original defect; the full committed test including that control already passed.
- Real PostgreSQL 17.11, task-owned isolated container: 3 selected public-command integration cases passed—SQLite→PostgreSQL→SQLite canonical roundtrip, resume after stage failure, and resume after preparing-journal publication failure. Verified canonical cells, 64-bit IDs/allocation facts, original captures, config restoration, and completed-manifest retirement. Assertions: 100.306s / 42.298s / 45.996s; Vitest wall 423.18s, wrapper 479.14s including cold compilation. Nine unrelated cases were intentionally filtered, not claimed as passed. Container stopped and removed; no operator DB or live Gateway touched.

### Review repair and exact architecture guards

Both hosted P2 findings are repaired without changing runtime behavior: canonical private-copy schema DDL now carries narrow local raw-SQL annotations, and both closed mocks have immediate one-line fixture-isolation reasons. No allowlist or baseline was expanded.

The exact previous head failed both architecture checks with the reported entries. The repaired candidate passes `pnpm lint:kysely` and `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914 --no-merge-base` (6,428 grandfathered factories, unchanged). Independent canonical P0–P2 review of the repair is scoped-clean.

Focused repair replay passed all 20 tests: 19 descriptor/migration cases and the public resume/local-scratch custody case (1.004s). The repository wrapper joined cleanup and exited 0 in 583.23s, dominated by cold worker preparation and host I/O. Targeted lint passed both repaired files (174.42s); formatting and whitespace checks passed. Existing production and test typecheck evidence remains applicable because this repair changes comments only.

### Latest-stable data compatibility

Latest stable was verified as **v2026.10.9**, source commit `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`. Its unmodified configuration reader, schema initializer, and session decoder produced and admitted isolated schema25 data with a retained session and queued/interrupted/cancelled inputs. The repaired public port owner then:

1. Preserved the original schema25 capture through an injected stage interruption.
2. Resumed into real **PostgreSQL17.11** with unchanged pending-input payloads/states, session identity, cache data, and authored settings.
3. Returned to **SQLite schema39**, reopened the result, and verified those same records/settings; original producer bytes stayed unchanged.

The complete compatibility rehearsal passed: **1 test, 9.045s assertions, 44.72s wrapper**, exit0 after joined cleanup. The documented `public.unaccent` prerequisite was installed only in the task-owned database; its container was stopped and removed. This is released-source-owner/public-command data compatibility proof, not a full installer or live-Gateway/model upgrade. No operator data or credentials were restored. The initial rehearsal fixtures were corrected for missing `unaccent` and the session decoder’s required `updatedAt`; those setup failures are retained in local evidence and are not product-regression claims.

Sanitized actual output:

```text
PASS interrupted port retained original schema25 capture and all3 pending input records
PASS resume published all3 retained pending inputs, session, cache data and stable settings to real PostgreSQL; producer bytes unchanged
PASS SQLite schema39 reopen retained session, pending-input states, cache data and stable settings; producer bytes unchanged
Tests  1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 44.72s
```

Simplification: removed migration-on-durable-image path and reused the existing byte publisher, schema compatibility owner, transaction owner and cleanup routine. No new schema, journal or cache. Regression growth +337 lines protects distinct schema-admission and public-resume boundaries.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

prs.title: fix(sessions): spread env for exact-entries worker reads
prs.body:
Fixes #157986 (also reported as #158788)

## Problem

On Windows, cron isolated agent turns fail at setup with `DataCloneError: #<Object> could not be cloned. | unavailable` (2026.9.6, see the issue for the full postmortem). `cloneEnvWithPlatformSemantics` returns a proxy-wrapped env on Windows; the proxy reaches the exact-entries worker input and cannot cross the structured-clone boundary at `worker.postMessage`.

## Solution

Spread env when preparing the `session-exact-entries` worker input in `session-transcript-worker-readers.ts`, matching the existing `readRowFacts` behavior two readers above. This is the one boundary every `readExactEntries` caller crosses, so the fix covers all callers regardless of which one passes a platform-semantics env.

## Impact

Windows-only defect; other platforms already submit a plain object, and the spread is a no-op for them. No behavior change beyond making the input cloneable.

## Evidence

- Production postmortem in #158788: all 9 isolated-agent cron jobs failed at setup (43–922 ms) on Windows; the failing task input was identified via field-level clone probing on the worker pool boundary, and `readExactEntries`' input shape (`kind, env, sessionKeys, lifecycleSessionKey, projection, includeMembers, includeAuthorization, continuation, database`) matched the `session-exact-entries` request exactly.
- With an equivalent boundary fix deployed, the same jobs completed normally again (e.g. a previously failing job ran 52.9 s end-to-end with model usage; a second one on a different provider chain ran 93.8 s and delivered).
- New regression test `session-transcript-worker-readers.test.ts` submits through a stubbed `runRequest` with a proxied env and asserts the prepared input survives `structuredClone`.

### After-fix run trace (production, redacted)

Before the boundary fix, the same job failed at setup in 43 ms:

```json
{
  "jobId": "b3b0aeb6-52c3-4574-8999-5f240551e9de",
  "action": "finished",
  "status": "error",
  "completionStatus": "failed",
  "error": "DataCloneError: #<Object> could not be cloned. | unavailable",
  "durationMs": 43,
  "runAtIso": "2026-09-26T16:57:18.617+08:00",
  "jobName": "<redacted: local OneNote sync job>"
}
```

After deploying an equivalent boundary fix (the deployed hot patch retries the same `worker.postMessage` input as a JSON round-trip at the pool boundary; this PR instead spreads env before submission — both act on the same env object at the same structured-clone boundary), the same job succeeded on manual trigger and then again on its natural schedule:

```json
{
  "jobId": "b3b0aeb6-52c3-4574-8999-5f240551e9de",
  "action": "finished",
  "status": "ok",
  "completionStatus": "succeeded",
  "durationMs": 25206,
  "runAtIso": "2026-09-26T17:57:18.687+08:00",
  "provider": "zai",
  "model": "glm-5.3-flash",
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 10374, "output_tokens": 180, "total_tokens": 26170, "cache_read_tokens": 15616 },
  "jobName": "<redacted: local OneNote sync job>",
  "summary": "<redacted>"
}
```

A second agentTurn job on the same instance (daily web briefing, different schedule) also completed after the fix:

```json
{
  "jobId": "0a648e82-4f2c-47ad-8a47-adc12e232b0e",
  "status": "ok",
  "completionStatus": "succeeded",
  "durationMs": 93799,
  "runAtIso": "2026-09-26T17:17:12.567+08:00",
  "provider": "zai",
  "model": "glm-5.3-flash",
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 31711, "output_tokens": 2193 },
  "jobName": "<redacted: daily web intel briefing job>",
  "summary": "<redacted: multi-section briefing generated and delivered>"
}
```

Job names, summaries, and delivery targets are redacted (local business content); all status, timing, usage, and error fields are verbatim from `openclaw cron runs <jobId>` on the affected Windows instance.

## Test cost

The new test is a single pure unit test with an injected request runner (no worker, no database, no timers). Measured locally on Windows (`pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-readers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`):

- Cold run (first transform of the shard): 41.8 s shard wall / 38.98 s vitest duration, transform dominates (95%).
- Warm rerun: 19.07 s shard wall / 16.20 s vitest duration; the test itself executes in under 1 s (worker 7%, the rest is local transform overhead that CI's warm vitest caches avoid).
- CI seconds: not yet available — this PR is from a first-time fork, so repo workflows are currently skipped pending maintainer approval.

prs.title: fix(update): let 2026.6 updaters finish plugin convergence again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since #188978 (`6fd646e86cd`), every update from the 2026.6 line to current main fails during post-core plugin convergence:

```
[openclaw] Reason: Plugin cohort convergence requires its live outer update executor.
```

2026.6.x updaters predate the update-run ledger. They start the post-core child with `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE=1` but never set `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_RUN_ID` (verified in the published 2026.6.34 `dist`). `resumePostCoreUpdate` therefore takes its run-less branch, which has no executor fence, and the guard #188978 added to `convergePostCoreUpdatePlugins` refuses.

## User Impact

Users on the 2026.6 line can update to a release containing this fix again; plugin convergence runs as it did before #188978. These parents never had plugin-cohort rollback and still don't get it (#188978 documents that older parents are not backported). Run-bearing post-core children without an executor fence still refuse.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fence requirement protects cohort recovery, which needs a run id and an outer executor. A run-less parent cannot supply either, and `withUpdatePluginCohortConfigCapture` already runs the operation directly when there is no run or fence. Exempting only that case (no `opts.run`, no run id in the environment, no `requiresCohort`) restores the shipped behavior without weakening the modern path. Rejected alternative: reverting #188978, which no longer applies cleanly because later work (#189624) builds on it.

## Evidence

- CI Update Migration, pinned to main `afbe0a8e8f2` (run 41381443817): `update-migration-2026.6.34` `legacy-operator-state` fails after 413 s with the message above. The same lane passed in scheduled run 40158661304 (2026-10-25, before #188978) and failed in scheduled run 41269014814 (2026-11-01).
- Regression test: the run-less legacy parent case in `update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts` fails on the base and passes with the fix; the run-bearing case still asserts the refusal. The file passes 18/18.
- `$autoreview` scoped-clean; independent `codex exec` review: no findings.
- Native Linux Crabbox proof (2026.6.34 → main vs → this head): see the follow-up comment.

prs.title: fix(cron): a job targeting another agent's session never runs
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #190123

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where a user on a multi-agent gateway who scheduled work into another agent's
  conversation with `openclaw cron add --session session:agent:<other>:…` and no `--agent` got a job
  that could never run. The create was admitted for one agent while the job's own session belonged
  to another, so the due run failed in milliseconds (`cron job agent is unavailable: worker`, or on
  the reporter's install `SQLite session store path belongs to agent main; requested agent worker.`)
  and the one-shot (`at`) job was then auto-disabled as a permanent error: the payload never ran and
  nothing told the creator why. On today's `main` the same command in a two-agent roster does not
  even reach that point — it is refused with `invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are
  configured, but this operation has no explicit owner.` Either way the scheduled work is silently
  lost.
- The CLI made this worse by naming the wrong owner: it printed `No --agent specified; the job will
  run with the configured default agent.` for a job whose session already named one.
- **Related:** #190123 (reporter's source trace names the create default and the owner resolver);
  #190156 (earlier attempt at this report, withdrawn by its author before merge — it changed the
  global owner-resolution precedence and left the due-run leg on `job.agentId` untouched). This PR
  takes the narrower route: name the execution agent once at `cron.add` admission, and leave global
  attribution precedence alone. Fix signal labels: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`,
  `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** one execution agent is named before any `cron.add` admission step reads it,
  so caller-scope matching, creator-session and inference capture, declaration matching, and the
  persisted row all agree on the same owner. `bindCronCreateExecutionAgent`
  (`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts`) resolves it — an explicit `agentId` wins,
  otherwise the job's own session reference decides (`sessionTarget` `session:<key>` first, the same
  precedence the run uses through `resolveCronSessionTargetSessionKey`, then the legacy scoped
  `sessionKey`) — and `cronAddHandler` applies it to the request *before* it builds anything else.
  That one resolved `jobCreate` then flows unchanged into `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope`,
  `captureCronCreatorSession`, the `matchesExisting` declaration matcher, and `context.cron.add`.
- This re-points the earlier revision of this PR, which bound the agent inside `CronService.add`.
  That happened *after* two gateway consumers had already read the unresolved input, leaving two
  real inconsistencies (both raised in review):
  - `cronAddHandler` handed `matchesExisting` the unresolved `jobCreate`, so
    `cronJobMatchesDeclarationScope` compared the configured default (`main`) against the stored
    owner (`worker`) and excluded the row it should have converged onto — repeating a declaration
    would have created a second job instead of preserving the first one's id and history;
  - `captureCronCreatorSession` ran before that binding, so it loaded the execution session and
    captured inference for the configured default agent while the job was stored for another.
  `src/cron/service/ops-mutations.ts` is therefore back to `main`: the service no longer re-resolves
  ownership, and there is exactly one binding point.
- Also removed: the previous revision's `manageAll` exception in `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope`. It
  was unreachable — `CRON_MANAGEMENT_METHODS` (`src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`) lists
  `cron.list/get/update/run/remove/bind` and excludes `cron.add`, `mintCronCreatorAuthorityGrant`
  throws for a management method outside that list, `getCronManagementAuthority` only returns inside
  a redeemed method-bound management context, and the one other caller (`cron.update`) passes a
  `creatorScope` built with `manageAll: undefined`. Its test fabricated the capability with
  `vi.fn()` instead of reaching it through admission. Creation authority is unchanged from `main`:
  an agent turn still cannot create a job that another agent would execute, and a scoped caller
  targeting a foreign session is refused exactly as before (`cronPatchSessionRefsMatchCaller` already
  refused it on `main`).
- Deliberately **not** changed: `tryResolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId`'s precedence (explicit id →
  scoped `sessionKey` → configured default), so visibility, scheduling, run receipts, and the Doctor
  heartbeat cutover keep their existing attribution semantics; already-stored jobs are never
  reinterpreted or migrated. Detached targets (`isolated` / `current` / `main`) name no agent and
  still fall back to the caller scope or configured default, and a malformed `session:` target names
  no owner instead of throwing out of a pure resolver.
- **Out of scope:** no change to run-time session resolution, delivery, the one-shot disable policy,
  the SQLite scope check, or existing stored jobs; no config surface added; no other create path
  (plugin `service-cron`, `templates-add`) is re-pointed; no refactor of the caller-scope module.
- **Highest-risk area:** `cron.add` admission — a job that used to be stored without an `agentId` now
  stores the session's agent, which is visible to declaration convergence, agent-filtered listings,
  and inference capture.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The value is written only when the input carries no `agentId` and
  its own session reference names one, and every consumer downstream reads that same value.
  Regression tests run through the real admission boundary (`handleGatewayRequest` +
  `cronHandlers["cron.add"]` + a real `CronService` on an on-disk store) and cover the persisted
  owner, repeated-declaration convergence, agent-filtered listing, both caller-scope outcomes, an
  ownerless row stored by an older build, the declaration matcher's input contract, and the CLI
  warning.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** on a gateway with per-agent session stores, `openclaw cron add --name probe
  --at <t> --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid> --message ping` (no `--agent`) warns
  `No --agent specified; the job will run with agent worker, named by its session.`, stores the job
  with `agentId: "worker"`, reports `worker` in `cron list`, and the due run really executes a turn
  in `agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid>` under `agentId=worker` instead of dying against `main`. An
  identical repeated `--declaration-key` converges onto the same job id. An agent turn still cannot
  create a job for another agent, and a job stored by an older build still loads and lists unchanged.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts`
  (`bindCronCreateExecutionAgent`, plus the reverted `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope` /
  `applyCronCreateCallerScopeDefault`), `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-add.ts` (the single binding
  point), `src/cron/agent-id.ts` (`resolveCronJobSessionRefAgentId`),
  `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts` (warning text), and the regressions in
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts` (`Gateway automation
  execution agent`), `src/gateway/server-cron.session-target.test.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts` (`create-time execution agent`), and
  `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — a real `openclaw gateway` process and the real `openclaw` CLI,
  both run from this branch's source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`, self-reported
  `OpenClaw 2026.10.9`), against an isolated state dir with per-agent SQLite session stores
  (`session.store: "<state>/sessions/{agentId}.sqlite"`), token auth, and a local
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint on `127.0.0.1` standing in for the model provider so a due turn can
  complete offline. Worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-190123`, head `c9b5ca8e25d`, base
  `origin/main` `36ddf502c84`, Node v26.12.1. The before legs restore `origin/main` copies of the
  four touched source files and re-run the identical commands against an identically configured
  gateway.
- **Distinct accounts, final effect (added in this revision):** the run above was repeated against a
  second isolated state dir whose two agents own **separate provider credentials** — `main` resolves
  `localmain/proof-model-main` (key tail `1111`), `worker` resolves `localworker/proof-model-worker`
  (key tail `2222`), both served by one local endpoint that logs the `Authorization` header it
  receives. This is the leg that shows target-derived agent selection picking the *account*, at the
  last observable effect (the provider HTTP call), rather than only in the stored row.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (canned streaming chat completion) on 127.0.0.1:18099
  node <proof-dir>/fake-openai.mjs

  # 2. real gateway from this branch's source: two agents (main, worker), per-agent SQLite stores
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof>/state OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway --port 18790

  # 3. real CLI create in the reporter's shape: no --agent, session belongs to another agent
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof>/state node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts cron add \
    --name probe --at 45s --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a --message ping \
    --no-deliver --url ws://127.0.0.1:18790 --token <redacted>

  # 4. repeated identical declaration (convergence), listing, then wait out the due time
  … cron add --name declared --declaration-key daily-probe --at 30m --session <same> --message ping \
      --no-deliver --disabled            # run twice, identical payload
  … cron list --all --json
  sleep 75 && … cron list --all --json && ls <state>/sessions/

  # before legs (identical commands, gateway restarted on main's sources):
  #   git checkout origin/main -- src/cron/agent-id.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts \
  #     src/gateway/server-methods/cron-add.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts

  # regression tests: RED on origin/main sources, GREEN on head
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/gateway/server-methods/cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-cron.session-target.test.ts
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts

  # format + lint + related suites + tsgo:core
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh <the eight changed files>
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real gateway log and CLI output from that run (token and host paths
  redacted):
  ```text
  $ openclaw cron add --name probe --at 45s --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a \
      --message ping --no-deliver                       # NOTE: no --agent
  No --agent specified; the job will run with agent worker, named by its session. Specify --agent to choose a specific agent.
  { "id": "08f3fffb-664c-4c4e-aab8-df0f99502fea", "agentId": "worker", "name": "probe",
    "sessionTarget": "session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a",
    "schedule": { "kind": "at", "at": "2026-11-01T15:56:35.608Z" }, "enabled": true, … }

  # an identical repeated declaration converges instead of duplicating
  1st: { "created": true,  "job": { "id": "e7c47cde-0e5e-493b-8f9e-acd1fb977a01",
         "declarationKey": "daily-probe", "agentId": "worker", … } }
  2nd: { "created": false, "updated": true,
         "job": { "id": "e7c47cde-0e5e-493b-8f9e-acd1fb977a01", … } }   # same id

  # gateway log: the due run really executed a turn as worker, in worker's session
  [gateway] cron: job added
  [auto-reply/reply-resolver-timing] … sessionKey=agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a agentId=worker
    … reply.resolve_default_model … reply.init_session_state … reason=before_run_prepared_reply
  [event-loop] main-thread stall: task="reply.run_agent_turn" …
  [local-provider] POST /v1/chat/completions #1 model=proof-model stream=true

  $ ls <state>/sessions/
  worker.sqlite  worker.sqlite-shm  worker.sqlite-wal        # main.sqlite was never opened
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the job created without `--agent` is stored with
  `agentId: "worker"`; the CLI names `worker` instead of promising the configured default; an
  identical repeated declaration converges onto the same job id (`created: false, updated: true`)
  rather than adding a second job; and the due run completes a real agent turn under
  `agentId=worker` in `agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid>` — it reaches the model provider, and the only
  session store created is `worker.sqlite`, so neither the store-scope guard nor the
  agent-availability guard that killed the run on `main` fires. An agent-turn caller is still
  refused a job another agent would execute (`job agentId outside caller scope`), and a job stored
  by an older build with no owner still loads, is served by `cron.get` / `cron.list`, and is not
  rewritten.
- **Evidence after fix (distinct accounts):** two jobs created with no `--agent`, one per agent's
  session, on the two-account gateway (head `c9b5ca8e25d`; token redacted):
  ```text
  $ openclaw cron add --name probe-worker --at 45s \
      --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:7c1a9f02 --message ping --no-deliver   # no --agent
  No --agent specified; the job will run with agent worker, named by its session. …
  { "id": "3b5a8a91-…", "agentId": "worker",
    "sessionTarget": "session:agent:worker:dashboard:7c1a9f02", … }

  $ openclaw cron add --name probe-main --at 45s \
      --session session:agent:main:dashboard:3d8b2c11 --message ping --no-deliver     # no --agent
  No --agent specified; the job will run with agent main, named by its session. …
  { "id": "efb39461-…", "agentId": "main",
    "sessionTarget": "session:agent:main:dashboard:3d8b2c11", … }

  # provider endpoint log — the account that actually served each dispatch
  [fake-openai] chat/completions #1 account=worker-account keyTail=2222 model=proof-model-worker stream=true
  [fake-openai] chat/completions #2 account=main-account  keyTail=1111 model=proof-model-main  stream=true

  # gateway log — each due run resolved its own agent inside its own session
  [auto-reply/reply-resolver-timing] … sessionKey=agent:worker:dashboard:7c1a9f02 agentId=worker totalMs=18600 …
  [auto-reply/reply-resolver-timing] … sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:3d8b2c11   agentId=main   totalMs=19937 …

  $ ls <state>/sessions/
  main.sqlite main.sqlite-shm main.sqlite-wal worker.sqlite worker.sqlite-shm worker.sqlite-wal
  $ openclaw cron list --all --json     # after both due times
  { "jobs": [], "total": 0 }            # both one-shots ran and were deleted (deleteAfterRun)
  $ grep -c "agent is unavailable\|autoDisabled\|SQLite session store path belongs" gateway.log
  0
  ```
  Each dispatch was paid for by the account that owns the session the job targeted: the
  worker-session job created with no `--agent` reached the provider under `worker-account` /
  `proof-model-worker`, the main-session job under `main-account` / `proof-model-main`. Selection is
  per target, not sticky — two jobs created seconds apart in the same gateway bound two different
  accounts, both runs completed, both one-shots were deleted after running, and neither the
  agent-availability guard nor the session-store scope guard fired.
- **Before evidence (distinct accounts):** the identical two creates against a gateway on
  `origin/main` sources with the *same* two-account config:
  ```text
  $ openclaw cron add --name probe-worker --at 45s \
      --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:7c1a9f02 --message ping --no-deliver
  No --agent specified; the job will run with the configured default agent. …
  { "ok": false, "error": { "message": "invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are configured,
    but this operation has no explicit owner. …" } }
  exit=1                      # leg B (main's own session) refused identically
  $ openclaw cron list --all --json → { "jobs": [], "total": 0 }
  $ ls <state>/sessions/            → (empty — no session store was ever opened)
  # provider endpoint log: zero chat/completions requests — no account was selected at all
  [fake-openai] listening on http://127.0.0.1:18098/v1
  ```
- **Before evidence:** the identical commands against a gateway on `origin/main`, same config shape,
  same state layout.
  Two-agent roster — the create never lands, so the work is lost at admission:
  ```text
  $ openclaw cron add --name probe --at 45s --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a \
      --message ping --no-deliver
  No --agent specified; the job will run with the configured default agent. Specify --agent to choose a specific agent, or set agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.
  { "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents
    are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. Select an agent explicitly; CLI callers
    can pass --agent <id>, channels can add a binding, and ambient services can set their agentId
    target." } }
  exit=1
  $ openclaw cron list --all --json → { "jobs": [], "total": 0 }
  ```
  Single-agent roster (`main` only, so a default resolves and the create is admitted) — the
  reporter's failure leg, including the auto-disable:
  ```text
  $ openclaw cron add --name probe --at 45s --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a \
      --message ping --no-deliver
  No --agent specified; the job will run with the configured default agent. …
  { "id": "3eb6aa59-d83d-49d2-adaf-2eef5436a1d3", "name": "probe",     # NOTE: no "agentId" at all
    "sessionTarget": "session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a",
    "schedule": { "kind": "at", "at": "2026-11-02T02:02:22.527Z" }, … }

  $ openclaw cron list --all --json          # after the due time
  { "id": "3eb6aa59-…", "name": "probe", "enabled": false,
    "state": { "lastRunStatus": "error", "lastDurationMs": 17,
               "lastError": "cron job agent is unavailable: worker",
               "consecutiveErrors": 1,
               "autoDisabled": { "reason": "consecutive-failures", "consecutiveErrors": 1 } },
    "effectiveAgentId": "main", "status": "disabled" }

  $ ls <state>/sessions/
  main.sqlite  main.sqlite.seal               # worker's store was never opened
  ```
  The stored owner (`effectiveAgentId: "main"`) contradicts the job's own session
  (`agent:worker:…`), the run dies in 17 ms, and the one-shot is disabled — the reported outcome.
  The new regression tests fail on those same `origin/main` sources:
  ```text
  # origin/main 4b35c8fbe0b sources, head's tests — gateway shard
  × cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts > Gateway automation execution agent >
    stores the session's agent and converges a repeated declaration onto that job
    → expected 'invalid cron.add params: Multiple age…' to be true
  × cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts > Gateway automation execution agent >
    reports the session's agent to operator listings and keeps it out of the default agent
    → expected 'invalid cron.add params: Multiple age…' to be true
  × cron-caller-scope.test.ts > create-time execution agent > names the agent that owns the
    session the due run opens                                        → bindCronCreateExecutionAgent is not a function
  × cron-caller-scope.test.ts > create-time execution agent > keeps an explicit agent and names
    no owner for a detached or malformed target                      → bindCronCreateExecutionAgent is not a function
  × cron-caller-scope.test.ts > create-time execution agent > matches a repeated declaration
    only against the bound create input                              → bindCronCreateExecutionAgent is not a function
  × cron-caller-scope.test.ts > create-time execution agent > keeps creation restricted to the
    caller's own agent                                               → bindCronCreateExecutionAgent is not a function
  × server-cron.session-target.test.ts > runs an operator-created job under the agent its
    session target names
    → cron.add was refused: invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are configured, but this
      operation has no explicit owner.
  Test Files  3 failed (3)   Tests  7 failed | 40 passed (47)

  # cli shard
  × cron-cli.test.ts > names the session's agent in the missing --agent warning
    → expected 'No --agent specified; the job will ru…' to contain 'agent worker, named by its session'
  Test Files  1 failed (1)   Tests  1 failed | 64 passed (65)

  # head (same tests, same shards): all green
  [validate] 1/4 oxfmt ✅  2/4 oxlint ✅  3/4 vitest — passed 3 Vitest shards  4/4 tsgo:core ✅
  [validate] 全部通过
  ```
- **What was not tested:** no gateway installed from npm with systemd units was used (this branch's
  source was run directly), and no real model provider was called — a local OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint returned a canned streaming completion. Two agents with separate provider credentials
  are now exercised end to end through that synthetic endpoint (account selected per target, shown
  above), but provider-side behaviour that only a live commercial provider has (profile
  availability, authorization identity, recorded-route checks, real credential validation) was not
  exercised. The agent-turn create leg and the
  declaration-matcher input contract are driven through the admission boundary in tests, not through
  a live model turn holding cron management authority, and creator-grant revocation mid-create was
  not replayed against the live gateway. Shared-store (`session.store` without `{agentId}`)
  multi-agent setups were not exercised. Jobs created before this change were verified to load,
  list, and stay unrewritten, but no long-lived store with run history was upgraded. Full CI lanes
  pending.
- **Proof tier:** L2 — real gateway process, real CLI, real cron store, real scheduler-driven due
  turn, two agents on distinct provider credentials; synthetic model provider.
- **Proof limitations:** the model provider is a local synthetic endpoint, so account *selection* is
  proven at the provider HTTP boundary but not against a live provider's credential validation. The
  agent-turn and creator-grant-revocation-before-HTTP legs are not reachable from the shipped CLI
  (they need a live model turn holding cron management authority), so they remain covered by
  admission-boundary regression tests rather than a live replay.
- **Review state:** Awaiting maintainer decision on the owner question ClawSweeper raised (infer the
  execution agent from a qualified session target vs. reject the combination). CI green on

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): prepare cached dashboard renderers [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Experiment only; do not merge. A signed-in warm reload of a dashboard deep link still cycles through loading placeholders while restoring an already-loaded board. The campaign's original evidence recorded fourteen visual states and widget paint at 11.75 seconds. Later synthetic attribution counted 60 shimmer animation identities.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 60 identities come from three consecutive board placeholders with 20 nodes apiece: the panel boundary, board surface, and board view. The per-widget discussion overlay is not involved in the reproduced workload. Module bytes are already cached, but warming an implementation import does not warm the separate readiness state in the rendered Solid lazy wrapper.

The dashboard route component loader now prepares its entry and both existing lazy wrappers together. This removes the speculative implementation-import path and keeps a single board loading surface while ticket-bound iframe content loads. Widget authorization, sandbox isolation, connection admission, and cold loading behavior retain their existing owners. No stored fields, protocol, config, dependency, or screenshot cache is added.

## User Impact

Candidate behavior: the first cached dashboard layout contains the real widget iframe, then its document fills the reserved area. This is not yet a qualified performance PR and does not establish the campaign's complete cached-page exit criterion.

## Evidence

All browser evidence uses synthetic data, an isolated real loopback Gateway, bundled Workboard plus synthetic native plugin modules, archived probe sessions, and the operator sidebar settings. No real browser, real account, Team service, or private capture was used for proof or uploaded.

Initial AWS attribution used c7a.4xlarge lease `cbx_053afc460164` (16 CPUs / 30.6 GiB; 93% idle preflight). It is released. Board snapshots contain the widget before reload; board/panel chunks are cache hits, the sandbox shell is an immutable disk hit, and widget HTML gets one fresh ticket-bound fetch. One warm sample starts its iframe before hello, so hello is not a universal admission dependency. About 61–72% of the observed placeholder interval occurs before iframe creation.

### Preliminary two-pair diagnostic — not qualification

| Dashboard metric | Pair 1 base → candidate | Pair 2 base → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sampled skeleton exposure (count × ms) | 14,232 → 7,062 | 9,950 → 6,862 |
| First sampled non-inert widget frame (ms) | 1,366.9 → 1,031.2 | 1,029.1 → 865.8 |
| Widget content-ready marker (ms) | 1,585.6 → 1,130.6 | 1,199.1 → 934.0 |
| Hello handled delta (ms) | +20.9 | −88.1 |
| FCP delta (ms) | +36.9 | +115.2 |
| First painted rows delta (ms) | +40.1 | −43.9 |
| LoAF blocking delta (ms) | +30.5 | +21.3 |

These instrumented samples identify the lever; they are not an improvement or non-regression verdict. FCP and LoAF need the full comparison and A/A control. Chat controls are mixed. Snapshot bytes are identical within each pair.

### Acceptance rule fixed before qualification

Fresh quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, repo Chromium, 80 ms network profile, eleven interleaved pairs plus A/A on both routes. Primary: viewport board skeleton count × duration and/or widget readiness, separated IQR or at least 9/11 improvements with negative median paired delta. Report hello, FCP, first/final rows, visible transcript, LoAF, CLS, snapshot bytes, and every paired delta. A secondary regresses with separated IQR or 9/11 adverse pairs and median rise > max(10 ms, 3%). Also run the Team-scale bench with its live-capped latency profile.

### Proof so far

- Existing cached-dashboard native e2e extended by four lines: candidate 2/2 pass, 30.29 s wall; baseline 1 pass / 1 fail at the intended first-frame iframe assertion, 37.86 s wall. `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/dashboard-cold-load.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Existing board-surface unit 2/2 pass; wrapper wall 3.91 s. Diagnostic headless init-probe smoke passed.
- Independent local review clean through P2, including final metrics tooling and docs.
- Runtime UI delta: +12 LOC. Growth carries the actual rendered lazy readiness into the existing component loader; no new runtime state. Four exact regression lines allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/coldload-board-widgets-warm.txt`. Diagnostic tooling is reported separately.
- Pending: final eleven-pair/A/A gates, inspected final frame strips, final-head full UI e2e, targeted changed checks, startup budget, exact-head ready-PR CI. Do not merge.

Session recovery, legacy shared-auth discovery, and physical engine inspection can synchronously prepare SQLite images while Doctor is waiting for large stores.

Await preparation through the existing read owners and migrate all internal consumers. Recheck auth adoption and cleanup inventory after awaited work; retain distinct physical-store and agent-family eligibility at their existing owners.

Doctor must leave signal handling available during snapshot preparation and clean up owned temporary output on cancellation. Existing owners retain admission, integrity, transaction, and final-effect decisions. This stage is part of the complete caller cutover; synchronous SDK/native contracts remain explicit.

Full scoped independent review and subsequent auth/adoption and eligibility reviews found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Focused formatting/syntax checks passed. Runtime owner checks and exact-head CI are pending.

Named owner/consumer tests, all state-migrations tests, agent-database-admission tests, and strict unused exports remain required before landing. Production-host restrictions put compiled worker staging, runtime tests, packaging, and broad checks on CI or configured Testbox. Native macOS/Windows large-database qualification remains unrun.

prs.title: fix(sessions): replay creation requests across Gateway restarts
prs.body:
## Problem

Process-local `sessions.create` idempotency loses the original binding when the Gateway restarts. Retrying can create another session and repeat preparation or its initial turn.

## Change

Commit the existing optional idempotency key's namespaced fingerprint and original key/session ID/lifecycle revision atomically with the session row. The existing history reader resolves receipts before label/resource preparation. Current requester, sharing, and lifecycle authority still gate replay; stored scopes only restrict it and never restore authority. Reset/deleted incarnations are refused, including same-ID resets. Renaming the original label does not break replay when another session takes that label.

The existing five-minute retry window remains. Replay does not allocate a worker, prepare a workspace, or resend the initial message. Restart replay returns `creationReplayed: true` and `runStarted: false`: no new turn was started, not a claim that the original never ran. Inspect that session for work recovery. Incognito remains memory-only; no default-agent, SQLite-only, caller-generated-ID, or purpose restriction is added.

Agent schema 39→40 uses existing SQLite/PostgreSQL migration, backup, witness, and historical-port owners. PostgreSQL 40 also adopts two deletion indexes expressly deferred by its generator; predecessor sealed catalogs retain their original layout. State 39 and resource/disk authority contracts are unchanged. No payload backfill or fork retention columns. Rollback requires the pre-upgrade backup and matching binary.

## Evidence

Candidate: `cd9a9424855f63fd4e83e5e671388ca90b737ae9`; base: `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`. Independent of the attended-permission feature. Clean cherry-pick range-diff confirms identical durable patch.

- Original public-handler regression reproduced a different generated session key after request-context loss. Final independent head passed lifecycle 15 + atomic-writer 1 tests (90.07s wrapper). Earlier 30 owner regressions and 11 historical/current port tests passed, including parameter conflict, current-scope downgrade, label reuse, same-ID reset refusal, concurrent receipt rollback, migration commit/forced rollback, and pre-40 catalog compatibility.
- **Actual two-process Gateway proof:** non-default agent, real agent runtime, deterministic local Responses endpoint, persisted first turn, changed PID on restart, original receipt after label reuse, no duplicate model call, successful subsequent turn, reset refusal. This is real process/runtime proof with fixed external model I/O—not live-provider inference. It preceded final mechanical helper relocations; final-head public-handler tests cover those relocations.

Actual runner excerpt:

```text
✓ replays a committed creation across Gateway processes without starting its task twice 31992ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 126.16s
```

- **Real PostgreSQL 17.11:** populated 39→40 migration, unchanged prior session bytes, native writer receipt close/reopen, and competing-row rollback passed. Owned disposable database stopped and removed.
- **Latest-stable source migration:** v2026.10.9/source `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` schema 25 image upgraded through the candidate's actual maintenance/migration owner to 40. Preserved all three pending states/message JSON, original session-entry bytes, cache sentinel, and settings bytes; a new atomic receipt remained readable after close/reopen. Producer image unchanged. Test 12.600s; total Vitest 313.77s / wrapper 348.56s, dominated by cold transform/host I/O.

Actual stable-proof result:

```json
{"fromAgentSchema":25,"toAgentSchema":40,"retainedPendingRows":3,"retainedSession":true,"retainedSettingsBytes":true,"retainedCache":true,"receiptAfterReopen":true,"originalSha256":"842a2c4a0fb2deb2389cb3d043557425977eef487e9cf041979e0d7a891f443f","originalUnchanged":true}
```

The stable schema image was created through released-source owners, with synthetic data seeded and validated by that fixture. This proves native migration compatibility, not a package install-over or a transcript produced by a released UI. No live credentials or operator databases were used.

Targeted types, type-aware lint, generated schema verification, docs/format/whitespace, line caps and the exact 542-line regression allocation passed. Worker ratchet remains 168→168 live main-thread calls. Fresh independent local review of the complete final candidate found no actionable P0/P1 findings.

## Qualification limits

Default thread-pool fixtures failed before receipt logic; supported fork-pool proof passed this writer and unchanged goal-receipt siblings without bypassing admission. Initial process proof had zero provider requests because the host proxy intercepted its loopback fixture; a fixture-local loopback exclusion corrected it. A combined hook test run passed four assertions but stalled cleanup; a separate handler rerun hit host-I/O timeout. Both failures remain recorded; subsequent final-head handler proof passed and is not claimed to fix those host/cleanup issues.

Production growth (763 added/164 removed lines excluding generated files/docs/tests) is necessary for atomic state, replay authority, versioned migration and historical compatibility. No parallel runtime or allocation manager. The process test exceeds 30s because process death/restart cannot be proved by a helper. CI time and hosted review remain separate gates; no merge is authorized by this proof.

## Credits

Requested and co-authored by Galin Iliev (@galiniliev).

Remaining session/legacy-auth sources and transaction-bound repair preservation are being completed in separate follow-up PRs within the same task. Cancellation can reach the owned snapshot child. Required copies check the database, WAL, and rollback-journal sizes against available cache space and report a clear refusal when capacity is insufficient.

New macOS/Windows leases use the existing platform boot identity reader. Same-boot dead owners can take the existing quick recovery gate; legacy, unavailable, or mismatched provenance still requires full verification. Existing leases are not backfilled. **Not yet released.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Async preparation belongs to the existing snapshot owner, and original-path readers retain their admission/quarantine checks. Reports share one read-owned image; mutable plugin images remain exclusive. Internal callers and their tests move together. Released synchronous SDK APIs and synchronous transaction/final-effect authority checks retain their contracts.

Artifact-preserving inspection still needs private images: native read-only SQLite can alter WAL/SHM coordination files, and some checks require writable private state. Capacity reservation is conservative even where copy-on-write could succeed; unknown capacity remains best effort. No schema or configuration migration is introduced by this PR. The candidate Doctor/worker must contain these fixes; an older installed updater cannot gain them from the candidate alone.

The integrated-main pass found one generated-preload newline defect; it is fixed, and the cooked script passed `node --check`. Earlier full-product and fixture passes were scoped-clean. Focused touched-file formatting/syntax lint and diff checks passed. The 569-line test allocation covers the distinct new regressions and required async consumer changes.

Updated those fixtures while retaining dispatch-refusal checks; advancing main alone did not trigger this integration.

- Core e44 PR CI [passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41387026569). All three strict unused-export scans passed in [job125090473831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41387047874/job/125090473831), and all178 required e44 owner files have observed passing execution, including state-migrations and agent-database-admission. Workflow successor tests rebuild the same signed Git fixture for 18 ordinary cases.

## User Impact

Captured JavaScript state stays read-only and cases remain serial. This removes 17 repeated ordinary-fixture constructions without a new cache/helper or production change.

prs.title: fix(worker-environments): isolate a corrupt profile snapshot from the environment list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
listRows decoded every worker-environment profile snapshot with an unguarded JSON.parse. A stored "null", "{}", or truncated snapshot threw inside the row map, so one bad environment made the whole list unreadable. null and {} also passed the shape check and later crashed on profileSnapshot.project or handed undefined settings to requireWorkerProfile.

## User Impact
Gateway placement and environment reads keep returning the healthy environments when one stored snapshot is corrupt. A direct read of the bad environment fails with an error that names it.

## Why
Snapshots are written as { install, settings } before a project exists, so the decoder requires a JSON object with a settings object. It does not require project or executionMode, which are added later. List reads skip the bad row and warn. A lookup of that one id still throws.

## Evidence
src/gateway/worker-environments/store-row-codec.test.ts covers null, {}, truncated JSON, a snapshot stored before project preparation, and a list that keeps the healthy row.

Closes #180197

prs.title: fix(cron): carry the failure-alert delivery outcome in repair briefs
prs.body:
Related: #186990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a channel-less gateway, a failing automation's operator alert cannot be delivered — the delivery failure (`Channel is required (no configured channels detected)`) is recorded only in job state fields, while the repair brief injected into the owner conversation says just `No failure alert was sent.` The operator's only visible signal omits the reason, and nothing points at the state that explains it.

## User Impact

User impact: the repair brief now carries the last failure-alert delivery outcome from job state — the recorded status and reason when a delivery failed (for the reporter's case: `not-delivered: Channel is required (no configured channels detected).`), the fact of delivery when it succeeded, and the original bare sentence when no attempt was recorded. The recurring variant keeps its consecutiveErrors counter, so each brief states both how many runs failed and why the operator alert is missing. This is the report's Expected second branch ("the repair brief carries the delivery-failure fact itself").

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildCronFailureRepairBrief` hard-coded `No failure alert was sent.` in both variants with no access to the delivery trace that `failureNotificationDeliveryFromJobState` already resolves from job state. The brief is the operator's only visible signal on a channel-less gateway, so the delivery-failure fact belongs in it. Because the streak's brief is emitted before its alert is attempted, the existing in-app fallback notice (the other operator surface) also carries the settled outcome when the delivery settles as not-delivered — rendered through the same bounded untrusted-data boundary.

## Evidence

- New `src/cron/service/failure-repair-brief.test.ts`: the bare sentence is preserved when no delivery attempt exists; an embedded transport error stays escaped inside its untrusted data block; a delivered alert is stated instead of the negative claim; the terminal one-shot variant includes the delivery state alongside the disabled notice.
- Service-level regression carries the prior settled outcome into the streak's repair brief; the fallback regression proves the settled reason reaches the in-app fallback notice and **fails on the pre-fix revision** (`9f4c836c69e`) and passes on head.
- Consumer suites `failure-alerts.outcome/persistence/account-routing` + brief suite: 37/37 green on head `c26ca18d10b`.
- **Real behavior proof — live channel-less Gateway** (revision 7): a real `openclaw gateway` at head `c26ca18d10b`, started on an isolated state dir with no `channels` config (`OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`), ran real automations through the shipped cron scheduler, transport, and session-event queue (nothing stubbed). The shipped transport settled a failure alert as `not-delivered` with `Channel is required (no configured channels detected)…`, and the next incident's **repair brief reached the owner conversation carrying that settled outcome and reason** — as did the in-app fallback notice on a scheduled failure. Outputs are the Gateway CLI's job state, run history, and the agent's `transcript_events` table: [revision 7 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188022#issuecomment-6541887935).

## Risk and Compatibility

- Error-string composition only; no delivery, scheduling, or incident-state change. The deduplication semantics are unchanged: the existing `!repair` push condition keeps one counted brief per incident (`consecutiveErrors` in the text is the counter the report asks for), so this change cannot increase brief frequency.
- The report's Expected offers "either" a doctor/status-line item **or** this brief wording; either branch satisfies it, and this PR takes the brief wording. The doctor/status-line branch is carried separately by #188946 / #189881 against `src/commands/doctor/cron/*` and `docs/cli/doctor/checks.md` — files this PR does not touch, so the two land independently.
- **Route selection is not in scope, and #189947 stays open.** #189947 (P1, `impact: security`) reports that failure alerts for `delivery: { mode: "announce", target: "owner" }` automations resolve the session's last route instead of the owner DM. This PR only composes the outcome of *whichever* route was chosen into the operator text — `failure-alerts.ts` passes the prior settled delivery through, `notification-dispatch.ts` appends the rendered note to the existing fallback text, `timer-outcomes.ts` captures it before the per-cycle reset. No target, channel, or recipient resolution changes, so this PR is not the resolution of that report; the report stays open until the route-selection work lands.
- **Different surface from #190598** (landed on main as `266002c36`, "let scheduled jobs read their own delivery receipts"): that work decides whether a scheduled job may *pull* its own run receipts and message IDs through the cron tool (`src/cron/delivery.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/*`, `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-runs.ts`). This PR writes the settled outcome into text the operator sees without asking (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts`, `notification-dispatch.ts`, `timer-outcomes.ts`, `failure-repair-brief.ts`). None of the seven files here were touched by it — main-side commits against this PR's seven paths since `c26ca18d10b` number 0 — so the two are additive, and a pull-based receipt reader leaves the un-asked-for signal in this PR still needed.
- **Merge order with #189953** (the owner-target route-selection work for that report): both PRs now carry `proof: sufficient` / `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look` — #189953 moved there at 2026-11-02T04:01Z and its two `merge-risk` labels were dropped in the same pass — so there is no proof-based tiebreaker left and either order is defensible on priority (P1 there, P2 here). The overlap is smaller than the shared file list suggests: `failure-alerts.ts` does **not** collide (its hunks sit at old lines 169-216 and 368-373, this PR's at 392, 497, 541 and 577), and the only textual collision is the single fallback call in `transportFailureAlert` — this PR replaces `params.payload.text ?? ""` with the joined note (old lines 236-245) while #189953 appends a `{ privateFallback }` argument to the same `enqueueCronNotification(...)` call (old lines 242-247). Combining them is mechanical: joined note **and** the `{ privateFallback }` argument. Whichever PR lands second owns that one-hunk rebase; if #189953 lands first, this branch will take it and re-run the five gate suites (`service.failure-repair`, `failure-repair-brief`, `failure-alerts.outcome`, `failure-alerts.account-routing`, `failure-alerts.persistence`) before pushing.

## LOC

production +71/−4 in 4 files; tests +176/−2 in 3 files. No docs or generated code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes onboarding and config writes failing on Windows when a state-directory path has different casing from its native resolved path.

## User Impact

Windows users can save configuration through case-insensitive directory aliases, including included config files. Existing symlink and target-replacement checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config publication mixed JavaScript and native resolved path spelling. Windows can return different casing for the same directory, so safe writes were rejected as a changed target. ## Evidence

prs.title: fix(plugins): authenticate native MCP servers with environment-backed headers
prs.body:
Closes #184192
Related: #160244

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes PostHog and other enabled native MCP plugins sending literal environment placeholders as authentication headers, resulting in failed tool discovery.

## User Impact
Native plugin header credentials resolve from the Gateway environment using the existing config grammar. Missing or empty required variables skip the affected server with a generic diagnostic; healthy siblings remain available. Enable only plugins whose declared endpoints you trust.

## Why This Change Was Made
Resolve at the native-manifest boundary, not the shared HTTP transport: already-resolved operator config must not be interpolated twice. Reuse the config parser for escaping and defaults; leave URLs, process fields, third-party bundle formats, and operator override precedence unchanged. Manifest metadata is not mutated.

The open stacked PR #160244 already identifies this fix direction. This is a small standalone fix against current main for the independently observed released PostHog failure, with fresh regression proof. It does not replace or close that work. No inspection-only option is added because current callers do not require it.

Simplification: no new parser, state, cache, public option, or per-provider code. Necessary growth is 44 production additions/1 deletion, 91 test additions/2 deletions, and two documentation lines.

## Evidence
- Base: `b17d07fc01e0ce6efdc569d890140f1a11488239`. Two added regressions fail on unmodified production source (literal headers; missing servers retained), while nine existing tests pass.
- `corepack pnpm test src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **11 passed**. Fixed run: 26.38s wall time, 23.48s runner duration; individual new tests 2ms each. Cold compilation dominates.
- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-config.cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **14 passed**, 10.13s wall time.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json src/plugins/bundle-mcp.ts src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts`: passed, no problems in two files.
- Targeted oxfmt check, plugin-extension import boundary, one-file docs MDX check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent isolated autoreview at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Regression coverage includes expansion, escaping, fallback, unsupported syntax, one-pass substitution, unchanged URL/manifest, undefined/empty variables, sibling retention, ownership metadata, and credential-free diagnostics.

Limits: these are production-loader boundary and consumer tests, not a live PostHog test of the patched package or a full Gateway end-to-end run. Original reported live evidence is 401 through the released plugin versus 200 with direct credential initialization. No real credentials were used in the checkout. Hosted CI timing/results are pending. A first consumer command named a nonexistent auth-status test and ran no tests; the corrected existing suites above passed. The contribution guide names a retired source-boundary script; the current plugin-boundary checker passed instead.
