prs.title: fix(cron): owner-targeted automation failure alerts go to the last chat, not the owner
prs.body:
Closes #189947

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: failure alerts for automations with `delivery.target: "owner"`, such as heartbeats migrated by Doctor, go to the job session's last conversation or the channel's default recipient instead of the owner DM, or fail with `Delivering to Telegram requires target <chatId>` when neither exists.

## User Impact

User impact: for owner-targeted automations without an alert-specific route, failure alerts, including the auto-disable alert when it is sent on that route, now go to the same owner DM as the automation's own delivery.

- **No identifiable owner, or DMs blocked.** When no owner can be identified (for example DMs open with `allowFrom: ["*"]` and no `commands.ownerAllowFrom`), or `delivery.directPolicy: "block"` is set, the alert is now recorded as Not delivered and the existing in-app fallback notification is queued; the automation's own delivery does not send in these cases either. Previously such an alert could go directly to the job session's last conversation, such as another DM sender, or, when the session had no last conversation, to the channel's `defaultTo` recipient. To keep receiving these alerts directly, set `commands.ownerAllowFrom` (for an unidentified owner), or configure an explicit failure-alert recipient (`failureAlert.to`, `delivery.failureDestination.to`, or `cron.failureAlert.to`).
- **In-app fallback.** When an alert on an owner-targeted route, or on a route with `directPolicy: "block"`, is recorded as Not delivered, its in-app fallback now stays in the session: the fallback turn runs in the job's delivery session (the agent's main session for an isolated job without a session key) and is recorded there, but its reply is not delivered automatically, and the turn has no current external conversation for implicit sends. Before, the fallback turn's reply could be delivered to the session's last conversation.
- **Alert-specific settings.** A `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` in the job's `failureAlert`, in `delivery.failureDestination`, or in global `cron.failureAlert` keeps its configured routing and does not inherit owner targeting.
- **Jobs that are not owner-targeted.** An alert that inherits the job's primary route now also honors its `delivery.directPolicy: "block"`: when the session's last conversation is a DM, the alert is blocked and recorded as Not delivered, as the job's own delivery to that DM is. A Not delivered alert on such a route also keeps its in-app fallback in the session, as above.
- **Upgrade.** When an alert newly inherits the owner target and the job already has an open failure incident with the same cause, the job may alert once more after the cooldown through the owner route. Repair-first handling and the auto-disable alert keep their existing timing. No config or schema change; existing jobs' `delivery.target` and `delivery.directPolicy` now also apply to their inherited failure alerts and to those alerts' in-app fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

With no alert-specific route, the failure-alert route comes from the job's primary announce target, the last tier of the documented route order ([`delivery.md` L163-L167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L163-L167)). Owner targeting (`target`, `directPolicy`) was added to the cron delivery plan in #179387; the alert-route projection carries channel, recipient, account, and thread only. Without `target`, the Gateway alert sender resolved the alert as an ordinary channel delivery (`channel: "last"` for the Doctor and setup shape) and did not reach the owner resolver that the automation's own delivery uses.

The alert route now carries `target` and `directPolicy` when it inherits the primary route and no alert-specific `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` is set in the job's `failureAlert`, `delivery.failureDestination`, or global `cron.failureAlert`. The dispatcher and the Gateway alert sender pass both fields to the existing `resolveDeliveryTarget`; owner resolution itself is unchanged. This follows the documented owner contract: owner delivery "does not follow the last group conversation or guess a recipient when owner identity is ambiguous" ([L118-L122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L118-L122)), and a missing owner route is recorded "without falling back to the last conversation" ([L124-L126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L124-L126)); see also [`troubleshooting.md` L60](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting.md?plain=1#L60) and [`heartbeat.md` L171-L172](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/gateway/heartbeat.md?plain=1#L171-L172). The route-order section of `delivery.md` now adds: "When this tier applies, failure alerts keep the primary target's owner targeting and `directPolicy`."

For owner-targeted jobs without an alert-specific route, the external alert send now resolves only a positively identified owner DM, or records Not delivered; it no longer resolves the session's last conversation or the channel's default recipient.

A Not delivered alert queues the in-app fallback: a session event that runs a turn with the alert text in the job's delivery session. That turn's reply follows the session's stored route, its last conversation, and this path does not check the owner target, `directPolicy`, or `allowFrom`. When an alert whose route carries the owner target or `directPolicy: "block"` is recorded as Not delivered, the fallback is now queued with `deliver: false` and an internal delivery context (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`), the combination `sessions_send` already uses for the agent turn it starts ([`sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts` L67-L77](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts#L67-L77)). Either setting alone keeps the turn's own reply, including an error reply such as an authentication failure, from being delivered automatically. The internal context also leaves the turn without a current external conversation, so a `message` send without an explicit target is rejected (`This turn has no current conversation`). `deliver: false` is also inherited when a tool in the fallback run hands off a session event, so that follow-up turn's own reply is not delivered automatically either; this PR does not change how a `message` send without a target resolves in that follow-up turn (see Not covered). The fallback turn still runs and is recorded in the session, so the documented in-app fallback remains. `delivery.md` now adds after its fallback paragraph: "When an alert on an owner-targeted route or a route with `directPolicy: "block"` is recorded as Not delivered, its fallback turn stays in-session: it is not delivered automatically and has no current external conversation for implicit sends."

The condition includes `directPolicy: "block"` because this PR also carries `directPolicy` on the inherited routes of jobs that are not owner-targeted. When a remembered recipient fails the channel's outbound check against `allowFrom`, implicit delivery switches to the first `allowFrom` entry ([`delivery-target.ts` L347-L359](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts#L347-L359)), and the DM block is checked after that switch ([L501-L513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts#L501-L513)); WhatsApp's outbound resolver rejects DM recipients outside `allowFrom` ([`resolve-outbound-target.ts` L29-L37](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/extensions/whatsapp/src/resolve-outbound-target.ts#L29-L37)). On such a channel, an inherited alert with `directPolicy: "block"` used to go to the first `allowFrom` entry; it is now blocked, and its fallback reply, which is not checked against `allowFrom`, would otherwise go to the session's last conversation, which the alert did not reach before. Explicit alert routes and required-delivery alerts do not inherit `directPolicy`, so their fallback is unchanged.

The route is computed per failure and not stored. The stored incident signature gains the target only when an alert inherits it, so a move from the session's last conversation to the owner counts as a changed destination ([L159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L159)). `directPolicy` is not part of the signature, and the signatures of all other jobs, including owner-targeted jobs with an alert-specific route, are byte-for-byte unchanged. There is no schema migration; `failureAlertIncident.signature` is the stored state whose comparison changes.

Unchanged: the owner resolver, alert-specific routes, repair-first escalation, the in-app fallback for routes without the owner target or `directPolicy: "block"`, the settlement of a blocked DM alert as Not delivered, and notices that do not use the alert route.

<details>
<summary>Which notifications use the failure-alert route</summary>

Every failure-alert intent takes its route from the same `resolveFailureAlert` result.

| Notification | Uses the failure-alert route | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Execution-failure alert (threshold and cooldown) | Yes | Inherits `target` and `directPolicy` with the primary route |
| Auto-disable alert for a recurring job, when an alert route is enabled | Yes | Same |
| Terminal one-shot failure alert, also used as the fallback of a repair request | Yes | Same |
| Required-delivery failure alert | Only through an alternate failure destination | Unchanged: explicit destination, no inheritance |
| Owner-conversation repair request | No: a turn in the owner conversation | Unchanged |
| Auto-disable notice when no alert route is enabled | No: in-app notice | Unchanged |
| In-app fallback after Not delivered | No | Alert route with the owner target or `directPolicy: "block"`: the fallback turn stays in the session; other routes unchanged |
| "Did not start" notice | No: session notice | Unchanged |
| Alert with no Gateway alert sender | No: goes straight to the in-app queue | Unchanged |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Alert destination before and after, by configuration</summary>

Owner-targeted job with no alert-specific route unless noted. Not delivered queues the in-app fallback notification in every row. "Before" is for a job whose alert follows its session's route; for an isolated job without a session key whose agent main session has a last conversation, the base refuses that inherited route (`Refusing implicit isolated cron delivery`), records Not delivered, and the fallback turn's reply goes to that last conversation instead. "Alert-sender test" is the new Gateway test, "fallback test" `src/cron/service.failure-alert-fallback.test.ts` (fallback only, after a stubbed Not delivered settlement), "resolver test" the existing `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.owner.test.ts`, "producer test" `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts`, and "live run" the isolated Gateway run in Evidence.

| Owner identity and session state | Before | After | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner identified; last conversation is the owner DM | Owner DM | Owner DM | Source reading |
| Owner identified; last conversation is another DM | That DM | Owner DM | Alert-sender test |
| Owner identified; last conversation is a group | That group | Owner DM | Alert-sender test (session fixture); live run |
| Owner identified; no last conversation, no channel `defaultTo` | Missing-target error, Not delivered | Owner DM | Alert-sender test; live log (before) |
| Owner identified; no last conversation, channel `defaultTo` set | The `defaultTo` recipient | Owner DM | Source reading |
| Owner identified; `directPolicy: "block"` | The session's last route | Not delivered (`dm-blocked`); fallback stays in the session | Alert-sender test (rejection, nothing sent); producer test; fallback test; live run |
| No owner identified; last conversation is a DM | That DM | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Resolver test; fallback test; issue reproduction (before) |
| No owner identified; last conversation is a group | That group | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Resolver test; live run |
| No owner identified; no last conversation, no `defaultTo` | Missing-target error, Not delivered | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Resolver test; issue reproduction (before) |
| No owner identified; no last conversation, `defaultTo` set | The `defaultTo` recipient | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Source reading |
| Not owner-targeted; `channel: "last"`, `directPolicy: "block"`, last conversation is a DM | That DM | Not delivered (DM blocked); fallback stays in the session | Producer test; fallback test; source reading |
| Any job with an alert-specific `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` | Configured route | Configured route | Producer test (`accountId` at each level, job-level `channel`); source reading for `to` |

</details>

## Evidence

Live, isolated Gateway: a Gateway on loopback with only a Telegram test bot configured. `session.groupScope: "main"` makes a private test group (the owner and the bot only) the main session's last conversation, and `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"` keeps the owner's DMs out of the main session; after every trigger, the main session's last conversation was checked again and was still the group. The bot was a group administrator, so it received group messages, and `channels.telegram.joinIntro` was `false`. The owner is identified through `openclaw pairing approve` (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`). The jobs are isolated agent-turn automations created with `openclaw automations add --delivery-target owner` (plus `--direct-policy block` for the blocked-DM jobs and `--session-key agent:main:main` for one job), with threshold 1 and cooldowns set through `openclaw automations edit`, and triggered with `openclaw automations run`. The Gateway had no valid model credentials, only a deliberately invalid model-provider API key (`automations add` requires an authentication source for the model), so every run failed with the provider's authentication error (`401 invalid_api_key`, cause `auth`). The same state was read and written in turn by the base `f47669efcec2`, the first revision `4697df95fb0c`, and the candidate `c4e527ec0c63`.

- Owner DM instead of the group: on the base, the owner-targeted job's alert was refused (`Refusing implicit isolated cron delivery`) and recorded as Not delivered, and its fallback turn's reply, an authentication-failure message (`⚠️ Couldn't sign in …`), was posted in the test group; for the job with `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`, the alert itself (`Automation "<session-key job>" failed 1 times`, `Cause: auth`) was recorded as delivered and posted in the group. The owner's DM received no alert during the base runs. Candidate, same state and same jobs: the owner-targeted job's alert was recorded as delivered, the owner's Telegram DM received `Automation "<owner-targeted job>" failed 2 times` (`Cause: auth`), and the test group received nothing; the same for the `sessionKey` job.
- Owner-route rejection and the fallback: on the first revision, an owner job with `directPolicy: "block"` and an owner job run after the owner entry was removed settled Not delivered, with delivery errors `Owner delivery unavailable (dm-blocked)` and `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)` respectively; each fallback turn ran in the main session and posted the authentication-failure message in the test group. On the candidate, the same two cases settled the same way, each fallback turn ran in the main session, and the test group received nothing.
- State written by the base build: the candidate Gateway started on the state written by the base build and listed all eight jobs that the base build's CLI had created; five of them, compared field by field, read back with the delivery and alert settings that the base build had stored. The owner-targeted job's base run had opened a failure incident for the same cause; on the candidate, its next failure after the cooldown alerted once more through the owner route (the delivered alert above, `failed 2 times`), as described under Upgrade. A second failure of the delivered owner-targeted job, after its one-minute cooldown, was not alerted again (same incident signature). An owner job with an explicit alert `channel`, whose incident the base build opened, was not alerted after its cooldown. An owner job still inside the cooldown recorded by the base build was not alerted. The no-owner and blocked-DM jobs above were also created by the base build's CLI; on the candidate, their alerts were rejected under the new owner and `directPolicy` handling.
- Before the fix: on 2026-10-30, a heartbeat that appears to have been migrated by Doctor failed once on a live Gateway and its failure alert was not delivered (`cron: failure alert delivery failed`, `MessageActionDeniedError: Delivering to Telegram requires target <chatId>`); the job row was not read. The linked issue has this log and a reproduction at the base through the same Gateway alert sender.

<details>
<summary>Live run excerpts (redacted)</summary>

Focused tests on `f47669efcec2` with this change (Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, Vitest on Node, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`); the pushed head `c4e527ec0c63` has the same changes.

- `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts` (extended), producer and dispatch: an owner-targeted primary route passes `target` and `directPolicy` to the alert route, including the channel-less delivery that Doctor and setup write and with an announce-only global alert config; the dispatcher forwards both fields to the Gateway alert sender. An `accountId` at each of the three alert-route levels, an explicit alert `channel`, and a webhook alert without a URL keep their own routing without the owner target. An open incident alerts again after the cooldown when its destination changes to the owner; an incident signature computed by the base code for a non-owner route still deduplicates; changing only `directPolicy` does not reopen an incident.
- `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts` (new): the alert route from the real `resolveFailureAlert` goes to the real Gateway alert sender (`sendGatewayCronFailureAlert`) and the real `resolveDeliveryTarget`, including its owner branch. An owner-targeted alert is sent to the owner DM (the final send's target is `111`) and settles as delivered when the session has no last conversation, has another DM, or has a group as its last conversation. With `directPolicy: "block"` and a DM last conversation, the alert is rejected with `Owner delivery unavailable (dm-blocked)` and nothing is sent. Mocked: session-store reads (the last conversation is a fixture), channel selection, and the final send (`sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`); the channel is a generic test plugin registered as `telegram`. Owner identity uses the test plugin's `user:` form; the linked issue's reproduction used a Telegram-style plugin with numeric IDs.
- `src/cron/service.failure-alert-fallback.test.ts` (new), the fallback after a Not delivered alert, using a fixture shared with the existing notification test (`src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test-support.ts`, new): a real `CronService` run fails, the route from the real `resolveFailureAlert` goes to the dispatcher, and after the alert send settles Not delivered the fallback is queued through the real Gateway cron target resolver (`createGatewayCronTargetResolver`) and runs as a real session-event turn in `agent:main:main`, whose stored route is Telegram recipient `999`; session-event admission and execution, the `message` tool, and the transcript are real. Mocked: the job's own run (it returns an error), the Gateway alert send (it records Not delivered for the route it receives, so the owner resolver does not run in this file), model output (`runEmbeddedAgent`), and the channel's final `sendText`; the channel is a generic test plugin registered as `telegram`. Cases:
  - "keeps an owner no-route fallback in the session": owner-targeted, the model replies normally; the turn completes with that reply, the session transcript contains the alert text, and nothing is sent.
  - "does not derive an external target for an implicit message send": owner-targeted, the model calls `message` with `action: "send"` and no target; the tool rejects with `Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation; pass an explicit target, or reply in normal text.`, the turn ends `failed`, and nothing is sent.
  - "does not silence the next ordinary inbound turn": after an owner-targeted fallback turn that sent nothing, an ordinary inbound event in the same session with the Telegram route is delivered to `999`.
  - "An owner blocked authentication error stays in the session.": owner-targeted with `directPolicy: "block"`, the model returns an error reply (`isError`, "Authentication failed."); the turn ends `failed`, and nothing is sent.
  - "A non-owner fallback still delivers to the configured conversation.": control, explicit Telegram recipient `999` without block; the fallback reply is sent (one send).
  - "A blocked non-owner fallback stays in the session.": explicit Telegram recipient `999` with `directPolicy: "block"`; the turn completes, and nothing is sent.
  - "A fallback-derived session event stays in the session.": inside an owner-targeted fallback turn, a session-event target is captured under a Gateway tool-caller identity bound to that turn's registered run, as in the existing "retains store, route and producer limits across lookup" case of `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.test.ts`. The captured target carries `deliver: false`; a `tool_handoff` session event queued with it runs (`executionStarted: true`; its model replies normally) and settles with `delivered: false` and `deliveryAttempted: false`, and nothing is sent.
- `src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts` (changed): its setup moved into the shared fixture with the same two-agent configuration; its four cases, their names, and their assertions are unchanged.
- `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.persistence.test.ts` (one case added), stored incidents across a reload: three jobs fail with the same cause and each opens a failure incident that is saved to the cron store: a job with `delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "last" }`, an owner-targeted job with an explicit alert `channel`, and a non-owner job with `channel: "last"`. The first job's delivery is then changed to `target: "owner"` and saved, and a new service state is loaded from the same store after the cooldown. On the next failure with the same cause, only that job alerts, and its alert route carries `target: "owner"`; the other two stay deduplicated. The stored signatures here are written by the new code for routes without a target, the same form the base code writes for an owner-targeted job; this is in-process evidence, not a store written by an earlier build. The cross-build check is in the live run above.
- Owner-route rejections: the owner branch's outcome for a missing owner (and for a blocked owner DM) is covered by the existing resolver tests in `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.owner.test.ts`. By source reading, the alert sender throws on a failed resolution and the rejected send settles as Not delivered; rejected alert sends for other causes are covered in `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`. The live run above shows both rejections settling as Not delivered through the alert sender.
- Before and after, routing tests: without the production change, `failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts` has 5 failed, 14 passed (19): the three inheritance cases (an owner target without a channel, with `directPolicy: "block"`, and with an announce-only global alert config), the dispatch case, and the post-cooldown owner alert; the explicit-selector (three `accountId` levels and a job-level alert `channel`), webhook, pre-change signature, and `directPolicy` signature cases pass on both. `server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts` has 4 failed (4): on the base the alert failed with the test channel's missing-target error (`Telegram target is required`) when the session had no last conversation, went to the other DM (`999`) or the group (`-100777`), and with `directPolicy: "block"` was sent instead of being rejected. With the change: 19 and 4 passed.

The four `service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts` cases and the added persistence case pass on both. With the change: 7, 4, and 13 (the persistence file) passed.

Without the alert-specific selector check, the three explicit `accountId` cases and the explicit alert-channel case fail; without the job-level `accountId` in that check, its case; without the target in the incident signature, the post-cooldown owner alert; with the target appended even when absent, the pre-change signature case; with `directPolicy` in the signature, the pre-change signature and `directPolicy` cases; without the Gateway passing `directPolicy` to the resolver, the blocked-owner alert case.

- Test lines: `config/test-lines-allocations/cron-failure-alert-owner-target.txt` records 660 net added test lines: 140 in the producer test, 163 in the Gateway file, 214 in the fallback file, 169 in the shared fixture, 56 in the persistence test, and −82 in `service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts`, whose setup moved into the fixture. Not run locally: the full `pnpm check:changed`; the PR CI result is below. Not run: `pnpm build` (no entry-point, packaging, or lazy-loading change) and the plugin and channel contract tests (no shared plugin or channel interface changes).

Under Node, the file passed in 5 of 5 runs on that head and 5 of 5 on the base `f47669efcec2` (11 tests each), so the failure did not reproduce there; the Bun runtime was not tried locally. No existing issue for this test was found, and its cause is not established. On the current head: the same test passed in the Bun shard of `checks-node-changed-compact-large-19` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41294676000/job/124813173834)).
- Local review: `autoreview` (Codex CLI 0.164.0, engine `codex`, local mode) on base `f47669efcec2` and an uncommitted local snapshot of this change (patch SHA-256 prefix `ecd151979a72`), `--max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.86)", no P0–P2 findings; remaining findings: none. The review covered the diff and the supplied source context; it did not execute code or tests.

- In tests, the owner-route rejection and the fallback are covered separately: the Gateway test asserts the blocked-owner rejection and that nothing is sent, and the fallback test starts from a stubbed alert send that settles Not delivered. The live run covers the two together for the no-owner and blocked-owner cases.

- A session event that a tool hands off from the fallback run (for example `plugins` `reloadAndResume`) inherits `deliver: false` but not the internal delivery context: its follow-up turn runs with the session's stored route, so its reply is not delivered automatically, while a `message` send without a target in that turn would resolve to that route. No test covers such a call.

- The in-process tests use a generic test channel plugin registered as `telegram`, and the live run used Telegram; no other channel was exercised, including one whose implicit delivery switches to the first `allowFrom` entry.

prs.title: fix(msteams): broadcast entries split group chat sessions and ignore the documented key form
prs.body:
Closes #190740

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Microsoft Teams group chats and channels, adding a documented `broadcast["msteams:<conversationId>"]` entry does nothing, while the undocumented `msteams:conversation:<id>` key fans out into a *different* session (`…:group:conversation:<id>`), so adding/removing broadcast splits the routed agent's history.

## User Impact

User impact: Teams broadcast entries now use the documented `"<channel>:<peerId>"` form with the bare conversation id, and the routed agent keeps the same session with or without broadcast.

**Existing prefixed keys / stored histories (no migration, nothing deleted):** configs that used the undocumented `msteams:conversation:<id>` key stop matching and fall back to the ordinary single-agent route; rename the key to `msteams:<id>`. Transcripts already written under `agent:<id>:msteams:group:conversation:<id>` are left untouched on disk and are not merged or deleted; after this change new turns continue in the ordinary `agent:<id>:msteams:group:<id>` session (the same one used before broadcast was added). Operators who want the in-between history can read or reuse those old sessions manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams built its inbound context without `conversation.routePeer`, so core group-thread dispatch fell back to the prefixed `OriginatingTo` (`conversation:<id>`) — or, for channels, the Graph `team/channel` native id. Teams now publishes the same peer it passes to `resolveAgentRoute` (bare conversation id; sender id for DMs), matching Slack and Discord. Plugin-local only; no core changes. Docs gain a Teams example of the key form.

## Evidence

New `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.broadcast.test.ts` runs real Teams inbound preparation (`createMSTeamsMessageHandler` + real `buildChannelInboundEventContext` + real `resolveAgentRoute`) into the real core `dispatchInboundMessage` (including group-thread fan-out); only the agent reply is stubbed.

Red on `main` (c268e6e), fix stashed:
```
 × keeps the routed agent's session when a documented broadcast entry is added or removed
   AssertionError: expected [ 'main' ] to deeply equal [ 'helper', 'main' ]
 × does not match the legacy conversation-prefixed broadcast key
   AssertionError: expected [ … ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
```
Green with fix: both pass; whole `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler` suite 9 files / 94 tests pass.

Before/after session keys for chat `19:Room-A@thread.v2` (same harness, probe not committed):
```
BEFORE no broadcast                  => main: agent:main:msteams:group:19:room-a@thread.v2
BEFORE msteams:<chat>                => main only (entry ignored)
BEFORE msteams:conversation:<chat>   => main: agent:main:msteams:group:conversation:19:room-a@thread.v2  ← split history
                                        helper: agent:helper:msteams:group:conversation:19:room-a@thread.v2
AFTER  no broadcast                  => main: agent:main:msteams:group:19:room-a@thread.v2
AFTER  msteams:<chat>                => main: agent:main:msteams:group:19:room-a@thread.v2  ← same session
                                        helper: agent:helper:msteams:group:19:room-a@thread.v2
AFTER  msteams:conversation:<chat>   => main only (legacy key no longer matches)
```
Local `pnpm check:changed`: format, typecheck extensions + extension tests, lint, plugin boundaries, mock-export ratchet, import cycles all ok. Live Gateway and upgrade runs: see *Real behaviour proof* below.

## Update (d7aa32f): Doctor migration for legacy keys
- `extensions/msteams/config-doctor-api.ts` now owns a legacy rule + `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` step that moves `broadcast."msteams:conversation:<id>"` → `broadcast."msteams:<id>"` on `openclaw doctor --fix`. Existing canonical entries are never overwritten (a warning is emitted and both keys are left as-is).
- The previous legacy-rejection test was replaced by a migration regression: migrate a legacy config, then run the real Teams inbound → core dispatch path and assert both participants fan out with stable `agent:<id>:msteams:group:<chat>` sessions; plus a no-overwrite test.
- Stored data: session keys are unchanged by this PR (`agent:main:msteams:group:<chat>` before and after), so existing transcripts keep resolving; only the config key is rewritten.

## Update (follow-up): collisions + channel keys
- Collision: when both `msteams:conversation:<id>` and `msteams:<id>` exist, Doctor now keeps the canonical value and removes the superseded key (warning if values differed), so the legacy rule no longer matches and repair completes; the second run is a no-op (tested for identical and differing values).
- Channel keys: `routePeer` is now published only for group chats. Teams channels keep their existing broadcast identity (`msteams:<teamAadGroupId>/<graphChannelId>` via NativeChannelId) and DMs are unchanged, so no working channel/DM broadcast entry silently stops matching.
- msteams monitor-handler + config-doctor suites: 10 files / 114 tests pass.

## Update: DM/channel scope
- Doctor migrates only group-chat legacy keys (`msteams:conversation:19:…@thread.v2`). DM (`a:…`) and channel keys are left alone and still resolve through their existing lookup; a new inbound→dispatch regression proves a personal-conversation `msteams:conversation:<dm>` entry still fans out to both agents.
- Docs now scope the bare-id form to group chats and spell out the retained channel and DM forms.



## Real behaviour proof
Environment: Linux cloud VM; scratch Gateway with the Teams plugin and the plugin's loopback Bot Framework QA stand-in (no Teams tenant), QA mock model, agents `main` + `helper`, group chat `19:proofroom@thread.v2`. Tokens and activity ids redacted. Branch head `93e544b`.

**Before (main, no `conversation.routePeer`)**
| Step | Agents replying | Session(s) | History |
|---|---|---|---|
| no broadcast | main | `agent:main:msteams:group:19:proofroom@thread.v2` | PROOF-BEFORE |
| `broadcast["msteams:<chat>"]` (documented) | main only, key ignored | same bare key | PROOF-BEFORE, PROOF-DURING |
| `broadcast["msteams:conversation:<chat>"]` (legacy) | main + helper | `agent:{main,helper}:msteams:group:conversation:19:proofroom@thread.v2` | only PROOF-LEGACY; main's room history is gone from context |
| entry removed | main | bare key again | PROOF-BEFORE, PROOF-DURING, PROOF-AFTER (PROOF-LEGACY stranded on the prefixed session) |

**After (this branch)**
| Step | Agents replying | Session(s) | main history |
|---|---|---|---|
| no broadcast | main | `agent:main:msteams:group:19:proofroom@thread.v2` | PROOF-BEFORE |
| `broadcast["msteams:<chat>"]` | main + helper | main unchanged; helper `agent:helper:msteams:group:19:proofroom@thread.v2` | PROOF-BEFORE, PROOF-DURING |
| entry removed | main | same bare key | PROOF-BEFORE, PROOF-DURING, PROOF-AFTER |

**Upgrade / data-model compatibility from `openclaw@2026.10.9` + `@openclaw/msteams@2026.10.9`**
- On 2026.10.9, one group turn under `broadcast["msteams:conversation:19:proofroom@thread.v2"]` stored history on the conversation-prefixed session keys.
- Switched the same state dir to this checkout. First `openclaw doctor --fix` upgraded the agent databases (schema v25 → v39) and printed:
  `Moved broadcast."msteams:conversation:19:proofroom@thread.v2" → broadcast."msteams:19:proofroom@thread.v2".`
- Second `openclaw doctor --fix`: no further broadcast change (idempotent).
- `chat.history` on both original keys still returns the stored turn (user `PROOF-LEGACY reply exactly: PROOF-LEGACY`, assistant `PROOF-LEGACY`). Existing transcripts load under their original keys; they are not silently merged into the bare-id session.

prs.title: fix(test): declare Workshop opt-out in legacy upgrade fixtures
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186506

## What Problem This Solves

The legacy upgrade-survivor fixture can fail its final Doctor check after authoring a restrictive plugin allowlist while leaving autonomous Workshop learning enabled by default. The 9.2 cell exposed this mismatch after candidate identity, migration, survival, and deferred-schema Doctor phases had passed.

## User Impact

Harness-only change. The legacy scenario explicitly opts out of autonomous learning while preserving its authored workspace skill and operator settings. Product defaults, plugin policy, and the strict final Doctor acceptance check remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both published baselines, 2026.9.2 and 2026.10.9, support `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode=off`. The fixture sets that value through each baseline's CLI and requires it to survive the update. Adding a Workshop plugin entry would be incorrect: both baselines treat that plugin identifier as retired.

Regressions cover loss or reactivation of the opt-out, retain the restrictive allowlist and ordinary hooks, and check that the actual current Doctor still warns for automatic learning with unavailable tools while accepting an explicit opt-out.

## Evidence

- Exact source: `e564340ef0be6473a1ff7d4ad1e04b7a50c0a1ea`, based on `ac6af4df297273b4d72f1d85971b5006c8b39530`.
- Fresh whole-owner source review completed with no findings. Published baseline schema/runtime and retired-plugin contracts were inspected directly.
- Full focused suites passed on Node and Bun: 15 unique cases per runtime (5 fixture cases and 10 actual Doctor-policy/bootstrap cases). Targeted formatting, lint, both relevant test type leaves, and line/test ratchets passed.
- Matched owner-only negative control: the original fixture produced exactly 3 intended assertion failures and 2 passes. Complete JSON and JUnit reports were independently validated against the exact test locations and pinned Vitest/Chai matcher frames; the fixture was restored before GREEN checks. The automated collector retained its original stack-frame rejection and nonzero `COLLECTED_UNQUALIFIED` result. Acceptance comes from the independently checked component evidence, not relabeling that aggregate exit.
- An earlier attempt stopped before tests with native exit 255 and earned no proof credit. Exact native cleanup completed separately after the final collection's reconciliation timeout; source and local process settlement were verified.
- The earlier [package acceptance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41380411856) remains failed overall: the 10.9 cell passed, while the 9.2 cell stopped at the extra Workshop warning. Repaired two-cell Docker acceptance, current-head CI/security, and native landing remain separate gates.

prs.title: fix(agents): run shell snapshot capture under the agent exec cgroup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent runs a shell tool on Linux, the snapshot shells spawned by `runShell` (`src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts`) had no explicit execution intent, so they fell back to the default `"gateway-internal"` and escaped the agent exec cgroup.

- Problem: the capture shell and the snapshot validation shell landed in the gateway exec cgroup instead of the agent's, bypassing the per-agent CPU/memory limits and kill boundary documented in `docs/platforms/linux.md`.
- Solution: pass `"agent-tool"` as the `executionIntent` to `spawnProcess` in `runShell` — the single call site both snapshot shells go through — matching the six existing agent-side spawn sites.
- What changed: `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` (one call gains the intent) and `src/agents/shell-snapshot.spawn.test.ts` (regression test at the broker placement boundary); the gateway-internal path, every other spawn site, and the capture/validation/caching logic are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

`spawnProcess(command, args, options, initiateSpawn?, executionIntent = "gateway-internal")` only enters the agent exec cgroup when `executionIntent === "agent-tool"`. That default was flipped from the legacy `gatewayWorker?: true` semantics (absent = agent cgroup), so an agent-side site that forgets the intent silently stops isolating its children; `runShell` was the only one. Changing the default back was rejected: it is intentionally gateway-internal for infra workers.

## User Impact

On Linux with the spawn broker and agent exec cgroup enabled, both snapshot shells — the interactive capture shell and the short-lived validation shell that sources the freshly written snapshot — are now in the agent exec cgroup, so per-agent CPU/memory limits and the kill boundary apply to them. No other user-visible change.

## Evidence

Real behavior on an isolated GHA `ubuntu-24.04` runner (systemd 255, cgroup v2 with `cpu io memory` delegated via `Delegate=yes` + `DelegateSubgroup=gateway`), driven from inside a transient delegated unit through shipped entry points only: `prepareHostExecSpawn` (owns the capture and validation shells), `spawnProcess(..., "agent-tool")` for the exec shell, `spawnProcess(..., "gateway-internal")` for a control child through the same broker. Three rounds use distinct workdirs so each re-runs the real capture and validation.

Placement is not inferred. The capture shell reports its own `/proc/$$/cgroup` from `~/.bashrc`; the exec shell and the control report theirs from inside the spawned command; the validation shell only sources a file and exits in milliseconds, so a separate sampler process records each new pid with the cgroup it was actually in. Capture and validation success is proven by the published snapshot containing a marker function defined only in `~/.bashrc`, and by every exec round printing it.

Post-fix (head `de2e3a404e0`) — all checks pass:
```
PROOF sampler stats: {"passes":3744,"scanned":76,"recorded":13,"elapsedMs":3021}
PROOF capture pid=3164 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF capture pid=3211 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF validation pid=3190 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec cmd=/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c . '.../shell-snapshots/<key>.<pid>.<ts>.tmp'
PROOF validation pid=3208 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF validation pid=3226 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF exec round=1 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF exec round=2 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF exec round=3 cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/agent-exec
PROOF gateway-control cgroup=oc-proof-postfix.service/gateway
PROOF published snapshot count: 3
PROOF marker file outputs: ["SNAPSHOT-WAS-SOURCED","SNAPSHOT-WAS-SOURCED","SNAPSHOT-WAS-SOURCED"]
PROOF exec exit codes: 0,0,0
PROOF check PASS: self in gateway before
PROOF check PASS: agent-exec cgroup available
PROOF check PASS: capture shell reported agent-exec
PROOF check PASS: validation shell observed in agent-exec
PROOF check PASS: exec shell reported agent-exec
PROOF check PASS: exec shell observed in agent-exec
PROOF check PASS: validation shell never seen in gateway
PROOF check PASS: snapshot published with marker function
PROOF check PASS: wrapped command sources snapshot
PROOF check PASS: snapshot used: marker printed by every round
PROOF check PASS: exec rounds exited 0
PROOF check PASS: gateway-internal control reported gateway
PROOF check PASS: gateway-internal control observed in gateway
PROOF check PASS: self remained in gateway after
PROOF VERDICT: PASS
```

Pre-fix control, same script with only `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` reverted to `main` — the two snapshot shells fall back to the gateway leaf while the exec shell and the control stay put, so the run fails:
```
PROOF capture pid=2904 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF capture pid=2924 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF capture pid=2945 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF validation pid=3340 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF validation pid=3361 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF validation pid=3381 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF exec round=1 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/agent-exec
PROOF exec round=2 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/agent-exec
PROOF exec round=3 cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/agent-exec
PROOF gateway-control cgroup=oc-proof-prefix.service/gateway
PROOF check FAIL: capture shell reported agent-exec
PROOF check FAIL: validation shell observed in agent-exec
PROOF check FAIL: validation shell never seen in gateway
PROOF VERDICT: FAIL
```

The regression test replaces the earlier argument-only spy: it drives `maybeWrapCommandWithShellSnapshot` through the real `spawnProcess` under `runWithSpawnBroker` and asserts the broker receives the agent exec cgroup at the placement argument of both the capture and the validation spawn. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR publication signature tests rebuild the same signed Git fixture in every case, adding avoidable time to CI.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The seven-case publication file's median wall time falls from **67.802s to 23.584s**, saving **44.219s (65.22%)**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the complete immutable setup in the existing `reuseBaselineFixture` helper, following the incoming, signing, and successor tests. It restores the whole private root to the same absolute paths, preserving registered worktrees and path-bound evidence. Each case still runs its real signing/verification, private mutations, publication or refusal, ancestry checks, and untouched-ref assertions. Captured JavaScript metadata remains read-only.

Only `test/scripts/pr-baseline-publication.test.ts` changes: **+5/-7, net −2 test lines**. All seven cases and all assertions remain. Production code and shared helpers are unchanged.

## Evidence

All benchmarks and mutations ran serially on the same **Blacksmith 16-vCPU Testbox** `tbx_01m6d6ex28n8sywqwf62gjx624`, provisioned through Crabbox: [Actions run 41385790177](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41385790177). Frozen-lockfile bootstrap was used. Baseline source: `ac6af4df297273b4d72f1d85971b5006c8b39530`.

| File | Baseline wall samples, seconds | Candidate wall samples, seconds | Median saving |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pr-baseline-publication.test.ts` | 68.787 / 67.802 / 67.422 | 23.584 / 23.611 / 23.388 | **44.219s (65.22%)** |

Each sample passed all seven cases. Wall time includes the repository runner, fixture construction or snapshot/restore, hooks, and subprocess settlement; bootstrap is excluded. This is a focused-file measurement, not a CI critical-path claim.

```sh
corepack pnpm test test/scripts/pr-baseline-publication.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

Paired mutations used unchanged original test bytes for baseline and the exact timed candidate bytes. **Killed** means the existing relevant assertions failed because the broken product behavior was admitted.

| Temporary product mutation | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bypass task-commit signature refusal | Killed: both first-parent and side-parent unsigned cases | Killed: same two cases |
| Bypass retained baseline-binding authority, deriving the baseline from the signed candidate's parent | Killed: missing, changed, wrong-anchor, and unbound authority cases | Killed: same four cases |

Signed publication remained successful under both valid mutations. No baseline-only kill survived on candidate. All product mutations and probes were removed, restored hashes matched the originals, and the product-source diff was clean. Temporary pristine-state probes passed before all seven publication cases, including immediately after authority-file mutations.

An earlier binding mutant incorrectly treated the binding hash as a stored Git object and failed fixture setup. That result was discarded; the paired parent-derived mutant above is the valid gate.

- Touched-file format, lint, and targeted typecheck passed remotely. The initial scratch typecheck config inherited unrelated UI setup and omitted ambient declarations; correcting its scope and declarations resolved setup errors.
- `pr-simplify`: the complete fix uses the existing helper and removes the redundant local cleanup tracker.
- Isolated Codex-backed autoreview of the final one-file diff against the pinned baseline, with the complete test/helper/sibling context: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no actionable findings.
- PR CI supplies broad validation.

<details>
<summary>REST-observation target: NOCHANGE after qualification</summary>

`test/scripts/pr-merge-prior-ci-rest-observation.test.ts` was benchmarked with the existing completed-setup restoration contract, but did not meet the required reproducible gain. It is byte-for-byte unchanged in this PR.

| Version | Three wall samples, seconds | Median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 84.169 / 83.767 / 83.770 | 83.770s |
| Candidate | 83.983 / 84.024 / 84.030 | 84.024s |

All 59 cases passed in every timing run. The candidate was **0.255s slower**, so it was reverted. Its paired mutation results also matched:

| Temporary product mutation | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omit final delegated-policy/writer recheck | Killed: both policy cases | Killed: same two cases |
| Accept REST projection contradicting known GraphQL facts | Killed: known-projection case | Killed: same case |
| Optimistically fill malformed REST projection | Killed: malformed-projection case | Killed: same case |

Temporary restore probes passed for all 57 completed-candidate cases; the two ordinary-route cases kept their independent fixtures. These probes and mutations are excluded from timing samples and from the diff.

</details>

prs.title: fix: keep accepted automation runs revocable after turn completion
prs.body:
Related: #168568. Builds on #188513; does not claim the broader Matrix report is resolved.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an accepted immediate automation can still perform work after its requesting turn is explicitly canceled or its authenticated source is revoked.

## User Impact

Owner/administrator requests retain main's after-turn execution behavior while remaining bound to the original live source and exact executable job. Cancellation, source/device revocation, and changed or ineligible jobs produce a visible terminal outcome. No configuration or storage migration is required.

The standalone proof covers authenticated Control UI administrator authority. Configured external-channel owner removal and literal owner metadata reassignment were not exercised; the public job-update API does not expose owner reassignment. The provider is deterministic local HTTP. Target command processes and provider HTTP I/O are real; isolated-agent, script and trigger consumers have focused tests and source review rather than standalone effect campaigns.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main #188513 independently supplies the after-turn handoff. Caller admission still consumes its one-use management grant with the original exact-run and 60-second expiry checks. Once durable, the scheduler retains a separate source check for that one request and executable definition. Ordinary settlement differs from cancellation, and the existing execution owners recheck the retained source after asynchronous preparation and before effects.

The actual merge conflict was resolved against main `bf2284a636c6ecd5b07f1de531a35f7fe93fbf23`: ordinary caller-scoped manual work keeps main's handoff; event and on-exit custody keep their existing guards. The queue owns disable/delete eligibility and its specific terminal messages. Fresh review found the initial launch-only check insufficient; its source assertion now reaches the existing executor/admitted-run checks and completion delivery. No receipt schema, policy setting or credential flow changed.

## Evidence

- Pinned main base `bf2284a636c6ecd5b07f1de531a35f7fe93fbf23`, real Gateway/agent regression: **1 failed, 1 passed**. The authenticated management cancellation case makes the fourth provider call and records `ok` instead of `skipped`; the caller-scoped control passes. The focused post-await source contract is **36 passed, 4 failed** on that base.
- Standalone base process proof: actual model-tool grant issuance and accepted `cron.run` receipt → successful actual `chat.abort` → queue opens → **one unwanted child-process effect**. Separate base preparation proof: accepted receipt → normal caller settlement → public cron `started` while the real target session remains busy → actual device-token revocation → target release → **one unwanted provider HTTP request**, `ok` history. Both fail their zero-effect assertions; these are product failures, not setup failures.
- Source-verified production commit `a9473dd6d46ee7f2df8c33c607c9d1831692a6db`: **2 Gateway E2E rows pass; 14/14 real-effect cases pass; all four container exits are 0**. Settlement/disconnect produce exactly one intended child effect; actual `chat.abort`, device/origin revocation, disable/delete and agent retarget produce zero. The forbidden command request is refused before receipt/history/effect. After public cron start and a genuinely blocked target session, settlement/disconnect produce one target provider HTTP request; actual abort/device/origin revocation produce zero and terminal `error` history. Independent audit matched every receipt/history ID, effect artifact and trace ordering. The published head differs only in the occurrence test consolidation; all 20 production files and the unchanged E2E input are byte-identical, so this effect proof is reused with its original head identity.
- **292 focused contract/consumer checks pass** on the repair, including the unchanged post-reservation zero-main-thread-SQL contract, caller scoping, prefix stability, script admission, command timeouts, plugin schedules and webhook delivery. Targeted production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. `pr-simplify` removes the guard alias and duplicate eligibility checks and shares repeated acknowledgement fixtures: **88 added / 90 deleted test lines (net −2)**; production **+172/−45 (net +127)** against the pinned main base. No test allocation or baseline exception was added.
- Fresh installed autoreview: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings after repairing its preparation-source finding and correcting the test consolidation. The final matrix retains all 32 healthy rows, all 32 paused rows, occurrence identity/release assertions and aggregate executor reachability. `childParent` destructuring removes repeated lookups to satisfy the existing file-line limit; typecheck, lint and affected consumers pass.
- Exact published head `fb8514aba1678f3df007bb047730b0c19138605d`: [CI run 41114327223](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41114327223), attempt 1, completed **failed**. The only failed test job, [124265221440](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41114327223/job/124265221440), has three cron fallback failures: the stored-session explicit/own-model fallback cases (line 160) and timeout fallback transcript (line 137). prs.title: fix(slack): match canonically equivalent names in allowlist resolution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An allowlist entry written in NFC form (e.g. `@Renée`, precomposed) fails to resolve a Slack profile whose display name is stored in NFD form (`Rene\u0301e`, decomposed), and vice versa. The two strings compare unequal under `===` even though they are canonically equivalent, so the user is reported `resolved: false` instead of being matched.

The same omission predicate affects the user's exact-name comparison against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, and `profile.real_name`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSlackUserAllowlist` in `extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts` compares the allowlist entry name against profile names with `===` on lowercased strings. Lowercasing does not canonicalize Unicode, so NFC/NFD-equivalent spellings of the same name never match. Both sides of the comparison are now normalized with `normalize("NFC")`.

This is the same shape already accepted for the feishu sticker-search path (`#190043`, `extensions/feishu/src/sticker-catalog.ts`) and the slack/feishu/msteams directory lookups that normalize query and candidate before matching.

**Security guard (P1):** canonical matching is a fallback, never a replacement. Exact (lowercased) spelling stays the primary comparison, preserving the pre-existing principal selection. If two active humans have display names that differ only by normalization form (one NFD, one NFC), the configured name resolves to the exact-spelling match even if the canonically-equivalent user appears earlier in the directory. This prevents NFC normalization from displacing the configured principal with a different Slack user id.

Production LOC is `+28/-3` across one file. No new validator, option, config item, or persistence strategy is added.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Allowlist entries that differ from the stored profile name only by Unicode normalization form now resolve to the correct user id instead of being reported unresolved. Matching for already-canonical names is unchanged. NFC normalization is a canonical-equivalence relation used as a fallback only: it never merges two distinct names, and it can never displace an exact-name match, so it cannot admit a different principal than the one the configured name denotes.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry-point proof (production WebClient over local fixture)

The real exported `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` is exercised through its production `createSlackLookupClient` WebClient path against a local `users.list` fixture, using the existing `SLACK_API_URL` seam the plugin itself supports. No Slack client is mocked: the same code path that ships resolves entries over the fixture.

- Product head SHA: `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`
- Current-main RED baseline: `632dced4affb7a338d0def2b7059c246ed33b0af`
- Production entry: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` (`extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts:99`) over the production `createSlackLookupClient` (`extensions/slack/src/client.ts:47`) and its `users.list` fetch.
- Decision surface: allowlist entry name matched against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, `profile.real_name`.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the `resolved` flag and resolved `id`/`name` in `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` output.

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
  - both NFC/NFD cross-form resolve cases fail (resolved: false)
  - both canonical-direction admission cases fail (no derived grant, sender denied)
  - competing-principal case fails (active grant never derives, intended sender denied)
  - removal case fails (first turn never admits)
  - exact-name / accent-stripped / same-form / ASCII controls pass
```

### Authority-chain proof: production DM ingress through final effect

The authority chain no longer stops at the resolver return value or a bare admission boolean. `createMonitorTestContext` returns a context whose `readRuntimeContext` is the real `createSlackRuntimeContextReader`, so awaiting it runs the production `resolveWorkspacePolicy` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/runtime-policy.ts:239-250`), which resolves the allowlist names through the real `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the local `users.list` fixture and merges the derived ids into `ctx.allowFrom` via `mergeAllowlist`. The resolved policy context is then handed to the production DM ingress entry point `prepareSlackMessage` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts`), the function the monitor calls for every inbound message; it runs the DM admission gate `authorizeSlackDirectMessage` and, on admission, returns the exact `PreparedSlackMessage` object the monitor dispatches to the agent/provider. No admission helper, Slack client, or dispatch seam is mocked.

- **Both canonical directions admit the intended Slack ID at final effect.** `@Renée` (NFC) against an NFD-stored profile, and the NFD spelling against an NFC-stored profile, each resolve to `U_ACCENT` through production policy reload, the id lands in the allow-from list, and `prepareSlackMessage` returns a non-null `PreparedSlackMessage` for sender `U_ACCENT` — the object that reaches agent/provider dispatch.
- **The competing principal is rejected while the canonical grant is active.** With `@Renée` derived to `U_ACCENT` and present in allow-from, a message from `U_OTHER` — a distinct sender with its own fixture display name and identity, resolved per user id exactly as production resolves sender names (`prepare.ts:381`) — returns null: the DM gate drops the event before any agent/provider I/O. The derived grant admits exactly the resolved principal and never a different Slack user id.
- **A distinct name is denied before any agent/provider I/O.** With the accent-stripped `@Renee` configured (unresolved), `U_ACCENT` never becomes a derived grant and both `U_ACCENT` and `U_OTHER` are dropped before dispatch.
- **Removing the name-derived grant denies subsequent messages on the same runtime policy reader.** First turn `@Renée` resolves and `U_ACCENT` is admitted at final effect. The published config is then replaced with one whose only entry is the stale `@Renee`; the same reader rebuilds policy on its next read (`runtime-policy.ts:116`, `current.cfg !== cfg`), the derived id leaves allow-from, and a subsequent message from `U_ACCENT` is dropped before dispatch — the same live-policy-change path the monitor uses, no reconnect or fresh monitor.
- **Exact-name principal is preserved (P1 regression).** With `U_OTHER` (NFD display name) before `U_INTENDED` (NFC display name) in the directory, `@Renée` resolves to `U_INTENDED`, not the canonically-equivalent earlier entry. This test fails on the pure-canonical head (selects `U_OTHER`) and passes on this head.

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.test.ts` — 9 passed on this head. The NFC/NFD cross-form cases are covered by the production-WebClient live-proof group instead of duplicated mocked-client cases; the focused unit suite retains its existing mocked-client coverage of resolution inputs and outputs.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts` — 10 passed, 1 shard, ~50s wall.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.test.ts` — 9 passed, 1 shard.

The authority chain runs the production policy reload and the production DM ingress over the fixture; the remaining runtime path (socket-mode event reception) is exercised by existing monitor tests, not re-driven here.

- Production LOC: `+28/-3`
- Test LOC: `+390/-0` (live-proof integration, including the authority-chain group); the focused unit suite is unchanged (added NFC/NFD mocked-client cases were dropped per review as duplicates of the live proof).

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve WebChat native subagent continuation
prs.body:
Closes #188524

Related: #153354

Targets `release/2026.10.10`. The WebChat scope argument still exists on this branch; `main` retired it in #181851. The catalog-continuity change is also submitted separately for `main`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188698.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native child completions losing their initiating WebChat context and replacing the parent thread before it can follow up with the same child.

## User Impact

WebChat users can receive an automatic child completion and continue with that child while keeping the same native parent thread and accepted tools, including when the session has saved external delivery history. No outbound recipient, configuration, or migration is added. Duplicate visible completion replies remain outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two existing boundaries need to remain connected. First, pass the normalized WebChat-only origin to the existing host-issued completion scope. Explicit channel precedence and the other channels' behavior are preserved.

Second, the last child's completion releases live-child execution protection before delivery. The existing catalog-recovery guard then misses that automatic continuation. Let the existing completion-delivery owner identify its exact in-flight parent/child/session/run/client custody and recover the native thread's accepted catalog for that delivery. Recheck that custody after awaited metadata reads. Keep runtime, home, transport, catalog fingerprints, current tool-execution authority, and ordinary-turn behavior intact. This is a bounded completion-lifetime fix, rather than the older deployment workaround that weakened runtime matching.

## Evidence

- The existing dispatcher fixture fails on the base in the three WebChat cases and passes with the origin fix. Its 39-test dispatcher, completion SDK, and requester-settle routing set passes, covering normalization, alias handling, explicit-channel precedence, and channel-only output without an external target.
- Completion-owner and catalog-loader regression cases are red before their respective production changes and green afterward. The release catalog scope's 41 focused tests pass, including current execution authority and related continuity consumers.
- Core and Codex production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing catalog regression cases grow by 118 net test lines, without additional fixture launches or a shared test-ceiling increase.
- Shared autoreview against release base `06d598c818155a5ac6ad00c9611bbb4b6ed57d45` found no actionable P0–P2 findings for the WebChat delta and, separately, the complete release catalog delta and owner/authority context. The reviewed catalog delta was applied unchanged on top of the WebChat commit. Tests were executed separately, not by the reviewer.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passes on exact combined head `12d7d8d051888503b68a4ce3ff1bd73ca2f63945` (53.1 s). A real-model authenticated WebChat run on that source/build completes parent → child → automatic completion → parent continuation → follow-up to the same child. The parent and physical client stay the same through both resumptions; the child returns its remembered marker; all 44 accepted functions and the canonical native metadata digest remain unchanged. Shipped CLI history confirms the visible result, preserved synthetic Telegram context/origin, and settled session.
- Full local Codex extension lane on the code-identical catalog candidate: **5,057 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped**, across 433 executed files (512.52 s). The three previously reproduced baseline macOS failures are the nonempty Git identity expectation in `thread-shell-environment.native.test.ts` and two process-inspection permission errors in `transport-startup.test.ts`. This full lane is not claimed as passing; no assertions, timeouts, retries, skips, or expected-failure settings were weakened. The separate WebChat delta is covered by the dispatcher/core checks above and current-head CI.

## Updated release base and isolated Linux verification (2026-10-31)

Current head: `92bc37d0739f288b25d1f9fc90081c68ee0c5d98`. Merged release base `6b96f139020b581adecfde84736331a710492c31` specifically to remove the inherited missing-helper CI failure described below. Upstream #188809 (`a1dbc50ba87819f2a42e8e554187898a59584571`) supplies `test/helpers/gateway-startup.ts`; its SHA-256 in this candidate exactly matches the repaired release base (`125a2b72ce8bcdcebf04dd323f90728778a711cc3893a0b62229093b758b32dd`). No local stub, check suppression, baseline relaxation, or failure exception was introduced.

Independent read-only review found no actionable integration findings: the PR's same ten-file delta and added/removed lines are preserved relative to the new base, including the newer release Stop/process-cleanup ownership. The merge is conflict-free and `git diff --check` passes.

On a fresh isolated Linux checkout with Node v24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0, `pnpm build:runtime` passes (8m23.3s), and `pnpm openclaw --help` passes using task-owned state/config paths. No operator Gateway, installed package, live service or production data was changed. Dependency-bundler warnings about direct eval in third-party web-tree-sitter remain warnings, not a clean-warning claim.

The real-model continuity trace below remains evidence from its stated prior head `12d7d8d`; it was not rerun or relabeled as fresh live proof after the base merge. Fresh hosted CI for the new head is in progress and is not yet claimed passing.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI failure on the previous head</summary>

**Historical CI on the previous head `12d7d8d`:** all jobs completed. The remaining failure is [`check-test-types-core-5`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41127106544/job/124309989805), with `TS2307` for `../../test/helpers/gateway-startup.js` at `src/gateway/server.required-placement-scopes.test.ts:5`; the aggregate gate also fails. The runner checked merge `f75e317e8cfe8816df932b2da73952600414e38c`, whose first parent is the newer release base `f47d762e6fbc30950bbb81a18d4a5eec22e76f6a` from #188692. That base already imports the missing helper. Its test blob and the merge's test blob are identical (`bb91488e5808fe5b86d39e119e2aad6f2b5a762f`), and the helper is absent from the base tree. The original release base and this PR's own head do not contain that import. `pnpm test:ci-failed 188526` initially calls this job new relative to main, without comparing the selected scope; the exact release-base source comparison above establishes the inherited omission. The remaining CI blocker is in the updated release base. No rerun or unrelated source change was used to hide it.

</details>

This exact-head live run supersedes the earlier routing-only probe that rotated the parent. It used Node 24.22.1 and Codex 0.164.0, one original request, isolated synthetic state, a synthetic non-recipient Telegram history with no external channels configured, and disabled model fallbacks. Two child completion announcements produced two identical final replies. The proof qualifies the requested routing/thread/catalog/child continuity; it does not qualify exactly-once visible delivery or general fallback behavior. CI and bot reviews of the prior head apply only to that prior head.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized exact-candidate runtime proof</summary>

```text
Exact-candidate real WebChat catalog-continuity proof
Source/build commit: 12d7d8d051888503b68a4ce3ff1bd73ca2f63945
Runtime: Node v24.22.1; workspace-pinned Codex 0.164.0.
Environment: isolated synthetic session, authenticated WebChat client, no external channels configured. Existing Telegram delivery history used a synthetic non-recipient. Model fallbacks were disabled.

One chat.send request was accepted. No manual continuation or retry was sent.
Initial native parent: 01a18e8d-a149-7c10-915d-f1e3bfa2b778
Native child: 01a18e8d-cd4c-7632-9f18-446d7adc82a0 (agent target /root/catalog_child)
Parent thread_ready events: started, resumed, resumed; all used the same parent and physical client.
Parent native transcript: exactly one spawn_agent and one followup_task to that same child.
Child terminal results: FIRST_READY; then FOLLOWUP_OK CATALOG_MEMORY_110.
Accepted native catalog: 7 top-level declarations / 44 functions.
Accepted catalog fingerprint before/after: sha256:eeffd1a561be4d614c6a715154aa3ae3d3679f341bf58ae744401b327cdb9b3f
The retained binding still identifies the same parent, client, and accepted catalog. Canonical native metadata digest was unchanged before and after both automatic continuations.

Shipped CLI verification:
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<isolated-config> pnpm openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:catalog-chain-proof","limit":100}' --json
Result: same logical session; visible CATALOG_CHAIN_OK /root/catalog_child; saved Telegram context/origin retained; hasActiveRun=false; pendingInputs.total=0.

Observed limitation: the two child completion announcements produced two identical visible CATALOG_CHAIN_OK replies. This run proves the requested catalog/thread/child continuity, not exactly-once visible replies or general fallback behavior. Inherited parent history in the child's rollout was not counted as another spawn.

Cleanup: the client exited successfully; the task-owned Gateway stopped cleanly after settlement; its listening port is closed. No production services or data were used.
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(discord): render agent message edits like sends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord `edit` (message tool `action: "edit"` and `openclaw message edit --channel discord`) PATCHes agent-authored content verbatim, while `send` of the same text runs through `prepareDiscordOutboundText`. An edited message therefore renders differently from the message it replaces:

- Markdown tables stay raw pipe text instead of the configured `markdown.tables` mode (Discord default: fenced `code` block).
- CommonMark `__bold__` reaches Discord unchanged, where `__x__` means underline; sends normalize it to `**x**`.
- `channels.discord.mentionAliases` handles (`@alice`) stay plain text instead of `<@id>`.

Tracking issue: #190479. Prior source PR #190018 was closed in favor of that issue with the defect still on main.

## User Impact

Agents that send a status table and later edit it with updated values no longer leave broken raw tables (or underline/broken mentions) in the channel. Edits and sends of the same text now match.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route only the non-`progressSnapshot` edit branch through the same `prepareDiscordOutboundText(...).textWithMentions` path already used by `sendMessageDiscord` and `sendWebhookMessageDiscord`. Progress snapshots stay on the compositor path with inert mentions.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI `openclaw message edit` (Gateway-owned Discord edit) against a local Discord REST loopback

Environment (synthetic only, no real Discord credentials):

- Isolated Gateway `ws://127.0.0.1:18901` (token auth, proof config/state under `/tmp`), Discord REST base `http://127.0.0.1:36557/api/v10`.
- Same edit input on both runs (table + standalone bold + alias):

```text
| svc | state |
| --- | ----- |
| api | up    |

**bold** and ping @alice
```

`channels.discord.mentionAliases.alice` → `123456789012345678`.

**Before (main source, this PR's base behavior):** CLI succeeded; loopback captured `PATCH /channels/222222222222222222/messages/555555555555555555` with **verbatim** content:

```json
{"content":"| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n\n**bold** and ping @alice"}
```

Raw pipes (no code fence), unresolved `@alice`.

**After (this branch head `81a94379e2f`):** same CLI command; loopback captured PATCH with **send-parity** content:

```json
{"content":"```\n| svc | state |\n| --- | ----- |\n| api | up    |\n```\n\n**bold** and ping <@123456789012345678>"}
```

Fenced table, alias expanded to `<@123456789012345678>`, bold left as Discord-native `**bold**`. CLI result `handledBy: "plugin"`, `action: "edit"`.

### Red / green regression (production path)

- `message-bodies.test.ts` case `edits agent content with the same outbound rendering as send`: fails when the source fix is reverted (edit keeps raw table / `@alice`); passes with the fix (edit body equals send body).
- Local: `vitest.extension-discord` on `message-bodies.test.ts`, `runtime.test.ts`, `handle-action.test.ts` — 185 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on both changed files.


### Discord message-surface rendering of the exact PATCH bodies (sanitized)

No live guild or real bot token was used. The image below renders the **exact** before/after PATCH `content` strings captured from the shipped CLI run above, in Discord-style message chrome (raw pipes vs fenced table; unresolved `@alice` vs mention chip for `123456789012345678`).

**Before / After**

![Discord before/after PATCH rendering](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f29ebc8-3f3c-40f5-9be0-0e3c61416b9b)

### Review findings addressed

- Patch quality: no findings; production change is one non-progress branch (+16/−5) plus the regression test (+22).

## Merge Danger

- Narrow: 2 files, one production branch (non-progress edit only).
- Snapshot/progress edit path intentionally unchanged.
- No schema, config, or public API changes.
- Discord Gateway websocket identity is not required for the REST PATCH path exercised above; proof loopback is synthetic and contains no real tokens or guild IDs.

prs.title: fix: reuse admitted worker transcript and cron stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker turns failing at the PostgreSQL thread boundary and Cron session runs reading scratch from a different partition than the scheduler that admitted them.

## User Impact

Worker launch and scheduled session execution retain their admitted transcript and Cron sources. There are no schema migrations, configuration changes, permission changes, or required operator actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the transcript source already held by the history worker instead of reopening the native database on the Gateway thread. Thread the admitting Cron service’s selected store path into session execution; direct callers still resolve their configured store, and explicitly prepared scratch retains precedence. Existing source-custody checks, revocation, and release behavior remain in place. This removes seven net production lines rather than adding another owner.

Integration adapted from Galin Iliev’s requested fixes; commits credit @galiniliev. This PR is independent of the database portability and scheduled-widget changes.

## Evidence

- **Red on the base:** the real worker-launcher fixture failed with “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker” before reaching its launch boundary. The Cron regression selected changed-partition scratch instead of the admitted partition.
- **Green:** 65 tests across the worker launcher (34), PostgreSQL thread-boundary regression (1), transcript source lifetime (5), Cron session execution (15), and Gateway Cron dispatch (10). Fresh and follow-up worker admissions both reach the expected worker-launch boundary without Gateway-thread SQL.
- Core TypeScript plus the Cron, Gateway-server, and Gateway-other test typecheck leaves passed; all nine touched code/routing files passed targeted lint. Formatting and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Independent canonical autoreview completed scoped-clean for P0–P2 with no actionable findings. Review covered the existing history-worker, session-accessor, launcher, and Cron-store contracts.
- Exact 95-line regression allocation; no global baseline increase.

The PostgreSQL boundary regression uses the real native launcher with the PostgreSQL main-thread SQL prohibition enforced; it does **not** claim a live PostgreSQL-provider or remote-worker execution. No live Gateway or operator database was changed. Broad CI and hosted review remain publication-time checks.
