prs.title: improve: bound transcript projection inserts to SQLite limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounds active-transcript projection inserts at the owning SQL boundary so an oversized supplied chunk does not exceed SQLite’s bind parameter limit.

## User Impact

This is maintenance hardening of the existing internal SQL owner. Large projection input stays inside the caller’s existing transaction; rollback and sibling rows are preserved. Current native reconciliation already sends 512-row chunks, finalization catches up at most 512 tail rows, and current database ports rebuild only FTS, not active projection rows. No current end-to-end native port failure is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing 512-row transcript insert limit instead of building one statement for every active row. No new option, API, schema, transaction owner, or competing implementation. This patch is independently reviewable and not a dependency of the database-port correctness change. Adapted from Galin Iliev’s batching fix. The 71-line regression allocation covers the real SQLite limit, row coordinates, rollback, and sibling isolation.

## Evidence

### Defect proof at the SQL owner

- Real-SQLite parameter-limit regression passed (0.266s), including rollback and sibling isolation; all 9 projection tests passed (38.95s wall, mostly transforms), retained from the original qualification.
- Exact baseline 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914 owner was loaded process-locally with unchanged dependencies. Its Git blob cbd995c69f76f9ff1624ed673ad32559d382c124 matches the retained baseline file. It fails the native SQLite fixture with “too many SQL variables”; the fixed owner passes and rollback leaves zero inserted target rows.

```text
BASE:  FAIL projection-bind-limit too many SQL variables
FIXED: PASS projection-bind-limit
```

### Runtime integration qualification

The existing production-worker publication test was selected without source or fixture edits: a cold compressed branch of 520 active messages crosses the native 512-row chunk boundary. Assertions cover exact canonical bytes across close/reopen, active order, FTS identities and mappings, abandoned-branch exclusion, sibling preservation, no-op reconciliation, and zero host data SQL. A second selected test checks failure-before-finalization notification suppression and notification after successful commit. Both selected tests passed: 11.985s for the compressed multi-chunk branch and 2.158s for finalization ordering. Vitest reported 2 passed / 6 deliberately filtered cases and 340.22s total, dominated by cold compiled-worker preparation (270.314s). The wrapper joined cleanup and exited 0 in 394.68s.

```sh
TMPDIR="$PROOF/tmp" \
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH="$PROOF/cache/transcript-publication" \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.publication.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t "publishes a cold compressed multi-chunk branch without host data SQL|publishes the session change only after finalization commits" \
  --reporter=verbose
```

`PROOF` is an isolated task scratch directory; no operator database or live Gateway was used. Actual log excerpt:

```text
✓ publishes a cold compressed multi-chunk branch without host data SQL 11985ms
✓ publishes the session change only after finalization commits 2158ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  2 passed | 6 skipped (8)
Duration  340.22s (transform 95%, tests 4%, import 1%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 394.68s
```

This runtime scenario is compatibility coverage, not a shipped-entry-point reproduction of an oversized active chunk. Its native caller still sends bounded chunks and would also succeed before this patch.

### Source and review qualification

- Qualification checkout: 41653af9e09596f1190724be941cd46d128d6d15. The entire src/config/sessions, src/state, and src/sessions trees match PR head 39b525583b2350cfec178313f9ab99ec770f3b46 exactly, as do scripts, test infrastructure, package metadata, and lockfile. Combined checkout additionally contains independent signed-identity and database-port changes; this is not represented as an exact independent-branch run.
- Core/config test types, focused lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed in original qualification. CI seconds not measured by this local run.
- Independent local review and hosted review of 39b525583b2350cfec178313f9ab99ec770f3b46 found no actionable findings. Hosted patch quality was Platinum, proof Gold.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): keep a lone leftover model inline
prs.body:
Fixes #188469

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI model picker collapsed a provider group's single remaining model behind an "All models (1)" row, so reaching that one model cost an extra click while offering no choice.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat-model-picker-panel.tsx` splits each provider group into `lead` (ranked/visible) and `more` (folded), then renders the "All models" toggle whenever `more.length > 0`. With one leftover the toggle is pure friction: it hides exactly one row and reveals nothing new.

A lone remainder is now appended to `lead`, so it renders inline and the toggle disappears. Groups with two or more folded models keep the existing disclosure behaviour (the `drops the All models row once expanded` cases still cover it), and the unranked-catalog overflow path is unchanged apart from the same single-leftover rule.

## User Impact

Providers that recommend one model and keep one extra model now show both directly; larger catalogs keep the fold.

## Evidence

Head `333c865ea6`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1
9 passed

# new regression with chat-model-picker-panel.tsx reverted to the branch base:
× keeps a lone unranked model inline instead of folding it behind All models
  AssertionError: expected null not to be null
1 failed | 8 skipped

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

Existing fold cases were widened to two leftovers so they still exercise the disclosure; the new case asserts the inline rendering and the absence of the toggle.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Followed the `lead`/`more` split in `chat-model-picker-panel.tsx`, added the single-leftover rule after both grouping passes, and updated the fixtures that relied on a one-entry fold. The implementer understands the code: the fold exists to bound long catalogs, and a one-entry fold only adds a click.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel import guardrails repeatedly parse the same core and extension sources, slowing focused contract checks. This optimization was requested for the test-health lane.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. All **13 existing cases and their assertions** remain. The setup-inclusive single-file median falls from **46.563s to 34.537s**, saving **12.026s (25.83%)**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collect plain module references once per source set while each native parser batch is live, then reuse those references across the existing policy cases. The private-path check keeps unfiltered references; the other policies keep their existing JS/TS-extension and import-meta filtering. Import-equals rejection and diagnostic/comment/example controls remain effective.

The change is confined to one test file. The module-scoped cache holds filenames and plain reference data. Native snapshots retain their existing lifecycle. ## Current integration (November 2, 2026)

Current head: `28c3ad2f2da758d59208c0c699ba1a8c5aaae96c`, retaining the author parent `f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769` and official main `eb4881915a08b3877cd75e3e0f971342e72319df` through a normal merge. Fresh proof at the reviewed integration tree:

- Overlaying current main's production command reproduces the two missing-cleanup failures; all four credential-preservation controls pass. The same existing regression is used without changing assertions.
- The integrated command, related CLI, and native credential-store suites pass **64 tests across three files**. Command RPC transport is controlled; credential operations use the real isolated SQLite owner. This run took **125.04 seconds** including native preparation; the before-control wrapper took **108.38 seconds**.
- Production types, the selected test-consumer closure, production/test typed lint, formatting, and native staged line/growth ratchets pass. The original **86-line** test allocation remains exact; no test or allocation is added by this integration. A fresh independent P0–P2 review of the full six-file introduced delta is scoped clean, and its tree matches the commit.

This new proof covers the command/native-store boundary on Linux with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. The packaged CLI/Gateway capture and released-state upgrade recorded below retain their original `f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769` head. New-head hosted CI and required maintainer/security review are separate.

Related: #189206 (reported by @AdoShan).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated device-token-mismatch warnings after this installation's own device is successfully removed from its default local Gateway.

## User Impact

`devices remove` and `devices clear --yes` now forget the removed local operator credential, so later CLI commands recover through their configured authentication. Other roles and remote Gateway credentials are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read-only RPC clients intentionally do not mutate credential storage. The explicit removal command now captures the existing local operator token before dispatch and conditionally clears it only after the Gateway confirms removal. A concurrently replaced token survives. Credential-store failures are reported without hiding the completed Gateway operation. The existing RPC setup and option type move to a sibling module to satisfy the command runtime’s line-cap ratchet.

This is the default-local operator recovery path; it does not change rotation/revocation, read-only diagnostics, cross-device token delivery, protocol versions, or schemas.

## Evidence

- Private Linux Gateway, normal pairing/native credential persistence, public token rotation, and independent bare CLI processes: before the fix, removal succeeded but the next two commands still retried the rejected cached token. After the fix, removal cleared the cache; both subsequent commands returned JSON without token-mismatch messages or matching Gateway log events. Read-only diagnostics before removal produced no observed credential-file changes; cross-device rotation still withheld the bearer.
- Six command/native-store regressions: before, the two removal assertions failed while four controls passed; after, all six passed. The controls cover another device, an explicit Gateway URL, failed removal, and concurrent credential replacement. All 64 tests across the touched CLI suite and related CLI/store suites passed.
- Core and targeted test types, production/test typed lint, formatting, test-line and max-line ratchets passed. P0–P2 independent review found no actionable defects; subsequent lint-only edits were separately checked for unchanged behavior.
- The required allocation records exactly 86 net new test lines, preserving the base's existing slack. The selected six-case Vitest run took 37.42s before and 42.06s after, including transform/setup; the new test bodies totaled about 12 seconds on this host.

Proof used a trusted source checkout and synthetic isolated state, not an operator Gateway or paid provider. The before/after CLI proof covers Linux's local primary operator flow; macOS and other origins were not exercised. The current main's relevant owner/caller inputs were checked against the pinned validation base.

Validation head: `f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769`, based on official `91695eeb9b73d41834eb6b439af98a5959fc1169`. Before publication, the five relevant CLI/RPC/credential-store inputs on main `c633ec6376e1ce6cdf6268f98d1c86eb9395b074` were byte-identical to that validation base, and a merge-tree check found no conflicts. prs.title: fix(telegram): batch album members that arrive a second apart
prs.body:
Fixes #188353

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram delivers album members about a second apart, but the media-group buffer flushed after the hard-coded 500 ms quiet window. When the next member arrived later, it started a second agent turn that saw only half the album, so the same album produced two replies that could contradict each other.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handleMediaGroup()` scheduled its flush at `MEDIA_GROUP_TIMEOUT_MS` (500 ms) for the first member. The hold added in #115325 only extended the window when a sibling was already sitting in the same lane backlog, so a member that Telegram delivered ~1 s later always arrived after the flush. `mediaGroupFlushMs` is retired (Doctor removes it), so operators had no supported way to widen the window.

The first member now waits a bounded **arrival window** (`MEDIA_GROUP_ARRIVAL_WINDOW_MS = 1_500`) that covers Telegram's per-member delivery gap; later members keep the 500 ms quiet window, so a burst still flushes quickly. The decision lives in `resolveMediaGroupFlushDelays()`, which is the single owner for both windows and keeps the existing `MEDIA_GROUP_MAX_HOLD_MS` (20 s) bound. Test timings still override both windows (`mediaGroupFlushMs`, `mediaGroupArrivalMs`).

## User Impact

A two-photo album now produces one agent turn instead of two, with no change for messages that carry no `media_group_id` (they never take this path).

## Evidence

Head `5b75d45fbf`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-updates.media-group-delays.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.media.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
11 passed

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <3 touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <3 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The contract test pins the scheduling decision: default `{ flushMs: 500, arrivalMs: 1500 }`, a flush-only override applies to both windows, explicit arrival overrides win, and sub-10 ms values clamp to the floor. The existing media suite (9 cases) still passes, so album warnings, failed attachments and the `more`/expand paths are unchanged.

**Known gap:** the end-to-end regression (two members ~1 s apart through the real Telegram ingress) needs `scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --with-ai-package`, which requires a full runtime build; this checkout did not have the space to run it. The decision boundary is proven here; the ingress-level case should run in CI, where that build exists.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Traced the double dispatch to the 500 ms flush plus the backlog-only hold, moved the two-window decision into one helper, and added the contract test. The implementer understands the code: the buffer must tolerate Telegram's per-member delivery gap without widening the window for messages that are not albums.

prs.title: fix(normalization-core): token budget under-counts Tangut, Khitan, and Nushu text
prs.body:
Closes #187849

## What Problem This Solves

The token-budget heuristic undercounts Tangut, Tangut Components, Khitan Small Script, Tangut Supplement and Nushu by eightfold. Their supplementary-plane code points fall through to the ordinary surrogate-pair weight of 2 rather than the existing supplementary-CJK weight of 16.

## User Impact

Large text results in these scripts now cross the same weighted budget thresholds as other supplementary CJK. A built-Gateway comparison demonstrates Tangut tool-result truncation that main skips; existing supplementary CJK and ASCII controls are unchanged. Provider-reported token usage is not changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add U+17000–U+18D0F to the existing supplementary bucket and extend the adjacent Kana range through U+1B2FF to cover Nushu. The lookup-array maximum stays unchanged. No helper, export, type, signature, SDK barrel, configuration, schema or dependency change.

Credit: @coaiMax, the reporter and contributor. Their original commit is retained. Current main was merged because the estimator owner acquired additional token-pressure behavior after the contributor base; the patch remains limited to the existing range table.

## Evidence

[Observed built-Gateway/CLI proof, model-input captures and public tool-card readback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187852#issuecomment-6568661516).

Exact candidate: `a2ed192cccce156ed7efae275f57b138a6969ab7`; frozen main: `ac6af4df297273b4d72f1d85971b5006c8b39530`.

Node 24.22.1 in secretless Docker, fresh isolated profiles/state/config. Built CLI submits `chat.send`; the local OpenAI-compatible provider invokes a declared plugin tool through the advertised public `dispatch_action` contract. The tool returns 6,000 code points. The shipped Gateway applies its existing 16,000-weighted-character live-result cap for the configured 32,768-token model window. The driver does not call a budgeting or truncation helper.

| Actual model input / public assistant readback | Main 1 | Main 2 | Candidate 1 | Candidate 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tangut U+17000 retained | 6000, no truncation | 6000, no truncation | 976, truncated | 976, truncated |
| Existing CJK U+20000 retained | 976, truncated | 976, truncated | 976, truncated | 976, truncated |
| ASCII `x` occurrences | 6004, no truncation | 6004, no truncation | 6004, no truncation | 6004, no truncation |

The ASCII count includes four envelope characters beyond the unchanged 6,000-character tool value. Candidate Tangut receives the shipped “9985 more characters truncated; rerun with narrower args if needed” notice. The actual `chat.history` toolResult card independently changes from its existing 7,999-unit preview on main to a 2,313-unit, 976-code-point budgeted result with that notice on the candidate. This is not merely an estimator replay or a synthetic final-response claim.

The final assistant reply reports facts measured from the provider's received payload. External tool data and provider responses are deterministic local fixtures; no public-provider account, semantic model quality, overflow or automatic-compaction behavior is claimed. Runtime proof covers Tangut; the range regressions cover Khitan and Nushu as well.

90 focused tests passed: 34 normalization cases and 56 truncation cases. Six regression assertions fail on main for the omitted ranges; existing controls pass. Typed lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. Production source hash matches the built candidate. Existing vectors absorb the six script samples rather than adding a duplicated block: production +2/−1 (net +1), tests +4/−6 (net −2), docs +5 against frozen main. No new test file or test-only production seam.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores the old estimates without a storage migration. Blast radius is heuristic budgeting for the newly covered scripts wherever the shared estimator is used; large results may be truncated or compacted sooner. Existing scripts, actual model token reports and public SDK contracts are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: accept signed filesystem identities in recovery receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database-port recovery and local client credential receipt loading when Node exposes a native device or inode identifier as a signed decimal string.

## User Impact

Operators can resume ports and use their existing client credentials on these filesystems. Exact file/root binding remains required: changed identities still refuse admission. No schema version, credential restoration, permission, or retention policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writers already serialize Node’s bigint identities verbatim. Both readers now accept the same signed decimal representation without normalization or precision loss. Adapted from Galin Iliev’s portability work.

Simplification: retain the two existing parsing owners; add no helper, state, or compatibility path. Production delta +6/-4 lines; regression delta +68 lines, allocated for native identity round trips and replacement rejection.

## Evidence

- Baseline: signed receipt round trips fail (2 cases); signed recovery manifest publication fails (2 cases).
- Fixed: 30 tests passed across receipt and recovery suites; wrapper wall time 3.51s, test time approximately 0.23s. Existing logs were retained rather than rerun solely for green. CI seconds not measured in this local qualification.
- Core and infra test typechecks passed. Focused four-file lint, format, and git diff --check passed in the original qualification.
- Independent local review found no actionable findings. Hosted review of head b612f55ebf698a6cc87eec12526fc50ae798d539 also found no actionable findings and rated patch quality Platinum; proof remains owner-boundary coverage, not an affected-filesystem command run.
- Additional read-only physical qualification: this Linux host uses btrfs for the workspace and scratch. Native bigint stat reported dev=39 and positive inode values; tmpfs/devtmpfs/proc/sysfs/vfat samples were also nonnegative. The existence of /dev/fuse does not establish an affected mounted filesystem. No mount, injected filesystem, or host changes were used.

### Source qualification and observed excerpts

The qualification checkout was 41653af9e09596f1190724be941cd46d128d6d15, not the independent PR branch. Both changed production owners and both focused test files are byte-identical (Git blob comparison) to PR head b612f55ebf698a6cc87eec12526fc50ae798d539. The combined checkout also contains transcript batching and database-port changes; no combined port run is attributed to this PR alone.

```text
BASE receipt: Tests 2 failed | 9 passed (11)
FIXED receipt: Tests 11 passed (11)
FIXED recovery: Tests 19 passed (19)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 3.51s
physical workspace: dev=39, ino=2868267822, filesystem=btrfs, negative=false
```

### Remaining proof limitation

No authorized filesystem returning a negative native device/inode identifier was available, so the shipped credential/port command on an affected physical filesystem has not been demonstrated. The signed device/inode regression cases use controlled observations at the existing receipt/manifest owners and check that identity replacement remains rejected. These are owner-boundary regression evidence, not physical filesystem proof.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

prs.body:
Fixes #190481.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram sticker sends ignoring the existing `silent: true` message-tool option.

## User Impact

Requested silent stickers now carry Telegram's notification-suppression option, matching ordinary silent sends. Telegram defines this option as a notification without sound; ordinary sticker sends retain their existing request shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing option through the Telegram action and its existing sticker sender. Read it once with the same nonthrowing boolean parser already used by text and poll sends.

Credit to @yetval for the report and original fix in #190005, which was closed unmerged with explicit permission to reuse it. This submission adds the missing running-Gateway and agent-message-tool proof requested there. No contributor fork code was executed.

## Evidence

- **Actual built Gateway and agent:** on main `bc097bf6404f34be1e57cdee8bd0b2d7f59a3070` and the final patch, ran `node openclaw.mjs agent --agent main --session-key <fresh-key> --message "Send the synthetic fixture sticker exactly once using the declared message tool." --json --timeout 120`. Each variant used a fresh session. The real agent called the declared `message` tool, through the Telegram plugin and real grammY HTTP client. External model responses used the official scripted Chat Completions fixture; Telegram used its public `apiRoot` setting pointed at a loopback Bot API fixture. No tool, runtime owner, or transport was replaced.

  | Message-tool argument | Main request | Patched request |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `silent: true` | `disable_notification` absent | `disable_notification: true` |
  | `silent: false` | absent | absent |
  | omitted | absent | absent |

  All six runs finished with CLI `status: "ok"`, a successful `message` terminal receipt, captured model tool calls/results, one physical sticker request each, and matching run IDs in Gateway logs. Both owned Gateways shut down cleanly.
- **Regression:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **39 tests** in **68.3 seconds wall time**. The new three-case HTTP regression first failed on the original production code for the missing flag, while both default-preservation controls passed. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/send.telegram-http.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **45 tests** in **58.3 seconds wall time**. Canonical wrappers used the verified repository-pinned Bun fork; the Gateway used Node 24.22.1. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41385355367) passed for head `94a32e7bc990eab4cd0abf00a823ad6635b4e1d0`, including the selected Telegram extension bundle and changed-code lane. Hosted Codex code review also completed without findings.
- **Checks:** changed-file format and typed lint, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p extensions/telegram/tsconfig.json`, a changed-test typecheck extending the existing extension-test config, test-line and line-cap ratchets against the pinned base, and `git diff --check` passed. The **15 net regression lines** receive a separate exact allocation; the shared ceiling is unchanged.
- **Build:** `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` passed on both base and final patch; the final Gateway run used the rebuilt candidate.
- **Independent review:** canonical local `autoreview`, complete four-file working-tree diff against the pinned base, **P0–P2**, one pass: **scoped-clean**, no findings. Frozen source inputs remained unchanged throughout review.

**Limits:** no real Telegram/Test Server account or device notification behavior was exercised. This proves the actual Gateway-to-HTTP wire contract. Full repository and Telegram-extension suites were not run locally; broad validation remains with PR CI.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid repeated config copies on catalog refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog refreshes repeatedly clone and freeze unchanged runtime and authored config during plugin registration, adding avoidable allocation pressure.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190564

## User Impact

This candidate reduces repeated config preparation during catalog refreshes. **No allocation or RSS saving is established yet; do not merge until the acceptance workload passes.** No config, storage, or operator action changes. This PR is open for CI because draft status skips the test jobs; readiness does not waive the performance hold.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker already publishes each restored config/source pair through the runtime snapshot owner, which retains an immutable capture across equivalent publications. Registration was still consuming each fresh transport clone and missing that reuse.

Pass the publisher's captured config into both initial registration and expanded provider-scope registration. The existing runtime-plugin loader retrieves its paired authored source. Keep the transport config for request-local synthetic-auth receipts, credentials, and catalog processing. Remote revisions still rebuild registrations; no new cache or invalidation policy is introduced.

Production delta: +11 lines. The explicit parameter carries the existing owner's captured pair across both registration paths. Test delta: +35 lines in the existing real-worker fixture, with a matching dedicated test-line allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source review: publisher equivalence includes runtime values, authored values, and resolution provenance. Existing capture projection preserves older generations' authored source.
- Independent read-only review of the full change: no actionable findings; executable proof pending.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of `7b5f7c6a4d8f1595a11cea77bf05179e235a26c7..98bda84c16b945fae15670f6bf5f4af8107ebef6`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The review included the unchanged publication, capture, projection, synthetic-auth, registration, and fingerprint owners; it explicitly notes unrun tests and measurements. This uses the documented fallback because the local ClawSweeper checkout contains unrelated untracked work. Request one hosted review when validation is complete and this PR is ready.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- New real-worker regression expects distinct registration captures `1, 1, 2, 2` across two catalog revisions, a config change, and another catalog revision, while registration count advances `1, 2, 3, 4`.
- Baseline negative control, candidate tests, types, lint, and compiled build: **not run yet**. The baseline Testbox request queued and was stopped under the current remote-proof policy; no test payload ran. Both attempted local dependency sources failed qualification. Allocation cleanup is confirmed completed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41385350891
- Required sibling proof: worker secrets and provenance, rejected refresh recovery, released/neighboring generations, runtime-source projection, policy rewrites, and synthetic-auth scope.
- Test wall time and CI seconds: pending.

### Performance acceptance — declared before measurement

Baseline: `7b5f7c6a4d8f1595a11cea77bf05179e235a26c7`. Candidate: this PR's reviewed head.

Use separate complete compiled builds and identical dependency inputs. Run five serial paired fresh-process comparisons, alternating order BC, CB, BC, CB, BC. Record actual CPU availability/affinity/quota, usable RAM, host load, Node version, source/build identities, and all results.

Committed workload:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts \
  --built-worker "$BUILD_ROOT" --output "$FRESH_FIXTURE_ROOT" \
  --workspaces 1 --models 1000 --configured-models 1000 \
  --providers 2 --discovery-models 100 --runtime-plugin \
  --task-rounds 20 --measure-tasks
```

Run separate allocation-profile pairs with the same workload plus `--sample-allocation`; do not mix profiled timings into the timing comparison. The 19 warm operations are catalog rebuilds after remote-revision changes, not chat turns or cached reads.

Acceptance:
- Equal catalog/runtime hashes and row counts for every paired operation; clean worker closure and process exit.
- At least 5% lower median warm allocated bytes, consistent with eliminating repeated registration captures.
- Report cold latency and post-GC heap separately from warm median/p95 latency, worker CPU, peak/final ordinary heap, GC time/p95, and aggregate RSS, with spread and all paired cells.
- Every adverse metric stays visible. A worse metric requires explicit owner acceptance before landing. Any 20% regression in any paired cell is a stop, not a noise dismissal.
- No unchanged rerun to replace an adverse result. Diagnostic attribution does not replace acceptance.
- This workload proves catalog-worker behavior. It does not establish whole-Gateway RSS, under-load client latency, or a smaller-device memory budget.

Results: pending.

### Next diagnostic

Generated plugin catalogs are emitted by `models-config.plan.ts` with `JSON.stringify`, then `ModelRegistry.loadCustomModels` sends them through two JSONC replacement passes. Investigate a strict-JSON fast path in `parseModelCatalogJson`, retaining its existing JSONC path after a syntax error. This is a source-grounded follow-up, not part of this patch or a measured saving.

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.10.9 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2584 -> 2588 on main `0405ef3`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `8eb4b7b` (on main `f980e01`). Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade and CLI:** 2026.10.9 from npm builds the index; this branch keeps its scope hash with no `excludePaths` (the re-chunk comes from main's #168867), then drops the 7 reports after `excludePaths` plus `memory index`; the curated note stays first and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.10.9 OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.595 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.489 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.477 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.467 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.456 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.445 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.10.9): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":5} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8eb4b7b) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.10.9 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v25 -> v38 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 11 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index chunking implementation changed (owner: openclaw, code: chunking_version) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn (a local chat-completions stub that calls `memory_search` once) opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within 1-2 s across runs and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" Done. # memory_search tool result (from the stub's log): path: memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~1s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +145, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch now merges main `0405ef3` at `2d45aa2`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. On `2d45aa2`, the test-line ratchet passes locally (slack 12,703, this PR +145 under its allocation), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `config:docs:check` pass, and the touched tests plus `memory-files-worker.test.ts`, `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` and `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` (files main also changed) pass. `checks-node-changed` on `a63b2b5` failed in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` after main's #188833 referenced an untyped SDK entrypoint in a guide; main fixed it in #188937, and that test passes locally on `2d45aa2`. prs.title: fix(macos): canvas present ignores a new placement until the next present
prs.body:
Closes #187483

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, `canvas present` with a placement does not move a Canvas panel that is already open; the requested placement only appears on the next `canvas present` or `canvas navigate`, even one without a placement.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent that repositions or resizes an open Canvas panel sees it move right away, and the panel remembers that new frame. Presents without a placement behave as before and use the remembered frame.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `CanvasManager.show` re-presented an existing panel before storing the new placement. `presentAnchoredPanel` → `repositionPanel` reads `preferredPlacement` and persists the resulting frame, so it applied and saved the previous placement. A newly created panel already stored the placement first, which is why only repeated presents were affected.
- The fix stores the placement first on both paths, then presents. `CanvasManager.show` is the only caller of `presentAnchoredPanel` outside `showCanvas`; `canvas.present`, `canvas.navigate` and the Debug settings entry points all go through it, so there is no sibling path with the same order.
- The new test `repeated present applies and remembers its own placement` (`CanvasWindowSmokeTests`) drives the real `CanvasManager.shared.show` three times for one session (placement A, placement B, no placement) and checks the panel frame and the remembered frame after each. When the runner has no screen, it uses a fixed area (the panel then keeps the requested frame unconstrained); with a screen it uses the screen's visible frame. It removes its frame default and its Canvas session folder.
- No docs change: `docs/platforms/mac/canvas.md` only says `canvas.present` accepts placement arguments.

## Evidence

Run on an AWS EC2 Mac (mac-m4.metal, macOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Apple M4) at main `6d6a2518bc1`, with `swift test --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --filter …` over SSH:

- main + new test only: **fails** at the second present. The open panel stays at the first placement, and that stale frame is what gets remembered:

```
✘ Test "repeated present applies and remembers its own placement" recorded an issue at CanvasWindowSmokeTests.swift:87:9: Expectation failed: reused.shown == second
↳   reused.shown → (40.0, 40.0, 400.0, 400.0)
✘ Test "repeated present applies and remembers its own placement" recorded an issue at CanvasWindowSmokeTests.swift:88:9: Expectation failed: reused.remembered == second
✘ Test run with 4 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.131 seconds with 2 issues.
```

- with the fix: **passes** (`CanvasWindowSmokeTests|WindowPlacementTests|LowCoverageHelperTests`: 28 of 29 pass). The one failure, `WindowPlacementTests` "ensure on screen does not move visible window", requires a screen (`screen != nil`) and fails the same way on main over SSH without this change.
- The same red and green results on main `e8d136f4`, run twice.
- `swift build --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passes. `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: only the two existing `file_length` errors in `DashboardManager.swift` and `GatewayConnection.swift`, which are on main without this change. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` (commit hook) passes.

### Live app run

AWS EC2 Mac (mac2.metal, macOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Apple M1), desktop session over VNC (1024x768). The app (`swift build --product OpenClaw`, debug) runs as a paired node of a local loopback Gateway. Each step is a real `openclaw nodes canvas present --node <mac> --target openclaw-canvas://main/placement.html` call, with `--x/--y/--width/--height` where shown. Coordinates are AppKit screen points (origin bottom-left). Same Gateway and node for both builds; only the app binary differs (main `6d6a2518bc1` vs this branch). Every call returned `canvas present ok`.

| Step | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1. present `--x 40 --y 200 --width 380 --height 380` (new panel) | ![main 1 placement A](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1883670b-8352-4bf7-981f-f7b92accbeea) | ![this PR 1 placement A](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db93cc48-df44-4c62-b31f-e05c24db7dc7) |
| 2. present `--x 560 --y 150 --width 420 --height 440` (panel already open) | ![main 2 placement B](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e0a11ad-01da-4211-8a1a-1f2568a64384) | ![this PR 2 placement B](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69711a57-767b-4230-a5cb-9b11799f0349) |
| 3. present with no placement | ![main 3 no placement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c0b47ba-fca2-4f7e-974b-be0fb0fb04c2) | ![this PR 3 no placement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42c6f586-0000-4153-97c9-1a9ce4f35be6) |

Proof artifice: the `canvas.present` node commands were sent from the CLI (the same `node.invoke` path the agent's canvas tool uses), not by a model turn; the Gateway was a local test Gateway with no model provider; `placement.html` is a test page I wrote into the session's Canvas folder.

On main, step 2 leaves the panel at step 1's frame, and step 3 (no placement) moves it to step 2's frame. With this PR, step 2 moves the panel at once and step 3 keeps it there.

Remembered frame (`defaults read OpenClaw openclaw.canvas.frame.agent_main_main`) after each step, same run:

```
# main 6d6a2518bc1
after A: (40,200,380,380)
after B: (40,200,380,380)
after plain: (560,150,420,440)

# this PR
after A: (40,200,380,380)
after B: (560,150,420,440)
after plain: (560,150,420,440)
```

prs.title: feat: gate personal instructions on private session audience
prs.body:
Related: #186068, #186067, #186066, #186065; parent #186050.

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps automatically selected personal USER.md content and canonical personal-instructions chat operations out of shared or unverified initial audiences, without replacing the existing human-profile registry, Settings editor, or session profile-selection rules.

## User Impact

This draft now contains three bounded improvements:

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the selected personal file. The final common filter also withholds personal-marked/origin hook entries. Shared defaults and existing allowlists remain intact.
2. The personal-file handler refuses agent-tool get/set operations with known group/channel origins or execution targets. Both actions return content; both are checked before file access or mutation.
3. Initial delivery also requires committed host sharing facts: an existing creator-private **Draft**, no public share, and a canonical creator matching the selected profile (bootstrap) or authenticated editor (chat tool). Shared/read-only/suggest, foreign-creator, and unverified audiences withhold the overlay or direct chat operations to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**. Distinct delegated origin and execution sessions must both qualify. A direct label alone is insufficient.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** Session selection remains assigned human owner, otherwise authenticated human creator; a new sender does not replace it. The authenticated editor remains separate from that selection. Canonical aliases and immutable creator stamps stay with their existing owners.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** These checks cover initial loader delivery and the canonical file handler's response/write boundary. Admission is not retained through every provider submission, tool-history append, or native thread. Widening an already-used private conversation can expose prior context or generated responses. Generic file/shell/native capabilities, inferred-to-file confinement, Knowledge/LCM audience admission, and retained history remain unqualified. Trusted administrators/host access are not hostile tenants. This is proposed narrowing for owner review, not upstream design acceptance. Nothing is merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small admission composes the existing profile catalog and retained session-sharing facts; no second registry, cache, SQL schema, configuration, public SDK contract, or model-supplied identity/audience argument is introduced. The existing public-share fact now participates in the internal sharing projection and its invalidation. Bootstrap checks after reads and hooks; the personal-file owner composes audience checks with its existing requester/role/agent and safe-writer pre-mutation assertion.

Author simplification retained one profile/file owner and one session-facts owner, rather than another authorization manager. Against base `194b10349b12ee8480e3837b2c90f28803f362cd`: production +179/−22 (net +157), tests +462/−21 (net +441), docs +421/−7. Necessary growth is the bounded admission, its two consumers, and owning-boundary regressions. The larger proposal remains documentation, not speculative Knowledge/history/permission implementation. Test budget passes without allocation or baseline changes.

## Evidence for this follow-up

Published head: `aa13a00d8f2e861f6496b27639ebfb9cbb2f0731`; draft remains open. Remote verification found all **13 expected changed paths**, without evidence files or dependency caches. The commit retains the requested human co-author credit.

- **Red → green:** the shared-web bootstrap regression originally exposed Alice's personal content after the session became shared. Committed Draft/sharing/public-link/creator facts now control delivery; no private overlay is admitted merely because chat type is direct. A public share added during a bootstrap hook invalidates the prepared release.
- **51 Gateway tests passed across two files**: 50 production tool → in-process dispatch → handler → guarded filesystem cases, plus the real isolated Gateway two-person Settings fixture. The tool suite uses synthetic admitted authority/mocked profile facts with real committed session rows. Shared web audiences, foreign creator, shared origin/private execution, and audience changes before read release or final write are denied. The real WebSocket fixture independently verifies each authenticated person's own file, other-file/shared-file denial, and final role/merge revocation. This is not a live-model/group-channel pass.
- **19/19 affected personal/remote bootstrap cases passed** in the final consumer rerun (13.36 s wrapper), including profile ordering, aliases, budgets, group/cron/subagent exclusion, metadata admission/revocation, and remote file provenance. The remote transport executes locally and does not qualify a remote-worker or native runtime.
- Other unchanged consumers passed in the broader invocation: memory provenance **4**, sharing-projection lifecycle **8**, collected-turn selection **2**, prompt-prefix stability **14**. That invocation executed eight files, with 96 passes and two fixture failures; it was not a clean whole-run pass. The fixtures were corrected at their owners: asynchronous cleanup drains SQLite borrowers before closing, and the remote provenance mock classifies the requested personal paths after supplying real session config. The affected 19-case rerun above is the repair proof; no second whole-flow rerun is claimed.
- An explicit **agents-support carrier run passed 5/5** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/harness/workspace-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The mixed-path invocation had not executed that suite. These are rendering/carrier tests with a mocked bootstrap producer, not native execution or audience-isolation E2E.
- Core, Gateway-methods, agents-root and remote/agents-other TypeScript checks passed. Scoped type-aware lint, targeted formatting, two-document MDX compilation, whitespace and exact-base staged test-line ratchet passed (24,614 lines of slack; no exception). Lint's missing braces were fixed, not suppressed.
- Fresh bound Auto Review inspected the full staged candidate and complete owner source context against the exact base: **scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings**. It did not execute tests. The old hosted documentation review does not certify this runtime head. Current-head CI is separate and is not claimed green here.

## Dependencies and owner decisions still required

- **Knowledge:** #186455 is agent-private conversation access, not person isolation. Separate draft #189822 at `ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4` proposes person/agent grants selecting **one space**, not a private-plus-shared union; it disables bootstrap and excludes broad file/execution/history capabilities in its qualified profile. Do not duplicate that lane. Its current body reports an executed installed Knowledge–LosslessClaw 1.2.0 save/compact/restart/grep/evidence/replay fixture—new bounded #186065 evidence, not merely source. Those are its author's reported results, not this PR's execution; the shared-owner continuity fixture and separate P/Q cases do not prove the combined person-private/shared history scenario. It remains unmerged/proposed.
- **Host/profile owners:** accept or revise this Draft-only initial-delivery rule, then define run/provider/tool-history lifetime admission and safe handling when a conversation that already contains personal context is shared. Do not silently rewrite history or reassign personalization.
- **Knowledge/LCM owners:** settle private-plus-shared person/audience grants and supported explicit-ID/delegated expansion authority, with pinned installed-version proof. Knowledge remains the durable record/evidence owner; LosslessClaw remains history/compaction owner. No private LCM database reader is added.
- **File/sandbox/harness owners:** choose and qualify a capability profile where every enabled direct read/write/exec/native route respects personal roots and inferred records cannot overwrite user-authored instructions. Prompt filtering or a read-only mount is not that boundary.
- **Runtime qualification:** real-model embedded and generic CLI execution, native Codex, delegated history, ACP, realtime, remote-worker, and Windows E2E remain untested here. No Gateway, local remote-file adapter, carrier, or prefix pass transfers to those paths. Keep the complete two-person fixture open pending these contracts and proofs. No merge, auto-merge, or deployment is requested.

Implementation proposal and named owner map: [authenticated profile audience](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/aa13a00d8f2e861f6496b27639ebfb9cbb2f0731/docs/architecture/authenticated-profile-audience.md).

<details>
<summary>Retained earlier-revision evidence and publication history (not current-head qualification)</summary>

Related: #186068, #186067, #186066, #186065; parent #186050.

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps personal USER.md content out of known group/channel bootstrap and personal-instructions tool results while preserving the authenticated person's Settings editor and stable session profile selection.

## User Impact

**This draft contains two bounded runtime improvements:**

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the automatically selected personal file. The common post-hook filter also withholds personal-marked or personal-origin entries. Shared defaults and existing subagent/cron allowlists remain intact.
2. The canonical personal-file handler refuses agent-tool get/set calls whose host-captured origin or execution session is a known group/channel. Both operations return profile content, so both are checked before file access or mutation. A group-origin request cannot evade this check by executing in another session; a direct-origin request cannot use a group execution target. The error points to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** No new model-supplied audience/profile parameter, registry, SDK contract, configuration, or schema is introduced. Session-selected owner/creator and authenticated editor remain separate. Host-resolved direct chat type retains precedence over a same-session group-looking key. This deliberately narrows chat-tool availability in known groups/channels and remains a draft for owner review—not a claim of upstream design acceptance.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** Direct/unknown/shared-web audiences, generic filesystem/native paths, previously delivered history, person-private Knowledge grants, LCM expansion, and inference-to-file confinement remain unchanged or unqualified. #186455 grants agent-private conversation access, not person isolation. Nothing is merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap classification now serves the pre-read decision and final file filter. The additional tool-result check belongs in the existing users.personalFile owner, where current requester/role/agent, hash conflict, cancellation and final-write assertions already run. It consumes the host's existing requester origin and execution key, not model arguments or another identity manager. The tool's description names the Settings fallback; its action schema is unchanged.

Production delta against refreshed base: +43/-11 (net +32). Regression delta: +167 lines across the two existing owner suites. Existing test-line budget passes without an allocation or baseline change. The wider architecture and implementation proposal stays clearly separated from these two implemented slices.

## Evidence

Base: `194b10349b12ee8480e3837b2c90f28803f362cd`. Current head: `7c4889ba5130d3bf074aab481e0aff0abc5b74f4`. All eight published file blobs match the validated local bytes; no task evidence or dependency caches are in the current diff.

### Current tool-result follow-up

- **Red → green:** new get/set regressions failed before the handler change: get returned Alice's private instructions, and set persisted and returned the replacement. Both pass after the fix. The final matrix covers authoritative group/channel origin, origin-key fallback, execution-key fallback, group-origin delegation, and direct-origin execution in a group; denied operations open no filesystem root and leave Alice, Bob, and shared files unchanged. A same-session authoritative direct override still succeeds.
- **60 tests passed across three files**: the 45-case personal-file/chat-tool suite, real isolated Gateway session-only self-edit fixture, and 14 prompt-prefix tests. The combined command took 59.13 s including compilation. A lint-required simplification of the test table preserved all cases; the final 45-case owner suite rerun passed in 12.00 s including compilation (about 0.9 s of test cases).
- The tool fixture uses the production tool → in-process dispatcher → handler → safe filesystem path, with synthetic admitted authority/profile state. Separately, the real isolated Gateway fixture confirms both authenticated people retain Settings self-edit access and role/merge revocation protection. It is not a live group-channel/model test, and captured-origin test cases are not a native delegation E2E pass.
- Core and Gateway-methods test TypeScript checks, scoped oxlint, targeted oxfmt, two-document MDX compilation, exact-base test-line ratchet, and diff whitespace checks pass. The first follow-up lint found an inefficient test-fixture map/spread; the fixture was simplified rather than suppressing the rule. Final lint and typing ran serially and exited 0.
- Fresh bound Auto Review over the full candidate against the exact base, with complete handler/tool/caller/origin/parser context: no P0–P2 findings, scoped-clean. It inspected source/tests but did not execute them. The subsequent fixture-table rewrite was mechanical and rerun green. The earlier hosted documentation review does not certify this runtime code.

### Retained bootstrap proof

The unchanged bootstrap slice previously passed 58 tests across seven files. Its three new owner regressions were red before the fix and green afterward; canonical Alice/Bob files, no personal opens, hook filtering, shared defaults, session selection, CLI transport, and prompt-prefix checks were covered. Those results remain scoped to that slice, not a second execution of the full combined feature. Its initial static run's preparation timeout/retained lock was recovered after process retirement, and serialized checks passed without bypassing a guard.

### Remaining qualification

No new real-model embedded, CLI executable, native Codex, delegated-history, ACP, realtime, remote-worker, or Windows E2E pass is claimed. Neither a common-loader pass nor a synthetic caller-origin case transfers to another harness. The complete two-person Knowledge–LosslessClaw save/compact/restart/recall/direct-file-denial scenario remains unqualified. Keep this draft pending owner review and the named live/harness proof; no merge/deploy is requested. Current-head CI is separate from the local checks above.

<details>
<summary>Current follow-up commands</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/users-personal-file.test.ts src/gateway/server.personal-instructions.session-scopes.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/users-personal-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/gateway/server-methods/users-personal-file.ts src/gateway/server-methods/users-personal-file.test.ts src/agents/tools/personal-instructions-tool.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --incremental
```

</details>

### Publication history

The initial documentation publication inadvertently included six synthetic baseline-evidence files. Commit `bd6029b8dcca12c68d722f28b106c11de5f4abdd` removed them from the current diff; the original commit remains in history. Those were synthetic fixtures and historical technical reporting, not live profile data. Retained local originals remain unchanged. The old 93-test packet is historical evidence, not a pass for the current code or wider proposal.


</details>

## Contributor credit

Requested by @TheAngryPit in the linked discussion.

prs.title: fix(format): round relative day labels from the original duration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: relative age labels (`2d ago`, `3d ago`) show one day more than the real age during the ~30 minutes before each day boundary, because hours are rounded from already-rounded minutes and days from already-rounded hours.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw status`, `openclaw sessions`, `openclaw skills list`, `openclaw nodes status`, the TUI, and Control UI timestamps show accurate multi-day ages (2d 11h now renders `2d ago` instead of `3d ago`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatTimeAgo` and `bucketRelativeTimeMs` now round hours and days once from the original duration. The open minute-boundary PR #186745 is left untouched; this only removes the extra hour/day rounding step. Pinned outputs (47h → `47h ago`, 48h → `2d ago`, 7d → `7d ago`) are unchanged.

Related: #186781

## Evidence

Same shipped modules, red/green on Node 24.14 + tsx:

- base (`origin/main` 80dead1a1e):
  - 214_185_600ms (2d 11h 29m 45.6s) → `3d ago`, `{ value: 3, unit: "day" }`
  - 300_585_600ms (3d 11h 29m 45.6s) → `4d ago`, `{ value: 4, unit: "day" }`
- with this patch:
  - 214_185_600ms → `2d ago`, `{ value: 2, unit: "day" }`
  - 300_585_600ms → `3d ago`, `{ value: 3, unit: "day" }`
  - 47h → `47h ago`, 48h → `2d ago`, 7d → `7d ago`

Regression cases added in `src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts` and `packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts`; `oxfmt --check` passes on all four files.

Not run locally: full vitest suite — this branch requires Node >= 24.16.0 and the host has 24.14.0; CI covers it.

prs.title: fix(workboard): clarify status when releasing claims
prs.body:
Supersedes #155650, thanks @mfurkanakinci.

Related: #155367

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: callers can mistake `workboard_release` without `status` for finishing or pausing work even though the card keeps its current status.

## User Impact

The tool description and status-field help now explain that omitting `status` only clears the claim and preserves the current status, including `running`. Callers can pass a status such as `todo`, `ready`, or `review` when pausing or handing off work. Runtime defaults remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue explicitly accepts clarifying this contract. Workboard already permits running cards without claims, release preserves status, and reclaim separately defaults running cards to ready. Inferring a new destination on release would change those semantics. The tool and documentation now describe the existing distinction.

## Evidence

- On main `00ac8e8642788759fab41461504e6ef3466656a0`, the extended real-tool/SQLite lifecycle regression confirms claim-only release preserves `running` and clears the persisted claim, then fails on the ambiguous tool description/schema. Result: 1 failed, 20 passed; 44.66 s wall time including cold worker compilation.
- With the clarification, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/tools.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes: 21 Workboard tests and 14 prefix-stability tests. Workboard file duration: 7.21 s; combined wall time: 27.46 s. The regression also retains explicit release-to-review coverage.
- Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox supplied focused proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41380977727. Touched-file oxlint passes (2 files, 3.32 s); touched-file format checks pass (3 files); `git diff --check` passes. PR CI workflow passed on the exact head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41383837477. CI job durations: extension test bundle 192 s, changed-node tests 283 s, PostgreSQL conformance shards 1,258–1,408 s. All 47 applicable checks passed.
- Post-CI autoreview P0–P3 reported `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings, on committed range `00ac8e8642788759fab41461504e6ef3466656a0..9d4957fe29cfea9f29f6c611f7c3014abc9dc1dc`. prs.title: improve(update): reduce POSIX package backup cleanup overhead
prs.body:
Related: #184658 (supporting research only; this does not diagnose or close the native Windows delay).

## What Problem This Solves

POSIX npm updates do avoidable work while removing the previous installed package during final cleanup.

## User Impact

Updates driven by a version containing this change spend less work retiring package backups, without changing configuration or migration requirements.

The installed updater owns this cleanup: installing the fixed candidate cannot accelerate an already-running older updater. Native Windows uses a different activation path and is not covered. The measured improvement below is for one cleanup phase, not total update time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing admitted SQLite reader for one artifact's removal rather than opening a new journal connection for every removed entry. Every callback still reads the current journal record and checks object identity and live executor authority. Each read releases its snapshot; the retained connection closes on success or error before settlement or archival.

There is no cached authorization decision, reduced check frequency, deferred cleanup, or deadline change. Shared removal cadence, Windows compensation, updater-runtime retention, and terminal-output ordering remain unchanged. This isolates a POSIX-only cost found while supporting DonnieFi's investigation, not a competing Windows repair.

## Evidence

The following commands and measurements were executed by Codex in Mert Başar's isolated Linux/WSL2/Docker environment. RoboClaw verified the source transfer and reused those receipts; it did not rerun or claim independent execution of the tests.

Measured baseline: `a0f10e38dea4244cfb22ad3f63139ef540e51587`. Original measured candidate: `d64336801477b849cb019c4bf721eedfdc5a6c3a`. The transferred candidate files match their recorded SHA-256 values.

### Qualified cleanup measurements

**Node 24.22.1**, five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, fresh process and fixture for each sample, the same committed **2,000-file / 40-directory** workload, warm/uncontrolled filesystem caches, no profiler in this series.

| Retirement metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 2,324.893 ms | 1,704.147 ms (−26.70%) |
| p95/max wall time | 2,499.576 ms | 1,858.149 ms |
| Median process CPU | 2,464.444 ms | 1,886.597 ms (−23.45%) |
| p95/max process CPU | 2,739.229 ms | 1,981.209 ms |
| Journal connections opened/closed, each sample | 2,091 / 2,091 | 35 / 35 |
| Journal preparations, each sample | 8,343 | 2,178 |
| Fresh current-record reads, each sample | 2,084 | 2,084 |

No recorded median/p95 metric regressed by 20% or more. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum, not a robust tail estimate. The original stronger preparation-scaling criterion is only partly met: the existing per-read journal-mode preparation remains. Total preparations are not constant.

The workload exercises real publication/retirement owners with private synthetic trees and an inert recovery-runtime fixture. It does not measure whole-update latency or establish a Windows/macOS improvement.

<details>
<summary>Reproducible workload and focused-test receipt</summary>

With supported Node 24.22.1 selected on PATH, the committed opt-in measurement entrypoint is:

```sh
OPENCLAW_BENCH_RETIREMENT=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \

Existing SQLite-owner proof covers snapshot-lock release and writer visibility. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and patch checks passed on the donor candidate.

</details>

- Published stable **2026.10.8 → candidate** completed with matching build identity and durable run, readiness HTTP 200, preserved synthetic durable conversation, and intended incognito cleanup. This is compatibility proof; cleanup in that first hop still belongs to the old installed driver.

prs.title: improve(gateway): reject scoped capability URLs with an empty inner path segment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizePluginNodeCapabilityScopedUrl` is supposed to give the built-in route checks, plugin route matching, and any `req.url` re-parse the same path. That stops being true when the path after the capability starts with an empty segment (`//...`): the one request ends up meaning two different paths.

## User Impact

No behavior change for normal requests, and no known exploit. It's a fail-closed guard: a scoped URL like `/__openclaw__/cap/<cap>//api/...` now returns 401 instead of being routed with an inconsistent path. Valid single-slash scoped links are unaffected (proof below).

## Why This Change Was Made

The function sets `url.pathname` to the inner path and builds the rewritten `req.url` from it, but never rejects an inner path whose first segment is empty. A leading `//` (literal, an extra slash, or a backslash the URL pathname setter turns into `/`) makes the rewritten URL parse as protocol-relative, so `new URL("//api/x", base).pathname` is `/x` and `api` becomes the host. The raw scoped path and the `startsWith`/exact checks still see `//api/x`, but a `req.url` re-parse sees `/x`, so they no longer agree. Simplest fix is to treat it as a malformed scoped path, like the other bad shapes the function already rejects.

## Evidence

**Real gateway proof.** Added `rejects a scoped url with an empty leading path segment before dispatch` in `server.plugin-node-capability-auth.test.ts`. It stands up the real `createGatewayHttpServer` on loopback with a live node capability and drives it with real HTTP requests:

- valid single-slash link `/__openclaw__/cap/active-node/__openclaw__/canvas/` -> `200 ok` (reaches the canvas handler)
- same live capability with a doubled leading slash `/__openclaw__/cap/active-node//__openclaw__/canvas/` (and the triple-slash form) -> `401`, rejected at the scoped-URL gate before capability auth or dispatch

Before/after through that same real-server test:

```
without the fix:  AssertionError: expected 404 to be 401   (malformed request falls through to the 404 path)
with the fix:     Tests  1 passed
```

The 404-vs-401 difference is the point: pre-fix the malformed URL slips past the scoped-URL gate and is handled downstream; post-fix it is rejected up front (`server-http.ts:314` and `server-http-upgrades.ts:295` both reject `malformedScopedPath` before routing).

**Unit coverage.** `plugin-node-capability.test.ts` adds a case for the `//`, `///`, and backslash `/\` forms; it fails against the pre-change normalizer (`expected false to be true`) and passes with it. Full file: 28 passed. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files.

Why only a leading empty segment matters:

| inner path | after `url.pathname =` | `new URL(rewritten).pathname` | same? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/channels/secret` | `/api/channels/secret` | `/api/channels/secret` | yes |
| `//api/channels/secret` | `//api/channels/secret` | `/channels/secret` | no |
| `/\api/x` | `//api/x` | `/x` | no |
| `/api//channels` | `/api//channels` | `/api//channels` | yes |

prs.title: fix(workboard): clarify release-without-status claim semantics
prs.body:
Closes #155367

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `workboard_release` looked like it finished/paused/handed off work when callers omitted `status`, even though the card stayed `running` after the claim was cleared.

## User Impact

User impact: callers and operators can tell from the tool contract that omitting `status` only clears the claim and preserves the current card status, so they must pass `todo`/`ready`/`review` (or similar) when they want an un-running state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Kept the existing preserve-status behavior and made the tool description plus `status` parameter docs state that contract explicitly, with a small code comment and a regression covering claim -> release without status.

## Evidence

- Focused workboard extension tests: `pnpm test:extension workboard -- extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts extensions/workboard/src/tools.test.ts`
- Result: 2 files passed, 175 tests passed
- Regression asserts claim `todo` -> `running`, then `releaseClaim` without `status` leaves `status: "running"` and clears `metadata.claim`

## Real-Setup Behavior Proof (patched head `bd55b597`)

A behavior-capture script was executed through the repo's real Vitest + SQLite toolchain, driving `createWorkboardTools` wrapped in the production `guardWorkboardToolsForWorkspaceAccess`, then a live claim -> `releaseClaim` without status against a real SQLite-backed `WorkboardStore`.

Registered `workboard_release` definition as an agent receives it:
> Release this agent's Workboard claim. Omitting status preserves the current card status and only clears the claim; pass status (for example todo, ready, or review) when finishing, pausing, or handing off to an un-running state.

`status` parameter description:
> Optional next card status after release. When omitted, the current status is preserved and only the claim is cleared; pass a status such as todo, ready, or review to leave an un-running state.

Live store behavior (real SQLite store, `create({status:"todo"})` -> `claim()` -> `releaseClaim()` with no status):

```json
{
  "statusAfterClaim": "running",
  "releaseCalledWithStatus": false,
  "statusAfterReleaseWithoutStatus": "running",
  "claimAfterRelease": null
}
```

The card kept `running` and only the claim was cleared. Control check: an explicit `releaseClaim(..., {status:"review"})` on the same card correctly moved it to `review`.

Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 1 passed (1)` — `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workboard/proof/pr-155650.proof.test.ts` (proof capture harness lives only in the local capture tree, not in this diff).
