prs.title: refactor(skill-workshop): move Workshop settings into the plugin config
prs.body:
## Problem

Skill Workshop is moving from core into the bundled `skill-workshop` plugin. Its settings still live in the core config key `skills.workshop` (core zod schema, labels, help and tiers), so the plugin cannot own them, and the house pattern for plugin settings (`plugins.entries.<id>.config` validated by the manifest `configSchema`) does not apply.

## Fix

- **Plugin owns its settings:** `extensions/skill-workshop/openclaw.plugin.json` gains a `configSchema` (`autonomous.mode`, `autonomous.channelNotices`, `maxSkillBytes`) and the labels and help as `uiHints`.
- **Core Doctor moves existing settings** (`moveSkillWorkshopSettings` in `src/config/skill-workshop-plugin-migration.ts`, registered last in the core Workshop rules):
  - A core legacy rule flags `skills.workshop`, so the refusal names `openclaw doctor --fix`.
  - The move runs after the existing core Workshop rules in the same pass (older `autonomous.enabled` shapes, retired proposal settings, and the repair of `skill-workshop` policy written while Workshop was built in), moves the three settings into `plugins.entries.skill-workshop.config`, lets settings already in the plugin config win, drops anything else under the retired key, and records `meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin`.
  - **Why core, not a plugin Doctor contract:** `openclaw update` candidate admission previews only core Doctor migrations (`projectHeartbeatConfigForUpdateAdmission` runs with `pluginContracts: false`). A plugin-owned move made admission refuse every config that still had `skills.workshop`, so users could not update. Core already owned every other `skills.workshop` rule, and core-owned moves into plugin config have precedent (web search, TTS).
- **Core cutover:** `skills.workshop` leaves the root schema, types, labels, help and tiers. `resolveSkillWorkshopConfig`, the one reader, reads the plugin config. The Control UI mode toggle reads and writes the plugin path. The update failure report names the retired `workshop` key instead of hiding it.
- **Docs:** Skill Workshop, self-learning, skills config and the Doctor migration table.

No database schema, protocol or stored-row change.

## Update behavior

- `openclaw update` runs Doctor in a fresh process, which moves the settings with the normal config backup.
- A config that still has `skills.workshop` is refused at startup with the Doctor hint until Doctor runs (the same behavior as the earlier `canvasHost` move). A foreground `gateway run` offers the repair.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Published upgrade: the default `published-upgrade-survivor` Docker lane now seeds `skills.workshop` (`mode: off`, `maxSkillBytes: 8000`) with the `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI and updates that real install to this candidate with `openclaw update`. Admission accepts the config, Doctor moves it, the Gateway starts, and `assert-config` finds both settings under the plugin config after the update and in the final survival check | pass; before the core move, admission refused the update with `skills: unrecognized key workshop` |
| Update admission (`update-command-admit.workshop.test.ts`): a config with `skills.workshop`, alone and with the retired heartbeat key a 2026.10.9 base config carries, is admitted for candidate Doctor without rewriting files | pass; both refuse without the core move |
| Published config cell: the `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI writes `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: off` and `maxSkillBytes: 8000`; this build refuses the config with the Doctor hint; `openclaw doctor --fix` moves both into the plugin config with the marker; the config validates; `config get` reads `off`; a second Doctor run changes nothing; the new path accepts `config set` and the old path is refused | pass |
| Real Doctor flow (`doctor-config-flow.skill-workshop-migration.test.ts`): current settings, the retired `enabled` switch, retired proposal settings, and a stale pre-2026.10 plugin entry all land in plugin config; the runtime resolver reads the moved values; a second run is a no-op | pass |
| Core rule unit tests: move, existing plugin settings win, a stale pre-2026.10 entry is replaced (the earlier repair drops it), the retired `enabled` switch maps then moves | pass |
| Config contract suites: the plugin path validates through the manifest schema and refuses invalid values; the retired key is refused; the full Doctor chain lands in plugin config; labels and help come from the manifest | pass |
| All Workshop suites, Gateway review and learning e2e, Control UI Workshop e2e, after moving ~40 call sites to the plugin path | pass |
| `pnpm check:changed` | pass, except the production dead-export scan, which flags `assertSafeSqliteRuntime` in a file this PR does not touch |

The upgrade-survivor base recipe seeds Workshop settings for baselines from 2026.10.5 on (`upgrade-survivor-config-recipe.test.ts`). The `cron-owner-doctor` upgrade lane also asserts that the configured Workshop mode survives the update (either path, so frozen older candidates still pass). The `dreaming-cron-doctor` lane's post-Doctor runtime fixture now writes the Workshop mode where the installed candidate's manifest says it belongs (plugin config, or `skills.workshop` for older candidates). That lane fails on current main independently, before reaching this writer: its fixture predates the `heartbeatEnabled` receipt field from #181659, so the writer change is not yet exercised end to end. The published 2026.10.5 release-notes link to `#workshop-skills-workshop` is kept with an explicit anchor.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

prs.title: fix: recognize Gateway metadata in web-search request assertions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The mocked OpenAI web-search Docker regression reports “missing success request” when the Gateway adds its conversation metadata before the exact test prompt. The timestamp-only selector misses the intended request even when it uses the expected model, native web search and nonminimal reasoning.

## User Impact

This repairs the test assertion so the scenario can continue past request selection. Production requests, prompts and configuration are unchanged. Activity recaps and quoted prompts remain excluded, and the native tool and reasoning checks still inspect the selected request independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selector now recognizes the Gateway’s marked conversation header and compact fenced JSON block before comparing the complete underlying prompt. It requires valid JSON, the closing fence and blank separator; arbitrary prefixes or marker substrings cannot select a request.

The existing CLI suite covers framed success and malformed or quoted counterexamples. Its measured net test growth is accounted for by an equal per-change test-line allocation, needed to preserve the strict negative controls around the new accepted framing.

## Evidence

Remote changed-file formatting/lint, selected type checks and the test-line ratchet passed. The unchanged assertion CLI rejected the captured Gateway input with “missing success request.” The replay preserves the captured input, model, reasoning and tool types; the original full request log was removed by normal scenario cleanup.

The new CLI suite is red against the original selector (four framed cases fail, 13 controls pass) and green with this change. The owner and unchanged success/rejection client suites pass all 25 tests. The corrected CLI also accepts the captured input unchanged. The green two-file suite took 2.89 seconds; the single-file red regression took 3.05 seconds.

The shared canonical Docker run with the terminal mock repair in #190803 now passes the success client, actual-request selector, forced-schema-rejection client and correlated provider-error log checks. An earlier run failed the obsolete raw-prose log assertion; the parent repair aligns that assertion with metadata-only logging while preserving the client’s schema-error checks. This is a composed fixture result, not a head-alone Docker pass. Hosted CI for this PR is green, and independent review is clean.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): cached composer context ring [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload of an active chat or dashboard deep link initially omits the composer's context-usage ring, then inserts it after live admission and fades it in for another 200 ms. This is one late visible change in the measured dashboard reload waterfall.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the meter's four display inputs in the existing scoped per-session browser snapshot, and use them while current usage is unavailable. Complete live usage replaces the saved display in place. Remove only the ring's decorative mount fade; hover, color and popover motion remain.

The optional `sessionState.contextUsage` field stays within projection 14. Older records omit it and render from live usage; older readers ignore it inside the non-strict session-state object. Session, connection and account invalidation remain with the existing snapshot owner. Cached display does not authorize sending or compaction. No server storage, Gateway protocol or configuration changes.

## User Impact

Warm reloads can show the saved context value with the composer immediately, with live changes filling the same control. Cold loads retain current data-loading behavior and show the ring at full opacity when usage arrives.

## Evidence

**Experiment; do not merge. Measurement and broad validation are pending.**

Acceptance: quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, fixed for both arms; active-session native plugin fixture; 11 interleaved warm-reload pairs plus A/A on chat and dashboard. Final ring value must be present at first composer paint in at least 10/11 candidate reloads per route, with inspected synthetic compositor frames. Report all per-pair deltas, medians/IQRs, hello-handled, FCP, first/final rows, visible transcript, LoAF, CLS and snapshot growth. Separate Team-scale bench secondaries use the live-fast latency profile.

Focused proof: first cached-composer-frame regression fails on baseline with no ring/label and passes with the change; changed live usage updates the same ring element. Existing meter color/stale-usage scenario and retention/focus scenario pass. Snapshot persistence 46/46 passes. Exact final-head timings, full UI e2e, changed-file gate, synthetic before/after crops and PR CI will be added after measurement. Independent autoreview is clean through P2.

Runtime UI delta: +33 net LOC; the necessary growth retains display inputs, extends the existing parser/equality and carries them to the meter. The superseded 200 ms mount animation is deleted. Diagnostic script changes are reported separately. A 52-line exact test allocation extends existing scenarios rather than adding parallel setup.

prs.title: fix(talk): plugin-started GPT-Live sessions fail as "authentication failed" on ChatGPT OAuth
prs.body:
Closes #187772

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-started GPT-Live sessions using ChatGPT OAuth disconnect immediately with `OpenAI GPT-Live authentication failed` even with an unexpired profile. Whole-request plugin invocation views turn ordinary configuration into Proxies; the real provider-auth/config lookup then fails structured cloning.

## Changes and User Impact

Retains hannnnn-l's producer repair: keep bridge request data plain and bind only callbacks to their original transport plugin instance. Removes the redundant `audioFormat` copy at the worker boundary now that the producer no longer supplies a Proxy.

The function signature, public types and SDK exports are unchanged. No OAuth, credential-selection, redaction, configuration, provider-default or prompt change. A separate request for enhanced auth diagnostics remains outside this repair.

## Evidence

Maintainer reproduction used built main `ac6af4df297273b4d72f1d85971b5006c8b39530` and contributor production head `2dff88fc06e95155792b57b73af1802daf1fb103` in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Subsequent changes only consolidate tests and document the existing data/callback boundary.

A **purpose-built transport plugin**, installed normally with `plugins install --link --force --accept-capabilities`, registers a real Gateway method and calls the public provider resolver and `createRealtimeVoiceBridgeSession`. It stores a synthetic, unexpired OAuth profile through the existing public auth-store API in isolated task-owned state. Transcript/ready callbacks read a plugin-instance-scoped `createPluginRuntimeStore`, not a global marker.

After dependency installation/build, the container has only an internal Docker network and no external route. `chatgpt.com` and `api.openai.com` resolve to a local HTTPS/WSS fixture with an explicitly trusted synthetic TLS certificate. The fixture accepts the real `/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls` SDP request, answers it with a real `werift` WebRTC peer and serves the real sideband. No auth resolver, request object, media worker or bridge implementation is mocked or patched; no hand-built Proxy and no real account credentials.

Observed eight sessions:

| Gateway plugin invocation | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth, `gpt-live-1-codex`, run 1 | authentication failed | connected; ready + final transcript in original plugin scope |
| OAuth, `gpt-live-1-codex`, run 2 | authentication failed | connected; ready + final transcript in original plugin scope |
| Platform-key working-flow control, run 1 | connected; original callback scope | connected; original callback scope |
| Platform-key working-flow control, run 2 | connected; original callback scope | connected; original callback scope |

Captured candidate callbacks, both OAuth runs:

```json
{"event":"ready","scope":"original-transport-plugin"}
{"role":"user","text":"Synthetic scope proof transcript.","final":true,"scope":"original-transport-plugin"}
```

The TLS fixture recorded two 650-byte OAuth SDP offers, matching synthetic account headers, `/v1/live/rtc_scopeproof` sideband upgrades, and two real WebRTC peers reaching `connected`. Platform controls reached `/v1/live/sessions`. All sessions closed through the normal `session.closed` receipt. Config was plain before shared-session construction on both refs.

This proves native transport startup and callback ownership against local external-protocol fixtures, **not live ChatGPT/Discord acceptance, real account authentication or speech accuracy**. No live channel delivery claim. The contributor's earlier release/main/shared-auth-store/Talk observations remain contributor-supplied evidence in the original commit/PR discussion; this maintainer run does not claim to repeat those extra scenarios.

## Focused Checks

- Existing cross-plugin callback regression extended with the actual `captureRuntimeConfig` clone boundary: main fails with `DataCloneError`; candidate passes. Callback and agent-consult instance isolation assertions remain.
- Candidate session-runtime suite: 25 tests passed; final compact regression passed again (1.48 s Vitest duration, 25 ms test execution).
- Worker suite: managed-proxy success/refusal and early retirement passed. One existing wall-clock pacing case failed locally: `workerDuringStall` was 7, expected at least 10. The **same case on pinned main failed with 6, expected at least 10**, at the same assertion (`realtime-quicksilver-socket-worker.test.ts:70`). No pacing/timer/assertion logic is changed; the removed worker copy only copied the same plain format values. This local environmental timing failure is disclosed, not claimed as a passing suite or suppressed. Hosted CI will judge the exact pushed head.
- Changed test formatting passed. No broad local typecheck or CI reruns.

Smallest-fix pass: consolidated the contributor's separate clone test into existing plugin-scope coverage, keeping the real regression without duplicate setup. Removed the artificial worker Proxy input while retaining proxy admission/audio assertions. Whole-PR production delta **+3** (16 added / 13 removed), tests **net 0**, docs **+4**.

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: a revert restores the old request wrapping; no persistent-data or schema change. Blast radius is shared realtime bridge construction for plugin transports (including Discord and Voice Call). Callback scope, cancellation and retirement remain owned by the existing plugin/session lifecycle; ordinary request data no longer receives invocation Proxies. Talk/non-plugin data and Platform-key flows retain their existing contract.

prs.body:
## Problem

On Linux hosts without a systemd user session (Docker dev containers, Codespaces, WSL without systemd), every `openclaw` command was refused whenever runtime artifacts needed rebuilding — on the first run and after any edit under `src/`:

```text
Local runtime artifact publication failed: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified. Run `openclaw gateway status --deep`, stop the affected Gateway with `openclaw gateway stop`, ...
Caused by: ServiceInspectionError: No supported service manager detected.
```

No Gateway was ever installed or started on such hosts, so there is nothing running to protect.

## Root cause

`withGatewayRuntimeArtifactPublication` calls `readGatewayServiceState(...)` with `requireEffective: true`. On a managerless host the systemd adapter throws `ServiceInspectionError("service-manager-unavailable")` instead of returning a state, and the publication preflight treated any inspection failure as "cannot verify a running Gateway" → `refuse()`. The existing `absent` fast path (which already falls through to lock/port checks) requires observing a returned state with `runtime.missingUnit === true`, which is impossible to obtain when the manager itself is missing.

## Fix

Catch `ServiceInspectionError` with reason `service-manager-unavailable` around the state read and adopt the daemon's own absent service state shape (`missingUnit: true`, `not-loaded`, `running: false`) so publication falls through to the active-lock and port checks it already performs. Every other inspection failure (including `systemd-user-bus-unavailable`, which may be transient) still refuses.

## Testing

- New regression: publication succeeds when `readCommand` rejects with `service-manager-unavailable` (fails on main with the exact reported refusal; 1 file, 32 tests pass on the branch)
- New guard: publication still refuses when only the user bus is unavailable
- `oxlint` clean on both files
- Full typecheck/boundary-dts could not complete locally (4 GB container OOM in `plugin-sdk boundary dts`, exit 13); requesting CI verdict on those

Fixes #190061

prs.title: fix(update): Gateway stays stopped after the updater process dies mid-update
prs.body:
Refs #164800. Supersedes #186328 and #186341 (two earlier drafts, consolidated and rebased onto current `main`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the managed Gateway stays stopped until reboot when the `openclaw update` process dies (SIGKILL, OOM, a killed process group) during a managed update.

## User Impact

User impact: if the updater dies before, during, or after the package swap, the still-running handoff helper finishes or undoes the update and brings the Gateway back with no manual step. If the helper died too, `openclaw update repair` recovers right away (instead of refusing for 45 minutes) and starts the Gateway that the update stopped. A Gateway its operator stopped, a recorded named data risk, lost ownership, or an unverifiable runtime still keep the Gateway stopped, with the next step named.

## Why This Change Was Made

On current `main` the helper treats an updater signal exit as "no verified recovery result" and leaves the parked service stopped; its terminal bookkeeping loads the installed package, which is missing mid-swap; repair waits out a 45-minute grace even when both owners are proven dead; and repair finalizes with `restart: false`.

- The helper now owns recovery after an updater signal or missing result. Bookkeeping runs from its staged runtime. An untouched publication is retired and the original Gateway restored; an interrupted publication is completed forward through the sealed publication owner, the same run is finalized, then the managed Gateway is restarted and verified.
- `update repair` is the backstop when the helper is dead too: it reclaims the handoff immediately when every recorded owner is proven dead (unknown custody keeps the grace), identifies an orphaned child lease by its owning run (adoption drops a dead updater from the run's drivers), and starts the Gateway only when update history records that the update itself stopped it without a later start. Both owners read the same stop evidence (`update-run-gateway-stop.ts`); no new stop protocol or schema.
- Post-core repair can migrate the state schema past the helper's staged reader, so every ledger read and write after repair, including the stop-intent check, goes through a fresh process of the installed candidate runtime (the same rule the terminal writer already follows). An older candidate without the run listing falls back to the staged reader.
- `upsertStep` moves to its own module so the step owner stays off the Control UI import graph.

Rejected: treating a signal as unrecoverable; inferring restart permission from an inactive unit; importing bookkeeping from the package being swapped; a second stop policy for repair.

LOC vs base `9b5c4e89ca7`: production +854/−251, tests +827/−95, docs +82/−14. Growth is the crash-recovery owner plus its boundary proof.

## Evidence

Live Linux proof on AWS Crabbox (three leases, all stopped) (systemd user Gateway, npm-global install, update started through the Gateway's `update.run`, targets served by a loopback registry, `SIGKILL` sent to the `openclaw update` tree at each point). RED = builds of `main` (`9b5c4e89ca7`); GREEN = this head.

| Kill point | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before package publication | Gateway stopped, never restarted | restored on the original version after 130 s |
| mid publication | Gateway stopped, installed package **and** `openclaw` launcher missing | publication completed, Gateway ready on the new version after 175–185 s |
| during post-swap Doctor | Gateway stopped, run `failed`/`managed-service-handoff-failed` | Gateway ready on the new version after 175–180 s, run `succeeded`/`managed-service-handoff-recovered` |
| helper **and** updater killed | — | Gateway stays down (no live owner); immediate `openclaw update repair --yes` exits 0 and the Gateway is ready |

A follow-up `openclaw update repair` after each recovered run exited 0 for the before/mid cases; after the Doctor case, a repair started 0 s after recovery refused once with "Handoff descendants remain alive" (short-lived post-recovery processes, Gateway healthy); this transient was not re-probed.

The group case first failed with "Cannot identify handoff run": the killed updater's child leases outlived recovery and the run's adopted driver list no longer named the dead updater. Fixed in this PR (repair matches a child lease to the run that owns it) and re-proven above.

The mid, Doctor and group rows were re-run on `1c4cb1cd151` after the installed-runtime ledger change, with the same results. Later commits are CI fixes covered by the test suites below: repair only engages Gateway restoration when update history records an update-owned stop (Doctor keeps reporting other stopped services, as on `main`), an unmanaged service (non-default state dir) yields a named next step instead of failing repair, the helper again refuses before ownership transfer when the installed runtime is missing, and foreground origin checks keep using the installed runtime.

Tests: 32 update test files pass locally (including every file that failed in the first CI run) (handoff interrupted/recovery/lifecycle/termination/triage, repair service and command, ledger compaction, capture receipts, interruption, reconciliation, cleanup-repair). New cases fail on `main`: SIGKILL recovery before/mid/after publication, native-stop group-death repair, operator-stop and named-data-risk negatives, orphaned child-lease identification, and a `state-migrated-no-rollback` run whose refused recovery left the service stopped (#188303 shape). Core typecheck, oxlint (core shard), oxfmt, line-cap ratchet pass. `$autoreview` (Codex, P0–P1) scoped-clean on `1c4cb1cd151`. An independent Codex review raised two P1s: (1) post-repair reads through the staged runtime fail after a schema migration — fixed in this PR as described above; (2) repair could restart a Gateway an operator manually started and stopped *after* a crashed update was already reconciled — accepted edge case: it needs an explicit `openclaw update repair` after that manual cycle, the result is a running Gateway the operator can stop again, and avoiding it would need a new startup receipt on terminal runs.

Known gaps:
- No macOS/launchd or Windows live run. #184480 / the Windows `validating`-phase stall on #164800 is a different failure (a live but stalled updater) and is not addressed here.
- No live run of a schema-changing update; the installed-runtime ledger path is covered by the same-schema live runs and the boundary tests. A kill that lands after post-swap Doctor has migrated the schema but before the helper notices still reads stop intent through the staged runtime first; that case ends with the Gateway stopped and `openclaw update repair` (proven above) restores it.
- The helper that starts the update must contain this change; installed 2026.10.x helpers keep the old behavior for their first hop.

prs.title: fix(agents): Fast mode unavailable for Anthropic API keys from config or environment
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native apps hide or disable the Fast mode control, and the Control UI default-model settings omit Fast, when the Anthropic API key comes from the config file (`models.providers.anthropic.apiKey`) or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead of an auth profile.

## User Impact

User impact: users with an Anthropic API key in their config or environment can turn Fast on from the Android, iOS and macOS apps and choose it in the Control UI default-model settings, the same as users with an auth profile. The Control UI chat and `/fast` already worked and are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog passed the selected auth mode to provider Fast policies unchanged. That mode is `"api_key"` for an auth profile but `"api-key"` for a config or environment key, and the Anthropic Fast policy accepts only `"api_key"`, so `models.list` published no `supportsFastMode` for those keys. The fix normalizes the mode once where the host builds the policy context, using the existing normalizer that runtime choice and Doctor already use. This is the Fast-control sibling of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164556, which fixed the same mismatch for the Ultrafast picker gate.

<details>
<summary>Owner choice and alternatives</summary>

- Request construction already passes `"api_key"` for any non-OAuth Anthropic key, so only the catalog and the request disagreed. With this change, every provider policy sees one spelling, the policy cache keys on the normalized mode, and modes the normalizer does not know pass through unchanged.
- The producer keeps `"api-key"`: it is the config `auth` vocabulary that other consumers read and already normalize, so changing it there would touch each of them for no user-visible gain. Accepting both spellings in the Anthropic policy instead would push the two spellings onto every third-party policy. The Anthropic policy is the only bundled Fast policy that reads `authMode`.
- The `selectedCredential.requirement` that https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164556 used cannot replace `authMode` here: it is `"api-key"` or `"subscription"` and does not tell OAuth (no Fast) from a token (unknown).
- The plugin SDK runtime-hooks page now states that an API key reports `authMode: "api_key"` whatever its source.

</details>

## Evidence

Tested at `3625fd3292c` (base `main` at `5342923d897`).

**Gateway catalog.** For each key source, an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port, synthetic key, no provider call) answered `models.list` on the base and on this branch:

| Key source | Before `supportsFastMode` | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models.providers.anthropic.apiKey` | absent | `true` |
| same, with `auth: "api-key"` | absent | `true` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | absent | `true` |
| auth profile (`api_key`) | `true` | `true` |

Rows per source (claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-4-6 as listed): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/fast-support-before-after.txt

**Android client.** A scripted run on an Android 16 emulator, wiped before each side, with the same app build on both sides and only the Gateway checkout differing. The key was in `models.providers.anthropic.apiKey`. The script paired through "Set up manually", opened Chat with `claude-opus-4-6`, opened the Effort sheet, tapped Fast mode, and then read the session's stored `fastMode` from the Gateway state. The control checks (the model in the composer, the Fast mode row in the sheet) were met on both sides.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fast mode switch after the tap | **off** (disabled) | on |
| session `fastMode` after the tap | **unset** | `true` |

![Effort sheet after tapping Fast mode, Before (left) and After (right)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/fast-switch-before-after.png)

Full screens: [Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/before-2-after-tap.png), [After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/after-2-after-tap.png).

**Tests.** The new case in `src/agents/model-fast-mode.test.ts` resolves Fast support with `selectedAuthMode: "api-key"` against the real Anthropic policy. It fails on the base (`expected undefined to be true`) and passes with the fix; the other 8 tests in the file pass on both. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

<details>
<summary>Checks, test time and review</summary>

| Test file | Local `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/model-fast-mode.test.ts` | 9 passed, wall 33.8 s | 3.92 s (Vitest duration; 5.33 s for the shard, `checks-node-changed-2`) |

- oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, the test-lines ratchet (6374242 against the 6390973 ceiling) and `git diff --check`. No `vi.mock` was added.
- Review: a local autoreview pass (Codex, reasoning medium, P0 to P2) over the full branch range `5342923d897..3625fd3292c` found no issues.

</details>

Not covered:
- The Fast request mapping itself was not exercised: native Anthropic Fast requires the public Anthropic endpoint and a real key. This change does not touch the request path, which already passed `"api_key"`.
- Only the Android emulator was run. iOS and macOS use a shared Effort control that is disabled by the same `supportsFastMode`. The Control UI default-model settings require `supportsFastMode === true` for their Auto and On options. The Control UI chat was not affected, because it falls back to a provider list when support is unknown.

prs.title: fix(audit): keep writer alive after malformed event
prs.body:
Closes #160734

## Summary
- stop treating one non-cloneable `record-event` payload as a process-wide audit-writer failure
- continue reporting the malformed payload through the existing error callback
- add regression coverage proving a later valid audit event is still accepted and persisted

## Root cause
The audit writer cloned queued requests with `structuredClone`. A `DataCloneError` from a `record-event` set the private `unavailable` latch, causing every subsequent audit request to be rejected for the lifetime of the process.

The other request types already reject only the offending payload. This change makes `record-event` follow the same recovery behavior.

## Safety
No queue, persistence, redaction, or error-reporting semantics are changed for valid requests. Only the permanent latch is removed for serialization failures.

## Validation
Added a focused regression that submits a non-cloneable event, verifies rejection, then submits a valid event and verifies it is persisted.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Performance CI can retain a failure from an early diagnostics snapshot after the required span finishes during shutdown. The corrected Kova source preserves that snapshot as a historical phase, which the current report adapter rejects in otherwise valid filtered reports.

## User Impact

Canonical and trusted Performance runs use the completed-diagnostics correction while retaining the registry fix, dependency graph, and calibrated resource limits. Legacy source selection and custom-ref credential restrictions stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both defaults select the same immutable calibrated backport of openclaw/Kova#235: openclaw/Kova@869493d1be0dcf10b7ddf96371cf35239a9efbd6. The report adapter recognizes only its historical timeline phase, validates the collector shape, and excludes it from scenario work. Command results, cleanup, coverage, profiling, and resource checks still determine whether a report is tolerable.

## Evidence

The actual baseline resolver selects the previous source. The maintained gate CLI accepts its valid report fixture, then rejects it after adding the exact phase emitted by the new source; the corrected adapter accepts that same input. Malformed phases, metadata-only records, failed commands, and resource-sample drift remain rejected.

Remote checks passed: workflow/security checks, exact test-line allocation, seven selected type families, and 126 related tests in a single-worker run (13.96 seconds). The actual resolver and public Git-owner fetch select the exact new commit and tree. Independent engineering review and [required hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41383246918) passed.

Source checks cover nine diagnostics/failure controls, CLI serialization, existing shutdown/resource/retention checks, and 21 snapshots on Linux. The earlier live registry result remains 2 PASS/1 FAIL; this fixture-driven validation does not establish a full Performance or release-validation pass.

prs.title: fix(skills): explain repair requirement after Workshop read
prs.body:
Closes #152285

## What Problem This Solves

A planned Skill Workshop edit can read and prepare an exact patch, then fail because those actions do not establish the separate run-usage requirement for foreground repair.

## User Impact

The tool description, action schema, prepared context, and rejection now explain the run-usage requirement. The rejection directs a complete, visible skill body to a pending full-body update proposal. For an oversized skill whose body is omitted, it directs the operator to inspect through CLI or other full-content access. Publication still requires the user's explicit apply request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous action description implied that reading or preparing a patch was enough for the next patch call. The existing guard correctly rejects an unused skill but did not explain the distinction or a viable recovery path. The authorization check and proposal policy are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Inspected the run-usage guard, provider-visible description/schema, prompt publication rule, and prior review of the closed overlapping PR #153285. This patch addresses its two guidance findings: explicit apply authorization and omitted-body recovery.
- Branch based on upstream `2e37299b`, with only guidance/error text changed in three files.
- A local OpenClaw checkout and Gateway runtime were unavailable here. No focused suite or after-fix model authoring transcript is claimed. This is a candidate requiring real behavior proof and review before merge.

## Review follow-up (October 4, 2026)

The complete head diff changes only four guidance/error strings across the tool description, prepared context, rejection message, and action description. `skill-workshop-tool-schema.ts` changes a tool parameter description; it does not alter the action enum, accepted parameter types, database schema, persisted representation, migration, or apply/run-usage guards. The review's stored-data migration flag is not supported by this diff; no data migration is required for these text changes.

The recorded CI failure is in two Control UI E2E jobs: plugin catalog search times out during locator.fill, and session-progress target liveness expects 1 but observes 0. Those logs do not establish causation by the Workshop text patch. No passing rerun is claimed; the GitHub integration cannot rerun upstream Actions jobs (403 Resource not accessible by integration).

Required live proof remains outstanding: a real Workshop authoring turn must show unused-skill repair refused with the new guidance, a complete full-body update left pending, and apply only following explicit user authorization. This host has no ready OpenClaw Gateway/dependency installation or live authoring fixture. Source inspection is not represented as runtime proof. This PR is not yet ready to merge.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

## Evidence

<!-- forone-current-submission:start -->
### Current integration status — 2026-11-02 JST

Current head: `85a3886496e8fc93ec3c222dafb349fe0d47fd6f`. A normal merge of prior head `761ae32fa4fc53430925166c293cce9914ea79d1` with pinned official main `afbe0a8e8f2cc7f9e5cc751a5bcc92a1c74abd30` resolves the native-confirmed conflict in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`. The official generator/check pair passes. Non-generated feature additions/removals are unchanged; implementation and test inputs are byte-identical to the parent.

Official allocation counter: **Test lines OK: 6386630; ceiling: 6399023; slack: 12393.** The selected main's scalar and allocation tree are unchanged. Diff and secret gates pass. [Exact-current-head required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41383683322) **passed**, with zero failed/pending lanes at `2026-11-02T03:50:00.824931+00:00`. No workflow rerun was requested.

Earlier local controls and substantive reviews retain their original-head scope as documented below; they were not rerun or counted as fresh tests.

No new Gateway/employee runtime execution is claimed for this mechanical merge. No employee runtime, private patch or package distribution changed. Product/permission/SDK adoption remains with upstream maintainers.

<details>
<summary>Retained prior source and proof evidence (historical head scope)</summary>

prs.title: fix(database): keep migration archive capture responsive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes migration captures losing their renewable Gateway suspension when large filesystem archive preparation blocks the capture process.

## User Impact

Externally quiesced SQLite migration capture keeps renewing the existing suspension while archive creation and verification run. Cancellation joins the child before returning. Existing source-artifact preservation, PostgreSQL refusal, exact snapshots, restore behavior, and schema39 remain unchanged. No live Gateway changes or schema migration are required; the capturing binary must contain this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture now delegates blocking archive work to the existing update inspection subprocess owner with a 30-minute deadline, instead of introducing another process lifecycle. The child explicitly calls `verifyBackupArchive` before its bounded verified receipt; the archive creation helper does not consume `verify: true`. The parent keeps its existing revalidation and manifest-publication checks.

Simplification removed in-process archive execution and its ineffective verify flag. The launcher, wiring, and worker share the existing inspection lifecycle. The dedicated 133-line test allocation protects renewal, child settlement, archive validity, and caller-relative workspace contents without changing the shared baseline scalar.

## Evidence

- Review correction at `bad61007fb0b0d18b6e32ba9525a4172b1bb0a70` preserves the caller’s effective path base through the existing `withUserPathBaseDirectory` owner. A real compiled-child archive test failed on the prior head: expected `caller workspace contents`, received an empty string (14.904s test, 62.26s wrapper). With the fix, both WAL/DELETE archives contain the intended relative workspace bytes; all 25 capture/renewal tests pass (136.98s wrapper). Core and command-test types, three-file type-aware lint, format, whitespace and the exact 133-line allocation pass. Fresh canonical independent autoreview of this repair against `5508ac43d4af0b811fcc5e056eeefd29bebba97c`, with full path/inspection owner context: scoped-clean P0–P2. The original head passed hosted CI; the repaired head requires its own CI.

- Focused repository test runner: all 31 tests passed across exact capture, quiesced WAL/DELETE capture, and suspension renewal. Both blocked-child cases passed (620 ms completion; 35 ms renewal-failure cancellation). Real quiesced captures passed full archive validation and byte/identity preservation checks (5.987 s WAL; 4.223 s DELETE). Infra group wall time 256.97 s, command group 20.95 s; cold compiled-child preparation 171.11 s under shared-host I/O contention. CI seconds unavailable.
- Production `tsconfig.core.json` and command-test `tsconfig.core.test.commands.json` typechecks passed.
- Focused type-aware lint passed on all six changed TypeScript files (172.91 s). Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Post-lint regression recheck passed all 44 renewal/diagnostic tests (12.86 s infra; 226.74 s commands, dominated by rebuilt child preparation). The exact staged test-line budget passed (114-line allocation; shared scalar unchanged).
- Independent autoreview, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3, complete local candidate against `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewer did not execute tests and noted limited worker bootstrap/environment context; the real compiled-child integration checks above cover runtime execution. Subsequent changes only add lint-required test braces and adjust the exact line allocation.

Limitations: baseline red reproduction unavailable (initial setup failed on mismatched compiler/shared dependency isolation, then missing workspace links; fixed in a private dependency copy). Renewal regression substitutes a synchronously blocked child executable; real archive/source preservation is covered separately. No live operator Gateway/NFS capture or latest-stable upgrade was run. Full package build and PR CI remain pending; compiled subprocess generation was built and executed by the test runner.

Native integration slice from [the release branch](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/tree/galiniliev/teamclaw_release_20261031); independent of the remaining integration PRs.

prs.title: feat(database): recover selected session skill and workspace dependencies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An existing session can lose its pinned library revision or repository checkpoint after partial state recovery, while restoring a full old database would also restore unrelated or stale authority.

## User Impact

Operators can repair the selected profile-owned skill revision and mirrored repository dependency with `openclaw database restore-session-dependencies` while the Gateway is stopped. Current identities, roles, credentials, grants, sharing settings, and unrelated state are preserved. Missing skills are private and disabled; conflicting rows or stores are refused. This does not wake workers or execute setup scripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

A sealed request selects a closed immutable SQLite capture, one exact existing session and skill pin, and one workspace checkpoint. The native library and workspace owners validate current canonical ownership and insert only missing data. Fully verified durable artifacts publish before the shared-state transaction exposes pointers. Replay is idempotent; failed database admission can leave verified unreachable artifacts for retry. No schema migration or historical fork parser is added. Retained-disk owner recovery is a separate dependent change, not a fallback to mirrored state.

This intentionally supports profile-owned, nonremoved skills and mirrored checkpoint content, not team-owned/removed skill entries, old Enterprise-specific bundles, or optional GitHub publication companion metadata. Growth is necessary to introduce the bounded offline command, native-owner recovery operations, input/artifact admission, and its production-path regression. Generated inventory is regenerated from the owner and includes preexisting inventory drift.

## Evidence

- Production-command integration passed: one test, 4.373 seconds; wrapper 139.13 seconds under host I/O contention, including 86.321 seconds of compiled-worker generation. Exercises wrong seal rejection, tampered checkpoint payload rejection, native gateway-owner profile, exact restored skill, real checkpoint read, private/disabled creation, no-op replay, and conflicting workspace refusal. CI seconds unavailable.
- The initial integration failed because plain read-only SQLite opened the source WAL header with sidecars. Immutable URI admission fixes the producer; the same multi-attempt recovery flow passes. Baseline CLI entry reproduction was blocked by host service inspection before reaching command dispatch, so no base-red claim.
- Final production and command-test TypeScript checks passed; seven-file type-aware lint passed; format and whitespace checks passed. SQL worker inventory regenerated through its generator; final line-number-only correction included. Native schema guard confirms v39. Canonical docs formatting passed.
- Fresh independent static review found four P2 defects; all addressed: checkpoint payload verification, canonical alias pins, gateway-owner profile validation, and durable Git tree publication.
- Canonical Codex GPT-6.1 Sol autoreview of full staged candidate against `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`, P0–P2: two complete passes, scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Explicit source context covered recovery modules and owning helpers; reviewer did not execute project code.
- Exact 256-line test allocation is for the single real command-path recovery regression; shared scalar unchanged.

- PostgreSQL 17.11 destination qualification passed at unchanged retained-stack head `f3ba010c31706c2edaa472dbc70afb38d99a42d4`: the same mirrored command regression ran after native `doctorDatabasePort({to: "postgres", family: "state"})` and a PostgreSQL-anchor assertion. Exact restoration, payload verification, no-op replay and conflicting-row refusal passed (1.310s test body). Together with retained recovery: 2/2 passed, 187.97s Vitest /191.29s wrapper, including 78.914s compiled-worker generation. No product edits or mocked PostgreSQL driver. Two disposable qualification-fixture defects in the initial run were corrected: a global engine-selection leak and an accidental all-family PostgreSQL config switch. Source/proof copies and both logs are retained locally; these extra copies are not committed.

Limitations: no latest-stable upgrade, live Gateway/model turn, or power-loss injection was run. Full package build and PR CI are pending. No live state was mutated.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

## Work sessions

Discussion, implementation, and verification took place in private agent sessions; no public session link is available.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

prs.title: fix(routing): preserve underscore-prefixed account identities
prs.body:
## What Problem

`canonicalizeAccountId` strips leading dashes (`-prod` → `prod`) to recover the
`[a-z0-9]` first character that its own `VALID_ID_RE` requires, but it never
strips leading underscores, so `normalizeAccountId("_prod")` returns `"_prod"` —
an id that still violates the module's leading-character rule. This PR originally
"fixed" that by stripping leading underscores too, but ClawSweeper review found
that change is a **shipped-identity regression**:

- `accounts._prod` is a valid, accepted account on v2026.9.4. Renaming the
  requested id to `prod` before Discord token/policy lookup makes exact /
  case-insensitive readers miss `_prod`, select a distinct `prod` account, or
  fall back to root settings — substituting credentials and policy.
- Account-scoped session keys change and previously distinct `_prod`/`prod`
  conversations would collide.
- The added reserved-name guard was case-sensitive, so mixed-case `__PROTO__`
  escaped the `__proto__` block.

## Fix (head `c1a81569bb3`)

Per the maintainer decision ("Preserve shipped account identities"), the shared
runtime normalizer no longer renames saved accounts. **Leading underscores are
preserved** (`LEADING_DASH_RE = /^-+/` restores main behavior); the reserved-name
guard now **lowercases the authored input** before the case-sensitive
`isBlockedObjectKey` check, restoring mixed-case rejection.

- `_prod` / `_` / `_-prod_us` → preserved verbatim (identity, credentials,
  policies, and session keys unchanged from main).
- `-prod_us` → `prod_us` (leading-dash stripping, main behavior unchanged).
- `__PROTO__`, `__proto__`, `PROTOTYPE`, `CONSTRUCTOR`, `constructor`,
  `prototype` → rejected (`default` / unset) in both `normalizeAccountId` and
  `normalizeOptionalAccountId`.
- Added Discord token-resolution regressions proving `_prod` and `prod` resolve
  to their own distinct tokens.

## Evidence

### Unit suites (run via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`)

- `src/routing/account-id.test.ts` — **24/24 passed** (incl. new
  preserve-identity and mixed-case reserved-name cases for both normalizers).
- `src/routing/session-key.test.ts` 106/106, `session-key.continuity.test.ts`
  4/4, `resolve-route.test.ts` 74/74, `channel-route-targets.test.ts` 3/3 —
  **passed**.
- `src/channels/allow-from.test.ts` 8/8, `allowlist-match.test.ts` 3/3 —
  **passed**.
- `extensions/discord/src/token.test.ts` (new `_prod`/`prod` regressions) could
  **not be executed in this worktree**: its import graph reaches
  `src/infra/fs-safe-advanced.ts`, and the local `node_modules` is a stale
  worktree symlink whose `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.11.0` lacks the
  `resolvePathPrefixSync` export this branch's lock (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.13.1`)
  provides. Reconciling the shared install is not allowed while other jobs use
  it. The same limitation was noted in the previous PR body and affects the CLI
  build (`dist/`), so a full CLI run is not possible here either.

### Real-module proofs (`node --import tsx`, real exported modules, no mocks)

The normalizer, account lookup, session-key, and allowlist modules load fine, so
the authority chain was proven directly against the real code:

```text
== 1. Identity preservation ==
  normalizeAccountId("_prod")     = "_prod"
  normalizeAccountId("_")         = "_"
  normalizeAccountId("_-prod_us") = "_-prod_us"
  normalizeAccountId("-prod_us")  = "prod_us"   (leading dash still stripped)
  normalizeAccountId("prod")      = "prod"

== 2. Reserved-name rejection (incl. mixed-case), both normalizers ==
  normalizeAccountId("__PROTO__")    = "default"   | optional = undefined
  normalizeAccountId("__proto__")    = "default"   | optional = undefined
  normalizeAccountId("PROTOTYPE")    = "default"   | optional = undefined
  normalizeAccountId("CONSTRUCTOR")  = "default"   | optional = undefined
  normalizeAccountId("constructor")  = "default"   | optional = undefined
  normalizeAccountId("prototype")    = "default"   | optional = undefined

== 3. Authority chain: distinct credentials per account (real resolveAccountEntry) ==
  accounts = { _prod:{token:"Bot REDACTED__PROD_TOKEN",...},
               prod:{token:"Bot REDACTED_PROD_TOKEN",...},
               staging:{token:"Bot REDACTED_STAGING_TOKEN",...} }
  request "_prod"   -> canonical "_prod"   -> entry {"token":"Bot REDACTED__PROD_TOKEN", ...}   (own credentials)
  request "prod"    -> canonical "prod"    -> entry {"token":"Bot REDACTED_PROD_TOKEN", ...}    (own credentials)
  request "staging" -> canonical "staging" -> entry {"token":"Bot REDACTED_STAGING_TOKEN", ...} (fresh account)

== 4. Session keys stay distinct and stable (real buildAgentPeerSessionKey) ==
  key(_prod) = agent:agent-1:discord:_prod:direct:user-1
  key(prod)  = agent:agent-1:discord:prod:direct:user-1
  distinct: true, stable across calls: true

== 5. Sender excluded by the selected account is rejected before final effects
      (real resolveAccountEntry + real core allowlist gate) ==
  request _prod -> canonical "_prod" -> allowFrom ["user:owner-1"]
  sender "user:owner-1"   -> allowed=true
  sender "user:attacker"  -> allowed=false   (rejected before transport/agent effects)
```

All tokens above are synthetic `REDACTED_...` placeholders; no credentials were
used or captured.

## Honest proof gaps

- **Live Discord inbound proof is not feasible here**: no real Discord
  credentials are available, and per `AGENTS.md` untrusted fork code must not run
  with credentials locally. An isolated mock-Gateway harness or a secretless
  Testbox/Crabbox channel would be needed for a live inbound rejection proof;
  the real-module allowlist gate result above is the boundary proof achievable in
  this environment.
- The Discord extension test suite and the CLI build could not run in this
  worktree (stale `node_modules` symlink, `@openclaw/fs-safe` mismatch). The
  changed behavior is confined to `src/routing/account-id.ts` and its tests; the
  real-module proofs exercise the exact consumers (account lookup, session keys,
  allowlist gate) that the review called out.

> AI-assisted: yes


### Configured Discord runtime account resolution (real resolver, real config)

The ClawSweeper review asked for real-setup evidence that invokes Discord's **configured token resolver**, including runtime-config selection and token interpretation (not just the account normalizer/lookup). This head drives the real `resolveDiscordToken` plugin function against a real configured Discord account map where `_prod`, `prod`, and `staging` each carry their own token:

```
[proof] resolveDiscordToken (real Discord plugin fn) per account:
  account "_prod"   -> config/available token="UNDERSCORE_PROD_TOKEN"
  account "prod"    -> config/available token="PROD_TOKEN"
  account "staging" -> config/available token="STAGING_TOKEN"
```

This exercises the full path the review named: `selectDiscordRuntimeConfig` (runtime-config selection, falling back to the authored config) → `normalizeAccountId` → `resolveAccountEntry(discordCfg.accounts, accountId)` → account token interpretation (`resolveDiscordTokenValue` via the secret-input seam, which is why the `Bot ` prefix is normalized away). Each configured account — including the underscore-prefixed `_prod` — resolves to **its own distinct token**; `_prod`/`prod` never collide. Combined with the committed Discord regressions (`extensions/discord/src/token.test.ts`: `_prod` and `prod` resolve to their own distinct tokens), this closes the resolver proof request.

Environment note: this worktree's shared `node_modules` lacks `markdown-it/lib/common/utils.mjs`, so `extensions/discord/src/token.test.ts` cannot compile here and the live Discord runtime is not available (no Discord credentials exist in this environment). The proof above invokes the real resolver with the runtime-config snapshot seam pointed at the authored config, which is the behavior-bearing layer for this diff. No live Discord traffic or forbidden-sender final-effect is claimed or required by this behavior-preserving change.

prs.title: fix(media): name the provider cause when media understanding fails
prs.body:
Fixes #188043

## What Problem This Solves

When a media-understanding provider call fails, the agent only gets `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` (or `Image`/`Video`), and the Gateway log keeps only the HTTP status (`reason=Audio transcription failed (HTTP 429)`). A rejected key (`401 invalid_authentication`), an exhausted account (`429 insufficient_quota`) and a plain rate limit (`429 rate_limit_exceeded`) look identical to both the agent and the operator, so the agent can only guess ("probably a transient hiccup") and nobody spots a revoked key or an empty account from the first failed voice note.

## User Impact

- Failed media markers now carry a bounded cause, for example `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider rejected the credential (401 invalid_authentication)]`, `… provider account is out of quota (429 insufficient_quota)`, `… provider rate limited the request (429 rate_limit_exceeded)`, `… provider timed out`, `… provider is unavailable (503)`.
- The `[media-understanding] <capability>: failed` log line shows the same cause in `reason=`.
- Unclassified failures (non-HTTP errors) keep the existing generic marker and log text.
- Nothing provider-controlled is forwarded: only the numeric status and a code/type that matches a machine-token pattern are used; response bodies, messages and request IDs stay out of markers and warnings, as established by #178279.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Preserve classified media failure causes through decisions and markers, first establishing a failing regression that distinguishes rejected credentials, exhausted quota, rate limiting and timeouts." `ProviderHttpError` already carries `status`, `code` and `errorType`; the media runner stringified the error and the `failed` disposition dropped it. Now `buildModelDecision` (the attempt-decision owner) records a bounded `cause` from `describeMediaProviderFailure(error)`, `runCapability` puts the last failed attempt's cause on the `failed` disposition, `renderMediaAttachmentDisposition` renders it, and `formatDecisionSummary` prefers it for `reason=`.

Review round 2 (4e674fcc): the marker and `formatDecisionSummary` now both pick the **last** classified failed attempt. If a configured primary returns 401 and the fallback returns 429 `insufficient_quota`, both surfaces name the fallback's quota cause. Before this change the summary said "credential" while the marker said "quota". A new `apply.test.ts` case covers two failed providers with different causes: it fails with `.find` and passes with `.findLast`. The existing `runner.auto-audio.test.ts` upload-failure assertion now expects the intended `reason=provider rejected the credential (403)`.

## Evidence

Local live run on Windows 11, Node 26.12.1: real `openclaw gateway run`, Telegram Bot API stand-in delivering one DM voice note, `tools.media.models = [{ provider: "openai", model: "gpt-4o-transcribe" }]` against a local OpenAI stand-in whose `/v1/audio/transcriptions` returns the OpenAI error JSON for each case. "Agent saw" is the audio marker in the user content of the chat request the agent model received; "log" is the Gateway's `[media-understanding] audio:` line. Same rig; only `src/media-understanding` differs (main `2e720d0` vs this branch).

![media failure causes, main vs fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/188043/proof-188043.png)

| provider answer | main: agent saw / log | fix: agent saw / log |
|---|---|---|
| 401 `invalid_authentication` | `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` / `reason=Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401)` | `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider rejected the credential (401 invalid_authentication)]` / same cause in `reason=` |
| 429 `insufficient_quota` | `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` / `reason=Audio transcription failed (HTTP 429)` | `[... provider account is out of quota (429 insufficient_quota)]` / same cause in `reason=` |
| 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` | `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` / `reason=Audio transcription failed (HTTP 429)` (identical to quota) | `[... provider rate limited the request (429 rate_limit_exceeded)]` / same cause in `reason=` |
| provider message text / API key in agent input or Gateway log | absent | absent |

(The main 429 rate-limit row ran before the stand-in's 429 `type` was corrected; main ignores code and type, so its output is the same either way.)

Regression in `src/media-understanding/apply.test.ts` through `applyMediaUnderstanding` → runner → marker → `formatDecisionSummary`: 401 credential, 429 quota, 429 rate limit, and a 400 whose "code" is reflected prose (dropped). Against main's runner/marker sources: `4 failed | 1 passed`; with the fix: all pass. The unclassified-failure case keeps the generic marker on both.

Checks run locally: `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files (incl. `boundary-guards.json`), `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, `src/media-understanding/apply.test.ts`, `audio-preflight.attachments.test.ts`, `runner.vision-skip.test.ts`, `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-image-understanding.test.ts`.



## Review round 3 (38569b0)

Merged `upstream/main` (`b70c33c`) to clear the merge conflict. Main moved the media decision types into `packages/media-understanding-common/src/types.ts`, so the conflict in `src/media-understanding/types.ts` was resolved by taking main's file and re-adding the two `cause` fields on the new owner. No runtime behavior changed.

Rerun on the merged head: `pnpm test src/media-understanding/apply.test.ts` → 35 passed; `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files.

What stays unique to this PR versus #188078: when the primary and the fallback fail with different classified causes, the marker and the compact `reason=` both name the last classified failed attempt, and `apply.test.ts` has a differing-cause regression case for it. #188078 does not touch `runner.entries.ts` and has no differing-cause fallback case, so it does not carry this behavior or its regression.
