prs.title: fix(agents): subagents of scheduled runs get the guest toolsBySender["*"] entry
prs.body:
Closes #188441
Related: #178815 (broader consolidation of child authority; this change only restores the spawn snapshot for one case)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent spawned by an isolated scheduled run gets the guest `toolsBySender["*"]` entry when it starts, even though the run itself does not apply sender policy (a run capped with `toolsAllow`, or a run of a job an owner created).

## User Impact

User impact: subagents (and their own subagents) of such runs now get the same sender policy as the run: the tool snapshot recorded when they were spawned, as released versions do. Current global, agent, provider, sandbox and sub-agent restrictions still apply.

The guest `"*"` entry no longer applies to these children in place of the run's policy, which has three visible effects, all matching the run itself:
- its denies no longer remove tools the run had;
- tools that only the `"*"` entry grants (for example an optional plugin tool in its `alsoAllow`) no longer reach these children, as they never reached the run;
- the children are no longer treated as sender-restricted: like the run, they may start helpers of other agents, and the sender-only confinement (working directory, agent and session-root pinning, ACP root rules, the delegated deny floor, the session permission policy) does not apply to them.

Unchanged:
- runs that apply sender policy themselves (for example a webhook run) and their subagents still get the `"*"` entry, like the run;
- children of turns that have a sender keep that sender's current entry;
- senderless work sent to such a child from any other session, from a later or retried run of the same job, or by any other turn opened on the run's own session (another job's `session:` target, a hook request naming that session key, an operator turn) still resolves current sender policy;
- runs on a shared or named session (`main` and `session:` targets, including names shaped like run keys) never record the exception;
- children spawned before this change keep today's behavior.

Not changed (same as `main`, no regression):
- turns placed on a worker environment do not record the exception yet: their tool authority is prepared before the run is admitted, so their children keep today's behavior;
- visible children (`sessions_spawn` with `visible: true`, or `sessions.create`) do not carry it: their creation path does not persist the record;
- uncapped runs on CLI backends (tools served over the Gateway MCP loopback) do not record it: that surface resolves a senderless turn with `when-sender-id`, so it is not marked;
- ACP children the run spawns directly (`runtime: "acp"`) get no sub-agent envelope from a scheduled run (as on `main`), so the record is not read for them;
- a capped run whose own turn has a group restriction records a sender restriction instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #157806, a child's admission that carries its requester's origin resolves current requester policy again from that origin. A scheduled run's origin has its run session key but no sender, so the lookup fell through to `"*"`, whether or not the run applied sender policy, and nothing a child's later admission can read recorded which it was.

The spawning turn now records it next to the child's inherited snapshot, and a later admission keeps the snapshot only when the request comes from that same run occurrence: its own turn stamps its requester origin with its fresh per-run session key, so another turn opened on the same session (another job, a hook, an operator) never counts as the run.

Docs: the `nesting.md` tool-policy line now describes `main`'s behavior since #157806 (senderless work that carries a requester origin re-resolves current sender policy; released versions kept the snapshot for every senderless child run) and states this exception, which restores the snapshot only for a run's own work.

<details>
<summary>How the exception is recorded and checked</summary>

The record is `inheritedToolPolicySource: "scheduled-run"` together with `inheritedToolPolicyRunSessionKey`, the run's own per-run session. The host writes both only when the spawning turn resolved without sender policy, with no sender and no operator, on a per-run session that the isolated runner created fresh for this run. That last fact comes from the run's admitted scheduled execution context (set only for detached isolated or `current` runs whose run key is new), never from the shape of the session key. `sessions.patch` does not accept either field, plugin extension slots cannot claim their names (reserved), and patching a child's inherited allow or deny list drops the exception.

A later admission keeps the snapshot only when the request origin is that same run: senderless, no operator, its session key equal to the recorded one, and stamped by that run's own turn. The run's own turn stamps the requester origin it hands to its tools with its per-run session key (`scheduledRunSessionKey`, set only from the same host fact that records the exception, copied only from an already captured origin, never from flat request input); its sub-agents inherit that origin unchanged. The new check reads only the child's own row; it adds no parent or intermediate row reads (an explicit delegation grant keeps its existing lineage check), so compaction, model fallback or the post-prompt sync of the run session cannot invalidate an admitted child's prepared policy. Nested children receive the exception and the run key from their parent's own admission. Completion batches keep it only when every completing child records the same run. Any other origin-bearing admission drops it. `SessionEntry` (exported through the plugin SDK) gains the `"scheduled-run"` source value and the optional run key.

Housekeeping (line caps): `hasCliSessionReuseMetadata` moves unchanged from `run-prompt-executor.ts` to `run-cli-session.ts`; the new `sessions.patch` rows live in `sessions-patch.subagent-policy.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

Built Gateway from this branch and, for the `main` column, the same build with every changed source file swapped back to `main` (`56eaffa43c2`); scripted model; `toolsBySender: { "*": { deny: ["read"] } }`; capped runs use a `toolsAllow` that includes `read`. Each cell is what the run's child got when it called `read` on a sentinel file in that turn (offered and returned the file / refused / not offered).

| Turn that reaches run A's child | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run A's own turn spawns the child | not offered | **returned** |
| Run A's own turn sends the child more work (`sessions_send`) | not offered | **returned** |
| Grandchild spawned by that child | not offered | **returned** |
| Run A's run session rewritten while the child is admitted (compaction-style row rotation) | not offered | **returned** |
| Fresh child after upgrading from `2026.10.8` (this PR: also from `2026.10.9`; the pre-upgrade child row stays unmarked) | not offered | **returned** |
| Another job whose `sessionTarget` is `session:<run A's key>` sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| A hook request naming run A's session key sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| A forced re-run of the job after run A failed (new run key) sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| Gateway restarted mid-run (run A aborted, never resumed), then a turn on run A's key sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| Operator `chat.send` on run A's key sends to the child | returned | returned |
| Job on a persistent `session:` target (not a per-run session) | not offered | not offered |
| Webhook-triggered run (applies `"*"` itself): its child | not offered | not offered |
| Group turn with a sender (the repo's QA-lab Telegram Bot API stub): its child | returned (sender's own entry) | returned |

"Refused" rows: the call is refused at execution with "read is not available in this turn" under the current `"*"` policy. Unlike `main`, where `read` is never offered, it stays listed because it was offered on the run's own earlier turn (definitions stay pinned within a session). Runs hosted by the Codex harness are not exercised end to end here.

- `src/agents/requester-tool-policy.test.ts`: the record (only a run's own turn on its fresh session; not a run-shaped key without the runner's fact, another session, sender policy, an operator, a sender or a group restriction), the check (child, nested child, blank sender kept; legacy child, a mark without its key, another session, the run's stamp on another session, a later run, operator, sender re-resolve), side effects, origin-free resume, completion batches, own-row capability reads, and a prepared read replayed after the run's row is rewritten.
- Stamp rows: `requester-origin.test.ts` (only from a captured origin, carried only for the same session), `conversation-capability-profile.test.ts` / `tool-resolution.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` (only the run's own turn on its fresh session stamps), `gateway-caller-context.test.ts`, `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts`, `mcp-http.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` (callers and loopback calls keep the stamped origin).
- `codex-subagent-tool-policy.test.ts`: the Codex harness's retained requester facts for a run child name only the child's row.
- Spawn rows (native; ACP via `acp-spawn-policy.test-support.ts`, mutant only): run key and exception persist only together. Execution context rows: the fresh run session is exposed only for a detached run on its own fresh session. `sessions.patch` rows (`sessions-patch.subagent-policy.test.ts`): a patched ceiling drops the exception, never a sender restriction.
- RED: each changed test file run alone against `main`'s production source fails its new rows on their assertions in 8 files, e.g. `keeps the sender snapshot for a child of a senderless scheduled run`: `expected { allow: undefined, deny: [ …(2) ] } to be undefined` (`main` applies the `"*"` deny to the child). `requester-origin.test.ts`, `execution-context-admission.test.ts` and `isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts` call helpers `main` does not have, so they fail on the missing helper rather than on a behavioral assertion and their rows are covered by the mutants below; `codex-subagent-tool-policy.test.ts` passes on `main` by design (it pins that a run child's harness facts name only the child's row).
- Mutants: 30 single-condition mutants of the fix (each dropping one check of the record, the occurrence check, the stamp or a carrier; one re-anchored after the code moved) each turn the intended row red; none survives.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt on the touched files, `check:test-lines-ratchet` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Test cost: +867 test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/scheduled-run-child-tool-snapshot.txt` (rows on each owner of the record, the run-key check and the stamp; the table above is the end-to-end proof). Per-file test time (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`), base -> head: `requester-tool-policy.test.ts` 8.8 -> 13.3 s (+38 tests); the other changed files within 0.5 s of base, including `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts` (36.4 -> 35.8 s, already over 30 s on `main` from its import graph; the three new caller rows were folded into it rather than adding a 35 s file); new files `tool-resolution.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` 10.0 s, `mcp-http.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` 8.9 s, `sessions-patch.subagent-policy.test.ts` 8.4 s (mostly transform of the Gateway modules they test). CI seconds once available.

prs.title: fix(update): stop Gateway respawn loops during Doctor maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway respawn loops during update Doctor maintenance when the outgoing Gateway has already released its state lease but launchd still has its KeepAlive job loaded.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor unloads the owned, enabled LaunchAgent before maintenance and retains the existing receipt so finalization can restore it, including with `--no-restart`. Unloaded or disabled services stay stopped; foreign installations and foreground-owner protections are unchanged. No schema, config, or CLI option changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process lease disappearing does not mean its supervisor is stopped. Remove the candidate's lease-liveness shortcut and let the existing native service owner decide whether a stop is needed. This is a candidate-side fix; it does not require changes in an already-installed updater.

Simplification: removes a duplicate ownership decision and obsolete lease mocks. The regression covers the missing-lease respawn window and the unloaded/disabled controls; worker tests cover native stop outcomes, receipt persistence, and uncertain cleanup refusal.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up (October 29)

- Addressed both ClawSweeper findings: create persistent fixtures under the real host platform before mocking Darwin, and make delegated-worker expectations follow the native service adapter result. Removed obsolete lease mocks and supplied the default no-stop service result for worker setup.
- Rebased onto `2f47962f2bdc`; retained both sides of the update-documentation conflict. Production behavior is unchanged from the original repair. The unrelated mock-export CI failure is fixed upstream by [#187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120), included by this rebase.
- Node local validation: **124 tests passed across four files** (service maintenance, delegated Doctor worker, service identity, and native launchd intent). The post-update suite separately passed all 94 cases on the rebased production patch.
- Fresh independent source audit and AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The source audit checked native foreground/foreign-owner protections; AutoReview covered the full five-file candidate.

- `check:changed` passed formatting, production/test typechecks, scoped lint, database/mock-export ratchets, and all other selected guards except dead-export scanning. A clean detached checkout of pinned main `2f47962f2bdc` independently reproduces the same five unused exports: `pluginReadiness` (knowledge scribes), `findDeliveryIntentOwners` / `enqueueSessionDelivery` (delivery queues), and `sanitizeVerboseQuery` / `writeRestartTitle` (test support). Those untouched baseline issues are excluded from this repair; this is not a claim that the aggregate local gate passed.
- Hosted CI on `802ab3a8af50` completed: 35 jobs passed, 26 skipped, and the mock-export baseline ratchet plus aggregate gate failed. This was PR-related: the worker repair removed two mocks without pruning their exact baseline entries. The native `--prune` generator removed only those two obsolete entries; the ratchet reproduced red and then passed against the actual tested base `4ec4620f6f0f`. No source or test behavior changed in this mechanical follow-up.
- ClawSweeper completed the preceding code head with no findings (patch quality: platinum hermit; overall/proof: gold shrimp). Fresh exact-head CI and review are pending for `998a57d815663e9d72eeec40f08c10bc84f875b4`; no merge requested. [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40940133217).

### Original regression and runtime proof

The following native results were collected for the original patch on `2a445f55db7e`, not rerun after this test-only repair and base integration.

- Regression reproduced against base `d5d681f676344`: the respawning case returned without stopping; unloaded and disabled controls passed. All three pass with this fix, using the real update receipt writer.
- Focused service-maintenance, post-update/finalization, and CLI failure-output suites pass. The original native proof took 12.24 seconds.
- Native macOS proof with a disposable product-generated KeepAlive LaunchAgent: predecessor exited with no Gateway lease, candidate stopped/unloaded the job, one restoration receipt persisted, and no process respawned across the next 11 seconds. Test service and state removed.
- Targeted CLI-update TypeScript check, scoped oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Private runtime package build and tarball integrity checks pass.
- Independent review and local ClawSweeper committed-range review completed with no actionable correctness or security findings. ClawSweeper reviewed the complete four-file range `d5d681f676344..2a445f55db7ec` (high reasoning); runtime proof was performed separately, not by the reviewer.

- Published `2026.10.8` driver → patched candidate (same version, distinct build) with `--no-restart`: activation and service/version/channel/HTTP/core readiness verified; 61.11 seconds downtime, with the service unloaded during Doctor custody and restored afterward. Update and health commands exited 0; seeded session, disabled cron job, and config settings survived. Candidate tarball SHA-256: `c618aecb3c712567dbbc2621031cb232265624ddcb31b2d24f6765a84007b8a8` (built from base `d5d681f676344` plus this patch before the commit was made).
- Upgrade limitations: Doctor emitted advisory fixture/account, legacy configuration, and retained-runtime warnings; automatic snapshot rollback was unavailable because the original Gateway held ownership during capture. No rollback/fault injection, Windows/Linux native run, or exhaustive timing sweep is claimed. The deterministic regression and native unloaded-job proof exercise the specific missing-lease window.
- Teardown: offline copies of both databases passed `PRAGMA integrity_check`; disposable services/state and artifact server removed. Existing host LaunchAgent hashes and live Gateway PID were unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): Code Mode models fail their first tool call with "Tool read not found"
prs.body:
Closes #188417
Related: #161072, #179823, #186718

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents running in Code Mode would start most tasks with a failed tool call. The model calls a catalog tool like `read` directly instead of inside `exec`, gets `Tool read not found`, and often fails a second time (`tools.read(...)` → `tools is not defined`) before the third try works. On Sonnet the task still finishes, one or two round trips late. Not every model recovers: in #161072, MiniMax-M3 sometimes concluded there was no read tool, and other times told the user Code Mode had no file access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nothing in the request told the model that catalog names only work inside an `exec` program, so this states that rule twice: at the top of the Code Mode catalog prompt, and in the per-turn runtime facts. The per-turn copy is needed because on direct Anthropic the runtime context is sent after the user message, and in testing a rule only in the static prompt never changed the first call.

Boundaries:

- Tool exposure, execution policy and the sandbox are unchanged. A direct call to a catalog tool that isn't in the provider tool list still fails as before, with the same error text.
- The per-turn sentence is only sent when Code Mode is on and some catalog tools aren't in the provider tool list, and it's left out wherever the other runtime facts are (raw model runs, settled-tool finalization). Embedded turns read that from the run's catalog; node-worker turns get it from the worker tool runtime, which renders it from its own catalog before clearing that catalog.
- `read`/`write`/`edit` are named in the first text only if those tools are bound.
- The catalog's shell line said "Use the shell tool `exec`", but the shell tool and the Code Mode `exec` share a name (#160272). It now says to run shell commands inside the program with `await exec({ command })`.

The two texts:

> Code Mode: every name in the index below is an async function inside an `exec` program. Unless the same name is also in your provider tool list, calling it as a tool fails; call `exec` with code such as `return await name({ ... })`. Prefer one program for dependent steps that need no user input. Programs cannot use `import()` or `require`; use `read`/`write`/`edit` for files.

> Code Mode is on for this turn: only tools in your provider tool list can be called directly. Call any other tool from the Code Mode index inside an `exec` program, and put dependent steps that need no user input in one program.

#186718 adds a recovery hint to the `not found` error, but only in Tool Search `tools` mode; a Code Mode version would fit alongside this, covering what still slips through.

## User Impact

Code Mode runs on Claude Sonnet 5.5 now almost always open with a working `exec` call instead of a failed direct one (Haiku 5.5, measured on an earlier wording, improves too but still slips on later steps). In the benchmark below, runs that started with a direct catalog call went from 40 of 48 to 1 of 48, failed tool calls from 61 to 5, and assistant turns from 220 to 152, with every task still passing. Total cost went down 6.8%, and the 48 runs took about 4% less time in total.

The trade-off is about 68 extra uncached input tokens per request, so a task that had no wrong call to begin with costs 1% to 5% more.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: Code Mode models call catalog tools (`read`, `write`, ...) as native tools first, fail with `Tool read not found`, and retry.  
Real environment tested: Anthropic Messages API, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, the repo's own `scripts/code-mode-model-matrix.ts`, Windows 11, source checkout. Main `b01de78ed44` vs this branch at `7119fd51b48`, run at the same time. The branch has since been rebased onto `66004e076d4` with no conflicts; both commits have the same `git patch-id` as before the rebase.  
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm qa:code-mode-models --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 --mode code --task read --task dependent-read-write --task parallel-independent-reads --task dependent-chain --task dependent-chain-long --task large-result-reduction --repetitions 8 --concurrency 3 --max-cells 100 --max-tokens 90000000 --max-known-cost-usd 15 --max-wall-seconds 14400 --keep-state`, once on each tree.  
Evidence after fix: transcript excerpts and per-task tables computed from each tree's `results.jsonl` and transcripts, below.  
Observed result after fix: 1 of 48 runs opened with a direct catalog call (main: 40 of 48). 48/48 passed on both sides.  
What was not tested: models from other providers; models other than Sonnet 5.5 on this exact commit (Haiku 5.5 was measured on an earlier wording, see below); a live node-worker turn (the benchmark runs the embedded path; the worker path is covered by a test that builds the real worker assignment, below).  
Proof limitations or environment constraints: `dependent-chain-long` is a 12-step version of `dependent-chain` that I added to the matrix locally; it isn't in this PR. The main tree also carried my benchmark variant patches, which are off unless `OPENCLAW_BENCH_VARIANT` is set; they were off for this run. The matrix ran on Windows, where its gateway doesn't pass `PATHEXT` to the shell, so PowerShell can't find `node`. The six tasks above don't use the shell. For `repo-invoice-repair` I patched the harness locally to pass it through; the gateway contract runs in the details below ran without that patch.

### Before and after, same task

`read` task on main (4 assistant turns, 2 failed calls):

```
1. read {"path":"facts.txt"}
   -> ERROR Tool read not found
2. exec: const r = await tools.read({path:"facts.txt"}); return r;
   -> ERROR ReferenceError: tools is not defined
3. exec: return await read({path:"facts.txt"});
   -> completed {"kind":"text","content":"project=openclaw\nverification_cod...
```

Same task on this branch (2 turns, 0 failed calls). 7 of 8 runs look like this; the eighth is the one remaining direct call:

```
1. exec: return await read({path:"facts.txt"})
   -> completed {"kind":"text","content":"project=openclaw\nverification_cod...
```

The 12-step chain, main (4 calls, the first one fails) vs. this branch (1 call):

```
main:
1. read {"path":"start.json"}                   -> ERROR Tool read not found
2. exec: const r = await read({path:"start.json"}); return r;      -> completed
3. exec: let f="hop-1-194.json";for(...){const r=await read({path:f}); ...}   -> completed
4. exec: await write({path:"result.txt",content:"CM-19404D24C20F"}); ...      -> completed

this branch:
1. exec: let p="start.json"; for(...){const r=await read({path:p}); ... await write(...) ...}   -> completed "CM-19404D24C20F"
```

### Results, 6 tasks × 8 runs, same batch

main → this branch, per run; all 48 runs passed on both sides.

| task | cost | assistant turns per run | failed calls per run |
|---|---|---|---|
| read | −10.3% | 3.50 → 2.13 | 1.50 → 0.13 |
| dependent-read-write | −10.4% | 4.75 → 3.00 | 1.75 → 0 |
| parallel-independent-reads | +1.0% | 2.88 → 2.75 | 0 → 0 |
| dependent-chain | −3.3% | 6.00 → 5.00 | 1.00 → 0 |
| dependent-chain-long ¹ | −15.6% | 4.75 → 2.25 | 1.00 → 0 |
| large-result-reduction | −3.0% | 5.63 → 3.88 | 2.38 → 0.50 |

¹ A 12-step version of `dependent-chain` I added locally; not part of this PR.

| total | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| runs that opened with a direct catalog call | 40/48 | 1/48 |
| failed calls | 61 | 5 |
| assistant turns | 220 | 152 |
| cost | $1.960 | $1.827 |
| run time (sum over 48 runs) | 1797 s | 1724 s |
| passed | 48/48 | 48/48 |

What the failed calls were:

| error | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `Tool read not found` (direct call) | 48 | 1 |
| `ReferenceError: tools is not defined` (`tools.read` inside `exec`) | 12 | 0 |
| `JSON.parse` error in the model's own program | 1 | 4 |

**One thing got worse.** The `JSON.parse` errors are all in `large-result-reduction`. With the "put dependent steps in one program" instruction, the model writes the whole paged read and parse in one go, but it doesn't know where `read` splits pages, so it sometimes parses half a line, then rewrites the program with a `try/catch`. Over two batches that happened in 5 of 12 runs vs. 1 of 12 on main. The task is still cheaper (turns 5.63 → 3.88). Telling the model to read results before chaining them made the 12-step chain much worse (see the details below), so I didn't add more text for this.

### A real repo task

`repo-invoice-repair` (the matrix's repo-fix task) ran before the final commit, on main with the same patch text switched on by a local env flag, 20 runs per side. Both sides fixed the repo 20/20 at the same cost ($0.0694 vs $0.0690, no measurable difference).

The `import()`/`require` line is there because of this task. With the contract but without that sentence, the model more often opened its edit program with `await import("node:fs")`, and `prepareSource` rejects that whole program before any tool runs. That happened in 10/16 and 9/16 runs across two batches (main: 1/15 and 2/12, counting runs with a readable transcript), and cost +16% and +4%. With the line: 1/14, cost back to main's level.

### Node-worker turns

The first revision of this PR forwarded the per-turn sentence on node-worker turns from a getter that reads the run's catalog, but the worker prompt never has one, so workers only got the static rule. The worker tool runtime now renders the sentence from its own catalog while it builds the model tool projection, and the worker prompt forwards that.

`carries the Code Mode turn contract into the worker assignment runtime context` runs a worker turn with `tools.codeMode: true` through the real launch path and asserts the launched assignment's `runtimeContext` contains the sentence (and its system prompt the catalog rule). Pointing the worker back at the old getter, i.e. the reviewed head `3081a564071`, turns exactly that test red.

### Where the runtime context sits

On direct Anthropic the per-turn context is a `system` message after the user turn (`packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-messages.ts:298-305`). To check that the fix doesn't depend on that, I also forced it into a `user` message (on the env-gated build used for `repo-invoice-repair`, with the same wording, not this commit): the first call was `exec` in 6 of 6 runs.

<details>
<summary>More runs, and wordings that didn't work</summary>

**Haiku 5.5** (`--mode code`, an earlier wording without the `import()` line), two batches of 6 tasks × 4 runs: cost −11% and −22%, turns per run 6.1 → 3.7 and 6.1 → 3.8, failed calls in total 27 → 13 and 30 → 18. It helps a lot, but Haiku still slips on later steps, so on Haiku it's a partial fix.

**The repo's gateway contract tasks** (earlier wording, 2 × 10 tasks): 12/20 pass the behavior checks on both sides. Half the failures on each side are the process tasks, where PowerShell on Windows couldn't find `node`.

Didn't work:

- **Only a static rule** (`exec` description, catalog prompt, or both; 4 variants × 4 runs): direct `read` first in 16/16.
- **Only the per-turn sentence:** fixed direct Anthropic in an earlier wording (failed calls 25 → 1), but with the context sent as a `user` message it still went direct 4/4.
- **A vague pointer** ("the system prompt's rules still apply"): direct 3/4.
- **Softer wording** ("this is how to call tools, not a limit on what you may do"): with the context as a `user` message, the first call was still a direct `read` in 4/4. The model only changes course when the sentence states the limit.
- **Dropping "put dependent steps in one program" from the per-turn sentence:** the 12-step chain took 9.8 turns per run, vs. 2.5 with it and 8.0 on main (one run took 15 requests).
- **Telling the model to return and read results with an unknown shape (`-> ?` in the index) before using them** (in place of the "one program" wording; that variant also reworded the shell line and opened the per-turn sentence with the softer wording above): in a separate 4-run batch (main took 8 turns there), the 12-step chain took 15.5 turns, +53% cost.
- **Running a direct catalog call instead of failing it:** removes the wasted turn, but widens direct execution authority, changes client/plugin name-clash handling, exposes tools Code Mode hides on purpose, and lets calls skip policy on the outer `exec`. Those are design decisions, so they're not in this PR.

</details>

### Tests and checks

New and updated tests:

- `src/agents/code-mode.test.ts`
  - `states the calling contract above a non-empty catalog index`
  - `names only the bound file tools beside the module-access limit`
  - `restates the calling contract per turn only while catalog tools sit behind exec`
  - updated: `removes shell-computation guidance when a client shadows the shell tool` now checks the new shell-line wording
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-context.test.ts`
  - `adds Code Mode turn fragments as turn facts that never make a blank turn runtime-only`
  - `leaves Code Mode turn fragments out of raw model runs` / `... out of settled tool finalization`
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-gateway-tool-runtime.test.ts`
  - `projects the Code Mode turn contract only while catalog tools sit behind exec` (Code Mode on, emptied by a tool allowlist, Code Mode off, and Tool Search)
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-execution.test.ts`
  - `carries the Code Mode turn contract into the worker assignment runtime context`

Each guard removed one at a time, to show the tests hold it:

| guard removed | test that fails |
|---|---|
| per-turn sentence never sent | `restates the calling contract per turn only while catalog tools sit behind exec` |
| per-turn sentence sent even when every catalog tool is directly visible | `restates the calling contract per turn only while catalog tools sit behind exec` |
| per-turn sentence no longer skipped for raw model runs / settled-tool finalization | `leaves Code Mode turn fragments out of raw model runs`, `... out of settled tool finalization` |
| per-turn sentence dropped from the runtime facts | `adds Code Mode turn fragments as turn facts that never make a blank turn runtime-only` |
| catalog rule dropped | `states the calling contract above a non-empty catalog index` |
| `import()`/`require` line dropped | `names only the bound file tools beside the module-access limit` |
| file tools named whether or not the catalog has them | `names only the bound file tools beside the module-access limit` |
| "for files" clause kept when no file tool is bound | `names only the bound file tools beside the module-access limit` |
| worker prompt forwards the old getter again (the reviewed head) | `carries the Code Mode turn contract into the worker assignment runtime context` |
| worker projection never renders the sentence | `projects the Code Mode turn contract only while catalog tools sit behind exec`, `carries the Code Mode turn contract into the worker assignment runtime context` |
| worker projection renders it without checking that Code Mode is on | `projects the Code Mode turn contract only while catalog tools sit behind exec` (the Tool Search case) |

The first eight were run against both agent test files on `7119fd51b48`, the last three against both worker test files on the worker fix; each turned exactly the listed tests red, nothing else. The unmutated baseline was checked first.

Local checks on `6e73b3a6fcb` (clean tree): `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on all 11 touched files, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` against main, `tsgo` core (0 errors), and all 29 core test type-check shards. `code-mode.test.ts` passes except `records Code Mode skills.read of a workshop skill as run usage and skill.used`, which fails the same way on main `b01de78ed44` on Windows (expects `/skills/learned/SKILL.md`, gets `D:\skills\learned\SKILL.md`). This change doesn't touch that test or the skills code. ## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway revoked-person test fails after correctly aborting Bob's queued followup because it expects the history response to contain no retained inputs. The history reader keeps cancelled records, so a total of one does not mean that work remains queued.

## User Impact

This is a test-only correction. It preserves the existing checks that Bob's revoked input aborts, never reaches the model, and never appears among executed runs. Gateway authorization, cancellation, storage, and history behavior do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final assertion now checks the retained record's cancelled state and exact run identity, together with `queuedCount: 0`. This distinguishes terminal history from executable queued work instead of changing the expected count alone. The separate strict-refusal fixture repair is covered by #190792.

## Evidence

The complete original revoked-person case reached its abort and no-model controls, then failed at the final `total: 0` assertion. That history response contained one cancelled record for Bob's exact queued run and zero queued inputs. The existing history-reader contract explicitly retains cancelled records.

Remote formatting, touched-file lint, and affected E2E types passed. The complete reader-contract file passed all seven tests. Pre-publication Gateway proof ran the complete collaboration and revoked-person cases, both passing; the strict-refusal fixture was repaired separately in #190792.

[Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41382542361/job/125076641092) then ran the full three-case fixture on the merged source, with strict refusal, collaboration, and revocation all passing. All selected CI checks passed, and independent review is clean.

The remote two-case Gateway command took 361.4 seconds including runtime preparation, with 25.2 seconds in the cases. CI's complete fixture command took 40.65 seconds, with 20.7 seconds in the cases.

prs.title: chore(ci): measure gateway cache preparation costs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

We need to establish whether preparing Gateway test code once can remove enough repeated CI work to cover its added cost.

## User Impact

No product or CI-policy change. This experiment rejects the proposed seed expansion under the existing cache budget; it makes no savings claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing protected seed does not explicitly collect the gateway-server configuration. Its archive was also close to the pruning threshold, so adding more preparation without measurement could displace useful entries.

The workload is designed to build the complete existing seed, measure five preparations of one unchanged Gateway test, then run five balanced baseline/candidate pairs with separate fresh-process and warm repeats. Both sides use the same checkout, live cache path and Node compilation inputs. Local compression and restore costs are measured separately. A fresh seed is not a replay of the historical archive, and Testbox measurements do not establish production billing or precise tail estimates.

## Evidence

Before timing, the acceptance rule is:

- The original one-test proof and assertions must pass in every real run; no inventory, timeout, resource-budget or production-policy change.
- Fresh whole-command time plus measured local restore improves by at least 10% in median, with candidate wins in at least four of five pairs.
- Reject a 20% adverse move in warm median, worst observed completion, CPU work or peak child RSS. Five pairs are screening evidence, not a precise tail estimate.
- Reject any baseline-entry eviction. Compare added transform bytes with the historical 81.15-MiB headroom, rather than assuming a freshly built seed reproduces archive aging.
- Count incremental producer CPU/wall, archive size/compression and restore work; report the measured consumer-count break-even. Backend transfer and actual invoice effects remain unmeasured.
- Stop on source/path/runtime mismatch, failed proof or cleanup, memory exhaustion, queueing or lease deadline. Incomplete preparation or missing samples are not a passing experiment.

## Measured result — reject this cache expansion

The complete baseline seed succeeded. The first added Gateway collection then violated the predeclared no-eviction rule, so the workload stopped before consumer comparisons.

| Observation | Measured value |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline transform cache | 2,050,616,126 bytes (1,955.62 MiB) |
| Baseline headroom under the existing 2-GiB cap | 92.38 MiB |
| First added preparation | 41.46 seconds wall; 66.56 seconds CPU |
| Existing entries evicted | 23,801 files; 544,257,474 bytes (519.04 MiB) |
| Transform cache after preparation | 1,610,611,012 bytes (1,536.00 MiB) |
| Consumer timing pairs / archive samples | 0 / 0 |

The final transform cache is only 1,724 bytes below the existing 1.5-GiB pruning target. The smaller cache reflects eviction, not an efficiency gain. This rejects the frozen candidate under the agreed space rule; it does not prove slower consumers. There are no consumer latency, archive-cost, break-even or invoice savings results.

The baseline producer took 541.22 seconds wall and 1,296.23 seconds CPU, with GNU time maximum child RSS 7,447,200 KiB. The first added preparation's maximum child RSS was 3,869,108 KiB. These are individual observations, not medians or aggregate concurrent memory measurements.

Provider: Blacksmith Testbox; requested 16-class; observed four available CPUs and 15.42 GiB physical RAM. The recorded cgroup v2 files were absent, which does not prove absent limits. Source: `d4dbbe932dfde73655e077fa5b7986b9692fd3ba`. [Execution run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41382830451), lease `tbx_01m6d4gvwvy1132ykc22nt1wzq`; wrapper settled and native status confirms completed.

The seed was produced freshly from the full current inventory, not restored from an aged historical archive. The decision applies to this source, preparation order and cache state. The workload's intended five-pair design was not completed because its first rejection guard fired. No assertions, inventory, cache cap, runner policy or production workflow changed.

Syntax, frozen formatter and scoped lint checks passed. Fresh independent code review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the substantive workload; the later source edit only adds lint-required braces. Independent interpretation review confirmed the arithmetic and the bounded conclusion.

Command: `node --import tsx scripts/perf/gateway-transform-cache-measure.mts --output <result.json>`, after the repository build with Node 24.22.1 and the checksum-pinned Bun runtime.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190815

prs.title: fix: confirming Dismiss keeps its idle label while the row's Approve claims to be loading
prs.body: Closes #147824 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: confirming **Dismiss** for a DM access request leaves the confirmation button reading "Dismiss" with no progress copy, while the same request's row changes its **Approve** action to "Loading…" — so two surfaces on one screen disagree about which operation is running, and the accessible name still describes approval. ## User Impact Each control now reports only its own operation. Dismissing shows "Dismissing…" on the confirmation and on the row action that is actually running; the row's Approve action keeps its idle label and its "Approve …" accessible name instead of claiming to load. Approving behaves symmetrically. Idle, settled, and failed states are unchanged, as is the single-mutation interlock that disables every action while one mutation is in flight. ## Why This Change Was Made `ui/src/lib/channels/index.ts` recorded only `pairingBusyRequestId`. The renderer could therefore tell *which request* was busy but not *which operation* held it, so `ui/src/pages/channels/view.pairing.ts` had to guess — it used `thisRequestBusy` for the Approve label and ignored pending state entirely on the confirmation. Rather than add a second field that could drift out of sync, the owner now holds one fact: ```ts pairingBusy: { requestId: string; operation: "approve" | "dismiss" } | null ``` That makes "a busy request with no known operation" unrepresentable. The operation also joins `PairingMutation`, so a stale approve can no longer satisfy the currency guard for a current dismiss. No new state owner, no change to the request lifecycle, no pairing policy change. ## Evidence Held `channels.pairing.dismiss` against the real Control UI with the repository's own mocked Gateway, then read the rendered DOM. English, dark, 1440 × 1100 — the viewport named in the report. **Before** — confirmation keeps the idle verb; the row's Approve action borrows the loading label **After** — the confirmation reports the dismissal it is running Rendered values from the same capture, with the dismissal held: | Reading | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Confirmation label | `Dismiss` | `Dismissing…` | | Row Approve label | `Loading…` | `Approve` | | Row Dismiss label | `Dismissing…` | `Dismissing…` | | Row Approve accessible name | `Approve 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Approve 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | | Row Dismiss accessible name | `Dismissing 555000111 …` | `Dismissing 555000111 …` | | Any `Loading…` copy in the row | present | absent | The before column is the reported defect reproduced; the after column is this branch. `ui/src/pages/channels/view.pairing.test.ts` gains a case asserting that a pending dismissal labels the dismissal while approval keeps its own idle label and accessible name, and that no `Loading…` copy remains in the row. The existing single-mutation case is kept and now asserts the operation carried with the busy state. Checks run on this branch: | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `view.pairing.test.ts`, `lib/channels/index.test.ts`, `view.test.ts`, `custodian-page.channel-onboarding.test.ts` | 86 passed | | `tsgo` ui project | exit 0 | | `oxfmt --check` on changed files | clean | | `ui:i18n:verify` | exit 0 | **Not run:** the `ui-e2e-bundled` Vitest project does not start in my environment; its runner stalls before executing any test, for this file and for pre-existing E2E files alike. The captures above come from driving the same repository helpers (`startBundledControlUiE2eServer`, `installMockGateway`) and Chromium directly. CI covers the shard.

prs.title: feat(update): allow explicit retirement of backed-up session archives
prs.body:
Closes #186088

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot intentionally retire retained session-import archives when import proof is unavailable or archive identity changed, even after preserving an independent backup.

## User Impact

Exact complete-group selection, verified independent raw backups, and separate `--accept-history-loss` consent allow deliberate retirement. Ordinary cleanup remains conservative. Updates shows retained sizes, reasons and recovery guidance; there is no UI delete control.

Archives may contain unique history absent from SQLite. Retirement permanently removes selected originals while preserving previous import evidence in version-5 receipts. Recovery from the independent backup is manual; older binaries reject these receipts. **Maintainer acceptance of this opt-in retention contract remains outstanding.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance/disposal owner handles selection, backup validation, durable multi-manifest claims and interruption/replay. No alternate deletion service or automatic retention rule is introduced.

The reviewed synchronous inventory call now runs through the existing Gateway-owned recovery worker, preserving database custody, cancellation and scan bounds. Normal status polling does not enumerate recovery. A real-ledger regression fails on the old main-thread SQL path and passes after this correction.

## Evidence

[Commit-pinned proof index and individually readable raw artifacts](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/bc34ff469ef24177f29da1efeea567d6064636ff/README.md) for `440f9f312feeeba735cb942491efd2cd52c40e47`. [Direct storage-compatibility index](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/bc34ff469ef24177f29da1efeea567d6064636ff/COMPATIBILITY.md) · [historical Gist mirror](https://gist.github.com/jason-allen-oneal/cce57bad7470dc6c18447b0b7bf7c324/40d9e4f43bd9695e84bc6499340099ab6552504f). The repository mirror contains the same sanitized evidence bytes; it avoids the previous reviewer’s Gist-access failure.

- **Real built Gateway → actual served Control UI:** 9/9 cases passed at 400/820/1280 px across empty, retained and malformed-manifest fixtures. Real WebSocket responses, 127 matching served-asset hashes, unchanged two-archive/manifest hashes, incomplete-inventory warnings, no overflow, stable Recovery Storage and measured visible shell geometry. All nine scans report partial `time-limit`; malformed cases also report `unreadable-manifest`. Existing Update Status layout shifts and console messages are retained, not hidden.
- **Worker correction:** 45 focused tests, core types, scoped lint/format, zero-cycle guard and independent source review passed. The 150 ms inventory budget is not a worker-startup/queue wall deadline.
- **Normal CLI + official 2026.10.9 upgrade:** ordinary refusal, read-only preview, consented retirement, interruption/replay, preserved SQLite history/backup bytes, schema 25→38 migration and older-reader refusal. This proof was captured at `2dee5c7` and is reused only for unchanged CLI behavior.
- **Original regression evidence:** 228 distinct tests + 5 mocked-Gateway browser tests passed; three selected backup-comparison mutations killed. The additional focused reruns are not counted as new unique tests. CI's split-diff animation race has a red→green fixture repair with 7/7 browser tests passing. The catalog fixture now advertises the tool APIs required by upstream admission; the exact merged-behavior red→green replay passes 3/3 without weakening guards or assertions.

The real-Gateway proof was captured at `bf1debacae768ac8da1a8ee496f99fc1b53323fe`; subsequent changes are test-fixture-only. Synthetic isolated data, not the reporter's installation. The harness initiates no model requests. No installed-updater/service-restart, successful downgrade, clean-console, whole-page zero-shift or new-proof SQLite-byte-preservation claim is made. Coverage/CRAP remains unmeasured; CLI autoreview authentication was unavailable. The latest [exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188378#issuecomment-6524905572) cleared all implementation findings (Platinum patch quality) but could not inspect Gist artifacts. The GitHub repository mirror above addresses that access failure; overall proof reassessment and settled CI remain separate gates.

Confirming Dismiss for a DM access request leaves the confirmation idle while the row's Approve button claims to be loading.

prs.title: feat(database): prepare an exact PostgreSQL state namespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Offline recovery needs an explicit way to prepare a selected PostgreSQL shared-state namespace without treating incomplete existing storage as a fresh database.

## User Impact

Operators can run `openclaw database prepare-state --expected-store-id <uuid> --expected-namespace <namespace> --json` against an existing matching local anchor. An absent namespace is prepared with the installed schema; an existing namespace must pass current-version identity and catalog admission. The command does not migrate or repair existing state. Shared-state schema remains 39. The canonical CLI reference now includes the command tree entry, exact identity options, existing-anchor prerequisite, offline custody, absent-only bootstrap, strict existing-store validation, outputs, and safe failure guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command reuses current config selection, schema custody, native bootstrap and existing-only PostgreSQL admission. It keeps the exact local anchor and closes owned native resources before releasing custody. No migrations or schema columns are added.

Simplification: narrowed donor dependencies to physical-store and PostgreSQL connection owners, and limited close to the selected path. Production growth: 160 lines; integration tests: 186 lines, allocated separately because this new command has no prior owner-boundary coverage.

## Evidence

- Documentation-only follow-up 64c84ce426f5cdf1fd50c5b7fc9b956d3d56a535 on implementation head 7f7aede6ca879462e13004aaece973f91a3ea350: `docs/cli/index.md` audited against command registration, implementation, schema lease, namespace derivation, and existing PostgreSQL integration tests. `pnpm docs:list`, targeted `pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/cli/index.md`, `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/cli/index.md`, and `git diff --check` pass. No production/runtime changes; prior implementation proof below was not rerun or relabeled as new proof. The repository-wide anchor audit checked 17,932 links and reported two unrelated failures in untouched content: duplicate `agent-process-environment` in `/tools/acp-agents-setup` and missing `/providers/openai/runtimes#agents-api-mvp` from `releases/2026.10.1.md:849`; no changed-page links failed. ClawHub fragments were not checked because the external docs checkout is absent. 
- Real PostgreSQL 17.11: three command-registration integration tests pass, including absent initialization, ready retry with unchanged anchor/data/metadata, mismatched anchor, incomplete namespace, current-version catalog drift, and store-ID drift.
- Final test file: 5.49 seconds of assertions; 82.71 seconds Vitest wall time (cold compiled-worker preparation dominates), wrapper 89.53 seconds. CI time unavailable; not published.
- Production and command-test tsgo leaves pass. Type-aware lint passes for all three changed TypeScript files; corrected fixture lint passes. Formatting and git diff --check pass.
- Fresh independent autoreview, Codex gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2, local candidate against 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914: complete, one P2 finding declined. The reviewer requested rejecting absent/changed schema seals. Current engine owner intentionally reconstructs and compares exact DDL for unsealed stores, changed build DDL bytes, and server-major changes, with preserveSeal=true leaving installed metadata unchanged (postgres-schema.ts:197–230; docs/reference/database-engines.md:723–734). This is catalog validation, not repair of the selected namespace. Adding a second seal policy in this CLI would reject owner-valid stores and violate the requirement to use current admission. Temporary scratch-schema validation remains an accepted owner behavior.
- Gaps: full source CLI proof was blocked before command execution by runtime-artifact publication admission (including an isolated profile retry); no live Gateway was changed or guard bypassed. Initial PG attempt failed at infrastructure setup, and the first runnable fixture lacked the CLI one-shot role; neither is claimed as product red proof. The final fixture uses the actual CLI one-shot role. No pre-change red command proof, upgrade proof, or hosted CI is claimed. This is an opt-in command and changes no upgrade/migration behavior.

Donor reference: refs/remotes/analysis-galin/teamclaw_release_20261031, implementation adapted onto current schema39 rather than replacing any schema owner.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

Discussion, implementation, and verification took place in private agent sessions; no public session link is available.

prs.title: fix(normalization-core): restore the dropped one-day rung in relative time labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: relative time labels skipped the one-day rung entirely, so anything between 24 and 48 hours old rendered as `24h ago` … `47h ago` and then jumped straight to `2d ago` nearly half a day early.

## User Impact

Only the localized Control UI timestamps change, and only in the 24–48h window:

| Elapsed | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 23.4h | `23h ago` | `23h ago` (unchanged) |
| 23.5h | `24h ago` | `24h ago` (unchanged) |
| 24.1h – 47.99h | `24h ago` … `47h ago` | **`yesterday`** |
| 48h | `2d ago` | `2d ago` (unchanged) |

`ui/src/lib/format.ts` feeds the bucket to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `numeric: "auto"`, which is what renders `-1 day` as `yesterday`. That label was always correct and simply never received a `1`.

Compact CLI timestamps (`src/infra/format-time/format-relative.ts`, which composes `${value}${unit[0]} ago`) now read **`1d ago`** in that window instead of `24h`..`47h` — they never say `yesterday`, because that path builds a unit-initial label. CLI **age** columns (`formatTimeAgo`, used by `openclaw status` and the session table) are unchanged: they still show `30h ago`, since they select their own unit. No configuration change and no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

`bucketRelativeTimeMs` derived every unit from the already-rounded unit above it: seconds → minutes → hours → days. Two defects followed.

First, error compounded across four rounding steps (23h29m30s became 24 hours).

Second, the day rung required `hours >= 48` **before** `Math.round(hours / 24)`, which made `{ value: 1, unit: "day" }` unreachable. A missing rung is the whole behaviour: values below `2` days could never display as `1` day, so anything from 24h to 48h had to render as `24h`..`47h` and then jump to `2d` at 47.5h — roughly 12 hours early.

Each rung now promotes on its own rounded value (`minutes < 60`, then `hours < 24`) and days floor off the raw duration. Rounding at a boundary stays meaningful — a duration that rounds up to a whole hour promotes to hours instead of being labelled `60m` — while the day count finally reflects whole elapsed days.

The second/minute and the 48-hour boundary are specified contracts (`59_499ms → 59s`, `59_500ms → 1m`, `48h → 2 days`) and are unchanged; all four original cases still pass.

`ui/src/components/session-hovercard.ts` had already worked around the missing rung with its own `days >= 1` guard. That guard stays, because it still supplies the week, month, and year rungs the owner does not own.

## Evidence

Focused tests, red on the base and green with the fix, in `packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts`.

**Base (`2fe0a234f29`), test added first, no source change:**

```
FAIL  keeps 86400001ms inside the one-day rung
FAIL  keeps 171000000ms inside the one-day rung
FAIL  reaches the one-day rung somewhere between one hour and two days
      AssertionError: expected false to be true      // units.has("1day")
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  6 failed | 9 passed (15)
```

**After:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  20 passed (20)
Duration  15.04s
```

`src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts` — 54 passed.

**Runtime proof through the shipped Control UI formatter** — `ui/src/lib/format.ts` is the module that renders these labels, and it calls `bucketRelativeTimeMs` then `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, { numeric: "auto", style: "narrow" })`. No mock sits between the owner and the label:

| elapsed | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23.4h | `23h ago` | `23h ago` | |
| 23.5h | `24h ago` | `24h ago` | |
| 24.1h | `24h ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 30h | `30h ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 36h | `36h ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 47.5h | `2d ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 47.99h | `2d ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 48h | `2d ago` | `2d ago` | |
| 72h | `3d ago` | `3d ago` | |

The `47.5h → 2d ago` row is the half-day-early rounding defect from the report: before this patch four of the seven samples in 24–48h still showed hour counts, and the other two jumped to `2d` about twelve hours early. Both UI entry points agree — `formatTimeAgo(30h)` and `formatRelativeTimestamp(-30h)` both return `yesterday`, and both still return `2d ago` at 48h.

**Owner-level boundary sweep:**

```
[1] minute -> hour promotion
      3570000ms  base=1hour   now=1hour  MATCH
      3599999ms  base=1hour   now=1hour  MATCH
[2] no sub-hour value labelled 60 minutes: offenders = 0
[3] no value labelled 0 across 0..60 days:  offenders = 0
[4] hour rung tops out at 24h, day rung starts at exactly 24h   (7/7 OK)
        86399999ms -> 24hour     86400000ms -> 1day
       172799999ms -> 1day       172800000ms -> 2day
[6] preserved base contracts   (4/4 OK)
RESULT: promotion=true; sixtyMinutes=true; noZero=true; edges=true; preserved=true -> PASS
```

**Gates:** `oxfmt --check` correct format; `oxlint` clean; `tsgo -p packages/normalization-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0.

**Known gaps, stated rather than hidden:**

- The table above renders the shipped formatter module in Node. It is not a browser screenshot of a running Control UI; that would additionally cover the DOM/CSS path and needs a `pnpm dev` Gateway plus the Control UI e2e route.
- `ui/src/lib/format.test.ts` reports 1 failure on this Windows host (`expected '30秒后' to match /^in (29|30)s$/`). It is a pre-existing locale-dependent failure: with this change stashed, the same file fails identically on the base commit (`1 failed | 65 passed`).

<details>
<summary>Diff shape</summary>

```
packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts | 36 ++++++++++++++++++
packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts      | 36 ++++++++++++++++--------
2 files changed, 63 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(memory): keep note frontmatter out of durable memory
prs.body:
Closes #148186

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes note bookkeeping such as `status: active` entering memory recall and durable-memory promotion when it appears inside complete leading YAML frontmatter.

## User Impact

Recall returns note bodies with their original citation lines, and promotion rejects stale frontmatter hits. Unchanged notes are reindexed after upgrade; YAML-looking session content and incomplete frontmatter remain eligible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Markdown Core's delimiter and newline grammar through one dependency-free extractor, preserve source-line offsets, and advance the chunking revision from 6 to 7. Indexing, `memory_get`, and promotion rehydration agree on LF, CRLF, and bare CR.

Thanks to @gisk0 for #148186 and the earlier #148190, closed **unmerged** for inactivity. This change addresses that PR's index-invalidation and CR-line findings, with committed regressions and an upgrade from genuinely contaminated pre-fix index rows. Its complete discussion and related PR discussions were checked again; open #151299 covers separate promotion-anchor ambiguity rules.

## Evidence


Current integration `5e0b26c810c55c16e59d7d002a5fdd25a764d0dc` merges pinned main `11eaf275705bb106275ce9071061464b016d8291` into the original branch to include the accepted monotonic-clock fixture repair [#187454](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187454), merged as `933304ebaa40c3bcc6503567cbce7a480df808db`. This addresses the exact `tools.index-upgrade.test.ts:197` warning assertion that failed on prior head `3adeaba9`; the detailed prior-head CI diagnosis is retained below. The correction advances the same `performance.now()` clock used by the cooldown owner and includes performance in the three sibling suites' fake clocks. It changes no production clock, assertion, timeout, check rule, dependency, or test budget.

On this exact merged tree (`c9042b04801ae2fe9ceef5a2cf5983b4b89e6443`), **182 tests passed across eight complete files**, using Node 24.22.1 and the repository runner in 272.86 seconds wall. This covers all four upstream clock-fixture files, the original three frontmatter indexing/promotion/readback suites, and Markdown Core's parser suite. The previously failing detached-maintenance/provider-cost case passed in 3.65 seconds. Scoped typechecking, lint and format for the ten PR-owned TypeScript files plus four clock fixtures, and `git diff --check`, passed. Command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/tools.index-upgrade.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-session-delta.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-reindex-resume.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-startup-close.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-index-preparation.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file-shared.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The merge uses both true parents (`3adeaba9` and pinned main), with historical merge base `50c3ff63`. All eleven PR-owned file blobs, including all product changes and original regressions, remain byte-identical to `3adeaba9`; the diff against main remains exactly those eleven files. Earlier feature/Gateway/stable-upgrade and canonical P0–P3 autoreview evidence below is retained for those unchanged product bytes and its recorded inputs; it is not relabeled as an execution or full-range review of this new head. This synchronization adds no product code or tests. An independent read-only integration review confirmed both parents, all retained upstream paths, unchanged PR-owned blobs, identical dependency manifests/lockfiles, and unweakened clock-fixture assertions; no actionable finding. Its scope is this mechanical integration, not a replacement canonical review of the full feature. Current-head hosted CI now passes, including test types, changed-extension/Bun, baseline ratchets, and all three PostgreSQL conformance checks. No additional Gateway build or release run was performed for this mechanical merge.

- **Original feature proof: 158 tests passed**: the three affected indexing, promotion, and readback owners (122 tests, 179.07s wall time), plus Markdown Core's existing parser suite (36 tests). Against the unfixed production owners, six regression cases fail; fixed owners pass. Coverage includes LF/CRLF/CR, metadata-only notes, incomplete blocks, session preservation, relocated promotion candidates, and citation readback at line 4.
- **Actual built CLI/Gateway upgrade passed** (547.28s including packaged bootstrap and rebuilding the fixed runtime). The old CLI indexed and recalled two YAML-contaminated notes at revision 6. Without editing those files or manually changing persisted revision metadata, the fixed CLI's ordinary `memory index --agent qa` rebuilt revision 7 with only the body chunk at line 4. Through real plugin registration and QA-channel ingress, `memory_search` then `memory_get` used `from: 4` and returned the body without YAML. The final channel reply contained the recalled fact.
- **Actual `memory promote --apply` passed**: one valid body was appended to `MEMORY.md`; both pre-fix metadata-only and mixed metadata/body recalls were rejected during source rehydration. The resulting durable memory contained the body and no `status: active` metadata.
- Baseline and fixed `qaRuntime` builds, scoped typechecking, source/test lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. Fresh independent Codex autoreview against the true base `b703c84a84c947e198b6a683408a3ddaba9179c4`: **P0–P3 scoped-clean**. Simplification retained one shared parser grammar, with no parallel parser or new persisted schema.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-index-preparation.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file-shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs "$PROOF_WORKDIR/gateway-proof-308.mts"
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p "$PROOF_WORKDIR/tsconfig-184308.json" --pretty false
```

`PROOF_WORKDIR` denotes the task-owned isolated proof directory.

The isolated QA harness extends the repository's `memory-tools-channel-context` scenario, runs the built `dist/index.js` with packaged plugins, and uses the normal Gateway stop/restart lifecycle for offline index and promotion commands. It does not replace the indexing, readback, promotion, plugin-registration, or Gateway owners. Its baseline reads confirmed revision 6 and actual contaminated SQLite rows before building the fixed runtime.

The 85 net test-line allocation covers the three existing owner suites. The new promotion regression uses the real record/rank/apply path (3.52s); the other added cases take milliseconds. Full suite timing includes existing storage fixtures and cold compilation. Those initial checks concern their recorded source snapshot; current-head validation is stated separately.

</details>

AI-assisted implementation, regression coverage, and validation. Model and embedding providers were loopback mocks; no live account, private tenant, special operating system, or device was required. A full release build and live-provider behavior are not claimed.


<details>
<summary>Captured main-index and Gateway output</summary>

This run proves the **pre-fix main revision 6 → candidate revision 7** transition; it does not claim to prove the released 2026.10.8 revision 5 transition. The separate release-artifact upgrade run below covers that additional boundary.

It starts the actual built OpenClaw CLI/Gateway and packaged plugins (`node <checkout>/dist/index.js`, `usePackagedPlugins: true`). The driver creates two ordinary notes, stops its private Gateway through `restartAfterStateMutation`, invokes the actual pre-fix CLI `memory index --agent qa --force` and `memory search`, then rebuilds the fixed runtime and invokes **`memory index --agent qa` without force on the same state and unchanged notes**. After the Gateway restarts, a QA-channel inbound message executes the real registered `memory_search → memory_get` tool chain. A final offline `memory promote --apply` uses the actual promotion owner.

The model and embedding HTTP providers are controlled loopback services. The memory manager, database, registered tools, agent turn, Gateway, promotion command and source-rehydration owner are production implementations, not replacements. The repository [testing policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82df040c9c584fce0decbac9ebf260ec134e04c4/.agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md#L49-L56) accepts isolated mock-Gateway channel boundary proof; this makes no live-provider or live-channel claim.

prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening. Scoped direct-chat allowlists could still reach an earlier refusal even after the first repair.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders, including senders excluded by a scoped direct-chat allowlist, are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for ordinary messages. Senders admitted by dmPolicy but denied by `commands.allowFrom` keep the deliberate refusal; explicit command grants, owners, and group-command behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Native dispatch has more than one visible authorization-refusal boundary. A scoped direct `allowFrom` rejection happens during base-access evaluation, before final command authorization, so a final-only silence check left that path visible. The shared refusal path now applies the same DM-admission decision at every visible boundary. The final gate uses the latest owner result, while earlier boundaries preserve their existing explicit-grant and scoped-restriction semantics.

## Evidence
- Registered Bot pipeline with an owned loopback Bot API fixture: on the previous head, scoped-direct `/think` still produced the refusal (base-red). After the repair, account-level and scoped excluded senders produce no outbound reply and start no turn. An admitted command-denied sender still receives the refusal, an explicitly authorized sender retains the `/think` argument menu, and the existing group refusal regression stays green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, `.delivery.test.ts`, and `.concurrency.test.ts`: 38/38 passed. `bot-native-commands.registry.test.ts`: 8/8 passed, including `requireAuth:false` plugin commands. Node 24.22.1.
- Both extension production and extension-test tsgo lanes passed. Targeted extension lint completed with 0 warnings/errors across 292 rules, oxfmt passed, the SQLite worker ratchet passed against the PR merge base, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader local coverage is not claimed green: `pnpm test:extension telegram` timed out after 30 minutes with the first 11 files passing and no observed test failure; it did not finish. The full changed-check also reports existing dead-export findings outside this diff.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof was not run: the standalone doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair, so no live trace or live cleanup is claimed. Independent `autoreview` produced no verdict because Codex returned HTTP 403.

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).

prs.title: improve(backup): omit Codex diagnostics from restart checkpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local-companion restart checkpoints unnecessarily capture Codex’s changing diagnostic SQLite log database and its companions.

## User Impact

Local-companion capture omits only the activated Codex plugin’s managed agent-home `logs_2.sqlite` and `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`. Full backups and unrelated same-name files remain unchanged. Codex state, credentials, session rollouts, and other databases remain preserved. Omitted diagnostic history is not recovered; Codex recreates the log store.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep vendor policy in Codex manifest `backupResources` and add an optional generic `local-companion` profile selector to the existing planner. No global filename exclusion, extra policy owner, schema/version change, or template-exclusion option is introduced. Native backup safety and source-preservation behavior remain intact.

The native contract was inspected in [Codex 8f73cde](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4): `codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs:29,59-65,146-148,297-310` separates logs from durable databases and recreates missing stores with WAL; `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/logs.rs:3-57` records bounded diagnostic/feedback history. OpenClaw’s managed-home owner is `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts:7-42`. Custom external Codex/sqlite homes are intentionally not inferred.

## Evidence

- Standalone head: `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`, directly parented by baseline `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`. Mechanically separated from `1346e4f6f80911f634b77a212aead087089e1143`; no dependency on template-option commit `84f84f4e818851746b93a78e0a29bcf5b652bc8d`. Eleven files have byte-identical added/deleted lines; the remaining archive-create call only expands the baseline formatting to pass `localCompanion`.
- Fresh standalone proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-local-companion.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-backup-resources.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with a unique filesystem cache: **27 passed**, three files, **44.74s** including compiler preparation. Companion create/verify/restore test **237ms** (runner **7.67s**); plugin declaration runner **3.04s**; inventory runner **1.14s**. CI seconds unavailable.
- Real archive creation, verification, and restore preserve diagnostic source bytes, state/auth/rollout bytes, a similarly named sibling, unrelated same-name database, client credentials, and PostgreSQL anchors while omitting declared diagnostics. Full-archive resource selection retains the diagnostics.
- Targeted `run-tsgo` passed for all eight changed TypeScript files and their import closure; `run-oxlint` passed all eight; formatter check passed eight TypeScript files and two docs; both docs passed MDX validation; Codex manifest JSON parsed and formatter stdin output was byte-identical; `git diff --check` passed.
- Reused original red proof: the same companion regression reached real restore and failed because `logs_2.sqlite` existed instead of returning `ENOENT`. Reused broader original lane proof: **73 passed, 1 Windows-only skipped**, **131.44s**. These are original reviewed-lane results, not new-head broad-suite results.
- Reused canonical autoreview: Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium, P0–P3, complete original local candidate against `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. That review included both independent original changes; this separation changes only context and removes the unrelated template change, so no substantive re-review was required. No claim of a new standalone autoreview run.
- Simplify: one profile conditional in the existing resource planner; no new vendor code in core or duplicate exclusion owner. Production TypeScript **+34/-6**, manifest **+24**, tests **+72/-3**, docs **+13**, allocation **+2**. The 69-line test allocation covers one archive/restore regression and independent metadata-profile admission/deduplication contracts.
- Gap: PostgreSQL discovery remains an external fixed fixture. No live PostgreSQL export/reconnect, real-agent Gateway, upgrade, Windows, or new broad CI run is claimed. The selected source-preservation and archive flow are exercised at the production owning boundary.
