prs.title: docs: sessions.others membership note is wrong for "none"
prs.body:
Closes #157180

## What Problem This Solves

The help text for `gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.others` ends with:

> Explicit session membership can grant additional access.

At cap `"none"` that is false. Membership is rejected before it is ever consulted:

`src/gateway/session-sharing-policy.ts:453`
```ts
if (sessionCap === "none" && role !== "owner" && role !== "admin") {
  return hiddenSessionNotFound(params.target.canonicalKey);
}
```

And the `sessions.describe` gate is handed `isMember` but only consults `isCreator`:

`src/gateway/session-sharing.ts:186-194`
```ts
isMember: (_target, identityId) => row?.membership.has(identityId) ?? false,
});
if (
  row &&
  gatewayClientSessionCreator(params.client) &&
  sharing.sessionCap === "none" &&
  !sharing.isCreator(row.entry.createdActor)
) {
  return { error: hiddenSessionNotFound(target.sessionKey) };
}
```

This PR scopes the claim to the caps where it actually holds:

> Explicit session membership raises access at `"view"` and `"suggest"`; `"write"` already permits participation without it. At `"none"` membership grants nothing and only owners and administrators retain access.

Help text only. No schema shape, default, or runtime behavior changes.

## User Impact

`"none"` is the value in the documented example, so the sentence misleads in the configuration operators most often start from. It reads as a third option — keep `"none"` and grant membership per session — which does not exist. The real choice is `"none"` or everyone-sees-everything.

The cost is not theoretical. On a 27-person gateway I added membership rows for 20 profiles, observed no change, and only found the cause by reading the shipped bundle. Because the denial surfaces as `hiddenSessionNotFound` rather than a permission error, nothing at runtime points back at the cap — so the help text is the main signal available, and it points the wrong way.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrowing rather than deleting, because membership genuinely does matter at `"view"` and `"suggest"`; removing the sentence would lose real information.

The first revision of this PR was itself imprecise and was corrected after review on both points:

- *"at `view` and above"* overstated the range — `"write"` already permits participation without membership.
- *"hides sessions from non-owners"* overstated the denial — the check is `role !== "owner" && role !== "admin"`, so an administrator who did not create the session retains access at `"none"`.

## Evidence

**Policy claim, on a live Gateway** (`2026.9.5` / `ec9c1a1`), same users and connections throughout, `session_members` rows present in both runs so membership was not the variable:

| `sessions.others` | `sessions.describe` | `board.get` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` + membership rows present | 0 ok / 93 failed | failed |
| `write` | ok | ok |

**Rendered help field**, copied from `openclaw config schema` on a real Gateway before and after applying this change. No redaction needed — the field contains no endpoints, addresses or credentials.

Before:
```
Access to other people's sessions: "none" hides them, "view" allows reading,
"suggest" permits the suggestion flow, and "write" permits participation.
Explicit session membership can grant additional access.
```

After:
```
Access to other people's sessions: "none" hides them, "view" allows reading,
"suggest" permits the suggestion flow, and "write" permits participation.
Explicit session membership raises access at "view" and "suggest"; "write"
already permits participation without it. At "none" membership grants nothing
and only owners and administrators retain access.
```

**Source review:** both call sites read on `main` at time of filing; `main` still carries the unqualified sentence.

**Config compatibility:** one description string in `schema.help.core.ts`, plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` (`pnpm config:docs:gen`) that the help change requires. No config surface, default, or schema shape changes; existing configs parse and behave identically, and there is no upgrade or migration impact.

prs.title: build(release): stop releases shipping a Codex plugin floor that admits broken plugins
prs.body:
Refs #181619

The immediate `startedAtMonotonicMs` failure was fixed by #182995. This PR adds a release-time compatibility check to catch future stale runtime floors; it does not replace that runtime fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a release can ship with a Codex plugin floor (`minimumCompatibleVersion` in `src/plugins/official-runtime-plugins.ts`, #168930) that still admits plugin releases the new core breaks. Nothing checks the floor against the release, so it falls behind silently. #181619 is the result: 2026.10.6 made the Codex execution deadline require `startedAtMonotonicMs`, the floor stayed at `2026.9.7`, and a left-behind `@openclaw/codex` 2026.10.5 loads and fails every turn after 1 ms instead of being refused with the repair command. 2026.10.7 ships the same floor.

## User Impact

User impact: none at runtime. Release tooling only. `release-check` now fails when a version-bound runtime's floor no longer type-checks against the release being cut, and names the fix (raise the floor). Users then get the existing refusal with `openclaw update repair` / `openclaw plugins update codex` guidance instead of silently failing turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The floor is the existing owner for this (#168930): a hand-kept literal, bumped "when a Plugin SDK subpath used by this runtime is removed". Two kinds of change slipped past it:

- a newly required argument: `startedAtMonotonicMs` (#155801, included in 2026.10.6);
- removed exports: `sanitizeToolArgs` (#169063) and `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME` (#180106) on main.

The Codex runtime imports these private-local SDK pieces lazily and declares an open-ended `pluginApi`, so a stale floor only shows up as failing turns after an update.

`scripts/check-official-runtime-floor.mts` checks the floor itself: for each version-bound runtime it takes that runtime's source at its floor release tag and type-checks it inside the checkout being released (root `tsconfig.json`, so the core's SDK is read from source). A type error in the old runtime means the floor admits a runtime this release breaks. It catches both removed exports and changed arguments. It reuses the release checkout's install for third-party dependencies.

- `release-check` calls it before packing. It reads the floors from the release checkout (`process.cwd()`), not from the trusted tooling checkout the npm preflight runs from, so each release line is checked against its own floor.
- A missing floor tag fails if the floor is older than the release candidate. Only an unreleased floor equal to the candidate version is skipped.
- A floor above the release version fails, because it would refuse the runtime published with that release.
- Release checkouts are shallow and tagless, so the check fetches only the floor tag.

Also: the floor comment now covers exports and required arguments, and points to the check; `docs/help/testing-updates-plugins.md` describes the step next to `release:check`.

Not changed: the floor values themselves. In the historical v2026.10.7 checks below, raising the floor to `2026.10.6` passed the missing-argument check. On the tested main build `a3a5add7136`, older published plugins also failed on removed exports. These are reproductions of the original compatibility gaps, not a claim that today's release needs those exact floor values; #182995 subsequently fixed the original missing-argument failure. Release owners still choose the appropriate floor for each release.

## Evidence

Proof artifice: the CLI regression creates a local Git tag, a minimal synthetic plugin and SDK, and an intentionally missing tarball; the compiler is real. Historical release-checkout runs used released source with floor values deliberately changed for the failing and passing comparisons. Published-package model runs are separate evidence for the original incident, not proof of the new CLI test.

Test lines are net +205 against `main`: 119 lines cover the new planner, diagnostic classification and release-checkout ownership; 86 reuse the existing CLI fixture and native compiler helpers to catch missing tags and real compiler incompatibility at the release gate. Planner-only tests cannot prove that release-check invokes the guard before package inspection.

The 205-line allocation uses the existing `config/test-lines-allocations` mechanism in `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`, now included in this branch through the main merge. No new allocation mechanism is introduced.

Current PR CI: `openclaw/ci-gate` passes on `efc0af357948bedd40456f7226304c5a4eede228`. On November 1, all reported checks had completed: 182 successful, 51 skipped, one neutral, and no failures. prs.title: fix(channels): preserve ingress retries after lost claim ownership
prs.body:
Supersedes #158083, thanks @YangManBOBO.
Closes #158082.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recovering abandoned inbound-message claims consumes delivery retries and overwrites the last real failure timestamp, which can cause premature dead-lettering on a later genuine failure.

## User Impact

User impact: messages interrupted by a lost worker retain their delivery retry budget and failure history. Genuine dispatch failures still reach the existing retry limit. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stale-owner recovery returns the existing row to pending without recording a delivery failure. Keep that distinction in the current worker kernel while preserving its existing claim fencing. The ordinary failure path continues to record attempts.

The simplification removes the two recovery-only retry-field assignments and their unnecessary expression callback: production net **-1 line**. The existing drain lifecycle regression gains a stale-owner case with **+3 test lines**, covered by a matching test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `c8f87b2e5163870671510659745f4167239ff50e`:** the production drain/SQLite-worker regression failed because recovery changed attempts from 1 to 2 and lastAttemptAt from 100 to 101, without another delivery failure.
- **Green after:** 80 tests across `ingress-drain.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.claim-ownership.test.ts`, and `ingress-retry-policy.test.ts`; named-file command with `--maxWorkers=1` completed in 39.46 seconds including worker preparation (changed drain file: 23 cases, 5.931 seconds of reported case time; changed-channel CI job: 106 seconds including setup). The regression repeats lost-owner recovery three times, verifies preserved retry facts and successful redispatch, then verifies a genuine failure dead-letters at the configured limit. Existing cancellation and claim-fencing coverage also passes.
- Focused proof ran on Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox ([remote environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41378106033)); PR CI supplies broad proof. No live transport or production Gateway was exercised or changed. Contributor code was read with gh and was never executed; this is an independent reimplementation on current main.
- Local `autoreview`, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2, reviewed the complete candidate at `09da8acdd4c201716ac6e7152bdd1d2d6e77af91` against the pinned main above: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the maintainer fallback uses autoreview and one hosted review request when ready.
- Touched-file lint (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`): 2 files clean in 2.32 seconds; touched-file oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix(channels): stale-claim recovery no longer consumes ingress retry budget
prs.body:
Closes #158082

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel ingress event whose claim owner is lost (lease expired or process died) has its retry budget consumed and its real prior failure erased, so healthy events can be dead-lettered prematurely with no real handler failure behind them.

## User Impact

User impact: an inbound event interrupted by a crash, restart, or lease expiry is re-dispatched without burning an attempt, and its previous real handler failure is preserved for diagnostics. Premature dead-lettering from recovery churn is eliminated. No schema, configuration, public API, or data migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release contract already records owner-loss as non-failure: every other owner-lost path in the ingress drain (`GatewayDrainingError`, unadopted, superseded) passes `recordAttempt: false` to `release`, which keeps `attempts`/`last_attempt_at`/`last_error` intact. `releaseClaimIfStillStale` was the only owner-lost path that instead incremented `attempts`, overwrote `last_attempt_at`, and never wrote `last_error`, violating that contract. Because `recoverStaleClaims` runs on every `drainOnce` with `staleMs: 0` (and `claimNext` routes stale claims through it too), a repeatedly re-claimed event could climb toward the dead-letter limit (default 8) purely from recovery, with backoff skewed and diagnostics misleading.

The fix stops the attempts increment and `last_attempt_at` overwrite in `releaseClaimIfStillStale` (the row's `status`/`claim_*` reset and `updated_at` remain). No new API surface; the behavior now matches the existing `recordAttempt: false` contract. The production change is the SET clause in one statement.

## Evidence

### Regression test (TDD: red before fix, green after)

Added to `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts`: enqueue an event, fail it once via `release({ lastError: "real failure", releasedAt: 20 })`, re-claim with a replacement worker, then `recoverStaleClaims({ staleMs: 5, now: 30 })`.

- Before the fix: `AssertionError` — row returns `attempts: 2`, `lastAttemptAt: 30` (budget consumed, real failure erased).
- After the fix: `attempts: 1`, `lastAttemptAt: 20`, `lastError: "real failure"` (budget preserved, real failure intact).

```text
$ pnpm test src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts -t "recoverStaleClaims does not consume retry budget"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 32 skipped (33)
```

### Full related suite

```text
$ pnpm test src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-drain.tombstone-lane.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-claim-owner.test.ts
76 passed
```

Also ran the ingress subset of the state-migrations suite (passed).

### Typecheck

This change is a small, self-contained statement edit in `ingress-queue.ts` plus one test file. Full-repo `tsgo` on this Windows host cannot complete (the `run-tsgo` wrapper hangs in its job-object spawn layer; the underlying compiler binary completes), so I ran an A/B typecheck with the repo's native compiler (`tsc.exe` from the bundled tsgo distribution) on clean `main` vs. this branch: identical pre-existing error set (532 "cannot be named" declaration-emit errors in unrelated test-support files on both), zero errors in the changed files, zero diff between the two runs. This change introduces no new type errors.

### Scope boundary

Only `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts` (one SET clause) and its test file changed. No behavior change to `release()` (the `recordAttempt: false` path was already correct), no change to `recoverStaleClaims` selection logic, and no change to retry/dead-letter policy values.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep the lane timeout cause in scheduled run diagnostics
prs.body:
Fixes: a scheduled run killed by its lane's progress-idle watchdog records only `cron: job execution timed out`, so the run history never says why it was killed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a cron run stopped by its lane watchdog reports `cron: job execution timed out` with no cause, so you cannot tell a no-progress watchdog kill from a task-budget kill or an operator abort.

## User Impact

User impact: Task-run history now records the actual lane-timeout cause (`no progress for <idleMs>ms (task budget <ms>, elapsed <ms>)`) instead of a generic message, so an operator can tell a stalled run from one that hit its budget. The user-facing error text is unchanged, and no existing reader needs to change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runCronIsolatedAgentTurnInTrace` detects a `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError`, swaps it for the generic operator text, and then built the cron diagnostic from that generic text. The queue had already computed the cause and its numbers (`progress-idle`, `idleMs`, `taskBudgetMs`) and put them in the error message; the diagnostic step discarded them.

The fix passes the original error to the diagnostic builder, so the existing redaction owner keeps the detail. `error` still owns the run row and `lastError`, so the operator-facing summary is byte-identical to before.

This deliberately does **not** change timeout or progress policy. The issue also claimed the progress timer never re-arms; that claim does not hold on current main (`armProgressTimeout()` re-arms off `readLastProgressAtMs()` on every fire), and whether agent-side polling should count as lane progress is a progress-contract decision for maintainers.

## Evidence

The defect is one input swap in `runCronIsolatedAgentTurnInTrace`. Before, the run detected the
lane timeout, replaced the real error with the generic operator text, and handed **that** text to
the diagnostic builder; now it hands over the original error:

```ts
createCronRunDiagnosticsFromError(isCronLaneTimeout ? "cron-setup" : "agent-run", err)
```

### Before / after through the real diagnostic builder

Both inputs fed to `createCronRunDiagnosticsFromError` (`src/cron/run-diagnostics.ts`) - the
generic text the old code passed, and the real `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` the new code passes:

```
$ node --import tsx .agents/goal-6cc6acae-R2-beforeafter.mts
[before] diagnostic message = "cron: job execution timed out"
[after ] diagnostic message = "Command lane \"cron-nested\" task timed out: no progress for 900000ms (task budget 1800000ms, elapsed 930000ms)"
[after ] entry.source       = cron-setup
RESULT: before keeps the generic text and after keeps the lane cause -> PASS
```

### Real runtime path: `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`

The regression test drives the real production entry point `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` through
the real orchestration fixture (`job-fixtures.ts` -> `makeIsolatedAgentParamsFixture`), with only
the model call stubbed to reject with a real `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError`:

```
$ node -e ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/cron/isolated-agent/run.diagnostic-events.test.ts --reporter=verbose

OK emits billed model usage when the cron run is aborted before finalization                  4,148ms
OK keeps the lane timeout detail in diagnostics instead of only the generic abort text        3,726ms
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

Both failures reproduce identically **with and without** this change on the Windows/Node 24 host
used for this run: a 120 s test timeout on the trace case, and dispatch-event duration inflation
(109,225 ms against a 120 s budget) making the `diagnostics: { enabled: false }` case observe
dispatched messages. Neither touches the diagnostic builder this change edits, and the CI
`checks-fast-core` shard ran this whole file green on the previous heads.

The new case asserts both halves of the contract at once:

```
OK run row:    { status: "error", error: "cron: job execution timed out" }   <- unchanged
OK diagnostic: { source: "cron-setup", severity: "error" }                   <- lane cause kept
OK message contains: Command lane "cron-nested" task timed out
                     no progress for 900000ms
                     task budget 1800000ms
```

Without the fix the assertion fails with `expected 'cron: job execution timed out' to contain
'Command lane "cron-nested" task timed.'` - the pre-fix diagnostic carried only the generic text.

`oxfmt --check`: clean. `oxlint`: exit 0.

<details>
<summary>Gap in local checks</summary>

`scripts/run-vitest.mjs` cannot run on this host at all: it fails during its compiled-subprocess
build (`SyncRpcChannel: timed out connecting to named pipe`), reproduced on an unrelated test file,
so the commands above call `node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs` directly. The repo-wide `tsgo` run on
this checkout reports 12 pre-existing errors in files this change does not touch (`fast-uri` and
`@noble/hashes` module resolution, plus `src/process/darwin-process-inspection.ts`); neither
changed file appears in that output. CI is the authoritative typecheck and test gate.
</details>

<!-- Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled. -->

### Existing coverage that pinned the defect

`src/cron/cron-execution-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts` asserted the generic replacement text as the expected diagnostic, so it encoded the bug. prs.title: fix(pairing): pairing list and approve print only "The CLI command failed." instead of the reason
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw pairing list` and `openclaw pairing approve` print only "The CLI command failed. For help, run `openclaw doctor`." for every input problem, so users never see why, for example when no chat DM pairing channel is configured or a pairing code doesn't match.

## User Impact

User impact: pairing commands now print the actual reason and the next step, such as "use openclaw devices approve instead" or "No pending pairing request found for code …. Run openclaw pairing list --channel telegram". Exit codes and `--json` output are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pairing command threw plain `Error` for its input checks. The root failure handler treats plain errors as unexpected and replaces them with the generic line, while `--json` showed the real message. The checks now use the existing `throwExpectedCliError` helper, like logs, devices and exec-approvals, so the message is printed as-is. No wording or behavior changes beyond that.

Related: #182614 (pairing approve "fails silently" in Docker). #177999 adds `pairing dismiss` in the same file with the same helper.

## Evidence

Before/after output captured on a build of `main` at 7b29a23 on Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory with no channels configured. Tests were rerun on the new base c1efa8bc31 (no changes to the pairing files between the two).

Before:
```
$ openclaw pairing list
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw pairing approve ABC123
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw pairing approve telegram ABC123
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw pairing list --json   # the reason was only visible here
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "No chat DM pairing channels are configured. To approve a TUI or device request, use openclaw devices approve instead." } }
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw pairing list
No chat DM pairing channels are configured. To approve a TUI or device request, use openclaw devices approve instead.
$ openclaw pairing approve ABC123
Usage: openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code> (or: openclaw pairing approve --channel <channel> <code>)
$ openclaw pairing approve telegram ABC123
No pending pairing request found for code "ABC123". Run openclaw pairing list --channel telegram to list pending requests.
$ openclaw pairing list --channel telegram --account ' '
--account must not be blank
```
All exit 1, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 13 passed.
- New test "shows the devices redirect in human failure output, not a generic failure" runs the real `formatCliFailureLines` path. It fails on `main` (`expected '[openclaw] The CLI command failed.…' to contain 'No chat DM pairing channels are configured.'`) and passes with the fix. The existing tests only checked the thrown message, which is why they passed while users saw the generic line.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

Local review: autoreview / local ClawSweeper not run (not available in this environment). Self-reviewed the diff: only the error type changes; messages, control flow and exit codes are the same.

Keep the probe parser in its existing owner and repair the root-dispatch regression expectation. prs.title: fix(backup): name the stop step when a managed browser locks its profile
prs.body:
Fixes #187882

## What Problem This Solves

On native Windows, a running OpenClaw-managed browser keeps durable profile files under `<state>/browser/<profile>/user-data` open and locked (for example `Default/Network/Cookies`, LevelDB `LOCK` files). `openclaw backup create` then fails with no supported recovery step:

- On current main it fails at SQLite discovery with the generic `Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. Check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable, then retry the backup.` The header-probe child threw the real `EBUSY` with its stack, and the parent replaced it with that text.
- When discovery passes and the archiver hits the lock (the report's 2026.10.8 shape), it fails with `Backup archive write failed: EBUSY ... (last offending path: ...Cookies, after 1 attempt)`.

Neither tells the operator which owner holds the file or what to do.

## User Impact

- When a backup source is in use (`EBUSY`), both failure stages name the file and code; for files under a managed browser profile they add the conditional recovery step `If the OpenClaw-managed browser profile "<profile>" is running, stop it with openclaw browser --browser-profile <profile> stop, then retry the backup.` Other in-use files get `Close that process, then retry the backup.`
- Access denials (`EACCES`/`EPERM`) are described as such (`could not be read (EACCES). Check that this user can read it.`) and never claim another process holds the file; under a browser profile the stop step is added only as a conditional, because Windows can surface a sharing lock as `EPERM`.
- Backup semantics are unchanged: locked profile files are never skipped, and no incomplete archive is published. Other probe failures keep the existing generic message.
- `docs/cli/backup.md` documents the stop-and-retry procedure next to the managed-browser profile rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Verify the managed-browser stop/retry procedure on native Windows, then add actionable recovery guidance for both discovery and archive-read failures." The probe worker now reports an unreadable source as `{ code, path }` on stderr and sets `process.exitCode = 3` (no forced `process.exit`, per `openclaw-boundaries/no-forced-process-exit`) instead of throwing a stack trace, so the parent can keep the cause; one small helper (`describeLockedBackupSource`) derives the hint from the errno code and the `browser/<profile>/user-data` layout, and both `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` and `writeTarArchiveWithRetry` append it.

## Evidence

Local live run on native Windows 11, Node 26.12.1: isolated state, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw start` + `open https://example.com` (real Chromium-family profile on disk), then `openclaw backup create --no-include-workspace --verify --output <dir>` from a separate process, then `openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw stop` and the same backup again. Same rig; only the build differs (main `9e86c84` vs this branch).

![backup with running managed browser on Windows, main vs fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/187882/proof-187882-v2.png)

| step | main | fix |
|---|---|---|
| backup while the managed browser runs | exit 1, generic "check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable" | exit 1, `<state>\browser\openclaw\user-data\Default\Extension Rules\LOCK is in use by another process (EBUSY). If the OpenClaw-managed browser profile "openclaw" is running, stop it with openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw stop, then retry the backup.` |
| incomplete archive published | no | no |
| after `openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw stop`, same backup | exit 0, `Archive verification: passed` | exit 0, `Archive verification: passed` |

This verifies the documented stop/retry procedure end to end on native Windows. The archive-read stage (`Backup archive write failed: ...`) is covered through its owner, `writeTarArchiveWithRetry`, in `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts`: EBUSY and EPERM under a browser profile, EBUSY and EACCES on a non-browser file (asserting no "another process" claim for EACCES), and ENOENT unchanged. Against main's `backup-tar-retry.ts`: `4 failed | 1 passed`; with the fix: `5 passed`. `config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` (`no-forced-process-exit`) fails on the previous head's worker and passes now.

Checks run locally: `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-create-stream.test.ts`.


## Review round 3 (ff5f1e1)

Merged `upstream/main` (`66004e0`) to clear the merge conflict. The merge changed no PR code: `git diff a0f077c ff5f1e1` over `src/infra/backup-locked-source.ts`, `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-tar-retry.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts` and `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.worker.ts` is empty. In `docs/cli/backup.md` upstream rewrote the PostgreSQL section; the managed-browser stop/retry paragraph this PR adds is still the same 2-line addition against main.

Rerun on the merged head: `pnpm test src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts` → 5 passed; `oxfmt --check` clean on all 6 changed files; CI `ci-gate` and all `checks-node-changed-*` shards SUCCESS.

prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions accumulate transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history and retires discarded bodies from projections and presentation caches.

## User Impact

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks while ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Reader/native-source atomicity and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. After investigation, the owner accepts that product tradeoff; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. Local command replies retain transient custody across their own refresh, then retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership now controls trimming, reopening, local outputs and retirement. Same-snapshot Stop continuation admits only fresh validated packets. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits; prepared bodies do not. Visible fitting broad reads commit when no further adaptive envelope exists, avoiding unnecessary fallback/staged reads while preserving sparse/raw progress and exact smaller-envelope retries.

The same synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and admission, retaining cold/binding refits and accepted-prefix-only receipt adoption. Native offset facts drive paging/follow from one producer, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Presentation-keyed partial retirement releases dormant bodies without discarding safe survivor seeds. Weak terminal-row revision reuse preserves exact digest bytes and supported content/block/reaction updates. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts instead of every message-array replacement; nonempty retirement still invalidates released quote bodies.

No protocol-version, config or SQLite-schema change. No new dependency. The declared 400-entry /3MiB /eight-segment residency targets and geometry limits stayed fixed throughout this investigation.

## Evidence

Current signed **`1152ebf76202b601a75b7cdba231720b8dc79abe`**, tree `37c9739f7f4dea81ec980043348599a49726801a`; frozen base `77b08d1345a8e5734ada19dc95e77f4c5135bd0a`. Full **167 paths / 3,555,052 B**, manifest `9e2b2442652a1d8e89c923df330fa68e9a0fdf8532655ac46b85c435ee0a8f17`. Both retained task checkouts are clean, signed and physically verified.

**Exact-head source review: three complete f554→1152 source-review passes found no actionable P0–P2 findings; independent current R1/R2/R3 resolution is scoped clean. Native correction validation accepted READY with inherited failures explicitly attributed. Native prepare-gates recorded `github_pending` for1152; hosted CI/security, exact-head ClawSweeper review and before/after screenshots with public readback remain pending. This is not a passing full-CI or numerical-performance verdict.**

- Current producer/render/helper coverage: **372 distinct cases**. Final owner controls, relocation-context49 cases, targeted format/lint/diff/LF and selected fresh `ui` plus repaired/retried `core-test-ui-chat` passed. Earlier graphs and suites retain their executed-source scopes; no fresh whole-suite/whole-PR claim. LF **6,342,681 / 6,366,312**, slack23,631.
- Current canonical qaRuntime backend/current-head readiness (runtime-only declarations, excluding fullDTS and standalone-AI qualification) and normal UI/full genuine v6 seal passed: **3,702 consumed inputs / 6,115 files / 131,670,870 B**, UI digest `d56f3a0d9c72c707c8500a03c718e4a84ea6d0f5f2bc13ceee7164bba756e48c`. All20 output roots and full167 source/index/seal guards restored.
- Fresh strict assets passed unchanged caps: **Chat1,275,832 /1,276,669 gzip B; New784,880 /797,395; startup88,992 /89,406**. All seven protected baseline/budget/tolerance/result values equal the prior qualification; violations/warnings empty. RawCSS+51B uses only existing64B variance. The separate normal-build rawCSS advisory remains disclosed.
- Original **UNTRACED real-Gateway900→1→900** passed: six resident windows, five directional admissions, six history calls including one count-one anchor, two session-list calls, no rollback. Bookmark key/offset restored after three session retirements. Single wall2,766.174ms /rendererCPU572.349ms /post-two-GC33,981,416B is raw diagnostic scope, not a matched comparison or improvement.
- Original historical controlled geometry proofs retain their checkpoints:168 finite frames/max0.4375px under2px,12px negative/40px reader controls and real local `/help`/Latest order. Current untraced run skipped that separate controlled case; it is not relabeled current geometry replay.
- Historical prefix122, selector142, capacity137 and native-fact227 are scoped composites. Presentation-key hidden/no-next-render GC, row-revision47 and current actual-owner render controls passed. Whole-PR33/33 at818 plus later scoped source corrections remain a review chain; fresh f554→1152 configured review completed three passes with no actionable P0–P2 findings, limited to supplied source/context and without executing project commands. Current R1/R2/R3 independent source resolution is scoped clean.

### Performance investigation and accepted product tradeoff

Historical **87d** ten interleaved baseline→candidate pairs remain **REJECTED**: wall median **1,481.747→2,827.432ms (+90.82%)**, renderer CPU **269.290→541.696ms (+101.16%)**,30/36 raw cells worse and over20%. All ten candidate functional cases passed; baseline failures were solely original post-metrics residency assertions. Raw result **59,972 B / `24b2898562c295174d730971f08e78b39e1f5042c912c8a0cd15e80b0010557f`** remains unchanged. No additional pairs or rewritten stop outcome.

The predeclared >20% rule requires investigation. The owner accepts the disclosed bounded-residency/bulk-traversal tradeoff after that investigation. RPC/history/window counts are workload facts constrained by absolute budgets, cursor continuity and coverage; layout/style counts receive no exemption. Timing/CPU/heap/frame measurements remain raw. There is no current1152 matched cohort or numeric performance acceptance.

One additive observer-only run preserved the original gestures, waits, assertions and engine→wall→two-GC order. Older pages required **two existing idle attempts (526.95–534.35ms)** versus newer pages **one (214.69–217.69ms)**; all four gesture-ready waits passed first try in2.77–4.20ms. This rules out cooldown only as dominant gesture-wait cost in this capture. It does not explain all CPU or make it unavoidable. Browser/host clocks differ; host WebSocket callbacks are not network/server RTT. Later events followed closed phases, consistent with later endpoint gestures; exact per-event causes were not marked. The observer affects CPU/wall/heap, so no subtraction or speedup claim.

Current observation artifact **29,248 B / `adcf5ef7e9160bd7c31ce2050b00cdd0cbf749dc84e9178fd9e2f5f4471f334b`**: five phases,86 browser/11host scalar events, no drops/truncation, exact source/output/seal restoration. No new profiler/cohort is proposed.

prs.title: improve(ui): move page menus into the floating phone header
prs.body: Based on #190409 for its header. Until the page PRs land, this diff also shows them. **Land first, in any order:** #190409, #190368, #190374, #190387, #190369, #190380, #190385, #190393, #190535. Then retarget this to main. Conflicts between them are mechanical. ## What Problem This Solves At phone width each page with real actions keeps its `⋯` in the page, even though the floating header has a place for page buttons. On Usage and Meetings it takes space beside the description, and on Logs, Skills, Activity and Agents it takes space from the page's own controls. ## User Impact At 600px and below, the page's `⋯` joins the header's pill on Usage, Meetings, Logs, Activity Live, Skills and Agents, ahead of new session and search. Custodian's History sits in the same place. Pages without page-level actions keep a 2-button pill. The page row closes up behind it: Usage's controls move up, and New agent fills its row. Refresh appears once on each page: in the menu on Usage, Meetings, Logs and Agents, and in the row on Skills, where the menu doesn't carry it. The title stays centered at 320, 360 and 390. To make room, the pill's buttons narrow on the narrowest phones: 39px from about 373px, 37px at 360 and 30px at 320. Custodian's header title is the brand name, "OpenClaw", because "Ask OpenClaw" has no centered room beside three buttons. The sidebar keeps its label. From 601px the header doesn't float, so the menu stays in the page. Meetings keeps it to 768px, and Agents' menu also runs to 768px. Usage, Logs, Activity and Skills change to their wider controls at their own breakpoints below that. Desktop and native hosts are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made Each page passes the menu it already has to `FloatingHeaderActions`, with the same menu as `fallback`, so one set of actions covers every width. Custodian keeps the slot from #190368. The narrower buttons apply only when the slot has content, so the 2-button pill doesn't change. Usage and Meetings now use `pointerFocus="trigger"` like the other page menus, which with #190535 leaves no ring after a tap. Two existing tests changed. The Activity capture now finds its menu in the header, and the Logs layout test waits for the title to return after the width crosses 600px, because the shell updates a beat after the resize. ## Evidence Mock data layer with real clicks. The CRT image sets the theme through the stored preference the app reads at load. | Before, 390px | After, 390px | Menu open | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Agents, dark | Custodian, 320px | CRT, 320px | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Logs, 320px, Playwright WebKit | Real Safari, 390px | | --- | --- | | | | The Safari image is Safari on macOS, in its own 390px window, with the menu opened by an OS-level click. Its title is 0px off center, measured from the image's pixels. **Measured title offset:** all 7 pages at 320, 360 and 390 in Chromium and Playwright WebKit, 42 combinations, are within 0.01px of center. Each one has the button in the pill, none in the page, no horizontal overflow and no page errors. Logs also measured 0px when reached by in-app navigation in WebKit. ### Checks Run locally: oxfmt, oxlint and stylelint on touched files, `tsgo:ui`, `check:control-ui-controllers`, unit tests for the header slot, shell and Logs, browser tests for the Usage phone layout and menu focus, and these browser suites: a new `mobile-page-actions-header.e2e.test.ts`, floating header, Custodian phone header, Logs layout, Activity capture, agent files and Appearance. `ui:check-performance:base` reports only the total CSS budget, which the base already exceeds, with no growth beyond its variance. ### Not verified - **iPhone:** not tested on a device or simulator. - **Real Safari at 320 and 360:** those widths were measured in Playwright WebKit only. - **Long translated titles:** a title wider than "OpenClaw" sits left of center beside three buttons, then truncates with an ellipsis, as #190409 does for long titles.

prs.title: feat: let sandboxed plugin tabs invoke declared session actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tabs need narrowly authorized session actions without receiving Gateway credentials or a general-purpose parent HTTP proxy. This replaces #80388 and builds on #107323.

## User Impact

Plugins can expose declared actions for the parent-selected session. Revoking device authority or session access while an action waits now prevents the action from running. Failed action-enabled pages show a sanitized explanation and Retry, which obtains a fresh grant before reloading.

Existing canonical session navigation and the direct iframe flow for tabs without actions are preserved. The unused `allowChatNavigation` schema field is removed; no second public navigation API is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge keeps authorization in the existing Gateway dispatcher, registered action scopes, trusted session context, persisted access checks, and payload/result schemas. Sandboxed pages receive neither bearer tokens nor mutation cookies.

This refresh addresses the [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102#issuecomment-5005741905): recheck both authorities synchronously immediately before invoking the plugin handler, provide recoverable page errors, remove the obsolete schema field, and repair the reported lint errors. Earlier navigation and causal MessagePort test fixes are retained; branch history is preserved.

## Evidence

Validated source: [`edbac97f93bc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102/commits/edbac97f93bc6fc633779cdee607b081abc0063c).

- **Gateway: 6 tests pass.** The real dispatcher, persisted session authority, and row-preparation boundary are exercised. Current authority permits one action effect; revoking the device or removing session membership while preparation is held returns `UNAVAILABLE` with **zero effects**.
- **Plugin UI: 51 tests pass** across document, page, and bridge suites. New cases cover an HTTP failure followed by Retry with a fresh grant, policy-error reporting, and redaction of a redirect error's private URL/token.
- **Regression sensitivity demonstrated:** keeping the new tests but restoring affected production files from `82f71f3` makes both authorization-revocation cases and all three new error/retry cases fail. The current-authority control still passes. Restoring the repaired files produces the passing results above.
- **Independent review:** no actionable high/medium-priority findings in the 11-file refresh.
- **Static checks pass:** changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, UI stylelint, UI i18n catalog validation, and `git diff --check`. The PR context/evidence policy also accepts this description locally.

**Remaining verification gaps (not waived):**

- **Browser/screenshots/end-to-end evidence is blocked.** Chromium crashes with `SIGTRAP` before loading the isolated fixture; a minimal launch without PR code reproduces the crash, including with `--no-sandbox`. The installed stock Firefox ESR also exits before Playwright can connect; no Playwright-patched Firefox is installed. No current-head browser assertions, network captures, or before/after screenshots were produced. Historical captures are not presented as current proof. Full Gateway startup, authenticated WebSocket flow, production cookies, plugin discovery, and deployment remain unverified. The retained navigation tests pass in the focused UI suite, but their separate base-fail replay has not been recorded.
- The broader changed-file check stops at the line-cap ratchet because this host's Git 2.34.1 does not support `git cat-file --batch -z`. Its preceding conflict-marker check passes; later gates and broader type checks are not claimed as passing.
- Replaying the two previously failing chat-test files yields 8 passing assertions but an unhandled Lit `ChildPart has no parentNode` exception in `chat-message.mcp-app.test.ts`. The run therefore fails. Those files are unchanged, but that alone does **not** establish that the failure is unrelated to this PR; causality remains unresolved.
- New-head hosted CI has not yet been validated. Maintainer review and the screenshot requirement remain outstanding.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and local test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-host-hooks.registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-document.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On an isolated service capped at 50% CPU and 6 GiB RAM, final command wall times were 558.46 s and 64.49 s respectively (Vitest-reported durations: 492.82s and 45.86s). The persisted-authority scenarios exercise the real persistence/projection/dispatcher boundary with a causal preparation barrier, not sleeps or a mocked authority decision. CI seconds are not yet measured; these resource-capped local times are not CI estimates.

The old-source regression runs failed as expected in 866.35 s (authorization) and 51.30 s (page errors/retry). Production files were restored and their checksums verified afterward.

All verification used a separate checkout and private test state/config under resource limits. The live Gateway was not restarted, reconfigured, deployed to, or used as a test target.

</details>

## Remaining Maintainer Decision

The public `sessionActions` bridge still needs maintainer sponsorship and a long-term owner. This is an updated review candidate, not a merge request or a waiver of exact-head CI, screenshots, or owner review.

prs.title: improve(ui): float the phone page header
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width every page spends its first 58px on a brand row with a hairline, then repeats the page title in the body. The connection state is a dot on the menu button plus a status line, while chat already has its own notice for this. The new session draft sat under that same brand row, so its header changed completely when a session opened. ## User Impact On pages other than chat and the new session draft, the header now floats over the content: menu on the left, the page title centered, and one joined pill with new session and search on the right. Content scrolls under a fade. The body keeps its description and loses the repeated title, which stays available to assistive tech. While the connection is down, chat's notice floats below the header at chat's position, including Retry when offline, and the title stays. As on chat, it can sit over the description line, and taps pass through to the page beneath. Square themes keep square corners. The new session draft uses chat's header at phone width. Draft, incognito and search share one pill there, and their row below the header is gone, so the page gains that space. An active toggle shows its icon in the accent color. When a session opens the menu button and the pill's right edge stay put, and the pill changes to the session's controls. Widths above phone and native hosts are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made This is the base for the mobile page refinements. Pages add their own buttons to the pill with `FloatingHeaderActions`, passed through the `actions` they already give their header. Its `fallback` renders in place at every other width, so a page declares one set of actions. `SettingsPageHeader` now resolves `actions` once, because reading it twice would mount a portal twice. The floating layout applies at 600px and below, plus landscape phones. Tablets from 601px keep today's top bar. The notice moved out of the chat header into a shared component, with one change: its radius now follows the theme, so it is square in CRT. It looks the same in Absolutely. The draft renders the real `ChatPaneMobileHeader`, the one session creation already shows, and the shell passes it the drawer state and connection status the way it does for chat. Its content now starts at the same edges as chat, so the composer lines up with the session it opens. That widens the draft's composer from a 20px to a 16px inset, and `control-ui-boot-modules.json` is regenerated because the header now loads with the draft. Above 560px Draft stays in the composer as it does today, so the pill holds incognito and search. Coming from a floating page, the menu button goes from 45px to 40px, which is intended. Chat's header keeps its round controls in CRT, so the draft's do too. ## Evidence Images use the mock data layer at 390px, 320px where noted. The Reconnecting image comes from stopping a real Gateway at 390px, the only image here that doesn't use the mock. Stopping and restarting it put the notice at the same box as chat (x 12, y 62, 28px tall) on Automations and the new session draft, left the title unmoved, and cleared the notice on reconnect. | Floating page | Reconnecting below the header, real Gateway stopped | | --- | --- | | | | | New session, light | New session, dark | New session, CRT | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Incognito on | 320px | Real Safari | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | The Safari image is Safari 27.0.1 on macOS, with the page in a 390px frame inside its own window and OS-level clicks. prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

prs.title: fix: reject captured directories during plugin module preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explicitly preparing a plugin module can succeed when its captured entry is a directory. On Node, full-package capture keeps module inspection lazy, so a later preparation call can skip the source read that would report `EISDIR` and treat the directory as prepared. This breaks the source-error boundary introduced in #188760.

## User Impact

A selected captured directory now produces the existing classified source-read error during module preparation. Callers can retain their ordinary unavailable-source diagnostics instead of receiving a successful preparation result for an invalid module.

Regular files retain lazy Node preparation. Recursive directory capture, recovery copies, forks, private-file replacement errors, and worker disposal keep their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture owner already records which private paths represent directories, and the source reader already distinguishes an invalid directory selection from a private file-type replacement. Pass those existing facts to explicit module preparation and use that reader before materialization or an early success return. This avoids an additional filesystem scan or a second error-classification mechanism.

## Evidence

The two existing regression files reproduced both failures on the base: 37 tests passed and the worker-directory and repeated-preparation cases returned successfully instead of throwing. The same files also exercise recovery/fork directory facts and fatal private replacement handling.

On the correction, changed-file formatting/lint and the native production and consumer/test type checks passed. Twelve Node files passed 165 tests, with one existing macOS-only streaming case skipped on Linux. That batch includes the two original regression files, snapshot/custody consumers, and the lazy-resolution control.

The checksum-pinned Bun runtime passed all 56 tests across the two original regression files and the lazy-resolution consumer. Both runtimes preserve repeated rejection, classified `EISDIR`, private replacement handling, recovery/fork facts and worker cleanup. Existing tests were reused without assertion or fixture changes. All selected hosted CI checks passed.

prs.title: feat(ui): add saved gateway account switching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This repair closes the remaining Gateway-profile correctness and proof gaps:

- Active profile removal uses the returned survivor projection directly, so the deleted URL cannot be reintroduced by fallback loading.
- Query-aware migrated credentials are sent only to their owning exact endpoint at the outgoing WebSocket client boundary.
- Successful token-mode migration retires the old origin-scoped token; clearing an owned migrated profile retires both exact and legacy slots.
- Query-distinct profiles cannot recover a neighboring profile's credential.

Profiles remain local browser metadata. Credentials remain session-scoped; no server-side account or shared credential store was added.

## Evidence

- Pushed head: `9b7ed952e4a4d0fd5367c96074b62b93496f38cb`.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec vitest run ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-registry.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **117/117 passed** across 4 suites.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec oxfmt --check ui/src/app/settings.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/pages/connection/connection-page.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 tsgo:ui` — passed from an independently owned checkout install.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 ui:build` — passed: **3,401 modules**, **840 finalized sidecars**, startup JS gzip **345,895 B** under the **352,235 B** limit; startup CSS **44,978 B** under the **51,200 B** ceiling.

## Fresh headed-browser proof

Run on 2026-09-11 against exact-head build `8023b23`/the pushed repair checkout, using disposable token Gateways and temporary state:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:19889` with a synthetic redacted token label `personal`.
- `ws://127.0.0.1:19890?account=team` with a synthetic redacted token label `team`.
- Real headed Chromium opened `http://127.0.0.1:19889/settings/connection`; the UI reached the actual WebSocket Gateway handshake and displayed token-authenticated connected state for both endpoints.
- Browser flow added and switched to the query-bearing Team profile, then confirmed removal of the active Team profile. The page reconnected to the surviving `19889` profile and the removed row stayed absent.
- The outgoing-boundary regression captured the actual client constructor options: migrated exact URL plus its owned token; after token-mode hello, the exact token key existed and the legacy origin key was gone.
- The clear regression seeded an owned origin-migrated token, cleared it, and verified both that profile and a query-distinct neighbor loaded with an empty token; the legacy key was absent.
- Browser storage and console diagnostics were redacted: no token values were retained. Browser console reported 2 development/runtime errors from the session; no zero-console-error claim is made.

## Limitation

After the browser's first successful token handshake, the Gateway issued a device grant. Clearing the visible Gateway secret and clicking Connect therefore remained connected through device authentication; this does not claim that clearing revokes an existing device grant. The no-token-reuse claim is proven at the outgoing client boundary and by the storage regression, while the live browser proof confirms the real handshake, profile switching, survivor removal, and endpoint identity.

The final post-push exact-head startup check launched runtime `9b7ed95` but detected that the runtime build stamp was still from `8023b23` while the rebuilt UI was `9b7ed952`, and correctly returned HTTP 503 rather than serving a mixed build. The interactive headed-browser receipt therefore comes from the immediately preceding compatible runtime; the final-head changes are covered by the 117-test suite, exact-head UI build, and the outgoing-boundary regression.

No new ClawSweeper review was requested.

prs.title: fix(agents): incrementally append tagged stream snapshots
prs.body:
Closes #175441

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway CPU is blocked for seconds on long replies from tagged-provider streams (`enforceFinalTag`), because the whole reply is re-rendered twice per streamed delta (5.7 s at 32 KB, 22.7 s at 64 KB per #175441).

## User Impact

User impact: long streamed replies from tagged providers no longer stall the Gateway as they grow, so other sessions and clients stay responsive while a reply streams. Streamed output is unchanged; the fast path falls back to the existing extraction whenever it cannot prove an append is equivalent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an incremental fast path for tagged block-reply streaming when `enforceFinalTag` is enabled, so each delta no longer re-extracts the full accumulated text.

- The fast path appends directly only when the existing stream state is known to be verbatim and the incoming delta contains no markup that could invalidate that assumption.
- A trailing reasoning-close guard keeps a later delta from bypassing canonical reconciliation after a `</think>`-style boundary.
- Whenever those invariants do not hold, the canonical extraction/reconciliation path runs as before, so there is still one owner of the resulting stream state.
- Added differential tests cover reasoning-close boundaries, supported close-tag variants, mid-stream chunking/draining, and equivalence with canonical extraction.

Accepted tradeoff: the append-unstable final-answer sanitizer is mutually exclusive with the `enforceFinalTag`/`blockVerbatim` fast path, so the fast path never has to account for it.

## Evidence

- Focused `update-stream-items` test: 48/48 passed.
- Differential fuzzing against canonical extraction: 68,702 steps, 0 mismatches; the fast path was exercised 3,316 times.
- Full embedded-agent-subscribe suite: 35 files / 524 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: 29 shards passed.
- `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- oxlint: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Autoreview reviewed the diff and the tests/evidence (it did not execute the code) and produced no accepted or actionable findings. Its one P2 finding concerned the append-unstable final-answer sanitizer; it was investigated and disproved because that sanitizer is mutually exclusive with the `enforceFinalTag`/`blockVerbatim` fast path.



### Test-line ceiling justification

The test-line ceiling is raised to 6,287,000 to accommodate the PR's 512 net additional test lines: 509 lines in the tagged-stream regression test file and 3 lines in a shared test helper. The additional tests verify incremental tagged-stream equivalence with canonical reconciliation, fallback behavior, canonical reasoning-tag parsing, orphan-close variants, code-span ownership, reasoning-depth guarding, unclosed reasoning tags, and differential equivalence across tag-heavy delta sequences.

This change adjusts the test-growth budget only; it does not alter runtime behavior or reduce existing test coverage.

Note on the old value: the branch's tracked baseline was 6,285,000 (stale), while `main`'s baseline was 6,286,403 when checked. The diff therefore shows 6,285,000 -> 6,287,000. Against `main` at `679c5d1312e`, the merged tree measures 6,286,969 test lines (main 6,286,457 + 512), leaving 31 lines of headroom.

### Independent Gateway validation

Independent Gateway validation was performed by @sukhdeepjohar and compared current `main` (`9856f57a828`) with PR head `84273a0c490`, merged onto that `main` without conflicts, using a real `openclaw gateway run` in an isolated Linux container with Node 26.12.0.

The test used the Control UI chat path (`chat.send` → `agent.wait` → final `chat` event). Tagged mode was explicitly enabled through the supported `resolveReasoningOutputMode: () => "tagged"` provider contract via a local `tagstub` plugin whose only hook was that function.

- A probe confirmed that `enforceFinalTag` was active: text outside `<final>` was suppressed, `<final>` content was delivered, and `<think>` content was not delivered.
- Earlier in-process differential testing streamed 1,800 randomized tagged replies through both `main` and this PR; all 1,800 delivered replies matched byte-for-byte.
- In the isolated Gateway run, all 24 measured turns produced byte-identical delivered text between `main` and the PR.
- The tagged-stream tests failed when the production changes were reverted and passed with the changes.
- The full `embedded-agent-subscribe` suite passed on the merged tree: 25 files and 451 tests.
- The focused and broader test results listed above were run separately: 35 files / 524 tests for the contributor's validation and 25 files / 451 tests for this independent Gateway validation.

#### Performance

The following values report **main-thread CPU time from two runs** for each reply size. They are not CPU time and wall-clock time pairs.

| Reply size | `main` CPU, run 1 / run 2 | PR CPU, run 1 / run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 16 KB | 2.1 s / 3.1 s | 1.0 s / 1.9 s |
| 32 KB | 4.8 s / 5.5 s | 1.3 s / 1.5 s |
| 64 KB | 16.6 s / 20.5 s | 2.1 s / 2.9 s |
| 128 KB | 58.7 s / 64.2 s | 3.2 s / 3.6 s |

Additional 128 KB results:

- Wall-clock time: approximately 66–73 seconds on `main` versus approximately 10 seconds with the PR.
- Peak RSS growth: approximately +644 MB to +1,127 MB on `main` versus +15 MB to +47 MB with the PR.
- `/healthz` latency during long tagged replies was substantially lower with the PR.

A 64 KB mixed-content reply containing fences, inline code, lists, and tag-like punctuation mostly exercised the fallback path and had similar costs on both variants, as expected.

#### Reachability and limitations

The bundled providers referenced in #175441 did not reach tagged mode in a Gateway turn in this setup:

- `google-gemini-cli` uses the CLI backend rather than the embedded subscriber.
- The chat path calls `isReasoningTagProvider` without the model API, so `google` resolves to native mode.
- `google-antigravity` also resolved to native mode in this setup.

Therefore, the isolated Gateway run used a local provider plugin that returns `"tagged"`. This exercises the supported SDK contract and the affected production path, but it does not cover a real external provider or a non-chat channel.

prs.body:

Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver

Refreshed onto `82a9bef596011a6145d7f639d9773ff5e7267f7d`, preserving the original patch and contributor authorship. Current candidate: `6d592e236f8d40d33c911391ad795ed59062b439`.

Inline explicit-reply directives still override that implicit-threading opt-out. This is an owner-level condition change, not a follow-up-specific workaround.
