prs.title: fix(macos): keep authored agent order when saving config
prs.body:
Closes #165055

## What Problem This Solves

An unrelated macOS config save alphabetizes the agent roster and can change which agent the Gateway treats as first.

The first PR revision also refused saves for valid configurations whose Gateway intentionally returns `raw: null` to protect secrets. The prior follow-up restored those saves through the existing `config.patch` contract. This follow-up fixes a separately reproduced Unicode scanner defect that rejected existing quoted keys beginning with a literal combining mark.

## User Impact

Existing configurations retain authored object-key order across local-file and Gateway saves. Valid redacted Gateway configurations remain editable, and quoted Unicode keys survive unrelated full-document saves. No config option, migration, or change to secret redaction is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing `.sortedKeys` alone is insufficient because Swift dictionaries do not retain JSON source order. Both full-document save paths use one source-aware writer. Local saves read the existing file under their existing lock; Gateway saves retain the source with the loaded document's route lease and revision hash.

When the Gateway intentionally withholds source text, the app instead sends only the differences from the loaded structured baseline through `config.patch`. Unchanged agent entries and redacted credentials are omitted, so the Gateway-owned source retains their order and values. Explicit `replacePaths` preserves full-array edit intent for reorder, shrink, and subtree deletion instead of invoking ID-keyed upserts. Revision, route, fallback, and local credential-preservation guards remain in place.

The writer scans Unicode scalars so a literal combining mark cannot absorb an opening quote into a Swift grapheme cluster. Foundation still owns JSON5 validation and key decoding.

The full-document writer retains existing keys, omits deleted keys, appends new keys deterministically, and accepts JSON5 comments, quoted/unquoted keys, escapes, and trailing commas. Retained array values keep their object order when moved or when neighbors are inserted/deleted. Arbitrarily moved-and-modified array objects without stable identity receive deterministic order; comments and whitespace are normalized as before.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `ae4cd9bbcab468fbde71ef994386d2a1aa81e0b6`. Unicode follow-up parent: `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Base: `c3b2b7d3fc1a053d2f6907e55e1629c16fc53706`. macOS arm64, Swift 6.4.

### Unicode compatibility control and repaired behavior

At the published parent `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, Foundation accepts a strict JSON document whose quoted key and string value begin with literal U+0301 scalars. An unrelated browser edit fails in both production save owners:

```text
BEFORE local save refused; original fixture unchanged
BEFORE raw-present Gateway save throws DecodingError; no config.set request
AFTER three local saves succeeded; combining-mark key/value and authored order retained
AFTER three raw-present config.set saves succeeded; key/value/order and baseHash retained
```

The exact production `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict`, `ConfigStore.load/save`, and `ConfigJSONWriter` sources were compiled with synthetic transport/peripheral adapters and run using `sandbox-exec -f proof.sb unicode-before-proof before` and `unicode-after-proof after`. The sandbox denies operator files, network, preferences/Keychain services, and child processes. Only disposable fixtures were used; this is not installed-app/live-Gateway E2E.

The new parameterized Swift regression fails before for both double-quoted JSON and single-quoted JSON5, then passes with scalar scanning. It creates literal combining marks through Swift scalar escapes rather than JSON escape tokens and checks preservation across repeated unrelated edits, including strings containing delimiter/comment text.

### Valid raw-null compatibility control and repaired behavior

The exact published first revision `21fa0613ea2f389d6d1eeb998d85ccd3c1c03a12` refuses a valid raw-null save with ConfigStore error 4. At prior head `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, the repaired production `ConfigStore.load/save` owner succeeds against the same boundary.

A synthetic configuration deliberately gives its token the same value as an unrelated configuration field. The exact production `redactConfigSnapshot` owner therefore returns `raw: null` while retaining structured configuration. The proof then exercises five edits through the compiled production Swift save owner and applies the captured requests using the exact production `applyMergePatch` owner:

```text
browser off, browser on, browser off, provider-model reorder, provider-model shrink
5/5 saves succeeded through config.patch
Every request retained baseHash=synthetic-revision
Unchanged gateway/auth and agents were absent from every patch
Auth credential retained; agent roster remained zmain,alpha
Model reorder and shrink retained exact replacePaths and final array intent
```

The Swift owner ran in an OS sandbox against disposable fixtures. Gateway transport and peripheral app adapters were synthetic. This is direct save-owner plus production redaction/merge-contract proof, not an installed-app/live-Gateway end-to-end run. No operator configuration, installed app, or live Gateway was changed.

### Original ordering control

At the earlier first PR revision, compiled exact baseline and repaired local/Gateway serialization owners showed:

```text
Baseline: three unrelated local saves and three config.set encodings -> alpha,zmain
First PR revision: all six retained authored zmain,alpha
All three config.set requests retained baseHash
```

The full-document writer was unchanged by the prior raw-null compatibility follow-up; the scalar scanner correction above is new on this candidate. The earlier raw-null refusal is superseded by the repaired behavior above.

### Tests and checks

- Current exact-source pure serializer and merge-patch tests: **10 tests / 13 cases passed in 0.002s** in a separately linked, audited OS-sandboxed Swift Testing executable. This includes the failing-before literal Unicode regression, existing JSON5 comments/escaped keys/trailing commas, array movement/insertion/deletion, minimal patches, and array replacement/subtree deletion.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passed in **20.72s**.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed in **21.36s**. This is test-bundle compilation, not native suite execution.
- Strict pinned SwiftLint on both follow-up files passed with zero violations. Full macOS SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Touched tests now use required failable UTF-8 conversions.
- Broad macOS lint / `check:changed` still report only the unchanged, previously documented `QuickChatFocusedTextCapture.swift:232` multiple-trailing-closure violation. All other changed-check lanes passed; no unrelated production fix is included.
- Current independent P2 AutoReview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings. Reviewed source bytes match this candidate. Scope is this two-file Unicode follow-up versus the published parent. The inherited Codex auth attempt failed with HTTP401 and is not counted as a clean review.
- Earlier raw-null repair retains its five production-owner saves, nine pure tests/eleven cases, and clean compatibility review at `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Those are explicitly earlier-head measurements; the compatibility owner was not changed by this follow-up.

### Remaining checks and limits

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper reassessment are pending. Previous-head green CI is not current-head validation. Full native test execution requires disposable macOS CI/VM and was not run on the operator desktop. The separate generic JavaScript full-suite attempt was interrupted without an aggregate result and is not claimed as passed or as native proof.

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width the same control changes size from page to page. Search and filter are 38 or 44, segmented is 38 or 44, refresh is 34x36, 38 or 44, selects run from 30 to 44, and a row's `⋯` is 28, 32 or 44. Settings Skills also draws its own refresh button instead of `RefreshButton`. ## User Impact Moving between pages on a phone, each control keeps one height. Desktop and wider touch screens are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made - **38px** for search, filter, segmented, refresh, select and page-level `⋯`, read from `--settings-control-height`. It's the phone value that token already had. It's a clear step below the 45px header pill, where 44 reads as a 1px miss, and it leaves segments at 32px, the composer's row control size. - **32px** for a row's `⋯`, from a new `--row-action-size`, also on the composer's row size. - Settings, Skills and Automations no longer force 44px at 640px and below. Wider touch screens keep 44. - Settings Skills refresh uses `RefreshButton`. - iOS's 16px input floor is unchanged. Left alone: the Model Providers model picker (its own 48px, same as desktop), phone filter sheets (their own 40px field rhythm), the native settings embed, and disclosure rows. ## Landing Order Based on #190369: land that first, then retarget this to main. `refresh-button.tsx` and its `components.css` block match #190390 and #190426, so they merge without conflict. #190369 and #190426 conflict with each other in `library-toolbar.tsx`, with or without this PR. prs.title: fix(browser): avoid shutdown delays from new start requests
prs.body:
Closes #147694

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browser shutdown can stall for each tab-request timeout when cleanup requests a browser start after the runtime has begun stopping.

## User Impact

User impact: browser-enabled OpenClaw processes can shut down promptly instead of waiting through avoidable per-tab timeout delays in this lifecycle race.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject browser-control starts as soon as the shared runtime is already stopping, before they queue behind shutdown. The existing queued generation check remains in place for requests that race before stopping state becomes visible.

## Evidence

- Regression test failed on the original code because the start remained `pending` while shutdown was held open, then passed with the repair.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-control-state.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/session-tab-cleanup.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/runtime-lifecycle.unhandled-rejections.test.ts` — 14 tests passed.

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Structured P0–P2 autoreview and independent Claude review — clean, no findings.

prs.body: Fixes #186024 ## What Problem This Solves The command palette mixes search with background-session creation and switches views automatically when text becomes long or multiline. ## User Impact Search and Compose sit on a sunken shelf docked to the top of the palette, sharing its edge and radius, with a Tab key hint on wider screens. Tab switches from the main input and reopening retains the last selected mode. New session opens Compose. Compose uses the chat composer's surface and controls: the add menu, agent, folder, worktree and send, with the shortcut in the send tooltip. Long text grows to eight lines and then scrolls. At phone width the chips become icons and the key hints go away. Text, mentions, attachments and foreground drafts are preserved, and square themes keep their corners. A failed start reports through the toast from main, with its Open session and Try again actions. ## Why This Change Was Made One explicit mode replaces the text-length heuristic. Building Compose on the composer's own surface and controls keeps the two in step across themes. The palette is one card: the panel sits in a shelf painted with the composer's attached surface, and the selected tab takes the panel's surface, so the switcher reads as part of the component. Radius follows the theme's scale, so CRT keeps its near-square corners. The field has the same size, line height and inset in both modes, so nothing shifts on Tab. The first-open loading view uses the same stack and passes its mode through the existing input handoff. ## Evidence - Palette and new-session unit and browser tests pass: 183 tests across 17 files. - Bundled browser suites pass on this merge: `command-palette-create`, `images`, `drop`, `first-open`, `shortcuts`, `mentions` and `composition` (27 tests), plus new-session host remediation, configured defaults, early submit and session writer (10 tests). - UI type check, oxfmt, stylelint, oxlint on touched files, and the line-cap and test-lines ratchets pass. - `ui:check-performance:base` reports over budget: chat boot JS gzip is 1249.5 KiB against a 1247.9 KiB limit because the tabs are on the boot path, and total CSS, which main already exceeds. Boot request counts are within budget. - Merging main removed the palette's recovery action; the Compose footer that used it is gone with it, which fixes the `recovery is not defined` crash on a merge with main. - Geometry sampled on every frame while switching Search, Compose and Tab, in Absolutely light and dark and CRT at 320, 390 and 1280, over Sessions and chat: the shelf, both tabs, the panel top and the field's position and size don't move in any of the 18 combinations. ## Risk and coverage Mode retention is in memory for the current application lifetime. Enter in Compose does not start a session; only Cmd/Ctrl+Enter or the send button does. The `tabs-runtime` chunk is removed so the tabs join the shared boot group. Search's field now uses the composer's size, 14 px instead of 15 px on desktop. Images use the real app on the mock data layer with real clicks and taps. prs.title: fix: avoid false skills watcher failures on Linux Node
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three skills discovery policy cases fail on Linux Node when they select the Windows watch-root policy. Node implements recursive watching by calling public `fs.watch` for descendant paths, so a spy on that API counts runtime internals alongside OpenClaw registrations. The tests report extra watches or the wrong final path even though OpenClaw registered the expected root.

## User Impact

The tests can exercise the existing watch-root policy consistently across Node and Bun. Production watching, configuration, and cleanup behavior are unchanged. These fixtures select Windows application policy on Linux; they do not establish native Windows filesystem behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the existing `watchDirectory` registration boundary with pass-through spies and read its directory, callback, and recursive arguments. This keeps the exact registration count and root expectations independent of the runtime's recursive implementation. The successful-opening filter, real native handles, missing-root callback, workspace replacement, disappearance, recreation, and original cleanup remain in place. The adapter still enforces nonpersistent watches.

## Evidence

On the unchanged base, the complete discovery owner reproduced all three reported failures, with the other 14 cases passing. With this change:

- Node 24.22.1: all 17 discovery cases and 14 related watcher cases passed.
- Checksum-pinned Bun: all 17 discovery cases and 12 related watcher cases passed; the two existing Node-only host cases skipped as expected.
- Changed-file formatting and lint, plus the affected test type graph, passed.

The discovery owner took 45.96 seconds under Node and 43.61 seconds under Bun, including transformation and setup. No test cases or production code were added. Hosted CI and independent engineering review passed for this commit.

prs.title: feat: fork threaded conversations with Telegram support
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Threaded channel conversations need a real context fork, not a fresh thread with an empty session or a subagent.

## User Impact

`/fork [title]` in a Telegram forum topic creates a sibling topic bound to an independent copy of the conversation. The original keeps its session. The new topic receives the last three available visible text excerpts, while the session inherits the full selected context snapshot. Busy sources copy only the last completed prefix. Manage Topics and existing thread bindings are required; DMs and unthreaded chats are refused.

Depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190763. Discord, Slack, and Control UI typed-command parity are separate dependent PRs. Existing Control UI menu forks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared command owns authorization, ordinary-session copying, source selection, history projection, and literal recap delivery. A lazy optional channel binding capability owns native sibling placement and live account/access authority. Telegram uses its existing topic API and current-placement binding owner; no new copy engine, store, schema, configuration option, dependency, or permission bypass. A fork copies conversation context, not a Git checkout or external side effects.

Core recording reuses the existing ancestry/header cut and command-transcript owners. It commits a copied-session checkpoint before native effects and records the final outcome before relying on the acknowledgment. A lost acknowledgment therefore does not erase a committed result. Recap mirrors are display-only, not another model-visible copy. Native creation, binding, and recap delivery remain separate outcomes; known copies/threads are retained after later failures and uncertain native effects are never blindly retried.

The completed-prefix owner now excludes OpenClaw-authored command artifacts from model-completion boundaries, preventing one fork checkpoint from making a later fork inherit an unfinished model turn. Copied directives, Markdown, mentions, and links are inert on delivery; hidden reasoning and tool output are not posted.

Simplification: shared decisions stay with existing session/transcript/delivery owners; plugins supply native placement only. The remaining growth is the smallest working core + one native adapter, with distinct durability, cancellation, privacy, and transport regressions. No updater or migration change is needed.

## Evidence

- Real shared dispatcher, SQLite copy/bind, lost-ack durability, literal directives, active-source repeated forks, source reset/plugin/abort/native-authority refusals: 10 passed.
- Telegram serialized outbound conformance: 34 passed, including literal recap on plain and rich transports with mentions/previews disabled. Native fork qualification/partial-binding failure tests: 3 passed. Combined `pnpm test` run with `--maxWorkers=1`: 47 passed, 55.73s runner wall.
- Parent-prefix regressions failed before the repair; 9 prefix tests and 46 transcript-owner tests passed in the implementation lane.
- `pnpm build`: passed, 5m15s. Existing advisory UI asset-budget warnings remain; no UI source changes in this PR.
- Scoped type-aware lint: passed. Independent isolated review completed: one P1 was verified false against the dynamic-assertion owner and real successful-flow tests (undefined pre-lease selection is intentionally a no-op; refusal only applies to a selection changing inside a prepared operation). No other P0-P2 findings.
- Core and extension production typechecks passed. Exact `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` full wall times: fork command 47.59s (10 passed); Telegram fork 35.86s (3); Telegram outbound HTTP 23.37s (34); parent-prefix 1.83s (9); transcript owner 18.45s (46). Cold worker compilation is included. Test growth: +683 lines, explicitly allocated.
- Real Telegram Test Server with compiled candidate and mock model: 5 action/reply pairs, exactly three ordered recap excerpts, distinct sibling topic, isolated Gateway restart, fork follow-up retaining source context, original follow-up excluding the fork turn. Four conversational provider requests (11 total including ancillary work). Owned forum deleted, runner processes joined, credential scratch removed. Source-mode QA was blocked before the first model turn by `Gateway SDK resource host is not bound`; compiled-candidate proof passed.
- Final registration-only refactor moves the unchanged lazy callback into the existing Telegram binding-support object to avoid growing an oversized channel entrypoint. Registered-channel HTTP suite passed again: 34 tests, 48.91s full wall. Final isolated review found no P0–P2 findings.
- Committed-head build passed again (4m7.7s). Qualified Telegram cold-import snapshot passed with no gaps; temporary home/process cleanup verified.
- SDK API comparison passed for A → B, digest `516f6fe2`: no entrypoints added/removed; additive optional `ChannelConversationBindingSupport.prepareFork` is reachable through 174 exports. No public breaking removal. CI seconds unavailable; no live Discord/Slack claim is made here.

Draft only; no merge or live Gateway deployment.

## Stack

[A · binding lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190763) → [B · shared command/core recording/Telegram](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190783) → [C · Discord](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190785), [D · Slack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190786), [E · Control UI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190787).

All are drafts. Retarget dependents to main only after their prerequisite lands; preserve incremental review and exact-head validation.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack thread conversations need a separate reply thread with inherited context, without replacing the source session.

## User Impact

Send @OpenClaw /fork [title] as a normal message inside an existing public/private channel thread. A new top-level root in that same channel becomes the fork's thread; the title is root-message text. Slack native custom slash commands cannot identify an in-thread source and are not advertised for this flow. DMs, top-level/synthetic threads and Enterprise Grid org installs are explicitly refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

Depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190783 (base: feat/channel-fork-command). Reuse authenticated native source facts, existing ordinary-session SQLite bindings, normal inbound routing and provider-owned links. Literal root/recap payloads disable mentions and unfurls. Live account/installation authority is retained through creation and recap. Known roots/bindings survive later failures, while ambiguous native creation is not replayed.

No second binding store, channel creation, broad child-spawn policy, configuration option, schema, or dependency change. Existing mention/access rules still apply to follow-ups; routing does not grant permission. Simplification keeps provider text encoding in its existing outbound owners.

prs.title: fix(memory): answer chunking-version upgrades from keyword rows instead of rebuilding inline
prs.body:
Fixes #189447

## What Problem This Solves

When a release bumps `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION`, the index identity becomes `mismatched` with `versionOrder: "older"`, so `shouldRepairIdentity` is true and the search runs the whole rebuild inline through `syncAdmitted`. Only after that does the code reach the `formatUpgradePendingKeywordOnly` check that would have answered from the existing keyword rows. On a real index the rebuild outlives the 30 s `memory_search` deadline, so the first search after an upgrade returns nothing even though the keyword index was usable.

- Problem: a chunking-version-only mismatch rebuilt inline before the keyword-only path could answer.
- Solution: answer from the keyword rows immediately and hand the upgrade to the existing search-maintenance owner, so the index still reaches the current format.
- Changed: `manager-search-orchestration.ts` hoists `formatUpgradePendingKeywordOnly` above the repair decision, excludes that case from the inline repair, and schedules `syncPublishedIndexInBackground` for it.
- Not changed: which identities are repairable, the keyword-only eligibility rules, the maintenance pipeline itself, and the existing "rebuild is pending" log.

## Why This Change Was Made

The keyword-only path already existed and is the right answer for a format-only upgrade: the rows are still lexically valid, so rebuilding before serving throws away the only deadline the caller has. Moving the existing predicate above the repair decision reuses that owner instead of adding a second eligibility rule.

Skipping the inline rebuild alone would strand the upgrade — the background-sync gate excludes the same identity, so an unchanged corpus would stay keyword-only forever. The pending-format branch therefore starts the same maintenance pass a dirty search would, reusing the in-flight set so repeated searches cannot stack rebuilds. Any mismatch that is not keyword-only still repairs inline as before.

## User Impact

The first `memory_search` after a chunking-version upgrade returns keyword results inside the deadline instead of timing out empty, and the index still upgrades in the background without a second search. Searches on a non-upgraded index, and upgrades that also change source or scope, behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Two regression tests, both bidirectional and both run for real. Production changes reverted with the tests kept:

```text
# with the fix
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts -t "chunking version moved"
→ PASS: serves keyword rows instead of rebuilding when only the chunking version moved
node … -t "hands a pending format upgrade"
→ PASS: keyword answer plus a search-maintenance pass for the same identity

# production file reverted
→ FAIL: expected false to be true            (inline rebuild ran first)
→ FAIL: maintenance never entered            (no repair was handed off)

# full suite on the fixed tree
→ 21 passed
```

The tests drive the real manager: they sync a real index, rewrite the persisted `chunkingVersion` to the previous version through the fixture's own database handle, and then assert both the keyword answer and that maintenance was actually acquired for the pending upgrade.

Not covered here: the 30 s deadline itself on a multi-gigabyte production index, and completion of the background rebuild against a live embedding provider. Both need a live provider and a large corpus.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used code tracing to find that the repair ran before the keyword-only check, then traced the maintenance pipeline to confirm work can be handed off. An earlier revision only skipped the inline rebuild; review correctly pointed out that this strands the upgrade, so the pending-format branch now starts maintenance as well. The implementer understands the code: a format-only upgrade keeps lexically valid rows, so serving them is intended, and the rebuild belongs to the maintenance owner rather than the search deadline.

prs.title: fix(exec): match manual wildcard rules with argument restrictions
prs.body:
Related: #184894 (manual wildcard entries with `argPattern` only).

## What Problem This Solves

A hand-authored execution allowlist rule such as `{ "pattern": "*", "argPattern": "^--version$" }` never matches, so even a matching command unnecessarily requests approval or is refused.

## User Impact

Manual wildcard rules now match resolved executables only when their argument restriction matches. An already configured rule of this form can begin authorizing the commands it describes. This changes execution-policy matching and should receive maintainer review before merging.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bare-wildcard shortcut excluded argument restrictions, while the general matcher skipped every wildcard. The existing general matcher now accepts manual wildcard selectors and applies its existing argument checks. Generated `allow-always` wildcard entries remain inactive because their argument hashes do not identify a binary. Normal basename/path rules, unresolved-path restrictions, invalid-regex refusal, and missing-argv refusal retain their behavior.

## Evidence

- On base `4a2143b81`, matching manual wildcard rules failed through both the matching API and the production shell authorization/approval decision. Three positive regression cases failed; the nonmatching-argument control passed.
- With the fix, all four new cases pass, including PATH and absolute executable forms, mismatch, missing argv, invalid regex, and generated-rule controls. A final replay on independent commit `7f190aebb` with its own frozen dependencies passed all four cases (47.77 seconds in Vitest, 54.63 seconds in the wrapper, mostly compilation); 28 other cases were filtered for this replay only.
- The four affected/adjacent suites produced 86 passes, three failures, and 31 platform skips on Windows / Node 24.22.1; repository-wrapper time was 27.73 seconds. The failures are existing Windows expectations: case-sensitive `RG`, a `/bin/tool` separator assertion, and a `nu.exe.exe` opaque-shell fixture. The same failures were reproduced with the original production matcher; none is reported as passing. POSIX-only controls remain for CI.
- Fresh independent review of the complete patch found no actionable P0-P2 findings. Canonical AutoReview was not run. The necessary test allocation is 35 lines for matcher rejection controls and the production authorization decision. `openclaw/ci-gate` is success on head `7f190aebb9bb7b7e2fb416647619259f0aef420a`.

Production types, the affected infra test type graph, changed-file typed lint, formatting, line caps, test budget, and `git diff --check` passed. The PR branch contains only this allowlist change.

### Additional shipped-entry-point evidence

Source / build:
- Candidate CLI: `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (7f190ae)`, commit `7f190aebb9bb7b7e2fb416647619259f0aef420a`. Built with `pnpm build` and launched with `pnpm openclaw`.
- Latest stable, from npm dist-tag `latest` at run time: `openclaw@2026.10.9`, CLI `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)`. This is not the PR parent commit.
- Environment: Windows, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 11.20.0. Each run used its own state directory, config, and workspace. A local OpenAI-responses stand-in supplied the `exec` tool call. The probe command itself was local.

Native entry point:
- `pnpm openclaw approvals set` wrote the isolated policy.
- `pnpm openclaw agent exec` invoked the exec tool. `approvals get` reported effective `security=allowlist` and `ask=off`.

Failure or policy setup:
- Agent `alpha`: manual `{ "pattern": "*", "argPattern": "^--version$" }` with no `source`.
- Agent `beta`: empty allowlist.
- Generated control: the same pattern with `source: "allow-always"`.
- Probe: `node --version`. Mismatch: `node --help`.

Baseline observation:
- On stable `8b18b55`, the same manual rule and `node --version` returned `exec denied: allowlist miss`, `isError: true`, with no exit code and no version text.

Candidate observation:
- On `7f190ae`, the same rule and command completed with tool text `v24.22.1`, `status: completed`, `exitCode: 0`, `durationMs: 487`. A separate upgrade copy completed again with `durationMs: 504`.
- After that run, `approvals get` showed `lastUsedCommand: "node --version"` and a resolved Node executable path for the manual rule.

Negative controls:
- `node --help` on agent `alpha`: `exec denied: allowlist miss`, `isError: true`, no exit code.
- `node --version` on agent `beta`: `exec denied: allowlist miss`.
- Generated `allow-always` wildcard: `approvals set` accepted it. `node --version` then returned `exec denied: allowlist miss` from the exec tool, so this request reached execution policy rather than stopping at schema admission.

Stable upgrade:
- Stable saved the manual rule and denied `node --version`.
- A separate copy of that state was opened with the candidate. `openclaw doctor --fix` was required for credential-migration custody. The copied rule was unchanged (`pattern: "*"`, `argPattern: "^--version$"`, no generated source) and then authorized `node --version`.
- Doctor also reported that a pre-repair backup was unavailable because the temporary directory ACL was too broad. The exec result above is from the copied state after that doctor run. Stable and the candidate did not share a live state directory.

Remaining limitations:
- One-shot `openclaw agent` with `ask=always` stopped before an approval wait: `Headless runs cannot wait for interactive exec approval.` No process output was produced. Revoking a matched rule during that wait was therefore not reachable from this entry, and this run does not claim the pre-spawn revocation guard was exercised.
- The exact PR parent `4a2143b81` was not rebuilt for this entry-point pass. The shipped-stable denial above is the upgrade baseline. The earlier in-process red run on `4a2143b81` remains the parent-commit test baseline.

Maintainer decision, if required:
- Should an already saved manual wildcard rule that did not match before upgrade start authorizing matching commands afterward? This patch does that. No maintainer approval of that transition is recorded here.

prs.title: fix(agents): retain causes when question prompt delivery fails
prs.body:
Related: #188171

## What Problem This Solves

When an `ask_user` prompt cannot be published, the warning can omit the underlying routing error, nested cause, error code, or dispatch outcome, leaving operators with only `ask_user prompt delivery failed`.

## User Impact

Operators receive a correlated failure diagnostic with the cause and publication outcome. This addresses the diagnostic portion of #188171; it does not claim a new Telegram card-delivery repair. The reporter confirmed that the original card-delivery symptom worked on beta.5.

## Why This Change Was Made

The routing boundary retains its specific error or suppression reason and original cause. The publication warning uses the existing error formatter and records the existing run, tool-call, question, channel, and account identifiers, plus a typed dispatch outcome when available. Delivery ownership, retries, and authorization are unchanged; logs retain the existing egress redaction policy.

## Evidence

- On base `4a2143b81`, the routed rejection lost its supplied cause, and two publication-warning cases lost cause/code or outcome. All three new diagnostic cases failed for those reasons before the fix.
- The complete related suites passed: 135 dispatch tests, 105 embedded tool-handler tests, and 29 `ask_user` tool tests. The repository wrapper took 149.97 seconds on Windows / Node 24.22.1, including compilation. After grouping prompt failures in the existing support module, the affected embedded suite passed again: 105/105, 59.12 seconds in Vitest and 66.18 seconds in the wrapper, mostly compilation. The other two suites and both production files were unchanged. The oversized suite shrinks by 23 lines.
- These tests exercise the production routing rejection and prompt-delivery owner with controlled external callbacks. No live Telegram or model call was made, so they prove diagnostic propagation rather than actual Telegram delivery.
- Fresh independent source review found no actionable issues, including both test-module moves. Canonical AutoReview was not run. The required allocation is 58 counted regression/support lines (101 net test/helper lines overall). Existing question-routing cases move together under their original hooks so neither oversized fixture grows; all assertions remain. The current head's CI gate passes.

Production types, affected agent/messaging/infra test type graphs, changed-file typed lint, formatting, line caps, test budget, and `git diff --check` passed. The messaging typecheck, lint, formatting, and budgets were repeated after the final routing-test move. The final dispatch suite passed 135/135 in 131.35 seconds of Vitest time, including cold worker compilation. Earlier checks also contained an independent allowlist patch; the diagnostic owners and their consumers are identical, and that patch is excluded from this branch.

### Shipped Gateway failure traces (2026-10-31)

The built CLI at head `9bddc581886678f28e8507b447fae763ad2498a1` ran two isolated Gateway scenarios on Windows / Node 24.22.1. The build stamp records that head with clean inputs. Each scenario had its own state, config, workspace, ports, and synthetic credentials.

Entry point: `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port <isolated-port> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, after `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --yes` initialized the isolated state. A local OpenAI Responses server supplied the actual `ask_user` tool call. A local Telegram HTTP fixture rejected the resulting button-bearing `sendMessage` request with HTTP 400 and `QUESTION_DIAGNOSTIC_PROBE_REJECTED`. The production agent, question manager, dispatchers, channel adapter, HTTP client, and logger ran unchanged.

**Routed publication:** An authenticated backend client called the public `chat.send` RPC with explicit Telegram channel, target, account, and delivery. At 17:36:23 +08:00, the publication owner emitted this redacted warning:

```json
{"runId":"diagnostic-public-1793439371229","toolCallId":"call_probe_1|fc_1","questionId":"ask_191c481c33114d30974dd33b710281d1","channel":"telegram","accountId":"default","level":"warn","message":"failed to deliver ask_user prompt: ask_user prompt delivery failed: Failed to route reply to telegram: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: QUESTION_DIAGNOSTIC_PROBE_REJECTED)"}
```

**Queued publication:** The same HTTP fixture supplied one inbound Telegram update through polling. At 17:36:04 +08:00, the actual queued delivery rejection reached the publication owner:

```json
{"runId":"b306a665-4e91-4ab0-a6bf-96c58ee89ac2","toolCallId":"call_probe_1|fc_1","questionId":"ask_9cdfb5437f06b5f11bd79efed62b3fad","channel":"telegram","accountId":"default","outcome":"failed-deliver","level":"warn","message":"failed to deliver ask_user prompt: queued reply delivery failed | REPLY_DISPATCH_DELIVERY_ERROR"}
```

The public `question.list` RPC then returned `{"questions":[]}`. The harness stopped its Gateways and local listeners after recording the checkpoints.

These traces prove the changed diagnostic owners through a shipped Gateway entry point with controlled external HTTP I/O. They do not prove Telegram Test Server behavior, client visibility, or a live model call. The HTTP 400 is an injected transport response, not a mocked internal callback or an observed Telegram outage. The earlier parent-commit regressions remain the red baseline; this pass did not rebuild the parent. Upstream main `8ec6c76b5c138ed0be1b68f4101be502bf81d0b9` still has both original diagnostic owners unchanged from the PR base. The current PR head's `openclaw/ci-gate` is success.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The tokenjuice plugin still installs 0.8.5 after the verified [0.10.0 release](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tokenjuice/releases/tag/v0.10.0). Existing tests mock the reducer, leaving real package exports and compaction untested.

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/189997.

## User Impact

The plugin installs tokenjuice 0.10.0. OpenClaw already exceeds its Node >=22 requirement. OpenClaw/plugin versions and release metadata stay unchanged; this PR publishes neither package.

prs.title: fix(android): false "Could not refresh models" banner after sending into a busy session
prs.body:
Closes #183031

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android chat shows "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." and flags the chat as needing attention right after a message is sent into a busy session.

## User Impact

User impact: sending messages no longer raises a false models-refresh warning. A real, persistent metadata failure still shows the same error as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a `chat.metadata` read overlaps the send that mutates the session, the Gateway rejects it with the transient, explicitly retryable "Session changed while preparing its metadata. Retry the request.". The client surfaced that as a refresh failure without retrying. This change retries only that case: at most 2 extra attempts, with 400/800 ms backoff, and cancellation is rethrown. Every other error keeps the current behavior. It also clears the stale refresh error after a later successful background load, so the banner does not outlive the condition.

This complements #185623, which improves the wording of metadata vs catalog errors but intentionally adds no retry.

## Evidence

- New `ChatControllerMetadataRetryTest` (Robolectric, scripted gateway):
  - superseded read once → retried, catalog loads, no error;
  - superseded on every attempt → bounded to 3 reads, error still shown;
  - non-transient failure (`FORBIDDEN`) → not retried.
- Against `main` without the fix, the two retry tests fail (2/3 failures), so the tests exercise the change.
- `ChatControllerCatalogTest` (8) passes. `:app:ktlintCheck` is clean.
- Live: Galaxy Z Fold8 with Gateway 2026.10.8. Before the fix the banner appeared on almost every send into a long-running session; the gateway logged the superseded `chat.metadata` followed by a successful later read. With this change in a local build, the banner no longer appears (owner-confirmed on device).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerMetadataRetryTest' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerCatalogTest' :app:ktlintCheck
```
</details>

prs.title: fix: subagent Stop waits out its own queued drain and reports success
prs.body:
Closes #189376

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent Stop issued from a source's own raw cleanup waits out the 15-second session-controller drain deadline and then reports success. The cleanup itself is waiting on Stop, so the two await each other until the deadline fires.

## User Impact

Stop from a subagent's own cleanup path returns promptly instead of stalling ~15 s. The queued-drain error is no longer incurred on this path at all (asserted below), per the issue's post-fix expectation.

## Why This Change Was Made

`settleQueued` (post-kill settlement walk) excluded the caller's current *operation* from the queued drain but not the caller's own *raw source*, then awaited `capturedExecution.execution.input.settlement.promise` for that self input. The sibling source-settlement owner (`settleSubagentKillSources`) already excludes this input correctly via `isCurrentSessionControllerTurnInput`; this change applies the same exclusion at the queued-drain boundary — the issue's first-named resolution ("the later scope drain should exclude that source, as the earlier settlement owner already does").

Scope note: the issue lists self-join refusal/report as an *alternative*, and its Notes say the fixed row "should run in milliseconds and could assert that no drain-deadline error occurs" — asserted. The described test-only replacement-fixture row is the issue author's separate test-only follow-up (#189394).

## Evidence

### 1. Dispatch regression (RED/GREEN, controlled clock)

New regression in `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts`: a terminal subagent whose raw disposal is held, with Stop issued inside that source's own async context. It runs on a controlled (fake) drain clock and leaves no timer scheduled.

- **RED on base** (`upstream/main`, source restored in-tree): Stop never settles before the fake deadline — `AssertionError: expected false to be true` (exit 1).
- **GREEN here**: settles promptly, returns `{ status: "ok" }`, and `result.error` contains no drain-deadline text.

Focused suites: `accepted-stop` + `kill-settlement` + `publication` **3 files / 42 tests pass**. `tsgo:core` clean; `oxlint` 0/0 and `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.

### 1b. Project-owned regression row: measured drain-deadline differential

The defect is observable in the repository's own shipped test suite, on a row that predates this PR (present identically on `upstream/main`). Row: `normal terminal cleanup preserves exact Stop ownership (self-disposal after turn completion, afterCleanup=true)` in `subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts`.

Command (same file, same row, only `subagent-control-kill-scope.ts` differs):

```
# BASE (upstream/main subagent-control-kill-scope.ts restored in-tree)
17408ms  normal terminal cleanup preserves exact Stop ownership (self-disposal after turn completion, afterCleanup=true)
 2282ms  ... (self-disposal, afterCleanup=true)
 2610ms  ... (self-disposal during wake cancellation, afterCleanup=true)
suite total: 73156 ms

# HEAD (this PR)
 2368ms  normal terminal cleanup preserves exact Stop ownership (self-disposal after turn completion, afterCleanup=true)
 2325ms  ... (self-disposal, afterCleanup=true)
 2277ms  ... (self-disposal during wake cancellation, afterCleanup=true)
suite total: 57320 ms
```

The affected row loses exactly one `SESSION_CONTROLLER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) and lands in line with its seven sibling rows (~2.2-2.4 s of shared fixture overhead); the suite total drops by 15,836 ms. This is the acceptance signal the issue's own Notes predicted: `Once this is fixed, the row should run in milliseconds`. No author-added scaffolding is involved — the row, the held raw disposal, and the Stop call all come from the existing suite.

### 2. Gateway product-path artifact (redacted)

A real Gateway process ran the bundled Matrix plugin against a local fake homeserver; one room message entered through the real sync ingress and reply pipeline (channel runs bind gateway subagents). The scripted model then executed the reachable self-cleanup variant through shipped tools: main turn → `sessions_spawn`; the child turn → `subagents list` → `subagents cancel <own runId>` **from inside its own controller turn**, with the kill executed by the shipped `subagents` tool.

```
[proof] model request {plan:"sessions_spawn"}   tools(51): spawn=true subagents=true
[proof] child cancel tool_call emitted {"runId":"cf548141-…"}
[proof] child cancel result returned {"elapsedMs":25,  "result":"{\"found\":true,\"killed\":false,\"runId\":\"cf548141-…\"…}"}
[proof] self-cancel tool latency: 25 ms
[proof] PASS: self-cancel returned promptly
```

Base comparison for this reachable variant is also prompt (~18 ms): cancelling a run from its own live turn aborts the turn, so the product path releases the source settlement quickly. The stalled join the issue reports needs the raw disposal to stay pending while the Stop awaits it — that held-disposal state is exactly what the controlled-clock regression pins (base fails, head passes). The external-cleanup control (Stop from outside still joining disposal) is covered by the existing `lifecycle cleanup joins terminal controller disposal` row, passing.

prs.title: fix: gateway stops accepting connections for 10–20 s after the first plugin-started subagent run ends
prs.body:
Closes #157935

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway stops accepting connections for 10–20 seconds after the first plugin-started subagent run in each process finishes.

## User Impact

User impact: gateways that serve plugin-started runs (`api.runtime.subagent.run`) stay reachable after a run ends, instead of timing out every request for 10–20 s once per process. Deployments that start fresh gateway processes on demand no longer pay this on every start.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin-owned subagent runs were registered without a workspace, so the subagent-ended lifecycle hook loaded the plugin runtime with no workspace. That misses the registry the run had just loaded and synchronously builds an unscoped registry of every plugin on the gateway thread. The run is now registered with its agent's workspace (`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, agentId)`), the same one it executes in, as native subagent spawns already do, so the hook reuses the cached registry.

## Evidence

- New test next to the existing plugin-subagent requester-lineage test: a plugin run for agent `work` is registered with that agent's workspace (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`).
- Observed on 2026.7.1 with the same one-line change applied as a local patch, on a real gateway serving a TypeScript plugin:
  - before: after the first run, 6 of 30 once-a-second HTTP probes to the gateway timed out; CPU profile shows 15.4 s in `ensureSubagentRegistryPluginRuntimeLoaded` → `loadOpenClawPlugins` (jiti 12.5 s, Babel 5.5 s);
  - after: 0 of 30 probes failed, and a trace of every plugin-load request during the first run shows no unscoped request from the subagent registry.

- Test cost (the one new test, `registers plugin subagent runs with their agent's workspace`):
  - CI: 57 ms (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-38`, shard `agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-2`, run 36099408981).
  - Local, `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 64 ms. Per-test durations for the file's other 365 tests are unchanged between the base (`9745d65a7e`) and this head: 324.7 s vs 324.5 s in total (JSON reporter, same host, back to back).
  - Whole-file wall on this host swung with load (3 runs each: 224/166/164 s at base, 238/208/208 s at head), so the per-test figures above are the like-for-like comparison.
- The one failing check, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-31` (and `openclaw/ci-gate` behind it), is `src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.task-missing.test.ts` › "retires a missing task after one announce attempt" (mock called 2 times, expected 1). This PR does not touch `src/agents/subagents/completion/`; that test passes 5/5 locally at this head (`13187abae2`).

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

### Actual compiled CLI behavior — October 21

Ten independent ordinary standalone invocations used credential-free synthetic private config/state, real loopback MCP transports and the compiled CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json \
  --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning
# Repeat each scenario with --severity-min error.
```

| Synthetic failure | Finding at warning threshold | Exit: warning threshold | Exit: error threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refused remote Streamable HTTP connection | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Initialized remote server delays `tools/list` beyond the real 10-second deadline | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Remote catalog repeats its pagination cursor | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Missing local executable | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Local stdio child exits during initialization | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |

Every invocation reported `checksRun: 1`. At error threshold, remote-only warnings were filtered out (`findings: []`, exit0). Representative sanitized output projection:

```json
{"scenario":"refused-http","threshold":"warning","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"warning","errorCode":"mcp-service-unavailable"}
{"scenario":"catalog-deadline","threshold":"error","code":0,"checksRun":1,"severity":"below-threshold","errorCode":null}
{"scenario":"closed-stdio","threshold":"error","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"error","errorCode":null}
```

**Build provenance/limit:** this CLI proof ran on [assembled fork commit dda926bb935](https://github.com/Grynn/openclaw/commit/dda926bb93528517d02666179d4478579af6e4a9), which contains this exact repair plus separately reviewed immutable-launcher/runtime fixes and other local units. All 13 files in this PR are byte-identical there to `92b501e7e5af68ad01b829ff005739fe69ed45b1`. Its full `pnpm build` passed with the live-service safeguard enabled. This is real compiled CLI evidence, **not an exact standalone PR-head build, a production deployment or a full installed-release Doctor certification**. No serving credentials, user state or model calls were used. The older blocked CLI attempt remains historical evidence, not a success claim.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(infra): keep the launchd recovery budget on elapsed time
prs.body:
Related to #186484

## What Problem This Solves

When the host clock is corrected during a service update (NTP step, VM pause/resume, manual change), the recovery wait was measured against that jumpy clock — it either ran far past the configured timeout or expired early and refused a healthy `launchctl` restart. The recovery budget now counts elapsed time, so a clock correction no longer stretches or cancels the wait.

- **Problem**: The managed-service handoff recovery loop seeded and consumed its budget with `Date.now()`:
  ```js
  const deadline = Date.now() + params.recoveryTimeoutMs;
  const run = (args) => runOwned("launchctl", args, undefined, deadline);
  for (let inspection = enabled; enabled.code === 0 && Date.now() < deadline;) {
    ...
    await sleep(Math.min(500, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())));
  }
  ```
  Everything in that loop is local elapsed time, so a backward clock step inflates `remaining` and polls `launchctl` past the budget; a forward step expires it early.
- **Solution**: Seed the budget with `performance.now()` and consume it monotonically — the loop runs while `remainingMs() > 0` regardless of wall-clock jumps.
- **What changed**: `command-source.ts` adds `createMonotonicBudget` (monotonic `remainingMs` + epoch `commandDeadlineAt`); `recovery-source.ts` seeds with it and gates the launchd loop/sleep on `remainingMs()`. Fixture clock preload now advances `performance.now()` with simulated command work.
- **What did NOT change**: Spawn deadlines stay epoch-valued (`Date.now() + remainingBudget()`), and persisted timestamps keep `Date.now()`, because those legitimately cross the process boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loop is process-local elapsed time but was seeded with the wall clock, which is the wrong clock domain for a duration. `performance.now()` is monotonic per process, so a host clock correction can no longer affect the recovery wait.

- **Best fix**: `performance.now()` for the process-local budget — the owner established by #186484, which this PR carries over to the launchd recovery side (the one path #186484 left untouched).
- **Alternative**: `process.hrtime.bigint()`, rejected as needlessly low-level; `performance.now()` matches the existing convention.
- **Risk / non-goals**: Dropped the parent-exit path (`params.parentExitDeadlineAt` is an epoch created in the parent process, so it must stay `Date.now()`-based — comparing it against `performance.now()` would mix clock domains). Persisted timestamps (`serviceStoppedAtMs`/`serviceDowntimeMs`) are untouched.

## User Impact

Self-updating macOS deployments no longer risk a stuck or aborted `launchctl` recovery when the system clock is adjusted mid-update. No user-facing configuration or behavior changes; recovery still respects the configured `recoveryTimeoutMs`.

## Evidence

Real generated-helper trace (current head). Both runs assemble the actual shipped `MANAGED_HANDOFF_COMMAND_SOURCE` + `MANAGED_HANDOFF_RECOVERY_SOURCE`, spawn a genuine `launchctl` stub subprocess, and rewrite `Date.now()` **backward by 60000 ms** immediately after the first `launchctl print` — after the monotonic budget is seeded, so a `Date.now()`-based budget sees the full offset and is not cancelled out. Identical fixtures (recoveryTimeoutMs=4000); the only difference is `createMonotonicBudget`.

| variant | recoveryTimeoutMs | wall-clock step | recovery loop wall time | launchctl prints | budget held? |
|---------|-------------------|-----------------|-------------------------|------------------|--------------|
| pre-fix (origin/main) | 4000 ms | -60000 ms | **64003 ms** | 125 | NO — inflated 16× by the clock step |
| post-fix (this PR)    | 4000 ms | -60000 ms | **4002 ms** | 9   | YES — monotonic, immune to clock |

```
# post-fix (this PR)   # pre-fix (origin/main)
[helper] verification {"runId":"run-186831-postfix","serviceRunning":false}
[helper] RESULT restored=false wallElapsedMs=4002
[clock] stepping Date.now() backward by 60000ms after first print
  (9 launchctl prints; loop exits when monotonic budget 4000ms is consumed)
```
```
[helper] verification {"runId":"run-186831-prefix","serviceRunning":false}
[helper] RESULT restored=false wallElapsedMs=64003
[clock] stepping Date.now() backward by 60000ms after first print
  (125 launchctl prints; loop keeps polling because Date.now()-based budget
   was inflated by the 60000ms backward step)
```

### Regression (clock-step, dual direction)

`update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts` runs the embedded command source in a VM with injected `Date` and `performance`: steps the wall clock **+1h** then **−2h** mid-budget and asserts the remaining budget stays `180_000`ms while `commandDeadlineAt()` still tracks the live wall clock. The native-lifecycle recovery-budget cases now advance the fixture's monotonic clock with simulated command work; the clock-step regression **fails on the original implementation** (elapsedMs+timeoutMs exceeds the asserted budget) and **passes with the fix** (native-lifecycle suite green).

Per review, added a real generated-helper trace of the recovery path under clock correction and advanced the fixture monotonic clock so the recovery-budget cases consume the simulated budget.

prs.title: docs(codex): RFC for recovering pending provider-review linkage
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178923

Builds on merged prevention PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179054.

## What Problem This Solves

An earlier failed acknowledgment can leave an existing conversation bound to a replacement native thread while its pending provider review still identifies the original; the normal review UI then rejects continuation with `Provider review no longer matches the native thread`.

## User Impact

**RFC/design only, not a working recovery fix.** This draft does not restore affected conversations or change runtime behavior. It proposes verifying current authority, restoring the original link through canonical ownership, and then requiring a separate normal acknowledgment with all existing safety checks intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #179054 prevents new replacements but explicitly does not repair an already-mismatched binding. This draft records the recovery contract, a data-only native policy comparator, and an already-mismatched regression specification. It implements no recovery endpoint, authority issuer, binding/review mutation, or acknowledgment path.

The OpenClaw coordinator and native broker remain unimplemented. Confirmation of the provider's ownership/configuration guarantees remains a dependency: Codex 0.160.0 exposes useful policy fields, but matching those fields does not establish exclusive native ownership or a configuration generation valid through canonical commit. If existing native semantics cannot supply that guarantee, provider support is required. Unknown evidence must refuse recovery.

Consistency repair must preserve the pending review and cannot approve continuation, fabricate ownership, spoof a channel sender, bypass catalog/current-policy checks, or replay held input.

## Evidence

- **23 supporting offline checks passed** for the data comparator and scenario fixture (22 data-comparison checks and one fixture consistency check).
- **31 actual recovery acceptance scenarios are specified but unexecuted**, including recovery of an already-mismatched state, authorization failures, changed policy/catalog/review, concurrency, idempotence, partial/uncertain recovery, rollback/crash disposition, and separate normal acknowledgment.
- No successful recovery, live provider acceptance, full Gateway/native integration, repository Vitest/build/typecheck or CI result is claimed.
- Local proposal diff syntax and full-content privacy scans passed. Only generic fixture identities and public source references are included.

Before this can become a recovery fix, implement and validate the coordinator/native broker and catalog preparation, resolve the provider-guarantee dependency, and prove the already-mismatched regression fails on prevention-only #179054 and passes on the implementation. This RFC should not close an existing-mismatch recovery report.

prs.title: fix: restore prepared registry reuse for plugin subagent completions
prs.body:
Refs #157935

Supersedes #157936, thanks @amoghasgekar.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-started subagent completions bypass a matching prepared plugin registry when registration drops the run's execution directory scope.

## User Impact

User impact: completion cleanup reuses the matching prepared registry, preserving the admitted agent directory and inherited or managed workspace. This removes an unnecessary plugin-loading path that is a likely cause of the stall reported in #157935. The regression proves registry reuse; end-to-end outage latency remains unmeasured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main's cleanup reuse path from #183996 requires `agentDir`, but plugin-run registration supplies neither directory. Carry the admitting runtime's `agentDir` and `workspaceDir` into registration and use the existing session workspace resolver for inherited workspaces and managed cwd values. The original contributor patch supplied only `workspaceDir`, which would still miss the current fast path.

The existing publication owner continues to decide whether a registry matches; historical or unpublished scopes retain its existing asynchronous fallback. No new cache, option, schema, or migration is added.

## Evidence

The new registration-to-completion regression uses the real registration record producer, prepared publication lookup, and context-engine completion consumer, with a spy on the fallback plugin loader. Registration persistence and plugin evaluation are isolated; this is owner-boundary proof rather than a live Gateway latency measurement.

On Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox ([lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41373754629)), the identical named test file fails on main `cd2f589dfe4c` and passes with this fix:

| Workspace scope | Main fallback loads | Fixed fallback loads | Fixed completion callbacks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Admitted runtime | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Inherited workspace | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Managed cwd | 1 | 0 | 1 |

Command: `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-subagent-cleanup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. All three baseline failures reach the zero-fallback assertion with `agentDir: undefined`.
