prs.title: fix(ui): accepted message shows "Waiting for reconnect" when a chat pane is shown again
prs.body:
Related: #158190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat message the Gateway already accepted shows "Waiting for reconnect" on a live connection when a chat pane is shown again and restores its composer while that message is still in flight.

## User Impact

User impact: messages sent while a reply is running keep their in-flight state after pane switches and split/dock handoffs, instead of briefly showing a false reconnect warning. Reload recovery is unchanged: after a real reload, an unconfirmed send is still restored as "Waiting for reconnect".

## Why This Change Was Made

The outbox deliberately stores in-flight sends under reload-safe aliases (`sending` is stored as `waiting-reconnect`), and the outbox owner normally overlays the live `sending` state when it presents the queue. Restoring a pane's composer copied the stored rows straight into the visible queue, bypassing that owner, so the alias showed until the next outbox publish. `restoreComposer()` now re-presents the outbox owner's projection right after the restore. All three restore callers (pane mount, composer handoff, outbox recovery) go through it.

This PR intentionally does **not** change the storage codec. Mapping `sending` to `waiting-reconnect` on write is the reload-recovery contract (see `needsReview` in `chat-outbox-owner.ts`), so the two storage-level tests described in #158190 fail by design.

<details>
<summary>Findings on the rest of #158190</summary>

I reproduced the reporter's flow against current `main` with the real submit, send, and drain code:

- After a follow-up gets a `started` ACK, storage holds `waiting-reconnect` / `sendAttempts: 1` while the live queue shows `sending` and a thread row with no reconnect label.
- The "third message held in `waiting-idle`, `sendAttempts: 0`" state reproduces when the third message is sent after the page sees the first reply finish while the Gateway still holds the second as queued custody. The drain keeps FIFO order behind that accepted head. Once the Gateway reports the second input as consumed, the next drain wake retires it and sends the third. That is ordering, not a permanent stall.
- If the third message is sent while the page still shows the reply as running, it is sent immediately and does not wait behind the second.

Follow-ups, deliberately left out of this fix:

- `restoreChatComposerState` still writes `chatQueue` itself. In production that write is now always superseded by the owner projection. Removing it means reworking several persistence tests that rely on it.
- `confirmQueuedMessageCustody` compares the live row (`sending`) with the stored row (`waiting-reconnect`), so custody stamping waits until the live send settles. I saw no user-visible effect from this.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression test in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-recovery.test.ts`. It mounts a real `ChatStateController`, sends a follow-up during an active run, and has the Gateway acknowledge it as `started`. It then restores the composer and asserts two things: the visible row stays `sending`, and storage still holds the `waiting-reconnect` reload alias.
  - Without the fix: fails at the post-restore assertion (`"sendState": "sending"` expected, `"waiting-reconnect"` received).
  - With the fix: passes.
- Test cost: the new test runs in 22 ms. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 86 s wall on my Windows machine, almost all of it Vitest import and transform (tests are about 2% of the time). No timers, sleeps, or polling.
- Related suites pass, 769 tests in total:
  - `composer-persistence`, `chat-send-submit`, `outbox-identity`
  - `chat-pane-attachment-handoff`, `chat-state`, `chat-state-queued-edit`
  - `composer-persistence-restore`, `chat-composer-queue`, `chat-send`
  - `chat-outbox-attention`, `chat-outbox-loading`, `chat-input-scroll-ownership`
  - `outbox-payloads`, `outbox-store`
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`:
  - Passed: conflict markers, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, the i18n catalog, and all core-test `tsgo` graphs, including `ui-chat`.
  - Not completed: the Knip dead-export scan timed out at 600 s on this host (this change adds no exports). That run also ended before its remaining lanes finished and was not rerun on the final commit; CI covers those gates.
  - `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- An independent code review found no correctness issues. It confirmed that the restore and the owner filter the same rows, so re-presenting cannot drop anything the restore intended to show. The `autoreview` skill was not available in my environment.
- Gap: no real-browser capture. This is a state-only fix with no styling change, proven at the controller boundary; my browser automation was unavailable. I also could not reproduce the "Reconnected before delivery was confirmed" copy quoted in the issue. That text needs a history read with no receipt for the send, while the reported trace shows the input as queued custody.

prs.title: fix(channels): preserve ordinary thread session bindings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary conversations bound to native threads are recorded as ACP sessions, so they can be reconciled with the wrong lifecycle after restart.

## User Impact

Ordinary session bindings now stay ordinary across creation, persistence, reload, and cleanup in Discord, Matrix, and Telegram. Existing ACP and subagent bindings keep their behavior. This is prerequisite A of the threaded `/fork` stack; it does not expose `/fork` by itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing public session/subagent contract in each plugin's private binding record. The existing worker-backed ACP metadata reader distinguishes supported main/global ACP aliases; canonical ACP keys remain ACP even if metadata is stale. Classification failures stop before native creation. Rebinding corrects a legacy ACP-coerced ordinary target without dropping same-target metadata. Historical explicitly tagged rows are not bulk rewritten.

No schema, configuration, dependency, retention, or permission changes. The updater is unchanged; no new migration step is needed. Simplification: reuse the binding and ACP owners rather than introduce a new manager, classification store, or fork-specific lifecycle. Production growth is necessary for the three plugin-private representations; tests add 223 lines.

## Evidence

- Ordinary-target regressions failed on all three original producers (`acp` instead of `session`).
- `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.creation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21 passed, 45.11s wall.

Draft only; not a merge request.

## Stack

[A · binding lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190763) → [B · shared command/core recording/Telegram](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190783) → [C · Discord](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190785), [D · Slack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190786), [E · Control UI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190787).

prs.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): recognize ambient aws-sdk authMode in runtime auth
prs.body:
Closes #163006

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Amazon Bedrock Mantle requests fail with a 401 "Invalid bearer token" when the provider is configured with `auth: "aws-sdk"` (ambient IAM credential chain), the same auth mode the standard `amazon-bedrock` provider already supports without issue.

## User Impact

User impact: Users can now set `auth: "aws-sdk"` on the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` provider and have it correctly generate an IAM-derived bearer token, instead of silently sending a generic internal auth sentinel to AWS as a literal bearer token and failing every request.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveMantleRuntimeBearerToken()` only recognized its own private marker string (`MANTLE_IAM_TOKEN_MARKER`) as a signal to mint an IAM-derived token. Core's generic `auth: "aws-sdk"` resolution path passes a different, generic sentinel `apiKey` along with `authMode: "aws-sdk"` (a field already present on `ProviderPrepareRuntimeAuthContext`), which this function never checked. This change widens the guard to also treat `authMode === "aws-sdk"` as ambient-IAM auth, mirroring the precedent already set by the standard `amazon-bedrock` provider for the same auth mode. No other behavior changes: the existing marker-based path (default/automatic-discovery, `auth` left unset) is untouched.

## Evidence

- Root cause and fix were validated live against a running OpenClaw instance before being ported to this source-level PR: an equivalent one-line hotpatch applied directly to the installed `2026.9.6` plugin's compiled `dist/discovery.js` resolved a real, reproduced 401 against the live AWS Bedrock Mantle endpoint under `auth: "aws-sdk"`, confirmed via before/after request logs.
- Added two regression tests in `extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts`:
  - `resolves Mantle runtime auth via ambient aws-sdk authMode without the IAM marker` — confirms the new path generates a real IAM token when `authMode: "aws-sdk"` is set, even without the internal marker string.
  - `returns the literal apiKey as-is when authMode is not aws-sdk and the IAM marker is absent` — confirms the pre-existing passthrough behavior for explicit `api-key` auth is unchanged.
- Type-checked `extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.ts` against the repo's own `tsconfig.json` with no errors reported for this file.
- Focused extension suite passed on the Windows node using the existing `C:\dev\openclaw-freshstart` checkout/package install: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-extension.mts amazon-bedrock-mantle` completed with **3 test files passed / 67 tests passed**, exit code 0. Vitest reported **119.97s** duration; external stopwatch elapsed **123.62s**. The run was performed on branch `fix/mantle-aws-sdk-auth-mode` at `c2abb033b` and the checkout was restored to its original `fix/plugin-catalog-loop` branch afterward.
## Live Before/After Proof

Both traces hit the exact same code path this PR changes: `amazon-bedrock-mantle`'s shared `prepareRuntimeAuth` hook (`resolveMantleRuntimeBearerToken`), with the provider configured for ambient `auth: "aws-sdk"`. This hook runs identically for every model under the provider, so a success on any model under this config is proof the auth-resolution fix works, not just the specific model.

### BEFORE fix — gateway PID 93277 (pre-patch build), repeated 401s, same session/day

```
2026-10-01T01:34:37.838-04:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=amazon-bedrock-mantle api=anthropic-messages model=anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 status=401 elapsedMs=204
2026-10-01T01:34:37.859-04:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: ... error=⚠️ amazon-bedrock-mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 request failed (authentication failed, HTTP 401). Re-authenticate the provider and try again. rawError=401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid bearer token"}}
2026-10-01T01:34:38.165-04:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: ... decision=fallback_model reason=auth from=amazon-bedrock-mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 rawError=401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid bearer token"}}

2026-10-01T08:05:35.411-04:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=amazon-bedrock-mantle api=anthropic-messages model=anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 status=401 elapsedMs=542
2026-10-01T08:14:17.465-04:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=amazon-bedrock-mantle api=anthropic-messages model=anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 status=401 elapsedMs=190
```
(Four separate request attempts across ~7 hours that day, all 401 "Invalid bearer token", all on the pre-fix build.)

### AFTER fix — gateway PID 311719 (patched build), same provider/auth config, success

```
2026-10-01T16:53:52.588-04:00 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=amazon-bedrock-mantle api=openai-responses model=openai.gpt-5.4 status=200 elapsedMs=91056 dispatcher=new contentType=text/event-stream
```

Full gateway restart confirmed between traces (new PID, new process start time); no other config changes made to the Mantle provider's `auth` setting between the before/after captures — only the `discovery.ts` auth-resolution patch in this PR was applied. The provider's `prepareRuntimeAuth` hook is shared across all models/APIs it serves (`anthropic-messages` and `openai-responses` alike), so the `openai.gpt-5.4` 200 after the fix demonstrates the same ambient-`aws-sdk` IAM token-generation path (previously 401ing for every model under this config, as shown above) now succeeds.

Session reference for the live test run that produced the AFTER trace: `18ea1aa5-0db4-40a4-9c04-658c44bd523a` (runId `6b44a5ff-e264-4c05-a8b5-558f3a16df2a`).

Redactions: hostnames, request IDs, and all AWS account/region identifiers in the originals have been scoped to the generic provider name here; no credentials were present in the source logs (bearer tokens are never logged by this subsystem, only the `invalid bearer token` error string from AWS's response body).

Merge and cleanup from master completed

prs.body: Based on a merge of #190499, #190374, #190387 and #190367, so this diff shows only this change. **Landing order:** those four first, in any order, then retarget this to main. ## What Problem This Solves Each long phone filter had its own surface. Meetings' five fields sat in a 366px popover over the page with a four-line paragraph. Usage and Sessions each built a sheet, with different titles and different choice controls. Workboard was a 336px card that scrolled inside itself, with its title on the left and a 26px close. ## User Impact At phone width every long filter opens the same way: a bottom sheet with a centered title, a plain 32px X in the same place, and labels above 40px fields on a 16px inset. Fields pair only when their values fit half the width; otherwise they take the row. Tablet and desktop keep their popovers. Meetings' paragraph becomes "Dates use UTC. IDs must match exactly.", the two facts that change how the fields behave. The long text stays on desktop. ## Why This Change Was Made Meetings, Usage and Sessions now use `PhoneSheet`, and their own surfaces and header CSS are gone. Sessions' choice pages become native selects, the same control as Automations and Usage. `headerAction` had no caller left, because #190367 moved search to the page. The date calendar and select truncation rules moved into `PhoneSheet` from Usage and Meetings, so all sheets share them. "Descending" doesn't fit half of a 320px phone, so Sort and Direction stack there, as dates already do. Workboard is a plugin and can't import `PhoneSheet` without a new SDK surface, so it takes the same shape in its own CSS. It closes with the dim, X and Escape, and has no grabber or swipe. Tablet and desktop are unchanged. Left alone, because they are short lists rather than forms: Dashboards, Logs, Activity, and the sidebar's Owners list. The sidebar's Filter & sort sheet has no title or X. It is a settings list with nested pages, and it is left as #190499 left it. `PhoneSheet.hide()` now ignores a call while closed. A search submits the same form, so its late dismiss could close the sheet if it was opened right after. ## Evidence Mock data with real taps, in Chromium and WebKit at 390x844 and 320x568. Absolutely light and dark and CRT were captured in Chromium, and Absolutely light in WebKit. Page PRs other than the four above aren't applied, so these show today's top bar. | Meetings before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Workboard before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Usage, dark | Sessions, CRT | | --- | --- | | | | | Meetings, 320x568, dark | Real Safari, OS click | | --- | --- | | | | Measured on all five sheets, at both widths, in every browser and theme captured: | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Title | none, 13.76px left, 14px or 15px | 14px, centered, 0px offset | | Title top from panel | 13px, 25px, 27px, or none | 25px | | X size | 26px, 32px, or none | 32px | | X from the right edge | 12px, 15px, or none | 12px | | X top from panel | 11px, 20px, 22px, or none | 20px | | Field height | 30px, 40px | 40px | | Field inset | 12px, 16px, 145px on Workboard's selects | 16px | | Horizontal overflow | 0px | 0px | - Meetings, Chromium and WebKit: Filter, a search from the closed form and Clear keep or clear the right params. A tap on the dim stays on the page and returns focus to the trigger. - Sessions and Usage: sort, Archived, Group by and UTC update the trigger's active state with the sheet open. In Sessions, Delete all archived and New group take the full width. - Workboard: a check, Clear, X and the dim all work, and the page stays put. - At 700px and 1280px Meetings, Sessions and Workboard keep their anchored or inline surfaces. Sessions keeps its search in the popover. - Real Safari 27.0.1 opened and closed the Meetings sheet and opened the Workboard sheet with OS clicks, in a 390px window. A temporary local proxy, not part of this change, set the theme through the mock's bootstrap preferences. - `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `stylelint`, `tsgo:ui`, `check:control-ui-controllers` and `ui:check-performance:base` pass. 233 unit and browser tests and 60 e2e tests across the 13 files that touch these filters pass. Tests that encoded the old surfaces were updated. ### Not verified iPhone: no device or simulator. The sheet above the software keyboard, native date and select pickers, and swipe weren't driven.

Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

## What Problem This Solves

Standing-grant approval cards and grant-list previews can cut a valid emoji between its UTF-16 surrogate halves at their 128, 256 and 512-unit display caps. Operators then see a broken replacement glyph in approval metadata.

## What Changed

Reuse the existing UTF-16-safe truncator after the existing approval-text sanitizer, through one internal display helper. Apply it to the automation/card-command labels and list command/cwd previews. Existing caps and sanitization remain unchanged.

The scope is display-only. Full command, cwd and requested environment still feed the unchanged operation-binding and grant-matching owners. No admission, authorization, approval decision, expiry, persistence or RPC schema changes; no new SDK exports.

The original contributor commit is preserved. Removed the standalone proof script and duplicate 275-line Gateway test from the product diff; cap regressions extend the existing display suite and use the native string well-formedness check instead of a custom surrogate scanner.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway WS, real Control UI screenshots and binding controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167259#issuecomment-6557429575).

- Secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker, full built Gateway and Control UI, real authenticated WS and Chromium. Main twice/candidate twice, with live automation ownership and genuinely minted SQLite standing grants.
- Main emits an unpaired high surrogate at all four preview sites; candidate emits well-formed bounded strings. Inbox screenshots show the visible broken-glyph fix.
- Actual stored operation binding is byte-identical across all four runs. Each artifact's canonical read-only grant validator accepts the complete operation and rejects command, cwd and environment changes identically.
- ASCII and bidi-sanitization controls unchanged.
- 16 focused display test cases and 38 existing standing-grant safety cases passed; changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.

Against frozen main: production +10/-10 (net 0), tests +14/-16 (net -2), docs +4. No standalone proof scripts remain in the PR.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores the prior preview formatting. No persisted data, permissions or approval semantics change. Blast radius is limited to sanitized standing-grant display previews in cards and listings; operation binding and execution continue using the full inputs.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): avoid search timeouts during source refresh
prs.body:
Related: #187429, #132296

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway-hosted Wiki searches exhaust their deadline when source import or compilation takes longer than the search budget, even when searchable Markdown already exists.

## User Impact

Users can search existing Wiki pages while the plugin refreshes sources and rebuilds missing indexes automatically in the background. No configuration migration or manual rebuild is required. Search still reads live Markdown, so it can reflect individual imported pages before a new index is published; results are not a snapshot of an entire refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `wiki_search` and Gateway `wiki.search` use plugin-owned background maintenance shared with dashboard refreshes. Queries initialize the vault before scheduling maintenance and then use the existing candidate selection and scan fallback. Successful refresh checks are reused for one minute; failed checks retry automatically with backoff from five seconds to one minute. Plugin shutdown cancels retries and joins active maintenance, and stale requests cannot schedule work into a restarted service.

This extends the maintenance lifetime handling in #187429 and consolidates the dashboard background refresh introduced in #132296. The search deadline still bounds the query without cancelling shared maintenance. Explicit imports, standalone operations, and callers without an active plugin service retain awaited synchronization; `ingest.autoCompile: false` remains respected.

## Evidence

- Regression proof against the original tool: a cold query blocked behind source import failed with `wiki_search timed out after 30s`.
- With the fix, cold and warm queries return existing pages while a paused importer holds the real vault mutation lease; concurrent queries share one import. After releasing the importer, the real compiler publishes updates and the next query finds the new content. Only the bridge importer is mocked in these two integration tests.
- All 50 focused tests passed across source synchronization, tool deadlines, Gateway dispatch, background query/compile integration, and plugin lifecycle. After simplifying test scaffolding, the Gateway suite passed again (29/29).
- Scoped production and test TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Full repository CI was not run locally.
- A compatible release backport was also exercised through the installed Gateway tool boundary with 1,200 synthetic pages: the original first search took 13.2s and waited for compilation; the patched first search returned in 3.9s before publication, then the plugin completed compilation automatically. Release backport typechecking and 22 focused tests passed; its separate lint artifact preparation hit a 300s SDK declaration-generation timeout.
- Independent production-code review and author simplification completed. Local ClawSweeper/autoreview was not run.

The two new real-flow cases took approximately 0.8s and 0.6s in the recorded run, excluding worker preparation. The scoped test-line allocation records 196 net new test lines for cold/warm queries, retries/shutdown, and service-generation regressions.

prs.title: fix(ci): terminate Android cleanup when emulator is unavailable
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190759.
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190004.

## What Problem This Solves

Android native qualification can hang in cleanup until the entire job is cancelled when its emulator never connects, hiding the boot failure and skipping diagnostic upload.

## User Impact

CI-only repair: failed qualification now reaches owned emulator disposal and report upload, preserving startup diagnostics and cleanup failures. App behavior and native qualification requirements stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound the unavailable-device operations and retain the emulator under a GNU timeout monitor. Cleanup signals only that owned monitor; its TERM/KILL escalation bounds the subsequent join. Copy and print the boot log before device operations. Failed trust restoration remains a contaminated-runner failure even after disposal.

This does not identify the underlying emulator boot cause or establish successful native Android qualification. The tokenjuice dependency update remains in its separate PR.

## Evidence

- Observed cancellation: [16 KB native job 124864883876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41312119326/job/124864883876); no Gradle/native tests executed, diagnostic upload skipped.
- Actual workflow cleanup replay hangs on base f0d3a2a. Both fixed fixtures pass: unavailable ADB preserves failure/contamination, boot diagnostics, AVD deletion and no running emulator; responsive ADB preserves the original boot failure.
- Local autoreview: complete candidate against f0d3a2a and fixture follow-up against 4b178a8 both P0–P2 scoped-clean. Independent process-ownership review found no actionable defects. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; hosted review started automatically on parent 4b178a8; a review of final head 555f153 is requested after the validated fixture follow-up.
- Native checkout: independent frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install, all 27 tests pass via `pnpm test test/scripts/android-access-workflow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (14.02s wall, 11.49s Vitest; hosted CI seconds pending).
- `pnpm check:workflows`, targeted type-aware oxlint, scoped TypeScript check extending the tooling test config, oxfmt checks and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base f0d3a2a038e1a09a444b1a25377376d4c8c31d87` pass. Native proof matches the signed 555f153 follow-up bytes. The code-only authoring hook was skipped; the relevant checks passed in the native checkout.
- Initial repository run exposed a fixture-only deadline error: healthy logcat exceeded the synthetic half-second budget. Only unavailable-ADB calls now use shortened deadlines; healthy commands keep production budgets, with the same outer fixture deadline and assertions.
- Regression allocation: exactly 62 added test lines for the real workflow cleanup/process boundary. No shared budget increase. Full change: 9 added/5 removed workflow lines, 62 test lines, four documentation lines and the allocation record.

Actual Android qualification: ordinary PR CI skipped this lane for the selected scope. [Documented manual main-tier validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41373442747) was dispatched once on exact 555f153 with Android enabled; it is queued. Native review artifacts validated READY with this platform-proof gap retained.

prs.title: improve(ui): show suggested tasks as a compact row above the composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Suggested tasks open as a large card floating over the top-right of the transcript, separate from everything else that waits above the composer. Its start button also uses a darkened copy of the accent, so it doesn't match Send when a custom accent is set.

## User Impact

User impact: a suggested task now lives in the stack directly above the composer, next to queued messages and the progress card.

- **Closed**, it's one quiet row: a muted lightbulb, the title and repository, a `1/2` pager when there are several suggestions, a plain accent-text **Start** action with its options arrow, and dismiss.
- **Open**, it reads like the question panel: the full title, the summary, and the instructions with their folder and a copy button. The footer carries the same small primary button the question panel submits with, nearest the composer.
- **On narrow screens** the closed row keeps only the title, position and dismiss. Opening it reveals paging and a full-width start button just above the composer.
- **When starting fails**, the card stays open. The lightbulb becomes a warning, and the error and recovery actions (Retry, choose a repository, Cancel) appear in the footer.
- The filled start button uses exactly the same fill and text color as **Send**, including custom accents. Its menu still offers a new session, a new worktree, or this session.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b28c92fc-e5c6-4d38-974a-31db2110ca36)

## Why This Change Was Made

- The tray renders in the composer's footer content, beside session suggestions. That content is shared by the built-in composer and plugin composer companions. The conversation's top-right gutter now holds only Details notices.
- The closed row uses the queue and progress card's surface and `--chat-stack-*` geometry. The open card mirrors the question panel's header → content → action-footer order, so the primary action always lands nearest the composer. The card is bounded at `min(30rem, 62dvh)`, and only its content scrolls.
- One start action, two weights: closed it is `btn btn--sm` with transparent ground and accent text, so the row stays quiet; open it is `btn btn--sm primary`, the question panel's Submit, with Send's hover step. The old lightness clamp and fixed white ink are removed, so a custom accent's computed ink applies to both.
- Copy moves next to the instructions it copies, and the instructions are shown in body text rather than a monospace block. The duplicate eyebrow and path boxes are removed.
- The disclosure state belongs to the tray, so paging keeps it. Starting a task doesn't open the card, but a failed start keeps it open until the user retries or dismisses.
- The open content is a flex column. A grid there sized its rows before the scrollbar appeared, which let a rewrapped long summary overlap the instructions and cover the copy button.
- Styles live in `composer-task-suggestions.css`, loaded by the lazy tray module. A new `Start` string was added to the English catalog.

## Evidence

Screenshots were captured from the real bundle against a mocked Gateway with synthetic data. They'll be attached in a follow-up body edit.

- `chat-flow.task-suggestions.e2e` + `chat-startup-priority.e2e` (13 tests, real bundle). The row renders inside `.chat-footer__context` and is closed by default. Opening it shows the summary, folder, prompt and copy, and moves Start to the footer. The footer's Start and its options trigger match Send's rendered fill and ink at rest and on hover, with `#da7756` and `#ffffff` accents. The menu opens above its trigger. Long summaries stay reachable, and copy and Start pass Playwright's trial-click hit check at 1280×720, 390×720 and 900×500. The draft is kept in all three start modes.
- Unit: `chat-task-suggestions` + `chat-pane-task-suggestions` (38 tests). These cover disclosure ARIA wiring, disclosure kept across paging, no opening while starting, a failure keeping the card open, the closed row's short label with its full accessible name, and Start moving from header to footer.
- Capture pass at 320 px and 1280 px with two suggestions, in both the plain failure and repository-chooser states: dismiss stays inside the row.
- `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt and `ui:i18n:verify` are clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2). On the first layout, the first pass found one P2, later fixed, and the second pass was scoped-clean. On the redesign commit the result was scoped-clean; the final weight-only refinement reran the suites above.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(cron): command jobs fail with spawn sh ENOENT on Windows Gateways
prs.body:
Closes #141038

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cron `--command` jobs on a Windows Gateway fail on every run with a permanent `spawn sh ENOENT`, because `cron add`, `cron edit` and Doctor always stored `["sh", "-lc", <command>]`.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw cron add|edit --command` now stores the shell of the Gateway host that runs the job. Windows Gateways get `cmd.exe /d /s /c`, including commands that contain their own quotes. macOS and Linux keep `sh -lc`, so their behavior does not change. `--command-argv` stays exact.

Existing Windows jobs keep their stored `sh -lc` argv. The docs give the recovery step: `openclaw cron edit <job-id> --command <shell>`. If the Gateway cannot report its platform, the CLI stops and asks for `--command-argv` instead of guessing.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **CLI:** `cron add` and `cron edit` read the platform from the Gateway's `system.info` (`operator.read`, already implied by the `operator.admin` cron writes). They never use the CLI's own platform, which would be wrong for a remote Gateway or for a Windows CLI driving a Linux Gateway in WSL. This addresses the fallback concern raised on the earlier attempt, #141043.
- **Doctor:** legacy prompt conversion runs on the host that owns the cron store, so it uses that process's platform.
- **Runner:** the cron runner now launches `cmd.exe /d /s /c` payloads the same way `system.run` does: the quoted command line, passed verbatim. Without this, Node's argument escaping breaks quoted commands under `/s`. The existing launch rule moved from `node-host/invoke-run-command.ts` to `infra/node-shell.ts`, next to `buildNodeShellCommand`, so both callers share one owner.

## Evidence

All Windows runs below use a fork-only workflow with built `dist`, isolated state and `sh` removed from the Gateway's PATH: [run 41064923463](https://github.com/nobrainer-tech/openclaw/actions/runs/41064923463).

**Windows, this branch**
- `system.info` reports `win32`.

| Command | Stored argv | Run result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `echo hello-from-windows-cron` | `["cmd.exe","/d","/s","/c","echo hello-from-windows-cron"]` | `ok`, summary `hello-from-windows-cron` |
| `"C:\...\node.exe" -e "console.log('quoted-ok')"` | `cmd.exe /d /s /c` wrapper | `ok`, summary `quoted-ok` |

**Windows, base commit `e85f97c81be` in the same run**
- Both jobs store `["sh","-lc",...]` and fail with `error: spawn sh ENOENT`.

**Windows upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.10.9)**

Jobs created by the stable release:

| Job | Stored payload |
| --- | --- |
| shell | `["sh","-lc","echo stable-shell-ok"]` |
| explicit argv | `["node","-e",...]`, `env: {PROOF:"1"}`, `timeoutSeconds: 45` |
| legacy prompt | `agentTurn` with `Command to run: - command: echo legacy-ok` and `toolsAllow: ["exec"]` |

Then `doctor --fix --non-interactive` from this branch ran (exit `0`), followed by the Gateway from this branch:

| Job | After upgrade | Run result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| legacy prompt | converted to `["cmd.exe","/d","/s","/c","echo legacy-ok"]` | `ok`, summary `legacy-ok` |
| explicit argv | unchanged, with its `env` and timeout | `ok`, summary `argv-ok` |
| shell | stored `sh -lc` kept | still `spawn sh ENOENT` |
| shell, after the documented `cron edit <id> --command "echo stable-shell-ok"` | `cmd.exe /d /s /c` | `ok`, summary `stable-shell-ok` |

The legacy job needed a configured provider route to be accepted, so the run used a synthetic `OPENAI_API_KEY`. No model was called.

**Native runner test on Windows**
- The quoted `cmd.exe` test in `src/cron/command-runner.test.ts` (Windows-only) passes on this branch.
- It fails when only `src/cron/command-runner.ts` is reset to the base commit.

**Isolated macOS Gateway**
- `cron add --command` stores `["sh","-lc",...]` and `cron run --wait` succeeds.
- `cron edit --command` rewraps the command.
- `cron edit --command-argv` stays exact.
- A Gateway that cannot report its platform fails before `cron.add`, with the `--command-argv` hint.
- Doctor converts a legacy prompt job to `sh -lc`.

**Regression tests**
- Red on base, green with the fix:
  - CLI add and edit on a Windows Gateway;
  - Gateway without `system.info`, and Gateway that omits the platform;
  - Doctor conversion on Windows.
- `trigger-options.test.ts` fixtures now answer `system.info`.
- All cron CLI, Doctor cron, cron runner, node-host run-command and node-shell suites pass locally through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: 22 files, 418 tests.

prs.title: fix(gateway): synchronous exec through the macOS app node still repeats as an Exec finished wake
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154474

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a synchronous `exec host=node` through the macOS app node still wakes the session a second time with an "Exec finished" notice when the node's `exec.finished` event reaches the Gateway after the command's inline result.

## User Impact

User impact: synchronous node commands through the macOS app produce one result (the tool result) and no extra completion turn, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164511 already does for the headless node host. If the Gateway stops waiting (timeout), the late "Exec finished" notice still arrives.

Affected: every synchronous `exec host=node` through the macOS app node with default `tools.exec.notifyOnExit`, intermittently (depends on delivery order; 1 of 3 calls in our production check on 2026.10.9). In Claude CLI sessions the extra wake also started a fresh CLI session without history (details in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154474#issuecomment-6565618629 ).

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164511 holds the finished notice on the pending invocation, which relies on the node sending `exec.finished` before its `system.run` result. The headless node host keeps that order (`sendSystemRunCompleted` awaits the event RPC before the result). The macOS app runs the same node host as a worker behind its Swift supervisor, and that bridge does not keep it: the worker's `node.event` and `node.invoke.result` are acknowledged immediately (`src/node-host/worker-support.ts`), and `MacNodeHostWorker.swift` resumes the invoke result at once while events go through a separate delivery task. When the result arrives first, the invocation is no longer pending, `holdNotice` is not set, and the late notice is queued.

The node registry now records that a `system.run` invocation settled with an inline result (`ok: true`) on its existing authorization record. A terminal `exec.finished`/`exec.denied` for exactly that node, connection, session and run is then consumed without a notification. The record keeps its existing lifetime (run timeout plus grace, or until disconnect); its event source is released at once because no notice will be delivered. Unchanged: notices after a Gateway timeout (the recovery path from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164511 ), a node failure result that arrives after the event (still notifies), `exec.started`, and the dedupe. No protocol, config or node-host change; the protocol doc states the added rule.

Alternative not taken: make the Swift supervisor wait for pending event delivery before resuming `invoke-result`. That would restore the documented order for this bridge only, and `sendEvent` would also have to await the Gateway's reply; the registry fix covers any node that reorders the two frames.

The existing custody test (`keeps original caller custody and delivery for remote exec`) used an inline `ok` result followed by a late `exec.finished` as its "late notice" case. That sequence is exactly the duplicate this PR removes, so its non-inline modes now settle through the invoke deadline (fake timers), which is the remaining way a late notice is delivered. Routing, custody and revocation assertions are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused tests (Crabbox on a Mac mini, arm64, `--maxWorkers=2`):

| Case | `main` 71becfa19f3 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Inline `ok` result, then `exec.finished` (macOS app order) | notice queued (duplicate) | no notice, authorization consumed |
| Invoke deadline expires, then `exec.finished` | notice queued | notice queued |
| `exec.finished` before the result (headless order, existing test) | no notice | no notice |
| Custody/routing of a late notice after the deadline (live, revoked, inline, unscoped) | pass | pass |

- New test: `src/gateway/server-node-events.session-events.test.ts` › `notifies a late exec.finished only when the Gateway stopped waiting` drives a real `NodeRegistry` with a macOS-app node session. The `result` case fails on `main` (counter-check with the fix reverted: 1 failed, 9 passed) and passes with the fix.
- Suites around the changed owners pass: 19 test files, 3 Vitest shards, 192 s wall (list in details).
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files, `tsgo` on the changed test file, line-cap ratchet: clean.

Live, real macOS app node (debug app packaged from `main` 71becfa19f3) against an isolated Gateway on a Mac mini, a mock OpenAI-compatible model that records every request, one session, 25 synchronous `system.run` per run through `node.invoke`. A wake turn is a model request carrying a new `Exec finished (node=… id=<runId>)`.

Without intervention the race did not occur locally: the app's `node.event` was answered before its `node.invoke.result` in all 25 runs, and both Gateways showed 0 wakes. To get the production order (1 of 3 calls on 2026.10.9, app connected through an SSH tunnel over Tailscale, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154474#issuecomment-6565618629 ) deterministically, both Gateway builds got one test-only line in `dist/` that delays `exec.finished` handling by 300 ms before `handleNodeEvent` (same idea as the fault injection in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164511 ). The app's Swift bridge resumes the invoke result without waiting for event delivery, so the result arrived while `exec.finished` was still pending in 25/25 runs on both sides (`--ws-log full`).

| Gateway build | inline results with output | runs that woke the session with "Exec finished" |
|---|---|---|
| `main` 71becfa19f3, 300 ms injected | 25/25 | 25/25 (50 model requests, 25 distinct run IDs) |
| this PR 561a5e43cd7, 300 ms injected | 25/25 | 0/25 (0 model requests) |
| `main`, no injection | 25/25 | 0/25 (race did not occur) |
| this PR, no injection | 25/25 | 0/25 |

Not verified live: the Gateway-timeout path with a real app node (the late notice after a timeout); it is covered by the `timeout` case of the new test.

<details><summary>Test output</summary>

```text
# fix (561a5e43cd7), Crabbox Mac mini, --maxWorkers=2, wall 192 s
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts
 Test Files  16 passed (16)
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 189.73s
 ✓ server-node-events.session-events.test.ts > notifies a late exec.finished only when the Gateway stopped waiting (result) 3ms
 ✓ server-node-events.session-events.test.ts > notifies a late exec.finished only when the Gateway stopped waiting (timeout) 2ms

# counter-check: production changes reverted, test kept
 × server-node-events.session-events.test.ts > notifies a late exec.finished only when the Gateway stopped waiting (result) 5ms
 ✓ server-node-events.session-events.test.ts > notifies a late exec.finished only when the Gateway stopped waiting (timeout) 2ms
 Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
```

Files: `src/gateway/server-node-events{,.session-events,.system-event-owner}.test.ts`, `src/gateway/node-registry{,-policy,.dispatch-authority}.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes*`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node*`.

</details>

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the previous notice timing; nothing is persisted, migrated or added to the protocol. Blast radius: terminal `exec.finished`/`exec.denied` for a `system.run` invocation whose inline result was already delivered successfully; everything else keeps the behavior from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164511 .

prs.title: fix: chat freezes when scroll anchoring makes no progress
prs.body:
Related: #149361

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes whole-page chat freezes when a retained reading anchor repeatedly requests a scroll that does not move the native viewport. Also preserves the retained reading position when WebKit applies that native write on a later frame with a rounded offset.

## User Impact

Users can continue clicking, typing, and scrolling while chat history and message grouping reconcile. A deferred correction keeps its original reading target; subsequent wheel input still takes over.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issuing a scroll command was treated as movement and immediately triggered another render. If the browser defers or ignores the write, repeated microtasks can prevent input, paint, and the virtualizer's frame reconciliation from running.

The anchor now checks actual native movement and yields further reconciliation to one animation frame. Incidental commits retain the pending anchor; reader takeover and disconnect cancel it.

Testing the original PR head in real Safari exposed a second defect: a delayed native correction was classified as reader movement, moving the held reading target. The offset observer now retains a pending non-smooth target until its rounded or clamped native receipt arrives. Reader input clears that provenance, and smooth scrolling retains its existing command lifecycle. A matching no-op does not invalidate delivery cleanup.

## Evidence

### October 18: resolve conflicts with the Solid migration

Current candidate: `409042227adf57834fd87a2bf7bee5af2ed6721a`, merging upstream `f585b0421821c15ce1d0e545a13bcea0f36ab764` without rewriting the three existing PR commits.

- Keep the ignored-write progress check and deferred/rounded native-scroll provenance. Adapt the host's queued reconciliation to the current Solid `invalidate()` owner, retaining cancellation on disconnect and reader takeover.
- Replace the retired Lit virtualizer-controller fixture with the current native `Virtualizer` mount/update/dispose lifecycle. Migrate the new offset-observer sibling tests to the pending/delivered maintenance state. No old Lit adapter or parallel scroll owner is restored.
- **105 tests passed across four owner/sibling files in 6.41 s** using the repository Vitest wrapper (prepend-anchor, offset-observer, transcript-controller, scroll-ownership). Both independent negative controls fail at the expected assertions with the corresponding unmodified upstream owner: ignored writes do not settle, and delayed native writes lose the reading target. The repaired candidate passes.
- UI typecheck and the `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json` leaf pass via `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`. Targeted five-file oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the changed-source line-cap ratchet pass. `pnpm ui:build` completes successfully, including the shipped-sidecar performance checks.
- Independent read-only review found one stale test-field migration; that finding was repaired and rechecked. No other actionable P0–P2 finding was reported. This was a collaboration-agent narrative review, not the autoreview helper's machine-certified result.
- **Inherited check:** the repository-wide max-lines-suppression ratchet reports the same three existing violations in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`. Reproduced against an index containing only the pinned upstream tree; those files and the baseline are byte-identical to upstream in this candidate. No baseline or suppression was changed.
- Local tooling limitation: an earlier parallel check was interrupted after artifact-lock contention; checks were rerun serially. The successful UI build wrapper reports child cleanup unverified and retains its local task-owned lock/recovery checkout. This is not reported as verified process cleanup.
- Simplification: remove the obsolete Lit test-host scaffold; retain the existing anchor/offset owners and their necessary native-delivery state. Relative to pinned upstream: five files, production +78/-30, tests +174/-4. No rendering style or user-facing API change.
- Current proof is Linux owner/integration tests and a production build. The real Safari traces below remain historical proof of `8eeed520...`; **Safari was not rerun after the Solid migration**, and prior-head CI is not current-head CI.

### Earlier repair and Safari evidence

- October 14 PR head: `e63ef9f6d80fb5e9f585eeeed36fa44d749717c8`; original base: `0348a2526c561d8ccce61bfd23931024a6b8f13e`.
- Test-only follow-up on October 14: CI found TS2322 in the new native `scrollTo` mock because its options parameter was required. The mock now accepts the native optional-argument overload. Exact failing leaf `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json` passes; all **15 affected owner tests pass in 1.08 s**, along with focused lint, formatting, and diff checks. Independent review confirmed the overload fix. No production file changed in this follow-up: Git blob identities for the prepend-anchor, offset-observer, and host match runtime-tested commit `8eeed52011767555ab040f442df857874160debc`. The Safari logs below retain their actual tested commit rather than claiming a new browser run.

- The original main fails the ignored-write regression because the retained anchor never settles. Original PR head `262975cc360e949da87a53cf56e4cbf54b5c1fda` fails the new delayed native-boundary regression: offsets 280/278 versus expected 240/239. The final candidate passes both rounding variants and subsequent reader takeover.
- Focused owner and sibling tests via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ... --maxWorkers=1`: **99 tests passed in 7.55 s** (three files: prepend-anchor, controller, scroll-ownership).
- UI typecheck, clean candidate build, formatting, `git diff --check`, and max-lines ratchet passed. Scoped lint has only the inherited `chat-transcript-virtualizer-host.ts` diagnostic: **709 counted lines versus 700**, unchanged from pristine base.
- Independent autoreview of the production repair and owning sources: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Regression audit confirmed actual native I/O and production observer entry points, with no fabricated scroll-provenance receipts.

- Real Safari 27.0.1 / macOS 27.0.1 runtime proof of the **unchanged production repair** passed both faults. Deferred native writes settle with the retained bubble shifting **0.666672 px** (within the 2 px assertion); ignored writes settle after **3 attempts**, with no further writes during twelve subsequent frames. Frame and timer tasks continue; the production composer/send/final path completes in 138/114 ms. Native user input and wheel events, subsequent native displacement, a new submission, and its rendered response are also recorded.
- This uses the current bundled app and canonical mock Gateway with deterministic native-boundary faults, not a live provider/Gateway. Original PR head's failed deferred trace is preserved and led to the additional offset-provenance repair. Button-click proof is scripted; no trusted send-click is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable Safari native-offset and interaction traces of the production repair</summary>

Runtime-tested production commit: `8eeed52011767555ab040f442df857874160debc`; clean checkout (`dirty=false`).

Environment: real Safari **27.0.1**, macOS **27.0.1**, Node **24.21.0**. Actual browser HTTP user agent includes `Version/27.0.1 Safari/605.1.15`. This tests the bundled Control UI with the canonical mock Gateway, rather than a live provider or operator Gateway.

Build ID: `2026.10.2-8eeed5201176-2026-10-13T09-08-02.456Z`. Entry: `assets/index-DbCEAPYp.js`; served SHA-256: `3a491436a0e50015dc3f47175f3be58367f67b0f0185b877acac93935f37a743` (matches the clean build). Captured **2026-10-13 09:11–09:12 UTC**. Both cases also passed on the user's preceding refresh; the excerpts below show the final refresh and its native interaction.

The fixture follows `ui/src/e2e/chat-history-prepend-anchor.e2e.test.ts`: 800 recent messages and six earlier messages extend the first assistant group, with more history remaining. It uses the repository's canonical mock bootstrap/transport and actual `chat.history` request, message adoption, production renderer, measurements, host, virtualizer, and offset observer. Original bundled assets are served byte-for-byte; only fixture setup is injected before app startup. The isolated fixture blocks the offline worker, matching the existing E2E worker-blocking setup.

Observational wrappers count existing host commits and anchor updates; they never invoke, clear, or force an anchor. Faults intercept only native `Element.scrollTo({behavior:"instant"})` for the active thread during production anchor updates. Ignored writes do nothing; deferred writes call the original browser native method on a later animation frame. No provenance receipts are fabricated. This is deterministic native-boundary fault proof, not a claim that Safari spontaneously failed again.

Each case requires actual fault delivery, anchor settlement, no queued native writes, twelve subsequent frames without another anchor write, animation-frame and timer progress, a native offset change, actual composer adoption, a matching `chat.send`, and a rendered final fixture response. Deferred mode additionally enforces a 2 px reading-position bound. Terminal records are durably acknowledged before automatic navigation to the next case, and any failed case stays failed. The final fixture source snapshots and hashes are retained locally alongside raw logs.

## Deferred writes — PASS

Two native writes applied: `0 → 240`, then target `618` rounded to `617`. Reading bubble top `120 → 120.666672` (**+0.666672 px**). Anchor retired, writes stopped, frames and timer tasks progressed. Scripted composer/send/final path completed in **138 ms** from input / **136 ms** from click.

```json

{"receivedAt":"2026-10-13T09:11:50.743Z","case":"deferred","kind":"native-deferred-applied","elapsedMs":1453,"before":240,"target":618,"after":617,"scrollTop":617,"anchorPending":true,"anchorWrites":2,"frames":43,"ticks":7}
{"receivedAt":"2026-10-13T09:11:50.960Z","case":"deferred","kind":"anchor-settled","elapsedMs":1669,"scrollTop":617,"anchorPending":false,"anchorWrites":2,"frames":55,"ticks":9,"beforeTop":120,"afterTop":120.66667175292969,"readerDelta":0.6666717529296875,"writesStopped":true,"maxFrameGapMs":55,"maxTickGapMs":124,"trustedInputEvents":0,"trustedClickEvents":0,"trustedWheelEvents":0}

{"receivedAt":"2026-10-13T09:11:51.099Z","case":"deferred","kind":"scripted-input-send-response","elapsedMs":1808,"inputTrusted":false,"clickTrusted":false,"humanInputClaimed":false,"composerAdopted":true,"sendRequestMatched":true,"finalRendered":true,"inputToFinalMs":138,"clickToFinalMs":136}

```

## Ignored writes — PASS

Three reachable anchor writes were ignored, with native offset staying zero. The production anchor retired and no further anchor writes occurred in twelve later frames. Scripted native scroll reached 40, and composer/send/final path completed in **114 ms** from input / **106 ms** from click.

The retained bubble shifts **618 px** when the browser permanently refuses scrolling; this case proves bounded retries and responsiveness, not preserved reading position under permanently ignored writes.

## Native user interaction after the fault

Actual Safari input and wheel events have `isTrusted=true`. A trusted wheel is followed by a native offset change `96254 → 96257`. Native input reaches length 2; the production client submits a new two-character message and renders the unique fixture response, with **40 ms** between request observation and rendered-final observation. Message contents are omitted. A trusted send-click was not captured; button clicks are covered separately by the explicitly scripted production path (`isTrusted=false`). The native submission's activation method is not inferred from these logs.

```json

{"receivedAt":"2026-10-13T09:11:54.028Z","case":"ignored","kind":"manual-native-scroll","elapsedMs":2849,"trusted":true,"before":96254,"after":96257}
```

prs.title: improve(ui): compact Settings Skills controls on phones
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width, Settings > Skills spends the first screen on controls. Four action buttons wrap across two rows, Refresh sits alone on its own row, and the search field has its own label. The first skill starts 686 px down a 844 px screen. ## User Impact On a phone the first skill now starts at 360 px, so the list is visible on arrival. Search skills, Workshop, Create skill and Import skill are one tap away in a menu announced as "More actions", and search and Refresh share a row. Switching library tabs no longer moves the content under them. Desktop does not change. ## Why This Change Was Made Below 640 px the library tabs stay first and the explanatory line stays under them. The search field, an icon Refresh and a three-dots menu share one row, on the same button surface as the Automations filter trigger in every theme. The menu uses the existing `Menu` component and runs the same actions as the desktop buttons. The Agent & workspace tab keeps its own filter toolbar and gets the same menu, so no action is lost on that tab. Every library tab sits 12 px under the tabs. That tab's text Refresh is handled by #190426. The search label stays available to assistive technology. Skill cards in the catalog that Search skills opens showed a bare status dot whose meaning lived in a hover tooltip, which a phone doesn't have, so on phones the state is written next to the dot. Desktop keeps the dot and tooltip. ## Evidence Mock data at 390 px with real taps. Page PRs branch from main, so these images show today's top bar until the header PR lands. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.title: fix(gateway): skill_workshop read budget falls back to 8k tokens on CLI runtimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `skill_workshop` `read` refuses any skill over ~2.8 KB as "the complete skill exceeds the selected-model read budget" when the agent runs on a CLI runtime (Claude CLI / Gemini CLI), even on a 1M-context model — the same skill reads fine on the embedded runtime.

## User Impact

User impact: operators running the main agent on a CLI runtime can read and update Workshop skills of normal size again (a 200K session now gets a ~70K-char read budget instead of ~2.8K; a 1M session ~350K), and every other tool projection sized by the model window on that runtime (read-tool result caps) is sized correctly instead of by the 8,192-token fallback. A session that selects a smaller catalog context window (Claude CLI `200k` on a 1M model) keeps that smaller bound for tool output too. No user-visible change on the embedded runtime. No config change required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loopback tool surface built its tools without `modelContextWindowTokens`. CLI preparation already resolves the run's finalized context budget (`contextWindowInfo.tokens` in `prepare.ts`: per-model minimum, the session-selected catalog `contextWindows` option, configured limits, alias-aware upper bound) and passes it to the in-process tool set and to `contextTokenBudget` — but the MCP loopback grant never carried it, and `resolveGatewayScopedTools` never passed a value into `createOpenClawTools` / `createOpenClawCodingTools`, so `resolveSkillWorkshopProjectionBudgets` (and `resolveToolResultBudget`) always fell back to `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS = 8192`.

The grant now carries `modelContextWindowTokens` as an explicit parameter of `buildCliMcpGrantContext`, set from `contextWindowInfo.tokens` at the single call site in `prepare.ts`. Preparation stays the only owner of the budget: the grant relays the finalized number and does not recompute it from the raw catalog inputs on the run params (the first revision did, which would have sized a 200k session's tools by the 1M catalog window — ClawSweeper P2 finding, addressed in the second commit). When preparation resolved nothing usable the key is omitted so the tools keep their conservative default. The MCP cache key spreads the whole context, so cached scoped tools are keyed on it automatically.

## Evidence

### Tests

Merged current `main` (`upstream/main` at merge time) into the branch. `main` deleted `prepare.context-window.test.ts` (#165336) and kept the budget resolution inline in `prepare.ts`, so this revision drops the earlier `prepare-context-budget.ts` extraction: the production change in `prepare.ts` is now the single `modelContextWindowTokens: contextWindowInfo.tokens` argument at the `buildCliMcpGrantContext` call site, and the regression case moved into `prepare.test.ts` next to main's "caps the context budget …" cases.

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/cli-runner/mcp-grant-context.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-grant-store.test.ts` → 4 files, 184/184 on the merged head.
- New `prepare.test.ts` case "carries the finalized session-capped budget into the loopback grant": Claude CLI backend with bundled MCP, catalog entry `contextWindow: 1_000_000` with `contextWindows` `200k`/`1m`, run params `modelContextWindow: 1_000_000, contextWindow: "200k"` → `contextWindowInfo.tokens === 200_000` **and** the minted grant's `modelContextWindowTokens === 200_000`. Re-verified on the merged head: red without the `prepare.ts` line (`expected undefined to be 200000`), green with it.
- `mcp-grant-context.test.ts`: the grant relays the prepared value (200k beats 1M raw catalog inputs on the run), omits it when the run has catalog inputs but preparation passed nothing, and on `0` / `NaN`.
- The existing exact-shape grant test in `prepare.test.ts` ("preserves already-admitted authority through MCP grant transfer") now expects `modelContextWindowTokens: 200_000` (`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS`), because every prepared run has a finalized budget.
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` clean on the six touched files. `pnpm tsgo:core` passes; `pnpm tsgo:core:test` shards `agents-root`, `agents-other`, `agents-tools`, `gateway-root`, `gateway-server`, `gateway-other` (and `infra`, `state-logging`, `commands`, `plugins-platform`) pass.

### Test cost

Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the merged head (Linux, 4 vCPU, warm transform cache):

| Changed test file | Tests | Vitest duration | Wall time | Added by this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/mcp-grant-context.test.ts` | 29 | 3.0 s | 6.0 s | 1 grant case (relay, omission, `0`/`NaN`), 0 ms (< 1 ms) |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 116 | 109.2 s | 152.8 s | 1 case, 690 ms; one existing expectation gains a field (no new time) |

`prepare.test.ts` is an existing file that is already above the 30 s target on `main`; this PR adds one 690 ms case to it and no fixtures, timers, or boots. The case needs the real preparation path (catalog option selection → `contextWindowInfo` → grant mint), which no cheaper layer exercises: `mcp-grant-context.test.ts` covers the relay contract but cannot prove that preparation passes the session-capped value rather than the raw catalog window.

CI seconds ([CI run 37559972873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37559972873), head `11d1d8e411a`, before the routing fix):

| Changed test file | CI job | Vitest duration | Shard wall time |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/mcp-grant-context.test.ts` | `checks-node-changed-1` (bun) | 0.85 s | 2.21 s |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | `checks-node-changed-2` | 73.51 s | 75.49 s |

Both pass in CI (29/29, 116/116).

CI routing fix (separate commit `8c9c95de5ae`): on the merged head, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-20` / `-22` failed all 16 cases of `src/gateway/tool-resolution.swarm-collector.test.ts` and `src/gateway/tool-resolution.terminal.test.ts` with `SqliteWorkerError: Shared-state admission requires the host broker`. Both files reach the shared-state store through `resolveGatewayScopedTools` but were not listed in `gatewayDatabaseWorkerTestFiles`, so they ran in the threaded `gateway-core` project, where the store refuses to open off the main thread. The failure predates this PR (same 16/16 with this PR's files reverted to `main`); `main`'s CI skips these shards, and they were selected here only because the PR touches `tool-resolution.ts`. The commit adds both files to the list next to `tool-resolution.test.ts`; locally they then pass 16/16 in `gateway-database-workers`, and the routing guards (`test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts`, `test-projects-routing.test.ts`, `test-projects.test.ts`, `test/vitest-cli-ownership.test.ts`, `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts`) pass 555/555.

### After-fix real behavior (Claude CLI runtime)

Built this branch (`pnpm build`, 6m15s) and ran a second Gateway from the build on the same Linux host, isolated state dir (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), port 18799, minimal config: `agents.defaults.model.primary = anthropic/claude-opus-5` with `agentRuntime.id = claude-cli`, `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode = auto`. prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.

The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.

Tailscale discovery launches an unnecessary `locate Tailscale.app` subprocess on Linux and Windows when no usable CLI is found.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the macOS-only fallback in `findTailscaleBinary`, with an injected platform for cross-platform coverage. Reuse the existing invalid-CLI regression instead of adding another suite. Production grows by three lines for the guard; there is no duplicate platform check or dead branch to remove safely in this owner. Tests grow by nine lines, covered by a dedicated test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- Verified on current main `cd2f589dfe4c98651f5ce435838736b58aa77ddd`: the unconditional fallback accepts only macOS app paths.
- Red before: the production discovery tests fail for Linux and Windows because `locate` runs once instead of zero; the macOS case passes.
- Green after: all 34 tests in `src/infra/tailscale.claim.test.ts` pass, including zero locate calls on Linux/Windows and one on macOS. Standalone Vitest with the repository infra config took 1.38s wall time (about 0.14s test time); The CI changed-node test job passed in 274 seconds including setup; per-file CI timing was not separately inspected.

The normal runner started broad worker preparation and was stopped; standalone Vitest preserves source imports without that build. prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.

prs.title: fix(infra): skip the POSIX locate fallback when Tailscale is not on a Mac
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`findTailscaleBinary()` falls through to a POSIX `locate` subprocess on every host whose PATH has no
Tailscale binary, even though the only candidates that fallback can return are macOS app paths.
On Windows and Linux the spawn is guaranteed to fail (`spawn locate ENOENT` on Windows;
`locate` is absent or its database is unpopulated on most Linux installs), so tailnet setup pays a
pointless failed-process launch before correctly reporting "Tailscale not found".

## Why This Change Was Made

Strategy 2 already probes the fixed macOS app path
(`/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale`), and strategy 3 exists solely to *find that
same path* via the `locate` database — it filters output with
`line.includes("/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale")`. The candidate set is therefore identical,
so on any non-darwin platform the fallback cannot change the return value; it can only add a failed
spawn.

The fix gates strategy 3 on `process.platform === "darwin"`, the only platform where its candidate
filter can match. No new helper, no new export, and no change to the return value on any platform —
the existing owner (`resolveExecutablePath`, `checkBinary`) is untouched.

I initially misdiagnosed this function: I believed strategy 1's explicit `process.env.PATH` argument
bypassed the PATHEXT probe and broke Windows `.exe` detection. Executing the code disproved it
(`resolveExecutableFromPathEnv` enumerates PATHEXT by default), so that patch was dropped as a no-op
and the reachability question above is what the evidence actually supports.

## User Impact

Non-macOS operators setting up `tailscale` exposure through `openclaw configure` or the setup wizard
no longer incur a failing `locate` spawn on the discovery path when Tailscale is not installed.
