prs.title: fix(cli): stop cloning the state database for Gateway RPC commands
prs.body:
Related: #178730 (separate snapshot-exit cleanup; unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

RPC-only CLI commands clone the whole shared state database during startup when a Gateway has held its lock for more than five minutes and plugin source captures exist. On a reported btrfs installation, an 11.8 GB database with about 555,000 extents made these repeated reflinks expensive enough to stall unrelated writers, including Gateway WAL commits.

## User Impact

Commands such as `openclaw team-reports list --period day --json` can check the live Gateway's readiness without copying its state database. No configuration, schema, retention, permission, or CLI contract changes are required. Artifact-preserving inspection and Doctor schema repair retain private snapshots.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lease reader now uses the existing synchronous native current-read path for its bounded lease lookup when `hasVerifiedLiveSqliteOwner` verifies the exact database's recorded process identity. It retains the existing schema/admission checks and synchronous reader cleanup. PostgreSQL, artifact-preserving scopes, and explicit schema-maintenance admission keep their existing paths. This is the existing native path used by synchronous lifecycle guards, rather than a new transport or cache.

The trigger chain is:

1. `src/cli/program/preaction.ts:174` → `src/cli/command-execution-startup.ts:60` → `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts:140` runs startup preflight before the RPC action.
2. `src/commands/startup-config-preflight.ts:113-118` → `src/commands/startup-plugin-source-captures.ts:36-58` attempts capture cleanup under the existing Doctor maintenance lock.
3. `src/commands/doctor-sqlite-maintenance-lock.ts:168` → `src/infra/gateway-lock.ts:561` reports live-owner contention through `captureStalledGatewayStartup`.
4. `src/infra/gateway-startup-owner.ts:30-53` checks the five-minute startup budget, then reads the current owner lease to distinguish a listening Gateway from a stalled startup.
5. `src/infra/gateway-owner-lease.ts:211-225` previously supplied no native-read permission. `src/state/openclaw-state-db-readonly.ts:669-680` consequently called `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationSync`; `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-source.ts:381-400` → `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts:539` spawned the full-database `sync` copy.

The actual command action only uses Gateway RPC (`extensions/team-reports/src/cli.ts:12-16,43-65`). Auth-profile reads and plugin metadata inspection were not the remaining copy trigger.

`git log -S startupPhase` and `git log -S listeningAt` both identify f84a3aafa3b7 (#171678): readiness deliberately lives in the existing owner lease. `startupPhase: "starting"` distinguishes modern holders from legacy leases; the payload schema only accepts that literal (`src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts:192`). `markListening` updates the lease, not that marker (`src/infra/gateway-lock.ts:663-671`, `src/infra/gateway-owner-lease.ts:350-370`). The marker cannot prove listening, and changing its producer would duplicate the existing readiness owner.

Snapshot history explains the retained boundary: 31d703061650 (#141451) added artifact-preserving reads because even read-only SQLite opens can create WAL sidecars; 73ace5dcefe0 (#148834) keeps schema maintenance on fresh private readers. Those reasons still apply to Doctor and artifact inspection, so those paths remain. A short live lease lookup needs current committed readiness, not preserved source artifacts or a long-lived WAL reader. The existing native exception comes from 6c1e1667bd61 (#163496).

Capture cleanup still attempts its existing lock. A separate early live-owner skip would repeat ownership policy and would not fix other current lease readers; lock contention now performs the bounded read.

Owners this process cannot verify keep the old snapshot read. `hasVerifiedLiveSqliteOwner` throws `GatewayLockNamespaceError` when the lock payload's process namespace is missing, null or from another host, for example a payload from an older Gateway during an upgrade, or a CLI in another container that shares the state directory. The lease reader treats that as "not verified" instead of failing, so restart, stop, update and recovery callers behave as before for those owners (`src/infra/gateway-owner-lease.ts`, `hasVerifiedLiveStateOwner`). `src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts` covers the missing, null and foreign namespace cases: without the fallback all three throw `GatewayLockNamespaceError`; with it they pass. The test-line allocation rises from 89 to 94 for those five lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: three successful RPC-only commands against each isolated dev Gateway, with capture presence and a real lock older than five minutes, must create zero snapshot staging directories and spawn zero read-only `sync` children on head. Only synthetic state and loopback ports were used; no live installation or real data was accessed.

The new subprocess regression seeds real SQLite state, publishes a real process owner and listening lease, and supplies a lock timestamp older than five minutes. A different process calls the real `captureStalledGatewayStartup` seam and counts snapshot allocations and child spawns.

```
pnpm test src/daemon/gateway-startup-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'without copying shared state'
Base 3012cdd6fa46 (origin/main at task start): exit 1
  expected: { stalled: false, syncSpawns: 0, snapshotDirectories: 0 }
  received: { stalled: false, syncSpawns: 1, snapshotDirectories: 1 }
Head: full owning suite exit 0, 4 passed
```

The current origin/main lease-reader method was also checked and still matches the failing base method.

Real end-to-end command, three times per build:

```
pnpm openclaw team-reports list --period day --json
```

| Build | Successful commands | `sync` children | Staging directories created |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base 3012cdd6fa46, Gateway age >5 minutes | 3/3 | 3 | 6 |
| Head 4351c8551311, Gateway age >5 minutes | 3/3 | 0 | 0 |

Each command exited 0 and returned `{"periods":[]}`. The final head Gateway was ready at 17:11:41 and its three RPC connections occurred at 17:17:05, 17:17:08, and 17:17:11 (local proof timestamps). After committing, the isolated Gateway was rebuilt/restarted before aging it again for the exact-head measurement.

Counts include nested snapshot staging; they measure creation even when cleanup later removes the directory. A preload observes `child_process` and staging allocation, and the Gateway logs confirm the real CLI RPC connections. Before the five-minute threshold, the base also produced zero copies, explaining the initial missed reproduction.

Focused verification: 161 tests passed, with one Windows-only process test skipped on macOS. This includes owner lease (45), startup recovery (4), capture cleanup (11), Doctor maintenance lock (23), CLI Gateway diagnostics process tests (2), existing interruption/reclamation tests (3), Gateway lock (24), and restart/stop/process/handoff/update consumers (49). Also passed production core typecheck, services test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, format, `git diff --check`, and the staged test-line ratchet (6,385,097 lines).

`pr-simplify` retained one owner change: production +13/-1 lines, one 89-line subprocess regression, four documentation lines, and a one-line allocation record. The regression needs a separate reader process because an in-process cached database handle bypasses the defect. Its exact 89-line allocation avoids deleting unrelated proof or raising the shared baseline.

Codex autoreview: local candidate clean through P2; committed branch review uses `--engine codex --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2` with frozen source context. Final status: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings on `4351c85513114916c412bb5d5cc03dc76c86eb50`.

### Snapshot leak findings

Normal preparation failures already discard partial payloads (`src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location-cleanup.ts:485-517`), and the synchronous source owner removes its staging directory on a thrown preparation error (`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-source.ts:381-400`). A `.partial` name marks preparation before publication (`src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts:319`, `sqlite-readonly-location-cleanup.ts:519-545`); hard interruption can prevent those cleanup paths. Existing SIGKILL/SIGTERM subprocess tests reproduce abandoned data and successfully reclaim it.

The normal one-shot exit gap is already owned by #178730: `src/cli/runtime-cleanup.ts:156-172` lacks its proposed async snapshot finalizer, while the synchronous exit hook cannot retire retained async owners (`src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location-cleanup.ts:210-225,300-306`). Leave that fix to its PR.

Dead-owner reclamation already runs through idle Gateway maintenance every 15 minutes (`src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts:666-682`) with a 15-minute grace and 512 MiB budget, allowing one oversized directory per pass (`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-staging.ts:36-37,83-111`). Frequent multi-GB interrupted copies can outpace that owner. Filenames and absent open handles alone cannot establish which exit path caused each production leftover or whether reclamation was deferred/refused. No independent cleanup defect was proven, so this PR removes the repeated copy trigger and adds no speculative cleanup policy.

## What Problem This Solves

The live CLI completion probe rejects supported native steering when the child result joins the active parent answer.

## User Impact

Test-only repair: live qualification can verify completion delivery and cache reuse against the current session-controller contract. Runtime behavior and configuration are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The probe compared server-side announcement settlement with a later client observation and required separate transcript rows, although native steering permits a combined answer. It now checks the held-parent barrier, exact child delivery receipt, and both actual results in canonical history. The child generates an opaque result so the parent must consume its completion.

When both results share a row, cache measurement uses the RPC result's final-call usage, bound to that child result. Canonical transcript counters deliberately aggregate the whole turn, including its cold start. The 90% completion and follow-up thresholds remain unchanged.

This updates the existing helper with four net test lines and a matching allocation; no new test case, runtime owner, or warmup call. Contract context: [unified session controller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175837), [completion cache-prefix fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172026).

## What Problem This Solves

In Usage "Started by", a long identity stays on one line. At 390px it runs over the Tokens, Cost and Sessions values and past the card edge. At 1280px a 66-character identity runs 81px past its column, into Tokens. The CSS meant to let identities wrap targets `td:first-child`, but the identity cell is a `th`. On phones, large costs also overflow the fixed-width column.

## User Impact

Long identities wrap inside their column at every width, and every number stays whole and readable. Selecting a row works as before. On phones, rows are separated by space instead of hairlines.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selector fix applies at all widths. At 1280px the column widths and short rows don't change; only rows with long identities grow, from 59px to 76px.

This table keeps its columns instead of using the stacked layout: it ranks people by comparing short numbers down each column, and those numbers fit at 390px. Stacking would add four lines per row and lose that comparison. Under `max-width: 640px`, the table sizes columns to their numbers and the identity takes the rest. Rows stay aligned without hairlines because values center on their row and each identity has its own bar. Desktop keeps its hairlines.

On phones narrower than about 380px, four columns leave a long identity about 38px of text, so it wrapped mid-word over 17 lines at 320px. There the identity takes its own line above the numbers, which stay in aligned columns, with no horizontal scrolling.

The images show today's top bar until the header PR lands.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(ui): agree with the server on loopback names
prs.body:
Fixes #190741

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the Control UI at a name under `.localhost` (for example `http://openclaw.localhost:18789`, which browsers resolve to this machine) made the Portals page report **Remote portal ingress required** for a portal on `127.0.0.1`. The UI's `isLoopbackHostname` accepted only `localhost`, `::1`, `[::1]` and `127.0.0.0/8`, so the gateway origin looked remote and the loopback portal looked unreachable from this browser even though it opens from the portal card.

- Problem: the UI loopback predicate disagreed with the server's definition of this machine.
- Solution: accept `localhost.localdomain` and every name under `.localhost`.
- Changed: `ui/src/lib/gateway-locality.ts`, plus four cases in the existing `isLoopbackHostname` table.
- Not changed: IPv4/IPv6 handling, the portal probe flow, and the server-side check.

## Why This Change Was Made

RFC 6761 §6.3 reserves `localhost` and every name under it for loopback, and the runtime already encodes that: `isExplicitLoopbackHostname` in `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts` counts `hostname.endsWith(".localhost")` and `localhost.localdomain`. The UI predicate was the only surface that disagreed, so the fix makes it agree with the owner that already answers this question instead of inventing a second rule. Both extra forms are covered here because leaving `localhost.localdomain` behind would preserve the same class of mismatch.

## User Impact

A Control UI served at `openclaw.localhost` now takes the local path, so a `127.0.0.1` portal opens instead of showing a false "ingress required". Remote Gateway and non-loopback origins behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

The existing `isLoopbackHostname` table was extended, and the predicate was reverted to confirm the new cases fail without the fix:

```text
# predicate reverted
→ FAIL: classifies openclaw.localhost as loopback: true
→ FAIL: classifies OpenClaw.LocalHost as loopback: true

# with the fix
→ 8 passed (7 loopback cases plus the unchanged negative controls)
```

Negative controls stay in the table, so a suffix match cannot swallow `localhost.example.com` or `notlocalhost`.

Not tested: a real browser session against a live Gateway at a `.localhost` origin. The bug is in the predicate that gates the portal probe, and that predicate is now covered directly; the probe flow itself is unchanged.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used code tracing from the reported probe decision to the predicate it calls, then compared it with the server-side check that already handles the same question. The implementer understands the code: one surface decides whether an origin is this machine, and the UI was the one that disagreed with it.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): show placed dashboard conversations immediately
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm dashboard reload can have a complete, measured, end-anchored transcript that remains invisible for another frame sequence. The campaign's original evidence recorded 14 visible loading states; this change targets the dashboard's ready-to-visible hold. Follow-up to closed #190430 on the same lane branch; that PR could not be reopened.

The transcript reveal owner is ready on time. A second gate exists in the ancestor desktop side surface: [`startup-layout.css` on the base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2ece68aa497ef3396ffea7f414b87d4e94e7c998/ui/src/styles/chat/startup-layout.css#L1458-L1481) starts side content and its header at opacity zero. Dashboard places the conversation there; ordinary chat places its transcript in the main surface. The transition is 280 ms (`--chat-details-motion`, lines 1260/1268), introduced with the resizable panel frame in #176356 (`fb0ad93d0143`). It is an entrance animation, with no plugin-selection or reading-position protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the four-line `@starting-style` block at its CSS owner. Initially mounted desktop side surfaces show their already placed content immediately. Geometry, opacity, and display transition declarations remain.

The measured-range and reading-edge reveal in [`chat-transcript-layout-solid.tsx:205`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f0356ca3ddf957b11c4f5c476b22ed116002a98a/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-layout-solid.tsx#L205-L208) and [`chat-transcript-virtualizer-host.ts:742`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f0356ca3ddf957b11c4f5c476b22ed116002a98a/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-virtualizer-host.ts#L742-L778) stays unchanged. Estimated rows remain hidden until measurement and placement complete. No new persisted facts, server storage, protocol, or runtime configuration changes.

The native fixture retains a saved narrow dashboard pane, the complete tall cached reply, collapsed activity at its top, and twelve trailing hidden custom messages. It also includes bundled Workboard and synthetic theme/board modules with lazy chunks on both plugin asset routes. The rig waits for each peer's actual viewer-declaration acknowledgment before pausing it; the existing three-viewer preparation check remains.

## User Impact

Reloading a saved dashboard layout shows the placed conversation immediately instead of replaying a side-surface entrance fade. Other newly mounted desktop side surfaces also skip that entrance fade.

The dashboard root cleared `visibility:hidden` at 536.5 ms; its first visible DOM sample arrived at 785.8 ms. Its assistant row remained 6410.5 px tall, scroll height 14261 px, and distance from the end 0. The 300 px client width excludes the scrollbar from the 320 px outer pane. Chat made two measurement calls and dashboard three; all returned unchanged. The initial 8–9 dashboard ResizeObserver callbacks already reported final sizes. The transient layout-ready change accompanies hello on both routes and does not re-hide the completed range.

Timed comparisons use unprofiled production UI bundles with the same browser probes in both arms, on one quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, repository Playwright Chromium 156.0.8078.4, 3,000-session native Gateway fixture, 80 ms CDP network shaping, and 11 interleaved AB/BA pairs per route plus A/A. prs.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): resolve room access groups under an outer group allowlist
prs.body:
Fixes #188204

## What Problem This Solves

A Nextcloud Talk room configured with `allowFrom: ["accessGroup:staff"]` inside an outer `groupAllowFrom: ["accessGroup:staff"]` never reached the agent: the nested room check only resolved literal ids and wildcards, so members admitted by the same shared access group were denied.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAccess()` (`extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/inbound.ts`) called `resolveNextcloudTalkAllowlistMatch()` for the room list whenever the outer `groupAllowFrom` was non-empty. That resolver understands literal ids and `*` only (`policy.ts:36`), not `accessGroup:` entries. Rooms are now resolved through the same shared membership resolver as the outer list (`expandAllowFromWithAccessGroups`) before the nested check, so a room entry `accessGroup:staff` expands to the group's members for this account and sender. Outer-only and room-only senders, guests, and revoked memberships keep the existing rejection behaviour.

## User Impact

Access groups work at both allowlist levels; a room can no longer silently deny every member the outer list just admitted.

## Evidence

Head `09bd55bcf0`, Node 26.12.1. The production change in `extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/inbound.ts` is committed on this head (an earlier revision carried the tests without it).

**Signed webhook, allow path** — real HTTP + signature, real spool, real handler:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/inbound.access-group.webhook.test.ts \
    --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks
✓ delivers a signed webhook from a room access group under an outer allowlist
1 passed

# same test with inbound.ts at the pre-fix revision (337fb5d508^):
× delivers a signed webhook from a room access group under an outer allowlist
  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times
```

The case is `describe.skipIf(!isMainThread)` because `createChannelIngressQueueForTests` requires host-broker shared-state admission (main thread only) and the spool needs a real adoption window (`adoptionStallTimeoutMs: 60_000`); run it with `--pool=forks`.

**Allow/deny matrix** — `inbound.authz.test.ts`, real handler + shared membership resolver:

| case | outer `groupAllowFrom` | room `allowFrom` | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| sender in both groups | alice | alice | **dispatch reached** |
| sender in the outer list only | alice | bob | rejected |
| sender in the room list only | bob | alice | rejected |
| guest in neither list | bob | carol | rejected |
| membership revoked after preparation | alice → removed | alice → removed | next message rejected (dispatch count stays 1) |

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/inbound.authz.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
14 passed
```

`oxlint` / `oxfmt` clean on the three touched files; PR CI has no failing checks.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Located the room-vs-outer resolver mismatch in `resolveAccess`, routed the room list through the existing access-group expansion owner, and added both the decision matrix and the signed-webhook proof. The implementer understands the code: the nested room check must resolve the same identities the outer check admitted, and only that expansion makes both levels agree.

Related: #168793. Reported by @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

An interrupted Wiki compile can leave an abandoned compiled snapshot in plugin storage after a later compile successfully publishes a replacement.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

## Evidence

Current head: `44065b390853254cb429b6df66340f4667208870`, normally merging author head `e5588dcc0fbff2c51e1c2fcd5315c800447b181c` with official main `bafe92f6d5c3fc4fc9b9cf5d16813f658ddc4730`. Retain the existing capture of prior candidates and cleanup after causal publication validation. The original orphan regression and Unicode/lone-surrogate payload assertions are unchanged. prs.title: feat(openai): opt in to Flex processing with longer timeouts and capacity retries
prs.body:
Closes #188213

## What Problem This Solves

Long agent runs on direct OpenAI cannot use the cheaper Flex tier: normal Flex queueing trips the two-minute watchdog and the short retry budget.

## User Impact

Users of direct OpenAI Responses endpoints can set `params.flexProcessing: true` on a model. At `high` reasoning or above, OpenClaw then sends `service_tier: "flex"` (unless a tier is already authored), waits up to 10 minutes for the first event and between events, and retries temporary capacity, overload, server and timeout failures with minute-scale backoff (up to 4 retries within 30 minutes). Without the param, nothing changes. Shorter operator timeouts, cron's 60-second cloud cap, saved `retry.provider.*` limits, `Retry-After`, cancellation, quota/auth exclusions and shared TPM fallback still win. Proxies, other providers and native Codex turns are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Flex is about half the price of Standard, but OpenAI documents multi-minute queueing and temporary 429 "resource unavailable" errors. A small `flex-processing` module resolves eligibility from the final request params (after provider, agent and per-request overrides), and the existing watchdog and retry controllers apply the longer budgets only when the effective request is Flex. The speed resolver no longer manufactures a Standard override when Flex is opted in, which would otherwise have replaced the automatic tier with `service_tier: default`. Retries continue the persisted transcript through the existing recovery owners, so settled tool effects are not replayed.

## Evidence

- [Focused fork QA](https://github.com/BlaisedEstais/openclaw/actions/runs/41028520223) on `2f4599af9`: 400 tests in 14 files, targeted typecheck, lint, format and the `qaRuntime` build pass.
- Regressions: the watchdog resolves to 120,000 ms on the base and 600,000 ms with Flex; the SDK payload test sends `default` on the prior speed resolver and `flex` on this branch, including explicit session speed overrides.
- Persisted-session test: tool effect, capacity error, timeout, recovery, then cold reopen gives one user request, one tool result and one effect.
- Live `openclaw agent exec` on the built commit: an injected HTTP 429, a 38.9 s backoff, then a real OpenAI response with `service_tier: flex` and high reasoning (HTTP 200, completed). The capacity error was injected, not a natural Flex incident.
- No dependency, lockfile or database-schema changes. Official upstream CI has not run yet.

prs.title: fix(cron): pause the setup watchdog during session persistence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An isolated cron run can be recorded as failed even though only the session-row write was slow. Setup waits for `persistSessionEntry()`, but the 60 s setup watchdog keeps counting that storage time and aborts before the runner starts; the write then completes and setup finishes after the deadline, leaving a failed occurrence for work that never ran.

This change reports the pre-run write as a new `session-persistence` wait. The setup watchdog pauses while that write is in flight and restarts with a fresh setup budget when it completes. The pause is bounded by the existing `CRON_AGENT_SETUP_WATCHDOG_MS`; a write that stalls for the whole budget still times out, so a hung cron slot cannot stay paused indefinitely.

Controller-admission waits are deliberately untouched. The existing `session-preparation` signal keeps its original behavior (pause the setup watchdog for the session turn, with lane-wait attribution), and a separate stage now distinguishes actual persistence from admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

`withCronSessionPreparation` already emits `stage: "session-preparation"` while waiting for the session turn, and that contract must keep pausing setup indefinitely while the session is busy. Reusing that stage for storage would cap admission waits at 60 s, so this revision adds a distinct `session-persistence` stage:

- The isolated runner wraps `persistSessionEntry()` with `waiting: true/false` and `stage: "session-persistence"`.
- The shared-session replay path wraps `prepareSessionEventTargetForHost()` the same way.
- `applyCronWatchdogWaitSignal()` routes `session-persistence` to `notePersistenceWait()` / `notePersistenceResumed()` and leaves every other signal on the existing lane-admission path.
- The persistence timer uses the same 60 s budget. Resuming clears it and starts a fresh setup budget; firing marks the existing setup timeout.

Cancellation is unchanged: the abort signal still governs the run, and the fix never revives a run after a timeout.

Scope note: this addresses the reported storage-accounting path. It does not add a configurable timeout or a general post-deadline revival path; a write that exceeds the bounded budget still fails with the existing setup-timeout message.

## User Impact

Scheduled automation no longer reports a false setup failure when a slow volume makes the session-row write outlast the deadline but preparation completes normally. Operators keep a bounded failure mode for genuinely hung storage. Controller admission, lane waits, cancellation, and command jobs keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Running Gateway proof from this PR head: a dev Gateway with a real isolated `agentTurn` cron job, real session/agent SQLite, and a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint returning `PROOF_OK`. Storage latency was injected at `pwrite64` with a local `LD_PRELOAD` shim (5 s on the state DB, then the agent-DB session write) to emulate the reported slow volume.

| Scenario | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Total setup 61.7 s, `session-entry.patch` 57.3 s | `status: ok`, `summary: PROOF_OK` |
| Total setup 60.2 s, `session-entry.patch` 65.3 s | failed: `cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`; no execution |

Why this is the reported case: with a 5 s pre-write stall, the 57.3 s session write is still in flight when the former 60 s setup deadline expires. The fix pauses the setup timer for that write and restarts it, so the occurrence executes; a write that exceeds the bounded allowance still fails.

Raw observed lines:

```text
success: status=ok completionStatus=succeeded durationMs=61716 summary=PROOF_OK
success: session-entry.patch elapsedMs=57303 queueWaitMs=0 writerExecutionMs=57302
bounded: status=error completionStatus=failed durationMs=60240
bounded: error="cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start"
bounded: session-entry.patch elapsedMs=65305 queueWaitMs=0 writerExecutionMs=65305
```

Watchdog/router real-timer matrix (60 s budget): admission wait 65 s -> `fired: 0`; persistence write 37 s -> `fired: 0`; persistence write 65 s -> `fired: 1`.

Regression tests (pre-fix failure confirmed by reverting production files, then re-applied): 21 passed across `src/cron/service/command-timeout.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lane.test.ts`, including the busy-admission and bounded-persistence routing cases. `timer-job-runner.interruption.test.ts` (6) and `agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts` (17) also pass; `tsc`, `oxlint`, and `oxfmt` are clean for the changed files.

What was not tested: operator cancellation during persistence through a Gateway cancel RPC (none is exposed). That path is unchanged and covered by `timer-job-runner.interruption.test.ts`; the model endpoint was a local mock, while persistence, the watchdog, cron admission, and settlement were real.

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import {createHash} from 'node:crypto';
import {execFileSync, spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';

export function fixture(name, checkoutArg, phase) {
  assert.ok(['red', 'green'].includes(phase));
  const checkout = path.resolve(checkoutArg);
  const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), `alix-${name}-`));
  for (const leaf of ['home', 'state', 'workspace', 'tmp']) fs.mkdirSync(path.join(root, leaf));
  const hash = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
  // Read-only containers receive a host Git attestation before the bind mount.
  const head = process.env.PROOF_CHECKED_HEAD ?? execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], {cwd: checkout, encoding: 'utf8'}).trim();

Fixes installed plugin metadata and discovery diagnostics emitting terminal control sequences during `plugins list` and `plugins inspect`.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect installed plugins without manifest strings changing terminal state. Normal plugin labels, versions, and trusted status colors remain readable. Report JSON retains its raw metadata values; there are no new settings, permissions, protocols, schemas, or migration steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: improve(ui): show running state with the accent across pages
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves "A run is in progress" looks different from page to page. Activity paints the same fact green in its header and terracotta on the avatar. Automations uses the theme's secondary accent. Dashboards and the Sessions details panel use green, which Sessions also uses for Done. Current Work and Live activity use the warning color. The sidebar, session rings and spinners already use the accent. ## User Impact A running session or automation now reads the same on Activity, Automations, Dashboards and Sessions: the theme accent, keeping each surface's label or spinner. Green stays for healthy, enabled or finished states, amber for waiting or queued, and red for failures. Labels, sizes and layout elsewhere do not change. In forced-colors mode, the status dots on these surfaces are now painted instead of disappearing. The Activity run dot also gets an accessible name, using the existing "Live" string. ## Why This Change Was Made Every surface was judged against what its state means, and only instances of "a run is in progress" changed. Chat panel running states are in a separate PR. Running uses one token, `--status-running`, which is the theme's accent. Three themes can't use it: Beacon's accent is the same amber as waiting, CRT's is neutral white and matches plain text, and Dash light's is close to its waiting rust. Those use the theme's blue. Every other theme follows its own accent. Every changed surface keeps a non-color signal: a label or a spinner, and on the Activity avatar, a pulse and a position separate from presence. ## Evidence Mock data at 1440px and 390px, in Absolutely dark and light, CRT and Beacon. Automations' running rows come from `runningAtMs` set in the mock's cron data, since the mock has no running job by default. **Automations, Absolutely dark** **Live activity, Absolutely light** **Dashboards, Absolutely light** **Sessions details, Absolutely light** **Automations, CRT** **Activity, Beacon** **Activity, 390px** **Dashboards, After in Safari** Checks: oxfmt and stylelint on touched files, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and `ui:check-performance:base` (no failure reported). prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(setup): Hermes import fails on Windows with EBUSY after the AI access test
prs.body:
Closes #156264

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Windows, onboarding's "Import from Hermes" passes the AI access test and then aborts with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink` on a file of the staged `openclaw-agent.sqlite` (the reporter saw the main file, one of my runs saw `openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm`), leaving no `openclaw.json` and the staged `.openclaw-migration-state-<id>` directory behind.

## User Impact

Onboarding imports on Windows that verify an imported model now promote the staged agent and commit the config, the same result `openclaw migrate apply hermes` already gives. On macOS and Linux a rename is not blocked by an open file, so I expect no change there; that is inferred from rename semantics, I did not run it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The AI access test runs against the staged agent directory and loads auth profiles through the pooled read-only reader in `src/agents/auth-profiles/sqlite-read-pool.ts`, which keeps its handle for a 30 minute idle window. Before promotion, `disposeDatabases` in `src/wizard/setup.migration-stage.ts` clears the staged auth snapshot and disposes the staged agent and state databases, but nothing closes that pooled reader, so the staged `openclaw-agent.sqlite` is still open. Windows refuses to rename a directory with an open file, so `fs.rename` of the staged agent directory fails with `EPERM` (setup.migration-stage.ts:453 on this branch), promotion throws, and the `finally` cleanup then fails with `EBUSY` on the same database, which is the only error the user sees. `disposeDatabases` now calls `closeAuthProfileReadPool({ kind: "database", ... })` for the staged agent database first, the same close-by-path the shared auth store migration does before closing its agent database, so both `promote` and `cleanup` run with no handle left on the staged tree. The agent-database cache and resource registries held no staged entries at rename time (`resources.active=0 resources.closing=0 cached handles=none` below), so the async drainage of the agent database is not what holds the file.

## Evidence

**Live run on Windows 11:** `runNonInteractiveSetup` with `--import-from hermes --import-secrets`, the code behind `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --import-from hermes`, against a fake Hermes home whose `config.yaml` points a custom `chat_completions` provider at a local OpenAI-compatible stub, no mocks inside OpenClaw. The harness wraps `node:sqlite` and `fs.rename`/`fs.rm` and prints which handles are still open on staged files at each step. The issue asks for the primary exception and the outstanding handle on a Windows reproduction; this is that, trimmed (both runs got "AI access works" after 1 stub request):

```
main (c07f1eb4a62):
fs.rename <root>\home\.openclaw-migration-state-WHSSU9\agents\main\agent: staged agent db owners: resources.active=0 resources.closing=0 cached handles=none
  node:sqlite handles still open on staged files: 1; live workers: 1
    OPEN openclaw-agent.sqlite opened at at openNodeSqliteDatabase (src/infra\node-sqlite.ts:151:9) <- at acquireAuthProfileReadDatabase (src/agents\auth-profiles\sqlite-read-pool.ts:130:10) <- at inspectAgentAuthProfileJsonCellReadOnly (src/agents\auth-profiles\sqlite-json.ts:133:20) <- at inspectAuthProfileJsonCellReadOnly (src/agents\auth-profiles\sqlite.ts:217:10) <- at readPersistedAuthProfileStoreRaw (src/agents\auth-profiles\sqlite.ts:288:18) <- at loadPersistedAuthProfileStore (src/agents\auth-profiles\persisted.ts:847:5)
fs.rename FAILED: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '<root>\home\.openclaw-migration-state-WHSSU9\agents\main\agent' -> '<root>\home\.openclaw\agents\main\agent'
THREW EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink '<root>\home\.openclaw-migration-state-WHSSU9\agents\main\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm'
openclaw.json exists: false
staged dirs left in home: .openclaw-migration-state-WHSSU9

this branch:
fs.rename <root>\home\.openclaw-migration-state-Wa6AoJ\agents\main\agent: staged agent db owners: resources.active=0 resources.closing=0 cached handles=none
  node:sqlite handles still open on staged files: 0; live workers: 1
runtime.log: Updated config: ~\.openclaw\openclaw.json
runtime.log: Migration complete. Run `openclaw doctor` next.
openclaw.json exists: true
config primary: "stubprov/stub-model"
staged dirs left in home: none
```

- `setup.migration-stage.test.ts` adds a case that opens the pooled reader on the staged agent database, promotes, and checks the reader is closed and the agent was promoted. With main's `setup.migration-stage.ts` it fails at the same `EPERM` rename (1 failed); with this change it passes. On Linux I expect it to fail at the `isOpen` check instead of the rename (not run).
- `pnpm test src/wizard/setup.migration-stage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 passed, 1 skipped, 4 failed. The same 4 fail on unmodified main on this machine (16 passed, 4 failed): two file-mode checks (expected `0o600` and `0o755`, Windows reports `0o666`) and two that need symlink rights.
- Test cost on a laptop: that command took 32 s wall (Vitest 29.3 s, 74% transform); the new test took 321 ms in the file run and 452 ms alone. No timers, sleeps, or gateway boots. In CI (Ubuntu, Node 24.21.0), after the 09-28 merge from main, the file passed in full: 15 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-33, 1532 ms of test time, the new one in 234 ms.
- oxfmt, oxlint via `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `tsgo` on `tsconfig.core.json` and on the commands core-test config, `git diff --check`, the assertion, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, `check-import-cycles` and the madge cycle check pass. The change does not touch a Windows CI scope path (`ci-changed-scope` reports `run_windows=false`).

Not covered: the interactive wizard itself was not driven; it reaches the same `runSetupMigrationImport` stage and required verification. The reporter's DeepSeek route was replaced by a local stub. Stage cleanup can still replace an earlier exception when some other promotion step fails; that is separate from this leak. `models list --probe` disposes its isolated agent database and removes the directory in the same order, but I have not checked whether it reads through the pooled reader.

prs.title: fix(ui): recover the shell surface from a stale module download without a click
prs.body:
Fixes #188186

## What Problem This Solves

When the Control UI development shell's module download fails, `ShellLoadError` only entered the shared recovery path from the user's Reload click. The document could be reachable and the reload guards satisfied, but nothing probed for recovery, so the "This view could not load" surface stayed until someone clicked. Ordinary route errors already schedule that recovery automatically.

- Problem: recoverable shell-download failures were handled as manual-only.
- Solution: a recognized stale shell-download error schedules the existing guarded recovery from the error surface itself.
- Changed: `ui/src/app/app-shell-loader.tsx` wires `scheduleStaleChunkReload` the way `router-outlet.tsx` already does, and `ui/src/app/boot-composer.ts` registers a reload guard while unsent boot text exists.
- Not changed: the manual Reload path, stale-error recognition, and every guard owned by the shared recovery (reachability probe, once-per-build bound).

## Why This Change Was Made

`router-outlet.tsx` already renders an automatic `scheduleStaleChunkReload()` for recognized route errors, and the shell loader had the same primitive available but connected only to Retry. Reusing that owner keeps loop bounds in one place.

That reuse also exposes one hazard: the boot composer from #188153 keeps early text only in its own textarea, so a document reload before the route adopts it would discard what the operator typed. The guard therefore lives at the text's lifecycle owner — `boot-composer.ts` blocks reloads while it holds non-empty text and releases the block when a pane takes the draft. A failed recovery still lands on the error surface with manual Reload available.

## User Impact

A source-backed Control UI preview that hits a transient shell module download failure now recovers without a click. If the operator has already typed into the boot composer, the automatic reload is held instead of discarding that text. When recovery cannot proceed (unreachable, guard tripped), behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Bidirectional, each run real. Production behavior reverted with the tests kept:

```text
# app-shell-loader: behavior reverted (recovery call removed, export kept)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/app-shell-loader.test.tsx
→ FAIL: "starts the guarded shell recovery without a manual retry"
→ PASS: "leaves an unrelated shell failure on the manual surface"

# boot-composer: guard registration removed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/boot-composer.test.ts
→ FAIL: expected true to be false (reload stayed allowed while text existed)

# both restored
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/boot-composer.test.ts ui/src/app/app-shell-loader.test.tsx
→ 2 files passed, 8 tests passed
```

Also rebased onto current `main` (95fa337a11e) so the boot-composer surface from #188153 is present, and the tree now passes the checks that failed on the earlier revision: `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types-core-*`, `mock-exports` (the app-host factory is gone), and the `control-ui-performance` startup budget.

Not proven: a live browser session against a real development server that aborts one shell request. That end-to-end run is the remaining gap; the tests above drive the same components and the same shared recovery function.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used code tracing to compare the shell error surface with the route-error surface, then applied the existing `scheduleStaleChunkReload` pattern and the existing `registerControlUiReloadGuard` contract. The implementer understands the code: the shared recovery owns reachability and loop bounds, the boot composer owns its unsent text, and neither surface should reload past the other's guard.

prs.title: refactor(ui): reuse shared UTF-16 hash
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI maintains a byte-identical copy of the existing shared UTF-16 FNV-1a hash.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Existing identity hues, seeded artwork, translation keys, credential fingerprints and transcript revisions retain their hash values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move all 19 UI imports to the existing dependency-free shared owner and delete the duplicate UI module. Retarget the transcript test's namespace spy to the same module used by production. Keep the distinct avatar palette hash, salts, normalization, cache versions and assertions unchanged.

The duplicate UI owner came from [PR 113649](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113649); the identical shared owner and seven fixed UTF-16 vectors came from [PR 181044](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181044). This maintainer-requested cleanup adds no API, SDK surface, runtime state, dependency or baseline. An existing locale-publication regression now also covers the shared hash input.

## Evidence

- Both hash modules are byte-identical; the shared owner is unchanged and imports no runtime dependencies. Source/history and all hash consumers were audited.
- Author simplification leaves direct imports, one implementation and no forwarding facade. Qualified formatting, whitespace and privacy checks passed.
- Fresh independent implemented-diff review: clean. All 19 changed non-import bodies and assertions are byte-identical; the production import and namespace spy share one module.
- Native isolated proof: seven existing fixed UTF-16 vectors passed (200ms Vitest). Eight existing UI consumer files passed with one worker: 155 unit cases / 8.76s Vitest and 25 browser cases / 1.76s Vitest, 14.84s total wall. This includes the transcript hashing work-count assertion. These inputs are unchanged by the generated-manifest commit.
- Canonical boot-manifest generation passed (50.45s wall), capturing ready New Session and Chat routes. A controlled regeneration on exact base source with the same install passed (49.45s); its two additional existing module entries match the candidate. Candidate versus regenerated base differs only by replacing the UI hash key with the shared hash key. Generated bytes were committed unchanged.
- Type-aware lint passed for all 19 migrated UI files (135.32s), with one existing string-style warning on an unchanged line in chat-subagent-activity.tsx. Owning UI and UI-chat test type checks passed (15.55s and 16.37s).
- Grouped production UI build passed on the committed manifest head (25.92s wall / 19.01s build). The later workflow/test correction changes none of its source, manifest or dependency inputs.
- Complete high-reasoning range review found one missing cutover: locale refresh still tracked the deleted hash path. Both push and stale-publication input lists now track the shared owner; fresh independent correction review is clean. The existing publisher boundary test also checks hash-input push admission and stale Control UI output rejection while native publication proceeds.
- The shared-hash regression failed on the old workflow as expected. Full locale-refresh, finalizer and CI workflow-guard validation passed in two shards (466.97s wall). The initial zero-selection attempts were discarded; Vitest truncated the former parameterized title, and the existing literal-title boundary case was extended instead.
- Correction lint and owning tooling-test type check passed (29.81s and 18.93s); canonical workflow checks passed (14.26s).
- Exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate. No visual, performance or live Gateway change is claimed.

## CI failure investigation

[Exact-head CI 41345590133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41345590133) completed with 40 successful jobs, 26 skipped, and two failed jobs: browser shard 2/7 and its aggregate gate. The [browser job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41345590133/job/124965041953) recorded 508 passing cases and one failure: `session-management.sidebar.e2e.test.ts:237`, opening the “Actions for Verify tests” menu, reported `locator.waitFor: Target crashed`. Check annotations identify the failed variant as nests spawned sessions (personal pin: false). The completed-job log confirms ui-e2e-bundled, actual shard 2/6 with four workers; the displayed job label is 2/7.

Initial native CI classification reports this as new: the matching main job passed, selected scopes were not compared, and the classifier could not obtain the job log through its route. A later completed-job API read recovered the full log and confirmed the failure above. A focused run of both `nests spawned sessions` variants at the unchanged PR head passed (2 cases, 9 unselected; 24.21s wall / 20.34s Vitest). This replay does not prove a repair or establish baseline attribution. The hash migration reaches avatar rendering used by the sidebar, so unchanged test files alone do not establish independence. No crash cause or safe repair is established; no retries, weakened assertions, baseline changes, or CI reruns were added.

prs.title: improve(ui): keep native selects in the shared select family
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves `SettingsSelect` spread its props after its own class, so any caller passing `class` silently dropped `settings-select`. Rows per page, Group by, the Usage time zone and the Usage creator filter all lost the shared select. Rows per page fell all the way to the browser's grey control with square corners. A few other selects drew their own box with a native arrow, including one hard-coded 5px corner that ignored square themes. ## User Impact These selects now look and open like every other select: same surface, corner, type size and chevron, and the same styled popup where the browser supports it. Square themes keep their corners. No option, behavior or copy changes. ## Why This Change Was Made The component now merges a caller's class, which fixes four selects at the source. The others join the same class. Local chrome that competed with it is gone. | Select | Page | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | Rows per page | Sessions | 21px, 0 radius, grey, native arrow | 30px, field tokens | | Group by | Sessions filters | 30px, 6px, native arrow | 30px, field tokens | | Group cell | Sessions, grouped | 33px, 6px, 13px type, native arrow | 32px, field tokens, fixed column width | | Time zone, creator | Usage | Gradient chevron, native popup | Shared chevron and popup | | Author, Sort | Dashboards | Gradient chevron, native popup | Shared chevron and popup | | Machine picker | Systems, phone | 37px, fixed 5px, native arrow | 32px like the icon buttons beside it, field tokens | | Desktop size | Systems | 6px, native arrow | Size kept, field tokens | Dense spots keep their size on purpose, set through the existing height token: the pager and filter popover stay 30px to match the controls beside them, and the desktop toolbar stays 32px, or 44px in its touch layout. In the Systems phone toolbars, the selects use the same border as the icon buttons beside them. A long value stays inside the select: the shared rule shows one line that truncates with an ellipsis, breaking anywhere in the word, and keeps the chevron in place. The ellipsis comes from a one-line clamp because the engine's value text ignores `text-overflow`. The shared popup stops growing with long names. It caps at 320px and stays inside a 16px viewport gutter. Long options truncate to one line beside the check, and rows keep one height. Popups with short options keep their width. The full name stays in the option's text for assistive tech and in `title` on the group cell, the Systems picker and `SettingsSelect` options with text labels. Safari's default margin and padding on `::picker-icon` pushed the chevron 3px up and slightly inward. The shared rule zeroes them, so the chevron centers with the value. Chromium's frames are byte-identical. The filter popover's row fields and toggles move from 6px to the field radius so they match the select beside them. No radius shrinks. The 16px phone type floor is unchanged. It prevents iOS focus zoom, is documented in `settings-design.md` and is covered by `form-controls.browser.test.ts`, so native selects stay 16px on touch devices. ## Evidence Mock data, real clicks. Sessions grouped, Absolutely light, Before and After: Sessions filters, Absolutely dark, Before and After: Systems at 390px on a touch profile, CRT, Before and After. The 5px corner becomes the theme's square one: Group cell popup opened with a real click, Absolutely dark, with a 46-character and a 94-character group name set in the mock's data: Real Safari 27.0.1, After, CRT, same names, same popup opened with a real OS click: Checks on the change: oxfmt, stylelint, `tsgo:ui`, `ui:check-performance:base`, and unit, browser and e2e tests for Sessions, Usage, Systems, the desktop panel and form controls. `view.invalidation.browser.test.tsx` has one undo test that fails with and without this change on the machine these ran on. `desktop-document-mode.e2e.test.ts` timed out once on a pop-out click and passed on rerun. Mobile PRs that move these controls on phone may overlap; this standardizes what is on main.

prs.body:
Closes #185317
Supersedes #185332, thanks @kaguranananana

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions_spawn` rejects a model override without explaining the configured model policy or how to recover.

## User Impact

Refusals identify the rejected model, the effective default or per-agent policy key, and where to add the model or its provider wildcard. Admission rules and rejection timing are unchanged; no credentials or config values are added to the error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the effective-policy resolver at the existing model-admission refusal. Preserve the lower-level rejection string because other callers parse it. This is a credited reimplementation on main; contributor code was read with `gh` and was never checked out or run.

Production delta: +7 lines. There is no safe dead-code offset in this message-only repair; no formatter or policy layer is introduced. The narrower helper assertion is replaced by two tool-boundary regressions (test delta +38 lines, with a matching allocation).

## Evidence

- On main `7cce68feca197b3f3d2e98528031f7cfe9fd38f9`, both new regressions fail with `sessions_spawn model "fixture/new-model" is not usable: model not allowed: fixture/new-model` and no policy guidance. The same production file remained unchanged on main at publication.
- After the fix: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts src/agents/model-selection-resolve.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 36 tests. Default/hidden and overriding per-agent/visible requests return policy-specific guidance before any gateway call. The shared resolver tests retain the lower-level error contract and policy precedence.
- Local wall time: regression red run 79.17s including cold compilation; green two-file run 82.73s including cold compilation. The changed test file takes 9.07s including setup/imports (3.4s test execution). PR CI passed in 506s wall time: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41369561476).
- Touched-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI to protect the production host; no full local typecheck or suite was run.
- Independent autoreview: Codex, P0–P3, local candidate against `7cce68feca197b3f3d2e98528031f7cfe9fd38f9`, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Later changes are formatting and the matching test-line allocation count only.

prs.title: feat(agents): let the system agent read usage cost
prs.body:
Related #181148

## What Problem This Solves

The system agent's `openclaw` tool exposed read actions (status, health, overview, models, agents, channels, plugins, config, audit) but had no action to report usage/cost, so "how much have I spent?" could not be answered from its own tool surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical usage/cost infrastructure already exists (`loadCostUsageSummary`, the `usage.cost` RPC). This adds a `usage` action following the same read-only precedent as the merged `health` (#171971) and `overview` (#177273): register the action and operation kind, parse it, and execute it through the existing operation executor with no side effects. It scopes to the host-bound inference owner (`requesterAgentId`) and formats the existing `CostUsageSummary` totals.

## User Impact

Users can ask the system agent about usage and cost ("show my usage cost", "cost usage", or "usage") and get the last 30 days of token and cost totals for the active agent. No state changes. The action appears in the tool's `Read now:` description and action enum, so the model discovers it as a free read alongside `health` and `overview`.

Because the rollup folds catalog estimates into totals for turns without a recorded provider charge, a bare dollar figure would read as billing. The cost line is now labeled a **session-derived estimate**; recorded totals and the existing incomplete/unpriced warnings are retained.

## Evidence

- `usage` operation kind added to `SystemAgentOperation` (`src/system-agent/operation-types.ts`) and the parse grammar (`src/system-agent/operations-parse.ts`), accepting `cost` / `cost usage` / `usage cost` aliases.
- `usage` executor case in `src/system-agent/operations-execute.ts` calls `loadUsageForOperation(agentId)` (from `operations-execution-helpers.ts`), which lazily imports and delegates to the real `loadCostUsageSummary({ agentId })`.
  - **Session-derived estimate label**: the measured total renders as `Cost: $X.XXXX (session-derived estimate; catalog prices used where no recorded charge)`, with the per-bucket split on the following line.
  - **Preserves the incomplete-data warning** and the **unpriced** distinction: when `totalCost === 0 && missingCostEntries > 0` it renders `Cost: unavailable (cost data missing for N entries)` instead of a misleading `$0.0000`.
- `usage` registered in `SYSTEM_AGENT_TOOL_ACTIONS`, `SIMPLE_ACTIONS`, the `Read now:` description, and the parse no-match message (`src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.ts`).
- Tests updated in existing files (no new test files): action enum/advertisement/routing in `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts`; executor formatting, `requesterAgentId` scoping, estimate label, unpriced case and missing-cost note in `src/system-agent/operations.test.ts`. Both suites pass (22 + 22).

### Shipped conversation proof

An isolated dev Gateway was started from this worktree on the current head (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway --dev`, `server.commit = 94436a5`, isolated state/config). A real WebSocket operator client connected (`hello-ok`, protocol 4). A real agent run for the host-default agent (`agent` RPC, `agentId: "dev"`) completed on a **real OpenAI-compatible model** with no scripted completions; its session recorded usage for `dev`. The shipped `openclaw.chat` turn then had the model call the `openclaw` tool with `{"action":"usage"}`. Agent selection comes from the host config (`dev` is the only agent), never from model arguments.

Verbatim tool return, printed by the model on request (`Cost` and totals from the real recorded run):

```
Usage (last 30 days, agent dev):
  Tokens: 13,962 (input 13,947, output 15, cache read 0, cache write 0)
  Cost: $0.0280 (session-derived estimate; catalog prices used where no recorded charge)
    input $0.0279 · output $0.0001 · cache read $0.0000 · cache write $0.0000
```

Seeded-total scenarios through the same shipped executor (real `refreshCostUsageCacheForAgent`, real `loadCostUsageSummary`, redacted fixtures):

```
Usage (last 30 days, agent main):
  Tokens: 1,750,000 (input 1,000,000, output 500,000, cache read 200,000, cache write 50,000)
  Cost: $2.1000 (session-derived estimate; catalog prices used where no recorded charge)
    input $1.0000 · output $1.0000 · cache read $0.1000 · cache write $0.0000

Usage (last 30 days, agent main):
  Tokens: 300,000 (input 200,000, output 100,000, cache read 0, cache write 0)
  Cost: unavailable (cost data missing for 2 entries)
  2 entries had no cost data; totals are a lower bound.
```

- Scope: current agent (host-bound, default 30-day window). The delegated non-default-agent path (`delegation.agentId`) is gated by active agent-run authority; per-agent `days`/`all-agents` scoping and the CLI renderer stay follow-ups on #181148.
- Environment note: `tsgo` cannot run on this host (`@tsrs` needs glibc ≥ 2.29; host is 2.28). Types are covered by `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and both vitest suites; CI `check-prod-types` / `check-test-types` / `check-lint` pass on this head.

prs.title: fix: honor explicit npm commands on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows command execution silently running the host’s bundled npm instead of the npm/npx executable or wrapper explicitly selected by a caller.

## User Impact

Plugin command-runner callers can use an explicit npm/npx path or native executable without losing the selected installation, version, or wrapper behavior. Missing explicit paths fail normally rather than falling back to another npm installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the bundled-CLI shortcut for generic npm/npx aliases, but send explicit paths and native executables through the existing Windows executable resolver and trusted batch wrapper. Existing unsupported-command and unsafe batch-argument checks remain intact. No dependency, configuration, or public API changes.

## Evidence

- Native Windows / Node 24.22.1: the real command-runner API previously substituted host npm for runnable task-local `npm.exe`, `npx.exe`, and an explicitly selected npm batch wrapper. After the fix, four direct-process/runner comparisons have matching output and normal exit code 0, with unchanged timeouts.
- Exact-base regression: **4 failed / 23 passed**; fixed owner suite: **27/27 passed**, including native batch argv checks, four existing real PTY cases, and unsafe-argument rejection. Affected Windows execution suite: **18/18 passed**.
- Targeted production and test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent source review and canonical exact-source P0–P3 review completed with no introduced findings. Canonical helper status: `scoped-clean`, exit 0, complete validated report; full caller and native execution evidence supplied.
- Cost: changed test file’s Vitest duration **99.76s**, predominantly transformation (93%); approximately 6s executing tests, mostly the existing PTY cases. Repository wrapper wall time **109.23s**. prs.title: fix(macos): exec host returns empty output for invalid UTF-8
prs.body:
Closes #187601

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app exec host returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` when a command's output contains any invalid or incomplete UTF-8 sequence, while still reporting `success: true`. A command killed at its timeout right after printing half of a multibyte character (spinners, box drawing, emoji) comes back with `timedOut: true` and no output at all.

## User Impact

Agents running `host=node` commands on a Mac now get the valid part of the output, with `U+FFFD` in place of the bad bytes, instead of an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ShellExecutor`'s file-backed capture decoded each whole buffer with `String(bytes:encoding:) ?? ""`. That decode fails for the entire buffer when any one byte sequence is invalid. It now uses `String(decoding:as: UTF8.self)`, which `runStreamingDetailed` in the same file already uses through swift-subprocess. Process, timeout, and capture behavior are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and other readers</summary>

- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ShellExecutor.swift:45-46` is the only failable decode of captured command output. The pattern has been there since the file-backed capture in #104827, which kept the earlier pipe-based decode.
- `PortGuardian.swift:461` decodes `ShellExecutor.run`'s payload, which is now always valid UTF-8, so its fallback can no longer trigger.
- `GatewayProcessManager.swift:1403` reads the Gateway log file. That's a different owner, outside this bug.
- The issue's related note about signal-terminated children being reported as `exit N` is a separate behavior change and is not part of this PR.
</details>

## Evidence

I packaged main (`c32556b0cea`) and this branch as ad-hoc macOS apps. Each ran under a named profile in remote mode against an isolated Gateway (private state and config, loopback port) started from that app's bundled runtime. Each case is a Gateway `node.invoke` `system.run` call to the paired app, the node command that `exec host=node` forwards and that runs `ShellExecutor.runDetailed`.

Main:
```
## control-ascii: /bin/sh -c "printf 'plain-ascii'; printf 'err-ascii' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"plain-ascii","stderr":"err-ascii"}
## invalid-byte: /bin/sh -c "printf 'abc\377'; printf 'abc\377' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
## split-multibyte: /bin/sh -c "printf 'abc\342\234'; printf 'abc\342\234' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
## timeout-split: /bin/sh -c "printf 'building \342\234'; sleep 5" (timeoutMs=1000)
{"success":false,"exitCode":null,"timedOut":true,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
```

This branch:
```
## control-ascii
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"plain-ascii","stderr":"err-ascii"}
## invalid-byte
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"abc�","stderr":"abc�"}
## split-multibyte
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"abc�","stderr":"abc�"}
## timeout-split
{"success":false,"exitCode":null,"timedOut":true,"stdout":"building �","stderr":""}
```

Tests: two new `LowCoverageHelperTests` cases (both streams for `\377` and a truncated `\342\234`, plus the timeout case) fail on main with empty output and pass here. `LowCoverageHelperTests` and `ShellExecutorTimeoutTests`: 26 passed. Run locally with `swift test --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --filter 'LowCoverageHelperTests|ShellExecutorTimeoutTests'`. The timeout test's budget went from 0.5 s to 1 s after the app capture; production code is unchanged since.

Not run locally: `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (pinned tools not installed); CI covers them.

Production delta +2/-2; test delta +22/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous decode with no state or config migration. Blast radius is output captured by `ShellExecutor.runDetailed` on macOS.

prs.title: fix #169718: memory search sync warnings hide the underlying cause
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw memory search` prints `memory sync failed (search): <wrapper>` warnings built with `String(err)`, which discards `Error.cause`; the real exception (e.g. an `ERR_INVALID_STATE`/`database is not open` use-after-close underneath a wrapper) never reaches the operator, so diagnosis dead-ends at a generic wrapper message (issue #169718).
- Solution: format both background-sync warnings with a policy-free formatter that keeps the nested cause chain and error codes. The plugin-sdk's `formatErrorMessage` redacts internally, but the repo log policy is "write raw; redact only at egress", so `openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime` gains a `formatErrorMessageRaw` re-export of the shared policy-free formatter and the two log-bound warnings use it without any redaction wrapper.
- What changed: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.ts`, `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/error-runtime.ts`
- What did NOT change: warning cadence, log level, and sync behavior are unchanged — only the rendered text gains the nested cause chain; masking still happens at the egress sinks (verified: the console transport renders `password=<redacted>` while the raw record keeps the full text); the neighbouring `search-bootstrap-fallback` warning keeps its `tools`-mode redaction because that text is model-bound; the `watch`-path warnings and the retired short-term-lock wrapper are out of scope.
- Data-model compatibility: logging-only change; no schema, stored-data, or index-format changes.

Fixes #169718

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Background memory sync failures during `memory search` surface as a bare wrapper string; the nested cause that explains the failure is dropped, so operators cannot tell what actually failed.
- **Real environment tested:** feat/issue-169718 worktree on current main (cc4315e0def), Node v24.20.0: (1) the shipped CLI flow — isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + workspace, FTS-only config (`memory.search.provider: "none"`), real `memory index` + `memory search` via the built `openclaw.mjs` launcher; (2) a render probe feeding a real `node:sqlite` use-after-close error (`ERR_INVALID_STATE database is not open`, the exact error class from the issue) through the old and new warning construction.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Shipped CLI flow: index real notes, then search (background sync warning path is live)
  export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated>/state OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=<isolated>/workspace
  node openclaw.mjs memory index
  node openclaw.mjs memory search "release checklist" --min-score 0
  # Render probe: real node:sqlite use-after-close error through old vs new formatting
  node --import tsx render-probe.mts
  # Regression tests
  npx vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  Render probe with a real `node:sqlite` use-after-close error (the issue's `ERR_INVALID_STATE` class) wrapped the way the sync path wraps failures:
  ```text
  real cause: ERR_INVALID_STATE | database is not open
  before: memory sync failed (search): Error: memory index maintenance failed
  after:  memory sync failed (search): memory index maintenance failed | database is not open | ERR_INVALID_STATE
  ```
  The same wrapper on the before code drops the cause entirely (`String(err)` renders only `Error: <wrapper message>`); after the fix the nested message and code are appended.
  Shipped CLI runs (real index + real search; the background sync warning path fires when the sync owner loses write admission during teardown) — before code vs this head:
  ```text
  $ node openclaw.mjs memory search "release checklist" --min-score 0
  No matches.
  # before: [memory] sync failed (search): Error: Memory database owner closed or changed before write admission
  # after:  [memory] sync failed (search): Memory database owner closed or changed before write admission
  ```
  (For single-level errors without a `cause`, only the redundant `Error: ` prefix disappears; the fix's value is the nested cause chain when one exists, as shown above.)
  Regression tests: `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` — the two new cases fail on the before code (`AssertionError: expected ... to contain 'database is not open'`) and pass on this head; the full suite passes (19 tests).
- **Observed result after fix:** Warnings from the search sync path now include the nested cause message and code (`memory index maintenance failed | database is not open | ERR_INVALID_STATE`), so the underlying failure is visible instead of dead-ending at a wrapper message; search results, exit code, and sync behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** the issue's original 2026.9.9 short-term-lock wrapper no longer exists on main, so that exact `storage-error` line cannot be reproduced today; natural single-level failures (e.g. `database is locked`) render identically before and after. No live gateway or embedding provider was involved — the proof exercises the real search/sync code path in the memory-core extension, which is where the warnings are emitted.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: a background search sync that fails with a cause-carrying error renders the wrapper message plus the nested cause message and code in both the `search` and `search-bootstrap` warnings.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the defect is the choice of string conversion at two adjacent log sites; driving the real manager search path with a failing sync pins the rendered warning text end to end.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the two search-path sync warnings interpolate `String(err)`, and `String()` on an Error yields only `Name: message` — `cause` and nested codes are silently discarded.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test pinned the rendered warning text for a cause-carrying sync failure; neighbouring warnings had already migrated to `formatErrorMessage`, leaving these two sites behind.
