prs.title: fix: retain Codex context after first-turn startup failures
prs.body:
Related: #169431, #168347, #171707.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes earlier context disappearing when a fresh Codex thread fails before its first input is accepted and the user retries the request.

## User Impact

For context engines using `thread_bootstrap`, the retry receives the history that never reached native Codex. Successful follow-ups continue using the accepted native history without resending the bootstrap. This applies to fresh startup; previously persisted false receipts are not migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh thread creation saves the bootstrap projection before `turn/start` accepts its input. A later startup or dispatch failure can leave a matching epoch that incorrectly suppresses history on retry.

Keep the engine/policy binding at thread creation and record the projection after validated native turn acceptance, only when the complete bootstrap block survived final input fitting. Guard the receipt update by the exact thread/client owner. If the receipt write fails or loses ownership, preserve the already-accepted turn and its result. Existing resume markers, transient ownership and warm/cancellation cleanup remain unchanged.

This is a narrow acceptance-ordering fix. It adds no retry machinery or context-retention policy. It does not provide crash-atomic delivery: an interruption or storage failure after acceptance can still leave conservative replay uncertainty.

Related PR #171707 proposes `thread/inject_items` for authored-cap history, with an earlier seed acknowledgment. This candidate fixes main's rendered `turn/start` carrier. The changes have not been composed or tested together; if that carrier lands first, reconcile the receipt boundary with its acknowledged seeding path.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311`.

**Hosted CI:** [successful run 38632947933](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632947933), 52 successful jobs and 29 skipped. All four previously failing leaf lanes and the required gate passed. Observed again on October 14 at 21:23 UTC.

**New compatibility evidence:** a supported native-session route now completes the stable 10.3 → current candidate upgrade, preserves the same stored session/native thread, and completes two real local-model continuations with the original facts. The additional archive below contains actual seed/import, migration, native/provider/terminal captures and durable-history checks. This is a bounded native-session result; the earlier legacy-provider-route comparison remains blocked and is disclosed separately.

### Inspectable sanitized artifacts

1. [Original Gateway/native/provider comparison and reproduction archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33455012/codex-bootstrap-acceptance-ce5296cf-evidence.zip)

   File: `codex-bootstrap-acceptance-ce5296cf-evidence.zip`.
   SHA-256: `caaed5e4d49d2e1f9211cd28252304f4fca9b4f12096eeead44faef9ffe23ba6`.

2. [Earlier stable-state preservation, route-barrier comparison and CI follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33459171/codex-bootstrap-18654634-upgrade-followup.zip)

   SHA-256: `758480e533c1342d166e732baddf035491911e7fcc7a84f24a1791506ce2c989`.

3. [codex-bootstrap-18654634-native-upgrade-proof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33463900/codex-bootstrap-18654634-native-upgrade-proof.zip)

   SHA-256: `a21af0ab8f7fb655b2ec21e772e4c85123b40e0b0297893077443b9e508a716f`.

The original archive includes actual rejection/acceptance inputs, actual provider user input and output, Gateway terminal receipts, the complete comparison matrix, check logs, runnable helpers and an offline correlation verifier. The earlier supplement adds retained stable-state reopening captures, Doctor receipts, pristine-main comparison and CI repair evidence. The new supplement adds successful native-session upgrade continuations. Each has source/artifact hashes, a reproduction recipe, offline verifier and redaction disclosure. Raw operator configuration, credentials, private endpoint/model inventory and real user sessions are excluded.

### Fresh startup: main versus candidate

Built and exercised main `24567afc232dfbcd8da3f1eb4e1b1466925d1352` and original candidate `06daa04093a9eab782ac72893b7c45c95318cbcd` with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.9.0. The shipped Gateway used real native Codex 0.160.0 and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. Four isolated synthetic cases, three successful turns each: **12/12 inference requests completed with HTTP 200 and `response.completed`.**

| Case | Bootstrap blocks in actual provider user input: first success / continuation 1 / continuation 2 | Actual model response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main, ordinary control | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on all three turns |
| Candidate, ordinary control | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on all three turns |
| Main, first dispatch rejected before acceptance | 0 / 0 / 0 | `MISSING` on retry and both continuations |
| Candidate, same preaccept rejection | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on retry and both continuations |

The fault cases reject exactly one first `turn/start` with JSON-RPC `-32602` before forwarding it to native; those two rejected dispatches make zero provider calls. This is controlled fault injection. Other native messages and provider payloads pass through byte-for-byte, with no response substitution or provider adapter.

The rejected request contains 634 characters including the synthetic history. Main's retry sends only the new 234-character request; the candidate retry sends 877 characters including the history and failed request. The accepted turn ID matches the Gateway terminal receipt. Both later turns retain the same native thread/client and send only their new 245-character request. At the provider boundary, successful history appears once in user messages; assistant echoes are excluded. Nonces are generated independently for each case.

The external fixture uses public context-engine registration, current-turn fencing and a real atomic idempotent SQLite worker commit. No legacy fallback occurs in the qualified matrix; every case commits three accepted turns. The engine supplies controlled history, while native binding/projection, Gateway dispatch and inference are real. It is not a benchmark of an external production context engine.

### Existing native-session upgrade: completed on the current head

Fresh isolated case `upgrade-i-native` ran the built stable `v2026.10.3` and exact current candidate with native Codex 0.160.0 and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. **Exit 0, 48.370 seconds, four HTTP 200 / `response.completed` results:** one native CLI seed, one stable Gateway follow-up, then two candidate Gateway continuations.

The real native CLI created a synthetic conversation. Stable adopted it using the public `sessions.catalog.list` / `sessions.catalog.continue` flow, saved settings, and performed an ordinary `agent` RPC. After all owned processes stopped, candidate Doctor migrated that same state with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and external service ownership. Candidate reopened the existing session and performed two ordinary `agent` RPCs. This uses native-owned model/provider configuration without a `models.providers` overlay, fabricated credential/model, direct database seed, admission bypass or payload translation.

| Check | Before upgrade | After upgrade and both continuations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent / global SQLite schema | 24 / 20 | 26 / 22; integrity checks pass |
| OpenClaw session ID and native thread | Saved by stable | Same IDs; genuine `thread/resume`, no replacement |
| Label, pin, verbosity, usage setting | Saved through public session API | Identical on reopening and after continuation |
| Historical messages | Four user/assistant messages | Exactly equal on reopening; content, IDs, sequence and other metadata retained after both continuations |
| Stored transcript events | 5 | 9; original five equal on all seven common stored fields |
| Original native rollout files | Two retained snapshots | Both preserved byte-for-byte as prefixes |
| Authored configuration | Retained bytes | Byte-identical; Doctor made zero model requests |
| Original goal, checksum and history fact | Present in native seed and stable reply | Present in actual provider history and both actual candidate replies |

Follow-up prompts do not repeat the original nonces. Imported user/assistant seed history is checked before the stable follow-up. Each of the three Gateway turns matches a genuine native acceptance, exact provider last-user input and Gateway terminal turn ID. Both candidate turns reuse the same candidate client and the native thread stored by stable. The binding is exact across Doctor; after continuation, runtime fields such as the client ID and covered-history watermark may advance. Whole final binding byte equality is not claimed.

Post-continuation display comparison excludes only `__openclaw.transcriptPosition.source`, a reader-generation coordinate; `rawSeq` and all other message fields remain exact. Separately, stopped SQLite snapshots prove byte equality of all seven original stored event fields. The source-generation change is not presented as ordinary append behavior; its exact runtime caller was not established. A prior attempt failed its overly broad display comparison and remains excluded. Only the fresh corrected case qualifies.

Inspect the new archive's `native-seed/`, `stable/`, `migration/`, `candidate/`, actual native/provider input-output files, `stored-transcript-preservation.json`, and `upgrade-summary.json`. The result was independently checked against raw synthetic SQLite/rollout snapshots and captured responses. No production Gateway participated.

**Scope:** both builds use default legacy mode with native context ownership. This establishes the tested existing native-session migration/continuation boundary. It does not establish custom-engine activation during upgrade or repair the legacy configured-provider route below. The original fresh-startup matrix independently proves the PR's custom-engine acceptance fix; the earlier supplement independently covers preservation of old custom projection/ledger data up to its route barrier.

### Earlier legacy-provider upgrade comparison: candidate versus pristine main

The latest stable release observed for this test was `v2026.10.3`, commit `59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1` (tag object `3a8c04b0832eabc4410ba7c7a30c9c27e4b5fc81`). Each case first created settings, a real user/assistant exchange and one committed fixture-ledger row through a stable Gateway. After stopping that Gateway, it retained the same synthetic state and native home, ran the supported Doctor migration, and reopened using the target build.

| Observation | Candidate `18654634e2a3` | Pristine main `24567afc232d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent / global schema | 24 to 26 / 20 to 22 | Same |
| Stable real provider completions | 1 | 1 |
| Exact old history reopened | Preserved | Preserved |
| Session ID, label, pin, verbosity and usage setting | Preserved | Preserved |
| Active native binding/projection, native history prefix and one-row accepted ledger | Preserved | Preserved |
| Post-upgrade native turn starts / provider calls | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Successful post-upgrade continuations | 0 | 0 |
| Full compatibility | NOT PROVEN | NOT PROVEN |

Both failed with:

```text
Requested agent harness "codex" does not support openai/lmstudio/<local-model> (Codex cannot reproduce the prepared provider route).
```

Doctor canonicalized the explicit local `codex` provider to `openai`. The canonical custom-endpoint route does not declare Codex compatibility, so admission stops before dispatch. The five inspected Doctor/routing owners are byte-identical between pristine main and this candidate; their hashes are included. The repeated main failure separates this barrier from the PR's acceptance-ordering change, without proving that every old stored binding works.

Doctor ran only in the new synthetic cases, with explicit operator approval and `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`. It exited zero, made no model request, and retained valid pre-migration snapshots/database backups. It also emitted an original-state JSON inspection warning; these were not warning-free runs. Configuration normalization was reviewed, not undone. No admission bypass, fabricated credential, configuration restoration or seeded database row was used.

The supplement's `candidate/` and `pristine-main/` directories contain the actual observations, not only integrity claims. Its verifier reports consistent exported evidence while retaining `fullCompatibility: NOT PROVEN`. The two stable setup completions are separate from the original 12-call matrix and must not be counted as upgraded continuations. All owned test processes stopped; the operator Gateway was untouched.

### Tests and CI follow-up

```text
Original baseline publication-failure regression: 1 control passed, 1 expected failure
Original candidate affected selection:             134/134 passed, 7 complete files
Original final formatted regression suite:          12/12 passed
Published-head provider-review shard:                8 failed / 25 passed
Same shard after two-line CI follow-up:              33/33 passed
Bootstrap regression follow-up:                      12/12 passed
Assertion ratchet, targeted lint/types/format:       passed
Stable and repaired-candidate QA builds:             passed
git diff --check:                                    passed
Hosted CI at current head:                           passed
```

The original 134-test selection covers the new bootstrap boundary plus neighboring active-engine, overflow, binding, warm cleanup and cancellation behavior. It took 143.892 seconds. Three test-only lint repairs and formatting followed it with unchanged runtime implementation; the final 12-test rerun took 50.322 seconds. Coverage includes post-start preparation and dispatch rejection, accepted provider failure/cancellation, indeterminate cancelled dispatch, replacement-owner preservation, receipt-write throw/conflict, fitted-away bootstrap and empty history. Existing expectations were not weakened.

Follow-up commit `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311` adds only the missing `promptState` slot to the provider-review fixture and the required rationale for a mutable bootstrap prompt type assertion. There is no runtime behavior change. The exact previously failing shard now passes; no assertion-ratchet baseline was expanded. Two inherited CI failures came from a wrapper inventory omission fixed upstream by `51afdbea12bb4bd733e5e3594828140194048195`. The successful CI merge includes that repair through its main parent; this branch does not copy it.

Independent Sol 6.1 High source reviews of the original patch and the scoped follow-up found no actionable P0-P2 findings. A separate evidence review checked artifact/source hashes, actual native/provider/Gateway correlations, retained raw synthetic database/prefix preservation and redaction. Source review alone is not counted as execution evidence. Local check receipts retain their actual precommit identities and source hashes rather than relabeling old runs as current-head runs.

### Reproduction and limits

Use each archive's `repro/README.md`: the original for the four-case fresh-startup matrix, the earlier supplement for the expected legacy-route failure, and the new supplement for successful existing native-session upgrade/continuation. Build pinned checkouts with `qaRuntime`; the live entry point is `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`, driven by ordinary `agent` RPCs through public `GatewayClient`. Runners create isolated state and require an explicitly selected already-loaded local model. The new archive's `repro/verify-upgrade-evidence.py` checks its complete file inventory, hashes and exported correlations without service access.

One original preliminary control used an incomplete fixture contract and fell back to legacy; it is excluded from the 12-call matrix. Upgrade setup attempts with missing session permissions, a response-field assumption and an unavailable stable SQLite SDK helper were retained and excluded; the supplement's attempt audit explains each. The earlier custom-engine preservation cases e/f use the common public transaction API and require a committed stable fixture-ledger row before migration. The new native-only case i has no synthetic engine ledger. No failed attempt was discarded or reclassified as success.

Original candidate patch SHA-256: `ce5296cf50997171390a897b9cfddc8311d4e9e3706f1dc46a1b203c35690812`. The immutable original archive remains tied to head `06daa04093a9eab782ac72893b7c45c95318cbcd`; the supplement records head `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311` separately.

The new setup audit also retains an invalid stable config attempt and the display-generation comparison failure; neither counts as a passing case. The corrected test does not ignore stored history changes: it checks all original raw event fields after shutdown. Test processes are stopped; retained fixtures are separate from the production Gateway.

The combined proof establishes local fresh-startup recovery under controlled preaccept failure and successful existing native-session upgrade with preserved history/settings/native thread. It does not establish every provider/engine upgrade combination, repair the separately reproduced legacy route barrier, migrate historical false bootstrap receipts, test remote OpenAI behavior, or prove production incidence, model-quality improvement, latency/cache/billing gains, live store-error/cancellation behavior or crash-atomic delivery. The new supplement has not yet been assessed by the upstream reviewer; acceptance of this bounded compatibility proof remains their decision.

prs.title: fix: preserve native child work during Codex context rotation
prs.body:
Related: #165808

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native child work losing its parent ownership when token pressure makes OpenClaw start a new Codex thread.

## User Impact

Token-pressure rotation preserves the existing child assignments, and a failed successor start leaves the original parent binding available. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The token-pressure helper currently clears the saved parent before the normal replacement owner can preserve its children. Carry the selected predecessor to that existing replacement path instead, validate it against the current thread/client identity under the lease, and commit through the existing compare-and-swap operation. Do not add a new postcommit unsubscribe step; existing child protection and idle retirement retain their responsibility for the physical subscription.

This is the pressure producer path. It reuses the normal preservation introduced by #160952 and does not import the restricted-continuation changes in #156651 or broaden the completion-delivery authorization proposed in #165809/#169320. Byte-limit clearing and ordinary claimed/protected rotation controls remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Pinned upstream base: `fa3e272e21361300a538c2ee1e21502ec5cd1e15`. Node 24.19.0, frozen dependencies, separate baseline/candidate installations and isolated state.

Published candidate: `c16048229a3a2c4c0350d530665ebf7fe80b35ba`. All 12 committed file hashes match the source used for the tests, builds, review and live comparison below. Publishing the commit did not change the tested source; these are the recorded local results, not a claim about later upstream revisions or hosted CI.

Built-Gateway comparison with real native Codex 0.160.0 and local `qwen3.8-27b-mtp-highest`, using synthetic input and fresh persistent state:

| Case | Actual initial tokens / native window | Pressure rotations | Child command and final | Gateway result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline, no pressure | 13,855 / 62,259 | 0 | Completed, exit 0 | Delivered once; observed at 3.059 s |
| Baseline, startup pressure | 13,738 / 31,129 | 1 | Completed, exit 0 | None during 90.927 s |
| Candidate, startup pressure | 14,176 / 31,129 | 2 | Completed, exit 0 | Delivered once; observed at 10.118 s |

All four helper hashes and the native binary hash match across these three runs. The reviewed source hashes match the built/executed candidate. All 20 provider calls returned HTTP 200; actual child and successor turns completed. The observed failure is lost delivery after rotation, not a model-unload or inference-timeout result.

The child executes real native shell work held on a FIFO. Only after the exact successor turn finishes does the controller release a unique nonce. The proof joins that nonce to the exact child's command item, exit zero and final marker. The successor must emit only its exact marker, with no tool items, so it cannot recover or terminate the child. Successful delivery is joined to its own Gateway-selected writer, native turn-start/completion, persisted final, Gateway lifecycle end and assistant history entry. The native client and physical requester session remain the same across rotation.

The candidate's small context triggers a **second** pressure rotation at announcement time; the result reaches the third/current writer. All distinct parent writers have zero native compactions. The successful cases show no duplicate in an additional five-second observation. The baseline's successful harness exit means the expected bounded non-delivery was observed, not that the product passed.

**Live-proof limits:** all three cases use the same disclosed test-only adapter to flatten/reverse five native delegation tool names for LM Studio, and a normal read/write client without admin scope. The adapter changes no model decisions, arguments, call IDs, results, usage or native RPC; it is not part of this production patch. This does not establish stock LM Studio namespace interoperability or repair the separate admin-client catalog/protected-parent failure found during setup. Child completion is released after successor restoration. One run per row is not a reliability or latency benchmark; the observation is not an unbounded exactly-once claim.

Source checks cover the additional pressure/failure paths:

- **Before:** the same entry-point regression has 3 failures and 1 pass. Startup pressure, projected-input pressure and failed successor start all lose the predecessor binding; the no-pressure control passes. Wall time: 43.242 s.
- **After:** 4/4 entry-point cases pass. Wall time: 58.598 s. The final affected suite passes **53 tests across five files**, including stale selection, changed connection, revoked authority, compare-and-swap conflict, claimed/protected predecessor controls, warm cleanup and subscription recovery. Wall time: 86.404 s. These counts overlap and are not additive.
- Baseline and candidate QA runtime builds pass. Targeted formatting, all three lint scopes, extension production/test types and script types pass.
- Independent Sol 6.1 High autoreview found no actionable P0-P2 issues in the exact diff and supplied unchanged ownership/retirement code. The reviewer did not run the tests.

The entry-point fixture uses real SQLite session/current-generation authority and production ownership logic, but its Codex binding store has an in-memory backing, native RPC is substituted, and completion reaches a substituted sink after restoration. The separate built-Gateway comparison above supplies real process/persistence/delivery evidence. Live coverage is startup pressure; projected-input pressure and failed successor start have source-regression evidence only.

The sanitized evidence bundle retains all 18 attempts, including unsuccessful ContextPilot controls, unadapted Qwen tool routing, corrected phase/live-process assertions, a separate admin-catalog failure and an initial native-home placement that did not activate pressure. These are setup findings, not additional defect reproductions. No model response, usage event or native RPC was fabricated to obtain a pass. The final comparison receipt is `main-live-final-comparison.json`; each final case includes its summary, provider receipts, native observations and source/helper/binary hashes. Reproduction helpers and their export transformations accompany the evidence.

Evidence archive: [main-evidence-export.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33453696/main-evidence-export.zip) (228 files plus manifest), SHA-256 `5809edb34892d4405a39cef7a745d249b94a2e68c45fd204fa8802a16486e8bb`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and proof boundaries</summary>

Identical entry-point regression in both source trees:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-rotation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Final affected candidate suite:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-rotation.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/startup-binding.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.warm-cleanup.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.subscription.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Build each pinned source through the repository owner:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
```

For the live comparison, place the four reproduction helpers and `main-overlay-manifest.json` together. Set `PROOF_ROOT` to the directory containing the independently built `main-baseline` and `main-candidate`, `PROOF_NODE` to Node 24, and `PROOF_LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` to the verified local `/v1` endpoint. Select the exact loaded model with `PROOF_MODEL` and set `PROOF_LOADED_CONTEXT` from its fresh model inventory; the observed loaded window here was 200,192. Run serially with fresh labels:

```sh
PROOF_NATIVE_CONTEXT=65536 python3 live-rotation-run.py baseline control1 --root "$PROOF_ROOT" --case control --translate-native-tools
PROOF_NATIVE_CONTEXT=32768 python3 live-rotation-run.py baseline proof1 --root "$PROOF_ROOT" --translate-native-tools
PROOF_NATIVE_CONTEXT=32768 python3 live-rotation-run.py candidate proof1 --root "$PROOF_ROOT" --translate-native-tools
```

The small declared native window is deliberate: its native-reported 31,129 tokens minus the existing 20,000-token reserve gives an active threshold of 11,129. Actual native usage exceeded that threshold without added padding or model-context overflow. Each fresh Codex home is inside its isolated agent root so the native writer and the pressure guard find the same store. These are synthetic proof settings, not production recommendations.

The final failed-start assertion checks retained inventory through the fixture store. It does not attempt to use a monitor whose directly injected native client was correctly retired after the startup error. The earlier invalid assertion and failed run are retained in the evidence ledger.

The live positive case releases the native child only after successor restoration. It does not establish the separate pre-restoration completion policy discussed in #169320 or deferred stale-owner transport rejection. All proof processes stopped, and their isolated files remain available. No production Gateway, session, credential or config was changed. Broad PR CI is not part of the local result.

</details>

prs.title: fix(plugins): install local file URLs on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin installation reporting “Plugin path not found” for local `file:///C:/...` and `file://localhost/C:/...` URLs on Windows.

Supersedes #185333, thanks @AmelioMansour.

## User Impact

Local plugin file URLs resolve to native paths, including spaces, Unicode, and escaped `#` and `%`. Literal `file:<path>` inputs retain their interpretation, remote URL hosts remain rejected, and malformed local URLs return an install error. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared source decoder manually sliced URL prefixes, leaving `/C:/...` and percent escapes. One native `fileURLToPath` branch now serves install planning and recovery metadata. The duplicate slicing branches are removed. Production grows by four lines to report conversion errors and validate malformed escapes consistently with Bun; unrelated code was retained. Simplification review found no additional machinery to remove.

## Evidence

- Verified the defect on main `3f678742aaf7118bc96edcde6dff749093327b8b`: the Windows regression received `/C:/plugins/demo%20%C3%BC%20%23%25.tgz` instead of `C:\plugins\demo ü #%.tgz`. Four decoder cases failed; both real CLI URL cases stopped before installer dispatch.
- After the repair, all **44 tests** passed in `src/plugins/install-source-spec.test.ts`, `src/cli/plugins-install-preflight.test.ts`, and `src/cli/plugin-install-config-policy.test.ts` (`pnpm test <these named files> --maxWorkers=1`, Node, 44.09 s wall time). The Windows test uses Node’s real `fileURLToPath` with `windows: true` through a test module adapter; production has no platform injection. The decoder file took 0.894 s; the two CLI files shared 40.06 s including cold compilation. CI durations: decoder 1.00 s, preflight 3.33 s, recovery policy 31.92 s (including cold compilation); all 44 tests pass under pinned Bun.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. PR CI supplies broad proof; no broad suites or full typecheck ran locally. An unrelated named E2E baseline replay unexpectedly expanded into build preparation and was stopped before test execution.
- Canonical local autoreview, P0–P3, compared the complete final local snapshot against the main commit above: **scoped-clean**, exit 0, no findings. This snapshot is committed as `baf01dcc59978247750a3e87e994034e1e33586f`.
- Added an exact 50-line test allocation for the missing Windows URL-decoding contract and CLI filesystem-to-installer handoff regression.

The contributor’s code was read through GitHub and was never checked out or executed. The replacement was independently implemented on main. CLI proof uses the real filesystem and decoder, then stops at the test installer failure; a successful archive installation and a Windows-host run are not claimed.

CI run [41368009158](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41368009158) completed with one unrelated test failure: the unchanged ClawHub search fixture returns HTTP 503, invoking the unchanged 44-second retry schedule inside a 30-second test. The fixture, HTTP client, retry owner, and scheduler have identical Git blobs in the recorded main baseline and tested merge. Search never calls the repaired file-URL decoder. CI remains failed; native inherited-failure admission was used to merge this change. A separate executable main replay was unavailable: the local setup was stopped before tests, and Testbox queued and was canceled. No timeout or assertion was weakened.

Merged as `9213d1759991fc32c7505c10ab66de76f052feed`; the inherited CI failure remains recorded.

Focused production typecheck is **not green**: it reports unrelated AbortSignal declaration-name diagnostics outside the changed files; replaying the original decoder produces identical diagnostic output. The normal wrapper also stops on an existing stale artifact-lock receipt; no lock was removed.

prs.title: improve(ui): keep the phone new-session draft still across Incognito
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves On a phone, turning Incognito on at `/new` inserted a four-line note above the composer. It pushed the project and workspace selectors up 75px at 390 wide and pushed the composer off screen at 320. The toggle also widened to fit its label, which moved the Draft button beside it. ## User Impact Turning Incognito on or off now moves nothing on a phone. The hint under the agent name changes to an Incognito line in the same slot, and the note opens from that line as a popover. Any tap dismisses it, and tapping the line brings it back. The note's text is unchanged and screen readers still get the status announcement. Desktop keeps the inline notice and the toggle label. ## Why This Change Was Made Three forms were tried on the real page: the full note in the hint slot, a popover from the toggle, and this line plus popover. The note in the hint slot collided with the selectors at 320. The popover from the toggle left no way to reread the note short of turning Incognito off and on again. This form shows the privacy limits at the moment they matter, then leaves a single line that keeps them one tap away. The rule applies to the docked layout, which covers widths up to 768px and short landscape phones. In short layouts the hint is normally hidden, so the Incognito line floats under the agent name without adding a row. ## Evidence Positions were measured with `getBoundingClientRect` before and after real taps: avatar, agent name, hint, both selectors, composer, composer buttons and both toggles. | Viewport | Absolutely light | Absolutely dark | CRT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 390 x 844 | 0px | 0px | 0px | | 320 x 568 | 0px | 0px | 0px | Each cell covers four states against the Incognito-off layout: note open, note dismissed, note reopened, and Incognito off again. Real Safari 27.0.1 at 390 x 848 also measured 0px in all four, in Absolutely light. On main, the same selectors moved 75px at 390. At desktop 1280 in all three themes, every measured position matches main with Incognito both off and on. `new-session-page.incognito-docked.e2e.test.ts` covers 390, 320 and 844 landscape, plus the unchanged desktop notice. The images use the mock data layer. They show today's top bar until #190409 lands, and that PR handles the Incognito icon. **Before: Incognito on, Absolutely light, 390** **After: Incognito off, Absolutely light, 390** **After: just turned on, nothing moved** **After: note dismissed** **After: Absolutely dark, 390** **After: CRT, 320, square corners kept** **After: note dismissed, Absolutely light, 320** **After: real Safari, Absolutely light, 390**

prs.title: improve(ui): open long filters as a shared phone sheet
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves On a phone, long filters open as narrow anchored popovers. Automations holds five selects plus Reset in a 280px popover that takes 57% of the screen and cuts off the list. Inside the Sessions filter, a native select, two compact inputs and two tinted toggles each use a different size. The mobile page PRs each decided this alone: two built separate sheets and one has a tall full-width popover. ## User Impact On phones, the Automations and Sessions filters open as a bottom sheet. It dismisses the same way everywhere: tap the dim, tap close, swipe the grabber or press Escape. Tapping the dim never reaches the page beneath. Every filter stays reachable, no copy is added, and desktop and tablet widths keep the popover. ## Why This Change Was Made The rule: **a phone filter is a sheet when it is a form, meaning three or more labelled text, date or select fields. Option rows, checkboxes, toggles and one or two fields stay a popover.** Height alone doesn't decide it: Dashboards reaches 50% with option rows, but each row applies with one tap and the popover scrolls its own author list. `PhoneSheet` in `components/solid/phone-sheet.tsx` is the one shared sheet. It sits beside `Popover` and takes the same trigger, ref and child props, so a surface swaps with one tag. It follows the structure from #190387, because a backdrop in the same top layer as the panel can't be beaten by page stacking. Children stay mounted while closed, because the Meetings form submits its closed fields. Every sheet has one header: a centered title with close on the right. Sessions' search sits directly left of close, in the same row, and doesn't move the title. While searching, the field takes the row and its own clear replaces close. The dim, grabber and Escape still dismiss. The sheet also sets one rhythm for its content: a 16px side inset, 12px between rows, a 13px label above a 40px field, a 16px value and a full-width action. The value size is iOS's input floor. Automations keeps Schedule and Last run side by side, and longer values such as "Recently updated" get the full width. Sessions pairs Updated within with Limit and Global with Unknown, and Group by is a normal labelled select. An unchecked toggle draws no check, and its slot stays so the label doesn't move, the same as #190367. Left alone: the sidebar's filter sheets and the Inbox sheet. They already work on phones, they share `sheet-dismiss`, and their desktop surfaces and nested pages are tied to them, so moving them changes nothing a person sees. The sidebar's sheets are settings lists of rows and switches rather than labelled forms, so the form rhythm doesn't apply to them. ### Conversions for open PRs Each one was tried locally on top of that PR's diff, including its sheet content refinement, at 390px. Meetings, Usage and Sessions all worked. - **Become a sheet:** #190374 Meetings and #190387 Usage swap their own surface for `PhoneSheet`. #190367 Sessions takes over this PR's Sessions conversion. Its select stays as it is in this PR and becomes a choice page in #190367, which also moves search to the page, so `headerAction` can go once it lands. - **Stay a popover:** #190376 Dashboards, #190380 Logs and #190393 Activity. Dashboards can drop its local outside-tap guard once #190505 lands. - **Nothing to change:** #190382 Automations already gets its sheet from this PR, and #190370 Page fixes has no filter surface. #190367 and #190387 overlap this PR on purpose, and resolve as described above. ## Evidence Mock data at 390x844 and 320x568, opened with a real tap, with default and long values. Page PRs are not applied, so these show today's top bar. | Automations before, light | After, light | | --- | --- | | | | | After, dark, long values | After, CRT (square theme) | | --- | --- | | | | | Sessions before, light | After, light | After, 320x568, dark, long values | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Real Safari at 390px, opened with an OS click | | --- | | | - Safari: an OS click opened the final Automations sheet. On the previous revision a real click on the dim over "Learn more" closed the sheet and stayed on the page. Swipe wasn't driven in Safari. - Chromium at 390px with touch input: dim, close, grabber swipe and Escape all closed both sheets and returned focus to the trigger. A short swipe springs back, and reopening after each exit starts in the right place. A filter applied in the sheet updates the trigger, and Reset clears it. - At 1440px both surfaces are still the anchored popover. - `oxfmt`, `stylelint`, `oxlint` and `tsgo:ui` pass. The `phone-sheet` and `view-jobs-filter` browser tests pass along with the Sessions and Automations unit tests and the cron and session-list e2e tests. - `ui:check-performance:base` fails only on the total CSS budget, which main already exceeds (no JS budget failure).

prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `b3ee56297f4075c471fd624aa085b252fd126ac6`. The GitHub web merge on 31 October combined prior head `a2c6197e80d459f03b88b8de3030e8ca67e6ddda` with main `f1c93577085244aa96aa87b53a2df9b59d293bd7`. All earlier proof below remains pinned to its actual revision; it is not current-head execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41214035584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41214035584) passed its selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n, and CI-gate jobs. Its preflight log records synthetic merge checkout `cc79321ee`, merging product `b3ee562` into main `f1c9357`. The [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41214232001) also reports success at `b3ee562`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. This is current PR composition evidence, not native runtime proof. Earlier [CI 40975271680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975271680) remains evidence for `a2c6197`, not this head.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Prior-head review:** [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) at `76ee71b` identifies no code findings; app-entry and upgrade evidence remains outstanding. Revision 14 above supersedes that historical review.

Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. ## Problem

RRI-56: nested fresh-checkout tests can inherit the release controller or outer process Git context. `createNestedGitEnv()` already removed several repository-routing variables, but retained counted `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n` entries and the caller global Git config. ## Solution

- Remove the remaining repository-routing variables used by linked/common Git contexts.
- Reset counted configuration and remove inherited indexed key/value entries.
- Isolate global and system Git configuration while retaining noninteractive Git behavior.
- Preserve the existing caller contract: callers can still overlay deliberate Git configuration after `createNestedGitEnv()`.

## Evidence

- Reproduced inherited counted/global configuration in the current helper.
- New direct regression passes.

- Tooling typecheck passed.
- Changed-file formatting and type-aware lint passed.

prs.title: improve(ui): remove tinted border and accent bar from request cards
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves The Approve card has a tinted border, a colored left bar, a tinted background and a tinted corner bracket. Requests should declare themselves through their content and their buttons. The bar also forced 4px left corners, and its 18px right corners ignored square themes. The standalone Ask page shares this card, and the Ask panel's secret-store details and the answered-question summary carry the same tinted left bar. ## User Impact - The Approve and Ask pages use a plain card, on desktop and phone. - A pending request states its severity in the existing status badge: critical is red, warning stays amber, info is neutral, and screen readers hear the severity word with the badge. On main, plugin severity showed only in the card tint, and the dot was always amber. - Terminal states no longer show an amber card behind a green or red status. - Host and Node read as plain label and value, like Expires, instead of a square box that left an empty grey cell on desktop. - Stacked boxes no longer touch: the two request detail boxes and two stacked warning notes now sit 8px apart, the card's gap between buttons. - The card is tighter on desktop and phone: less padding and space between its sections, and 44px buttons. The critical plugin card goes from about 569px to 492px tall at 1280px. - The warning note loses its tinted border and keeps a quiet fill. - Corners come from the theme: 20px on desktop and 14px on phone in Absolutely, 6px and 4px in CRT. Copy, states, button order and accent-filled primary buttons are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The card is the shared rule, so Approve and Ask change together. prs.title: fix(queue): stop exposing ignored timeout options
prs.body:
Closes #184737

## What Problem This Solves

Direct command-queue callers could pass execution-timeout options that the queue never consumes. The embedded-run controller owns execution deadlines after admission, while the command queue owns admission and scheduling.

## Change

The direct queue boundary now accepts `CommandQueueAdmissionOptions`, which excludes execution-timeout fields. Embedded-run callbacks retain the timeout-capable `CommandQueueEnqueueOptions` contract. This is a type-contract correction; deadline ownership and runtime behavior remain with the existing controller.

## Evidence

### Direct-call type regression

The same direct call was checked against the actual queue option declarations at base `main` (`60aaedd81245e7366998c4ea5c0956a503f7545b`) and PR head (`064d9132f9`):

```ts
enqueueCommandInLane("proof", async () => undefined, { taskTimeoutMs: 50 });
```

- Base: compiles successfully because the direct queue type includes `taskTimeoutMs`.
- PR head: rejected with `TS2353`: `taskTimeoutMs` does not exist in `CommandQueueAdmissionOptions`.
- The standalone strict `tsc` probe is the contract guard: it compiles on base and reports `TS2353` on the PR head for this exact literal.

### Gateway behavior

- Test: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts`, “delivers a child completion once while parent timeout recovery is active”.
- Command: `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`.
- Result: **1 test passed** on local PR revision `d72a21db`.
- The test launches the real local Gateway against a loopback mock provider and verifies timeout recovery, child terminal settlement through compaction/retry, and exactly one outbound child completion. It requires no external provider or service.
- Windows denied the QA fixture's regular-file symlink during initial startup. For the successful run, regular staged files were copied and directories used junctions; that local-only workaround was restored and is not part of this PR.

### Captured local product trace

On 2026-10-28 I reran the shipped local Gateway entry point with the loopback provider and captured its redacted stdout. The run shows the model execution deadline path, recovery, terminal child settlement, and exactly one outbound delivery:

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=mock-openai api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.6-luna elapsedMs=4000 name=LlmIdleTimeoutError message=LLM idle timeout (4s): no response from model
[openai-transport] [responses] error provider=mock-openai api=openai-responses model=gpt-5.6-luna name=LlmIdleTimeoutError abortReason=idle_timeout
[agent/embedded] [timeout-compaction] LLM timed out with high prompt token usage; attempting compaction before retry
[agents/agent-command] [agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
[agent/embedded] [timeout-compaction] compaction succeeded; retrying prompt
OPENCLAW_PROOF_TRACE {"product":"local Gateway","parentContinuationStartedAt":152554.8462,"childReleasedAt":156736.2847,"compactionStartedAt":156735.0364,"compactionReleasedAt":157069.7555,"childExecution":{"status":"terminal","outcome":{"status":"ok","elapsedMs":3671}},"childDelivery":{"status":"delivered","disposition":"retryable"},"outboundMatches":1}
```

The corresponding controller custody trace was captured from the real lane controller during the same local validation. It records cancellation at the deadline while the raw producer still owns the lane, followed by release only after raw settlement:

```text
OPENCLAW_DEADLINE_TRACE {"event":"execution deadline cancellation","firstAborted":true,"secondAborted":false,"lane":{"queuedCount":1,"activeCount":1},"rawProducerSettled":false}
OPENCLAW_DEADLINE_TRACE {"event":"raw producer settlement","firstAborted":true,"secondAborted":false,"lane":{"queuedCount":0,"activeCount":0},"rawProducerSettled":true}
```

The latest PR commits only narrow the queue type boundary, correct test-only type references, and remove duplicate test lines required by the repository ratchet; they do not change the runtime path represented by these traces. The temporary Windows staging workaround and trace print statements were reverted before the PR update.

### Focused queue/controller coverage

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/process/command-queue.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/lane-controller.test.ts`: **62/62 passed** on `d72a21db`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the focused Oxlint/format checks passed on the rebased PR worktree before the final stale-helper cleanup.
- The final cleanup removes an unused helper left by the rebase, and the follow-up type-only test fix keeps the injected queue helper on `CommandQueueTaskOptions`; the latest CI has confirmed the production types, test types, and completed core lint shards pass.
- Commits after the behavioral proof only remove stale code or correct test-only type names; they do not change queue runtime behavior.

prs.title: fix(queue): stop advertising ignored execution timeouts
prs.body:
Closes #184737
Supersedes #185284, thanks @SC-10749

## What Problem This Solves

Direct command-queue callers can currently configure execution timeouts that the queue silently ignores.

## User Impact

Internal TypeScript callers can no longer pass execution-timeout literals to queue admission. Runtime behavior, valid user configurations, and the existing exported enqueue callback contract remain compatible. Execution deadlines and raw-task capacity retention remain controller-owned.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queue-local timers were deliberately retired in #177986 after deadlines moved to the embedded-run controller. Separate admission options from the retained callback options instead of restoring another timeout owner. Current `QueueSchema` and queue docs never advertised these internal fields, so no config key is removed or migrated.

Remove the two unused queue-timer error variants and correct their stale capacity-release comment: production delta **-5 lines**. The single compile-time boundary regression adds 19 test lines, with a matching allocation to protect all six rejected timeout keys and callback compatibility.

## Evidence

- Main audited at `3f678742aaf7118bc96edcde6dff749093327b8b`: `enqueueCommandInLane` accepts the broad options type but never reads the six timeout fields. The controller still consumes deadline budgets and subscriptions.
- Red/green compiler proof: emit declarations from the actual queue source files with the repository compiler, then typecheck `command-queue.types.test.ts` against those declarations. Main fails at the direct-admission assertion with TS2554; the fix passes. Full source/test type graphs are left to PR CI.
- Six named test files passed (96 tests): `command-queue.types.test.ts`, `command-queue.test.ts`, `command-queue.cancellation.test.ts`, `lane-controller.test.ts`, `lane-controller.lifecycle.test.ts`, and `model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`. Process command wall time 40.88s; controller command 48.24s, including cold imports. The new test itself took 1ms (165ms shard wall time). CI timings are available in the linked successful run (changed-node shards 1 and 2 took 272s and 342s of job wall time, including setup).
- Touched-file Oxlint using `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, touched-file oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. An initial lint command began package-boundary preparation and was stopped; the source-backed lint route passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local snapshot against the main SHA above: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Subsequent changes only format the type assertion. Hosted ClawSweeper review of `19fcca776f98b229927837caef6b0f6015a26a06` also found no actionable findings and judged the fix complete. Required [exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41368011183), including the aggregate gate.
- Contributor source was read using `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and independently reimplemented; it was never checked out or executed. No live Gateway or deployment was changed. prs.title: fix(mxc): resolve literal sandbox file paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190077

## What Problem This Solves

The mxc sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath`; only the optional invocation base (`cwd`) keeps its blank-check via `trim()`, matching the shape accepted in #187554. The mount-containment guard is unchanged and still operates on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the mxc bridge owner).

## User Impact

Agents working in the mxc sandbox backend now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and outside-root rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `ed26a563f` (branch `fix/mxc-literal-file-path`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.18, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts:178`, through the public `readFile` with real filesystem files
- Decision surface: the `filePath` parameter of sandboxed agent file tools (`Type.String` schema, no pattern constraint; no upstream trim in the tool chain)
- Recorder/readback boundary: the file bytes returned by `readFile`, asserted byte-for-byte against distinct literal/decoy contents
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy's contents (`"decoy-data"` instead of `"literal-data"`); the two pre-existing test variants passed (1 failed / 2 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 3 tests pass, with both `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge over real files
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the pre-existing native-tool-paths matrix (workspaceOnly true/false) and its mutation denials are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: isolated temp workspaces only; no mxc runtime, Gateway, or production config touched (the bridge owner is host path math plus real fs access checks)

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3 (RED run on main: 1 failed / 2 passed at the new assertion)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files — clean
- Not tested: live mxc container end-to-end (the changed owner is pure host-side path resolution + fs, exercised with real files here); Windows container-path normalization

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/-1`
- Test LOC: `+29/-0` (existing test file only)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing mount-containment guard (`isPathInside`) and mount table; no new validator or export
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Two-way door: reverting restores trimmed-path resolution

## Maintainer edits

<details>
<summary>land-ready notes</summary>

- Maintainer edits are allowed on this branch (small, single-owner change).
- Alternative considered: normalizing only in the containment check — rejected: the resolved host path itself must stay literal or the fs target is wrong.
- Scope declaration: this PR changes the mirror/local mapping only; the mxc spawn launcher and readiness owners are untouched.

</details>


## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

Reviewer demand: terminal evidence of **shipped file tools selecting ` x.txt` rather than `x.txt`**, with the Windows-flow boundary disclosed (no shipped Windows MXC flow was captured).

**Entry point: compiled shipped module + real fs** — no vitest, no tsx, no mocks.

- Class: `MxcFsBridge` compiled from this PR's sources by the repo's own extension build (same tsdown build that emits `dist/extensions/mxc/index.js`).
- The mxc Linux registration path is intentionally dormant (`registerMxcPlugin` warns and returns early off-Windows before registering any backend), so the class was imported through a **scratch-only re-export entry** (`extensions/mxc/proof-entry.ts`, worktree-local, never committed) that the same build emitted as `dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js`. It was instantiated with the **exact shipped construction expression** from `mxc-backend.ts`: `new MxcFsBridge(sandbox)` — the same call the backend's `createFsBridge` performs for agent file tools. The compiled class is the shipped build output.
- The mxc read/write path under test is pure Node path-mapping over the mount table plus a real fs-safe root: no MXC binary and no Windows host is required for the code this PR changes.

**Boundary disclosure:** no Windows host is available for this run. The changed owner (`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget`) is OS-agnostic Node path-mapping; Windows-specific container-path normalization (drive-letter/case semantics) is out of scope for this change and untested. This run is the strongest Linux shipped evidence for the mxc bridge.

Exact commands (scratch worktree at `b17f25996` + this PR's disjoint `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts`; local-only, nothing pushed from it):

```
export PATH=/tmp/node24/node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH
cd <scratch-worktree>
pnpm openclaw --version            # full build; emits dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # head run -> GREEN below
# red pairing: restore base bridge, rebuild, rerun
git show c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711:extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts > extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # base run -> RED below
# restore head and rebuild
git checkout ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737 -- extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
```

Seeds: ` x.txt` = `PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content`, `x.txt` = `PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content` (0o644) under the rw agent-workspace mount.

Base `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711` (pre-fix `.trim()`) — exit 1:

```
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"          <-- trimmed to the decoy
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"                   <-- literal untouched
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE" <-- decoy received the write
FAIL  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
FAIL  relative write landed on literal file
FAIL  relative write left decoy untouched
OVERALL: RED
```

Head `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737` (this PR) — exit 0, full output:

```
read '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"
read '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"          <-- literal selected
read '/sandbox/plain.txt' (control) -> "PROOF_PLAIN_77AA00-roundtrip"
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE"   <-- literal updated
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"                       <-- decoy untouched
resolvePath '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/ x.txt     <-- literal identity kept
resolvePath '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/x.txt
PASS  read selects literal (absolute)
PASS  read selects decoy for unpadded sibling
PASS  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
PASS  relative write landed on literal file
PASS  relative write left decoy untouched
PASS  resolvePath keeps literal identity
PASS  resolvePath keeps decoy identity
PASS  control plain round-trip read
PASS  control plain round-trip write
OVERALL: GREEN
```

Controls: absolute-path read/write with only an interior space (`/sandbox/ x.txt`) is not affected by the trim bug and behaves identically on base and head; plain unpadded `plain.txt` round-trips on both. The defect scope is exactly a tool-supplied **relative** name with leading whitespace — the scenario the added regression test pins.

Cleanup: proof temp workspaces under `/tmp` removed; the scratch worktree (including the local-only `proof-entry.ts` re-export and its package.json build-config tweak) was never pushed; the PR branch itself is unchanged — head stays `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737`, no commit/push was needed.

Not tested: Windows container end-to-end (no MXC-capable Windows host available; see boundary disclosure above) and a live mxc runtime turn. The changed owner is host-side path resolution + real fs access, which this compiled-module run exercises directly.

prs.title: improve: speed up session-management E2E tests
prs.body:
Related: #190724

## What Problem This Solves

Desktop session-management E2E tests spend time waiting for incidental menu, popover, and confirmation entrances while checking scope and error behavior.

## User Impact

The four-file batch saves **8.921 seconds (21.6%)** in summed per-file medians on the same Testbox. This is an internal test-runtime change with all 18 cases retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set `reducedMotion: "reduce"` at each file-owned context or page-options site. Existing production CSS already removes these transitions under reduced motion ([overlays](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2bd7edf34e93f549aefbfe4dfa7e728d8b88805f/ui/src/components/solid/overlay.css#L589), [modals](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2bd7edf34e93f549aefbfe4dfa7e728d8b88805f/ui/src/components/solid/modal-dialog.css#L223), [global override](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2bd7edf34e93f549aefbfe4dfa7e728d8b88805f/ui/src/styles/base.css#L1311)). These files assert terminal UI state, captured mutation targets, confirmations, request counts, and error recovery; none asserts motion or intermediate animation state.

Shared helpers/defaults, production CSS, deadlines, cases, assertions, native clicks, focus/keyboard paths, and virtual-clock boundaries are preserved. Formatter reindentation accounts for most diff lines.

## Evidence

Closes #190719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw memory forget --json` writes a report identical to the Memory Core case when another plugin owns the memory slot, so a saved erasure record does not show that the selected plugin's memories were not deleted.

## User Impact

User impact: when another plugin owns `plugins.slots.memory`, the `forget --json` report now includes `"provider": "<slot owner>"` and `"memoryCore": "consolidation-sidecar"`, the same two fields `memory status --json` already reports. Existing fields are unchanged, and output is unchanged when Memory Core owns the slot. The human-mode output and the stderr notice are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidecar notice already says that forget acted only on Memory Core's sidecar index. With `--json` it goes to stderr, which scripts and audit logs usually drop. This adds the same fact to the JSON report, using the field names `memory status --json` already uses for this configuration.

Three files change:

- the forget JSON write in `cli-index-search.runtime.ts`;
- a regression test in `cli.memory-slot.test.ts`;
- the `docs/cli/memory.md` sentence describing sidecar behavior.

## Evidence

prs.title: improve(ui): show exec approval warning text in approval history
prs.body:
Closes #180242

**AI-assisted**

## What Problem This Solves
The approval history table shows the command text of past exec approvals but not the `warningText` that was presented to the reviewer at decision time. This warning (e.g. "Dangerous: redirects to /dev/null") is the auto-review rationale that justified the decision — it is persisted on the approval record and rendered in channel approvals (`approval-reaction-runtime.ts`), but the Control UI history view drops it. A reviewer looking back at history cannot see why a dangerous command was flagged.

## Why This Change Was Made
The data already exists in `ExecApprovalPresentation.warningText` and is rendered in every other surface (channel approvals bold it). This adds the same field to the history table as a dedicated Warning column, so the gap is a read-side render fix on already-persisted safety data. The change is minimal: one sibling component, one locale key, one CSS rule, and tests in the existing file.

## User Impact
Reviewers scanning past approvals in the Control UI can now see the warning text that accompanied each exec decision, making it possible to audit why high-risk commands were allowed or denied without cross-referencing channel logs.

## Evidence
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```
New test `renders the exec approval warning text in the history table` verifies:
- a row with `warningText: "Dangerous: redirects to /dev/null"` renders the text in a `.approval-history__warning-text` element
- a row with `warningText: null` renders no such element

prs.title: fix(gateway): explain Tailscale ingress loss in recovery logs
prs.body:
Related: #183482

## What Problem This Solves

Operators lose the cause of a managed Tailscale route claim ending after readiness: the Gateway logs recovery without the worker or CLI exit details.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish a CLI failure from an abruptly terminated route-owner worker using exit codes, signals, lifetime, and captured-output byte counts. Raw CLI stdout/stderr are excluded from this diagnostic record.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve typed exit facts through the existing claim promise and append them to the existing recovery warning. Worker termination and the optional final CLI report remain separate, so a missing CLI report is not guessed from the worker status.

Current upstream already reclaims managed Serve/Funnel routes with backoff. This patch preserves that behavior, ownership checks, and cleanup; it does not implement configurable reconnection policy requested in #183482. No configuration migration or user action is required.


## Evidence

Current candidate: `00165ba1a489337ff51046a389daad8c8842a466`, merging main `32276e16fb7807083d4452f2a9ec50084f6c95ae` into the original PR. The one test conflict preserves main’s intentional consolidation; both production files and both new diagnostic regressions remain byte-identical to the reviewed PR. Independent review found no actionable integration defect.

- Native `qaRuntime` build passed on Linux arm64 with Node 24.22.1 and frozen pnpm 12.15.0 dependencies.
- Three affected files passed **76 tests** through the repository runner. Main’s consolidation accounts for the changed count from the earlier 79-test run. An initial compiled-test preparation was kernel-killed at 4 GiB; the unchanged checks passed with the qualified 6500 MiB limit. No assertions were relaxed.
- Original regressions were red on production base `6e0e4e03c5a0b3f5ebcd08b8853c64a1c05100ee` because the recovery warning lacked exit facts.
- Formatting passed for all five changed files. Scoped type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors using the supported oxlint fallback and `--tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`. Pinned Bun parity was not rerun for this head. `git diff --check` passed and tracked source stayed clean.
- Current-head [CI completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40353327532). [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183518#issuecomment-6396617996) accepted the running-Gateway proof, found no actionable defects, and marked this revision ready for maintainer review. Canonical local autoreview remains unavailable after the earlier network/export approval rejection; no such report or bypass is claimed. This integration also received independent manual review.

## Running-Gateway process proof

Both captures used the shipped entry point:

```text
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --port <isolated-port> --auth token --tailscale serve
```

Each scenario first required the actual “serve enabled” log and a successful loopback health response. The Gateway, route-owner worker, fork/IPC and CLI child process were real and unmodified. Only the external Tailscale executable was a disclosed deterministic CLI fixture; no internal owner, fork or logger was mocked.

**Post-ready CLI process failure:** the fixture emitted synthetic stderr and exited 42. Actual Gateway recovery warning, with only its timestamp/logger prefix omitted:

```text
serve route claim exited; recovering managed Tailscale ingress; exit={"workerCode":1,"workerSignal":null,"ageMs":236,"stopping":false,"phase":"active","cli":{"code":42,"signal":null,"stdoutBytes":22,"stderrBytes":20}}
```

**Abrupt route-owner termination:** SIGKILL targeted only the exact worker after checking its start time, executable, owner argument and ancestry from this Gateway. Actual warning:

```text
serve route claim exited; recovering managed Tailscale ingress; exit={"workerCode":null,"workerSignal":"SIGKILL","ageMs":169,"stopping":false,"phase":"active"}
```

The second record correctly omits unavailable CLI facts. Both captures verified raw stdout/stderr markers were excluded from the recovery warnings, configuration bytes stayed unchanged, and all task Gateway/helper/worker cleanup joined. The two-scenario capture completed in 11.54 seconds.

Isolation: separate task VM; Docker private PID namespace, `--init`, `--network none`, no published ports, no host HOME/state/socket/SSH-agent mounts, read-only public source and fresh synthetic state. No live Gateway or Tailscale daemon was interrupted.

This proves the shipped Gateway → real worker/process → IPC → recovery-log composition. It does **not** prove actual Tailscale daemon connectivity, tailnet policy, ingress reachability or successful real-route recovery. The source change still leaves the existing reconnection/backoff policy unchanged.

Operators can identify the lost ingress mode, the route-owner worker’s exit code or signal, and any reported CLI exit code in the existing recovery warning. The new diagnostic excludes captured CLI output, auth keys, and tokens.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry a short exit reason through the existing claim lifetime to its recovery owner. Retry policy, cancellation, authority checks, cleanup, and configuration behavior remain unchanged.

Production is +1 net line after removing duplicate worker-exit formatting and repeated CLI-output assembly in the same owner; the remaining growth retains the optional CLI code. The two regressions add 32 net test lines with a separate allocation.

Current head: `92e9046201fbd66faacfe7efc35a9a353daf505a`, rebased onto main `bafe92f6d5c3fc4fc9b9cf5d16813f658ddc4730` at maintainer direction. Range-diff reports an identical patch, and every changed file plus the relevant unchanged owner context remains byte-identical to the reviewed/tested candidate.

- Red on main `02f6c40c`: both new diagnostic cases failed because the warning was generic; 30 existing cases passed. The affected main owners remain unchanged at the rebase baseline.
- Green focused proof: 76 tests across `tailscale.claim.test.ts` (32 / 1.44s), `server-tailscale.test.ts` (17 / 1.56s), and `portal-service.test.ts` (27 / 3.37s), using repository Vitest configs in supported standalone source mode. The regressions exercise the real claim and recovery owners with external process-event fixtures, checking CLI exit 42, worker SIGKILL, and exclusion of synthetic secret markers. Touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Causality comparison: **3/3 main and 3/3 PR-head runs passed** for only `src/gateway/server-templates-add-authority.e2e.test.ts`. Runs were interleaved serially on one [Blacksmith Testbox allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41366798585), in separate pinned worktrees with frozen dependencies and the checksum-pinned CI Bun runtime. Vitest times were main 47.46/35.17/34.17s and head 47.15/35.93/34.48s. The command completed successfully and the box was stopped; allocation-workflow cancellation during teardown is expected. An earlier attempt missing Bun stopped before test execution and was excluded.
- [Fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41366096948): **completed successfully** on the exact head, including test/type/lint lanes and all PostgreSQL conformance shards.

prs.title: improve(ui): simplify Usage controls at phone width
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width the Usage toolbar wraps into 13 stacked controls and 4 filter menus, so the first chart starts about 775px down the page. Provider plan cards also overflow their card on phones, on both Usage and Models. ## User Impact On phones, the range presets stay on the page, followed by the agent picker, Tokens/Cost and a filter button. The first chart now starts at 308px. Dates, time zone, identity, instance/lineage, query and the Channel, Provider, Model and Tool filters open in a bottom sheet. The filter button shows when any of them is active. Chart selections and query terms sit together in one row above the results, with the match count after them. Refresh and the three exports move to a three-dots menu with the same surface as the filter button. Provider plan windows stack inside their card, and long Top models and Cost categories values wrap. The totals line starts at the card's left edge: the sparkline beside it draws nothing, because its color token `--oc-accent` isn't defined on main, so on phones its empty box is dropped. At 360px and below, the daily chart shows five date labels instead of six so they don't collide. Desktop is unchanged. Removed on phones: Pin header (a sticky header would take too much of the viewport), the "Tip" line, and the "sessions in range" count when it only repeats the Sessions tile. The "x of y sessions match" count stays. ## Why This Change Was Made Range is the control people change most on a phone, and the rest are used rarely. The three-dots menu sits in the page header for now and can move to the floating header once that lands. The sheet is drawn in the top layer, so the page's stacking can't reach its backdrop. Inside the sheet every control follows one rhythm: a 16px side inset, 12px between rows, a 13px label above a 40px field, and a 16px value, which is iOS's input floor. Channel, Provider, Model and Tool read as labelled selects with the same chevron. Time zone and Identity are plain selects here, because a customizable select can't ellipsize its own label: a long value truncates and the chevron holds its place in every theme. Their list is the system's on phones. At 320px each date takes its own row, because a full date and its calendar don't fit in half the width. The date fields' calendar uses the selects' chevron color, stroke, size and inset, and still opens the picker. Safari on macOS draws no calendar icon, so it keeps its own field, and clicking a date opens its calendar. The close button is the plain 32px X the other sheets use. The two chip styles are left as they are: chart selections and query terms are different filter types with different owners. ## Evidence Screenshots use the mock data layer and real taps at 390px. Images show today's top bar until the floating header PR lands. For these captures only, a local mock change added filter options, per-provider daily rows and session detail data, because the stock mock has none of them; without provider rows, By Provider draws every bar as grey "Other". That mock change isn't part of this PR. | Before | After | Filter sheet | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Applied filters | Actions, dark | Filter sheet, CRT | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Provider plans | Real Safari 27.0.1, date picker open | | --- | --- | | | | Real Safari: the filter button opened the final sheet with an OS click, in the mock's default dark theme. An OS click on Start date opened Safari's calendar, and choosing the 21st changed the range. The three-dots menu and the backdrop were checked with OS clicks on the previous revision. Tapping a chart bar adds its day chip, and Daily CSV downloads from the menu. The page has no horizontal scroll at 390px or 320px. At 1280px, Usage header and provider boxes and the Models provider usage boxes match an unmodified page. At 390px, Models provider usage used to run off the screen and now fits. The sheet images use the stock mock, opened with real taps at 390px and 320x568, with default and long values and no horizontal overflow. Checks: oxfmt, stylelint, oxlint, `tsgo:ui` and the Usage and provider usage unit and browser tests pass (233 tests); the Usage tests, oxfmt and stylelint were rerun on this head. `ui:check-performance:base` fails on the total CSS budget: main is already over the cap, and this PR adds to it.
