prs.title: fix(voice-call): preserve spaces after Unicode transcript overlaps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Realtime voice consultations can lose characters when overlapping transcript fragments contain a Unicode letter whose lowercase form expands: `Meet in İstanbul` followed by `İstanbul tomorrow` becomes `Meet in İstanbultomorrow`.

## User Impact

Consultations started from partial transcripts retain the complete wording, including the space after the overlap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Map the existing case-insensitive overlap length back to an original code-point boundary before slicing the incoming fragment. Keep the current comparison rules, overlap thresholds, and separator fallback. The existing partial-settle test table now covers ASCII and Unicode; it adds 13 regression lines with an independent allocation record. Production code grows by 12 lines without adding another owner or public API.

## Evidence

- [Original-source regression](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/41290517377), base `39629c6aa82ce444f14c37fc1d4d47e5c7f661d0`: the same regression test fails on the exact corrupted consult question above. One selected test fails, 32 are skipped, and JUnit reports zero runtime errors; production source is unchanged.
- [Fixed-head proof](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/41292327019), head `a5b140c444bc8eecc9fcf50de2d3bfd58eb29492`: complete handler **33/33** and adjacent lifecycle **28/28**, zero skips/todos; production and test type graphs, typed lint (0 errors/warnings), canonical format/oxfmt-Bun parity, and allocation ratchet pass. Tracked source stays clean; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.
- [Shipped Gateway and actual agent proof](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/41299041337/job/124825952685), the same exact product head `a5b140c444bc8eecc9fcf50de2d3bfd58eb29492`: the stock CLI starts a real Gateway and registered Voice Call plugin. A normally signed carrier webhook issues the single-use stream URL; an invalid signature is rejected with 401. Carrier audio traverses the official realtime adapter, whose overlapping external transcript events trigger the real registered consultation and built-in agent runtime. The controlled model HTTP request contains both `Caller: Meet in İstanbul tomorrow` and `User request:` followed by `Meet in İstanbul tomorrow`; the corrupted missing-space text is absent. One actual agent model request completes, and its result returns through the official adapter as `function_call_output` for `fixture-consult`. Public `voicecall.status` observes answered then completed. All owned listeners close, the Gateway process tree joins, configuration/source stay unchanged, and cleanup succeeds.
- The readable [external-service fixture driver](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/blob/5aec0860ca4f690073f2c841ac86d89898d0e629/proof/voice-transcript-unicode-gateway.mjs) and [raw artifacts](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/41299041337/artifacts/13080891162) retain the redacted model request, realtime messages, terminal output, call-status results, source identity, and cleanup receipt. Carrier/transcription/model services are synthetic; the Gateway, plugin, signature validation, realtime adapter, consultation, and agent runtime are unmocked. This is not vendor-live phone, speech recognition, or model-inference evidence.
- The earlier Gateway run `41297483321` remains **FAILURE**: its external fixture wrongly expected every incremental `session.update` to include a tools array. The new controller accepts the supported partial updates and normally settles the greeting before user input; the product head is unchanged.
- Handler command wall time: **52 s**, including cold worker preparation (49.01 s Vitest, 93% transform; 0.72 s test execution). Lifecycle command: **45 s** (42.24 s Vitest; 2.35 s test execution). CI jobs consumed 217 s for tests and 386 s for checks. The existing loopback carrier/provider-callback fixture exercises transcript settlement into the actual host-consult input; a text helper assertion alone would miss that boundary.
- Independent autoreview against the pinned base of the change committed as this head, P0–P3: no actionable findings. Pre-PR execution used stock secretless fork Actions. The regression suite covers callback-to-consult behavior; the shipped-entry-point proof above additionally covers the real Gateway and agent path. No restart/durability claim is made.
- [Ready PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41293327491) and its required `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded on exact head `a5b140c444bc8eecc9fcf50de2d3bfd58eb29492`. Maintainer review remains pending.

prs.title: fix(macos): screen.record reports requested instead of recorded duration/fps
prs.body:
Closes #187604 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the macOS node's `screen.record` result reports the requested `durationMs`/`fps` instead of the values it recorded with, when the request is outside the allowed range or omits them. ## User Impact The agent and `openclaw nodes screen record` read `durationMs` and `fps` from this payload. A request for `{"durationMs":100,"fps":120}` produced a 0.25 s clip at 60 fps but reported 100 ms at 120 fps. A request with no values produced a 10 s clip at 10 fps and reported neither field. With this change the payload always carries the duration and frame rate the recording used. ## Why This Change Was Made `ScreenRecordService.record` already clamps both values (`CaptureRateLimits.clampDurationMs`, `clampFps(maxFps: 60)`), so it now returns them, and `MacNodeRuntime` reports those instead of echoing `params`. This matches `camera.clip`, which already reports the service's `durationMs`. No TypeScript change: `parseScreenRecordPayload` already treats both fields as optional numbers, and they are now always present.
Root cause `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/NodeMode/MacNodeRuntime.swift` built `ScreenPayload` with `durationMs: params.durationMs, fps: params.fps`. The clamped values only existed inside `ScreenRecordService.record` and were not returned. The echo dates from 95ea67de289 (the original mac screen recording commit); nothing relied on it being the requested value. `LiveMacNodeRuntimeMainActorServices` is the only caller of `ScreenRecordService` on macOS.
## Evidence Real app, before and after: the same isolated Gateway (`gateway run --port 19387`, temp state and config), an ad-hoc packaged macOS app paired as a node, `openclaw gateway call node.invoke` with `command: "screen.record"`, the returned mp4 decoded and measured with `ffprobe`. macOS 27.2. | params | main payload | fix payload | recorded file (ffprobe) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `{"durationMs":100,"fps":120}` | `durationMs: 100, fps: 120` | `durationMs: 250, fps: 60` | 0.25 s, 15 frames | | `{}` | no `durationMs`, no `fps` | `durationMs: 10000, fps: 10` | ~10 s, 100–104 frames | | `{"durationMs":2000,"fps":10}` (control) | `durationMs: 2000, fps: 10` | `durationMs: 2000, fps: 10` | ~2.1 s, 21 frames | The recorded mp4s are not attached because they captured the tester's real desktop; the payloads and ffprobe measurements above are taken from them.
main (upstream/main 5f6f15fed0d) ``` ## main / clamp $ openclaw gateway call node.invoke --json --timeout 45000 --params '{"nodeId":"","command":"screen.record","params":{"durationMs":100,"fps":120},...}' exit=0 payload (base64 omitted): {"durationMs": 100, "format": "mp4", "fps": 120, "hasAudio": false} ffprobe of recorded mp4: nb_frames=15 duration=0.250000 ## main / omitted $ openclaw gateway call node.invoke --json --timeout 45000 --params '{"nodeId":"","command":"screen.record","params":{},...}' exit=0 payload (base64 omitted): {"format": "mp4", "hasAudio": false} ffprobe of recorded mp4: nb_frames=104 duration=10.466667 ## main / control $ openclaw gateway call node.invoke --json --timeout 45000 --params '{"nodeId":"","command":"screen.record","params":{"durationMs":2000,"fps":10},...}' exit=0 payload (base64 omitted): {"durationMs": 2000, "format": "mp4", "fps": 10, "hasAudio": false} ffprobe of recorded mp4: nb_frames=21 duration=2.100000 ``` The first clamp attempt on main, the first capture after the app launched, returned `UNAVAILABLE: The operation could not be completed`; the two retries above succeeded with the same params.
fix ``` ## fix / clamp $ openclaw gateway call node.invoke --json --timeout 45000 --params '{"nodeId":"","command":"screen.record","params":{"durationMs":100,"fps":120},...}' exit=0 payload (base64 omitted): {"durationMs": 250, "format": "mp4", "fps": 60, "hasAudio": false} ffprobe of recorded mp4: nb_frames=15 duration=0.250000 ## fix / omitted $ openclaw gateway call node.invoke --json --timeout 45000 --params '{"nodeId":"","command":"screen.record","params":{},...}' exit=0 payload (base64 omitted): {"durationMs": 10000, "format": "mp4", "fps": 10, "hasAudio": false} ffprobe of recorded mp4: nb_frames=100 duration=10.066667 ## fix / control $ openclaw gateway call node.invoke --json --timeout 45000 --params '{"nodeId":"","command":"screen.record","params":{"durationMs":2000,"fps":10},...}' exit=0 payload (base64 omitted): {"durationMs": 2000, "format": "mp4", "fps": 10, "hasAudio": false} ffprobe of recorded mp4: nb_frames=21 duration=2.116667 ```
The before build was packaged with a separate bundle ID only so it could hold its own Screen Recording grant next to the fix build; the code is upstream/main unchanged. Tests: - New `MacNodeRuntimeTests` case `handle invoke screen record reports the duration and fps the recorder used` (over-limit and omitted params). On main it fails with 4 expectation failures (payload `120000`/`120.0` and `nil`/`nil`); with the fix `swift test --filter MacNodeRuntimeTests` passes 45/45. - `pnpm test src/cli/nodes-camera.test.ts src/agents/tools/nodes-tool.test.ts`: passed. - `swiftformat --lint` on the 4 files: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: only the existing `file_length` violations in `DashboardManager.swift` and `GatewayConnection.swift`, which this change does not touch. `git diff --check`: clean. Production delta +8/-8; test delta +35/-4. Merge risk: two-way door. Blast radius is the macOS `screen.record` result payload; `durationMs` and `fps` become always present and match the recording. iOS `NodeAppModel` has the same echo of requested values; that is a separate owner and is left for a follow-up.

prs.title: fix(browser): Chrome extension reports "Not installed" when macOS blocks profile reads
prs.body:
Closes #172272

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenClaw reporting an installed, connected Chrome extension as "Not installed / manual setup required" when macOS privacy protection blocks reading Chrome's profile files.

## User Impact

User impact: when Chrome profile files are unreadable, status reports unknown install state instead of "extension missing", and that unknown fact now survives a successful connection check, so the Mac app's Chrome setup card never flips to "Not installed" while the extension shows connected. `openclaw browser extension status` prints the discovery warnings its summary references (including the Full Disk Access remedy), and `setup` steers to the live relay check instead of Store reinstall guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile discovery conflated "cannot read Chrome's profile files" with "extension not installed". Blocked reads now surface as `discoveryBlocked` on status and, as an installation-level fact, inside the setup `installation` projection (CLI JSON, the macOS Swift bridge, and the dashboard card), because the connection reason replaces the inspect reason during verify and previously erased the uncertainty. The CLI status command now prints issue lines before the summary. Review follow-ups from @clawsweeper are addressed: the blocked fact is independent of the connection reason (`installation.discoveryBlocked`, covered by the inspect→verify transition in the new e2e), and human-readable status prints the warnings it references.

## Evidence

Real-machine repro (macOS 27.0.1, OpenClaw 2026.10.3, TCC-blocked Chrome profile, extension connected — the exact contradiction from #172272):

```text
BEFORE (released openclaw 2026.10.3):
  setup --action inspect:
    {"phase":"needs_browser_action","reason":"extension_missing","nextAction":"install_from_store","nativeHostRegistered":true,"installedProfiles":0}

AFTER (this branch, built from source, same machine, same block):
  setup --action verify  (unknown install state survives a connected verify):
    {"phase":"ready","reason":"connected","connection":{"state":"connected","extensionVersion":"2.3.0"},
     "installation":{"installedProfiles":0,"discoveredProfiles":0,"discoveryBlocked":true}}
```

`extension status` on the same machine now starts with the previously hidden warning:

```text
Google Chrome: could not list profiles (Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, scandir '.../Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome'); on macOS, grant Full Disk Access to the app running OpenClaw, then check again
```

After-fix CLI behavior in a clean hermetic environment (owned native-host registration, profile directory made unreadable → same EACCES blocked-read path):

```text
status (human-readable; warnings now printed above the summary):
  Google Chrome profile Default (Preferences): EACCES: permission denied, lstat '.../Chrome/Default/Preferences'
  ...
  Setup:          unknown (Chrome profile files unreadable for Google Chrome; check the warnings above)

setup --action inspect:
  {"phase":"waiting_for_connection","reason":"profile_inspection_blocked","nextAction":"check_connection",
   "installation":{"nativeHostRegistered":true,"installedProfiles":0,"discoveredProfiles":0,"discoveryBlocked":true}}

setup --action verify (relay not running here; no false extension_missing, fact preserved):
  {"phase":"waiting_for_connection","reason":"relay_unavailable","nextAction":"check_connection",
   "connection":{"state":"unavailable"},"installation":{"discoveryBlocked":true,...}}
```

Desktop card before/after — the dashboard row driven through the macOS native bridge reply contract (the same `chrome-extension-setup` reply shape the Mac app posts back), captured via headless Control UI e2e:

- Before (base `ff22ecbe` build): after inspect, the card renders **Not installed**; after a connected verify it renders **Not installed** alongside **Extension connected on this device** — the reviewer's exact P2. Captured card text: `...Not installedExtension connected on this device....`
- After (this PR): inspect renders **Status unavailable** + the Full Disk Access hint; after a connected verify the card keeps **Status unavailable** and the hint alongside **Extension connected on this device**.

Four screenshots below: **before** (base `ff22ecbe` build — the reviewer's exact P2) and **after** (this PR):

Before — inspect says "Not installed", and a connected verify keeps saying it:

![Before fix: blocked inspect renders Not installed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4db56ba5-974b-4d32-9acb-69b7d24dae26)

![Before fix: Not installed alongside Extension connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b06ab479-ad38-4d4b-ad94-b845784dd75d)

After — "Status unavailable" with the Full Disk Access hint, preserved through a connected verify:

![After fix: Status unavailable with Full Disk Access hint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a1601b6-48d3-4abc-8c00-b0e42a2eecc1)

![After fix: unknown survives connected verify](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7ae34e5-6c12-4d9a-9638-ba3939015759)

Regression run for the transition (failing base / passing head):

- Added `ui/src/e2e/chrome-extension-status.e2e.test.ts` → "keeps unknown install state through blocked inspect and a connected verify".
- Base UI build: `FAIL ... expected 'Chrome extensionSet up Chrome on this…' to contain 'Status unavailable'`.
- This head: `✓ keeps unknown install state through blocked inspect and a connected verify 743ms` (`vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`).

Suites on `1e2ad88e`:

- `vitest.extension-browser.config.ts`: 82 passed (incl. blocked status/inspect/verify, survives-verify, CLI warnings test).
- `vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` Chrome setup file: passed; UI unit suites touching the card (`chrome-setup`, `native-device-settings`, `device-pages`): passed.
- `tsgo` extensions, ui, core-test ui-e2e projects: clean. `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, docs format, line-cap + assertion-safety ratchets: clean. Full `pnpm build`: clean.
- The Swift bridge change cannot be covered by CI on fork PRs (`macos-swift` skips); it is verified with a local `swift test --filter ChromeExtensionSetupTests` run, and the result will be posted as a follow-up comment on this PR.

Known-unrelated CI flake observed on the previous head: one UI shard (`chat-transcript-end-follow`, then `canvas-widget-view`) — neither file is touched by this PR.

prs.title: fix(outbound): retain delivered receipts after heartbeat renewal fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A failed producer heartbeat can discard an accepted outbound message receipt and
leave the delivery unresolved even when its original queue claim still survives.
The accompanying lifecycle cleanup removes parallel mailbox summary state and
clarifies ownership boundaries identified in the same maintainer-requested audit.

## User Impact

Already-started sends can settle their unchanged claim after heartbeat failure.
Cancellation still blocks later sends; replacement claims remain protected, and
partial batches retain recovery custody. Mailbox and UI behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep send admission separate from receipt settlement inside the existing delivery
owner. Replace parallel mailbox source/text arrays and the derived elision count
with paired entries, preserving original-to-compact identities. Clarify existing
mailbox, subagent, plugin, reload, update handoff, transcript teardown and UI save
contracts without introducing a state-machine framework or changing public APIs,
configuration, dependencies, schemas or protocols.

## Evidence

- The accepted-receipt regression fails on base `ba51135a5962` and passes with the
  fix. Paired cases protect replacement claims and prevent another payload send.
- 380 selected tests across 16 files passed through repository test wrappers with
  one worker. The production queue uses controlled external adapters; no live
  channel delivery claim is made. Affected tests passed again after final fixture
  and simplification edits.
- Targeted Gateway/messaging type checks, changed-file lint, formatting, docs lint,
  MDX/link checks, test-line budget and commit hooks passed.
- Local autoreview assessed the complete local change against `ba51135a5962`,
  through P2, with no actionable findings. Later edits corrected names/types and
  removed redundancy; the final committed bytes match the tested source snapshot.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190318#issuecomment-6558336305)
  assessed head `2d6d636b5097` and found no actionable findings. Its remaining
  proof limitation is the absence of a live transport-client recovery trace.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41308102248/job/124852964480)
  remains red: the blocked-store:false case in
  `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts` exceeded its existing 180-second timeout.
  CI tested merge `dd1398ab7753` against main base `d2710e1efaa7` using the pinned
  Bun runtime on Linux. The timeout is unattributed; no pre-existing-failure or
  successful-repair claim is made.
- A focused macOS replay at this PR's audited source revision passed both restart
  cases (2/2). This is supporting local evidence, not a reproduction of CI's
  Linux merge environment. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- A paired Linux comparison completed successfully through Blacksmith Testbox
  [run 41365620562](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41365620562):
  **212/212 tests on the exact CI merge and 212/212 on its main base**. Both used
  the original four-file shard order, independent frozen installs/runtime
  builds, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, and the same pinned Bun revision
  `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. The requested 4-class profile supplied 2 CPUs and
  8,218,361,856 bytes of RAM, matching the original job's observed resources.
- Both restart cases passed on both revisions. The blocked-store:false case took
  56.126 seconds on the merge and 62.236 seconds on main. Temporary diagnostic
  gate logging was applied equally; assertions and the 180-second timeout were
  unchanged. The wrapper exited 0. Lease cleanup can mark the linked Actions run
  cancelled; the wrapper result records the actual payload outcome.
- This comparison did not reproduce or attribute the original timeout. It is
  neither a proven repair nor evidence that the failure is inherited. The exact
  main base's [original CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41307017856)
  was cancelled with zero jobs. No production change or CI rerun was made for
  this investigation.
- Local timings include a cold compiler-artifact build; the main focused batch
  took 221.87 seconds and the UI batch 7.63 seconds. These are local wall times,
  not measured hosted CI cost.

prs.title: improve(ui): keep approve and ask documents on one scroller at phone width
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width the standalone `/approve` and `/ask` documents put content inside a second scroller, so part of what you are deciding on stays out of sight. - **Approve:** a long command sat in a box capped at 34vh with the decision buttons directly below it. In macOS Safari at 390px, scroll events over the box moved the page and never reached the end of the command. Touch scrolling on iOS was not tested, but even where the box does scroll, only about 13 of 60 wrapped lines show at once. In the proof command, the `rm -rf` on the last line was hidden. - **Ask:** the panel kept the chat dock's height cap. A long question scrolled inside the panel with Submit out of view, while about 290px of the page below stayed empty. - **Ask frame:** the panel sat inside the document card, a card inside a card, which left option text 257px wide on a 390px screen. - **Ask actions:** Submit was a 33px button on the right, after Skip. - **After answering:** the summary inherited centered text, which reads badly once it wraps. - **Corners:** the document card's phone radius was hardcoded, so themes with squarer corners didn't apply to it. ## User Impact On a phone the whole command is readable before deciding, and the page is the only scroller on both documents. `/ask` now has one surface in every state, including Answered, Skipped and load errors, and option text is 292px wide instead of 257px. The primary action comes first and takes the free width at 44px, and Skip holds still while the label changes to Submitting. Both documents are also tighter. On `/ask`, the prompt is 16px, option labels 14px, descriptions 13px and buttons 14px, up from 14, 12, 11 and 12. Rows are at least 44px and 6px apart. Placeholders are 14px while typed values stay 16px, iOS's input floor. Own answer takes the round marker on single-choice questions, and the load-time focus ring is gone. Answered and Skipped stay on the same card, with the status in the small header and no accent bar. On `/approve`, the header is 52px instead of 68px, the title 22px and actions 44px. Stacked previews no longer touch, and Host and Node have no line between them. The collapse button isn't on the standalone phone `/ask`. It exists so the chat dock can get out of the way of the conversation, and on this document nothing sits under the panel. With the button forced visible and tapped, the options and Submit disappeared and the only control left on the page was the bar that reopens the panel, so it wasn't providing anything here. The chat dock keeps it. The document card and the `/ask` surface follow the theme's radius. The chat dock's panel and desktop don't change: every rule is inside the existing `max-width: 640px` block, and the `/ask` rules are scoped to `.question-page`. A very long command now means a longer scroll to reach the buttons. That is the tradeoff for not being able to approve a command whose end you never saw. ## Why This Change Was Made Both documents are where people make a decision from a phone, often arriving from a link. The cap and the outer card were reasonable elsewhere, but on a narrow document of their own they hide content and take width from the text being read. Approve's actions already work at this width (permit first, full width, accent fill), so they are unchanged. ## Evidence Real data through the mock Gateway at 390px, with real taps in Chromium with touch emulation unless marked as Safari. Before and After use different sample requests. The themes come from saved preferences. `approval.get` and `question.get` come from an uncommitted local fixture, along with `approval.resolve` and `question.resolve`: the stock mock doesn't serve them, and the fixture is not part of this diff. Both documents sit outside the app shell, so they have no top bar in any of these images. Approve, long command, end of page: | Before | After (390px) | | --- | --- | | | | Ask: | Before, long question, Submit is inside the panel's scroller | After (390px), option chosen | | --- | --- | | | | Ask, after answering (390px): CRT and real Safari 27.0.1: | Ask, real Safari | Ask, CRT | Approve, real Safari | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | Real Safari: a 390px window in the mock's default theme, with an OS click choosing the option on `/ask`. `/approve` is one frame of a critical plugin request, with no click. Number shortcuts appear on the options there because that window uses a mouse. They don't show on touch, where the option text measures 292px. Checks on this branch: oxfmt and stylelint pass. `approval-page.e2e` and `question-flow.e2e` pass, including a phone-width `/ask` test for one scroller, no outer frame, option width, action order and the placeholder and value sizes. The approval phone layout test now asserts no nested overflow. `approval-page` and `question-page` unit tests pass (53). `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui` and the controller guard pass. `ui:check-performance:base` fails on the CSS budget: base is already over the cap and this adds to it. Not verified: the iOS keyboard and safe area on a device. Safari here is macOS Safari in a 390px window. From source, `openclaw-app` owns the safe-area padding and `connectShellViewport` shrinks the document to the visual viewport when the keyboard opens.

prs.title: fix: personal MCP sign-in fails in authenticated Webchat
prs.body:
## Summary

Authenticated Webchat has a verified profile but no transport `SenderId`. With a personal (`oauth.identity: "per-requester"`) MCP server, asking to connect an account therefore exposes no personal sign-in tool.

Capture the exact live single-participant Webchat authority at the admitted human-turn owner, before private admission state is projected away. Both native execution and the public harness bridge consume that host capture. The transport sender, existing requester credential tuple and OAuth callback owner are unchanged.

## Scope and authority

- Direct and admitted visible human Webchat turns only. The profile, connection, session, run, tool fingerprint and live participant must agree.
- Recheck authority after awaited preparation and at HTTP/OAuth effects. Releasing a view closes its executors without attaching a turn guard to a reusable cached runtime.
- Preserve verified transport senders. Do not infer personal access for queued follow-ups, ambiguous multi-person steers, scheduled/spawned work, memory flushes or control operations.
- No new config, storage schema, public SDK export or provider-specific integration. The JSON result projection is an unchanged move to its existing content owner to respect file size.

**Maintainer scope decision remains open:** this is the narrow direct-Webchat capability from #138113. #177356 covers broader authenticated ingress; its separate proof does not validate this patch. #187952 concerns memory attribution rather than MCP credential authority.

## Inspectable behavior proof

[Reproduction script, instructions and redacted observed results](https://gist.github.com/apps3000/b0405ddf7299f71b763256d2dddf3134).

The same standalone script was run against two independently built checkouts, with only synthetic accounts, local HTTP servers and a deterministic local model fixture:

| Source | Observed outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Original merge base `315380c4789590e3aff9be3cfc6fcfcb9e1f6eee` | Gateway and authenticated chat run; `personal_cloud__connect` is missing, dispatch reports unknown tool ID, no OAuth HTTP request occurs. |
| Current head `6e19a6441567c8bcc1a695a91b26aa5876c6344a` | Two verified profiles in one shared session obtain distinct personal links. Each native OAuth callback completes **after its chat reply**. Subsequent real MCP identity reads return Ada, Grace, Ada. |

The fixed runtime was rebuilt from this exact head (`build-info.json.commit` matches), then the proof was rerun: **5 chat.send turns, 15 model-fixture requests, 2 token exchanges**. This reaches the actual Gateway, native agent, MCP discovery/connect, HTTP transport, OAuth callback and SQLite credential owners. The script checks PKCE and rejects a reply containing the other account's identity.

This is protocol/frontdoor proof, not a browser-rendering test or a claim about a real Google/Composio provider.

## Review feedback addressed

- The OAuth mock export finding was already fixed in `63d0af3` by preserving real exports; the current mock-export ratchet passes without baseline changes.
- Removed the low-value native acquisition-argument echo test.
- Replaced the synthetic awaited-effect test with **four real OAuth-boundary cases**: native/harness × revoked/second-person-steered during the first discovery response. Authorization delegates to the real first-party implementation, MCP SDK, guarded HTTP and SQLite store. Each case checks the intended authority error, **exactly one HTTP request**, and **no stored token, verifier or authorization URL**.
- Routed that suite to the existing host-owned SQLite broker/fork lane because these cases now use actual persistent state.
- Kept the narrower identity and released-view tests. The change-local regression allocation is exactly **461 lines**, with no shared budget or mock baseline relaxation.

The negative cases deny subsequent network/persistence after authority changes during preparation. They do not claim coverage of revocation during an already-published post-reply callback; that existing callback lifecycle is unchanged.

## Validation

At current head:

- Focused native wrapper: **24 tests / 2 files pass**, **15.06 s** wall time; Vitest **8.76 s** (includes the four HTTP/SQLite cases and the affected native owner suite).
- Targeted test types (`agents-root`, `agents-other`), type-aware lint, format, test-line and mock-export ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Runtime build `qaRuntime` passes (**70 s**), followed by the exact-built-head Gateway proof above.
- Shared **autoreview**, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol / medium, reviewed the review-feedback delta and supplied unchanged authority/OAuth owners through **P0–P2**: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. It is source review, not maintainer approval; the reviewer did not execute tests. The only later source edit added lint-required braces without changing behavior.

Earlier broader evidence remains revision-specific: 93 focused tests and full build with 161 SDK subpaths at `b9c8ce0f`; [upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41024843137) passed at `63d0af3`. The new head changes tests/routing/allocation only. Those earlier CI results are not presented as new-head CI.

## Remaining gates and limits

- This external contribution still requires the upstream maintainer's security-sensitive-path approval and the scope decision above.
- New-head [CI 41107237106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41107237106) completed with failures. The failure attribution and unchanged-main controls are documented below; no failed check is represented as passing.
- A full Codex app-server process, real Composio/Google sign-in and production rollout were not exercised. Harness coverage here reaches the public requester materialization boundary.
- Production remains on the official release; no candidate patch was deployed.


## New-head CI failure attribution

CI executed GitHub merge `da94d17e26fa60d6ccd192b51296c68c96de8f1f` against main `9e8a058de8afcdaf03f5774979e7d2e494b80a1c`, rather than the old source base used for the original reproduction. A separate unchanged-main checkout with fresh frozen dependencies reproduces the same failures. [Commands, exact scope and observed results](https://gist.github.com/apps3000/b0405ddf7299f71b763256d2dddf3134#file-ci-baseline-md).

| Failed CI owner | Unchanged-main evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Cron admission, large-18 | Native abort/owner-abort/permission/revocation cases and Gateway mutation revoke/abort expect `skipped`, receive `ok`. |
| Cron isolated fallback, large-22 | Explicit and stored fallback ladders are not reached. Both matching cases reproduced without this PR. |
| Gateway spawn fallback, small-11 | `configured agent ladder` returns `error` instead of `ok`; `hidden child control` omits the expected backup. Both reproduced without this PR. |
| Reply/session fallbacks, small-9 | Matching streaming-recovery and fallback-transcript failures reproduced on unchanged main. The scheduled-session variant is covered by the separate control in the linked evidence. |
| Test-line ratchet | Main itself has 6,307,252 lines against a 6,304,616 ceiling: **2,636 inherited excess lines**. The merge adds exactly our 461-line allocation to both values and retains the same excess. The guard accepts zero-delta debt but rejects a positive-delta tree still above its ceiling. |

All seven failed test files are byte-identical in main and the CI merge. No unrelated runtime repair, baseline raise, additional inherited-debt allocation, expected-failure marker or guard change was added to make these checks green. Maintainer resolution of the existing failures/debt and security/scope approval remain pending.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain compatible tool catalogs on settled local threads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A user can lose their settled native conversation after an otherwise compatible tool addition. Another user-visible failure occurs when a tool waiting on approval receives permission after its original session has been replaced and still performs the old action.

## What changes

A follow-up can keep a settled local Codex thread when the host adds a tool. The native thread keeps its original declarations. Each must still match the requested and executable catalogs, and effective plugin policy must remain equivalent. If current policy instead requires a new thread, the replacement uses the policy just resolved for this attempt. A failed policy lookup still stops the attempt.

A host tool now rechecks the original session immediately before its implementation starts. Configured MCP tools check again after interactive approval. The session worker admits the start and the implementation runs in the caller’s context, so it can queue its own database writes. Automatic catalog replacement also stops before it would overwrite a binding with an unrecognized tool handoff. A temporary no-tool thread can continue if it leaves the binding intact.

## Evidence

**Exact release evidence.** These runs use `e446d9ef2575db0dbefdf619dd3dd9d94c894615` (tree `0a115c176debbf39da095a74005ac12274f22f1d`). The two deliberately red controls and stock run are labeled individually. The complete diff from the previous tested head changes only two Slack test/test-support files. The eight directly audited Git blobs are shown below.

prs.title: improve(slack): render flat Markdown bullet lists natively
prs.body:
Related: #21010, #57708

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Markdown bullet lists sent to Slack appear as text with bullet characters, rather than native Slack lists.

**Slack-owner decision requested:** Should ordinary Markdown text sends automatically use native lists for supported flat bullets? This PR proposes that bounded default, with conservative fallback for unsupported constructs. It does not implement the broader rich-text RFC.

## User Impact

Flat bullet lists render natively in ordinary text sends, including supported emphasis and links. Existing account settings for link previews and threading continue to apply. Unsupported list constructs fall back to the existing rendering; streaming previews, edits, media captions, and explicit blocks are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Slack sender derives native Block Kit lists and notification fallback text from the same parsed Markdown and existing chunker. This keeps rendering in the Slack plugin without introducing another model-facing argument, configuration option, or dependency.

## Evidence

Reproduction input for an ordinary Markdown text send:

```markdown
**Synthetic support summary — formatting test**

- **P1 · Premium content unavailable** *(enterprise user, l1 user)*: We are investigating.
- **P2 · Certificate download** *(pro user, l2 user)*: We restored access. [Example ticket](https://example.com/tickets/2)

Synthetic data only; no customer incident.
```

Before: the send contains the existing mrkdwn text, with no native list blocks. After: it contains a native `rich_text_list` and text fallback, without duplicating the visible summary. The sender regression failed before the patch and passes with it.

**Preview repair (`5b36782ffe0c2880ecbc7d62dc03a0bed7630fbb`):** draft creation disables native lists through a Slack-private sender option, retaining the existing Markdown parser, chunker, table policy, and per-chunk protections. Updates keep the existing mrkdwn edit path. A draft-owner regression exercises real send/edit implementations with mocked Slack API methods and verifies text-only creation and editing, plus balanced bold formatting when entity expansion forces chunking. All 54 affected tests pass; targeted types, lint, formatting, and test-line checks pass. Independent review found no remaining actionable issue. No new public configuration or tool argument is introduced.

**Whitespace repair (`50b3f47226bf601b659b489af5756cf9257ebdad`):** preserve code-owned boundary spaces in both list items and surrounding prose. A sender regression first failed on the original PR head because native text lost spaces preserved by the fallback; it now passes. All 86 tests across the affected sender and formatter suites pass, along with targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and test-budget checks. An independent review found no remaining actionable issue.

The original head passed 137 focused tests across six files, the full build, and [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41021243506). The whitespace-repair head also passed [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41026136493). CI for the preview repair is pending.

**Live baseline/candidate proof:** sent the identical fixture through each built CLI and the normal Slack plugin to a real workspace. Both sends succeeded. API readback on upstream shows literal `•` characters inside a text section; the candidate stores one rich-text block containing a two-item native `rich_text_list`. Bold titles, italic customer labels, and the link are preserved. The heading occurs once in the candidate block tree, and both messages remain top-level.

Baseline: `c49e07385f8d17601efbed7746381213d5326ba9`. Live-tested candidate: `a3ff3501a8604c5e88051d6cc33e41a8d90251f7` (before the whitespace-only repair; this synthetic fixture contains no inline code), patch SHA-256 `0f051942b1f88fdc15a18e42d7b36da6834fce6cd12240bc7434cedfbbf333be`. The clean baseline runtime build passed in 244.7 seconds. Tests used isolated configuration/state, with no change to the running Gateway. The screenshot and server-readback observations above use synthetic data only.

**Visual evidence:** inspected a user-supplied screenshot of both synthetic messages. Top: patched candidate, with native list indentation and more compact paragraph spacing. Bottom: upstream baseline, with inline bullet characters. Both preserve bold titles, italic labels, and the link; neither duplicates the summary. The image contains only synthetic fixture content.

![Slack comparison: top is the patched native list; bottom is the upstream text bullets.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/262ee521-1016-434f-aac9-52ccccf77435)

**Limitations:** hosted CI results are pending. No model-generated reply or Gateway event flow is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Validation details and limitations</summary>

- Original-head focused verification: 137 distinct tests; 147.45 seconds including compiler preparation. Repair verification: 86 tests across two affected suites; 20.09 seconds including preparation.
- Full build: passed in 812.2 seconds. UI bundle-size warnings remain (startup JS gzip 88.7/88.6 KiB; CSS gzip 301.6/301.3 KiB); the same warnings occur in the clean baseline runtime build.
- Slack cold import succeeded at 103.4 MB peak RSS. This ran before committing, so performance qualification was unavailable; this is not a qualified benchmark.
- Local independent agent review identified chunk-boundary transcript-role protection and bare-URL/emoji compatibility issues. Both were addressed and re-reviewed with no remaining concrete findings. This was not ClawSweeper or the autoreview CLI.
- The 180-line test allocation covers native-list delivery, fallback, chunking, role-header protection, code-owned whitespace, and draft creation/editing regressions. No generated bundles or runtime dependencies change.

</details>

prs.title: improve(ui): keep provider meta readable beside status on phones
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width, a provider's status sits beside its name and meta. A long status such as "Credentials configured" squeezes the meta, so "3 models · Signed-in account" truncates to "3 models · Signed…". ## User Impact On a phone, the provider meta shows in full and status gets its own line under it, with no information moved behind the expand control. Each connected row is about 21 px taller. Not connected rows and desktop do not change. Expanding a provider no longer scrolls sideways inside the block. Quota cards stack, Top models, Cost categories and the requests line wrap, and the chevron stays visible. ## Why This Change Was Made Below 640 px, status moves to a second grid row in the identity column, and the icon and chevron span both rows. An expanded row took the width of its longest unwrapped line, about 500 px, because the list and detail grids had no shrinkable track. Below 640 px those tracks now shrink and the empty spacer in usage rows drops out. prs.title: fix(slack,feishu,zalouser): multi-line /btw and /loop arguments arrive on one line
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/185266

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Slack, Feishu and Zalo Personal, a slash command with a multi-line argument (`/btw` with a pasted stack trace, a multi-line `/loop` prompt) reaches the command on one line, with its line breaks and indentation gone. In Zalo Personal this happens when the message mentions the bot.

## User Impact

User impact: Slack, Feishu and Zalo Personal users can paste traces, code and lists into `/btw`, `/side` and `/loop`, and the model receives them as typed, as it already does in channels whose mention stripping runs in core.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183606 made core `stripMentions` keep the whitespace of text that starts with `/`. These three channels build the command body in their own helpers (`stripSlackMentionsForCommandDetection`, `normalizeFeishuCommandProbeBody` and Zalo Personal's `stripOwnMentionsForCommandBody`), which strip mentions and then collapse every whitespace run to one space, so core never sees the line breaks. Each helper now applies the same rule as core: after mention stripping and trimming, text that starts with `/` keeps its whitespace; any other text is collapsed as before, so command detection for text like `Please /help` is unchanged.

Behavior note: a command followed by more lines (for example a mention, `/stop` and a second line) now reaches command matching with its line break, so these channels read it the way core already reads the same text since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183606.

Size: production +10/-10 lines in three helpers (the Zalo Personal one also drops an `if` around a `slice` that already returns an empty string past the end); tests +21/-2 lines (one new file beside the Slack helper, one case added to an existing Feishu inbound test, one test beside the existing Zalo Personal inbound normalization tests). No config, state or SDK surface changes.

## Evidence

Tested at `844005b38fa` (base `upstream/main` `e68d5552923`).

An isolated QA Gateway ran the real Slack plugin against a local fake Slack API with signed Events API deliveries; the model is the mock OpenAI provider, which records each request. The scenario sends a warmup DM (so the DM has a session), then this DM, and reads the `/btw` question from the recorded model request. Same scenario on both sides.

```text
/btw QA-BTW-MULTILINE why does this fail?
  at first (a.ts:1)
    at second (b.ts:2)
```

Before (base `e68d5552923`):

```text
Status: fail
model received the /btw question as "QA-BTW-MULTILINE why does this fail? at first (a.ts:1) at second (b.ts:2)"
```

After (this PR):

```text
Status: pass
receivedQuestion: "QA-BTW-MULTILINE why does this fail?\n  at first (a.ts:1)\n    at second (b.ts:2)\n"
```

Observed result: before, the model received the stack trace joined into one line; after, it receives the three lines with their indentation.

Regression tests, one per channel, each failing on the base and passing with the fix:

- Slack: the helper whose result becomes `CommandBody` (through `textForCommandDetection`) keeps the lines of a mention-prefixed multi-line `/btw`. `prepare.test.ts` already covers the collapse of non-command text (`Please /help continue`); it is over its line cap, so the new case sits beside the helper.
- Feishu: a mention-prefixed multi-line `/btw` added to the existing DM command test in `bot.test.ts`, which checks `CommandBody` and `BodyForCommands` in the inbound context.
- Zalo Personal: `normalizeZaloInboundMessage` keeps the lines in `commandContent` (the value `monitor.ts` passes as `CommandBody`) for a multi-line `/btw` that mentions the bot.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file at 844005b38fa in the table below), plus `extensions/feishu/src/sequential-key.test.ts`, `monitor.message-handler.ingress.test.ts`, `monitor.message-handler.debounce-policy.test.ts`, `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts`, `message-handler.test.ts`, `message-handler.debounce-policy.test.ts`, and `extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts`, `ingress.test.ts`, `zalo-js.listener.test.ts`; `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, `oxfmt --check` and oxlint (type-aware) on the changed files, `git diff --check`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/slack/src/monitor/commands.test.ts` | 2.3 s (1 test, Vitest 0.49 s) | 1 ms of test time (1 test) in `changed-extensions-config-3` (16 files, Vitest 91.84 s), CI run 40428675605 at 844005b38fa |
| `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` | 25.2 s (62 tests, Vitest 23.01 s) | 19.64 s of test time (62 tests) in `changed-extensions-config-5` (3 files, Vitest 26.51 s), CI run 40428675605 at 844005b38fa |
| `extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-quote-metadata.test.ts` | 10.0 s (12 tests, Vitest 7.87 s) | 1.97 s of test time (12 tests) in `changed-extensions-config-6` (6 files, Vitest 75.03 s), CI run 40428675605 at 844005b38fa |

`bot.test.ts` is an existing file of 62 tests; this PR adds one case to an existing DM command test.

Not covered, and why:
- No run in a real Slack workspace: the author has no Slack workspace for this, and the maintained Slack e2e lane leases its workspace credentials from the maintainers' pool, which the author cannot use. The Slack run above drives the real Slack plugin and Gateway, but the Slack API is a local fake and the model is the mock provider. The mock provider records the request the Gateway sends, so the after run shows the exact `/btw` text a real model would receive; no real model was called.
- No live Feishu or Zalo Personal run. The author has no Feishu tenant or Zalo account, and the QA harness has no local API for either. In each, the fix is the same rule in the helper that produces the command body, and its regression test checks the value passed on as `CommandBody` (for Zalo Personal, `commandContent`, which `monitor.ts` passes as `CommandBody`). For Feishu, that test goes through the inbound handler.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep commentary line breaks in preamble progress text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a very visible rendering glitch in the Control UI WebChat during tool-calling turns. The assistant's text streams in correctly formatted (paragraphs, bullet lists, tables), and then at the moment a tool call begins it snaps into one long paragraph. Bold text and links survive, but every line break, list marker, and table row is flattened into a single line.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the provider resolves commentary at the tool boundary, `createReplyDelivery` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.reply-delivery.ts` emits the commentary-phase text as a keyed `preamble` item whose `progressText` had all whitespace collapsed to single spaces (`text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()`). The WebChat's `handlePreambleProgress` then takes that item as the owner of the text it had already streamed and renders `progressText` as Markdown in its place. Markdown without newlines has no paragraphs, list items, or table rows, so the block structure disappears exactly when the item replaces the stream.

The collapse was introduced with the native commentary progress work (#128793). No consumer needs it: the CLI runner path already emits multi-line commentary as `progressText`, the channel progress compositors (`pushPreambleHeadline`, `pushCommentaryProgress`) and the session-observer digest normalize their own single-line headlines, and the WebChat and history snapshot store the text verbatim. This change sends the trimmed text with its line breaks intact.

Non-goal: this does not change how commentary is phased, deduplicated, or persisted; the commentary signature used to suppress duplicate emissions still keys on the (now uncollapsed) text.

## User Impact

Pre-tool commentary in the WebChat keeps its paragraphs, lists, and tables through the tool boundary instead of collapsing to a single line. Other channels are unchanged because they already normalize the text themselves.

## Evidence

The existing "preserves aggregate commentary for providers without Responses item boundaries" expectation encoded the collapse (`"First. Second."`) and now expects the actual `\n` join. A new test streams multi-line Markdown commentary (paragraphs and a bullet list) through an Anthropic-style tool handoff and asserts both the update and end preamble events carry the text unchanged. Both fail without the fix.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe
  Test Files  34 passed   Tests  866 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-chat src/gateway/session-observer src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-progress.test.ts
  Test Files  8 passed    Tests  348 passed
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>   # clean
oxfmt --check <changed files>                 # clean
```

Observed on the 2026.9.2 release with an `openai-completions` transport driving tool-calling turns in the WebChat.

prs.title: fix(exec): macOS app node exec with timeoutSeconds 0 ends after 20 seconds
prs.body:
Related: #185429 #139706 #163978 #162789 #135272 #166652 #142874

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `exec` on a macOS app node with `timeoutSeconds: 0` ("0 disables" the process lifetime) ends after about
20 seconds with `TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown`, and the result is
lost.

## User Impact

User impact: no-expiry commands on a macOS app node return their result instead of an unknown outcome after 20 s.
The node host ships inside OpenClaw.app, so users get this with the next macOS app build. Runs stay bounded by the
Gateway invoke deadline (default 1805 s for `timeoutSeconds: 0`), which cancels the node invocation, the same bound an
explicit `0` already has.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway forwards an exec timeout of `0` to the node as `timeoutMs: null`, documented as "no expiry". The macOS app
runs a null timeout without a timer. The node host's socket client exempted only `0` from its response deadline, so
`null` got the 20 s default. #172117 fixed every finite timeout; this is the one input it left out. The change treats
`null` like `0`.

Reach: the node host collapses an absent nested timeout into `null` before calling the app, so every `system.run`
without a nested timeout loses the node-side 20 s deadline, not only `timeoutSeconds: 0`. Those calls stay bounded
by their Gateway invoke deadline plus `node.invoke.cancel`. Example: the remote-skills bin probe uses a shorter Gateway
deadline, so nothing changes for it in practice. One accepted edge case: if the Gateway link drops mid-run, the node
host waits as long as the companion runs, as it already does for `0`.

Overlap: draft #163978 (last updated 2026-10-15) reworked the same deadline before #172117 landed and targets the
code from before it. This is the minimal residual on current main. The 20 s default for direct callers that omit
`timeoutMs`, pinned in `src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts`, is unchanged.

<details><summary>Root cause path (origin/main 2bf23407639)</summary>

- `src/agents/exec-tool-timeout.ts:24-27`: `timeoutSeconds: 0` gives `runTimeoutMs: 0`, sent as nested `timeoutMs`.
- `src/gateway/node-registry.system-run.ts:71-81`: `timeoutMs <= 0` becomes `null` ("preserving null for no expiry").
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:328`, `:747`: the exec host request carries `timeoutMs: null`.
- `src/infra/exec-host.ts:59-65`: only `=== 0` disables the deadline; `addTimerTimeoutGraceMs(null)` is `undefined`, so the `?? 20_000` fallback applies.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ExecHostExecutor.swift:139`, `ShellExecutor.swift:212-219`: a nil timeout runs with no timer.

The test imports the Gateway normalizer on purpose, so the wire value in the test is the one the Gateway really
sends.

</details>

## Evidence

Focused test `src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` "waits past the 20 s fallback for a Gateway no-expiry run". It runs a
real Unix-domain-socket peer with fake timers: it derives `timeoutMs` from `normalizeSystemRunInvokeParams`, advances a
fake day, then replies.

- Base (`src/infra/exec-host.ts` from origin/main), `pnpm test src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` (excerpt, lines in log order):
  ```text
  FAIL   infra  src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts > exec host real UDS boundary > waits past the 20 s fallback for a Gateway no-expiry run
  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
          "code": "TIMEOUT",
          "message": "TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown",
  Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)
  ```
- Branch, `pnpm test src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.socket.test.ts`:
  ```text
  Test Files  4 passed (4)
       Tests  26 passed (26)
  ```
- Neighboring node-host suites on the head, `pnpm test src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.environment.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 59 passed (59)`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: 33 phases ok, including format, lint, typecheck core and core tests, and import cycles. The dead export scan fails on `extensions/browser/src/browser/client.types.ts: BrowserGraphicsDevice`, a file this diff does not touch (not re-run at base).

### Real behavior proof (macOS app node)

After (app built from this head, `81b290c95b4`):
- Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/40554854403 (mac/proof-3, macos-26-intel, Xcode 26.6)
- App: OpenClaw.app 2026.10.7 debug (adhoc); bundled private runtime build `2026.10.7-81b290c95b4b-2026-10-27T17-58-06.000Z`
- Node: `clientId openclaw-macos`, packaged app, node `8f10b9bf3873…`
- Request: `node.invoke system.run`, `sh -c 'sleep 45; echo done'`, `timeoutMs: 0`
- Result: `ok: true`, `exitCode: 0`, `timedOut: false`, `stdout: "done\n"`; gateway logged `node.invoke 55802 ms`; scenario `PASS 3 head: done after 59s`

Before (same command on a real installed app node, pre-patch):
- App 2026.10.6, commit `41c5d94f722c`, built `2026-10-22T19:35:02Z`; bundled runtime `Contents/Resources/runtime` contains `request.timeoutMs === 0 ? 0 : …` only.
- Gateway `exec` tool, `host=node`, `timeoutSeconds: 0` → `TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown` after ~20 s; no stdout.

Gaps: the after case ran through `node.invoke system.run` (the same Gateway → node host → exec-host route, including the patched `exec-host.ts`), not the agent `exec` tool, because the hosted runner exposes no `exec` tool on `/tools/invoke`. The `exec` tool on a patched app node was not run. The test peer proves the TypeScript transport, not Swift policy or native execution. The Swift side needs no change because it already runs a nil timeout without a timer, but its behavior on the cancel path (whether the child dies when the socket closes) was not observed natively.

prs.body:
Supersedes #185434, thanks @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: commands on macOS app nodes lose their result after 20 seconds when `exec` requests `timeoutSeconds: 0`.

## User Impact

User impact: no-expiry commands can return their output after 20 seconds. Gateway invocation bounds, cancellation, configured policy, finite timeout caps, and explicit socket deadlines remain in effect. Delivery requires a macOS app build with the updated bundled node runtime; no Team Gateway deploy is needed for the fix itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway normalizes zero to `timeoutMs: null`, which Swift already executes without a process timer. The socket client must distinguish an omitted timeout (`undefined`, retaining its 20-second default) from explicit zero or null. This repairs that decision at the existing owner without changing Swift or execution policy.

The existing socket tests now cover null alongside zero and verify that an explicit finite socket deadline still overrides null. Production LOC delta: 0; test LOC delta: 0. No new machinery or test harness was needed.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41365038582) and the required `openclaw/ci-gate` pass for `a908e6808cdc25fdc3e3c42f4791952831c1f1ae`, including changed-test lanes, type/lint checks, baseline ratchets, and security checks.

- Main checked at `71becfa19f32a86eb3e62bccf713f5be7107884f`: traced exec timeout resolution → Gateway zero-to-null normalization → node-host forwarding → socket response deadline → Swift nil timeout handling.
- Red before: the null case in `src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts` fails on main because a response timer is installed (1 failed, 15 passed; wrapper 2.59 s).
- Green after: `pnpm test src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 passed, wrapper 1.76 s. The real Unix socket receives output after a simulated day; explicit 50 ms override, finite command budgets, omitted default, and cancellation retain coverage. CI timing is reported by the PR checks.
- Touched-file lint, format check, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, final local snapshot against the main SHA above): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. It reviewed the changed files plus the Gateway, node-host, exec timeout, and Swift callers; it did not execute tests.
- Baseline failure retained: the additional `src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` run fails in the malformed matching response case with `read ECONNRESET` at its peer cleanup assertion. The same failure reproduces with the unmodified main socket owner (1 failed, 7 passed). Its finite 5,000 ms command and explicit 1,000 ms response budget are unchanged by this patch; other sibling cases pass. Socket reset behavior remains an investigated baseline uncertainty, not a passing check.
- Local node-host test preparation began compiling the broader worker bundle and was stopped to respect production-host limits. PR CI owns node-host and broad proof. This Linux host has no macOS toolchain; no native app execution or Swift build is claimed. The TypeScript transport regression does not prove native process cancellation.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` only and was never checked out, installed, built, or run. This replacement was implemented independently on main and credits Mitchell Etzel in the commit.

## What Problem This Solves

The committed Talk transcript test fails while valid automatic title work is still running.

## User Impact

CI waits for the existing title request to finish persisting its result. Product runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the title request through its existing runtime publication and join successful persistence. A control-only completion cannot finish the test. Preserve both real Talk transcript calls, the exact generated title, and the single OpenAI-compatible transport request.

The 27-line test allocation covers the completion observer and cancellation cleanup.

## Evidence

prs.title: improve(ui): move Meetings filters and page actions into popovers on phones
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Reading notes is the main phone use for Meetings, but at phone width the filter block pushes the first meeting about 425 px down the page, and Meeting capture and Refresh take a row of their own. Rows spend three lines on metadata. In the Reader, a long title takes four lines, the content sits 20 px inside the page margin, and the transcript search wraps. ## User Impact On phones: - **List:** a search field and a filter button replace the filter block, with the first meeting about 145 px higher. Search still submits on Enter. The button shows when a filter is active. - **Filter popover:** all five filters, the hint, Filter and Clear filters. Fields, dates and buttons are 40 px with 16 px values, which is iOS's input floor. At 320 px each date takes its own row, because a full date and its calendar don't fit in half the width. The date fields' calendar uses the selects' chevron color, stroke, size and inset, and still opens the picker. Safari on macOS draws no calendar icon, so it keeps its own field, and clicking a date opens its calendar. - **Three-dots:** Meeting capture and Refresh. - **Rows:** people and utterance count share a line, with people truncating first. The In progress badge stays on the first meta line, and text sits closer to the rail. - **Reader:** content aligns with the page margin and the title uses the page-title size. Downloads share a row when they fit: they do at 390 px and stack at 320 px. Transcript search stays on one row, with Clear search when present. The three-dots glyph sits centered in its button. From 641 to 768 px the title, search and rows share one left edge. The empty state keeps its copy and link. Desktop widths don't change. ## Why This Change Was Made The filter fields stay in the same form, so search and filters still submit together through the URL, with free-text IDs as before. Three-dots stays in the page header in this PR; it moves into `FloatingHeaderActions` from #190409 once that lands. ## Evidence Screens use a new `--fixture meetings` mock with a live capture, a silent capture, a meeting with no summary and a second page. Taps are real, at 390 px. These images show today's top bar until the floating header PR lands. The Reader's tab track is removed by #190370, not here. | Before | After | Filter open | Reader, Transcript | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | Active filter, dark | Filter open, CRT | Date picker, real Safari | Filter at 320 px, long values | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Real Safari 27: 390 px window, default mock theme, OS pointer events. An OS click on Started on or after opened Safari's calendar, and choosing the 25th set the date. Three-dots and the Reader were checked the same way on an earlier revision. The CRT filter popover was checked with an OS click too: fields and hint stay legible over the list. Local checks: oxfmt and stylelint on touched files, `tsgo:ui`, Meetings unit and browser tests (41 passed), `meetings` and `transcript-library` e2e (9 passed, including a phone test). `ui:check-performance:base` reports the CSS budget, which main already exceeds; this change adds to it.

prs.title: fix(computer): preserve field and browser typing whitespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Computer input silently trims intended text in **`set_value.value` and `browser_type.text`**. Leading/trailing whitespace is lost, and whitespace-only input becomes empty.

Disable trimming only at those two payload readers, preserving arbitrary strings, including explicit empty input. Identifier normalization remains unchanged. No model-facing tool parameter schema/description, SDK exports, configuration, permissions or native-integrity changes.

Original repair by @huidongchen148; contributor commit preserved. A maintainer follow-on narrows this PR to the two independently proven actions. **`browser_dialog` is unchanged from main and left for separate work**; its proposed change, regression and documentation were removed. Current main is merged to include the separate native-reference prerequisite #190700.

## Evidence

[Built-Gateway/native and real-Chromium proof, independent readbacks, screenshots, and dialog blocker receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190594#issuecomment-6565424242).

Both runtimes fully built with `pnpm build`, including Control UI. Frozen main `8873aeb433fd931c87e2bd5ba45f38b67215ae27`; exercised candidate production `86e56ed7709669581c580fb39d9ac2f57baa2c38`. The narrowing restores only the unproven dialog path; **both remaining field/typing code paths are identical to the exercised candidate**. No new runtime execution is claimed for the narrowing commit.

| Proven action | Main twice | Candidate twice | Independent outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native `set_value` | mixed text trimmed; whitespace-only becomes empty | exact mixed and whitespace-only text retained | Read-only observer reads the file saved by real Mousepad through computer keyboard actions |
| `browser_type` | mixed text trimmed; whitespace-only becomes empty | exact mixed and whitespace-only text retained | Actual Chromium textarea readback button renders and POSTs its real `value` |

Explicit-empty and ASCII controls pass on both refs. Unchanged keyboard `type` also passes actual clipboard readback on all four native runs.

The proof uses actual admitted agent turns, built computer-tool execution, real managed CUA/X11/Mousepad, and managed Chromium in an isolated Debian VM with its normal namespace sandbox. Public DOM-event routing activates the fixture readback button; normal `browser_type` uses `insert_text` with actual observed DOM capabilities. No fabricated refs, mocked tool/transport/native provider, direct setter, sandbox disabling, seccomp changes or capability bypass. The deterministic local model fixture supplies ordinary tool calls; this is not a live-provider claim. Physical desktops, macOS/Windows and Wayland were not exercised.

**Deferred dialog receipt:** main twice and candidate twice failed before acceptance: CDP `Runtime.callFunctionOn` timed out during real prompt activation, followed by `COMPUTER_REFUSED_browser_action_unavailable` after `Page.enable` timed out and no dialog capability was minted. The linked receipt retains those results. Empty-versus-omitted prompt semantics are **not fixed or claimed by this narrowed PR**.

Committed regressions extend the existing native reference and browser mapping cases through actual `createComputerTool.execute` request construction. Both use valid observations and check exact mixed whitespace, whitespace-only and explicit-empty payloads. Existing coordinate-free click, stale-reference rejection, browser drag and schema-guidance assertions remain. Shared refs and observation fixtures remove duplicated setup: **tests +36/-37 (net -1)**, source **+10/-2**, docs +2 against merged main `8873aeb433fd931c87e2bd5ba45f38b67215ae27`; no allocation added.

Final focused schema/common-parameter checks: **68/68 passed**, 8.75s runner wall with cached compiler outputs. On frozen main, both extended cases fail specifically because `"  hello\t\n"` is dispatched as `"hello"` (2 expected failures, 34 skipped; 7.43s runner wall). Candidate passes all mixed, whitespace-only and empty iterations. Targeted Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted CI owns exact-head broader checks.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. Revert restores trimming; no persistent migration or new contract. Blast radius is native field values and browser typing text only; identifiers, dialog handling and other actions retain main's semantics.
