prs.title: fix(config): preserve whitespace in secrets provider file paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set … --provider-source file --provider-path` trims the path before writing `secrets.providers.*.path`, so a credential file whose name ends in a space is silently rewritten to a neighboring path (or a missing path). The same trim hits `--provider-command` and `--provider-trusted-dir`, and resolution/exec validation previously re-trimmed via `resolveUserPath`, so a whitespace-bearing trusted directory could authorize the wrong neighbor executable.

## User Impact

User impact: provider builder paths keep their literal whitespace (matching `--batch-file` / `connect --target-file`), so trailing-space filenames no longer retarget the wrong secret file on disk. Whitespace-bearing `trustedDirs` authorize only executables literally inside that directory; the nearest neighbor without the trailing space is rejected before process creation. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildProviderConfig` used `opts.providerPath?.trim()` (and `.trim()` on command / `normalizeStringEntries` on trusted dirs) before persisting into config. File/exec resolution used trimming `resolveUserPath`. Alix’s `#167116` already preserved connect target-file literals via `readNonBlankString`; this applies the same contract to the secrets provider builder and adds `resolveUserPathLiteral` for resolution + `assertSecureExecCommandPath`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (`resolveUserPathLiteral`), `src/secrets/exec-provider-path-validation.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.ts`; regressions in `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.test.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI on head `bd8f2287fe3`: **shipped file-provider consume** (literal path beats distinguishable neighbor) + **real upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.5`** (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: file+exec providers still load/validate/resolve) + exec allow/deny-before-start (below)
- Dedup: no open PR on provider-path whitespace; distinct from Alix `#167116` (connect only) and `#167118` (UTF-8 config bytes)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. `--provider-path` ending in a space must be stored literally.
2. **Shipped CLI must consume that literal file-provider path** (not a trimmed neighbor): `node openclaw.mjs config set … --dry-run` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readSecureFile(resolveUserPathLiteral(path))`.
3. Existing `secrets.providers` written by published **v2026.10.5** must still load, validate, and resolve after upgrading the same state dir to this PR head.
4. (Already shown) Whitespace-bearing trustedDirs authorize only the literal helper; neighbor rejected before process creation.

### Canonical reachability path (file-provider consume)

Packaged `node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.<alias> --provider-source file --provider-path '<path with trailing space>' --provider-mode json` → persist literal path → `config set channels.discord.token --ref-provider <alias> --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json` → `collectDryRunResolvabilityErrors` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readFileProviderPayload` / `resolveUserPathLiteral` → `readSecureFile`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses `readNonBlankString` for builder persistence and `resolveUserPathLiteral` for file (and exec) resolution. No direct library `resolveSecretRefString` call in this proof — only the packaged CLI entrypoint.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`, OpenClaw 2026.9.9) on head `bd8f2287fe3` with Node v24.16.0; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Paths redacted to `/tmp/oc168261.*/…`.

### Exact steps — shipped file-provider consume + neighbor

```bash
# Node 24.16+ (packaged CLI) on head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"
SECRET_SPACE="$ROOT/secret "          # trailing space
SECRET_NEIGHBOR="$ROOT/secret"        # no trailing space
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"GOOD"}' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' 'NOT_JSON_WRONG' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"   # distinguishable: INVALID JSON
chmod 600 "$SECRET_SPACE" "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"

node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$SECRET_SPACE" --provider-mode json

# Shipped consume (resolvability via packaged dry-run — neighbor is invalid JSON)
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json

# Flip: corrupt spaced file; leave neighbor as VALID {"token":"WRONG"}
# Expect dry-run FAIL (still targets literal spaced path; trim would succeed via neighbor)
printf '%s\n' 'CORRUPT_NOT_JSON' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"WRONG"}' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
```

### Evidence after fix — shipped file-provider consume

```text
=== SETUP (file-provider consume) ===
node=v24.16.0
head=bd8f2287fe3
secret_space_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
secret_neighbor_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret'
space_content= {"token":"GOOD"}
neighbor_content= NOT_JSON_WRONG

=== A1) Persist file provider with trailing-space path ===
Updated secrets.providers.vault. No gateway restart needed.
stored_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
stored_source= file
stored_mode= json

=== A2) Shipped consume: config set --dry-run (neighbor INVALID JSON) ===
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true },
  "refsChecked": 1,
  "skippedExecRefs": 0
}
consume_dryrun_exit=0
# Success with invalid neighbor ⇒ packaged CLI read the literal spaced file (GOOD).

=== A3) Flip: spaced file CORRUPT; neighbor VALID {"token":"WRONG"} ===
{
  "ok": false,
  "errors": [{
    "kind": "resolvability",
    "message": "Unexpected token 'C', \"CORRUPT_NOT_JSON\\n\" is not valid JSON",
    "ref": "file:vault:/token"
  }]
}
flip_dryrun_exit=1
flip_result=DENIED_AS_EXPECTED (literal spaced path still targeted; neighbor not used)

=== A4) Restore spaced GOOD; consume green again ===
restore_ok= True
restore_dryrun_exit=0
```

### Exact steps — data-model compatibility / existing settings

```bash
# Simulate pre-fix stored settings (stable-style: no edge whitespace on provider path)
STATE2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-compat.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE2" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE2/openclaw.json"
LEGACY_SECRET="$ROOT/legacy-secret.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"apiKey":"LEGACY_OK"}' > "$LEGACY_SECRET" && chmod 600 "$LEGACY_SECRET"
# write openclaw.json with secrets.providers.legacy.path = $LEGACY_SECRET (no edge whitespace)
# and channels.discord.token SecretRef → legacy:/apiKey

node openclaw.mjs config get secrets.providers.legacy
node openclaw.mjs config validate --json
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider legacy --ref-source file --ref-id /apiKey --dry-run --json

# Ordinary (no-whitespace) path still works via CLI; legacy provider retained
ORD="$ROOT/ordinary.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"ORDINARY"}' > "$ORD" && chmod 600 "$ORD"
node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.ordinary \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ORD" --provider-mode json
```

### Evidence after fix — compatibility / upgrade retention

```text
=== B) COMPAT: legacy provider paths (no edge whitespace) on this head ===
wrote_legacy_config= /tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json
legacy_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/legacy-secret.json'

--- config get (loads existing stored provider) ---
{ "source": "…", "path": "…", "mode": "…" }   # redacted by CLI; loads OK

--- config validate ---
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json", ...}
validate_exit=0

--- shipped consume of legacy file provider ---
legacy_consume_ok= True
legacy_resolvability= True
legacy_refsChecked= 1
legacy_consume_exit=0

--- ordinary no-whitespace provider + legacy retained ---
Updated secrets.providers.ordinary. No gateway restart needed.
ordinary_path= /tmp/oc168261.*/ordinary.json
legacy_still_present= True
legacy_path_unchanged= True
ordinary_consume_ok= True
ordinary_consume_exit=0
```


### Exact steps — real upgrade from published v2026.10.5

```bash
# Authentic release binary (npm registry, not a hand-built fake):
#   npm install openclaw@2026.10.5
#   → OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
#   npm pack shasum 158d80b43644e2feba2a50647803562aa394e080
#   tarball sha256 dbb1bdcf2346292e25f672822b6a9928c234909abe6fee0df5fc4556e769d40e
export PATH="/path/to/node-v24.16.0/bin:$PATH"
OC_OLD=…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs   # 2026.10.5
OC_NEW=…/openclaw.mjs                         # PR head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"

# 1) ON v2026.10.5 — create real secrets.providers (file + exec)
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"UPGRADE_OK","apiKey":"LEGACY_KEY"}' > "$ROOT/vault.json" && chmod 600 "$ROOT/vault.json"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/helpers"
# exec helper speaks protocolVersion 1
cat > "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' '{"protocolVersion":1,"values":{"secret":"EXEC_OK"}}'
EOF
chmod 755 "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh"

node "$OC_OLD" config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ROOT/vault.json" --provider-mode json
node "$OC_OLD" config set secrets.providers.execvault \
  --provider-source exec --provider-command "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" \
  --provider-trusted-dir "$ROOT/helpers" --provider-json-only

node "$OC_OLD" config validate --json
node "$OC_OLD" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
node "$OC_OLD" config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider execvault --ref-source exec --ref-id secret --dry-run --json --allow-exec

# 2) UPGRADE: same OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR / openclaw.json → PR head packaged CLI (no rewrite)
```

prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck only; the throwaway Gateway run above predates them. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

Follow-ups: `openclaw automations runs <id> --follow` (needs a polling loop, abort handling and a `--json` decision); live agent-turn transcripts; `public-schema.ts` is at its line cap, so the new live-output schema types are not re-exported there and a maintainer may prefer a sibling file.

prs.title: fix(outbound): failed media spool removals leave artifacts behind without a warning
prs.body:
Closes #153498.

## What Problem This Solves

When the outbound queue cannot remove a spooled media artifact after delivery or during orphan pruning, the existing best-effort cleanup catches the error without a diagnostic. The file remains on disk without an explanation.

## User Impact

User impact: operators get a warning explaining unexpected leftover media artifacts without enabling verbose logging. Delivery and cleanup policies do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Report unexpected removal failures through the existing `outbound/deliver` subsystem. Already-missing artifacts stay quiet; cleanup remains nonthrowing and continues through the remaining artifacts. Delivery, queue settlement, retention, retries, and recipient-facing text are unchanged.

This preserves @changeroa's original commit and applies its warning to the current inline release owner, without restoring the removed forwarding helper. The issue was reported by @aniruddhaadak80. Existing expiry tests share one fixture; the release regression uses the real filesystem and diagnostic reporter rather than an added removal mock. Production delta: **+7**; test delta: **-1**, against main `00bfbf1f7ca54`.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway before/after evidence and replay details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160806#issuecomment-6534944589); [rebuilt exact-head integration proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160806#issuecomment-6535055440).

Built Gateway proof uses the shipped `send` WebSocket RPC and a task-owned HTTP channel plugin. A real non-root filesystem permission refusal occurs only after the fixture accepts the media; the queue then performs its ordinary settlement and cleanup. The baseline retains the artifact silently; the candidate retains it with a warning. Successful cleanup and already-removed artifacts are controls. No private helper is called, no queue or logging owner is replaced, and no Telegram behavior is claimed.

The local channel fixture deliberately changes directory permissions to expose the operating-system failure. This proves a diagnostic for refused cleanup, not that the change repairs permissions or guarantees deletion.

Main and candidate each exercised refused cleanup twice, successful cleanup twice, and already-gone cleanup twice. All 12 sends delivered identical media bytes and returned successful native receipts. Main produced no removal warnings; the candidate produced exactly one per refused cleanup and none for the controls. Both Gateways shut down cleanly.

The focused suite passes **13/13** on the candidate; the same regression on main fails specifically because the warning is absent (**12 passed, 1 failed**). Focused type-aware lint, format, and whitespace checks pass.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully removes the diagnostic change; there is no migration, new configuration, dependency, SDK surface, or stored-data format. Blast radius is the shared outbound queue's media-release logging, including orphan pruning.

prs.body:
<!-- Related: none -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI Browser panel feels laggy. Soft-keyboard, composition and pasted text sent faster than the Gateway round trip goes out as one request per chunk and queues, so characters land hundreds of milliseconds late. In screenshot fallback, every action also waits a fixed 350 ms before the refresh.

## User Impact

User impact: queued soft-keyboard, composition and pasted text reaches the page sooner, and fallback frames refresh sooner. Desktop key presses still go one request per key, as on main. A live screencast is unchanged for clicks, slow typing, panel open and tab switch. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Text queued behind an in-flight request joins one `insertText`. A click or key starts a new batch, so order is kept.
- The post-action refresh counts the time the action already took toward the 350 ms settle delay. If a capture is still pending, retries stay 350 ms apart.

"Typing" means text input events (soft keyboard, composition), not desktop key presses. prs.title: fix(active-memory): recognize Italian recall intent
prs.body:
Fixes #188550

## What Problem This Solves

With `mode: "escalate"`, active-memory never recalled anything for Italian messages: the localized recall-intent table covered Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish and French, but had no Italian entry, so `hasRecallIntent()` always returned false and the escalation lane never fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

`LOCALIZED_RECALL_INTENT_PATTERNS` in `extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts` is the owner for non-English recall intent, with one entry per language holding `intent`, `future` and `retrospective` patterns. Italian is added with the same three-pattern shape and the same suppression rule (a future cue suppresses unless a completed past discussion is also present):

- intent: recall questions (`ti ricordi …`, `come avevamo deciso …`) and completed-discussion phrases (`ne abbiamo parlato`, `ieri … parlato`, `la settimana scorsa … deciso`);
- future: `domani`, `la prossima settimana`, `tra due giorni`, `più tardi`, `in futuro`;
- retrospective: the past-time marker combined with a discussion verb, which re-admits `Ne abbiamo parlato ieri e abbiamo scelto …`.

Ordinary and future-only Italian sentences (`Domani prenotiamo il volo`, `Ricordati di comprare il pane domani`) stay quiet.

## User Impact

Italian users on `escalate` mode get recall for genuine retrospective questions, while future-facing reminders keep their existing behaviour.

## Evidence

Head `c8bd7a060b`, Node 26.12.1 (single commit, rebased on current `main`).

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/active-memory/escalation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
103 passed

# reverting escalation.ts to the branch base:
× recognizes recall intent in "Ti ricordi cosa abbiamo deciso per il volo?"
× recognizes recall intent in "Ne abbiamo parlato ieri e abbiamo scelto l'hotel in centro."
× recognizes recall intent in "Come avevamo deciso di configurare il database?"
3 failed | 100 passed

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <2 touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <2 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The added cases cover Italian positives (question, completed discussion, retrospective decision) and Italian negatives (future reminders, ordinary narration).

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Followed the existing per-language entries in `LOCALIZED_RECALL_INTENT_PATTERNS`, added the Italian triple, and extended the shared positive/negative tables. The implementer understands the code: the future cue suppresses a bare plan, and only a completed past discussion re-admits the sentence.

prs.title: docs(gateway): add Windows notes for running multiple Gateways
prs.body:
Adds a `## Windows notes` section to the multi-gateway guide.

Running two Gateways on one Windows host works, but five Windows-specific behaviors
are not covered by the current page and each one cost real debugging time:

1. **Environment inheritance** — a Gateway started from a shell inside another Gateway
   process inherits `OPENCLAW_*` and silently reads the first instance's config/state.
2. **`gateway.tailscale.mode` is copied with the config** — `serve` on both instances
   contends for port 443 and the second one exits with code 78.
3. **engines range `>=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1`** — version managers without a matching
   shim fail the install even when a suitable runtime is on disk.
4. **Scheduled-task ACLs** — a task registered from an elevated shell gives the
   interactive user read-only access, so `Disable-ScheduledTask` fails with
   *Access is denied* / `0x80070005`.
5. **`200` on `/` proves nothing about tokens** — the UI and health endpoints answer
   before RPC auth; isolation must be proven with an authenticated `gateway call health`.

Docs only; no code or behavior changes. Happy to trim any item that the maintainers
consider out of scope.

Fixes: newly spawned child sessions show a frozen activity ring while their workspace is being prepared.

## User Impact

The activity ring animates from accepted startup through execution. Real turn, global-lane, and recorded capacity waits still show a paused ring labeled **Queued**. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued presentation was inferred from execution not having started yet. A visible worktree child can spend several seconds preparing its checkout before that marker is set. Project accepted preparation as active instead, retaining explicit wait facts for queued presentation in both RPC-backed and native runs. Execution clocks, admission, cancellation, and scheduling are unchanged; no CSS is changed.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix(discord): channels named in non-Latin script resolve to a different channel
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord channel configured or looked up by a name without ASCII letters or digits (for example "чат") resolves to a different channel, so its per-channel settings, including its tool policy, apply to the wrong channel.

## User Impact

User impact: guild channels named in Cyrillic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean and other non-Latin scripts now resolve to the channel with that name, at Gateway startup and in `openclaw channels resolve`. A name that matches no channel stays unresolved instead of taking another channel's ID, and so does a key made only of emoji or punctuation. The live directory search returns only matching channels for a non-Latin query. ASCII keys resolve exactly as before, to the same channel IDs, including `general` for a channel named "общий-general" and "alerts" for "⚠️-alerts". The channel label in agent context for an emoji-prefixed name such as "⚠️-alerts" becomes `#alerts` instead of keeping the emoji's variation selector.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord channel name matching used an ASCII-only slug, which turns every non-Latin name into an empty string, so all such names matched each other and the first one in API order won. At startup the configured entry (mention gating, system prompt, tool policy) is then bound to that channel's ID.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187148 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188003 fixed the same class of problem for directory searches by comparing lowercase NFC text. Discord already has a Unicode-aware slug for channel labels, `normalizeDiscordDisplaySlug` (NFC, lowercase, keeps letters, marks and digits of any script). Channel resolution and the live directory search now use it for keys with letters outside ASCII, and resolution refuses an empty slug, as guild name matching already does.

For the review's Decision needed, this implements Preserve existing ASCII selection: ASCII keys keep the ASCII-only match (`extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.ts:156-160`), so every existing ASCII key binds the same channel ID as before. A resolved name key is bound to its channel ID (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171829), and that binding is what keeps other channels and threads with the same name from using the key's policy; changing which channel an ASCII key binds, or leaving it unbound, would move or widen its policy on upgrade. A key with other letters (Japanese letters followed by `-ops`) never matches by its Latin part, which on the base bound it to a channel named `ops`.

The slug now drops emoji variation selectors and the keycap mark (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/allow-list.ts:88-91`). They are combining marks, so the slug kept them: emoji-only names such as "⚠️" and "❗️" both slugged to the selector and matched each other. Now they slug to "" and are refused.

## Evidence

Head `7a984a8f337` (base `upstream/main` `f9257898216`). The Gateway runs below are at `1fca9f16ee6`; the later commits change only tests and the test-line allocation. All data is synthetic: no real Discord account or token, no provider key.

### Real Gateway, message in, tool call, reply out

Each run started an isolated Gateway (`openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured`) with its own state directory, config and synthetic bot token, inside `unshare -rn` (loopback only). Discord was Crabline's local Discord server (REST and Gateway WebSocket) behind a small proxy that names its channels and lists the guild's channels for startup resolution. The model was a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in: on each turn it asks for `exec` with `echo tool-ran-<probe>`, whether or not `exec` was offered, and replies with the tool output once one arrives, so the Gateway's own tool gate decides. `tools.exec.mode` is `full` so a granted `exec` runs without a human approval; the only command ever run is that `echo`.

Guild: новости …10, чат …20, general …30, a thread named "чат" in новости …50 and one in general …60. Config: `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, guild `tools.deny: ["exec"]`, key `чат` = `{ requireMention: false, tools: { allow: ["exec", "read"] } }`, key `general` = `{ requireMention: false }`. One message was sent into each channel or thread.

Startup log, base:

```text
[discord] channels resolved: 135000000000000011/135000000000000010 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:новости; aliases:135000000000000011/чат), 135000000000000011/135000000000000030 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:general; aliases:135000000000000011/general)
```

This PR:

```text
[discord] channels resolved: 135000000000000011/135000000000000020 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:чат; aliases:135000000000000011/чат), 135000000000000011/135000000000000030 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:general; aliases:135000000000000011/general)
```

| Target | Before (base) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| чат …20 | admitted; `exec` not offered (13 tools); the turn stops on "unknown tool" | `exec` offered (5 tools) and run; reply `ack probe-chat tool-ran-probe-chat` |
| новости …10 | `exec` offered and run; reply `ack probe-news tool-ran-probe-news` | dropped, no model turn |
| general …30 | `exec` not offered; "unknown tool" | same |
| Thread "чат" in новости …50 | `exec` offered and run (inherits новости) | dropped |
| Thread "чат" in general …60 | `exec` not offered; "unknown tool" | same |
| Key `чат` removed | чат, новости and the новости thread dropped; general and its thread without `exec` | same |
| Policy moved to key `новости` | новости and its thread run `exec`; чат dropped | same |

With this PR, `exec` ran only in чат; no other channel or thread, including the two threads named "чат", got it. On the base it ran in новости and in the thread under it.

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9

The same config and guild ran on the latest stable release (`openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm with `@openclaw/discord@2026.10.9` installed by `openclaw plugins install`). It resolves чат to новости like the base. The thread rows differ from the base because 2026.10.9 predates https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171829, so threads still match keys by name:

| Target | 2026.10.9 |
| --- | --- |
| чат …20 | `exec` run |
| новости …10 | admitted (the `чат` key resolves to it), `exec` not offered |
| general …30 | `exec` not offered |
| Thread "чат" in новости …50 | `exec` run |
| Thread "чат" in general …60 | `exec` run |

The config hash was the same before and after the run. Then this branch ran on that state directory and config: `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` upgraded the agent database (schema 25 to 38) and changed no `channels.discord` setting. The Gateway (with the branch's bundled Discord plugin, which overrides the installed npm copy) logged the same "channels resolved" line as above and gave the same rows as "After": `exec` ran only in чат, and neither thread named "чат" got it.

### Tests

The case in `resolve-channels.test.ts` and the non-Latin query in `directory-live.test.ts` fail on the base and pass on this branch; the other 14 tests in the two files pass on both. In CI at `458bd869c7f` (run 41011581230) the two files took 50 ms and 25 ms of test time.

Checks at `7a984a8f337`: the two touched test files and `provider.allowlist.test.ts` (the startup channel-binding tests, with the resolver mocked), oxlint and format check on the changed files, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

The test-lines ratchet failed on the previous CI run because the base was already over its ceiling. This PR's net test lines (+40) are covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/discord-unicode-channel-resolution.txt`; they are the regression tests above.

<details>
<summary>Per-case test notes, CLI and directory search, local timing</summary>

`resolve-channels.test.ts` "matches channel names by their letters in any script" covers a non-Latin name, a missing non-Latin name, "alerts" for "⚠️-alerts", `general` for "общий-general", `ops` for the first channel whose ASCII letters are "ops" ("чат-ops", as on the base), a Japanese `-ops` key that stays unresolved, and an emoji-only key "⚠️" that stays unresolved next to a "❗️" channel. Without the selector strip the "⚠️" key binds "❗️" and the test fails.

CLI and directory search at `458bd869c7f`, same synthetic guild (новости …01, чат …02, general …03):

```text
$ openclaw channels resolve --channel discord --kind group --json "900000000000000001/чат"
before: "id": "910000000000000001", "name": "новости"
after:  "id": "910000000000000002", "name": "чат"

$ openclaw directory groups list --channel discord --query чат --json
after: channel:910000000000000002 "чат"   (новости and general are not returned)
```

A single local run with `--maxWorkers=1` at `7a984a8f337`:

| Test file | Tests | Wall (Vitest duration) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.test.ts` | 10 | 6.9 s (4.7 s) |
| `extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts` | 6 | 7.0 s (4.8 s) |

</details>

Not covered: a real Discord guild. Messages went through Crabline's local Discord server, not Discord itself; the shared Discord end-to-end lane leases a QA guild with one fixed text channel and cannot hold the non-Latin channels this needs. The upgrade run used this branch from a source checkout on the 2026.10.9 state, not a packaged release.

Left for a follow-up: guild names are still matched on the ASCII-only slug, so a guild name that mixes scripts matches by its Latin part alone, and a guild name written only in non-Latin script does not resolve by name at all (it fails closed and never binds another guild). That behavior predates this change and is not touched here. A directory query made only of emoji or punctuation still returns every channel, as every non-Latin query did on the base.

prs.title: feat(ui): start diagnostic conversations from the command palette
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators need a way to prepare local OpenClaw diagnostics from the Control UI without copying CLI output by hand.

## User Impact

**Cmd/Ctrl+K → Diagnose a problem** opens a new conversation with the selected agent and a sanitized diagnostic attachment. The user describes the issue and sends it when ready. Opening the command does not start a model turn or a repair, and the previous conversation's draft is preserved.

The action requires administrator access and a locally executing agent. Existing tool permissions remain in force. Offline Gateways and incompatible remote or sandbox execution continue to use `openclaw triage` on the Gateway host.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shares the existing Doctor subprocess and diagnostic export collectors, then uses ordinary session creation and attachment handoff. The session starts in the running installation's directory; its normal local CLI retains the Gateway's profile. Diagnostic collection does not change configuration. The large generated-validator diff is mechanical renumbering from the new request schema.

## Evidence

**[Full lifecycle video — 1:04 at original speed (1×)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188125#issuecomment-6516251661)**

- Focused Gateway, export, triage, palette, and attachment tests passed.
- Core/UI typechecks, focused lint, and the test-line budget passed.
- Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Real isolated Gateway: the command prepares an ordinary empty session, the Doctor subprocess returns findings, no chat send or title inference is requested, and returning restores the original draft. Seeded credentials are absent from the diagnostic context. The complete lifecycle recording also covers an explicit send, a real model inspecting the installed source in Read Only mode, and the completed diagnosis.
- Base UI `16f4fe84` and updated UI `2338de54` were served by an isolated Gateway using synthetic configuration. The palette images are crops of the captured frames; the conversation images retain the full viewport.

prs.title: fix(memory): one binding's dmScope pauses memory search for every agent
prs.body:
Closes #188120
Closes #163581

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory search stops returning results for every agent when one route binding sets `session.dmScope`, including a binding set to `"main"` that isolates nothing.

## User Impact

User impact: adding DM isolation for one agent (for example a shared team bot) no longer switches off the `rememberAcrossConversations` default, drops `sessions` from the memory sources, or leaves the index `mismatched` for the other agents on the Gateway. A binding with `dmScope: "main"` behaves like global `"main"`.

Unchanged: global `session.dmScope` isolation still defaults recall off for every agent, a binding with an isolating scope still defaults it off for its own agent, and an explicit `true` or `false` always wins. Recall still only reads the agent's own private transcripts (`session-search-visibility.ts` is not touched).

Upgrade note: an agent whose index was built while another agent's binding had switched its default off now gains the `sessions` source. Upgrading from 2026.10.9 needs no action, because those indexes already get an automatic rebuild for main's chunking change, and that rebuild picks up the new sources (shown below). Without such a rebuild, the change is an ordinary configuration mismatch, and memory search prints the existing `openclaw memory status --index --agent <id>` hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveRememberAcrossConversations` is the only owner of this default. Memory search sources, Active Memory and Doctor all read it. It treated any binding with a `session.dmScope` as install-wide isolation. Routing applies a binding's session override only to the agent it routes to (`resolveAgentRoute` → `choose(binding.agentId, …, binding.session)`), and `"main"` isolates nothing. So the gate now counts a binding only for its own agent (`normalizeAgentId`, matching config validation and routing), and only when its scope is not `"main"`. Core already reads binding scopes this way in `src/infra/outbound/agent-delivery.ts` (`binding.session.dmScope !== "main"`).

The narrow config type now declares `bindings` with the fields it reads, which replaces the `unknown` property probes. Production code is a net 5 lines shorter. Docs (`reference/memory-config.md`, `concepts/active-memory/enabling.md`, `concepts/main-session.md`) and the config help text describe the per-agent rule. The new QA scenario `qa/scenarios/memory/remember-across-binding-scope.yaml` is the Gateway proof below.

## Owner decision: per-agent reading of the #110597 gate

#110597 turns the implicit default off when DM isolation is configured, because "recall is per-agent/private-shaped rather than per-sender". This PR keeps that reasoning and applies it at the same per-agent granularity that routing and recall already use:

- A binding's `session.dmScope` only changes session keys for the agent it routes to. Another agent's DMs still land in its single `agent:<id>:main` session.
- Recall candidates for an agent come only from that agent's own private transcripts (`filterMemorySearchHitsBySessionVisibility` drops other owners, group/channel sessions, and transcripts with a shared alias). Another agent's isolation adds no candidate to this agent's recall and removes none.
- An agent whose DMs all land in one session is the shape the docs call single-user. If several people DM it, they already share that one session (`concepts/session.md`: "Without it, all users share the same conversation context"). Turning recall off for that agent does not make that setup safe.
- Still default off: global isolation for every agent, and an isolating binding for its own agent. An explicit value still wins.

If the memory owner prefers to keep the install-wide gate, #188120 still needs a fix: adding a binding for one agent should not leave every other agent's existing index `mismatched` with no matches. The alternative would be to keep `sessions` indexed for those agents and turn off only the recall step, which is a larger change across the source and index layers. I can rework this PR that way if that is the call.

## Evidence

### Gateway proof: `remember-across-binding-scope` QA scenario

Real Gateway child, `qa-channel`, `mock-openai`, Active Memory with `toolsAllow: [memory_search]`. The config has no global `session.dmScope` and no explicit `rememberAcrossConversations`, so the implicit default decides. Bindings: agent `peer` gets the direct conversation `dm:remember-scope-peer` with `dmScope: per-channel-peer`; agent `qa` gets the rest of the account with `dmScope: main`.

Flow:
1. Seed a private fact in qa's direct conversation (`agent:qa:main`), a group-only fact in a qa channel, and a peer-only fact in the peer's direct conversation (routed to `agent:peer:qa-channel:direct:dm:remember-scope-peer`).
2. `sessions.reset` on `agent:qa:main`, then `memory index --agent qa --force --verbose` (offline, inside `restartAfterStateMutation`).
3. Ask the recall question in the same qa direct conversation. Assert the reply, the Active Memory helper transcript (accepted `memory_search` evidence) and every mock model request in that turn.
4. Switch qa's binding to `dmScope: per-channel-peer`, restart, and ask again from the same conversation.

Branch head (`9a644c1fe9` on `d67aa60864`), `pnpm openclaw qa suite --scenario remember-across-binding-scope --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1`:
```
- Status: pass
  - [x] keeps another agent's isolating binding out of this agent's recall default
{"verdict":"PASS","scenario":"remember-across-binding-scope","channel":"qa-channel","provider":"mock-openai","gateway":"ephemeral-child",
 "peerRoutedToOwnSession":"agent:peer:qa-channel:direct:dm:remember-scope-peer",
 "qaIndex":"Memory Index (qa)\nProvider: openai-compatible (requested: openai-compatible)\nModel: text-embedding-3-small\nSources: memory (MEMORY.md + $QA_ROOT/workspace/qa/memory/*.md), sessions (current transcripts + retained transcript artifacts)\n\nMemory index updated (qa): 3 files indexed.",
 "privateRecallAccepted":true,"groupExcluded":true,"peerAgentExcluded":true,
 "recallReply":"Protocol note: you usually want lemon pepper wings with blue cheese for QA movie night.",
 "isolatedSession":"agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:dm:remember-scope-private","isolatedRecallStarted":false,
 "isolatedReply":"Protocol note: I do not have enough context to say what you usually want for QA movie night."}
```
The scenario asserts:
- The helper transcript contains `memory_search`, the private fact and the pre-reset qa session id.
- The helper transcript contains neither the group nor the peer marker, nor either session id.
- No mock model request in the recall turn (helper and reply) contains the group or peer marker. The reply request carries `<active_memory_plugin>` with the private fact.
- After qa's own isolating binding, the turn routes to `agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:dm:remember-scope-private`, writes no helper transcript, and no model request contains the private fact or `<active_memory_plugin>`.

Gateway log from a rerun of the same scenario with `OPENCLAW_QA_KEEP_TEMP=1` (previous head on `d33f833650`, `$QA_ROOT` redacted). The two seed turns outside qa's direct session are skipped, the recall turn returns a summary, and the turn after the binding switch is skipped:
```
[plugins] active-memory: recall skipped reason=destination-not-allowed        # qa group seed
[plugins] active-memory: recall skipped reason=destination-not-allowed        # peer direct seed (peer defaults off)
[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down                                     # offline memory index
[gateway] ready
[plugins] active-memory: agent=qa session=agent:qa:main … start timeoutMs=15000 queryChars=117 searchQueryChars=117
[plugins] active-memory: agent=qa session=agent:qa:main … done status=ok elapsedMs=3862 summaryChars=74
[gateway] config.patch write … changedPaths=bindings restartReason=config.patch
[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
[gateway] ready
[plugins] active-memory: recall skipped reason=destination-not-allowed        # qa direct turn after its own isolating binding
```

Same scenario with `config-utils.ts` from `origin/main` (`d33f833650`, red), failing where the peer's binding turns qa's default off:
```
- Status: fail
qa index did not include its session transcripts: Memory Index (qa)
Provider: openai-compatible (requested: openai-compatible)
Model: text-embedding-3-small
Sources: memory (MEMORY.md + $QA_ROOT/workspace/qa/memory/*.md)
Memory index updated (qa): 1 file indexed.
```
The fixed file was copied back afterwards and `cmp` matches the committed file; the branch run above was rebuilt from the committed tree.

### Live CLI on an isolated home

<details>
<summary>2026.10.9 vs this branch, binding-scope cases and upgrade (from the previous revision; resolver unchanged since)</summary>

`OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under a temp dir, `env -i`. Two agents `main` and `support`, memory provider `none`, `main`'s `MEMORY.md` holds "The synthetic project codename is Apricot Lighthouse." Each block starts from `openclaw memory index --force` for both agents with no bindings.

Release 2026.10.9 (bug):
```
$ openclaw config set bindings '<support-only Telegram DM binding, dmScope per-channel-peer>' --strict-json
Updated bindings. No gateway restart needed.
$ openclaw memory status --json
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index sources changed","code":"sources","owner":"configuration"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index sources changed","code":"sources","owner":"configuration"}}
$ openclaw memory search apricot --agent main
Memory index is stale: index sources changed (owner: configuration, code: sources). Search results may be incomplete. Run: openclaw memory status --index --agent main. Rebuilding uses keyword indexing only and does not call an embedding provider.
No matches.
$ openclaw config set bindings[0].session.dmScope main
$ openclaw memory status --json
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index sources changed","code":"sources","owner":"configuration"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index sources changed","code":"sources","owner":"configuration"}}
```

This branch, same steps:
```
$ openclaw memory status --json   # no bindings
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
$ openclaw config set bindings '<support-only Telegram DM binding, dmScope per-channel-peer>' --strict-json
Updated bindings. No gateway restart needed.
$ openclaw memory status --json
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index sources changed","code":"sources","owner":"configuration"}}
$ openclaw memory search apricot --agent main
0.397 MEMORY.md:1-2
- The synthetic project codename is Apricot Lighthouse.
$ openclaw config set bindings[0].session.dmScope main
Updated bindings[0].session.dmScope. No gateway restart needed.
$ openclaw memory status --json
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
```

Upgrade: index built on 2026.10.9 with the support binding already present, then the same home switched to this branch (`config validate` → valid, `doctor --fix --non-interactive` → exit 0):
```
$ openclaw memory status --json   # 2026.10.9
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
$ openclaw memory status --json   # branch
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index chunking implementation changed","code":"chunking_version","owner":"openclaw","versionOrder":"older"}}
{"agent":"support","sources":["memory"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"mismatched","reason":"index chunking implementation changed","code":"chunking_version","owner":"openclaw","versionOrder":"older","chunkingVersionOnly":true}}
$ openclaw memory search apricot --agent main
Automatic memory index repair was requested. To rebuild manually, run: openclaw memory status --index --agent main. Rebuilding uses keyword indexing only and does not call an embedding provider.
0.397 MEMORY.md:1-2
- The synthetic project codename is Apricot Lighthouse.
$ openclaw memory status --json
{"agent":"main","sources":["memory","sessions"],"indexIdentity":{"status":"valid"}}
```
(The chunking-version mismatch comes from main vs 2026.10.9 and is unrelated to this change.)
</details>

### Regression test red on base

`pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/config-utils.test.ts`, with `config-utils.ts` from `origin/main`:
```
×  resolveRememberAcrossConversations > limits a binding with dmScope per-channel-peer to its own agent
AssertionError: expected { main: false, support: false } to deeply equal { main: true, support: false }
×  resolveRememberAcrossConversations > limits a binding with dmScope main to its own agent
AssertionError: expected { main: false, support: false } to deeply equal { main: true, support: true }
Tests  2 failed | 26 passed (28)
```
With the fix: 28 passed. The existing `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` case (a binding for the same agent defaults off) still passes unchanged. `config-utils.ts` and its consumers are unchanged between the old base and `d67aa60864`.

### Checks

- The CI failure on the previous head was `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` → assertion-safety: the fix removed both grandfathered assertions in `config-utils.ts`, so its baseline entry is dropped. `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main`: max-lines, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-exports, config-docs and plugin-inventory OK. See Gaps for the other three.
- `pnpm test` for `config-utils.test.ts`, `extensions/active-memory` and `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts`: 4 shards passed (4 m 22 s). qa-lab `scenario-catalog.test.ts`, `scenario-catalog-memory-recall-proof.test.ts`, `coverage-report.test.ts` and `coverage-report.commands.test.ts`: 57 passed.
- The merge conflict was only in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. `pnpm config:docs:check` OK.
- After the rebase: `pnpm tsgo:core` (25 s), `tsgo:extensions` (29 s) and `tsgo:test:packages` (36 s) are clean. Before it, `tsgo:test:src` and `tsgo:extensions:test` were clean too, and `run-oxlint`, `docs:check-config-examples` and `docs:check-links` passed. This revision changes no TypeScript. `run-format --check` on the scenario and `git diff --check` pass.

### Gaps

- The database-dialect, test-lines and database-worker ratchets, and `check:line-cap-ratchet`, need `git cat-file --batch -z` (git ≥ 2.36). The local git is 2.34, so those ran in CI only, and commits skipped the pre-commit hook after its other checks ran by hand.
- The scenario shows that qa's `--force` index includes the `sessions` source. It does not show a search hit for the group marker. On this host, `memory search` and `memory status` under the QA CLI runner end with "process-tree cleanup unconfirmed", so group exclusion is shown on the recall output and the model requests instead. The peer's transcript stays in the peer's own agent database, and its own isolating binding keeps sessions out of even the peer's index.
- On this host, the existing `remember-across-reset-private` scenario fails on current main at its online `memory index` step ("This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership"). The new scenario runs that CLI inside `restartAfterStateMutation`. Not changed here.
- After a bindings-only `config.patch`, qa-channel kept routing the conversation to the old session key until a restart, while Active Memory read the new binding immediately. The scenario restarts after the patch. Not investigated further.

AI-assisted implementation.

prs.title: feat(workboard): make card note and comment URLs clickable
prs.body:
Closes #141472 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Workboard users who paste URLs or markdown links into card notes or operator comments would see dead plaintext in the Control UI, even though the notes placeholder already says "Notes, acceptance criteria, links." The same text is shown on compact cards, in the detail drawer, and in the edit-card comment list. Operators currently have to copy the URL out by hand during triage. ## Why This Change Was Made Workboard now linkifies two conservative patterns in notes and comments: - Markdown links: `[Anrop](https://anrop.no/)` - Bare `http://` and `https://` URLs Links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Other text, including newlines, stays unchanged. This is not full markdown: no bold, lists, headings, images, or HTML, and no `innerHTML`. `javascript:` / `data:` URLs stay plaintext. Balanced parentheses inside a destination are kept, so Wikipedia-style paths such as `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)` stay intact in both the markdown and bare-URL forms. Trailing `.,;:!?` on a bare URL stays outside the href. A wrapping `(https://example.com)` still leaves the surrounding parentheses as text. Clicking a link on a compact card does not open the detail drawer (the existing `a` action-target guard). Native `` links remain keyboard-activatable. The edit-card comment list uses the same linker as the drawer, so the three surfaces stay consistent. ## User Impact Operators can click research, docs, PR, and competitor URLs directly from Workboard cards instead of copying them out of notes. ## Evidence **Before** (current Control UI): notes interpolate as escaped plaintext. ![Workboard notes before, with markdown and a raw URL shown as text](https://github.com/schjonhaug/openclaw/releases/download/workboard-pr-141481-proof/workboard-notes-before.png) **After, production compact card:** markdown labels and bare https URLs become anchors on the real Workboard card renderer. Clicking `Example` opened `https://example.com/` in a new tab and did not open the detail drawer. Dummy fixture only (`example.com` / `example.org`). ![Workboard compact card after, with Example and example.org as clickable links](https://github.com/schjonhaug/openclaw/releases/download/workboard-pr-141481-proof/workboard-compact-card-after.png) Focused Control UI unit tests passed on this revision: - `vitest --project unit` on `linkify-text.test.ts` and `view.test.ts`, including: - markdown + bare https become `` - balanced parentheses in bare and markdown destinations (`Function_(mathematics)`) - wrapping parentheses around a bare URL stay outside the href - trailing punctuation stays outside autolinked URLs - `javascript:` / `data:` markdown is not turned into anchors - compact-card link click / Enter / Space do not open the detail drawer - edit-modal comments use the same linker This revision also formats the Workboard view files (`oxfmt`) and regenerates `extensions/workboard/openclaw.plugin.json` so the bundled control-ui asset hash matches the source. Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.2 before this change: card detail notes render as `

${card.notes}

`, so a note such as `[Anrop](https://anrop.no/)` is escaped text. After this renderer, that note is a real anchor.

prs.title: fix(codex): inference fails with ChatGPT fake-IP routing
prs.body:
Related: #152765, #122533 (similar Fake-IP/SSRF reports on other paths).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex inference requests can fail in the parent-local relay when a trusted DNS proxy resolves `chatgpt.com` to Fake-IP addresses, despite OpenClaw already supporting these ranges in other provider paths.

The affected operator uses **Clash Verge Rev (Mihomo-based)** with Fake-IP routing. Client and kernel versions were not captured.

## User Impact

Operators using trusted Fake-IP routing can forward Codex HTTP requests and direct WebSocket handshakes to the existing ChatGPT upstream. This PR is being marked ready for maintainer review with hosted CI still unverified; it does not establish that every local 502 has the same cause. No configuration migration or global private-network allowance is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing SDK SSRF policy only to the exact credential-free `https://chatgpt.com` origin, in both guarded HTTP fetch and the non-environment-proxy WebSocket DNS lookup. The narrow policy permits `198.18.0.0/15` and `fc00::/7`; other origins retain the default policy. Authorization revalidation, HTTPS, disabled redirects, protected-address checks and DNS pinning where the relay owns resolution remain intact. Environment proxies retain their existing DNS ownership. The ULA exception also admits real ULA destinations for this exact origin, not only Fake-IP mappings; that security-boundary tradeoff still needs a maintainer decision before merge.

The merged OAuth fix #110096 is analogous but does not cover this inference-relay call path.

## Evidence

- New transport-boundary regression: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-proxy.fake-ip.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **24/24 passed**, 4.51s Vitest / 6.08s wrapper wall time. The unpatched source failed 6 of these tests.
- Tests use production relay/SSRF logic with synthetic DNS and transport boundaries, covering IPv4/IPv6 Fake-IP, default-policy origins, loopback/LAN/link-local/metadata denial, DNS pinning, redirects, environment-proxy ownership and authorization revalidation. No upstream socket or paid inference is used.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, extension production/test typechecks and `git diff --check` passed. Full formatting passed. Full build logged completion of all phases in 153.1s; its original enclosing shell exit capture was interrupted.
- **Local full CI did not pass.** Full-repository lint reported 15 max-lines errors in files verified unchanged from base `76f4fdd41acf06621fe5b4605f67816f63a7f698`. The broad test run encountered a missing Playwright Chromium executable, database-worker heap OOM/channel failures, and other assertion/timeouts; it ended with SIGTERM after 6070.68s. The remaining test failures have **not** been proven to exist on the unpatched baseline, and the termination caller is unknown.
- Hosted CI is not claimed passing. Main hosted CI was skipped while this PR was draft; the ready-for-review transition enables broad PR CI. A subsequent local runtime replacement and real-use observations are recorded below, without changing the disclosed local full-CI gaps.

### Real-use follow-up (2026-10-13)

- **Real native model-reply smoke:** at approximately 02:13 Asia/Shanghai, one actual native OpenAI Codex request (runtime source: `codex-app-server`) returned the exact requested short marker. The native runtime identity was separately verified. This was a real model reply, not the mocked transport regression.
- **User-observed recovery after applying the local patch:** the supported runtime replacement was applied at 02:50 Asia/Shanghai. At 06:11, the operator reported that multiple newly opened sessions could converse normally. The runtime/model of those additional sessions was not independently audited.
- **Coverage limit:** these are native smoke and user-observed real-use evidence, not independent proof that the successful sample exercised the exact corrected guarded-relay policy. The contemporaneous smoke window still contained 30 blocked SSRF events and no diagnostic route-fingerprint entries. HTTP versus direct WebSocket, IPv4 versus IPv6, a fresh installation, and an upgrade from v2026.10.2 were not separately verified; no-error logs alone do not prove the fix. Full CI and complete causal/root validation are not claimed.

prs.body:
## What

Russian docs localization is wired up but nearly empty: `docs/.i18n/glossary.ru.json` was 21 entries (1.2 KB) against 107 KB for `zh-CN`, and `ru-navigation.json` did not exist at all, so the Russian sidebar fell back to English while the pages themselves were already 75% translated.

This PR fills in the two files that drive the Russian locale:

- `glossary.ru.json`: **21 → 250 entries** (1.2 KB → 18.6 KB). Existing entries and their order are preserved; 6 target terms were corrected for consistency with the pages: Compaction → Сжатие контекста, Gateway → Шлюз, Node → Нода, Plugin → Плагин, Skills → Скиллы, Webhook → Вебхук. Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.
- `glossary.ru.json` parses as valid JSON and keeps the original key order (`json.load` round-trip diff on the untouched prefix).
- Note: `check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` only validates `zh-CN` today, so this file is not CI-gated — I verified it manually as described above.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`, locale `ru`, same tree, only `docs/.i18n/ru-navigation.json` added.

| Before (`main` — no ru overlay) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-after.png) |

Behavioural comparison of the two composed configs:

```
before: tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308
after : tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308      # page inventory identical
before tabs: Get started | Install | Channels | Agents | Capabilities | Models |
             Platforms | Gateway & Ops | Reference | Releases | Contributing | Help
after  tabs: Начало работы | Установка | Каналы | Агенты | Возможности | Модели |
             Платформы | Шлюз и эксплуатация | Справочник | Релизы | Участие в разработке | Помощь
```

Only labels change; every route and its order is preserved, which is the guarantee the overlay functions (`applyLocaleNavLabelOverlay`) are supposed to give. Screenshots are generated from the composed `docs.json` (sidebar label tree), not from a live docs host, so nothing is redacted and no endpoint is involved.

prs.title: fix: name the last tool in the fallback shown when a tool run ends without a summary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent turn ends after only calling tools and the tool-free summary pass returns nothing (both attempts), the user sees a fixed placeholder: "The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions." The message gives no hint of what ran last or whether the last step worked, so users and operators cannot tell a harmless silent finish from a failed final step without opening the transcript.

## User Impact

The fallback keeps its existing sentence verbatim and appends a short digest:

| Last tool result | Appended digest |
|---|---|
| `isError === false` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (succeeded).` |
| `isError === true` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (failed).` |
| `isError` absent or `undefined` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (outcome unknown).` |

Example (interactive turn: `read`, then `exec`, then two empty summary attempts):

- Before: `The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions.`
- After: `The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions. Tool calls: 2; last: exec (succeeded).`

Unchanged: cron and other silent runs stay silent, and failed or timed-out turns keep their original outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner already holds the settled tool batch (`toolMetas`) when it builds the placeholder, so the digest is derived locally with no extra model call, no new setting and no new flag.

- Only the last tool name (truncated to 64 characters), the call count and the outcome are used. Arguments, results and tool metadata are never echoed, so the fallback cannot leak command lines or output.
- An absent `isError` is reported as "outcome unknown" and never as success. This follows the existing "outcome unknown" style and the producer contract that leaves the field absent for unknown terminal outcomes (this was the P2 finding from the automated review on the first revision, now fixed in the second commit).
- The change lives in the shared finalization owner (`settled-turn-finalization.ts`, new exported `buildSettledToolFallbackText`), so every channel that shows this fallback gets the same text.

Compatibility note: any consumer that matches the old fallback text exactly would need a prefix or substring match. I found one such assertion (`embedded-agent-runner.run-embedded-agent.finalization-scope.test.ts`) and relaxed it to `stringContaining`; the qa-lab e2e only checks `not.toContain`, and `chat.directive-tags` uses a fixture string.

## Evidence

Verified:

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.test.ts`: 23 of 23 pass locally. New tests cover no tools (plain placeholder), last tool succeeded and failed with call count, an omitted `isError` and an explicit `undefined` (both "outcome unknown"), and that tool metadata is not echoed. Existing fallback assertions were updated.
- In CI the same test file passes in the shard that runs it (32 of 33 tests in that shard pass, including the new "reports an unknown outcome when isError is absent" test).
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the touched files.

## Runtime proof (added after the first review)

One real agent turn through the locally built `openclaw agent` command (embedded runner, Windows, Node 24), run against the PR head. A credential-free local stub that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions wire format answered as follows: request 1 returned a single `read` tool call; every later request (the tool follow-up and both tool-free summary attempts) returned empty text. This is the exact path the PR changes.

Stub request log (one line per model request):

```
{"request":1,"stream":true,"tools":11,"hasToolResult":false,"respond":"tool_call:read"}
{"request":2,"stream":true,"tools":11,"hasToolResult":true,"respond":"empty-text"}
{"request":3,"stream":true,"tools":0,"hasToolResult":true,"respond":"empty-text"}
{"request":4,"stream":true,"tools":0,"hasToolResult":true,"respond":"empty-text"}
```

Gateway log lines from the same run (ids shortened):

```
settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=3527b60a... provider=stub/stub-1 - running isolated finalization
settled-turn finalization completed without a visible answer: ... - retrying 1/1 with tools disabled
settled-turn finalization completed without a visible answer: ... attempts=2/2 - using terminal fallback reply
```

Reply delivered by the run (`final` and the single payload of the JSON output):

```
The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions. Tool calls: 1; last: read (succeeded).
```

Run summary from the same output: `toolSummary: {calls: 1, tools: ["read"], failures: 0}`, `assistantTurns: 4`, `status: ok`.

Limits, stated plainly:

- The "before" text in the table above is the unchanged placeholder from the base branch; I did not capture a second run on base.
- This was the embedded agent command, not a Telegram or other channel run, so no Telegram Test Server output is attached.
- The stub is a few lines of Node I can attach or turn into a committed e2e scenario if maintainers want it.

Known CI failure, not caused by this diff:

- `settled-turn-finalization.unavailable.test.ts` ("preserves a failed cron turn and its transcript when finalization is unavailable") fails at the `assistantTranscriptOwned` assertion (`expected undefined to be true`). That test does not assert the digest text. It fails the same way locally with this PR's four original files reverted to base `a7b8ae74`, and the main run is also red across many shards. I have not root-caused it.

Not verified, stated plainly:

- `finalization-scope.test.ts` fails 8 of 8 in my local Windows environment with and without this change ("Runtime config is not prepared"), so my one-line edit to that file is unverified locally and relies on CI.
- `pnpm check` stopped at two preflight guards unrelated to this diff, and I could not complete a full `pnpm build` locally.

Offer: I can commit the stub scenario as a test if wanted.

## Maintainer decision

The automated review marks this as a product preference that needs an owner decision: should the conservative missing-summary fallback include a tool count, last tool name and known or unknown outcome? I think it is a small, safe diagnostic gain, but I am happy to adjust wording, drop the docs sentence, or close the PR if the existing message is intentional.

AI-assisted PR (written with Claude); the author owns the change and will address review feedback.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): add decision-model recall gate
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Knowledge only injects context automatically from owner-approved `knowledge_recall` summaries, and the standing index gives the main model labels but not content. This adds an opt-in **recall gate**: per user turn, a small local decision model (an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with logprobs, or a System One `/systemone` decision endpoint) sees the Knowledge page list plus the user message and picks the relevant pages. The list goes only to the decision model, never into the main prompt. It is off unless configured, and starts in `shadow` mode (log only).

### What changes

- New `plugins.entries.knowledge.config.recallGate` block: `mode` (`off` | `shadow` default | `live`), `api` (`openai` default | `systemone`), `baseUrl`, `model`, `apiKey` (SecretRef-capable via `configContracts.secretInputs`), `highThreshold` (0.85), `mediumThreshold` (0.5), `timeoutMs` (1500), `maxIndexChars` (24000), `maxCandidates` (5).
- New `before_prompt_build` handler (`recall-gate-hook.ts`), registered only when the block is present and not `off`, user-triggered turns only:
  1. Reads every current page (not `source`/`artifact`) as one label line through a new worker op `gateIndex`, using the standing index's label rules (`buildGateEntries` in `memory-index.ts`, same `promptLabel` / exact-alias handle).
  2. `api: "systemone"`: one request with one `choice` question per 254 entries plus a "None of these" option, state = the user message. Each entry's score is its option probability, so picking and scoring are a single forward reading. The top `maxCandidates` are tiered.
  3. `api: "openai"`: one selection call (the model returns entry numbers), then a one-token yes/no call per pick with `logprobs`; score = P(yes) / (P(yes) + P(no)) from top logprobs.
  4. `live`: high tier prepends the page body (existing `memoryGet` op, clipped to 2,000 chars), medium tier prepends a one-line `knowledge_lookup` pointer, low adds nothing; whole block capped at 6,000 chars. Injection goes through `prependContext` (user turn), never the system prompt, so the cached prefix is untouched.
- `openai` without logprobs (or neither answer in top logprobs): a yes counts as **medium** (pointer only), anything else low. An uncalibrated answer never injects a body.
- Whole-gate deadline (`timeoutMs`) with an abort signal; timeout, HTTP error or any failure injects nothing and never fails the turn. Authority (`access.assertCurrent`, hook lifetime, memory audience) is re-checked right before publication.
- One info log line per turn: mode, outcome, latency, entries offered, and per decision the record ID, score, tier. No message or record text.
- Same audience gate as the standing index: shared via a small extraction, `openPrivatePartition()` in `memory-index-hook.ts`. Ungranted conversations, sandboxed sessions and agents without a store never reach the endpoint.
- Docs: new "Recall gate" section in `docs/plugins/knowledge/memory-provider.md`, config row in `docs/plugins/knowledge.md`, and the "Automatic recall" trust sentence now names the gate.

### Scope boundary

- Plugin-only; no core changes.
- The standing `## Knowledge Index` in the system prompt is unchanged. Dropping it when the gate runs `live` is a possible follow-up once the gate is proven on real traffic.
- No new agent tool ("ask the gate directly"): left out to keep this PR small.
- Config surface budget: `plugin` count raised 4889 -> 4900 in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` for the 11 new `recallGate` keys; this is an opt-in feature block with no defaults that change existing behavior.

### Trust note

In `live` mode the gate injects page bodies chosen by a model, not owner-approved summaries. That is an explicit operator opt-in (`mode: "live"`), the injected block is labeled as stored records that are evidence, not instructions, and `source`/`artifact` pages and instruction-like titles are never offered. The endpoint receives page labels and the user message; docs say to point it only at a model you trust with both.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/recall-gate.test.ts`: 11/11 pass. Mocked decision endpoints cover: shadow logs and injects nothing (and logs carry no message/record text); live high body / medium pointer / low nothing for both protocols; `openai` logprob parsing incl. case/space variants and the missing-logprobs binary fallback; `systemone` request shape, 254-entry chunking, duplicate-label suffixing, probability-ordered top candidates, and "None of these" winning -> nothing injected; no-match -> single call; HTTP 503 and a hung endpoint cut at the 100 ms budget -> no injection, no throw, logged; the index text reaches only the decision request and the hook returns only `prependContext`; ungranted conversation audience and non-user triggers never call the endpoint.
- `pnpm test extensions/knowledge`: 60 files, 461 tests pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: only failure is the dead export scan flagging `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer-width-ref.tsx: loadComposerWidthEdge`, a file this PR does not touch. SAFETY ratchet, format, typecheck and tests pass.
- Local live smoke (this branch's hook, temp vault of 10 fake pages, `live` mode, `api: "systemone"`, a 4B decider checkpoint served by its own `/v1/systemone` server):

| message | top entry, score, tier | injected |
|---|---|---|
| Is Nova due for her shots? | Nova 0.80 medium | pointer |
| Turn on the TV | Living room TV 0.59 medium | pointer |
| When did I last change the oil? | Car maintenance log 0.97 high | body |
| How is the pizza oven coming along? | Pizza oven build 0.91 high | body |
| What roast do I like? | Coffee preferences 0.86 high | body |
| Book my next dental cleaning | Dr. Patel 0.20 low | nothing (miss) |
| What's the weather tomorrow? | 0.03 low | nothing |
| Tell me a joke | 0.03 low | nothing |
| What's 17 times 23? | 0.01 low | nothing |
| Who won the game last night? | Living room TV 0.08 low | nothing |

  All 6 should-hit messages rank the right page first; 5 clear the 0.5 pointer threshold. All 4 should-miss messages stay below 0.09. The dental miss is a label limit: the page label is just "person: Dr. Patel", and the gate sees labels, not bodies. Measured gate time was 410-520 ms per turn for 10 entries, including a relay hop to the remote model host.
- The same checkpoint behind the `openai` path (a chat-template shim) answered "No" to every yes/no score (P(yes) <= 0.005, even on obvious hits). It was trained on a fixed decision layout, not chat, which is why `systemone` exists. The docs point decision-format models at `systemone`.

### What was not tested

- No Gateway run; the smoke drives the hook directly against a fixture vault. Thresholds are untuned beyond this 10-page sample; `shadow` is the default for that reason.
- The `openai` path against a real chat-tuned model.
