prs.title: fix(codex): carry workspace persona and memory on the thread developer carrier
prs.body:
Builds on #140422 (skill catalog carrier) and includes its commits, merged with current `main` (that PR currently conflicts with `main` in `run-attempt-context.ts` and `run-attempt-prompt.ts`; the resolution is in the merge commit here). The persona change itself is the single commit `fix(codex): carry workspace persona and memory on the thread developer carrier`. If #140422 lands first, this rebases onto it and shrinks to that one commit. Related: #95058.

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex-backed OpenClaw agent silently loses its persona when the active model supplies its own collaboration-mode instructions. `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, and the workspace-memory pointer were carried in `turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.developer_instructions`. Codex prefers `model_messages.collaboration_modes` over that field (openai/codex#36351), so on a catalog-backed model such as `gpt-6-astra` the model never sees them, while the OpenClaw prompt report and the recorded turn context both show them as loaded.

Observed on two gateways. On the affected agent's recorded Codex rollout, every `turn_context.collaboration_mode.settings.developer_instructions` is 30,364 chars and contains `<AGENT_SOUL>`, yet no developer-role item in the model-facing history contains it. Switching the same thread to `gpt-5.6-sol` (no catalog collaboration message) makes the first developer message 37,320 chars and it contains the block. Switching a second, unrelated production agent from `gpt-5.6-terra` to `gpt-6-astra` reproduced the loss; the model reported USER, IDENTITY, SOUL, and the skills list as absent with zero tool calls, while tools stayed available.

#140422 fixes the same mechanism for the skill catalog and explicitly leaves persona and memory for a follow-up. This is that follow-up.

Prior art on the same carrier: #96773 traced the turn-scoped SOUL/IDENTITY/USER channel as the cause of an unstable message prefix (DeepSeek prompt-cache hit rate alternating between ~20% and ~99%), and #96795 proposed the same move to thread-level developer instructions before being withdrawn by its author; that issue was later auto-closed as stale, not fixed. #125783 already moved the agent-workspace `AGENTS.md` to the thread carrier for the same reason. This PR completes that move for the remaining workspace files, so it also gives those files a stable position in the prompt prefix.

## How to reproduce

1. Take any Codex-backed OpenClaw agent whose workspace has `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, and `USER.md`. Set its model to a Codex catalog model that ships its own collaboration-mode text. `openai/gpt-6-astra` does; `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-5.6-terra` do not. You can check the agent's Codex home:

   ```bash
   jq '.. | objects | select(.slug? == "gpt-6-astra") | .model_messages.collaboration_modes' <codex-home>/models_cache.json
   ```

   Non-null means the model will replace caller collaboration instructions.
2. Start a fresh session (`/new`) and send:

   ```text
   Without opening files or using tools, quote one short line each from the SOUL, IDENTITY and USER content already in your instructions.
   ```

3. On `main` the model reports the files as missing (or paraphrases the chat history), while `openclaw system-prompt` and the OpenClaw prompt report both list the files as loaded. The recorded rollout confirms where they vanish:

   ```bash
   F=$(ls -t <codex-home>/sessions/$(date +%Y/%m/%d)/rollout-*.jsonl | head -1)
   jq -c 'if .type=="turn_context" then {model:.payload.model, collab_has_soul:(.payload.collaboration_mode.settings.developer_instructions//""|contains("<AGENT_SOUL"))}
          elif (.type=="response_item" and .payload.role=="developer") then {dev_chars:(.payload.content|map(.text//"")|join("")|length), dev_has_soul:(.payload.content|map(.text//"")|join("")|contains("<AGENT_SOUL"))}
          else empty end' "$F"
   ```

   Expected on `main` with `gpt-6-astra`: `collab_has_soul: true` on every `turn_context`, `dev_has_soul: false` on every developer item.
4. Switch the same agent to `gpt-5.6-sol` (no gateway restart needed) and repeat step 2: the quotes come back and the first developer item now has `dev_has_soul: true`.
5. With this branch, repeat step 2 on `gpt-6-astra`: the quotes come back with zero tool calls, the turn's `collaboration_mode.settings.developer_instructions` no longer carries any OpenClaw workspace text, and the first developer item contains `<AGENT_SOUL>` and `<available_skills>`.

Automated form: the added cases in `run-attempt.skills.test.ts`, `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts`, and `run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts` fail against the pre-change plugin code and pass with it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persona and memory pointer now ride the thread developer carrier (`thread/start` and `thread/resume` `developerInstructions`) after the generic policy, exactly like the skill catalog. The existing refreshable section from #140422 is generalised from `skillsInstructions` to `refreshableInstructions` = skills catalog + persona block + memory pointer, in that order, so there is one refresh path and one post-compaction restore path instead of two. The collaboration-mode slot no longer carries any OpenClaw workspace text; only the cron collaboration text remains there.

Behavior change, intentional: native Codex sub-agents now inherit the persona and memory pointer through the thread carrier, the same way they already inherit `AGENTS.md` and the skill catalog. The previous "turn-only, never inherited" property was a side effect of using a field the model can replace, not a designed isolation boundary. Docs say so explicitly.

The file loader, privacy filters, size budget, and `<AGENT_SOUL>` rendering in `attempt-context.ts` are unchanged; only the carrier moved.

## Maintainer decision (carried over from #140422)

ClawSweeper blocked #140422 on a product decision: whether native Codex children may inherit the thread-carried catalog. This PR makes the same choice for persona and memory and documents it as intentional. The previous "turn-only, never inherited" behavior was a side effect of using a field the model can replace, not a designed isolation boundary; the same thread carrier already hands children `AGENTS.md`.

## User Impact

- Agents on catalog-backed models (`gpt-6-astra` today) get their SOUL, IDENTITY, USER, and memory guidance back without switching models.
- Editing SOUL/IDENTITY/USER reaches a live conversation on the next turn, including incognito threads, without `/new` and without a policy-change refusal.
- After a native compaction the current persona is re-delivered, matching the skill catalog behavior.
- Native Codex sub-agents now see the parent agent's persona and memory pointer.

## Evidence

- New regressions (fail on the pre-change code, pass after):
  - `run-attempt.skills.test.ts`, `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts`: thread start and resume `developerInstructions` contain `<AGENT_SOUL>` and the memory pointer after the generic policy and skills; collaboration settings no longer carry them.
  - `run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts` (real Codex binary against a recorded Responses wire): a model whose catalog owns collaboration instructions still receives the persona; an edited SOUL reaches a live incognito thread; after compaction the current persona is delivered again.
- Existing suites in `extensions/codex/src/app-server` for run-attempt, thread lifecycle, compaction, turn params, attempt context, and client runtime pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` on the changed files pass.
- Live gateway verification: with this branch deployed and the affected agent switched back to `gpt-6-astra`, a fresh Telegram turn's first developer message was 38,889 chars and contained SOUL, IDENTITY, USER, and the skills list; the model quoted all three files with zero file reads (its only tool call was the message send).
- Prompt snapshot fixtures regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`; the Codex happy-path fixture now shows `developer_instructions: null` in the turn collaboration settings and the persona in the thread developer instructions.
- Docs updated: `docs/concepts/system-prompt.md`, `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference.md`, `docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`, plus the in-code bootstrap notice.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep emoji avatar initials intact
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes broken avatar initials when dashboard authors or the assistant name start with emoji or another supplementary Unicode character. Dashboard cards and collapsed environment chrome selected one UTF-16 code unit, displaying a replacement glyph instead of the leading character.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both renderers now use the existing grapheme helper. Dashboard capitalization and shell casing stay with their respective owners. Tests exercise normal bootstrap and session-list inputs.

## User Impact

Emoji, flags, joined emoji and supplementary letters retain complete initials. Existing lowercase, capitalization, default-name and environment visibility behavior is preserved. The existing code-point fallback remains unchanged on browsers without `Intl.Segmenter`.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(codex): use the literal bound workspace cwd for plugin discovery
prs.body:
Fixes #190076

## What Problem This Solves

`createCodexPluginsTool` resolved the workspace for native-plugin discovery with `binding?.cwd?.trim() || options.context.workspaceDir?.trim() || ...` (`native-plugin-tool.ts`). The bound cwd is stored untrimmed (`app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts` persists `cwd: params.cwd` verbatim at session start), so this leaf trim rewrote the session's literal workspace identity before building the `plugin/list` request. The Codex app-server then scanned the trimmed impostor directory for marketplace plugins instead of the real one — discovery silently returns nothing for a workspace whose name carries edge whitespace.

## Solution

Use `readNonBlankString` on each fallback level. Blank or whitespace-only values still fall through to the next source (`context.workspaceDir`, then the configured default workspace), but non-blank values flow verbatim into the discovery `cwds` request parameter. This matches the whitespace-preserving convention already used for the app-server binding `workspaceDir` in `conversation-binding-data.ts`.

## Impact

- Marketplace plugin discovery scans the literal bound workspace directory.
- Fallback semantics for blank/whitespace-only values are unchanged.
- No other consumer of the binding store is affected: the stored record itself already kept the raw cwd.

## Evidence

Red-green on a pristine `origin/main` worktree (remote runner, vitest):

- **Before:** 1 failure — `expected cwds ["/bound/company"] to equal [" /bound/company "]` in the `plugin/list` request.
- **After:** `native-plugin-tool.test.ts` 9/9 passed; consumer regression `plugin-marketplace-discovery.test.ts` 5/5 passed.

Real behavior proof (2026-10-30): the shipped tool, driven against the pinned `codex-cli 0.164.0` app-server (`plugin/list` over stdio, no mocked catalog), returns `literal-ws-bundle@literal-ws` for a session bound to `/tmp/pr188122-proof/ws/company `, while the `.trim()` selection returns the sibling's `trimmed-sibling-bundle@trimmed-sibling`. Full transcript: [#issuecomment-6524133566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188122#issuecomment-6524133566).

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187554 (configured directory identity) and #187739 (session cwd identity). Sibling sweep PRs: #187751, #187766, #187777, #187816, #187825.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep literal node-binding cwd values without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190067

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex CLI node-conversation binding record persisted the session cwd after `.trim()` (`conversation-binding-data.ts`), the record reader re-trimmed it on restore (`normalizeOptionalString`), the session-file discovery summary trimmed it too (`node-cli-sessions.ts` `readSessionFileSummary`), and the resume path trimmed it again right before spawning (`node-cli-sessions.ts`: `cwd: ... params.cwd.trim()`). A session whose true cwd is a literal whitespace-padded directory (e.g. `/workspace/project `) was therefore discovered, written, read, and resumed as the WRONG directory: the spawned `codex exec resume` runs in the trimmed impostor, which usually does not exist. Same defect class as the merged literal-path fixes #187739, #187554, and #187777.

## Solution

Use `readNonBlankString` (the same helper the app-server branch of this file already uses for `workspaceDir`) at every site that handles the binding cwd: **discovery** (`readSessionFileSummary` keeps the session_meta `payload.cwd` verbatim), **write** (persist the raw cwd into the binding record), **read** (restore the raw cwd), and **resume spawn** (pass the literal cwd to `runCodexExecResume`). Blank or whitespace-only cwd values still omit the field / fall back exactly as before: `readNonBlankString` keeps the trim-based blank check and only preserves the value, so the old `""`-is-falsy behavior at both write and read is unchanged.

## Impact

- Session discovery and binding records preserve the session's literal cwd identity end to end.
- `codex exec resume` spawns in the directory where the session actually lived, even when its name carries edge whitespace.
- Identity-comparison sites elsewhere trim both operands and are unaffected by verbatim storage.

## Test growth

No net test lines: the regression coverage rides on existing tests instead of adding new ones. The diff is `6 insertions / 6 deletions` across three existing test files, with no new test cases; the earlier 71 added test lines are gone, and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.

- Discovery keeps the literal `session_meta.cwd`: `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` "keeps history usable with hydrated cwd" now uses a whitespace-padded rollout cwd (existing assertion).
- Resume passes the binding cwd to the spawn: the same file's "anchors relative CODEX_HOME for legacy/catalog-user commands" now resumes in a `project `-style directory (existing spawn-cwd assertion).
- Binding write: `commands.test.ts` "binds only a listed Codex CLI node session" now asserts the stored record carries the discovered literal cwd.
- Binding restore: `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` "revalidates a queued node binding that is …" now restores a literal cwd (existing resume-argument assertion).

## Evidence

### Shipped runtime proof: discovery and resume through the real CLI, Gateway, and node host

Entry points are shipped product surfaces: a real `openclaw nodes invoke --node … --command codex.cli.sessions.list` / `codex.cli.session.resume` (CLI → Gateway `node.invoke` → paired node host). The Gateway and node host ran the production `dist` built from the reviewed head with `scripts/build-all.mts`; the node host is `openclaw node run` and advertised `codex.cli.sessions.list` + `codex.cli.session.resume`.

Fixture: a genuine session created by the real Codex CLI running inside `…/work/codexproj ` (trailing space), so the rollout's `session_meta` is Codex's own output. A sibling directory `…/work/codexproj` carries `identity.txt=TRIMMED-DIR`, the literal directory carries `identity.txt=LITERAL-DIR`; a `/proc` watcher records the real spawned Codex process tree's cwd and the marker it sees.

| Observation (same fixture, same CLI, same node host) | head `ee4d6c3e5` | base `3cd0dd638` |
|---|---|---|
| `codex.cli.sessions.list` session `cwd` | `…/work/codexproj ` (literal, trailing space) | `…/work/codexproj` (trimmed) |
| `codex.cli.session.resume` with binding `cwd` = `…/work/codexproj ` → Codex banner `workdir:` | `workdir: …/work/codexproj ` | `workdir: …/work/codexproj` |
| `/proc/<pid>/cwd` of spawned `codex exec resume` (node wrapper and native binary) | `[…/work/codexproj ]`, marker `LITERAL-DIR` | `[…/work/codexproj]`, marker `TRIMMED-DIR` |

Head transcript (abridged; the base leg runs the identical commands from the base `dist`):

```
$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.sessions.list --params '{"limit":5}'
{ "ok": true, "payload": { "sessions": [ { "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…", "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj " } ] } }

$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.session.resume \
    --params '{"sessionId":"01a18f8e-…","cwd":"/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ","prompt":"…"}'
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj 
model: gpt-5.6-sol
provider: openai
session id: 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7
user
continue in the literal directory
# the provider hop then fails: 403 "Country, region, or territory not supported"

# /proc watcher, spawned process tree
pid=211617 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] identity=[LITERAL-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … - 
pid=211637 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] identity=[LITERAL-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … -
```

Base transcript (same commands, base `dist`):

```
$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.sessions.list --params '{"limit":5}'
{ "ok": true, "payload": { "sessions": [ { "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…", "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj" } ] } }

$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.session.resume \
    --params '{"sessionId":"01a18f8e-…","cwd":"/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ","prompt":"…"}'
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj
session id: 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7

pid=583566 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume … -
pid=583589 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume … -
```

What the capture proves and what it does not: Codex's own `workdir:` banner and the kernel-observed `/proc/<pid>/cwd` show the CLI was launched in the literal directory on this head and in the trimmed sibling on the base commit — exactly the user-visible difference. The model turn is not part of the claim; this machine's region blocks `api.openai.com` (403 "Country, region, or territory not supported"), so the run stops at the provider hop after loading the genuine session in the recorded directory. Setup facts, disclosed because they are not product behavior: the isolated Gateway used the operator opt-in `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["codex.cli.session.resume"]` (the documented dangerous-node-command allow, needed for a direct `nodes invoke`), and the one-time node pairing was approved with `openclaw nodes approve`. Binding serialization and restoration to that same resume argument are covered by the existing tests above and by the Control UI persistence capture below.

### Binding persisted and restored through the shipped Control UI

Entry point: the shipped Control UI (`openclaw dashboard` issues the owner handoff URL), a real Gateway built from the reviewed `dist`, a paired node host (`openclaw node run`), and a genuine Codex 0.164.0 session created inside `…/work/codexproj ` (trailing space). The only UI action was: open the node's Codex catalog row, type a message, press send. The Control UI calls the shipped `sessions.catalog.continue` RPC, which installs the Codex plugin's session binding.

The Gateway persisted the binding in its SQLite store (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, table `current_conversation_bindings`); the row is inspectable:

```
binding_id:        generic:webchat<US>default<US><US>agent:main:harness:codex:node-session:ea0f1088de7be187158b1b7ea154048bb85bcf2e30e6d7862400df57b3ae5793
target_session_key: agent:main:harness:codex:node-session:ea0f1088…5793
metadata.data:     {"kind":"codex-cli-node-session","version":1,
                    "nodeId":"ff118971…7008a",
                    "sessionId":"01a19233-7502-7512-b65b-fd1fa5f782c7",
                    "agentId":"main",
                    "cwd":"/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj"}
```

Then the Gateway was restarted (the binding existed only on disk), the same adopted session was reopened in the Control UI, and a message was sent. The plugin restored the binding and continuation spawned Codex in the stored cwd — the kernel-observed process tree:

```
pid=1539699 cwd=[/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message …/last-message.txt 01a19233-…-fd1fa5f782c7 -
pid=1539725 cwd=[/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message …/last-message.txt 01a19233-…-fd1fa5f782c7 -
```

The turn then stops at the same region-blocked provider hop described above (403), after the session was loaded in the bound directory.

Compatibility with existing state:

- The same store was opened by the pre-fix build `3cd0dd638` (the released 2026.10.9 line): the pre-fix reader restored the same row and spawned `codex exec resume … 01a19233-…` in the same cwd, so the store written by the fix build is readable by existing code without migration (no schema change, `kind`/`version` unchanged).
- For this session the stored `cwd` is exactly the value the pre-fix writer produces: Codex's own app-server catalog already normalizes the thread cwd, so the fix's writer stores `/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj` unchanged. Existing rows written by the pre-fix build therefore take the same read path.
- Latest published stable `openclaw@2026.10.9` does not bundle the Codex extension (67 bundled extensions, no `codex`), so there is no released producer of this data model; `3cd0dd638` is the pre-fix behavior for it.

Known capture gap: the two asks above needing a messaging channel are environment-blocked here. The literal-cwd *binding write* path runs through the `/codex resume … --bind here` command, which requires a channel that implements `bindings.resolveCommandConversation` (Discord/Telegram/Matrix/LINE/Feishu/iMessage). This host has no leased Telegram/Discord QA credentials (the shared Convex credential broker is unavailable), and the webchat surface is not a binding channel by design, so the shipped-Control-UI capture necessarily goes through the Codex catalog path, which receives an already-normalized cwd from Codex's app-server. Literal cwd at the writer/reader boundaries is covered by the existing tests, and literal cwd at the node resume boundary by the direct node capture; a channel-credentialed or maintainer-run `/codex resume --bind here` capture is required to show the literal value stored through the binding itself.

Scope note: the Codex app-server catalog normalizes `cwd`, so the catalog-continue binding path stores an already-normalized value; literal whitespace preservation is what the direct node `codex.cli.sessions.list`/`codex.cli.session.resume` capture above shows, and what the writer/reader tests assert.

### Red-green for the consolidated tests

Remote Linux runner, `vitest run <file> --maxWorkers=1`. With only these test edits applied and the two production files reset to `3cd0dd638`, the coverage fails; on the reviewed head it passes.

Base (`3cd0dd638` production files):

- `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` — 3 failed: both "anchors relative CODEX_HOME for legacy/catalog-user commands" cases (spawn cwd expected `…/project `, got `…/project`) and "keeps history usable with hydrated cwd" (listed cwd trimmed).
- `commands.test.ts` — 1 failed: "binds only a listed Codex CLI node session (listed: true)" (stored record cwd trimmed).
- `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` — 4 failed: every "revalidates a queued node binding that is …" case (restored binding reached resume with a trimmed cwd).

Head `ee4d6c3e5`:

- `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` → 1 file passed (23.7s).
- `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` → 4/4 passed (15.1s).
- `commands.test.ts` → 1 file passed (525s wall for that file; the touched case is one of its fast unit tests).

### Checks

- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 3cd0dd6380a1a1586c6db4574b6fc231eb3367df --no-merge-base` → `Test lines OK: 6287170; ceiling: 6330844`.
- `git diff --check` clean.

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187739, #187554, and #187777. Sibling sweep PRs: #187751, #187766, #187816, #187825.

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: fix(memory): resolve literal extra-memory root paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes openclaw/openclaw#189914

## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeConfiguredMemoryExtraPaths` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/config-utils.ts`) trimmed every configured extra-memory root with `.trim()`. Memory `extraPaths` are operator-authored filesystem identities: a literal directory whose name carries edge whitespace (e.g. `/srv/notes `) was rewritten to a different, typically nonexistent directory before `path.resolve`. The dedup key `` `${configuredPath}\0${pattern}` `` was also computed from the trimmed value, so two genuinely distinct literal roots such as `/srv/notes` and `/srv/notes ` silently collapsed into one entry, and the other directory was never indexed for memory search.

## Solution

Stop trimming the path. Keep the blank guard (`configuredPath.trim()` still decides whether an entry is kept) but store and key the raw value — the `readNonBlankString` convention used across the codebase (blank-check via trim, value preserved). Glob patterns are still trimmed; a pattern is not a filesystem identity. Updated the helper doc comment and every consumer expectation that encoded the old trimming behavior:

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts` (shared normalizer consumer)
- `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` (memory-search config consumer; previously expected `" docs "` → `"docs"`)
- `docs/reference/memory-config.md` documents the literal-path contract and how padded entries from earlier releases now resolve.

## Impact

- Memory search/index roots now point at the literal configured directory instead of a trimmed impostor.
- Distinct literal roots keep separate dedup keys; last-policy-wins for truly identical keys is unchanged.
- Blank or whitespace-only entries are still dropped exactly as before.
- Existing padded entries such as `" docs "` now select the literal `" docs "` directory; the docs note tells operators to correct entries that relied on the old trimming.

## Evidence

Unit tests (remote runner, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ... --maxWorkers=1`):

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/config-utils.test.ts` + `internal.test.ts`: **68/68 passed** (wall 48s).
- `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts`: **39/39 passed** (wall 66s) — this is the consumer assertion that failed the prior head's `checks-node-changed-2` job at line 323.

Shipped CLI proof (built dist `2026.10.9-07bc3fe8c`, real `openclaw memory` CLI, FTS-only `provider: "none"`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Fixture: workspace with `notes/` (trimmed sibling), `notes /` (trailing-space literal root) and `archive/` (ordinary root), `memory.search.extraPaths = ["notes ", "archive"]`.

**Fresh configuration (head):**

```
$ openclaw memory index --agent main --force
Memory index updated (main): 2 files indexed.
$ openclaw memory status --agent main --index
Extra paths: …/workspace/notes , …/workspace/archive
Indexed: 2/2 files · 2 chunks
$ openclaw memory search beta-space --agent main
0.415 notes /NOTE.md:1-2
literal content: beta-space marker
$ openclaw memory search alpha-notes --agent main
No matches.
$ openclaw memory search delta-archive --agent main
0.471 archive/NOTE.md:1-2
ordinary content: delta-archive marker
```

**Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, data written by the published release):**

Published `openclaw@2026.10.9` (8b18b55) with the same config trims the entry and indexes the impostor:

```
Extra paths: …/workspace/notes, …/workspace/archive
$ openclaw memory search beta-space --agent main
No matches.
$ openclaw memory search alpha-notes --agent main
0.877 notes/NOTE.md:1-2
trimmed sibling content: alpha-notes marker
```

After `openclaw doctor --fix` (documented pending-schema upgrade step) and the head build on that same state dir, existing data loads (`Dirty: no`) and the literal root takes over:

```
Extra paths: …/workspace/notes , …/workspace/archive
Indexed: 2/2 files · 2 chunks
$ openclaw memory search beta-space --agent main
0.415 notes /NOTE.md:1-2
literal content: beta-space marker
$ openclaw memory search alpha-notes --agent main
No matches.
$ openclaw memory search delta-archive --agent main
0.471 archive/NOTE.md:1-2
ordinary content: delta-archive marker
```

Ordinary roots keep indexing and searching normally in both legs, and the literal root survives an in-place upgrade of the existing store.

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187554 (hooks `extraDirs` — "the configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity") and #172869 (cron cwd CLI). Sibling PRs from the same sweep: #187751, #187766, #187777, #187816, #187825.


---

## Decision requested (not an approval claim)

This PR changes the interpretation of configured `memory.search.extraPaths` entries (stop trimming edge whitespace so a literal root keeps its filesystem identity). That is a **behavior change to an existing configuration contract**, so it needs an owner decision before merge — the `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` label reflects that, not a code-quality issue.

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | A configured `extraPaths` root with edge whitespace resolves to the literal directory instead of a trimmed impostor; distinct literal roots keep separate dedup keys. | Operators who relied on the old trimming must correct padded entries (documented in `docs/reference/memory-config.md`); blank entries are still dropped. |
| **Decline and close** | The trimmed-value behavior stays; a literal `notes ` root silently points at `notes` and the two directories collide. | No config-semantics change; the defect remains for operators with edge-whitespace roots. |

Same defect class as merged #187554 and #172869 (precedents in the body above).

prs.title: fix(zalouser): match canonically equivalent names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `channels.zalouser.allowFrom: ["Nguyễn Văn A"]` while Zalo reports that friend's `displayName` in decomposed Unicode form (NFD) leaves the sender unresolved: startup logs `zalouser users unresolved: Nguyễn Văn A`, and the DM is rejected even though the name is exactly what the operator sees in the Zalo app.

- Problem: every Zalo name comparison lowercased but never normalized, so NFC and NFD spellings of the same name produced different keys. The startup allowlist resolver (`allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `groups` keys), the `friends`/`groups` lookups, and group-name resolution all missed.
- Solution: name matching now compares canonical keys. `extensions/zalouser/src/directory-index.ts` owns `normalizeZaloNameKey` (trim + lowercase + NFC), and the five comparison sites use it.
- What changed: `directory-index.ts` (new key owner, index build), `zalo-js.ts` (`resolveZaloEntries`, `listZaloFriendsMatching`, `listZaloGroupsMatching`), `monitor.ts` (startup name-resolution lookups), `channel.ts` (group name selection).
- What did NOT change: original spellings still flow to logs, prompts and outbound text untouched; numeric `userId`/`groupId` comparisons keep the lowercase-only helper; no config schema, manifest or API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner decides what "same Zalo name" means, and every comparison asks it. Keeping the key inline at each site would have left five copies of the same convention in three files, which is how the gap appeared in the first place.

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- Inline `.normalize("NFC")` at each call site: smaller diff, five duplicated key definitions.
- Normalizing on ingest (rewriting `displayName` when it arrives): would silently change the spellings surfaced to users, logs and captured messages, far beyond matching.
- A shared `plugin-sdk` canonical helper: no such owner exists; the tree keeps this per-channel (feishu, discord, matrix, mattermost normalize inline).

Boundaries:

- `group-policy.ts` matches operator config group keys/substrings exactly; a different contract, unchanged.
- Numeric ids are compared with the existing `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`; only names get the NFC key.
- Production delta is +4 lines: the key function plus comment replacing the four inline lowercasing sites it supersedes.

Same family as merged per-channel fixes #187953, #188003, #187988; no upstream helper was lost.

## User Impact

Operators whose allowlists, group config keys or lookups use a diacritic-bearing Vietnamese (or other composed/decomposed) name now reach the person they meant, regardless of which Unicode form their device or the Zalo server stored. Before this change the failure was silent: the startup resolver logged `unresolved`, the DM was rejected, and `friends`/`groups` queries came back empty with no error.

Users who already match exactly keep identical behavior, because the canonical key preserves every currently-failing-to-match distinction except the composed/decomposed one.

## Evidence

### Regression: red on base, green at head

The four production files were swapped for `origin/main` (`git checkout origin/main -- extensions/zalouser/src/{directory-index,monitor,channel,zalo-js}.ts`), PR tests kept.

```console

$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-zalo.config.ts extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.matching.test.ts extensions/zalouser/src/channel.test.ts -t "canonical|unlisted sender|opt-in is off|grant removed"
Tests  7 failed | 6 passed | 20 skipped (33)   # 6 friend/group/allowFrom + group-name pick
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts -t "resolves canonically|unauthorized|grant removed"
Tests  2 failed | 3 passed | 21 skipped (26)   # startup resolve + canonical sender dispatch

# head source restored, same two commands
Tests  13 passed | 20 skipped (33)
Tests  5 passed | 21 skipped (26)
```

9 of the 12 added tests are red on base and green at head; the three rejection cases (unlisted sender, opt-in off, grant removed after restart) pass on both refs by design. Pre-existing ingress-verdict cases stay flaky on both refs.

### Running Gateway, authority chain (head 2df8019 vs origin/main 1e906e9)

Real `openclaw gateway run`, isolated state dirs, same config on both refs: `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, `allowFrom: ["Nguyễn Văn A"]` (NFC), `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching: true`. Only the Zalo network client is a fixture: `require("zca-js")` resolves to a proof file serving a friend stored as NFD (shared `node_modules` untouched), plus a loopback stub model; startup resolution, admission, dispatch and outbound are shipped code paths. No real Zalo login.

```console
scenario        startup resolution  sender 123  outbound
cand-accept     resolved ->123      dispatched  SEND_MESSAGE threadId=123 text=PROOF_AGENT_REPLY
main-accept     unresolved          blocked     none
cand-optin-off  not attempted       blocked     none

[zalouser] users resolved: Nguyễn Văn A->123
message processed: chatId=zalouser:123 ... sessionKey=agent:main:zalouser:direct:123 outcome=completed
[zalouser] Blocked unauthorized zalouser sender 999 (dmPolicy=allowlist)   # unlisted, same run

# main-accept (origin/main 1e906e9, same config and fixture)
[zalouser] users unresolved: Nguyễn Văn A
[zalouser] Blocked unauthorized zalouser sender 123 (dmPolicy=allowlist)
```

### Ownership, differential, gates

`normalizeZaloNameKey` is the single key owner: `buildZaloNameIndex` builds with it; startup lookups in `monitor.ts` and group resolution in `channel.ts` query with it. Shipped `openclaw directory peers/groups list --channel zalouser`, 9 queries per ref: main returns `[]` for both cross-form cases (NFC vs NFD, peers and groups), head resolves them, same-form/ASCII/numeric-id/negative controls match on both. `oxlint` 0 errors, `oxfmt --check` clean; tsgo here hits the known `Declaration input escapes checkout` limit as on the base, so CI's extension type check is the authority.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): flush media-stream upgrade rejects before destroy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice-call media-stream upgrade rejects (shutdown and connection-cap) could destroy the HTTP socket before rejection bytes flushed, so clients saw a hard disconnect instead of HTTP 503. Peer reset during that write could also become `uncaughtException`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rejectMediaStreamUpgrade` attaches `socket.once("error", () => {})` then reuses `rejectWebSocketUpgrade`, which calls `socket.end(response, () => destroy())`. Cap and shutdown rejects share that owner.

## User Impact

**Before:** Capacity/shutdown upgrade rejects could reset the client with no HTTP status, and a reset peer during write could crash the process.

**After:** Clients receive `HTTP/1.1 503` with the reject body; peer-reset errors during flush are swallowed.

## Evidence

- Production: `extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.ts` `rejectMediaStreamUpgrade`
- Tests: `extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts` — real HTTP 503, injected-hold flush on a real TCP socket, and RST during pending `socket.end`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Media-stream upgrade rejects could drop the HTTP status on buffered/reset sockets.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `MediaStreamHandler.handleUpgrade` → `rejectMediaStreamUpgrade` → `rejectWebSocketUpgrade` against a live loopback upgrade.
- **Boundary crossed:** Real `node:http` / `net.connect` transport. Buffering is injected by holding `socket.end` on that real socket, then releasing so the 503 bytes flush. RST destroys the client only after the server has entered `socket.end`.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `openclaw/plugin-sdk/websocket-runtime` `rejectWebSocketUpgrade`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Vitest extension-voice-call lane, loopback TCP. No carrier/video.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ git diff --check
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "returns HTTP 503 over a real upgrade"
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "flushes a buffered 503 over real transport"
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "peer resets during a 503 reject"
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
✓ |extension-voice-call| ... > returns HTTP 503 over a real upgrade when the connection cap is reached 13ms

stdout | ... > flushes a buffered 503 over real transport after an injected hold
[media-stream buffered transport proof] pending_before_release=true status=503 body=Too many media stream connections
 ✓ ... > flushes a buffered 503 over real transport after an injected hold 65ms

stdout | ... > does not surface uncaught errors when the peer resets during a 503 reject
[media-stream rst proof] rejection_started=true uncaught=0
 ✓ ... > does not surface uncaught errors when the peer resets during a 503 reject 65ms
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real transport returns HTTP 503. Holding `socket.end` keeps the reject pending until release, then the client reads the 503 body. Destroying the client at `socket.end` does not emit `uncaughtException`.
- **What was not tested:** Live Twilio/Telnyx media-stream against a full carrier call.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: fix(discord): false "couldn't finish" notice when a queued message is answered in its thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord shows "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request" after the agent answered a message in a thread it created from that message, when the message arrived while the session was still busy with an earlier turn.

## User Impact

User impact: in Discord channels, a message that waits in the queue behind a running turn can be answered in its own thread (thread-create from the message, then thread-reply, ending with `NO_REPLY`) without a false failure notice in the channel. Messages handled right away were already fine.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord registers an active thread route for each inbound message so that a thread created from that message counts as replying to it (thread replies are tagged `sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"`). The route was released when the message's dispatch returned. A message queued behind an active turn returns from dispatch right after it is enqueued, so its queued run started later with no route. Its thread was never adopted, the thread replies did not count as the source reply, and the required-reply check reported an empty response.

The queued run now holds the same route from `onQueuedFollowupAdmitted` until `onQueuedFollowupSettled`. Route registration counts its holders, so a queued run admitted before its dispatch returns keeps the route after the dispatch releases its own hold. Those two hooks are now always set on Discord dispatches (before this change they were set only when a draft stream existed); the draft handling inside them is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live observation on a 2026.10.7 Gateway (Discord guild channel, `claude-cli` backend, automatic visible replies). Two turns in the same session did the same thing: thread-create from the source message, several thread-replies, then `NO_REPLY`. The turn that started right away completed silently. The next message had arrived during that turn (`injection_unavailable`, `disposition: followup-policy`) and ran about 2.5 minutes later as a queued follow-up. It logged `cli empty response diagnostics: backend=claude-cli reason=exit exitCode=0 … useResume=true` and posted the failure notice. The route lifecycle in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts` is the same on `main`.
- New regression tests in `message-handler.process.draft-final.test.ts`:
  - `keeps the source-message thread route for a queued turn until it settles`: the queued run is admitted after its dispatch returned.
  - `keeps the route for a queued turn admitted before its dispatch returns`: covers the holder count.
  - Both fail on `main` (`expected false to be true` when the thread reply is checked) and pass with this change.
- `pnpm test:extension discord`: 259 files, 2,637 tests passed. Focused `pnpm test` on the touched process and action tests: 91 passed.
- `pnpm format:check` and type-aware oxlint on the changed files are clean. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Gap: I did not run the Discord e2e skill against an isolated Gateway because I don't have Discord test bot credentials. The live evidence above is from the reporting Gateway before the fix.

prs.title: fix(media): carry provider status and code into failure markers
prs.body:
Fixes #188043

## What Problem This Solves

When a media provider call fails, the agent marker was the fixed string `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` and the operator log kept only `reason=ProviderHttpError`, so a rejected credential, an exhausted account, a rate limit, and a timeout were indistinguishable. The agent now sees a bounded structured summary, and the operator warning keeps the provider code.

- Problem: status and code were dropped; the previous revision of this branch fixed that by forwarding the provider's whole error message into agent context, which also forwarded response-body detail and request ids.
- Solution: the marker renders only `provider request failed (HTTP <status> code=<code>)`; the full message stays on the diagnostic attempt reason and verbose log; the compact operator summary carries the code because it is annotated into the message head before the response detail.
- What changed: `src/media-understanding/media-failure-reason.ts` (owner of the two representations), `runner.ts` / `apply.ts` (which representation each audience receives), and `runner.entries.ts` (helpers moved out to stay within the lint budget).
- What did NOT change: provider transport and request payloads, marker text for non-provider failures (still the plain marker, as on `main`), and the bounded-marker/overflow budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

An agent marker and an operator log are different audiences: the marker crosses a disclosure boundary into the conversation model, while the log stays local. Keeping one string for both is what produced the leak and the truncation. The split reuses the shape `ProviderHttpError` already carries (`status`, `code`/`errorType`, `requestId`) instead of new plumbing, and accepts only a bounded taxonomy-shaped code (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`) so arbitrary text can never reach the marker.

- Best fix: yes — one owner decides the two representations; callers do not re-derive them.
- Alternative: sanitizing the message (whitespace, redaction, length caps) — rejected; it does not establish a disclosure boundary for arbitrary response detail.
- Risk / non-goals: an existing provider error without `code` renders status only; a CLI-backend failure keeps the plain marker because its message is arbitrary output, not a taxonomy.

## User Impact

The agent can now say whether a failure was authentication (`HTTP 401`), quota (`HTTP 429 code=insufficient_quota`), rate limiting, or a provider outage, without the conversation model receiving provider response bodies, request ids, or account detail. Operators see the code in the Gateway warning instead of a bare status.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway flow (real `openclaw gateway --port 18999`, real `gateway call chat.send` with an audio attachment, media provider pointed at `api.deepseek.com` with an invalid key). Gateway log — the operator warning keeps the code:

```console
[media-understanding] audio: failed (0/1) reason=Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)
```

The marker the agent actually receives, read from the shipped session transcript (`agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`):

```console
Transcribe this voice note.
[media attached: media://inbound/note---793f0547-….ogg]

[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider request failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)]
```

Reviewed head vs new head, same in-process script, real provider through the compatible audio adapter:

```console
# reviewed head 153b421b1e6
agent marker: [Audio attachment could not be analyzed: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401): Authentication Fails, Your api key: ****8078 is invalid (request_id: 72ddece0-…) [type=authent…]
operator compact summary: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401)
marker leaks provider body: true

# new head 69203e57e1a
agent marker: [Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider request failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)]
diagnostic attempt reason: ProviderHttpError: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error): Authentication Fails, … [type=authentication_error, code=invalid_request_error]
operator compact summary: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)
marker leaks provider body: false
```

Tests (`546 passed`, media-understanding + status) and gates:

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/media-understanding src/status
 Test Files  52 passed | 1 skipped (53)
      Tests  546 passed | 5 skipped (551)
```

`media-failure-reason.test.ts` covers: provider summary carries status+code only; arbitrary runtime errors produce no summary; unsafe codes are dropped; the adapter-shaped message keeps `code=` through `summarizeDecisionReason`; a 180-character detail does not push the code out. `oxlint`, `run-format`, and the changed-file `tsc` pass; CI is 56/56.

What was not tested: Windows runtime, and providers that report the code only in the response body without a `code`/`errorType` field (they render status only).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git log -S`, source tracing across the media runner/disposition/renderer owners, and a real-provider `node --import tsx` script for before/after evidence. The implementer understands the code: the provider error's structured fields feed a bounded label for the model while the full message stays on the diagnostic attempt reason. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(discord): avoid false failure notices for queued thread answers
prs.body:
Supersedes #183192, thanks @hannnnn-l.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes false Discord failure notices after a queued message is successfully answered in a thread created from that message.

## User Impact

Queued thread answers fulfill the original request without an extra failure notice in the parent channel. Genuinely unanswered turns still notify. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transfer the source-message route from dispatch into the existing queued delivery-correlation lifecycle before queued execution. The queued run owns its own registration through settlement, including when it starts before dispatch returns. Thread creation alone and replies to unrelated threads do not count as answers.

This avoids adding route reference counts or a second lifecycle helper. Removed the optional thread-adoption forwarder and redundant primitive aliases in the same owner. Production delta: +35/-31, net +4 lines required for the ownership transfer; regression tests: +39 lines, with an exact test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- Current main verified at `8873aeb433fd931c87e2bd5ba45f38b67215ae27`. Both new early/late queued-execution cases fail there at source-reply recognition (`expected false to be true`); the existing 20 cases pass.
- Fixed Discord handler, reaction/history, and message-action tests: 84 passed across three named files. Shared queued delivery-outcome tests: 63 passed, including notices for empty required replies and current-source receipt requirements.
- Final touched regression file after simplification: 22 passed; Vitest wall time 9.34 seconds (11.15 seconds including wrapper). The first [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41361126156) caught TS2454 in the new test cleanup variable; it now initializes explicitly. The 22 focused cases and touched-file checks pass after that correction. [Fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41361715626) and all 42 PR checks passed, including the full test-type graph and required gate. The containing changed-tests CI job took 270 seconds; per-file CI timing is not exposed. Auto-merge was retired before publishing the correction.
- Touched-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: clean. Broad tests and typechecking are delegated to PR CI under the production-host execution limits.
- Local autoreview against the main commit above, P0–P2: the implementation review was scoped-clean. prs.title: improve(cli): show workspace binding in sessions text output
prs.body:
Related to #181155 (this PR covers the Workspace column only; filtering & worktree metadata remain separate)

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions --json` already emits `spawnedWorkspaceDir`/`spawnedCwd`, but the default text table does not surface the workspace binding. With concurrent worktrees, a user scanning the plain `openclaw sessions` output cannot tell which session belongs to which workspace, so session ownership is effectively undiscoverable in the default view.

## Why This Change Was Made

The binding was already computed and available on the display row (`toSessionDisplayRow` exposes both `spawnedWorkspaceDir` and `spawnedCwd`), and the JSON path already projected it; the text-rendering path simply never wired it into a column. Adding the column at the text-rendering boundary is the minimal, owner-respecting fix: it consumes existing fields through the same cell-formatter pattern already used for `Key`/`Age`/`Model`/`Flags`, without a new owner or duplicated state.

The column shows the workspace directory **basename** (via `path.basename`) to keep rows narrow; sessions with no bound workspace render `-`. Managed-worktree sessions persist their binding in `spawnedCwd` and leave `spawnedWorkspaceDir` undefined, so the cell falls back to `row.spawnedWorkspaceDir ?? row.spawnedCwd`.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions` (default text output) now shows a `Workspace` column (next to `Tokens (ctx %)`, before `Flags`) with the basename of each session's spawned workspace, so operators can immediately attribute a session to its worktree across concurrent worktrees without `--json`. Sessions with no spawned workspace render `-`; JSON output is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Gap confirmed on `origin/main` (`src/commands/sessions-table.ts:21` exposes `spawnedWorkspaceDir`; the text table in `src/commands/sessions.ts` had no `Workspace` column).
- New cell formatter `formatSessionWorkspaceCell` added next to `formatSessionModelCell` (same `sanitizeTerminalText` + `theme.muted`/`theme.info` pattern).
- Column wired into the text table render in `src/commands/sessions.ts`, before the flex `Flags` column. The cell consumes `row.spawnedWorkspaceDir ?? row.spawnedCwd` so managed-worktree sessions (which persist `spawnedCwd` and clear `spawnedWorkspaceDir`) render their worktree basename.
- Test extended in `src/commands/sessions.test.ts` (`shows the spawned workspace basename in the text table`): asserts the `Workspace` header, correct basenames (`openclaw-wt-181155`, `openclaw-main`), `-` for an untethered session, and a `spawnedCwd`-only managed-worktree row (`agent:main:managed`) rendering `openclaw-wt-189857`.
- The existing `sanitizes persisted identifiers only for terminal output` test was made robust to the narrower `Flags` column by pinning a 240-column terminal (same pattern already used by the `aligns ... columns` test), preserving its sanitization intent.
- Validation: `run-vitest src/commands/sessions.test.ts` → 28/28 passed (incl. new managed-worktree assertion); `run-vitest src/commands/sessions-cleanup.test.ts` → 13/13 passed. Pre-fix (column read only `spawnedWorkspaceDir`, kept new assertion) → managed row failed (RED), confirming the guard.

### Real CLI render (shipped `openclaw sessions`, built from head `11b1cba`)

Real terminal output from the shipped CLI (built from this head, version `2026.10.9 (11b1cba)`) against a real persisted session store with the same producer-contract fixtures (wide PTY):

```
$ openclaw sessions --limit all
Session store: /tmp/.../openclaw-agent.sqlite
Sessions listed: 4
┌────────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────────┐
│ Kind   │ Key                   │ Workspace          │
├────────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────┤
│ direct │ agent:main:managed    │ openclaw-wt-189857 │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain      │ core               │
│ direct │ agent:main:untethered │ -                  │
│ direct │ agent:main:wt         │ openclaw-wt-181155 │
└────────┴───────────────────────┴────────────────────┘
```

(The full table also carries Age/Model/Runtime/Tokens/Flags columns unchanged; excerpt focuses on the changed `Workspace` column.)

Fixture mirrors the producer contract: `wt` persists `spawnedWorkspaceDir`; `managed`/`plain` persist only `spawnedCwd`; `untethered` persists neither. The Workspace column renders:
- `agent:main:managed` (`spawnedCwd=/home/code/openclaw-wt-189857`, `spawnedWorkspaceDir` undefined) → `openclaw-wt-189857`
- `agent:main:plain` (`spawnedCwd=/home/code/repos/core`) → `core`
- `agent:main:untethered` → `-`
- `agent:main:wt` (`spawnedWorkspaceDir=/home/code/openclaw-wt-181155`) → `openclaw-wt-181155`

Contrast vs `origin/main` (no `Workspace` column at all): every row gains a readable workspace binding; `managed`/`plain`/`wt` show their worktree basename, `untethered` shows `-`. The fallback (`spawnedWorkspaceDir ?? spawnedCwd`) is what distinguishes `managed`/`plain` (which persist only `spawnedCwd`) from a version reading `spawnedWorkspaceDir` alone (those two would render `-`). JSON output is unchanged by this PR.

prs.title: improve(ui): show plugin approval severity in approval history
prs.body:
Closes #180243

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI approval history table (`ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.tsx`) renders each row's `kind` as `Exec`, `Plugin`, or `System agent`, but never shows the plugin approval `severity` (`info` / `warning` / `critical`). That severity already drives the review flow — `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-approval.ts` treats `critical` as forcing a human decision — yet an operator auditing past approvals cannot tell a critical plugin approval from a routine `info` one without extra context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history RPC already returns `presentation.severity` for plugin approvals, so this is a rendering-only gap. Surfacing severity on the history row lets operators scan for high-risk plugin approvals at a glance, matching the emphasis the gateway already gives `critical` at decision time. The chip sits next to the existing `kind` label instead of taking a dedicated column, so non-plugin rows stay unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators auditing plugin approvals in the Control UI now see a small colored severity chip (info = blue, warning = amber, critical = red) beside the `Plugin` kind label. Exec and system-agent rows are unchanged. Additive and cosmetic only: no data, config, migration, or RPC change.

## Evidence

Captured from the built Control UI of this branch served by a local Gateway. The history rows are real ledger entries created through the shipped RPCs — three `plugin.approval.request` calls with `severity` `info`, `warning`, `critical`, plus one `exec.approval.request` — then read back through `approval.history`. The Gateway has no approval channel configured, so the no-route fallback recorded them as `denied`; that still produces the terminal rows the table renders.

**Before — `main` sources, same data.** Plugin rows show only `Plugin`.

![approval history before the change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shuisadev/openclaw/proof/189858/base-history.png)

**After — this branch, same data.** `Plugin Info`, `Plugin Warning`, `Plugin Critical`; the exec row is unchanged.

![approval history with the severity chip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shuisadev/openclaw/proof/189858/head-history.png)

```
warning  color rgb(146, 64, 14)    background 12% alpha    border 45% alpha

```

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channel-routes.test.ts` on current `main`: 1 passed (gateway-server project).
- **Mutation check.** The mutation removes the `target.httpRoutes.push(...)` line from `projectPluginHttpRoutes` in `src/plugins/http-route-owner.ts`.
  - The new test fails at the first reload: `status: 404`, expected 200.
  - Under the same mutation, `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` still passes 3/3 and `plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` fails 3/8.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the file: clean.
- `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`: clean. A type error injected into the file makes it fail, so the file is in that project.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:database-worker-ratchet`, run against the parent commit: OK.

prs.title: docs(discord): correct preview streaming default from off to progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared config reference (`docs/gateway/config-channels/community-chat.md`) states that Discord preview streaming defaults to `off` in two places. This is incorrect: the runtime default is `progress`, and the channel-specific doc (`docs/channels/discord/messaging.md`) already documents the correct default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime fallback for Discord's stream mode is `resolveChannelPreviewStreamMode(config, "progress")` in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts:57`, and the doctor migration registers `defaultMode: "progress"` in `extensions/discord/src/doctor-contract.ts:31`. When no `streaming.mode` is configured, streaming is enabled with mode `progress` — not `off`. The two contradictory statements in the shared config reference were confusing users and disagree with both the implementation and the sibling channel doc.

## User Impact

Users reading the shared config reference now get the correct default. They will no longer believe Discord streaming is off by default and wonder why a live "work in progress" message appears; they now know they can set `streaming.mode: "off"` to disable it.

## Evidence

**Runtime default**

```ts
const discordStreamMode = resolveChannelPreviewStreamMode(params.discordConfig, "progress");
```

**Doctor migration default**


**Sibling channel doc (already correct)**

prs.title: fix(google): Gemini models ignore configured topP
prs.body:
Closes #190468

## What Problem This Solves

Gemini models ignore a configured `params.topP` (or the documented `params.top_p` alias) on Google routes, while `temperature` from the same params block is sent.

## User Impact

Configured nucleus sampling now reaches the default Interactions route, GenerateContent custom endpoints and explicit `api: "google-generative-ai"`, and Vertex. Requests without topP remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already normalizes topP/top_p into a topP stream option. Google dropped it at two boundaries: native request builders omitted the field, and Google simple adapters lost it through the shared base-options projection. This repair preserves the option in Google-specific adapters and maps it to `generation_config.top_p` for Interactions and `generationConfig.topP` for GenerateContent/Vertex. The generic projection and other providers are unchanged.

Original implementation by @Yigtwxx; the contributor commit is retained. This completes the earlier closed [#190054](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190054) by @yetval, whose builder mappings did not address the simple-adapter loss.

`GoogleProviderOptions` remains an internal provider type; no public SDK export or generic SimpleStreamOptions change. No schema, config-shape, Doctor, migration, dependency or default change.

## Evidence

[Inspectable shipped-CLI wire captures and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190695#issuecomment-6565141692) compare main `e99c7b529d8e9d5d7c0062d48457ae8f71a13002` with exact head `ab73fca88db2d0050893c220ad93f30c6c77955e` in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker:

- **All three routes:** main drops topP **2/2**, candidate forwards it **2/2**. Cases cover `topP: 0.4` and `top_p: 0.7` through real CLI/config/plugin/HTTP execution.
- Vertex uses a faithful project/location/publisher/model wire URL through the existing base-URL override and synthetic credentials. Fixtures emit the native SSE response format; all 18 matrix turns complete with the fixture reply.
- Unset control omits topP on every route on both builds. Complete generation configs, excluding only the corrected topP field, are identical in all nine before/after comparisons; temperature, output limits, stops and thinking fields are unchanged.
- Focused regressions: main **11 fail / 43 pass**; candidate **54/54 pass** across three files. Targeted lint/format pass.
- Net line deltas: production **+15**, tests **0**, docs **0**. Existing request-capture cases retained, with handwritten capture boilerplate consolidated into the existing helper and fetch spy.

No live Google acceptance, GCP OAuth/ADC, or statistical sampling-quality claim is made.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores the previous forwarding behavior; there is no persisted-state or configuration migration. Blast radius is Google request serialization and Google simple adapters. If wrong, Google requests with configured topP could be rejected or sampled differently; unset topP and neighboring sampling options are covered by controls.

prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`.
