prs.title: fix(active-memory): detect German recall intent in escalate mode
prs.body:
Closes #151766
Related: #151841

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory skips deep recall in its default escalate mode when users ask about earlier conversations in German.

## User Impact

German questions such as "Weißt du noch, was wir letzte Woche besprochen haben?", "Was hat Petra gestern gesagt?" or "Wie hieß noch mal der Handwerker?" now trigger recall when the lane-1 lookup has no strong hit. Both "ß" and "ss" spellings are supported ("weisst", "hiess"). Recall stays off for reminders ("Erinnere mich morgen an …"), storing ("Merk dir …"), future questions ("Was machen wir nächste Woche?") and everyday commands. Other languages and configuration defaults are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a German entry to the existing localized `{ intent, future, retrospective }` structure, next to French. A question counts as recall when it has one of these:

- recall phrasing (*weißt du noch*, *erinnerst du dich*, *kannst du dich erinnern*, *wie war/hieß das noch mal*)
- a W-question or verb-first question with *haben/hatten* (or a past-tense modal such as *wollten/sollten*) and a past-time marker or a completed-discussion verb (*besprochen*, *gesagt*, *ausgemacht*, …)

Questions about a third person (*Was hat Petra …*) need both a past marker and a completed verb, so "Was hat der Wetterbericht gesagt?" stays quiet.

On its own, *letzte/letztes* is not a past marker, because German uses it for "final" ("das letzte Wort"). Only *letzte Woche*, *letztes Mal* and similar phrases count.

The imperative *Erinnere mich* is a reminder request, not a question, so it never matches.

#151841 has been open since September. Its four outstanding review findings are reminder commands, future-plan discussions, *ss*/infinitive spellings and umlaut-leading future words. This PR covers all four, with regression cases (see Evidence).

## Evidence

**Unit tests on `893a3de7`:**
- `pnpm test extensions/active-memory/escalation.test.ts`: **213 passed**. 51 of these are new German cases, 27 positives and 24 negatives.
- `pnpm test:extension active-memory`: **311 + 97 passed**.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` were clean on `d6db4f71`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` was clean on `893a3de7`.
- All on Node 24.22.1.

The negatives include:
- the three reminder forms that review flagged on #151841, for example "Erinnere mich morgen an das, was wir gestern besprochen haben"
- "Weißt du noch, ob wir übermorgen Zeit haben?"
- "Weißt du noch mehr darüber?"
- "Der letzte Termin war schön"

**Live Gateway** (OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Debian 13):
- Active Memory `mode: "escalate"`, `promptStyle: "balanced"`.
- The recall model is a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model.
- Messages go through the OpenResponses endpoint on a group session. That is the path a German home voice assistant uses.
- This PR's German entry as of `d6db4f71` was applied to the installed `dist/escalation-*.mjs` chunk and reverted afterwards.

| Message | Before (2026.10.5) | With this entry |
|---|---|---|
| "Weißt du noch, was wir letzte Woche über die Heizung besprochen haben?" | no recall start (`no-recall-intent`) | recall started, see note below |
| "Wie hieß noch mal der Wasserzähler, über den wir geredet haben?" | not tested | recall started, `done status=ok`, 200-char summary |
| "… Gestern habe ich Pizza gegessen." | no recall start | no recall start |

Note on the first message: the recall sub-agent passed `limit`, an argument `memory_search` does not accept. Recall ended with `status=unavailable reason=search-unavailable`. That failure comes from the recall model's tool call and is independent of the escalation gate. It is already fixed on main by #172630, which is not in a release yet. With that fix applied locally, recall runs finish with `status=ok`.

<details>
<summary>Redacted gateway log lines (with this entry)</summary>

```
15:15:14.510 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=<test> activeModel=<recall-model> start timeoutMs=12000 queryChars=406 searchQueryChars=70
15:15:20.677 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=<test> activeModel=<recall-model> done status=unavailable reason=search-unavailable elapsedMs=6168 summaryChars=0
15:15:32.028 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=<test> activeModel=<recall-model> start timeoutMs=12000 queryChars=460 searchQueryChars=63
15:15:38.838 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=<test> activeModel=<recall-model> done status=ok elapsedMs=6810 summaryChars=200
```

The "Pizza" message (15:15:28) produced no `start` line. On the unpatched build, the first message produced none either.
</details>

prs.title: feat(sessions): split deleted archive retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` previously applied the same age cutoff to both reset and deleted transcript archives. This adds `session.maintenance.deletedArchiveRetention` as an independent duration-or-`false` control.

When omitted, `deletedArchiveRetention` inherits `resetArchiveRetention` for backward compatibility. An explicit duration or `false` overrides it independently. Both settings age archive artifacts; they do not age retained SQLite reset history or transcript rows.

## Implementation

- Resolves independent deleted/reset rules from configuration.
- Applies those rules through legacy file-backed maintenance, cron reaping, and ordinary SQLite maintenance.
- Ordinary SQLite maintenance runs archive cleanup even when no session rows are removed.
- Removes a derived archive file before deleting its published SQLite recovery row; failed file cleanup leaves the recovery row intact.
- Preserves inherited deleted retention for older resolved-maintenance callers while retaining explicit disablement.
- Fences archive-row pruning against maintenance-owner invalidation before and inside each SQLite writer callback.
- Updates schema help, examples, and session-management documentation.

## Evidence
- Exact pushed head: `5460eaf7b0ab2221938f1b7a4dbfc052e69d9588`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused runtime command:
  `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-retention.integration.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-writer.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.archive-retention.test.ts src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.fix-missing.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  Result: **4 test files passed, 22 tests passed**.
- The unmocked integration proof loads a real config file and exercises both paths:
  - a fresh configured store is initialized (`configuredFreshStore: true`);
  - an existing configured store is maintained with independent cutoffs (`configuredExistingStore: true`);
  - the expired deleted archive file and its SQLite recovery row are absent after cleanup (`deletedArchiveFile: false`, `deletedArchiveRow: false` — `false` here means absent);
  - the reset archive remains (`resetArchiveFile: true`).
- The focused tests additionally prove inherited retention for older resolved callers, explicit `false` disablement, ordinary SQLite archive cleanup with no session removals, maintenance-owner invalidation without reopening the store, file-before-row deletion ordering, and lifecycle-deletion failure recovery.
- This proof is on the exact pushed head above; no claim is made that it resolves the separate current-base merge conflict or pending maintainer acceptance.
## Known Gate

This change affects persistent retention and upgrade behavior. Maintainer acceptance of the independent retention contract, ordinary-maintenance deletion timing, and the accessor cleanup boundary remains required before merge.

- Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen)

prs.title: fix(ui): keep pre-final assistant text visible after a completed turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users chatting in the Control UI WebChat would watch a long assistant reply disappear once the turn completed, leaving only a short closing message visible, when the agent ran on an `openai-completions` transport and a tool call followed the reply text.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openai-completions` transports retag already-streamed answer text as commentary once a tool call follows it. The WebChat's completed-turn grouping then folded that text behind the "worked for" row together with the tool activity, so the substantive reply vanished from view.

The fix changes `chat-thread-grouping` to fold only tool groups and text-less assistant groups when a turn completes. Assistant groups that carry text stay visible regardless of how the transport phased them.

## User Impact

Long replies that precede a tool call remain visible after the turn completes. Tool activity still collapses as before.

## Evidence

New cases in `chat-thread-grouping.test.ts` and `chat-thread.test.ts` cover a text-bearing commentary group before a tool call, a text-less group, and the existing tool-only collapse.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): queued turn re-compacts a small context when preflight accounting is refused
prs.body:
Related: #140819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a busy chat session would compact its context again on the very next queued turn, even though the context was far below the compaction budget. Each spurious pass spent minutes summarizing, appended another summary on top of the previous one, blocked the queued message behind the session lane, failed that queued message with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded`, and surfaced another "Context compacted" card. On one Signal session this repeated four times in fourteen minutes; three of the four ran against a context of roughly 84k, 120k, and 91k tokens against a 252k budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token-triggered preflight compaction committed the compaction to the transcript inside the queued compactor's session-lane task, but recorded the session-row accounting (count, `totalTokens`, byte latch) only after that task returned and the lane was released. A run waiting on the lane claims the session writer as its first lane write, so the accounting compare-and-swap was correctly refused, the row kept its pre-compaction fresh total, and the next preflight projected pressure from that stale total and compacted again. The queued compactor already exposes a host commit callback that runs while the lane and writer fence are still held; the Codex transcript-byte path used it and the token path did not. This change routes accounting through that callback for every runtime, and supplies the transcript-settled callback for byte-triggered compaction on every runtime so the byte latch keeps measuring the post-maintenance transcript. Nothing about the writer, lifecycle, or session guards changes: a writer that replaces the row before the host commit is still refused, and the after-return path remains only for compactors that emit no host commit.

Non-goals: no retry against a replacement writer, no schema or config change, no change to projection inputs or context limits.

## User Impact

After a preflight compaction, the session's recorded context and compaction count match the transcript, so the following queued turn no longer re-compacts a small context, the queued message is delivered instead of failing, and users stop seeing back-to-back "Context compacted" cards for a session that was not over budget.

## Evidence

- Regression test `lands before a run waiting on the session lane claims the writer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`) models the queued-execution contract against a real SQLite session store: successor acceptance and host commit inside the lane, then a replacement writer claim once the compactor returns. Red/green on this head: with the pre-change `agent-runner-memory.ts` from `upstream/main` swapped in, that test fails with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded` thrown from `recordCompactionAccounting` (1 failed, 125 passed); with the change it passes, the count and `totalTokens` land, the replacement writer's claim is intact, accounting runs exactly once, and the next preflight does not compact again.
- Guard test `does not account against a writer that replaced the row before the host commit` keeps the newer-writer protection on the in-lane path.
- The byte-latch test now runs for both the Codex and the embedded runtime and asserts the persisted latch right after the first compaction equals the settled (post-maintenance) transcript size. The embedded case would fail if the settled-latch callback were supplied only for Codex, because the in-lane host commit measures the pre-maintenance size.
- Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, one invocation): `agent-runner-memory` (126), `session-updates.lifecycle` (17), `compact.queued-successor` (25), `agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens` (7), `agent-runner-execution-compaction` (14), `commands-compact.lifecycle` (8): 197 passed. `compact.queued-successor` already pins that `onHostCompactionCommitted` is awaited before the checkpoint and maintenance steps.
- Changed-path gate on this head (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`): all 29 checks pass, including `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt` on the changed files, the max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, dead-export scan, and import-cycle check; `git diff --check` is clean. A second red check confirms the byte-latch asymmetry: with the settled-latch callback supplied only for Codex, the embedded case fails (`activeBytes` 314 persisted instead of the settled 186).
- Production correlation (sanitized, from the reporter's gateway): each refused accounting was preceded by `lane wait exceeded` on the same session lane 50 to 330 ms before the accounting error, and the one compaction with no lane waiter recorded its accounting normally. Effective harness was `openclaw`; the model route was an OpenAI subscription Responses route.
- Independent review: repository `autoreview` helper on the Claude engine (`claude-fable-5-1`, xhigh), branch mode against `upstream/main`, P2 threshold: `scoped-clean`, no findings. An earlier Codex-engine autoreview of the pre-amend commit (P1 threshold) and an adversarial read-only concurrency review of the diff and tests were also clean at P0/P1; that review's P2 notes (byte-latch timing on non-Codex byte triggers, comment precision, two test-fidelity cleanups) are addressed in this head.

Known gap: this is a source-only repair validated with focused tests; it has not been applied to a live Gateway. The branch includes a merge of current `upstream/main`; upstream did not touch the changed files.

prs.title: fix: resume native parents when saved channel aliases fail
prs.body:
Related: #166022

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native worker results failing to resume their parent when the parent's saved channel alias no longer resolves.

## User Impact

Parents can consume completed worker results and continue their tasks. Sending a visible reply still requires the parent's permitted messaging tools. No configuration or schema migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route native completions through the existing private parent-input owner instead of resolving an external destination first. Keep current session-controller custody and exact host-issued source/requester authority. Bind runtime completion facts to the durable processing identity so replay reuses a consumed result and rejects a changed result under the same identity. Processing receipts do not count as external delivery.

This is a separate pre-admission routing failure from the interrupted-input recovery reported in the linked issue; it does not claim to resolve that broader report.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual SDK and isolated Gateway on upstream `8e0ae0da7bd5`: a throwing saved-alias resolver ran once, no parent command started, and delivery failed. With the correction, the resolver is not called and the parent runs once.
- 97 focused cases pass across seven files: the three changed test files passed all 40 cases after the CI correction; 57 unchanged sibling cases retain their passing proof. Coverage includes durable replay after clearing warm dedupe, changed-result rejection, forged-source refusal, strict external routing, current/revoked/replaced ownership during compaction, incognito actor admission, and registered completion siblings.
- Removing only the new runtime-event fingerprint reproduced the changed-result replay defect; the reviewed production bytes were then restored.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the production and test changes completed with no actionable findings. Core and affected test types, targeted typed lint, formatting, docs checks, import cycles, assertion safety, line and mock-export ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The unused-file scan passed for production but failed for one full-tree path, `scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts`. That file, its documented command, the Knip registrations/runner, and package/lock/workspace inputs are byte-identical to the pinned base; neither snapshot registers this maintained command. No changed path was flagged. The original aggregate failure is retained; a pristine-base scan was not rerun, and no unrelated fix or suppression was added.

The Gateway fixture uses real isolated session storage and controlled parent execution. It does not establish a live Codex thread identity or delivery of an external final message. Hosted CI on the corrected head is pending.

The retired-caller success cases use the real Gateway. A separate restart-drain negative verifies that a fabricated warm-cache result cannot claim private consumption or leave an input, transcript, queued controller, or retained root. This preserves the existing restart guard. The CI correction changes tests only; production bytes remain unchanged. The origin mock now preserves real exports, and its one obsolete grandfathered baseline entry was removed through the native guard.

The 172-line test allocation covers these distinct boundary regressions using existing fixtures; the prior compaction table was adapted rather than duplicated. No sleeps, retries, timeout increases, or new production test seams were added.

Changed-test costs from separate single-worker canonical wrapper invocations:

| File | Tests | Wrapper wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/agent-harness-completion-authority.test.ts` | 14 passed | 107.983 s |
| `src/gateway/server.native-completion-authority.test.ts` | 10 passed | 110.191 s |
| `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-completion.test.ts` | 16 passed | 20.874 s |

The original authority fixture reproduced the CI failure locally: 13 passed, one failed, 109.131 seconds. These wrappers include worker preparation; transformation accounts for most of their time. The Gateway suite exercises actual SDK dispatch, controller serialization, SQLite processing receipts, and compaction admission; helper-only tests cannot prove that wiring. The earlier six-file batch took 390.580 seconds, including 96.333 seconds of shared worker preparation; its unchanged sibling proof is retained.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-harness-completion-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.native-completion-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix: restore CLI message sends with agent tool policies
prs.body:
Related: #184964

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw message send` failing with `Cannot verify the installed tool authority for Template-managed agent "main"` when the selected agent has its own tool profile or allowlist. Even text-only sends and `--dry-run` fail for ordinary agents with no Template installation.

## User Impact

CLI message sends work again without changing agent policies or repairing a healthy state database. Explicit attachment read restrictions and genuine Template-consent failures remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression was introduced by [3c23d52c93b in #184964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3c23d52c93b2479d8685564b7e5b4e3dcb47cc1e): the new `resolveEffectiveToolPolicy()` call in `src/media/read-capability.ts` reads Template consent during message preparation, including text-only sends.

The CLI config guard publishes its configuration synchronously, before that consent provenance has been initialized. Initialize the provenance and bind it to the effective command configuration before dispatch, using the same preparation owners as standalone agent commands. No media-policy checks are removed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the installed CLI: `openclaw message send --channel discord --target channel:123456789012345678 --message regression-probe --dry-run --json` exits 1 with the error above.
- New command-boundary regressions: **2 fail / 1 pass before**, **3 pass after**. They exercise real config, policy, and dispatch with isolated consent-row I/O. Both an agent-owned profile and a restrictive allowlist can send text; unreadable consent remains rejected.
- **35 focused tests passed** across the command, media workspace-access, and consent-preparation suites. Existing attachment-denial tests remain green. Command-suite wall time was 5.14 seconds for 14 tests; the three sequential test shards completed in 23.93 seconds.
- A separate Node process with no module mocks, isolated empty state, and a local channel adapter reproduced the same consent error before the fix. Afterward, dry-run succeeded without delivery, and a non-dry-run delivered the exact message to the local adapter once with `deliveryStatus: "sent"`. No external channel API was called.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The final isolated regression run also passed all 3 cases (33.16 seconds including cold worker compilation). The 76-line test allocation covers the missing CLI initialization boundary and fail-closed control.

### Shipped-CLI proof pinned to `a9bd00376c21`

Source builds of the CLI (`pnpm openclaw` → `scripts/run-node.mjs`) at head `a9bd00376c21` and PR parent `43af01b15c96`. Each case uses a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and `HOME`. Delivery cases use the bundled Mattermost channel pointed at a local `127.0.0.1` recording endpoint (`network.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: true`). The endpoint logs each request and whether the body contains the attachment bytes. The token is a placeholder; no external API was called.

| Case | Agent `tools` / consent state | Parent `43af01b` | Head `a9bd003` | Channel requests (head) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text dry-run (Discord) | `allow:[message] deny:[read]` | ❌ `Cannot verify the installed tool authority…` | ✅ dry-run payload | — |
| Text send | `allow:[message] deny:[read]` | ❌ same error, 0 requests | ✅ `deliveryStatus: sent` | 1 (`POST /posts`) |
| Attachment send, read denied | `allow:[message] deny:[read]` | — | ❌ `path-not-allowed`, `sentBeforeError: false` | **0** |
| Attachment send, read allowed (control) | `profile:full allow:[read,message]` | — | ✅ sent | 2 (`/files` with bytes, `/posts`) |
| Template consent: current v2 row, matching digest | `profile:full allow:[read,message]` | — | ✅ sent | 2 |
| Agent config edited after consent (`allow += exec`), attachment and text-only | same row | — | ❌ `Cannot verify the installed tool authority…` | **0** |
| Row digest invalidated (config unchanged) | v2 row, wrong digest | — | ❌ `Cannot verify…` | **0** |
| Unsupported provenance schema | `…templateInstallRecord.v999` | — | ❌ `Cannot verify…` | **0** |
| Legacy v1 provenance | `…templateInstallRecord.v1` | — | ❌ `…uses a legacy dynamic tool policy…` | **0** |
| State database unreadable (overwritten with random bytes) | — | — | ❌ `file is not a database` | **0** |

`openclaw templates add` in this build does not write `template_installs` rows (0 rows after a successful add). The consent rows were therefore inserted into the isolated state database in the shape an earlier install leaves (`agent_id`, `schema_version`, `agent_config_digest`, `status=complete`). The matching digest comes from `collectTemplateToolPolicyCandidates`.

<details><summary>Head transcript excerpt (Template consent cases)</summary>

```
owned-config digest: sha256:57b65b3c495c57930df557688a15487b6148c9573895acee1a9eb497fa5685b1
## P1 consented: current v2 provenance row matching the agent config
$ openclaw message send --channel mattermost --target channel:<id> --message p1-consented --media <state>/tpl-ws/report.txt --json
    "deliveryStatus": "sent",
exit=0
{"method": "POST", "path": "/api/v4/files", "bytes": 321, "hasAttachmentBytes": true}
{"method": "POST", "path": "/api/v4/posts", "bytes": 89, "hasAttachmentBytes": false}
## P2 mismatched: tools edited after consent (allow += exec); row unchanged
$ openclaw message send ... --message p2-mismatch --media <state>/tpl-ws/report.txt --json
    "message": "Cannot verify the installed tool authority for Template-managed agent \"tplagent\". Repair the OpenClaw state database before running it."
exit=1
local channel endpoint requests for this step: 0
$ openclaw message send ... --message p2-mismatch-text-only --json
    "message": "Cannot verify the installed tool authority for Template-managed agent \"tplagent\". ..."
exit=1
local channel endpoint requests for this step: 0
## P3 invalidated: matching config, row digest replaced
exit=1  (Cannot verify ...)  requests: 0
## P4 unsupported provenance schema (v999)
exit=1  (Cannot verify ...)  requests: 0
## P5 legacy v1 provenance
    "message": "Template-managed agent \"tplagent\" uses a legacy dynamic tool policy. Its tool consent cannot be refreshed in place. ..."
exit=1  requests: 0
```
</details>

prs.title: fix: stop stale quarantine rows from slowing database opens
prs.body:
Closes #190683

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a repaired agent database remained associated with a stale quarantine generation, causing every runtime admission to hash the database file family again even when identity or size already proved the record obsolete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine reads now reject definitive database, journal, or non-empty WAL identity, size, and presence mismatches before invoking the SHA-256 worker, while retaining digest comparison for possible matches and empty-WAL equivalence. Doctor now notices any persisted quarantine record, performs a full integrity check, and clears it only after verification succeeds.

## User Impact

Agents no longer repeatedly scan large repaired databases because an obsolete quarantine row remains. A later `openclaw doctor --fix` retires the stale row after verifying the database.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the new regression observed `readSqliteFileGenerationSync` once after a primary-file size mismatch. With this change, primary, journal, and WAL-only mismatch regressions all prove the worker is not called.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-database-verify.test.ts -t 'without hashing the database'` (3 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts src/state/openclaw-quarantine-store.test.ts` (36 passed)
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/sqlite-file-generation.ts src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.ts src/state/openclaw-database-verify.test.ts src/state/openclaw-quarantine-store.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts --base origin/main`
- `git diff --check`

The Doctor regression confirms `PRAGMA integrity_check` runs before the stale row is removed.

Limitation: no live 422 MB Gateway timing run was performed; behavior proof uses exact worker-call and SQLite lifecycle regressions.

Disclosure: AI was used to understand the codebase and review the fix.

prs.title: fix: transcript reads fail after concurrent database preparation
prs.body:
Related: #184511.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes transcript reads failing with a physical-owner validation error when database preparation completes ahead of a queued read.

## User Impact

Queued reads use the current validation receipt for the same physical database. Revocation and foreign-file checks remain in force; no retry, schema, configuration or permission change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker captured a validation receipt before awaiting read admission. A preceding writer can renew that receipt during the wait, leaving the real worker with revoked proof. Capture now occurs inside the existing admitted operation, after its predecessors settle. The owner is byte-identical on guest-stack head a17fcb30 and main base 8da85beb, establishing an inherited race rather than a membership change.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, the original filtered-sharing file passed 10/10 in three separate runs on each side (30/30 on a17fcb30, 30/30 on main 8da85beb); those passing replays alone did not establish a fix.
- A deterministic owner-bound regression warms a real worker, holds the next admission, renews the same file's writer validation and releases the read. It fails on main with the exact CI error, `Session reader validation does not match its current physical owner`, and passes with this repair. The test does not replace worker execution or returned data.
- Node 24 owner, schema-freshness and original filtered-sharing suites passed 27/27. Core and affected test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. SQLite T1 calls remain 168 → 168. Main's test ceiling is unchanged: 6,283,332 lines against 6,329,653 allowed.
- Combined scoped wall time was 129.98 s, including compiler preparation and real-worker lifecycle. The new owner case took 25.719 s; it boots/joins the real native worker to prove receipt transfer, which a mocked result cannot establish. Hosted CI timing remains pending.
- Independent AutoReview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2, full changed modules plus admission/physical-owner context) reported scoped-clean. It did not execute tests. Simplification retained the existing admission owner and moved the existing capture; production net growth is one line, with one 51-line boundary regression and no new state or helper API.
- No CI rerun or dispatch was requested. The historical CI attempt was not instrumented, so the controlled reproduction proves this pre-existing mechanism, not the exact scheduling of that attempt.

### CI typecheck correction

The first head's CI caught a missing `databaseAgentId` in the new regression input. The follow-up binds the request to the fixture's actual database agent; production behavior and the demonstrated admission repair are unchanged. Node 24 reader tests passed **7/7** after this correction, and the actual owning `tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json` leaf, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Prior 27-test and independent source-review evidence remains scoped to the original production move; one exact-head re-review is requested for the corrected head. No test deadline, check or ceiling was relaxed.

### Current exact-head build gate — 2026-10-30

The corrected head `bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6` has [clean exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188055#issuecomment-6513913355), with no Before-merge items or findings, and its typecheck failure is cleared. [CI run 40998529819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819) is blocked by [build-artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819/job/123877673340): the bundled root-help renderer timed out after **120,000 ms** in `scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.ts`. This leaves `openclaw/ci-gate` red.

One bounded local `pnpm build` at this exact head passed under verified Node **24.22.1**, with isolated HOME/config/state: total build phases **3m 30s**, startup metadata **4.22s**. The previous [6c62e05e build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40994523700/job/123864788070) also passed; the only source delta to the corrected head is the regression input binding, not production code. The later main build passed too, and no intervening repair in the helper or root-help owner was found. These passing controls do not establish a causal fix for the failed hosted build. The timeout remains **unattributed / unreproduced locally**, not waived or labeled green. No CI rerun, dispatch, no-op push or timeout increase was used. The PR remains unmerged under the requested green-only gate.

### Bounded root-help timeout audit — 2026-10-30

The [failed bundled root-help child](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819/job/123877673340) reached its **120,000 ms budget, 120,008 ms elapsed**, on Node 24.22.1. The hang remains **unattributed**, not established as inherited or a shared flake.

Read-only run-creation window: **2026-10-29 04:18:24Z through 2026-10-30 04:18:24Z**. Logs were observed October 30 at **04:22:31Z–04:29:38Z**, not backdated to the creation cutoff. All 24 completed scheduled-main runs returned in that window were inspected. The other-PR sample selected the latest six completed non-cancelled distinct branches per four-hour bin, from at most 100 returned candidates per bin, excluding the guest stack and its two repairs. This is a bounded sample, not an exhaustive incident-rate estimate.

- Main: **0 matching timeout hits / 24 readable log misses**; 23 target jobs succeeded and one was cancelled after metadata completed.
- Other PRs: **0 hits / 3 readable executed-job misses**; **33 skipped target jobs** do not count as executions.
- **No unresolved read gaps.** Initial job-list 502s were recovered through the attempt jobs API, reconciling both pages against total counts.
- Successful main metadata phases: **23 samples, min 2.95 s / median 3.75 s / max 6.59 s**. Other-PR phases: **3 samples, 3.23–3.79 s**. These enclosing-phase durations are not individual-child measurements and do not justify increasing its deadline.

The failed job actually built synthetic merge **c87bcb9ca45e19b2f986840c500a471837028fbb**, with main parent **acb102d176c49d7df4360edb58e7b3fc1b490c9e** and PR parent **bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6**. The previous and corrected PR heads had different hosted integration bases. The prior passing local build was the raw PR head, not this synthetic merge; it cannot exclude a base/composition effect. This audit did not replay the exact synthetic merge locally.

At that executed merge, renderBundledRootHelpText imports the root-help bundle and calls outputRootHelp with fresh isolated HOME/state/workspace and a fixed synthetic config. Root help assembles command descriptors rather than registering live command runtimes. The repository-owned runtime-emitted import graph, erasing type-only imports, visited **1,582 eager source modules** without reaching either changed file. The dynamic legacy-plugin loader requires a nonempty external-plugin list; the isolated render uses bundled assets, not user-installed legacy plugins. Resolution gaps were confined to external fs-safe/proc-safe packages, whose boundaries were inspected; this is not a complete native/bundled runtime trace. The production delta adds no imports or top-level initialization: it moves validation capture inside an already-invoked admitted reader operation. **No causal path from this repair to the help hang was found.**

Existing [#147932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147932) states a live-config fast-path scope; [#187644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187644) explicitly changes exit-code diagnostics, not timeouts. Neither provides a proven repair for this hang. With no matching comparison timeout, no reproduced original hang and no demonstrated cause, no speculative owner patch, timeout increase, rerun/dispatch, empty push or chase rebase was made. The requested green-only landing remains blocked and is escalated to the requesting maintainer.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(android): keep realtime Talk alive through slow audio acknowledgments
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk over the Gateway relay ends with "Talk failed: request timeout" when the Gateway's answer to one audio append takes longer than 8 seconds, on the phone and through a paired Watch.

## User Impact

User impact: a short network stall or a busy Gateway no longer ends an Android realtime Talk call. Audio past about three seconds in flight is dropped, Talk says "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part", and "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" once the Gateway catches up. A paired Watch shows its own shorter text ("Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part.", "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part.") in place of the elapsed time; each notice stays until the next Talk state change, as on the phone. Talk still ends on an explicit Gateway error, a lost connection, or an append left unanswered for 30 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser relay and the Apple apps already follow this contract (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155839, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572, `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`); https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 did not reach Android. Both Android relays sent every frame with an 8 second deadline, no limit on audio in flight, and ended Talk on the first timeout.

A small `RealtimeInputAudioBudget` owns the three-second budget and the two notices, and both relays use it: the phone's append loop in `TalkModeManager` and the Watch relay in `WearRealtimeTalkController`. To release audio from the budget when the Gateway answers, `GatewaySession.sendRequestFrameForEndpoint` gains an optional success callback, and the Watch relay's send callback now reports success as well as errors. The append deadline is the 30 second liveness limit from the same contract. The Watch shows the notices from its own strings: the relay's snapshot gains an optional `notice` field (older watches ignore it), and the Watch Talk screen shows it in place of "Listening · 0:00" while listening. The notices are registered for translation; the docs page now says Android follows the same budget.

Trade-off: a Gateway that keeps the socket open but stops answering is now noticed after 30 seconds instead of 8, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 states for the Apple apps.

## Evidence

Tested at `170d5c59956` (base `upstream/main` `315fba74e12`). The Before/After runs below used a build of an earlier revision of this branch with the same phone-side code; the stall run was repeated on a build of this head (see "Re-run at this head").

Real app: the Android app (play debug build of each side) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway (empty state directory, loopback port, no outside traffic) whose realtime Talk provider is a local fake that only counts audio. The Gateway is an older source build (2026.9.6, `19afe35954`) on both sides; the bug and the fix are in the Android client. A local WebSocket proxy between the app and the Gateway sets the answer delay: while a stall is on, it holds each `talk.session.appendAudio` answer for a fixed time and logs every 50th held answer as `hold`. Same steps on both sides: open the chat, start realtime Talk, let audio flow, turn the stall on.

Proxy lines are UTC; logcat lines are the emulator's local time (UTC+9), whose clock runs about 1.06 s behind the proxy's. On the proxy clock, Talk closes 8.0 s after the stall starts on the base and 30.0 s after it in the 40 second run.

Before (base, 12 second stall per answer):

```text
11:58:35.244Z req   talk.session.create
12:00:20.447Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
12:00:25.441Z hold  held=51  stallMs=12000      (every frame still sent)
21:00:27.401 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:00:28.448Z req   talk.session.close
screen: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"
```

After (this PR, same stall):

```text
12:17:39.337Z req   talk.session.create
12:17:48.405Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" (held answers start coming back, about 12 s in)
(stall turned off by the operator at about 12.7 s, not logged)
12:18:03.915Z append appends=151
12:18:13.912Z append appends=251
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat, Talk stays on

40 second stall per answer:
12:19:02.948Z hold  held=1   stallMs=40000
21:19:31.897 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:19:32.953Z req   talk.session.close
```

![Before: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/before.png)
![After: "Realtime audio input fell behind" notice during the stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-fell-behind.png)
![After: "Microphone input recovered" notice, Talk still on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-recovered.png)

Re-run at this head (`170d5c59956`, same Gateway, fake provider and proxy, each held answer delayed 12 s; screenshot times are the host clock, which matches the proxy's):

```text
13:14:31.185Z req    talk.session.create
13:14:44.146Z hold   held=1   stallMs=12000
13:15:01.746Z append appends=301
13:15:08      screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
13:15:15.876Z append appends=351      (14.1 s for 50 appends instead of 5 s: frames past the budget were dropped, not sent)
13:15:16      screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part", Talk still on
13:15:20.854Z append appends=401
...
13:17:30.856Z append appends=1701
13:17:57.360Z close  who=client code=1006 appends=1952 held=31   (held: running count of held answers; the operator closed the app)
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat
```

Watch display (rendered by `WearVoiceLayoutTest` under Robolectric, round 192 dp, not on a watch): before this commit the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" while the relay reports the notice; now it shows each notice.

![Watch before: "Listening · 0:00" while input fell behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-before.png)
![Watch after: "Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-fell-behind.png)
![Watch after: "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-recovered.png)

Mixed versions with the latest stable (`v2026.10.9`, `8b18b5578f6`): the new `notice` field crosses the phone-Watch protocol in both directions while one side still runs the stable release. A throwaway JUnit test (not committed) ran in `:wear-shared` of each tree and passed the real encoded bytes between them: this head's `WearProtocolCodec.encode` of a Talk event with each notice, decoded by the stable `WearProtocolCodec.decode` and `WearRealtimeTalkCodec.decode`, and the stable encoding of a listening event decoded by this head.

```text
head wrote    {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"notice":"INPUT_FELL_BEHIND"}}
stable read   WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(attemptId=attempt-1, active=true, listening=true, speaking=false, status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[])
stable read   (same for INPUT_RECOVERED)
stable wrote  {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"conversation":[]}}
head read     WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(..., status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[], notice=null)
```

An updated phone with a stable Watch keeps Talk working and the Watch shows its usual status text; a stable phone with an updated Watch sends no notice and the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" as before. In the stable release both codecs already share `WearProtocolCodec.json`, which sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `explicitNulls = false`.

Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same emulator, same isolated Gateway and proxy, no stall): the stable play debug build was installed on a wiped Android 16 emulator, paired with the Gateway (operator and node approved), and the Talk speaker set to "Muted" in Voice settings. This head's build was then installed over it with `adb install -r` (no uninstall; both builds are version code 2026080201, `firstInstallTime` unchanged, `lastUpdateTime` changed).

```text
14:57:11.572Z close  who=client code=1006   (the install stops the stable app)
14:57:14.909Z req    connect                (same device ID, no pairing request, no onboarding)
screen: Overview with Gateway "Online"; Voice settings still show "Enable speaker · Muted"
14:57:44.825Z req    talk.session.create
14:58:05.492Z append appends=201            (Talk "Listening")
```

After the upgrade the Overview's Nodes row shows "Review node access" instead of "1 online": `openclaw nodes list` on the same Gateway shows the node in `pending-reapproval` with the same 7 caps and 14 commands as approved and one changed permission, `microphone` false to true, because the microphone was granted after the node was approved and 14:57:14 was the first reconnect since; the stable build, installed back over this head, reconnects into the same `pending-reapproval` and shows the same row, so it does not come from this change.

Observed result: on the base, Talk ends 8 seconds into the stall; with this PR it drops audio past the budget with the notice, recovers when the answers arrive, and ends only after an append is unanswered for 30 seconds.

Regression tests: `TalkModeManagerTest.stalledAppendsDropInputPastThreeSecondsWithoutEndingTalk` feeds 31 frames while every append is unanswered, expects 30 appends, the fell-behind notice and Talk still on, then answers one append and expects the recovered notice and the next frame sent. It fails on the base (the 31st frame is sent) and passes with this PR. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest` has the same case for the Watch relay and also asserts the 30 second deadline on every append, which pins the deadline constant both relays share; it changes the relay's callback type, so it does not compile on the base. It also asserts the notice the relay sends to the Watch. `WearVoiceLayoutTest` has two new listening cases with each notice; they fail with the previous Watch screen code (the notice text is not on screen) and pass with this PR, and they check the text fits the round screen at font scale 1 and 1.3 in English and in the German locale (which shows the English text until the native locale refresh adds the translation).

Checks at this head: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*' :wear:testDebugUnitTest :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:lintDebug` (848 tests, 0 failures); `:app`, `:benchmark`, `:wear` and `:wear-shared` `ktlintCheck`; `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; `git diff --check`. `TalkModeManagerTest` was run again on the base with the test file carried over: the new test times out at 31 appends there, and the other 111 tests pass on both sides. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI: the previous head failed `preflight` with "Native generated locale artifacts must be isolated from source changes", and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed because of it. That head carried English placeholders in 21 Watch `values-*/strings.xml` files. This head leaves those files unchanged, so the native locale refresh workflow fills them. `node scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs --base 315fba74e12` exits 1 with that message on the previous head and exits 0 on this one.

CI at this head ([run 41094221772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772)): `preflight`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `android-test-wear`, `android-ktlint` and `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` passed. `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772/job/124196671436) while installing the Android Emulator, before the emulator started or any test ran: `sdkmanager` reported "Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel" while preparing the Android Emulator package, and the job uploaded no test results. `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because of that job. The same job passed on main in [run 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777/job/124295092007) (that run is red for unrelated Node and UI jobs). That job has not passed on this head; it needs a rerun.

The CI seconds below come from the JUnit reports of `android-test-play` (phone files) and `android-test-wear` (Watch file). CI tests the PR merged into main, where `TalkModeManagerTest` has 113 tests.

| Test file | Local wall (Gradle, this head) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 0.84 s for the new test (file 17.8 s, 112 tests, Gradle `--max-workers=4` with other modules running) | 0.77 s for the new test (file 14.8 s, 113 tests) |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` | 0.16 s for the new test (file 1.1 s, 26 tests) | 0.01 s for the new test (file 0.38 s, 26 tests) |
| `apps/android/wear/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/wear/WearVoiceLayoutTest.kt` | two more cases in the existing layout loop (file 7.9 s, 12 tests) | file 4.5 s, 12 tests |

Simplify pass: no change. One budget type serves both relays instead of two copies of the policy, and each new test covers a different relay. Against the merge base: production +147/−15 lines, tests +135/−6, docs +2, Watch English strings +2, translation source +4.

Not covered: no real phone and no real Watch. The phone runs used the Android 16 emulator. No Wear OS device is available, and no Wear OS emulator image is installed; pairing an emulator also needs the Play Store companion app and a Google sign-in. So there are no Watch screenshots or recordings with transport logs from a live call. The phone-side Watch relay is proven by its unit test, the Watch screen by Robolectric renders, and the phone-Watch payload against the latest stable by the codec run above. The device runs used an older Gateway build (see above); the change is client-only. Non-English locales show the English notices on both the phone and the Watch until the native locale refresh translates them.

Follow-up: the microphone transcription stream (`NodeRuntime` `appendTranscriptionAudio`, used by `MicCaptureManager`) also sends `talk.session.appendAudio` with an 8 second deadline. It is a separate feature outside the realtime Talk contract, so it is left for its own change.

prs.title: fix(cua-computer): restore desktop element references with CUA 0.37
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CUA 0.37 defaults native window accessibility trees to Markdown, but the OpenClaw adapter consumes structured `elements`. A real desktop can be visible and accept keyboard input while `get_window_state` returns no usable element references, preventing element-based actions such as `set_value`.

Explicitly request `tree_format: "elements"` at the existing driver boundary. Keep the normal opaque-reference lifecycle, permissions, observation requirements and native integrity checks unchanged. No model-facing schema/description, configuration, SDK or string-normalization changes.

Original one-line repair and regression by @huidongchen148; the contributor commit is preserved. Consolidate the driver's default behavior into the existing shared test fixture instead of duplicating setup, and remove the now-unneeded test allocation. Production **+1/-0**; tests **+6/-7 (net -1)** against merge base `94451cf42bb910c8eaa4c4fc13873a8b787708ce`. Provider documentation explains structured observations.

## Evidence

[Built runtime proof, exact results and inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190700#issuecomment-6565031850).

Four fresh runs through the **built Gateway → admitted agent turn → computer tool → real managed CUA/X11 → Mousepad** in secretless Debian 12/arm64 Docker, Node 24.22.1, CUA 0.37.0:

- Frozen main `e99c7b529d8e9d5d7c0062d48457ae8f71a13002`, twice: no usable native element refs.
- Candidate, twice: seven real refs; `set_value` using the actual observation/editor capabilities writes `restored native editor`.
- Independent actual clipboard readback and fresh accessibility observation verify both native edits.
- Unchanged keyboard `type` control succeeds on all four runs with exact clipboard readback.

Focused checks: commands, driver-result and reference-lifecycle suites **52/52 passed** (36.61s runner wall time; 29.04s Vitest duration including cold compilation). The focused regression fails on frozen main at `expect(elements).toHaveLength(1)` because the elements array is absent (one expected failure, 39 skipped; 32.46s runner wall time). Targeted Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted CI owns broader checks and type/lint gates.

## What Problem This Solves

- Automatic speech needs its own persistent language or phrasing preference while retaining the full written reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the existing per-agent preference path and summary request. Bound instructions to 2000 characters and preserve the original short text when the model fails.

Bumps the swift-deps group with 1 update in the /apps/macos directory: [github.com/openclaw/peekaboo](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo). Updates `github.com/openclaw/peekaboo` from 4.9.6 to 4.9.7
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/openclaw/peekaboo's releases.

v4.9.7

4.9.7 - 2026-10-23

Highlights: Report window close through the daemon as closed when an app keeps the closed window alive; let see observe Chrome windows whose titles carry the app name or are elided; close apps that re-exec themselves with --foreground; and keep the Mac chat, menu bar and Inspector accurate.

  • Report window close through the daemon or Bridge as closed when the app keeps the closed NSWindow alive, instead of exiting 1 with an indeterminate postcondition: the Bridge readback now applies the same exact-window Accessibility presence check as the in-process path. Thanks @​goutamadwant! #1131, fixes #1129.
  • Let peekaboo see observe Chrome and other apps whose Accessibility window title appends the application name or whose WindowServer title is middle-elided, instead of failing with "inconsistent response evidence: window-context window title". Thanks @​L1uYun! #1130.
  • Close windows of apps that re-exec themselves with window close --foreground, whose frontmost PID AppKit reports as -1. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1124.
  • Classify Dock separators and the Trash from their Accessibility subroles, so peekaboo dock list hides separators unless --include-all is passed, reports included separators as separator instead of blank unknown items, and identifies a localized Trash (such as "Papierkorb") as trash. #1120.
  • Use the Mac app's saved Vision model for image analysis even when its provider does not report vision support (OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, LM Studio and many Ollama models), surfacing the provider's error instead of silently switching models. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1127.
  • Keep the Mac chat's streaming answer together when you queue a follow-up, and keep Retry on the prompt that failed. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1126.
  • Show a failed Mac agent tool as failed, not completed, in the menu bar, while cancelled tools stay cancelled. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1134.
  • Highlight the Inspector control in the front window under the pointer, including floating panels and popup items past their window, instead of the smallest control anywhere on screen; windows of untracked apps such as the Dock now stop the hover from reaching what they cover. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1133.
  • Place Inspector highlight boxes on the correct display when a display does not start at the primary display's origin. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1132.
  • Restore source builds after the pinned MCP Swift SDK commit became unreachable upstream when its pull request branch was rebased. #1135.
  • Remove the unused public DialogError.inputSuppressedUnderTests case from PeekabooAutomationKit along with the dead test-only dialog typing hook that threw it; release builds could never throw it, so only SwiftPM consumers that switch over every DialogError case need to drop that branch. #1123.

prs.title: fix: avoid blocking database writes while copying inspection snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: database writes can stall behind a read-only inspection snapshot when reflinking a large, fragmented live SQLite database.

Related: #187989 addresses a separate history-read writer-admission stall.

## User Impact

Artifact-preserving inspections no longer request source-inode cloning or copy offload. They still copy and validate the full database image, so they can consume substantial I/O, time, and temporary disk space. This does not defragment existing databases or establish that all reported latency is resolved. No schema, durability, retention, or live deployment changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

A read-only incident trace caught a snapshot worker in `FICLONE`/Btrfs metadata reservation while a database writer waited on the same source inode. Use the existing fs-safe byte-copy mode for both synchronous and asynchronous artifact-preserving inspection. Keep source identity checks, coherent-family verification, private recovery, publication, and cleanup unchanged.

The shared file-copy owner accepts the transfer policy; verified offline snapshot publication retains its existing clone-first behavior and space-admission callback before byte-copy fallback.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on the base: the synchronous inspection returned a clone/offload transfer rather than a byte copy. It passes with the fix and also checks the asynchronous owner, retained data, and cleanup.
- 52 focused tests passed across inspection copies, file-copy admission/publication, verified snapshot transfer, and copy-on-write snapshot ownership.
- Native Linux/Btrfs probe exercised both real inspection-copy owners with SQLite data: expected rows, unchanged source bytes, and successful cleanup; `strace` observed zero `FICLONE` or `copy_file_range` calls. This is a local mechanism proof, not a production-scale latency benchmark or live Gateway rollout.
- Final focused regression run: 9 tests passed, including the extracted sync/async byte-copy regression. Core and storage-test TypeScript checks passed. Focused lint/format, documentation MDX, and test-line budget checks passed.
- Fresh independent review of the final patch found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review was diff/evidence-based; native execution and focused test receipts were verified separately.
- One bounded regression adds 55 test lines, explicitly allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/sqlite-inspection-byte-copy.txt`; no broad snapshot/test expansion.

The exact top-level caller of the incident snapshot and the remaining cost of existing shared extents are not established by this change.

prs.title: fix: session archive read exhausts memory when an archive expands past its stored size
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reading a retained transcript archive can exhaust memory and crash the process when the stored bytes expand far past their size on disk, because the reader decoded the entire payload into a single string.

An 8 KB `.zst` archive could declare a 256 MB payload and the reader allocated all of it. A 16 KB archive expanded past Node's maximum string length and threw only after already allocating about 1 GB.

## User Impact

User impact: oversized archives now decode through a bounded stream straight into the read cache, so a crafted or corrupt artifact can no longer take the gateway down while history is being read.

- Existing history stays readable. Decoding is size-independent: streaming keeps peak memory near one chunk, and the byte budget reflects cache-volume exposure (4 GiB per artifact) rather than any limit on valid content. Multibyte archives above 512 MiB — which the incremental archive path and UTF-8 encoding can both produce — remain readable.
- Refusals are visible and actionable. A limit failure propagates out of the archive reader instead of being caught and reported as "no archive", and the error states that the archive is unchanged and tells the operator to export the session again or move the archive out of the sessions directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reader decoded whole archives into a string, so memory scaled with plaintext regardless of archive size. Two follow-on problems appeared once a bound was added: failures were swallowed by three consumers and surfaced as missing history, and the bound was derived from V8's string limit, which is not the producer's limit.

Writers bound **encoded** bytes (`MAX_SESSION_MAINTENANCE_BATCH_ARCHIVE_BYTES`, 64 MiB), not plaintext. The incremental archive path (`transformArchiveBytesIncrementally`, #170853) stages rows without an archive-sized string, and multibyte content can exceed 512 MiB of UTF-8 while staying inside every producer limit. A string-derived ceiling therefore refused history the product had written successfully.

This change addresses all three:

- `materializeSessionArchiveForRead` streams `read → zstd → cache file` through `zlib.createZstdDecompress`, counting decoded bytes as chunks arrive; peak memory is one chunk.
- The budget is 4 GiB, sized for the cache volume rather than for content compatibility, and the cold-storage envelope keeps its own independent 64 MiB bound.
- Archive readers rethrow `SessionArchivePlaintextLimitError` instead of treating it as a corrupt or mismatched generation, and the error carries the stored size, the budget, and a recovery action that leaves the archive intact.
- The budget belongs to the stream only. `readSessionArchiveContentSync` keeps its original unchecked behavior: its result has to be a string in memory anyway, and Node rejects any zstd `maxOutputLength` above 4,294,967,296 outright, so reusing the cache budget there broke publication checks for ordinary archives. `materializeSessionArchiveForRead` owns the 4 GiB cache-volume bound; the synchronous reader owns nothing.
- No production code exists only for tests. The earlier revision restored `decodeSessionArchiveBytes`, which main had removed in #183130; it is gone again, and the format assertion uses Node's independent `zstdDecompressSync` so the encoder cannot validate itself.

## Evidence

Measured against the real modules on Node v24.15.0. Archive bytes come from the real encoder; RSS is process peak for a read-only run, so payload construction is excluded.

| Input | Plaintext | Result | Peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,211 B `.zst` | 256 MB | materialized, 743 ms | 142 MB |
| 57,613 B `.zst` (CJK, 3 bytes/char) | 600 MiB | materialized, 2.5 s | 147 MB |
| before, 8,211 B `.zst` | 256 MB | materialized | 855 MB |
| before, 16,403 B `.zst` | 512 MB | threw `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG` after ~1 GB | — |

The 600 MiB run is the compatibility case: it exceeds the previous 512 MiB ceiling and still reads through the stream.

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs read-bomb.mts bomb-256.jsonl.deleted.2026-10-26T00-00-00.000Z.zst
{"plaintextBytes":268435456,"ms":743,"outcome":"materialized"}
peak-rss-kb=142252

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs read-bomb.mts cjk-600.jsonl.deleted.2026-10-26T00-00-00.000Z.zst
{"plaintextBytes":629145600,"ms":2499,"outcome":"materialized"}
peak-rss-kb=146892
```

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs e2e-read.mts
{"case":"normal archive read","storedBytes":6574,"plaintextBytes":355328,"records":5001,"header":{"type":"session","id":"sess-9f2c","version":3},"lastMessage":"m-4999","ms":69}
{"case":"oversized archive","error":"SessionArchivePlaintextLimitError","message":"Session archive /tmp/e2e-read-5NKbmj/oversized.jsonl.deleted.2026-10-26T00-00-00.000Z expands past the 4 GiB cache budget (4294967297 stored bytes). Decoding stopped before anything was written and the archive itself is unchanged; export the session again, or move the archive out of the sessions directory, to read it."}
```

That run uses the real encoder, the real materializer, and parses the cache the way history readers do: a retained archive with a session header and 5,000 messages reads back as 5,001 records with the expected first and last ids, and the oversized case returns the refusal text quoted above rather than an empty page.

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs read-via-gateway.mts proof-256.zst
{"case":"gateway history read","storedBytes":24665,"totalMessages":0,"messages":0,"transcriptSource":"reset-archive","ms":7733,"outcome":"read"}
peak-rss-kb=558516

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs read-via-gateway.mts proof-bomb.zst
{"case":"gateway history read","storedBytes":412889,"error":"SessionArchivePlaintextLimitError","message":"Session archive /tmp/comind/proof-bomb.zst expands past the 4 GiB cache budget (412889 stored bytes). Decoding stopped before anything was written and the archive itself is unchanged; export the session again, or move the archive out of the sessions directory, to read it.","ms":21905,"outcome":"refused"}
peak-rss-kb=539776
```

Both runs go through `ArchivedTranscriptReader.readRecentWithStats`, the entry point gateway history uses for a retained archive. The first reads a 256 MiB archive; the second expands a 4.3 GiB archive and the refusal reaches the caller as `SessionArchivePlaintextLimitError` instead of an empty page. Peak RSS is nearly identical across a 17x plaintext difference (558 MB vs 540 MB), and both numbers are dominated by the tsx harness and the transcript index scan, not by decoding: the materializer itself stays at 142 MB for the same 256 MiB input above. The index scan cost is pre-existing and unchanged here.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/archive-compression.test.ts --run
5 tests passed
```

The remaining suite (`session-transcript-readers`, `session-cost-usage-worker-io`) passed on the same change set before the rebase; they are re-verified by CI on the rebased head.

Compatibility: the budget no longer encodes a content limit, so archives that were readable before remain readable, including large multibyte ones. The synchronous reader is unchanged from `main`, so publication verification and header matching behave exactly as before; only the streamed history read carries the cache budget.

Not covered here: no real installation was sampled above 600 MiB; the streaming path is size-independent, so that run stands in for larger archives.

<details>
<summary>Changed files</summary>

- `src/config/sessions/archive-compression.ts` — stream decoding to the cache file with chunk accounting and a shared budget
- `src/config/sessions/archive-limits.ts` — stream cache-volume budget, structured error with stored size, budget, and recovery action
- `src/infra/zstd-codec.ts` — streaming decompressor alongside the sync one
- `src/gateway/session-transcript-archive-reader.ts`, `src/gateway/session-transcript-files.fs.ts` — rethrow limit failures instead of skipping the archive
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.ts`, `src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts` — await the now-async materializer
- `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` — inventory the new module
- tests — independent Node zstd format assertion, cache invalidation, corrupt-archive rejection

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): stop expanding archive reads from exhausting memory
prs.body:
Supersedes #182366, thanks @xydt-tanshanshan.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes archive reads exhausting memory when compressed session transcripts expand far beyond their stored size.

## User Impact

Archive reads now stop at the stored byte count plus 1 MiB and report an actionable error without changing the source archive. History fallback surfaces that refusal instead of returning missing history.

Compressed artifacts exceeding this expansion budget, including otherwise valid files, must be exported as uncompressed JSONL to read them through this file-reader path. Publication verification uses the original plaintext byte count it already knows, preserving compression and existing disk-budget retention. There is no schema, configuration, or archive-format change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared archive reader passed no output limit to the existing zstd codec. Its native chunk loop now enforces the limit before concatenating decoded output. The writer supplies its authoritative original UTF-8 byte count for bounded publication verification and reuse checks; ordinary archive reads do not trust a frame's declared size.

The simplification pass retains the existing codec, synchronous API, encoder, and streamed writer. The final change adds 24 net production lines for the limit, clear errors, propagation, and bounded writer verification. No unrelated deletion offsets were added.

## Evidence

- On main source `34de4be3eff02b3e6b002d10dd7ec9c8b9f42928`, an 82-byte crafted frame expands to 2 MiB: both shared-reader rejection cases fail, and the real history facade returns a page instead of rejecting. The reader remains byte-identical on inspected main `324dfc78`.
- All 74 tests pass across the six named archive-compression, archive-publication, archive-worker, history-reader, usage-worker, and history-eviction files. They cover refusal, unchanged bytes, near-budget compressed content, compressed publication/readback/reuse, large archive preservation, visible history errors, usage cancellation, and disk-budget retention.
- CI found a retention regression in the first head's encoding fallback. The exact failing retention scenario passes with main's reader/writer source (2 selected cases) and with the final fix; the final encoder and streamed writer are unchanged from main. The full six-file replay passes in 97.74 s, including compiler-cache preparation. Earlier isolated owner and history-reader runs took 0.675 s and 13.48 s. Exact-head [CI run 41355778736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41355778736) passed in 24 min 11 s wall time. The separate 64-line test allocation funds the regression contracts.
- Touched-file formatting and typed lint pass; `git diff --check` passes. PR CI supplies broad proof; no broad local suites, packaging, containers, browser tests, deployment, or live-state changes were run.
- Independent Codex autoreview covered the complete final working-tree candidate against `34de4be3eff02b3e6b002d10dd7ec9c8b9f42928` at P0–P2. It found no additional defects in that candidate. Its sole finding was explicitly INDEX-only, identifying the previous encoding fallback; staging the reviewed working tree removes it. The earlier writer/readback finding is resolved by the authoritative source-byte bound. This is a findings report with those resolutions, not a claim of a machine `scoped-clean` verdict.
- Contributor code was read through GitHub and was never checked out or executed on this host. This is an independent implementation on main with human contributor credit preserved.
