prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact candidate head: `f1c66eb055618f0aa79505abd7bfacb1498445c8`; frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree: `de8299f6f3c4776fce1a0e00db9843f8289c8f7a`.
- Focused test command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.watch-subscribe-retry.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.session-patch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts` → 5 files, **43/43 passing** on the merged tree. Core and extension TypeScript gates and touched-file formatting pass under Node 26.7.0.
- Production path exercised by the mock-Gateway proof: `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` → `createIMessageGroupActivationResolver` in `group-activation.ts` → runtime `getSessionEntryInWorker` → SQLite worker-backed read; admission uses `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`. The test calls the production decision function with a routed group and real isolated SQLite store, not Apple's Messages transport.
- The proof harness writes persisted activation entries through `runtime.agent.session.upsertSessionEntry` (simulating the command's persistence), rather than issuing live `/activation` commands. Command owner-gating/persistence is separately covered by `commands-session.activation.test.ts`. This distinction matters: it is not a single end-to-end live Apple/command receipt.
- The exact frozen-base deterministic preflight is green after a lockfile-frozen dependency refresh. It passes extension production/test type graphs, touched-file formatting/lint, dead exports, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. The refresh exposed and the branch repaired a strict session-entry test fixture that lacked required identity/timestamp fields and literal activation typing.

Related: #184848, #188229. This addresses collected-receiver restoration; pending catalog custody and host completion-handoff changes remain separate.

## What Problem This Solves

Sending new input to a completed native child after its monitor entry is collected can recreate the child's initial assignment instead of giving the accepted follow-up its own completion identity.

## User Impact

Follow-ups to a completed child produce a separate completion; duplicate notifications do not redeliver it, and retiring the parent prevents late receiver execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Input preparation and receiver notifications now restore an observation without recreating executable work. The existing admission owner retains the accepted source and creates the assignment for the exact native turn. Initial spawns, current source/tree checks, cancellation and completion delivery keep their existing owners.

## Evidence

- Base: `9f3da25c107e88380e84f8a70f8f703422ba5995`. Candidate: `95f06b12bbeaec0403cbcb1c1d8fc5995ebf57ff`.
- Base reproduction: all five new regressions fail at the premature initial-assignment claim; nine existing scope-denial controls pass (Vitest 260.68s). The first sandbox attempt failed during compiler setup and is not counted as reproduction.

Node 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, Windows repository wrapper with its supported Node fallback.

It exercises the real monitor/admission/delivery owners with fixed external RPC/delivery I/O. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve persistent restricted continuation
prs.body:
Related: #144917. Builds on #156651 (mywondvision).

Related to #148329, but does **not** resolve it: authority/client-dependent tool descriptions, schemas, and catalog membership can still change the durable fingerprint. This PR addresses compatible restricted continuation and temporary-grant isolation.

## What Problem This Solves

A persistent tool restriction can make an ordinary Codex follow-up start a new native thread and resend assembled history. The host must distinguish a conversation-owned restriction from a temporary run-owned restriction or additive grant.

## User Impact

Compatible persistent restrictions retain the native conversation across warm turns and Gateway restarts. Temporary restrictions and additive grants use isolated owners and return to the durable conversation afterward. No-op wildcard and scheduled policies retain ordinary continuation.

When a persistent creation policy changes, the existing guarded replacement operation prepares a successor using already-assembled history. Failed startup preserves the previous binding and protected owners retain their refusal behavior. In the covered configured-MCP ownership transition, predecessor cleanup follows replacement commit; independent rotation reasons retain their existing behavior. Automatic guarded recovery is approved under the current maintainer repair-and-land authority: see [the recorded decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173383#issuecomment-6209963483). Temporary grants remain isolated and protected-owner refusals remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restricted-resume and creation-policy fingerprint foundation adapts mywondvision's #156651 at `7e56f0b802b8fe9deb3d5ed95b469fb50aa69278`, with attribution retained. This contribution adds host-produced policy lifetime, guarded recovery, prepared-history replay, and regression coverage. If merged, maintainers or the original author can close #156651 as superseded; no prior agreement is claimed.

The optional persisted fingerprint needs no schema migration. Legacy unattested owners transition once through existing guards. No compaction implementation, retry subsystem, replacement database, or separate bootstrap-acceptance PR #172450 is included.

The follow-up commit `27e2843f8901d45174b19bf0cd90503e86d107b2` fixes a static import cycle, aligns ordinary-run test fixtures without weakening assertions or shared defaults, preserves temporary grant lifetime across the private-state boundary, and orders restricted replacement checks after configured-MCP ownership classification. The follow-up is 13 files, +59/-21; the full PR is 31 files, +1252/-95, including its adapted foundation and tests.

## Evidence

The latest prepared head is `9fbda548dcc9e3dbb77859eeca8ba4a8ef4102a3`. It adds one test-fixture correction to the production candidate below: the retired-owner fixture now explicitly enables tools and verifies that its session binding exists before testing handoff. The default disabled-tools policy correctly selects transient ownership and must stay isolated.

- Original-order reproduction at `436af482425d1845f4d6aab18ab84e02c7bcd39f`: 2 timed-out retired-owner tests, 15 passed; 287.23s Vitest / 296.29s wrapper.
- Corrected file: **17 passed**, 45.31s Vitest / 49.11s wrapper (`pnpm test -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`). No tests added; both lifecycle assertions remain intact. On [exact-head CI38870439836](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38870439836), all 17 startup cases passed; reported test time totals 3.973s, with the two repaired cases taking 209ms and 190ms. The containing shards passed 243 tests across 17 files.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace validation, and fresh independent correction review passed. Production source is unchanged by this correction.
- The previous CI run also reported the unrelated UI `consistent-return` failure already fixed in [PR173976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173976) (`8425c9a0cf88a08614785703753dea3c92811feb`), and one self-hosted runner lost communication without reporting a test failure. No jobs were rerun to obtain green; the real fixture correction receives normal new-head CI.

The production candidate `436af482425d1845f4d6aab18ab84e02c7bcd39f` integrates frozen main `d4babe8e8ba448bd21bdc4c89de0d223a4353faa`, preserving its context-engine assembly boundary. Review also found that a trusted scheduled wildcard incorrectly inherited turn scope from an unchanged conversation denylist/profile. The correction preserves conversation lifetime for that case while retaining account-scoped scheduled policy isolation, finite caps, and temporary grants.

The same review also caught a raw wildcard fingerprint mismatch. Host-attested no-op wildcard changes now preserve the native thread in both warm and cold transitions; unscoped, finite, empty and symbol-restricted policies remain isolated. The existing system-agent allowlist predicate is shared by selection and policy preparation.

Validation on the integrated candidate:

- 113 tests passed across selection, restricted continuation, configured-MCP ownership and context continuity before the two review corrections.
- Both new warm/cold wildcard regressions failed on the uncorrected candidate. The scheduled-policy regressions also failed before correction.
- Final policy and restricted-continuation suites: **44 passed** (22 each); 54.57s combined wrapper wall. Per-file single-worker times: policy 25.92s; lifecycle 22.98s. Existing fixtures were extended.
- Five final plugin-handoff cases passed (79 unrelated cases unselected), 49.68s Vitest / 60.82s wrapper. Scoped core type-aware lint and formatting passed. Fresh independent final review found no actionable P0-P2 defects.
- Full extension/type gates were not rerun locally after the known SDK declaration-build prerequisite limitation; hosted CI remains authoritative.
- Incoming-head validation passed 115 tests in five focused files; that remains prior-head evidence.

No current live-model, ShellBench token, latency or resident-memory improvement is claimed.

## Prior contributor evidence

Current source: `27e2843f8901d45174b19bf0cd90503e86d107b2`; tree `1480084c7962f6afa41959a9f37da43e9d03a46f`. Follow-up patch from reviewed head `604bc2738a19ec85085801a72451bf41b681d536`: SHA-256 `b8ecd1aac3d0cb68904fa85018484be58da59e57daf597a29e424ecea5899c32`.

- Focused source verification passed: 35 tests for the first failed CI bundle; 129 tests covering the second failed bundle and affected restricted lifecycle; 108 tests for the grant handoff regression. These runs overlap and are **not** an additive unique-test count. The grant regression first failed before its correction. All 29 failures from the second original CI bundle are present in the passing run. Scoped types, lint, formatting, and the import-cycle check pass.
- Canonical `qaRuntime` build passed on Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.10.1. Linux smoke and all 22,247 built-file hashes match the admitted manifest before and after the effect proof. Generated build metadata embeds the pre-commit base; the full source/patch/runtime manifest establishes exact equivalence to the published commit.
- Real isolated Gateway and native Codex 0.160.1, with a deterministic local Responses provider: **12 completed turns, 24 requests, six actual permitted receipt-file writes and six rejected calls** in one physical OpenClaw session. Temporary grant withdrawal returns to the original native owner; cold restart retains it. Policy narrowing and broadening create and then reuse the appropriate successor. Native accepted/completed IDs match terminal Gateway receipts; all owned processes stopped.
- Sender isolation passed through real QA channel ingress: Alice -> Bob -> Alice, one physical session, native A-B-A, six provider requests; Alice writes succeed, the forced Bob call is rejected, and channel processing acknowledgments plus final replies complete.

CI tested merge `1383e0296ac2b8dac9543796d7a3e1ab4c17cade` (source head27e2843f into basecfbbe0c2); runtime proofs above bind the published source tree separately.
- Independent review and canonical Codex autoreview found no confirmed P0-P2 findings within the supplied changed scopes and contracts. Reviews did not execute the tests themselves.

The new provider intentionally forces tool calls; this is final-effect and ownership evidence, **not real-model recall or reasoning evidence**. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve configured context budgets during assembly
prs.body:
Related: #158606, #158740, #168986, #172010, #171495.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes context engines assembling more Codex history than the following projection can retain, causing useful earlier context to be discarded after assembly.

## User Impact

History assembly uses the same existing reserve and ceiling as projection, while the current request, instructions, tools and images retain upstream budget protection. Host assembly limits remain separate from native model-window metadata. No configuration migration or user action is required; token-to-character estimates remain approximate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the assembly allowance and rendered-history limit together. For an 80,000-token allowance, the existing reserve yields an assembly ceiling of 60,000; the upstream input reservation can lower it further. Large allowances remain bounded by the existing 1,000,000-character projection ceiling (250,000 approximate tokens). Unknown native budgets retain the existing fallback.

The October 16 integration of main (`5f05696bc73c0ed47b6e00cd97d9ad5cd042ca26`) preserves #171495's host-policy owner, current-input reservation and durable completion propagation. The earlier custom host-policy override and its dispatch-test delta are removed. The remaining production changes cover assembly/projection limits and native metadata separation; limits combine with a minimum, without subtracting the output reserve twice.

Residual diff against that main revision: 7 files, +239/-37; production is 4 files, +36/-15. The native input-character limit and approximate conversion policy are unchanged. This is not a universal overflow or lossless-memory solution.

## Evidence

Current head: `e77a4713e0982483d7c3e4fff6bd6f0461074ac8`.

- Five focused suites passed 117 tests after main integration. Lint then identified a test-file line limit; two regressions moved into the existing native context-budget suite. Both final affected suites passed 32 tests (22 lifecycle, 10 native budget). The other four suites and production files were unchanged; these are incremental runs, not a newly repeated full-suite run.
- Three discriminating assertions fail against pinned main owners: runtime assembly allowance, large-window assembly ceiling, and the unconfigured projection ceiling. Candidate owners were restored byte-for-byte.
- Final formatting, diff checks, changed core/plugin lint and scoped TypeScript checks pass. Scoped roots retain repository compiler options and lint rules; this is not a full-repository typecheck. Resource-limited preparation attempts are excluded from successful results.
- Independent canonical Codex autoreview assessed the exact seven-file residual diff plus unchanged owner/helper context: no actionable P0-P2 findings. It was source review, not test execution or live inference.
- Historical real CLI A/B proof below remains pinned to its original revisions. No new live model call or Gateway deployment is claimed for this main integration. Hosted CI must validate the new head independently.

The final native budget suite covers model matching, stale observations, unknown windows, authored caps, reserves and the projection ceiling. The lifecycle suite retains current-input/image reservation and thread/bootstrap ownership controls. The large-window fixture observes actual emitted input, including the current request and retained latest history marker.

<details>
<summary>Historical real-model proof and October 14 validation (original revisions)</summary>

Built and exercised the exact parent `56686ac65bc6e1922d0787d2cbb1afcfe687ba50` and candidate `f667624337a596f4e86ecb89de6900e8e77a3b53` with Node 24.19.0. The shipped `openclaw.mjs agent --local` path ran through native Codex 0.160.0, real Lossless Claw 1.1.1, and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. Four synthetic cases, two continuations each: **8/8 real Responses requests completed with HTTP 200, no model fallback.**

| Case | LCM allowance, both turns | Rendered history characters, turns 1 / 2 | Actual model input and response |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Parent, short control | 128,000 fallback | 4,533 / 4,879 | Goal and constraint retained; exact markers returned |
| Candidate, short control | 12,000 | 4,533 / 4,879 | Goal and constraint retained; exact markers returned |
| Parent, pressure | 128,000 fallback | 24,000 / 24,000 | Goal and constraint absent; model returns `UNKNOWN` for both |
| Candidate, pressure | 12,000 | 36,789 / 37,135 | Goal and constraint retained; exact markers returned |

The configured cap is 32,000 in every case. Pressure history contains 28 synthetic messages, 41,443 characters of canonical message JSON. LCM imports all 28 and estimates 10,198 tokens on its first assembly. Its own logs establish the received assembly allowance; native rollout records establish the rendered history lengths; a transparent local recorder establishes the actual model input and streamed response. These character counts concern projected history, not the full native request.

Each pair of continuations keeps the same native thread. All 28 original canonical events retain their hashes; parent/candidate fixture hashes and normalized configurations match. Both versions separately report the same native window observation, 30,400 with source `runtime-configured`. The host assembly allowance does not replace it. Ordinary sessions remain unpinned.

The local fixture uses supported native `model_catalog_json` and a custom Responses provider to reach `contextpilot-e4b@q8_0`; native discovery is enabled. Isolated, non-secret credential placeholders satisfy route setup, and authorization is discarded before forwarding to LM Studio. Host native registration, route selection, runtime preparation, LCM, projection, and inference are real; no changed owner is mocked. This proves the local shipped CLI path, not remote OpenAI inference. Six preliminary fixture-setup failures made zero provider requests and are excluded from the eight completed calls.

Build and execution entry points:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
node openclaw.mjs agent --local --agent proof --session-key agent:proof:budget-pressure --model openai/contextpilot-e4b@q8_0 --thinking off --timeout 120 --json --message '<synthetic marker recall request>'
```

The same command runs twice per fresh isolated case after seeding synthetic history through public session SDK APIs. LCM uses its own isolated database, `bootstrapMaxTokens: 20000`, `freshTailCount: 64`, and no plugin-side assembly-budget override. No operator Gateway, private history, or model-load setting is modified.

**Follow-up at `b9ab8c8d7bba2ed4bb777e4571bf4afb1280f239` (October 14):** corrected the stale companion expectation identified by review and added executable coverage for the smaller-caller allowance and upper assembly bound. This commit changes only three test files; production behavior is unchanged from its merged parent `c12a13ce6e9bd3eeade36ba9a318d438a60bec56`.

| Regression or control | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Previously failing dispatch companion | Full file: 12/12 pass. Preserve no-cap behavior and native start/resume assertions while expecting the separate authored host allowance. |
| Caller allowance with an authored 80,000 cap | The runtime-preparation path yields 32,000 for a 32,000 caller and 80,000 for a 120,000 caller. Native window metadata remains separate. Full file: 10/10 pass. |
| Oversized external-engine result with a 2,000,000 host allowance | Production attempt supplies 250,000 to assembly. Actual emitted `turn/start` text contains at most 1,000,000 history characters, a truncation notice, the latest history marker, and the current request; total fixture input fits the native 1,048,576-character limit. Full lifecycle file: 20/20 pass. |
| Existing ownership and projection controls | Setup 39/39, projection 32/32, native start/resume 11/11 pass, including pinned-session ownership. |

**Red/green:** the new selection against the five production owners from main parent `31da13925c12b292d67af88a7c0706ddfeb0a5b9` produces four expected assertion failures and one passing non-native control. Restoring the candidate owners byte-for-byte yields **124/124 passing tests across the six complete files**. Four serial runner commands took 180.553 seconds in total, with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.9.0. This composition evidence uses an external-engine/transport fixture; it is separate from the real local inference above.

```text
Pre-fix owners, new boundary selection: 4 failed, 1 passed
Candidate full files:                  6 passed, 124 tests passed
Targeted core/extension lint:           pass
Owning core and extension test types:  pass
Formatting and git diff --check:       pass
Independent scoped review:             no actionable P0-P2 findings
```

Equivalent focused command (executed through repository `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`):


prs.title: fix(sessions): retain early requests under tool-output pressure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large tool results can push the original goal and constraints out of bounded model context even when those requests would fit after omitting result bodies.

## User Impact

The existing `toolResultOverflow: "omit"` mode now prefers retaining earlier requests under tool-output pressure. Omitted bodies have explicit notices in the detached view; canonical transcript contents and strict readers retain their existing behavior.

Maintainer decision (Peter, October 13, 2026): approve proactive result-body omission in the existing `omit` mode so original goals and constraints survive, with canonical transcripts unchanged and SDK semantics updated. This view is lossy and can change reusable prompt prefixes; cache-performance effects have not been measured. Byte/event limits, required compaction/reset boundaries, and tool-result ownership still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing selector applies useful omissions before choosing its bounded suffix and restores the newest result bodies that fit after any prefix is dropped. The old empty-selection rescue is removed because proactive omission already accounts for the eligible result bodies. Saved-byte facts stay with each replacement rather than copying the full size map. SDK docs and caller/type comments now describe this policy.

Current main was merged into the contributor branch, preserving the original commits and regression coverage. Thanks @YuriyPopovDev.

## Evidence

- Red regression proof on exact main base `5d3d1bffdf98f062fa477309ee7ee409a06be1e1`: both added pressure cases fail because the original goal disappears (one oversized result and cumulative results). The focused run reports 2 failures, 25 skipped; 77.11 seconds in Vitest, 470.08 seconds including worker preparation and verification.
- Scoped source/test typecheck passed in 18.06 seconds; scoped full type-aware lint passed in 54.03 seconds. Formatting and diff checks passed.
- All 30 focused tests passed across the session limits, prompt-prefix, and selector suites (1,262.31 seconds wall time, including worker preparation and verification; 342.09 and 373.27 seconds in the two Vitest shards). All seven required ratchets passed: max-lines 326.87 seconds, line-cap 94.31 seconds, assertion safety 179.24 seconds, timeout race 108.06 seconds, mock exports 178.29 seconds, config docs 25.89 seconds, and plugin inventory 2.61 seconds. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed in 2,305.83 seconds wall time (37m55s of build phases on this filesystem-constrained host).
- Local macOS real-entry-point proof uses `pnpm openclaw --profile memory-overflow agent --local --agent proof --session-key ... --thinking off --timeout 300 --json`, through the native Codex harness to LM Studio `google/gemma-4-e4b`. All state, config, workspace, native homes, and recording ports are isolated.
- Before the fix, the small-result control includes all three synthetic markers and answers them correctly (8.703 seconds provider; 113.570 seconds CLI). With three 400 KB results, the actual provider request loses the goal and constraint and the model replies `UNKNOWN UNKNOWN` plus the recent-status marker (12.427 seconds provider; 113.256 seconds CLI).
- After the fix, the same cumulative-result continuation includes all three markers in the actual provider request and returns all three exactly, with zero observed tool calls (8.793 seconds provider; 555.222 seconds CLI including artifact synchronization). Post-run verification passed in 97.46 seconds: all original canonical rows remain byte-identical; the continued cumulative fixture has three appended rows.

The large results are seeded historical fixtures, not model-generated bodies. The native renderer separately elides tool-result text, so the proof checks goal/constraint presence in actual provider requests and replies; generic rendered elision alone is not counted. SDK checks at a 1,024,000-byte budget cover a single 1.1 MB result, cumulative pressure, strict-reader controls, and unchanged original transcript rows. The candidate retained every marker with one omission per pressure case (80.28 seconds to seed and check). The CLI config caps native context at 32K and the runtime reports 31,129 tokens. Proof is local macOS only. A pre-inference attempt failed during native startup (494.188 seconds CLI, zero provider requests). The successful candidate run explicitly selects the installed Codex 0.162.1 used by the baseline and uses the existing 60-second model-discovery setting after a 10-second discovery timeout on this busy host. Native one-shot runs can emit an existing client-cleanup warning after a successful turn. No latency or cache-performance improvement is claimed.

CI follow-up: the first run failed only the mock-export ratchet at `src/process/terminal-pty.test.ts:40`, inherited from its exact main base `5e9b5749d7104ab17302543a74576be9641e5841`. prs.title: fix(voice-call): forward brief language to realtime transcription
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #190682. Outbound realtime calls accept `brief.language`, but Voice Call currently supplies it only as voice instructions. The separate input-transcription language hint is dropped before the existing realtime bridge/provider path.

## Changes

Resolve a recognized ISO 639-1 language from the existing brief at the Voice Call owner and pass it through the bridge's existing `language` field. `cs` and regional tags such as `cs-CZ` supply `cs`. Malformed tags, unknown codes and free-form descriptions do not become provider language codes. Free-form descriptions still reach the existing voice instructions unchanged.

No language-name dictionary, configuration option, SDK/schema expansion, provider default, prompt change or Azure routing change.

## Evidence

Built main `528aef21ceabf96862a75096b9408592db2f1fd6` and the candidate in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Used the shipped authenticated Gateway `tools.invoke` → `voice_call` → `initiate_call` path, the real call registry, signed Twilio webhook admission, issued one-use carrier stream token, real media WebSocket handler and the OpenAI realtime bridge. The external boundary is a faithful local Twilio REST/protocol fixture with a synthetic account/token and an OpenAI realtime WebSocket fixture capturing actual `session.update` messages. No real Twilio/provider credentials or calls and no webhook/authentication bypass.

The built-in mock carrier cannot reach realtime streaming: only Telnyx outbound placement issues stream credentials, while Twilio issues them from its signed TwiML webhook. Therefore this proof uses the Twilio protocol fixture rather than claiming mock-carrier coverage. The proof-only HTTP transport adapter redirects synthetic-account Twilio REST traffic to loopback after the shipped request/SSRF admission. The provider WebSocket uses the supported configured `baseUrl`; no bridge parameters or language values are injected.

Each case below ran twice per ref, 24 calls total:

| brief.language | main transcription language | candidate transcription language |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cs` | omitted, twice | `cs`, twice |
| unset | omitted, twice | omitted, twice |
| `Czech spoken politely` | omitted, twice | omitted, twice |
| `not_a_language!` | omitted, twice | omitted, twice |
| `zz` | omitted, twice | omitted, twice |
| `cs-CZ` | omitted, twice | `cs`, twice |

Captured initial GA payloads:

```json
{"ref":"main","audio.input.transcription":{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-transcribe"}}
{"ref":"candidate","audio.input.transcription":{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-transcribe","language":"cs"}}
```

Both refs retained every supplied language string in the original `Language:` voice instruction. This proves the missing provider-request handoff, **not transcription accuracy, Czech audio recognition, call outcomes or report quality**. No model-generated audio/transcript is claimed.

Focused checks: 4 files / 76 tests passed (`realtime-handler`, `call-brief`, `runtime.realtime-routing`, OpenAI `realtime-voice-bridge-connection`), 58.12 seconds reported wall time. The extended existing outbound regression failed on main with `expected undefined to be 'cs'`; candidate passed. Final compact regression passed again; changed TypeScript formatting passed. Broad type/lint/test coverage is left to PR CI.

Smallest-fix pass: reused existing brief parsing and bridge language ownership; no parallel transport or fallback. Necessary production growth is 19 lines for safe language normalization and the missing handoff. Test net growth is 0 lines; docs +5.

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the former omitted transcription hint. No state schema, config migration or published contract changes. Blast radius is realtime Voice Call input transcription for calls carrying recognized language tags; calls without a usable hint retain their current provider payload. Existing spoken-language instructions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: preserve per-message context in collected turns
prs.body:
Supersedes #182553, thanks @goslingmanagment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when queued messages are collected into one turn, the agent cannot tell which message a sender, message ID, or timestamp belongs to.

## User Impact

Each runtime context stays labeled with its queued message, even when only one of several messages has context. Single-message turns retain their existing rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared collector already labels legacy text, but the model-facing fragments dropped those labels. Label each source at that owner, which also serves overflow summaries, and decide whether labels are needed from the number of messages.

Production LOC: **−3**. Inlined the equivalent single-use exclusive-admission predicate in the same owner to offset the label construction; batching policy is unchanged. The regression extends the existing queue-drain test; its **+6 test lines** have a dedicated allocation.

Human commit credit: Dmitriy (@dmsrg399), `Co-authored-by: Dmitriy <dmsrg399@gmail.com>`.

## Evidence

- On main `528aef21ceabf96862a75096b9408592db2f1fd6`, both regression cases fail for missing source labels: two contexts lose labels in model projection; a lone message #2 context also loses its legacy label.
- Final focused checks: `queue.collect.test.ts` **88 passed**, `queue.pending-inputs.test.ts` **7 passed**, `queue.overflow-context.test.ts` **2 passed**; combined command wall time **53.48 s**, including a cold worker preparation. The added cases took **2 ms each**. `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` **14 passed**.
- Touched-file oxlint and oxfmt checks, plus `git diff --check`, pass. PR CI supplies broad proof and compiler checks; no broad local suites were run.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the final working snapshot against `528aef21ceabf96862a75096b9408592db2f1fd6`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The commit contains that reviewed snapshot.
- Contributor source was read through PR metadata/diff only and was never checked out or run. This is an independent implementation. No live-model/channel run; the regression drains real queued messages and pins the model-facing runtime projection.

prs.title: feat(plugins): prepare automation tools before approval
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins requesting approval for an automation need a supported way to prepare its default tools against the creating turn's executable permissions and retain that authority through the approval handoff.

## User Impact

The optional `ctx.prepareCronToolSelection` callback prepares the concrete tool selection before approval. It preserves explicit empty/null/omitted selections, exact opt-out, aliases, plugin groups and execution-target restrictions. The approval-submission callback captures the original proposal and selection, rejects stale sources, and retains in-flight broker effects until their owning run settles. Preparation does not create an automation or grant execution; consumers still own approval and adoption.

**This remains a draft; full acceptance is incomplete.** Native tool availability, selected-model executor/route evidence and live consumer qualification remain open. A supported custom-model configuration can expose no shell while the existing native projection infers `read`/`exec`; a partial native bridge list is not proof of the full callable tool set.

The embedded runtime now binds this approval source during its actual tool factory assembly. It uses the admitted turn's completed tool capture after policy filtering and schema quarantine. Preparation before that capture, and callbacks retained after the tool generation retires, are rejected. This embedded path does not depend on a native Codex tool manifest.

## Why This Change Was Made

The callbacks reuse default selection, creator authority, plugin admission and invocation lifetime. Discovery is followed by current authority checks; expired or unavailable authority is rejected. The branch also preserves offered exec schemas independently of per-turn execution restrictions.

When configured MCP authority is unresolved, successful app discovery must not certify the remaining dynamic tools as a complete automation selection. The async resolver reuses the startup incompleteness predicate and rejects before app capture can recertify that partial list. This does not resolve the separate native executor-evidence gap.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: collected turns lose which queued message each runtime context belongs to
prs.body:
Related: #182176
Narrowed at a maintainer's request: the drain-side restore of overflow summary context moved to #187833. This PR now holds only the model-facing `Queued #N context:` labels, which need the prompt owner's call. It does not depend on #187833.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several queued messages are answered in one turn, the model cannot tell which queued message a runtime context (sender, message id, room-event framing) belongs to, because the per-source labels are dropped from what the model sees and a lone context among several messages is not labeled at all.

## User Impact

User impact: in a collected turn (and, with #187833, a multi-source overflow summary), each runtime context the model sees is labeled with the queued message it belongs to, so one message's sender is not read as the sender of every queued message.

## Why This Change Was Made

`collectCurrentInboundContext` already labels each source's context (`Queued #N context:`) in `text`, but session v4 projects the `fragments` to the model, and the fragments were concatenated without those labels. It also skipped labeling whenever only one source had context, so a lone context read as covering every queued message. Each context now gets a `runtime-instruction` label fragment before its own fragments, and labeling applies whenever the turn has more than one source.

This adds model-facing prompt text (one short label line per context in multi-source turns). Single-source turns are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Regression** (red on base production file, green here): `queue.collect.test.ts` › "labels a lone source context in collected text and model fragments": two collected messages, only the first with context; the turn's `text` and the projected fragments both read `Queued #1 context:` before the context.

**Gates:** `tsgo` core and `oxlint` on touched files clean; `oxfmt --check` clean; `queue.collect.test.ts` 88/88 pass.

**Cost:** one test, about 2 ms, in the existing `queue.collect.test.ts`.

**Gaps:** no live-model run for this label change; it is a prompt-content change and the regression pins the exact projected text.

**History:** the branch keeps the earlier commit and adds a merge of current main whose tree is main plus only these labels, so the PR diff is the two files above.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): named-account groups get a duplicate approval card
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a WhatsApp group attended by a named (non-default) account gets two approval cards for one exec/plugin approval, the native one and a generic forwarded copy.

## User Impact

User impact: in a group served by a named account, the requester sees one approval card (the native one) instead of two. Default-account groups, DMs, real platform threads and explicit forwarding targets behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A named account keeps its group session apart from other accounts in the same group with an internal thread id, `<channel>-account-<accountId>`. The session forwarding target carries that thread, but a standard native origin target never carries one, so the "is this the same chat as the native card?" comparison failed and the generic forwarder sent its fallback card as well.

When a standard native approval route compares a session forwarding target, it now leaves out exactly that isolation thread. The thread id is built by one new helper, `resolveGroupAccountIsolationThreadId`, which the group dispatcher also uses, so the two cannot drift apart. Real threads, another account's isolation thread, and explicit (non-session) targets are still compared as-is.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/routing/session-key.ts`: `resolveGroupAccountIsolationThreadId({channel, accountId})`, `undefined` for the default account.
- `src/auto-reply/group-thread-dispatch.ts`: builds the isolation thread with that helper (same key as before).
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-delivery-helpers.ts`: `resolveForwardingTargetForMatch` of the sync and async standard routes drops only the matching isolation thread for `source: "session"` targets.
- Tests in `session-key.test.ts`, `approval-delivery-helpers.test.ts` and `extensions/whatsapp/src/approval-native.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

- Focused tests:
  - `extensions/whatsapp/src/approval-native.test.ts`: a named-account WhatsApp group whose session target carries the isolation thread suppresses the forwarded fallback; another account's group session and a different group do not.
  - `src/plugin-sdk/approval-delivery-helpers.test.ts`: same matching rules on the sync and async standard routes: real threads, another account's isolation thread and explicit targets keep the fallback.
  - `src/routing/session-key.test.ts`: helper output for named and default accounts.
- With the three source files from `main`, the new WhatsApp and plugin-sdk cases fail (3 tests); with this PR they pass.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/whatsapp/src/approval-native.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-delivery-helpers.test.ts src/routing/session-key.test.ts src/auto-reply`: all changed-area tests pass. 9 tests in 4 unrelated `src/auto-reply` files (`stage-sandbox-media.history`, `reply.stage-sandbox-media.ssh`, `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle`, `reply-turn-admission.module-identity`) fail on this macOS machine identically with and without this change.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and oxlint on the changed files: clean.

Live run on a real WhatsApp account (one install, state kept across the update):

- Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VM. Baseline: published `openclaw@2026.10.9` (`8b18b5578f66`) + `@openclaw/whatsapp@2026.10.9` from npm. Candidate: this branch (`0363dce913b`), packed and applied with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz> --yes`; build-info commit `0363dce913b9b27055d2804a6b3bca768eca783f`, tgz sha256 `b629afc2…6d4d`. The WhatsApp plugin is unchanged (2026.10.9) and imports the approval routing from core.
- WhatsApp linked as named account `proof` by QR; `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` with only the test group, `dmPolicy: "disabled"`, `approvals.exec` `mode: "session"`, `tools.exec.mode: "ask"`. The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` with a scripted `exec` call, so no provider key is used.
- Step: one message in the test group from the phone → the agent requests the command → exec approval pending. Nobody approved; the approval was denied from the CLI afterwards.

Outbound WhatsApp sends from the gateway log when the approval was created (target is the gateway's own hash of the group JID):

```
# baseline 2026.10.9
2026-10-30T19:01:50.649Z Sent message 3EB05BAF71758D4C1E45EE -> sha256:beee5c3f0c5a (544ms)
2026-10-30T19:01:50.681Z Sent message 3EB0DA9E32F2153532C96C -> sha256:beee5c3f0c5a (542ms)

# candidate 0363dce913b
2026-10-30T19:14:27.360Z Sent message 3EB0886845D8D0C6ED96B0 -> sha256:beee5c3f0c5a (255ms)
```

| | Baseline 2026.10.9 | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Approval cards in the group (phone) | 2 | 1 |
| Sends when the approval is created | 2, 32 ms apart | 1 |
| Sends after the CLI deny (resolution notices + agent reply) | 3 | 2 |

Phone numbers, the group JID and names are left out. The linked device was removed and the VM purged afterwards.

prs.title: fix: unblock Doctor upgrades from beta v16 agent databases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #190666. An npm update from 2026.7.2-beta.6 can leave Doctor refusing every v16 agent database for missing derived triggers, blocking later migrations and Gateway startup. Reported by @katie-hemus.

## User Impact

Doctor preserves the original database, validates session identities, and restores missing canonical invalidation triggers inside its existing schema transaction. Invalid rows and unrelated schema drift still refuse with preservation/support guidance. Complete-trigger v16 databases retain their existing flow. No schema-version or public-config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Beta.6 [shipped v16 without the validity projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/4d6bdbdbf33fe3ece3c53853fab9931882ff3f3c/src/state). [#116703](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cd8a96491e2677a2330991884a5ee41396affaf5) added it without a version bump; the same-version preparation omitted trigger convergence. Historical validation retained that requirement after [#167932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6a8b0dceaf858e1ffd5d4c662aa88a095a564519).

The repair uses the existing schema facts, typed Kysely stream, parser, trigger definitions, transaction, and SQLite backup owners. Independent config-only repairs remain a follow-up: changing fail-stop ordering needs dependency classification and consistent config/agent-discovery snapshots.

## Evidence

- RED locally on `8f3da9e8e46e`: exact beta.6 SQL produces the three reported missing-trigger errors through Doctor media-persistence.
- GREEN on final `c6421baf59b3a` tree: 42 named media-persistence/historical tests, including beta repair, original backup, invalid identity, unknown column/table/index, missing table, unexpected uniqueness, drifted trigger, rollback and repeat-run controls. Vitest wall 77.70s including worker compilation. Agent DB owner suite: 60 passed, 3 existing skips (unchanged-contract proof reused).
- [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41351544566): published beta.6 package owner created v16 with app_version 2026.7.2-beta.6 and zero validity triggers. Final source candidate built successfully; real `doctor --fix --non-interactive` completed twice. Read-only verification confirms v39, integrity/FK checks, original session fields and transcript bytes. Existing Doctor delivery/title/header repairs were source-audited and checked explicitly.
- Fresh `$autoreview`: Codex P0–P2, complete `8f3da9e8e46e` to final-candidate scope; scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Assertion-safety and database-dialect ratchets pass; touched-file lint has zero errors and one 704-line owner-dispatch advisory. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head PR CI owns broad/type proof and must be fully green before landing.

The local shared dependency cache disappeared after RED proof; remaining named checks ran on Testbox. This proves published-package state to candidate CLI Doctor migration; no full installed-updater package-swap, Gateway restart, latest-stable matrix, or large-state benchmark is claimed.

Added upgrade work for a missing-trigger database: one existing full-file backup, a streaming O(session_nodes) identity read/JSON parse, catalog comparison, and up to three trigger definitions. Existing projection/index/version migrations are unchanged. The report describes 12 databases; their sizes and row counts are unavailable. No canonical session/transcript rewrite is introduced by this fix.

Simplification: no new migration manager, duplicate catalog SQL, unchecked row assertion, or duplicate trigger definitions. Production delta +89/-8; 110 regression-test lines plus the immutable 603-line published SQL fixture. The separate test-line allocation covers this previously untested published upgrade boundary.

The author simplification pass kept the response allowlist in the existing handler and removed the earlier proposal's separate helper and direct-handler mock scaffolding. prs.title: fix: personal memory hooks miss authenticated webchat users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal-memory hooks receiving no user identity for authenticated Control UI turns, causing integrations such as Honcho to fall back to an owner peer even when the transcript identifies a different person.

## User Impact

Hooks can observe the verified initiating user for each accepted UI turn, including successive turns by different people in one shared session. This does not add command, tool, or MCP permissions. Expired personal bindings skip hook dispatch or discard returned enrichment instead of becoming anonymous owner turns.

Attribution remains per accepted initiating turn; this does not add separate authorship for every coauthor merged through steering. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI intentionally omits the legacy transport sender to preserve authority boundaries. The fix carries a live, host-bound profile observation through the existing run projections solely for hook context. Dispatch rechecks it before invoking a plugin and before accepting returned results, including cached contexts and delegated ingress. The private observer reads in the captured ingress async context, so a later agent tool context does not misclassify the original human request. Live grant checks still run on every read; plugin callbacks never run in that captured context. Existing channel senders retain precedence, and the private resolver is removed before plugin delivery.

An existing pure finalize-result merger is moved unchanged to keep the edited hook runner within the repository line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against the original Gateway turn preparation path: an authenticated profile was recorded, but the hook sender was undefined.
- Eight focused test files initially passed (248 tests); the final Gateway/requester/hook bundle passed **175 tests** after adding the real agent-context regressions, covering Gateway identity, prepared-run projections, CLI/embedded hook consumers, prefix stability, profile switches, delegated revocation/abort, copied bindings, cached contexts, and revocation while handlers resolve or reject.

prs.title: Private/issue 144980 whatsapp login dm notice
prs.body:
# fix(whatsapp): explain pairing default after bare CLI login

Related: #144980

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` links an account without asking whether the number is personal or dedicated. That question only exists in the setup wizard (`openclaw onboard` / `openclaw channels add --channel whatsapp`), which writes `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` + the owner's number + `selfChatMode: true` for personal numbers.

With no `channels.whatsapp` block, the runtime falls back to `dmPolicy: "pairing"`. On a personal number, every contact who messages the owner first then receives an automated pairing code from the owner's own number. Login finishes with "✅ Linked!" and says nothing about it, so owners hear about it from their contacts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue asks for one of two things: change the runtime default for personal numbers, or warn at login. It describes the warning as "worth doing anyway". Changing the default (inferring "personal" from self-chat, or adding a login-time question) is a product decision. The issue carries `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`, so this PR leaves it alone.

This PR adds only the warning, in the WhatsApp plugin's `auth.login` hook (the CLI `channels login` path):

- After a **successful** link, if the resolved account has no explicit `dmPolicy` (channel root, `accounts.default`, or the account), print:
  > WhatsApp DMs use the default pairing policy: anyone who messages this number gets a pairing code sent from it.
  > If this is your personal number, run `openclaw channels add --channel whatsapp` and choose the personal phone setup so OpenClaw answers only you.
- Non-default accounts get `--account <id>` in the command.
- Nothing is printed when a `dmPolicy` is configured or when linking fails.
- The setup wizard calls `loginWeb` directly and then asks the personal/separate question itself, so it does not get this warning twice.
- `docs/channels/whatsapp.md` describes the reminder in the "Link WhatsApp (QR)" step.

No config, schema, default, or runtime admission behavior changes.

## User Impact

Owners who link a personal number with bare `channels login` now see at link time what `pairing` will do to their contacts, plus the exact command that switches to owner-only DMs. Existing configs with any `dmPolicy` see no change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.login.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4/4 passed. Wall time 67s locally, dominated by Vitest startup; the tests themselves take <30 ms.
  - with no config, prints the pairing explanation and `openclaw channels add --channel whatsapp`
  - for a named account, prints `--account work`
  - stays quiet with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` configured
  - prints nothing and rethrows when `loginWeb` fails
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `oxfmt` / `oxlint` on touched files: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not exercised: a live WhatsApp QR link. The change runs after `loginWeb` resolves and depends only on resolved config, and the test covers that boundary.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Product decision from the issue: default personal-number accounts (self-chat in effect, no `dmPolicy`) to owner-only `allowlist`, or have bare login ask personal vs. dedicated.
- The issue also notes that the Gateway summary line "DM + all groups; no group allowlist configured" reads broader than the effective policy.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): add allowBots mention policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost has no equivalent of Slack's `allowBots` policy. When thread participation is enabled, implicit activation also applies to other bot authors, so an allowlisted bot can trigger a turn in an engaged thread without a new explicit mention.

## Solution

- Add `allowBots: true | false | "mentions"` at account and group scope.
- Identify bot authors through the post's `from_bot` property (both boolean and Mattermost's string form) or the Mattermost user's `is_bot` field.
- In `"mentions"` mode, require explicit activation for bot authors even when thread participation would admit a human follow-up. Authorized control-command behavior is preserved.
- Keep `allowBots: false` for disabling bot-triggered turns and the default `true` for existing behavior.
- Avoid a new sender lookup in the default mode when Mattermost already supplies `sender_name`.
- Document the setting and regenerate channel config metadata.

Human thread participation and existing sender/channel restrictions remain unchanged.

The intentional `+4` channel config-surface entries are the root/account and group variants of the new `allowBots` policy (including account-scoped group overrides). This is required for Slack-compatible policy precedence, not an unrelated budget increase; the generated config docs baseline is refreshed with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19/19 passed on the fixed tree; the same regression test fails on the pre-fix schema (1 failed / 18 passed), then passes after restoration.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <changed files>` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent read-only review (xai/grok-4.7) found two P1 issues; both were fixed and covered with regressions for string/boolean `from_bot`, failed sender lookup, and group precedence. No post-fix independent re-review is claimed.
- Live Mattermost API contract check: the tested bot account returns `is_bot: true`; the tested human account omits the flag, which the `=== true` check handles.

## Local environment gaps / CI-required proof

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-posts.bot-threads.test.ts` includes the behavioral regressions, but the local suite did not start: its compiled worker was killed with exit 137 twice on the 8 GiB host, including with a 2 GiB heap cap. No passing behavioral result is claimed locally.
- Targeted `run-oxlint` did not reach linting: plugin-sdk boundary dts preparation timed out after 300 seconds. The source tree was verified clean of interruption artifacts.
- PR CI is required for the behavioral suite, lint/typecheck, and broader compatibility proof.

Closes #190151

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS session menu's "Open Session Log" action doing nothing when VS Code is installed without its `code` command on the GUI search path.

## User Impact

Session logs open in the installed VS Code app, or appear in Finder when the editor is unavailable or cannot open them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve VS Code through macOS Launch Services and observe the open result through the existing app-activation owner. This preserves the activation policy and Finder fallback.

## Evidence

### Attached production-menu screenshots

These are saved, unedited window captures from a repeat of the same production-menu checks on November 1 at 4:54–4:55 PM ET. Brian clicked the native menu and saved the Screen Sharing window; I inspected both PNG files before uploading them. They contain only the disposable guest and synthetic fixture.

The native executable is still at reviewed head `4a375b5278d01e90346e586b7ebf0020e85e968a`, SHA-256 `d1442816618c18cf3643d8a0af3a7dfeaad0c98ebb939ded1796ffdeba3eacd6`. The exact transcript is `fd4be50b-93c8-40db-a31b-e225c5087b60.jsonl`, with SHA-256 `fceff4d1096421809122302f0342d1c71dcd735f1fd0c4b175e685675da50e11`.

**VS Code outcome.** After choosing OpenClaw → Session log proof → Open Session Log, real Microsoft VS Code displays the transcript tab, full task-state breadcrumb path, and synthetic marker. The native app launch PATH still has no `code` command.

![Real Microsoft VS Code displaying the exact synthetic session transcript after the production menu action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e77da68-2348-454c-b0e7-37ab15c2e638)

**Finder outcome.** After making the task-installed editor unavailable to Launch Services, the same menu action brings Finder forward with the JSONL selected in its `agent` folder. Finder abbreviates the selected icon label; the full matching filename remains visible in the editor tab behind it. This was the menu's reveal action, not a separate manual Finder selection.

![Finder selecting the synthetic JSONL after the same production menu action with the editor unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/834a0670-ef43-4949-8cc2-10ca8336edba)

The read-only Launch Services query returned `resolvedEditorPath: null` before the Finder capture at 21:54:58 UTC and afterward at 21:57:01 UTC. The reviewed native process was PID 828. The already-running Code process, PID 393, remained behind Finder but was unavailable to bundle lookup. The app and transcript hashes above were rechecked afterward. The editor bundle and registration were then restored, and its signature and lookup were verified.

### Native menu with real Microsoft VS Code and Finder

Validated November 1 on an isolated macOS 27.0 guest, build `26A428`, at unchanged PR head `4a375b5278d01e90346e586b7ebf0020e85e968a`.

The app's exact launch PATH was `/Users/admin/macos-menu-proof-190645/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`. The task bin contained the OpenClaw runtime wrapper, and `command -v code` found nothing. Installed the official Microsoft VS Code 1.144.0 arm64 build, commit `2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf`. prs.title: fix(update): enable process-tree termination and signal forwarding in runUpdateStep
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI-driven update step (`runUpdateStep` in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:218`) spawns a package-manager child tree (such as `npm i -g --prefix <stage-dir> openclaw@<version>`) that hangs in `ep_poll` and ignores `SIGTERM`, timeout or operator cancellation previously did not enable `killProcessTree: true` and `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:65`) did not forward `signal?: AbortSignal` to the underlying command runner. Unlike `buildUpdateCommandRunner` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:223`), which already sets `killProcessTree: true`, `runUpdateStep` dropped explicit `AbortSignal` cancellation and left `SIGTERM`-ignoring child and descendant processes alive instead of escalating through `createCommandTerminationController` (`src/process/exec-termination.ts:22`) to force-kill the process group and wait for descendant settlement.

### Root Cause & Architectural Fix

- **Architectural owner**: `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts` (`runUpdateStep`), `src/infra/update-runner-command.ts` (`runStep`), and `src/infra/update-runner-types.ts` (`RunStepOptions`).
- **Canonical fix**:
  - Enable `killProcessTree: true` in `runUpdateStep`'s default runner (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:230`) while preserving caller-supplied `runCommand` overrides.
  - Add `signal?: AbortSignal` to `RunStepOptions` (`src/infra/update-runner-types.ts:98`), forward `signal` in `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:96`), and derive `runUpdateStep`'s parameter type directly from `Parameters<typeof runStep>[0]` (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:219`) so `runUpdateStep` forwards `signal` and stays in sync with `RunStepOptions`.
  - Removed all unrelated layout/expression changes so 100% of touched production lines are inside `runUpdateStep`, `runStep`, and `RunStepOptions`.
- **Production LOC delta**: Net `-1` line across 3 production files (`+11 / -12`), plus `+69` test lines in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped CLI Update Flow: Timeout / Cancellation Stopping a `SIGTERM`-Ignoring Tree Before Recovery + Latest-Stable Upgrade Preserving Settings & Data

I executed the CLI package-update entrypoint (`runPackageInstallUpdate` in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-package.ts:484`) against a global npm prefix initialized at `openclaw@2026.10.5` with `openclaw.json` (`gateway.port: 18789`, `agents.defaults.model.primary: "openai/gpt-5.4"`) and `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`kv` row `operator-setting = preserved-across-upgrade`):

1. **CLI timeout/cancellation on a `SIGTERM`-ignoring `npm` + worker descendant tree**: During `package-install`, the `npm` process and its spawned worker both ignore `SIGTERM` and hang. Under the CLI timeout, `runUpdateStep` force-terminates the entire process tree (`npmPidExitedBeforeRecovery: true`, `workerPidExitedBeforeRecovery: true`), discards the staging directory, and verifies recovery of the existing `2026.10.5` installation (`recovery: { serviceRestartSafe: true, version: "2026.10.5" }`).
2. **Transient hang auto-recovery (`package-install` hangs -> killed -> fallback `package-install-omit-optional` succeeds)**: When only the first `npm i` hangs, the timeout kills the hung `SIGTERM`-ignoring tree and the fallback install completes `2026.10.5 -> 2026.10.10` (`status: "ok"`).
3. **Latest-stable upgrade (`2026.10.5 -> 2026.10.10`) with settings and data intact**: Upgrading to `2026.10.10` completes with `status: "ok"`, updates `package.json` to `2026.10.10`, and preserves both `openclaw.json` (`configIntact: true`) and `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`sqliteDataIntact: [{ key: "operator-setting", value: "preserved-across-upgrade" }]`).

```text
=== 1. CLI Timeout / Cancellation on SIGTERM-Ignoring npm Tree ===
{
  "status": "error",
  "reason": "global-install-failed",
  "failedStep": {
    "name": "package-install-omit-optional",
    "termination": "timeout",
    "exitCode": 1
  },
  "npmPidExitedBeforeRecovery": true,
  "workerPidExitedBeforeRecovery": true,
  "recovery": {
    "serviceRestartSafe": true,
    "version": "2026.10.5"
  }
}
=== 2. Latest-Stable Upgrade Preserving Settings and Data ===
{
  "status": "ok",
  "mode": "npm",
  "beforeVersion": "2026.10.5",
  "afterVersion": "2026.10.10",
  "installedPackageJsonVersion": "2026.10.10",
  "configIntact": true,
  "sqliteDataIntact": [
    {
      "key": "operator-setting",
      "value": "preserved-across-upgrade"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 2. Red / Green Real-Process Regression Proof (Failing on Base `d4b913d4689`, Passing on PR)

Running `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts` (`terminates SIGTERM-ignoring child and descendant processes when runUpdateStep is aborted`) against base `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts` and `src/infra/update-runner-command.ts` (`d4b913d4689`) fails because `runStep` drops `signal` (so `controller.abort()` is ignored until the step timeout fires):

prs.title: fix: stop update child processes on timeout and cancellation
prs.body:
Supersedes #180977, thanks @MertBasar0.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes package-manager descendants surviving a timed-out or cancelled CLI update step.

## User Impact

CLI update steps terminate their owned process trees before reporting completion, and explicit cancellation reaches the command runner. The installed updater must contain this fix; a newer candidate cannot repair an older updater's already-running step. No configuration or data migrations are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable the existing command runner's process-tree cleanup in `runUpdateStep` and forward its optional abort signal through `runStep`. The shared termination controller continues to own graceful signaling, forced escalation and settlement; caller-supplied runners retain their existing behavior.

The simplification removes the CLI adapter's duplicate step-option declaration by deriving it from the shared owner. Production delta: **+9/−12, net −3 lines**. The **104-line** regression file has its own test-line allocation for the two distinct failures.

## Evidence

- On current main `8f3da9e8e46eefafc7d081c8b89c9552986566c3`, the fake-tree regression fails twice: timeout leaves worker `4243` alive; explicit abort is ignored and reports `timeout` instead of `signal`.
- With the repair, **60 tests pass across 3 named files**: `shared.process-tree.test.ts`, `shared.command-runner.test.ts`, and `git-network-retry.test.ts`. The new regression uses fake clocks and fake OS processes while exercising the real CLI step, command runner and termination controller. It checks extinction before completion reporting. Focused wrapper wall time: 47.64 s (including cold worker preparation); new cases: 8 ms combined. The final fixture rerun passes both cases (37 ms combined; wrapper wall time 65.97 s, including 57.9 s of worker preparation). The [current-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41352493614) passed: 1,512 s elapsed, 10,101 summed job seconds; per-file CI time is not isolated.
- Touched-file type-aware lint/type checking, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The fixture uses a mutable child subclass for Node's read-only native exit state.
- The first CI run caught a mock-export contract violation in the new test. The correction preserves the real reaper exports while replacing native reaping. Both regressions pass again (33 ms combined; 7.07 s wrapper), as do touched-file type checking and formatting. The original failed CI result is retained; the corrected head passed CI, including the baseline ratchet.
- Canonical autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) covered the complete change against the main SHA above. The initial review was scoped-clean; the final pass identified the still-staged pre-repair mock (P2, INDEX-only), which was corrected before the repair commit. The reviewer found no further production or regression defects.
- Hosted [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190674#issuecomment-6564358011) of the final head found no actionable code defects; the installed-CLI proof gap remains explicit.
- Contributor code was read through GitHub and was **never checked out or executed**. This is a credited replacement implemented on main. No real update/upgrade flow, Gateway restart, container, browser, broad local suite or packaging run was performed on the production host. The unit proof does not claim installed-CLI upgrade or native Windows process-tree coverage.

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A primary model configured with `@profile` can block Chat or event-Cron fallback to another CLI provider by treating that configured account as a conversation-wide pin.

## User Impact

Fallback can use the destination runtime's account. Explicit user/user-link pins still take precedence and are checked against the selected account after preparation waits. Scheduled inference keeps its recorded-account and current-credential checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth owner retains configured-account provenance as a runtime-only fact and distinguishes a native login's selected identity from a forwarded credential ID. Existing admission and dispatch owners carry those facts to the final effect. Legacy V1 CLI registration signatures remain compatible; bundled/internal consumers use the additive V2 admission contract. Current main classifies this CLI SDK entry as private/local; no new public subpath or removal window is introduced.

This revision integrates official main `3bf7eedacd401109de8579e0a116112d489a51f8` to resolve verified conflicts, preserving its compaction accounting, Cron lease and prompt/context owners. The operator-input adapter is moved intact and duplicate selection/preflight checks are removed to meet the existing line caps. No config, dependency, schema, protocol version or test allowance changes.

## Evidence

Head `a80133d3390fc8b04c914dcd448b3a731e021542` is a normal merge retaining the prior author head and the pinned official main; all 70 reviewed file blobs match the committed tree.

- 25 related test files / 642 tests passed, including the 16-case production Chat/Cron process suite and Anthropic protocol tests. Two additional private owner mutation variants reject changed user/user-link pins before delivery.
- Core and six matching core-test type graphs passed; plugin production/test types were rerun after the final one-call simplification. Source/test typed lint, format, export checks and native ratchets pass. The existing +1298 test-line allocation is unchanged.
- Full `pnpm build` passed before that final simplification; the current plugin runtime and canonical SDK declarations were rebuilt afterward. A canonical local V1/V2 source consumer passes; this is not a packaged public SDK certificate.
- Fresh independent review of the complete 70-file delta found no actionable P0–P2 issues. No test assertion, timeout or threshold was relaxed.

The production Chat/Cron process suite uses the real reply and isolated-Cron entry points, canonical account/session owners and an owned Node CLI. Replacing only the two dispatchers with their exact main versions makes the two cross-provider cases fail before destination execution; this is an integrated main-dispatcher control, not a pristine whole-main run. The candidate suite passes the configured-account, unchanged/changed user and user-link, recorded scheduled-account and native-identity controls.

Verification uses isolated synthetic state. It does not certify a real vendor CLI, a listening operator Gateway, legacy V1 deferred-I/O behavior, npm upgrade behavior or a released version. The checked Codex sibling source and installed reviewer are different versions; no installed Codex runtime claim is made. Listed-owner review and current-revision CI authorization remain upstream merge requirements.

prs.title: feat: configure chat attachment file and message size limits
prs.body:
Related: #166757

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot configure incoming chat document size limits independently of media processing budgets.

## User Impact

The new attachment controls are **additional to**, not a replacement for, the existing media option:

- `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb` stays available and active for incoming **images, audio, and video only**. It does not cap PDFs, text, archives, or other documents. Media files must satisfy both the media cap and the general attachment cap; documents use only the attachment caps.

- `attachments.maxFileMb` — **Maximum attachment size**, default 20 MiB per file.
- `attachments.maxTotalMb` — **Maximum total attachment size per message**, default the larger of 20 MiB and the per-file cap.
- All incoming chat files, including media and duplicate entries, count toward the decoded total. The server rejects an oversized batch before attachment preparation/storage.
- Doctor preserves the old inherited file cap when the new field is absent, retaining explicit attachment settings, media settings, and retention.

The approximately 18.56 MiB WebSocket decoded batch ceiling remains. This does not add streaming uploads or change every channel/outbound document contract. **Not release-qualified:** installed latest-stable upgrade and external live-model proof remain unrun. A real isolated Gateway/agent flow with a deterministic provider now passes.

For example: with media set to 5 MiB, per-file attachments to 10 MiB, and the message total to 15 MiB, an 8 MiB PDF is permitted but an 8 MiB video is rejected. Two 8 MiB PDFs exceed the total. Classification is based on sniffed content, not merely the filename or supplied MIME type.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends the existing attachment policy/parser and config schema rather than adding a second upload owner. Chat, session, agent/node, companion, worker-transfer, handshake and Control UI consumers use the separate budgets. New labels/help expose the actual scope and MiB units; retention is unchanged.

Simplification retained one policy owner, one batch preflight and the existing Doctor writer, with no new transport, persistence system, or permanent document-limit fallback to mediaMaxMb.

## Evidence

### Merge-readiness repairs (head `2afe0ec95d14`)

- Fixed the two diagnosed CI defects: schema narrowing in the rendered settings test (`check-test-types-core-1`) and the missing migration module in the extracted PR wrapper inventory (`checks-node-compact-small-1`). The exact UI E2E type leaf and both affected wrapper-closure tests pass locally; this is not a new-head CI verdict.
- A real isolated Gateway process and agent completed the new `chat.send` integration test using the existing deterministic provider. Disguised image, per-file overflow, and total overflow are rejected without provider requests. A document larger than the media cap is accepted, appears in history, and its original bytes are retained. The standard runtime build and test command completed successfully.
- Full Doctor integration exposed a valid-config upgrade gap: ordinary noninteractive Doctor previewed but did not persist the inherited attachment cap. The regression failed before adding this migration to the existing automatic-repair admission, then passed with exact original backup, retained media/TTL, and second-run idempotence. All 39 selected migration and safety tests pass. Existing include, read-only, future-version and handoff boundaries remain unchanged.
- Gateway E2E and Doctor test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, changed-doc MDX checks and diff checks pass. Simplification reuses existing Gateway, test fixture and Doctor owners; no new runtime subsystem or test-only hook.
- Independent Auto Review of the complete candidate against `f2f8500facc1eb80a7bc68e8335133675c32b17f` returned scoped-clean through P2 (no actionable findings). It did not independently execute tests. Earlier evidence below remains attributed to its tested candidate.
- Remaining proof gaps: installation of official latest stable `2026.10.9` was refused by the environment's seven-day package-age rule; a one-off package-specific exception is awaiting approval. No authorized external live-model test credential binding is available in this sandbox. Neither gap is represented as passing.
- Current-head dependency and security-sensitive review statuses pass, but `openclaw/ci-gate` remains pending; the review workflow log explicitly says it is waiting for CI. These statuses do not establish product CI success.
- GitHub reports merge conflicts with main. A read-only three-way diagnostic against pinned main `8d2c49f924925415b408d330c74a56131b2c4480` confirms a generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` conflict. The upstream comparison returns only its first 300 files, so this is not a complete conflict inventory. Preserve both core attachment additions and upstream plugin changes, then regenerate through the baseline owner after supported base integration; do not choose either generated hash wholesale.
- The November 1 retry no longer refuses base refresh, but it reports the old `f2f8500facc1eb80a7bc68e8335133675c32b17f` target as current and makes no changes. Same-head PR preparation does not change that outcome. The PR API reports that same old base while the pinned live `main` ref is `d6bda829e24b83962579ce48f8f0629e656b4b43` (773 commits ahead). This target-readback mismatch still blocks supported integration; the metadata/refresh owner needs to reconcile the existing `main` destination, without retargeting to another branch or rewriting source. No merge or release-readiness claim is made.

### Media-only correction

- Image/audio/video cap regressions failed on the previous implementation and passed after restoring `mediaMaxMb` as a media-only admission constraint. A document above that cap still passes its independent attachment limits.
- 98 focused tests passed: parser/policy (51), MIME sniffing (5), client admission/video preparation (42), including worker-backed preparation and accepted noncanonical Base64 padding.
- Core/UI production typechecks, Gateway root/method test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and 3 changed-doc MDX checks passed. Protocol and native projections regenerated through their owners.
- Independent review identified only the stale staged policy; staged content was updated to the reviewed working-tree correction and verified. No other actionable P0–P2 issue was reported.
- These changes affect limit enforcement/preflight, not settings layout; existing rendered-control evidence remains below.
- Prior-head CI failures in `check-test-types-core-1` and `checks-node-compact-small-1` were subsequently diagnosed from Actions job logs and repaired as described above.

### Earlier implementation evidence

- New mixed-batch and duplicate-file aggregate regressions failed on the original parser and passed with the implementation.
- Focused parser/policy, migration/schema, chat admission/staging, node, worker transfer, UI admission and reload tests passed on the original implementation candidate.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, docs MDX/link/config-example checks passed on that candidate. Protocol/native artifacts and config-doc baselines were regenerated through their owners.
- Independent Auto Review found no actionable P0–P2 findings on the original candidate.
- Integrated main at `f2f8500facc1eb80a7bc68e8335133675c32b17f`, preserved its newer deferred-staging/cancellation owner, and regenerated config baselines. Refreshed-base migration tests (6), parser/policy/chat-admission tests (56), and rendered settings E2E (1) passed; reconciled core/UI typechecks and targeted lint passed. Earlier node/worker/UI-admission/reload results remain prior-base evidence. Those results are evidence for that earlier head, not the latest correction's CI.
- Public screenshot URLs were fetched without authentication and their SHA-256 digests matched the inspected images.
- Rendered Control UI browser test verified both numeric values are saved to the correct config keys. Screenshots below use the real Control UI with a synthetic Gateway response, not a live-model claim.

### Before

![Before: attachment retention settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45856cc5-feda-4100-9a17-41aa96aa15dd)

### After
