prs.title: fix(ios): refresh location status after authorization changes
prs.body:
Closes #138936 (iOS reports location denied while precise location requests succeed).

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iPhone users granting location access could leave the gateway with an outdated location permission declaration, even while location requests succeeded. Changes made outside OpenClaw Settings were not propagated to registration, and startup or target-review resume could install options captured before authorization changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway connection controller now observes authorization and active registration changes and uses its existing refresh flow. It samples authorization after the asynchronous services check and discards a refresh if reconnect was disabled or its captured route/config was superseded. Registration waits for current and superseding connection handoffs/resets and skips unchanged options, so it does not restart deliberately paused transport loops. Connection-generation invalidation schedules a fresh reconciliation even when a canceled attempt leaves the active route unchanged.

The change preserves gateway approval rules: a corrected false-to-true declaration may still require the existing permission-upgrade approval. It neither silently grants permissions nor changes pairing policy. Production delta is +28 lines: lifecycle observation, route fencing, and coordination with the existing handoff/reset barriers reuse the canonical refresh path; no new setting, protocol, permission manager, or test-only production seam.

## User Impact

The iPhone keeps its advertised location permission current after grants, revocations, and delayed installation of connection options. An intentionally disconnected phone stays disconnected. This PR requires a future iOS app build; it has not been deployed to the reporting phone.

## Evidence

Current head: `533fe31d33e6dfcbf945a8533573df0679b94c5f`, rebased on upstream `main` `10334ec913d7b18f32e6e1d16e9ac10bdc760534` (see **Rebase onto current main** below). Original base: `f9b94860bd73b4061ee92319b149ed1abb517665`; previous head `a0f169ebf85c8257ace3ac5e1a014a8e37031e72`. The initial regression proof used native commit `7476029fc3ea5c361ab3b074e13ad9c6e36de3fb`.

- **Before:** added regression test against unmodified production base fails for all four combinations of initial `.notDetermined`/`.denied` and grant before/after registration: `Expectation failed: granted`. The 23-test suite reports four issues.
- **After:** the original identical suite passes all 23 tests. The initial broader location and connection run passes **105 tests across three suites**. The regression also covers revocation, preserving gateway identity/auth choice, and keeping target-review suspension disconnected.
- The exact combined CI native selection also passes locally: **427 app Swift tests plus 6 logic tests**, with Xcode reporting TEST SUCCEEDED. This checks the newly selected suites together with the existing lifecycle suites.
- Existing gateway approval tests separately pass **4 tests** covering widening/reapproval, false-only metadata, downgrades, and the connection-declared ceiling.
- Required `check:changed` gate passes for all five touched Swift files, including pinned Swift lint/format and native schema guard.
- Independent repository `autoreview`, pinned base/local candidate, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no findings**.
- Release device build: **passed**, including optimized main app and embedded Watch targets.
- CI now includes the location regression and connection suites in its existing native lifecycle command. Workflow validation passes **437 tests** (2 intentional skips), workflow changed checks pass, and the complete updated patch again passes independent P0–P2 autoreview with no findings.

Focused native command (Xcode 26.6, iOS 26.5 simulator):

```sh
xcodebuild -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw \
  -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' \
  -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  -only-testing:OpenClawTests/LocationPermissionSummaryTests \
  -only-testing:OpenClawTests/GatewayConnectionControllerTests \
  -only-testing:OpenClawTests/GatewayReconnectErrorRetentionTests test
```

The before run selects only `LocationPermissionSummaryTests`; the after run adds the connection suites. Actual local invocations pin the simulator UUID and use dedicated DerivedData/SwiftPM directories and separate `.xcresult` bundles.

Release command:

```sh
xcodebuild -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw \
  -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Changed gate:

```sh
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- \
  apps/ios/Sources/Gateway/GatewayConnectionController.swift \
  apps/ios/Sources/Gateway/GatewayConnectionController+Capabilities.swift \
  apps/ios/Sources/Model/NodeAppModel.swift \
  apps/ios/Tests/LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift \
  apps/ios/Tests/GatewayConnectionControllerTests.swift
```

**Version/device boundary:** the reporting phone says 2026.8.11; gateway is 2026.9.1. The [current public App Store version](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/openclaw/id6780396132) is 2026.8.11, and immutable mobile ref `refs/openclaw/mobile-releases/ios/2026.8.11-1` resolves to `93706992214eae5785e8dbf9ea9020a3c2bd7511`. The affected registration pattern is present there and on the tested upstream base. Installed phone build number was not independently recovered.

**Live app-to-gateway proof:** the patched Debug app ran through normal onboarding on iPhone 17 Pro Simulator (iOS 26.5), paired with a real isolated OpenClaw 2026.9.1 gateway. No MockLocationService, fake gateway, or screenshot fixture was used. After establishing OS denial and approving the initial node surface, the app stayed on Chat throughout the OS grant, gateway approval, and OS revocation. There was no manual reconnect or return to OpenClaw Settings during those transitions. Apple's `simctl privacy` changed the Simulator's OS authorization for the running app.

Sanitized gateway status receipt:

| Step | Connected | Effective location | Approval state | Pending declared location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initially denied, fresh pairing approved | true | false | approved | none |
| OS location grant, automatic registration | true | false | pending-reapproval | true |
| Existing permission-upgrade request approved | true | true | approved | none |
| OS location revoked, automatic registration | true | false | approved | none |

The final revocation leaves zero pending requests. This demonstrates recovery for a previously approved false declaration while preserving the existing approval ceiling. This complete sequence was repeated on the exact final production source, whose three native-file SHA-256 hashes were verified against the committed files. Only the disposable local gateway's requests were approved; it was stopped after proof. Node identifiers, credentials, and endpoints are omitted from this receipt; no coordinates were requested.

**CI follow-up:** [the initial native job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33953142656/job/101271637979) failed asynchronous completion assertions. Both affected polling helpers now actually suspend between checks instead of spinning on `Task.yield()`; their three-second deadlines and assertions are unchanged. Three synthetic capability fixtures now use the real registration builder with the existing deterministic location service while retaining full-config equality checks; initial OS authorization callbacks must not silently mutate route-stability fixtures. This stronger execution exposed a premature transport restart during forced reset. A new regression fails against `99d719ce` on both premature permission publication and restarted-loop assertions; the owner fix waits for current and superseding handoff/reset ownership and skips identical options. Additional red/green regressions cover a replacement handoff and generation-only invalidation with an unchanged route; neither may strand stale permissions or restart a paused route.

**Physical-device boundary:** `xcrun devicectl list devices` reports no developer-paired devices. The patch has not been installed on the reporting iPhone. The live proof above covers real Simulator OS authorization and gateway pairing/status; physical hardware, Always/background behavior, and the reporting phone's precise initiating timing remain unproven. These limits also explain why the reporting phone has no before/after screenshot pair. The issue contains its earlier successful precise location request and contradictory status observation.

### Rebase onto current main (answers both "Before merge" items)

The branch is now a single commit on current `main` (`10334ec9`), head `533fe31d33e6dfcbf945a8533573df0679b94c5f`. The three-way merge conflicted in three files; resolution:

- `GatewayConnectionController.swift`: `main` inlined the refresh into a `Task` in `refreshActiveGatewayRegistrationFromSettings()` and dropped the `stableID:` parameter from `makeConnectOptions`. The settings entry point now calls the shared `refreshActiveGatewayRegistrationFromSettingsAsync()`. That function keeps `main`'s `var refreshedConfig = cfg` construction and applies this PR's handoff/reset waits, route fence, and unchanged-options skip.
- `GatewayConnectionController+Capabilities.swift`: kept `main`'s `LocationService.servicesEnabled()` and still samples authorization after the await.
- `ci.yml`: added the two suites to `main`'s new `test_args` array for the `tests` phase.
- Tests: removed the dropped `stableID:` argument at each `makeConnectOptions` call.

**One new finding during exact-head validation, fixed here.** `main` added `held reset retains recovery until replacement commits or cancels`. On the straight port it failed (25 issues across 6 outcomes). The new observer saw the failed switch's generation change. After the held reset finished, it re-applied the previous route and restarted its loops inside the recovery window. Fix: refresh now defers while `unresolvedGatewayPreconnectStableID` is set (checked before and after sampling). The observer also tracks that value, so a retry, trust, or cancel decision still reconciles. After that guard, 3 issues remained, all `hasSameConnectionInputs(as: currentConfig)` on the test's synthetic capability fixture. That fixture now uses the real registration builder with a denied `MockLocationService`, the same treatment as the three fixtures adjusted earlier in this PR.

Exact-head results at `533fe31d` (Xcode 27.0, iPhone 17 Pro Simulator):

- Focused native command above (`LocationPermissionSummaryTests`, `GatewayConnectionControllerTests`, `GatewayReconnectErrorRetentionTests`): **100 tests in 3 suites passed**, TEST SUCCEEDED.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <6 changed files>`: passed, including pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0 / SwiftLint 0.65.1 (0 violations in 477 files) and the native state schema guard.

The live Simulator-to-Gateway receipt above was captured on the pre-rebase head. The production change it exercised is the same apart from the conflict adaptations above and the new preconnect deferral. It has not been re-run on `533fe31d`. Physical iPhone installation is still unverified, as stated above.

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix(agents): hand delegated failures back to their parent
prs.body:
## Summary
- Return failed subagents' cause and saved progress to their owning parent without waiting on the failed root's descendants.
- Quiet inherited error attention only after durable input/result custody, while preserving child diagnostics, collector ownership and genuine native human questions.
- Keep failure diagnostics in the committed handoff, preserve ready unconsumed failed-collector findings, and count handed-off failures correctly.
- Acknowledge failure custody only for children represented in the committed input. A bounded batch keeps omitted failures unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Collector results: acknowledge only failures whose diagnostics survive in the final persisted tool result, after transcript truncation and detail reduction, and only for the expected host completion. Failures dropped from the stored result stay unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Bind private settle retries to the findings they replay: a retry that reuses the retained message acknowledges only failed runs whose diagnostics are in those exact bytes and that are still in the current cohort. A legacy retained message without that record adds no acknowledgement, and a new run generation under the same ID does not inherit it.
- Keep the 160,000-character findings budget, with its truncation markers, per-result floors, stable order and overflow summary.
- Keep the receipt in cold reads: the compact SQL session-list projection now selects the four `failureHandoff` fields, including the `parentCompletion` mirror. No schema, writer, codec, migration or retention change.
- Leave ordinary session rows unchanged on the wire: `failureHandedOff` is sent only when true.

## Delivery contracts
- Settle (`subagent_settle`): the complete bounded cohort message, including healthy children's findings, is stored as the hidden replay input, exactly as on `main`. Private retries keep their own retained input and failure IDs.
- Direct completion (`subagent_announce`): a healthy child's result stays in runtime context only; a failed child's diagnostics are saved with the handoff.
- Collector: results remain an ordinary durable tool result; failure custody follows what was actually stored.

## Integration with `main`
- This branch merges `main` at `68fbe4a` (#188180) with no conflicts and no resolution edits. All 96 feature files are byte-identical to the pre-merge commit `46ab0a0`.
- Against `main`, the PR changes 96 files, +4189/−392. The larger first-parent diff of that merge is upstream `main`, not new feature code.
- Earlier merges brought in `315380c` (#188047) without conflicts and `445e566` with a conflict in the three Control UI end-to-end test inventory files, resolved by keeping both sides' entries.
- Test repairs merged on `main` and included through the merge: #188178 (widget retention fixture), #188156 (empty-leaf admission), #188195 (thinking-claim ordering) and #188180 (keyed commentary in refreshed history). Earlier: #188047, #187979, #187933 and #188056. None is copied as a separate patch.
- `main` has moved since `68fbe4a`. The Copy-feedback repair landed on `main` as #188311; #188299, which overlapped it, was closed without merging. Separate test-only corrections for the new-session draft and quota tests are being prepared and are not yet published. This branch has not yet integrated the newer `main`.

## Stream-budget test readiness
- `chat-stream-runtime-budgets.e2e.test.ts` ("commits a streamed delta burst in frame-bound transcript batches") could count native pane commits caused by lazily loaded menu translation catalogs. Those landed after the measurement reset but before the first measured delta.
- The test now waits until the menu modules already requested by the page, and their dependencies, have loaded and the active pane has finished updating, before it measures. The original assertion, thresholds, timers and production code are unchanged. A new line allocation of 136 covers this test-only code.
- On `53ee37c`, Linux CI passed all six tests in that file.

## Verification
- Independent QA of the current source (`d70644f`): PASS with notes, no findings or blockers.
  - One fresh private Gateway build and matching Control UI (build `2026.10.9-d70644fb5c3c-2026-10-30T10-03-19.128Z`) ran a real Gateway and browser test through all four modes: default, parent-target, yielded and collector.
  - Each mode asked a native question, survived a reload, accepted a suggested choice or free text, kept durable custody, delivered the final reply in the same run as the answer, and showed no failed-child attention. Each mode verified that the served UI asset matched the build byte for byte.
  - In default mode, a descendant that finished late did not revive the failed child.
  - Five new test cases in four files ran: the four-mode Gateway case, three native legacy and cold-read cases, and one historical import case. The author's 215 tests and 6 boundary checks were not rerun; the two sets overlap and are not added together.
  - The provider was scripted locally, not a hosted model. Screenshots were inspected locally; none are attached.
- Independent review of the `main` integration effects on `d70644f`: PASS with notes, no integration defect or new missing context. All 96 feature files are unchanged, and `main`'s 522 changed paths do not overlap them. The `main` changes to outer authorization, the QuickJS namespace copy, collector inputs and attention inputs leave the delivery, persistence and custody paths unchanged. This is a source assessment, not a new canonical review or tests.
- Current source (`d70644f`, author): 215 tests across 15 files plus 6 targeted boundary checks pass, along with core and UI type checks, four test type graphs, inventory types, lint, format, mock, line-allocation and whitespace checks. Four UI lint warnings are unchanged from `main` and outside the feature's changes.
- Persisted-collector fix (`46ab0a0`): scoped canonical and independent reviews of that change. They do not cover the whole PR.
- Hosted review of `cb024b5` (current head): no findings; the earlier `53ee37c` collector P2 is addressed. It held the PR for data-model compatibility proof, which is added below. That hold stands until a fresh hosted review of a later head.
- Earlier proof is tied to its own source and does not cover `d70644f`:
  - Independent QA of `3a82cc7`: PASS with notes, including the stream-budget mutation checks and a Gateway runtime proof reused from `ad5a535` (build `2026.10.9-ad5a5354de4a-2026-10-30T05-25-28.209Z`).
  - Independent shipping verification of `43ddaef`: PASS with notes, 110 native tests and four Gateway and Control UI modes (build `2026.10.9-43ddaef1f7a6-2026-10-30T04-25-21.835Z`).
  - Scoped reviews: readiness fix (`ad5a535..3a82cc7`, two passes, zero findings), diagnostic step (`4bf61ee..ad5a535`), private-retry fix (`a296cbe..801b1a4`, eight passes, zero findings), `315380c` integration (PASS with notes).
  - Review of `f27f807..a296cbe` (36 passes): incomplete; no clean result is claimed for that range.
  - Baseline review (source `4599951`): eight passes, scoped-clean.
- CI on earlier published heads found missing mocks, test inventory gaps, an unconditional wire field, unbounded findings, a lint miss, the dropped settle findings and the stream-budget failure. Those failed runs remain history.
- Pending, not approval: a fresh whole-PR hosted review of the next head, and passing CI.

## Data compatibility
- This PR changes no schema, writer or retention.
- **Upgrade from the latest stable release (independent, PASS with notes):** data written by the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` package was opened and upgraded by this PR's source (`d70644f`).
  - Stable artifact: npm `openclaw-2026.10.9.tgz` (published 2026-10-29), tarball SHA-256 `43c61a00ef2c73416a072a7216cb3be80555d6740199f07194da2714283b04ab`; npm SHA-512 and SHA-1 integrity checked; signed tag `v2026.10.9` at build commit `8b18b55`. The npm provenance and signature chain was not separately audited.
  - The unmodified published compiled code, with its exact 66 production dependencies and no modules from this PR, wrote 6 sessions, 4 subagent runs and a 7-row transcript (header, 6 events, 4 model messages). The data included a retained private settle input and a collector's structured result and usage.
  - This PR's Doctor command then migrated the stores (shared schema 20→36, agent schema 25→38). Every original registry and transcript column and payload byte was preserved. The migration added the expected transcript navigation-index columns with their default values (for example `navigation_valid` = 1 and `navigation_display` = 0). Existing session-entry fields were preserved, and one expected display title was added. No represented-failure IDs or failure custody were invented.
  - Fresh processes then read the data through the production paths: the full and bounded registry readers, the session manager, Gateway row projection and presentation, and the Control UI attention and tree aggregation. Old failed children without a receipt still show failed-child attention (3 failed children, attention "error").
  - A new native write after migration, then a separate cold reopen, kept both the old and new bytes (7 events, 5 messages, 4 runs).
- **Historical import:** a frozen schema-v24 SQLite fixture went through the current Doctor import and a fresh read-only read. All three rows kept their full payload, IDs, keys, run ID and recovery data; the only changes were `main`'s existing queued→interrupted rule and a new empty `consumed_event_id`.
- A legacy retained settle message, replayed with its original run and idempotency IDs but without a record of represented failures, adds no new acknowledgement.
- Scope: this proves stored-data and schema activation. It does not cover a stable Gateway daemon boot, managed package replacement, service cutover or restart, a full packaged install of this PR, or live user data. Doctor completed both migrations, but its overall health check is not green in this isolated setup (plugin and model setup warnings, unset gateway mode). The stable data had no pending-input mailbox rows, so that path rests on the v24 import proof.

## Limits
- Runtime proof uses a scripted local model on macOS arm64/headless Chromium, not Linux or hosted-model compliance. Active-steering failure timing was not separately exercised. No latest-stable service activation (daemon boot, package replacement or restart) and no PostgreSQL run is claimed.
- The required `openclaw/ci-gate` check is not waived. No live Odin update, restart or deployment. CI and landing remain separate gates.

prs.title: docs(macos): distinguish automatic first run from manual setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS onboarding guide describes the manual wizard as the default fresh-launch path and incorrectly says the bundled app installs Node.

## User Impact

Readers can distinguish automatic fresh-local setup, manual recovery, and developer installs without changing existing Gateway connections or installation ownership. Older app builds can still open the manual wizard first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align the detailed onboarding and bundled Gateway guides with the production launch path. Explain **Set up manually**, retain existing permission/security/Git guidance, and identify the existing screenshots as earlier manual-flow illustrations. No runtime behavior changes.

Related: #183245 (its permission-prompt explanations are preserved).

## Evidence

- Re-audited the production launch path at `9e86c84aada48fc104c11be9af1e7e5bcf868248`. The pre-change documents and the first-run owner/progress files are byte-identical to the original audited base `8deb38c8955e37ef9ea00ea7fb774bd84ca21cdd`. The supplied patch applies unchanged: two documentation files, +63/-12; no runtime, screenshot, or generated-file changes.
- Release distinction: the two first-run owner files match the source tagged `v2026.10.10-beta.4` (`5a94eab2146e558b3ebcd41cb174fc5adc469c2a`). prs.title: docs: propose retained protection and native Codex coding lane
prs.body:
Related: #187891, #189827, #189600


## What Problem This Solves

Users need a normal coding subagent that works in an authorized native Codex home, returns useful findings and tests, and accepts same-thread revisions without leaking protected content through retained artifacts or parent context.

## User Impact

**Design-review draft only: no runtime behavior changes, implementation readiness, activation authority, or maintainer acceptance is claimed.** This proposes a generic retained-protection prerequisite followed by a dependent native Codex lane as two eventual implementation PRs.

The proposal intentionally breaks legacy content-bearing approval wire/SDK formats for ordinary and protected payloads together. Complete replacement human reads and ordinary remote publication, retirement, restore and rollback qualification must land before activation. Protected remote redistribution is unsupported; authorized human reads do not create publication custody. Retained original protected-lineage policy permits authorized reads after live-session deletion; original execution authority does not survive by implication. Existing-parent visibility changes require consent, with an explicit protected coordinator when in-place promotion is unsafe.

## Why This Change Was Made

Early owner feedback can resolve the public protocol, retained-policy, parent UX and migration trade-offs before implementation is presented as ready. The document reuses existing storage/sharing, approval/delivery, startup/restore, plugin/harness, binding and paired-node transport owners; it does not introduce a parallel dispatcher or grant service.

The dated native design and subsequent coding-lane contract select owned direct stdio, superseding the earlier shared-daemon proxy proposal. The later retained-policy contract also supersedes the earlier deny-on-live-session-deletion alternative. This draft preserves those decisions while requesting maintainer assessment; it does not make new upstream acceptance claims.

## Evidence

- One documentation file only: `docs/design/protected-content-native-codex-lane.md`, including dependency order, alternatives, review questions, and a claim/evidence limitations map. No implementation candidate, raw log, credential, private path or advisory transcript is included.
- Focused oxfmt formatting/check passed; repository MDX checker passed for the one document; staged `git diff --check` passed; public-sensitive-string scan returned no matches.
- Independent document/security-claim review found no actionable P0–P2 finding in its scoped pre-final draft. The lead subsequently corrected retained-policy wording against the later acceptance contract and added dated transport provenance. That review is not claimed to cover those later edits or constitute runtime security certification.
- Prior source-pinned fixture/design reports are summarized only as **reported evidence**. Failed checks and unvalidated corrections remain explicit; no compiler-green, whole-lane, two-user, old-helper, or deployed-runtime proof is claimed. Private reports are not presented as accessible artifacts. Full accessible sanitized exact-head proof remains required for the later implementation PRs.
- No full test suite/build/runtime campaign was run for this docs-only draft. No hosted ClawSweeper verdict or CI acceptance is claimed. The PR remains a draft for early design feedback.

Review requested on existing owner seams, the all-payload compatibility break, retained policy after deletion, parent consent/coordinator behavior, and completeness of first-party consumer/restore/rollback acceptance requirements.

prs.title: fix(config): report write-safety refusals during dry runs
prs.body:
Related: #166718

## What Problem This Solves

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.
- Real CLI proof uses the normal `pnpm openclaw config patch --file <patch> --replace-path models.providers.bounty.models` entry point in isolated task-owned home/config/state, with 409 synthetic provider models and no provider calls or credentials. The original live failure was reproduced at `2b988ee83444` (the affected owner code is unchanged at this PR's base `80322af5c7e5`).
- Committed candidate `9982d96b8c1d` results: 409→32 root preview and actual write both reject with `size-drop`; the preview preserves original bytes and creates no artifact. 409→300 root and 409→32 include-owned changes pass preview and persist the exact requested model count. Include-owned writes preserve the root file. A real provider-builder shrink also rejects in both preview and commit; its preview has `checks.schema:false` and still returns `write-safety`, directly proving the review correction.
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 99 passed; 51.68 s runner wall time. The materially changed integration file has 34 tests and takes 29.83 s Vitest wall time; the cases reuse its existing real config-command fixture.
- Unchanged writer/reference coverage, run at `9982d96b8c1d`: `pnpm test src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 130 passed; 62.96 s total. Covers existing canonical-format/BOM sizing, references, include ownership, refusal, and rollback contracts.
- The supported CLI wrapper completed the production build for live proof. Core and core-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The aggregate changed check stopped at the unrelated existing `observePlacementAuthority` unused export in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts`; this file and its references are unchanged by the patch. The subsequent ready-for-review CI result and current follow-up are documented below.
- Follow-up `9b8e17b2b06`: parser-validated builder/batch inputs and thrown persistence refusals have registered-command regressions that failed before their corrections. For the empty-roster refusal, the old JSON path returned `operations:0`, empty `inputModes`, and false checks; its text-output control already passed. The corrected real CLI returns `operations:1`, `inputModes:["json"]`, all completed checks true, preserved counters, and the original schema refusal. It exits 1, leaves config bytes unchanged, and creates no backup/rejected file. The matching non-JSON regression preserves the exact original diagnostic.




### CI and conflict follow-up (2026-10-10)

Integrated main `0c94b6966078` to resolve the real `src/config/io.write.ts` import conflict. Both intents are retained: upstream `composeConfigWriteAssertions` and this PR's shared payload preparation. The PR delta against the new base remains the same nine files; no Doctor test, timeout, assertion, or CI workflow was changed.

The previous CI run [37805483456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37805483456/job/113409493434) failed on `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting` at 30.228 s (30 s limit), causing the aggregate gate to fail. Diagnosis did not reproduce that failure:

- Exact old PR source `9b8e17b2b064`: original seven-file shard order, separate file processes, macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0: all 87 tests passed; the named test took 10.582 s. A standalone diagnostic retained all assertions and the deadline, observed maintenance admission in 65 ms and overall completion in 12.939 s, and was removed afterward.
- Same old source in a credential-free Linux arm64 container, Node 24.19.0, 2 CPUs / 8 GiB: all five Doctor-file tests passed; the named test took 18.558 s. This matches the CI Node version and resource limits but not its Linux x64 hardware. The container was removed after diagnosis.

prs.title: fix(browser): avoid repeat DNS checks for unchanged action URLs
prs.body:
Related: #178058

## What Problem This Solves

Browser actions repeat a DNS policy check while preparing the response URL, even when that same address was admitted earlier in the request.

## User Impact

Unchanged-tab actions avoid one redundant lookup and return the same result and URL. This draft addresses the response-only duplicate; it does not claim to eliminate all per-action DNS checks or prove meeting audio recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action route opts in to reuse its admitted address only for response URL projection, with an exact URL and complete navigation-policy match. Changed URLs, changed policies, missing admission and cancellation retain validation. Execution and navigation guards remain authoritative. There is no cross-request cache, new setting or protocol change.

## Evidence

Actual Browser Bridge HTTP actions against an isolated Chrome 155 tab on macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0, with the default browser policy and real system DNS. Five serial baseline/candidate pairs used fresh processes; all 30 actions per revision returned identical page data and response URLs. All ten `about:blank` controls performed zero hostname lookups.

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DNS lookups per unchanged action | 4 | 3 |
| Warm action median (25 samples) | 270.30 ms | 270.70 ms |
| Warm action p95 | 289.54 ms | 287.59 ms |
| Cold completion median (5 samples) | 4770.63 ms | 4827.54 ms |
| Cold completion p95 | 5633.91 ms | 5371.78 ms |

The committed opt-in workload is rerunnable with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs extensions/browser/scripts/bench-act-dns.ts --chromium <chromium-executable> --output <result.json>
```

Cold completion includes isolated browser/page/bridge startup and the observer positive control. Action timing excludes observer flushing. Host load and controller CPU/RSS are recorded; aggregate metrics did not regress by 20%. The workload's initial lint overlapped the first two pairs. No delayed DNS or simulated browser/provider results were used; slow-resolver stalls and meeting audio loss were not reproduced.

- New unchanged-URL regression fails on the base because it performs two policy validations rather than one; the other nine cases pass. All ten pass with the fix, including changed URL, in-place policy mutation, missing admission and cancellation controls.
- Three focused owner/action/navigation suites passed all 90 cases (7.07 seconds wrapper wall time). After the final test-only adjustment, the changed 10-case file passed again (19.94 seconds including cold compiler setup); CI case time is pending.
- Browser package production types, targeted test/workload types, typed lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed.
- One independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no actionable findings.

Full PR CI is currently skipped because this PR is a draft; the local results above are not a full-CI claim.

Production delta: 25 insertions / 3 deletions in two files. The remaining additions are the focused regression coverage and opt-in measurement workload.

prs.title: docs(workboard): document card field limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Workboard "Card fields" table describes `labels` only as "free-form strings", so users do not learn that each label is capped at 40 characters or that labels beyond the first 12 are dropped without an error; title, notes, `parents`, and `skills` limits are not documented either.

## User Impact

User impact: operators and agents writing cards can see the enforced limits up front instead of discovering them through a failed create or a silently shortened label list. No behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The table now lists the limits the Workboard store already enforces: `title` up to 180 characters (required), `notes` up to 4000, labels up to 40 characters each with only the first 12 distinct labels kept, and up to 20 entries for `parents` (120 characters each) and `skills` (80 characters each) on card creation. Only `docs/plugins/workboard.md` changes; translations are generated elsewhere.

Question for maintainers: should more than 12 labels be rejected like the other caps instead of being shortened silently? This PR only documents the current behavior.

## Evidence

Values are taken from the validators (`normalizeTitle`, `normalizeNotes` and `normalizeStringList` in `extensions/workboard/src/store-normalizers.ts`, `normalizeCappedStringList` in `extensions/workboard/src/store-string-lists.ts`) and checked live against an isolated test Gateway built from this branch (`2a8d393b9be`, on top of `cff88c2d21d`, own state directory, loopback port, 2026-10-14 17:06–17:08 UTC):

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| label with 40 characters | card created, label stored (40 chars), rc 0 |
| label with 41 characters | rejected: `labels must be 40 characters or fewer.`, rc 1 |
| 13 labels `l01…l13` | card created, 12 labels stored (`l13` dropped), rc 0 |
| labels `x,x,y` | card created with `["x","y"]` |
| title with 180 / 181 characters | created / `title must be 180 characters or fewer.` |
| notes with 4000 / 4001 characters | created / `notes must be 4000 characters or fewer.` |
| `skills`: 20 entries / 21 entries | created / `skills supports at most 20 entries.` |
| `skills`: entry with 80 / 81 characters | created / `skills must be 80 characters or fewer (got 81).` |
| `parents`: 21 entries | `parents supports at most 20 entries.` |
| `parents`: entry with 121 characters | `parents must be 120 characters or fewer (got 121).` |

Labels, title, and notes were created with `openclaw workboard create`; `skills` and `parents` with `openclaw gateway call workboard.cards.create`.

Docs checks on this branch (VPS, Node 24.21.0): `pnpm format:docs:check` (48 s), `pnpm lint:docs` (23 s, 0 issues), `pnpm docs:check-mdx` (18 s), `pnpm docs:check-links` (23 s, 0 broken), `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` (9 s), `pnpm lint:templates`, `pnpm changelog:check`, `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary`: all pass. `oxfmt --check docs/plugins/workboard.md` passes.

<details>
<summary>Unrelated failures in optional docs checks</summary>

`pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports two missing fragments in other pages (`gateway/config-tools.md:60`, `releases/2026.10.1.md:849`), and `pnpm docs:spellcheck` reports words in `docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime/hooks.md` and `docs/channels/x.md`. Neither touches this change.

</details>

Related #170018

## What Problem This Solves

`/status` and `session_status` can report a model's scalar 1M context capacity even when the selected window or catalog default is 200K. The same discrepancy affects a real active fallback model.

## User Impact

The denominator follows the existing effective-window selection for selected and active models, while retaining smaller authored runtime caps and the current locked-session/provenance rules. A model whose real window is 1M remains 1M. Model choice, catalog defaults, request selection and token accounting are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `resolveModelContextWindowProfile` before the existing context-limit and provenance projections. The selected-window limit caps a wider authored model limit, matching runtime budgeting. No configuration, schema, prompt, dependency, provider contract or migration is added.

Credit: @nyl199310. Original contributor commits and the production patch are retained.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway/CLI captures, actual catalog declarations and both public status outputs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190530#issuecomment-6564027957).

Exact candidate: `927f5b9704040c3fbfba17c06bc3dcbb3d473fe1`; frozen main: `1cbfa2c57741c0a69037077bd9bf0730bd220a93`. The contributor's refreshed head was merged and the complete candidate rebuilt; both candidate runs and all focused checks were repeated successfully.

The same driver ran four fresh, isolated Node 24.22.1 Docker profiles. A normal plugin manifest supplies the actual catalog windows; a local OpenAI-compatible provider completes real Gateway turns. Built CLI submits `/status`, then the driver reads its committed reply through `chat.history`. Authenticated HTTP invokes `session_status` with its normal public session key. No private status arguments or database rows are injected.

| Both `/status` and `session_status` | Main 1 | Main 2 | Candidate 1 | Candidate 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog default 200K | 45k/1.0m | 45k/1.0m | 45k/200k | 45k/200k |
| Explicit selected 200K | 45k/1.0m | 45k/1.0m | 45k/200k | 45k/200k |
| Real active fallback, 200K | 45k/1.0m | 45k/1.0m | 45k/200k | 45k/200k |
| True scalar 1M control | 45k/1.0m | 45k/1.0m | 45k/1.0m | 45k/1.0m |

Fallback is exercised by a configured agent primary receiving a local billing error and the ordinary fallback owner completing with a different provider. Catalog fields/defaults and the captured provider model sequence are identical across all four runs. The default-model control receives no model patch.

68 focused status tests passed; the final consolidated two-case regression also passed after fixture cleanup. On main its new selectable-window branch fails (96k instead of 50k), while its original scalar admitted-cap control passes. Focused typed lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. Real public-provider accounts, native CLI inference runtimes and microphone/audio behavior are not claimed.

The original added cases were consolidated into the existing admitted-cap regression rather than adding a second prepared-input matrix. Production +32/−4 (net +28), tests +9/−11 (net −2), documentation +5 against frozen main. The temporary 41-line allocation is removed; no new test files or production test seams.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores the old display calculation; no persistent format or state migration is involved. Blast radius is status context denominators and percentages for models with selectable windows, including an active fallback. Model routing, defaults, token accounting and actual runtime budgets retain their existing owners.

## What Problem This Solves

Pending-input history repeats the same eligibility rules in its count and page queries.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Ordinary history still shows cancelled inputs and live queued inputs; graceful-restart reads still select only captured queued inputs whose live custody has ended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the identical predicate into one private typed Kysely expression in the existing history kernel. Keep session identity, consumed-input exclusion, current-session checks, byte bounds, paging, worker ownership, and the existing snapshot versus single-statement paths unchanged. The memory backend keeps its own row predicate.

The cut removes 22 production lines. The existing graceful-shutdown case gains an assertion that captured IDs cannot be read while live custody remains held, before preservation and settlement. Its dedicated three-line test allocation covers this missing negative boundary without adding a new case or fixture.

## Evidence

- Three focused files pass in two shards: pending-input history, consumed-input accessor, and Gateway chat reader (135.13 seconds wall).
- Both actual isolated Gateway graceful-restart/resume cases pass against their deterministic provider, including queued-input FIFO, blocked-store shutdown, crash-inert history and resumed turns. CLI wall time was 522.75 seconds including runtime preparation; Vitest was 136.87 seconds.
- Production and changed-test type-aware lint, core and owning test typechecks, test-line ratchet, qualified format, whitespace/privacy checks, and normal commit hooks pass.
- Fresh independent review and full committed-range local ClawSweeper review at high reasoning found no actionable correctness or security findings (base f278c086c76a, head 842f96947fc8).
- Both query paths, callers, history worker, memory sibling, introduction history, and installed Kysely expression-builder contract inspected. The duplicate remains at the verified landed main anchor.
- Exact-head PR CI passed: [run 41349606879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41349606879) (35 successful jobs, 27 skipped). Local proof did not exercise PostgreSQL; no live provider, production Gateway, visual, or performance claim.

prs.title: feat(feishu): add opt-in replaceable public-body previews
prs.body:
Related: #143915

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu users can see a processing card until a whole answer appears when a reasoning-enabled Completions response defers public text for terminal classification. Operators who accept provisional prose currently cannot opt into seeing that body while it is generated without changing the canonical output policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit, default-off `channels.feishu.streaming.bodyPreview` option (also available per account). The built-in Completions transport emits a separate replaceable public-text snapshot, which the existing Agent and reply callback path carries to Feishu cards without inserting it into assistant history, committed blocks, or final text. The generic contract and opt-in policy are proposed for maintainer review in #143915.

The preview owner filters native/tagged reasoning and tool arguments, bounds snapshot growth, and resets on reasoning transitions, tool calls, cancellation, and failure. Feishu keeps provisional text separate from its canonical buffer, accepts newer revisions, and gives committed delivery/finalization precedence. Existing silence, approval, message-tool-only, and deferred-output/hook guards remain in force.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

Is the following Feishu-first contract acceptable in principle?

- Preserve terminal-classified canonical delivery as the default. Only an explicit `bodyPreview: true` enables provisional public text.
- Allow readers to see public prose that may later be replaced or removed. Replacement cannot undo prior exposure; native reasoning is excluded.
- Accept a shared ephemeral snapshot contract: preview identity, increasing revisions, replacement, empty reset, and finalization precedence. Only consumers that explicitly opt in must implement those preview obligations; ordinary partial replies retain their behavior.

This PR implements the built-in Completions producer and Feishu consumer. The [independent WebChat report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143915#issuecomment-5968966631) supports reuse of the same boundary, but WebChat support is follow-up scope and is not claimed here. Keeping this PR Feishu-first lets maintainers assess one concrete consumer before expanding adoption.

The author is holding routine main refreshes pending that direction. Acceptance in principle would not waive client screenshots, conflict resolution, or passing integration/CI before merge.

## User Impact

With streaming cards enabled, operators can set:

```json5
{ channels: { feishu: { streaming: { mode: "partial", bodyPreview: true } } } }
```

Readers may see public tool-preface or commentary text that is subsequently replaced or removed. This tradeoff is explicit; native reasoning display is not enabled. Missing/false settings retain existing behavior. The initial producer is the built-in OpenAI-compatible Completions transport and the initial consumer is Feishu; this does not promise support for every transport or channel.

This is separate from CardKit queue coalescing discussed in #103928. It does not claim to eliminate slow platform-write backlogs.

## Current Status (October 9)

- Published head: `ee8b552c2457f695c5f9a9a4a077b11e1d2a93c7`; open and unmerged, with conflicts against main.
- [Latest review, October 4 / revision 9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143944#issuecomment-5617516005): no actionable code/security findings; patch quality 4/6, overall/proof 3/6 because the required client images are missing. Maintainer product/API acceptance remains outstanding.
- [Head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34919423534) completed with two failed test shards and the aggregate gate. Local focused checks below do not replace hosted CI.
- Sanitized before/after Feishu client images have not been delivered in both the originating chat and this PR. Historical CardKit acknowledgements are platform-write evidence, not proof of client rendering.

## Evidence

### Published candidate: `ee8b552c2457f695c5f9a9a4a077b11e1d2a93c7`

Refreshed against pinned upstream `25155c466de25f99011166eb2e885fc3fdf533ea` on September 15. The two generated configuration-documentation conflicts were resolved with the canonical generator/check. The automatic runtime merges preserve the preview path alongside upstream Responses output-limit recovery and cooperative scheduler updates.

Validation on this frozen candidate:

- 506 tests passed across 10 files: transport/options/Agent loop 134, Gateway plugin-startup regression 1, reply execution progress 24, subscriber 10, complete runtime-refresh integration 23, and Feishu schema/dispatcher 314.
- Frozen pnpm 12.3.4 install, core production types, canonical packages test types, typed lint for PR-owned core/package files, formatting of 35 PR files, and scoped whitespace checks passed.
- Canonical configuration-doc generation, scope and check passed. Removing only the two bodyPreview entries restores the pinned base's combined/channel hashes; core/plugin hashes are unchanged. The metadata source itself did not change in this refresh.
- Independent complete-diff review completed both passes with no actionable P0-P2 findings (scoped-clean).

The [previous CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34805295607) failed in three lanes. The source-contract lane stopped during dependency installation on a GitHub release-asset HTTP 504; its source checks never ran. The other failures match upstream fixes now included in the pinned base: [Gateway reload-settlement test synchronization #147571](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147571) and [Git 2.54 fetch maintenance/worktree containment #147828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147828). The Gateway regression passed locally. The Linux-specific containment suite is not claimed as passed on Windows. A job rerun request was rejected by GitHub; no rerun was queued. The [head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34919423534) has since completed with failures: `checks-node-compact-large-29` reported a V8 heap out-of-memory worker failure, and `checks-node-compact-small-14` reported `write EPIPE` in the update-command service-custody test; the aggregate gate also failed. These failures remain unresolved for this head. The PR does not modify the failing update/process owners, but that does not establish that rerunning or refreshing main would pass.

No new full build, current-head live-platform run or Gateway deployment is claimed. Historical exact-SHA evidence below retains its original scope.

### Visual acceptance follow-up (September 15)

The latest durable review explicitly requires inspected, sanitized before/after Feishu client images, rendered in both the originating chat and this PR. **That delivery gate remains open.** An isolated replay of the earlier accepted `208b1423` source with 8-second synthetic chunks passed the disabled and enabled assertions again, including real CardKit acknowledgements, but the transient growing-body client frame was not successfully saved while the desktop window was minimized. These replay receipts are not offered as a replacement for the missing image pair. No private chat history or unsanitized desktop screenshot has been uploaded.

<details>
<summary>Historical candidate validation (SHA-qualified; not current-head checks)</summary>

### Prior integrated candidate: `7837644d4b77d81b9d93e13daa08ff797af6e14b`

Refreshed against pinned upstream `bd463dc1fed8e188c03443bb831c64c387dec016`. The previous local installation blocker no longer reproduced: the same pinned pnpm 12.3.4 entry point completed a frozen install. The simple-options conflict preserves both the preview opt-in and upstream service-tier forwarding. Channel metadata and configuration-documentation baselines were rebuilt with their canonical generators; the previous CI fixes remain present.

At the frozen integrated candidate:

- 575 focused tests passed across 12 files: transport/options/Agent loop 134, Gateway worker inference 30, reply progress/presentation 63, subscription 10, complete runtime-refresh integration 23, Feishu schema/dispatcher 314, and the per-attempt opt-in binding case 1. The other 24 cases in that last file were outside the selected test filter; this is not a claim that the full attempt-settle suite ran.
- Core production types and the canonical packages test-type route passed.
- Typed lint for all PR-owned core/package TypeScript files, formatting for 35 PR files, and the PR diff whitespace check passed.
- Canonical metadata has exactly the two expected Feishu boolean additions. Configuration-doc generation/check passed; removing only those two entries restores the pinned main's combined/channel hashes. Core/plugin hashes remain unchanged.
- Fresh independent review of the complete candidate completed both passes with no actionable P0-P2 findings.

An initial generator run loaded stale build artifacts from the previous candidate and failed. Those task-owned artifacts were retained separately, the resolver was verified to use current source, and the successful canonical regeneration used that source. No product workaround was added.

This update does not add a new local full build or live-platform run. Earlier exact-head platform observations remain identified below; the refreshed source has focused integration validation. Full repository CI and maintainer product/API acceptance are still required before merge.

### Prior CI follow-up: `38edddf640d9633ffc7ab9359b50208d1456637c`

Addresses the PR-owned failures in [the previous CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34695630026):

- Explicitly ignores the new `text_preview` event at the worker inference adapter. That adapter does not opt in to previews and has no preview wire contract; existing runtime behavior is preserved while the shared event switch is exhaustive.
- Gives the Completions test helper explicit direct/managed options branches, checked against the real transport parameter type.
- Regenerates the configuration documentation baseline for the two already-proposed channel/account `bodyPreview` options. Removing just those two entries exactly restores the previous combined/channel hashes; core/plugin metadata is unchanged.

Local validation: 17 body-preview tests and all 30 worker inference tests passed; the canonical packages test-type route, typed worker lint, config-doc baseline check, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent P0-P2 review of this follow-up: scoped-clean, with no actionable findings. No new full build or live Feishu run is claimed for this follow-up; the preview production path covered by the earlier proof is unchanged.

That follow-up retained the old base because the frozen installer was then blocked by local policy. The current integrated candidate above supersedes that installation/conflict blocker; the earlier CI fixes remain intact.

### Prior candidate validation: `c4aa165465c3fb3109f8cf497d5637f2a7126024`

Updated against upstream `21f4b69f97a1fdc60ea48ebdda1e4056154d30c3`. The generated channel metadata conflict was resolved using the canonical generator. Integration review also identified an upstream refresh-continuation wrapper that drops empty partials: this candidate preserves preview resets through that wrapper and clears a prior preview when a replacement is suppressed by inherited message-tool deduplication. Ordinary partial deduplication and already-delivered message-tool-only suppression remain intact.

At this candidate, with a fresh frozen pnpm 12.3.4 install:

- 517 tests passed across 9 files: transport/options/Agent loop 131, subscriber 10, presentation 39, complete runtime-refresh integration 23, Feishu schema/dispatcher 314.
- The new refresh integration cases exercise the actual refresh-to-successor callback composition: preview -> empty reset -> new preview -> dedupe-induced clear, plus unchanged message-tool-only suppression and no canonical block promotion.
- Core production typecheck, typed lint for the changed refresh implementation/tests, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Canonically regenerated metadata differs from the pinned main only by the two Feishu boolean fields (channel and account scope).
- Fresh independent review of the complete candidate found no actionable P0-P2 findings.

A new full build and full repository suites were not claimed locally for this SHA. Its CI subsequently failed on the three issues addressed above (plus the aggregate gate); the earlier full build is identified below. Product/API acceptance remains a maintainer decision.

### Prior candidate validation: `208b1423023a4ea954aed433b810b910ce5ccac4`

The following full-build and live CardKit observations belong to that exact earlier SHA; they are not relabeled as a new-head build or live run. ClawSweeper's [September 12 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143944#issuecomment-5617516005) accepted this platform-write evidence, reported no actionable findings, and left product/API acceptance to maintainers.

Refreshed against `e4129b6375e3179be5d9ed0a56a35f2871f4e73b`; candidate `208b1423023a4ea954aed433b810b910ce5ccac4` (2026-09-12). Resolved the Agent stream lifecycle conflict by preserving upstream's `runAgentCoreStream` wrapper and the preview-only event path. Regenerated channel metadata with the canonical generator; structural comparison against the base shows only the two expected Feishu boolean fields.

With Node 24.18.0 and pinned pnpm 12.3.4:

- Full `pnpm build` passed on the frozen candidate (16m 16s), including runtime, all declaration shards, Plugin SDK export checks and UI build. An isolated Linux ARM64 build of the same source also passed `build:ci-artifacts` with its own frozen dependencies and Node 26.8.2.
- 130 transport, Completions integration, simple-options and Agent-loop tests passed: before-terminal previews, canonical output/history preservation, reasoning/tool exclusion, reset/error/abort and bounded copying.
- 314 Feishu schema/dispatcher tests, 24 reply-presentation tests and 10 subscriber tests passed.
- Attempt-stream-settle: 20 passed, one failed in the existing snapshot/TTL/reopen case while removing a Windows SQLite sidecar. Independently running the original test file on the exact untouched base, with its own frozen dependencies, reproduced the same `EBUSY` cleanup failure (19 passed, one failed; base `.sqlite-shm`, candidate `.sqlite-wal`). No test was skipped or changed to make this pass.
- Core and extension production typechecks passed. Changed core and Feishu lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation configuration examples: 1,230 validated.
- Fresh independent review of the merged candidate found no outstanding P0-P2 findings; the two subsequent lint-only edits were independently reviewed as well.

</details>

### Real Feishu / CardKit qualification at `208b1423`

An isolated source-level harness exercised the real Completions parser -> `runAgentLoop` -> embedded subscription -> Feishu reply dispatcher -> live CardKit APIs, using timed synthetic provider chunks and one test DM. The sequence is native reasoning, two provisional public paragraphs, native reasoning/reset, then canonical public text. The provider HTTP boundary alone is synthetic; CardKit acknowledgements below are actual HTTP 200 / API `code: 0` responses.

Times are seconds after each case starts; the fixture intentionally pauses 2.2s per chunk, so these are lifecycle evidence, not a model-speed benchmark.

| Configuration | Accepted body changes | Terminal event | Confirmed cleanup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| omitted | No preview; canonical body at 11.296s | 11.035s | Streaming disabled at 11.847s |
| `false` | No preview; canonical body at 11.262s | 11.009s | Streaming disabled at 11.812s |
| `true` | 42 chars at 2.481s -> 87 chars at 4.662s -> reset placeholder at 6.866s -> canonical body at 9.068s | 11.040s | Streaming disabled at 11.583s |
| `true`, cancelled after first draft | 42 chars at 2.457s -> reset at 4.669s -> empty body at 4.986s | Abort at 4.418s | Streaming disabled at 5.550s; provisional text cleared |

No native-reasoning sentinel reached any recorded body write. Final subscriber output excludes both provisional paragraphs. The completed enabled/cancel run exited 0, with one fixture request per case. Observer harness SHA256: `e4363a60b3b6b2ca9282e93d946c6616a8c29fcc6fa9d9374a535e4d4f847d8e`.

The observer forwards to the same runtime fetch with the SSRF-pinned dispatcher and clones actual responses. Default-mode cases passed in an earlier run; enabled/cancel cases passed a subsequent run with the observer restricted to the body element (excluding footer updates). Candidate source was unchanged across runs. Failed harness qualification attempts are retained separately and are not counted as passed.

Boundary: these are real platform-write acknowledgements with a synthetic provider, not a screenshot/recording or a claim about client paint timing. The source-level harness bypasses normal Gateway ingress, admission/scheduling, the runner presentation wrapper, and persistent session storage. Separate tests cover the relevant callback/suppression and canonical-history invariants. No live Gateway restart or deployment replacement was needed. Full inbound, real-model and visual acceptance have not been verified at this head.

Remaining before merge:

- Complete the sanitized before/after Feishu client screenshot delivery and verify rendering in both the originating chat and the PR, as required by the latest durable review and repository UI gate.
- Maintainer agreement on the default-off shared preview contract and its provisional-text tradeoff is still requested.
- After maintainer direction, resolve main conflicts and validate the resulting integration with passing CI. Full repository `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` have not been run locally.

Maintainer edits are enabled. AI-assisted implementation and review.

prs.title: fix(memory): add reusable read-only search managers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Gateway `memory.search` requests should reuse Memory Core's query-only SQLite reader without losing search-triggered discovery of new or changed notes. Index creation, upgrade repair, source scanning, embeddings, and publication must remain writer-owned, including when no default writer/watch loop is active.

## Solution

Retain the registry-owned search reader, but run nonempty `onSearch` requests through **writer check → incremental sync/native publication → writer drain/close → reader revalidation → query-only query**. An existing registry-owned transient maintenance writer performs the scan, with unchanged hashes and embedding cache reuse; this is not an unconditional forced rebuild. Initial missing/invalid index preparation still uses the existing writer recovery path.

This update normally merges main `acbeb3a07197dbdbe89dd674f40b27279c912382`, retaining the native SQLite publication worker and `MemoryIndexDatabase.openPublished` owner introduced upstream. No rebase or force push was used.

## User Impact

- The same Gateway reader sees a newly created or edited note before returning the next search, with or without a running default writer.
- Reader connections remain `PRAGMA query_only=1`; they do not sync, migrate, write vector tables, start watchers/listeners, or own native publication.
- Search freshness can wait for source scanning, embedding changes, and publication. It is no longer published-index-only behavior and does not promise a latency improvement for every request.
- Legacy runtimes without the optional private reusable-manager hook retain transient CLI acquisition and request cleanup.
- This does not change the default model-facing `memory_search` tool's acquisition purpose or its 30-second deadline, and does not claim to fix the production slow-point report.

## Lifecycle and Compatibility Contract

- **Writer authority:** refresh uses the retained reader's registry, resolved settings, database path, and captured state-owner environment. It delegates authority, never its query-only connection, to canonical writer admission. A changed cwd cannot select a different state owner or evade the original admission refusal.
- **Settlement:** accepted writer work settles before reader query/close; cancellation rejects the result without releasing native cleanup custody. Failed transient-writer close remains registry-owned for retry. Late maintenance acquisition declines during global teardown rather than waiting on the reader that teardown is draining.
- **Reader lifetime:** one retained reader per resolved key, until close, replacement, failed-candidate cleanup, plugin retirement, or shutdown. Gateway does not close reusable readers after each request.
- **Recovery:** missing/invalid indexes and schema/identity repair remain writer-owned. Valid empty indexes remain usable after writer preparation and discover a later first note. Configured fallback indexes are adopted before refresh. Native-vector debt may be repaired by the writer; the reader checks persisted vector readiness without entering write admission.
- **Disclosure:** acquisition repair warnings remain request-scoped and survive both successful and failed Gateway retrieval. The maintenance writer shares the reader's automatic-rebuild notice.
- **Data model:** this PR's FTS changes export canonical validators and reconcile derived FTS state through the existing writer savepoint, without a new PR-owned schema-version/table/column declaration. The merge inherits upstream agent schema 21. Canonical-schema preservation and legacy migration tests are not a published-updater replay.

## Evidence

Current pushed head: `12b5dc8c2b3c9e1e16ae72f9067dc0077d27f73c` (2026-09-19).

All runtime commands used one Vitest worker and one test-plan shard at a time:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONCURRENCY=1 \
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts <explicit files>
```

Fresh verification and observed regressions:
