prs.title: fix: require approval for dynamic shell predicates
prs.body:
## Summary

Require normal exec approval for predicates whose shell source can expand or be interpreted differently from parsed argv. This narrows the safe-builtin exemption introduced by #79363 and extended to predicates in the later builtin work, while retaining ordinary literal predicate checks. It complements the exact `-v` guard from #180880 and corrects the quote scanner added with the shared authorization planner in #84172.

## What Problem This Solves

### What this Problem Solves

In gateway `exec` allowlist mode, a predicate can appear harmless to `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts` while Bash later synthesizes a different operand and runs an external command. `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts` can also miss a glob after an escaped quote in an ANSI-C string. Together, these mismatches can let a model supplied command cross the approval boundary without a matching allowlist entry or operator approval. The classifier now withholds automatic trust from ambiguous predicate source, and the renderer catches that escaped quote form before dispatch.

## What was wrong

1. `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts` checked the parsed `test` or `[` argv for an exact `-v` token. Shell expansion could produce a different operand after that check.
2. `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts` treated an escaped single quote inside `$'...'` as the end of an ordinary single-quoted string, hiding a following glob from the enforced renderer.

The combined effect was automatic authorization of a command whose final Bash behavior exceeded the reviewed predicate.

## Why this design

- Grant the safe-builtin exemption only to predicate source with static operand syntax; route ambiguous forms through the existing approval policy.
- Track ANSI-C quoting and escaped quotes in the renderer so a later glob fails closed. Consume each `$$` PID parameter as a pair so the following ordinary single quote keeps Bash semantics.
- Keep literal `test -d` and `[ -d ]` checks, including quoted paths with spaces, on the existing automatic path.
- Use the existing policy modes and configuration surface.

## Why this does not conflict with related PRs

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #79363 | Safe-builtin convenience | Retains automatic handling for static predicates and other closed builtins. |
| #84172 | Shared authorization planning and source scanning | Corrects one ANSI-C quote-state case in that scanner. |
| #119351 | Preserve shell builtin semantics during enforced rendering | Keeps builtins in the shell; changes whether a predicate is automatically trusted. |
| #180880 | Exact parsed `-v` rejection | Preserves that guard and closes the residual source/argv mismatch. |
| #188780 | Shared test-budget headroom | Integrates the already merged upstream repair that unblocks exactly allocated regression growth; this PR adds no separate shared-baseline change. |

These changes are based on `main` after those PRs and change only the predicate trust and renderer checks.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and mode | Command or probe run | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shared allowlist, no matching entry | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module` source probe of the benign ANSI-C quote plus glob regression shape | `analysisOk=true`, `allowlistSatisfied=true`, `safeBuiltins`; new classifier test failed | `allowlistSatisfied=false`; classifier test passes |
| Enforced renderer | Same source probe and renderer regression test | Returned the unchanged command as `ok=true`; new renderer test failed | Returns `shell expansion in enforced arguments` |
| Renderer quote tracking after PID parameters | Real prompt-only plans for `eval git status $$'a\'?v` and the four-dollar variant, with null satisfaction metadata | At PR head `8bca86cd`, the renderer returned `ok=true` for both; the two new rejection cases failed. Ordinary direct `$$` arguments were already blocked upstream as `dynamic-argument` | The renderer rejects both with `shell expansion in enforced arguments`; one- and three-dollar ANSI-C quoted-glob controls remain accepted |
| Gateway allowlist, approval off | Real Gateway E2E command in Testing; benign dynamic `test -e *.txt` plus allowlisted `printf` | Full gateway baseline was not run; the direct evaluator and renderer results above show the prerequisite automatic authorization | Rejects with `exec denied: allowlist miss` before process launch |
| Gateway allowlist, allow-once | Same real Gateway E2E with operator `exec.approval.resolve` RPC | Baseline approved path was not run | Actual process completed with exit code 0 and output `approved` |
| Gateway policy changed while approval was pending | Same real Gateway E2E; operator `exec.approvals.set` changed security to deny before allow-once resolution | Baseline revocation path was not run | Rejects stale approval with `Exec approval changed before execution`; no process result |
| Model-planned agent turn through a separate Gateway process | Deterministic local mock provider sent `chat.send` turns with `test -e proof.txt && pwd` and `test -e *.txt && pwd` under the same real allowlist/off policy; observed the paired `exec` tool outputs | With the original classifier and renderer temporarily restored, the new QA case failed at its dynamic-denial assertion while the static control passed | Static predicate returned the workspace path; dynamic predicate returned `exec denied: allowlist miss` and no `pwd` output |
| Ordinary static predicates | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | Existing literal checks passed | Literal `test` and `[` checks pass, including a quoted path with spaces |
| Published stable policy to patched head | Published `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI `approvals set --file <synthetic-policy>`; patched `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `approvals get --json`, then shared evaluator, all in isolated state | Stable CLI stored version-1 allowlist/on-miss policy with one agent allowlist entry | Doctor migration completed; patched CLI and canonical SQLite row retained defaults and allowlist. With that stored policy, `test -d .` remained automatic and `test -e *.txt` required approval |
| Focused suite | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-render.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | New classifier and renderer tests failed red before the implementation: 4 failures, 31 passes, 1 skip in the two-file run | 57 passes, 2 skips in the final three-file run, including the upstream arithmetic/assignment regressions |

The real-owner gateway test exercises operator approval RPC and the process supervisor; its approved outcome is observed at the process output, and its denied and policy-changed outcomes stop before execution.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

Callers using ordinary static predicates keep automatic execution. Predicates with dynamic or ambiguous source syntax require the existing allowlist or approval decision; with approval disabled, they are denied. A policy written by the latest published stable CLI remained readable after the patched runtime's supported doctor migration, with the same defaults and agent allowlist. The classifier and real Gateway boundary tests cover these outcomes.

## Boundary decision

1. **Accepted by repository maintainer `art22s`:** quoted literal filenames containing shell metacharacters, such as `[ -f 'report[v2].txt' ]`, use the existing allowlist/approval authority. With approval disabled and no matching entry, these forms are denied. Retain the current static-source gate; ordinary static predicates and quoted paths containing spaces remain automatic. The explicit decision is [recorded on this PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187884#issuecomment-6535185770).

## Testing

- Added classifier, renderer, and gateway boundary regressions; final focused run after integrating `main`: 57 passed, 2 skipped (10.47 s Vitest). The two new PID-prefixed quote rejection cases failed at the intended renderer assertion before the dollar-pair repair; both pass after it, and ANSI-C quoted-glob controls remain green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 3 tests passed on the final integrated candidate (17.42 s Vitest). The new predicate test uses the real Gateway and approval/process owners with no RPC or process mocks; the existing hook reload test now updates config through the Gateway's managed `config.patch` path to avoid a missed file-watcher event.
- Previously verified at `8bca86cd`, cross-process QA agent-turn E2E: focused case passed after matching each model-planned tool call to its result; the complete QA file passed 10/10 before that final assertion refinement (110.22 s Vitest, 127.03 s wrapper). The local provider is deterministic and does not represent a live model decision.
- Final candidate infra and agents-root TypeScript checks, targeted core oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The four-file validation wrapper took 338.64 s including a fresh 271.3 s runtime build required after integrating `main`.
- Existing literal predicate tests and gateway authorization integration tests remain green.
- Independent Codex review verified the source and regression contracts; the upstream integration retains every PR-owned blob byte-for-byte. Hosted Clawsweeper reviewed final head `640fd5d1ff47` with no findings or Before merge items, sufficient proof (4/6), and Ready for maintainer review. The quoted-literal authorization decision is explicitly accepted above.
- Test budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/static-predicate-approval.txt` allocates exactly the 221 added LF lines for distinct classifier, renderer, real approval/revocation, and agent-turn contracts; carry this reason into the squash body. Integrated canonical main commit `4368b276f5a3`, which includes the published budget repair [#188780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188780). The eight PR-owned file blobs remain byte-identical to reviewed head `9f951bd673cf`, and the shared baseline matches canonical main exactly. The staged canonical test-line check now passes: 6,313,918 lines, effective ceiling 6,345,942, slack 32,024. Hosted [CI run 41143275791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143275791) completed successfully on `640fd5d1ff47`. The baseline check, aggregate CI gate, and required CI status all pass.

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes setup-token login selecting an incompatible profile when the Anthropic default profile is configured for an API key.

## User Impact

- Users with this mismatch can repeat setup-token login to save a usable profile. Existing API-key declarations used by other agents are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Anthropic setup reuses compatible token or OAuth profile IDs and skips incompatible configured slots. Interactive and noninteractive setup use the same selection rule.

## Evidence

- HEAD `2767cdbdc5397eb87cda6d2ba16807c338aff699`.

- Published OpenClaw 2026.10.9 completes login but its native Gateway rejects the turn before a provider request.
- At this head, login saves `anthropic:setup-token`, and a native Gateway turn completes using the same setup-token.
- A transparent recording relay forwarded exactly one Anthropic request: HTTP 200, request ID `req_011CgX5J7pApJqZpVr7FNkVX`.

prs.title: fix(codex): omit unavailable question-tool and redundant mode guidance
prs.body:
Closes #187061

## What Problem This Solves

Codex has native collaboration modes, such as Default and Plan, with their own model-facing instructions. Ordinary OpenClaw-managed sessions always select Default and do not expose a mode switch, but still receive a `Collaboration Mode: Default` block explaining mode changes. They also receive instructions for the native `request_user_input` question tool even when it is unavailable.

In the reported configuration, this is intentional tool suppression: when OpenClaw's `ask_user` is callable and no native-question opt-in is configured, OpenClaw disables `request_user_input` to avoid a duplicate question interface. The native collaboration prompt is rendered independently, so its question-tool guidance remains. Even when the native tool is registered, using it in Default mode requires a separate opt-in.

The result is a mismatch between the instructions the model reads and the capabilities the integration provides. The existing "only when it is listed" condition prevents an unconditional instruction to call a missing tool, but leaves irrelevant tool-specific guidance and mode boilerplate in the prompt. This PR removes that noise without enabling extra tools or removing native modes from paths that use them.

## User Impact

The agent receives collaboration guidance matching its available question capabilities, without announcing a mode that ordinary managed sessions cannot switch. Explicit native-question opt-ins and native-supervised modes remain supported; OpenClaw's `ask_user` keeps its own contract.

Existing history is not rewritten. On managed resume, an explicit supersession notice withdraws earlier collaboration instructions, including retained Plan-mode guidance. This is a prompt-quality change; no latency, cost, or answer-quality improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already decides which collaboration mode and question tools an ordinary managed session can use; its instructions should describe those actual capabilities. Enabling native questions just to match the existing prompt would change behavior rather than fix the mismatch. Replacing every `request_user_input` reference with `ask_user` would also be incorrect: the two tools have different contracts.

A shorter caller-supplied collaboration block is not enough, either. Codex can take its effective collaboration text from the selected model's catalogue, overriding that fallback. This PR therefore suppresses the native collaboration block only for ordinary managed sessions and places concise, capability-aware guidance in the existing thread developer instructions, where it survives compaction.

Native `request_user_input` guidance requires both tool registration and Default-mode eligibility. General guidance about autonomy, genuinely required input, and approval boundaries remains. Supervised starts/resumes/forks and specialized cron/side-question policies retain their existing owners. No new user configuration or dependency is introduced.

## Evidence

Current head: `adb0f8db5e18955d503aaea8f5ab035f5d1663b6`. Base: `1a881c5ff7850f03c8e8f1ada9302ba7fd939dab`. Validation dates: October 29-30, 2026.

### Review and CI repairs

- Updated successful managed-lifecycle configuration fixtures to include the `origins` map required by the native protocol. Production handling was not weakened to accommodate incomplete fixtures.
- Corrected canonical prompt reconstruction to use the developer instructions actually returned by thread configuration, including the managed collaboration policy. Regenerated snapshots through the existing generator and added two focused assertions.
- Fixed a related diagnostic undercount exposed by the consumer tests: prompt reports and trajectory rendering now consume the assembled developer instructions, including the collaboration block. Removed a now-duplicate configured-MCP notice from trajectory assembly.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727) is green: 58 successful checks, 55 conditionally skipped, none pending or failed. Both previously failing jobs now pass: [canonical prompt snapshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727/job/123711976572) and [changed extensions bundle 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727/job/123711976931).
- Local verification includes all 14 app-inventory consumer checks, 13 snapshot checks, the unchanged prompt-report regression after its repair, current generated snapshots, relevant project typechecks, targeted lint/formatting, both line-budget checks, and a complete `pnpm build`.

### Native request-boundary proof

The repository-pinned real Codex **0.164.0** app-server was exercised with a local fixture provider. These tests use synthetic model metadata and fixture responses, not a live model.

- **Red/green:** the original prompt-owner code failed because captured developer input still contained the catalogue-owned Default policy; the fixed implementation passed.
- **Four question surfaces:** neither question tool; callable OpenClaw Ask User with native questions disabled; native registration without Default eligibility; and explicit Default eligibility. Only the last receives native-question usage guidance. All four omit the catalogue-owned Default announcement while preserving skill delivery.
- **Retained history and controls:** native replay retains the earlier Plan message, verifies that a later managed-resume notice supersedes it without another Default heading, and confirms that a native-owned sibling still receives native mode guidance. WebSocket refresh and native compaction cases also pass.
- The original native/policy run passed all 10 checks. The reorganized lifecycle/turn-parameter suites passed 191 checks; all 14 prompt-prefix stability checks and two selected canonical-fork cases also passed. These are overlapping focused runs, not a full-suite total.

### Real Gateway/model output

These are selected fields from captured real Gateway RPC, native requests and persisted native developer messages, not expected-output examples. Replies are actual Gateway payload text with whitespace trimmed. Every model turn used **GPT-6 Luna** with native ChatGPT authentication and principal-match checks; no provider responses were mocked. UUIDs identify disposable fixtures.

The observer's `nativeCollaborationInstructions` field records `config.include_collaboration_mode_instructions`; `nativeToolEnabled` records `config["tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled"]`. Null means the request did not supply an override, not false. `askUserDeclared` is derived from the actual dynamic-tool names. Only known collaboration-policy lines are retained, not the full developer prompt.

**Fresh managed session.** Real native Codex **0.164.0** received this request surface. The same quoted policy sentence was read back from that thread's native developer message:

```json
{
  "request": {
    "method": "thread/start",
    "nativeCollaborationInstructions": false,
    "nativeToolEnabled": false,
    "askUserDeclared": true,
    "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": false,
    "collaborationExcerpt": [
      "Prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Ask the user directly when required input prevents progress; silence is not an answer or approval."
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  }
}
```

**Latest-stable upgraded retained OpenClaw session.** Registry `latest` was independently checked as **2026.10.9** for both OpenClaw and `@openclaw/codex`. The official stable runtime used native **0.160.0**. After a real seed turn, the fixture stopped, selected the fixed core/bundled plugin/native **0.164.0**, and ran supported `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` against its retained state (exit 0). Service repair was disabled for the fixture. This exercises a retained-state runtime upgrade, not the update installer.

The second input asked for the previous marker without supplying it again. Actual replies and identities:

```json
[
  {
    "phase": "stable-seed",
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "BLUE-271",
    "threadId": "01a189c7-f180-7d20-9972-88f5ef1a4d94",
    "action": "started",
    "sessionId": "b7da0c91-3a6a-4d9c-b997-0c31e304cd0b"
  },
  {
    "phase": "stable-upgraded-retained",
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "BLUE-271",
    "threadId": "01a189c9-94d0-7170-991e-61d16fa90021",
    "action": "started",
    "sessionId": "b7da0c91-3a6a-4d9c-b997-0c31e304cd0b"
  }
]
```

Stable's actual persisted collaboration excerpt:

```json
{
  "collaborationExcerpt": [
    "Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>"
  ]
}
```

Fixed Gateway request for the retained OpenClaw session; its persisted native developer message independently contains the same new sentence:

```json
{
  "method": "thread/start",
  "nativeCollaborationInstructions": false,
  "nativeToolEnabled": false,
  "askUserDeclared": true,
  "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": false,
  "collaborationExcerpt": [
    "Prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Ask the user directly when required input prevents progress; silence is not an answer or approval."
  ]
}
```

**Upgrade limitation:** the OpenClaw session ID and history survived, but the native thread was recreated (`action: "started"`). The strict upgrade test exited 1 because it required an unchanged native thread ID; that failure is preserved in `upgrade-evidence.json`, not relabeled as a passing native-resume test. Later assertions in that test were not reached; the excerpts above come from independently captured request/rollout records. Existing runtime/tool-catalogue rotation guards are unchanged by this PR, and both surfaces changed between stable and fixed versions; the exact first rotation trigger was not logged. This evidence establishes a retained OpenClaw-session upgrade, **not native-thread continuity across versions**.

**Same-build cold native resume.** A separate successful run stopped/restarted the fixed Gateway and retained both identities while recalling the earlier marker:

```json
[
  {
    "phase": "fresh-managed",
    "sessionId": "5f0a0cbd-f477-4558-80c7-be84d5ba7b72",
    "threadId": "01a189c3-422e-71d1-9aa3-eef40e47f891",
    "action": "started",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  },
  {
    "phase": "retained-managed",
    "sessionId": "5f0a0cbd-f477-4558-80c7-be84d5ba7b72",
    "threadId": "01a189c3-422e-71d1-9aa3-eef40e47f891",
    "action": "resumed",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  }
]
```

**Explicit native-question opt-in.** A separate fresh control set both `features.default_mode_request_user_input=true` and `tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled=true`. The captured request did not override native questions to false. Its actual persisted developer-policy observations and real reply were:

```json
{
  "policy": {
    "managedPolicy": true,
    "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": true,
    "oldModeAnnouncement": false
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "NATIVE-OPT-IN-OK"
  }
}
```

This control verifies authored configuration/guidance with a real completed turn. It does not claim execution of a blocking question or same-thread opt-in refresh.

**Native-supervised control.** A separate real native seed was continued through `sessions.catalog.continue`. The Gateway completed a real turn with lifecycle action `forked`. Native collaboration rendering was not disabled, the turn did not impose managed Default mode, and the persisted native policy remained native-owned:

```json
{
  "request": {
    "method": "thread/fork",
    "nativeCollaborationInstructions": null,
    "managedPolicy": false
  },
  "nativeDeveloperPolicy": {
    "managedPolicy": false,
    "oldModeAnnouncement": true,
    "collaborationExcerpt": [
      "Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>"
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "action": "forked",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "SUPERVISED-NATIVE-OK"
  }
}
```

This control passed separately; it was not reached by the strict upgrade test. Native questions remained disabled by the existing tool-selection policy; this checks collaboration-prompt ownership, not native question-tool callability.

**Build provenance:** the checkout and final build stamps identify `adb0f8db5e1`. Generic `dist/build-info.json` retains `d39a5cc5daf8` from build start before the follow-up commit. A read-only reconstruction of the canonical Codex-plugin compiler fingerprint matches current clean source, and all **180** stamped Codex output hashes match. The attached verifier/result document that scope; no metadata was rewritten and no whole-Gateway artifact-equivalence claim is made.

The supplemental 
[openclaw-187856-live-proof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34158233/openclaw-187856-live-proof.zip)
 contains sanitized per-run records, exact prompt excerpts, source harness/observer/companion modules, package provenance and reproduction instructions. Runs are reported separately, including the strict upgrade failure. No credentials, account identifiers, IP addresses, private endpoints or full private prompts are included. Existing user Gateway/channels/sessions were untouched.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce focused checks and inspect test cost</summary>

Native request-capture and policy tests:

```sh
pnpm test \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.handoff.native.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-policy.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Recorded original result: 3 policy checks plus 7 native checks passed; 111.95 seconds total runner wall time, including worker preparation.

Lifecycle and turn-parameter checks:

```sh
pnpm test \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/turn-params.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Recorded original result: 91 unit checks and 100 lifecycle checks passed; 102.67 seconds total runner wall time. Existing test groups were moved to focused sibling modules without changing their bodies, avoiding growth in already oversized suites.

Review-failure reproduction and snapshot verification:

```sh
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.app-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts \
  --testNamePattern 'routes AGENTS.md natively and MEMORY.md through tools' --maxWorkers=1
pnpm prompt:snapshots:check
```

The recorded failed-consumer rerun passed all 14 app-inventory checks in 53.09 seconds including runner preparation. The prompt-report regression, discovered separately, passed after its repair.

The dedicated allocation now covers **185 net test lines**, including the two snapshot assertions added during review. The shared test-line baseline is unchanged. Timings are local measurements, not CI estimates.

</details>

prs.title: feat(sessions): add creator-only and named-audience confidentiality
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Personal chats and closed working groups on multi-user Gateways need a read/write audience that is independent of visual Draft status and participation membership.

## User Impact

Operators can configure creator/admin-only conversations or exact named audiences without using Draft as the confidentiality mechanism. The policy applies to discovery, reading, events and mutation admission, while existing agent restrictions and incognito behavior remain in force.

This is an opt-in permission-model change. Enabling the source policy also restricts existing sessions without an explicit access override. Explicit per-session overrides remain authoritative. Restrictive access prevents public-share disclosure. Older binaries ignore the new access metadata, so staged adoption and rollback containment are required; this draft is not deployment-ready.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a separate session access policy with creator-only, named-audience, source-bound and explicit unrestricted modes. Only direct-human creator/admin authority can manage access; existing-session changes are identity-fenced.
- Resolve source-bound audiences from exact agent/channel/account/chat rules and explicit migration aliases. Numeric Telegram topics inherit the exact chat audience; ambiguous or unknown routes fail closed. Audiences are trusted canonical profile IDs supplied by the operator, never inferred from display names, chat categories or participation members.
- Persist source access before the first publication of inbound, web and child sessions. Private or unknown sources do not inherit a shared parent's audience.
- Reuse one access decision across existing read, sharing, storage and transport owners. Recheck current access for revocation, retained mutation/media authority and cached discovery; stale bookkeeping cannot restore revoked access.
- Keep visual creation defaults, Draft, incognito and role/agent ceilings separate. No existing live configuration or session migration is included.

The smallest coherent stage is the access boundary plus atomic creation: exposing the setting without covering its read/write consumers would leave confidentiality incomplete. Canonical validator regeneration accounts for most changed-line churn; no unrelated refactor or dependency changes are included.

## Evidence

Passed locally on the exact committed source:

- 24 focused policy/creation tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-access.test.ts src/config/sessions/creation-visibility.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- 2 compiled-wire validator regressions: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/session-access.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Canonical Gateway validator generation and `--check`; formatting on all 72 changed paths; syntax-only lint on all 70 changed TypeScript files; diff and source-hash integrity checks.
- Additional isolated synthetic handler/owner probes passed for selected audience, creator and admin versus equal-role nonmembers: list/describe/history/search, access management, send/mutation admission, event filtering, cached discovery and revocation. These probes used local synthetic state and are not committed CI tests or provider/model sends.
- Isolated inbound SQLite, persistent-child and web-create-service probes observed source access at first publication without Draft. Unknown identity denial, exact alias/topic rules, explicit controls, stale writes, agent ceilings, incognito and retained roleless media-ticket revocation were also exercised at their owning boundaries.

Known validation gaps remain:

- Full typecheck and type-aware lint stopped at the repository's external-dependency-link/declaration-input guard, before a code verdict. Syntax lint is not a substitute.
- The broader admission/gateway/lifecycle test wrappers did not complete; timeouts are not passing results.
- No full authenticated WebSocket, Control UI, Telegram, real-model, upgrade or deployed-runtime acceptance has been completed. The isolated probes are narrower than those workflows and do not exhaust every awaited-read interleaving or HTTP widget route.
- Two scoped independent read-only reviews produced findings that were repaired and checked. The canonical autoreview helper was unavailable; no fresh helper-clean or CI sign-off is claimed.

Please retain draft status while the permission model, compiler gates and remaining runtime coverage are reviewed.

prs.title: fix(doctor): allow config promotion after plugin migration guidance changes
prs.body:
Fixes #190658

## What Problem This Solves

Git-checkout updates and `update repair` can refuse Doctor’s config promotion after Doctor rewrites its own pending plugin migration guidance, leaving retired heartbeat config in place and the Gateway stopped.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor can promote the repaired config while unfinished plugins retain their settings and migration obligations. This fix must be present in the update candidate; it requires no change to the installed updater.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compare obligation identity and protected fields at the existing migration fence, excluding only the presentation fields `reason` and `command`. Plugin-set changes, protected paths, validation exclusions, migration requirements, transaction exclusion, and live writer authority remain checked. The same comparison serves publication and settlement.

## Evidence

- The new production Doctor-preflight regression is RED on `2be13a6bdc761deaf59efceccb343852bbaee3c1`, with `changed=[fixture:command, fixture:reason]` during config publication, and GREEN with this fix. It checks heartbeat-key retirement, retained settings and obligations, a repeat update Doctor pass, and standalone Doctor convergence.
- 86 focused named Doctor, config-publication, and migration-ledger tests passed (Doctor files: 37 tests, 190.41 s combined wall); guidance-only publication succeeds and changes to all five protected fields refuse. Existing detached-writer and revoked-authority controls remain green. Config-publication file: 19 tests, 17.63 s wall; migration-ledger file: 30 tests, 21.76 s wall. After moving the unchanged comparator beside its schema, all seven new regression/control cases passed again; touched-file type-aware lint and formatting passed. PR CI supplies broad types, lint, and tests.
- Shared autoreview, medium reasoning, P0–P2, on the final staged change (same tree as `bff1f42b61207`) against the base above: scoped-clean. Complete owner context covers publication, settlement, completion, and rollback; no actionable findings.
- Simplification: one existing owner, +14 net production lines and +80 regression-test lines. The separate 80-line test allocation covers the reported failure and protected-field refusal controls. No new state or caller workaround.
- Blacksmith Testbox passed the published `2026.10.9` updater → candidate smoke: update exit 0, recorded completion, readiness HTTP 200, running version verified, and retained durable/incognito state checked. [Remote run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41348757182). This used the working tree before the comparator’s file move; exact-head PR CI covers the final layout. Updater recovery fixtures stay with CI because their wrapper requires broad runtime preparation. The exact macOS LaunchAgent / historical git-checkout sequence has not been replayed.

Reported and diagnosed by @saariuslystoned.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve literal remote-shell file paths without trimming
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The remote-shell sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath` for both container-mount and host-mount mapping; the containment guards are unchanged and still operate on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the remote-shell bridge owner, closing the sandbox-backend trio: mxc #187766, OpenShell #187777, remote shell here).

## User Impact

Agents in remote-shell-backed sandboxes now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and boundary rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `091ce5a1b` (branch `fix/remote-shell-literal-file-path`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.18, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.ts:423`, through the public `readFile`, with the bridge's GNU shell scripts executed locally by the test harness's established runner (real fs, real scripts; only the transport boundary is local)
- Decision surface: the `filePath` parameter of sandboxed agent file tools
- Recorder/readback boundary: the file bytes returned by `readFile`, asserted byte-for-byte against distinct literal/decoy contents
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy bytes (`Buffer.from("decoy-data")`); the 23 pre-existing tests passed (1 failed / 23 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 24 tests pass, with `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the pinned-read-source, copy-streaming, ownership-mapping, and mutation-guard tests are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: fixture-scoped temp dirs only; no Gateway, session, token, or config touched

### Shipped-entry-point remote-shell proof (real SSH backend, two legs)

Setup (identical for both legs): fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; shipped CLI entry `node openclaw.mjs agent --local --json -m "…"` (embedded runner; dist built from the exact commit under test, `dist/build-info.json` commit-stamped); sandbox `mode: "all"`, `backend: "ssh"`, real sshd at `sandbox-user@10.x.x.x:2223` (publickey only) with an initially empty remote `workspaceRoot`; agent workspace pre-seeded with sibling files `" x.txt"` (`literal-data`) and `"x.txt"` (`decoy-data`), uploaded by the real tar-over-ssh provisioning on the first sandbox fs call. The model endpoint is a deterministic local stub scripting a fixed 5-call sequence (read `" x.txt"`, read `"x.txt"`, write `" x.txt"` ← `literal-write-data`, read both back); every production byte — CLI, runner, provisioning, fs bridge, remote GNU shell scripts, SSH transport — is shipped code. Tool results are recorded from the model-facing request log; byte forensics read the persisted remote workspace after the run.

**Base leg — `c77cfc122` (dist `2026.10.8-c77cfc122d28`, defect present):**


prs.title: fix(signal): bound monitor waitForIdle on hung receive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators stopping the Gateway or restarting the Signal channel could wait forever when a Signal receive never finished. Teardown used to await ingress stop (admission, pump, and active deliveries) before the task-runner idle window. A hung attachment fetch or handler delivery never started that window, so `gateway stop` and channel restart never returned.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal monitor already tracks receive and reply work so teardown can drain. The runner in `extensions/signal/src/monitor/task-runner.ts` still returns after 30 seconds with no task or ingress-stop completing. Ingress stop shares that progress-aware window, so a delivery that finishes at 25s resets the deadline for later work. Observed daemon exit stays outside that window: a stuck signal-cli cannot report the channel complete while it still owns the port or config lock. On non-abort teardown, accepted work drains before the daemon is stopped. Leftover receive/reply work is logged and left running. Accepted ingress claims stay in the queue. The 15-second tool-result idle workaround is gone; #142775 now owns that synchronization.

## User Impact

Operators can stop the Gateway or restart Signal even when one inbound receive or reply is stuck. After that idle drain gives up, a later text chunk or a send that finished loading an attachment does not call signal-cli. An allowed send still does.

## Evidence

Live `node`/`tsx` against production `monitorSignalProvider` plus the native Signal HTTP SSE client, after the daemon-exit and progress-aware drain repair. A local fake signal-cli accepted the SSE connection, emitted one `receive` event, and held `dispatchReplyFromConfig` as an unfinished reply. After abort, receive-work drain returned at 30004ms, logged leftover tasks and pending ingress stop, and kept the durable claim. Releasing the reply after return did not drop the accepted message.

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-141305-state-rq45 pnpm exec tsx ./proof-141305-signal-monitor-shutdown.ts
[   12ms] HTTP fake signal-cli at http://127.0.0.1:63932
[   87ms] SSE client connected
[  105ms] SSE receive event written
[  233ms] REPLY dispatchReplyFromConfig entered; holding unfinished reply
[  235ms] QUEUE before abort claims=1 pending=0 ids=["number:+15550001111",1]
[  236ms] STOP abort signaled
[30239ms] ERR signal waitForIdle made no progress within 30000ms; continuing teardown with 1 task(s) still in flight and ingress stop pending
[30239ms] DONE monitorSignalProvider returned after 30239ms (abort at 235ms)
[30240ms] QUEUE after return claims=1 pending=0 ids=["number:+15550001111",1]
[30240ms] LEFT signal waitForIdle made no progress within 30000ms; continuing teardown with 1 task(s) still in flight and ingress stop pending
[30240ms] REPLY unfinished reply released
PROOF_OK returned_after_abort_ms=30004 leftover=1
```

Head `2dc45ba5a4ca8a9b489762ba630c1f85497bc3b2` merges current main and keeps that idle fence and the send handoff. The shutdown-bound monitor tests passed on that tree: hung reply returns after the idle window, an accepted attachment claim stays queued, and teardown does not finish while daemon stop is still pending.

The signal-cli and chunk transcripts below are from parent `b4f81417f4c5397ccaaf793d469e3a6e9c8e376e`, which this merge still contains. That head passes the retirement check through the send handoff. A local JSON-RPC peer accepted the first 4-character chunk of `abcdefghij` and did not receive `efgh` or `ij` after retirement. A media read that retired the caller produced no RPC. signal-cli 0.14.8 on `127.0.0.1:8765` answered an allowed send with `Method requires valid account parameter`. The same send after a media read retired the caller with `signal delivery retired before send` and did not receive that account error.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** After the Signal monitor idle drain gives up, later chunks and a send that finished loading media do not call signal-cli. An allowed send still reaches it. Teardown still returns after the 30 second idle window and keeps the accepted claim.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.10.0, signal-cli 0.14.8, head b4f81417f4c5397ccaaf793d469e3a6e9c8e376e. Local JSON-RPC peer at 127.0.0.1, and signal-cli's HTTP daemon at 127.0.0.1:8765 with no registered account.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Start signal-cli 0.14.8 with `daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8765 --receive-mode manual`. Call production `sendMessageSignal` once with the handoff allowed, then again after a media read marks the caller retired. Separately, call production `deliverReplies` against a local JSON-RPC peer with a 4-character chunk limit.

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-141305-state-rq45 pnpm exec tsx ./proof-141305-signal-monitor-shutdown.ts
  [   12ms] HTTP fake signal-cli at http://127.0.0.1:63932
  [   87ms] SSE client connected
  [  105ms] SSE receive event written
  [  233ms] REPLY dispatchReplyFromConfig entered; holding unfinished reply
  [  235ms] QUEUE before abort claims=1 pending=0 ids=["number:+15550001111",1]
  [  236ms] STOP abort signaled
  [30239ms] ERR signal waitForIdle made no progress within 30000ms; continuing teardown with 1 task(s) still in flight and ingress stop pending
  [30239ms] DONE monitorSignalProvider returned after 30239ms (abort at 235ms)
  [30240ms] QUEUE after return claims=1 pending=0 ids=["number:+15550001111",1]
  [30240ms] LEFT signal waitForIdle made no progress within 30000ms; continuing teardown with 1 task(s) still in flight and ingress stop pending
  [30240ms] REPLY unfinished reply released
  PROOF_OK returned_after_abort_ms=30004 leftover=1
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The first chunk `abcd` was sent. `efgh` and `ij` were not. A media read that marked the caller retired produced zero RPC requests. signal-cli answered the allowed send with Method requires valid account parameter. The retired media send stopped with signal delivery retired before send.
- **What was not tested:** A registered phone account and a same-account restart while the old handler is still alive. Production getAttachment HTTP still uses a 10-second client deadline, so a live RPC hang cannot last the full 30-second window. signal-cli was not started again on the merge commit.

## Related

- Same hang class as Matrix monitor waitForIdle: [#133862](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133862)
- Matrix drain that made this family user-visible: [#134033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134033)
- Canonical tool-result ingress idle: [#142775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142775)
- Daemon exit fence: [#107409](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107409)
- Loop introduced in [#79092](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79092) ([`a0fb7fb04547`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a0fb7fb04547), 2026-05-10)

prs.title: fix(gateway): strip __controlUiReconnectResume from chat.send params before validation
prs.body:
<!--
Closes: #165433
-->

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `chat.send` requests from non-Operator-UI clients (e.g. webchat on a browser reconnect with a preserved `sessionId`) are rejected with `invalid chat.send params: at root: unexpected property '__controlUiReconnectResume'`. `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` only strips the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker when both `value === true` AND `isOperatorUiClient(clientInfo)` returns true; in every other case the `__`-prefixed marker leaks into the AJV-strict `chat.send` schema and the request is dropped before dispatch.

## User Impact
User impact: Webchat and other browser-based reconnect paths that emit the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker now have their messages admitted and dispatched normally on reconnect. No user-visible change for Control UI clients — their behavior is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made
`__controlUiReconnectResume` is an internal `__`-prefixed wire field added by the Control UI to signal "treat this as a reconnect resume, not a fresh run." Such fields should never reach the public `chat.send` schema. The patch decouples "strip the field before validation" from "record that a resume was requested" — the field is now stripped whenever it is present on the input record, and the `resumeRequested` flag is still gated by both the strict-value check and the Operator UI client check, preserving the downstream semantics. The strict-value check is unchanged on purpose so a non-true value (e.g. `false`, `1`, the wrong type) still does not mark a resume even from an Operator UI client.

## Evidence
- Six focused unit tests added in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-server-timing.test.ts` (new file) cover the regression and the surrounding cases: field absent, non-object input, true value with operator UI client, true value with non-operator UI client (the regression), true value with missing `clientInfo`, non-true values with operator UI client, and input-record immutability.
- A local reproduction on the bundled `dist/chat-server-timing-soo795Of.mjs` (the same logic, minified) confirmed the bug and the fix: pre-patch, a `webchat` clientInfo with `__controlUiReconnectResume: true` returned the marker in the result params; post-patch, the marker is stripped and `resumeRequested` is `false`.
- `diff -u` of the patched file vs. upstream main shows changes confined to the `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` function body; no other exports, signatures, or unrelated fields are touched.

prs.title: Request speakerphone output for Android Talk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, `RealtimeCommunicationAudio` sets `AudioManager.mode =
MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` to start a Talk session but never requests the
loudspeaker as the output device. Android's default routing for
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` is the earpiece unless a Bluetooth/wired headset is
attached, so continuous Talk plays back quietly through the earpiece
instead of the main loudspeaker - unexpected for a hands-free,
phone-away-from-the-ear conversation.

iOS already has an explicit speakerphone setting for Talk (see the Talk
settings page in the iOS app / dashboard). Android has no equivalent
request anywhere in the realtime audio path - this looks like a parity gap
rather than an intentional platform difference.

Any custom realtime voice provider plugin (via `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider`)
used through Android's Talk feature is affected equally to the built-in
OpenAI/xAI providers, since the audio routing logic is shared and
provider-agnostic.

## Evidence

Confirmed from the current Android source
(`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/RealtimeCommunicationAudio.kt`)
that `start()` sets `audioManager.mode = AudioManager.MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`
and requests audio focus, but never calls `setCommunicationDevice(...)` or
`isSpeakerphoneOn = true` anywhere - there is no output-device request in
this file or in the related `RealtimePlayout.kt` / `AndroidAudioInputSession.kt`
/ `TalkModeManager.kt` files (checked via direct source review, not
assumption). This matches standard documented Android behavior: apps using
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` get earpiece-by-default routing unless they
explicitly request another device.

This PR requests the speaker explicitly when a Talk communication-audio
session starts, and releases it cleanly when it ends - using
`AudioManager.setCommunicationDevice()` on Android 12+ (the documented
replacement for the deprecated speakerphone API), falling back to
`isSpeakerphoneOn` on older versions. Existing Bluetooth/wired routing in
`AndroidAudioInputSession` still takes priority when an external device is
actually connected, since device selection there is handled separately by
the OS once a route is active - this change only affects the otherwise-
silent default when no other device is connected.

Not yet verified on-device or via a local build - no Android SDK/Gradle
toolchain was available in the environment this patch was written in. The
change is a minimal, targeted addition using documented public
`AudioManager` APIs, confirmed against the current Android platform API
surface and against this repo's actual current source, but it has not been
compiled or run. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming it's been
tested - would appreciate a maintainer or anyone able to build the Android
app confirming it compiles and actually fixes the earpiece-default
behavior on a real device before merging.

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: improve(ui): tighten the Plugins hub at phone width
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width the Plugins hub spends its first screen on controls. The settings gear sits alone on a row, the catalog chips stop at the edge with nothing saying more exist, and the Skill workshop controls stack on three rows. In the workshop, tapping a skill shows nothing new, because the reader sits below the whole list, about 360 px past the bottom of a 390 x 844 screen. ## User Impact On a phone: - Plugins and Skills: the gear joins the tabs row and cards start 42 px higher. - Plugins: chips that run past the row fade toward the side with more to scroll to. The fade appears only when the row overflows, and it changes as the row scrolls. Templates shares these chips, so it gets the same fade. - Skill workshop: the agent picker and Learn from history share one row, the Learning label and mode control share the next. The first row starts 53 px higher. - Skill workshop: tapping a row or draft brings the reader into view. Desktop is unchanged, and no capability moved or went away. ## Why This Change Was Made Everything here is a layout change inside the existing phone breakpoints, except the reader. It renders correctly at 390, but off screen, so the fix is to scroll to it on tap. The list and reader stay as they are, and the scroll respects reduced motion. The scroll runs on the tap, before the reader's content loads, so the reader lands about 175 px down with its title visible. The tab track is removed at phone width for this hub's tabs and for the reader's Instructions, Files and History tabs. The search autofocus is left alone, since #190370 covers it, which is why the search field shows a focus ring in these images. ## Evidence Mock data at 390 x 844 with real taps. prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: improve(ui): make the sessions page a phone list
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves At phone width the Sessions page spends 284 px on controls before the first row, and the table sits in its own scroller with a 106 px column that cuts every session down to "agent… Sam…". The session's title can't be read. ## User Impact At 640 px and below: - Tabs and the agent picker share the first row. Session search, transcript search, refresh and the filter button share the second. Transcript search has its own icon, so it no longer reads as a second copy of the search field. - Rows read as a list: checkbox, title, key · updated, expand, `…`. An unread dot follows the title, so the title stays in line with the row's meta. Tapping the title or the line under it opens the chat. Rows scroll with the page. - The filter opens as a bottom sheet with a title and a close button. It holds the existing filters plus sort and direction. Delete all archived stays at the end of it for Archived. - The section label and the toolbar `+` are gone. The header's new session button covers it. - The big page title hides at 560 px and below, and the heading stays for assistive tech. From 561 to 640 px it stays on the page. #190409's floating header carries the title up to 600 px. Bulk select, pagination, per-row details and the row menu all stay. Wider layouts don't change. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Toolbar `+`:** the toolbar falls back to `resolveUiDefaultAgentId` when no agent is selected and the header to `assistantAgentId`. Run through the real selection owner, they only differ when the visible roster is empty and the hello default is stale or missing, and `/new` then resolves both to no agent. Native shells don't render the header button, so they keep the toolbar one. - **Sheet:** it reuses the sidebar's `SidebarSessionFilterPopover`, because a 262 px popover is cramped for this many fields. The title and close button use a new optional `header` prop, which the sidebar's sheets don't pass, so they don't change. - **Choices in the sheet:** Group by, Sort and Direction use the same picker as the sidebar's sheet, with options on a page of the sheet. Inside the sheet every control follows one rhythm: a 16px side inset, 12px between rows, a 13px label above a 40px field, and a 16px value, which is iOS's input floor. Global and Unknown read as fields, and the check carries their state: an unchecked one draws no check, and its slot stays so the label doesn't move. The close button sits at the same position as #190499's sheets. - **Select-all:** the phone list has no header row, so select-all moves into the bulk bar and appears once a row is selected. - **Copy:** sort labels reuse the Automations strings and the search placeholder reuses "Search sessions", so there are no new strings. - **Windowing:** long pages still window rows, now against the page scroller. ## Evidence Mock data layer at 390 px with real taps. Images show today's top bar until the header PR lands. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Filter sheet | 620 px, title kept | | --- | --- | | | | | Absolutely dark | CRT (square) | | --- | --- | | | | Real Safari 27.0.1 at 390 px in the mock's default dark theme, with the sheet opened by a real click, beside 320 px with long values in Chromium. - The close button, a backdrop tap and a touch swipe on the grabber each closed the sheet in Chromium. Choosing a sort from its page reordered the list. - With #190409 merged locally, up to 600 px shows the title once, in the header, and 601 to 640 px shows it on the page. - `session-kinds` e2e passes, with the phone toolbar tested at 390 and 620 px. Sessions unit tests pass, 155 of 155, including two new phone tests. `tsgo:ui`, oxfmt, stylelint and oxlint pass. - The browser test for windowing, focus and selection passes at 1280 and 390 px, updated for the list. `retains native label selection and undo` fails here and on clean main, because it sends Ctrl+Z on macOS. - `ui:check-performance:base` fails on the CSS budget. Base is already over the cap, and this adds about 9.3 KB raw (about 1.3 KB gzip).

prs.body: Based on #190535 so this diff shows only the modal change and reuses that PR's helper. In real Safari, a real click on Submit and on Deny moved focus to the terminal heading with no ring. ## Evidence Real clicks and keys against the mock's data, with no DOM changes. Safari 27.0.1 images use real OS clicks; no keys were sent to Safari. ## What Problem This Solves

Empty agent tool catalogs register an extra cleanup callback, breaking the one-shot supervisor cleanup contract after #190627.

## User Impact

One-shot runs with no constructed tools retain their single process cleanup callback. Nonempty tool catalogs keep their existing schema publication behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return the empty finalized catalog after preparation-stage callbacks and before registering schema settlement, because there is no schema to publish. This adds three production lines and changes no tests; the existing supervisor tests cover the regression without relaxing their assertions.

## Evidence

- Main full run [41346811341](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41346811341/job/124968544113) fails both one-shot supervisor tests: expected one cleanup callback, received two. The regression comes from b70c33caa866 (#190627).

prs.title: fix: retain unfinished work independently of progress display
prs.body:
## Summary

Separates retained unfinished work from how progress is presented. Whether planned work is kept and followed through no longer depends on what the progress display shows.

- Retained unfinished work stays with the existing SQL store and private actor owners. It is gated by native acceptance facts and compare-and-swap lifecycle fences.
- Explicit plan/card intent records the work. Ordinary later turns follow it through, while respecting pause, cancel, wait and unknown coverage.
- The hidden host reconcile writer is guarded.
- Adds no new registry, scheduler or authority bypass.

Source `c0846a586cda6179272a9bf855b7e4192fbc9003` (tree `c69d0581fc987aca3908048d79ed1690a741beb1`) merges the landed base `e2427099948c059859fdf54daae4133c72b2a13c` (#187152). Relative to that base, 105 files change (+7582/−705).

## Verification

- Source identity: the source paragraph above describes the initial publication. The current reviewed source is `5d92d2783c8852a68772accd1a0139b84d3cbe62` (tree `5d14f951b78b999db27eb01690b43a878e086205`). The published head `65d72a0d04ca2452a5f181ac05d6baa156ef1873` is an empty publication commit with that single parent and the same tree. The PR now changes 121 files (+8067/−771).
- Reviews (static, not test runs): an independent full review (Astra) of the repair found no issues in any touched file or its full test file. A partial review (Opus) of full-test coverage raised 2 warnings and 2 nits, all validated by the lead: the canonical inventory doc and a meaningful reload decode budget were fixed, a rename suggestion was dismissed as an existing pattern, and the closed witness enum stays fail-closed for the stored format. A short review of the final 2-file delta passed with notes.
- Focused tests on the current source: 38 selected cases passed with no timeout or guard changes.
  - 2 catalog denial cases.
  - 2 ordinary/conditional controls using real async reads, the private actor and native facts. The ordinary path ran 1 semantic check; the conditional path ran none, with no aborts and actionable unknown coverage.
  - 8 SQL/private-memory authority cases. An offline embedded agent run drives the native `progress_card` producer through the registered reconcile path and the awaited commit guard into the real SQL and private-actor stores. Both allowed cases committed exactly once (revision 1→2). Six foreign, replaced or revoked cases, rejected after prepare, wrote no entries and made no commits; stored state and foreign hashes were unchanged. Replacement baselines are taken after a real reset, and admission closes after the awaited prepare. Only offline provider I/O is scripted; handlers, authority, guards and native facts are not mocked. The fixture is private.
  - 26 maintained cases: custody 10, requester yield 6, registry 4, spawn authority 2, spawn resources 1, swarm 3.

  173 other cases were intentionally not selected; none failed. The swarm cases mock spawn and collector seams and are not a live child or provider end-to-end run. The conditional control does not exercise real retained-send delivery. An earlier interrupted custody run and an earlier catalog host error remain unexplained; the current passes do not establish their cause.
- Schema and migration: 16 focused cases cover preservation, migration, partial values, defaults, rollback and tampering, and 35 wrapper-closure checks found 0 cycles. Canonical inventory generation and check passed (708 files, 2499 calls, T1 count 168 unchanged), and 19 ratchet behavior cases passed with no scoped T1 growth. These do not replace the full CI ratchet.
- Memory: all 10 cases passed. The work budget now counts up to 3 actual decodes, alongside exact-byte, replay, media and forged-fact cases. This is not a CPU regression: byte preservation now counts decodes the old string filter missed.
- Doctor: the original v17 repair and its repeat run passed in 37.9 s and 50.4 s within the unchanged 60 s limit, with all original assertions, using a qualified source build fixture. This is not a shipped-package or live deployment proof.
- Local static checks: formatter, lint, syntax and diff checks passed. The full local type check's declaration guard refused before producing diagnostics, so it is not a pass.
- CI (including full types, ratchet and security) and a fresh hosted review on the published head are separate required gates; see the current checks. No CI, review or merge pass is claimed here. No live Gateway, provider or deployment was updated or tested.

## Limits

- Makes no universal privacy claim.
- Local focused QA is complete. Full CI and a fresh hosted review on the current head remain separate gates.

prs.title: improve(ui): align the Plugins search fields with Skills
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Plugins and Skills are tabs of the same hub with the same search slot, but Plugins used a different input class. Switching tabs changed the type size, corner and focus treatment of the search field. The installed plugins search in Settings had the same mismatch next to the settings fields around it. ## User Impact The search field stays the same when moving between Plugins and Skills, and the Settings search matches other settings fields. Heights don't change: 44px for the catalog search, 32px for the Settings search on desktop. No capability or copy changes. ## Why This Change Was Made Both fields move to the shared `settings-input`. | Field | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Plugins catalog search | 14px type, 10px radius, 3px focus ring | 12px type, 12.5px radius, focus border | | Settings installed plugins search | 14px type, 10px radius | 12px type, 12.5px radius | The Plugins search now measures the same as the Skills search: 12px type, 12.5px radius, 44px height. Radius never shrinks. CRT's field radius is 2.5px and its control radius is 3px, so these searches use the larger of the two. Plugins and the Settings search stay at 3px in CRT, and Skills, which shares the catalog search rule, grows from 2.5px to 3px. Touch devices keep the 16px type floor, so nothing changes in type size there. It prevents iOS focus zoom. The Labs Templates search shares the catalog search wrapper but stays on `oc-input`. The radius rule targets `settings-input` only, so that field doesn't change. It sits behind a Labs flag the mock doesn't reach, so it isn't pictured. ## Evidence Mock data. Plugins, Absolutely light, Before and After: Skills, the same field, Absolutely light: Settings plugins, Absolutely dark, Before and After: CRT and 390px on a touch profile, After: Real Safari 27.0.1, After, in the mock's default theme: Local checks pass: oxfmt, stylelint, `tsgo:ui`, Plugins unit and browser tests, `form-controls.browser.test.ts` and `templates-catalog.e2e.test.ts`.

prs.title: improve(ui): keep the focus ring to keyboard input
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Opening a menu with a mouse or finger could paint the thick accent focus ring on its first item, and the ring could move to the trigger afterwards. It looked random: the same menu showed it on the first open after a page load and not on the second. Menus focus their first item from script, and their triggers cancel `pointerdown`, so the click itself moves no focus. Both Chromium and Safari then decide `:focus-visible` for script focus from how focus last moved. A page load with no earlier focus gives a ring; an earlier click that focused something, such as `main`, gives none. The result depended on what had been clicked before, not on the menu. Measured on current main, real Safari and Chromium agree: first open after load shows the ring on Automations and Usage, and a second open after clicking elsewhere does not. `/ask` has the same cause: its question panel takes focus from script on load, so the whole panel showed the ring until the first tap. ## User Impact Mouse and touch no longer show the ring when a menu opens, when focus returns to its trigger, or when `/ask` loads or collapses its question. Keyboard users keep it: opening with Enter, Space or arrows shows the ring on the first item, and Escape returns to a ringed trigger. Any key press in a mouse-opened menu shows the ring on the current row, including Home on the first row and a one-item menu; modifier keys alone don't. After a full page load `/ask` has no input to go on, so a keyboard user sees its ring on the first key press; arriving by keyboard from inside the app shows it at once. ## Why This Change Was Made Focus still moves to the same elements, so keyboard behavior doesn't change. A key press that leaves focus where a pointer put it refocuses that element once to paint the ring, after the page's own key handlers have run, and a screen reader can announce it again at that moment. A small helper records whether the last input was a key or a pointer and passes `focusVisible` to `focus()`, which Chromium and Safari both honored here. Because the browser's own state changes, every existing `:focus-visible` rule follows it and no CSS or per-page override is needed. Text fields keep their native indication. It is applied in the shared `Menu` and overlay return focus, so every page gets it. Pages don't need `pointerFocus="trigger"` to avoid the ring. Outlines aren't removed anywhere. Left alone: - Modals: Cancel in a confirm dialog still shows the ring after a mouse open in Safari, and so does the trigger after `dialog.close()` restores focus. Both are native dialog focus, not script, so this helper doesn't reach them. Changing that means changing how every modal opens, so it needs its own decision. - Search autofocus ring: handled in #190370. - Rings that follow Tab or arrow keys: these are the keyboard behavior being kept. ## Evidence Real clicks and keys against the mock's data, with no DOM changes. Safari 27.0.1 images use real OS clicks; no keys were sent to Safari. Before, Safari, Absolutely dark, first click: After, Safari, Absolutely dark, first click: After, Safari, CRT, first click: After, Chromium, Absolutely light, first click: After, Chromium, Absolutely dark, 390px, tap on Usage Export: Keyboard, Chromium, Absolutely light, Tab then Enter keeps the ring: `/ask` before, Safari, Absolutely light, on load: `/ask` after, Safari, Absolutely light, on load: Local checks: oxfmt, oxlint, `tsgo:ui`, menu, overlay, modal, question and sidebar menu tests, and `ui:check-performance:base`.
