prs.title: fix(message): retain local final replies in conversation history
prs.body:
Related: #186688
Related native-completion work: #111020, #174490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing conversation-history answers when a local message-tool send delivers the current turn's reply, including Discord's prepared core-delivery path.

## User Impact

Confirmed source answers are persisted and made available to context-engine consumers in the accepted-turn range, and prevent unchanged answered requests from being re-injected as recent channel history. Downstream capture still depends on each consumer selecting the answer from that range. Explicit final replies and the normal omitted-final default retain terminal evidence; progress and the existing run-level default-false override remain nonterminal. Failed/partial delivery, dry runs and other destinations do not mark the source answered.

This repairs the persistence portion of #186688, not native Codex interruption. Native completion remains separate; no configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [installation report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187795#issuecomment-6512626002) correctly identified that the initial patch covered only plugin-action fallback, while ordinary Discord sends use prepared core delivery. Move local source persistence to their common settled-send boundary, reuse the existing mirror owner, and persist the actual delivered payload after preparation/hooks. Gateway-owned source persistence stays with its existing RPC owner.

Use the harness's existing finality resolver for transcript evidence and forward its existing run-level default override. This changes no native completion policy and introduces no new state owner.

## Evidence

- Red before repair: the real shipped Discord preparation/outbound adapters, with only network I/O substituted, delivered both explicit-final and omitted-final messages but persisted zero assistant answer rows. Both regressions pass after this repair.
- Composed proof exercises the real message tool, canonical SQLite transcript, accepted-turn outbox and commitTurn consumer, then recent-history reconciliation. It verifies delivered content, source-turn/tool-call identity, terminal versus progress behavior, run-level default override, and failed-send handling. Fallback-plugin cases retain receipt-replay and failure/partial/suppressed/dry-run/other-recipient controls.
- Final candidate: 13 focused files / 290 tests passed (80.57 seconds runner wall time), including source matching, destination history, outbound contracts, shared finality and prompt-prefix stability. This is the selected repair scope, not a full repository test run.
- Agents-tools test typegraph, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, test-line budget and diff checks passed.
- Simplification replaces fallback-only persistence with one shared local settlement call. Gateway RPC retains its separate transport boundary and the same mirror owner. Against the base, production changes are +84/-27 lines; the 442-line integration allocation covers producer-to-capture composition and distinct controls.
- Bound Auto Review completed on base `53071cea572c54568f76c0f487403528bf46508c` and candidate tree `986cf3c944fd5eaa594e573a8f979a00c441745b`: `scoped-clean`, no findings at its P0-only threshold. This is not a review clearance for lower-priority defects. Tests were independently executed by the implementer, not rerun by the reviewer. The reporter-provided live validation below is separate from this review.
- Implementer-run live Discord readiness failed at QA lease acquisition; the implementer did not verify live Discord transport, native Codex completion, or a third-party Universal Capture installation. The local capture assertion uses the real commitTurn boundary with a synthetic consumer.
- Reporter-provided live validation: [lastguru-net’s October 30 follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187795#issuecomment-6530379567) tested the ten-file patch from `7b06dd03108b1e53871c9875e63c25b5822e0579` on main `5f6f15fed0d6ba618cf781c9686a8b93f499564b` with a real Discord/native Codex-backed agent. Explicit `final:true` sends (turns 72–74) and an omitted-final send (turn 75) each delivered one visible answer, persisted exactly one canonical final delivery mirror, and stopped the answered requests from recurring in subsequent history. Ordinary-final turns 70, 71 and 76 served as controls. These are the reporter’s observed results, not an implementer-run live test.
- Separate consumer limitation: the same report reproduces Universal Capture 0.7.1 with `commentary:false` omitting the already-persisted answer because its selector reads only the last row. The valid order is `user → assistant toolCall → assistant final delivery mirror → toolResult`; the accepted-turn contract does not require the assistant answer to be the last row. This consumer-side selection bug is outside this PR and is not evidence of continued canonical answer loss. Native Codex interruption also remains unchanged and separate.
- Hosted [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41088039623/job/124180953526) passed on `7b06dd03108b1e53871c9875e63c25b5822e0579`; its prerequisite results contain only success or unselected/skipped jobs, with no failures or timeouts.

Co-authored with Mert Başar (@MertBasar0).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3f4efc7e-8bac-4302-a572-1d15c0906de2)

## Worked on by

- @MertBasar0

prs.title: fix(infer): sanitize terminal controls in human output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared inference human-output formatters can emit terminal controls from legal input or provider/result values. For example, `infer embedding create` sends text containing screen-clear/cursor/title sequences unchanged to its configured provider, then prints those sequences as raw terminal bytes.

## User Impact

Shared human envelopes and provider summaries use the existing terminal text policy. Metadata, errors, paths and scalar displays stay on owned lines; output text retains real newlines and Unicode, and tabs display as literal `\t`. Structured `--json` output and provider input preserve their original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply existing `terminalText`/`sanitizeTerminalText` at the complete shared display owner. Reuse the existing transcripts per-LF pattern for multiline text. Human serialized values also need this boundary because JSON.stringify leaves C1/bidi controls. Seven inference families share the owner; no per-field renderer, new escape algorithm, public option or caller policy is added.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Shared human envelope and provider-summary displays remove terminal controls while preserving owned line layout and ordinary Unicode; Multiline output keeps LF, tabs display literally, and provider input plus structured JSON retain their original values.
- Entry: node openclaw.mjs infer embedding create --agent main --model openai/text-embedding-3-small --text <fixture-value> [--json]; disputed owner ran unmocked: src/cli/capability-cli/output.ts formatEnvelopeForText and providerSummaryText human projections; emitJsonOrText runs the existing shared owner unmocked from the shipped OpenAI-compatible embedding route.
- Same command on base `5598c3d` and head `3ce6ab4`: `python3 infer-terminal-output-proof.py --checkout "$CHECKOUT" --output "$OUTPUT" --expect "$PHASE"`
  - Before (base): RED legal embedding input reaches actual nativeHTTP unchanged and text stdout contains3 raw ESC bytes; ordinary LF/tab/Unicode and exact JSON controls work. All3 commands exit0 with1POST each.
  - After (head): GREEN the same plain text has0 raw ESC, retains actual LF/Unicode and renders tab as literal backslash+t; normal multiline control works and JSON stdout is byte-identical betweenrefs with original control values/vectors preserved. All3 commands exit0 with1POST each.
- Readback (subprocess,http,config-file,network-recorder): Actual CLI raw stdout/stderr/status and stdoutHex, native POST request model/input/count, config before/after hashes and peer-thread-port cleanup receipts.
- Proof harness: Unchanged final collector48ed92223c586aeaf52d6bf4bf64c2b3c8851219a99691def6486dafa47becb2 on bothrefs,3samecases/inputs/config/protocol/deadlines. Public portable source has its ownffa14dd3d5e01e9230def4969d9fa89596bd44d7d7017bbe3991bdcb675b6e97 hash and exactly2 documented local path substitutions; it is not claimed executed byte-identical source.
- Control: RawESC count3→0 on the same control input; normal rawESC0 and structuredJSON rawESC0 controls pass on bothrefs. Six actual POSTs carry exact original model/input and invented authorization placeholder,6commands exit0; all config hashes unchanged and both peerThreadStopped/peerPortClosed true. The source objects remain unchanged in independent owner tests.
- Other callers checked: Complete shared envelope/provider-summary owner serves7inference families through7unchanged production importer projection sites. Unit/source coverage includes error/header/path/text/embedding-scalar and human serialized C1/bidi states; live native proof is embedding only. Separate providers-command default JSON formatter and other runtime exception writers are outside this claim.

This covers shared human projections only; default JSON fallback and runtime exception writers remain outside scope. Owned local fixture directories are retained after actual peer cleanup.


Product head `3ce6ab49e5c4a75401b57e592c8a2692ce57da5c`, BASE `5598c3d76bcb28cacaf864724d52ccb4c8ccdd26`. Exact complete source snapshot `9fa8ac0f8f2ca7bf8e00d41c18aceeb21e8c542aaf23a5ce30aa5a8ccb00686f` and3whole-file hashes are embedded below. Normal clean exact-HEAD cliStartup build passes253.434s; its build-info/stamp match the actual executed head. Runtime: Linux x64, Node26.12.1, OpenClaw2026.10.8.

The normal public command invokes the shipped OpenAI-compatible embedding provider with isolated existing config/env/state and a native loopback `/v1/embeddings` peer. `plugins.enabled:false` selects that supported generic route, as in the existing registered integration fixture. It is product code, not a custom plugin or direct helper. The peer receives actual JSON and returns fixed indexed vectors. All credentials are invented; no external provider account is used.

Same frozen48ed collector command on both refs:

```sh
python3 infer-terminal-output-proof.py --checkout "$CHECKOUT" --output "$OUTPUT" --expect "$PHASE"
```

| Native scenario | BASE rawESC | HEAD rawESC | BASE / HEAD process wall | Native POSTs BASE / HEAD |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| normal-multiline | 0 | 0 | 7.241s / 8.137s | 1 / 1 |
| terminal-controls | 3 | 0 | 6.484s / 7.275s | 1 / 1 |
| json-control | 0 | 0 | 6.488s / 7.194s | 1 / 1 |

The normal text fixture has real LF, tab and emoji. HEAD keeps LF/emoji and displays tab as a literal backslash+t, following existing terminal policy. The control fixture contains CSI screen-clear/cursor-home and OSC title/BEL: BASE prints3rawESC bytes; HEAD prints `beforeafter`, real LF, then `next\tcolumn` and the emoji. The same JSON control retains the original ESC/BEL/LF/tab text and full3-value vector/dimensions; its complete serialized stdout bytes match betweenrefs. Every native POST carries the exact original input/model, with1request per command and no fallback provider. The formatter does not alter provider data.

All6 commands exit0. Config before/after hashes match for each case; native peer/thread/port close normally. Owned isolated state/raw directories remain retained locally for review. Actual stderr is preserved below with only its local Config path presented as `$FIXTURE_CONFIG`: the secret resolver reports that Gateway secret resolution lacks credentials, then resolves the synthetic env reference locally. That diagnostic is part of the observation, not hidden or counted as a product failure.

The scope is `formatEnvelopeForText` and `providerSummaryText`, shared across model/image/audio/TTS/video/web/embedding. Source and focused owner tests cover metadata/error/path/multiline text, empty/short/bounded-long embeddings, scalar display values, C1/bidi in human JSON, empty/undefined summary entries, nonmutation and JSON bypass. The separate providers-command default JSON formatter and other runtime exception writers are outside this scope. Native runtime proof covers embedding only; no all-family live claim is made.

Canonical new owner10/10 passes9.540s (Vitest3.71s). The original owner failed6intended cases with4controls passing in12.249s. Four unchanged registeredCLI text/JSON controls pass128.175s;99cases were explicitly unselected. Its cold compiler preparation takes108.341s for18,046inputs/22,874outputs, while the selected cases take1.909s/76ms/15ms/76ms. Targeted types117.174s; typedlint380.768s includes artifact ownership/declaration generation and an unsuccessful automatic pinnedBun staging attempt followed by the existing oxlint fallback. Format0.762s, linecap1.478s/max17.176s/testlines5.098s/mock39.419s/diff0.191s all pass. No deadline/assertion relaxation or fixed-code retry. Production+27/−11LF, test125LF with exact125LF allocation; shared scalar unchanged. Independent source review passed; final publication review is separate.

Harness history is retained honestly: the initial attempt assumed provider=openai and failed its assertion because the supported config selects openai-compatible. This was a HARNESS_ONLY failure, not product RED. After correcting the provider assumption, a BASE preflight succeeded. The final collector then added explicit base/head display expectations before freezing48ed; that identical final source ran once on each exact ref. Older runs are not relabeled as the final paired execution. Their hashes are below.

Limits: live external accounts/providers, terminal-emulator appearance/screenshots, native macOS/Windows, all7family runtime runs, fullsuite/generalCLI suite, hostedCI and upgrade are not executed. Evidence establishes terminal bytes/data semantics at these shared projections, not global safety of every inference stdout writer or a visual styling claim.

<details><summary>Actual paired native HTTP and CLI readback</summary>

Every actual stdout byte is included as UTF8 with JSON escapes and as original hex, plus its SHA256. Native input/body/count, config hashes and cleanup are retained. `Only the owned Config path inside the local-secret-fallback stderr diagnostic is presented as $FIXTURE_CONFIG; all other stderr text is retained. Raw original stderr SHA256 remains available beside the projected UTF8 SHA256. No stdout/input/HTTP-body/config-hash/cleanup field is redacted.` The invented bearer placeholder in the portable-source JSON uses one Unicode escape solely to avoid mistaking it for a real key; decoding restores it exactly.

prs.title: docs(cron): document subagent model steps in isolated-job precedence
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #190607

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where operators following the published isolated-job model precedence would expect their agent's own `model` to run a job, while a configured `agents.defaults.subagents.model` (or per-agent `subagents.model`) actually wins. The run log then shows a model the precedence list never mentions.
- Also fixes the follow-up ClawSweeper finding on the first revision: the fallback sentence promised "the selected `subagents.model` entry's fallbacks", which is wrong for a supported fallback-only per-agent override. Fallbacks resolve separately from the primary, and the agent's own `subagents.model` fallback override wins first even when the primary came from `agents.defaults.subagents.model`.
- **Related:** #190607 (reporter identified the docs gap; #58823 intentionally aligned cron with subagent spawning, so only the docs are behind). ClawSweeper labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` now expands the "Agent/default model selection" step into the real shared-selector order — per-agent `subagents.model`, global `agents.defaults.subagents.model`, the agent's own `model`, then default model selection — and documents the subagent fallback rule the way the fallback owner actually resolves it:
  - a fallback override on the agent's own `subagents.model` wins first, independently of which entry supplied the primary (so a fallback-only `agents.entries.*.subagents.model: { "fallbacks": [] }` keeps the global primary but disables inherited fallbacks for that agent);
  - otherwise the fallbacks configured on the selected entry apply;
  - explicit per-job `--fallbacks` always win, a per-job `model` keeps its own candidate chain, and steps 6/7 use normal fallback resolution instead of the subagent policy.
  The `--clear-model` flag description drops the same abbreviation.
- **Out of scope:** No runtime behavior change (the selection order and the fallback override rule are the intended contract from #58823 and are already pinned by shipped tests). The FAQ page (`docs/help/faq/skills-and-automation.md`) has a similar abbreviated list; left untouched to keep this correction bounded.
- **Highest-risk area:** Docs-only. The previously added `src/cron/isolated-agent/model-precedence.docs.test.ts` was dropped in this revision per review: its fallback-policy group repeated existing owner coverage and its prose guards pinned wording without checking the policy (they passed while the fallback sentence was wrong). The contract stays pinned by its owners — `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` (`resolves subagent model fallbacks from the selected subagent model source`, including the fallback-only override) and `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.sandbox-admission.test.ts` (`admits a sandboxed session when per-agent subagents.model overrides the global CLI default`). This makes the PR docs-only.

## User Impact

- Operators setting `agents.defaults.subagents.model` can now predict which model an isolated job runs, and operators setting a per-agent `subagents.model` fallback override (including a fallback-only entry) can predict which fallback chain applies, instead of discovering either only in run logs.
- **Success criteria:** The precedence list matches `resolveCronModelSelection` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`) and the shared selector `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` (`src/agents/agent-scope.ts`); the fallback paragraph matches `resolveSubagentModelFallbacksOverride` (`src/agents/agent-scope.ts`) as consumed by `resolveCronFallbacksOverride` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-fallback-policy.ts`), including the fallback-only per-agent override.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`: the 7-step precedence list and the new fallback bullets (per-agent override first, else the selected entry's fallbacks).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-190607` at head, Node v26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0. Docs-only change: no runtime surface to launch, so proof is (a) the shipped selector/fallback functions called directly against the exact configuration from the review finding and (b) the owner test suites that pin the documented contract.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # (a) real behavior of the shipped owners, no mocks (script kept outside the repo)
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence-dir>/subagent-fallback-proof.mts
  # (b) owner suites that pin the documented contract
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts \
    src/cron/isolated-agent/run-fallback-policy.test.ts \
    src/cron/isolated-agent/run.sandbox-admission.test.ts
  # (c) type check for the affected core test shard (the previous revision failed here)
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --builders 1
  # (d) docs gates
  pnpm format:docs:check && node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md && node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs && git diff --check
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # (a) shipped selector + fallback owner, called directly (JSON lines, one per configuration)
  {"case":"A: per-agent subagents.model primary beats global default","selectedPrimary":"openai/agent-sub","selectionSource":"subagent","fallbacksOverride":["openai/sub-backup"]}
  {"case":"B: global default beats the agent's own model","selectedPrimary":"openai/global-sub","selectionSource":"default-subagent","fallbacksOverride":["openai/global-backup"]}
  {"case":"C: agent's own model when no subagents model is configured","selectedPrimary":"openai/agent-primary","selectionSource":"agent","fallbacksOverride":[]}
  {"case":"D: review P2 case - fallback-only per-agent entry keeps the global primary but clears fallbacks","selectedPrimary":"openai/global-sub","selectionSource":"default-subagent","fallbacksOverride":[]}
  {"case":"E: per-agent subagents.model written as a plain string clears inherited fallbacks","selectedPrimary":"openai/agent-sub","selectionSource":"subagent","fallbacksOverride":[]}
  {"case":"F: no per-agent override -> the selected global entry's fallbacks apply","selectedPrimary":"openai/global-sub","selectionSource":"default-subagent","fallbacksOverride":["openai/global-backup"]}

  # (b) owner suites (3 files, 69 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)   # cron shard: run-fallback-policy.test.ts + run.sandbox-admission.test.ts
       Tests  26 passed (26)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   # agents-core: agent-scope.test.ts
       Tests  43 passed (43)
  [test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 152.76s

  # (c) core test-types shard that failed on the previous head
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --builders 1
  exit code 0 - no type errors (previous head: TS18048 in the now-removed test file)

  # (d) docs gates
  Docs formatting clean (1412 files).
  Docs MDX check passed (1424 files, 27451ms).
  checked_internal_links=16220
  broken_links=0
  git diff --check: clean
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Case D is the configuration from the review finding (`agents.entries.main.subagents.model: { "fallbacks": [] }` + `agents.defaults.subagents.model: { primary: "openai/global-sub", fallbacks: ["openai/global-backup"] }`): the shipped code selects the **global** primary (`selectionSource: "default-subagent"`) while the fallback override is the agent's **empty** list — i.e. the per-agent override wins independently of the selected primary. That is exactly what the corrected paragraph now states; the previous sentence ("fallbacks configured on the selected `subagents.model` entry apply") would have promised `["openai/global-backup"]` here. Cases A/B/C/F confirm the documented 7-step order, and case E confirms that a plain-string per-agent `subagents.model` also clears inherited fallbacks. The documented list now has 7 steps ending in default model selection, matching the code path the reporter traced (`resolveCronModelSelection` → `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult`).
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** Before this revision: `check-test-types-core-5` failed on the added test file (`src/cron/isolated-agent/model-precedence.docs.test.ts(243,72): error TS18048: 'step' is possibly 'undefined'`), and the docs paragraph misdescribed the fallback source. After: the test file is gone (review asked to drop those groups), the shard type-checks clean, and the paragraph matches the real override order shown above.
- **What was not tested:** Full CI lanes (`pnpm check`, whole cron shard test run) not run locally — CI lanes pending on this PR. No rendered docs-site screenshot: this revision changes only files under `docs/`, so the all-files-under-docs exemption applies; the rendered page content is the markdown quoted above and is verified by the docs MDX/format/link gates.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (shipped selector/fallback functions called directly against the reviewed configuration + owner test suites; deterministic terminal output above).
- **Proof limitations:** No browser render of docs.openclaw.ai (the site is built from the `openclaw/docs` checkout, not from this repo); the docs gates above validate the shipped markdown instead.
- **Review state:** ClawSweeper P2 finding addressed; low-value test groups removed as requested; awaiting re-review.

prs.title: fix: preserve output-limit termination after summary recovery
prs.body:
Related: #178300

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a successful tool-free summary changes an output-limited task's recorded stop reason from `length` to `stop`, even when some work remains unfinished.

## User Impact

Callers retain the original cutoff in run metadata, completion metadata, and lifecycle events while still receiving the recovered summary and its existing warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the settled attempt's canonical terminal outcome when it hit the output limit. The summary supplies the final text without replacing that outcome or adding a second truncation notice. This addresses the terminal-outcome portion of #178300.

## Evidence

- Official CLI on Linux / Node 24.22.1 with an isolated local Anthropic SSE fixture: one file is written, the next response ends with `max_tokens`, and a tool-free summary claims both files are complete. Before the fix, run and completion metadata report `stop`; after the fix, both retain `length`. The second file remains absent and the existing cutoff warning appears once.
- Five focused test files: 114 tests pass. The cutoff and normal-stop regression also checks terminal lifecycle metadata.
- Normal-stop CLI control passes with `stop` metadata and no cutoff warning. Core and agent-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep an outside tap from activating the page beneath
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves On a phone, tapping outside an open popover or menu closes it and also activates whatever is under the finger. In Live activity, tapping a session row to dismiss the filter opens that session. #190376 added a guard for this to Dashboards alone, and every other surface still has the problem. ## User Impact On touch, a tap outside an overlay closes it without activating the control under the finger. A tap on a text field also focuses that field, since only the click is held back. The next tap acts on the page as usual. Scrolling still leaves an overlay open, as it does today. Mouse behavior doesn't change. ## Why This Change Was Made The overlay registry already decides when an outside press dismisses an overlay, so one rule there covers every popover and menu. It absorbs one click, only when a touch release has just dismissed something. The next press clears it, even when the tap produced no click and took the registry's last root with it, so a long press can't swallow a later click. Keyboard activation still goes through. With this landed, #190376 can drop its local `pointerdown` and `click` guard in `dashboard-filter-popover.tsx`. Sheets aren't involved: #190499 and the sidebar's sheets take the tap on their own backdrop. ## Evidence Mock data at 390x844, real touch input, same tap on the second session row. This changes behavior and no pixels, so there are no theme images. | Filter open | Before: the tap opened the session | After: the tap only closed the filter | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | - After: the second tap on the same row opens the session. Tapping "Learn more" with the Automations filter open closes the filter and opens nothing. - At 1440px with a mouse, the same click still closes the filter and opens the session. - `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:ui` and `ui:check-performance:base` pass. Browser tests for popovers, overlay lifecycle, menus, session menu, pickers and multi-select pass, along with the mobile sheet e2e tests. - WebKit touch: Playwright's WebKit on macOS with touch emulation reports `pointerType: touch`. The first tap on a Live activity row closed the filter and stayed on the page, the second opened the session, and a tap on the search field closed the filter and focused the field. Real Safari isn't captured: OS clicks reach it as a mouse. iOS Safari isn't run.

prs.title: fix: GitHub identity setup failures report no cause in Gateway logs
prs.body:
Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub identity setup recordings contain no cause in the Gateway log when `tools.github.configure` fails; the operator sees only a generic `GitHub identity setup failed` error.

## User Impact

Operators can read the actual failure cause from the Gateway log (for example a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use setup handoff, or a store error) instead of reproducing the failure and guessing across the several fallible setup steps covered by the single try block.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler's catch block discarded the caught error completely, so nothing about the failure reached anywhere. This change binds the error and logs it using the established gateway logging convention (`logWarn` + `formatErrorMessage`, matching the sibling `mcp-app.ts` catch paths) before responding with the unchanged generic error. There is no behavior change: same error code, same message, same response shape.

## Evidence

- Before (observed in production logs): 10 failed `tools.github.configure` calls on 2026.10.5 (Gateway journal, 2026-10-22 01:44–02:00 UTC), each logging only the `res ✗ … errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed"` response envelope, with no cause-bearing log line anywhere near them. Method and context: #181165 (full journal slices inspected, not just grep hits).
- Regression test (per the review's next-step ask), run locally on this change: `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts` — *"logs the unavailable-handoff cause while retaining the generic response"* — handoff consumption throws; the test asserts `logWarn` carries the thrown cause (`tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: setup handoff expired before use`) while `respond` keeps the byte-identical generic UNAVAILABLE error shape. **Red on the base** (fix stashed): `1 failed | 12 passed` — only the new test fails, at the `logWarn` expectation. **Green with the fix**: 13/13 (`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, vitest 5.0.3 on Node v24.22.1).
- Runtime note, stated plainly: local runs used Node v24.22.1 (sha256-verified from `nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt`); this host does not have the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork, so vitest fell back to Node (printed by the harness). PR CI runs the standard lane.
- Scope check: 2 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) — production: `catch (error)` binding, one `logWarn` line, two convention imports (+4/−1 vs base); the rest is the regression test and its spy setup.
- Known upstream-main statuses observed while running the local check graph (all empty-diff, none from this change): the max-lines suppression ratchet reports three `ui/` files (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`) that are identical to base `d5ce64b7` — inherited `main` state, zero hunks from this patch.

prs.title: fix(gateway): tools.github.configure failures now log the real cause before the generic response
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where operators running the GitHub identity setup flow (Control UI / CLI save path) would only ever see the generic "GitHub identity setup failed" response: every failure inside `tools.github.configure` — a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use handoff, an installer failure — collapsed into the same opaque message with zero cause-bearing log lines on the Gateway host, forcing reproduce-and-guess triage (10/10 failures in the reporter's session left no cause in the journal).
- **Related:** #135028 (its fix surfaced `GitHubCliUnavailableError` on the sibling `tools.github.authorize.start` path but left the `configure` catch unchanged); #140576 (different defect on the same UI surface). Fix signal labels: `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** bind the caught error and log it server-side so Gateway diagnostics record the real cause; the client-facing response stays byte-identical.
- **Logging contract:** the cause is formatted with the shared normalization formatter from `@openclaw/normalization-core/error-coercion` (no redaction callback — the same raw formatter the sibling `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-delete-drain.ts` catch path uses) instead of the pre-redacting wrapper in `src/infra/errors.ts`. The owner-only file record keeps the raw cause text (deployment-specific `logging.redactPatterns` can no longer erase diagnostics before storage), and masking is retained at the subsystem logger's console/egress boundary.
- **Out of scope:** mapping `GitHubIdentityError` to more specific client error codes (explicitly named a possible follow-up in the issue); no change to the credential lifecycle or response shape.
- **Highest-risk area:** credential material in the new log line. **How is that risk mitigated?** The handler hands the raw cause to the logging owner, which stores it in the owner-only file record and redacts its console/egress presentation; the regression test rejects with a token-bearing error and asserts the raw text reaches the logging owner intact (a pre-redacting formatter collapses `token=ghp_…` text, so the test discriminates the two implementations).

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** any `tools.github.configure` failure now produces a `tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: <cause>` warn record in Gateway diagnostics while the client response remains `UNAVAILABLE "GitHub identity setup failed"`, letting operators distinguish a missing `gh` CLI, an expired handoff, and hard failures by reading one log line.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts` (the configure catch block); regression tests `logs the setup failure cause while responding with the generic error` and `hands the raw cause to the logging owner without pre-redaction` in `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts`; the committed real-transport proof `test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — a real Gateway server was booted over its shipped WebSocket RPC transport in an isolated state directory (token auth, isolated `HOME`, isolated config/workspace dirs), and the `tools.github.configure` request was sent through that live transport with a well-formed but never-registered one-use handoff, before and after the patch (committed proof: `test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # red on base: revert the handler to unpatched main, run both regression layers
  git checkout origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts       # 2 failed | 12 passed
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts          # FAIL: no tools-github cause record
  # green with the patch applied
  git checkout HEAD -- src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts       # 14/14 passed
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts          # 1/1 passed
  # targeted type checks on the rebased head
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --builders 1   # passed
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.e2e.json --builders 1               # passed
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --builders 1        # passed
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** (running isolated Gateway, shipped WS RPC transport, missing one-use handoff)
  ```text
  client RPC rejection:            {"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"GitHub identity setup failed"}
  owner-only file record (WARN):   {"subsystem":"tools-github","message":"GitHub identity setup failed: temporary GitHub credential is unavailable"}
  console presentation (egress):   [tools-github] GitHub identity setup failed: temporary GitHub credential is unavailable
  ```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path set` reports success for a blank Markdown item-field value, but that field cannot be resolved or edited after the file is reloaded.

## User Impact

Empty or whitespace-only item-field replacements return `parse-error` without changing the file. Normal replacements and empty frontmatter strings keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Markdown item fields already require a nonblank value when parsed. Enforcing that contract in the existing editor before writing preserves the original field and its address instead of accepting an unreadable replacement. No schema, config-shape, Doctor, or migration changes.

Original implementation by @LinzeShi; the contributor commit is retained. The maintainer revision consolidates the regressions without dropping blank-value, insertion-string, duplicate-key, or immutability coverage.

## Evidence

[Inspectable built-CLI and Gateway captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190644#issuecomment-6563647440) compare main `02e6735d3db4758067917d81cc5c48a1e7247e6a` with exact candidate `1086d48218489067e5020863e65e0526eb3a9993` in secretless Docker on Node 24.22.1 with isolated state:

- Main **2/2 reproduced**: empty-value write succeeds, subsequent `path resolve` fails; Gateway readback confirms the damaged field bytes.
- Candidate **2/2 passes**: write refuses with `parse-error`, file bytes remain identical, CLI resolves `original`, and Gateway returns the unchanged file. LF and CRLF covered.
- Normal nonblank writes/reads and empty frontmatter strings pass on both builds in both runs.
- Identical focused regression cases against main production: **3 fail, 20 pass**. Candidate: **23/23 pass**. Targeted Oxlint and Oxfmt pass.
- Whole-PR line deltas against merge base: production **+3**, tests **−1**, docs **+2**.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores the previous editor behavior; this patch does not migrate or rewrite existing data. Blast radius is Markdown item-field replacement through the oc-path editor. If wrong, valid item-field writes could be rejected; normal values and the separate empty-frontmatter contract are covered by controls.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading repair advice when a Gateway listener is available but an agent is still completing normal startup preparation.

## User Impact

Operators see that startup preparation is pending, its current phase and elapsed background-preparation time, and a request to retry when preparation finishes. Actual failures retain their repair guidance.

This does not speed up startup or change readiness, queueing, retry policy, configuration, or database schemas. It does not claim that rejected input was queued. No migration or operator configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending admission currently suggests stopping the Gateway and running `doctor --fix`, even when no failure has occurred. The existing startup owner already tracks phase and elapsed time; this change reuses its phase transitions and progress timer to update the pending refusal instead of introducing another state owner or timer. Elapsed time is refreshed at those existing progress points, not continuously.

## Evidence

- Regression on the base: 23 tests passed; the new pending-message assertion failed against the old startup reason.
- Patched focused suites: **51/51 tests passed**, covering pending retry metadata, phase/elapsed updates, successful admission, and actual failure repair guidance.
- Targeted format, lint (0 warnings/errors), and whitespace checks passed.
- Core plus Gateway-server and state-logging test typechecks passed.
- Independent supplied-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; source-owner context was inspected separately.
- Gateway preparation suite: 24 tests in 2.93s. Combined focused run: 117.14s including compilation and existing native SQLite integration suites. CI timing is not yet available.

The focused tests exercise the production admission/startup owners with controlled external preparation and native database integration. Separately, an installed-runtime backport was activated and verified through a clean Gateway start. That runtime check is separate from the exact-head isolated RPC proof below; it does not claim that pending or genuine failure responses were captured on the live Gateway.

## Additional real Gateway operator-facing proof

Exact head: `80ddc37d056e5939341bbdcbc22c779502188254`. Full `pnpm build` passed (4m4.5s); previous focused tests were not rerun.

Ran the built Gateway in isolated synthetic state with channels, cron and providers disabled. A supported index-repair fixture (40 queued agents plus the probe) kept real background preparation pending; a separate agent had a required table deliberately removed. No production admission hooks, fabricated refusals, or copied helper implementation were used.

**Authenticated `sessions.create` WebSocket response while pending:**

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "Agent probe is still preparing (phase: open-wait; background preparation elapsed: 4s).\nStartup inspection and preparation are still running. Retry the request after preparation finishes; no repair action is needed while it is pending.",
  "details": {
    "reason": "startup-sidecars",
    "method": "sessions.create"
  },
  "retryable": true,
  "retryAfterMs": 250
}
```

**Genuine schema failure through the same RPC:**

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <isolated-state>/agents/broken/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: missing table session_key_contract; missing or drifted index idx_agent_session_nodes_active; run openclaw doctor --fix to repair it.\nSessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.",
  "retryable": false
}
```

Captured 35 pending error frames across phases `open-wait`, `open`, `migration`. Every pending frame retained `retryable: true`, `retryAfterMs: 250`, phase/elapsed text, and no Doctor/stop/restart advice. Genuine failure frames retained `retryable: false`, no retry delay, and Doctor repair guidance. The real GatewayClient retried the pending request and `sessions.create` succeeded after admission (`runStarted: false`; no model call).

Capture used an unchanged-byte loopback WebSocket forwarder because GatewayClient intentionally hides retryable startup refusals behind automatic retry. Raw responses were inspected before sanitization; only isolated filesystem roots were replaced in the failure excerpt. Gateway runtime: Bun1.4.4/Linux; observer: Node24.22.1.

**Limits:** This adds current-head RPC/operator-message proof, not a base-runtime before/after recording, channel/UI screenshot proof, or a restart-performance claim. The large synthetic queue is a fixture, not a proposed production configuration.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep live standing grants through approval retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Always allow on a gateway automation mints a standing grant that should last until it is revoked, or until the expiry frozen at mint time. `tools.exec.grantExpiryDays` and `grantExpiresInDays` allow that expiry to be unset or as long as 3650 days.

Terminal approval rows are deleted 30 days after they resolve. The standing grant's `minted_by_approval_id` references that row with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and the state database opens with foreign keys on. The same delete runs again when a later approval is inserted. After the parent row is gone, grant lookup returns `approval-missing` or `no-grant`, so the next matching automation run prompts again. A missing approval still stops the grant. Routine retention should not delete an approval that still anchors an unrevoked grant with no expiry, or with an expiry still in the future.

## Test-line ceiling

The standing-grant retention tests add 298 lines. Current main is already past `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`. The merged tree counted 6286755 test lines, 352 over the previous ceiling of 6286403. This branch sets the ceiling to that counted total.

## Evidence

Proved head `2be949460ef7840830bfea2f4c1c4a1cf8456ca7`. macOS arm64, Node v26.11.0. Isolated state directory and config. Gateway bound to loopback. `tools.exec.mode` is `ask` and `tools.exec.host` is `gateway`. Commands were `node scripts/run-node.mjs` from this branch. No Control UI click.

A connected operator client with the `approvals` and `exec-approvals` capabilities stayed on the gateway so an automation run could wait. Each answer was the shipped `approvals resolve` command. A one-shot CLI call does not stay connected as an approval route.

The cron job `aged-grant` (`4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e`) asks the agent to exec `/bin/echo aged-grant-launch` once. `approvals resolve <id> allow-always` minted grant `c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504` from approval `22c9052e-0a5d-4f83-8be3-bb4c4018596e`, with `expiresAtMs` null. That in-flight exec completed. Its tool result was status `completed`, exit code 0, text `aged-grant-launch` (session `db29f7e1`). The grant's `useCount` was still 0, because that spawn was the live approval.

The gateway was then stopped. That approval's `created_at_ms` and `resolved_at_ms` were moved 31 days earlier (`2678400000` ms). The grant row was not rewritten. After `gateway run` again, `approvals grants list` still returned the same grant, `expiresAtMs` null, `useCount` 0. The schema files in this diff did not change.

The next `cron run` of the same job launched with no new `exec.approval.requested` event. `useCount` became 1 and `lastUsedAtMs` became `1791976462271`.

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run 4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e --wait --json
status: ok
completionStatus: succeeded
summary: aged-grant-launch
jobId: 4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e
sessionId: 351851a8-e2fa-42e1-ab19-cd5432532da0
durationMs: 24633
model: grok-4.3
```

Tool result for session `351851a8`: status `completed`, exit code 0, text `aged-grant-launch`.

Three forbidden runs then asked for a new approval. Each was `approvals resolve <id> deny`. None completed an exec, and `useCount` stayed 1.

| Run | Shipped result | Tool result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job `130223bb-67bf-49e4-b07d-6e6561852c56`, command `/bin/echo not-the-grant`, agent `main` | approval `d8841a88-a776-45b1-a535-b0a6bcfe9dd6` denied. Cron status `error`: exec denied by gateway | status `failed`, no exit code |
| Job `b5364a97-eb7d-41d0-a6eb-4953ef4deb86`, same echo command, agent `main` | approval `5ee56dca-4bc8-420d-b325-49fb109b5a80` denied. Cron status `error` | status `failed`, no exit code |
| Job `58f6abf4-c3a5-4a47-b56e-c1b9f99aefe3`, same echo command, agent `other` | approval `e6817cc9-7fc0-41cf-9b6b-73276166a56d` denied. Source agent `other`. Cron status `error` | status `failed`, no exit code |

`approvals grants revoke c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504` returned `outcome: revoked`. The following list still showed that grant, `useCount` 1, `revokedAtMs` `1791976920376`, `revokedBy` `cli`, `lastUsedAtMs` unchanged. The next `cron run` of `4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e` emitted a new approval, `350726f9-2bae-48eb-9f0c-7f158b74d9c6`. Deny left the tool result status `failed` with no exit code. Cron status was `error`. After that write, `approvals grants list` returned no grants. The revoked grant no longer kept the 31-day-old approval.

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants list --json
{"grants":[{"grantId":"c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504","mintedByApprovalId":"22c9052e-0a5d-4f83-8be3-bb4c4018596e","agentId":"main","cronJobId":"4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e","cronJobName":"aged-grant","command":"/bin/echo aged-grant-launch","expiresAtMs":null,"revokedAtMs":null,"lastUsedAtMs":1791976462271,"useCount":1}]}
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants list --json
{"grants":[]}
```

The first list is after the aged launch and the three denials. The second list is after revoke plus the denied rerun.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A standing grant minted by allow-always still launches its cron command after the parent approval is 31 days old and the gateway has restarted. A different command, a different cron job, and a different agent do not launch. Revoking the grant before the next run makes that same job ask again, and denying the ask does not launch.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v26.11.0, OpenClaw head `2be949460ef`. Isolated state directory. Loopback gateway. Exec mode `ask`, host `gateway`. Shipped `node scripts/run-node.mjs` gateway, cron, and approvals commands. A connected operator client received approval events.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run` on the branch. `node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run <job> --wait --json` for the aged job, the forbidden command, the other job, the other agent, and the same job after revoke. `node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals resolve <id> allow-always` once, then `deny` for every later request. `node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants list --json` and `approvals grants revoke <grantId>`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from those shipped commands.

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run 4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e --wait --json
status: ok
summary: aged-grant-launch
sessionId: 351851a8-e2fa-42e1-ab19-cd5432532da0
tool: status completed, exit code 0, text aged-grant-launch
grant useCount: 1
approval event during that run: none
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants revoke c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504 --json
{"outcome":"revoked"}
```

Forbidden command, other job, and agent `other` each produced `exec.approval.requested`, then a denied tool result with status `failed` and no exit code. After revoke, job `4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e` did the same. The later grants list was `{"grants":[]}`.

- **Observed result after fix:** The aged grant launched `/bin/echo aged-grant-launch` through cron after the gateway restart, with exit code 0 and no new approval. The three mismatched runs did not launch and did not increase `useCount`. After revoke, the original job asked again and the denied exec did not launch.
- **What was not tested:** A Control UI click. A revoke that lands after the grant is consumed and before the process is created. A second gateway built from the merge base. A copy of a production state database from another machine.

## Summary

Startup recovery and the retention delete inside approval insert share one query. That query skips an approval while an unrevoked standing grant names it and `expires_at_ms` is null or still in the future. Revocation, and a later approval write, still drop a parent that is past 30 days. This trace replaces the earlier helper-script transcript. It does not time a revoke between consume and spawn.

## Request

Add Iris Chat as a native channel. Per the contributor policy, this is an issue for maintainer review before proposing a core PR.

[Iris Chat](https://irischat.org) provides Signal-like Nostr Double Ratchet messaging without phone numbers or signup. A working external channel package is available now: [installation and source](https://github.com/irislib/iris-chat-channels/tree/v0.2.0/nanobot).

It uses nanobot 0.4.0's `ChannelPlugin` discovery and `BaseChannel` APIs, with no core patch. A single paired contact can send tasks and receive text replies, seen receipts, and typing status. It keeps nanobot's model/tool settings. The installed Iris CLI handles identity and encrypted transport; prompts are decrypted for nanobot and its model provider. Groups, attachments, and in-flight remote approvals/cancellation are unsupported.

Tested the installed wheel with the real nanobot gateway in a network-disabled container: throwaway Iris accounts, local relay/model fixture, real file tool, encrypted reply, second turn, seen receipt, and successful typing refresh/stop all passed. Four additional runtime tests cover contact restriction, progress suppression, and turn correlation. [Pins and test recipe](https://github.com/irislib/iris-chat-channels/blob/v0.2.0/tests/README.md).

Would you prefer keeping this as an external channel package or reviewing an upstream channel contribution? I can provide the existing implementation in the form you prefer.

Prepared and tested with AI assistance.

issues.title: [Feature]: Android app: register as a selectable default digital assistant
issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case
On Android, the system lets you choose a default digital assistant app (Settings > Apps > Default apps > Digital assistant app). That app is what the power-button hold, home-button/gesture long-press and similar assist gestures launch, in place of Gemini or Bixby. The Hermes Android beta (ai.nousresearch.hermes.mobile 1.0.0) isn't offered in that list, so there's no quick way to reach Hermes from anywhere on the phone. The only routes today are the app icon, the Quick Settings tile, the widget and the LiveVoiceShortcut entry, all of which need the screen on and a swipe or tap.

I mostly use live voice hands-free, so a single-gesture launch matters.

For reference, Herald, a third-party Android client for Hermes, already appears as a selectable digital assistant, so this is achievable for a Hermes client app.

### Proposed Solution
Smallest useful version: declare the components Android needs to list the app as an assistant, and have the assist gesture open Hermes (a new chat, or live voice if the Collapsed Voice Button setting says so).

- A `VoiceInteractionService` with a voice-interaction XML (`supportsAssist="true"`) and a session service. The session's `onShow()` launches the app.
- An activity with an `android.intent.action.ASSIST` intent filter.
- A `RecognitionService` stub, since some Android versions/OEMs only list the app if one is named.

This is manifest plus a thin launcher, not a new voice stack. It reuses the existing Live Voice and New Chat entry points. The services have to be native code even if the rest of the UI isn't.

Later, optional, and out of scope for this request: pass screen context from `onHandleAssist` (opt-in, with a clear privacy explanation).

Not requested: a hotword ("Hey Hermes"), which needs privileged access that third-party apps don't get.

### Alternatives Considered
- Quick Settings tile, widget and LiveVoiceShortcut already exist, but need a swipe or tap with the screen on.
- On Samsung the side key can be remapped to open an app, which isn't the same as the system assistant role and isn't available on other phones.

### Feature Type
Other

### Scope
Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution
- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)
N/A. This is a feature request, not a problem report.

issues.title: Desktop BOTS: idle bot chat's finished task list bounces open/closed every ~5 s while another session in the same profile is running
issues.body:
## Summary

In the BOTS tab, an **idle** bot chat's finished task list keeps bouncing open and closed above the composer: **"Tasks N/N"** (expanded) for 4 s, then **"Previous tasks N/N"** (collapsed) for about 1.2 s, then again, for as long as **another session in the same profile is running a turn**. The list shown is the bot chat's own last finished list, not the other session's.

Cause: the roster's inbound-activity check treats activity anywhere in the bot's profile as activity in the open bot chat. On every 5 s roster poll it runs a background force-resume of that chat, and each resume re-shows the finished list for the 4 s linger.

Related, but different: #127429 (no way to dismiss a finished list) and #133390 (the retained snapshot collapses at turn end).

## Observed

- macOS, packaged Hermes.app built from `71d34bad` (v0.21.7). The relevant files are unchanged on `main` as of 2026-11-02 (`plugins/hermes-bots/roster-actions.ts` `refreshOpenBotChat` / `trackInboundActivity`, `plugins/hermes-bots/data.ts` `botActivitySession`, `store/todos.ts` identical).
- The bot chat had been idle for about 11 hours. Its last turn ended with a finished 2-item `todo_list` (2/2 completed).
- Frame timing from a 20 s screen recording at 60 fps, measured on the status-stack region:

  | State | Start (s) | Duration |
  |---|---|---|
  | Previous tasks 2/2 (collapsed) | 1.47 | 1.20 s |
  | Tasks 2/2 (expanded) | 2.67 | 4.00 s |
  | Previous tasks 2/2 | 6.67 | 1.23 s |
  | Tasks 2/2 | 7.90 | 4.03 s |
  | Previous tasks 2/2 | 11.93 | 1.25 s |
  | Tasks 2/2 | 13.18 | 3.97 s |
  | Previous tasks 2/2 | 17.15 | 1.20 s |
  | Tasks 2/2 | 18.35 | (end of recording) |

  The cycle is 5.20–5.26 s. The expanded phase matches `FINISHED_LINGER_MS` (4 000 ms) exactly. The collapsed phase is the gap until the next 5 s roster poll plus its resume round trip.
- During the recording two other desktop sessions in the same profile were mid-turn, with tool and API calls every few seconds. Neither wrote a `todo_list` during the window (the next write came 12 s after the recording ended), so this isn't a cross-session todo leak.
- The bot's roster row showed **"now"** throughout, although the bot chat itself had no new messages for hours. That is the same `last_session` value (see below).
- `desktop.log` shows no connection switches or other window events during the recording.

## Code path (`main`)

1. The roster query refetches every 5 s (`plugins/hermes-bots/data.ts`, `refetchInterval: 5000`). `usePublishRosterSnapshot` calls `trackInboundActivity(roster)`.
2. `trackInboundActivity` watermarks `botActivitySession(bot)`, which returns whichever of `canonical_session` and `last_session` has the newer `last_active`.
3. Backend: `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py` `_latest_profile_session_rows` sets `last_session` to the newest human-facing session **anywhere in the profile**. A running turn bumps that session's `last_activity_at` every few seconds (`touch_session_activity`, plus message writes).
4. So on each poll `ts > prev`. The bot is `$selectedBot`, so `refreshOpenBotChat(bot)` runs. The focused stored session is the canonical chat and it isn't busy, so it calls `openBotCanonicalChat(bot, { background: true })` → `host.openSession(..., { forceResume: true, refreshInPlace: true })`.
5. The activate/resume path in `use-session-actions` calls `restoreSessionTodosFromSnapshot(..., todo_state, running=false)` and then `restoreSessionTodosFromSnapshot(..., latestSessionTodoSnapshot(...), false)`. For a finished list, `todosForHydration` returns it and `setSessionTodos` puts it back in `$todosBySession`. `acceptRevision` accepts an **equal** revision, so the same snapshot restarts the linger. The stack shows the live "Tasks N/N" group for `FINISHED_LINGER_MS`, drops it, and falls back to the retained "Previous tasks" disclosure until the next poll.

It also costs a forced resume (activate RPC plus transcript read) every 5 s for as long as the other turn runs.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In profile X, have a bot chat whose last turn ended with a finished `todo_list` (all items completed).
2. Start a long-running turn in a **normal** desktop chat of profile X, for example one with several tool calls.
3. Open profile X's bot in the BOTS tab and leave its chat in view.

Expected: the bot chat's composer shows a stable "Previous tasks N/N".
Actual: it alternates "Tasks N/N" (4 s) / "Previous tasks N/N" (~1 s) on a ~5 s cycle until the other turn ends.

Control: a bot in a profile with no running session stays still. The loop stops within one poll after the other turn finishes, which makes it look intermittent.

## Suggested direction

- In `trackInboundActivity`, call `refreshOpenBotChat` only when the bot chat's **own** activity (`canonical_session.last_active` / its `resolved_id`) advanced past a watermark kept for it. Profile-wide `last_session` activity can keep driving the unread mark and toast, but it doesn't mean the open transcript changed.
- Separately, consider not re-lingering a finished snapshot on resume when its revision equals the current watermark and the list is unchanged (`restoreSessionTodosFromSnapshot` / `acceptRevision`). Any reload of an idle chat otherwise flashes its last finished list as live progress.
- Optional: the roster row's relative time ("now") reflects profile-wide activity, not the bot chat's. That could be intended, but it's confusing next to a chat that hasn't changed.

issues.title: Statusbar context meter shows another session's numbers when the focused row has no live runtime
issues.body:
# Desktop statusbar context meter keeps another session's numbers when the focused row has no live runtime

## Observed

With the `context-usage` status bar item enabled, switching between sessions in the sidebar leaves **both** halves of the readout unchanged — e.g. it stays at `95k/262k · 36%` for every session, including ones whose real occupancy is completely different. The number looks like a per-session figure but describes whichever session last reported usage.

Measured ground truth from `state.db` (`sessions.model_config._usage_anchor.prompt_tokens`) on the same machine at the same moment:

| session | anchor prompt tokens |
|---|---|
| 903b6e86… | 95,261 |
| a482bb04… | 86,952 |
| ec7cccbb… / 62c56d02… | 14,220 |

The meter showed one of those values for all four.

## Why it happens

Three links in the chain:

1. `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/hooks/use-statusbar-items.tsx:238`
   ```ts
   const activeSessionId = primaryFocused ? primaryActiveSessionId : (focusedRuntimeId ?? null)
   ```
   Focusing a stored session row that has **no live runtime** leaves `focusedRuntimeId` null, so `activeSessionId` is null.

2. `useContextBreakdown` then never fetches at all — its effect guard is
   ```ts
   if (!enabled || !sessionId || busy) { setFetched(null); setLoading(false); return }
   ```
   so `contextBreakdown` stays null (no request, no error, nothing to evict).

3. With no breakdown, the gauge falls back to the global `$currentUsage`:
   ```ts
   const gaugeUsage = contextMidTurn ? … : currentUsage
   ```
   and that store is updated with `mergeUsage` (`apps/shared/src/usage-tick.ts:148`, `{ ...previous, ...next }`) — a partial tick keeps the fields it omits. A resumed / no-runtime session reports **no** context fields, so the previous (primary) session's `context_used` / `context_max` survive the switch untouched.

The code already documents this hazard for the case where a breakdown *does* exist ("the store merges rather than replaces, so the PREVIOUS session's gauge numbers survive the switch"), and the retry-exhaustion path deliberately goes dark in that situation. The gap is the `sessionId === null` case: nothing fetches, nothing evicts, so stale numbers stay on screen indefinitely — under a different session's name.

## Impact

The meter is the only place most users read context occupancy from, and it is what they compare against the compaction trigger (`compression.threshold`, raised to 0.75 for windows < 512K). A frozen figure reads as "compaction will never fire" / "this session has plenty of room", when in fact the reading belongs to another conversation.

## Repro

1. Enable the context meter (status bar → right-click → *Context meter*; it is hidden by default via `STATUSBAR_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT`).
2. Run a turn in session A so the gauge shows real numbers.
3. Focus an older session row in the sidebar whose runtime has been reaped (no live agent).
4. The gauge still shows session A's used/max; opening the popover lists session A's category breakdown too.

## Expected

When nothing describes the focused session, the meter should go dark (`—`, no bar, empty popover) — exactly like the evicted/zeroed-breakdown path — rather than showing another session's numbers.

## Proposed fix (tested locally)

Gate the readout on having a live runtime for the focused row:

```ts
const gaugeTrustworthy = Boolean(activeSessionId)

const contextUsage = useMemo(() => (gaugeTrustworthy ? usageContextLabel(gaugeUsage) : ''), [gaugeTrustworthy, gaugeUsage])
const contextBar   = useMemo(() => (gaugeTrustworthy ? contextBarLabel(gaugeUsage) : ''),    [gaugeTrustworthy, gaugeUsage])

// the popover must not list another session's occupancy either
const panelUsage = useMemo<UsageStats>(() => gaugeTrustworthy ? gaugeUsage
  : { ...gaugeUsage, context_max: 0, context_used: 0, context_percent: 0, context_estimated: false },
  [gaugeTrustworthy, gaugeUsage])
```

Mid-turn behaviour is untouched (`activeSessionId` is set there and the streamed usage belongs to that session), so the existing lifecycle tests still pass. A regression test — `goes dark instead of showing another session numbers when no runtime is live` in `use-statusbar-items.lifecycle.test.tsx` — asserts label `'—'`, `detail === undefined`, and a popover free of the stale figures.

Verified locally: `npx vitest run src/app/shell/hooks/{use-statusbar-items.lifecycle,use-statusbar-items}.test.tsx src/app/shell/statusbar-context-menu.test.tsx src/app/shell/context-usage-panel.test.tsx` → 27 passed; `npm run typecheck` clean; eslint adds no new warnings.

## Environment

Hermes desktop (packaged) on macOS 15.8.1, repo at `bf0203a794`. Provider: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LM Studio), several sessions on the same model + route — which is also why `context_max` legitimately matches across them; it is the numerator being stale that misleads.

issues.title: [Bug]: Subagent credential leases ignore model-scoped entitlement cooldowns
issues.body:
## Bug Description

Normal anonymous (availability-based) subagent lease selection does not pass the child's model to the credential pool. An entitlement cooldown for one model therefore excludes that credential from anonymous leases for other models, even though model-aware selection still considers it available. Separately, the explicit-ID / endpoint-fallback lease path bypasses availability filtering altogether; this exception is based on code reading and was not separately executed.

[PR #115760](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115760) specifies that an entitlement rejection benches only `(credential, model)` and the account keeps serving other models. The existing conservative behavior for callers that genuinely do not specify a model is intentional ([PR #113171](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113171)); the child lease path has a model available but does not pass it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Save the script below as `repro_public.py` and run it against a Hermes checkout with its runtime dependencies installed:

```sh
python repro_public.py --src /path/to/hermes-agent
python repro_public.py --src /path/to/hermes-agent --contract
```

It uses synthetic credentials, an isolated temporary home, and blocked network access. The default run exits 0 and prints `RESULT: reproduction confirmed` when the bug is present. `--contract` invokes the actual child-lease helper and exits 1 on affected code (0 once fixed).

<details><summary>repro_public.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline repro: model-A cooldowns incorrectly exclude model-B child leases.
Run: python repro_public.py --src /path/to/hermes-agent [--contract]
Source fallback: HERMES_AGENT_SRC, then a checkout in the current directory.
Default exits 0 on reproduction; --contract exits 1 on affected code (0 if fixed).
Needs only the project's own runtime dependencies. Synthetic credentials only;
isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME before imports, blocked network, temporary files cleaned.
"""
import argparse
from collections import Counter
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import sys
import tempfile
from types import SimpleNamespace

def check(condition, message):
    print(("PASS: " if condition else "FAIL: ") + message, flush=True)
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--src", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--contract", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    src = (args.src or Path(os.environ.get("HERMES_AGENT_SRC", os.getcwd()))).resolve()
    if not (src / "agent" / "credential_pool.py").is_file():
        parser.error("Hermes source not found: use --src PATH, HERMES_AGENT_SRC, or run from a checkout")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="fake-hermes-home-", dir=Path(__file__).resolve().parent) as home:
        os.environ.update(HERMES_HOME=home, HOME=home)
        os.environ.pop("HERMES_PROFILE", None)
        sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
        network_attempts = []

        def no_network(*a, **kw):
            network_attempts.append(True)
            raise AssertionError("Network access forbidden in this reproduction")

        socket.socket.connect = socket.socket.connect_ex = no_network
        socket.create_connection = socket.getaddrinfo = no_network
        from agent.credential_pool import CredentialPool, PooledCredential, AUTH_TYPE_OAUTH
        from agent.credential_pool_model_cooldowns import model_cooldown_until
        from hermes_constants import get_hermes_home
        from hermes_cli.auth import _auth_file_path

        check(get_hermes_home() == Path(home) and _auth_file_path() == Path(home) / "auth.json",
              "Hermes home and auth.json are isolated in the disposable directory")
        entries = [PooledCredential(
            provider="openai-codex", id=f"entry-{i}", label=f"fake-credential-{i}",
            auth_type=AUTH_TYPE_OAUTH, priority=i, source="manual",
            access_token=f"fake-access-token-{i}", expires_at="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        ) for i in range(3)]
        pool = CredentialPool("openai-codex", entries)
        pool._strategy = "fill_first"
        check(pool.select(model="model-B").id == "entry-0", "baseline model-B selects entry-0")
        baseline = [pool.acquire_lease() for _ in range(3)]
        check(baseline == ["entry-0", "entry-1", "entry-2"], "baseline leases spread across three entries")
        for entry_id in baseline:
            pool.release_lease(entry_id)

        def deny_model_a(entry_id):
            pool.mark_exhausted_and_rotate(
                status_code=400, credential_id=entry_id, failure_reason="model_entitlement",
                model="model-A", error_context={"message": "The 'model-A' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."})

        deny_model_a("entry-0")
        first = next(e for e in pool.entries() if e.id == "entry-0")
        check(model_cooldown_until(first, "model-A") is not None and
              model_cooldown_until(first, "model-B") is None, "cooldown applies to model-A only")
        check(first.last_status not in ("dead", "exhausted"), "entry-0 is not credential-wide dead/exhausted")
        check("model-A" in json.dumps(json.loads((Path(home) / "auth.json").read_text())),
              "real entitlement path persisted model-A cooldown in temporary auth.json")
        check(pool.select(model="model-B").id == "entry-0", "model-aware model-B selection still uses entry-0")
        if not args.contract:
            leased = pool.acquire_lease()
            check(leased == "entry-1", "BUG: anonymous lease skips eligible entry-0")
            pool.release_lease(leased)
        deny_model_a("entry-1")
        available, _ = pool._available_entries(model="model-B")
        check([e.id for e in available] == ["entry-0", "entry-1", "entry-2"],
              "all three entries remain available for model-B")
        if args.contract:
            from tools.delegate_tool_child_run import _lease_child_credential
            child = SimpleNamespace(model="model-B", provider="openai-codex", base_url=entries[0].base_url,
                                    _credential_pool=pool, _swap_credential=lambda entry: None)
            _, actual = _lease_child_credential(child)
            print("Contract: model-B child should lease entry-0; actual:", actual)
            pool.release_lease(actual)
            check(not network_attempts, "zero network attempts")
            check(actual == "entry-0", "model-B child must lease the highest-priority eligible credential")
        else:
            leased_ids = [pool.acquire_lease() for _ in range(6)]
            print("six outstanding (unreleased) leases acquired sequentially:", leased_ids)
            print("Lease counts:", dict(Counter(leased_ids)), "; configured soft cap:", pool._max_concurrent)
            print("The per-credential cap is soft by design; exceeding it is not itself the bug.")
            for entry_id in leased_ids:
                pool.release_lease(entry_id)
            check(Counter(leased_ids) == {"entry-2": 6}, "BUG: leases concentrate despite model-B eligibility")
            check(not network_attempts, "zero network attempts")
            print("RESULT: reproduction confirmed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except AssertionError:
        sys.exit(1)
```
</details>

Relevant default output, verbatim:

```text
PASS: Hermes home and auth.json are isolated in the disposable directory
PASS: baseline model-B selects entry-0
PASS: baseline leases spread across three entries
PASS: cooldown applies to model-A only
PASS: entry-0 is not credential-wide dead/exhausted
PASS: real entitlement path persisted model-A cooldown in temporary auth.json
PASS: model-aware model-B selection still uses entry-0
PASS: BUG: anonymous lease skips eligible entry-0
PASS: all three entries remain available for model-B
six outstanding (unreleased) leases acquired sequentially: ['entry-2', 'entry-2', 'entry-2', 'entry-2', 'entry-2', 'entry-2']
Lease counts: {'entry-2': 6} ; configured soft cap: 1
The per-credential cap is soft by design; exceeding it is not itself the bug.
PASS: BUG: leases concentrate despite model-B eligibility
PASS: zero network attempts
RESULT: reproduction confirmed
EXIT CODE: 0
```

Contract output, verbatim:

```text
Contract: model-B child should lease entry-0; actual: entry-2
FAIL: model-B child must lease the highest-priority eligible credential
EXIT CODE: 1
```

The six leases are acquired sequentially and remain outstanding (unreleased) together; they are not six production agents or a lock-contention test. The per-credential cap is soft by design, so exceeding it is not claimed as a bug.

## Expected Behavior

A credential benched for `model-A` remains eligible for a `model-B` child lease, subject to the normal availability and concurrency rules. Model-less callers can retain their conservative behavior.

## Actual Behavior

**Observed:** In a six-account ChatGPT OAuth `openai-codex` pool (accounts A–F), `auth.json` readback showed that three accounts acquired a 365-day model cooldown for `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest-900k` after entitlement 400s; none had credential-wide errors. The `-900k` ID is a Hermes alias whose suffix Hermes strips on the wire; both `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest-900k` and `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest` appear in logs, and the recorded cooldown key was the `-900k` ID. Two other accounts were in an ordinary 429 usage window. The operator assessed one account as entitled, based on entitlement errors on the others.

**Inferred from code and the offline reproduction:** With these markers, normal anonymous child leases would have only one eligible account for Codex subagent models `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6.1-terra`, while model-aware `select()` for the main session would still be able to use the three model-benched accounts. We did not trace production child-to-account allocations.

As a temporary workaround, `hermes auth reset openai-codex <id>` clears **all local error state** on that credential, not just the model cooldown; the cooldown returns on the next entitlement rejection.

## Affected Component

Tools (delegation) / Agent Core (credential pool)

- [`tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py:473–500`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5aa8df742c81ca7d993d94a0bc80b27edd65dc0c/tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py#L473-L500): child leasing omits the model; the endpoint fallback leases by ID without model availability filtering.
- [`agent/credential_pool.py:2335–2362`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5aa8df742c81ca7d993d94a0bc80b27edd65dc0c/agent/credential_pool.py#L2335-L2362): lease methods accept no model and call `_available_entries` without one.
- [`agent/credential_pool_model_cooldowns.py:37–47`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5aa8df742c81ca7d993d94a0bc80b27edd65dc0c/agent/credential_pool_model_cooldowns.py#L37-L47): without a model, any active model cooldown blocks the entry.

## Debug Report

Installed version: `v0.22.5+3251.g9a56be3` (commit `9a56be3d860533bd6c5551476ed0a65a6f4a3917`). The three affected files are byte-identical on upstream main at `5aa8df742c81ca7d993d94a0bc80b27edd65dc0c`. Provider: `openai-codex`; six-account OAuth pool, `fill_first`, advanced-delegation plugin `model_map` routes.

`hermes debug share` was not run because it uploads configuration and logs. A redacted report can be provided on request.

## Operating System

Linux, Debian in a Proxmox LXC container.

## Related

No exact duplicate found in our searches.

- [#125695](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125695): auxiliary routing ignores model scope.
- [#126768](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/126768): auxiliary “no credentials found” after a per-model cooldown due to unscoped pool selection.
- [#146385](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/146385): rotation after 429 ignores the request model; [PR #146450](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/146450) fixes rotation but explicitly leaves `_acquire_lease_under_lock` unchanged.
- [#127917](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/127917): visibility of the 365-day entitlement bench.
- [#140495](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/140495): child leases concentrate on the priority-0 credential.
- [#71970](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/71970) (closed): entitlement rotation.

## Suggested fix

Consider threading a keyword-only `model` from child leasing through `acquire_lease` and both `_acquire_lease_under_lock` attempts into `_available_entries(model=...)`. Also validate model availability in the endpoint-fallback/direct-ID lease path, which currently bypasses that filter. Keep the conservative behavior when the model is unknown. A behavior-contract test should verify that a credential benched for `model-A` is still leased for `model-B`; that test is red on the base version. This complements #146450.
