prs.title: fix(desktop): the approval chip on a remote-only profile reads that gateway, not a local backend
prs.body:
When you switch Desktop to a profile that lives only on a remote or SSH gateway, the status-bar approval chip asked *this computer* for that profile. This computer doesn't have it, so the chip showed the wrong mode ("Smart" when the profile is set to "Off") and desktop.log filled with `Hermes backend for profile "gamma" failed to start: Profile "gamma" no longer exists`. Now the chip asks the gateway you're actually on. It shows that profile's real mode, and no local backend is attempted.

**Outcome:** on a remote-only profile the approval-mode chip reads its mode from the active gateway, so Electron main is never asked to start a local backend for a profile name this machine does not have. The voice-engine switch and the Appearance display toggles write their `config.set` to that same gateway, so the change lands in the remote profile's config.yaml instead of being lost.

## Changes
- `use-statusbar-items.tsx`: the approval-mode requester now goes through `requestGatewayForActiveRoute`, which pairs the profile with the active connection (`requestGatewayForAgent(activeConnectionId, profile)`). Before, it called `requestGatewayForProfile(profile)`. A bare name has no gateway, so main resolved it through the local profile pool.
- `approval-mode-menu.tsx`: the sync effect also re-runs when the active socket changes. `default` on Box and `default` on This device have the same name, so a profile-only key never re-read the mode across that move.
- `lib/plugin-catalog.ts`: the active-profile catalog lookup has the same shape, so it now uses the same requester.
- New `store/active-route-request.ts` (one helper). A profile other than the active route's still takes the profile-only route, so session-owner routing is unchanged.
- `store/voice-live.ts` and `store/display-toggles.ts`: their `config.set` writes now go to the active gateway too (they no longer use the bare-name route); details in "Same class" below.
- `store/display-toggles.ts`: the connect-time re-send of a saved toggle reads the route from the registry (`activeGatewayRoute()` in `store/gateway.ts`). See "Review round" below.

## Root cause
`useStatusbarItems` → `syncApprovalModeForProfile` → `requestGatewayForProfile(activeProfile)` → `gatewayForProfile` → `getConnection("gamma")` twice (once for the shared-primary probe, once for the secondary dial). Main's `hermes:connection` treats an explicit profile as the legacy route → `ensureBackend("gamma")` → `assertLocalProfileCanStart` refuses → `logPoolSpawnFailure`. I found it live by setting a CDP breakpoint on the preload `getConnection` (renderer frames: `syncApprovalModeForProfile → requestGatewayForProfile → gatewayForProfile → sharedPrimaryRoute / openSecondary`).

## Live A/B (native Electron, real `hermes serve` backends)
Rig: This device (default, alpha, writer) + URL remote Homelab (default, marina, ops) + SSH remote Box (default, gamma, delta), 21 seeded sessions. The run is a 3-round switch loop (alpha → Box default → marina → Box gamma → local default), then a relaunch with All profiles.

| tree | `failed to start: Profile "X" no longer exists` lines | approval chip on gamma · Box (`approvals.mode: off`) | rows at relaunch | max switch ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| origin/main e8639fd | **15** (marina 6, gamma 9) | **Smart** (wrong) | 21/21 | 4080 (alpha) |
| main + #147763 | **12** (marina 6, gamma 6) | **Smart** (wrong) | 21/21 | 294 |
| this PR | **3** (gamma 3, see below) | **Off** | 21/21 | 4095 (alpha, same as main) |
| this PR + #147763 | **0** | **Off** | 21/21 | 282 |

The 3 lines left on this PR alone come from a different caller: `ensureRegistryBackend("local", "gamma")`, fired on the switch from gamma · Box to This device. It's the (new connection, old profile) request-scope race that #147763 fixes ("publish the request connection and its profile in one frame"). The slow alpha switch on main is also gone with #147763. Both PRs now touch `store/gateway.ts` in separate hunks; `git merge-tree` of the two heads is clean, and each lands on its own in either order.

Screenshots (gamma · Box selected, REM-gamma rows listed, vision-checked: no error card on either):

| main | this PR |
|---|---|
| ![main](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/405eb511c4a47189c0c1e17dcabf6600/raw/main-gamma-box-chip.png) | ![head](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/405eb511c4a47189c0c1e17dcabf6600/raw/head-gamma-box-chip.png) |

## Tests
`use-statusbar-items.approval-route.test.tsx` (2 cases, real gateway store, both red on origin/main, green here):
- on a remote-only active route, the chip's `config.get approvals.mode` is served by that route's socket, and `getConnection("marina")` is never called;
- moving between two gateways that both serve `default` re-reads the mode from the new one.

Also green: `vitest run src/app/shell src/lib/plugin-catalog.test.ts` (190 tests), `tsc -p .`, eslint on the touched files.

## Same class: voice mode and display toggles (commit 7b565eb21cd)
`store/voice-live.ts` `setVoiceChatMode` and `store/display-toggles.ts` `push` sent `config.set` through `requestGatewayForProfile(activeGatewayProfileKey(), …)`, the same bare-name route as the chip. On a remote-only profile the write never reached the remote gateway. Both now go through `requestGatewayForActiveRoute`.

Live readback on the same rig (Box gamma and Box default seeded with `voice.voice_chat_mode: gpt-live`; flip voice engine to "Speech-to-text + Hermes voice" and Appearance → In-App Tips off on gamma · Box, then voice on default · Box; read each `config.yaml` back from disk):

| tree | Box gamma `voice_chat_mode` | Box gamma `display.in_app_tips` | Box default `voice_chat_mode` | This device default / alpha |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d53e317e30c (this PR before the commit) | gpt-live (write refused: `Could not change the voice chat engine: … Profile "gamma" no longer exists`) | not written (2 refusal lines) | gpt-live (`Hermes gateway is not connected`) | unchanged |
| 7b565eb21cd | **chained** | **false** | **chained** | unchanged |

The "worse" variant (a Box `default` write landing in This device's `default` config.yaml) did not reproduce on this rig: on Box default the old route failed with "not connected" rather than writing locally. Either way the write was lost.

Screenshots (head, gamma · Box, vision-checked: no error card): [voice engine](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/405eb511c4a47189c0c1e17dcabf6600/raw/a26c45f5389256567d94ac1f73e86cc5455b821a/v2head-gamma-voice.png), [In-App Tips off](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/405eb511c4a47189c0c1e17dcabf6600/raw/3799301f52ec1b17da1584a171ab6e43fd9a9836/v2head-gamma-tips.png).

Tests updated: only the patched call moved. `voice-live.test.ts` and `display-toggles.test.ts` (from 96ae4ee44a6) now assert `requestGatewayForAgent(activeConnection, 'work', 'config.set', …)` instead of `requestGatewayForProfile('work', 'config.set', …)`. The mocked module gained the two names the helper imports. The key, value and target profile (`work`) assertions are unchanged, and so is every other case. New `store/active-route-config-writes.test.ts` drives the real gateway store on gamma · Box: both writes land on Box's socket and `getConnection("gamma")` is never called (red on d53e317e30c with `Profile "gamma" no longer exists`).

Other callers checked (`grep requestGatewayForProfile src/`): `sdk/profile-request.ts` takes a caller-chosen route (an object route already goes through `requestGatewayForAgent`). `store/session-request-router.ts` routes by the session owner's route object and falls back to a bare name only for a legacy string owner, not the active profile. `store/active-route-request.ts` is the helper itself. No other caller passes the active profile name alone.

Also green: `vitest run` on the 4 touched/related files (10 tests), `tsc -p .`, eslint on the touched files, `scripts/check --only health`.

Related: #107828 (same log line from a different mechanism: a pool scope key used as the profile name).

## Review round (ffe83d72fec)
- **Display auto-push wrote to the new gateway's OLD profile (7014321abfa).** A saved display toggle is re-sent on every socket change from a `$gateway` listener. `applyActive` notifies that listener before it publishes the route's profile, so the push paired Box's connection with the previous route's profile. A local/default -> box/gamma switch wrote `config.set display.in_app_tips` to **box/default**, and gamma never got it. The push now reads connection and profile from the registry together (`activeGatewayRoute()`; `applyActive` uses the same `activeRouteProfile()`). This works with or without #147763, which also batches `applyActive`'s publication. New case in `active-route-config-writes.test.ts`: it seeds a saved toggle and switches local/default -> box/gamma, then checks that the write lands on Box's gamma socket only, that no box/default connection is requested, and that the primary gets no write. It is red on 7b565eb21cd (gamma socket empty) and green here, alone and merged with #147763.
- **CI red at `tutorial-lifetime.test.tsx:75` (73448713c79).** The test's gateway mock lacked the names the new route helper imports. This is a harness fix only, and the assertions are unchanged.
- **ffe83d72fec** moves the `Secondary` interface, unchanged, into `store/gateway-socket-entry.ts`, so `store/gateway.ts` stays under its line ratchet.

prs.title: fix(desktop): SSH gateways list every profile at launch and switch without a per-profile remote backend (salvage #128187)
prs.body:
On an SSH gateway, Desktop started a separate Hermes backend on the remote machine for every profile you opened. So the first click on each SSH profile waited ~3.7 s, and the "All profiles" list never showed SSH profiles you had not opened yet. Now one remote backend per SSH gateway serves every profile, the way URL gateways and this device already work: every SSH profile's chats are listed at launch and switching takes ~165-263 ms. Salvages #128187 by @dskwe (All-profiles half, commits cherry-picked with authorship) and adds the shared-backend switch. Fixes #128177. ## What changes - **All-profiles list (salvage #128187):** SSH registry sources are read like URL remotes: one cross-profile `/api/profiles/sessions?profile=all` call through the connection's backend, keeping the profile tag each row comes back with, instead of one read per pooled per-profile backend (which skipped every profile not opened yet). - **Switch lag:** a named profile on an SSH gateway now rides that gateway's default remote backend as a `sharedRemote` descriptor (REST `?profile=`, socket `profile`), the same contract URL remotes use. No remote `hermes --profile

serve --isolated` spawn, one remote serve per SSH gateway (multiplex-only ruling). - **Narrow fallback:** the per-profile isolated backend stays only for a source pinned to one remote profile (`remoteProfile`), an older remote runtime without `/api/profiles` (404), and a profile that already holds its own pooled backend. A roster that answers without the requested profile means the profile does not exist on that host: the dial fails fast with `remote-profile-missing` instead of spawning a remote serve that can only exit. A timeout or 5xx on the roster read surfaces as an error rather than pooling an isolated serve. - **SSH gateway as the primary:** when the SSH gateway is the window's primary, its routes reuse the primary backend, so nothing for it sits in the backend pool. The All-profiles collector (`electron/registry-session-sources.ts`, moved out of `main.ts`) now counts that running primary backend as the gateway's source, together with the profiles it serves, and never starts one. Without this, selecting box/gamma listed only Box's chats. - `apps/desktop/electron/ssh-shared-profile-backend.ts` holds the decision; `main.ts` gets one hunk in `ensureRegistryBackend` (`managedSshConfig` moved into the new module, which also replaced a duplicate inline copy, so `main.ts` does not grow). ## Why per-profile SSH backends existed `883b57cbd84` (registry pool, Aug 15) gave each (connection, profile) its own tunnel + remote serve; that predates the one-serve-per-host ruling. `3d9ddb725e2` (#89756/#89769) then stopped hover pre-warm from dialing SSH because sweeping a roster spawned one isolated serve per bot and the cascade dropped the main chat (WS 1012). With a shared backend a named profile spawns nothing, so that cascade cannot form; the hover guard is left as is. ## Live A/B (real Electron + real `hermes serve`, private sshd, remote = default + gamma + delta, plus local and a URL remote) Cold relaunch with "All profiles" on, remote serves killed first; 40 s window. | | main `557254f` | head | |---|---|---| | All profiles: SSH default rows | 5.4 s | 4.5 s | | All profiles: SSH gamma / delta rows | never (40 s) | 4.5 s | | All profiles rows listed | 13 / 17 | 17 / 17, every row tagged with its gateway + profile | | First switch gamma (SSH) | 3810 ms | 263 ms | | First switch delta (SSH) | 3730 ms | 165 ms | | Remote `hermes serve` processes after both switch passes | 3 (`serve`, `--profile gamma serve`, `--profile delta serve`) | 1 | | Control: alpha (this device) / eps (URL) / default (URL) | 115 / 115 / 118 ms | 135 / 168 / 133 ms | Re-run on the pushed head `e30f08f` (cold relaunch): first switch gamma 437 ms, delta 155 ms, default 146 ms; remote serves 1 after both passes; every listed row's gateway + profile tag correct (checked through the same `profile=all` call the list makes). Main chat crash check (head): two rounds of switch + streamed turn (gemini-2.5-flash via Nous) on this device's default chat, SSH gamma, local alpha, SSH delta, SSH default. All 10 assistant replies landed only in their own profile's `state.db` (remote `profiles/gamma/state.db` etc.), remote serve count stayed 1, no WebSocket 1012 in `desktop.log`. All profiles at launch, main (SSH gamma/delta chats missing): ![main](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/7e3ace57a69ffbe81d58df474d3d5ce4/raw/main-allprofiles-at-launch.png) All profiles at launch, head (all 17): ![head](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/7e3ace57a69ffbe81d58df474d3d5ce4/raw/head-allprofiles-at-launch.png) ### SSH gateway as the primary (review fix `e0336ff`) Rig: Box (SSH) set as the primary, plus This device and a URL gateway (Lan). Box/gamma selected in the UI, then the same `profile=all` call the list makes. | | main `557254f` | `896e1fd` | `e0336ff` | |---|---|---|---| | All profiles from box/gamma | 12 (Lan 5 + Box 7) | **7 (Box only)** | 15 (Lan 5 + Box 7 + this device 3) | | All profiles from box/default | 7 (Box only) | 7 (Box only) | 15 | | Remote `hermes serve` processes | 3 | 1 | 1 | (main's box/default row shows main had the same gap; the fix closes it too.) ## Behaviour notes - A named SSH profile now reads provider keys from its own `.env` (multiplex secret scope), not from the remote shell environment a per-profile serve inherited. Same rule as URL gateways and this device. - `profile-session-routing.test.ts` "registry sources: ssh backends …" (from #88880) asserted the per-profile SSH read; the salvaged commit updates it to the one-call aggregate. ## Tests - `electron/ssh-shared-profile-backend.test.ts`: a listed profile rides the default backend (one roster read, `profile` on the socket URL); pinned / unlisted / older-runtime / default / non-SSH keep the isolated path. - `electron/registry-session-sources.test.ts`: with the SSH primary reused, box/gamma still passes the pinned-source guard and the merged list has both Box and Lan rows. It fails when the collector skips the reused primary (the `896e1fd` logic). - `vitest --project electron`: touched files 189/189 (incl. profile-session-routing, connection-registry); full project 4 failures that also fail on `origin/main` or pass in isolation on head (portal-session-live, checkout-source on both; backend-probes-runtime, source-backend pass alone). `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json`, eslint, `scripts/check --only health` clean. ## Infographic ![ssh-one-backend](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0c920/uaWl2RtB-Ve4d6LZS4QoZ_dGkeGKOb.png)

prs.title: fix: propagate trusted Bot identity through plugin hooks
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A plugin today **cannot implement a secure Bot-to-Bot communication policy**. Two information-flow gaps, one on each side of a Bot Mode DM:

1. **Receiving side — no authorization boundary.** `pre_gateway_dispatch` (the one pre-inference, blockable hook) fires for platform/webhook/relay ingress but **never** for a Bot Mode DM delivery: `message_agent` → `bot_relay.deliver` / `hermes peer dm` → `gateway/session_bot.py` admits straight into the receiving profile's Bot Chat with no plugin pass. And although the receiving turn already tracks the trusted turn author (`agent._turn_author`, stamped by the delivery door and consumed for memory attribution), `pre_llm_call` never received it — so even an observational plugin could not tell a Bot DM from a human turn without parsing message text.

2. **Sending side — authorization on the wrong value.** `pre_tool_call` for `message_agent` sees the model's raw `target` string. The recipient only resolves *after* the hooks fire (roster/friendly-name/@-slug/peer/relay resolution happens inside the tool), so a plugin allowing `watch_tracker` could be bypassed by an alias (`"Tracker"`, `"@tracker"`, `"Dr. Foo"`…), and recipient rewriting had no policy checkpoint at the actual dispatch boundary.

### The fix (smallest change on the existing mechanisms)

- **`pre_llm_call` payload gains `turn_author`** (`agent/turn_context.py`): the door-stamped `{"id", "name", "is_bot"}` every turn already normalizes (`agent/turn_author.py`) — `None` when no door stamped one (unverified), the platform user for chat traffic, `bot:<profile>` for a bot on this install, `bot:<origin>/<profile>` for a remote one. Additive payload: narrow-signature callbacks are unaffected. New helper `agent.turn_author.bot_origin()` classifies `local` vs the origin string (hostname on a peer dm, Desktop connection id when relayed).
- **Bot Mode DM deliveries now offer `pre_gateway_dispatch` before they commit** (`gateway/session_bot.py::_offer_bot_dm_pre_dispatch`, called from `_admit` and `_maybe_retry` before the receipt pin): the same pre-inference authorization boundary platform messages get, under the receiving profile's plugin scope. Trusted sender is `event.metadata["turn_author"]` — never message text or a self-declared flag. A `skip` refuses the delivery as `authorization_refused` with **nothing committed** (no pin, no admission row), so a same-id resend re-evaluates the (possibly changed) policy. The derived retry is a new admission id and gets its own pass. Hook-exception behavior stays the documented gateway contract (fail-open dispatch; a mandatory policy plugin catches its own errors and returns `skip`).
- **`message_agent` runs one `pre_tool_call` pass at the actual dispatch boundary** (`tools/bot_mode_dm.py`), after resolution and before any transport starts (local/peer/relay): hooks receive `bot_sender` (the exact turn-author identity the delivery will carry) and `bot_recipient` (canonical resolved identity — `kind` `local`/`peer`/`remote`, `id` in the same `bot:<profile>` / `bot:<origin>/<profile>` grammar). **Aliases and display names never reach this pass.** A `block` (including `pre_tool_call`'s existing fail-closed timeout/raise behavior) refuses the send with `{"error": ..., "reason": "policy_refused"}` and nothing dispatched. `approve` is not re-escalated (the whole-directive pass already ran before the tool call); `modify` is not applied.

No new hook, no new framework surface: the three existing hooks each get the identity information they were missing, at the point where they can act on it.

None found — searched issues and PRs (open and merged) for `turn_author pre_llm_call` and `bot identity plugin hook` before starting.

- `agent/turn_author.py` — new `bot_origin()` classifier (local / origin string / not-a-bot).
- `gateway/session_bot.py` — `_offer_bot_dm_pre_dispatch` gate wired into `_admit` and `_maybe_retry`; skip → `authorization_refused`, nothing committed.
- `tools/bot_mode_dm.py` — dispatch-boundary `pre_tool_call` pass with `bot_sender`/`bot_recipient` on all three transports (local, peer, Desktop relay), before `_start_delivery`/`enqueue_envelope`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): steer native image follow-ups into active turns
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

With `display.busy_input_mode: steer`, an ordinary image follow-up is queued for a later turn instead of correcting the active run. A screenshot intended to guide ongoing work therefore arrives only after that work finishes.

This change delivers the caption and actual images together to a vision-capable running model at a safe boundary, without cancelling tools. It preserves durable admission and falls back to the original queue when native delivery is unavailable. Acknowledgements describe the actual outcome rather than announcing queueing before image transfer has been attempted.

## Related Issue

Fixes #146835

Related proposals: #75683 steers cached image paths with a `vision_analyze` instruction; #141140 adds opt-in text enrichment for busy media. This proposal instead delivers native image content to the active model under its existing image-input policy. These approaches overlap in user intent; this is not a claim that no related PR exists. Desktop image steering (#97888) and explicit slash-command attachments are outside this change.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/content_steering.py` and turn-loop integration: consume structured image corrections after a complete tool batch or before accepting a final answer, and retain them in conversation history without duplicate delivery.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`, `gateway/run_image_steering.py`, and `gateway/session_ingress_media.py`: persist and deduplicate uploads before generation-bound transfer, using the receiving agent's effective runtime and profile. Retain queued uploads when native preparation or acceptance fails; avoid speculative replay after uncertain writes.
- `gateway/run_inbound.py` and `gateway/run_busy.py`: defer media acknowledgements until transfer resolves. Successful native delivery uses parent-only wording, even when subagents are active; text/voice acknowledgement behavior remains unchanged.
- Add agent and gateway regression coverage for native pixels, policy, transfer, recovery, and enabled acknowledgements; document behavior in `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/index.md`.

Native steering requires a vision-capable running model and a native-image input policy. Unsupported or unread uploads retain their complete original event rather than steering only the caption. Explicit `/queue` remains queued. Codex app-server turns are unsupported.

## How to Test

1. Set `display.busy_input_mode: steer` and select a vision-capable model with native image input.
2. Start a task that keeps the agent busy with tool calls, then send an image with or without a caption into the same conversation.
3. Verify the active run receives the actual image at the next safe boundary, does not cancel its tools, and records the correction once.
4. Verify rejected or unsupported native delivery retains the complete upload for the next turn. Repeat with acknowledgements enabled, disabled, and debounced, and with active subagents.

The full repository suite and CI have not been run.

prs.title: fix(cron): satellite cron delivery reaches the primary's routed bot when a LOCAL adapter exists
prs.body:
## What this fixes A credentialless satellite profile's cron output is supposed to ride the **primary** gateway's adapter for targets an exact, enabled `gateway.profile_routes` entry maps to that profile (#101113, documented in `user-guide/multi-profile-gateways.md`). In practice it never does: - `run_multiplex_ticker.tick_adapters_for()` only built the `SharedRouteAdapters` view when the satellite's own adapter map was **empty**. - The gateway gives **every** served profile a Desktop `local` adapter (Bot Chat), so the map is never empty — the fallback was dead code. - Every routed satellite cron target therefore failed closed with `platform '

' not configured/enabled`, and the job's output was never delivered. Reproduced on macOS, one multiplexed gateway (7 served profiles), Telegram forum-group routes, a credentialless satellite whose job carried `deliver=telegram::` matching an exact route: ``` cron.scheduler: Job '0da07a1e4de8': platform 'telegram' not configured/enabled ``` with `_profile_adapters[''] == {Platform.LOCAL: }`. Fires identically from a scheduled tick and a manual `hermes cron run`, in-process in the gateway. ## Change `cron/scheduler_preflight.py` gains `SatelliteRouteAdapters` (a `SharedRouteAdapters` subclass) and `satellite_route_adapters()`: - a platform the satellite **owns** → its own adapter, no route gate (it is its own bot); - a platform it does **not** own → the primary's adapter only when an exact enabled route authorizes the target; - a route miss stays fail-closed — the primary's bot is never used for an unauthorized target. `tick_adapters_for()` and `_drain_restart_safe_cron_deliveries()` (restart-safe worker queue) use the composition instead of testing for an empty map; the drain no longer skips a satellite outright when it has no adapter-map entry. ## Tests `tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_shared_route_delivery.py`: new regression test drives the **pre-fix** effective input (the satellite's own map alone) to the reported failure, then asserts the composed map delivers through the routed primary adapter, keeps fail-closed behaviour for unrouted/disabled/other-profile targets, and never route-gates an adapter the satellite owns. Two smaller tests cover own-platform precedence and the single-profile passthrough. All 7 tests in that file pass locally (run with `pytest tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_shared_route_delivery.py`). Related open reports: #139825, #141910, #144455.

prs.title: feat(optional-mcps): add clutch MCP catalog entry
prs.body:
## Summary
- Add Clutch's official hosted Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint (`https://bot.clutch.co/mcp`) to the MCP catalog: find and compare B2B service providers (agencies, consultants, vendors), read verified client reviews, and browse fixed-price service packages on Clutch.co.
- Native OAuth 2.1 + DCR via `account.clutch.co`. Search, profile, review and package tools work anonymously; only `send_message_to_provider` requires sign-in.
- Only the 4 read-only tools (`readOnlyHint: true`) are enabled by default. `send_message_to_provider` (`destructiveHint: true`, sends a message to a provider on the user's behalf) stays unchecked until the user selects it with `hermes mcp configure clutch`.
- Adds `contributors/emails/stan@clutch.co` for the Contributor Attribution Check.

## How sign-in works with a mixed anonymous/authenticated server
`initialize` and `tools/list` are served anonymously, so the probe behind `hermes mcp login clutch` never receives a 401 and cannot start OAuth. Sign-in instead starts from the per-tool HTTP 401 (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... resource_metadata=...`) on the first `send_message_to_provider` call in an interactive session, and the token is then cached. `post_install` documents this, including that headless setups (gateway, cron) need one interactive message first to cache a token.

## Validation
- Live `tools/list` on `https://bot.clutch.co/mcp` returns 5 tools: `recommend_service_providers`, `get_provider_info`, `get_service_provider_reviews`, `get_service_packages` (read-only) and `send_message_to_provider`.
- `hermes mcp catalog` lists `clutch`; `hermes mcp install clutch` installs it with the 4 default tools (throwaway `HERMES_HOME`).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_catalog.py` + `test_mcp_catalog_env_boundary.py`: 54 passed; `tests/scripts/test_contributor_map.py`: 9 passed.
- An anonymous `send_message_to_provider` call returns HTTP 401 with `resource_metadata="https://bot.clutch.co/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`, and Hermes's `HermesMCPOAuthProvider` starts the flow from it.

## Known issue (server side, fix in progress)
Our RFC 9728 document currently lists `https://account.clutch.co/` (a trailing slash added by the server framework), while the authorization server's `issuer` is `https://account.clutch.co`. The MCP SDK's RFC 8414 issuer check rejects the mismatch, so **messaging sign-in fails until our fix is deployed**. The read-only tools are unaffected. The fix (serving the issuer verbatim) is done on our side; we'll confirm here once it is live and the full sign-in + send flow passes.

Submitted by the Clutch engineering team from Clutch's GitHub org fork (`clutch-ai`). The same endpoint and OAuth setup already serve ChatGPT and Claude as MCP clients.

prs.title: feat(catalog): add Cartograph repository analysis tools
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds Cartograph to the community catalog. It maps a local repository and retrieves task-focused source excerpts with file paths and line ranges. For example, asking where CLI providers and API keys are validated returns the relevant implementation and tests.

I maintain the plugin and its external runtime. This PR adds only `plugin-catalog/cartograph.yaml`.

## Related Issue

Catalog submission; no linked issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Changes Made

- Pins `assets/hermes` in `anthony-maio/cartograph` at `e2e06db1c79f3de60760d9045ae6908ddf4e4b21`.
- Native plugin version `0.1.0`; requires Hermes `>=0.22.2` and the separately installed npm runtime `@anthony-maio/cartograph@1.3.0` with Node 20+.
- Registers `cartograph_analyze` and `cartograph_context` using public `ctx.register_tool`. Settings use `ctx.get_config`; cache placement uses `ctx.state.data_dir`. No hooks, middleware, environment secrets, or core overrides.
- The pinned [README](https://github.com/anthony-maio/cartograph/blob/e2e06db1c79f3de60760d9045ae6908ddf4e4b21/assets/hermes/README.md) covers setup, configuration, behavior, and access.

## Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H[Hermes tool call] --> P[Native Python plugin]
    P --> N[Configured Node and Cartograph CLI]
    N --> R[Requested local repository]
    N --> C[Profile plugin cache]
    N --> P
    P --> O[Bounded JSON and source line ranges]
```

## Behavior and Access

The plugin starts the configured Node executable with a fixed CLI argument list, without a shell. Child output and runtime are bounded. It reads the requested repository outside its own directory and rejects resolved symlink escapes; optional allowed roots further restrict access. Analysis and source excerpts are cached in the active profile's plugin data directory. Removing the plugin preserves that cache.

Static analysis reads local Git information and makes no model API or intentional web requests. Returned source enters the Hermes conversation and may reach its configured model provider. Repository content is untrusted data. The child environment strips credentials; the plugin reads no credential stores, sends no telemetry, and starts no persistent background service.

The npm runtime is installed explicitly outside the Hermes environment. No dependencies download during a tool call, and the plugin does not update itself. No binary payload or UI is bundled in the plugin directory.

## How to Test

1. Check out the pinned commit and run `hermes plugins validate /path/to/cartograph/assets/hermes --install-deps`.
2. Install the npm runtime, then follow the README's pinned Git installation and `node_path` / `cli_path` configuration.
3. Use both tools on a real repository. Verify returned source against its reported line ranges.

Validation against the pinned tree passed all 15 official plugin checks, with zero warnings and a safe security scan. The catalog entry passed schema validation with zero warnings. On Debian WSL, pinned Git installation, configuration, discovery, native dispatch, accurate source ranges, profile cache isolation, missing-path rejection, and unload all passed. These checks used actual Hermes dispatch; they do not claim autonomous model selection.

Package gates passed: 108 Node tests, 20 Python plugin tests, TypeScript, build, and clean packed-install checks. Release CI passed on Windows and Linux.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide; conventional commit; searched for duplicate PRs.
- [x] One catalog entry, with no unrelated changes.
- [x] Public API and behavior disclosures reviewed; README and schemas included at the pin.
- [x] Tested on Debian WSL and checked cross-platform package behavior.
- [x] Full Hermes core pytest suite and `python scripts/check` were not run for this data-only submission. The official plugin and catalog validators above were run.

- Native plugin version `0.1.0`; requires Hermes `>=0.22.2` and a separate Python 3.10+ environment containing `pulldown==0.5.0`.
- Uses public `ctx.register_tool`, `ctx.get_config`, and `ctx.state.data_dir`. No hooks, middleware, environment secrets, or core overrides.
- The pinned [README](https://github.com/anthony-maio/pulldown/blob/ca16dc479714e59f8b361e8dd1c3714110b9da75/src/pulldown/hermes_plugin/README.md) covers setup, rendering dependencies, behavior, and limitations.

## Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H[Hermes tool call] --> P[Native Python plugin]
    P --> W[Configured external Python worker]
    W --> F[HTTP fetch]
    W --> B[Optional Chromium render]
    F --> C[Profile plugin cache]
    F --> O[Bounded Markdown and metadata]
    B --> O
    O --> P
```

## Behavior and Access

The plugin starts a fixed Python worker with JSON input, without a shell. Workers and browser children have timeouts and bounded output. Requested public pages receive HTTP requests; rendering also requests their subresources. It offers no login cookies, custom headers, proxies, private-address overrides, or disabled TLS verification.

Destinations and HTTP redirects are checked for private addresses. Rendering rejects redirects and blocks workers and WebSockets. DNS checks are not network isolation against rebinding or proxy resolution. The 2 MiB page-content check happens after download; it is not a streaming transfer or process-memory limit.

It reads the configured Python and Chromium installations outside the plugin directory and caches fetched public pages in the active profile's plugin data directory. Rendered requests bypass that cache; uninstall preserves caches. Returned page text enters the Hermes conversation and may reach its model provider. Treat it as untrusted source material.

The worker environment strips ambient credentials and proxies. The plugin reads no credential stores, sends no telemetry, and starts no persistent background service. External PyPI dependencies and optional Chromium are explicit setup steps; the README pins Playwright's release and uses its official browser installer. No packages download during tool calls, no binary payload or UI is bundled in the plugin directory, and the plugin does not update itself.

## How to Test

1. Check out the pinned commit and run `hermes plugins validate /path/to/pulldown/src/pulldown/hermes_plugin --install-deps`.
2. Install the external runtime, then follow the README's pinned Git installation and `python_path` configuration.
3. Fetch Python's asyncio documentation, compare HTTP and rendered output on the [example board](https://pulldown.making-minds.ai/examples/live-board.html), and confirm a loopback URL is rejected.

Validation against the pinned tree passed all 15 official plugin checks, with zero warnings and a safe security scan. The catalog entry passed schema validation with zero warnings. On Debian WSL, pinned Git installation, configuration, discovery, native dispatch, HTTP versus Chromium results, private-address rejection, profile cache isolation, and unload all passed. These checks used actual Hermes dispatch; they do not claim autonomous model selection.

Package gates passed: 207 tests, wheel and sdist metadata validation, and fresh Windows installed-wheel checks covering CLI, MCP, five extraction modes, plugin installation/removal, rendering, and redirect rejection. Release-commit CI passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide; conventional commit; searched for duplicate PRs.
- [x] One catalog entry, with no unrelated changes.
- [x] Public API and behavior disclosures reviewed; README and schemas included at the pin.
- [x] Tested on Debian WSL and Windows.
- [ ] Full Hermes core pytest suite and `python scripts/check` were not run for this data-only submission. The official plugin and catalog validators above were run.

prs.title: fix(tools): allow zero-width joiner inside emoji ZWJ sequences
prs.body:
## Problem

The invisible-unicode scanner (`tools/threat_patterns.py`) flags **any** U+200D (zero-width joiner) via set intersection, with no context awareness. But U+200D is a **required, legitimate part of standard emoji ZWJ sequences** — surfer 🏄‍♂️, family 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, heart-on-fire ❤️‍🔥 — which are structured as `[emoji][U+FE0F]?[U+200D][emoji][U+FE0F]?...`.

Real-world impact: a project context file (`AGENTS.md`, `.hermes.md`) containing one such emoji is dropped wholesale as `invisible_unicode_U+200D` and never reaches the system prompt — reported as 9,437 silent rejections over 30 days in #114047. The same false positive blocks the memory/skill-write path (`first_threat_message`) and any `SKILL.md` (`tools/skills_guard.py` carried the same duplicated check). On current `main` a *user-authored* `SOUL.md` in `HERMES_HOME` warns-and-loads since #112570 — but it still logs a false injection hit on every session start, and a profile-distribution `SOUL.md` (``distribution.yaml``-owned) still blocks outright.

## Fix

Allow U+200D when **every occurrence** sits inside an emoji ZWJ sequence (emoji bases on both sides, skipping optional VS15/VS16). Bare ZWJs glued between plain characters — the classic text-hiding trick — are still flagged.

- `tools/threat_patterns.py`: shared `is_zwj_in_emoji_sequence()` / `zwj_is_emoji_only()`; the neighbour test is derived from the Unicode emoji properties (`Extended_Pictographic` ∪ `Emoji_Modifier`, generated from `emoji-data.txt` 18.0) rather than a hand-rolled codepoint block list, so skin-tone modifiers and pictographic partners outside the old blocks are handled.
- `tools/skills_guard.py`: same rule in the per-line invisible-char check (imports the shared helper so the two scanners can't drift). `SCANNER_VERSION` → `v7` — main already shipped v6 for a different detection change.
- `tools/cronjob_prompt_scan.py`: drops its private copy of the predicate and imports the shared one, so the cron tripwire, the context-file scanner and the install scanner share one definition.
- The exception is scoped to U+200D only — all other invisible/bidi codepoints are flagged exactly as before.

## Tests

- `test_threat_patterns.py`: emoji ZWJ allowed (surfer, family, teacher, black cat, head-shaking, skin-toned worker), bare ZWJ between ASCII still detected, one-sided emoji+ZWJ still detected, mixed emoji+bare still detected, zero-width space next to an emoji still detected, VS15/VS16 skipped on either side.
- `test_skills_guard.py`: SKILL.md with emoji ZWJ is clean; SKILL.md with a bare ZWJ still yields `invisible_unicode`.
- `test_cronjob_tools.py`: the cron tripwire accepts the partners the old block list missed and still strips/blocks a bare joiner.

All 195 tests across the three affected files pass (2 skipped); `ruff check` clean.

## Rebased and re-measured (current `main`: `81279c5279`)

Re-implemented against the tree as it is now, not mechanically rebased. The two conflicts: a `SCANNER_VERSION` v6/v6 collision (this change now takes v7) and main's deletion of the `test_invisible_chars_set_is_frozenset` change-detector pin (main's deletion kept, the ZWJ tests added beside it).

- RGI ZWJ corpus (`emoji-zwj-sequences.txt`, 1614 sequences containing U+200D): **1614 accepted / 0 flagged**, versus 0 accepted / 1614 flagged on unpatched main.
- Negative controls still flagged 8/8: `pay\u200dload`, `A\u200d<emoji>`, `<emoji>\u200dA`, `→\u200d→`, `1\u200d2`, VS16-only flank, U+200B next to an emoji, CJK `\u200d` CJK. A mixed line (legitimate sequence + bare joiner) still reports `invisible_unicode_U+200D`.
- E2E through the real consumer (`agent/prompt_builder._scan_context_content`): a `.hermes.md` containing 🐈‍⬛ is BLOCKED before / LOADED after; an `AGENTS.md` with a bare joiner is still BLOCKED.
- Fail-on-unpatched proof: 7 of the new tests fail against unpatched main (4 threat_patterns, 1 skills_guard, 2 cron).

prs.title: feat(desktop): unify every new-session gesture on openNewSessionTab
prs.body:
## What

The tab-strip "+" and the new-session shortcut were two different functions minting two different artifacts: `openNewSessionTab` created a real, unlisted session that fell back to `sessionTitle()`'s **"Untitled session"**, while `session.new` (⌘N / alt+N) was a pure view-reset draft reading the **"New session"** placeholder — and the "+"-created tab never painted the new-session splash because `shouldShowIntro` gated on `primary`.

One creation path now serves every "new chat" gesture:

- **`session.new` (⌘N / alt+N), the sidebar New Session row, the command palette and ⌘T all dispatch the same `openNewSessionTab`** — a real, unlisted session fronts the workspace as its own tab; the previously occupied chat survives as its own tab. The pure view-reset draft (`startFreshSessionDraft`) remains for the gateway-event fresh-session flows.
- **Minting from a workspace page (Settings, Profiles, …) leaves the page** for the primary chat's session route (or the new-chat route when no session is selected), so the new tab is never hidden behind an overlay route (`leaveWorkspacePageForChat`).
- **Draft title unified on "New session"**: unlisted draft stubs are stamped `NEW_SESSION_TITLE` client-side, so every surface resolving them via `ownerLookupSessionRows` (`tileTitle()`, the document header) reads "New session", not "Untitled session". The backend row stays untitled, so derived/llm auto-titling still lands on the first exchange. Stub helpers live in a topical sibling (`unlisted-owners.ts`); the sidebar handler in `select-sidebar-item.ts` — both their old homes sit on code-health ratchets that may only go down.
- **The splash paints for draft sessions too**, via a tested predicate (`isDraftSessionRow` in `draft-session.ts`): a row must positively exist and carry an explicit zero `message_count`, so a resumed-but-not-yet-loaded session never flashes the splash next to its loading spinner. Hidden rows (canonical Bot Chat, group plumbing) and bot-scoped chats are excluded — their empty state belongs to the owning plugin's `CHAT_EMPTY_AREA` contribution, not the Hermes splash.

## Notes / tradeoffs

- ⌘N now requires the gateway (it performs a real `session.create`); without one it surfaces the existing create-failure notification instead of an offline blank draft. Repeated presses reuse the one blank draft (`frontUntouchedDraftTab`), so no twin minting.
- `KeybindRuntimeDeps.startFreshSession` is removed — the keybind map no longer calls it; test mocks updated, and `tool-pane-toggle`'s ⌘N test models the unified flow (fronts the new session's tile pane; the terminal stays open behind its tab).

## Tests

- `intro-visibility.test.ts`: draft-session suite (tile + primary binding, emptiness, aux-window and toggle gates, non-draft bypass).
- `draft-session.test.ts`: the draft predicate — explicit-zero acceptance, unknown-session / undefined-count / hidden-row / bot-scoped rejections.
- `new-session-tab-route-leave.test.ts`: page-leave behavior (no-op off pages, session route on selection, new-chat fallback).
- `unlisted-draft-title.test.ts`: stub placeholder title, owner-lookup visibility, same-id replacement.
- `use-keybinds-browser.test.tsx`: alt+N and alt+T (and the ⌃⌘ defaults) assert the shared action.
- `npm run typecheck` green; `eslint` clean on all touched files; `python scripts/check --only health` green (ChatViewContent, ContribWiring and the session-actions ratchets all offset via topical-sibling moves).

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add handydandy
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/handydandy.yaml`, submitted by the owner of [percyhendrux123-prog/hermes-handydandy](https://github.com/percyhendrux123-prog/hermes-handydandy) (MIT).

Long sessions get slow, expensive and forgetful. handydandy watches the estimated input tokens and message count Hermes already reports. When a limit is reached it either adds one notice to the reply (`advise`, the default), or, in `handoff` mode, asks the agent on your next message to finish your request and write a structured `HANDOFF-*.md` file. You open the next session yourself with `from handoff <path>`. It makes no extra model calls and never starts a session on its own.

| | |
|---|---|
| Repo | [`percyhendrux123-prog/hermes-handydandy`](https://github.com/percyhendrux123-prog/hermes-handydandy), repo root, MIT |
| Pin | [`7cc035707f18590db3957fbcc73e3e4064bc8f38`](https://github.com/percyhendrux123-prog/hermes-handydandy/tree/7cc035707f18590db3957fbcc73e3e4064bc8f38) (v0.3.0) |
| `requires_hermes` | `>=0.22.5`, declared in the entry and in `plugin.yaml` |

## Hermes surfaces used

- Python plugin: `register()` registers three hooks: `pre_api_request`, `transform_llm_output` and `pre_llm_call`. No tools, middleware, skills, providers or Desktop code.
- Settings come through `ctx.get_config` and the `config_schema` in `plugin.yaml`.
- No private core imports (it does not import `agent.model_metadata`) and no runtime rebinds of core.
- No dependencies outside the standard library.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Writes:** `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/handydandy/` — `state.json`, `state.lock`, `events.log`, and short-lived `.state.<pid>.<thread>.tmp` files during atomic saves. These hold profile/session ids, paths, thresholds and error details, never conversation text.
- **Asks the agent to write:** `HANDOFF-*.md` files in `handoff_dir` (default `<HERMES_HOME>/handoffs/`). These can contain work details from the conversation; the agent is told not to copy secret values. The writing happens in the agent's normal turn under normal tool approvals.
- **Optional:** one row per completed handoff appended to a `session_log_csv` the owner sets. Off by default.
- **Reads:** its own state and lock, the last byte of `events.log` before appending, the size, modification time and first byte of recorded handoff files, plugin settings, and `HANDYDANDY_<KEY>` / `HERMES_HOME` from the environment. It does not read the session database, transcripts or credential files.
- **No** network calls, shell commands, background processes, stored credentials or telemetry. It does not auto-approve tools or change safety settings.
- Known limits are listed under `known_issues`: handoff mode is an instruction rather than a guarantee, the percentage check needs `context_limit` set, and the state keeps the 200 most recent session records.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

1. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/handydandy.yaml` returns `OK: 1 file(s) valid` locally (full directory: `OK: 911 file(s) valid`).
2. `hermes plugins validate .` against a fresh clone at the pinned sha returns `Validation passed` on Hermes 0.22.5.
3. `python -m pytest -q tests` in the repo: 26 passed.
4. Live check: set `HANDYDANDY_MAX_MESSAGES=4`, enable the plugin, chat for a few turns, and confirm one notice appears; switch `mode` to `handoff` and confirm the agent writes a handoff file at the stated path.

## How it was made

I designed it, set the rules for what it may do, and run it on my own agent team. AI agents wrote the code to my spec and under my review, and an independent code review signed off on v0.3.0 before this submission.

prs.title: fix(nix): don't stamp a placeholder release version on a tagless pin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`nix/hermes-agent.nix` stamps `baseVersion = version`, and `version` defaults to `"0.0.0"` — a **placeholder,
not a release version**. For a tagless pin (a moving branch revision) that is worse than stamping nothing:
`"0.0.0"` parses as a real version and compares as *older than every requirement*.

The chain, read in-tree rather than inferred:

```
plugins_manifest.running_hermes_version()                      # hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py:461
  -> hermes_cli.version_info.get_version_info().base_version   # version_info.py:171: data.get("baseVersion") or "unknown"
  -> version_satisfies(spec, current)                          # plugins_manifest.py:486: unparseable => permissive
```

So with the placeholder, **every plugin manifest declaring `requires_hermes` is un-installable and un-loadable**
on a Nix install pinned to a branch — `requires_hermes_error` is load-blocking. The same install with no stamp at
all would have worked, which is what makes this worth fixing rather than documenting.

The fix adds `isRelease ? false` and selects the tagless convention the repo already defines in two places:

- `scripts/write_install_stamp.py` (~line 201): *"No reachable release tag: record the commit, the way a tagless
  checkout reads from Git."*
- `scripts/verify-bootstrap-version-stamp.py:152`: *"baseVersion is null when no release tag is reachable."*

i.e. record the commit, leave `baseVersion` unset so the runtime reads `"unknown"`, and leave `tag` null.
`isRelease = true` together with a real `version` preserves today's behaviour for a build pinned to a release tag.

**Files:** `nix/hermes-agent.nix`

## Related Issue

No issue filed. The observable symptom is that plugin manifests declaring `requires_hermes` fail to install and
fail to load on a Nix install pinned to a branch revision. (Related in effect to #140765 — `hermes plugins enable`
on Nix — but that cause is the PM/uv path, not the version stamp.) Happy to file one if you'd prefer that route.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `nix-instantiate --parse nix/hermes-agent.nix` → parses.
- The reader chain above was read in this tree, not assumed: a null `baseVersion` becomes `"unknown"` at
  `version_info.py:171`, and `version_satisfies` returns `True` for an unparseable current version, so the gate
  cannot block. `plugins_manifest.running_hermes_version()` is the function the gate actually calls
  (`plugins_manifest.py:507`), which is why this field and not another.
- Cherry-picked onto current `origin/main` (`088f657ecf`): one trivially cosmetic conflict (main reflowed the
  `stampDistance` if/else and collapsed `writeText … (builtins.toJSON {…})` onto one line — same expressions,
  new line breaks), resolved by keeping main's formatting with the semantic edits spliced in.
- `python scripts/check --only health --base origin/main` → ok.

## Reviewer note (deliberately out of scope)

`hermes_cli/__init__.py` (`__getattr__` for `__version__`, lines ~36 and ~39) still coerces a null `baseVersion`
to `"0.0.0"`. That is a **display** path — banner, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`, the plugin-host digest — not the
gating path fixed here, and `__version__` is consumed by shipped older updaters, so changing its fallback is a
separate judgement call. Flagging it rather than smuggling it into this diff.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump honcho to 1.1.0 (pin 7dd3702)
prs.body:
`sha` `2108daf` → `7dd3702`, `version` `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`, and `image:` follows the pin. The description is unchanged.

This bump fixes catalog installs and updates of honcho. At `2108daf`, `hermes plugins install honcho` and `hermes plugins update honcho` fail at `uv lock` (plastic-labs/honcho#1485), and a restart over those files moves honcho to `plugins.disabled`.

`version` now matches `plugin.yaml` at the pin. The plugin had said `1.0.0` since it was added, so every earlier pin, including the broken `2108daf`, showed the same version in `hermes plugins list` and in its `X-Honcho-Plugin` header.

## What moved

The range `2108daf..7dd3702` touches `hermes-plugin-honcho/` in five commits. `[project].dependencies` and the declared capabilities are unchanged; `plugin.yaml` changes only its `version`.

- plastic-labs/honcho#1488 ([`5ca089e`](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho/commit/5ca089e70ac0b3ad6888086500dd68ce5c173039)): removes the `test` dependency group and its `extra-build-variables` from the plugin's `pyproject.toml`. The group pinned `hermes-agent` from git, and uv parses every workspace member's groups when PM locks, so the lock failed with "`hermes-agent` is included as a workspace member, but is missing an entry in `tool.uv.sources`". The test environment moves to `tests/pyproject.toml`, `tests/uv.lock` and `tests/.python-version`; PM reads only the plugin's top-level `pyproject.toml`. This corrects #145212, which said the group left installs unchanged.
- plastic-labs/honcho#1461 ([`18fe5dd`](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho/commit/18fe5dd10a3b1bdc1195b5b2554f37eff3a56ddf)): `sync_turn` drops a turn whose content starts with `[Group chat:` or `[Discussion:` (Bot Mode group chats and hosted-room Discussions), so those orchestration prompts are no longer stored as user speech.
- plastic-labs/honcho#1487 ([`105093e`](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho/commit/105093e301b38f5d8ea1e7fe9887808c8a2b912f)): local gateway keys (`agent:<namespace>:local:...`, used by CLI, TUI, Desktop and ACP) follow the configured `sessionStrategy` instead of getting one Honcho session per chat. Messaging-platform keys keep per-chat isolation. After updating, new local chats write to the session their strategy names (the directory's, by default).
- plastic-labs/honcho#1490 ([`f8d1fc9`](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho/commit/f8d1fc9fe52556a86b70c7115f35ca420dee2abd)): `honcho_search` also falls back to peer-authored search when the `peer_perspective` search returns empty, which Honcho servers before v3.1.0 can do for history the peer was present for. The fallback no longer creates a peer.
- plastic-labs/honcho#1499 ([`7dd3702`](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho/commit/7dd3702933d5cc1ce1f0a44bba6525cc61ee6e16)): `version` 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 in `plugin.yaml` and `pyproject.toml`, so the plugin now sends `X-Honcho-Plugin: hermes-plugin-honcho/1.1.0`.

## Disclosure

Unchanged. #1461 sends less: harness turns are no longer synced. #1490's fallback is a second search call to the same Honcho API under the same key.

## Verified

Hermes 8acb7f6 in a clean Docker sandbox, with the live catalog blocked and the in-tree `honcho.yaml` pinned:

- At `7dd3702`: `hermes plugins update honcho` from an install at `e2d2aba`, and again from `f8d1fc9`, both print `✓ Plugin honcho updated to 7dd37029.`, and `hermes plugins list` shows honcho enabled at `1.1.0`.
- At `f8d1fc9`, whose plugin tree differs from `7dd3702` only in the version fields and `tests/uv.lock`:
  - Starting the gateway after the update (`hermes gateway ensure`) leaves honcho enabled, with no `plugins.disabled_by_update` entry.
  - A fresh `hermes plugins install honcho --yes-deps --enable` installs, enables it and sets it as `memory.provider`. `hermes memory status` lists only `HONCHO_API_KEY` as missing.
  - `hermes plugins validate` on the installed tree: `Validation passed`. It warns about private core imports (rule 9); this range adds none, its only new import being `from honcho import Peer` from the Honcho SDK.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/honcho.yaml`: `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.

Not run: a chat turn against a live Honcho.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add Decisions predicate API plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Add `decisions`, a community standalone predicate-only OpenAI Decisions API plugin for Hermes. Source is MIT-licensed, publicly cloneable, and pinned to `eeac2eac98a3d1f566dc020912bb378aece431f8` (version 0.1.0, deliberately pre-release).

- `decisions_submit`: background by default, optional foreground.
- `decisions_status`: session/home-owned structured decoded JSON results.
- No Hermes core patches, self-updater, persistent queue, recovery service, or telemetry.
- Requires Hermes >=0.22.5, matching the manifest; tested against release bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e.

## Disclosures

- Network: sends submitted text/questions, model and scoped bearer key to the configured endpoint; defaults to `https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions` / `gpt-6-luna`. Requests can be billable. Alternate endpoints require explicit matching credential-destination configuration. No ambient proxy auth, redirects or retries.
- Credentials: declared `OPENAI_API_KEY` / native secret field; read only via Hermes `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`. No credential-file access/storage, subscription-token extraction or OAuth handling.
- Background: one context-preserving daemon thread/asyncio loop per loaded plugin, native task leases; max 4 active requests, 32 terminal results, volatile memory only. Best-effort origin completion injection requires native consent; acceptance is not a delivery guarantee.
- No shell execution or plugin filesystem-content reads. Hermes owns config/secret retrieval. HTTPX >=0.23,<0.29 is the only declared runtime dependency, compatible with Hermes's 0.28.1 pin.
- Restart/unload loses jobs. Timeout/transport interruption may leave remote outcome uncertain; no automatic resubmission.

## Validation

- 44 isolated native discovery/dispatch + deterministic loopback HTTP journeys passed against released Hermes v0.22.5 using Python 3.14.7/httpx 0.28.1. Tests cover background post-return liveness, structured results, profile/session ownership, scoped credentials, notices/consent, foreground, transport failures, bounds, retention, capacity and unload.
- Independent source review found no blocking source defect. Noninstalling native validation passed: security scan `safe`, capabilities match, no core overrides.
- Admission warning disclosed rather than hidden: `worker.py:11` imports `gateway.session_context.get_session_env` (explicitly documented in the public plugin guide) and `async_delivery_supported` (available in the tested release, a compatibility coupling without an equivalent dedicated public plugin-doc section). README documents both.
- Exact native `plugins validate <candidate> --install-deps --json` passed in a disposable released-Hermes environment. Native PM actually committed a fresh dependency generation (PM outcome `ok`, rebuild successful); the capability probe ran with its selected Python 3.14.9/httpx 0.28.1. No managed runtime generation was changed. Candidate hashes remained unchanged.
- Anonymous HTTPS clone at the pinned SHA matched all published source hashes. Public repository has clean source-only history; no private configuration/history is included.

Live direct OpenAI inference and delivery across every transport are not claimed. The plugin intentionally supports only string input and unnamed predicates, a subset of the upstream API; no choice/score/images. Maintainer admission/merge is requested, not assumed.

## Tool icon update

Both tools now register the Unicode balance emoji (⚖️). A native discovery/registry regression test verifies both icons; all 44 tests pass and changed-code STANDARD quality passes. Runtime dependencies and transport/worker behavior are unchanged; the previous dependency-installation receipt covers those unchanged inputs.

## What does this PR do?

The sidebar navigation spends six full-width rows on destinations most people learn once. This renders the group as a six-column grid of square icon tiles, so the same six entries cost one line of height, and a nav entry contributed by a plugin lands in the next free cell instead of appending another row.

Labels move into the tooltip `SidebarMenuButton` already renders for the collapsed rail. That tooltip was gated on `state !== 'collapsed'`, so it never appeared while the rail was expanded: the tiles pass `hidden: false` to opt out of the gate, and `aria-label` carries the name for assistive tech. Nothing else in the sidebar changes, every other row keeps the collapsed-only gate.

## Related Issue

No tracking issue: this is a small Desktop layout change with no bug behind it. Happy to file one first if the project wants it recorded.

prs.title: Add Nous Girl to the plugin catalog
prs.body:
Adds **Nous Girl** to the plugin catalog: a Desktop-only theme with real light and dark palettes, plus matching CLI skins.

## What the package does

- Registers **one** theme through the Desktop plugin SDK (`THEMES_AREA`): a light palette in `colors` and a dark one in `darkColors`, achromatic surfaces built from value rather than hue, and `terminal`/`darkTerminal` so the desktop terminal pane matches. The Desktop keeps its own fonts and layout — the palettes carry no art and no typography override.
- Injects **no CSS**, touches no DOM, no `MutationObserver`, no network, no background process. It is a palette, not an overlay: everything it paints comes from the theme contract.
- Ships two optional CLI/TUI skins (`nous-girl-light`, `nous-girl-dark`) as plain YAML files. Hermes only reads skins from `~/.hermes/skins/`, so the README tells the user to copy them once after installing and again after updates. Both skins carry `banner_hero` and `banner_logo`, and every ramp stop is a value from that skin's own palette, so the banner art and the Hermes wordmark do not fall back to `HERMES_AGENT_LOGO` and its hardcoded gold.
- Ships an inert `__init__.py` whose `register()` does nothing, so the Agent loader imports the package cleanly instead of logging `No __init__.py`. It registers zero tools and zero hooks.

## Disclosure

Theme-only plugin. No network requests, no credentials, no files read or written, no shell commands, no background processes, no settings page, and no agent tools, hooks or middleware. The only user-visible side effect outside the theme picker is that selecting a CLI skin sets `display.skin` for the active profile, which is how Hermes stores that choice and is documented in the README.

## Verification

At the pinned commit (`227ec2d`), from a clean clone of the repository:

- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` → passes every check, including `security scan — safe`, `no core override`, `desktop surface` and the capability probe; `0 tool(s), 0 hook(s)`.
- `node --check desktop/plugin.js` → clean.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` from this PR → `OK`.

The test suite (`node --test tests/`, 24/24) runs in the development working copy; `.gitignore` keeps it out of the published tree, so the pinned clone ships the manifest, the Desktop theme, the two skins and the images — nothing else. It covers the registration contract (exactly one theme, the 26-key palette in both modes, no DOM observers or injected styles), WCAG AA contrast for interface and terminal in both modes (4.5:1 text, 3:1 controls, icons and focus states), the skins' 38-key schema, banner geometry (15 rows of at most 30 cells, 6-row wordmark) and a cross-check that keeps every value shared by the skins and `desktop/plugin.js` identical.

## Notes on the pin

`version: "0.1.1"` matches `plugin.yaml` at the pinned commit. `images/cover.png` is 1200×600 — exact 2:1 for the catalog card; the gallery carries the CLI and both Desktop modes, captured from the actual app window.

I own the upstream repository and will bump the pin in a new PR for each release.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add hermes-tabs
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/hermes-tabs.yaml`, submitted by the owner of [ai-ag2026/hermes-tabs](https://github.com/ai-ag2026/hermes-tabs) (MIT).

hermes-tabs lets Hermes work in individual tabs of the user's real, signed-in Chromium browser (Chrome, Vivaldi, Edge, Brave): a Manifest V3 extension built on `chrome.debugger` connects outward to a small MCP relay, which Hermes uses as the MCP server `tabs`. Permissions (which tabs, which websites) are enforced inside the extension, and the user sees an overlay and can stop the agent in the tab.

The catalog entry is only the Hermes plugin in `hermes-plugin/`. It adds a settings page in nine languages that follows the language set in Hermes (which browser Hermes works in when several are connected to the relay, master switch, safety level and switches — tightening applies at once, loosening must be confirmed by the human in the browser — default for all websites, temporary "allow all", allowed and blocked sites) and a `pre_tool_call` guard. The extension and the relay are installed from the repository as described in its README.

| | |
|---|---|
| Repo | [`ai-ag2026/hermes-tabs`](https://github.com/ai-ag2026/hermes-tabs), `subdir: hermes-plugin`, MIT |
| Pin | [`05d4a3c5c224cc1dbe575928f8ca2d04aa3abf55`](https://github.com/ai-ag2026/hermes-tabs/tree/05d4a3c5c224cc1dbe575928f8ca2d04aa3abf55/hermes-plugin) (plugin 0.4.1) |
| `requires_hermes` | `>=0.22.5`, declared in the entry and in `plugin.yaml` |

## Hermes surfaces used

- Python plugin: `register()` registers one hook, `pre_tool_call`. No tools, middleware, skills or providers.
  - Switched off in the settings: calls to `mcp__tabs__*` are rejected early.
  - Opt-in, off by default: blocked sites also apply to Hermes' own `browser_exec`, `browser_cdp` and `web_extract` when the domain appears in the arguments.
  - Hosts in `HERMES_TABS_OWN_HOSTS` (the agent's own UI) are never operated, so the agent cannot grant itself permissions through the browser.
- Dashboard backend routes (`dashboard/plugin_api.py`) that proxy GET/POST of the settings and the browser choice to the relay.
- Desktop plugin (`desktop/plugin.js`): one settings page via `ctx.registerSettingsPage`, using only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` components, `ctx.rest` and `ctx.setInterval`.
- `HERMES_TABS_ADMIN_TOKEN` is declared under `requires_env` and read with `agent.secret_scope.get_secret_str`.
- No dependencies outside the standard library, no private core imports, no runtime rebinds of core.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Network:** HTTP requests only to the hermes-tabs relay the user configures (`HERMES_TABS_RELAY`, default `http://127.0.0.1:8766`), paths `/admin/settings` and `/admin/select` (picks the browser Hermes works in), with `HERMES_TABS_ADMIN_TOKEN`. No third-party services, no telemetry.
- **Writes:** `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/hermes-tabs/settings.json`, a cache of the last seen settings of the browser Hermes works in, so the guard keeps working while the browser is closed.
- **Reads:** that cache, `HERMES_TABS_RELAY`, `HERMES_TABS_OWN_HOSTS` and `HERMES_HOME` from the environment, and the admin token through the secret scope. No other files or credential stores.
- **No** shell commands, background processes, self-updates or stored credentials. It does not auto-approve tools or change safety settings.
- The browser control itself happens in the separate extension and relay (outside the plugin). It is documented in the repository README, including its limits: no CAPTCHAs, password entry off by default (only the user can switch it on, with confirmation in the browser), per-site permission before clicks and typing.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

1. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-tabs.yaml` returns `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
2. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps hermes-plugin` against a fresh clone at the pinned sha returns `Validation passed` on Hermes 0.22.5 (security scan safe, no core override, desktop surface inside the SDK).
3. `hermes plugins doctor hermes-tabs` on a live install: runtime discovery, import and registration pass, 1 hook.
4. The repository's end-to-end test (`smoke_test.py`, headless Chromium with the extension and relay) passes at the pinned sha.
5. Live use on Hermes 0.22.5 with Vivaldi on Windows 11: the settings page shows and changes the extension's values. The guard's decisions are covered by the self-test `python3 hermes-plugin/__init__.py`.

## How it was made

I designed it, set the rules for what it may and may not do, and run it with my own Hermes agent. The code was written with AI assistance (Claude Code) to my spec and under my review, including an independent critical review before the first public release.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add limits-monitor
prs.body:
## Summary
Adds `limits-monitor`, a read-only Hermes Desktop pane that displays provider allowance windows already exposed by Hermes for reachable profiles. It uses only the public Desktop SDK RPC surface (`profiles.list` with `include_sessions: false`, `host.profileRoutes()` / `host.requestProfile()`, and `host.request('model.options', ...)`); it declares no tools, hooks, middleware, environment variables, or plugin backend.

This is an independent, narrower implementation—not derived from the catalog's `ai-usage-tracker`. It displays only allowance fields returned by Hermes and does not make provider-specific usage requests or handle credentials itself.

## Rule 13 disclosures
- **Network:** No plugin-owned calls to vendor or other third-party endpoints; no telemetry. Requests use Hermes's existing RPC surface. For a remote profile, its `model.options` request goes to that profile's configured Hermes gateway, which may perform its normal provider refresh/cache behavior.
- **Reads:** Profile names via `profiles.list` (`include_sessions: false`) and allowance metadata via `model.options`. No session lists, transcripts, chat contents, credential files, `.env`, `auth.json`, cookies, or keychains.
- **Shell/processes:** No shell commands or separate backend/worker process. Polling runs only while the pane is visible: two initial attempts five seconds apart, then every two minutes.
- **Persistence:** No plugin-owned persistent storage, credential storage, raw-response logging, or telemetry; results remain in the in-memory query cache.
- **Screenshot:** The original, unredacted capture is included in the repo and embedded in its README; it visibly shows the `default` profile label, live quota percentages, progress bars, and reset times.

## Validation
- `npm test`: 17/17 passed.
- `node --check desktop/plugin.js`: passed.
- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps`: passed on the pinned release copy.
- Catalog entry validator: `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
- `npm pack --dry-run --json`: exact reviewed five-file allowlist.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/olympus.yaml`. It pins [`AIEngineerX/Olympus`](https://github.com/AIEngineerX/Olympus) at `fbf7a8c1114f62a6dbc7e378045b17bc86e515f3` (release [v2.0.1](https://github.com/AIEngineerX/Olympus/releases/tag/v2.0.1)), repo root, `category: desktop`, `tier: community`.

Olympus is a dashboard plugin for operators who run several Hermes agents (profiles) with cron jobs and Kanban workers and find out late that one failed, stalled, or is waiting on them. One tab in the Hermes dashboard, plus a Hermes Desktop page:

| Surface | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `dashboard/manifest.json`, `dashboard/dist/index.js`, `dashboard/dist/style.css` | The Olympus tab: agent roster, the Needs-you queue, per-agent inspector, Performance view. Hand-written SDK React, no build step |
| `dashboard/plugin_api.py` | FastAPI router mounted at `/api/plugins/olympus/`; reads Hermes' stores and builds every view |
| `desktop/plugin.js` | Hermes Desktop page, plugin SDK only |
| `__init__.py` | `register()` adds one CLI command, `hermes olympus` (alerts). No tools, hooks or middleware |
| `alerts/olympus_alerts.py` | Script for an opt-in Hermes no-agent cron job that delivers new alerts (no model runs) |

Controls (pause, resume or run a cron job; answer, retry, reclaim or reassign a Kanban task) are confirmed in the UI, logged under the plugin's own data, and executed by Hermes' own dashboard endpoints (`/api/cron/jobs/<id>/pause|resume|trigger`) and the Kanban plugin API. `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off.

The problems it targets, with the Hermes issues showing people have them, are in the repo's [`PRODUCT.md`](https://github.com/AIEngineerX/Olympus/blob/fbf7a8c1114f62a6dbc7e378045b17bc86e515f3/PRODUCT.md).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Reads Hermes' own stores read-only, across every profile under `HERMES_HOME`: `state.db` (sessions, messages), cron jobs and their run output, the Kanban database, gateway state, `config.yaml`, skills, and the cron ledger. Every SQLite store is opened read-only.
- Writes only under `plugin-data/olympus/` (alert state, the fixes and actions log).
- Never opens a profile's `.env`. Configured gateway platforms come from Hermes' own helper (`hermes_cli.profile_channels.channel_platforms_configured`). `hermes plugins validate` reports that import as a rule 9 warning (private core import); there is no documented public API for "which platforms are configured" today. If a maintainer prefers, I will open an issue asking for that seam and drop to config.yaml-only until it exists.
- No network calls to third-party services. The page talks only to the Hermes dashboard it is served from. No shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry, no self-updater.
- Local labels, task titles, agent questions and file paths stay hidden unless `dashboard.olympus.expose_local_labels: true`; payloads are redacted before they leave the API.
- The alert cron job is opt-in: `hermes olympus install-alerts --deliver <target>` copies the script into `$HERMES_HOME/scripts/` and prints the `hermes cron create --no-agent` command for the user to run.

## Related Issue

None. This is a new catalog entry. It supersedes #53951, which bundled Olympus into core; that PR should be closed in favour of this listing.
