## What does this PR do?

First presentation tranche for #146434: show configured agent names consistently on Desktop profile/settings/capability surfaces, the Web scope switcher/banner, and canonical gateway rooms. Encoded profile IDs remain the routing, permission and storage identity.

This deliberately does **not** claim every surface is covered or change profile identity.

## Related Issue

Partially addresses #146434. Display-name uniqueness and remaining surfaces are outside this tranche; this PR should not close the whole issue. Existing no-name fallback policies are preserved, not redesigned.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking presentation change)
- [x] Tests (behavioral regression coverage)

## Changes Made

- Resolve configured names with `profileVisibleName()`: flat/nested Bot title → core `display_name` → canonical fallback. Export it through the Desktop plugin SDK rather than crossing plugin import fences. Ordinary/Desktop Settings/Web keep `default` when no name is configured; Bot Mode's existing humanization and `Hermes` fallback are untouched.
- Route Desktop `profileLabel`, Settings scope and single-connection capability labels through configured-name resolution; preserve the capability selector's existing `Hermes (default)` fallback and keep selector values canonical.
- Preserve profile metadata in Web's `ProfileProvider`, refresh labels on window focus without reapplying the management target, and use names in the switcher/banner. Keep the empty clear-scope sentinel and canonical URL/API parameters. Reuse `ProfileNameMetadata` in the Web API profile type.
- Include configured visible member names when creating canonical groups; leave absent labels omitted so the gateway's existing handle fallback applies. Omit over-limit actor labels instead of failing the whole creation.
- Resolve existing room labels using `profiles.list` on the room's own captured authority. Apply a read-time projection to seated local members, authors, working state and pending actions, with stored actor/member fallbacks when metadata is unavailable. Never borrow a foreground/local name for a peer.
- Preserve stored rooms/logs, member IDs, profiles, frozen handles/targets, approval request IDs and execution generations. No database migration or history rewrite.

## How to Test

1. Use separate test profiles with different Bot titles and core display names, a core-display-name-only profile, and an unnamed default. Inspect profile/settings/capability labels.
2. In Web, select a named profile: the switcher and scope banner should display its name while the URL and API scope retain its canonical ID. Return to "this dashboard" to clear explicit management scope. Refocus after changing a title in another surface.
3. Create a canonical group and inspect member names. Also open an older/synthetic room whose stored labels are absent or equal to IDs: current names should render without changing stored member IDs or frozen handles. Verify lookup failure and peer identity isolation with the regression tests.

### Automated verification

On macOS with Node 26:

- Desktop, Web and shared typechecks pass.
- Desktop targeted regression suites: 12 files / 137 tests pass, including ordinary/default scope, canonical groups, plugin installation/ownership, local-model surfaces and upstream Bot label behavior.
- Web: 70 files / 478 tests pass, including a regression that keeps the unnamed dashboard default and non-humanized canonical fallback.
- Shared: 16 files / 182 tests pass. The naming matrix is in Desktop's CI-collected `profile-label.test.ts`, not an ungated shared-only test file.
- ESLint on the changed files: zero errors; warnings remain (including padding warnings in the new group workspace test).
- `python scripts/check --staged --base fcc26fbd9f1641755e49793d7ed608f3b7214c3d`: all 14 checks pass on the complete candidate, including the oversized-file/code-health ratchet.

The earlier full Desktop UI run exited **1**: 1480 of 1481 files passed, 12528 tests passed and 9 were skipped. Its one failed suite was a 60s `beforeAll` timeout in `hidden-bots.test.ts`; that suite passed 9/9 in a separate 10s run. This is disclosed as a full-run failure, not an all-green full-suite claim.

### Manual verification

The initial presentation tranche was exercised in the development Electron app and built Web dashboard against a real, isolated, credential-free test gateway: new-group member labels, a synthetic legacy-ID-label group's read-time projection, and Web's visible-name/canonical-URL split. The fallback-compatibility amendment was reverified with automated tests/types/lint, not a fresh GUI pass. No fake gateway responses or model replies were substituted. Real inference/approval flows and packaged installers were not manually exercised.

## Known follow-ups / non-goals

- No display-name uniqueness enforcement, profile rename, identity migration or new alias scheme.
- No new default-name or creation policy: Bot Mode retains its upstream humanized fallback, while ordinary Profile/Web labels retain their upstream canonical fallback. These differences are deliberately not part of this repair. Bot creation and label implementations remain byte-identical to the upstream base.
- Not every Desktop multi-connection/menu/mention/management surface, Web management page, Ink prompt or classic `/profile` output is covered. Technical identity views and submitted mention tokens intentionally remain canonical.
- Each open room currently reads `profiles.list` on its refresh; a source-scoped cache is deferred.
- `Hermes (default)` remains where upstream already used it as an unnamed capability-scope fallback; it is not replaced merely to standardize copy.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide; conventional commit; checked for duplicate PRs.
- [x] Changes limited to this presentation tranche, with behavioral regression tests.
- [x] `python scripts/check --staged --base fcc26fbd9f1641755e49793d7ed608f3b7214c3d` passes (14 checks).
- [x] Typechecks, targeted tests, Web/shared suites and manual local UI smoke completed as detailed above.
- [ ] Full Python suite (not run; no Python implementation changes).
- [ ] Packaged Electron installers / real-provider E2E.
- [x] No config keys, credentials, production profile data or deployment changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): fail promptly when the plain-text approval prompt is undeliverable
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The plain-text execution-approval lane is the **last** delivery lane, but it reported success unconditionally:

- `fut.result(timeout=15)` was called **without inspecting the `SendResult`** — `success=False` looked delivered;
- a missing scheduling future (`fut is None`) was skipped silently;
- a send exception was logged and **swallowed**.

`_approval_notify_sync` is the `notify_cb` for `_await_gateway_decision`, so a normal return told the central waiter the prompt had been delivered. The approval entry stayed pending and the guarded command blocked for the full approval timeout (default 300s) over a prompt the user never saw — surfacing as `BLOCKED: ... timed out without user response` with no card and no text ever reaching the chat. An operator hit this **19 times** (13 on GPT-backed models, 6 on others); re-running the same command reproduced it, because nothing about the environment had changed.

The button lane above already classifies every outcome through `_approval_send_outcome`. The text lane now uses the same verdicts.

## Related Issue

Fixes #125950

Refs #125961 (independent parallel fix — see the duplicate note below).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py`
  - **Definitive failure raises `_ExecApprovalUndeliverable`** (send raised / no scheduling future / `SendResult(success=False)`), so `_await_gateway_decision` drops the queue entry and returns `notify_failed` immediately instead of parking the session for the whole window.
  - **Only the send-wait deadline is "possibly-delivered".** The `self._schedule(...)` call sits in its own `try` because `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` **is** the builtin `TimeoutError` on Python 3.11+. A broad handler wrapping the whole block silently converted a genuine scheduling failure into the very 300s stall this PR fixes. `except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` now guards `fut.result(timeout=15)` alone; the scheduler's exception is wrapped and raised.
  - **The ambiguous button-card send now arms the timeout notice.** It keeps the registration alive and never re-sends (correct), but the card was never *observed* posted: if it never arrived, the tool waited out the window and the chat said nothing — the same silent-stall class as the text path. When the card did post, the tap resolves the wait and the settle hook never fires, so arming costs nothing.
  - `_ExecApprovalDeclined` is now a subclass of `_ExecApprovalUndeliverable`; its existing `raise` behaviour and the "never fall back to text into a refused destination" guarantee are unchanged.
- `tests/gateway/test_exec_approval_text_undeliverable.py` (new) — drives the real callback, and for the non-delivery case the real `_await_gateway_decision`, asserting the queue entry is dropped and `notify_failed` returned.

## How to Test

1. Have a text-only adapter return `SendResult(success=False, error="session not ready")` (or raise) for the approval prompt. The waiter now returns `notify_failed` immediately instead of entering its approval poll.
2. `env -u HERMES_HOME HOME=/tmp/hermes-fakehome python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_exec_approval_text_undeliverable.py tests/gateway/test_exec_approval_timeout_notice.py tests/gateway/test_decline_fallback_suppression.py tests/gateway/test_approval_send_timeout_ambiguity.py tests/tools/test_approval.py -q` → **198 passed**.
3. Wider approval surface: 349 passed across 16 related gateway/tools modules.
4. `python -m ruff check` on both files → clean; `git diff --check` → clean.

Six of the ten new tests fail on the base tree (verified by stashing the source change), so the suite is red without the fix rather than green on both.

`env -u HERMES_HOME` is needed on this host only because the checkout lives at `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent`, where a lazily-imported `gateway.run` trips the test suite's real-home I/O guard.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — see below
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — focused suites only (198 / 349 passed); full suite not run
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8), Python 3.14 test env

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — N/A, no user-facing config changes
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the change is platform-agnostic and lives in the shared gateway runner
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## For New Skills

N/A.

## Duplicate note (please read before merging)

**#125961 is an independent fix for the same issue and it is still OPEN.** I found it during the duplicate sweep required by the contributing guide, after my own implementation was already written and verified; the overlap was not known while writing it. Its `mergeable_state` is `blocked` and it has a conflict against current `main`.

Rather than open a competing PR, I am flagging it explicitly:

- if #125961 is preferred, **close this one** — its approach (reusing `_approval_send_outcome` for the text lane) is a reasonable alternative to the explicit raise/classify steps here;
- if this one is preferred, note that it also fixes a defect #125961 does **not** cover: that PR classifies the text lane with `_approval_send_outcome(fut, timeout=15)` while keeping the `self._schedule(...)` call inside the same `try`. Because `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError is TimeoutError` on 3.11+, a scheduler-level timeout there is still classified as "possibly-delivered" and the session parks for the full window — the exact silent stall being fixed. This PR isolates the scheduler call in its own `try` and only treats the send-wait deadline as ambiguous. It additionally arms the timeout notice for the ambiguous **button** path, which is the same silent-stall class.

Happy to reduce this to whatever subset the maintainers want.

AI assistance: implemented and reviewed with AI assistance (test-first, then independently verified by a separate agent in a read-only sandbox, which caught the `TimeoutError` capture-width defect described above before submission).

prs.title: fix(delegation): finished async delegations stop pinning the parent session's agent
prs.body:
## What this fixes (plain words)

When an agent hands work to a background helper (`delegate_task` running async), the gateway keeps a short list of finished helpers so it can report on them. Each entry also kept a snapshot of the conversation's "turn state" from the moment the helper was started. That snapshot is only needed while the helper is still running (to clean up a stuck one). Once it finished, the snapshot kept the parent conversation's whole agent (history, callbacks, locks) alive, even after the user closed that session and the gateway evicted the agent. Up to 50 finished helpers are kept, so up to 50 closed conversations' agents could stay in memory.

Now a helper drops that snapshot the moment it finishes. The finished entry, its result and the bounded history of finished helpers are unchanged.

**Old:** finished background helper -> pins its parent session's agent until 50 newer helpers push it out.
**New:** finished background helper -> keeps only its own bookkeeping; the parent agent is freed when its session closes.

## Change

`tools/async_delegation.py` `_finalize`: when the record turns terminal, `pop("_context")` next to the `interrupt_fn` / `progress_fn` closures `_finalize` already clears. `_context` is read only by the stale monitor's forced finalization of an ACTIVE record (`_stale_monitor_loop`), which a terminal record never reaches (the second `_finalize` call is a no-op for non-active records).

No limits changed: the 50 retained completed records, their status/result fields and every user-visible behaviour are the same.

## Evidence (real gateway, real model)

Scratch `gateway run --force` (scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME/lock dir), driven through the canonical local-session RPCs (`session.create` -> `prompt.submit` tool turn -> `/compress` -> async `delegate_task` -> `session.detach end_reason=cli_close`) plus 2-turn api_server sessions, model `google/gemini-3.8-flash` on Nous. Heap probe loaded via a scratch `sitecustomize` (first-reference walk from module globals). Per cycle: 5 local + 2 api sessions, 90 s idle (agent-cache idle TTL 45 s) before each snapshot.

| | base `e99ab8c7` | head |
|---|---|---|
| Completed delegation records still holding the dispatch `Context` after sessions closed (warmup + 2 cycles) | 3 | 0 (3 completed records present, none holding `_context`) |
| `AIAgent` objects whose first reference path is `tools.async_delegation._records -> deleg_* -> _context -> ... -> cell -> AIAgent` | 3 (one per closed delegating session) | 0 |
| Bytes reachable only through those Contexts (other known leak, adapter post-delivery callbacks, simulated fixed) | 0.42 MB for 3 short sessions (~140 KB each; grows with the parent's history) | 0.00 MB |

RSS: not claimed. At this scale (short sessions) the freed graph is ~140 KB per delegating session, below RSS noise; the win grows with the parent's history and with the number of finished helpers (up to 50). Model spend for the base + head runs: ~$0.66 (estimated, Nous).

CPU: one dict `pop` per finished delegation; nothing on the turn path.

Tests: `tests/tools/test_async_delegation_record_retention.py` binds a sentinel in a contextvar before dispatch and asserts it is collectable once the record completes (the record itself stays listed). Fails on base (`AssertionError`, the record's Context still holds the sentinel), passes on head (`scripts/run_tests.sh`). `tests/tools/test_async_delegation_stale_profile_scope.py` (forced stale finalization under the dispatcher's Context) passes.

Found by the gateway-memory soak harness (lane D); the other retention paths it measured (adapter `_post_delivery_callbacks`, `_MSG_TOKENS_CACHE`) are handled in their own PRs.

## Infographic

![Finished helpers let go](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0ce9f/xd8OYLvRRXFoIerGdBC2G_5ZiKysPd.png)

prs.title: One malformed MCP tool no longer parks the whole server (salvage #101804, fixes #101669)
prs.body:
One MCP tool with a definition the SDK rejects now costs only that tool, instead of parking the whole server with zero tools.

Salvage of #101804 by @hyeonsang010716 (their commit cherry-picked, authorship kept), slimmed to the salvage bar. Same fix class as anomalyco/opencode#58350 ("skip malformed MCP tools instead of failing the server").

Fixes #101669

## What changes

| Server offers | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `good_echo` + `broken_tool` (no `inputSchema`) | `hermes mcp test` → `✗ Connection failed: 1 validation error for ListToolsResult tools.1.inputSchema Field required`; agent log: `failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking`; 0 tools | `✓ Tools discovered: 1 (good_echo)`; WARNING `dropping tool 'broken_tool' … (inputSchema: Field required); the server's other tools remain available` |
| 312 tools, one with a shape the SDK model rejects (#101669) | all 312 gone | 311 load, the bad one is named in the log and in `get_mcp_status()["dropped_tools"]` |
| Custom/extension method whose result happens to carry a `tools` list | passed through | passed through, unchanged |

**Root cause:** the mcp 2.x SDK validates a `tools/list` page as a whole against the negotiated protocol version's wire schema, so one invalid tool fails the response and Hermes parks the server.

## How

- `tools/mcp_listing_guard.py` wraps the session's stream pair between the transport and `ClientSession` (both the stdio and HTTP/SSE sites in `mcp_tool_transport.py`, so discovery, `tools/list_changed` refreshes, the keepalive fallback and `hermes mcp test` are all covered).
- The write proxy records each outbound request's method by id; the read proxy only touches the response to `tools/list`, validates each tool alone against the SDK's own per-version `Tool` model (`mcp_types.methods.SERVER_RESULTS`), and drops just the failing ones. Anything unexpected passes through as before.
- Dropped tools are recorded on the server (`_dropped_tools`, reset on rediscovery/refresh) and surfaced by `get_mcp_status`.

OpenCode does the same at its transport `onmessage` hook (validate the page with the tools stripped, then each tool alone via the SDK's era codec). The Python SDK has no such hook, so the guard sits on the anyio streams instead.

## Salvage notes

- `95a751fff00`: @hyeonsang010716's commit, cherry-picked onto current main (28k commits of drift; conflicts in `__slots__` and `_refresh_tools` resolved additively).
- `72c71663de7`: slim pass. Guard 321 → 178 lines (dropped mcp 1.x root-model unwrapping since Hermes pins mcp 2.x, the separate ledger class, and pragma-no-cover try/excepts); tests 627 → 92 lines, two invariants through a real `ClientSession`. `get_mcp_status` reads `_dropped_tools` with `getattr` like its `_registered_tool_names` neighbour (two status tests use `SimpleNamespace` servers).

- `c1647382008`: guard verdicts are cleared inside the RPC lock right before the fetch they belong to, so a queued `tools/list_changed` refresh can't leave a stale drop entry (review finding).

## Verification

- **Live repro (real `hermes chat -q`, OpenRouter `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, scratch HERMES_HOME, raw stdio MCP server offering `good_echo` + a tool without `inputSchema`):** main answered `NOTOOL` (server parked, `registered 0 tool(s) from 0 server(s) (1 failed: badsrv …)`); this branch answered `echo:{"x": "ping"}` after a real `mcp__badsrv__good_echo` call. Each leg used a fresh backend process.
- Sabotage: disabling the `_isolate` call turns `test_invalid_tool_is_dropped_by_name_and_the_rest_load` red.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp*.py`: 101 files, 887 passed, 0 failed locally (CI is the verdict).
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

## Infographic

![mcp-skip-malformed-tools](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab06345/0CVdmbSb6LgIFs_Rvalzb_ZcIPieHd.png)

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add FilmEase movie discovery and tracking
prs.body:
## FilmEase movie discovery and personal tracking

Add FilmEase as a community portable Agent Plugins v1 package, published by Filmease LLC. It uses a bundled movie-workflow skill and FilmEase's existing remote Streamable HTTP MCP server to find streamable films and read or update watchlists, ratings, private reviews, viewing history, taste, and country/service preferences.

Repository: https://github.com/Filmease/filmease-hermes-plugin
Pinned release: `80c57614048fade106063c8e38d332d3e88b66e5` (0.1.0)

### Hermes surfaces and setup

- `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, and one `skills/filmease/SKILL.md`; no native Python tool, hook, middleware, Desktop, or dashboard registration. Remote tools are discovered at connection time, so the native `provides_*` declarations are empty.
- Requires Hermes >=0.22.5. The remote server declares `trust: untrusted` so write-capable calls require Hermes approval.
- The portable format has no OAuth declaration. The README explicitly requires a same-name native `mcp_servers.filmease` entry with `auth: oauth` and `trust: untrusted`, followed by `hermes mcp login filmease`. Hermes owns credential storage and refresh. This is a documented manual configuration step, not a claimed one-click OAuth connection.
- No custom UI or screenshot claims.

### Rule 13 disclosures

- HTTPS requests go to `filmease-mcp.fancy-fire-1eba.workers.dev`; sign-in uses FilmEase's web consent flow. User-supplied movie intent, titles, filters, or requested personal-state changes are sent to FilmEase. Its existing backend uses Supabase and movie/search/streaming infrastructure.
- Authorized personal tools can read/update the signed-in account's movie state, private reviews, private companion labels, taste profile, region, and streaming preferences. No arbitrary user ID is accepted by the skill.
- No local executable, shell invocation, filesystem reader, background process, binary payload, self-updater, API key, environment variable, or plugin-owned credential storage.
- No client telemetry is added by this package. **The existing remote FilmEase service does record authenticated connection/tool activity, request summaries, latency, errors, and product outcomes for service analytics. This is disclosed in the README and is not described as opt-in plugin telemetry. Please assess whether this hosted-service behavior meets rule 13; no exemption or approval is assumed.**
- Privacy: https://www.filmease.net/privacy ; terms: https://www.filmease.net/terms ; support: info@filmease.net.

### Validation and remaining verification

- Passed the official `hermes_cli.plugin_validate.validate_plugin_dir` admission implementation against released Hermes v0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`) and main (`088f657ecf77674c7b8e2ededf4e3576d82e042c`) in an isolated Python 3.14 environment. Security scan: safe; zero warnings; loader: one skill, expected remote server, untrusted policy, strict redirect-header protection.
- No Python dependencies. The full managed-runtime CLI `--install-deps` path was not run locally; upstream catalog CI should run its normal pinned validation.
- Live OAuth metadata discovery returned 200 with registration, S256 PKCE, authorization-code and refresh grants. Unauthenticated MCP initialize returned the expected 401 OAuth metadata challenge.
- **Interactive Hermes browser login and authenticated movie tool calls have not yet been completed for this package.** These limitations are recorded in the public VALIDATION.md; the discovery checks are not represented as an end-to-end test.

prs.title: Tool schemas with draft-07 tuples no longer 400 on Claude and Kimi (salvage #63674)
prs.body:
MCP and plugin tools whose schema uses a draft-07 tuple (`items: [int, int]`) no longer make Claude (direct or through OpenRouter) and Kimi reject the whole request.

Salvage of #63674 by @jarrod-wright (both commits cherry-picked, authorship kept), widened from the native-Anthropic path to the shared tool-schema sanitizer so every provider route gets it. Same bug class as anomalyco/opencode#59207 (tuple schemas for Kimi).

## What changes

Real `hermes chat -q`, scratch HERMES_HOME, a stdio MCP server whose `set_size` tool takes `size: {type: array, items: [{type: integer}, {type: integer}]}`, `tools.tool_search.enabled: off` (so MCP schemas sit in `tools[]`):

| Route | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| OpenRouter → Anthropic (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`, `provider_routing.only: [anthropic]`) | `HTTP 400 … tools.7.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid. It must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12`; turn fails | model calls `set_size` with `[800, 600]`, answer `echo:{"size": [800, 600]}` |
| OpenRouter → Moonshot (`moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`, `only: [moonshotai]`) | `HTTP 400 … not a valid moonshot flavored json schema … items must be an object` | same successful tool call |
| OpenAI, Google AI Studio (raw probes) | accept `items: [...]` | accept `prefixItems` (probed both spellings) |

With the default `tool_search: auto`, MCP schemas are deferred behind the bridge, so this mostly bites users who turned Tool Search off, and any non-deferred tool with a tuple schema.

**Root cause:** Anthropic and Moonshot validate tool schemas as JSON Schema 2020-12, where tuple positions are `prefixItems`; the draft-07 list form 400s the whole request.

## How

- `tools/schema_sanitizer.py::convert_tuple_items_to_prefix_items` (from #63674): list `items` → `prefixItems`, sibling `additionalItems` → `items`, empty `items: []` dropped, hand-authored `prefixItems` wins; recursion only through schema-valued keywords, so `default`/`enum`/`examples` data is never rewritten.
- New: `_sanitize_single_tool` runs it first, so the output of `sanitize_tool_schemas` (every tool definition, every provider) is 2020-12 shaped. The Moonshot sanitizer already handles `prefixItems` and passes it through.
- Gemini's legacy `parameters` route (explicit `/v1` URLs, Vertex express) has no `prefixItems`: `agent/gemini_schema.py` folds the positional schemas plus any trailing rule into one `items` anyOf, so no position inherits only the trailing rule (review finding, b0a50d93a04; live-accepted by gemini-3.5-flash-lite).
- Not carried: #63674's hook in `anthropic_adapter._normalize_tool_input_schema`. That function moved to `anthropic_message_convert.py` since the PR was opened, and the shared sanitizer now covers its input.
- History: Moonshot once had a tuple rule (#27104, itself a port of opencode#24730) that was lost in a later merge; this restores the protection at the shared layer.

## Verification

prs.title: tool_search returns the tool a query names first, including namespaced MCP/connector tools (port pi#11440)
prs.body:
When the model searches for a tool by its name, `tool_search` now returns that tool first, including the short name of a namespaced MCP or connector tool (`report` → `mcp__nous_support__report`).

Port of earendil-works/pi#11440 ("rank tools first when the search query is their name").

## What changes

Real tool definitions from a live session's deferred catalog (Blender + nous-support MCP servers, Cashfree/Statsig connectors), `search_catalog(..., limit=3)`:

| query | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `execute_blender_code` | 1. `mcp__blender__execute_blender_code_for_cli` 2. `mcp__blender__execute_blender_code` | 1. `mcp__blender__execute_blender_code` 2. `…_for_cli` |
| `report` | `GET_REPORT_STATUS`, `LIST_REPORTS`, `DOWNLOAD_REPORT` (`mcp__nous_support__report` missing) | 1. `mcp__nous_support__report` 2. `GET_REPORT_STATUS` 3. `LIST_REPORTS` |
| `nous_support__report` | `mcp__nous_support__report` first | unchanged |
| `get_prompt` | both `*__get_prompt` first | unchanged |

The same ranking was observed through the running agent's own `tool_search` (888-tool catalog) before the change: `execute_blender_code` put `…_for_cli` first and `report` did not return `mcp__nous_support__report` in the top 3.

## Changes

- `tools/tool_search_catalog.py::search_catalog`: a tool is "named" by the query when the normalized query equals its full name (tier 2) or the part after a `__` separator (tier 1). Named tools skip the rare-token admission gate (as the exact name already did) and sort above BM25 score; ties fall back to BM25.
- Names compare lowercased with non-`[a-z0-9_]` characters as `_`, so `nous-support__report` also names it.
- One invariant test in `tests/tools/test_tool_search_multiquery.py` (red on main, green here).

Root cause: only the full exact name got a boost, so BM25 length normalization ranked a longer sibling name, or short descriptions that share the word, above the tool the model actually named.

Adaptation from pi: pi's `isNameQuery` treats the full name and the `__` suffix the same. Here the full name still wins over a suffix match, so a query that is one tool's full name and another's suffix keeps returning the full-name tool first.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over every test file referencing `tool_search`/`search_catalog`: 1233 passed, 0 failed.
- New test fails on `origin/main` and passes here.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.
- Not covered: a head-tree run against the full 888-tool live catalog. Starting MCP discovery from a cron-run shell registered 0 MCP tools, so the head leg used the real definitions of the tools in the table.

prs.title: fix(desktop): the launch restore never closes a chat the person opened (stacked on #147734)
prs.body:
Stacked on #147734 (which stacks on #147711). Review the top commit only (`fix(desktop): the launch restore never closes a chat the person opened`).

## What the person saw
Launch mode "last used" is set to a gateway other than the one main opens first. The window paints on This device and the person clicks a stored chat. A few seconds later the window jumps to a blank draft on the saved gateway and the chat is gone.

## Why
That window is not the startup profile re-home (`reconcileStartupProfile`): its `unchanged` guard and #147711's `yieldToOpenedSession` already cover it. The chat is closed by the **launch restore onto the last-used gateway**: `restorePreferredConnection` -> `restoreConnection(preferredId)` when the live connection is not the preferred one (`src/store/connections.ts`). That restore dials in the background and never yields. The #147711 review ruled out letting it yield to any selected chat, because a chat selected while it dials may itself be automatic (the cold-start route resume).

## Fix
- `openSession` (`src/app/open-session.ts`) bumps a user-open revision (`src/store/session-open-intent.ts`). It is the one door every surface opens a chat through in this window: sidebar row, ⌘K, notification, switcher, refs. Pop-out windows are excluded.
- Each launch restore (default route, last-used gateway, startup re-home) carries the revision captured when `initializeConnectionsRegistry` started. Its `beforeActivate` gives way once the revision has moved, and a restore that has not started yet skips. The click sets the revision synchronously, so a click whose resume RPC is still in flight also counts.
- Route effects that select a chat on their own (cold-start route resume, runtime recovery) never bump the revision. Those restores still land as they do on main, so none of the other silent restores yields wholesale.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New `store/connections-launch-user-open.test.ts`, red on fe1e88c20d8 (`connections.ts` + `open-session.ts` swapped to base) | user-open case red on base (window moved, chat cleared), green on head. Automatic-selection control green on both |
| `vitest run src/store/ src/app/open-session* src/app/gateway` | 217 files / 2324 tests pass |
| `tsc -p . --noEmit` | clean |
| eslint on touched files + pre-commit desktop lint | clean |

### Live A/B: native Electron, built `dist`, rootless Xvfb, CDP
Rig: This device (local `serve`), Homelab (real `hermes serve --isolated`), Box (SSH to a private sshd with a scratch HOME; its serves are killed before each launch so the restore dials slowly). Registry `launchMode=last-used`, `lastUsed=box`. The probe clicks the `LOC-default-1` sidebar row as soon as it is visible after This device paints (~+1 s), or 2.5 s after paint.

| Leg | base fe1e88c20d8 | head |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar click at first paint | **closed**: re-home to Box at 12.2 s and 5.7 s (2/2) | **kept** on This device until the 22-25 s probe end (5/5) |
| Sidebar click 2.5 s after paint (during the dial) | **closed** at 6.6 s | **kept** (2/2) |
| Control: no click, the launch's own route resume reopens `LOC-default-1` | lands on Box at 5.9 s, chat closed | same: lands on Box at 5.6 s (cold-start resume unchanged) |
| Hash written before the router's first route (composite E2E row G1 edge) | lands on Box | lands on Box (as on main: the app reads it as its boot route, the same as the cold-start resume) |

Screenshots (end of the click-at-paint leg, md5 matches the capture):
- base: ![base](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3268808c173187a0de4743a6a25a01f8/raw/base-click-at-paint.png) Box, blank New session
- head: ![head](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3268808c173187a0de4743a6a25a01f8/raw/head-click-at-paint.png) This device, `LOC-DEFAULT-1` transcript open

## Infographic

![launch-restore-keeps-opened-chat](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0cce9/iCrEAoQn70KKm7cQtqHZP_oSnNv7t5.png)

prs.title: fix(execute_code): forward session identity to nested tool calls
prs.body:
Tool calls made from inside `execute_code` reached `pre_tool_call` hooks with an empty `session_id`. The RPC dispatchers called `handle_function_call` with only `task_id`, so in a gateway serving several conversations from one process, a hook could attribute a nested call to whichever conversation bound a turn most recently — hooks that authorize edits or apply per-conversation policy could not tell which conversation made the call.

Thread the outer call's `session_id` and `turn_id` through every nested dispatch path:

- `model_tools` passes `turn_id` alongside `session_id` to the `execute_code` handler;
- the local session kernel's `CellAuthority` captures both at cell start and forwards them on dispatch;
- both remote paths (the per-call file-RPC poll loop and the remote session kernel) forward them through `_default_dispatch`.

Nested calls now fire hooks with the same identity fields as direct calls from the same conversation.

Closes #145870.

## What does this PR do?

Update the existing FXMacroData community plugin from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0. Per catalogue rule 4, this is a new reviewed SHA bump; it preserves the existing plugin name and lineage.

## Related Issue

No new issue. Existing entry landed through #133718; this update does not recreate the earlier #133564 submission.

## Type of Change

Plugin catalogue update, limited to `plugin-catalog/fxmacrodata.yaml`.

## Changes Made

- Pin the published 0.3.0 source commit `9d07f0f9ba5303488b11cffd8133b5342f7e05c4` and require Hermes >=0.22.5, matching the plugin manifest and tested stable release.
- Declare all 100 registered tools: 41 public REST operations, 57 MCP operations, the USD brief and a version-pinned history snapshot.
- Use native optional secret settings and `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` for profile-isolated credentials, with no direct process/file credential fallback.
- Expand the network/input disclosure, including research-panel arguments, finite SSE capture and structured rather than interactive MCP App results.

## How to Test

1. Run `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/fxmacrodata.yaml`.
2. Load the pinned plugin and run `hermes plugins validate` with its four declared dependencies installed.
3. Verify registrations and configure an optional profile-scoped key through native plugin settings; public USD catalogue, history and calendar need no key/account/card.

Validation completed: catalogue structural validator passes without warnings; 108 isolated handler/transport/snapshot tests pass. Official native validators load and register all 100 tools on stable Hermes 0.22.5 and the current development version; real profile-isolation tests pass on both. Final source and assembled archive scans are clean. Core full-suite/check was not run; no claim of full live dataset execution, subscriber access or model execution. Dependency installation was restricted to the plugin's checked requirements rather than the host's audio/Android dependency closure.

## Documentation and compatibility

The source README, capability inventory and native manifest describe 0.3.0 and the Hermes 0.22.5 minimum. Earlier releases are not certified. No core API, bundled plugin, config example or workflow is modified. Existing contributor email mapping is reused.

## Disclosure

FXMacroData maintains this vendor plugin. Invoked tools send their arguments over HTTPS only to api.fxmacrodata.com and mcp.fxmacrodata.com; this can include user-entered research or positions. An optional FXMACRODATA_API_KEY comes through Hermes's profile-scoped secret route and travels in request headers. Public USD access is keyless; other data depends on entitlement. Host/model costs are separate. The plugin writes no files, launches no shell/background process and adds no telemetry. It adds research guidance to the system prompt. Remote MCP behavior is not pinned by the source SHA. No credentials, backend source, internal operating logic, proprietary observations or customer material are included.

prs.title: catalog: pass-secrets 1.1.0 — /s chat lane, generic defaults
prs.body:
SHA bump for an existing catalog entry: `pass-secrets` 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, pin `485f105` → `6513470`.

## What changed in the adopted range

`485f105..6513470` (github.com/dyiapanis/pass-secrets):

- **New: `/s` chat lane.** Stores a secret from any Hermes chat channel, as a `pre_gateway_dispatch` hook. The hook fires at ingress, so the value is handled and skipped before it can reach the agent loop or conversation state; it goes to `pass insert` on stdin.
- **Module split.** `source.py` (SecretSource) + `chat.py` (`/s`), with `__init__.py` reduced to registration. No behaviour change to the source half.
- **Generic defaults.** The `subdirs` example is `[shared, work]` rather than a profile-specific name, in docs and the config schema.
- **Portable self-check.** `selftest.py` runs from a checkout with no absolute paths, and skips the store-dependent check when no `pass` store is present.

## Entry changes

- `version`: `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`
- `capabilities.provides_hooks`: `[]` → `["pre_gateway_dispatch"]`
- `sha`: exact 40-char pin, `6513470189220a437d8435505776ca4019b220c6`
- Description extended: `/s` applies **no sender policy of its own** — the hook runs before Hermes' authorisation check by design, so channel access is the boundary; and an entry in a shared subdir becomes an environment variable inside every agent process.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/pass-secrets.yaml` → `OK: 1 file(s) valid`
- Upstream `selftest.py` at the pinned SHA → `ALL CHECKS PASSED` (registration, source contract, usage text, name rules, injection hint, no-sender-gate behaviour)
- No network calls, no Python dependencies, stdlib only; unchanged from the previously reviewed 1.0.0 on that axis.

## Notes for the reviewer

The `/s` lane depends on the `pre_gateway_dispatch` hook only (`requires_hermes` unchanged at `>=0.21.4`, which already ships it). Nothing in the plugin fetches, downloads or self-updates; the SHA pin remains the trust model.

prs.title: Saved GPT Image 1.5 picks keep working after OpenAI's Dec 1 shutdown (image_gen)
prs.body:
Saved `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` picks keep working after OpenAI shuts GPT Image 1.5 and 1 Mini down on **2026-12-01**: they now run on GPT Image 2 instead of breaking or quietly switching to Klein.

## Why

OpenAI's [deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) (notice dated 2026-06-02, page updated 2026-10-22) shuts down `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5` and `chatgpt-image-latest` on **Dec 1, 2026**. Hermes still lists two of them:

- `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` in the FAL image catalog (fal only proxies OpenAI, so it dies the same day)
- `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` in the OpenRouter Image API list, where it is the only model offering `background=transparent`

## Changes

- Removed `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` from `FAL_MODELS`, plus the `gpt_literal` size style that only this model used.
- New `RETIRED_FAL_MODELS = {"fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5": "fal-ai/gpt-image-2"}`. A config that still has the old id is read as GPT Image 2 by both `_read_configured_image_model` (managed dispatch), `_resolve_fal_model` (config or `FAL_IMAGE_MODEL`), and `managed_backend_for_model` (router + `nous_subscription` status). No config migration needed.
- OpenRouter: replaced `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` with `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and a saved Mini pick (kwarg, `OPENROUTER_IMAGE_MODEL`, `image_gen.openrouter.model` or `image_gen.model`) resolves to Flare via `_RETIRED_IMAGE_API_MODELS` in `_resolve_model_chain`. Flare keeps `background=transparent`; its params come from OpenRouter's live `GET /api/v1/images/models` (9 ratios incl. 16:9, quality auto…max, n≤10, 16 refs).
- Docs (en + zh-Hans): removed the 1.5 rows and aspect column, and added a note about the remap.

## Before / after (stored `image_gen.provider: nous`, `image_gen.model: fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5`)

| | resolved model | managed route | after Dec 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` | FAL | upstream 4xx, generation fails |
| removing the entry with no successor map | Klein fallback (FAL path) | **`portal`**: the dead id is sent to the Portal gateway | wrong backend / failure |
| **this PR** | `fal-ai/gpt-image-2` | FAL | works |

## Validation

- **Live (real managed Nous gateway, runtime interpreter, worktree code):** stored `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` + provider `nous`. `_resolve_fal_model()` → `fal-ai/gpt-image-2`. Real `image_generate_tool("a red apple…", "square")` returned `success: True` with a fal.media PNG. On main the same config resolves to `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5`.
- Clearing the map on head makes `managed_route("nous", "fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5")` return `portal`. That routing bug is why the map is needed, not just the deletion.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_image_generation.py tests/tools/test_image_generation_managed.py tests/plugins/image_gen/ tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py tests/tools/test_managed_media_gateways.py tests/hermes_cli/test_nous_subscription.py`: **343 passed, 0 failed**.
- New invariant tests: `test_retired_saved_pick_resolves_to_successor` (OpenRouter) and `TestRetiredModels`, which also covers the `FAL_IMAGE_MODEL` path: each retired id is gone from the catalog, its successor is present, and the retired id resolves to the successor on the FAL path and the managed router. It fails on main, which has no `RETIRED_FAL_MODELS`.
- ruff clean, `scripts/check --only health` ok, `check_doc_links` ok, `check_no_tmp_literals` ok.

## Notes

- Pricing: GPT Image 2 medium costs $0.04–0.06/image on fal, up from 1.5's $0.034. It is already metered on the managed gateway (`_PORTAL_DUPLICATE_OF` maps it), so no portal work is needed.
- Not touched: `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality` (retires Nov 2), which is already covered by open #128430. `openai/gpt-image-1` shut down Oct 23 and was never in Hermes's curated list.
- Timing: the replacement models are live today, so this can merge now or any time before Dec 1.

prs.title: fix(gateway): completions of sessions routed through another profile's bot reach that bot (salvage #129054)
prs.body:
Background `delegate_task` results (and other completion wakes) from a chat that reaches its profile through another profile's bot sat at `pending` forever and were dropped after a restart. This makes the routed turn, its saved route and the later wake all agree on which profile runs it and which bot answers it.

| Live, real `hermes gateway run` (Discord stand-in = default bot, Telegram stand-in = profile `tg`'s bot, profile `work` has no bot) | origin/main 557254faa24 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| control: Discord DM on default | delivered, 1 attempt | delivered, 1 attempt |
| `tg`'s bot → runtime `default` (`bot_profile: tg`) | pending, `Watch notification not admitted … not_found` ×5 | delivered, 1 attempt, `transport_profile=tg` saved |
| `tg`'s bot → runtime `work` (`bot_profile: tg`), the #139726 shape | pending, `not_found` ×5 | delivered, 1 attempt |
| same, gateway restarted while the child runs | `Restored 1 undelivered …`, then silently pending, 0 attempts | delivered after restart, parent woke |
| default bot → `tg` (owns Telegram only), live | delivered (live transport ref) | delivered |
| same, row with no `transport_profile` + restart, the #141219 shape | `Restored …`, silently pending, 0 attempts | delivered after restart, parent woke |

Each fix is load-bearing live: with any one hunk removed on the head tree, its row goes back to pending (checked: the destination borrow → #141219 restart row; the runtime scope → `work` live row; the identity re-pin → `work` restart row).

## What was wrong (three separate holes, all on main)

1. **The turn was admitted by the wrong profile.** `run_adapters._make_profile_message_handler` (and its busy twin) scoped a secondary bot's event under the bot's own profile, even when a `bot_profile` route sends it to another runtime. The bot profile's authority admitted the turn while the route lives in the runtime profile, so the wake's automation admission found no committed turn there (`not_found`) and the completion retried forever. Both handlers now scope under `identity.runtime_home`, the same as the primary's handler. Authorization still reads the transport home through `_under_authorization_profile`.
2. **The receiving bot was never saved.** The durable FIFO drain rebuilds the turn's source with `restore_provenance`, which restored the adapter ref but not the `RoutingIdentity`. So `sessions.transport_profile` stayed NULL for every messaging session, and after a restart nothing remembered which bot received the chat. `restore_provenance` now re-pins the identity (one line in `gateway/session_ingress_context.py`).
3. **Detached injections ignored the saved bot.** `_resolve_injection_adapter` looked the platform up in the runtime profile's adapter map. It now reads the pinned transport profile, as `_delivery_adapter_for` already does: never the default bot by guesswork, and nothing while the named bot is down. For rows with no saved bot, a profile that owns a bot on one platform but reaches another through the shared bot now borrows the primary for that destination only (#129054).

The transport matrix in `gateway/AGENTS.md` is unchanged. The restored row now finds a saved `transport_profile` instead of always falling back.

## Salvage and credit

- **#129054** by @rungmc357 (cherry-picked, authorship kept): destination-gated shared-bot borrow plus a one-time warning when a completion has no transport. It is the earliest open PR for #141219, and it borrows the primary only for the satellite's routed chats, never through platform-wide lookups (`send_message`, `_authorization_adapter`).
- **#141220** by @levinkin: superseded. It fixes the same #141219 hole by borrowing per platform through `_adapters_for_profile`. That also hands the primary bot to platform-wide callers for any chat, so #129054's per-destination gate was kept instead. Thanks for the clear repro in #141219.
- **#140009** by @kouyichi (closed for the open-PR cap, not on design): its `_resolve_injection_adapter` identity read is in commit 2 (`Co-authored-by`).
- Overlaps: **#136832** (@ericcurtin) also routes restored notices through the recorded bot. On main that record was always NULL (hole 2), so on its own it cannot change these rows.

Fixes #139726, fixes #141219

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_transport_matrix.py`: a restored inverse row (`team_b`'s bot → default) injects through `team_b`'s bot, and through nothing while that bot is down; a `bot_profile` route's event runs in the runtime's scope while the bot's own traffic keeps its own scope.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/native_ingress_trust_multiplex.py`: the existing real-admission multiplex probe now also asserts the drained turn's route saved `transport_profile`.
- `tests/gateway/test_satellite_per_platform_borrow.py` (from #129054).
- Red on origin/main: the matrix tests and both `test_native_ingress_trust` multiplex modes fail with the base sources swapped in (run from a tree copy). Green on head: 28 gateway files covering multiplex, identity, automation wake, relay and busy-path scope.

prs.title: fix(mcp): an OAuth-protected MCP server that parks, runs short tokens or revives mid-turn recovers inside the session
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Three fixes from running Hermes against an MCP server behind OAuth 2.1 (Keycloak, 300 s access tokens, server-side introspection on every call). Each is one commit with its own test, red on `main`; the three share one scenario and touch disjoint files, so they come together, and can be split on request.

1. **`reload.mcp` reconnects a parked OAuth server once its saved grant changed** (`tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py`). A server parked on an auth failure (`_arm_auth_park`) is registered, so `reconcile_mcp_servers_with_config` had nothing to add after the user signed in; the tools came back only with the parked task's own self-probe. `_reconnect_reauthorized_servers` now drives `_signal_reconnect_and_wait` for a parked, session-less server whose token storage carries a grant with a new credential stamp, and the reload returns once discovery ran. Same-named servers of another profile scope are untouched; an unchanged stamp does nothing; serialized under `_RESTART_LOCK`. `mcp_servers_not_connected` stops reporting a parked server whose fresh session is ready (`_parked_without_ready_session`).

2. **A short-lived access token is refreshed before it expires mid-request** (`tools/mcp_oauth_manager.py`). The SDK refreshes only once `time.time()` passed the expiry, so a call that starts a second before expiry reaches a server that re-introspects the token mid-request and fails with an application error, not a 401: nothing retries. `HermesMCPOAuthProvider._hermes_force_refresh_if_near_expiry` runs at the head of `async_auth_flow` and marks a refreshable token with at most `oauth.refresh_margin_seconds` (default 120, `0` disables) left as expired, so the SDK's own refresh branch runs first. Tokens without a refresh grant are never touched; the margin is capped at half the token's known lifetime. A value that is not a non-negative number is refused where it is read, naming the key. Documented in `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md`.

3. **A server that revives mid-turn lands in the turn's next request** (`agent/turn_iteration_prep.py`, `tools/mcp_tool_agent.py`). The between-turns refresh had already run when the server reconnected seconds into the turn, and `_merge_preserving_prefix` keeps the tool_search bridge's sent bytes, so the catalog listing the model reads never learned the new names and the model guessed for the rest of the turn. `prepare_iteration` now calls `refresh_agent_tools_after_registry_move` behind the same `tools.mcp_tool` import gate as the between-turns refresh; when the registry generation moved past the snapshot it runs the prefix-preserving refresh with `refresh_bridge=True`: every sent tool keeps its slot and bytes, new tools append, only the bridge entry takes its fresh bytes. Nothing moved: one integer compare. The frozen cache-parity fork and an agent with no MCP tools never rebuild. Narrows #72560 (its mid-turn half; the between-turns name-only compare it also describes is not changed here).

## Related Issue

Related: #72560 (commit 3). No issue exists for commits 1 and 2; both reproduce on `main` with the tests below.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py`: `_reconnect_reauthorized_servers`, `_parked_without_ready_session`; `reconcile_mcp_servers_with_config` reports revived servers under `added`.
- `tools/mcp_oauth_manager.py`: `refresh_margin_seconds` constructor argument, `_hermes_resolve_refresh_margin`, `_hermes_force_refresh_if_near_expiry`, the pre-flow hook in `async_auth_flow`; `_build_provider` passes `oauth.refresh_margin_seconds`.
- `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md`: the new per-server key.
- `tools/mcp_tool_agent.py`: `refresh_agent_tools_after_registry_move`; `refresh_bridge` on `refresh_agent_mcp_tools`, `_publish_tool_snapshot` and `_merge_preserving_prefix`.
- `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py`: the hook in `prepare_iteration`, before the request is built.
- Tests: `tests/tools/test_mcp_reload_after_authorization.py` (8), `tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth_early_refresh.py` (8), `tests/tools/test_mcp_revive_mid_turn_refresh.py` (6).

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_reload_after_authorization.py tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth_early_refresh.py tests/tools/test_mcp_revive_mid_turn_refresh.py` → 22 passed.
2. Red on base: copy the three test files onto `main` and run the same command → `test_reload_adopts_new_credentials_and_waits_for_tools` fails ("reload must wake the existing parked task after authorization"), every early-refresh test fails (`_hermes_force_refresh_if_near_expiry` missing; the MCP request goes out with the expiring token), every mid-turn test fails (`ImportError`; the bridge listing keeps its sent bytes). The negative cases (unchanged, disabled, live, foreign-scope, non-auth-parked, missing-token servers never reconnect) pass on both.
3. Related suites on this branch: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth*.py tests/tools/test_mcp_reconcile_with_config.py tests/tools/test_mcp_parked_*.py tests/tools/test_refresh_agent_mcp_tools.py tests/tools/test_tool_search*.py tests/agent/test_turn_iteration_prep.py tests/agent/test_background_review_cache_parity.py tests/gateway/test_mcp_reload_*.py tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_reload_all_sessions.py tests/tui_gateway/contracts/` → green (367 passed, 1 Windows-only skip).
4. Live: an OAuth server that parks on first connect; sign in (Desktop MCP card or `hermes mcp login <server>`), trigger Reload MCP: the server's tools are back in the same reload result. With a 300 s token, a long turn no longer loses a tool call to a mid-request expiry (the gateway log shows `access token expires in <n>s (refresh margin 120s); refreshing before the request`). A server that reconnects during a turn is callable by name in the model's next step.

prs.title: Make (make.com) hosted MCP joins the catalog (OAuth, scenarios + data stores)
prs.body:
Adds Make (make.com) to the MCP catalog, so `hermes mcp install make` connects Make's vendor-hosted MCP over OAuth and lets the agent run Make scenarios and manage connections, webhooks and data stores.

## What it is

- **Vendor:** Make, the visual automation platform (Celonis). The catalog already has `n8n-official` but not Make.
- **URL:** `https://mcp.make.com/v2`, the URL [Make's docs](https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-oauth) give for OAuth (stateless Streamable HTTP). The API-key URLs are zone-specific (`<MAKE_ZONE>/mcp/u/<KEY>/v2`) and are not cataloged.
- **Listed in** the official MCP Registry as `com.make/mcp-server` (updated this week).
- **Tools are dynamic.** Each scenario exposed for MCP becomes a tool. Management tools (scenarios, connections, webhooks, data stores, teams/orgs) need a paid plan and the matching scope, which the user picks on Make's consent screen. Since there is no fixed tool table to curate, the entry ships **uncurated**, following the beehiiv precedent.

## Validation (live)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `POST /v2` initialize, no auth | 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v2"` |
| RFC 9728 resource metadata | `authorization_servers: ["https://www.make.com/mcp-openai"]` |
| AS metadata | `registration_endpoint`, PKCE S256, `client_secret_post`, refresh_token grant |
| DCR with `client_name: "Hermes Agent"` + loopback redirect | **201** (Make adds a per-client suffix to the name) |
| Hermes's own OAuth stack (`prepare_oauth_config` → `build_provider_kwargs` → `OAuthClientProvider` over `sdk_httpx()`, scratch `HERMES_HOME`) | captured authorize URL `https://www.make.com/oauth/v2/authorize?...&code_challenge_method=S256&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.make.com%2Fv2`, which redirects to Make's sign-in page (renders in a real browser; plain httpx gets the site's bot-wall 403) |
| Real `install_entry(get_entry("make"))` into a scratch home | writes `make: {url: https://mcp.make.com/v2, auth: oauth, enabled: true}`; the probe parks on non-interactive OAuth as expected |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_catalog.py` + `test_mcp_catalog_env_boundary.py` | 54 passed |

Not covered: browser consent and `tools/list`, which need a signed-in Make account. The cron run that opened this PR has none.

## Cost / trust notes

- Scenario-run tools work on every Make plan, including free. Management tools need a paid plan. Scenario runs consume Make operations/credits like any other run.
- Access is limited to the organization and scopes the user grants on Make's consent screen. Management scopes can modify scenarios, connections and data stores, and the post-install text says so.
- Scenario runs over this URL time out after 25 s but keep running in Make. The post-install text tells the user to grant `scenarios:read` so the agent can fetch the result by `executionId`.
- Suggest keywords are multi-word (`make.com`, `make scenario`, `make automation`) because "make" alone is an ordinary verb and would match constantly.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab06a5d/3KsWlC5LLQC8u5FKHRVIp_wRwxkDHj.png)

Nous Research

prs.title: plugin-catalog: fish-audio v1.9.0
prs.body:
Re-pins `fish-audio` from the live 1.8.0 (#141843) to **v1.9.0** (`606afb54aa1a354cc8eac0b17f3da3a105ac55a7`, tag v1.9.0). This release adopts Fish's new native realtime speech-to-text model, `transcribe-stream-1`.

**What changed since 1.8.0**
- **Word-by-word live dictation:** live dictation (`stt.streaming: true`, Hermes 0.21.6+) now uses Fish's native realtime STT (`transcribe-stream-1`, Preview) by default. Draft captions appear word by word, and sound and speaker tags are removed. If Fish never finishes the session, reports a degraded turn or returns an error, Hermes falls back to transcribing the recording as a file, so a partial transcript is never kept.
- **The old endpoint stays available:** the new `live_transcription` setting (`realtime` | `compat`) keeps the earlier phrase-caption endpoint one switch away.
- **Transcribe 1 is deprecated:** status warns about Fish retiring it on 2026-12-31. From that day, provider and tool requests use `transcribe-1-pro` at the same price, without rewriting config.
- **Filter your own voices:** the `fish_voices` `mine` action accepts a public, unlisted or private visibility filter.

**Catalog entry changes**
- `sha`, `version` and the image URLs.
- **Description, two clauses:** "live dictation captions" now reads "word-by-word live dictation captions". The live-dictation clause of the disclosure now gives the realtime billing ($0.36 per hour of open session, per second, including silence), when a session opens and closes, and that the `compat` setting keeps the older per-phrase billing.
- Everything else is unchanged: the rest of the disclosure, the known issues, `requires_hermes` (`>=0.21.6`), capabilities and screenshots.

**Checks**
- The release acceptance suite ran on the merged tree before tagging, driving the real CLI, chat commands, tools, gateway routes and Desktop.
  - Hermes v0.22.5: gate passed, 74 rows pass and 6 xfail on filed host bugs.
  - evaOS runtime: gate passed.
  - Live dictation is checked on both settings: A-STT-3 (realtime) and the new A-STT-4 (compat). The new A-VOICE-1 row checks the visibility filter against the live account.
- `validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes, every image URL returns 200, and `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` (rule 17) is clean on the pinned tree.

No new routes, tools, hooks or dependencies. The `websockets` floor moved from `>=13` to `>=15`; Hermes 0.21.6 already locks `websockets` 15.0.1, so the catalog floor holds.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add vidbyte-memory
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/vidbyte-memory.yaml`. It is submitted by the owner of [cerredz/vidbyte-memory](https://github.com/cerredz/vidbyte-memory) (MIT).

vidbyte-memory is a repo template for correction-driven agent memory. Each correction the owner gives a coding agent becomes three things:
- a slim fact or rule;
- a pytest test that fails if the mistake comes back;
- a footprint commit.

Its `scripts/guard.py` checks three things before a request may end: the tests pass, no feedback is pending, and nothing is uncommitted or unpushed. This plugin runs that guard from `pre_verify`. When the guard blocks, the plugin returns `{"action": "continue", "message": reason}` and Hermes keeps working until the request is actually finished.

| | |
|---|---|
| Repo | [`cerredz/vidbyte-memory`](https://github.com/cerredz/vidbyte-memory), subdir `integrations/hermes`, MIT |
| Pin | [`2fe35cf12fc0205fbc1997afbae1264eb724cee4`](https://github.com/cerredz/vidbyte-memory/tree/2fe35cf12fc0205fbc1997afbae1264eb724cee4/integrations/hermes) (v0.2.0) |
| `requires_hermes` | `>=0.21.6`, declared in the entry and in `plugin.yaml` |

## Hermes surfaces used

- Python plugin: `register()` registers one hook, `pre_verify`. No tools, middleware, skills, providers or Desktop code.
- Public imports only: `agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_agent_cwd` for the session directory, and `hermes_cli.config.load_config_readonly` to keep the guard under `plugins.hook_callback_timeout`. No runtime rebinds of core.
- Standard library only, no dependencies.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Runs:** in a project that has `memory/MAP.md` and `scripts/guard.py`, that project's `scripts/guard.py`, on the host. It uses the project's Python (its `.venv`, else `python` on PATH). This is outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without terminal approval. The guard runs the project's pytest suite (whatever test code the repo holds), `git status` and `git rev-list`.
- **Writes:** `.claude/.guard_state.json` in the project, which holds the guard's round counter.
- **When:** the guard is stopped just before Hermes's hook timeout. It does nothing in any directory without `memory/MAP.md`.
- **No** network calls, credentials or telemetry.
- **Known gap:** `pre_verify` fires only on turns where `write_file` or `patch` changed a file, so a turn that edits only through the terminal is not gated. The plugin README says so.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

1. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/vidbyte-memory.yaml` returns `OK: 1 file(s) valid` locally.
2. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps integrations/hermes` at the pinned sha returns `Validation passed` on Hermes main (`903230b1`, 2026.9.24). The security scan reports safe, there is no core override, and the declared hooks match the registrations.
3. `python -m pytest -q integrations/tests` in the repo: 11 tests pass. They load the plugin the way the Hermes loader does, call `pre_verify` with Hermes's keyword arguments, and run the real guard on a copy of the template: a green repo ends the turn, and a failing test continues it with `G-001`. Template CI runs them on Linux and Windows.
4. Live check: in a repo with the memory installed, add a failing test with `write_file` and ask Hermes to finish. It should be nudged with the guard's reason. Not yet run in a live session.

## How it was made

Built with Claude Code at the owner's request, from the Hermes source for the `pre_verify` contract, the loader, the validator and the catalog rules. The owner maintains the repo.

prs.title: Draft: one durable per-profile agent inbox for wake-ups (not wired, for discussion)
prs.body:
**Draft for discussion. Nothing imports this module and no behaviour changes.**

**Why.** Six producers wake an agent today: message_agent DMs, the cross-machine relay, cron → Bot Chat delivery, background-process completions, async delegation completions, and the kanban notifier. Each uses its own queue, storage and claim rule, which leaves gaps:
- Process-completion events live only in memory.
- A `claimed` DM mailbox or `bot_chat_pending` record is never recovered.
- Kanban loses its claimed range if it crashes before sending.
- The CLI marks a delegation delivered before the turn runs.
- The relay turn flock does nothing on Windows.

**What.** `agent/agent_inbox.py` sketches one SQLite-backed inbox plus a turn scheduler, generalising two existing designs rather than adding a seventh:
- From `tools/bot_live_delivery.py`: the record state machine (idempotent admission, oldest-first claim, immutable terminal receipts, cancel-vs-claim under one lock, a shared waiter).
- From `cron/delivery_queue.py`: the storage idiom (conditional-UPDATE claims, owner stamps, dead-owner fencing).

It adds lanes (interactive/agent/background), coalescing keys and a recovery policy per source. Waiting uses `agent.deadline.poll_until` (#135282). The module docstring has a migration map for each of the six paths: what moves into the inbox and what stays path-specific. Session turn exclusivity stays with `session_turn_leases`.

**Verified.** `tests/agent/test_agent_inbox.py`: 24 tests (admission conflicts, claim ordering and lanes, coalescing, cancel races, per-source recovery, expiry resolving a waiter, stale-claim surfacing, pre-emption). 84 passed together with the `agent.deadline` tests it builds on; 5 back-to-back runs of the inbox file stable; `scripts/check` clean.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add stablelens 0.1.0
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a catalog entry for **stablelens** 0.1.0 ([erhnysr/stablelens](https://github.com/erhnysr/stablelens) at `4555b3e`): read-only tools for Arc Network, the stablecoin-native L1 where USDC is the gas token.

With it the agent can answer "did this payment go through and what did it cost", "what does this address hold in USDC and EURC" and "what is this token contract" from the chain itself, on mainnet (chain 5042) and testnet (5042002):

| Tool | Answers |
|---|---|
| `arc_network_status` | latest block and time, gas price, cost of a plain transfer in USDC |
| `arc_balance` | native USDC plus USDC, EURC, USYC, cirBTC, WETH and any ERC-20 asked for, all read at one block |
| `arc_transaction` | success / reverted / pending, block time, fee in USDC, decoded ERC-20 transfers |
| `arc_address` | account or contract, nonce, balance, Circle's name for published contracts |
| `arc_token` | name, symbol, decimals, total supply |
| `arc_block` | number, hash, time, transaction count, gas, base fee |

Standard library only, no dependencies. It never signs, sends or holds keys.

## Disclosure

- **Network:** each tool call sends JSON-RPC requests carrying the addresses, transaction hashes, token addresses and block numbers asked about to Arc's public RPC endpoints (`rpc.mainnet.arc.io` / `rpc.testnet.arc.io` and the Blockdaemon, dRPC and QuickNode endpoints Arc publishes). If the user configures a private endpoint, it is tried first. Registration makes no network calls.
- **Credentials:** none needed. The optional private endpoint URL (which usually embeds a provider key) is a `type: secret` setting (`STABLELENS_MAINNET_RPC_URL` / `STABLELENS_TESTNET_RPC_URL`) read through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`. Only its host name ever appears in tool output or errors.
- **Nothing else:** no file writes, shell commands, background processes, hooks or telemetry. Every request has a timeout, every tool call a 25 s deadline, and failures come back as JSON errors instead of raising.

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/stablelens.yaml` (new; the only file touched)

## How to Test

Run against the pinned sha on GitHub Actions:

1. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes on current main (0.22.5) and on 0.21.5, the declared `requires_hermes` floor. Security scan: safe. Declared tools match registrations.
2. `hermes plugins doctor --ci` registers 6 tools. `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` is clean. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` passes with the entry added.
3. The plugin's own CI is green: unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.11 to 3.14. Live tests against Arc mainnet and testnet check every listed token's `symbol()` / `decimals()` against the chain and confirm code exists at every labelled contract.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched for existing PRs and the catalog for an Arc entry; none exists
- [x] My PR contains only the catalog entry
- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] Tested on: Ubuntu, macOS and Windows (GitHub Actions)
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -q` / `python scripts/check`: N/A, data-only catalog change

prs.title: fix(mailbox): keep one task payload per recurring series
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops recurring tasks from growing a session's `inbound.db` by one full copy of the task payload per run.

- **Problem**: every re-arm copies the full content (prompt + script) into the next occurrence, and finished occurrences are never trimmed. Size grows as payload × runs, without bound. On a real install, one 21 KB prompt on a `*/10` cron reached 238 MB over 11k runs.
- **Fix**: inside the existing `armNextTask` transaction, the content of the series' older finished occurrences (`completed`/`failed`, recurrence already cleared, `seq` below the new occurrence) is replaced with `{"superseded":true}`.
- **Why rows stay**: `getTaskStats` (runs, failed runs, last run) and `trailingFailedRuns` (script-failure auto-pause) count rows by status. Deleting rows would change both; replacing only the payload changes neither.
- **Why nothing notices**: once a later occurrence exists, every content reader resolves to the newest row of the series: `getTask`, `listLiveTasks`, `findTaskBySeriesSlug`, `updateTask` (future rows only), and the re-arm itself (it reads the just-completed row before compacting). Retries only touch `pending`/`processing` rows. `sessions history` already renders task rows as empty text, because task content has no `text` field.
- **Existing installs**: a series' backlog is compacted on its next re-arm. No migration is needed.
- **Out of scope**: reclaiming file size. SQLite reuses the freed pages, so the file stops growing. `VACUUM` is left to the operator.

<details><summary>Only observable difference</summary>

`ncl tasks get <id>` with the row id of a *superseded* occurrence (not the series id) now shows an empty prompt. The series id and the live occurrence still show the full content.
</details>

## Related work

No existing issue. Searched open and closed issues and PRs for inbound.db growth, retention, prune and recurring tasks. #3289 / #3291 are about the pending backlog, not finished rows.

Open PRs in the same area, all compatible:
- #3696 and #3741 add fields to task content. They read them from the just-completed row at re-arm time, or from the live row at spawn. Neither row is compacted.
- #2915 and #3247 touch the pre-`armNextTask` recurrence path.
- #3594 is container-side.

Happy to rebase whichever lands second.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/mailbox/sqlite/arm-next-task.test.ts` -> 7 passed. 5 are new:
  - a payload is kept once per series, and every row, `getTaskStats` and `trailingFailedRuns` are unchanged;
  - a cancelled series keeps its payload;
  - a pre-existing backlog is compacted on the next re-arm;
  - other series and non-task rows are untouched;
  - when the insert fails, the compaction rolls back with the pair.
- Same file without the one-line call in `armNextTask` -> the two compaction tests fail. The three guard tests still pass, as intended.
- `pnpm run build` -> ok.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 4242 passed, 1 skipped. The clean base had 4237 passed, 1 skipped, so the 5 new tests are the only change.
- Copy of the 238 MB production `inbound.db`, through `wrapSqliteInbound`:
  - stats identical before and after;
  - 203 MB of pages freed;
  - first re-arm 105 ms, which compacts 11k rows once;
  - steady-state re-arm 8 ms.
- Live install, same patch:
  - after the next sweep re-arm, all 11,072 finished rows of the series hold the marker;
  - the pending occurrence keeps its full 12 KB payload;
  - `ncl tasks get <series>` shows the full prompt and an unchanged `completed_runs`;
  - no new host errors.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Recurring tasks no longer grow the session database by one copy of the task prompt per run.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Host-only write to the session's `inbound.db` (its single writer), inside an existing transaction.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): read document captions, and stop downloading media nobody wants
prs.body:
> **Depends on #3711** (`InboundMessage.resolveContent` in trunk). Until that lands and `channels` re-syncs, the `resolveContent` field here is simply ignored and the adapter behaves exactly as it does today — it compiles and passes either way, it just isn't lazy yet.

## Two inbound bugs, both about attachments

### 1. Captioned documents never reached the agent

The text extraction read `conversation`, `extendedTextMessage.text`, and the image and video captions — but **not `documentMessage.caption`**.

A PDF captioned `@Bot ...` in a wired group arrived at the router with empty text, so a pattern-engage wiring could not match it and the whole message — attachment included — was dropped as `no_agent_engaged`. The same words typed on their own routed fine, which makes it a confusing one to report: the group works, the bot answers, but documents silently vanish.

Extraction moves into an exported `extractMessageText()` so the caption-bearing types are one reviewable list. A type missing from that list fails exactly this way — silently — so it's worth having in one place with the media list it must stay in sync with.

### 2. Media was downloaded before anyone wanted it

Every inbound image, video, audio and document was fetched from WhatsApp's CDN as it arrived: for every chat the account is in, whether or not any of them is wired to an agent, and before the engage test that drops most of what is left.

Attachment handling now splits into the two views #3711 adds — `content` is the routing view (text, sender, attachment metadata, no bytes), `resolveContent()` is the delivery view with the bytes fetched.

## Shape of the change

`downloadInboundMedia` splits in two:

- **`detectInboundMedia()`** — names attachments from the envelope alone, no network. The traversal guard on the attacker-controlled `documentMessage.fileName` moves here, since it belongs with naming rather than with the fetch. This is also what now answers *"does this message have media?"* for the empty-protocol-message guard, so that guard no longer depends on a successful download.
- **`fetchInboundMedia()`** — takes those refs and does the network part, unchanged otherwise (same `reuploadRequest` handling, same `DATA_DIR/attachments` destination, same `localPath` result).

`appendMediaFailureNote` moves onto the delivery view with the fetch. It used to run **before** routing, where a failed download could change the very text the engage pattern was about to match against.

## Tests

`src/channels/whatsapp-inbound-content.test.ts` — extraction per caption-bearing type (including the document caption that regressed), and detection: sender-supplied filenames, generated fallbacks, the traversal guard, and multi-attachment ordering.

All WhatsApp tests on this branch pass: 5 files, 72 tests. The change introduces no new type errors (28 before, 28 after — all pre-existing on `channels`, from `local-web`/`deltachat` against modules this branch doesn't carry yet).
