prs.title: feat(router): defer expensive inbound content until an agent will receive it
prs.body:
## Problem

An adapter that has to do real work to produce a message's full content — a network fetch, a download — has nowhere to put it. `InboundMessage.content` must be complete before `routeInbound` ever sees it, so the work happens for **every** message that arrives: including the ones in chats no agent is wired to, and the ones that fail their wiring's engage test.

On a personal WhatsApp number that means every image, video and document across every chat the account is in, fetched from WhatsApp's CDN on arrival and thrown away moments later.

## Approach

An optional second view of the same message:

- **`content`** — the ROUTING view. Cheap, always present, complete enough for every routing decision: text to match an engage pattern against, sender, attachment metadata with no bytes.
- **`resolveContent()`** — the DELIVERY view. The same object with the expensive parts filled in.

The router calls the resolver at most once per message, and only from `deliverToAgent` — i.e. only once some agent is actually going to persist the message — then writes that result instead of `content`.

Details worth reviewing:

- **Memoized on the promise, not the value**, so a fan-out to several engaged agents shares one fetch rather than racing several.
- **Placement is deliberate.** After the command gate (a filtered or denied slash command shouldn't pull attachment bytes, and the gate only reads text, which both views share) and after `backfillNewSession` (which reads sibling sessions, never this message's content) — so the work sits behind everything that can still abort the write.
- **Fail-soft.** If the resolver rejects, the router logs and persists the routing view. The agent loses the bytes, not the message; the container formatter already renders metadata-only attachments as `[document: report.pdf]`.
- **`fanInboundMessage` and `dispatchSessionCreated` keep the routing view on purpose.** Session-echo rows and hook payloads want to know an attachment exists; they shouldn't each carry another copy of it.

## Compatibility

Adapters that leave `resolveContent` undefined are completely unaffected — `content` is delivered as-is. That is every adapter in trunk today, so this lands as a no-op for existing installs.

## Tests

`src/router-deferred-content.test.ts` covers the laziness contract itself, through the real `routeInbound` path:

- never resolved for a chat with no wiring at all
- never resolved when the engage test fails
- resolved exactly once across a fan-out to several engaged agents
- resolved on the accumulate path (that message is still persisted)
- falls back to the routing view when resolution throws

Full suite: 188 files, 2247 tests passing.

## Follow-up

The WhatsApp adapter is the first consumer — mmv/nanoclaw@`feat/whatsapp-lazy-media`, which I'll open against `channels` once this lands. It also fixes a `documentMessage.caption` omission that was dropping captioned PDFs outright.

## Note

I could not run the full suite on this machine (linux/arm64, Node v23.1.0) without temporarily pinning `better-sqlite3` back to 11.10.0 — the 13.0.3 prebuild loads but segfaults in `new Database()`, killing the vitest workers. That pin was local to verification only and is **not** in this diff.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route forum and private-chat topics as threads
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Telegram topics become threads, both in forum supergroups and in a bot's private chats (threaded mode), so replies land in the topic they came from and a `per-thread` wiring gets one session per topic.

- **Problem**: the adapter declares `supportsThreads: false`, so every topic of a forum supergroup shares one session and replies go to General. Same for private-chat topics (Bot API 9.3 threaded mode, toggled in BotFather): replies leave the topic.
- **Fix**: `supportsThreads: true`, defaults `threads: true` for groups and DMs. The inbound interceptor normalizes thread ids:
  - forum supergroup (`getChat` → `is_forum`, cached per chat): keep `telegram:<chat>:<topic>`;
  - private chat while the bot has topics enabled (`getMe` → `has_topics_enabled`, cached 5 min, a "disabled" answer re-checked after 30 s): keep `telegram:<user>:<topic>`;
  - a private-chat message outside any topic gets no thread id, so a `per-thread` DM wiring resumes its thread-less session instead of opening a `telegram:<user>` one beside it;
  - anything else (reply chains in ordinary groups) folds back to the chat.
- **Why the is_forum check**: in ordinary groups Telegram also stamps reply chains with `message_thread_id`. Without the check (as in #2892), every reply chain in a plain group would open its own session.
- **getMe failure**: if it can't be read and nothing is cached, the private-chat topic is kept (Telegram only sends a private-chat `message_thread_id` for topics), rather than merging topics into one session.
- **DM sessions**: a DM wiring stays one shared session unless it opts into `session_mode 'per-thread'`; replies go back to the topic either way.
- **Out of scope**: per-topic auto-registration (#1626).

## Related work

Supersedes #2892 (closed; flipped the flag without the non-forum fold). Related: #1699.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/channels/telegram-forum-topics.test.ts`: forum keeps the topic; non-forum folds to the chat; chat-level group ids need no lookup; a DM outside any topic gets no thread id; private-chat topic kept while `has_topics_enabled`, dropped when disabled, kept when `getMe` fails; `is_forum` and `has_topics_enabled` cached -> 8 pass. Without the second commit, 4 of them fail.
- `telegram-pairing-interceptor` / `telegram-connect-group` / `channel-defaults` tests pass
- `tsc --noEmit`: no new errors vs. `channels` HEAD. `telegram-registration*` / `telegram-instances-registration` tests need every channel package installed; they fail identically on `channels` HEAD in a Telegram-only checkout (the DM `threads` expectation there is updated)
- Manual: checked against a running bot: forum topics and private-chat topics each get their own session with `session_mode=per-thread`, replies land in the topic, and a private-chat message outside topics resumes the existing DM session
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Telegram: forum topics and topics in a bot's private chats are now separate threads; replies go back to the topic. Set a DM wiring to session_mode per-thread to get one session per topic.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. One extra `getChat` call per group chat and a cached `getMe`, using the bot's own token.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(approvals): expire unanswered cards and allow reject by id
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Approval cards that nobody answers stay `pending` forever, and the agent that asked is never told.

- **Problem**: module-initiated approvals (`install_packages`, `cli_command`, `create_agent`, …) have no TTL. `pending_approvals.expires_at` is written only by the OneCLI flow, so any other card whose reply is lost — a native adapter restarting, a newer card taking the reply — is unresolvable. The requesting agent waits on a request that will never land.
- **Fix (expiry)**: the host sweep expires module-initiated approvals unanswered for 7 days. `finalizeExpired()` relays a **context-only** note (`trigger: false`), so the agent reads it on its next wake instead of being woken days later to hear that a request lapsed. OneCLI rows keep their own gateway expiry and are excluded by action.
- **Fix (manual clearing)**: `ncl approvals reject <id> [--reason]` clears a card whose buttons can no longer be used. The requesting agent is told exactly as if Reject had been pressed; if its session is gone the row is simply removed.
- **Deliberately not added**: a by-id *approve*. Approving stays a human decision made on the card; only rejecting and expiring are recoverable out-of-band.
- **Out of scope**: the adapter-side half of this (a reply to an already-resolved card saying so, instead of confirming) — that belongs with the WhatsApp card work in #3752.

## Related work

Closes #

No issue. Related: #3752 observes that `pending_approvals.expires_at` "exists in the schema, but nothing outside its migration reads or writes it" — this PR is the host-side half of that gap, and is independent of the adapter change proposed there. The two do not touch the same files.

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/modules/approvals/ src/cli` → 251 passed, including the new `src/modules/approvals/stale.test.ts` (expiry of a stale card, OneCLI rows left alone, missing-session rows removed, reject-by-id outcomes, and the already-resolved race).
- `pnpm test` (full suite) → 2626 passed. The 15 failures in `scripts/add-dial-tool-scope.test.ts` and `setup/lib/restart*.test.ts` reproduce identically on an unmodified checkout of this base commit; they need `jq` and a systemd user instance, neither present on the test host.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check "src/**/*.ts"` → clean; `eslint` → 0 errors.

```release-note
Approval cards left unanswered for 7 days now expire and tell the requesting agent, and `ncl approvals reject <id>` clears a card whose buttons no longer work.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

`ncl approvals reject` is registered with `access: 'open'`, matching the existing `list`/`get` on this resource. It can only ever *reject* — it cannot approve, so it grants no privilege and cannot be used to push a held action through. The caller is recorded as `agent:<group>` or `host` in the same way as other CLI-initiated actions. Expiry runs host-side on the existing sweep and takes no input from a channel.

Release notes

Sourced from rstest's releases.

v0.28.0

[0.28.0] 2026/10/18

Changed

  • #[case(...)] argument attributes other than #[case(opt)], #[case(default)] and #[case(default(...))] are now rejected: before they were silently accepted as #[case]. #[case()] is still accepted as #[case].
  • rstest_reuse 0.7.1: when the function where the template is applied defines a #[case(...)] argument modifier, it replaces the template's #[case] attribute.

Added

  • Cases can omit the values of #[case(default)], #[case(default(expr))] and #[case(opt)] arguments: the trailing values can be omitted and _ can be used to skip a value. #[case(opt)] wraps the given value in Some() and uses None when omitted. Magic conversion works for #[case(default(expr))] expressions and #[case(opt)] values. See #325 and #327, thanks to @​Atreyagaurav.

Updates `tower-http` from 0.7.0 to 0.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from tower-http's releases.

tower-http-0.7.1

Added

  • fs: add ServeDir::redirect_to_trailing_slash() to serve directory indexes directly instead of first redirecting to the trailing-slash path. The redirect remains the default (#728)
  • fs: add ignore_multi_range_requests() to ServeDir and ServeFile, serving the full representation when a request asks for multiple byte ranges. The existing 416 Range Not Satisfiable response remains the default (#727)
  • request-id: the constructors and accessors on the request-id layers, services, and RequestId are now const fn, so they can be used in const context (#716)

Changed

  • fs: the minimum http-range-header requirement is now 0.4.2 (#661)

Fixed

  • behavioral change: fs: make ServeDir::try_call propagate expected filesystem I/O errors when no fallback is configured, as documented, instead of converting them to 404 Not Found responses (#718)
  • decompression: don't end the body when a data frame with no remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream. Trailers following such a frame were dropped and could not be recovered (#722)
  • decompression: return a body error when a data frame with remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream, rather than silently truncating. This regressed in 0.7.0 (#712)
  • fs: multipart range requests are now rejected before range validation, so they consistently return 416 Range Not Satisfiable with a Cannot serve multipart range requests body instead of a generic unsatisfiable-range response (#661)
  • fs: range error responses no longer carry representation headers such as Content-Type and Content-Encoding (#727)
  • set-header: SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer and SetMultipleResponseHeader are now Clone regardless of the response body type, matching the fix applied to the request-side types in 0.7.0 (#714)

**发现问题时间**：2026-10-25 上午，桌面客户端登录时提示「账号已被禁用」（欢迎页登录跳转后直接报错，无法进入应用）

3. 此后仅通过官方 LobsterAI 客户端使用内置模型，不再以任何方式将接口转发到客户端之外。

### 请求

恳请协助审核解封。如需核对注册信息、设备信息或使用记录，可随时通过本账号（133****1280）与我联系。感谢！

---

prs.title: feat(release): add codown SVN publish workflow
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds release tooling that builds signed installers and submits them to the internal SVN drop used by Codown. Deployment stays manual: the scripts print the ticket URL and the public download URLs, and never open a browser or create a ticket.

## New commands

- **`npm run release:codown -- --target <target> [--keyfrom <channel>] [--silent] [--dry-run]`**
  - Targets: `mac-arm64`, `mac-x64`, `mac-universal`, `win-channel`, `win-web`, `linux-x64`. Each target must be built on its native host.
  - Checks signing credentials and the SVN working copy before building.
  - Builds into an isolated, locked `.work/codown-build-*` directory, then verifies signatures (Authenticode on Windows, `codesign` + `stapler` on macOS).
  - Stages renamed artifacts with size and sha256 in `release/codown/<keyfrom>/<version>/<target>/manifest.json`, then submits them to SVN.
- **`npm run codown:publish -- --manifest <path> [--dry-run]`**: retries SVN submission from an existing snapshot without rebuilding.
- **`npm run codown:verify -- --manifest <path>`**: after manual deployment, downloads every artifact from the public URL and checks its size and sha256.

## Changes to existing scripts

- **`dist-win-web.cjs`**: new `--codown` mode. It bakes the final `.nsis.7z` URL (from `CODOWN_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`) into the web installer, so the build takes one pass instead of upload-then-stub-rebuild.
- **`build-env.cjs` / `electron-builder-config.cjs`**: new `LOBSTERAI_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR` overrides the electron-builder output directory. Without it, the output directory is unchanged.
- **`.env.example`**: documents the six optional `CODOWN_*` settings. Real URLs and paths stay in `.env` or CI secrets.

## Safety

- SVN credentials are removed from the build subprocess environment. The password goes through stdin with `--no-auth-cache` and is redacted from error output.
- Refuses to overwrite an SVN file that already exists with different bytes; identical files are reused.
- Refuses to publish from a dirty working copy, or when the working copy changes during publication.
- On failure, reverts only the files this run added. Committed nodes are left alone.
- Lock directories prevent concurrent builds and concurrent publishers.

## Electron-specific notes

- Build and release scripts only. No app runtime, IPC, preload, storage, or OpenClaw config changes.
- Existing `dist:*` commands behave the same unless `--codown` or `LOBSTERAI_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR` is set.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run tests/codownPublish.test.ts tests/channelInstallPolicy.test.ts`: 37 passed.
- `npm test`: 759 files, 8167 tests passed (177 skipped).
- ESLint (CI rules) on the changed test files: clean.
- Not verified end-to-end against the internal SVN drop and Codown deployment as part of this PR.

issues.title: [Feature]: Surface stale (unprocessed) daily notes as deduplicated Inbox reminders
issues.body:
## Background

This is **not** a re-filing of #4652 or of agentscope-ai/ReMe#393 — both already discuss memory lifecycle, and both were answered with "ReMe v4 covers it". This issue is the specific residual gap that neither side covers today, verified in code.

- **#4652** (closed as completed) — maintainers explained that ReMe v4 addresses lifecycle, status tracking and condensation.
- **agentscope-ai/ReMe#393** (open) — maintainers replied: *"the reminder policy is likely better owned by QwenPaw, while ReMe provides generic, read-only daily-note primitives"*, and suggested *"a scheduled QwenPaw check with deduplicated inbox reminders"*.

So the field exists on the ReMe side and the reminder is supposed to live here — but **nothing on either side actually consumes it yet**.

## The gap (verified in this repo)

ReMe v4 stores hot-tier daily notes at `daily/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<slug>.md` with a `status` frontmatter field (absent = pending, plus `completed` / `skipped`), and its Digester flips that field after processing.

In QwenPaw:
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py` uses `status` for **auto-memory task state** (`pending` / `running` / `completed` / `failed` / `cancelled`) — same word, unrelated concept.
- Nothing reads the daily-note `status` frontmatter.
- `app/inbox_store.py` can append events, but there is no producer for "notes still pending", and no dedupe.
- Consequence: a daily note that never got processed simply goes quiet. Nothing surfaces it at day 8, day 30, or ever.

## Proposal (opt-in, read-only)

A check that:

1. scans daily notes older than N days (default 7, configurable);
2. treats a note as pending when `status` is **absent** (per the ReMe v4 convention) — `completed` / `skipped` are skipped;
3. takes the date **from the path** (`<daily_dir>/YYYY-MM-DD/...`), using `mtime` only when the path carries no date;
4. posts one Inbox event per `(file, slug)`, deduplicated against existing `source_type="stale_notes"` events — re-notify only after the event is read/deleted or the note disappears;
5. never edits, deletes, or rewrites notes; never writes memory; **off by default**.

## Integration question

`app/crons/executor.py` only dispatches prompts to the agent — there is no subprocess/shell job type — so scheduling has to be agent-driven. Options:

- **(a)** a built-in tool (e.g. `check_stale_notes`) that an agent or a cron prompt can call, plus a documented cron prompt example;
- **(b)** a CLI subcommand — not sufficient alone, since cron cannot run shell commands.

I would implement **(a)**. Which layer should own it — `agents/tools` or `app/` — and is this the shape you want? Happy to adjust before writing any code.

## Scope

~150 lines of new module plus focused tests (has-pending, no-pending, resolved-only, path-date vs `mtime` fallback, dedupe across runs). No new dependency, no default config change, no memory writes.

issues.title: Creator: TTS cannot use an Aliyun Token Plan key — the qwen-audio-tts family speaks a different DashScope service, and the protocol option is missing from the model-config UI
issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.2.2.post1**, Windows Server 2022
- Plugin **QwenPaw Creator 2.0.4** (installed from Apps)
- Credential: Aliyun **Token Plan (team edition)** API key, `sk-sp-` prefix
- All measurements below were taken live on **2026-11-02** against
  `token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com`.

## Summary

In Creator's model configuration, **LLM / VLM / image / video already offer
`Aliyun Token Plan` as a protocol**, and switching them over works. **TTS and
digital-human (s2v) still offer only `DashScope（百炼）`.**

For TTS this is not just a missing dropdown entry — even hand-editing
`model_config.json` to point `tts.base_url` at the Token Plan gateway cannot
work, because the model a Token Plan subscription serves
(`qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus`) is on a **different DashScope service** than the
one Creator implements.

## Root cause

### 1. Two different DashScope synthesis services

`backend/models/tts_model.py` posts synthesis requests to a hard-coded path:

```
services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation      # qwen-tts family
```

`qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus` / `-flash` instead live on:

```
services/audio/tts/SpeechSynthesizer                # qwen-audio-tts family
```

and they nest **every** synthesis parameter inside `input` (there is no sibling
`parameters` object):

```json
{
  "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus",
  "input": {
    "text": "...", "voice": "...", "format": "mp3",
    "sample_rate": 24000, "rate": 1.3, "volume": 50, "pitch": 1.0
  }
}
```

The response shape, however, **is** the same `{output:{audio:{url}}, usage:{characters}}`,
so `_download_audio()` and the usage accounting can be reused unchanged.

Two further family differences worth encoding in `tts_capabilities.py`:

- `qwen-audio-tts` accepts a numeric `rate` (0.5–2.0) **over HTTP**. The current
  gate `if rate != 1.0 and transport != "websocket"` therefore rejects a rate
  this model actually supports.
- Its system-voice catalogue is **597 voices per model**, named with a
  model-name prefix (`qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus-longcanzhuyue`). That is far too
  large to inline in the capability table, so it wants a data file.

### 2. The UI protocol list has no Token Plan entry

In the built bundle the per-capability protocol option arrays are:

```js
Do = [..., "Aliyun Token Plan"]   // image  ✓
Po = [..., "Aliyun Token Plan"]   // video  ✓
Io = ["DashScope（百炼）"]         // tts    ✗
Ao = ["DashScope（百炼）"]         // s2v    ✗
```

plus a load-time normalisation that silently rewrites anything unlisted:

```js
Io.includes(q.tts.protocol) || (q.tts.protocol = Io[0])
```

So a hand-edited `tts.protocol = "Aliyun Token Plan"` is **reset back to
DashScope** the moment the model-config panel is opened and saved. The
per-protocol defaults table (`tts` → `{"DashScope（百炼）": {base_url, models}}`)
also has no Token Plan row.

Interestingly the i18n bundle **already ships** a `ttsTokenPlanHint` string
("Token Plan supports CosyVoice synthesis models; voice cloning and voice
design need a general DashScope API key"), so this looks half-finished rather
than deliberately excluded.

### 3. The connectivity probe hard-codes the same wrong path

`_probe_payload()` in `backend/api/model_routes.py` rebuilds the TTS probe URL
from `urlparse(base_url).netloc` plus a literal
`/api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation`, so the "test
connection" button would validate the wrong service for this family.

## Measured evidence

`GET https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/models`
with a Token Plan key returns **21 models**. Speech-relevant ones:

```
qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus        <- the only speech-synthesis model in the plan
qwen-audio-3.0-asr-flash
qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus
```

`contains 'cosyvoice': []` — no CosyVoice model is in the plan, so the
WebSocket transport in `tts_model.py` is unreachable on Token Plan regardless
(the `dashscope` SDK is pinned to `wss://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api-ws/v1/inference`).

`POST /api/v1/services/audio/tts/SpeechSynthesizer` with
`model=qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus`, `voice=longanhuan_v3.6`, `text="嗨"`:

```
HTTP 200   content-type: application/json
{"output":{"audio":{"data","expires_at","id","url"},"finish_reason":"stop"},
 "usage":{"characters":2},"request_id":"c38d8ff4-ceb4-4b31-92ff-ce19b1123a5c"}
```

A full 30-character sentence returned a 4.54 s / 24 kHz mono / 160 kbps mp3
(90,811 bytes) and billed `characters: 47`; the same text at `rate=1.3`
returned 1.54 s and billed 17. So **`rate` works over HTTP** for this family.

Voice management is absent on Token Plan —
`POST /api/v1/services/audio/tts/customization` returns
`404 {"code":"InvalidParameter","message":"Model not exist."}` for all three of
`qwen-voice-enrollment`, `voice-enrollment` and `qwen-voice-design`. Voice
cloning/design therefore genuinely needs a second, general DashScope key.

System voices were verified by live probe rather than scraped, because the
naming is inconsistent: `longanhuan_v3.6`, `longanlingxin`, `longanlufeng` and
`longanlingxi` all return HTTP 200, while 13 other plausible names
(`longanfengyue`, `loongmary`, `longanhuan_v3.1`, `Cherry`, ...) return
`400 [cosyvoice:]Engine error [411]: TTS speak operation failed`.

## Suggested change

Backend (+200/−35 across three files, plus one generated data file):

1. `models/tts_capabilities.py` — add a third family `qwen-audio-tts` with a
   per-capability `http_suffix`, a `supports_rate` flag (replacing the
   `transport != "websocket"` test) and a `supports_clone` flag; load the 597
   voice ids from `models/tts_voices/<model>.json` (regenerated from the
   official 基础音色 workbook) instead of inlining them.
2. `models/tts_model.py` — branch the payload on family: `qwen-audio-tts` posts
   to `capability.http_suffix` with `format` / `sample_rate` / `rate` inside
   `input`; refuse clone/design with an actionable message when
   `supports_clone` is false, instead of letting a 404 surface mid-project.
3. `api/model_routes.py` — build the TTS probe URL from
   `capability.http_suffix` rather than a literal, and fall back to the
   existing zero-cost `_token_plan_models_probe()` when the model has no system
   voices and no management surface.

Frontend (`ui/src`, two spots): add `"Aliyun Token Plan"` to the TTS protocol
array and a `{base_url: "https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/api/v1", models: []}`
row to the TTS defaults table. (`models: []` because the TTS model dropdown is
already served by `GET /models/tts-capabilities`.)

## Not fixable in code: digital human on Token Plan

Reporting this so nobody else spends time on it. `s2v` cannot run on a Token
Plan subscription, for two independent reasons:

1. **The model is not in the plan.** The 21-model list contains no s2v /
   lip-sync model at all — neither `wan2.2-s2v` nor `wan2.2-s2v-detect`. Only
   `wan3.0-video` (plain video generation).
2. **There is no media-upload channel.** `wan2.2-s2v` only accepts
   `image_url` / `audio_url`, so local media must first go through the
   model-bound temporary storage API. On the Token Plan gateway
   `GET /api/v1/uploads?action=getPolicy` answers **404 with an empty body**
   for both `wan2.2-s2v` and `wan3.0-video`. This matches the note already in
   `models/config.py::is_token_plan_protocol()`. `video_model.py` works around
   it by passing public HTTP(S) URLs through untouched, but a digital-human
   portrait and its driving audio are normally local artefacts.

The workable configuration today is to leave `s2v` on a general DashScope key
(`reuse_llm_key: false`) while everything else runs on Token Plan — which the
schema already supports, so this part only needs documenting.

## Minor doc bug (Aliyun side, FYI)

The Token Plan "接入多模态生成模型" page shows the TTS call as
`curl ... -o "speech.mp3"`, implying a binary response. The endpoint actually
returns `application/json` with `output.audio.url`; the Qwen-Audio-TTS HTTP API
reference is the correct one.

## Happy to help

I have this working locally (offline request-construction tests plus a live
end-to-end synthesis through `tts_model.synthesize()`). I don't have push
access to open a PR, but I can supply the full diff and the voice-catalogue

issues.title: [Bug]: Codex/Qoder 后端的定时任务将非空请求误判为空
issues.body:
### 现象

智能体使用 `codex`（或其他第三方后端）时，包含完整文本指令的 `agent` 类型定时任务会立即失败：

```text
ValueError: Third-party agent requests require text or attachments
```

失败发生在交给第三方智能体之前。

### 复现步骤

1. 为智能体选择 Codex 后端。
2. 创建一条包含非空文本指令的 `agent` 类型定时任务。
3. 手动执行或等待调度触发。
4. 观察执行记录中的上述异常。

已在当前 `main`（`c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`）通过单元测试复现；原问题也出现在 `2.2.2`。

### 原因和预期行为

`CronExecutor.execute()` 将 `job.request.model_dump(mode="json")` 得到的字典传入 `Workspace.stream_query()`。内置 `Runtime` 会将字典转换为 `AgentRequest`，但第三方后端直接进入 `HarnessRuntime`，其中通过 `getattr(request, "input", None)` 读取输入，因此把非空字典请求误判为空。

预期在共享请求入口统一转换字典，再选择后端；已有请求对象保持原样。文本、附件、`session_id`、`user_id`、`channel` 和 `request_context` 都应保留。

### 修复验证

准备的最小修复仅在 `Workspace.stream_query()` 中增加字典到 `AgentRequest` 的转换，并增加 Codex/Qoder、字典/已有对象、附件和执行上下文的回归测试。

```text
修复前：3 failed, 4 passed
修复后（Harness 和 cron 相关单元测试）：249 passed, 3 skipped
```

将提交对应的修复 PR。

issues.title: [Bug]: v2.3.0b2 在受限环境(fnOS 应用沙箱)启动即崩:dependency_maintenance 锁根目录优先按 pwd home 推导,绕过了 $HOME,且覆盖变量 QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR 未在文档中说明
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2(PyPI wheel)

## Description

在受限部署环境(飞牛 fnOS NAS 应用沙箱)中,`pip install qwenpaw==2.3.0b2` 后以专用应用用户运行 `python3 -m qwenpaw app`,**import 阶段即崩溃**,进程无法启动。

根因:`qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py` 的 `state_root()` 在解析依赖托管锁根目录时,**优先取 `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir`(passwd 数据库的 home),而不是 `os.environ["HOME"]`**。fnOS 这类托管环境会为应用创建专用用户(passwd 中 home 为 `/home/<appuser>`),但该目录实际不存在且 `/home` 对应用用户不可写,于是 `_open_lock()` 内的 `Path(...).mkdir(parents=True)` 抛出 `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'`,发生在 `qwenpaw/__init__.py` 的 import 期,进程必然退出。

代码中其实已提供覆盖变量 **`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`**(优先级最高),实测设置后可正常启动——但该变量未在任何文档中出现,受限环境的用户无从得知。

建议(任选或组合):
1. 解析顺序改为 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` → `$HOME` → `pwd.pw_dir`(与多数工具一致,pw_dir 在托管环境往往是错的);
2. `state_root()` 失败时给出可操作的错误信息,指明可设置 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`;
3. 在文档中说明该变量。

**Related PR(s):** 无

**Security considerations:** 无(仅涉及部署环境下的路径与权限)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b2
- **OS:** 飞牛 fnOS 1.x(Debian 系 NAS 系统)
- **Install method:** pip(从 PyPI 镜像安装到专用 venv)
- **Python version:** 3.12(fnOS python312 依赖应用)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 创建专用用户且不创建其 home 目录,例如 `useradd -M qwenpaw`(`/home` 为 root 所有,应用用户不可写)
2. 以该用户运行 venv 中的内核:`python3 -m qwenpaw app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18088`
3. import 阶段立即崩溃

注:同类环境的 b1(2.3.0b1)不受影响——b2 才在 `qwenpaw/__init__.py` 引入了 import 期的 `lease_environment` 调用。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'`,启动即崩,且错误信息未指向任何可操作的解决方案
- **Expected:** 尊重 `$HOME`(或至少在 pw_dir 不可用时回退),或给出指向 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` 的清晰错误

## Logs / Screenshots

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 189, in _run_module_as_main
  File "/vol2/@apphome/qwenpaw/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/qwenpaw/__init__.py", line 11, in <module>
    _environment_custody.lease_environment(_environment_custody.host_sites())
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 386, in lease_environment
    _lease_environment(sites, parent_pid, timeout)
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 421, in _lease_environment
    with admission():
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 414, in admission
    with file_lock(
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 323, in file_lock
    descriptor = open_coordination_lock(path)
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 310, in _open_lock
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'
```

相关代码(`state_root()` 解析顺序,`dependency_maintenance.py` 约 205-230 行):`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` 覆盖 → `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir` → `$HOME` → 报错。问题在于 pw_dir 的优先级高于 `$HOME`,且失败信息未提示覆盖变量。

## Additional Notes

- 已验证的 workaround:`export QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR=<可写的绝对路径>`(我们指向应用数据区),设置后 b2 可正常启动并运行。建议将此变量写入文档。
- 部署背景:我们是 QwenPaw 的飞牛 fnOS 第三方打包维护方([QwenPaw for fnOS](https://github.com/yaozy2020/QwenPaw-for-fnOS)),b2 的依赖托管子进程机制我们在打包层已配合进程组保底;锁路径问题修复后我们会跟进升级测试。

issues.title: [Feature]: Make skill-pool download a cancellable background job (progress + explicit cancel)
issues.body:
Follow-up from the review of #8055.

`POST /pool/download` currently waits for the whole copy before responding.
#8055 removes the event-loop freeze by moving the copy to a worker thread,
but the request itself is still synchronous, so a large skill still trips
the client's 30 s timeout and the UI still reports a failure for a download
that is actually progressing.

The end state we want:

* The download runs as a server-side job; the request returns immediately
  with a job id.
* Progress is pollable (files copied / total, current skill).
* Explicit cancellation that **reaches the worker** — aborting the HTTP
  request does not stop an already-running copy, so cancel needs to be a
  real signal to the thread doing the work.
* The frontend stops treating 30 s as a failure and shows pending state
  until the job reports done or cancelled.

Scope note: this changes the API contract and the UX, which is why it was
not folded into #8055.

Related: #8013

issues.title: [Bug]: DingTalk final reply silently dropped when sessionWebhook expires — on_event_message_completed has no Open API fallback (errcode=300001)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2 (also reproduced against `main` @ `210f5aa` — the code below is identical there)

## Description

When a DingTalk reply takes longer than the `sessionWebhook` TTL, **the final reply is silently dropped**. The user receives nothing: no text, no error, no fallback — while the framework still emits the "done" reaction, which makes it look like the task succeeded.

The root cause is that `on_event_message_completed()` — the function that actually sends the agent's final reply in markdown mode — calls `_send_via_session_webhook()` and **discards the return value**. It has neither the Open API fallback nor the delivery-error surfacing that the other two send paths in the same file already have.

`src/qwenpaw/app/channels/dingtalk/channel.py` has 4 call sites of `_send_via_session_webhook()`:

| line | enclosing function | Open API fallback | raises delivery error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2029 | `send_content_parts` | ✅ | ✅ |
| 3551 | `send` | ✅ | ✅ |
| **2503** | **`on_event_message_completed`** | ❌ | ❌ |
| 573 | `_on_consume_error` | ❌ | ❌ |

The docstring of `on_event_message_completed` even claims the behaviour that the code does not implement:

```python
    """Send completed message via AI Card or sessionWebhook.

    ...
    Markdown mode: send via sessionWebhook or fallback to send().
    """
```

but the body calls `_send_via_session_webhook(...)` directly and drops the `bool` it returns.

Because DingTalk's `sessionWebhook` is a short-lived credential (per the official docs: *"SessionWebhook 通过 TLS 安全信道和短周期的过期时间确保了其安全性…… 如果你的场景是收到请求后立即回复，可以忽略该过期时间的约束。"*), any reply that takes longer than that TTL is lost.

**Impact is worst for long-running tasks** — exactly the case where a human is most likely to be waiting for an answer.

### Why the existing fallback does not save it

All the required configuration is already present in the reported setup:

- `channels.dingtalk.client_id` / `channels.dingtalk.client_secret` — configured
- the stored session-webhook entry → `conversation_id`, `conversation_type: "dm"`, `sender_staff_id` — present

so `_try_open_api_fallback()` would succeed if it were ever called. But it is never reached: the reply path does not call it. In the log of the reproduction below, `Open API fallback` appears **0 times**, while `errcode=300001` appears 10 times in a row.

### Related history

- #2221 (closed) reported the same `errcode=300001` for the **cron/proactive** path.
- #710 (PR, closed) added fail-fast delivery errors for **proactive** sends, and explicitly stated: *"keep reply-context behavior unchanged (no new exception for normal reply path)"*.

So the proactive path was hardened while the **reply** path was intentionally left as-is. That decision is reasonable for a request that is answered immediately, but it leaves long-running replies unprotected — the reported case.

### Proposed fix

Mirror what `send_content_parts()` already does, in `on_event_message_completed()`:

```python
            delivered = await self._send_via_session_webhook(
                session_webhook,
                body.strip(),
                bot_prefix="",
                at_user_ids=at_uids,
                at_dingtalk_ids=at_dids,
            )
            if not delivered:
                await self._invalidate_session_webhook(to_handle)
                logger.warning(
                    "dingtalk on_event_message_completed: sessionWebhook send "
                    "failed, trying Open API fallback for to_handle=%s",
                    to_handle,
                )
                if not await self._try_open_api_fallback(
                    body.strip(), to_handle, send_meta
                ):
                    self._raise_delivery_error_if_api_send(
                        self._api_send_delivery_errors(send_meta),
                        "DingTalk send failed via sessionWebhook and Open API fallback",
                    )
```

Note `_invalidate_session_webhook()` intentionally keeps `conversation_id` and the other metadata, so the Open API fallback still works on subsequent sends without a redundant failed POST.

The same treatment would apply to `_on_consume_error()` (line 573), where an error message to the user is currently swallowed the same way.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2 (reproduced on `main` @ `210f5aa` as well)
- **OS:** Linux 5.19.17 (x86_64), Docker container
- **Install method:** pip (in Docker image)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a DingTalk DM to the bot requesting a task that takes longer than the `sessionWebhook` TTL (observed here: ~90 minutes).
2. The agent completes the work and produces its final reply.
3. Observe: the user receives **no reply**, no error notification, and no fallback attempt — only the "done" reaction.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the final reply is silently discarded. The log shows a repeating `errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期` (WARNING level only, no exception raised, no retry, no Open API fallback attempt). The stream then ends as if everything succeeded.
- **Expected:** the reply is delivered — by falling back to the Open API (already implemented and already configured in this setup) — or, if that also fails, the failure is surfaced instead of being swallowed.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
2026-10-20 16:59:54 | INFO | dingtalk/channel.py:956 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST ok: msgtype=markdown status=200 errcode=0
2026-10-20 17:00:18 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: msgtype=markdown session_from_url=a84d6434... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:00:44 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:01:18 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:01:31 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:01:44 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:02:31 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:02:53 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:08 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:36 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:37 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:37 | INFO | dingtalk/channel.py:3074 | dingtalk _send_emotion: reply 🥳Done on msg=msg3NrJtjbugT5fq3dWUzmlx
2026-10-20 17:03:38 | INFO | dingtalk/channel.py:2594 | dingtalk stream thread stopped
```

Grepping the same log confirms the fallback never ran:

```
$ grep -c "Open API fallback" qwenpaw.log
0
$ grep -c "_send_via_open_api" qwenpaw.log
0
$ grep -c "accessToken" qwenpaw.log
0
```

The "Done" reaction at 17:03:37 is sent through a different API path and therefore succeeds — which is exactly what makes the failure look like a success to the user.

## Additional Notes

- The 84-minute gap between the last successful send (16:59:54) and the user noticing something was wrong (18:27) was entirely this silent drop.
- DingTalk's official guidance (智能交互概述) confirms the design intent: `sessionWebhook` expiry "会满足绝大多数场景，如果你的场景是收到请求后立即回复，可以忽略该过期时间的约束" — i.e. it assumes an immediate reply. Long-running replies need the Open API path.
- A complementary hardening would be to also honour a `robot_code` / proactive-send configuration for final replies, so that delivery does not depend on a short-lived credential at all.

issues.title: [Bug]: 仅启用 console 渠道时启动仍需 30-45 秒 —— _load_builtin_channels() 无条件导入全部 18 个渠道模块(lark_oapi 单个包约 18.5 秒)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: **正文:** ## QwenPaw 版本 2.1.0(reme-ai 0.4.1.5) ## 问题描述 **只启用 `console` 一个渠道**时,服务启动仍要 30-45 秒。根因:每次进程启动时,第一次调用 `get_channel_registry()`(发生在 workspace 启动期间的 `ChannelManager.from_config()` 中)会**无条件 import 全部 18 个内置渠道模块**,其中包括大量根本不会被使用的重型第三方 SDK。 在 Windows 11 + pip 默认全量依赖的环境下实测: - `lark_oapi`(飞书 SDK):**10727 个 .py 文件、48.8 MB,冷 import 约 18.5 秒** - `aibot`:2.4 秒 - `telegram`、`slack_bolt`:各约 0.5 秒 - 其余渠道模块:合计数秒 因此 `channel_manager` 这个 workspace 服务在隔离复现中占了 **`Workspace.start()` 总耗时 35 秒里的 32 秒**。 单机一周内的启动耗时趋势(来自 `~/.qwenpaw/qwenpaw.log` 的 `Background startup completed in ...`): | 日期 | 启动耗时 | 备注 | | ----------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------ | | 08-22(lark-oapi 安装前) | 9.7s / 12.8s | | | 08-22 18:26 | — | 安装 `lark-oapi` 1.7.3 | | 08-24 | 11-22s | | | 08-25 ~ 08-28 | 33-46s | 每次启动都有稳定的 35-39s 空档 | ## 受影响组件 - [x] Core / Backend(app、agents、config、providers、utils、local_models) - [x] Channels(DingTalk、Feishu、QQ、Discord、iMessage 等) ## 环境 - **QwenPaw 版本:** 2.1.0 - **操作系统:** Windows 11(AMD64) - **安装方式:** pip - **Python 版本:** 3.12 ## 复现步骤 1. `pip install qwenpaw`(会装上全部渠道 SDK,包括 `lark-oapi`、`aibot`/`wecom-aibot-python-sdk` 等) 2. 只配置 `console` 渠道(`channels.console.enabled = true`,其余渠道全部禁用) 3. 运行 `qwenpaw app` 4. 观察到 `Background startup completed in ~35-45s`,且日志中 `Initializing ReMe Application` 与 `Console channel started` 之间存在约 35-39 秒的完全空档 ## 实际 vs 预期 - **实际:** 启动约 45 秒;`channel_manager` 服务约 32 秒(逐 service 计时:`local_workspace` 0.01s、`session` 0.00s、`chat_manager` 0.00s、`driver_manager` 0.30s、`memory_manager` 1.30s、**`channel_manager` 32.21s**、`cron_manager` 0.01s) - **预期:** 只 import 实际启用的渠道;启动约 10-15 秒 ## 日志 / 截图 ``` 09:28:49 | Server ready in 2.423s (background startup follows) 09:28:50 | Starting workspace: default 09:28:50 | Starting workspace: <第二个 agent> 09:28:51 | Initializing ReMe Application v0.4.1.5 09:28:51 | WARNING: memory_manager failed to start for <第二个 agent>: No active model configured. [ 约 39 秒完全无日志输出 ] 09:29:30 | Console channel started 09:29:31 | Workspace started successfully: default 09:29:32 | Background startup completed in 45.250s ``` 隔离复现(把 workspace 目录复制到临时路径,在独立进程中跑 `Workspace.start()`,对 `ServiceManager._start_service` 打点): ``` service local_workspace = 0.01s service session = 0.00s service chat_manager = 0.00s service driver_manager = 0.30s service memory_manager = 1.30s service channel_manager = 32.21s <-- 时间全部消耗在第一条渠道日志之前 service cron_manager = 0.01s workspace.start() TOTAL = 35.02s ``` 冷 import 耗时(全新进程;.pyc 已全量存在;Defender 实时防护已关闭——纯 import 机制成本): ``` lark_oapi 18.46s (10727 个 .py 文件) aibot 2.40s telegram 0.50s slack_bolt 0.57s dingtalk_stream 0.04s paho.mqtt 0.01s ``` ## 补充说明 - `QWENPAW_ENABLED_CHANNELS` / `QWENPAW_DISABLED_CHANNELS` 环境变量**救不了**:`get_available_channels()`(config/utils.py)自己就先调用了 `get_channel_registry()`,完整 import 发生在任何过滤之前。 - `qwenpaw/app/channels/__init__.py` 已经对 `ChannelManager` 做了懒加载,注释写明是 *"to avoid pulling feishu/lark_oapi on CLI"*,但注册表(`qwenpaw/app/channels/registry.py` 的 `_load_builtin_channels()`)在 server 路径上仍然全量 import。 - **已有一个可用的本地补丁**(已应用到 site-packages 并验证):只急切 import 必需的 `console` 渠道,其余 17 个渠道包一层懒代理,首次属性访问时才 import 真实模块并缓存结果。已验证:import 注册表后 `sys.modules` 中不再出现 `lark_oapi`;`registry["feishu"].from_config` 首次使用时能正确解析出真实的 `FeishuChannel`(一次性 21.8 秒,只在渠道真正被启用/使用时才付出)。打补丁后启动预期 ≈ 10-15 秒。 - 上游 PR 需要处理的一个行为变化:急切加载时,某个渠道依赖缺失会在注册表构建阶段被静默跳过;懒加载后,import 错误会在该渠道首次使用时才暴露。`ChannelManager.from_config` 中 `inspect.signature(ch_cls.from_config)` 这行位于包装实例化的 `try:` 之前——应挪进 `try` 内,让依赖损坏的渠道退化为现有的 "skipping: ..." 告警,而不是直接中断 workspace 启动。 -

issues.title: [Discussion] QwenPaw Hub, the multi-tenant edition, released in 2.2.0: what should we build next? / QwenPaw 多租户版 Hub 已于 2.2.0 推出：你希望我们接下来做什么？

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

issues.body:
QwenPaw started as a personal AI assistant, but the community has repeatedly asked for a better way to run it for a team. QwenPaw Hub is our first response to that call.

Related community requests:

- [#2324 — Multi-user access and admin-managed skills](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/2324)
- [#1884 — Isolated agents and workspaces for multiple users](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1884)
- [#2233 — User-scoped data and configuration](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/2233)
- [#4702 — RBAC and enterprise administration](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/4702)
- [#5780 — Multi-user account management for team use](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/5780)
- [#6335 — Deploying QwenPaw for company users](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/6335)

### What is coming in 2.2.0?

QwenPaw Hub will provide one self-hosted entry point for a team:

- Each member signs in with their own account and gets their own QwenPaw.
- Workspaces, configuration, credentials, and sessions are stored separately.
- Administrators can manage accounts and start, stop, restart, or disable user runtimes.
- Administrators can choose the Local or Docker runtime and configure shared Docker resource limits.

This is an early release for trusted companies, labs, and internal teams. Local sandboxes and Docker containers still share a host or Docker VM kernel, so 2.2.0 is not intended to be a public multi-tenant service for mutually untrusted users.

### What should come next?

Here are some directions we are considering. They are ideas for discussion, not a committed roadmap:

- **Kubernetes and operations:** Helm charts, one runtime per Pod, persistent storage, Secrets integration, multi-node scheduling, autoscaling, upgrades, backup, and disaster recovery. The community has already explored [Kubernetes deployment](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1740) and [non-interactive administrator bootstrap](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1668).
- **Central model governance:** administrators configure Model Providers, endpoints, and API keys once. Users only see an approved model catalog or friendly model aliases, without seeing credentials or, when desired, any Provider and endpoint details. This could also include defaults, fallbacks, rate limits, quotas, and cost controls.
- **Roles and policy:** user groups, RBAC, and per-user or per-group access to Agents, Skills, MCP servers, channels, and models.
- **Usage and observability:** per-user resource usage, token and cost reports, quotas, alerts, runtime logs, health status, and audit trails.
- **Pluggable runtime and isolation backends:** keep the Hub control plane independent from the execution layer and expose a stable Runtime Provisioner interface. Beyond Local and Docker, the community could add Kubernetes, gVisor, Kata Containers, MicroVMs, dedicated VMs or nodes, and remote runtime backends. A backend should declare and verify its security capabilities and fail closed when it cannot provide the promised isolation boundary.

### Tell us what you need

Which three capabilities matter most to you? What should administrators control centrally, and what should individual users be allowed to configure?

You can use this template:

```text
Team size and use case:
Deployment environment (single server / Docker / Kubernetes / other):
Trust boundary (trusted internal users / mixed trust / public users):
Top 3 requested features:
What should administrators control centrally?
Which Provider or credential details should be hidden from users?
Which runtime or isolation backend do you need?
Anything else:
```

Preview the [Hub introduction](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/website/public/blog/introducing-qwenpaw-hub.en.md) and [deployment documentation](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/website/public/docs/hub.en.md) on `main`.

---


QwenPaw 最初是一款个人 AI 助手，但社区一直在呼吁更好用的团队部署方式。QwenPaw Hub 正是我们对这些社区呼声的第一次回应。

相关社区诉求：

- [#2324 — 多用户访问与管理员分配技能](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/2324)
- [#1884 — 为多用户提供独立 Agent 与工作区](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1884)
- [#2233 — 按用户隔离数据和配置](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/2233)
- [#4702 — RBAC 与企业管理](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/4702)
- [#5780 — 面向团队的多用户账户管理](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/5780)
- [#6335 — 面向公司用户部署 QwenPaw](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/6335)

### 2.2.0 会带来什么？

QwenPaw Hub 将为团队提供一个统一的自托管入口：

- 每位成员使用自己的账户登录，并拥有自己的 QwenPaw。
- 工作区、配置、凭据和会话分别保存。
- 管理员可以管理账户，以及启动、停止、重启或禁用用户运行环境。
- 管理员可以统一选择 Local 或 Docker，并配置 Docker 资源上限。

这是一个面向公司、实验室和内部团队可信成员的早期版本。Local 沙箱和 Docker 容器仍会共享宿主机或 Docker VM 的内核，因此 2.2.0 暂不适合作为面向陌生用户的公网多租户服务。

### 接下来可以做什么？

下面是我们正在考虑的一些方向。它们是用来讨论的设想，并非已经承诺的路线图：

- **Kubernetes 与运维：** Helm Chart、每个运行环境一个 Pod、持久化存储、Secret 集成、多机调度、弹性扩缩容、升级、备份和容灾。社区已经探索过 [Kubernetes 部署](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1740)和[管理员账户自动初始化](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1668)。
- **模型统一治理：** 管理员集中配置 Model Provider、Endpoint 和 API Key；用户只看到经过批准的模型目录或易懂的模型别名，看不到凭据，并可按需隐藏 Provider 与 Endpoint 细节。还可以进一步支持默认模型、故障切换、限流、额度和成本控制。
- **角色与策略：** 用户组、RBAC，以及按用户或用户组控制 Agent、Skill、MCP、Channel 和模型的访问权限。
- **用量与可观测性：** 按用户统计资源、Token 和成本，支持配额、告警、运行日志、健康状态和审计记录。
- **可插拔运行时与隔离后端：** 让 Hub 控制面与执行层解耦，并开放稳定的 Runtime Provisioner 接口。除了 Local 和 Docker，社区还可以接入 Kubernetes、gVisor、Kata Containers、MicroVM、独立 VM 或节点，以及远程运行时。后端应声明并验证自身的安全能力；无法满足承诺的隔离边界时，应当拒绝启动而不是降级运行。

### 告诉我们你的需求

你最需要的三个能力是什么？哪些配置应该由管理员统一控制，哪些应该允许用户自己修改？

可以直接使用下面的模板回复：

```text
团队规模与使用场景：
部署环境（单机 / Docker / Kubernetes / 其他）：
信任边界（可信内部成员 / 混合信任 / 公网用户）：
最希望支持的三个功能：
管理员应该统一控制什么？
哪些 Provider 或凭据细节应该对用户隐藏？
需要哪种运行时或隔离后端？
其他补充：
```

你也可以在 `main` 分支预览 [Hub 介绍](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/website/public/blog/introducing-qwenpaw-hub.zh.md)和[部署文档](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/website/public/docs/hub.zh.md)。

issues.title: [Bug]: Markdown preview rewrites relative image/link paths to /api/files/preview/..., so links in subdirectories 404
issues.body: ## QwenPaw Version 2.2.2.post1 —— 同时核对了 `main` 分支，`console/src/components/FilePreview/FilePreview.tsx` 的链接改写逻辑在两处一致（本报告基于源码阅读，未附运行时截图）。 ## Description Console 文件抽屉里的 Markdown 预览会把文档内的**相对链接 / 相对图片路径**改写成 `/api/files/preview/...` 这类 Web 绝对路径再交给 React 渲染，但 `FilePreview` 只知道自己被 打开的那个文件，不知道改写后的 URL 在磁盘上该指向哪里，于是每个相对链接都会变成 `/api/files/preview/...`，最终 404。相对路径是 Markdown 最常见的写法，预览里几乎必然踩到。 关键代码 `console/src/components/FilePreview/FilePreview.tsx:275-304`：以 `/^([a-zA-Z][\w+.-]*):/` 判断是否带 scheme，再以“不是 `/`、`#`、`?` 开头”判定为相对路径并改写为 `api files preview`； `:389-391` 只把 `/^https?:\/\//`、`mailto:`、`#` 以及 `/` 开头的路径视为不可改写，其余一律按 相对路径重写；`:404` 渲染 ``， 而 `console/src/components/FilePreview/externalLinkComponents.tsx` 只对 `external` 链接加 `target="_blank"`。结果就是把“相对路径”归一化成了全站绝对 URL。 **相对图片同样受影响**：`![x](相对路径)` 渲染为 ``，浏览器原生 img 请求无法携带 `Authorization: Bearer`，所以即便路径正确也会 401。`buildReadOnlyHtml` 里已有的 base64 内联 分支（`hasStaticContent` / `hasDynamicContent`）并未被 `FilePreview` 使用。 **Related PR(s):** 无 **Security considerations:** 相关但非本 issue 重点——`api/files/preview` 的 URL 带 `token=` 查询参数，若被浏览器当作导航 URL 使用，token 可能经 Referer 外泄；修复时建议一并考虑。 ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [x] Skills ## Environment - **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1 - **OS:** Linux (Debian 12 容器) - **Install method:** pip（`venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/qwenpaw`） - **Python version:** 3.11 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. 工作区中创建 `docs/a.md`、`docs/b.md`、`docs/img.png`。 2. Console 文件抽屉打开 `docs/a.md`（Markdown 预览模式）。 3. 在 `a.md` 中写入：`[b](./b.md)`、`[b2](b.md)`、`[c](/docs/b.md)`、`![img](./img.png)`、`[ext](https://example.com)`。 4. 逐个点击/观察加载。 ## Actual vs Expected - **Actual:** 两个相对链接被改写为 `api/files/preview` 形式并落在文件所在目录下，目标不存在 → 404； 相对图片 `` 请求无 Bearer → 401；以 `/` 开头的链接与外部链接表现正常。 - **Expected:** 相对链接以“被打开文件所在目录”为基准解析为同源 `?path=` 绝对路径； 相对图片走 base64 内联或带 Bearer 的 blob URL，不出现 404/401。 ## Logs / Screenshots 未附运行时截图；依据为上列源码行。相关接口的鉴权行为另见 `qwenpaw/.../auth` 的 `AuthMiddleware`：缺少 Bearer 时返回 `401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"}`。 ## Additional Notes - `#anchor` 与 `?query` 未被改写（正确），`./x.md` 被改写（错误）——两者判定分支不一致。 - 已排查重复：#7900 / #3641 / #8420 均不是本问题。 - 建议修复方向：在 `FilePreview` 中以被打开文件的 `path` 为基准解析相对路径后统一走 `getFileDownloadUrl`；图片改为 base64 或 blob URL。

prs.title: feat(desktop): add approval notifications (#8460)
prs.body:
## Summary

Added desktop notifications for approvals in QwenPaw Console and the Tauri desktop application.

When QwenPaw is running in the background, new approval requests will trigger system notifications. These notifications do not expose tool-call parameters; clicking a notification takes the user directly to the relevant chat or the list of pending approvals.

Closes #8460

## What changed

- Added a toggle for desktop approval notifications, a permission status indicator, and a "test notification" button within the Inbox.
- For the browser-based version, notifications are triggered when the page is hidden or loses focus, with logic in place to prevent duplicate notifications across multiple browser tabs.
- In the Tauri desktop version, a Rust-based background process polls for approval status, ensuring notifications are sent even when the application window is minimized or hidden in the system tray.
- On macOS, the implementation utilizes native `UserNotifications` and the application's own Bundle Identity.
- On Windows and Linux, the compatible Tauri Notification Plugin is used.
- Clicking a notification opens the originating chat and highlights the specific approval request; if the source cannot be located, it defaults to the list of pending approvals.
- Added a "View Pending Approvals" option to the system tray menu, which dynamically updates based on the application's selected language.
- Implemented cleanup logic to remove notifications when an approval is completed, times out, is dismissed, or if the feature is disabled.
- Fixed an issue where notifications would fail to trigger if an approval was created while the application was in the foreground, but the window subsequently moved to the background.
- Added internationalization (i18n) resources for approval notifications, supporting Chinese, English, Japanese, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Vietnamese.

- [x] New feature

- [ ] Documentation

Add an optional Baizhi Cloud Browser (CapyBrowser) example to the English and Chinese MCP guides. It uses the existing Streamable HTTP client and private Authorization header, starts disabled, and explains that page actions require a separate compatible CDP client. It also covers rotation/removal and the responsibility to end billable cloud runs.

prs.title: fix(plugins): report an unusable dependency state root at startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a managed host whose advertised passwd home is not writable — fnOS-style
application sandboxes, read-only images — `qwenpaw` used to die during import,
before any command could run:

```
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.qwenpaw/dependency-environments'
```

The traceback names a directory the operator never chose and never mentions
`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`, the override that does work; diagnosing it
meant reading `state_root()` and knowing to look for that variable, so the host
simply looked unsupported.

After this change the same host fails during *directory selection* instead, with
a message that names the source, the reason and the remedy:

```
RuntimeError: DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE: the startup passwd home cannot host the
coordination directory (not writable); set an absolute shared
QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR to a writable directory.
```

This covers items 2 and 3 requested in #8515 (fail loudly at the point of
selection, and document the override); item 1 is deliberately not taken, for the
reason given below.

## Summary

Fixes part of #8515: on managed hosts (fnOS-style application sandboxes,
read-only images) the advertised passwd home is not writable, and startup used
to die with a bare `PermissionError` from the lock helper's first `mkdir`
while `qwenpaw` was still importing — with nothing pointing at the override
that does work.

`state_root()` now probes the coordination directory it is about to select and
fails during selection with:

```
DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE: the startup passwd home cannot host the
coordination directory (not writable); set an absolute shared
QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR to a writable directory.
```

`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` is documented in
`deploy/DEPENDENCY_MAINTENANCE.md`.

## Why not "prefer `$HOME` over `pw_dir`" (option 1 in the issue)

- `HOME` is listed in `_PRIVATE_ENVIRONMENT_CONTROL`
  (`src/qwenpaw/plugins/execution/bootstrap.py`).
- `LocalProvisioner.runtime_environment()` sets `environment["HOME"] =
  str(record.working_dir)` (`src/qwenpaw/hub/local_provisioner.py`). A host
  process and a hub runtime process therefore see different `HOME` values.

If the passwd home were unwritable and we fell back to a *different* `HOME`,
those two processes would select two different coordination roots, and the
gate/marker/lease files below them would no longer exclude each other — a
silent loss of mutual exclusion, which is worse than a loud, actionable
startup failure. The probe here only decides *whether to fail*, never *which
directory to use*, so precedence is unchanged.

Happy to rework this as option 1 if maintainers prefer availability over that
property; it is a small change on top of this one.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py`
  - `_unusable_root_reason()`: walks from the coordination directory up to the
    closest existing ancestor, returning a fixed-vocabulary reason
    (`not a directory`, `not writable`, `not searchable`,
    `no existing ancestor directory`, `unstatable (<CODE>)`) or `None`.
    Writability uses `os.access(..., effective_ids=True)` so it follows the uid
    that really creates the directories.
  - `state_root()` probes before `canonical()` and raises the actionable
    `DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE`. The explicit override branch is
    untouched and never probed; Windows keeps `USERPROFILE` with no probe.
  - The probe starts at the deepest path, so an already prepared and writable
    coordination directory under a read-only home keeps working.
- `tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py`: three cases — unusable passwd
  home, read-only home, and the "prepared root under a read-only home" guard.
- `deploy/DEPENDENCY_MAINTENANCE.md`: new "Coordination state directory"
  section.

## Evidence

Real permissions, unprivileged uid 65534 (passwd home `/`, unwritable), module
loaded straight from the checkout:

| | baseline `c26d31c0` | patched |
|---|---|---|
| no override | `PermissionError: [Errno 13] ... '/.qwenpaw/dependency-environments'` | `RuntimeError: DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE: the startup passwd home cannot host the coordination directory (not writable); set an absolute shared QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR to a writable directory.` |
| `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` set | OK | OK |

Tests:

- `tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py`: 31 passed / 5 skipped as root.
  The two permission-bit cases need a non-root uid, so they were also run as
  uid 65534: 7 passed (including the read-only-home guard).
- New tests against unpatched code: 1 failed with a bare
  `NotADirectoryError` — that is the "no actionable context" shape being fixed.
- `tests/unit/hub/test_process_isolation.py` +
  `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py`: 5 failed / 63 passed /
  8 skipped / 4 errors, identical on base and patched (pre-existing and
  environment-related: bwrap sandbox runtime, pip overlay installs).
- pre-commit on the changed files: check-ast, check-docstring-first,
  fix-encoding-pragma, detect-private-key, trailing-whitespace,
  add-trailing-comma, mypy, black, flake8, pylint — all passed.

## Notes / out of scope

`_open_lock()` still does `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` without
`O_NOFOLLOW` and without per-component link checks. That is a pre-existing
issue and unrelated to this failure, so it is deliberately left alone here;
happy to file it separately if wanted.

AI assistance: an OpenCodeReview pass (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) was used as an
independent automated reviewer of the final diff; the reproduction, the fix
and its verification were done by me.

Refs #8515

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

- `OllamaProvider.fetch_models`: after listing models, probe:
  1. `GET /api/ps` — loaded runtime `context_length` (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`)
  2. `POST /api/show` — Modelfile `num_ctx`, then GGUF `*.context_length`
- Set `max_input_length_auto_detected` so existing resolution precedence applies (explicit user config still wins)
- Keep catalog opt-out; if probes fail or return nothing usable, behavior stays at the 128k default

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 78 passed
```

Coverage includes parser precedence (served → num_ctx → GGUF), fetch enrichment with mocked `/api/ps` + `/api/show`, catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer a different probe order or want this folded into a broader local-provider detection pass.

prs.title: fix(matrix): recover cached sessions and missing device keys
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8365. Password-authenticated Matrix channels log in again on restart. If a homeserver loses a device's encryption keys while the local crypto store marks them as shared, startup does not restore the keys and the channel can appear healthy while decryption fails.

Adapt session recovery to main's native Matrix plugin and per-instance `channel_state/matrix` ownership. Reuse a session only for the same homeserver, login identity, device and password, then verify its canonical user/device pair with `whoami`. Fall back to password login only for `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`; preserve explicit tokens and main's atomic state writes and ownership checks.

Reconcile E2EE device keys at startup and re-upload a missing identity from the existing SQLite crypto store, preserving sessions. Refuse conflicting remote keys and distinguish query failure from deletion. Bound health checks, report failed key health to the plugin host, and log the first undecryptable event at error level.

## Security considerations

Use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and the session token as salt for the password fingerprint, with an explicit format version. Legacy fast-hash fingerprints cannot authorize cache reuse and require a fresh password login. Passwords are not persisted. Conflicting remote identities are never overwritten.

## Evidence

Validated on Linux/Python 3.11 against main `c26d31c0`, using real matrix-nio HTTP calls, local aiohttp homeserver fixtures, python-olm and persisted SQLite crypto stores:

```text
pytest tests/unit/channels/test_matrix_recovery.py tests/unit/channels/test_matrix.py -q
34 passed
```

Cases cover restart reuse, expired-token fallback, temporary authentication failure, changed credentials/server/device, localpart names, old unversioned fingerprints, explicit tokens, key loss, upload retry, conflicting identities, bounded health checks and the host's failed-state notification. Missing keys are restored using the original identity.

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
  The field is **derived from the instance's per-file cap** when it is not
  set explicitly: `max(8 MiB, 4 × max_bytes)`. A raised per-file cap is
  therefore no longer undercut by a fixed total — with a 16 MiB per-file cap
  a 10 MiB file reaches the wire instead of being dropped by the total — and
  a lowered per-file cap never tightens the total below the 8 MiB default.
  An explicitly configured `max_total_bytes` always wins.
- The budget is spent in two passes. A **measuring** pass records the size of
  every media block in wire order; only when the measured total exceeds the
  budget does an **enforcing** pass run, replacing the oldest media (a byte
  prefix of the wire order) with placeholders. The newest media is what the
  request keeps.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- `inline_media_size()` also sizes inline `data:` URLs, and the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters route PDF attachments through `_format_file_source()`,
  so `data:` URLs and PDFs count toward the budget like any other media.
- The per-request media **dedup scope** lives next to the budget policy
  (`SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS`) and is reset between the measuring and the enforcing
  pass — both passes have to observe the same media, otherwise the enforcing
  pass sees every source as "already shown above" and drops all media,
  including the newest one the budget keeps.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`:

- The Anthropic formatter now only remembers a media source as *seen* once it
  has actually reached the wire. A source the budget dropped is not part of
  the request, so a later copy of it stays eligible: with **A → B → A**
  (512 bytes each, 900-byte budget) the request keeps the newest **A**
  instead of folding it as "already shown above" while the dropped copy is
  nowhere in the request.
- A folded duplicate still occupies a slot in the wire order, but it is never
  sent, so it costs the budget nothing: the plan drops oldest occurrences only
  until the *deduplicated* payload — the distinct sources that actually reach
  the wire — fits the budget, and a folded copy is re-inlined when the budget
  dropped every earlier copy of its source (so A → B → A still keeps the
  newest A).
- **Video is bounded by the budget too.** Video never reaches a media hook:
  Anthropic routes it through `_format_anthropic_video_data_block`, and the
  OpenAI Chat / Responses / DashScope paths substitute it into the request
  around the formatter's `format()` call. The Anthropic path now caps the
  video before formatting it, and the OpenAI-family paths *mark* the video
  block (its `name` becomes the substitution placeholder) instead of
  replacing it, so the formatter's media hook still sees it and the budget
  can account for it at its own position in the wire order. A marked block is
  rendered as the substitution placeholder and resolved to the video wire
  dict afterwards, exactly as before. Assistant-role video is unaffected (it
  was never substituted and still is not).

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
77 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetThroughProductionWrapper` drives the same scenario
through the production formatter wrapper, and
`TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget` pins the repeated-source case through
the Anthropic wrapper, the same case with the newest copy arriving in a tool
result, and the OpenAI Chat / Responses paths:

```
A (512 B) -> B (512 B) -> A (512 B), 900-byte budget
  before:  A dropped by the budget, B inlined, newest A folded as
           "[Image omitted - already shown above]"
  after:   A dropped by the budget, B dropped by the budget,
           newest A inlined
```

The two Anthropic cases fail without the fix (verified by reverting the
`model_factory.py` change):

```
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_media
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_tool_media
2 failed, 62 passed
```

`TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget` pins the video case on all five provider
paths through the production wrapper (three 312-byte `video/mp4` blocks, a
900-byte budget → two videos inlined, one dropped):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q -k TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget
9 passed
```

Wider runs — no regressions. The failure below is pre-existing in this
environment (a file-permission assertion that depends on the process umask)
and is identical on the unmodified head commit:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers tests/unit/agents -q
# this branch:        1 failed, 5108 passed, 3 skipped
# unmodified head:    1 failed, 5098 passed, 3 skipped   (+10 = the new tests)

$ pytest tests/unit -q
# this branch:        4 failed, 18629 passed, 25 skipped
# unmodified head:    the same 4 failures (file mode, docker, sandbox paths)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

### The 8 MiB budget is raw media, not wire bytes

`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` counts the **decoded** media bytes; base64
encoding expands them by 4/3 on the wire. An 8 MiB raw budget therefore
becomes roughly **10.7 MiB** of base64 in the request body — still above the
**6 MiB** limit of the `dash_anthropic` gateway. To stay inside that gateway
the raw budget has to stay at or below ~4.5 MiB (6 MiB x 3/4).

This is deliberate: the budget bounds the *media a request carries*, in the
same unit as the per-file cap and the file sizes reported to the user. The
alternative — budgeting encoded bytes — would mean the limit no longer
matches the number a user sees for a file, and it would still not track the
provider's own overhead on top of the media.

The default is therefore a bound on the request body, not a guarantee that
every gateway accepts it: deployments behind a 6 MiB gateway should lower
`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (or set `max_total_bytes` explicitly on the
model) to match their gateway limit.

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- The per-request budget now covers **video** as well, on all five provider
  paths. One path is still outside it: the OpenAI-family / Gemini
  **tool-result video promotion** (`_promote_tool_result_videos`) injects the
  video after formatting, so it is capped per file but not per request. The
  Anthropic tool-result video goes through the media hook and is covered.
  Covering the promotion would mean moving it inside the budget's scope —
  worth a follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.
