prs.title: fix(xiaoyi): emit working frames so long turns stop looking dead in the client
prs.body:
## Description
Issue #8394: the XiaoYi channel writes nothing user-visible during a long turn — the only traffic is the invisible 30s protocol heartbeat, so a multi-minute turn shows a blank client and users reasonably conclude the bot hung (report: 7m36s of silence, then cancelled).

Minimal plugin-side fix (host contract untouched):

- **codec**: `build_working_msg()` — the A2A `status-update` envelope with `state=working` (same shape as the existing `build_completed_msg`, empty text parts, `final=False`).
- **platform**: `send_working(route)` — best-effort effect-wrapped send, returns False on delivery errors instead of raising, so a keepalive tick can never take down a turn.
- **driver**: after the first outbound send of a response route (`_perform_send`), spawn a per-route keepalive loop from `_platform._spawn` (reusing platform task accounting — cancelled on `stop()` via `_tasks` and explicitly via the new `_working_tasks` map). The loop sends an immediate first working frame (the "received" cue the issue asks for), then one frame every `working_frame_interval` (default 12s). It self-cancels when a later send replaces it, when `_before_cleanup_complete` starts (completed/final frames are about to land), and is hard-bounded by `WORKING_FRAME_MAX_WAIT=1800s` so an abandoned session cannot tick forever.
- **channel.json**: new `working_frame_interval` integer property registered in `config_fields` (set 0 to disable), read `config.get()`-style like `task_timeout_ms`.

The frames ride the existing `agent_response` envelope and keepalive loop never touches the shared driver's delivery journal, mirroring `send_finish_step` best-effort semantics (`continue_on_delivery_error=True`).

## Evidence
- `tests/unit/channels/test_xiaoyi.py` — 9 passed, including 2 new cases:
  - `test_working_frames_tick_between_sends_and_stop_at_cleanup`: a send triggers the keepalive (a `status-update.state=working` frame lands on the wire after the artifact), the loop is alive after `send`, and `channel.response.finish` cancels it (task done).
  - `test_working_frame_interval_zero_disables_keepalive`: config interval 0 → `_working_frame_interval()==0.0` and `_resume_working_frames` registers no task.
- The 4 pre-existing count-based assertions were updated to filter by frame kind/`state` instead of exact totals (working frames now appear between sends by design); frame sequences asserted (artifact → completed → final) are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(creator): release 2.0.4 with media and probe hardening
prs.body:
## Description

Release QwenPaw Creator **2.0.3 → 2.0.4**, containing only work completed **after the previous upstream release** at `45c754ee6` (merged 2026-10-27, from fork head `4d88e9b6`). The previous release's skills panel, narration safety, scratch cleanup, script import, and version badge are already upstream and are not presented as new features here.

**Fork sync completed before opening this PR.** The head is the actual **`xuanrui-L:dev/creator`** branch at `df983dd5dc960e4e98f5a8dea421c00960f44a6a`. Latest upstream `main`, `c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`, was first merged through https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/239 using a **merge commit**, preserving the upstream ancestry. The five conflicts caused by the previous squash baseline were resolved against the exact prior fork head and checked against a clean reference merge. Upstream's Docker/Node and Windows storage fixes are preserved, not overwritten.

**Scope:** **28 files under `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/`, +5,463 / −442**. The entire tree outside this plugin is byte-identical to the recorded upstream baseline. No host application, Console, other plugin, dependency declaration, or CI/release workflow change is contributed by this PR.

### What's new since 2.0.3

- **Provider-correct local media transport.** Local source images/videos, document pages, and extracted frames now use the configured VLM's transport rather than unconditionally going through DashScope temporary OSS. Non-DashScope gateways receive inline Base64; Bailian MaaS retains its supported upload path, while Token Plan credentials use inline media rather than an upload API they cannot authorize. Grounding verification carries the protocol of the credential it actually borrows, avoiding mismatched transport and wire format. Oversized decodable images step down a bounded JPEG ladder with EXIF orientation and transparency preserved appropriately; undecodable or still-oversized inputs retain a clear refusal. MIME handling respects recognizable image bytes and meaningful declarations instead of losing media behind `application/octet-stream`, including direct Anthropic/Gemini paths. Inline media is charged against the model-context budget by a bounded representative cost rather than its full Base64 text length, so normal media-bearing messages are not rejected locally before reaching the provider.
- **Connection tests report what they actually prove.** ASR tests now exercise the production-selected Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, or Fun-ASR route with one second of silent WAV audio, rather than treating a model-list or upload-policy response as transcription success. Responses are graded according to the production reader: empty/HTML/error-wrapped 2xx responses and malformed transcription structures no longer report success. A queued asynchronous task is not claimed to be a completed transcript. The optional `capability_verified` response field separates credential acceptance from verified capability; the model-settings UI shows an explicit bilingual warning for credential-only results and retains the existing success/error flows. **An operator-triggered ASR connection test can incur the provider's charge for the short sample.** No real provider calls were made during this release validation.
- **Saved credentials stay within their configured probe boundary.** A probe borrowing a saved key must target an operator-saved origin normalized by HTTPX's own scheme/host/port interpretation. LLM/VLM credential reuse follows the actual key owner; built-in default addresses are not silently treated as authorization. Probe transports filter credential-bearing GET values, do not follow redirects, reject unsupported schemes and embedded URL credentials, and apply cloud-metadata address checks including IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings. Destination checks also run before ASR sample-upload side effects and the relevant save-time probes. These are configuration-bound checks, not a restriction against legitimate operator-configured localhost/LAN model gateways.
- **Visual guidance no longer silently selects animation.** The Creator prompt and the two mandatory visual skills distinguish camera/layout language from rendering medium. Final visual variants and video prompts explicitly preserve the project/user's medium; narrative, micro-film, and documentary work without a declared style defaults to photographic texture rather than animation. Intermediate storyboard drawings retain their separately requested pencil/charcoal/etc. medium, without forcing that sketch appearance into the finished video. Existing assets are not automatically regenerated. The specialist-cancellation regression also uses the test file's existing bounded wait helper instead of a separate two-second wait; production behavior and the assertion are unchanged.

**Version and dependencies.** The existing fork version bump is included: `plugin.json`, `ui/package.json`, and both root package-lock version fields all read **2.0.4**. The host minimum remains **2.1.0**. No Python or npm dependency changes are introduced relative to current upstream. Publication still uses the unchanged version-driven main-branch workflow; this PR does not overwrite an already published artifact.

**Related Issue:** Release follow-up to https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8357. The source increments were integrated through https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/233, https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/234, and https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/237.

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, user projects, runtime directories, or generated media are committed. Saved-key origin checks constrain credential reuse; request-supplied credentials and explicitly configured local gateways remain supported. Cloud-metadata literal checks happen before dispatch, while connected-peer checks inspect the response path; behind an HTTP proxy that peer is the proxy, so this is not claimed as complete DNS/proxy isolation. Existing secure media-materialization boundaries remain unchanged. Real provider probes may be billable as noted above; automated tests and browser smoke used synthetic fixtures, not production credentials or paid calls.

prs.title: fix(dingtalk): Open API fallback when sessionWebhook expires on final reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #8343.

In markdown mode, DingTalk's final reply is sent by `on_event_message_completed()`. That path called `_send_via_session_webhook()` and **discarded the return value**, so when `sessionWebhook` expired (errcode `300001`) the user got nothing — while the "done" reaction still fired and made the task look successful.

The same file already has the correct pattern in `send_content_parts` / `send`: invalidate the webhook → `_try_open_api_fallback` → `_raise_delivery_error_if_api_send` for proactive API sends. This PR mirrors that for:

1. `on_event_message_completed` (the actual final reply path called out in the issue)
2. `_on_consume_error` (same silent-drop bug for error notices)

Media parts are still delivered via webhook only when the text webhook send succeeds, matching prior behavior.

prs.title: fix(agents): drop empty media blocks before formatting requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A media `DataBlock` whose base64 payload is empty (e.g. a tool returning a
zero-byte image) was serialized by the formatters as an empty data URI:

```json
{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"}}
```

Every provider rejects this — OpenAI answers with *"Image data cannot be
empty"*.

## Fix

- Add `_is_empty_media_block()`: a media/data block whose `base64` source has a
  zero-length `data` payload.
- Strip such blocks in `normalize_messages_for_model_request()` **before** the
  multimodal branching — no endpoint accepts an empty data URI, so this runs
  regardless of multimodal support.
- Reuses the existing strip machinery via a new `empty_only` mode, so tool-result
  nesting and the `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` fallback behave like the other
  media-stripping paths.
- URL sources are left untouched: their emptiness cannot be determined without
  fetching them.

## Evidence

Reproduced and verified locally:

- Before: a `Msg` with `DataBlock(source=Base64Source(data="", media_type="image/png"))`
  formats to `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"}}`.
- After: the empty block is dropped (only the sibling text remains); no empty
  data URI is emitted.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed>` → all 17 hooks passed.
- `pytest tests/unit/agents/test_message_request_normalizer.py` → 41 passed; the
  normalizer + cross-provider + model-factory suites → 380 passed.

## Notes

- Based on `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Building the channel registry used to import every builtin channel module up front, so a console-only workspace still paid for heavy SDKs such as `lark_oapi` (often tens of seconds of startup). Root cause: `_load_builtin_channels()` eagerly imported all ~18 builtins before `QWENPAW_ENABLED_CHANNELS` filtering.

Eager-load only the required `console` channel; resolve other builtins lazily on first use (`from_config` / `from_env` / class access). Keep ChannelManager's existing skip-on-failure behavior when an enabled channel cannot be imported. Leave `_BUILTIN_SPECS` as a static literal so contract checks can still enumerate all builtins. Add unit/regression tests (including a subprocess check that heavy SDKs stay out of `sys.modules` when only building the registry).

prs.title: fix(console): tolerate DOM-mutation render errors and add chunk-error retry (#7889 rebased on main)
prs.body:
## Rebase of #7889 on top of the latest main

Supersedes the base-fix request in https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7889#issuecomment-6096046042 — the base of #7889 still pre-dates #8154, so its diff shows every locale file as "new file" (+4470 / -305).

This PR points the same rebase at `main` (`c26d31c0`), so the diff is the actual rebase work.

### Rebased onto the current main

Upstream reworked `ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx`, its test file and `main.tsx` after the previous base (`2744a976`), so this branch re-applies the change on top of the current implementation rather than replaying the old diff — that keeps every upstream feature (chunk diagnostics, server-readiness wait, copy diagnostic, automatic recheck/reload, Hub "Restart runtime", route reset on `resetKey`) intact and adds the retry path on top.

* `console/src/utils/domInsertTolerance.ts` and `.test.ts` — new.
* `console/src/main.tsx` — installs `installDomInsertTolerance()` before React takes over the DOM (the console entry point now boots `ConsoleApp` + `ThemeProvider`).
* `console/src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx` — retry path:
  * New `isRetryableError` state field.
  * Per the review, the local `isDomMutationError` heuristic is dropped in favour of `isErrorLike` (cross-realm-safe) from `utils/chunkRecovery`.
  * `MAX_RENDER_ERROR_RETRIES = 2` caps the retry budget; `retryCount` is an instance field so `getDerivedStateFromError` cannot reset it.
  * The retry button is suppressed for chunk-load errors and while the boundary is still recovering.
* `console/src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx` — the upstream suite is kept intact and the retry cases are added alongside it.
* `console/src/locales/{en,zh,ja,id,pt-BR,ru,vi}.json` — each gains a `chunkError.retry` key.

Either close #7889 and land this one, or close this and just move the base of #7889 — both end up with the same code on `main`.

cc @zhijianma

## What Problem This Solves

When a chat runtime (e.g. a tool call or skill load) mutates the DOM outside React's reconciliation, the console's lazy-loaded routes crash with a render error that the existing `ErrorBoundary` cannot recover from. The user sees a permanently blank pane and must reload the whole page. The root cause is that React's render path is interrupted by the external mutation; the error then propagates without any retry path, and the route's chunk is no longer recoverable for the lifetime of the page.

This is the same class of failure that #7889 attempted to fix, but #7889 was opened before #8154 (`fix(console): improve chunk error recovery and diagnostics`) and the resulting diff showed every locale file as "new file" (+4470 / -305), which made review impossible. This PR rebases the same code on top of the current `main` (`c26d31c0`), so the diff now shows only the actual changes (12 files, +349 / -2), and the conflict with #7889 can be closed in favor of this one.

## Evidence

Rebased and verified locally against `main` (`c26d31c0`) with the repository toolchain (Node `22.23.4` per `.nvmrc`, `npm ci`):

* `vitest run src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx src/utils/domInsertTolerance.test.ts` — **27 passed** (22 in the chunk-error suite, 5 in `domInsertTolerance.test.ts`).
* `tsc -b --noEmit` — clean, no diagnostics.
* `prettier --check` on all 12 changed files — `All matched files use Prettier code style!`
* `eslint` on the changed TypeScript files — clean.
* The upstream suite in `ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx` is preserved unchanged; the retry cases are added next to it, so the existing chunk-recovery coverage still runs on every push.

prs.title: feat(config): honor QWENPAW_LANGUAGE for fresh agent defaults
prs.body:
## Description

Fresh installs hardcode `agents.language` and `AgentProfileConfig.language` to `"zh"`, and `migrate_legacy_config_to_multi_agent` re-derives both from those defaults (`fallback_language=config.agents.language or "zh"`) — so an unattended Docker first boot always produced Chinese agents, and pre-seeding `config.json` loses the race against migration re-derivation (issue #8481).

This change introduces one helper, `_default_agent_language()`, in `config.py`:

- `QWENPAW_LANGUAGE` names a language in `SUPPORTED_AGENT_LANGUAGES` → used as the default;
- unset / invalid / unsupported values → `"zh"` (existing behavior unchanged);
- both `Field(default="zh")` sites (AgentProfileConfig + AgentsConfig) now use it via `default_factory`; the migration's two `fallback_language` call sites pick it up automatically through `config.agents.language`.

Minimal core by design: bootstrap / prompt / md-copy layers read the same config fields downstream, so they follow without further edits; a later PR can wire the remaining defaults named in the issue if maintainers want the broader sweep.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8481

**Security Considerations:** None (a deployment-provided language selection; validated against the bundled-language set so invalid values cannot leak arbitrary strings into persona paths).

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests

## Testing

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/config/test_config_model_validators_and_legacy_migration.py -q
...........................................       [100%]
116 passed in 3.63s
```

New tests:
- `QWENPAW_LANGUAGE=en` → fresh `AgentProfileConfig`/`AgentsConfig` default `en`
- invalid (`klingon`) or empty → `zh` fallback
- unset → `zh` (regression against the old default)
- environment variable flows through `migrate_legacy_config_to_multi_agent` into the first agent's `agent.json.language`

Red check: reverting `config.py` fails the override + migration tests (2 failed) while the unset-regression test still passes — exactly the intended behavior delta. `ruff check` on touched files passes; the 7 F541 it reports are pre-existing on `main` (verified via stash) and out of scope for this PR.

(Note as documented in the issue: md-file template copying and bootstrap prompts consume these fields downstream; this PR keeps the surface minimal and consistent — a maintainer may request the broader default sweep separately.)

prs.title: fix(plugins): trust HOME over the passwd home when locking dependency state
prs.body:
## Description

在受限部署环境（fnOS NAS 应用沙箱）里，专用应用账户的 passwd home 目录往往不存在且 `/home` 不可写。`qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py` 的 `state_root()` 在解析依赖锁根目录时**优先取 `pwd.getpwuid().pw_dir`**，只有在该值为空或非绝对路径时才回落到 `os.environ["HOME"]` — 于是 `_open_lock()` 的 `Path(...).mkdir(parents=True)` 在导入期直接抛出 `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'`，进程必然退出（issue #8515）。

现在代码里其实有覆盖变量 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`（优先级最高），但错误提示里没有它的名字，受限环境的用户无从得知。

本 PR：

1. **解析顺序改为 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` → $HOME → pw_dir**（与多数 Unix 工具一致；HOME 反映的是实际启动环境）；
2. 非绝对路径候选一律跳过（不再回落依赖路径的可用性假设）；
3. 兜底 RuntimeError 的提示改为**点名覆盖变量**：`Set an absolute shared QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR (checked first) or fix HOME for the service account.`，给出可操作的恢复路径。

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8515

**Security Considerations:** 无（仅路径解析顺序与错误消息；锁目录定位逻辑本身不变，覆盖变量原本就是最高优先级入口）

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] CLI
- [x] Tests

## Testing

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -q
5 failed, 20 passed, 10 skipped
```
- 5 failed 与改动前（`git stash` 后同号 baseline）完全一致，均为 `test_observation_child_custody_is_temporary[*]` 既存失败（Windows 基线），与本改动无关。
- 新增 `test_state_root_missing_home_error_names_the_override`（POSIX-only，Windows 上 skip）：passwd 指向不存在/不可写目录、HOME 未设时，错误信息必须点名 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`。
- `test_state_root_selection_is_stable` 增补 `home_wins_over_passwd` 用例：HOME 与 passwd home 同时存在且 passwd 目录无效时，选择 HOME（旧顺序时它是选 passwd → 改前该用例会失败意义上的行为契约变化）。

## Evidence

```
$ uv run pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -q
..ss.....ss..s........ss             [100%]
5 failed, 20 passed, 10 skipped in 8.06s

$ git stash && uv run pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -q | tail -1
5 failed, 20 passed, 8 skipped in 7.16s     # same 5 failures (pre-existing Windows baseline)
```

改动只改变 POSIX 家目录选取顺序与错误文案；Windows 分支（`USERPROFILE`）与 override 分支行为不变。`ruff check` 对两个触点文件通过；`ruff format --check` 报出的 hunks 均为该文件既存未格式化区域（与 stash 后基线一致，未触碰）。

prs.title: fix(desktop): open workspace HTML via the decoded local path
prs.body:
## Description

The legacy desktop bridge (`WebViewAPI`, pywebview shell) opened workspace HTML previews by handing the percent-encoded `file://` URI from `GET /api/workspace/html-file-uri` (`Path.as_uri()`, UTF-8 percent-encoded) straight to `webbrowser.open`.

On Windows, `webbrowser`→`os.startfile`→ShellExecute percent-decodes with the **ANSI code page** — GBK on Chinese systems — so the UTF-8 encoding of a Chinese workspace path is decoded to garbage and Windows reports `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (issue #8502 复现 A; the same failure mode was verified with `ShellExecuteW` in the issue).

This change decodes the URI host-agnostically with `urllib.request.url2pathname` (UTF-8 aware, converts URI separators to native ones) and passes the **native local path** to `webbrowser.open` instead of the `file://` URL.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8502 (复现 A — the pywebview legacy bridge layer)

**Security Considerations:** None — the resolved URI already passed the loopback + `/api/workspace/html-file-uri` gate; this only changes how the resolved `file` URI is handed to the OS opener (same file the endpoint validated — suffix recheck unchanged).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI) — symptom surfaces here; the change is in the desktop bridge
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py -q
..ss...                       [100%]
5 passed, 2 skipped in 0.43s
```

New regression case: `test_open_workspace_html_opens_the_decoded_local_path` builds a real workspace file at `workspace_dir/工作区/report.html`, feeds its `as_uri()` (percent-encoded) through the endpoint payload the same way the bridge consumes it, and asserts `webbrowser.open` receives the decoded native path. The test fails against `main` (assertion showed the encoded \'/C:/Users/.../%E5%B7%A5...\' arriving at the opener).

## Evidence

```
$ uv run pytest tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py -q
......ss                       [100%]
5 passed, 2 skipped in 0.43s

$ uv run pytest "tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py::test_open_workspace_html_opens_the_decoded_local_path" -q   # with the fix reverted
F                                                                                                                 [100%]
1 failed in 1.45s
```

FAIL output (fix reverted) — the opener received the encoded URI instead of the decoded native path:

```
E       AssertionError: assert [\'/C:/Users/T...imn6jmm_e7/工作区/report.html\'] == [\'C:\Users\...\report.html\']
E         At index 0 diff: \'/C:/Users/Tony/AppData/Local/Temp/tmpn6jmm_e7/工作区/report.html\' != \'C:\Users\Tony\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpn6jmm_e7\工作区\report.html\'
```

(The diff shows the pre-fix `unquote`-only form retaining the URI-leading \'/\'; with `url2pathname` the opener gets exactly the native path. The issue's复现 A error dialog — `file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/... Windows 找不到文件` — corresponds to that same encoded form reaching ShellExecute.)

Note: 复现 B (workspace-root-external file with pure-ASCII path, no reaction) involves a different layer (the Tauri shell invoke of `open_workspace_html` when the file sits outside the workspace root); that path resolves through the backend resolver and is not addressed by this bridge change.

prs.title: fix(mcp): fall back when discover returns HTTP 404 and -32601
prs.body:
## Description

`HttpStatelessClient._negotiate()` treated a `server/discover` reply of HTTP 404 with JSON-RPC `-32601` (method not found) as a hard `RuntimeError`. Servers that only speak the legacy streamable-HTTP protocol answer an unknown method exactly that way, so `HttpAutoClient` never tried the legacy `initialize` handshake and the MCP server failed to connect (#8424).

This PR treats every `-32601` reply to `server/discover`, whatever the HTTP status, as legacy-protocol evidence (`_LegacyProtocolError`), the same way 400/422/500 replies were already handled. `HttpAutoClient` then tries the legacy handshake once. HTTP 404 with the modern-protocol errors `-32020` (header mismatch) or `-32021` (missing capability) still fails hard, so a real modern-server error is not hidden by the fallback.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8424

**Security Considerations:** None. No auth, header, or config handling changes; the existing OAuth guard (`test_auto_still_reports_oauth_when_legacy_also_denies`) is unchanged and still passes.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

```bash

```

Test changes in `tests/unit/drivers/handlers/test_mcp_dual_protocol.py`:

- `test_discover_jsonrpc_status_classification` (parametrized): `-32601` with HTTP 404, 200, or 400 raises `_LegacyProtocolError`; HTTP 404 with `-32020` or `-32021` still raises `RuntimeError`.
- `test_auto_discover_404_method_not_found_falls_back_once`: with a server that answers `server/discover` with 404/`-32601`, `HttpAutoClient` connects through the legacy client, calls discover once and legacy `initialize` once, and lists the legacy tools.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep control-command routing on the user's own text in quoted replies
prs.body:
## Description

Replying to a message with a control command such as `/stop` in Feishu, QQ, WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk, OneBot or Yuanbao never routed as a command. These channels prepend the quoted (replied-to) message before the user's own text, so the inbound text becomes:

```
[quoted message: Alice: quarterly report]
/stop
```

Three shared consumers classify or dispatch on that first text block:

- `manager.enqueue` -> `CommandRegistry.get_priority_level`: `/stop` received normal priority 20 instead of critical 0.
- `BaseChannel._consume_one_request` -> `CommandRegistry.is_control_command`: the reply took the normal tracked-message branch instead of the control branch.
- `Runtime.run` -> `SlashCommandRegistry.dispatch`: even when routed fast, the command was not resolved and reached the agent as plain chat text.

Root cause in all three: they must look at the user's own text, but see the quote-first rendering (source probes in #8342).

### Fix

Add one shared recognizer, `strip_quote_context_prefix()` (`src/qwenpaw/utils/quote_context.py`), that removes leading `[quoted ...]` context blocks (some channels stack more than one, e.g. `[quoted media: download failed]` before `[quoted message: ...]`), and apply it at the two extraction points those consumers share:

- `BaseChannel._extract_query_from_payload`: command classification, queue priority, and the ACL "first message" record now see the user's own text, for both dict and `AgentRequest` payloads.
- `Runtime.run` slash-command dispatch text.

Behavior contract (pinned by tests):

- Quote + own `/stop` -> classified and dispatched as the command.
- Command only inside the quoted text -> not a command (unchanged).
- Quote-only reply (no new text) -> no command.
- Normal quoted chat -> unchanged; quote-first input still reaches the model, and text without the prefix is extracted byte-identically.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8342

**Security Considerations:** None. Quoted content is not modified; only the text used for routing and classification is stripped. The full quoted message still reaches the model.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Testing

- New `tests/unit/utils/test_quote_context.py` (16 cases): prefix variants, stacked prefixes, multi-line quoted content, command-only-in-quote, quote-only reply, and safe degradation when quoted content contains `]`.
- New `tests/unit/runtime/test_runtime_command_dispatch.py` (3 cases): `Runtime.run` dispatches `/stop` (not the quoted context) for a quoted reply; plain command unchanged; normal quoted chat does not dispatch.
- `tests/unit/channels/test_base_core.py`: new `TestExtractQueryQuoteContext` (6 cases) covering dict and `AgentRequest` payloads through the real `CommandRegistry`.
- Regression check: with the source change stashed, 7 of the new cases fail on current `main` (`7 failed, 2 passed`); with the fix applied, all 25 pass.
- `pytest tests/unit/utils/ tests/unit/runtime/ tests/unit/channels/`: 2699 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pytest tests/contract/channels/`: 357 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pytest tests/unit/` (full): 18657 passed, 25 skipped, 2 deselected; the 25 failures are pre-existing on this host (docker / bubblewrap / network-dependent tests, plus a timing-sensitive compaction test) and were verified to fail identically with the source change stashed.
- `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`: all checks passed (2026 passed, 1 skipped).
- `pre-commit run --files` on the six changed files: all applicable hooks pass (only `actionlint` was skipped; it needs Go module downloads that are blocked on this host and does not lint Python sources).

This PR was prepared with AI assistance. I ran and verified every command and result above locally.

prs.title: fix(console): persist market install provenance so 'Update All' covers third-party plugins (#8176)
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8176.

When a plugin is installed from the AgentScope plugin market, the install URL is discarded after download. The console later re-derives the market identity by string-matching the local `author` field against the market `owner`/`developer` logins. Real plugin.json `author` strings frequently differ from the market owner login (the issue's reporter has owner `onesix` but author `onesixth`), so third-party plugins never match, never enter the `updates` map, and the `Update All` button silently skips them.

Changes:

- Stamp a small `.qwenpaw-market.json` marker with the scoped market id (e.g. `@onesix/qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task`) into the freshly extracted plugin tree before the loader copies it into the install directory. The marker rides through install, gets overwritten on update, and is removed with the plugin on uninstall.
- Expose `market_id` on every entry in `GET /api/plugins`, in both the loader path and the pre-loader disk-scan fallback.
- `marketPluginMatches` treats a recorded `market_id` as authoritative; the existing author heuristic is the fallback for legacy installs that have no provenance yet.

Non-market install sources (local paths, third-party hosts, uploads) are untouched — the marker is only written for official-market archive URLs that match `{host}/plugins/{owner}/{name}/archive/zip/{ref}`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8176

**Security Considerations:** None. The marker is derived from the install URL after the hostname is verified to match the official market; no user-supplied path or query is persisted. Local-path and third-party-host installs do not write the marker.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

## Testing

- New backend: `TestMarketProvenance` (9 cases) covers URL parsing, marker writing, malformed-marker tolerance, and the disk-scan path surfacing `market_id`.
- Updated: `TestListPluginsRoute` accepts the new `market_id` field.
- New frontend: 3 cases in `marketPluginIdentity.test.ts` (provenance match, provenance authoritative over author, blank-falls-back).
- New frontend: 1 case in `usePluginManager.test.ts` that reproduces the reporter's exact plugin shape (`author: 'onesixth'`, owner `onesix`) and verifies `Update All` triggers `installPlugin`.

Before the fix, `marketPluginMatches` short-circuits at the author check (`onesixth` ≠ `onesix`), the third-party plugin is missing from the `updates` map, and the red "Update All (n)" badge only counts official plugins.

prs.title: fix(skills): offload pool skill download to a worker thread
prs.body:
## Summary

`POST /skills/pool/download` ran its whole pipeline inline in the async
handler: target preflight, rollback snapshots (`shutil.copytree` of the
existing skill), and the per-target copy itself. All of that is blocking
filesystem work that scales with the skill's file count, so downloading a
skill with thousands of files blocks the event loop for minutes — every
other API stops answering and the console's 30 s `AbortController` timeout
fires, so the operation fails in the UI even though the backend is still
copying.

This moves the blocking body into a sync helper and awaits it with
`asyncio.to_thread`, the same pattern `/pool/import-builtin` and
`/pool/{name}/update-builtin` already use.

Refs #8013

## What Problem This Solves

Downloading a large skill from the skill pool (e.g. 12,994 files / 80 MB)
freezes the whole backend. While the copy runs, the event loop is blocked
so no other request is served — the console looks hung, and the frontend's
hard 30 s timeout aborts the request even though the copy is still in
flight. Users see `Request timeout after 30000ms: POST /skills/pool/download`
and the skill never lands in the target workspace.

The reported reproduction is a large skill downloaded 4 times in a row,
each one failing at the 30 s mark with the backend unresponsive for the
whole copy window.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/skills.py`: extract `_download_pool_skills_blocking`
  (preflight + `preview_only` short-circuit + per-target download + rollback
  + backup cleanup, all unchanged) and call it from the handler via
  `asyncio.to_thread`.

## Behaviour

Unchanged: `preview_only`, the 400/404/409 conflict paths, the
`SkillScanError` → 422 payload, and the all-or-nothing rollback all still
run in the same order with the same semantics. Only the thread they run on
changes.

## Evidence

Regression test `tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router.py::test_pool_download_runs_off_the_event_loop`
patches the blocking helper with a 0.2 s `time.sleep` and runs a 10 ms
heartbeat task concurrently. The two waits must overlap:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router.py::test_pool_download_runs_off_the_event_loop
1 passed

# with the handler calling the blocking body inline instead of via to_thread:
assert elapsed < blocking_seconds * 1.5
E   assert 0.40799228847026825 < 0.3
```

Full validation:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router.py      # 14 passed
$ pytest tests/integration/test_skills_pool.py             # 18 passed
$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

`tests/unit/app/routers/test_git_router_endpoints.py` has 20 failures on
clean `main` in this environment (git-version dependent) — unrelated to
this change.

prs.title: fix(tauri): stop reconciling away a live desktop instance's backend
prs.body:
## Summary

On the Windows desktop app, relaunching while an instance is already running
opens a second window, and the second instance's backend **terminates the
first instance's still-in-use backend** during its startup reconciliation.
Quitting the second window then leaves the first permanently broken: model
list requests fail and the chat history list empties.

`reconcile_singleton_backend()` terminates whatever backend PID the previous
launch recorded, after checking only that the PID still belongs to a QwenPaw
backend. That check assumes the previous *desktop* process is gone — which is
exactly what is not true in a double launch.

Refs #8000

## What Problem This Solves

`~\.qwenpaw\desktop.log` records, on every double launch:

```
Terminating orphaned QwenPaw backend pid <first instance's backend>
```

The recorded backend is a genuine QwenPaw backend, so the PID-reuse check in
`_looks_like_backend` passes it straight to `terminate()`. What actually makes
it an orphan is that the desktop process which spawned it has exited — and
that is the one thing the guard never checked. Instance A's window keeps
talking to a backend that instance B just killed, and both instances' global
state (`desktop_backend.pid`, `desktop_port`) now belongs to B, so A never
recovers.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/tauri/backend_guard.py`:

- `_write_pid` now records the spawning process too — the pid file becomes
  JSON `{"pid": <backend>, "ppid": <spawner>}`, with the spawner taken from
  `os.getppid()`. The Tauri shell spawns the sidecar directly
  (`command.spawn()` in `console/src-tauri/src/backend.rs`), so this is the
  desktop shell process; in dev builds it is the `uv`/`python` wrapper, which
  lives exactly as long as the launching shell.
- `_owner_is_live` treats a backend whose recorded spawner is still running
  (and not a zombie) as **in use**, so `_terminate_previous_backend` leaves it
  alone and logs why.
- `_read_recorded_pids` / `_parse_recorded_pids` accept both the new JSON form
  and the bare-integer form older builds wrote.

The `#5550` guarantee is unchanged: when the spawner is gone the backend is
the leak this guard exists to reap. A legacy pid file (no owner recorded) also
still reaps, so an upgrade performed while a backend is running behaves
exactly as before.

## Tests

`tests/unit/tauri/test_backend_guard.py` — 93 tests (was 70).

`TestDoubleLaunchSequence` reproduces the issue's steps 1-4 directly:

- `test_second_launch_leaves_the_first_backend_alive` — instance A records
  itself with a live spawner, instance B reconciles, A's backend is untouched.
  On the previous code this fails: `first_backend.terminate` is called.
- `test_relaunch_after_a_crash_still_reaps` — spawner gone, backend reaped
  (the `#5550` case).
- `test_legacy_pid_file_from_an_older_build_still_reaps` — bare-integer file,
  still reaped.

Plus `TestOwnerIsLive` (running / exited / zombie / unknown / access-denied
spawner), `TestReadRecordedPids` (JSON, JSON-without-owner, legacy, torn write,
non-dict JSON, garbage, non-positive and non-integer pids), and updated
`TestWritePid` cases.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/tauri -q
93 passed

$ pytest tests/unit -k "tauri or backend_guard" -q
93 passed, 5 skipped

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

## Scope / follow-ups

This is the backend half of the report. The reporter's other two points are
out of scope here and would need the console shell:

1. no `tauri-plugin-single-instance`, so the second launch still spawns a
   second process/window — the Rust fix;
2. per-instance backend state instead of the global
   `desktop_backend.pid` / `desktop_port` pair.

With this change a double launch is still confusing (two windows) but no
longer destructive: the first instance keeps working. I can't build or test
the `console/src-tauri` side in this environment, so I deliberately left the
Rust change out rather than ship it unverified.

prs.title: feat(chats): add keyword and agentic conversation search
prs.body:
## Description

Automatically generated titles do not reliably contain the words users remember from a conversation. With a large history, a title-only filter can miss the exact discussion even when its messages contain the requested information.

This PR adds content search and agentic search to the existing conversation-history sidebar. For example, searching `PostgreSQL` now finds a conversation titled “A technical discussion” when its messages describe a PostgreSQL migration. Users who remember the intent instead of the wording can select **AI search** and describe the conversation in natural language.

Related: #1578.

### User experience

| Mode | Interaction | Retrieval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keyword | Type in the existing sidebar field; results update after a 275 ms debounce | Case-insensitive literal matching across titles and saved user/assistant messages, with pagination |
| AI search | Enter a description and explicitly submit with Enter or the search button | The current agent's configured model refines queries, pages through candidates, reads matching conversations, and selects relevant results |

Results show the conversation title and a highlighted excerpt. Clicking opens the existing conversation; clearing the field restores the normal grouped history. The compact mode switch and results use the existing sidebar styling and theme variables. Loading, empty results, retry, and partial results have dedicated states. Switching agents or editing the query cancels the client request and prevents stale results from entering the current view.

### Design and implementation

- Add agent-scoped `POST /chats/search` with `query`, `mode`, `limit`, and `offset`. Both modes search the selected agent's unarchived conversations and exclude app-owned dialogues.
- Read current and legacy session snapshots plus the configured Scroll history database, including imported history and older messages removed from live context by compaction. Extract user/assistant text while filtering reasoning, tool results, and tagged runtime messages. Restore original attachment input when snapshot metadata is available, and prefer snapshot message IDs over duplicate durable representations. Older durable attachment turns without original-content metadata can retain generated file-upload descriptions in search results.
- Keep keyword search independent of model configuration. Use existing persistence and SQLite support, with no new dependency, embedding service, index migration, or vector database.
- Implement an ephemeral model-driven search loop with only `search`, `read`, and `finish` actions. It can reformulate terms and inspect older pages. Final results are resolved from retrieved server-side candidates, so invented IDs cannot become links. The search does not instantiate the general-purpose agent or write conversation history.
- Bound each corpus scan to 64 MiB and five seconds; cap individual snapshots/history rows at 16 MiB. AI search allows six model responses in 45 seconds, 60 candidates, and bounded transcript/output sizes. Preserve retrieved results and mark them partial when a budget is exhausted. Missing models, invalid responses, and provider failures return explicit errors.
- Preserve canonical result IDs through sidebar navigation, including results discovered before the next session-list refresh. Add English/Chinese UI strings and Console documentation.

**Security considerations:** reuse the existing agent-scoped request dependencies; constrain transcript files to the session directory; open history SQLite connections read-only and filter by exact agent/session identity. Historical text is treated as data and the model has no filesystem, command, or network tools.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests

## Evidence

Validated against main `c26d31c0`. Sidebar navigation retains main's abortable session preloading and preserves canonical IDs when opening search results, including results absent from the current list.

```text
pytest tests/unit/app/chats tests/integration/test_chat_search.py tests/contract/runner/test_control_command_contract.py -q
442 passed

npm run test:run -- src/layouts/Sidebar.test.tsx src/layouts/Sidebar.render.test.tsx src/layouts/SidebarSessionList.test.tsx src/layouts/useSidebarSessionListData.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed
Tests       151 passed

npm run test:run -- src/layouts/useConversationSearch.test.ts src/api/modules/chat.test.ts src/pages/Chat/components/ChatSessionInitializer/ChatSessionInitializer.test.tsx
Test Files  3 passed
Tests       49 passed
```

Backend tests cover snapshots, durable/imported history, literal/Unicode matching, pagination, agent boundaries, bounded scans, model-guided retrieval and a real HTTP app. Frontend tests cover search submission/cancellation, API integration, canonical navigation and existing sidebar behavior. TypeScript (`tsc -b --noEmit`), ESLint for changed TypeScript files, all applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

Earlier browser verification used three synthetic Chinese conversations: a `PostgreSQL` body query returned two conversations with unrelated titles, opening a result showed its matching transcript, and clearing the query restored grouped history. An earlier local scan of 1,000 synthetic conversations / 10,000 messages found the expected body-only match in 0.431 seconds with `partial=false`.

prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #3361. A consumer awaiting asynchronous shutdown cleanup can otherwise lose its last strong reference when its queue manager is replaced, producing `Task was destroyed but it is pending!` during garbage collection.

Retain stopping consumers in a module-level set until completion, retrieve their exceptions, and release them through a done callback. Integrate with current main's bounded shutdown: the five-second timeout still raises `TimeoutError`, retains queue ownership for retry, and does not cancel a consumer a second time while it is already cancelling.

## Evidence

```text
pytest tests/unit/app/channels/test_unified_queue_manager.py -q
22 passed
```

The regression runs real asyncio consumers through the five-second grace period, observes the timeout, releases the manager, invokes garbage collection, and verifies the cleanup remains alive without pending-task destruction. Completing or cancelling cleanup releases both the task and manager. Existing queue lifecycle and retry tests pass.

issues.body:
### Summary

`[sop] sops_dir` is documented as optional with a resolved default, but both daemon start paths gate the entire SOP subsystem on `sops_dir.is_some()`. If an operator relies on the documented default, the SOP engine never loads — with no error, no warning, and no log line. Cron and channel triggers never fire, and `sop approve` has nothing to talk to.

I lost a couple of hours to this while building a payment agent whose refund flow is an approval-gated SOP, so it seemed worth reporting rather than just working around.

### The mismatch

The schema documents a default (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:21341-21344`):

```rust
/// Optional override. When omitted, the runtime and CLI both resolve the
/// default `<workspace>/sops`; SOPs load from there whenever it exists.
#[serde(default)]
pub sops_dir: Option<String>,
```

Both daemon paths require it to be `Some` (`src/main.rs:4057` and `src/main.rs:4821`):

```rust
let (sop_engine, sop_audit) = if current_config.sop.sops_dir.is_some() {
```

The comment immediately above the first one is accurate about the behaviour — it is the schema doc comment that is stale:

```rust
// SOP loading is gated on `[sop] sops_dir`: unset disables all
```

### Reproduce

1. Put a valid SOP at `<workspace>/sops/<name>/SOP.toml` (a `manual` trigger is enough).
2. Leave `[sop] sops_dir` unset.
3. `zeroclaw daemon`
4. `zeroclaw sop list` → the SOP is listed (the CLI resolves the default).
5. But the engine is not running: cron/channel triggers never dispatch, and approvals cannot be resolved.

Setting `sops_dir` explicitly fixes it completely.

### Why it is worth fixing

The failure is silent and the CLI actively disagrees with the daemon: `sop list` shows the procedure, so the natural conclusion is "SOPs are loaded, my trigger must be wrong." Anything approval-gated simply never runs.

### Suggested fix

Any one of these would have saved the time:

1. Make the runtime resolve the same default the CLI and the doc comment describe, or
2. Correct the doc comment to state that unset disables the subsystem, and
3. Log at `warn` on daemon start when `sops_dir` is unset but `<workspace>/sops` exists and is non-empty.

(3) alone would be enough to make this self-diagnosing.

Happy to open a PR for (2)+(3) if that shape is welcome.

Verified against `master` @ `b4d20c5`.

### Purpose

This tracker coordinates implementation follow-through for accepted RFC #9488 after the RFC issue was closed as accepted. It carries the unified file model, intake, resolver, projection, retention, and delivery work that is broader than #9998 and broader than the already-merged Web upload slice in #10544.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope:

- Implement one `FileId` / `ContentPart::File { file_id }` path across Web chat, channels, TUI/RPC, ACP, internal runtime origins, provider context, tools, and outbound delivery.
- Add the `FileEntry` resolver projection, selected/managed/inline-only source handling, attach-time observations, managed storage, rendition handling, quota, retention, deletion, and GC behavior required by #9488.
- Make Web Upload and Select independently default-closed and migrate the #10544 Web upload path away from host-path returns and marker syntax.
- Keep provider path projection aligned with the accepted trust-boundary decision while keeping Web/channel/ACP clients and normal logs path/digest-redacted.
- Retire legacy markers, RPC upload maps, channel media records, content-addressed upload names, and raw-path `ToolArtifact` delivery as parallel file authorities.
- Track regression coverage for streaming/bounded intake, cancellation, quotas, resolver authorization, rebuildable caches, client projection redaction, and outbound delivery.

Out of scope:

- #10526 session-event vocabulary, event ordering, protected-payload semantics, replay, branching, and erasure authority.
- #9600 concrete L2 backend/schema implementation sequencing.
- #9487 generic ingress and turn-coordination contracts except where file intake consumes them.
- #9998 session-scoped prompt attachment behavior except as one consumer of the shared file model.
- A new path-private provider mode; future path-private behavior belongs at the broader #9487 provider-projection seam.

### Linked work

- #9488 - accepted unified file and attachment architecture RFC.
- #10526 - append-only session-event authority consumed by file history.
- #9487 - runtime ingress and provider-projection seam.
- #9600 - L2 backend/schema implementation sequencing.
- #9998 - session-scoped persistent prompt attachments.
- #10544 - merged Web upload path that must be inventoried and migrated.
- #10908 - legacy image-marker promotion bug related to marker retirement.

### Routing evidence and next decision

Reason to stay open:

#9488 is closed as accepted, but related work is split across #9998, #10544, #10526, #9487, #9600, and specific cleanup bugs. Search found child and sibling issues, but not one public implementation home for the accepted #9488 file architecture.

Next decision/revisit:

Identify the first shared file-contract slice, then split concrete Web, channel, ACP, RPC, provider-projection, retention, and delivery work into child issues or PRs. Revisit this tracker when the base `FileId`/resolver contract lands and when legacy marker or upload paths are either migrated or assigned to child homes.

Visible owner, assignee, milestone, linked tracker, or review cadence:

No single implementation owner is assigned by this tracker. Child issues and PRs should carry slice ownership. Refresh this tracker after major child slices land or when #10330 is updated.

### Close criteria

Close when:

- The shared `FileId`, `ContentPart::File`, `FileEntry`, and resolver foundation has landed or has a more specific public home.
- Legacy marker, RPC upload-map, channel media, Web upload, and raw-path delivery paths are migrated, explicitly deferred to child issues, or declared out of scope by a later accepted decision.
- Client projection redaction, provider path projection, managed storage, retention/deletion, and outbound delivery have testable implementation homes.
- #10330 points to the final child homes or records that #9488 implementation follow-through is complete.

### Stale-exemption requested?

Yes - tracker itself is the active coordination surface

issues.title: [Feature]: Web managed document upload (first #9488 Phase 2 Web slice)
issues.body:
### Summary Let the dashboard web chat attach documents as #9488 Managed files: stored once under `/attachments`, referenced by an opaque `FileId` through `RuntimeIngress`, and off by default, as the first #9488 Phase 2 Web slice. ### Problem statement Web users can't attach documents to a chat. #7138 records the need. Since then, #10544 added `POST /api/upload`, but on master it: - accepts images only; - writes into the agent workspace (`webui_uploads/`) with no session binding, quota or cleanup; - buffers the whole body in memory (up to 20 MiB), while #9488 asks for bounded streaming; - returns the host path and an `[IMAGE:]` marker, which the dashboard embeds in the message. Accepted #9488 retires that pattern. Web intake should produce Managed files with opaque ids, behind a default-closed capability, and never expose host paths to clients. #11013 tracks that work, and this issue proposes its first Web slice. ### Proposed solution Child of #11013; user need from #7138. Builds on #11921 (session events and the gateway session authority) and #9487 / #11012 (runtime ingress). This is a design proposal for review before any code. @NiuBlibing, you said on #11013 that you planned to implement #9487 and #9488, including both the file-upload and the local file-selection paths. Audacity88 has since invited me to take the managed Web-upload slice. The split under "Slices and owners" below is my attempt to reconcile the two, and it's the part I'd most like to agree with you on. Several choices here sit on foundation work you own; I've marked those as questions rather than guessing. Let a dashboard chat attach documents: - The browser streams a file to the gateway. - A runtime-owned managed-file service stores it once under `/attachments` as a **Managed** file. - The next user turn references it as `ContentPart::File { file_id }` through `RuntimeIngress`. - The browser only ever sees an opaque `FileId` and safe display metadata. Upload is a separate capability, off by default. The main text covers the design and the questions. The detailed protocol, error codes and test list are in the collapsed section at the end of this section, for anyone who wants to check them; most of that will be pinned down by tests in the PR. #### Design at a glance The numbers match the sections in the collapsed detail below. 1. **Managed-file service (runtime-owned).** - The storage logic lives in the runtime, behind a port in `zeroclaw-api`. The gateway is a thin adapter: Web owns no execution, file resolver or session writer. - An upload streams to `tmp/`, then moves durably to `files///`. A receipt outside `files/` tracks the file's state: `committing`, `pending`, `claiming` or `committed`. - Nothing is appended to session history at upload. When a turn using the file is accepted, the runtime claims it, and #11921's `admit_user_input` registers it in the same batch as `TurnAccepted`. - The section states the invariants the PR must keep and the approach for each. They include never deleting registered bytes, claiming a file at most once, and recovering from every crash point. 2. **Intake route.** - `POST /api/sessions/{id}/uploads?agent=` takes the raw file as a streamed body. `Content-Length` is required, and the filename header is only a display hint. - The route has its own idle timeout and overall deadline, instead of the gateway's 30 s request timeout. - The upload binds to the WS chat family `gw_{session_id}`. A `DELETE` route discards a pending file. 3. **Authorization, capability and limits.** - Config lives under `[gateway.uploads]`, with `enabled = false` by default. It sets per-file, per-turn, pending and per-agent limits, alongside a process-wide staging budget. - Upload is unavailable while pairing or session persistence is off. - Access goes through #11921's session authority. In practice that means *any paired operator, plus binding to the session*; it isn't per-user isolation. - An `Origin` check adds CSRF defence in depth. `/api/status` advertises the capability and its limits. 4. **Submitting the turn.** - The WS `message` frame gains `files: [FileId]` and a `client_message_id`. The server answers each send with a correlated accepted or rejected frame. - Managed files never go through #11921's path-bearing `attachments`. - They are registered through #11921's `EngineFileInput` under a new reference-only codec, so the bytes aren't stored twice. 5. **What the model sees, and tool access** (slice D; question 4). - A minimal provider projection gives the model the name, resolved path, media type and size, with the RFC's live-path note. `FileUsed` is recorded through #11921's `record_file`. - Under the default security policy, file tools can't reach `/attachments`. Fixing that needs either a narrow per-file grant (a new hook) or storing files in the workspace. 6. **Dashboard.** - Uploads show as composer chips with progress, cancel and remove. Chips stay until the server accepts the turn. - Non-image files are offered only when uploads are enabled. Image upload is unchanged until slice E (or C; question 9). - Chips in history get their display metadata from a new `file_meta` field. 7. **Redaction.** - Clients, logs and observer events never see paths or digests. - The existing leaks (#10544's `path`, #11921's `attachments` replay, tool output) are listed, with the slice that closes each. #### Slices and owners Proposed split, with owners to agree here: | Slice | Contents | Depends on | Proposed owner | |---|---|---|---| | A. File contracts (Phase 1) | `FileId`, `ContentPart::File`, `FileEntry`/`FileSource`/`ObservedFileFacts` (resolving the name clash with the RPC `file/attach` wire types), Managed-only `FileResolver`, binding #11921's file events to `FileId`, architecture ratchet against new marker writers | #11921 | @NiuBlibing, or me if you'd prefer | | B. Runtime ingress (Phase 1 of #9487, #11012) | `RuntimeIngress` / `InboundTurn` in `zeroclaw-api`, append-backed acceptance delegating to `execute_turn` | #11921 | @NiuBlibing | | B2. WS chat on `RuntimeIngress` (#9487 Phase 4, gateway part, pulled forward) | Option (b) in section 4: move the whole WS `message` path, text and files alike, onto `RuntimeIngress`. Not needed under option (a). | B | to agree (question 3a) | | C. Web managed upload (this issue) | Sections 1-4, 6 and 7: the managed-file service and receipts, intake and discard routes, config and capability, status advertising, WS `files`, dashboard chips | A, B (and B2 under option (b)) | me | | D. Minimal Managed provider projection and tool access | Section 5 | A, C | me, with C, unless the Phase 3 owner prefers otherwise | | E. #10544 image upload | Move dashboard image upload onto Managed `FileId`s (with an optional rendition), capability-gate it, and stop returning host paths to Web clients. (Whether the gating happens here or in C is question 9.) With #11921 the marker is already gone; the `path` and `attachment.target` remain. The closing record lists migrating #10544 as an implementation-handoff boundary, and Stalesamy's ballot puts it in Phase 2 ("Phase 2 must migrate it to `FileId` intake"). This is a dashboard-visible change, noted in that PR. | C | me, after C | C can be built and tested against its dependencies as they land; it would not merge before them. Local file selection (Select) stays with whoever takes it. You mentioned it, NiuBlibing, so I've left it out of this table. #### Questions for maintainers and @NiuBlibing 1. Is the pending-receipt lifecycle (file durable at upload, registration at turn acceptance) the right reading of Managed step 5, together with #9487's "Pending uploads/selections are resolved by #9488 before the durable content reference is accepted"? 2. Tool access: a new dynamic-grant hook in `SecurityPolicy` for the attached file's directory (best-effort for shell), or storing managed files inside the agent workspace? 3. Ingress and #11921 (section 4): - 3a. Option (a), file turns only through the Phase 1 facade, or (b), pull the gateway part of Phase 4 forward as B2? If (b), who takes it: you with B, or me with C? - 3b. Can #9487's `InboundTurn.idempotency_key` be carried through to the kernel by B or #11921 (with a stream-scoped derived `TurnId` only as a fallback)? - 3c. Can #11921 expose the admission outcome separately from the turn future, unless B's `RuntimeIngress` returns `Accepted` first? - 3d. Is a reference-only `representation` under a new `session.managed-file-reference/v1` codec acceptable? - 3e. Should gateway recovery and requeue support managed parts? 4. Should the minimal provider projection and tool access (section 5) be part of this work, or wait for Phase 3? 5. The shared operator is trusted but not a distinct authenticated identity. Is "paired bearer → shared operator, plus session binding" enough for Upload's "authenticated session ownership" until per-device or OIDC principals reach chat? 6. Is a service-owned agent scope the right scope, or should it be per session? Should `[gateway.uploads]` be global or per agent? And should the store-level settings (`max_managed_mb_per_agent`, `pending_expiry_mins`) live with the runtime store rather than under `[gateway]`? 7. Does this belong in the v0.9.0 session-contract window via #9600 (the registration event shape belongs to the #10526 contract, with L2 owned by @tidux)? 8. Managed files are plain files at rest, and #10526 encryption covers only its protected payloads. Is that right? 9. Which slice is the "cutover" that capability-gates Web upload: C, which would gate `/api/upload` too and change the dashboard, or E? And may C ship before E?
Implementation detail (for the PR): requirements, protocol, error codes, tests #### Requirements this design follows These come from accepted #9488 Rev 10, its closing record, and the #11013 brief. **Managed storage:** - Bytes are stored once, at an opaque path under the fixed `/attachments` root. - Each `FileId` has its own file. There are no content-addressed or shared blobs. - ZeroClaw owns storage, quota, backup, retention and deletion. **Intake:** - Authenticate and authorize Upload, then reserve quota. - Stream to a unique staged file while computing SHA-256, byte length and byte-detected media type, while staying bounded in memory. - Move the file durably. Only then append registration and content events. - A committed event never points at missing bytes. - Pending uploads and leases protect in-flight work. Cancellation and timeouts are bounded. **Ownership:** file intake and resolution are runtime-owned, and Web is a thin adapter (closing record). From #9487: Web owns no execution, file resolver or session writer. **Authorization:** - Upload is its own capability, closed by default. - It needs authenticated session ownership, streaming limits, quota and CSRF/origin protection. - Possessing a `FileId` is not authorization. **Client projection:** - Clients get only the `FileId`, safe display metadata and lifecycle state. - They never get host paths, the managed relative path or digests, including in replayed and live events. - Normal logs and observer events stay scrubbed too. **Submission:** - Turns are submitted only as #9487 `InboundTurn` values. - Committed content holds `FileId`s, never upload tokens, base64, markers or paths. #### 1. Managed-file service (runtime-owned) The storage logic lives in the runtime, behind a port in `zeroclaw-api`, so later RPC and channel migrations can reuse it. The gateway route (section 2) only authenticates, enforces transport limits, and streams bytes into it. ```text ManagedFileStore async begin(authority, agent, session, principal, declared_len, display_name) -> Result async UploadGuard::write(&mut self, chunk) -> Result<(), UploadError> async UploadGuard::commit(self) -> Result async discard(authority, agent, session, principal, file_id) -> Result<(), UploadError> async claim(authority, agent, session, stream, principal, idempotency_key, file_ids) -> Result async ClaimGuard::settle(self, outcome) // committed | rejected | unknown; the guard's Drop alone can't know ``` - `begin` checks quota and reserves budget. - `write` hashes, counts and sniffs each chunk. - `commit` returns `PendingFile { file_id, display_name, byte_len, media_type, expires_at }`. - `authority` is the adapter's per-request session access policy. #11921's gateway builds a `GatewayAuthority` from the live pairing subject. `SessionAccessPolicy` lives in `zeroclaw-kernel`, and `zeroclaw-api` can't name it, so the gateway wraps its `GatewayAuthority` in an api-level access trait. The runtime store calls that trait for its checks. Crash resolution and the sweep run with no request at all, so they use a runtime system read authority limited to the resolution check, the way #11921's session host reads with a `System` actor. The per-request adapter authority is used only for `begin`, `claim` and `discard`. - `claim` runs at turn acceptance. Its `ClaimGuard` carries each file's registration facts, which are what #11921's `EngineFileInput` needs (section 4). At claim time the receipt records everything `EngineFileInput` needs: a representation `PayloadId` derived deterministically from the `file_id` (the representation is the only `PayloadRecord`), plus the `registered_at` time and the policy limits that applied, so the `registration` and `policy_evidence` values come out byte-identical. Every retry rebuilds them from the receipt, so a retried admission matches the original even after a reload changes the live limits. (#11921's replay check compares the representation's payload id too, and `PayloadRecord::json` would otherwise mint a new one.) - `claim` and `begin` both run the session-access check (through that api-level trait) and the quota checks in the runtime, not the gateway. `claim` re-checks `gateway.uploads.enabled`, `max_files_per_turn` and session access at use time, as the RFC's point-of-use rule asks. **Layout.** This keeps the RFC's `files///`. The RFC's `tmp/` becomes a directory rather than a single file, so it can hold the data and its metadata together. Receipts sit outside `files/`, so file tools given a managed file's path can't reach them. Shell confinement is best-effort (section 5), so the store integrity-checks receipts and never treats one as authority beyond what it can verify: ```text /attachments/tmp// staging, never exposed /attachments/receipts/.json receipt: committing | pending | claiming | committed /attachments/files/// managed file (the live path tools receive) ``` **Receipts.** Each receipt carries a positive state. Committed files keep a `committed` receipt rather than losing theirs, so the RFC's "crash-recovery receipt distinguishes committed, pending, and unreferenced generations" holds directly. A receipt holds: - the agent's scope id (see Scope below); - the session family; - once claiming, the turn's idempotency key and target stream (section 4); - an opaque principal id; - the observed facts; - the display name; - its timestamps. It never holds the bearer token or its hash: #11921 keeps credential proof in memory only, and #11012 asks for "authenticated opaque references rather than persisted bearer tokens". **What a receipt is authoritative for.** Receipts are the authority only for *pending* and *claiming* files, which have no history yet. Once a file is committed, its receipt is just a crash-recovery marker. Committed files are resolved and authorized from their `FileRegistered` registration through `FileResolver`, and deletion is never decided from a receipt; that is left to Phase 5's event-derived reachability. This keeps receipts from becoming the second file table the RFC rejects ("A materialized cache/index is allowed only when fully rebuildable and non-authoritative"). **Invariants the implementation must keep** (the PR will pin each one with crash and cancellation tests): 1. Bytes with a `FileRegistered` event are never deleted by this slice. 2. A file is attached to at most one accepted turn. This is a choice for this slice, not a kernel limit: #11921's `admit_user_input` can already re-attach a file within a stream without registering it again, so later slices could relax it. 3. Every crash or cancellation point leaves a state the service can recover. This covers mid-stream, mid-commit, mid-claim, after the session append but before the receipt update, and a caller dropped while #11921's blocking commit continues. 4. A pending file is only claimed by the same agent, session family and principal, before it expires. 5. Unsent uploads and orphaned staging are reclaimed; nothing is leaked silently. **Approach** (exact protocol in the PR): - **Cleanup is RAII and uncancellable.** - `UploadGuard` cleans up on drop, handing removal to a blocking task so `Drop` doesn't block. - `commit` runs to completion in `spawn_blocking`, holds a lease while it runs, and rolls back on error. - Before moving the data into `files/`, it writes a `committing` intent receipt; it marks the receipt `pending` only after the data is `fsync`ed in `files/`. So every `/` directory always has a receipt. A `committing` receipt left by a crash is rolled back: no turn could have referenced it, because its `FileId` was never returned. A directory with no receipt at all means tampering and is reported and quarantined, not deleted. - **Claims are leased.** - A claim takes per-file locks in sorted `FileId` order, validates every file, and marks them all `claiming`. - Its in-process `ClaimGuard` is held by a task that awaits the admission outcome, so it lives until #11921's blocking append finishes, whether or not the caller is still there. That task calls `settle` with the outcome. - This needs an admission-outcome signal. #11921's `SessionExecutionPort::execute` runs admission and the turn as one cancellable future, with `admit_user_input` awaited inside it. So this relies on slice B's `RuntimeIngress` returning `Accepted`, or on #11921 exposing the admission result separately, for example a oneshot fired from the blocking admission task (question 3c). A dropped sender is treated as `unknown` and resolved through history under the stream lock, which serialises with the append. - The append outcome then moves the receipts to `committed`, or back to `pending`. - A `claiming` receipt with a live guard is busy: discard, a claim for a different turn, or the sweep get `file_busy`. - A claim for the *same* turn (same idempotency key and target stream) on a `claiming` or `committed` receipt is an idempotent hit, not "already claimed". - **Unknown outcomes are resolved through history.** #11921's append can itself fail with `CommitOutcomeUnknown`. So `settle` takes an `unknown` outcome for any error that isn't definitely a rejection, which keeps the receipt `claiming`. A `claiming` receipt with no live guard, whether left that way or by a crash, is resolved through history. The check reads session history for the recorded turn's `FileRegistered{file_id}` under the session-stream lock, through the kernel. The idempotency key on the receipt tells "this turn committed" apart from "another turn has it". The expiry sweep makes the same check before deleting any `pending` file. - **Single writer, and reload.** - One process owns the store. It reuses the daemon's existing process-ownership guard where that covers ``, or adds an exclusive lock on `/attachments`. Either way, a second process can't sweep live staging. - `/admin/reload` re-runs the whole daemon generation in-process, carrying across the process-ownership guard (and in-flight SOP drivers), so a per-generation service would be rebuilt on every reload. - The store, its lock, its live `ClaimGuard`s and its sweep therefore live outside the generation loop, handed over the way the ownership guard is. The start-of-service sweep runs once per process, never on reload. - A reload still stops the gateway, which drains and then cancels its connections. Uploads still running after the drain window (300 ms, so in practice every in-flight upload) are aborted: their `UploadGuard`s clean up staging and release quota, and the client sees a failure and retries. Pending files, receipts and live claims survive. - **Deletion.** Removing a file removes its whole `/` directory, because tools may add files there. Then it `fsync`s, then it updates the receipt. **Scope.** - `` is a random id the service mints the first time an agent uploads. Managed `FileId`s, upload ids and scope ids all carry at least 128 bits of CSPRNG entropy (the RFC's floor for `FileId`, applied here to upload and scope ids too), through slice A's `FileId` type. That isn't UUIDv4, which has 122 random bits and is what #11921's gateway file ids use today; slice A's binding would replace those. - Receipts hold the scope id, not the alias, so renaming an agent never touches receipts. - A small alias → scope map lets the upload and claim checks compare "the named agent" with "the agent on the receipt". Receipts also store the alias at mint time as a non-authoritative hint. The map is small, durable, `fsync`ed state, rebuildable from those hints and from registrations if it is lost. It is a lookup only and never grants access by itself: access still needs the session family's owning agent and the session authority. - Renaming an agent updates its one map entry in the existing rename cascade (`cascade_rename_agent`). - Deleting an agent tombstones its scope, so a new agent with the same alias gets a new scope. The tombstone is durable on its own, as a marker under `files//`, so losing the map can't undo it. A map rebuild fails closed for any scope it can't verify. A mint-time alias hint that conflicts with current owning-agent evidence (for example after a rename, followed by a new agent taking the old alias) counts as unverifiable. - Neither agent aliases nor `ensure_agent_uuid` is used as the scope: aliases change on rename, and `ensure_agent_uuid` returns the alias on memory backends without an agents table. **Hardening.** - All access goes through a `cap-std` directory handle on the fixed root, with `create_new` and no-follow, as `persist_content_addressed` does, plus owner-only permissions. - Its content-addressed naming isn't reused. **``** comes from the display name: - path separators, control characters, leading dots and reserved names are replaced; - Unicode is normalised to NFC; - the name is capped at 100 bytes; - an empty result becomes `file`. Names can't collide, because each `` has its own directory. **`display_name`** is normalised separately, because it is shown to clients and placed in the provider block. Control and bidi-override characters are stripped, Unicode is normalised to NFC, the name is capped at 255 bytes, and a missing header, or a name that is empty after stripping, becomes `file`. A newline in a filename therefore can't forge lines in the provider block. **Media types.** Media types are detected from the bytes using `zeroclaw_api::media` sniffing, extended for common document types. Anything else is accepted as `application/octet-stream`. The service stores bytes and never executes or interprets them. **At rest.** Managed files are plain files at rest, so tools can open them. Encryption applies to #10526 protected payloads, not to the live managed file (question 8). #### 2. Intake route (gateway adapter) `POST /api/sessions/{id}/uploads?agent=`, next to the existing `/api/sessions/{id}` routes. The request body is the raw file (no multipart). **Which session and agent:** - `{id}` is the WS chat `session_id`. The upload binds to `gw_{session_id}`, exactly as the WS chat derives its family. That isn't the REST `family()` lookup, which can resolve an id to an ACP, RPC or channel family. Webhook and HTTP sessions share the `gw_` namespace (`gateway_session_key`), so the id alone doesn't decide. When the family exists, its descriptor's `owner` must be the shared operator principal. WS chat opens families with a `Principal` actor, while the gateway ingress opens them with `System { component: "gateway_ingress" }` and leaves no owner. A family that doesn't exist yet is opened by WS chat on the first send. `claim` re-checks this too. Known edge: legacy-imported WS chats from before #11921 are rooted with a default actor and have no owner, so they are refused uploads; a new chat works. - When the family exists, `agent` must match its owning agent. - A new chat that hasn't been saved yet (before its first message) has no descriptor. It is authorized against the family's deterministic stream id, and the receipt binds the file to the family and the named agent. - The receipt binds to the session family `gw_{session_id}`, derived from the id the client knows. For a new family, #11921 derives the stream id deterministically from it. - #11921's session delete closes the family (`history_retained: true`, reason `gateway_session_delete`). Uploads to a family closed by deletion are refused. The delete handler calls the store to discard that family's pending files. - TTL expiry is different. It appends `SessionClosed { reason_key: "session_ttl_expired" }` to the same stream, which the catalog and rules don't count as closed, and later turns continue on that stream. So uploads to a TTL-expired session still work. **Headers:** - `Content-Length` is required (411 otherwise). It is checked against the configured limit before any byte is read. Hyper already enforces Content-Length framing, and the handler also stops at the declared length. Known edge: a proxy or tunnel that re-chunks request bodies would get 411. If that turns out to matter, chunked bodies could be accepted with the cap and quota enforced while streaming. - `X-ZeroClaw-Filename` (percent-encoded) is a display-name hint. It is never used raw as a path component. Only the sanitised `` derived from it (section 1) is used, as the final component inside a server-minted `/` directory. It never selects a directory or affects authorization; the RFC treats `display_name` as presentation metadata. - `Content-Type` is not trusted; the media type is detected from the bytes. **Streaming and limits:** - The handler reads the body as a stream (`axum::body::Body::into_data_stream`) and feeds it to the `UploadGuard`. - It runs in its own sub-router, without the gateway's `TimeoutLayer` (`gateway.request_timeout_secs`, default 30 s), which master's `/api/upload` sub-router still applies. - An idle timeout (`idle_timeout_secs`) wraps each chunk read. An overall deadline (`max_upload_secs`) runs inside the handler, so a slow-drip client can't hold an upload open indefinitely while a slow phone upload still completes. Both return the `upload_timeout` envelope. - A fixed body-limit layer (proposed: 100 MiB) is only a safety ceiling. Config validation rejects a `max_file_mb` above it, so the handler's own size check, against the live config as `api_upload.rs` does, is what clients normally hit. Above the ceiling, the layer answers a bare 413 before the handler runs.
