The report includes the exact configuration and synthetic prompt. The later master merge preserves these renderer and finalization paths.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`) — the reasoning rides the existing `editMessageText` /
  `chat.update` draft edits.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the model's reasoning becomes user-visible on
  these two channels when an operator opts in. That is the point of the feature, and it is why the
  default is `off`. Reasoning text is passed through the same `zeroclaw_runtime::security::scrub` +
  `scrub_credentials` redaction the Matrix progress draft uses before it reaches a transport, and —
  unlike a per-delta scrub — the *joined* reasoning buffer is also scanned with the configured
  outbound leak detector (`redact_channel_outbound_leaks`) before every draft edit, so a credential
  a provider splits across several reasoning fragments is redacted instead of being reassembled on
  screen. Telegram HTML-escapes the text; Slack emits mrkdwn quote text, which still has mrkdwn semantics. Reasoning is kept out of the final answer and conversation history by these draft paths. A failed final edit triggers best-effort deletion and a fresh answer. Full mode intentionally discloses reasoning to the conversation; redaction and later replacement cannot guarantee confidentiality or recall content already seen.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`) — two new optional fields with a default of `off`:
  `channels.telegram.<alias>.stream_reasoning` and `channels.slack.<alias>.stream_reasoning`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps
  for existing users: none required. Existing configs keep working untouched and keep the current
  draft behavior; the fields appear in `zeroclaw config schema`, the config dashboard and the
  generated channel field lists with their `off` default. To opt in, set the field on the alias and
  restart the channel.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk PRs: `git revert <sha>` is the plan unless otherwise noted.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`, or set `stream_reasoning = "off"` (the default)
  on the affected alias and restart the channel.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** the `stream_reasoning` field itself is the toggle; `off` is
  the default and restores the pre-PR behavior.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** none expected. If a Telegram draft edit fails after the HTML
  blockquote is rejected, the code logs
  `editMessageText (reasoning draft) failed; falling back to plain text` at `DEBUG` and retries the
  plain-text edit.

prs.title: fix(config)!: forbid /mnt,/media,/run/media and Windows drive/UNC defaults
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #12134.

Under Full autonomy (`workspace_only = false`), the default denylist stopped at OS directories and left WSL DrvFs (`/mnt/c/...`), `/media`, `/run/media`, non-system Windows drives, and UNC shares open while the matching Linux/Windows system homes were refused.

- **Unix defaults:** add `/mnt`, `/media`, `/run/media`.
- **Windows defaults:** deny every drive-letter root (`A:\`…`Z:\`) in addition to the existing `C:\Windows` / Program Files spellings; refuse UNC shares in the path checkers when no allow entry matched.
- **Most-specific-match unchanged:** a workspace or `allowed_roots` entry under those trees (common WSL layout) still wins by depth.
- **Filesystem channel:** reject single-letter `/mnt/<x>` watches unless `allow_broad_roots = true`; named binds such as `/mnt/inbox` stay allowed.
- **Docs:** `docs/book/src/security/model.md` lists the new defaults.

This is a deliberate behavior change for operators who relied on Full autonomy to roam those trees; `allowed_roots` remains the opt-in.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test mnt_forbidden_paths`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib checklist_default_forbidden`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib filesystem_validate_rejects_drvfs`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib filesystem_validate_allows_named_mnt`

## AI disclosure
Prepared with AI assistance. I reviewed the diff, ran the tests listed above, and take responsibility for the change.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Remove the obsolete 5/15 MiB advisory warnings from the binary-size script. Preserve measured bytes, summary output and hard-limit failures. Add process regressions to the existing required Repository Structure job.
- **Scope boundary:** The advisory-removal slice of #11580. The Stable workflow, its 80 MiB cap, default 20 MiB script cap, build budgets and release contents are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Size-check log output and a fast local-file test step; no new runner, permission or workflow trigger.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11580. This does not close the issue.

### What this does, simply

The old warnings fire on normal release binaries and no longer identify a useful limit. The script now reports the size and enforces the caller's actual cap. A binary exactly at the cap still passes; one byte over still fails.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — automated process tests cover the changed output and pass/fail boundary with sparse files.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The [Repository Structure job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41389759758/job/125098332406) on 46086361fee9b22c8dd6e4981f4b30357806641b runs all seven size-gate process tests successfully. That job is a direct dependency of CI Required Gate. Local validation also rejects the two fault-injected guards. The [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41389759758/job/125101742158) passes, including Security and Test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No release build, new binary-size measurement or native macOS run. The existing stat implementations are unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `bash -n scripts/ci/check_binary_size.sh`; `python3 scripts/ci/check_binary_size_test.py -v`: `Ran 7 tests`, `OK` (13 gate invocations). Disabling the hard gate causes four assertion failures; rejecting equality causes three. The unchanged source then passes all seven tests again.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Rebased the single commit onto 9dbb57231f48e26fee56243de4f7845924ce4f04; range-diff reports an unchanged patch. Checked cap overrides, exact bytes, missing-file refusal and summaries on failure. Exact workflow comparison against this base permits only the new three-line test step; its owning job remains required. The Stable workflow is unchanged.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text CI output.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 46086361fee9b22c8dd6e4981f4b30357806641b; local WSL Linux, noninteractive plain-text output from the actual gate on synthetic sparse files. [Earlier harness, fault-injection logs and receipts](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/tree/34c07e81a39bec6ee40806c33cc71308a2cc6288) are historical at 340a7d5a57826098b7f489aa910b86e3623f67e3.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** At 83,886,080 bytes with that cap: `Binary size: 80MB (83886080 bytes)`, `Binary size within safeguard.`, exit 0. At 83,886,081 bytes: `::error::Binary exceeds 80MB safeguard (80MB)`, exit 1. Existing display-unit spelling is unchanged; the byte count is exact.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Run the actual gate on sparse files below, at and above its caps. Obsolete warnings disappear; over-limit and missing-file failures remain.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No Cargo or release run: shell/Python regression work only. No new size, feature-removal or release-readiness claim.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for pass/fail and summary contracts.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes — obsolete advisory text is removed; the success line now names the safeguard.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: None. Consumers retain the same byte counts and exit codes.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Prefer successful `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` or a glibc/GNU-libc `ldd --version` result before checking installed musl loaders. A glibc host can have musl installed for cross-compilation.
- **Scope boundary:** Installer libc detection and its existing target-test suite. The updater's separate target selection (#12156) is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** x86_64/aarch64 Linux archive and feature-target selection. Existing musl/distro fallbacks, unknown-host GNU fallback, ARM32, macOS and Termux rules remain.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12153.

### What this does, simply

Installing musl alongside glibc should not change which ZeroClaw archive a glibc host receives. The installer now checks the system libc first. Alpine still selects musl.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if a native Alpine or glibc-with-musl host is available.

- **Steps to run:** `sh install.sh --prebuilt --dry-run --skip-quickstart --no-modify-path`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The [Installer Drift job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41389761870/job/125098339627) on 5afea5fe50e837b3813b66a79f0ae860b9f5ce6c passes all 27 target/probe cases, three version-parser cases, nine offline version-display cases and generated-installer checks. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Host facts are mocked. No native Alpine/ARM archive execution or updater fix is claimed.

Three complete offline installer dry runs pass. Restoring only the old detector in a temporary source copy gives `passed: 24`, `failed: 3`, all glibc-with-musl cases. The production entrypoint was rerun after the upstream CLI-only and version-parser changes. No new supported failure survived the two source/control passes.

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5afea5fe50e837b3813b66a79f0ae860b9f5ce6c; local WSL Linux, noninteractive C.UTF-8. The three controlled `sh install.sh --prebuilt --dry-run --skip-quickstart --no-modify-path` runs check Platform and the emitted URL with no network or installation. - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Glibc fixture: `Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; Alpine fixture: `Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. Each emitted download URL uses the same target.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Execute the complete dry-run entrypoint with controlled getconf/ldd/uname and release metadata; verify the selected platform and URL. No network or real install.

prs.title: fix(tool-call-parser): recover DeepSeek DSML tool calls
prs.body:
> Maintainer note: I carried forward the contributor's DSML support and added the declaration, argument-boundary and example-context repairs. I updated this description to match the structural reader and retained `Refs #11130` because runtime classification and streaming remain separate work.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Recover complete DeepSeek DSML tool calls from response text. Read the structural tags directly so DSML saved inside JSON arguments or existing tool payloads does not become a separate invocation. Preserve DSML string values, including whitespace, literal quotes, marker-shaped text and empty strings; accept whitespace around attribute equals signs.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/src/lib.rs`. No provider, runtime, configuration, dependency or permission changes. Mixed-format call retention/order, malformed-output classification and streaming suppression remain follow-ups.
- **Blast radius:** The shared `parse_tool_calls` text-fallback entry point. Responses without DSML use the existing parser path. Recovered calls still enter the runtime's known-tool filter and normal approval and execution flow.
- **Linked issue(s):** Refs #11130.

### What this does, simply

Some DeepSeek models write a tool request into their reply instead of returning the API's native `tool_calls` field. DSML wraps that request in tags such as `<｜DSML｜ calls>`, `<｜DSML｜ invoke>` and `<｜DSML｜ parameter>`. ZeroClaw needs to recognize those tags to recover the reported non-streaming shell request.

Removing marker prefixes throughout a reply is unsafe. For example, a legitimate `file_write` request can contain DSML as text to save. Scanning that text as another invocation can turn the saved example into a tool call, while normalizing its markers can change the file's contents.

This PR reads DSML structure separately from argument data. It skips existing JSON values and tool-payload boundaries before looking for DSML. Within a DSML call, a parameter's value remains data through its reserved closing delimiter. A value marked `string="true"` keeps its exact bytes rather than being trimmed or decoded as JSON. A genuine call after an enclosing declaration or JSON wrapper remains recoverable. Example cues come only from surrounding prose, not descriptions or argument contents inside skipped payloads. Genuine teaching prose still suppresses example calls.

Complete valid calls use the existing tool registry and approval flow. Runtime handling of malformed DSML and live streaming output is unchanged. Mixed DSML and legacy formats can still lose or reorder calls, as identified in the existing reviews.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The reader stays in the shared parser and reuses its call representation, wrapper boundaries, JSON deserializer and GLM-line admission. It adds no general XML parser or provider-specific dispatcher. Direct parameter reading is needed because the older normalization path cannot distinguish structural tags from literal parameter contents. The parameter's own closing delimiter remains reserved, and existing global thinking-tag preprocessing is unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Deterministic parser-entrypoint tests exercise the changed data-versus-call boundary without depending on a model emitting a particular response. The broader runtime and streaming behavior is not established by these tests.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-api --features tokio/time --lib -- --quiet
# Parser: 215 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored. API: 310 passed; 0 failed.
cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-api --features tokio/time --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Passed with no warnings.
rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/src/lib.rs
# Passed.
git diff --check
# Passed.
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Passed.
```

Nine added regressions cover DSML inside JSON and legacy arguments; literal markers, empty strings and spaced attributes; incomplete spans; strict tag names; ordinary prose quotes; GLM-line argument data; and preservation of a genuine following call. Two further regressions cover example/sample words inside skipped declarations and arguments, teaching prose before and after those payloads, and separate prose fragments that must not join into an example cue. Existing tests cover the reported fullwidth and ASCII DSML calls, declaration rejection, examples, literal quotes and whitespace. The one ignored test is the unchanged `close_alias_inside_arguments_should_not_expose_nested_call` regression outside the `<tools>` alias.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI supplies workspace compilation, lint and consumer/test coverage. Its results must be checked against the published repair head; the local results above establish the parser-level behavior.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** No end-to-end DSML model/channel or streaming smoke was performed. Runtime classification and streaming remain on #11130.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source tracing confirmed that the existing runtime caller filters recovered calls against known tools and sends them through normal approval preparation. I did not run a live model or channel smoke.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No visual interface state changes.
- **Tested revision:** `5c00f9bd00bcdb24fec78f4f2c14276600dec2e7`; parser-file SHA-256 `a329c10eb1f997b7c8ca47a363bbc1fcdcc5404759dd0f4f98b034473b90b97e`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No additional local workspace build was run because the focused crate checks cover the edited parser and required CI supplies broader build coverage.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. No new tools or execution permissions; DSML requests use the existing registry and approval path.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The repair fixtures use synthetic tool requests and paths.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. DSML is untrusted model output that can request tool execution. The extraction scan preserves existing argument boundaries, parameter contents are not recursively parsed, and incomplete recognized DSML does not expose its payload to legacy executable fallbacks. Ordinary tool approvals remain in effect.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing supported protocols. Complete DSML calls gain parsing support; malformed recognized DSML is consumed by the parser rather than offered to legacy fallbacks.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed squash commit for this PR with `git revert <squash-merge-sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Existing `strict_tool_parsing = true` disables text-protocol fallback when the provider supplies native tool calls; it also disables other text-only tool protocols.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A DSML-emitting model returns markup without a recovered call, a recovered call has altered arguments, or unexpected additional calls appear. Inspect the response and tool-call records with sensitive argument content redacted.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(channels): classify telegram transcription failures and bound transient retries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every error from `manager.transcribe` in the Telegram voice path became `UpdateDisposition::RetryTransient`, so a terminally rejected voice update pinned the long-poll offset and head-of-line blocked every later message until an operator intervened (#10863; production incident reported in #10640, where an ASR endpoint's persistent HTTP 413 wedged the channel for ~8 minutes and survived restarts).
  - Transcription providers now classify failures: substantiated payload-specific terminal rejections (HTTP 413/415, plus local pre-flight byte-cap and format rejections) are `Permanent`; credential (401/403), rate-limit, 5xx, transport, and unrecognised failures stay `Transient` — the same conservative philosophy as the `getFile` classifier (#9314/#9315): retrying a recoverable failure is safe, skipping a recoverable one loses a message.
  - The Telegram voice parser acknowledges terminal rejections with a new sender notice (`VoiceDropReason::TranscriptionRejected`, Fluent key added in en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN) instead of retrying forever — the same contract as the existing duration and file-lookup drops.
  - A bounded transient budget (10 consecutive attempts per update) acknowledges a persistently failing update with a loud ERROR (update id + attempt count) instead of retrying it forever, so failures that can never be classified as permanent but never recover either (e.g. an endpoint returning 500 for one corrupted file) cannot wedge the channel indefinitely. Giving up is explicit and observable, never silent.
- Deepgram, AssemblyAI (upload step), and Google STT now check `!status.is_success()` before JSON deserialization, so a proxy/gateway 413/415 with a plain-text or HTML body classifies as `Permanent` instead of falling into an untyped JSON-parse failure (misread as retryable `Transient`). Error bodies are read as text, extracting the vendor JSON message when present. AssemblyAI `create`/`poll` carry no audio bytes, so their non-success statuses stay explicitly `Transient` instead of masquerading as a payload rejection.
- **Scope boundary:** media-group batch retry machinery unchanged; `getFile`/download classification unchanged; other channels' transcription call sites unchanged (they do not acknowledge vendor offsets); no config, CLI, or schema changes; `TranscriptionProvider` trait signature unchanged (classification rides inside the `anyhow` chain).
- **Blast radius:** Telegram channel update-disposition path (voice parse + single-update retry gate); transcription error construction sites in `zeroclaw-channels/src/transcription.rs`; one new Fluent key in runtime locale catalogs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10863. Related #10640, #9314, #9315.

### What this does, simply

When someone sends a voice note, the Telegram channel downloads the audio and hands it to a transcription endpoint. If that call fails, the channel used to retry the update forever — including failures that could never succeed, like the endpoint rejecting the recording as too long. Because Telegram redelivers unacknowledged updates first, one poisoned voice note blocked every message behind it, for every chat of the bot, and restarts did not help.

This PR makes the failure handling distinguish two cases. If the endpoint rejected *this recording* (too large, unsupported format), retrying is pointless: the channel now tells the sender why their voice note was dropped and moves on — the same way it already handles over-duration recordings and expired files. If the failure might recover (endpoint down, rate limit, bad credentials awaiting an operator fix), the update is still retried as before. As a safety net for failures that claim to be recoverable but never actually recover, an update is given up loudly after 10 consecutive attempts: an ERROR log names the update id and attempt count, so the message loss is explicit and observable rather than silent — which is the recovery policy the issue asks for.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the behavior boundary is covered by new wiremock-driven listener tests that replay the production incident shape (persistent 413) and the recovery shape (500 then 200); no manual Telegram setup adds signal beyond them.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `telegram` (voice transcription path)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

New focused tests, all at the real behavior boundary:

- `listen_terminally_rejected_transcription_does_not_block_later_updates` — the incident replay: voice update, ASR endpoint consistently answers 413 `audio duration exceeds limit`; the voice update is acknowledged with exactly one sender notice, and the text update behind it is delivered with the offset advancing past both.
- `listen_recoverable_transcription_failure_retries_and_delivers` — 500 once, then 200: the same update is retried at the same offset and delivered as `[Voice] recovered words`.
- `process_update_acknowledges_update_after_transient_budget_exhausted` — the transient budget gate: an update at the attempt cap is acknowledged with no further I/O; below the cap or for a different update id, routing is unchanged.
- `try_parse_voice_message_terminally_rejected_transcription_notifies_sender` — the sender notice carries the new dedicated wording to the right chat.
- `transcription.rs` unit tests: status classification (only 413/415 permanent; 400/401/403/408/409/422/425/429/451/5xx transient), local validation rejections classified permanent, `failure_kind` recovery through `anyhow` context layers and its transient default, and a wiremock pass over the Groq provider proving 413 → permanent while 500/429 → transient.
- Provider-path regressions (wiremock, added with the review fix): `deepgram_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent` (HTML 413 body → `Permanent`; vendor-JSON 413 keeps the readable message), `assemblyai_upload_413_is_permanent_but_metadata_413_stays_transient` (upload-step 413 → `Permanent`; create-step 413 → `Transient`), `google_stt_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent`.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** workspace `fmt` / `clippy` / test jobs cover `zeroclaw-channels` and the locale catalogs; the new tests run in the standard channels suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** 5 `link_enricher` tests fail in this Windows/localhost/VPN environment — pre-existing on clean `master` (localhost networking restriction), unrelated to this diff. CI (Linux) is expected green.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean (after one `cargo fmt --all` normalization pass over the new tests).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` → `Finished dev profile` (no lints in the crate; `--no-deps` because path-dependency `zeroclaw-config` trips pre-existing Windows-only `collapsible_if` lints on this host that Linux CI never compiles).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram` → `test result: FAILED. 1958 passed; 5 failed` — the 5 failures are the pre-existing `link_enricher` localhost cases above; every telegram/transcription test passes.
  - Filtered re-runs of the 9 new tests (`terminally_rejected`, `recoverable_transcription`, `transient_budget`, `failure_kind`, `http_status_classification`, `local_validation`, `whisper_style_http`) → all `ok`.
  - Review-fix round at `19293ef9a` (rebased onto master `4e82ce46e`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` → clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib transcription` → 82 passed / 0 failed; the 3 provider-path regression tests re-run after the rebase → all `ok`.
  - `cargo fluent check` → all catalogs `ok`, including the 5 edited `cli.ftl` files.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The classification mirrors the existing `FileLookupError::classify` philosophy and the voice-drop notice plumbing (`notify_voice_drop`, bounded notice timeout) is shared with the three existing drop reasons. Not verified: a live Telegram bot end-to-end run (covered instead by the wiremock listener tests at the same boundary the existing offset tests use).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface state changed; the only new user-facing string is a chat notice delivered through the existing `sendMessage` path, asserted by exact text in tests.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head `19293ef9a` (rebased onto `4e82ce46e`); interface `channel` = `telegram`; evidence = test tails above plus filtered re-runs.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** persistent-413 voice update: channel acknowledges it, notifies the sender once, later updates flow (before: channel retries the update forever and all later updates stall).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full `cargo test` workspace run — the change is contained to `zeroclaw-channels` (+ one locale key); focused crate suite plus CI covers the rest.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes` — no config/CLI/schema changes; behavior change is limited to updates that previously wedged the channel)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` restores the previous retry-everything behavior.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None` (no new surface; the existing `[transcription] enabled` switch disables the voice path entirely)
- **Observable failure symptoms:** regression would show as repeated `"Voice transcription failed"` WARN entries with `classification` flipping unexpectedly, ERROR `"Transient failure budget exhausted"` in healthy operation, or senders reporting spurious "audio message skipped" notices — grep `runtime-trace.jsonl` for `Voice transcription failed` / `budget exhausted`.

prs.title: feat(channels): add optional Telegram rich messages
prs.body:
Send headings, lists, quotes, and tables through Bot API `sendRichMessage` when `channels.telegram.<alias>.rich_messages` is enabled. The flag defaults to false. With it off, replies stay on the existing HTML path, and markdown tables are sent as preformatted text so they are not split or interpreted as inline HTML.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram has no HTML table tag, so markdown tables were sent as ordinary text and could be split mid-table. Native rendering now exists behind `channels.telegram.<alias>.rich_messages` because some clients still cannot show rich messages.
  - With the flag on, final replies use `sendRichMessage` for headings, lists, quotes, and tables. Tables wider than 20 columns are fenced as code. Math delimiters outside code are removed so amounts like `$400` are not parsed as formulas, and markdown images become links.
  - With the flag off, the HTML path is unchanged except that every markdown table is wrapped in `<pre><code>`. A table that fits stays in one chunk. A longer table continues on the next message between rows, with the header repeated, and `(continues...)` / `(continued)` markers when a message is split.
  - Inbound updates that have a `rich_message` and no `text` are turned into plain markdown so the agent can still read them.
  - Streaming drafts stay plain text. On finalize, a prepared reply that fits the rich-message limit is edited in place. If that edit fails, the existing HTML edit, plain edit, and delete-then-send path runs. A failed delete on that path skips the replacement send.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change other channels, the bot token, pairing, attachments, or draft streaming while a reply is still being generated. It does not turn rich messages on by default, and it does not add a client-capability probe.
- **Blast radius:** Every Telegram reply that contains a markdown table, including aliases that leave the flag off. With the flag on, final replies and over-long splits use `sendRichMessage`, falling back to HTML if Telegram rejects the rich payload. Inbound rich-only messages become normal user text.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #8415

### What this does, simply

Telegram replies are HTML. HTML cannot draw a table, so a markdown table showed up as pipe characters, and a long answer could cut the table in half. Telegram's newer rich-message API can draw headings, lists, quotes, and tables, but not every client understands it yet.

This adds `rich_messages` on each Telegram alias. Leave it unset or `false` and ZeroClaw keeps sending HTML. Tables are then placed in a preformatted block so the grid stays intact. A table longer than one message continues with the header repeated. Set it to `true` and final replies go out through `sendRichMessage`. A running channel reads that alias setting from the live config on each send. If that call fails, the same text is sent as HTML, and a later retry continues at the first HTML piece that did not arrive. Draft updates while the model is still writing stay plain text either way. A message that arrives with only a rich body, and no normal text, is converted to markdown before the agent sees it.

```toml
[channels.telegram.home]
rich_messages = true
```

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`telegram`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Telegram bot token, a configured alias, an authorized peer, and `zeroclaw channel start`. Use a client that can render rich messages, and if possible a second client that cannot. Compare `master` and this branch with the same chat.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On `master`, start the Telegram channel and ask the bot for a short markdown reply with a heading, a quote, and a 2-column table.
  2. Check the same reply on this branch with `rich_messages` omitted or `false`.
  3. Set `rich_messages = true` on the alias, restart the channel, and ask again.
  4. Ask for a table with 21 columns.
  5. Send the bot a rich message that has no plain `text` field, if the client can do that.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With the flag off, the table is a monospaced block and the rest is HTML. With the flag on, the heading, quote, and 2-column table render as rich content. A 21-column table stays fenced as code. A rich-only inbound message is answered instead of ignored. If `sendRichMessage` fails, the reply still arrives as HTML.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same table is inline pipe text, and a long reply can split it. There is no `rich_messages` key. A rich-only inbound update is not read as the user message.

### How I tested

Rebased onto current `master` (`5162ca01b`) and rechecked the channel and config crates. No live Telegram client was available. Workspace clippy, `cargo nextest`, and the release builds were not re-run after the rebase.

```sh
cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- rich_
cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- table_i
cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The unit tests cover table wrapping, currency and image rewriting, wide-table fencing, protected splits, inbound rich-message projection, and the `rich_messages` default. Clippy on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-config` covers the new Rust. GitHub CI still needs to run the workspace lint, full test, and release jobs.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** GitHub CI on the rebased branch was not watched from here. The live Bot API, a real Telegram client, the macOS and Windows release builds, and the 32-bit check were not run.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- rich_
test result: ok. 8 passed (zeroclaw-channels); 1 passed (zeroclaw-config)

cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- table_i
test telegram::tests::telegram_markdown_to_html_wraps_table_in_pre ... ok
test telegram::tests::split_keeps_markdown_table_intact ... ok

cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 12s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing against api.telegram.org or a Telegram client. Not verified: native rendering, the HTML fallback after a rejected `sendRichMessage`, draft finalize against a real chat, or client-specific unsupported-message placeholders.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `24946811c` on `feat/telegram-rich-messages`, rebased onto `e8d2e5fc8`. Evidence is unit-test assertions on the HTML and markdown strings, the live-config read, the rich HTML resume, and rich-only unauthorized updates. Not a Telegram client.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** None. No Telegram client was exercised.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The automated tests assert the prepared markdown and HTML. They do not show how a client paints the message.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo nextest run --locked` were not repeated after the rebase. `cargo build --profile ci` was skipped because that job needs `clang` and `mold`. `cargo audit` and `cargo deny` were skipped because dependencies did not change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`Yes`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: With the flag on, final replies call `sendRichMessage` on the same Bot API base URL and bot token the channel already uses. A failed rich send falls back to `sendMessage`. Inbound updates that contain only `rich_message` are projected to plain text and then follow the existing allowed-peer path, so a rich body is not a new trust boundary. The projection is lossy markdown, not executed HTML.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No upgrade is required. Existing aliases load with `rich_messages = false`. To opt in, set `rich_messages = true` under `[channels.telegram.<alias>]` and restart the channel. Even without that, markdown tables in Telegram replies now go out as preformatted text instead of inline pipe characters.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk aside from the always-on table formatting change. Reverting this commit restores the previous HTML path.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert this commit, or set `rich_messages = false` to leave the rich API unused. Revert is required to restore the old inline table formatting.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channels.telegram.<alias>.rich_messages` (default `false`)
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Log lines `Telegram sendRichMessage failed; falling back to HTML` and `Telegram finalize_draft rich edit failed; falling back to HTML`. Users then see the HTML fallback. If a later draft delete fails, the existing path logs `Telegram finalize_draft delete failed; skipping sendMessage to avoid duplicate` and does not post a second copy.

prs.body:
## Summary

> **Draft proposal 7/12.** This remains an incomplete, stacked proposal—not a request to merge or enable Goal execution. Required CI for the current head passed, including Windows recovery and finding-backed Semgrep OSS. Five expected skips and a superseded risk-report cancellation are explained below. The resolved Windows compile error, local aggregate failures and coverage limits remain recorded separately. Independent review passed that repair; this is not Core Team approval or a readiness decision.

Candidate: `28def6291d016bb82dc1d4222111d1b017abfeeb`; frozen comparison base: `0bb1d4a801ac7dbecc9e9a91128c0a96ace98ab3`. This PR targets `master`; until its predecessors land, its diff includes the inherited stack. Do not merge or enable an incomplete prefix.

Before merge, the residual runtime integration requires a recorded Core Team exception or authoritative ownership decision through normal review; this proposal requests that decision and does not grant it. Before enabled rollout, comparable binary/startup/memory footprint measurements and operator acceptance remain required. The current tests do not supply those approvals or measurements.

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds native IPC/WSS handling for typed `session/goal` and `session/goal_update`, wiring ZeroCode's `/goal` command, lifecycle notifications, and client decoding to the existing Goal runtime.
  - Carries ordinary Agent admission policy and the shared usage ledger through Goal execution, while preserving the existing session and Goal across ordinary client EOF; explicit session disposal and daemon-generation shutdown remain distinct lifecycle operations.
  - Separates candidate presentation from verifier verdict and durable persistence acknowledgment, with typed admission, transition, and failure states.
- **Scope boundary:** This is slice 07 after slice 06, and depends on PR #11883. It integrates native IPC/WSS with the ordinary Agent policy/ledger and session continuity; it does not include the later policy-cutover or durable-pairing slices. Native support is not Web Goal admission. This incomplete prefix is not enablement, deployment, or operator acceptance.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime RPC registration/dispatch, ordinary Agent policy and usage accounting at Goal execution, session/daemon lifecycle, native IPC/WSS, ZeroCode `/goal` command/wire/chat consumers, and public Rust/wire contracts. This slice adds no dependency, MSRV floor, configuration field, or schema migration; the cumulative stack does change schema.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303. Depends on PR #11883 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11883. Related tracker #10341 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341. None is claimed closed.

### What this does, simply

Goal is ZeroClaw's durable, budgeted background-work feature. This slice lets native RPC clients and ZeroCode observe and control Goal sessions using typed requests and lifecycle updates. Disconnecting an ordinary client does not itself delete the session or its Goal; explicit close/kill/delete operations and daemon-generation shutdown own disposal. A displayed candidate is not proof that verification succeeded or that the candidate was durably saved. This remains one incomplete part of a larger stack, not a standalone deployment.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

prs.title: feat(rpc): stable denial reason identifiers and localized selector denials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every RPC authorization denial now carries an `RpcDenialReason`, a stable identifier set by the typed constructor that builds it. The constructor also derives the JSON-RPC code from the reason and renders the message from the reason's Fluent key. `AuthDenied`'s `reason` field is private, so a denial cannot be built without one; the free-text `auth_required(message)` and `forbidden(message)` constructors are gone.
  - The denial audit record (`RPC authorization denied`) emits the identifier as `reason` and the localized text as a separate `denial_message` attribute, so operators can group and alert on refusals without depending on wording or the daemon's locale. The attribute is not named `message` because log exporters copy attributes out flat and log backends reserve that name.
  - The coarse grant denial and every selector refusal (config path, agent, cron, session workspace, `fs/list_dir`, attachment source, session environment, global streams, SOP) resolve through 12 new `rpc-auth-*` Fluent keys with arguments instead of inline English literals. Request values are quoted and escaped exactly as the old `{:?}` literals quoted them, so the English text is byte-identical. The one exception is the global-stream refusal, whose key carries the wording #11326 gives it, naming the persisted log.
  - A denial after failed revalidation now records the principal id and auth provider of the binding it drops. Before, the dispatcher cleared the binding first and the record carried nulls. The same change removes a production `expect()`.
  - The branch merges current master, so the denial sites #11171 added (the authority lease, the expiry helper, and the chunked-upload recheck) use the typed constructors too. The upload recheck's session-ownership refusal gets its own `session_not_owned` reason. The later merge converts #11132's sites the same way: `require_additional_grant` refuses with `grant_missing`, and steering admission records its ownership refusal as `session_not_owned` and its remote local-capability refusal as a new `session_local_capabilities` reason instead of rebuilding denials from message text, while the binding checks it calls record their own refusals once rather than twice.
- **Scope boundary:** The JSON-RPC wire shape is unchanged: codes and English message bytes are identical (apart from the global-stream refusal's #11326 wording), and the identifier is not sent to clients. Gateway HTTP denial bodies, handshake (`initialize`) auditing, the refusals that bypass `AuthDenied` (session ownership outside chunked uploads, shared memory plane, SOP decision authorization, TUI signature, remote-WSS SOP methods), and translated catalogues are unchanged. The cron refusal's client text ("Cron job not found: ...") stays an inline English literal on purpose: it must match the genuinely-missing-job answer, which comes from the cron store, so the refusal does not confirm that a job exists.
- **Blast radius:** The audit record's `reason` attribute changes from prose to an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`. The prose field is present in released v0.8.6 and v0.8.7, so existing log consumers must switch to `denial_message` for display and the stable `reason` identifier for grouping. Retained older records keep their old field meaning; consumers reading both formats must handle that difference. Open PRs that build denials with `AuthDenied::auth_required`/`forbidden` or struct literals will stop compiling at rebase; the fix is a variant, a key, and a typed constructor per new site.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11005. Depends on #12062, the approved holding-crate exception row for this change, which must land before this merges. Related #11326 (merged; this PR's denial-records docs and the global-stream refusal describe the `logs/query` and `logs/get` scoping it implements), #8289, #10259.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

When the daemon refuses an RPC request because the caller lacks permission, it writes a warning to its log. Until now the "reason" in that warning was the English sentence the client saw, so it changed whenever the wording changed and would change with the daemon's language, which makes it a poor thing to alert on. It is now a short fixed code such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, and the sentence moves to its own field. Several refusal sentences were written directly in the code instead of in the translation catalogue; they now live in the catalogue like the rest. Finally, one kind of refusal, when a policy change invalidates an existing connection, forgot who the connection belonged to before logging; it now records that. Clients see the same error codes and English messages as before, apart from the refusal for daemon-wide logs, which now also names the persisted log.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the changed output is a structured log record, and the new tests drive real refused requests through the dispatcher and assert the record each one writes.

### Documentation correction at `2c8cdbb2ec94ac1bcd41d8acaa039d830a1c6677`

This documentation-only update appends to `3ab104bdacaf930f35f383f710bdb82e8229ea6c` and changes no runtime code, catalogues, tests, or dependency versions. The audit compatibility notes now account for released consumers. The attributes table also distinguishes the record's classification code from the immediate steering response: `session_local_capabilities` is recorded as `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` (`-32003`), while a refused immediate steering admission returns `FORBIDDEN` (`-32012`). Both existing codes remain unchanged.

On that exact commit, `BASE_SHA=3ab104bdacaf930f35f383f710bdb82e8229ea6c DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` and the same scoped `docs_links_gate.sh` both passed on macOS. `git diff --check 3ab104bdacaf930f35f383f710bdb82e8229ea6c 2c8cdbb2ec94ac1bcd41d8acaa039d830a1c6677` passed. No new runtime tests were needed for the documentation-only correction.

The runtime results below remain bound to their stated earlier revisions. This update does not claim a fresh runtime, translated-locale, native Windows, or full mdBook rendering run. The approved exception in #12062 still needs to land, and current-head Core review and required CI remain merge gates.

### Earlier runtime validation

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Parallel Runtime Test` run the new unit and dispatcher tests; `Lint` covers the Rust changes; `Docs Style` and the links gate cover the documentation section.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Head 3ab104bdac** (merges master 1c1cd118ac, which includes #11326): the merge's one conflict was `GLOBAL_STREAM_SCOPED_DENIAL`, which #11326 reworded and this PR deletes; the deletion stands, and `rpc-auth-global-stream-scoped` carries #11326's text byte for byte. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `5909 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, #11326's persisted-log tests included; `-- rpc::`: `867 passed; 0 failed`. `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, clippy (no findings in changed files) and the docs quality gate on `authentication.md` pass; the comment hygiene scanner was run directly on the touched files because ripgrep is broken on this host. Earlier heads: 0a386d6cce converted #11132's two denial sites (`require_additional_grant` and steering admission), da62caf7e1 dropped c94abbf93e's configure-race synchronization in favor of #11330's fence.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1, head 2e3f2e5101, which merges master a0f70b7925, unless noted):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `5455 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored`. The two failures are `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` and `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`. Master a0f70b7925 itself fails the same way under the same command (the configure test in 2 of 2 runs, the cost test in 1 of 2), each passes alone 3 of 3 times on this branch, and neither touches code this PR changes. Before merging master (2d96dfa52d, on 2443af29ea) the same command passed clean: `5313 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: `637 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `ws::tests::websocket_handler_projects_anthropic_empty_terminal_stream_as_user_error` hitting its response deadline under load; it passes alone 3 of 3 times, and `ws.rs` changes only in master's commits.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`: no findings in changed files. Under `-D warnings` it stops on four findings in files this PR does not touch, byte-identical to master: `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, macOS test builds) and three `clippy::drop_non_drop` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, which appear only when `-p zeroclaw-gateway` builds channels without `channel-telegram`.
  - `cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps`: 0 warnings.
  - `cargo fluent check`: all FTL files ok. `cargo fluent scan`: no `rpc-auth-*` key reported stale.
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (markdownlint 0 errors), `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each restored afterwards:
  - Emitting the message text as `reason` again fails all six dispatcher capture tests.
  - Auditing after the binding is cleared (the old order) fails `denial_after_failed_revalidation_keeps_the_principal_it_dropped` with a null principal.
  - Renaming one identifier fails the identifier-pinning test and the matching dispatcher test.
  - Deleting one new key from `cli.ftl` fails three tests that render the `{rpc-auth-agent-not-entitled}` missing-key marker.
  - Not verified: a live daemon under a translated locale; Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface changes; the changed output is a log record whose attributes the tests assert.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No `--no-default-features` check: nothing in `rpc/` is feature-gated, so no constructor can lose its only caller in that build.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The record carries the principal id and provider label it already carried, never bearer material; the attribution fix stops dropping data the dispatcher already held.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test principals are synthetic roster names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Request values that appear in denial messages (agent aliases, paths, job ids, procedure names) are quoted and escaped, so control characters cannot break a message or its log line.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for clients: codes and English messages are unchanged, apart from the global-stream refusal's wording. The audit record's `reason` attribute now holds an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`; this changes the meaning of a field already shipped in v0.8.6 and v0.8.7. Log consumers must update display and grouping logic, including when reading retained records in both formats.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records whose `reason` is not one of the identifiers documented in `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md`, or a `denial_message` or client error message that is a `{rpc-auth-...}` missing-key marker.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Refusal cost:** argumented Fluent lookups parse the catalogue on each call. On an Apple Silicon Mac that measured about 180 µs per refusal for an English daemon and about 530 µs for a translated locale that lacks the new keys (every translated locale until a translation pass). This affects only refused requests. Caching parsed bundles would remove it, but it changes every argumented call site, so it is left for a separate PR. The same cost makes a cron refusal for another agent's job slightly slower than one for a missing job; the answers themselves are identical.
- **Unbound selectors:** the five selector helpers that refused an unbound dispatcher with a bare literal now use the existing first-call key and write a record. They are unreachable once the gate has run.
- **`code` stays a public field** derived once from the reason at construction, so the gateway's readers are untouched.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Expose `reason` on the wire and in gateway HTTP denial bodies.
- Audit handshake denials and the refusals listed as unrecorded in the new docs section.
- Translation fill for the `rpc-auth-*` keys, and parse each Fluent catalogue once.

prs.title: fix(channels): re-apply the system prompt cap after per-turn skill refreshes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The channel-turn system prompt is modified after the initial `max_system_prompt_chars` finalization (skills refresh splice on fresh sessions or mode changes, per-message signal block, peer-map append, thinking prefix prepend), so the operator's cap silently stopped applying exactly when the prompt was largest.
  - Re-apply `finalize_system_prompt` with the agent's cap as the last step before the system message enters history (message-processing path), and at the provider-switch retry path (`refresh_channel_history_skills`) and after the startup builder's own post-finalize additions (tool instructions, deferred section, receipts addendum), so the cached prompt starts in-cap too.
  - `finalize_system_prompt` now strips existing `TIMESTAMP_ORIENTATION` occurrences before head-retention truncation, making re-finalization idempotent (a re-finalized cached channel prompt previously always gained a duplicate orientation, since the base orientation survives into the retained head).
- **Scope boundary:** no new settings, no canonical-source duplication; the no-op path of `finalize_system_prompt` (prompt within cap) is untouched; compaction/history trimming behavior unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** channel system-prompt assembly only. Agents whose prompts already fit the cap see no change (finalization is a no-op for them). Agents with large skill sets on fresh sessions now get a capped prompt; the previously possible over-cap prompt instead reached the context-floor budget refusal (`context_floor_exceeds_budget`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12044 (deferred bootstrap sections), Related #12056 (identity-head truncation, whose zone-aware finalize this reuses).

### What this does, simply

`max_system_prompt_chars` is the operator's ceiling for what the system prompt may occupy. It was enforced only when the prompt was first built at startup. Later, on the first message of a new conversation (or after a skills-mode change), the runtime replaces the skills section with a freshly rendered one — in Full injection mode that is every skill's full instructions — and appends per-message extras. None of those steps re-checked the ceiling, so a fresh conversation could dispatch a system prompt several times larger than the configured cap. In production this surfaced as a hard refusal for brand-new conversations (`system prompt and tool definitions (148706 tokens) exceed context budget (100000)`) while long-lived conversations kept using the older, capped cached prompt and worked fine. This PR applies the existing cap, with the existing identity-aware truncation, after all of those modifications — and makes re-applying it safe by de-duplicating the runtime-owned timestamp orientation block first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — behavior is fully covered by new regression tests that reproduce the incident shape (skill refresh exceeding the cap before the fix, capped after), and the pre/post delta is asserted in-test.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (telegram path in the repro test, mechanism is channel-generic)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

- New `process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh` (zeroclaw-channels): builds a real startup prompt under a 4000-char cap, drops a ~26KB-body skill on disk in Full mode, and asserts (1) the refresh splice really exceeds the cap (incident reproduction), (2) the refreshed history prompt is ≤ cap with exactly one timestamp orientation, (3) end-to-end, the provider receives a system prompt ≤ cap with one orientation.
- New `refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation` (zeroclaw-runtime): re-finalizing an already-finalized prompt does not duplicate the orientation.
- Before the fix the e2e assertion fails (~26K chars vs cap 4000 reaching the provider); after, green.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI on this PR (build/test/clippy across feature matrix) — the change touches the channel orchestrator and system-prompt finalization used by all channels.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** local run covered lib targets of the two touched crates; full-workspace integration binaries were not built locally (CI covers them).
- **Commands run and tail output:** both new tests and neighbors (`final_prompt_budget*`, `timestamp_orientation_respects_budgets`, full `agent::system_prompt` module — 35 tests, `process_channel_message_refreshes_available_skills_after_new_session`) pass; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` exits 0 with no new warnings in the changed lines.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Idempotence of the added finalization on under-cap prompts (no-op path) via the orientation-count assertions; not verified: full workspace integration binaries and non-Linux platform runs.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- Document an optional local Sem MCP configuration for repository lookup.
- Show explicit executable/repository paths and how to attach the server to an agent through a bundle.
- Explain that the server exposes more than lookup tools and that MCP auto-admission is not a read-only permission boundary.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only; no default configuration, runtime, dependencies, or authorization changes.
- **Blast radius:** Readers of the MCP tools guide who opt into this example.
- **Linked issues:** None.

I work on Sem at Ataraxy Labs.

### What this does, simply

Adds a concrete local-code example to the MCP guide. It explains where the process runs, what repository it can access, and what authorization assumptions readers must not make. It does not require Sem or change existing servers.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: documentation-only addition; local checks and a server smoke test are described below.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on:** Local documentation style and added-link gates. The original head passed Docs Style but failed Security on unchanged TLS dependencies; CI for the correction must be evaluated separately.
- **Known coverage gap:** Full ZeroClaw runtime was not exercised. Optional HTTP link checking was skipped by the gate because lychee is not installed.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Linting: 1 file(s)
Summary: 0 error(s)

Ran 6 tests
OK
Collected 1 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).

git diff --check
(no output)
```

The temporary Git environment override prevents a machine-specific external diff from affecting the link gate's temporary-repository tests; it changes no repository or global configuration.

- **Beyond CI:** Parsed the documented TOML, substituted local paths, and launched Sem through the Python MCP SDK using its command, arguments, and environment. Initialization/tool listing succeeded; `sem_find` returned a fixture function and its caller. Checked the configuration fields and process environment handling against ZeroClaw's schema and transport implementation. This is a server-level smoke test, not a ZeroClaw end-to-end test.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no application interface or styling changed.
- **Tested revisions:** `b495fa7` for the original MCP stdio smoke test; `b0f9a51` for the corrected Markdown, documentation gates and TOML validation. The runtime smoke test was not repeated for the corrected recipe.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Documentation gate output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** MCP initialization and fixture lookup succeeded.
- **Intentionally skipped:** Rust workspace builds/tests because no Rust code changed; live model/provider calls and production authorization behavior were not tested.

### Follow-up correction

Adopted IftekharUddin's focused documentation correction from commit `85fd5883b7e9818a45814e76cf4d5d533dab7c15`, preserving authorship, as `b0f9a51`. Added `SEM_LOCAL=1` and `SEM_MCP_NO_SHARED=1` and narrowed the networking claim. Verified both variables against Sem 0.27.0 source.

Validation on the corrected head:

```text
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md BASE_SHA=b495fa789e7f161f6d773845bfd650c9899aab9e bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh

GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md BASE_SHA=b495fa789e7f161f6d773845bfd650c9899aab9e bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
Ran 6 tests: OK
Collected 0 added link(s)

git diff --check HEAD~1 HEAD
(no output)
```

The complete example parses with Python 3.12 `tomllib`; all four environment flags and the agent bundle assignment were checked. No new runtime or network-isolation claim is made.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No** runtime change. The optional example grants a local MCP process repository access and documents that explicitly.
- New external network calls? **No** runtime change. The recipe disables Sem's MCP cloud client with `SEM_LOCAL=1`, requests a dedicated stdio process with `SEM_MCP_NO_SHARED=1`, and sets CLI network/telemetry controls. These settings do not restrict network access by commands exposed through the server. Existing model-provider data exposure is explained.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**, if a reader opts into the configuration, repository content can become model context. The guide warns about tool authority, model exposure, and existing authorization controls; it does not recommend blanket approval.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? **Yes**.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**, only existing configuration documented.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**.

## Rollback

prs.title: fix(config): cascade agent renames into permission-profile selectors
prs.body:
## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` - **What changed and why:** - `rewrite_agent_refs` now rewrites every `permission_profiles.

.allowed_agents` entry that names the renamed agent and marks `permission_profiles.

` dirty. `rename_with_cascade` used to move the `agents` key and leave the selector naming the old alias, so `config/map-key-rename` was rejected in `validate_auth` (`permission_profiles.

.allowed_agents names "" but [agents.] is not configured`) and an explicitly selected agent could not be renamed at all. - `collect_agent_refs` now reports each such selector as a hard reference at `permission_profiles.

.allowed_agents[]`. `validate_auth` rejects a selector that names a missing agent, so the delete cascade (`plan_delete` / `delete_with_cascade`) refuses up front and names the selector instead of relying on a later generic validation error. The rename post-condition reuses the same collector, so it also proves that no selector still names the old alias. - Collect and rewrite share one predicate that follows `Config::validate_auth` and `PermissionProfileConfig::resolve`: the selector is trimmed, and a blank selector or the `"*"` wildcard (`zeroclaw_api::grants::WILDCARD`) never names a particular agent. Wildcards and unrelated selectors keep their text and position; a matched selector is written back as the bare new alias, which is what `resolve` compiles it to anyway. - Profiles are walked in sorted key order, like the existing agent and peer-group walks (`permission_profiles` is a `HashMap`), so blocker order is deterministic. - The multi-agent walkthrough's list of common delete blockers now includes a profile that names the agent. - **Scope boundary:** - Only `allowed_agents` selectors join the cascade. `config_write_paths` entries that spell an agent path, such as `agents..*`, are path grants and are left stale by a rename. The holder of such a grant silently loses config-write access to the renamed agent, and an agent created later under the old name would be writable by them. Both effects already occur on `master` when an unselected agent is renamed or an agent is deleted and recreated. Rewriting such grants, or at least reporting them as rename warnings, is left for a follow-up. - The refreshed base includes RPC agent deletion through the supported lifecycle handler from #10244: `config/map-key-delete` for an agent delegates to `handle_agent_delete`. It uses the shared reference cascade, so the selected-agent blocker applies there too. - No change to `scrub_agent_refs`, the persisted format, or Fluent strings. The only docs change is the one walkthrough line above. - **Blast radius:** Every agent lifecycle surface built on `alias_refs`: RPC `config/map-key-rename`, the gateway agent rename and delete routes (including the dashboard delete-impact preview), and `zeroclaw agents rename|delete`. The gateway authorizes a rename's complete write set, so a scoped principal renaming a selected agent there also needs write access to `permission_profiles.

`. `zeroclaw agents rename|delete` saves without an authorization check, so on `master` it could write a file whose selector names a missing agent (a daemon started on that file installs a deny-all authorization policy until it is repaired); with this change the rename writes a valid selector and the delete is refused. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11009. Related #10244 - **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `config`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:L`, `topic:identity-access`. ### What this does, simply A permission profile can grant access to specific agents by name, for example `allowed_agents = ["researcher"]`. Renaming such an agent did not work: the agent moved to its new name, but the profile still pointed at the old one, and the authorization check refused to save a profile that names an agent that no longer exists. For a configuration that already passes authorization validation, the rename now updates those profile entries in the same save, so the profile keeps granting the same agent under its new name, and the old name stops working in the same step. A `"*"` entry (every agent) and entries for other agents are left untouched. Deleting an agent that a profile names is now refused immediately, with a message pointing at the exact profile entry to change first. Wildcard and unrelated selectors retain their existing text and positions. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`. A two-command CLI check shows the delta on the surface that saves without an authorization check. - **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw agents rename|delete`). The RPC `config/map-key-rename` boundary is covered by the regression test below. - **Setup / preconditions:** A throwaway config dir containing only this `config.toml`: ```toml schema_version = 3 [agents.alpha] [permission_profiles.reader] allowed_agents = ["alpha", "*"] ``` - **Steps to run:** 1. `zeroclaw --config-dir

agents delete alpha --dry-run` 2. `zeroclaw --config-dir agents rename alpha beta`, then read `/config.toml`. - **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 1 prints `deleting agents.alpha is BLOCKED by 1 hard reference(s):` with `✗ permission_profiles.reader.allowed_agents[0] (hard reference)`; the `"*"` entry is not a blocker, and `--yes` is refused without writing the file. Step 2 prints `renamed agents.alpha → agents.beta (rewrote 3 reference path(s))`, and the file holds `[agents.beta]` and `allowed_agents = ["beta", "*"]`. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 1 reports no blocker, so `--yes` deletes the agent and leaves `allowed_agents = ["alpha", "*"]`. Step 2 moves the agent to `[agents.beta]` but leaves `allowed_agents = ["alpha", "*"]`. Either file fails auth validation (`[dangling_reference] permission_profiles.reader.allowed_agents names "alpha" ...`). ### Current integration validation Updated from source `6c04a2d22195ca593843e81e8b4d6d7052c2076b` by adding a merge of `master` `9dbb57231f48e26fee56243de4f7845924ce4f04` and repair `84b434e8039c665bc96a9c75e8c48fa88c53aa3f`. The merge preserves the original PR ancestry. The integration repair passes the retained `ConfigCommit` to the complete write-set recheck and restores accepted authorization-policy publication inside the retained fresh rename transaction, immediately after successful persistence and before lifecycle changes or an await. The original test assertions are unchanged. The final source tree `c25f4a8141f95e1bf0eb4524a97d3f6bfa35631b` was explicitly rebuilt after cleaning the two affected packages, then committed unchanged as `84b434e8039c665bc96a9c75e8c48fa88c53aa3f`. milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
