prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded password auth provider exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the roster password verification in #11264 (the provider-only first slice of #8076). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the blocking item in the 2026-10-06 review on #11264, which named the scope: the password provider, its credential kind and provenance pair, its registration, and the `is_auth_input_path` line that #11265 carries for whichever of #11264 and #11313 lands second.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #11264 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime`: `PasswordAuthProvider` in `src/security/auth_provider/password.rs`, compiled from the roster entries that carry a `password_hash`, with one scrypt verification per attempt on the blocking pool, the same `BadCredential` denial for every miss (against a decoy when the name has no hash to check), and a match resolving to the entry's durable roster principal; the `Credential::Password` kind, redacted in `Debug`, and the `(Password, Roster)` provenance arm in `src/security/auth_provider/mod.rs`; registration in `AcceptedAuthState::from_config` in `src/rpc/auth.rs` only while `security.password_auth.enabled` is on and pairing is required, and `security.password_auth` joining the `auth_inputs` the accepted authorization state is compiled from; and, for whichever of #11264 and #11313 lands second, the `security.password_auth` arm of `is_auth_input_path` that #11265 carries in commit 9707c30981. It also names the `password_hash: None` field in the existing roster literals of tests in `src/rpc/{auth,dispatch}.rs`, `src/security/auth_provider/peercred.rs` and `src/security/principal_resolver.rs`, the `config/set-many` doc comment and the updated `users.bob has no credential` refusal in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, and focused tests. The scrypt hash policy, the `password_hash` roster field and the `[security.password_auth]` switch live in `zeroclaw-config`, and `AuthMethod::Password` in `zeroclaw-api`, so they need no runtime permission. It excludes any transport that presents a password, login sessions, rate limits or lockout, principal sources beyond the `[users]` roster, new grant sources or operator-authority paths, and #11265's own runtime changes (its Fluent keys), which need their own decision.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8076, #11264 (head `ab4fe4c72a`), #11265 (commit `9707c30981`) and #11313. Precedent: #11701, #11963, and the #11286 row already in the table, which covers the same files but explicitly excludes a new auth provider or credential kind.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #11264 lets a `[users.<name>]` roster entry carry a password hash and verifies a name and password against it through the auth-provider seam the crate already holds: the provider sits in the same `ProviderRegistry` as the native, peer-credential and OIDC providers, and a verified password resolves through the same principal resolver to the same roster principal that entry's peer credential resolves to. No transport presents a password yet; the provider is registered in the running daemon only while the switch is on and pairing is required, which also lists `password` among the `initialize` handshake's `auth_methods`, and a bearer that selects it is refused as the wrong credential kind (covered by `a_bearer_selecting_the_password_provider_is_refused`). The login boundary that will present passwords (with its rate limits, lockout and sessions) is a later slice of #8076. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the auth-provider and RPC authorization-state owners in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

Why not a new crate now: the provider plugs into the existing `AuthProvider` registry and principal resolver in this crate, and its registration lives in the accepted authorization state that `rpc/auth.rs` compiles. Moving it out on its own would split that seam ahead of the kernel extraction that owns the auth-provider boundary, which is the case the exception policy describes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; documentation-only change to a Markdown table. Please review the row's scope against the #11264 head (`ab4fe4c72a`) and the `is_auth_input_path` arm in #11265's `9707c30981`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the docs-links and comment-hygiene gates. `Docs Style` lints only `docs/book/src`, so it does not cover this file; markdownlint was run by hand below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no CI markdown lint for `crates/*/AGENTS.md` (run by hand below). No check can confirm that a row matches the code it covers or that a Core decision exists; that is this review.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
git diff --check origin/master HEAD                          passed
BASE_SHA=5d4b18d335 scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh            No added links detected in changed docs lines.
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-runtime   Comment hygiene gate passed.
python3 -I scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py --root crates/zeroclaw-runtime

npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md
                                                             Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The row names every runtime path #11264 changes at `ab4fe4c72a` (`git diff --stat origin/master...origin/feat/8076-password-provider`, six files under `crates/zeroclaw-runtime`) and nothing else; every type, function, field and config key it names exists at that head, or in `9707c30981` where the row says so; the table still has four cells per row, the new row is the last row directly under the previous one, and the file has no prose em-dash. No Rust was built: no code changes.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`; no user-visible interface changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `N/A`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Rust gates do not apply to a Markdown-only change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`; once approved, the row permits only the named additions in the holding crate and grants no execution or data-access authority.
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

Low-risk, documentation only: `git revert <sha>`. Before approval, withdrawing the row grants nothing; after approval, narrowing or revoking it is a reviewed docs change and does not remove code that already landed.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded agent owned-state retirement exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the agent owned-state retirement and knowledge-graph scoping in #9745 (which fixes #9647). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #9745 (`src/agent_owned_state.rs:741-745`, 2026-10-25), which found that the knowledge export-and-purge flow has no covering exception.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #9745 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `123b8396f3`, eighteen files: `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local,types,wss}.rs`, `src/tools/{mod,delegate}.rs`, `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`, `src/i18n.rs`, `locales/en/{cli,tools}.ftl` and `locales/{es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`. Most of it is continued work on a subsystem the crate already holds. On `master`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` carries `live_acp_session_count`, `archive_agent_workspace`, `OwnedStateReport`, `cascade_owned_state`, `RenameStateReport` and `cascade_rename_agent`, and the gateway reaches them through a three-line `pub use` shim; #9745 moves them into the new `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, re-exports the four functions from `agent_lifecycle` for compatibility, deletes the gateway shim, and extends them. The additions the row names are: the `PathPresence` classifier `inspect_lifecycle_path`, which re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe so an uninspectable path is residue on Windows as on Unix; the committed delete and rename residue contracts `committed_delete_residue_exists` and `committed_rename_residue_exists`, which probe the workspace, cron, control-plane (through the new read-only `SqliteTaskStore::count_existing_by_agent`), ACP, memory, knowledge and session stores; the shared resolvers that both contracts and both cascades use to reopen the configured memory or session backend when the live handle is absent, or for memory is the `none` placeholder, while config still expects persistence, so a delete or rename cleans or re-points that store instead of skipping it (on `master` the RPC delete substituted `NoneMemory` and warned, and the cascades returned zero for an absent backend); `AgentDeletionArchive`, which replaces `WorkspaceArchiveReport`, with an exclusively created leaf, `create_new` artifact writes and directory syncs up to the data directory, so a successful export gates the memory, knowledge, cron and ACP purges and a failure is reported in `warnings`; `prepare_knowledge_retirement` and `cascade_owned_state_with_retirement`, which export the agent's knowledge rows before the config commit, archive them as `knowledge.json` and purge through `KnowledgeGraph::purge_archived_owner` only while the store still matches the archived snapshot, plus the knowledge rename follower and the knowledge counts on both reports and the manifest; `plan_agent_delete_recovery_with_acp_count`, the recovery-mode preflight for a committed delete; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `run_agent_delete` behind `agents/delete` and `config/map-key-delete` (alias-grammar validation before any probe, so a reserved or malformed alias is now an `INVALID_PARAMS` error on `agents/delete` where `master` returned a `deleted: false` result; config-write authority for `agents.<alias>`, which `agents/delete` did not require before, and for every scrubbed path rechecked inside the commit, which neither method required before; a committed-delete retry that resumes the cascade without a config publication; and, on the map-key adapter only, refusing an agent with active RPC sessions as rename already does and answering `deleted: false` rather than an error for an unblocked alias with neither a config entry nor residue), the rename adapter validating both aliases and probing the old workspace through the classifier, `alias_create_refusal_message` for `config/set`, `config/set-many` and `config/map-key-create` when the alias they would create still owns knowledge or its store cannot be inspected, and the optional `owned_state` field on `ConfigMapKeyDeleteResult`; in `src/tools/mod.rs`, `knowledge_scope_for_agent` and the knowledge tool registration that binds a `KnowledgeScope` from the trusted agent alias, resolved per graph operation through the existing read-only live config handle (it registers no live-config consumer and acknowledges nothing) or from the configured `read_knowledge_from`, assigns unattributed legacy rows to `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` or the sole enabled agent, and withholds the tool when ownership is ambiguous; in `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `knowledge_tool_for_target`, rebinding the knowledge tool to the delegation target as the memory tools already are; the seven Fluent keys (five in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, two in `locales/en/tools.ftl`), of which `cli-alias-create-knowledge-{retained,uninspectable}` and `delegate-knowledge-init-failed` are translated in `es`, `fr`, `ja` and `zh-CN` with every-locale tests in `src/i18n.rs`; and the tests, including the test-only `pause_knowledge_archive_under` and negative-probe hooks and the `memory` parameter on the test-only `RpcContext::for_persistence_tests` with its call sites in `src/rpc/{dispatch,local,wss}.rs`. The row leaves out, as an implementation detail, the boxed `handle_config_map_key_delete` future that keeps `process_line` inside its stack budget. Everything else #9745 does lives in its owning crate and needs no runtime permission: `KnowledgeScope`, grant resolution, legacy assignment, `export_existing_owner`, the generation-checked `purge_archived_owner` and `rename_owner` in `zeroclaw-memory`; the scoped `KnowledgeTool` and the `model_routing_config` retirement check in `zeroclaw-tools`; the alias admission rule (`create_map_key_checked`, `ensure_knowledge_owner_retired`, `Config::ensure_map_key_for_path`) and the `read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` settings in `zeroclaw-config`; the HTTP adapters in `zeroclaw-gateway`; and the CLI paths in the `zeroclaw` binary. The row excludes per-principal ownership, the unwired Postgres graph (`knowledge_graph_pg.rs` is untouched), any new RPC method (the `Method` enum gains no variant), grant source, config key, store or persisted schema in the runtime (the existing archive bundle gains the `knowledge.json` artifact and its manifest counts), the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` (which still removes an agent without the cascade), the environment-override creation path (applied at config load without the retirement check), and any non-English locale beyond the three keys named. The `remove_agent` and environment-override items are pre-existing gaps #9745's body lists as out of scope. The row also says that it does not ratify the cascade's own landing in the crate (see below).
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge, so merging this pull request is what records the vote.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9647 and #9745 (head `123b8396f3`). Precedent: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062, the four row proposals open at the same table position.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #9745 gives every knowledge-graph row an owning agent and makes an agent's delete and rename carry that ownership with the alias: deletion exports the agent's knowledge, archives it next to the memory, cron and ACP exports the cascade already wrote, and purges it only when the archive is durable and still matches the store; rename moves ownership to the new alias; a committed delete or rename whose cleanup failed, or whose stores cannot be inspected, stays retryable on the RPC and gateway surfaces instead of reading as finished (the CLI's committed-rename retry is #10373); and no explicit config write can recreate an alias while its knowledge remains (an environment override that names a new agent is still applied at load, a pre-existing gap #9745 documents). The runtime half of that is the cascade itself, the RPC adapters that run it, and the knowledge tool's binding to the calling agent. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

### Why a row rather than relocation

Every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. The owned-state cascade sits in `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` on `master`, next to the delete preflight, and the RPC delete and rename adapters in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` already call it; the gateway and CLI call the same functions. It landed there on 2026-09-30 through #10621, after this table existed, and has no row of its own; this row covers #9745's changes to it and says so, and does not ratify that landing, which is a separate Core decision if one is wanted. The cascade reaches the cron store (`crate::cron`), the control-plane task store (`crate::control_plane`) and the runtime's Fluent catalogue (`crate::i18n`), all of which the holding crate still contains, so a crate of its own today would either pull those along or invert the dependency the kernel extraction is meant to settle. ADR-016 describes that case: extraction would establish a crate boundary the roadmap does not intend. #11701's proposed row (open, approved) names the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction as this subsystem's destination, and this row uses the same destination. The knowledge-specific logic that can live elsewhere already does: scope, grants, export and purge are in `zeroclaw-memory`, the tool in `zeroclaw-tools`, the admission rule in `zeroclaw-config`. What remains in the runtime is the lifecycle wiring between them.

### Coverage analysis

No row on `master` covers this work. All 47 active rows were read for the paths #9745 touches:

- `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`: no row names it. #11701 (open, approved) is the first row to touch the file, for #11301's rename recovery, and its scope cell excludes exactly this work: "No delete recovery, knowledge-graph follower, new follower store, new lifecycle operation, or non-English locale".
- `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`: named by the #10905, #10407, #11466/#11506, #10911, #11181, #10513/#10522, #11607, #9872/#10391, #11692, #11622, #11513, #11698, #11730, #11221, #11463 and #11286 rows. Each is limited to its own pull request and behavior (compaction, session prompts, config receipts, live-config publication, steering provenance, `sops.run`, the refresh pre-filter, the delegation ceiling call, budget warnings, message times, the profile projection, personality reload, delegate activity, tool selection, diff capture, one WSS regression). None covers the agent delete or rename adapters, alias admission, or the map-key delete response's `owned_state` field and `deleted: false` answer (the #11466/#11506 row covers only that response's `revision` receipt).
- `src/tools/mod.rs` and `src/tools/delegate.rs`: the #9872/#10391 bounded-delegation row covers rebuilding "a bounded delegate's context-sensitive tools for the target workspace", but is limited to #9872/#10391 and the caller ceiling; the #11221 row covers built-in tool selection and name reservation; the #11462 row covers delegate operator approvals; the #11465, #11473, #10331/#11450, #11292, #11730, #11456, #9579, #9447, #11698, #10911 and #10407 rows cover cancellation context, schema deferral, worker-loss recovery, progress, activity forwarding, resident-memory supervision, the docs skill, terminal handling, personality reload, live-config publication and session prompts. None covers binding the knowledge tool to a `KnowledgeScope` or rebinding it for a delegate. The #10911 row excludes a "new live consumer" of the live-config authority; the knowledge scope only reads the existing read-only handle per graph operation and registers nothing, which the row states.
- `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`: the #9597 row (task registration and settlement) and the #11292 row (progress persistence) do not cover a read-only residue count.
- `src/i18n.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,types,local,wss}.rs` and the locale files: each row naming them is limited to its own keys, fields, exports and tests.

The row therefore records the moved cascade and its additions together, so the holding crate's debt for this subsystem is legible in one place.

### Rebase note

Four other row proposals are open and append at the same table position: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062. milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(oidc): bind enrollment callbacks to the initiating browser
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, true-rebased onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bind gateway OIDC enrollment to the browser that started it. A copied callback URL can no longer reveal a token in a different browser.
  - Generate a separate 32-byte random secret for each flow. Keep only its hash in the existing `PendingPkce` record. Check the cookie before code exchange; refuse and consume mismatched flows.
  - Preserve concurrent tabs, one-time consumption, issuer/provider checks, and the original deadline for a valid capacity retry. The cookie grants no session or API access.
  - Add four endpoint regressions, update existing callback tests to carry their actual issued cookie, and document cookie scope and recovery.
- **Scope boundary:** Enrollment start/callback and their documentation. Dashboard sign-in remains in #11965. Configured origin (#12048), same-host HTTP ports (#12088), broader availability (#12049), and response zeroization (#12090) remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Clients that complete `/oidc/login/<alias>` through `/oidc/callback` must keep the issued browser cookie. Device flow and bearer-authenticated API routes retain their current behavior. The existing gateway `rand` dependency moves from dev to normal dependencies; no new package or lockfile change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12050. Related #11965 and #8289.

### What this does, simply

The browser login page returns a token that a user can copy into a client. Before this change, someone could start a login under their own account, then send its final URL to another person. That person could receive and use the wrong account's token.

The gateway now gives the starting browser a short-lived cookie. The final page requires that cookie. A different browser gets the existing refusal page, and no code is exchanged. Start a new login in the intended browser after a refusal; do not forward callback URLs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: independent review of the callback boundary and an A/B browser check are useful for this security change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, gateway enrollment HTTP routes and the callback page. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a test OIDC alias and two isolated browser profiles. Use dedicated test accounts. Keep the gateway scheme/host consistent. The captured mock-provider recipe and source hashes are in [the evidence bundle](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/README.md).
- **Steps to run:** Start a login in browser A. Capture the final callback URL before following it. Open that URL in browser B. Then retry it in A. Start two fresh flows in separate tabs of A and finish both normally.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** B receives `Sign-in not completed`, with no token exchange. A cannot replay that consumed flow. Both fresh tab flows succeed, each once. A normal same-browser return succeeds and clears only its flow cookie.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The callback lacks this browser check. The guard-removal negative control reproduces acceptance of a missing-cookie callback (200 instead of 400). A live provider or a full unpatched-daemon A/B run was not performed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical evidence: a bounded Ubuntu 24.04 job applied the exact patch to base `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`, checked all four source hashes, and ran Rust 1.98.0 tests, strict Clippy and the native browser fixture. Fresh upstream CI on the rebased head is recorded below. Independent Core/CODEOWNER security approvals remain required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The native browser check uses production enrollment routes, prefix and security headers over loopback HTTP, with a mock IdP. It is not the complete daemon, native TLS, dashboard popup integration, or real-provider acceptance. HTTPS cookie attributes and rejection of an unprefixed cookie have router assertions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
git diff --check
exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_oidc::tests:: -- --nocapture
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.95s
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0

# Temporary guard removal; require the selected regression to fail:
enrollment_binding_refuses_other_browsers_before_exchange_and_consumes_the_flow ... FAILED
left: 200
right: 400
# Exact bytes restored; repeat the OIDC suite:
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.89s

# Native browser fixture, then exact restoration and final suite:
5 browser assertions passed; same browser, isolated context, consumed replay and concurrent tabs
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 6.96s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes checked missing/wrong/duplicate cookies, consume-before-refusal, cookie-only API denial, concurrent flows, provider changes, issuer checks, original TTL and capacity retry. Source and dependency hashes were checked again. Both changed Markdown files passed pinned lint. No added documentation links need a new link target check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the existing success and refusal pages after the changed browser interaction; no layout redesign.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical source head `759ae4a5f1e4dffaa5d995503b222fc863e863d8`, exact four-file patch hash `945c228cff4dd8bf0a046630f7df1a22d3a14b34e6981eb64290d1e3fc9d55a9`; native Chrome `Chrome/156.0.8078.47`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway `localhost`, mock IdP `127.0.0.1`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Same-browser success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-same-context.png), [other-browser refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-other-context.png), and [machine receipt](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/receipt.json). All data is synthetic.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Follow the mock IdP page's link back to the prefixed callback: success with one exchange. Open a copied callback in another browser context: refusal with zero extra exchanges. Replay in the original context: refusal. Complete two fresh tab flows: both succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust execution was blocked by Application Control, so this source was validated on Linux. No full workspace suite or live IdP run is claimed. The first Linux attempt passed the Rust checks but failed because the mock page had a plain-text MIME type. That fixture was corrected; the complete successful run above uses the corrected harness. No browser assertion was relaxed.

### Refresh and dashboard integration — 2026-11-02

Current head: `4ef9abef542eb90153587669f2650cefc1abcb1d`. This is a true rebase onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. All four enrollment files and the exact patch are byte-for-byte unchanged from the historical tested revision above; range-diff reports the same single commit. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125043937233) passes, including Security, Lint and Test. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125040616464) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four new browser-binding regressions. Its checkout `0b80216b67e102089eebff5e2f6b7ff598a1e2bb` was verified to include this exact head. The earlier browser captures retain their named revision; no new native-TLS or real-provider acceptance run is claimed.

I also compared #11965 at `13486a064d2be1c05086e4ceaf6b08e94f2bc8b5`. Its delayed-start browser-family finding remains open and is separate from this per-flow enrollment binding. The branches overlap in `api_oidc.rs`; integration must keep one canonical binding in `PendingPkce`, checked before either exchange mode, with shared cookie parsing/cleanup and the original retry deadline. Preserve the dashboard's required ID token, provider pin, return/popup behavior and separate session-family/sign-out repair. Binding cleanup must coexist with the dashboard session cookie. This PR does not contain or validate that combined integration.

@IftekharUddin's [dependency and native-TLS proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6553383007) remains useful, separately attributed candidate evidence. The dependency repair is now inherited from master; no proposal commit was cherry-picked and no contributor source was replaced.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the existing discovery and token endpoints remain the only provider calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A new per-flow secret is sent only in an HttpOnly binding cookie; its hash is stored with the pending flow and compared in constant time. Cookies use SameSite=Lax and root Path with no Domain; HTTPS adds Secure and the __Host- prefix. A terminal consumed-flow response clears its cookie. The recorded transport scope preserves the cookie attributes chosen at issuance. A valid 503 retry keeps its original expiry. Remote deployments should use HTTPS; plain HTTP does not isolate applications on different ports of the same host.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for callers that complete an enrollment callback without the starting browser's cookie; this is the intentional security correction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Finish enrollment in the same browser that starts it and permit its cookie. If a callback was copied, the gateway restarted, or the cookie expired/was blocked, start a new login. Existing bearer clients and the device flow require no migration. The new field creates the browser-binding fact in the existing pending-flow store; it does not copy live policy.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the resulting squash commit through a reviewed PR, then restart the gateway. This restores the login-CSRF exposure, so use only as an incident response with an explicit exposure decision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Device flow is the alternative if browser cookies cannot be used.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A fresh same-browser login reaches `Sign-in not completed`; investigate cookie blocking, scheme/host changes and callback provenance. Do not log cookie secrets or token-bearing callback URLs.

Required CI passes. This is ready for independent Core/CODEOWNER security review, with Jordan for the manifest and Audacity for the gateway and documentation. The default high-risk review requirement is two independent Core approvals. I have not approved my own change. After adoption, #11965 should use one binding fact in `PendingPkce` for both modes while preserving its dashboard-specific return, popup and ID-token behavior.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The `call_channel!` doc comment in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/component.rs` said Wasmtime refuses every later call into a store whose call failed, for all four failure kinds it lists: a guest trap, exhausted fuel, a failed host import, and a result that could not be lifted.
  - In Wasmtime 48 only the first three set the store's `trapped` flag. `invoke_wasm_and_catch_traps` calls `set_trapped()` on an error from inside wasm, and `concurrent_disabled::may_enter` reads only that flag. A lift failure returns from `call_raw` before `post_return_impl`, so the export's post-return cleanup never runs and the call scope opened by `enter_guest_sync_call` stays open, but the next call still enters.
  - The comment now says so. The discard rule itself is unchanged and still right: a store whose cleanup was skipped is not one to reuse either.
- **Scope boundary:** Comment only. No code, behavior, test, docs-page, WIT, or config change.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. Related #11356, which introduced the comment, and #11402, which makes the same correction for `call_plugin_frame!`. The two PRs touch different macros in `component.rs` and merge in either order.

### What this does, simply

A code comment explains why the channel host throws away a plugin's loaded instance after certain failures. It got one of the four cases wrong: it said the WebAssembly runtime refuses to run anything in that instance again, which is true after a crash but not after a result the host could not read back. In that case the plugin's cleanup step was skipped instead, which is still a good reason to throw the instance away. This PR corrects the comment; nothing about how the host behaves changes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A, comment-only change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, and `Lint`, which also runs the comment-hygiene gate, cover the edited comment. Nothing else can change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The Wasmtime 48.0.3 sources behind the corrected sentence: `set_trapped` has one caller, `invoke_wasm_and_catch_traps` in `src/runtime/func.rs`; `TypedFunc::call` in `src/runtime/component/func/typed.rs` returns on a lift error before `post_return_impl`, which is where `exit_guest_sync_call` runs; and `may_enter` in `src/runtime/component/concurrent_disabled.rs` checks only `trapped`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no interface output changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Builds and tests, since a doc comment on a `macro_rules!` cannot change compiled output. The local comment-hygiene gate could not run (its `rg` binary fails to load `libpcre2` on this machine); the added lines contain no issue references or process notes, and the `Lint` job runs the gate.

prs.title: feat(channels): Gemini speech-to-speech broker channel (PR1: daemon-side core)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** PR1 of the accepted Gemini speech-to-speech broker
  RFC (#8780, tracker #10406). Adds a feature-gated `speech_to_speech` channel
  where a realtime voice model (Gemini Live) owns the caller audio and reaches
  the ZeroClaw agent through exactly one bridge function, `consult_agent`
  (+ `end_session`) — the voice model never sees tools; only the agent does.
  Vendors a small MIT `gemini-live` crate for the wire protocol. Adds config
  surface (`channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>`), broker-persona resolution
  confined to the agent workspace, consult-history binding, and a startup
  retention/cost privacy warning.
- **Scope boundary:** No audio-frame transport (mic in / speaker out) yet — the
  channel ships its session engine and config surface and stays inert (parks
  until cancelled) until the transport lands in a follow-up PR. No changes to
  existing channels, the tool pipeline, or provider wiring.
- **Blast radius:** Off by default (`channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature).
  When the feature is off, nothing compiles in. Touches `zeroclaw-channels`,
  `zeroclaw-config` (new optional section + one warning), `zeroclaw-api`
  (`ChannelKind::SpeechToSpeech`), and adds the vendored `gemini-live` crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8780, Related #10406.

### What this does, simply

A phone call is answered by a voice model, not by the agent. It chats with the
caller and, whenever something needs the agent, passes the question through one
bridge function and speaks the answer back in its own words. The agent's tools
stay out of the voice model's reach entirely.


- **Review rounds addressed (refreshed onto current master).** The branch was
  re-applied on top of master; the conflicts were content conflicts
  (workspace members, the config warning collector, the generated feature
  lists) and were resolved keeping master's side plus this branch's addition.
  The blocking findings are answered as follows.
  - *Control messages lost on reconnect.* Every `ClientText` and
    `ToolResponse` now carries a receipt the transport driver resolves to
    `Written`, `Discarded` or `Failed`: written once the transport accepts the
    frame, discarded when the command is dropped in the backoff window, failed
    when the transport refuses the write. Commands queued during reconnect and
    setup stay queued and are written after the reopen, so nothing is replayed
    twice. `Channel::send` waits for that verdict (bounded) and reports a lost
    reply as a delivery failure instead of a silent success; no backlog is
    re-sent behind the caller's back, and an older turn completion no longer
    retires a newer reply because there is no shared pending list to clear.
    A tool acknowledgement has no caller to answer, so a discarded or refused
    one is logged with its call id and listed again when the call ends.
    Exactly-once across a broken connection is not attempted.
  - *A timed-out reply written late.* The queued command and its receipt now
    share one claim. When `send()` runs out of time it expires the receipt:
    a reply the driver has not started writing is withdrawn (the driver skips
    it when it reaches it), so a reply reported undelivered is never spoken
    after the agent has answered again; a write already in progress cannot be
    withdrawn and is reported as undecided, not as a confirmed failure.
    Teardown gives the acknowledgements still undecided the same budget before
    counting any of them lost: the session handle is released so the driver
    drains, the verdicts are awaited up to the deadline, and only an
    acknowledgement the driver never started is reported as unanswered.
  - *History and delayed replies.* Every attached call mints its own identity
    and carries it in `sender` and `reply_target`, so two calls on one alias no
    longer share a conversation history. The orchestrator echoes that address
    back as `SendMessage::recipient`, and a reply naming a call that has ended
    is dropped with a log instead of being spoken to whoever is on the line.
  - *Staged outbound surfaces.* Both spellings are declared in the one-shot and
    announcement intentional-unsupported dispositions, so the feature-enabled
    registration guards pass without new outbound functionality.
  - *SOP identity.* `ChannelKind::VoiceBroker` is renamed to `SpeechToSpeech`,
    so configuration, inbound topics (`speech_to_speech/<alias>`), attribution
    and discovery all use one token; the sender label follows the same name. A
    configured alias now appears in the trigger projection with its setup path,
    covered by a new registry test.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the channel has no audio transport
  yet, so there is no end-to-end caller flow to exercise; behavior is covered
  by unit tests on setup assembly, the security tool-set invariant, persona
  confinement, history binding, and the parked-listen contract.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `00bad6402b1e6e209862ba37b7d05d0f5fa7cefc`, the required CI run is linked from the checks tab; the `Test` job compiles the feature-enabled channel and runs its tests, and `Lint` runs clippy with `-D warnings` over the workspace, which is what caught the dead test helper in the previous iteration. Before pushing, the same head passed a fork-side Linux run of fmt, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` with `-D warnings`, clippy, and the `gemini-live` and `zeroclaw-channels` lib tests with `channel-speech-to-speech` enabled: https://github.com/metalmon/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39140694835. That run's one failure is `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` in `zeroclaw-providers`, a local-mock HTTP test on a file this branch does not touch, which fails on that runner on every current head; the `gemini-live`, feature-enabled `speech_to_speech` and full `zeroclaw-channels` suites pass there. The branch sits on master at `dc8c850891`; the master head `c473221313` fails `cargo fmt --check` on `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`, which is not from this branch. `Security` is green on this head. The `Source Image Build` jobs fail on every current PR, including this one: the Dockerfile prefetch stage does not stage the `sign_manifest` example that master added to `zeroclaw-plugins`, so cargo refuses the manifest before any source from this branch is involved; an upstream fix is open.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live audio round trip was run; audio transport remains deferred. The lifecycle follow-ups the last round listed as nonblocking (an awaited queue send delaying `stop()`, cancellation of `run_session` skipping detachment, `goAway` after a successful connection counting toward the reconnect budget) are not addressed here and are carried into the audio-transport PR.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p gemini-live                                   # 45 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-speech-to-speech --lib speech_to_speech
```

- **Tests added for this round:**
  - `an_expired_control_is_never_written_and_an_in_flight_one_says_so`
    (`gemini-live`) — with the transport stalled on one write, expiring the
    queued control reports `Unwritten` and the driver skips it once the stall
    lifts, while expiring the stalled one reports `InFlight`; `FakeTransport`
    gained `stall_writes_after` so a hanging write is actually exercised.
  - `a_reply_that_expires_during_the_reconnect_is_never_written_after_the_reopen`
    — the gated reconnect outlasts `CONTROL_ACK_TIMEOUT`; `send()` reports the
    reply undelivered, and after the reopen the reply never reaches the new
    connection.
  - `a_reply_whose_write_is_still_in_progress_is_reported_as_unknown_not_lost`
    — a write the transport has taken and not completed is reported as
    undecided, not withdrawn.
  - `model_end_session_closes` now asserts the final acknowledgement is on the
    wire before `run_session` returns, which is the bounded teardown settle.
  - `a_written_control_reports_written_and_a_refused_one_reports_failed`
    (`gemini-live`, previous round) — the receipt resolves to `Written` when the transport
    accepts the frame and to `Failed` when it refuses it; `FakeTransport`
    gained `fail_writes_after` so a refused write is actually exercised rather
    than ending through the idle timeout.
  - `a_reply_enqueued_while_the_driver_reconnects_is_written_once_after_the_reopen`
    — a reply queued during connect/setup reaches the reopened connection
    exactly once; a control dropped in the backoff window reports `Discarded`
    and is not replayed.
  - `an_earlier_turn_completion_does_not_cancel_a_newer_reply` — a buffered
    `TurnComplete` from the previous turn does not affect a reply queued after
    it.
  - `a_reply_the_provider_refuses_is_reported_as_a_failure` — `send()` returns
    an error naming the refusal instead of `Ok`.
  - `an_acknowledgement_that_is_never_written_is_reported_with_its_call_id` —
    a tool acknowledgement discarded with the dead connection shows up in the
    call's unanswered-tool-call report under its id.
  - `a_reply_for_an_ended_call_is_not_spoken_into_the_next_one` and
    `speech_to_speech_alias_projects_under_its_ingress_identity` carry over
    from the previous round.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The setup builder emits exactly `{consult_agent, end_session}` in `setup.tools[]` (security invariant test); the broker persona path is resolved relative to and confined to the agent workspace and never falls back to `AGENTS.md`; `listen()` parks until cancelled rather than returning `Ok(())` immediately; the configured `model` id is threaded onto the wire via `SetupConfig.model_id_override` without the crate guessing api-version compatibility (Gemini rejects an incompatible combo itself). Reconnect: a `sessionResumptionUpdate` with `resumable: false` now clears the stored handle so a stale handle is never replayed; the crate discards commands during backoff and emits `SessionOpened { is_reconnect, resumed }`. Not verified: live audio round-trip (no transport yet).
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** — reads a
  broker persona file, resolved relative to and hard-confined within the agent
  workspace (path canonicalized and checked to stay under the workspace root);
  it never reads `AGENTS.md` or escapes the workspace.
- New external network calls? **Yes** — the session API opens a connection to a fixed `wss://` Gemini Live endpoint. The configured channel listener remains inert in this slice, so enabling an alias does not yet open that session. The separately exported raw `connect_ws` helper accepts a supplied URL and does not enforce `wss://` on its direct, no-proxy branch.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes** — adds a channel-local `api_key: Option<String>` field marked `#[secret]` and `x-secret`. This slice does not yet wire that key into a live session; production credential resolution is deferred with the listener integration. It does not currently resolve an existing Gemini provider profile.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?
  **No**.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes,
  bounded** — the voice model can only reach the agent through `consult_agent`;
  it never receives tool schemas or results, so a compromised/confused voice
  turn cannot invoke tools. Caller audio flows to the provider; a startup
  warning (`speech_to_speech_provider_retention`) discloses provider retention
  and that enabled transcription is billed as text tokens on top of audio.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — new optional config section; absent config and
  the default build are unaffected (feature off by default).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — adds
  `[channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>]` (all fields optional with defaults).
  No env or CLI changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** — vendored crate is edition 2021;
  workspace crates stay edition 2024 on the existing floor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>`; or simply build
  without `--features channel-speech-to-speech` — the channel is off by default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature
  (off by default); per-alias `enabled = false`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** startup warning
  `speech_to_speech_provider_retention` per enabled alias; a live session logs a
  `wss://` connect. With the feature off, no code path is reachable.

prs.title: test(rpc): cover competing TUI signing keys
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, rebased onto b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855.
- **What changed and why:** Extract the remaining 42-line regression from #11422. It verifies that a valid key in the runtime-data directory cannot become the TUI signing authority when the canonical config key is corrupt.
- **Scope boundary:** One existing test copied without changes. No production code, key derivation, key provisioning, configuration, authentication policy or inherited OIDC stack changes.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime unit-test coverage for canonical signing-key selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11576. Supersedes #11422's own supplemental test slice only. The old draft's inherited prerequisites and downstream history are not replaced by this PR.

### What this does, simply

The signing key belongs beside `config.toml`. A second valid key in the data directory must not substitute for it. The test checks separate directories, a competing data key, a colocated control, and refusal when the canonical key is corrupt. It also checks that the corrupt key is not overwritten.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; the deterministic unit test and fault-injection control cover this test-only extraction.

### How I tested

Historical tested revision: 90a828b72e8fa0c68fc341122a85bc4ab69e6069. Local Ubuntu 24.04, Rust/Cargo 1.98.0, default runtime features, two test threads.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::tui_identity::tests -- --test-threads=2
test result: ok. 25 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5848 filtered out
```

I temporarily made `for_config` fall back to an existing data-directory key after canonical-key failure. The suite then reported `24 passed; 1 failed`; only the new test failed, at the signing-disabled assertion. I restored the source byte-for-byte and reran the suite: `25 passed; 0 failed`. The fault is not in this commit.

The focused `rustfmt` check and `git diff --check` passed. The first offline attempt lacked dependency metadata; the locked online retry and final offline run passed without a lockfile change. The original head also passed [hosted Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40070750874/job/120803442887), including this named regression, and its required gate. These results predate the refresh below. Those historical local checks were focused; the refreshed hosted matrix is recorded below.

**Refresh (2026-11-02):** True-rebased the single test commit onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. New head: `ec328eeec20b366b3b2856240923e1be238fdd3d`. The complete `tui_identity.rs` file and the 42-line patch are identical to the original reviewed test. Production source is unchanged from current master. `git diff --check` passes. New-head [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41366100918/job/125029752578) passes, including Security, Test and the required platform/feature jobs. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41366100918/job/125026483558) records `config_signing_key_is_used_when_runtime_data_lives_elsewhere` passing. CI checked out `9b1de55ff68612abb741061577936df61bc8de83`, verified against this head. Two static adversarial passes checked fresh registry instances, the valid competing-key control and preservation of the corrupt canonical key. Self-review does not replace independent approval.

- **Known coverage limits:** No live remote-TUI session or historical-signature migration smoke is claimed. Hosted execution is the linked matrix; cross-compilation does not establish native execution on another platform. The test confirms the registry boundary; existing callers retain their signing-required policy.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface changes.
- **Beyond tests:** Two adversarial passes checked the incremental coverage against #11576, the fresh registry instances, the negative-key oracle, and preservation of the production source. The complete production prefix is identical to pinned master.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions or filesystem access scope: No.
- New external network calls: No.
- Secrets or credentials handling changed: No. Production behavior is unchanged; the test uses temporary generated keys.
- Personal data or real identities in fixtures: No. Fixture text is synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text changed: No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible: Yes.
- Config, environment, CLI or wire surface changed: No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor or dependencies changed: No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback

Revert the test commit. No data migration or feature toggle. A regression in signing authority selection causes the test to fail.

## Supersede Attribution

- Superseded slice: #11422 by @Aarlington, supplemental test only.
- Scope carried forward: The single regression is copied unchanged from my #11422 slice, whose own diff is one test relative to #11411.
- Human co-author trailers: No; this extraction carries my own test. #11576 by @tidux already landed the production fix, which remains unchanged in the base.
- The conflicting stack is not required to land this coverage. The old draft remains open until its replacement and downstream dependency handling are settled.

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Agent` renders the `## Project Context` block (the personality files: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md` when injected) once, on its first system-prompt build, and reuses that text every turn. Before this, `IdentitySection` re-read the files on every turn's rebuild. The system prompt heads the provider's cached prefix, so any edit to one of those files made the next request of every live session of that agent miss the prompt cache for the whole conversation (#11696).
  - New `PromptContext::identity_snapshot` carries the pre-rendered text. `prompt::render_identity_section` is the shared renderer, and `None` keeps today's read-now behavior for other builders.
  - New `Agent::reload_personality` re-reads the files on purpose and rebuilds the system prompt. It's exposed as `session/reload_context` (RPC, `sessions:update` grant, owner-only, refused with `SESSION_BUSY` while a turn holds the agent) and as the ZeroCode `/reload-context` command. After its session lookups, the handler re-resolves the caller's current grants and holds it to ownership of the admitted record right before the reload, as `session/append` and `session/abort` do. ZeroCode says whether anything changed and that the changed prompt may reduce cache reuse on the next request.
  - A turn now makes sure the history starts with a system prompt. A resumed session whose snapshot failed (for example a broken `identity.json`) used to keep its history with no system message, and later turns never added one. Now each turn inserts it once the snapshot succeeds; until then the turn fails with the load error.
- **Scope boundary:** this doesn't touch the CLI `loop_::run` path or the channel orchestrator (the channel path already builds once). It also doesn't touch the `tool_search` deferred-tools section, which still changes the prompt when a tool is activated (noted in #11696). No config switch.
- **Blast radius:** long-lived `Agent` sessions (ZeroCode/ACP, gateway WS). **Behavior change:** an agent that edits its own rules mid-session no longer sees the new text in its system prompt on the next turn. It already has the edit in its conversation context, and other live sessions get it on `/reload-context` or in a new session.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11696. Related #8321.
- **Holding-crate exception:** every `zeroclaw-runtime` file this PR changes (`src/agent/{agent,prompt}.rs`, `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`) is inside the merged personality-snapshot row from #11697 (ADR-016). Since `eb4822217`, `src/agent/personality.rs` is unchanged from `master`: the snapshot path calls the existing `load_personality_files` and rereads only the files it reported missing. If a reread finds text that the first read missed (a file saved mid-read), it captures again, up to 3 times, and then fails rather than pin a partial snapshot. Any read error other than not-found also fails. So no amendment to that row is needed.

### What this does, simply

Each agent has a few notes files that are pasted into the start of every conversation. ZeroClaw re-read those files before every turn. If anything in them changed, even one line, the provider couldn't reuse its cached copy of the conversation, and the next request was billed at full price. That happened for every open session of that agent, not just the one that edited the file. With long sessions this cost about $1–2 per session per edit.

Now a session reads the notes once and keeps that copy. New sessions see edits right away. An open session picks them up when you type `/reload-context`. Its prompt then changes, so the next request may get less use out of the provider's cache; you choose when that happens.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a provider that reports cached input tokens. Two ZeroCode sessions of the same agent, each a few turns in.
- **Steps to run:** append a line to the agent's workspace `AGENTS.md`. Send one message in each session. Check `cached_input_tokens` in the cost ledger. Then run `/reload-context` in one session and send one more message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first request after the edit stays cached in both sessions. `/reload-context` shows "Context reloaded…", and only that session's next request reads less from the cache. A second `/reload-context` says "Context unchanged".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the first request after the edit is uncached (`cached_input_tokens` null/0) in both sessions.

### How I tested

- **AIEOS failure path (head `51e26a3c3564`):** a configured `identity.json` that can't be read or parsed now fails the snapshot capture with `Could not load AIEOS identity: …` instead of silently falling back to the Markdown files. A failed `/reload-context` keeps the previous snapshot and system prompt, and a failed first capture isn't pinned, so the next build after the file is fixed captures the full identity. The non-snapshot renderer stays lenient. New tests: `mixed_aieos_markdown_reload_failure_keeps_previous_snapshot` and `mixed_aieos_markdown_failed_first_capture_is_not_pinned` (each covers malformed JSON, a directory in place of the file, and a missing file, with `AGENTS.md` still present, then recovery after repair), plus `legacy_identity_renderer_tolerates_aieos_load_failure`. With only the test commit applied to `19c478e3b0`, both mixed tests fail (`0 passed; 2 failed`: the old renderer accepts the degraded render). On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5889 passed; 2 failed`, the two being `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `19c478e3b0`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/clippy jobs for `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Current head `650ab4b2a761`** (`de9462e2f` plus the fixes for Greptile 4429288963 and 4429288973), Linux x86_64:
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-fail-fast` → `5914 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, including the new `resumed_history_gets_its_system_prompt_once_the_identity_loads`, `personality_capture_rereads_a_file_that_gained_text_during_the_read`, `personality_capture_fails_when_a_file_keeps_changing` and `personality_capture_accepts_files_that_are_really_missing_or_empty`.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.
  - CI for this head is pending. The Security job fails on every current PR run because of new wasmtime advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424) until #12129 lands. This PR doesn't touch wasmtime.
- **Earlier head `de9462e2f8ec`** (`eb4822217` plus a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`): `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc:: tools::delegate` → `2547 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored`. Clippy and fmt clean.
- **Earlier head `51e26a3c3564`:** CI Required Gate green.
- **Commands run and tail output** at `3794bcf4a254` (rebased onto `ee2f5f58f7d7`), through the remote cargo wrapper:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- reload_context a_reload_` → `4 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5811 passed; 2 failed`. The two failures are `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `ee2f5f58f7d7` in a clean detached worktree. This PR doesn't touch `relay`.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode` → `1550 passed; 2 failed`. `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` also fail on `ee2f5f58f7d7` (the second is timing-sensitive; it passed once and failed three times there).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → clean.
- **Earlier runs** at `f0fd4f895a78`, before the rebase:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- personality_edit_mid_session session_reload_context new_session_methods_are_classified remote_dispatch_rejects_every_foreign build_system_prompt_omits_memory_md method_all_no_duplicates method_from_wire_roundtrip agent::prompt::` → `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc::dispatch tools::delegate` → `2149 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which fails the same way on the base `f12da7462a0f` in a clean detached worktree (`0 passed; 1 failed`). It isn't caused by this change.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode -- input_bar chat::tests::old_daemon reload` → `160 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files → clean.
- **Regression guard:** `personality_edit_mid_session_keeps_system_prompt_byte_stable` runs two streamed turns with an `AGENTS.md` edit between them and asserts the provider-visible system prompts are byte-identical. It then checks that `reload_personality` reports the change and that turn 3 carries the new text. With the snapshot disabled (render every turn) it fails: `assertion left == right failed: a mid-session AGENTS.md edit must not change the cached system prompt`.
- **Authority regression guard:** `a_reload_is_refused_when_its_grant_is_revoked_while_it_waits` and `a_reload_by_a_demoted_administrator_is_held_to_ownership` pause the reload after its gate, republish the policy, then release it. Both expect `FORBIDDEN` and an agent that still holds its first snapshot. `a_reload_of_an_own_session_survives_an_unrelated_policy_change` is the permitted control. With the recheck removed, the first two fail and the control still passes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live provider cache check on this head. Real screenshots of the `/reload-context` outcomes, built from `725dcbbf69`, are linked under Screenshots below.
### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11698#issuecomment-6514495140 (macOS Terminal.app captures of `725dcbbf69`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new RPC re-reads the same workspace files the prompt already read, for the session's own agent, and needs `sessions:update` plus session ownership like `session/rename`.
